title: Grill-me needed: how should automatic transcript Provenance lookup identify adapter layouts?
description:
Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing -- it needs a focused decision.

## Question

The maintainer wants Provenance transcript lookup to work for every supported adapter by default, without adding transcript_layout to the louiselm config.

Today transcript_layout is explicit because Agent names are arbitrary labels and the locator intentionally avoids guessing which external on-disk transcript store belongs to a Session.

## Decision required

Choose the automatic lookup contract:

1. Infer a layout from the configured Agent name or command/args (with explicit override for custom adapters). This is convenient but command wrappers and arbitrary names make inference incomplete or potentially wrong.
2. Search all supported transcript layouts and accept one unique match, reporting ambiguity explicitly. This removes the config burden but broadens filesystem discovery and could encounter identical ACP Session ids in multiple stores.
3. Another maintainer-approved identity/registration mechanism.

## Context/evidence

- lua/louiselm/session/locator.lua currently searches only layouts explicitly declared by Agent definitions.
- Supported layouts are claude, codex, openai-compatible, and copilot.
- lua/louiselm/config.lua defaults agents to {} and transcript_layout to empty.
- Live chat transcripts are already louiselm-owned and automatic; this request concerns Agent-owned historical transcripts shown through Provenance.
- Existing Provenance behavior renders unresolved Sessions explicitly when no layout is configured.

## Threads worth pulling

- Whether the maintainer accepts implicit discovery under known default roots (~/.claude, CODEX_HOME, etc.).
- How to handle collisions and missing layouts without presenting the wrong transcript.
- Whether adapter identity from ACP initialize/serverInfo is stable enough to map to a layout.
- Whether custom adapters must remain explicitly configured.
- Security/privacy expectations when Provenance inspects external Agent transcript stores.
close_reason: Design resolved by maintainer approval of unique-match automatic lookup.

comments.author: codex/01a05142-72b8-73b0-9123-9fbef695a8cd
comments.text: Maintainer approved option 2: search all supported transcript stores, accept exactly one match, and report ambiguity instead of guessing. This is the confirmed contract for implementation.

title: Automatically resolve Provenance transcripts across supported adapters
description:
Implement the approved automatic Provenance transcript lookup contract from louiselm-00tq.

## Contract

- When no Agent transcript_layout is configured, inspect all supported transcript layouts using their default roots.
- Return the path when exactly one layout contains the requested Session.
- Return an explicit unresolved/ambiguous error when zero or multiple layouts contain it.
- An explicit transcript_layout remains authoritative and searches only that layout.
- Preserve arbitrary Agent names and do not infer layout from names or commands.

## Testing

- No configured layout + exactly one match resolves.
- No configured layout + no matches remains unresolved.
- No configured layout + duplicate matches reports ambiguity and never chooses.
- Explicit layout preserves existing behavior.
- Keep filesystem roots injectable in tests.
close_reason: Automatic unique-match Provenance lookup implemented; 749 MiniTest cases and all quality gates pass.

comments.author: codex/01a05142-72b8-73b0-9123-9fbef695a8cd
comments.text: Implemented in session/locator.lua. No transcript_layout now searches every supported layout with injected/default roots; exactly one match resolves, multiple matches return an explicit ambiguity error, and explicit layout configuration remains scoped. Added locator regressions and updated Provenance expectations. Lesson: omission is now automatic discovery, while an explicit layout is a narrowing override; no AGENTS.md rule or unresolved design question remains.

title: Reject unsupported ACP reverse requests with method-not-found
description:
LouiseLM silently ignores every agent-to-client JSON-RPC request except `session/request_permission`. `lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:52-65` transfers ownership of every request to the Session callback, but `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:507-510` returns without responding for unknown methods. A blocking extension request therefore remains unanswered and can park the Agent turn indefinitely.

Evidence: xAI Grok Build explicitly blocks its tool loop while awaiting reverse-request responses (`crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/session/pending_interaction.rs:1-8` at xai-org/grok-build commit 72a61251fcffb464bcc687aeb5a998e5a98ec0c9). CodeCompanion PR #3357 adds a `-32601 Method not found` fallback at `lua/codecompanion/acp/init.lua:787-815` for this reason.

Acceptance:
- Every valid unsupported agent-to-client request receives one JSON-RPC error response with code `-32601`.
- Supported permission requests retain existing behavior.
- Notifications remain ignorable and receive no response.
- Regression coverage proves an unsupported request cannot remain pending.

This is protocol-generic. Grok question/plan support is separate.
close_reason: Unsupported Session reverse requests receive -32601; notifications remain one-way. gate:tests/session/api_spec.lua:1685

comments.author: codex/01a068c9-6a59-7580-a997-39c4371b86ae
comments.text: Red: Session spec observed 2 writes, expected 3. Green: unsupported request gets one -32601 response; matching notification adds none. Gates: 64/64 focused, 819/819 full, StyLua, LuaLS, API appendix, LuaCATS, vimdoc, diff check. Lesson routing: issue-local evidence here; no AGENTS.md rule or design question warranted.

title: Root cgroup CI fixture creates rejected Sessions root
description:
GitHub Actions cargo (skills-core) fails before exercising root-owned Session cgroup containment because its test fixture creates the Sessions root with a mode masked by the workflow umask.

## Observed

GitHub Actions run 33901757840, job 101117237965, 2026-09-04, step "Test root-owned Session cgroup containment":

`the pinned backend prepares the Session: Refused("Sessions root '/tmp/.tmp9Toy0D/sessions' must be a root-owned 0711 directory")`

The step exits 101; every later privileged skills-core acceptance step is skipped.

## Symptoms

- GitHub CI reports cargo (skills-core) failed although format, lint, ordinary tests, and the preceding host-identity acceptance pass.
- The intended cgroup migration attack is never attempted.

## Root cause

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:330` starts the library test under `umask 077`. `skills-core/src/sandbox.rs:2218-2221` creates the fixture Sessions root with `DirBuilder::mode(0o711)` but does not reset its permissions after creation, so the umask yields mode 0700. Production validation at `skills-core/src/sandbox.rs:1124-1131` correctly requires root-owned 0711 and rejects the fixture.

## Why it was not caught

The ordinary `cargo test` invocation does not set `LOUISELM_TEST_PINNED_CGROUP_ESCAPE`, so this root/cgroup acceptance returns early. The failure appears only in the dedicated sudo workflow step.

## Fix direction

Keep the strict workflow umask. After fixture creation, explicitly set the Sessions root to 0711, matching the fixture's explicit permission handling for its parent and runtime root. Do not weaken production validation or remove the umask.

## Acceptance

- The dedicated GitHub Actions cgroup-containment step reaches and passes the migration-attack assertions.
- The later privileged skills-core acceptance steps run instead of being skipped.

## Not covered

The failed run provides no evidence about the cgroup containment behavior itself because setup stopped before the sandbox was prepared.
close_reason: Root fixture remains 0711 under strict umask and all privileged gates pass. gate:.github/workflows/ci.yml:308

comments.author: codex/01a06a99-3443-7843-b88d-52c47007cd42
comments.text: Fix: explicitly chmod the root-owned Sessions fixture to 0711 after creation, so workflow umask 077 cannot change its required contract. Production mode validation and the strict workflow umask remain unchanged. Local fmt, clippy, and full cargo test pass; the exact root/cgroup acceptance requires GitHub Actions because this workstation has no passwordless sudo or writable root cgroup.

Local cargo fmt, clippy, and full cargo test also pass. title: Beads inspector prompts instead of using the valid issue under the cursor
description:
Pressing <leader>lB in a LouiseLM Session while the cursor is on a valid louiselm Beads issue ID opens the manual prompt instead of invoking br show for the issue. Manual ID entry is a workaround, but cursor-based inspection is unreliable.

## Observed

Seen in the live Neovim session on 2026-08-28, ACP Session claude/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d. Screenshot evidence: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260828_0812_1920x1200_1787897545.png

The screenshot shows a LouiseLM chat buffer named louiselm://session-1 with a valid issue reference visible in the transcript, including louiselm-k1fv, while the command-line prompt is active with the exact text:

> Beads issue id:

The prompt appeared immediately after invoking <leader>lB.

## Symptoms

- The user invokes <leader>lB on a valid louiselm Beads issue ID.
- Instead of opening the issue detail view, LouiseLM asks for the issue ID.
- Entering the ID manually is required as a workaround.

## Root cause

Unknown. The prompt is the fallback in lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:208-230, reached when current_issue_id at lines 162-166 returns nil. The likely fault is in issue_id_at_cursor at lines 32-52 or in the buffer and cursor coordinates supplied to it. This needs a reproduction that records the exact line text and zero-based cursor column. The issue ID grammar itself is accepted by valid_issue_id at lines 24-27.

## Why it was not caught

tests/ui/beads_spec.lua covers a simple one-line case with the cursor explicitly placed inside louiselm-kpod and the no-ID and multiple-ID prompt fallbacks. It does not cover long wrapped transcript lines, the real chat buffer cursor position, or a valid issue reference in the live rendering context.

## Fix direction

Capture the exact live buffer line and cursor position at the point of <leader>lB, then fix the narrowest shared cursor-ID detection boundary. Preserve the existing ambiguity behavior: prompt when there is no valid issue under the cursor or multiple issue IDs on the line. Add a regression using the observed live line shape and cursor location without copying sensitive prompt content.

## Acceptance

- With the cursor on a valid louiselm Beads issue ID in a LouiseLM Session, <leader>lB invokes br show for that ID without opening the manual prompt.
- The existing prompt fallback remains for no-ID and ambiguous multiple-ID cases.
- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.

## Not covered

The screenshot does not preserve the exact pre-command cursor byte column or prove whether the failure is caused by wrapped display coordinates, cursor placement, or parser matching. No code change was made in this report.
close_reason: done

comments.author: claude/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d
comments.text:
Fixed in 729c3f2: restored the br-where prefix-scoped cursor matcher that louiselm-fxsp had added, which a3467a5 (this morning's cwd fix) unintentionally dropped in favor of a fully generic hyphenated-token matcher. That generic matcher counted ordinary prose compounds ("time-travel", "vocabulary-drop") as candidate issue IDs, inflating the line's ambiguity count past 1 even when only one real issue ID was present.

Regression test added (tests/ui/beads_spec.lua) reproducing the exact false-positive shape. Full suite green (0 fails), StyLua clean, LuaLS zero diagnostics.

Live-verified against the running Neovim instance (after syncing the installed plugin copy at ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim to 729c3f2, which had been pinned at bbe82e7): reproduced the exact scenario -- a line containing louiselm-f8r1 plus the unrelated hyphenated words -- with the cursor on the real ID. Before the fix this prompted; after, it opens louiselm-f8r1 directly with no prompt.

Not yet closed per AGENTS.md live-acceptance: this was reproduced via RPC against the live instance, not by the maintainer's own <leader>lB keypress. Leaving open for that confirmation.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Additional finding from live use 2026-08-28: <leader>lB matches a bare louiselm-xxx issue ID under the cursor, but not a markdown-bold-wrapped **louiselm-xxx** (e.g. in a rendered chat transcript). The cursor matcher likely doesn't strip/account for surrounding ** markers when extracting the hyphenated token, so bold-formatted issue refs fall through to the manual-prompt fallback.

comments.author: claude/b59dc4cb-7c9d-4efc-908a-2cca0884acca
comments.text:
Live-accepted by the maintainer. The remaining open question wasn't the fix itself -- 729c3f2's prefix-scoped matcher was correct on inspection and in the unit suite -- but that the maintainer's own long-running Neovim process had loaded lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua (and its module-load-time 'local Beads = require("louiselm.ui.beads")') a few minutes *before* 729c3f2 was committed. Lua's require() cache means the fixed file on disk had no effect on that process; retesting live only reproduced the pre-fix behavior (still prompted on a line with louiselm-04cy + time-travel).

Confirmed root cause via live RPC introspection: nvim start time (09:33:29) predated the fix commit (09:37:37) by ~4 minutes. Recommended a full Neovim restart + :LouiselmResume rather than hot-patching the running plugin state, since command.lua's M.register() would reset the live chat upvalue backing the maintainer's active session.

After restarting Neovim and resuming claude/05f3738e-26f0-4f87-8d8e-2af8dfd11aca, the maintainer confirmed <leader>lB now works as intended. Closing per AGENTS.md live-acceptance. --json

title: Grill-me needed: how does initial conformance waiver approval precede launch?
description: Do not resolve this lifecycle choice in passing; confirm the initial-admission workflow with the maintainer. Existing policy ucj1/j8phy/85btg fixes launcher-owned measurement and broker-owned exact approval, but not the pre-admission interaction. Current launch_supervisor.rs consumes the single-use authorization, acquires identity and prepares the confined tree before inspect_conformance; refusal cleans up. Broker waiver control requires an already admitted Session worker, and initial broker exchanges have a five-second deadline. Remaining d6fv.6.3 work needs authenticated evidence and approval before admission. Proposed choice: separate prepare/approve phase, no prepared Agent tree during human review, exact request/policy binding, bounded trusted launcher observation, broker-owned durable preview/receipt, and fresh conformance revalidation at actual launch; alternative is keeping an initial launcher awaiting operator approval. Confirm lifecycle before choosing a new privileged inspection entrypoint or extending the launch handshake. Existing live-waiver path and non-conformance refusals remain valid. No root install, policy activation or automatic launch authorized. Source Session codex/01a0d1d7-2bbb-77b2-90f2-5e87840a2e6b, 2026-09-24.
design: Confirmed by maintainer with ok on 2026-09-24, Session codex/01a0d1d7-2bbb-77b2-90f2-5e87840a2e6b: use separate prepare -> approve -> launch. No prepared Agent process tree while human reviews. Preparation grants no launch authority. Broker owns exact authenticated preview/approval and durable receipt; launcher owns protected host measurement. Bind exact Session/request/policy; actual launch freshly reevaluates conformance and waiver validity. Ordinary approval policies unchanged. No installed activation or root deployment implicit. Implementation stays in d6fv.6.3; this decision alone proves no executable behavior. Lesson: separate human review from bounded single-use launch transaction.
close_reason: none:design-confirmed Separate prepare/approve/launch confirmed; exact contract and provenance in design. Implementation remains d6fv.6.3.

title: Live process-tree snapshot comparison intermittently fails
description:
The full skills-core gate intermittently fails the process-tree handle test when two consecutive reads observe different live cgroup membership. This prevents a clean full-gate verdict for unrelated changes.

## Observed
2026-09-17, codex/01a0ad78-35bc-77a1-b528-8d9d8e1538b9, while verifying louiselm-qbr.5.1.4. Outside ACP:
systemd-run --user --pipe --wait --collect --working-directory=/home/lotso/code/louiselm --setenv PATH="$PATH" --setenv CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only ./scripts/test-skills-core --quiet -- --test-threads=1
Unit run-p2172584-i6379063.service. tests/sandbox.rs:404:
prepared_and_running_sessions_expose_their_dynamic_process_tree
assertion left == right failed
left: [2194875]
right: [2194875, 2194877]
Sandbox target: 24 passed, 1 failed. Earlier full targets, including broker (140 passed, 4 ignored), passed.

## Root cause
Not established. The assertion compares process_tree.processes() and cloned_tree.processes() at different instants while the prepared bubblewrap/bootstrap tree is live. Membership changing between reads is a hypothesis supported by the extra PID; clone inconsistency is not proved. No sandbox implementation or test was changed by this dependency-fetch work.

## Fix direction
Establish which process joins between observations. Preserve the contract that cloned handles observe the same live tree, without assuming two separate snapshots are atomic or weakening containment checks. Avoid an arbitrary sleep.

## Acceptance
- Reproduction establishes actual lifecycle timing or a process-tree defect.
- A deterministic test checks cloned-handle ownership and dynamic membership.
- Repeated full serial and parallel gates pass with real cgroups.

## Not covered
Deferred from dependency-fetch work. Production process-tree correctness and the exact joining process remain unverified.

title: Grill-me needed: should louiselm build a graph linking git commits, beads issues, and agent sessions
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing -- it wants full attention.**

Raised as an explicit "idea on the side" on 2026-08-21, unprompted, outside
any specific triage or QA context.

## The question

Should louiselm build a graph connecting git commits to the beads issues they
relate to, and further to the agent conversations/sessions that produced
them -- so that starting from a commit, you can answer "which beads issue(s)
was this for" and "which conversation/session produced this"?

## Context

louiselm.nvim already leans on `br`/`bvr` for issue tracking and has a
convention (this repo's own commits, e.g. `chore(beads): close pairing QR
bug`) of closing beads issues alongside commits. The Global rules in the
user's CLAUDE.md already require carrying a referenced issue/PR/bead id/session
id into the commit body as `Refs <id>` when a commit request names one. This
idea would generalize that ad hoc convention into a queryable graph: commit ->
bead(s) -> session(s), and possibly the reverse direction (bead -> all commits
that touched it, session -> all commits/beads it produced).

## Threads worth pulling

- Whether `Refs <id>` trailers in commit messages are sufficient raw material
  to reconstruct the graph (parse git log), or whether a dedicated index/store
  is needed -- and if so, where it lives (beads itself via comments/links, a
  separate artifact, git notes).
- Session identity: how is a "session" or "conversation" identified and
  referenced today (see the session-vocabulary-preference note -- "session"
  is the preferred term over "chat")? Is there already a stable session id
  format used across adapters (Claude, Codex, DeepSeek, GLM) that this could
  key off?
- Whether beads already has a graph primitive (bvr's PageRank/betweenness/
  critical-path machinery) that this could extend, versus a wholly separate
  concern layered on top.
- Query surface: is the payoff a CLI/`br`-integrated lookup ("what bead was
  commit X for"), a visualization, or both? Who is the consumer -- the user
  doing archaeology later, or an agent needing context when picking up
  related work?
- Cross-adapter concern: same as louiselm-3od/louiselm-slo -- if this becomes
  real, it needs to work for every adapter driving louiselm, not just Claude
  Code, since commits/sessions/beads all cross adapter boundaries.

## Out of scope for the grill

Re-deriving the above. React to it.
close_reason: Design resolved: derived Provenance/Decision browser, question anchors, shared current/historical model, explicit trust evidence, and implementation slices recorded on the parent epic.

comments.author: claude/ce71a8b9-3415-4247-a8a5-9e1ecf6ff943
comments.text:
Evidence gathered 2026-08-26 against the live repo and bvr 0.2.1, then a
maintainer direction decision. Recorded here so the grill reacts to measured
state instead of re-deriving it. This does NOT resolve the question; the
threads about transcript resolution, query surface shape and cross-adapter
behaviour are untouched and still want a full session.

## Two of the three edges already exist and already resolve

bead <-> commit: bvr already does this, today, no new storage.
`bvr --robot-history --bead-history louiselm-w726 --history-since 2026-08-10
--history-limit 500` returns real SHAs, authors and created/closed milestones:

    louiselm-w726,created,ca69b3c...,"chore(beads): file louiselm-w726, ..."
    louiselm-w726,closed, 043e634...,"docs(agents): add Monitor CI-loop guidance, close w726"
    method_distribution: co_committed: 2, explicit_id: 1

Trap worth recording: the default git range is the last N commits, so a bare
`bvr --robot-history` reports `beads_with_commits: 0` on this repo and reads as
"unimplemented". It needs an explicit `--history-since`. bvr also carries a
curation loop for these inferences (`--robot-confirm-correlation`,
`--robot-reject-correlation`, `--robot-correlation-stats`), so the correlation
is auditable rather than blindly trusted.

commit <-> session: already present in git trailers. All of the last 200
commits carry a `Refs` line, and the trailers already mix both node types --
`Refs claude/8b826fbf-...`, `Refs deepseek/session-5b4fb715-...`,
`Refs louiselm-w726`. The maintainer's global commit convention has been
building this edge for weeks without anyone calling it a graph.

bead <-> session: already present in beads itself. The
`br update --claim --actor "<session id>"` rule (AGENTS.md section 2) puts
session ids in `assignee`/`created_by`: `codex/01a0343a-...`,
`claude/ef57bf0a-...`. 135 of 304 issues predate the convention (`assistant`,
`lotso`), so coverage starts partway through the history and is complete only
for recent work.

Consequence for the "dedicated index/store" thread: answer is no on evidence.
Nothing needs to be stored. What is missing is a query surface and one edge.

## Time travel: what works, what does not

- `--robot-diff --diff-since <historical jsonl file>` works and gives a full
  issue-level diff. Since `.beads/issues.jsonl` is committed, git holds a
  snapshot at every commit, so arbitrary-vintage state is reachable today.
- `--diff-since <git ref>` is broken in bvr 0.2.1. `HEAD~20`, an explicit sha,
  and a date all fail with "could not resolve ... to a historical beads JSONL
  snapshot" while the file provably exists at that ref. Workaround, verified:
  `git show <ref>:.beads/issues.jsonl > /tmp/x && bvr --robot-diff --diff-since /tmp/x`.
  The error also swallows its own cause (`map_err(|_| ...)`,
  beads_viewer_rust src/main.rs:3366), so it is indistinguishable from
  "unsupported". Upstream defect, not louiselm's; filing it in
  beads_viewer_rust is blocked because that repo's beads db reports
  "runtime schema remains incompatible after repair".
- `--save-baseline <text>` is weaker than its name suggests: the argument is a
  *description*, not a name, and it always writes the single overwritten
  `.bv/baseline.json` holding graph stats + top PageRank/betweenness/hubs +
  cycles, not issue state. One baseline per design decision is therefore NOT
  supported. Do not design around per-decision baselines; git snapshots cover
  the need without asking upstream for anything.
- `.beads/.br_history/` is a rolling ~100-snapshot local cache, gitignored, and
  currently reaches back barely one day. Convenience, not an archive.

## The edge bvr cannot supply

session id -> transcript. `claude/<uuid>` resolves under
`~/.claude/projects/...`, codex elsewhere, deepseek elsewhere again. None of it
is in the repo, all of it is local-machine and per-adapter, and it is the one
part that actually evaporates. This is the hard thread in this question and the
only part that needs new code.

## Maintainer direction, 2026-08-26

Presented as two doors: (A) a shell/skill join over `bvr --robot-history` plus
`git log --grep`, delivering lookup only; (B) treat bvr as the graph-and-time
engine and have louiselm own the surface -- a `louiselm://history/...` buffer
plus a per-adapter transcript resolver, with A contained inside it.

Maintainer chose door B ("2nd door yes we are in line").

The capability that motivates B over A is decision archaeology, not lookup:
combining the closed question bead, the backlog snapshot at its closing commit,
the diff since, and the session transcript makes a past decision
re-interrogable on evidence -- "here is what we knew then, here is what has
drifted, does the decision still hold". Precedent that this is a real need
rather than a nice-to-have: louiselm-ce6.27 revisited louiselm-iexg's accepted
boundary two days later and had to re-derive the context by hand.

Refs claude/ce71a8b9-3415-4247-a8a5-9e1ecf6ff943

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text:
Maintainer agrees with the recommended Provenance surface: canonical louiselm://provenance/... views with commit/<sha> and issue/<id> entry points, later session/<session-id>, cross-links, and derived-on-demand data over git, Beads/bvr, and transcript locators rather than a new graph store.

Slicing constraint: keep implementation tasks independently doable by lower-tier models. Split work when a task combines a new boundary, multiple adapters, and UI behavior; route unresolved policy choices into separate design/grill questions before implementation. The current commit-buffer slice remains the first implementation target.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Maintainer agrees with the transcript-resolution boundary: keep lookup local, adapter-specific, and best-effort; store only attributed Session IDs; use adapter-specific resolvers; represent missing/inaccessible/unsupported transcripts explicitly; never copy or normalize transcript data or promise cross-machine resolution; and keep unresolved Session rows visible in Provenance views.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Maintainer wants the end goal to be ambitious: intuitive browsing of Session/design history for onboarding, preserving not only implementations but the decisions, compromises, and context that produced them. Concern raised: a two-step implementation could lose learning and require migration when history is added. Direction under consideration: define the historical end-state and shared abstraction now, while still using lower-tier-model-sized vertical implementation slices.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Maintainer agrees that the ambitious end-state should be designed now: current and historical Provenance are projections of one abstraction, not separate models. Decision is a first-class conceptual browsing subject, but not a new persisted Beads entity.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Maintainer agrees that Beads question issues are the initial canonical anchors for browsable Decisions. The issue ID remains the stable identity; related Sessions, commits, implementation issues, and later changes are derived around it without creating a new persisted Decision entity.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Maintainer clarified the trust model: rapid sliced implementation after a grill-me shared understanding intentionally transfers execution speed to Agents, so QA review is the mechanism that restores human confidence. Provenance should therefore represent trust as an evidence lifecycle—not merely an edge confidence score—covering agreed design, implementation slices, observed evidence, QA findings/retests, and human outcome acceptance. The current QA process is acknowledged as weak and is part of the opportunity.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Maintainer agrees that human QA acceptance should be an explicit Beads event/comment tied to the accepted commit, with Provenance deriving the trust/evidence timeline from Beads, QA records, commits, and Forensics pointers. This follows existing ownership boundaries and avoids a separate Provenance/QA database. Constraint for the next design step: acceptance must be machine-detectable and attributable; issue closure or arbitrary prose alone must not count as acceptance.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text:
Maintainer agrees with the small human-readable QA acceptance marker:
QA accepted: <commit-sha>
Scope: <issue-or-feature-id>
Evidence: <qa-round-or-forensics-id, optional>

The marker is human-authored and attributable. A helper/shortcut may reduce typing and prepare the metadata, but it must preserve the human gate: it cannot infer acceptance from tests, issue closure, or commit existence and must require explicit confirmation before recording acceptance.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Refinement: an editable acceptance buffer is likely overengineered. Prefer a deterministic helper that derives the commit/issue/evidence fields, displays the exact comment for review, and submits only after explicit human confirmation. Corrections can fall back to the ordinary Beads comment path; the helper does not need to become a second editor.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Maintainer agrees with low-friction scope inference for the QA acceptance helper: infer candidates from commit Refs and a uniquely attributable current issue; prefill one unambiguous candidate; prompt for selection when multiple; allow omission when none exist only with an explicit confirmation; never silently guess the wrong issue.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Scope clarification: this is not an onboarding process, tutorial, checklist, or codebase-tour workflow. Newcomer onboarding is only a motivating use case for discoverable project history. The actual capability is a general Provenance/Decision browser for maintainers, Agents, reviewers, and newcomers.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Maintainer agrees with strict Session-linking: the main Decision history uses only attributable signals (Refs Session trailers, Beads created_by/assignee Session IDs, and explicit Session IDs in comments or QA evidence); temporal/file-overlap guesses remain separate possible-related context. Adjacent idea noted but kept out of this Provenance design: a small executable minimal.lua/example configuration could document first use with the maintainer-default setup.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Maintainer agrees with the later-change model: explicit new question issues or relationships represent reconsideration/supersession/drift; Provenance may label only explicit relationships; unrelated later changes remain context; LouiseLM does not judge whether an earlier Decision was wrong.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Maintainer agrees with recording explicit reconsideration/supersession through existing Beads relationships where possible, supplemented by a small human-authored comment marker such as `Decision relation: supersedes <issue-id>` when needed. The design discussion has reached shared understanding; next step is to reflect the resulting end-state and implementation slices in Beads before closing this design question.

title: Configured skills.paths are not exposed to LouiseLM agents
description:
## Problem

LouiseLM no longer appears to discover or expose skills from the configured global `skills.paths`. A `louiselm.lua` configuration points at a directory containing 34 skills, but asking the active LouiseLM agent which skills are available reports only one unrelated built-in/session skill. Skill loading previously worked with this configuration.

This suggests the configured skill catalog is being dropped between setup, discovery, chat construction, and agent context/native loading.

## Investigation

- Reproduce through the normal `louiselm.setup()` plus `:Louiselm` chat path, not only by calling `require("louiselm.skills").discover()` directly.
- Determine whether the regression is specific to `skills.policy = "native"`, `"inject"`, or both.
- Compare `:checkhealth louiselm` discovery results with the skills actually made available in the resulting session/chat.
- Preserve and surface discovery errors instead of silently reducing the catalog.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a configured `skills.paths` directory containing multiple valid `SKILL.md` entries, a newly opened LouiseLM chat makes every valid discovered skill available according to the effective skills policy.
2. The normal setup/command integration path is covered by a regression test using multiple skills; coverage must fail if the catalog is omitted or reduced to a single skill.
3. Invalid skill entries do not hide valid siblings, and actionable discovery errors identify rejected paths/metadata.
4. `:checkhealth louiselm` and the session/chat behavior agree on whether configured skills were discovered and are available.
5. Focused tests and the full project quality gates pass.
close_reason: Fixed configured skill discovery end to end: follow SKILL.md symlinks after resolving targets, ignore unconsumed optional YAML metadata while validating required fields, remove the unused lyaml dependency gate, keep valid-sibling counts visible in checkhealth, and cover setup-to-chat injection of multiple skills. The real configured generated tree now reports 34 skills and 0 errors. Verification: focused red-green tests; full MiniTest 150/150; stylua --check passed; lua-language-server reported zero diagnostics; git diff --check passed.

title: QA round: Neovim Agent workflow through 60724f3
description:
# Manual QA review — Neovim Agent workflow since 2026-08-22

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I inspect the pinned
evidence and edit this file as we learn. Both this file and `QA_INIT.lua` are
untracked scratch files; neither will be committed.

**Build under test:** `c527bfc..60724f3`. **Re-run the setup embedded in
the affected case after any fix.**

Origin: the last completed manual round was `louiselm-6e5p` on 2026-08-22. It
tested the protected-quit fix at `5146007`; all four cases passed. Since its
closing commit, the Neovim plugin gained Handoff, parallel tool folding,
Session options/usage presentation, phase routing and approval, multi-Session
attention indicators, and a current real-Agent bootstrap. Automated tests are
green, but they cannot prove real ACP payloads, focus, picker sequencing,
winbar presentation, or proxy logging.

Android/device changes and GitLab CI are outside this round. They require a
physical-phone or runner-specific round rather than pretending this Neovim
session exercises them.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Current manual bootstrap starts Claude through `acp-proxy` | **passed** — exact Session log contains one prompt, eight updates, and `QA CLAUDE READY` |
| 2 | Missing Agent configuration warns without opening UI | **passed** — three actionable warnings; clean Neovim has no Agent-process descendant |
| 3 | Real parallel tools form one inspectable fold | **passed** — real tool calls overlapped; one fold and two matching inspectors worked |
| 4 | Background Session attention survives switching and clears on focus | **failed, non-blocking finding** — attention and direct selection work, but physical mouse selection does nothing (`louiselm-u6j6`) |
| 5 | Reviewed Handoff retains the source Session | **passed** — Handoff remained editable, targeted the second Agent, and retained two distinct Sessions |
| 6 | Phase-tagged skill produces feedback and explicit routing approval | **passed** — picker order, explicit CONTINUE approval, same-Session behavior, and bounded `qa` routing evidence all worked |
| 7 | DeepSeek usage presentation consumes a real optional payload | **failed, live telemetry passed** — context/cost render correctly, but real camelCase turn usage is discarded before presentation/persistence (`louiselm-4tum`) |

## Round constants and evidence roots

Run every case from `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`. The cases below repeat their
own exact launch and reset commands; do not return to this section to assemble
a setup recipe.

```sh
git rev-parse --short HEAD
test "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)" = 60724f3
```

Cases 1–4 used `/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.1PgDov` where the process inherited it;
Case 1 otherwise fell back to normal proxy state as recorded below. Case 5
used `/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.7OA8R5`; Cases 6–7 continue with that exact root.
The split happened because the shared Setup recipe was easy to re-run as if it
were case-local setup. Preserve both roots until the round closes.

Run `:checkhealth louiselm` after each launch. Report an unavailable executable
or missing `lyaml` as a setup blocker, not a product failure.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Use a fresh Session per case. A remembered permission or prior routing
  decision changes the path under test.
- Dismiss the initial Session-options picker only after noting whether it was
  coherent; dismissal deliberately keeps Agent defaults.
- A prompt asking for parallel tools does not prove the Agent actually emitted
  them in parallel. I will classify case 3 from its pinned ACP log before
  judging the UI.
- `qa_state` contains raw, potentially sensitive ACP evidence. Report its path
  and Session id; do not paste log contents into chat.
- After each launch, run `:echo $XDG_STATE_HOME`; it must print the exact path
  embedded in that case. The Case-1 live process did not retain that variable,
  so its proxy log correctly fell back to normal state. Session ids, not
  “latest file,” remain the evidence pin.
- Tool payload inspectors are ordinary floating windows and close with `:q`;
  they do not map plain `q`. Plain `q`/`<Esc>` are deliberate mappings only in
  the editable Handoff review buffer.

## Cases

### 1. Current manual bootstrap starts Claude through `acp-proxy`

Exercises `60724f3` / `manual_init.lua` and
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua`.

Steps:

1. Launch exactly:

   ```sh
   XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.1PgDov nvim -u ./manual_init.lua
   ```

2. Run `:checkhealth louiselm`; confirm `claude`, `acp-proxy`, and
   `claude-agent-acp` are recognized without an `acp-debug.sh` error.
3. Run `:LouiselmChat` and select `claude`.
4. Dismiss the initial options picker, if offered.
5. Submit: `Reply with exactly QA CLAUDE READY. Do not use tools.`
6. After completion, run `:LouiselmSessionId` and save the copied id.

Expect: a chat buffer opens with `skills=native`, the response is
`QA CLAUDE READY`, insert-mode/cursor behavior is usable, and no DeepSeek key or
deleted wrapper is consulted.

Failure signature: ENOENT for `acp-debug.sh`; a DeepSeek authentication error;
no Agent picker; no chat buffer; the Claude process starts but the Session
never becomes ready; or the options picker leaves focus unusable.

Evidence: Session `claude/bc7bdd37-a75e-4f9f-b855-a41b98ecb9ce` resolves to
`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/bc7bdd37-a75e-4f9f-b855-a41b98ecb9ce/log.jsonl`.
Without printing payloads, its shape proves one `session/prompt`, eight real
`session/update` frames, two Agent results, and one occurrence of the expected
marker. This proves the proxied real ACP conversation; the usable picker,
focus, and cursor result rests on the tester's observation. The originally
promised `$qa_state` proxy location was a recipe error: the live process had no
`XDG_STATE_HOME`, so `acp-proxy` used its documented fallback.

### 2. Missing Agent configuration warns without opening UI

Exercises `60724f3` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:31`.

Exit the prior Neovim, then launch:

```sh
XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.1PgDov nvim --clean \
  -c "set runtimepath^=$PWD" \
  -c 'lua require("louiselm.ui.chat.command").register()'
```

Confirm `:echo $XDG_STATE_HOME` before running the commands below.

Run these separately and inspect `:messages` afterward:

```vim
:LouiselmChat
:LouiselmResume
:LouiselmInline
```

Expect: each command warns
`louiselm: no Agent configured; add one to require('louiselm').setup({ agents = ... })`.
No chat buffer, resume picker, inline prompt, or Agent process opens.

Failure signature: any command launches an executable, opens a picker/prompt,
mentions DeepSeek, honors `LOUISELM_AGENT_COMMAND`, or fails silently.

Evidence: the tester received the exact actionable warning three times, once
per command. While that Neovim remained live, its process tree contained only
the TUI client and embedded Neovim server: no `acp-proxy`,
`claude-agent-acp`, or `acp-llm-adapter` descendant existed, and no ACP file
appeared under the pinned QA state. The automated regression independently
proves that no picker/prompt boundary is entered; the manual result proves the
warning presentation is useful.

### 3. Real parallel tools form one inspectable fold

Exercises `8e89831` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` against a real Agent
payload.

1. Launch
   `XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.1PgDov nvim -u ./manual_init.lua`,
   confirm `:echo $XDG_STATE_HOME`, open a fresh `claude` Session, and dismiss
   its options picker.
2. Submit exactly:

   > Invoke two Read tools in the same assistant turn, one for the first three
   > lines of `/home/lotso/code/louiselm/README.md` and one for the first three
   > lines of `/home/lotso/code/louiselm/AGENTS.md`. Do not use a subagent.
   > After both finish, reply exactly PARALLEL DONE.

3. Do not approve one request and delay the other; answer any permission UI as
   one batch if the Agent asks.
4. After completion, place the cursor on the closed tool block and press `zo`.
5. Put the cursor on each tool row and run `:LouiselmInspectTool`; close each
   inspector with `:q`.
6. Copy the Session id with `:LouiselmSessionId`.

Expect: if the ACP log confirms overlapping tool calls, the two contiguous
completed rows form one fold; `zo` reveals exactly two rows, each inspector
shows its own raw payload, and normal response text is outside the fold.

Failure signature: confirmed parallel calls remain as two unrelated folds;
one call vanishes; the fold consumes prose; an inspector shows the other
call's payload; or closing the inspector disturbs the chat cursor/window.

Evidence: recovered Session
`claude/d1342ebd-0c71-472d-ab65-2058221bb45a` from the pinned QA state. Its
real ACP sequence starts tool `toolu_01Mo...` at `05:17:57.348Z`, starts
`toolu_015U...` at `05:17:58.873Z`, then completes both at
`05:17:58.918Z`; the second therefore starts before the first finishes. Both
absolute fixture paths occur in the log. The tester confirmed one fold, two
matching raw-payload inspectors, and clean closure via `:q`. The original
plain-`q` instruction was a recipe error: that mapping is not part of the tool
inspector contract.

### 4. Background Session attention survives switching and clears on focus

Exercises `7b31438` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:559`.

1. Launch
   `XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.1PgDov nvim -u ./manual_init.lua`,
   confirm `:echo $XDG_STATE_HOME`, open a fresh `claude` Session, and rename
   it `source` with `:LouiselmRenameSession`.
2. Run `:LouiselmNewSession`, choose `claude`, and rename it `foreground`.
3. Switch to `source`, submit
   `Write a coherent 400-word explanation of why manual QA complements automated tests.`,
   then immediately use `:LouiselmSwitchSession` to select `foreground`.
4. Watch the right side of the winbar. While the source is active it should
   read `… source`; after unseen completion it should read `● source` using
   `LouiselmStatusWarning`.
5. Run `:echo &winbar` to capture the encoded highlight group, then click the
   `source` entry (enable `:set mouse=a` if needed).
6. Confirm the source transcript is complete and run `:echo &winbar` again.

Expect: attention remains visible while the source is in the background;
clicking selects the correct Session; focusing it clears only the unread
warning, without deleting the response or closing `foreground`.

Failure signature: the background Session disappears; completion produces no
warning highlight; switching clears it before focus; clicking opens the wrong
Session; or focusing source closes/mutates foreground.

Evidence check: the source Session log proves completion occurred while its
buffer was not current only when paired with the observed timing. The two
`:echo &winbar` values prove the actual warning/ready highlight transition.

Observed so far: lifecycle and unseen-completion presentation pass through
step 4. The live winbar contains a warning-highlighted `%1@...winbar_click@`
target for `● source`, but left-clicking it does nothing even after
`:set mouse=a`. The direct production handler call
`require("louiselm.ui.chat.command").winbar_click(1, 1, "l", "")` correctly
switches to `source`, while clicking ordinary buffer lines also fails to move
the cursor and `:messages` remains empty. The target and LouiseLM handler pass,
but the physical input path fails. This is tracked as the non-blocking bug
`louiselm-u6j6`, pinned to Agent Session
`claude/9efb19db-aa0b-4f45-8cab-18eab9d86937`; it will not be fixed in this
round.

### 5. Reviewed Handoff retains the source Session

Exercises `8c22da4` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2262` using two explicit
Agent entries for one installed Provider.

1. Launch exactly:

   ```sh
   XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.7OA8R5 nvim -u ./QA_INIT.lua
   ```

   Confirm `:echo $XDG_STATE_HOME`, run `:checkhealth louiselm`, then run
   `:LouiselmChat` and choose `claude_fast`.
2. Dismiss options and submit `Remember the marker COBALT-17 and reply SOURCE READY.`
3. When idle, run `:LouiselmHandOff` and select `claude_coding`.
4. In the markdown review buffer, confirm the source transcript is readable,
   append `Reply exactly HANDOFF RECEIVED COBALT-17.`, then press `<C-s>`.
5. Wait for the target response and inspect `:LouiselmSwitchSession`.
6. Copy both Session ids by switching and running `:LouiselmSessionId`.

Expect: the editable review buffer is `nofile`/markdown; `<C-s>` sends its
reviewed contents and focuses the target; the target replies with the marker;
the source remains attached, unchanged, and selectable as a distinct Session.

Failure signature: Handoff mutates or disposes the source; sends before review;
loses the marker; binds the target buffer to the source Agent; leaves focus in
the wiped review buffer; or creates only one Session in the switcher.

Evidence: source Session
`claude_fast/507980d2-b202-4231-9b62-3505b4c8ef17` and target Session
`claude_coding/c8087639-0d59-4ac4-8bb8-61ae7f0976ad` resolve to distinct proxy
logs under `/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.7OA8R5`. Each contains one prompt, two
Agent results, and eleven updates. The tester confirmed the readable/editable
review, `<C-s>` send and focus behavior, expected response, and both retained
Sessions; raw payload contents were not copied out of Forensics.

### 6. Phase-tagged skill produces feedback and explicit routing approval

Exercises `e79f9b7..1a97d39` / `lua/louiselm/workflow/` and the Chat picker
sequence. `QA_INIT.lua` gives `claude_fast` the `speed` capability and
`claude_coding` the `coding` capability while using the same Provider.

1. Launch exactly:

   ```sh
   XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.7OA8R5 nvim -u ./QA_INIT.lua
   ```

   Confirm `:echo $XDG_STATE_HOME` and run `:checkhealth louiselm`, then open a
   fresh `claude_fast` Session and dismiss options.
2. Run `:LouiselmPickSkill`, select `qa-review`, and submit
   `Using the selected skill, state the single most important property of a manual QA case.`
3. After the turn completes, choose `Good` in
   `louiselm workflow feedback:`.
4. In `louiselm workflow recommendation:`, confirm `CONTINUE` is present and
   at least one Handoff candidate names `claude_coding` with reasons/confidence.
5. Choose `CONTINUE`, then `Approve`.

Expect: pickers appear only after the turn is idle and in feedback →
recommendation → approval order. Approval keeps the same Session and appends a
`[workflow] approved CONTINUE:` transcript line. No Handoff or Model change
happens merely because it was recommended.

Failure signature: no feedback picker; recommendation appears mid-turn; phase
is not inferred from `qa-review`; approval happens without confirmation; the
Session changes after approving CONTINUE; or raw prompts/tool payloads appear
in routing evidence.

Evidence check after exiting Neovim:

```sh
jq '{version, records: [.records[] | {phase, agent, samples, successes, quality_samples}]}' \
  "/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.7OA8R5/nvim/louiselm/routing-evidence.json"
```

Pass condition: valid version 1 records include phase `qa` for `claude_fast`
with completed and quality samples. This proves bounded metadata persistence,
not picker order or absence of sensitive fields; I will inspect the full key
shape without printing values before closing the case.

Evidence: the tester confirmed the idle-only feedback → recommendation →
approval sequence, the `claude_coding` Handoff candidate, explicit CONTINUE
approval, and retention of the same Session. The version 1 evidence file
contains a `qa` / `claude_fast` record with one sample, one success, and one
quality sample. Its complete key set is limited to routing metadata (`agent`,
`phase`, Agent options, counters, and timestamps); it contains no prompt or
tool-payload fields.

### 7. DeepSeek usage presentation consumes a real optional payload

Exercises `23a8325` / `lua/louiselm/workflow/usage.lua` and the real
`acp-llm-adapter` payload. Skip as **blocked** if `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is absent.

1. If `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is absent, mark this case blocked and stop. Otherwise
   launch exactly:

   ```sh
   XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.7OA8R5 nvim -u ./manual_init.lua
   ```

   Confirm `:echo $XDG_STATE_HOME`, run `:checkhealth louiselm`, choose
   `deepseek`, and note the initial options.
2. Submit `Reply with exactly USAGE READY.`
3. After completion, inspect the transcript footer, header, winbar, and
   `:LouiselmSessionOptions` values.
4. Copy the Session id.

Expect: only fields actually reported by the Agent appear. A real usage update
adds a `[usage]` line and persists a sample; context/cost remain absent if the
Agent omits them. No counter is invented. The options picker remains usable.

Failure signature: authentication succeeds and the ACP log contains usage,
but LouiseLM shows none; counters are swapped or duplicated; missing optional
fields become zero; or the options picker becomes unusable after telemetry.

Evidence check:

```sh
jq '{version, record_count: (.records | length)}' \
  "/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.7OA8R5/nvim/louiselm/usage.json"
```

I will compare the pinned Session's raw usage event with the visible values;
the aggregate count alone cannot prove field mapping.

Evidence: Agent Session
`deepseek/session-25790698-4242-41d4-af23-cfe0e512d90c` completed with a real
`session/prompt` result whose `usage` object contains camelCase token keys,
including `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, and `totalTokens`. No `usage.json`
was created and the tester saw no observed values in
`:LouiselmSessionOptions`. LouiseLM's validation fixture and implementation
read snake_case names at the wire boundary, producing an empty internal usage
record. Filed as `louiselm-4tum`; raw values remain only in the original log at
`/tmp/louiselm-qa-review.7OA8R5/acp-llm-adapter/sessions/session-25790698-4242-41d4-af23-cfe0e512d90c/log.jsonl`.
The live notification path independently passes: `:echo &winbar` showed
`context=912/1000000 (0%)` and `cost=0.000399 USD` using the expected ACP and
derived-value highlights. The defect is therefore confined to completed-turn
token normalization, its `[usage]` line, and per-option persistence.

## Round conclusion

All seven cases were run against `60724f3`: five passed completely and two
produced open, non-blocking findings. The mouse finding escaped automation
because tests can invoke the winbar handler but cannot prove physical
terminal/TUI mouse-event delivery. The DeepSeek finding escaped because the
session test fabricated snake_case token keys that match LouiseLM's internal
representation instead of the Agent's real camelCase ACP payload.

The recipe itself also produced a durable design question. Shared setup forced
the tester to jump between distant sections and contributed to using two QA
state roots. The immediate correction is self-contained setup in every case;
the larger native `louiselm://qa-review` workspace remains `louiselm-fw0k`.

The scratch recipe and init file are deleted after this description becomes
the sole durable Beads round record. Both QA state roots remain in place as
primary evidence for the open findings; they are not copied, normalized,
committed, or treated as safe to share.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- Close all QA Neovim instances and their Agent processes.
- Preserve both QA state roots after the round closes because open findings
  point to their raw evidence.

## Findings and process feedback

- `louiselm-u6j6`: physical mouse click on a Session winbar entry does nothing.
  Open, P3, deliberately not fixed in this round.
- `louiselm-fw0k`: grill-me question for a native `louiselm://qa-review`
  workspace. The immediate recipe rule is already adopted here: each case owns
  its complete setup and evidence commands. The screenshot motivating the
  question is
  `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_0708_1920x1200_1787548138.png`.
- `louiselm-4tum`: real DeepSeek camelCase token usage is absent from Session
  options and persistence. Open, P2; the real payload exposed a wire-shape gap
  hidden by the invented snake_case test fixture.
- Archive this file into one `qa-round` Beads chore, parent every finding to
  it, then delete `QA_REVIEW.md` and `QA_INIT.lua`; neither is committed.
- Retain both QA state roots in place after closing. They contain sensitive raw
  ACP logs, so never commit or paste them; open findings reference them as
  primary evidence.

## Reporting back

Run one case at a time. Send the case number, `qa_state`, copied Session id(s),
what you saw, and anything surprising. Do not paste raw ACP logs. I will pull
the objective evidence, classify the result, update this file, and give you the
next case.

## Findings this round

- `louiselm-u6j6` — physical mouse click on a Session winbar source does
  nothing; non-blocking and left open for a later reproduction/fix.
- `louiselm-4tum` — DeepSeek reports token usage, but LouiseLM validates the
  ACP wire object using internal snake_case names and silently records nothing.
close_reason: QA complete against 60724f3: five cases passed; Case 4 filed non-blocking mouse finding louiselm-u6j6; Case 7 live context/cost passed and filed token-normalization finding louiselm-4tum; QA workspace question louiselm-fw0k recorded. The open children are retained outcomes, not blockers to closing the completed round. Raw evidence roots retained in place.

title: LouiseLM reports Codex ACP outdated despite executable being current
description:
LouiseLM emits a false outdated warning for Codex ACP: it reports `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.2` as installed and `1.7.0` upstream, while invoking the configured `codex-acp --version` executable reports version 1.7.0. The warning misleads users into believing their active Codex ACP installation needs upgrading.

## Observed

Reported 2026-08-28 in a LouiseLM session. The warning shown was:

> louiselm: codex is outdated (@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.2 installed, 1.7.0 upstream)

In the same environment, the executable resolved by PATH is:

> /home/lotso/.asdf/installs/nodejs/24.16.0/bin/codex-acp

Running it produced:

> @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.7.0

The warning is generated by `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:215` from `result.version` and `result.latest_version`; version comparison is performed in `lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:216`.

## Symptoms

- LouiseLM warns that Codex ACP is outdated.
- The user-visible installed version is 1.6.2, but the executable currently available as `codex-acp` reports 1.7.0.
- The warning can prompt an unnecessary upgrade or undermine trust in health checks.

## Root cause

Unknown. Possible causes include a different executable or environment being used by LouiseLM than the shell command, stale/cached health output, or the version check and runtime process resolving different installations. Trace the exact `vim.system` command/environment and timing for both the version check and the active adapter before assigning a mechanism.

## Why it was not caught

The health tests cover parsing and comparing synthetic version outputs, including package-name normalization, but do not assert that the health check and the user-facing runtime resolve the same `codex-acp` executable and environment.

## Fix direction

Instrument or otherwise test the resolved command path and environment at the health-check boundary, then ensure the reported installed version comes from the same executable LouiseLM is configured to run. Avoid suppressing the warning or changing comparison semantics until the source of the 1.6.2 value is identified.

## Acceptance

- With `codex-acp --version` reporting 1.7.0 and upstream reporting 1.7.0, LouiseLM does not emit an outdated warning.
- The health check and active adapter use the intended executable/environment.
- A regression test reproduces the mismatch and fails before the fix, then passes after it.

## Not covered

The report does not establish whether the mismatch is caused by PATH/environment differences, a stale process or notification, or an alternate configured `version` command. No claim is made that the active ACP process itself is running 1.7.0.

The 1.6.2 installed value therefore belongs to the patched binary LouiseLM actually checks; no LouiseLM version-health defect is established. The original report compared different executables.

title: Transcript.render_compact: compact renderer for handoff context
description:
## Goal

A deterministic compact transcript renderer that produces the Handoff Context section: the task sequence and decisions without scratchpad or raw payloads.

## Scope

- In scope: new `M.render_compact(entries, state)` in `lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua`, consuming the same `transcript:snapshot()` shape as `M.render`:
  - user and assistant entries render as today (`## User`, `## Assistant`, full text, including the `Handoff from Session:` provenance marker);
  - `tool_call` entries render the existing `<sub>` title+status caption with **no** `<details>` payload block;
  - reasoning entries are skipped entirely;
  - `[resource] <uri>` blocks embedded in replayed user text are stripped (only resumed sessions can carry them — live `record_user` stores bare typed text, so nothing is lost at record time).
- Out of scope: any change to `M.render` (it is a documented dependency of blog tooling, louiselm-mia, and keeps full fidelity); buffer composition; transport; the no-progress loop guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `render_compact` of a snapshot containing user/assistant/reasoning/tool entries returns markdown containing every user and assistant text and every tool title+status caption, in order.
2. The same snapshot's compact output contains no reasoning text and no tool raw payload content.
3. A user entry whose text contains a `[resource] <...>...` block renders without that block; surrounding text is preserved.
4. A user entry carrying `handoff_source_session_id` keeps its `Handoff from Session:` marker line.
5. `M.render` output for the same snapshot is byte-identical before and after this change (regression guard).
6. Output is deterministic: same input, same text, same LuaJIT runtime.
7. stylua, lua-language-server, and full mini.test gates pass.

## Testing

- Unit tests in `tests/session/transcript_spec.lua`, beside the existing render tests.
- One regression case asserts `M.render` output unchanged for a snapshot containing all entry kinds.

## Notes

- Design record: louiselm-93wl (settled grill). This is the pure render half; the review-buffer half is louiselm-mtte, which depends on this slice.
- Keep `render_compact` a plain, deterministic mapping — same constraint the module comment already imposes on `M.render`.
close_reason: Implemented in 785cd53: Transcript.render_compact keeps user/assistant prose, reduces tool calls to their title+status caption, drops reasoning blocks, and strips injected [resource] blocks from replayed user text (embedded form bounded by a later marker; unbounded trailing body kept so typed text is never destroyed). M.render unchanged for exports. Gates: focused transcript spec 27/27, full mini.test suite green, stylua and lua-language-server clean, generate-api-appendix check clean. Real-data verification: this session's own first prompt (skills index + AGENTS.md link + typed text, 8722 chars flattened) compacts to the 718-char typed prompt.

title: Repeated za on thinking fold errors or loses line
description:
Repeated fold-toggle failure in the thinking UI: pressing za on a thinking fold can open it, but pressing za again without moving the cursor sometimes reports a fold error instead of restoring the prior collapsed state; in worse cases a thinking line disappears. This was observed by the maintainer 2–3 times in session codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee.

## Observed

Seen in LouiseLM's Neovim chat UI while interacting with a thinking fold. Maintainer report date: 2026-08-26. Reported session: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee. Reproduction was described from the live application; no log path or captured error text was provided.

## Symptoms

- Pressing za on a thinking fold opens it.
- Pressing za again on the same fold, without moving the cursor, can produce a fold error instead of closing it back.
- Sometimes a thinking line disappears after the repeated toggle.
- Reproduced approximately 2–3 times.

## Root cause

Unknown. Likely involves fold state or buffer-line mutation between the first and second toggle, but this is a hypothesis and needs live reproduction/tracing to discriminate.

## Why it was not caught

No regression test currently covers repeated za toggles on the same thinking fold while the cursor remains stationary, including the error and line-disappearance outcomes. No captured error output is available yet.

## Fix direction

Reproduce in the live chat UI and trace the thinking-fold range and buffer contents across both toggles. Fix the narrowest shared fold/rendering boundary; preserve the thinking line and make a second za restore the prior collapsed state.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after for repeated za on an unchanged thinking fold.
- In the live chat UI, opening a thinking fold and pressing za again at the same cursor closes it without an error.
- No thinking line disappears during the toggle sequence.

## Not covered

The exact Neovim version, agent/model, fold method, error text, and deterministic trigger are unverified.

title: Installed launch gate reads delegated effect before completion
description:
Installed launch acceptance can report failure after a delegated command was granted because its effect file is observed before its contents are written.

## Observed
2026-09-14, codex/01a0a13a-d078-7662-aecf-e0d916c9b262, disposable launcher VM. Command: LOUISELM_REQUIRE_BROKER_LAUNCH=1 library-test launch_supervisor::system::installed_tests::privileged_installed_broker_launch_and_effects --exact --nocapture.
Output at skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/installed_tests.rs:762: assertion left == right failed; left: []; right: [97,117,116,104,111,114,105,122,101,100]. 0 passed, 1 failed, 30.98s.
Source under test: /home/vm/receipt-history.auyGow; executable /var/tmp/louiselm-skills-target/debug/deps/louiselm_skills-2873ba885db59fb7. This assertion/helper is unchanged by receipt-history implementation.

## Root cause
assert_denial_and_helper polls only workspace/effect.exists() before fs::read. The command is printf authorized > effect; printf done: shell redirection creates/truncates the file before printf fills it. CommandOperation::Granted confirms delegation, not completion. Existence therefore permits an empty read during valid execution.

## Fix direction
Wait for the existing authoritative delegated-completion boundary when available, then assert exit status and exact bytes. If the fixture can only observe the file, use a bounded complete-content observation with explicit errors; do not erase the assertion or add a fixed sleep.

## Acceptance
Expose the create-before-write interval deterministically and prove the helper waits for completion. Preserve denial, helper attribution and exact effect assertions; run the installed VM gate plus full affected gates.

## Deferred
Separate fixture race, outside louiselm-d6fv.13.1. No production command failure inferred. No fixture repair made; gate rerun pending.

title: Broker Attention CI exits before readiness after explicit capability opt-ins
description:
The installed broker Attention gate fails before exercising provisioning or cross-UID delivery.

## Observed
GitHub run 35064484556, job 104691645076, 2026-09-16: scripts/test-broker-attention.py:139 start(observer), line 128 AssertionError: 1 is not None : capture-service exited before readiness.
Local reproduction: env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/nonexistent capture-service/target/debug/louiselm-capture serve exits 1: louiselm-capture: invalid command: serve has no capabilities enabled; set the required LOUISELM_*_ENABLED=true choices in capture.env.

## Root cause
scripts/test-broker-attention.py constructs a clean environment without LOUISELM_ATTENTION_ENABLED=true. capture-service/src/cli/service.rs Features::read now requires explicit capability opt-ins. The fixture also discards child diagnostics, hiding the cause in CI.

## Why it was not caught
The privileged installed-consumer fixture retained the old implicit Attention startup assumption after service capability selection changed.

## Fix direction
Enable only Attention in the fixture environment; retain the separate unset broker-policy check. Surface child startup diagnostics on failure.

## Acceptance
The existing installed gate passes initial Attention readiness without broker policy, provisioning, identity/capability rejection, replay after restart and permission-drift refusal. Show pre-fix failure and post-fix success using the actual CLI.

## Not covered
No production capability defaults change. Local sudo is unavailable; attempt the privileged fixture in isolated mapped user/mount namespaces and report any limitation.

title: Android backup opt-out lacks explicit device-transfer exclusions
description:
Android backup opt-out is incomplete for OEM device-to-device transfer on Android 12+. This is a verified missing configuration, not a reproduced transfer or data leak.

## Observed
2026-09-06, codex/01a074f5-e592-72d1-9ccf-69e162d8cdfe: ./gradlew lint with warningsAsErrors=true exits 1. app/build/intermediates/lint_intermediate_text_report/debug/lintReportDebug/lint-results-debug.txt reports AndroidManifest.xml:10 [DataExtractionRules]: "Consider adding the attribute android:dataExtractionRules". Manifest sets allowBackup=false but has no dataExtractionRules resource. minSdk28/targetSdk36; CaptureStore stores original recordings under files/captures and PairingStore stores encrypted credentials in shared preferences.

## Root cause
android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:10 relies only on allowBackup=false. Android documents that some manufacturers still allow D2D transfer with this setting on Android 12+: https://developer.android.com/about/versions/12/behavior-changes-12#backup-restore . Actual phone/OEM transfer behavior remains untested.

## Test gap
No manifest/resource test establishes the cloud and device-transfer exclusions; capture durability and protocol tests do not exercise platform extraction policy.

## Fix direction
Declare explicit cloud-backup and device-transfer exclusions for sensitive app data while preserving older-device opt-out. Audit credential restore behavior because a transferred encrypted preference does not transfer its Keystore key. Do not perform a transfer using the maintainer's recordings.

## Acceptance
A manifest/resource regression fails before the configuration change and proves the packaged rules exclude capture and pairing data for both channels. Android gates pass. Verify supported platform semantics using disposable synthetic data if device-level acceptance is needed.

## Not covered
No leak, restoration failure, or OEM behavior has been reproduced. Filed rather than fixed because current work is Android contract/test enforcement, not changing installed backup policy.
close_reason: gate:android/app/src/test/java/dev/louiselm/capture/BackupPolicyTest.kt Packaged cloud/D2D exclusions; API28/34 opt-out preserved. Red-green and Android test/lint/assembleDebug pass. OEM transfer untested.
