title: QA round: native ACP command invocation (louiselm-2w4)
description:
# Manual QA review — native ACP command invocation (louiselm-2w4)

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `9322523` (main). **Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: louiselm-2w4 made the skill picker invoke adapter-native slash
commands (Codex `$name`, Claude bare `name`) instead of always injecting the
full `SKILL.md` body. Everything shipped with full mock/unit coverage, but all
of it uses hand-typed ACP fixtures. Before running a single human case, I
inspected real ACP debug logs already on this machine (this very session runs
through `claude-agent-acp`) and found a confirmed bug: Claude's real adapter
appends `" (user)"` to every advertised command description sourced from a
configured skill path, which broke exact-match description correlation for
every skill, every time. Filed and fixed as **louiselm-s88** (see Findings)
before this round started. What's left needs a live interactive Neovim, which
I can't drive myself:

- Does the fix actually work against the real `claude-agent-acp` end to end?
- What does the real `codex-acp` actually advertise — is the `$name`
  assumption (never observed in the available logs) correct at all?
- Chip rendering / cursor position in a real buffer.
- The "pick before any `available_commands_update` has arrived" race.

**Second finding, also before any human case ran:** asked for the skill
picker to be invoked and there was nothing to invoke it with — `pick_skill`
(and its siblings `pick_file`/`mention_buffer`/`send_selection`) had no
command, keymap, or reachable instance from the documented
`Louiselm.setup()` + `:LouiselmChat` path at all. Filed and fixed as
**louiselm-j8j** (see Findings) — `:LouiselmPickSkill` now exists.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Native pick + submit round-trips through real Claude | **passed** — `claude/8d6e76d1-e4e8-4a13-9bad-0337bbae6ea5`: response opens "I'll start by understanding the current state of louiselm before interviewing you on the rewrite decision," then reads AGENTS.md, explores lua/capture-service/android trees, checks `br list` — grill-me's own documented behavior verbatim |
| 2 | Native pick + submit round-trips through real Codex | **passed** — `codex/01a01ea6-c458-70f0-9140-d51d52ae42a6`: `available_commands_update` advertised `$grill-me` (first real observation, confirms the dollar-prefix assumption); response narrates "Using `grill-me` for the invocation test," with a `tool_call` reading the real `grill-me/SKILL.md` |
| 3 | Picking immediately after opening chat, before commands arrive | **not human-testable** — real adapter responds too fast to race by hand; already covered deterministically by `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` ("re-resolves a queued native command against the latest cache only when the turn releases it" et al.) |

## Setup

1. Pull the new commits into the installed plugin (it's a `vim.pack` clone
   pinned to a rev, not a live symlink):

   ```
   :lua vim.pack.update({"louiselm.nvim"})
   ```

   Confirm the running copy matches source:

   ```sh
   git -C /home/lotso/code/louiselm rev-parse HEAD
   python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('/home/lotso/.config/nvim/nvim-pack-lock.json'))['plugins']['louiselm.nvim']['rev'])"
   ```

   Both must print `35a83fb...`. If `vim.pack.update` reports nothing to do,
   restart Neovim after it — pack updates on a running instance don't always
   reload already-loaded Lua modules.

2. Clear stale ACP debug logs so the evidence check below only sees this
   round's sessions:

   ```sh
   mkdir -p /tmp/qa-round-2w4-old-logs && mv ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*.log /tmp/qa-round-2w4-old-logs/ 2>/dev/null
   ```

3. Skill fixture already exists at `~/.config/agentskills/generated/grill-me/SKILL.md`
   (`disable-model-invocation: true`, so it's picker-only — expected, that's
   what native mode is for). No changes needed there.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- `grill-me` has `disable-model-invocation: true`. That's fine for native
  mode (explicit-only skills stay picker-visible), don't read it as a config
  error if you see it in the SKILL.md.
- Both `codex` and `claude` agents in `~/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua`
  leave `skills.policy` unset, so they inherit the global `native` default —
  no config change needed to test either.
- ACP debug logs land in `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/<ts>-<pid>-<binary>-<label>-stdout-jsonrpc.log`,
  one pair (stdout+stderr) per spawned adapter process. `label` is the
  backend name for multi-backend agents; codex/claude sessions get no label,
  just `-codex-acp-` / `-claude-agent-acp-` in the filename.
- **`acp-debug.sh` only tees the adapter's stdout (its replies to us), never
  its stdin (what we send it).** The original "Evidence check" below assumed
  `session/prompt` requests would show up in the log — they never can, since
  that request travels the direction this script doesn't capture. Judge cases
  1/2 from the *response* side (does the reply read like the skill actually
  engaged), not from grepping for the outgoing request.
- **"just say hi and stop" is not a discriminating test prompt.** A Claude
  that correctly loaded grill-me and honored an explicit stop-override says
  "Hi," and so does a Claude that never saw `/grill-me` at all and just
  complied with the literal plain-text instruction — both paths produce
  identical output, so a bare "Hi" proves nothing either way. Use a prompt
  that would look obviously different if the skill engaged (e.g. "we should
  rewrite louiselm in Rust" — grill-me should start interrogating that claim
  one question at a time, unprompted).

## Cases

### 1. Native pick + submit round-trips through real Claude

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` (`Chat:pick_skill`, `build_content`,
`submit_prompt`) and `lua/louiselm/skills/native_command.lua`'s fixed
`description_matches`.

Steps:

> `:LouiselmNewSession` → pick `claude`
> wait for the session to become ready (status line stops saying "starting")
> `:LouiselmPickSkill` and choose `grill-me`
> confirm the buffer shows `[context: skill: grill-me]` in the prompt line
> type `we should rewrite louiselm in Rust` and submit (not "just say hi and
> stop" — see Ground rules, that prompt can't distinguish success from
> failure)

Expect: the chip disappears, the prompt line shows your typed text (not the
resolved command — that's expected, see Ground rules), and Claude starts
interrogating the Rust-rewrite claim one question at a time, unprompted —
grill-me's own documented behavior, not a normal direct answer.

Failure signature: notification `louiselm: advertised command 'grill-me'
description does not match the skill`, or a response that just answers/
discusses the claim directly instead of interviewing you about it.

**Status: passed**, `claude/8d6e76d1-e4e8-4a13-9bad-0337bbae6ea5` — see
Status table for the evidence.

### 2. Native pick + submit round-trips through real Codex

Exercises the same code path, but this is the **first-ever observation** of
what `codex-acp` actually sends for `available_commands_update` — every log
available to me from this machine only had a 1-line (`initialize`-only)
codex-acp transcript, so the `$name`-prefix assumption in
`native_command.lua` (`dollar_name = "$" .. skill.name`) is unverified
against a real payload.

Steps:

> `:LouiselmNewSession` → pick `codex`
> wait for ready
> `:LouiselmPickSkill` and choose `grill-me`, same as case 1
> type `we should rewrite louiselm in Rust` and submit

Expect: same as case 1 — chip clears, Codex responds as if `/grill-me` (or
whatever it actually names the command) were invoked.

Failure signature: same notification as case 1.

**Status: passed**, `codex/01a01ea6-c458-70f0-9140-d51d52ae42a6` — see Status
table for the evidence. This was also the first real observation of what
`codex-acp` advertises: confirmed `$grill-me` (dollar-prefixed), validating
the `native_command.lua` assumption.

### 3. Picking immediately after opening chat, before commands arrive

Exercises AC6 from louiselm-2w4: "picker activation before advertisement
waits safely and is late-bound at submission" — i.e. picking a skill in the
gap before the agent has sent its first `available_commands_update` should
not error or hang, just defer.

Steps:

> `:LouiselmNewSession` → pick `claude` (or `codex`)
> as fast as possible after the command opens the buffer (before "Session:
> status=ready" settles), run `:LouiselmPickSkill` and choose `grill-me`
> then type text and submit

Expect: either it resolves fine (if the update already arrived by the time
you typed and hit submit — likely, given how fast this is), or if you
genuinely submit before any advertisement, you get the "no advertised
command matches" notification with your text and chip preserved — not a
hang, not a crash, not lost input.

Failure signature: Neovim hangs, an unrelated Lua error, or the typed text
disappears.

## Evidence check

`acp-debug.sh` cannot show the outgoing `session/prompt` request (see Ground
rules — it only tees stdout). Judge from the response side instead: find the
session's log by its ACP session id (visible via `:LouiselmSessionId` or in
whatever you paste back to me), then dump what the agent actually said and
did:

```sh
python3 -c "
import json, sys
path = sys.argv[1]
for line in open(path):
    try:
        msg = json.loads(line)
    except Exception:
        continue
    params = msg.get('params', {})
    update = params.get('update', {}) if isinstance(params, dict) else {}
    su = update.get('sessionUpdate')
    if su == 'available_commands_update':
        names = [c['name'] for c in update['availableCommands']]
        print('available_commands_update: grill-me as', [n for n in names if 'grill' in n])
    elif su == 'agent_message_chunk':
        print('text:', repr(update.get('content', {}).get('text', '')))
    elif su in ('tool_call', 'tool_call_update'):
        print(su, update.get('title'), update.get('status'))
" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/<the-matching-file>-stdout-jsonrpc.log
```

Pass condition: `available_commands_update` shows the expected command name
shape (`$grill-me` for Codex, bare `grill-me` for Claude), and the assembled
response text/tool calls read like the skill actually engaged (interrogating
the claim one question at a time, or in Codex's case an explicit `tool_call`
reading `grill-me/SKILL.md`) — not a direct answer to the literal prompt
text. This cannot prove the exact wire text sent; it proves what the agent
did in response, which is what actually matters.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- Old logs stashed in `/tmp/qa-round-2w4-old-logs/` can be deleted.
- No other fixtures or state created this round beyond the two already-closed
  beads (louiselm-2w4, louiselm-s88).

## Reporting back

Send me the case number, what you saw, and paste (or point me at) the
relevant `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*-stdout-jsonrpc.log` file if
something looks wrong — I'll pull the evidence myself. If something's broken
I'll fix it and you'll need to redo Setup step 1 before retesting.

## Findings this round

**F1 — Native bare-name matching never resolved against the real Claude
adapter** (`louiselm-s88`, fixed in `c230f8c`). `description_matches()` in
`lua/louiselm/skills/native_command.lua` required exact whitespace-normalized
equality between the advertised and local skill description. Real
`claude-agent-acp` appends `" (user)"` to every command sourced from a
user-configured skill path, so the comparison always failed — verified
against all 76 commands in a real `available_commands_update` payload from
this session's own ACP transcript, 27 of which are user skills, all 27
carrying the suffix. Found by reading a pre-existing debug log before running
any human case, not by a live test. Fixed by matching on the advertised
description *starting with* the local one instead of equaling it. Regression
test added using the real captured description pair.

**F2 — No command/keymap reached the context-picker API at all**
(`louiselm-j8j`, fixed in `9e553a1`). `pick_skill`/`pick_file`/
`mention_buffer`/`send_selection` were defined on `Chat` but never wired into
`command.lua`, and the `Chat` instance `:LouiselmChat` builds was never
exposed, so nothing following the documented `Louiselm.setup()` +
`:LouiselmChat` setup could ever reach them — including this QA round.
Discovered when asked to invoke the skill picker and there was nothing to
invoke. Fixed by adding `:LouiselmPickSkill`, `:LouiselmPickFile`,
`:LouiselmMentionBuffer`, `:LouiselmSendSelection`; README updated.
close_reason: Round complete. Cases 1 (real Claude) and 2 (real Codex) both passed with strong evidence pulled from real ACP debug logs (see description). Case 3 (early-pick race) is not human-testable — real adapters respond too fast to race by hand — and is already covered deterministically by tests/ui/chat_spec.lua. Two findings surfaced and fixed before this round finished: louiselm-s88 (Claude's scope-annotation suffix broke bare-name matching) and louiselm-j8j (no command reached the context-picker API at all). Both children closed and parented under this issue.

title: Place the demo guide above Neovim at every desktop width
description:
## Goal
Keep the active guide step and demo status above the Neovim wrapper on wide desktop screens, matching the clearer reading order already used at narrower widths.

## Scope
- In scope: replace the wide two-column guide/sidebar layout with one vertical content flow; make the full-width top guide compact enough that the current step, status, and a useful portion of Neovim are visible together at 1920x1200; preserve the existing narrower stacked layout and DOM reading order.
- Prefer a CSS-only change in demo/demo.css because demo/index.html already places the guide before the editor.
- Out of scope: guide copy or step logic changes, Neovim runtime changes, mobile interactive support, fallback-content redesign, and a new breakpoint/layout system.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. At a 1920x1200 desktop viewport, the demo guide is above the editor rather than in a left sidebar.
2. The active step, its actions, and Status remain easy to scan above a usable Neovim viewport; step/status updates do not require looking away to a side rail.
3. At the narrower desktop width represented by the reference screenshot, the existing guide-above-editor order remains intact with no horizontal overflow.
4. Profile selection, language switching, assisted entry, Skip, Reset, completion, editor focus, and fallback behavior remain unchanged.
5. The result remains accessible in source/reading order and does not duplicate or move live regions through JavaScript.

## Testing
- Add or update deterministic browser layout coverage that compares guide and editor bounding rectangles at wide and narrow representative viewports.
- Run npm run site:test and npm run site:build.
- Visually compare against /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260905_0827_1920x1200_1788589645.png (current wide sidebar) and /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260905_0827_1920x1200_1788589675.png (preferred stacked order).

## Notes
- Current cause: demo/demo.css gives .demo-shell two grid columns by default and switches to block only below 63.99rem; demo/index.html already has .demo-guide before .editor-panel.
- Parent feature: louiselm-q58u.
close_reason: consumer:demo/index.html:42 — compact guide stage remains above the editor at wide and narrow desktop widths.

comments.author: codex/01a06d85-2ee2-7863-898b-f68a140beed2
comments.text: Verification: Playwright at 1920x1200 measured guide bottom 532px, editor top 552px, 648px visible editor, source order preserved, no horizontal overflow; 960x1200 retained guide-before-editor with no overflow. Wide fallback and Chinese switch passed. `npm run site:test` passed. `npm run site:build` reached unrelated pinned Neovim asset 404, tracked as louiselm-q58u.9. Lesson routing: issue-local only—the static guide-stage wrapper keeps live-region IDs and order; no standing contract or design question warranted.

title: in_progress issues carry no session identity, so concurrent agents collide on the same claimed work
description:
Two sessions independently selected louiselm-n3y1 as the next task. The second
had no way to know the first was live.

Evidence (2026-08-21):
- louiselm-n3y1 is status=in_progress, assignee=benoit, with ZERO comments and
  no session id in any field, while claude/77bea574-1f32-4551-8514-89064881695e
  was actively working it.
- Session ids DO appear in 17 issues, but only in `description` (issue origin),
  `close_reason` (retrospective), or `external_ref`. None on an open issue at
  claim time.
- All 5 in-progress issues are assigned to `benoit`, the sole human. Assignee
  therefore carries no signal about which agent session holds the work.

Why this compounds: AGENTS.md section 2 tells agents to "prefer finishing
in-progress work to starting new work". With no session identity on
in_progress, that rule actively concentrates independent agents onto the same
small claimed set. The contract's collision-avoidance guidance is a collision
magnet.

Per AGENTS.md section 2: "Anything an agent knows that another adapter cannot
read is a defect in the record." The holding session is precisely such a fact.

Candidate fix (narrowest): on claiming, post a `br comment` carrying the
session id, and read comments before selecting an in-progress issue. Requires
an AGENTS.md convention so all adapters do it, not just Claude Code.

Thread worth pulling before settling on that -- possibly grill-me shaped:
a claim comment is a lock with no lease. A session that dies mid-task leaves a
claim that never releases, and the next agent cannot distinguish "held by a
live session" from "abandoned three days ago". Does the claim need a
heartbeat, a staleness horizon, or is a human-readable stale claim good enough
at this scale? Note louiselm-qbr.5 (policy-controlled agents executing Beads
graphs sequentially) will hit this same problem harder.
close_reason:
Fixed in AGENTS.md section 2. Root cause was contract, not tooling: br already ships claim-aware commands (br scheduler excludes claimed work; br coordination status carries a 120m stale / 480m abandoned lease; br update --claim atomically sets assignee=actor and refuses to steal a live claim), but AGENTS.md pointed agents at br ready + bvr and told them to 'prefer finishing in-progress work' without scoping that to their own claims -- which actively steered independent agents into each other's claimed set.

Three changes: (1) claim via 'br update <id> --claim --actor <session id>', never bare --status=in_progress, with a warning that bvr's own claim_command field suggests the identity-less form; (2) the in-progress preference now reads 'your own' in-progress work explicitly; (3) new bullet requiring a br coordination status check before touching someone else's claim, preferring br scheduler over hand-scanning br list --status in_progress.

Proof: br scheduler now omits both claimed issues (n3y1 while it was live, and 101q itself once claimed) and recommends louiselm-ini instead. Claiming 101q with --claim recorded assignee=claude/37c1ce37-b25d-4d18-b73a-9f2895d39ee1, giving in_progress the session identity it lacked. stylua --check . passes; no Lua changed, so the mini.test suite and lua-language-server were not re-run.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Lease question resolved without a grill-me: br already implements it natively. `br coordination status` reports stale_threshold_minutes=120 and abandoned_threshold_minutes=480 per claim, plus classification and next_action, and `br update --claim` refuses to overwrite a live claim (verified: attempting to re-claim louiselm-101q errored with 'already assigned to ...'). So no heartbeat or custom staleness horizon is needed; the gap was purely that AGENTS.md never pointed at these commands.

Also confirmed the collision was real rather than theoretical: louiselm-n3y1 was closed by claude/77bea574-1f32-4551-8514-89064881695e while this fix was in progress. Two sessions editing lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua concurrently was the averted outcome.

title: Preserve multiline chat prompts entered with Shift+Enter
description:
## Problem

In the Markdown chat buffer, Shift+Enter can insert a continuation line while editing the `> ` prompt. Pressing Enter afterward submits only the tracked first line. The continuation is omitted from the ACP prompt, remains visible below the newly inserted response/prompt area, and the model begins responding to incomplete input.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a louiselm chat session and type the first line in the `> ` prompt.
2. Press Shift+Enter to create a new line inside the Markdown quote block.
3. Type a second line.
4. Press Enter to submit.

## Observed

Only the first line is sent to the session. The second line remains stranded at the bottom of the chat buffer while the model responds.

## Expected

The submitted prompt contains every line in the editable prompt block, in order, with intentional newlines preserved. After a successful submit, no submitted continuation line remains as an orphaned draft.

## Code evidence

`Chat:submit()` reads only `view.prompt_line` via `nvim_buf_get_lines(..., view.prompt_line, view.prompt_line + 1, ...)`. `submit_prompt()` then inserts the response separator and next prompt immediately after that one line, so any continuation lines are shifted below the new chat area rather than consumed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A two-line prompt entered with Shift+Enter is sent as one prompt containing both lines and their newline.
- All submitted prompt lines are rendered as transcript history and removed from the editable prompt region.
- The next `> ` prompt appears after the response area; no continuation text is left below it.
- Single-line submission and queued-prompt behavior remain unchanged.
- Headless UI tests cover multiline submission through the buffer-facing behavior, including the sent payload and resulting buffer layout.
close_reason: Fixed multiline chat prompt submission by reading and rendering the full prompt block. Added a headless regression test covering payload and buffer layout. Verification: focused chat suite 35/35, full mini.test suite 127/127, stylua --check passed, lua-language-server reported zero diagnostics, git diff --check passed.

title: Make Android Lint warnings fatal after auditing existing diagnostics
description:
Enforce Android Lint warnings after a bounded review of current diagnostics. Current compiler warnings and lint errors are fatal, but lint warnings are not. This follow-up avoids silently turning a documentation/regression task into SDK upgrades and runtime policy changes.

Evidence 2026-09-06: ./gradlew lint with warningsAsErrors=true failed with 17 errors promoted from warnings, AGP9.2.0/Gradle9.4.1. Report: android/app/build/intermediates/lint_intermediate_text_report/debug/lintReportDebug/lint-results-debug.txt.
Diagnostics: OldTargetApi x1 (targetSdk36); AndroidGradlePluginVersion x1 (wrapper9.4.1); GradleDependency x2 (compileSdk36, core1.17.0); NewerVersionAvailable x1 (test org.json20240303); PluralsCandidate x3 (confirm_first_pair, confirm_receiver_migration, attention_count); CustomX509TrustManager x1 (PinnedHttps.kt:218, intentional SPKI authority needs review, not automatic replacement with public CA validation); DataExtractionRules x1 (AndroidManifest.xml:10, separate privacy bug); IconLauncherShape x5 (mipmap launcher PNGs); UseKtx x2 (MainActivity.kt:534, PairingStore.kt:44). PairingStore checks commit() Boolean; suggested KTX edit returning Unit must not discard that durability check.

Acceptance: classify each diagnostic before fixing; use narrowly justified exceptions only for demonstrated false positives/boundaries, not a baseline or global suppressions. Split independently completable runtime fixes into child issues if claiming this work. Keep SDK/dependency updates intentional and tested. Enable warningsAsErrors=true, run ./gradlew test lint assembleDebug, prove failure on an introduced warning, and remove the explicit transitional caveat from android/AGENTS.md and README.md. No claim or implementation yet.
close_reason: gate:android/app/build.gradle.kts warningsAsErrors enforced; injected UnusedResources makes lint exit 1, removed probe restores passing test/lint/assembleDebug. Narrow documented exceptions; version upgrades tracked in louiselm-myd5.

comments.author: codex/01a07aa3-6afa-7673-877a-5578a88d0a42
comments.text: Audit: 17 warnings remain after 0u2t. PluralsCandidate x3 = quantity-text fix; IconLauncherShape x5 = native adaptive launcher fix (child slices). title: OpenCode approval hides the command as unknown, details unavailable
description:
OpenCode command approval shows "louiselm permission (unknown, details unavailable)" even though the permission payload contains the exact command. The operator cannot identify what Allow once / Always allow authorizes from the active picker. P1: informed approval is obstructed; no execution bypass or data loss established.

## Observed

Maintainer screenshot, inspected directly: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260909_0610_1920x1200_1788927022.png, 2026-09-09 06:10 Europe/Paris. Header: "Waiting for permission", Agent/Session opencode/ses_f7bbb4e43fferTp4BCTGDPkVt6. Picker title: "louiselm permission (unknown, details unavailable)". Choices: "Reject", "Allow once" (selected), "Always allow". Background transcript shows tool chatcmpl-tool-a530a7676e5b4b0f started.

Matching primary evidence: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ses_f7bbb4e43fferTp4BCTGDPkVt6/log.jsonl:11698, 2026-09-09T04:10:11.564Z, session/request_permission id=11, toolCallId=chatcmpl-tool-a530a7676e5b4b0f.
Verified fields: toolCall.kind="other", status="pending"; rawInput keys=["command","directories","patterns"]; rawInput.command equals toolCall.title and contains the full multiline shell command. Command begins: br create "Enable opencode auto mode in dotfiles-managed config". locations[1].path="/home/lotso/dotfiles". Options are once/allow_once, always/allow_always, reject/reject_once.
Earlier requests at log lines 11372, 11419, 11491 carry the same kind="other" plus rawInput.command structure. No sensitive payload copied.

## Reproduce

1. Use OpenCode in LouiseLM with a permission request for a shell command (observed request also carries directories/patterns for /home/lotso/dotfiles).
2. Wait for the picker before approving.
3. Observe unknown/details unavailable despite a command in the request and transcript.

## Root cause

Source inspected at 69045c7: lua/louiselm/permission/gates.lua:161 from_acp only extracts commands for kinds command/execute/shell (:183); other falls through to {kind="unknown"} (:190), losing command presentation context. lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1684 permission_prompt displays command details only for normalized kind=command; fallback at :1696 matches the screenshot.
This explains the observed payload/source combination; exact installed-source revision and live normalized event were not inspected.

## Why it was not caught

Prior fix louiselm-bjl covered Claude/Codex-shaped normalized commands. tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:4244 checks a command and explicit unknown fallbacks; that coverage does not prove this captured OpenCode other+rawInput.command request reaches a useful approval display.

## Fix direction

Preserve available request details at the normalization/presentation boundary. Inspect OpenCode directories/patterns grant semantics before reclassifying "other" as command: display clarity must not silently broaden policy or remembered grants. Do not infer the approved command from neighboring transcript lines. Related prior work: louiselm-bjl (closed; normalized command display), louiselm-us9 (genuinely pathless request fallback).

## Acceptance

- Captured OpenCode-shaped regression fails before the fix and proves the active permission UI exposes the exact command and applicable approval scope before selection.
- Long/multiline commands remain fully inspectable while approval is pending.
- Preserve rejection-first ordering, exact option IDs, dismissal cancellation, and permission policy/remembered-grant semantics.
- Truly missing details retain an honest fallback.
- Maintainer confirms the OpenCode live reproduction shows what will be authorized; keep open until confirmation.

## Not covered

Tracking only, deferred because the user requested filing rather than implementation. No fix or test execution. "Only OpenCode" is the maintainer's observation, not an established cross-Agent comparison. Screenshot proves pending approval, not its eventual outcome. Exact notification ordering beyond the pinned permission frame remains to be captured for any ordering-dependent regression.

not prove an unrelated remote does not exist, only that no usable configured
destination was found. VM stopped after inspection. Remote creation still needs
explicit scope/authorization; admission-only checks can be scoped separately.

- Dedicated witness Git remote URL and protected test branch, plus evidence of
  protection. Do not reuse project source remotes without explicit authorization.
- Approved bounded authentication/network route from disposable guest. VM has
  restricted egress and no forwarded SSH agent; do not loosen either implicitly.
  Never copy/read existing private credentials or ask for tokens in chat.
- Store scope: admitting and activating a QA Generation changes supply state.
  Obtain explicit approval for the exact protected store and intended change.
  Avoid another recovery ceremony until needed; no re-enrollment is queued.

## Status and cases

| Case | Status / required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Trusted package/Dossier fixture and public state baseline | Passed; exact harmless package and Dossier reviewed |
| Retired Primary refuses new Admission | Blocked: two key-decryption failures, not retired-authority refusal |
| Current Primary admits exact harmless package | Passed; fresh sequence2 terminal output shows passphrase/PIN/presence prompts and accepted hardware signature |
| Protected remote witness and activation | Passed after F1 exact-rule workaround; remote1962019b, current generatione0af9ac1 |
| Same-digest activation idempotence; verification without token | Passed; single pin byte-identical, no USB attached |
| Witness failure preserves prior active Generation | Passed; connection-refused exit1, current sequence1/pins/remote unchanged, sequence2 pending |

## Planned bounded sequence

1. Read-only guest preflight: installed identity, public recovery/generation state,
   current/retired public fingerprints, and fixture availability. No raw trust
   dump (contains paper/passkey material). Stop if old credentials unavailable.
2. Prepare one harmless complete Skill candidate, invoke installed packaging and
   trusted Dossier, record exact digest and literal Agent membership. Human reviews.
3. Give one command at a time in private human terminal: retired-key refusal,
   then current-Primary positive control. Check signature refusal reason and
   public before/after state; never count signing-helper failure as authorization
   refusal. Stop on unexpected behavior; don't generate/rotate keys as a workaround.
4. Witness exact approved bytes to selected protected remote/branch and verify
   readback before activation. Never call local-only bare Git production witnessing.
5. Activate agreed QA supply only, verify status/lineage and exact-digest retry
   idempotence. Disconnect token for verification check.
6. Exercise witness outage only against dedicated QA route with a new candidate;
   existing active Generation must remain unchanged. No disruption of real remotes.
7. Stop VM and record retained artifacts/state changes. Do not silently restore
   old trust or claim aggregate acceptance beyond actually exercised cases.

Failure signatures: retired key authorizes new payload; missing human touch/UV;
activation before exact remote readback; duplicate lineage pin on retry; witness
outage changes active Generation. Evidence must name exact Session/build/digests,
remote commit/branch, public state and human observations, never secrets.

## Closure

F1 is an unresolved GitLab access finding, not a proven LouiseLM code defect.
Further GitLab diagnosis needed before continuation. Prior reset round is
closed as louiselm-kpkc6; dtwil remains pending a natural capacity error.
Archive final working record as qa-round Bead and delete scratch at round end.

title: Trust-lock admission test flakes only under full-suite parallel load
description:
## Evidence

`./scripts/test-skills-core` (full suite, default parallelism) on commit
`898bc62` plus the `louiselm-qbr.5.1.2.4` composition change:

```
test a_held_trust_lock_refuses_activation_readers_and_other_writers ... FAILED
test result: FAILED. 23 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured
```

Run again immediately with no source change: clean, zero failures. Run the test
alone (`--test admission a_held_trust_lock`): passes, 0.15s.

So it fails only under whole-suite parallel load, not deterministically.

## Why it matters

The test at `skills-core/tests/admission.rs:399` asserts that a held trust lock
refuses activation readers and other writers — a contention property. A test
about lock contention that is itself flaky under contention cannot distinguish
"the lock works" from "the test lost a race", in either direction. It will be
read as noise and re-run until green, which is exactly how a real regression in
this property would ship.

## Not caused by the change that found it

Found while running the gates for `louiselm-qbr.5.1.2.4`, which touches only
`broker/lifecycle.rs`, `broker/lifecycle_service.rs` and `broker/installed.rs`.
Admission and trust are a different subsystem; the composition change adds no
lock, thread or filesystem contention. Filed rather than fixed, per the rule
against fixing another Agent's in-flight work.

## Next step

Decide whether the flake is the test's own timing assumption or a real
contention window in the trust lock. The second reading is the one that would
matter, so rule it out explicitly rather than stabilizing the test first.

title: Cancelling a turn leaves a zombie diff review and a blocked chat
description:
Predicted while writing the QA recipe, confirmed manually in session claude/8ee77329-247a-4f60-914f-9cb38bfed818 (case 5).

:LouiselmCancel during an open diff review works at the protocol level - the log shows PERMISSION id=2 kind=edit followed by TURN END cancelled, so the agent is released - but the UI is left broken:

- the review buffer stays on screen
- q and d appear to do nothing, because send_response only clears the review when the response succeeds and the request was already answered
- a opens the lifetime picker, and answering it fails the same way
- chat.decision_active stays set, so every guarded command keeps refusing with "a louiselm permission decision is open; answer it first"

Cause: Session:cancel answers outstanding requests through the raw ACP responder in cancel_permissions (lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua), which the chat never sees. The chat wrapper that owns the decision slot is downstream of the session responder, so the session cannot call it.

Fix: the session emits a typed permission_cancelled event carrying the request ids it answered; the chat marks those decisions answered, closes an open review, releases the slot and pumps the queue. The decision slot is now compared by identity so a stale picker answering late cannot release the decision that replaced it.

An open picker still cannot be closed programmatically - vim.ui.select has no cancel handle - so answering a stale picker reports "permission decision was already answered". That is accepted.
close_reason: Fixed in c0ae0aa. Tests: tests/session/api_spec.lua asserts the permission_cancelled event carries both request ids; tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'closes a review and frees the chat when its request is cancelled' and 'drops queued decisions whose requests were cancelled'. Full suite 203 cases, stylua and lua-language-server clean. Needs a live retest of QA case 5.

title: QA private Android capture across LAN, overlay, and recovery
description:
# Manual QA review — private Android capture reachability and recovery

Working file for `louiselm-1chb`. The user drives the physical phone; Codex
prepares the receiver, checks durable evidence, and updates this file after
each case. This file is intentionally untracked. When the round closes, its
final content becomes the durable record on `louiselm-1chb` and this scratch
copy is deleted.

**Build under test:** `efe6a15` (`feat(capture)!: bind queues to receiver
identity`) on top of `9440eaa` (`feat(capture)!: configure private receiver`).
APK SHA-256:
`06a7b8f11055bbff996fdf00753a7d32773865e5be7c750c1a7e076874b252ed`.
**Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: the receiver used to bind loopback while advertising an
address-bound pairing identity, making both LAN and off-LAN Android delivery
unreliable. The two implementation slices now provide one explicit private
network profile, a stable public-key identity, receiver-owned phone queues,
safe endpoint retargeting, and two-sided delivery health. Automated gates are
green; this round tests the physical network, process, reboot, certificate,
and consent boundaries they cannot reach.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Default loopback pairing refusal | **passed** — exit 1, zero stdout bytes, actionable `configure-network` error; listener pinned to `127.0.0.1:7391` |
| 2 | First pairing assigns an offline capture and drains over LAN | **passed** — counted LAN confirmation; same UUID/audio uploaded once; owner and per-device delivery persisted |
| 3 | LAN departure/return and force-stop/reboot preserve one UUID | **passed** — both captures survived force-stop/reboot and drained once each on home Wi-Fi with exact audio hashes |
| 4 | Forced acknowledgement-loss retry is idempotent | **passed** — existing receiver UUID accepted; phone re-marked uploaded; immutable hashes and capture count unchanged |
| 5 | Overlay delivery works on Wi-Fi and mobile data | **routed blocker** — no desktop overlay is installed; follow-up `louiselm-1chb.2` |
| 6 | Certificate renewal keeps trust; replacement key is rejected | **passed** — renewed cert retained trust; different key produced actionable mismatch and left capture local |
| 7 | Same-identity endpoint update preserves enrollment | **passed** — no migration dialog; endpoint changed to 7392; original device/credential drained queued UUID once |
| 8 | Different-identity migration requires counted consent | **passed** — cancel preserved old state; count-2 confirm migrated owners/enrollment; manual workaround drained both UUIDs once |
| 9 | Phone and receiver status are useful and sanitized | **passed** — healthy phone/LAN status and degraded paired-on-loopback warning are actionable and sanitized |

## Setup

Current preflight, before changing anything:

- receiver host LAN address: `192.168.10.121`;
- `adb` exists at `/home/lotso/Android/Sdk/platform-tools/adb` but no phone is
  connected yet;
- the APK exists at
  `/home/lotso/code/louiselm/android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`;
- the running receiver service and installed binary are stale: its unit still
  calls `serve --bind ...`, which the build under test removed;
- no new network-profile file exists, so the build under test will start in
  loopback-only mode;
- the old pairing registry is schema 1 with one Xiaomi device. The new build
  intentionally requires schema 2. Archive that registry before starting the
  new receiver; do not touch the 17 canonical captures.

Case-1 setup completed at 2026-08-21 13:31 CEST. Recoverable archive:
`/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm/qa-efe6a15.S3frcl`. It contains the old
binary, systemd unit, and schema-1 pairing registry. The 17 canonical captures
and existing TLS identity were not moved. The installed release binary has
SHA-256
`18dbc46914917abfc4255321b9c52a5bead470582922ccb5d725d0f8630382b8`;
systemd now invokes exactly `louiselm-capture serve`, and the new registry is
schema 2 with zero paired devices.

Phone preflight completed after USB authorization:

- Xiaomi `21081111RG`, Android 14 / API 34, build
  `V816.0.19.0.UKWEUXM`;
- installed debug app 0.1.0, last updated 2026-08-21 05:29, APK SHA-256
  `275d4c598b9a84ca1d95f31222ba12d90cc0e5626999665ddb1b6fb47cd1f718`
  (not the build-under-test APK);
- `run-as` works;
- 17 capture directories exist and all have an `uploaded` marker;
- all 17 mutable `upload.json` files predate receiver ownership and lack the
  new schema/version field; only old `pairing.xml` exists.

This is a setup incompatibility, not a failed case: the project explicitly
chose a breaking v2 queue/pairing schema and has no external users or migration
path. Installing the new APK over this data would make its status reject the
old mutable state. The safe recommended fixture reset is: create a mode-0600
local archive of the entire app-private data through debug `run-as`, verify its
checksum and inventory, then—only with explicit user approval—clear the app and
install the exact build-under-test APK. The receiver already retains the 17
canonical copies; neither side is touched until approval.

The user approved that reset. The private backup is
`/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm/qa-efe6a15.S3frcl/phone-app-data-before-v2.tar`,
mode 0600, SHA-256
`66111eca00562252a533879249f3ccabcf8af311143fc978bc9c8fa0aa424afa`.
Its verified inventory contains 17 capture directories, 17 audio files, 17
manifests, 17 upload states, and 17 uploaded markers. It also retains the old
app-private preferences for forensic reference, but the old encrypted pairing
credential is not considered restorable because Android Keystore state is
outside that archive. After verification, `pm clear` succeeded and the exact
QA APK was installed: the on-device base APK SHA-256 is now
`06a7b8f11055bbff996fdf00753a7d32773865e5be7c750c1a7e076874b252ed`.
The fresh app has no capture files or pairing preferences.

Before case 1, Codex will:

1. Confirm the connected phone's model, Android version, installed app, and
   existing capture inventory with read-only `adb` commands.
2. Preserve any existing phone capture data before considering an app-data
   reset. Never use `pm clear` without explicit user consent and a verified
   backup.
3. Stop the user service; archive (move, do not delete) the schema-1 pairing
   registry; install the release receiver and current systemd unit; reload and
   restart the service.
4. Install the exact APK above with `adb install -r`, which retains app data.
5. Record the installed APK/version and receiver commit in this file.

The user must keep the phone and receiver on the same Wi-Fi for cases 1–2.
Cases 3 and 5 explicitly change networks. Do not expose the receiver on a
public IP or forward a router port.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Invoke `adb` by its absolute path; it is installed but absent from `PATH`.
- A green systemd state from before Setup is not evidence: the old process is
  still running the removed `serve --bind` interface.
- Preserve app-private originals. A clean fixture is convenient but never
  worth silently deleting prior recordings.
- `adb install -r` preserves app data, but that is not useful here: all 17
  installed upload-state files are deliberately incompatible with v2. Do not
  mistake the resulting schema error for a product regression.
- No Tailscale/WireGuard command is currently installed on the receiver host.
  Overlay testing needs an already-approved external overlay; LouiseLM must
  not install or manage one.
- Xiaomi's always-on display can replace the app after an `adb` launch while
  the phone is locked. Unlock it before judging any app UI or recording case.

## Cases

### 1. Default loopback pairing refusal

Exercises `9440eaa` / the default `NetworkProfile` and `pair` guard.

Steps:

> With no `capture-network.json`, start the new service. Run
> `louiselm-capture status`, then `louiselm-capture pair`.

Expect: status reports loopback `127.0.0.1:7391`, no advertised receiver URL,
and phone reachability false. Pair exits nonzero with guidance to run
`configure-network`; it prints no QR or token.

Failure signature: pair succeeds, a QR is printed, the receiver binds a
wildcard/public address, or the error does not say how to configure a private
profile.

Evidence: save the sanitized status JSON and the pair exit code/error. This
proves receiver behavior; no phone action is involved.

Result: passed. `status` reported the loopback bind, null profile/URL,
`phone_reachable: false`, zero paired devices, and unconfigured delivery.
`pair` exited 1, wrote zero stdout bytes, and told the operator that phone
pairing requires `configure-network`. `ss` showed one listener on
`127.0.0.1:7391`, not a wildcard. Evidence is archived as
`case1-status.json`, `case1-pair.stdout`, and `case1-pair.stderr` under the QA
archive named in Setup.

### 2. First pairing assigns an offline capture and drains over LAN

Exercises `efe6a15` queue ownership plus `9440eaa` LAN pairing.

Steps:

> Before pairing, open the app, record one short phrase, and stop. Confirm the
> phone says one capture is pending. Codex configures LAN bind and URL as
> `192.168.10.121:7391`, restarts the service, and generates a fresh QR. Scan
> it. Read the confirmation carefully: it must state the count of unowned
> captures and the LAN endpoint. Confirm once, then tap **Sync now** if needed.

Expect: the dialog says exactly one affected capture for a clean fixture; the
phone becomes paired, the pending count drains, and the receiver stores that
same UUID once. Receiver device status gains a non-null last-delivery time.

Failure signature: no count is shown, upload starts before confirmation, the
capture stays unowned after confirmation, a new UUID appears, or the original
phone audio disappears.

Evidence: pin the UUID from `files/captures/<uuid>` before pairing, then compare
it with `~/.local/share/louiselm/captures/<uuid>/capture.json`. Receiver
`status` must show one paired device and `last_delivery_at_ms`. The evidence
cannot prove the dialog wording; that rests on the user's observation.

Pre-pair evidence: the user reported prefix `05a6`; `run-as` resolved exactly
`05a655b1-d602-4a1f-b543-2540899e4c7d`. Its manifest records Android source,
4.761 seconds, 76,525 bytes, and audio SHA-256
`62080f4e450476ff003ea36cdfa57af5611faebd0dc4186a59151e585480668e`;
the live audio hash matches. Its upload state is schema 1, pending, with
`receiver_identity_sha256: null`; the uploaded marker and receiver directory
are absent. This proves durable pre-pair ownership and pins the immutable
before-state.

LAN setup is now active at `192.168.10.121:7391`. Status reports profile `lan`,
phone reachability true, zero paired devices, and no warning. `ss` shows the
single explicit LAN listener, and `/v1/health` returned `ok` plus public
receiver identity
`2a12f204a92d8850b76c6af6e88eed57e8431f2cdab16ca2223c9810a1d8aaa3`.

Dialog boundary: the user reports that the dialog names the LAN IP and shows
an affected count of 1; confirmation of the exact word `unowned` is still
pending. Before consent, objective evidence shows the phone owner remains
null, no v2 pairing preference exists, the receiver has zero devices and only
one pending one-time offer, and the capture is still absent from the receiver.
Scanning alone therefore changed neither ownership nor enrollment.

Result: passed. The user confirmed the count-1 LAN dialog (wording was
paraphrased rather than transcribed) and tapped Confirm. The phone created the
encrypted `pairing-v2` preference, changed only mutable upload state to receiver
owner
`2a12f204a92d8850b76c6af6e88eed57e8431f2cdab16ca2223c9810a1d8aaa3`,
then marked the capture uploaded at `1787314290836`. The original audio and
manifest hashes remained exactly
`62080f4e450476ff003ea36cdfa57af5611faebd0dc4186a59151e585480668e`
and `349821e8c58af6f480d1cdb6078bc51664e60bb78b0f245151af3da5ba848fce`.
The receiver has one canonical directory for the same UUID and matching audio
hash, one paired Xiaomi device (`a738ac6c-2d94-4220-8d02-fc0735e84e06`), and
last delivery `1787314291031`. Live UI evidence showed the LAN URL, pending 0,
last sync 2026-08-21 14:11, attention 0, and latest failure none.

### 3. LAN departure/return and force-stop/reboot preserve one UUID

Exercises WorkManager scheduling and durable app-private queue recovery.

Steps:

> Disable Wi-Fi so the phone is on mobile data and cannot reach the LAN-only
> address. Record capture A and note its UUID/pending status. Force-stop the
> app, reopen it, and confirm A remains. Record capture B, reboot the phone,
> reopen the app, and confirm A and B remain with the same UUIDs. Re-enable
> home Wi-Fi and tap **Sync now** once.

Expect: neither capture uploads over mobile data; both survive force-stop and
reboot; both drain after LAN reachability returns; the receiver contains each
UUID exactly once.

Failure signature: either pending capture vanishes, its UUID changes, mobile
data reaches the private LAN receiver unexpectedly, or return-to-Wi-Fi creates
duplicates.

Evidence: record both UUIDs before lifecycle changes, inspect the same phone
directories after each, then compare receiver directories after drain.

Capture A evidence: with Wi-Fi setting 0 and validated LTE as Android's active
default network, prefix `4deb` resolved exactly to
`4deb4e34-4b17-4545-a1ee-3558a6dbc300`. It is pending under receiver identity
`2a12f204a92d8850b76c6af6e88eed57e8431f2cdab16ca2223c9810a1d8aaa3`,
has no uploaded marker, and is absent from the receiver. Audio and manifest
hashes are
`780ba574e52cf36d39dbf4c24f99fc5748cf8428f744a525b44d112c338125b3`
and `8b385476e538a8f66f3811462b99e273d2132b01eaf3d2323d519f69a7b0f24c`.
ADB force-stop left no app PID; both hashes, UUID, owner, and pending state were
unchanged while stopped and after a cold relaunch. The relaunched UI reported
the paired LAN endpoint, pending 1, oldest 1 minute, the prior last-sync time,
attention 0, and no latest failure. Force-stop/relaunch therefore passes; the
reboot half remains.

Capture B evidence: while the same Wi-Fi-off/LTE isolation remained active,
prefix `b5bf` resolved exactly to
`b5bf51ad-79ef-448a-86c7-e28bba2b2a10`. It is pending under the same receiver
identity, has no uploaded marker, and is absent from the receiver. Audio and
manifest hashes are
`98d15d44ef36252451e5b1abdd3e0b7319094fed6b1d2eec118dd8c7ce5dbcb3`
and `6f79fd785c6a616b2e853439df59f33f54d002231757a1e50a971bae1c5d6a92`.
Capture A's UUID, pending state, ownership, hashes, and receiver absence also
remained unchanged. The phone UI reported 2 pending before reboot.

Post-reboot evidence: Android reported boot complete, the user performed the
required first unlock and opened LouiseLM, and `pairing-v2.xml` remained in
app-private preferences. With Wi-Fi still disabled, both capture directories,
UUIDs, receiver ownership, pending states, missing uploaded markers, and exact
audio/manifest hashes matched their pre-reboot values; both UUIDs remained
absent from the receiver. Reboot persistence therefore passes. The final
return-to-Wi-Fi drain remains.

Return-to-Wi-Fi evidence: one manual **Sync now** changed both phone upload
states to uploaded and created their markers at `1787314849359` and
`1787314849491`. The receiver contains exactly one directory for each UUID;
their audio hashes match the phone's pinned values, their canonical manifests
retain the same UUIDs and embedded audio hashes, and receiver delivery advanced
to `1787314849471`. Receiver status reports 20 captures, 20 completed
transcriptions, zero pending/retrying/failed, and the same single paired device.
Case 3 therefore passes.

The visible app status remained `Upload work queued.` after background success
until the user pressed Home and returned, when it showed pending 0. This did not
affect delivery correctness and is filed separately as `louiselm-qbr.1.11`.

### 4. Forced acknowledgement-loss retry is idempotent

Exercises the receiver's `Created`/`Existing` contract and one UUID per retry.

Steps:

> Upload one capture normally and pin its UUID. With the app stopped, Codex
> uses debug `run-as` to archive then remove only that capture's mutable
> `uploaded` marker and set its upload state back to pending, leaving audio and
> `capture.json` unchanged. Reopen the app and tap **Sync now**.

Expect: the receiver answers the retry as existing/success, the phone marks it
uploaded again, the receiver still has one directory for the UUID, and the
device last-delivery timestamp advances.

Failure signature: a second receiver capture appears, a conflict is reported,
the phone enters operator-action state, or any immutable phone file changes.

Evidence: hash phone `audio.m4a` and `capture.json` before/after, count the
single receiver UUID directory, and compare the device delivery timestamp.

Result: passed with capture `b5bf51ad-79ef-448a-86c7-e28bba2b2a10`.
While the app was force-stopped, its prior mutable upload state and marker were
archived under app-private `cache/qa-case4-b5bf`; only the live marker was
removed and the live upload state reset to pending for the same receiver
identity. Pinned pre/post-retry phone hashes remained
`98d15d44ef36252451e5b1abdd3e0b7319094fed6b1d2eec118dd8c7ce5dbcb3`
and `6f79fd785c6a616b2e853439df59f33f54d002231757a1e50a971bae1c5d6a92`.
After one **Sync now**, the phone returned to uploaded at `1787315251593`, its
marker reappeared, and the receiver still had exactly one directory for the
UUID with matching audio hash and canonical manifest fields. Receiver capture
count remained 20 and device last delivery advanced from `1787314849471` to
`1787315251580`; transcription remained 20 completed and zero pending,
retrying, or failed.

### 5. Overlay delivery works on Wi-Fi and mobile data

Exercises the explicit `overlay` profile without making LouiseLM manage the
overlay.

Steps:

> After the user supplies an approved overlay address already installed on
> both devices, configure the receiver's one overlay bind/URL and pair or
> retarget to it. Upload one capture on Wi-Fi, disable Wi-Fi, then upload a
> second over mobile data without changing the endpoint or pairing.

Expect: both UUIDs arrive once; the phone retains the same endpoint, receiver
identity, device ID, and credential across the network transition.

Failure signature: an overlay package must be installed by LouiseLM, the
endpoint changes automatically, re-pairing is required, or mobile-data upload
cannot reach an otherwise working approved overlay.

Evidence: the external overlay's own device/address status plus both receiver
capture manifests. No credentials or full environment dumps belong here.

### 6. Certificate renewal keeps trust; replacement key is rejected

Exercises public-key pinning rather than exact-certificate pinning.

Steps:

> Codex archives the current certificate, generates a new self-signed
> certificate from the same receiver private key, restarts the service, and
> the user uploads capture A. Then, with capture B queued, Codex archives the
> whole TLS identity and lets the receiver generate a different key. Restart
> and tap **Sync now** without scanning a QR.

Expect: A uploads through the renewed certificate. B remains local and shows
the actionable receiver-identity mismatch; it is not uploaded under the new
key.

Failure signature: same-key renewal breaks trust, different-key replacement is
accepted silently, B disappears, or a generic retry hides the identity
mismatch.

Evidence: compare public-key SHA-256 before/after each change, pin A/B UUIDs,
and inspect receiver/app queue state. Certificate files and private keys are
never copied into this record.

mode 0600 outside the repository. Its certificate SHA-256
`13889ad12cf6cb7645d6c714c128e0584914988455fb6d8f82595216eb7999c0`
changed to
`dbebae0cd5d287b1063508f820be7881b314c0d91581ae10c2821b02841240e5`,

`2a12f204a92d8850b76c6af6e88eed57e8431f2cdab16ca2223c9810a1d8aaa3`.
The restarted receiver is active and `/v1/health` reports that same identity.
No key contents were printed or copied into this record. Awaiting capture A to
exercise the already-paired Android trust path.

Same-key renewal result: capture A
`77abf209-3b19-40e7-9763-037027cb4850` uploaded without a new QR or endpoint
change. Phone audio/manifest hashes are
`4d48c43db40a85776023cd12cf1d3336266a19f5f7e5a590af5d7c0fe57b2c62`
and `25e9908420abded626bcc9d1262dfcf08bb84c33c559e068f642ecd689125d18`;
the receiver contains one matching canonical UUID/audio hash, capture count is
21, and last delivery advanced to `1787315432044`. This half passes. Awaiting
offline capture B and a different-key replacement for the rejection half.

Different-key setup: with Wi-Fi off, capture B
`fb43f905-2cdf-4af9-8fe3-fd47a46921f2` remained pending under the trusted
identity, unmarked and absent from the receiver. Its pinned audio/manifest
hashes are
`bf6115a59e86d89ac67606c0157891fa2af170203b62bb37b82e29867f87cb70`
and `0803693451b9f538f6a3871099faabb20d1c1d67e9fce2013b3bee6ea841f52d`.
The complete trusted TLS directory was moved recoverably into the mode-0700 QA
archive with both files mode 0600. A fresh receiver identity was then generated:

`d1bbe682...7712a2`; the service and health endpoint are active under the new
identity. Awaiting the old-pairing upload attempt.

Different-key result: the upload worker set capture B to `operator_action` with
the exact sanitized failure `receiver identity does not match pairing`. The
user confirmed the receiver-mismatch text became visible after the known
lifecycle-refresh workaround. B retained its owner, UUID, exact pinned hashes,

### 7. Same-identity endpoint update preserves enrollment

Exercises the pinned `/v1/health` check and endpoint-only save.

Steps:

> Restore the trusted key from the first half of case 6. Record one queued
> capture. Change the LAN receiver from port 7391 to 7392 while retaining the
> TLS key, restart, and generate a fresh QR. Scan it.

Expect: no migration-count dialog appears; the app verifies health through the
old public-key pin, changes only the URL to port 7392, and uploads with the old
credential. Receiver paired-device count and device ID remain unchanged.

Failure signature: a second device is enrolled, credentials are rejected,
queued ownership changes, the old URL is saved after failed health, or a
migration confirmation appears for the same identity.

Evidence: compare sanitized receiver status before/after (same device ID and
paired count, changed endpoint, later delivery time) and the phone's displayed
endpoint. The encrypted credential itself is never printed.

Setup/result so far: still-local capture `fb43f905-...` is reused as the queued
same-owner fixture. The receiver moved from `192.168.10.121:7391` to port 7392
while retaining public identity `2a12f204...d8aaa3`, paired-device count 1,
device ID `a738ac6c-...`, and last-delivery time `1787315432044`; `ss` showed
only the explicit 7392 listener and the old port was closed. The first QR was
not visible in the Neovim session despite a completed View Image tool row; this
is filed as `louiselm-ce6.21`. A clickable temporary QR was subsequently tried
three or four times without updating the endpoint. The user observed stale
queue/status lines after camera confirmation followed by a standalone error;
that presentation defect is `louiselm-qbr.1.12`. The exact terminal error and
root cause of the failed attempts are still pending; QR expiry caused by the
delivery delay remains a hypothesis, not a finding.

Controlled follow-up: the native QR in the user's dark Neovim terminal failed
with `No LouiseLM pairing QR was found. Move closer and try again.` A fresh
native QR forced to black-on-white decoded and updated the phone display to
`https://192.168.10.121:7392`; no new receiver enrollment appeared. This
contrast defect is filed as `louiselm-qbr.1.13`. The screen still showed the
old Case 6 latest-failure text, demonstrating `louiselm-qbr.1.12`, and reported
3 pending. Inventory found the expected `fb43f905-...` plus two newly recorded
short captures, `ab3f5431-...` (1377 ms) and `67ffeb3d-...` (605 ms), all owned
by the same trusted identity. Their intent is awaiting user confirmation; no
audio or queue state has been removed or rewritten. Endpoint-update drain is
not yet proven because background work currently retries.

Final result: passed. The user confirmed no migration-count dialog appeared
and that the two short recordings were accidental button mispresses; the
control-spacing defect is filed as `louiselm-qbr.1.14`. One **Sync now** drained
the expected `fb43f905-...` and both preserved accidental captures. Each phone
state is uploaded with a marker, and the receiver has exactly one canonical
directory with matching audio hash for each. `fb43f905-...` retained its pinned
audio/manifest hashes. Receiver capture count advanced 21 to 24, device ID and
paired count remained unchanged, last delivery advanced to `1787319102206`,
and both sides report pending/attention/failure zero/none at endpoint 7392.
The accidental recordings remain preserved on both sides; no deletion was
requested or performed.

### 8. Different-identity migration requires counted consent

Exercises the cross-identity consent and mutable-only migration path.

Steps:

> Queue one capture under the currently paired identity. Switch the receiver
> to a different archived/generated TLS key and scan its fresh QR. Record the
> displayed affected count, then cancel. Confirm the capture remains pending
> and unchanged. Scan another fresh QR, confirm the migration, and sync.

Expect: cancel leaves ownership and enrollment unchanged; the mismatched
receiver cannot upload the capture. Confirm shows the same count, changes
ownership/retry eligibility, and uploads the original UUID/audio to the new
identity.

Failure signature: upload or reassignment happens before confirmation, cancel
changes the endpoint/credential/owner, the count is absent or wrong, or
confirmation rewrites/deletes the immutable files.

Evidence: hash phone audio/manifest before both scans, inspect the sanitized
owner in `upload.json` after cancel and after confirm, and compare the receiver
UUID. Dialog/count correctness also requires the user's observation.

Setup: with Wi-Fi off, intentional capture
`c30cc720-e07a-44e1-9338-19289e568ddd` is pending under trusted identity
`2a12f204...d8aaa3`, unmarked, absent from the receiver, and pinned to
audio/manifest hashes
`d33e14b0c9a9975d372772404504ce4233364fdd50f7454caebfc774be8e6303`
and `b36b9336d809171880d285b77dfec2fc1ca00404168fbe99099189aa43cfc905`.
The capture acknowledgement did not refresh the pending summary until
Home/return; filed separately as `louiselm-qbr.1.15`.

QR diagnosis: the original terminal-contrast theory did not survive a clean
physical retry. `louiselm-capture pair --svg` generated a private mode-0600,
1095-by-1095 SVG with deterministic black modules, white background, quiet
zone, and crisp edges. Displayed directly in GIMP, it looked clean to the user,
but the Xiaomi camera/ML Kit path still returned exactly `No LouiseLM pairing
QR was found. Move closer and try again.` The failure is therefore before
payload parsing and networking and is not explained by Neovim terminal colors.
The actual camera JPEG handoff must be inspected before choosing the fix.

The retained handoff proved Xiaomi wrote a valid 3000-by-4000, 3.75 MB JPEG;
the photographed version-12 QR had a 65-by-65 data grid with visible screen
moire and perspective. Compact v2 wire keys reduced the same security-bearing
payload to a 57-by-57 grid without shortening the 256-bit receiver identity or
256-bit one-use token, removing expiry, or weakening server enforcement. The
matching receiver/APK passed all automated gates and the same physical camera
path decoded the compact QR on its first reported attempt. The private SVG was
deleted after scanning; the retained JPEG evidence is mode 0600 in the QA
archive and contains only the now-expired prior offer.

The migration dialog reported 2 rather than the originally pinned 1 because a
new local capture `4e9a8a1d-b337-495a-8202-f91d82262c7e` appeared at 16:13
during the retry. It is 2408 ms, pending under the old identity, absent from
the receiver, and pinned to audio/manifest hashes
`028a35e1deed4094959a74a337fa359c1d2a1894038fbecfdeb61ff65314d19d`
and `89b91a9a1f323b74c49b503afcb32c5a088216548971ce8cb166a6fb3ed7570a`.
This makes the displayed count correct; its intent awaits user confirmation,
and it remains preserved. The repeat is recorded on `louiselm-qbr.1.14`.

Cancel result: the user confirmed the second successful scan was cancelled and
that `4e9a...` was another accidental recording. Objective post-cancel state
settles the forgotten dialog details: the receiver still had exactly one old
device enrollment, both `c30cc...` and `4e9a...` remained pending under old
identity `2a12f204...d8aaa3`, neither had an uploaded marker, and neither was
present on the receiver. Thus scanning/cancelling changed no enrollment,
credential, capture owner, immutable file, or receiver copy. The confirm half
will use a fresh QR after restoring LAN reachability.

Confirm result: on restored home Wi-Fi, the fresh dialog again reported 2 and
the user confirmed. Both mutable upload states changed to new identity
`d1bbe682...7712a2` while all four immutable hashes stayed pinned. The receiver
created exactly one new Xiaomi enrollment (`8a2ae949-...`) and retained the old
one. No upload preceded consent. However, five seconds later both captures
were still local/unmarked/absent from the receiver because WorkManager retained
the old unreachable receiver retry delay: `dumpsys jobscheduler` showed the
upload job blocked only by `TIMING_DELAY`, with minimum latency about 25m54s
and earliest run about 19m49s away. Filed as `louiselm-1chb.1`; one manual Sync
is the documented workaround and will complete this case without fixing the
new finding inline.

Final result: passed with the routed `louiselm-1chb.1` workaround. One manual
Sync replaced the stale retry. Both phone states became uploaded under new
identity `d1bbe682...7712a2` with markers and timestamps
`1787322377627`/`1787322377545`. Receiver total advanced 24 to 26; new device
`8a2ae949-...` gained last delivery `1787322377578`; both UUID directories
exist exactly once. Phone/receiver audio hashes match exactly, and canonical
manifest fields (schema, UUID, source, recorded time, duration, MIME, byte
count, SHA-256) match for both captures. The phone foreground remained on
`Upload work queued.` after completion, reconfirming `louiselm-qbr.1.11`.

### 9. Phone and receiver status are useful and sanitized

Exercises both operator surfaces after the preceding state transitions.

Steps:

> Observe phone status while unpaired, pending, failed on identity mismatch,
> and successfully synced. Run receiver `status` once with a private profile,
> then once in loopback-only configuration while a paired device exists.

Expect: phone status shows endpoint, pending count/oldest age, last sync,
latest actionable failure, and **Sync now**. Receiver status shows profile,
bind, advertised URL, paired count, per-device last delivery, and a degraded
warning for paired-on-loopback. Neither side shows tokens, credentials,
environment variables, audio, prompts, or capture contents.

Failure signature: healthy is shown for paired-on-loopback, useful timestamps
or endpoint are missing, queue depth is invented on the receiver, or sensitive
material appears.

Evidence: sanitized screenshots plus receiver status JSON. Visual layout and
button usability rest on user observation.

Result: passed. After Home/reopen, the phone showed endpoint
`https://192.168.10.121:7392`, pending 0, oldest none, last sync 16:26, attention
0, failure none, and the Sync now action. Receiver LAN status showed profile,
explicit bind/URL, 26 captures, two paired devices, per-device delivery times,
and reachable delivery. With the mode-0600 network profile recoverably moved
aside, the service listened only on `127.0.0.1:7391`; status showed null
profile/URL, `phone_reachable: false`, `delivery.state: degraded`, and exact
warning `paired devices cannot reach the loopback-only receiver`. The profile
was restored automatically and the service returned to the sole explicit
`192.168.10.121:7392` listener with reachable status. Neither surface exposed
pairing tokens, device credentials, environments, audio, prompts, or capture
contents.

## Evidence checks

Use the exact UUIDs recorded per case, never “the newest” capture:

```sh
ADB=/home/lotso/Android/Sdk/platform-tools/adb
$ADB shell run-as dev.louiselm.capture find files/captures -maxdepth 2 -type f -print
louiselm-capture status
jq '{id, source, recorded_at_ms, duration_ms, bytes, sha256}' \
  "$HOME/.local/share/louiselm/captures/<uuid>/capture.json"
```

Before trusting a phone-state check, validate that `run-as` succeeds against
the installed debug APK and that the listed UUID matches the one visible before
the tested transition. These commands prove durable state and identity; they
do not prove dialog wording, focus, or whether the user perceived the status
as actionable.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- Restore the chosen long-term receiver TLS identity, port/profile, installed
  service unit, and any archived pairing registry the user wants to retain.
- Remove only QA captures the user explicitly approves; originals are not
  automatically deleted.
- Keep or uninstall the debug APK according to the user's choice.
- Route every finding as a child bead of `louiselm-1chb` before fixing it.
- Replace `louiselm-1chb`'s description with this final round record, close it
  only when all cases pass or blockers are explicitly routed, flush beads, and
  delete this untracked file.

## Reporting back

Report the case number, exactly what appeared on the phone, and anything
surprising. Codex will pull the receiver and `adb run-as` evidence, classify a
recipe miss versus a product bug, update this file, and give only the next case.

## Findings this round

- F1 `louiselm-qbr.1.11` — manual Sync foreground status stays stale until resume.
- F2 `louiselm-ce6.21` — completed image tool output is invisible in Neovim chat.
- F3 `louiselm-qbr.1.12` — QR result is composed behind stale queue failure/status.
- F4 `louiselm-qbr.1.13` — dense pairing QR failed physical decoding; fixed and
  physically accepted in `9e194da` with compact wire keys and secure SVG output.
- F5 `louiselm-qbr.1.14` — tightly spaced controls caused three confirmed
  accidental recordings (`ab3f...`, `67ff...`, `4e9a...`).
- F6 `louiselm-qbr.1.15` — pending count after capture stays stale until resume.
- F7 `louiselm-1chb.1` — successful receiver migration remains behind old
  WorkManager retry backoff; manual Sync is the workaround.

## Round conclusion

Cases 1-4 and 6-9 passed on the physical Xiaomi. Case 5 is not represented as
passed: no private-overlay client exists on this host, so its externally owned
setup and physical Wi-Fi/mobile verification are routed to
`louiselm-1chb.2`. The core product guarantee was proven: recordings persist
while unreachable and drain exactly once on restored private reachability.

Automated tests missed the findings primarily because they cannot photograph a
real screen through Xiaomi camera software, exercise foreground Activity
refresh timing, reproduce physical button mispresses, or retain Android
WorkManager backoff across a live identity transition. The compact QR fix added
a deterministic density bound; the remaining behavioral gaps are preserved in
their child beads.

Final live state: receiver identity `d1bbe682...7712a2`, LAN profile
`192.168.10.121:7392`, service active, 26 canonical captures, two paired-device
records, and zero receiver transcription backlog. Phone Wi-Fi is enabled on the
home LAN, the exact `9e194da` debug APK remains installed, all nine app-private
captures remain preserved, and phone queue status is pending/attention/failure
0/0/none. The verified pre-v2 phone backup and prior trusted TLS identity remain
recoverably archived under the mode-0700 QA directory. The mode-0600 camera
JPEG evidence remains there and contains only an expired pairing offer; all
live SVG pairing artifacts and the temporary app-private JPEG copy were
removed. No recording was deleted.

title: Receiver migration leaves uploads behind old retry backoff
description:
After a user successfully confirms migration to a reachable receiver identity, newly migrated captures can remain pending behind the WorkManager retry delay created while the old receiver was unreachable. The workaround is Sync now, which replaces the work.

## Observed
Physical QA louiselm-1chb on 2026-08-21, commit 9e194da, Xiaomi 21081111RG Android 14/API 34. Two captures were pending under old receiver identity 2a12f204...d8aaa3 while the phone was offline. After home Wi-Fi returned and the user confirmed migration to d1bbe682...7712a2, both upload.json files immediately changed owner and a second receiver device enrollment appeared.

Five seconds later both captures still lacked uploaded markers and receiver copies. dumpsys jobscheduler dev.louiselm.capture showed the WorkManager SystemJobService job with Minimum latency +25m54s230ms, Unsatisfied constraints: TIMING_DELAY, Run time earliest +19m48s712ms, while connectivity, quota, charging, battery, and doze constraints were satisfied. App UI still reported Pending: 2.

## Symptoms
- Confirming a reachable receiver migration does not start uploads promptly.
- The user must press Sync now or wait roughly 20 more minutes even though pairing just succeeded.

## Root cause
android/app/src/main/java/dev/louiselm/capture/MainActivity.kt:342-344 enqueues ordinary automatic work after pairing. android/app/src/main/java/dev/louiselm/capture/UploadWorker.kt:46-62 uses APPEND_OR_REPLACE for automatic work, so the new request remains behind the unique work chain and its retry backoff from the old unreachable identity. Manual work uses REPLACE and clears it.

## Why it was not caught
Unit tests assert the selected ExistingWorkPolicy values but do not model an existing retry with backoff followed by a successful receiver migration. Physical QA previously used Sync now as an allowed recovery step.

## Fix direction
At the successful pairing boundary, replace obsolete upload work because the endpoint or identity and retry conditions have materially changed. Keep ordinary background enqueue semantics for captures and connectivity retries.

## Acceptance
- A regression test distinguishes successful pairing enqueue from ordinary automatic capture enqueue and requires replacement of obsolete retry work.
- After confirming migration with a backed-off old-receiver job, eligible captures start without manual Sync and without waiting for the old delay.
- UUIDs, immutable audio/manifests, queue ownership, and retry idempotence remain unchanged.
- Android test, lint, and assembleDebug gates pass.

## Not covered
Foreground status refresh after manual Sync is louiselm-qbr.1.11. Tightly spaced controls are louiselm-qbr.1.14.

title: Launcher receipt
description: A canonical machine-signed record of one privileged Session lifecycle outcome, linked by sequence and previous digest into that Sessions receipt chain.
design:
Established by the louiselm-ruxl grill-me and louiselm-ax-design-review, confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-09-03. Source Sessions: codex/01a067ef-6521-7ce2-8388-87f49972d615 and codex/01a0684c-d410-7292-97ff-4fdddeeff0e9.
Authority/startup refinement confirmed by the maintainer in louiselm-9onz on 2026-09-09; source Session codex/01a083f4-469e-7351-97fb-205f6aa39a6f.
notes:
Use Launcher receipt for launch, Park, resume, interrupt, Disposal, abnormal exit, and broker-loss freeze outcomes produced by the Launch supervisor. It binds the authorization or cause, action, resulting state, key ID, release ID, sequence, and previous digest. Distinguish it from broker authorization, operator audit, and capture-service projections. Its persistent root-only software key protects against unprivileged forgery or tampering, not root compromise.
Confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-09-04 in codex/01a068c6-2ca1-7be3-88ff-96c887e50df0: resulting_state names the state actually reached after that receipt action. Sequence 0 records Launch to Starting after preparation; only its durable ACK permits capability enablement and Agent start. Sequence 1 then records Start to Running and must be durably acknowledged before launch success. Running never means mere authorization-to-run.
Refined by louiselm-9onz (2026-09-09): after the exact sequence-0 durable ACK, restricted Agent initialization may run while brokered effects remain disabled. Actual Agent process identity and enforced tool isolation must both verify before capability enablement and the sequence-1 Start-to-Running receipt. Launch success still requires that exact sequence-1 durable ACK. Verification failure ends the launch; neither a first connector nor the reaper establishes Agent identity.
