title: Health check permanently reports codex as outdated even when versions match
description:
`:checkhealth louiselm` permanently reported `codex` as outdated even
immediately after upgrading it to the exact version npm reports as latest —
"— @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.0 (latest 1.6.0 available)" with both
numbers identical.

## Observed

Live user report after upgrading via `npm install -g
@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp@latest` and confirming `codex-acp --version`
prints `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.0`:

```
louiselm health: /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh — @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.0 (latest 1.6.0 available)
```

Reproduced directly against the real binaries with `Health.check`:

```
{ ..., latest_version = "1.6.0", outdated = false, version = "@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.0" }
```
(after the fix; before it, `outdated` was unconditionally `true`).

`claude` never showed this symptom — `claude-agent-acp --version` prints a
bare `0.70.0` with no name prefix, which happens to already match npm's bare
`0.70.0` output as a raw string.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua`, the `outdated` computation inside `M.check`'s
`finish()` (previously line ~205): `health_result.outdated =
health_result.version ~= latest_version` — direct string equality between
the installed-version banner and the latest-version check's output. These
are apples to oranges for `codex-acp`: its own `--version` banner is
`"@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.0"` while `npm view
@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp version` returns the bare `"1.6.0"`. Those
strings can never be equal, so `outdated` was unconditionally `true` for any
agent whose version banner carries a name prefix, regardless of actual
version — a permanent false positive, not something an upgrade could ever
clear.

## Why it was not caught

Every existing "matches" test used a *bare* installed-version string
(`"1.3.0"`) against a bare latest-version string (`"1.3.0"`) — never the
"banner has a name prefix, latest check does not" shape that `codex-acp`
actually exhibits. The only test with a prefixed installed version
(`"codex-agent-acp 1.3.0"`) paired it with a genuinely different latest
version (`"1.4.0"`), so raw inequality was still the correct answer there
and never exposed the false-positive/prefix issue.

## Fix

Added `extract_version(value)` (`lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua`): pulls the
trailing semver-looking token out of a version string via a Lua pattern
(`v?(%d[%d%.%-%+%w]*)%s*$`), falling back to the whole string when no such
token is found. `outdated` now compares `extract_version(health_result.version)
~= extract_version(latest_version)` instead of the raw strings. The
*displayed* message still shows the full raw banner — only the comparison is
normalized.

## Acceptance

- `tests/agent/health_spec.lua`: new case "reports outdated false when the
  installed banner carries a name prefix the latest check doesn't" — fails
  (`outdated=true`) before the fix, passes after.
- All prior latest-version tests unchanged and still passing (genuinely
  outdated and genuinely-bare-matching cases both still correct).
- Verified against the real binaries: `Health.check` with `codex-acp`'s real
  `--version` output and a live `npm view` result now returns
  `outdated = false`.
- Full suite 277/277 (was 276 before this new test), `stylua --check` and
  `lua-language-server --checklevel=Warning` clean.

## Not covered

`extract_version`'s pattern is a heuristic (last digit-leading token), not a
full semver parser — a version banner with no digits at all, or digits
embedded in unrelated trailing text, could still compare incorrectly. Not
observed in practice for any agent in this codebase's test fixtures or the
user's real config; not hardened further per the existing file's lightweight
string-matching style (see `first_line`).
close_reason: Fixed in lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua: added extract_version() to pull the trailing semver token out of a version banner before comparing, instead of raw string equality. Verified against the real codex-acp binary (1.6.0) and live npm registry query (1.6.0): outdated now correctly reports false. Test: tests/agent/health_spec.lua 'reports outdated false when the installed banner carries a name prefix the latest check doesn't'. Full suite 277/277, stylua/lua-language-server clean.

title: QA round: handoff takeover brief
description:
# Manual QA review — Handoff takeover brief (claude error-state source → deepseek target)

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `785cd53` (render_compact), `45bf34a` (takeover brief),
`4d74859` (typed resource transport). **Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: louiselm-93wl — a full-transcript Handoff looped the receiving deepseek
Session for 52 turns. The new payload is a mandatory operator-authored takeover
task plus a compacted transcript, sent as a typed resource block when the
target advertises embeddedContext. The live acceptance the test suite cannot
reach: a real claude→deepseek Handoff from `claude/70be7a6a` (currently in
error state in your other Neovim), and the receiver actually acting on the
brief.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Build under test is running | **passed** — `render_compact` is a `function` |
| 2 | Handoff buffer: three sections, compact context | **passed** — user confirmed the new brief rendered correctly; current receiver is itself a prior handoff |
| 3 | Submit refuses while takeover task is blank | **passed** — user confirmed cases 1–3 passed; no target prompt was observed |
| 4 | Filled task submits; focus lands on target | **passed** — user reported the handoff worked; target ACP session `01a04279…` received the prompt |
| 5 | Transport: text + resource blocks at the ACP boundary | **passed** — target log has exactly `text`, then `resource`; URI/mime and section boundaries correct |
| 6 | Receiver acts on the brief (no loop) | **passed** — target continued the grill through Questions 4–7 with normal completed turns; no replay loop |
| 7 | Source session retained after Handoff | **blocked** — source Neovim/session was closed before the switcher check |

## Setup

The running Neovim instances loaded the old code; lua changes need a restart.
The source claude session lives in your other instance — a fresh Neovim must
resume it before any Handoff can start.

1. Quit the other Neovim (the one holding the claude session) — or open a fresh
   instance next to it; only one instance may resume the session.
2. In the fresh instance: `:lua print(type(require('louiselm.session.transcript').render_compact))`
   → must print `function`. That is the build proof; anything else means the
   instance is running old code.
3. Resume the source: `:LouiselmResume` and pick `claude/70be7a6a-8674-45f2-ae6e-37ab67c8eac9`.
   **Prediction P1:** the claude adapter may refuse to resume an errored
   session, or sit waiting on it. If it refuses or hangs, report the exact
   message — that is a finding, not a pass.
4. Confirm the resumed session's status shows `error` in the header.
5. Target session permission mode: the deepseek receiver will run tools for the
   takeover task. Confirm its permission policy lets the needed commands run
   (a stuck permission prompt looks like a product bug but is a recipe issue).

Fresh session per case: the target is created per Handoff, so nothing to reset.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

(none yet — append as cases misfire)

## Cases

### 1. Build under test is running

Exercises: none — guards the whole round. Steps: Setup step 2.

Expect: the `:lua` prints `function`.

Failure signature: `nil` or a require error — the instance is on the old
code and every later case is void.

Evidence: the printed value. What it cannot prove: that the claude session was
resumed in that same instance; the buffer checks in case 2 cover that.

### 2. Handoff buffer: three sections, compact context

Exercises `45bf34a` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:open_handoff`.

Steps:

> `:LouiselmHandOff`

Pick `deepseek` in the agent picker.

Expect: a new review buffer opens, first line `## Handoff`, then:

- line 4: `- takeover task: <replace with the concrete action the target must take>`
- a `## Context` section containing the compacted transcript: user/assistant
  prose and `**title** — status` tool captions, with **no** `<details>`,
  **no** `## Reasoning`, and **no** skills-index/AGENTS resource text
- a `## Source` section naming claude and the ACP session id

Failure signature: first line is `# louiselm session transcript` (old build
still loaded), or the buffer contains raw tool payloads / reasoning blocks.

### 3. Submit refuses while takeover task is blank

Exercises `45bf34a` / `submit_handoff` task check.

Steps:

> `<C-s>` on the untouched buffer

Expect: an error notification `louiselm: handoff takeover task must be filled
in before submitting`, the review buffer stays open, and the target deepseek
session is never prompted.

Failure signature: the buffer closes, or the target session starts a turn —
the refusal is the entire point of the design.

### 4. Filled task submits; focus lands on target

Exercises `45bf34a` / `submit_handoff` send path.

Steps: replace the placeholder on the `takeover task:` line with exactly this
text (the source claude session was a grill on `qbr.3.2.6.5`; I pulled its
transcript and this is the concrete continuation):

```
Continue the qbr.3.2.6.5 grill from Q3. Locked decisions: Q1 no
interim-rejection, Q2 option C, Q3 pure observer (i). State the shared
plan for the C+(i) child, then route to beads: file the child task with
acceptance criteria and record A, B, and (ii) as rejected.
```

then:

> `<C-s>`

Expect: the review buffer closes and focus switches to the new deepseek
session, whose first turn is running the brief.

Failure signature: buffer stays open with no notification, or an error about
the prompt, or focus stays on the source session.

### 5. Transport: text + resource blocks at the ACP boundary

Exercises `4d74859` / `handoff_content`. **I pull this evidence; you just
report the deepseek session id you landed in** (or I take the newest session
dir).

Evidence check (I run):

```
ls -t ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/sessions | head -3
```

then inspect the first `session/prompt` frame of that session's `log.jsonl`:

- exactly two blocks: `text` then `resource`, in that order
- the text block holds `## Handoff` with your filled task line
- the resource block: `uri = "louiselm://handoff/claude/70be7a6a-8674-45f2-ae6e-37ab67c8eac9"`,
  `mimeType = "text/markdown"`, text contains `## Context` through `## Source`,
  **no** takeover-task line, **no** `<details>`

Pass = all of that. Failure signature: a single text block (transport not
engaged — target advertised embeddedContext=false or the split failed), or
the takeover task inside the resource block.

What this cannot prove: how the adapter flattened it for the model — that is
covered by case 6, via the receiver's `history.jsonl` first message showing
`[resource] <louiselm://handoff/...>` framing.

### 6. Receiver acts on the brief (no loop)

Exercises the whole chain, against the real peer.

Steps: watch the deepseek session run its first turn to completion.

Expect: it takes the takeover task as its instruction and works toward it; the
turn ends with a concrete result.

Failure signature: the original incident — repeated state re-verification
(`git status`/`br sync` cycles) with no action, or the turn dies immediately
having done nothing.

Evidence: I read the session's `log.jsonl` — tool calls and their order, and
the final assistant text. The loop signature is the same command replayed
many times with no effect.

### 7. Source session retained after Handoff

Exercises the Handoff vocabulary (louiselm-7rjr) through the UI.

Steps:

> `:LouiselmSwitchSession`

Expect: the claude source session is still listed and switchable, still in
error state.

Failure signature: the source session is gone from the switcher, or was
mutated out of error state by the Handoff.

## Evidence check

See case 5/6 — the verdict artifacts are the target session's ACP
`log.jsonl` (`session/prompt` frame block shapes) and `history.jsonl` (the
flattened first message). Pinned by session id, never by "most recent file"
alone — I confirm the id with you before reading.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- The deepseek target session: leave or close, your call — it was created for
  this round.
- The resumed claude source session: stays in its own instance; nothing to
  revert.
- `QA_REVIEW.md`: becomes the round bead's description, then deleted (never
  committed).

## Reporting back

Send me: which case, what you saw, the deepseek session id (header or
`:LouiselmSessionId`), and what you put on the takeover-task line. I pull the
evidence myself.

## Findings this round

(none. Case 7 remains unverified because the source session was closed before
the required UI check; no product failure was observed.)

handoff: `codex/01a0427e-4d12-7962-869f-9767d4c61069`). Its first handoff

`mimeType=text/markdown`, `## Context` through `## Source`, no takeover-task
line, and no `<details>`. The receiver then produced ordinary grill turns
through Question 7 rather than repeating state checks.

title: Copilot reports outdated at matching version
description:
Copilot can be reported as outdated even when its installed and upstream versions are both 1.0.80. This produces a misleading warning whenever the CLI's version banner ends in punctuation.

## Observed

2026-08-22 in `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`.

```console
$ copilot --version
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.80.
```

The observed louiselm notification was:

```text
louiselm: copilot is outdated (GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.80. installed, 1.0.80 upstream)
```

## Symptoms

- Users see an "outdated" warning for an already-current Copilot CLI.
- The warning asks users to update despite identical installed and upstream semantic versions.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:23` uses `value:match("v?(%d[%d%.%-%+%w]*)%s*$")`. The character class admits `.`, so `GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.80.` extracts as `1.0.80.`, while an upstream bare `1.0.80` extracts as `1.0.80`. `lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:215` compares those unequal values and marks the agent outdated. The notification is emitted by `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:173-180`.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/agent/health_spec.lua` covers name-prefixed and exactly matching banners, but no installed banner ending in punctuation.

## Fix direction

Tighten version extraction at `lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:23` so terminal punctuation outside a semantic-version token is excluded. Do not weaken the staleness check or normalize the displayed version strings.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix for `GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.80.` versus upstream `1.0.80`, then passes after it.
- That pair produces `outdated = false` and no `louiselm: copilot is outdated` warning.

## Not covered

The configured command that returned upstream `1.0.80` was not inspected; the user-supplied warning establishes its value. Other vendor-specific non-semver banners are unverified.
close_reason: Implemented in current commit: terminal banner punctuation is excluded before comparing semantic versions. Regression: tests/agent/health_spec.lua: ignores terminal punctuation after an installed version. Gates: focused agent health test, full mini.test (323 cases), stylua --check ., and lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning passed.

title: Usage-line spacing: accumulated blank lines pile up during resumed multi-turn replay
description:
## Symptom

After resuming a session with 2+ replayed turns, blank lines accumulate before
the live `> ` prompt instead of staying at a single blank. Live single-turn
sessions are unaffected (exactly 1 blank after `[usage] ...`); each additional
replayed turn adds one more orphaned blank line to the pile.

## Evidence (real session, not synthetic)

deepseek/session-f7dbeaea-b8d8-469a-8332-0bedf50ea18d, dumped via
`nvim_buf_get_lines` after resuming a 2-turn session:

```
  10: "[usage] total_tokens=993 · ..."
  11: "> hi again"
  17: "[usage] total_tokens=1028 · ..."
  18: ""
  19: ""
  20: "> "
```

Two blank lines (18, 19) between the final `[usage]` line and the live prompt,
vs. zero blank lines between the first `[usage]` line (10) and the next
replayed prompt (11) — spacing is not just excessive, it's inconsistent.

Reproduced deterministically headless via `tests/minimal_init.lua` +
`MiniTest`-style fixtures (fake_session/fake_api matching
`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`), replaying 2 turns with usage recorded only for
turn 2 — exact repro script available on request, or re-derive from
`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:2344` ("restores client-owned usage beside its
replayed Session turn"), which currently *asserts* the buggy double-blank
output as expected (lines ~2406-2409):

```lua
"second answer",
"",
"[usage] total_tokens=30 · input_tokens=20 · cached_read_tokens=7",
"",
"",
"> ",
```

That double-blank was already present before this QA round (introduced in
commit `ee9e541` "fix(usage): restore resumed turn telemetry", well before
`acb65c7`). `f75e2a6` "fix(ui): space usage transcript lines" (this round)
only added the missing blank *before* the usage line and left the
already-broken *after* spacing untouched — not a regression from this round,
but directly in the area this round's commit touched, and surfaced during its
QA pass (louiselm-7rup-successor round).

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`, `chunk` event handler, first-response-chunk
branch (~line 2195-2219 as of `c56805f`): when a response block ends in prose,
it writes its own trailing blank line directly into the buffer:

```lua
local response_line_count = #lines
if view.last_block_kind ~= "tool" then
  lines[#lines + 1] = ""
end
nvim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(view.buffer, insertion_line, insertion_line, false, lines)
view.response_line = insertion_line
view.response_tail = insertion_line + response_line_count - 1
view.transcript_tail = view.response_tail        -- excludes the blank just written
```

`response_tail`/`transcript_tail` are set using `response_line_count`, which is
captured *before* the trailing `""` is appended — so the trailing blank is
physically in the buffer but invisible to the tracked "last written line"
bookkeeping. This is not accidental: `tool_call_started`/`tool_call_finished`
and the reasoning-block-start handler each check
`if view.last_block_kind == "prose" then table.insert(lines, 1, "")` and rely
on the untracked blank being reusable as their own leading separator (lines
~2299-2301, ~2329-2331, ~2250-2252). Every future insertion computed from
`transcript_tail + 1` lands exactly on that untracked blank and pushes it
further down without ever consuming it. During a single live turn there's
exactly one such orphan (which happens to look correct: 1 blank after
`[usage]`). During N-turn replay, N orphans pile up with nothing to consume
them, landing all together wherever the next content — here,
`restore_turn_usage` → `insert_usage`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1994` /
`1974` — gets inserted.

## Why this is not a quick patch

Tried two fixes, both regressed something else:

1. **Make `transcript_tail` include the trailing blank** (fix the accounting
   at the source). This correctly fixed the resume-usage spacing, but broke
   tool-call spacing: `tool_call_started`'s `last_block_kind == "prose"`
   separator-insert became redundant and needs to be conditioned on whether
   a trailing blank was already tracked. Doing that for all 3 sites
   (`~2250`, `~2299`, `~2329`) fixed tool spacing too, and the full
   `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` suite (123 cases) passed after adjusting the one
   test that had asserted the old buggy output. This is the architecturally
   correct fix, but touches shared bookkeeping (`response_tail`,
   `transcript_tail`, a new `response_trailer` field) used by prose, tool,
   and reasoning rendering — needs careful full-suite verification, not a
   30-second patch.
2. **Leave the untracked-blank mechanism alone; collapse any run of blank
   lines immediately at the `insert_usage` insertion point via direct
   deletion.** This crashed: `view.prompt_line` is a plain cached integer
   (not re-read from its extmark on demand), and deleting buffer lines
   without going through `mark_prompt` desyncs it — the next
   `insert_transcript` call's `mark_prompt` then tries to place an extmark
   past the (now-shorter) buffer end (`E5113: Invalid 'line': out of range`
   at `init.lua:1249`).

## Recommended direction

Approach 1 (fix the accounting at the source, propagate to all 3
`last_block_kind == "prose"` separator sites) is the right shape — it was
working before revert, full suite green. Whoever picks this up should:
redo that change, update
`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:2344` ("restores client-owned usage beside its
replayed Session turn") to expect single blanks throughout, run the full
suite, and specifically eyeball the two tool-spacing tests
("renders session events and forwards slash prompts",
"keeps interleaved response and tool events chronological") since those are
what the accounting fix affects.

Filed during manual QA round (session ids: deepseek/session-25703dab...
unrelated case 3, evidence session here is
deepseek/session-f7dbeaea-b8d8-469a-8332-0bedf50ea18d). Working tree was left
clean — both attempted fixes were reverted.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree. Root cause was exactly as diagnosed: transcript_tail undercounted the trailing blank a completed prose block writes, so every downstream insertion (insert_usage, tool/reasoning separators, user_chunk's quoted prompt) computed transcript_tail+1 one line short and either duplicated or orphaned a blank. Fix: prose blocks now always write AND count their trailing blank (removed the old 'skip when preceded by tool' asymmetry, which only worked by accident via the orphan); the three last_block_kind==prose leading-separator sites (thought_chunk, tool_call_started, tool_call_finished) now skip their own blank when trailing_blank is already true instead of duplicating it. Spacing is now uniformly single-blank everywhere it was previously 0-or-2. tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:2344 updated to the corrected single-blank expectation; two other tests eyeballed as recommended needed no change (one lost its coincidental blank in a mid-turn, pre-turn_done snapshot -- see louiselm-o9uf comment for why that's correct, not a regression). Full suite 544/544, stylua and lua-language-server clean.

title: Grill-me needed: how should the retrospective mechanism fit into the current workflow so it doesn't require re-explaining each time?
description:
Do not resolve this design question in passing. Facilitate a dedicated decision about the retrospective step of docs/example-workflow.md's loop.

Question:
How should the retrospective mechanism (issue-comment / AGENTS.md / needs-design routing described in docs/example-workflow.md §5 and "Process findings") fit into the day-to-day loop so the maintainer stops having to explain or invoke it by hand each session?

Context/evidence:
- On louiselm-w726 (this session, 2026-08-24), the agent closed a documentation-only bug fix without spontaneously routing a retrospective note anywhere. The maintainer had to ask "surely one friction i feel like i have to explain every retrospect workflow" before the agent filed the comment on the issue.
- docs/example-workflow.md already describes the three-way routing (issue comment / AGENTS.md / needs-design question) and states the loop "holds together because each stage is designed to trigger the next rather than merely precede it" -- but the retrospect stage did not trigger on its own here; it needed an explicit maintainer prompt.
- AGENTS.md section 2 already has "Emit, don't narrate" and other Work Tracking bullets, but nothing that says a retrospective handoff is a mandatory last step of closing an issue, the way "run br sync --flush-only before committing" is mandatory.

Threads worth pulling:
- Is this a missing AGENTS.md rule (a "close an issue only after considering handoff to comment/AGENTS.md/question" bullet), or a missing tooling nudge (e.g. br close reminding/prompting for it), or is the friction acceptable because retrospection should stay a deliberate, not automatic, act?
- Should the trigger be scoped to certain issue types (bug/task) versus all closes, given trivial closes (typos, pure chores) don't need a retrospective?
- Is "the agent forgot" a one-off, or does it recur across sessions/adapters (deepseek, codex) -- is there evidence already in beads history worth checking before deciding this is systemic?
close_reason: Design settled with the maintainer and promoted to AGENTS.md section 2: close-time retrospective routing for bug/task/feature, plus the br search -a retrieval convention. Retrieval deliberately scoped to a standing convention rather than a mandatory pre-close search step.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Retrieval-side constraint discovered while scoping this question (filed as louiselm-o2jh). Retrospectives routed into issue comments live on CLOSED issues almost by definition, since they are written at close time -- and 'br search' excludes closed by default, hiding 222 of this backlog's 249 issues. Within minutes of choosing 'issue comment' as the destination, this agent fell into exactly that hole: searched for prior occurrences without -a, got nothing, and reported the absence as evidence of a first occurrence. A second error compounded it -- 'br list --json' carries no comments field, so a scripted comment scan over it returns 0 by construction rather than by evidence.

Implication for this grill: any rule adopted here must specify the RETRIEVAL side, not just the routing side. A handoff that cannot be found later is equivalent to no handoff, which is the exact failure this question exists to fix. Concretely, a rule that says 'route the lesson to a comment' is insufficient; it needs to also say how a future agent is expected to find it (e.g. 'search comments with br search -a', or route to a durable searchable surface instead).

Also worth weighing: beads_rust#416 ('br search does not search comment bodies', closed 2026-08-17) means comment search only became reliable very recently. Any prior-art check for 'has this lesson already been recorded' run before that fix would have returned false negatives, so absence of retrospective comments in older closed issues is weak evidence about past practice.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Resolved with the maintainer, 2026-08-24.

Decision 1 -- mechanism: an AGENTS.md rule, not a br close tooling gate and not the status quo of case-by-case deliberateness. A tooling gate is the strongest guarantee but costs an out-of-repo beads_rust change and taxes every close including trivial ones; status quo is what failed on louiselm-w726, where the maintainer had to prompt for the retrospective.

Decision 2 -- scope: bug/task/feature closes only. Chores and mechanical closes are exempt.

Decision 3 -- retrieval: name the retrieval path as a standing one-line search convention ('always pass -a'), NOT as a mandatory pre-close prior-art search step. The maintainer explicitly rejected taxing every close task. Accepted tradeoff: the convention is inert if nobody searches, and in that case only the upstream fix in louiselm-o2jh actually helps. Chosen anyway because it costs one line, cannot be got wrong once written, and the write-side rule without a read-side path optimises for writing lessons nobody can find.

Promoted to AGENTS.md section 2 (Work Tracking) as two bullets: the close-time routing rule, and the br search -a convention with the br list --json no-comments-field caveat.

title: Grill-me needed: should agent-authored beads handoffs (close reasons, comments) be trusted as durable context, or does self-summarization reintroduce the poisoning failure mode they're meant to prevent?
description:
Do not resolve this in passing — it needs a full grill-me session, not a quick take folded into other work.

## The question

AGENTS.md requires agents to write their own beads close reasons and comments
("emit don't narrate," "route what the work taught... to a `br comment`").
That's the mechanism louiselm relies on to make context durable across
sessions and adapters. But an agent summarizing its own work is exactly the
failure mode described as "poisoning" in context-rot literature: a stale or
subtly wrong note that outlives the correction that would have invalidated
it, except here the agent that might be wrong is also the one writing the
record everyone else will trust.

Is agent-authored beads content (close reasons, comments, handoff notes)
structurally different enough from agent-authored session-scratch context
that it doesn't carry the same risk — or does louiselm need a check on it
before it's trusted as canonical?

## Context / evidence that raised this

From a conversation analyzing
https://towardsdatascience.com/governed-context-managing-context-rot-in-claude-code/
against louiselm's design (2026-09-01, session claude/52ec46c6-b444-4920-a853-e1a6c154c1c0).

The article's own prescription is that handoff briefs should be
*human*-extracted, not model-generated, specifically because a model
summarizing its own state can't reliably tell whether that state is correct.
Louiselm's AGENTS.md currently goes the other way on purpose: durable context
must live in the repo (beads), not in private agent memory, and it's the
agent's job to write it at close time ("silence is the failure mode").

Both rules are independently well-motivated:
- AGENTS.md's rule prevents cross-adapter memory fragmentation (a Codex
  session's private notes are invisible to a DeepSeek session).
- The article's rule prevents a wrong agent from writing the record that
  future agents (and the article would say: future *selves*) treat as ground
  truth.

They haven't actually been tested against each other. Louiselm has never had
an incident traced to a bad agent-authored close reason propagating forward
(or if it has, it wasn't captured as evidence here — worth checking `br
search -a` for prior art before the grill session).

## Threads worth pulling

- Does the *type* of record matter? A close reason citing `file:line` and a
  decision (already the house style — "state the outcome," not prose) is a
  narrower, more falsifiable claim than a free-form handoff summary. Does
  format constrain the poisoning risk enough on its own?
- Is there a cheap verification point already in the workflow that could
  catch this — e.g. does anything re-read a close reason against the diff it
  describes, the way code review re-reads a diff against a claim?
- Would a "two corrections on the same issue" signal (the article's proposed
  reset trigger) be detectable from beads history — repeated reopens of the
  same issue, or repeated comments walking back a prior comment — and if so,
  is that a job for `bvr`/`br coordination status` rather than a new
  mechanism?
- Does this differ by issue type or closer? A `bug` closed by the agent that
  introduced the fix is a different trust situation than a `chore` closed by
  a different agent than the one who did the work.
- Is the real fix upstream of beads entirely — i.e. is this actually about
  whether *any* single agent's self-report should be trusted uncorroborated,
  which would point at review/verification practice rather than at the
  beads-comment convention specifically.
close_reason: Resolved by grill-me 2026-09-01: close-reason poisoning is a referent failure (agents report the act, not the effect), not a truthfulness failure, so the fix constrains what a reason is about rather than adding a checker. Adopted the Close verdict partition (consumer:/gate:/live:/inert:/none:) over br's native close policy; rejected a repo-side JSONL script (AGENTS.md:70) and self-close prohibition (louiselm-psz9 was live-confirmed and still wrong). Vocabulary louiselm-yx1g promoted to reference. Work filed: louiselm-beads-export-bypass-audit-da3h, louiselm-adopt-close-verdict-gate-xfoj (blocked by it), louiselm-park-observer-inert-puha (P1 bug found by the measurement), louiselm-agents-md-vimdoc-gate-qosg, louiselm-close-verdict-scope-width-x456 (unsolved scope-width class). title: Privileged supervisor CI acceptance deadlocks on terminal receipt
description:

title: Cold-Park startup failure completes resume twice
description:
A synchronous ACP startup failure can invoke the cold-Park load completion twice, causing duplicate Run finalization/error handling.

## Observed

Code inspection on 2026-09-03. `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:227-232` invokes the ready callback when `Session:start()` fails. `lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua:428-432` then returns nil to its caller. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4338-4344` forwards the callback error once, and `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4371-4373` forwards the returned startup error again.

## Symptoms

- One cold-resume attempt can run its completion/finalization path twice.
- Duplicate user notifications or conflicting Run finalization requests are possible on immediate Agent startup failure.

## Root cause

`load_cold_run` treats the ready callback and the synchronous `load_session` return as independent terminal paths without an exactly-once settlement guard.

## Why it was not caught

Cold-resume UI tests model successful loading; failure tests live at the Session and ResumeController boundaries separately and do not compose an immediate Session startup failure through Chat.

## Fix direction

Give one cold-load attempt an exactly-once completion function shared by the ready callback and immediate return path.

## Acceptance

- A regression makes `load_session` invoke its callback with an error and return nil.
- The Run finalization/error path is observed exactly once.

## Not covered

Deferred while louiselm-waa0 fixes successful replay delivery; no behavior change is included in that fix.
close_reason: Existing recovery owner settles startup failure once; characterization and lesson recorded. gate:tests/workflow/recovery_spec.lua

Full 1044 Lua tests and required Lua gates pass. Lesson: inspect current shared owner after extraction before reimplementing an old UI defect.

title: Installed broker Attention CI hits 120s timeout
description:
The installed broker Attention gate intermittently exceeds its outer 120-second CI deadline, preventing complete CI acceptance despite unchanged capture-service/fixture code and passing neighboring runs.

## Observed

15:03:30.1171509Z Finished dev build in 6.52s; 15:05:30.7239432Z Process completed with exit code 124.
Command from capture-service:
sudo env LOUISELM_REQUIRE_BROKER_ATTENTION=1 LOUISELM_TEST_CAPTURE=$PWD/target/debug/louiselm-capture timeout 120 unshare --mount --propagation private -- python3 ../scripts/test-broker-attention.py
Run only inside a disposable VM, never on the maintainer desktop.

## Symptoms
No fixture progress or traceback between successful build and the outer timeout. Cargo tests and cross-service durable requests pass first. Other candidate runs passed capture-service, as did all three exact9b29492 baseline workflows (35356424348/35356424263/35356424098).

## Root cause
Unknown. git diff 9b29492 eacdcc8 -- capture-service scripts/test-broker-attention.py scripts/install-broker-attention.py is empty, and the capture-service workflow job is unchanged.
scripts/test-broker-attention.py:91 copies /etc before the fixture try/finally; setup, service lifecycle, clients and cleanup lack phase markers. .github/workflows/ci.yml:377 supplies the unchanged timeout120. Existing per-command/readiness timeouts do not identify the phase when the outer watchdog kills the fixture. Capture bounded phase/stack diagnostics in an isolated reproduction to distinguish setup, subprocess, receiver/client or cleanup hangs. Do not infer the cause or extend deadlines from this log alone.

## Why it was not caught
The privileged gate catches the timeout but emits no progress identifying the slow or blocked phase. Ordinary tests do not exercise this installed cross-UID workload. Three green baseline executions do not exclude intermittent failure.
Distinct from closed louiselm-0txse (missing explicit Attention opt-in and startup exit) and open louiselm-y2j3o (hardened user-service identity mapping).

## Fix direction
Diagnose the exact stalled boundary with bounded, sanitized phase/timeout evidence, then fix its synchronization or resource lifecycle at the narrowest boundary. Preserve real CLI/provisioning, cross-UID/capability refusals, restart/replay, unset case, permission-drift assertions and current deadline. Do not rerun until green or relax security.

## Acceptance
- Capture the timeout phase and encode a failing regression before implementation.
- Full installed Attention gate and complete capture-service gates pass on the repaired exact revision.
- Complete hosted CI passes; preserve all original refusal and cleanup checks.

## Not covered
No production capture failure or root cause is proven. No fix attempted: outside the bounded skills CI split, which is withdrawn under the stop rule (campaign3/3). No maintainer desktop privileged tests.

title: Thread agent Definition.options._meta into session/new and session/load params
description:
## Goal

Let a per-agent `options._meta` config value (already validated and stored by
`lua/louiselm/agent/config.lua`'s `copy_options`, but never read anywhere else)
flow into the ACP `session/new` / `session/load` request params, so a user can
set e.g. `_meta = { claudeCode = { options = { thinking = { type = "adaptive" } } } }`
per agent.

## Why

`claude-agent-acp` reads `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` from its process environment to
set `thinking: { type: "enabled", budgetTokens: N }` (fixed-budget mode), which
louiselm.nvim's README now documents as the way to get `agent_thought_chunk`
reasoning to show up in chat (see louiselm-exw0). That `budget_tokens` config
is deprecated and rejected with a 400 on the current Anthropic model family
(Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 / Fable 5) - only Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 still accept it as a
transitional escape hatch. `claude-agent-acp`'s own test suite
(`src/tests/create-session-options.test.ts` ~L559-573) shows a session-level
`_meta.claudeCode.options.thinking` override (e.g. `{ type: "adaptive" }`)
takes precedence over the env-var default and works regardless of model tier.

Today louiselm has no passthrough for this: `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua`
builds the `session/new`/`session/load` params (~L522, ~L526) with only
`cwd`/`mcpServers`/`sessionId` - no `_meta` field is ever constructed, and
`agent.Definition.options` (config.lua:426) is validated/stored but never read
by `lifecycle.lua`, `acp/init.lua`, or anywhere else.

Not urgent today: the env-var fix works fine as long as `claude-agent-acp`'s
underlying model still accepts `budget_tokens`. This becomes load-bearing only
once the adapter defaults to (or the user configures) a 5-series/4.7+ model,
at which point `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` stops no-oping and starts erroring.

## Scope

- Thread `agent_definition.options._meta` (when non-nil) into the params
  tables built in `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua` around the `new_session`
  and `load_session` call sites.
- Confirm the resolved `agent.Definition` (with `.options`) is actually
  reachable from `Session` at that point; if not, that's part of the change.
- No new config-schema validation needed - `copy_options` already accepts
  arbitrary tables, so `options = { _meta = {...} }` already passes
  normalization today.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An agent definition with `options = { _meta = { claudeCode = { options = {
   thinking = { type = "adaptive" } } } } }` results in that `_meta` table
   appearing verbatim in the `session/new` (and `session/load`) request params
   sent over ACP.
2. Agents/tests without `options._meta` behave exactly as today (no `_meta`
   key sent).
3. Regression test asserts the request-building call sites forward `_meta`
   from the agent definition.

## Notes

Estimated small: 1-2 functions, few lines, threading an already-stored field
into two existing request-building call sites.
close_reason: All 3 acceptance criteria met: _meta threaded verbatim into session/new and session/load params, absent-case unchanged, regression tests added. All quality gates pass.

comments.author: claude/35e4614f-fbee-450f-887c-39360cfdae52
comments.text: Implemented: lifecycle.lua's handle_initialized now reads self.definition.options._meta (when present, and only when it's a table) and threads it verbatim into both the session/new and session/load params as _meta, alongside the existing cwd/mcpServers/sessionId fields. Absent options._meta, no _meta key is sent (unchanged behavior). Also documented the contract on louiselm.agent.Definition.options in agent/config.lua and regenerated doc/api.md. Regression tests added to tests/session/api_spec.lua: _meta threaded into session/new params, into session/load params, and omitted when absent. Surfaced while implementing louiselm-5tuq (Claude sessions show no [thinking] blocks), which needs exactly this plumbing to set thinking.display; this issue is the generic mechanism, 5tuq is its first real consumer.

title: health.check --version drops normalized.args, breaking wrapper-script agents
description:
In lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua, M.check's primary --version check builds
its command as:

    local command = { normalized.command, "--version" }

This drops normalized.args entirely. For any agent definition where
`command` is a wrapper script that expects an argument selecting the real
binary (e.g. real-world usage: command = "acp-debug.sh", args =
{"codex-acp"}), the check actually runs `acp-debug.sh --version` instead of
`acp-debug.sh codex-acp --version`.

Confirmed by hand: acp-debug.sh --version makes the wrapper's own
`basename "$1"` call receive the literal string "--version", which GNU
basename interprets as its own --version flag, so the wrapper prints
"basename (GNU coreutils) 9.7" (and license text) to stdout instead of
running the wrapped binary at all. The health check then reports that
garbage as the "installed version" -- both in :checkhealth louiselm and in
the outdated-version warning added in commit ee59c4b, which depends on this
same version string.

Confirmed via `git show fde8c6a:lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua` that this bug
predates ee59c4b -- it is not a regression from today's work, just newly
visible because of it.

Fix: build the command as normalized.command followed by all of
normalized.args, then "--version", matching how start_latest_check in the
same file already does it correctly.
close_reason: Fixed: M.check now builds the --version command as normalized.command + normalized.args + '--version', matching start_latest_check. Verified by hand against the real acp-debug.sh wrapper (reports @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.1.14 instead of basename's own version string) and added tests/agent/health_spec.lua case 'includes wrapper args before --version' using the deferred async vim.system stub. Full mini.test suite green (266 cases), stylua/lua-language-server clean on touched files.

title: Warn when configured agents are outdated (checkhealth + chat open)
description:
Agents (codex-acp, claude-agent-acp, etc.) are npm-installed binaries with no
auto-update mechanism. louiselm already checks each agent's own --version
(lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua, lua/louiselm/health/init.lua). Add an optional
"latest available version" check per agent, and a warning when the installed
version doesn't match, surfaced both in :checkhealth and when a chat session
opens (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua ensure_chat()).

Design:
1. lua/louiselm/agent/config.lua: optional `latest` key on an agent
   definition, structurally identical to command/args/env (reuse
   copy_args/copy_env). Add `louiselm.agent.LatestCheck` LuaCATS type.
   Vendor-agnostic: "how to find latest version" is just another arbitrary
   command (e.g. `npm view <pkg> version`), same pattern as the existing
   --version check. No npm-specific code in louiselm.nvim.
2. lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua: when definition.latest is present,
   M.check also spawns that command via vim.system and compares its
   output (first line, trimmed) against --version. Extend HealthResult
   with latest_version?/outdated?. Two independent async vim.system
   calls must coordinate so on_result fires exactly once (AGENTS.md
   section 10).
3. lua/louiselm/health/init.lua: report_agent_result/_safely mention the
   latest version; use health.warn for "ok but outdated" (not
   health.error).
4. lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua: ensure_chat() fires Agent.check per
   configured agent (non-blocking) and vim.notify(...) a WARN when
   outdated, mirroring the existing skills-error notify calls in that
   function. Must not block/delay chat/session creation.

Only codex/claude will set `latest` in the maintainer's dotfiles config
(npm view); deepseek/glm run a local Rust binary with no upstream, so
`latest` must stay fully optional with zero behavior change when omitted.
close_reason:
Implemented optional per-agent `latest` version check + staleness warning.

Files changed:
- lua/louiselm/agent/config.lua: optional `latest` key (command/args/env,
  reuses copy_args/copy_env), new louiselm.agent.LatestCheck LuaCATS type.
- lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua: M.check spawns the configured `latest`
  command alongside --version when present; combines two independent
  vim.system() completions into one HealthResult (latest_version/
  latest_error/outdated), firing on_result exactly once regardless of
  completion order (AGENTS.md section 10).
- lua/louiselm/config.lua: mirrored `latest` in the top-level setup()
  schema (agents.*.latest), since Louiselm.setup() validates against this
  schema before agent/config.lua ever normalizes anything.
- lua/louiselm/health/init.lua: report_agent_result/_safely now mention
  the latest version and use health.warn (not health.error) for "ok but
  outdated".
- lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua: ensure_chat() fires Agent.check per
  configured agent right after agents resolve; notifies
  "louiselm: <name> is outdated (<installed> installed, <latest> upstream)"
  at WARN when outdated, scheduled off the fast event when needed. Fully
  async, never blocks chat/session creation.

Tests added: tests/agent/config_spec.lua (schema-level latest
accept/reject), tests/agent/health_spec.lua (async coordination: both
orders of completion, exactly-once firing, outdated true/false, missing
latest executable, no latest configured = no extra process), tests/
health_spec.lua (checkhealth warns not errors), tests/schema/setup_spec.lua
(Louiselm.setup() accepts/rejects latest), tests/ui/command_spec.lua
(end-to-end: chat opens before the async checks resolve; warning fires
once both resolve).

Gates: stylua --check . clean (only pre-existing unrelated diff in
blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua, same as main). Full mini.test suite: 265
cases, 0 fails. lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning: 9
problems, identical to a clean main checkout, all in
blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua (unrelated, pre-existing).

Discovered and fixed en route (louiselm-tpw, closed): return-type-mismatch
(userdata? vs real table) and duplicate-set-field lua-language-server
warnings that were pre-existing but latent, surfaced once this feature's
code was added to the workspace.

title: Handoff recommendation offers the current Codex Agent as target
description:
A Handoff recommendation made while the current Session is the configured Codex Agent proposes Codex as the target instead of offering a different configured Agent. This makes the proposed Handoff semantically invalid because a Handoff must create a Session with another Agent; the source Session remains bound to its current Agent.

## Observed

Reproduced/reported in LouiseLM Session codex/01a04b99-4100-74e3-aa2a-3a49e92e2352 on 2026-08-29 (Neovim plugin).

User report: "while in codex/01a04b99-4100-74e3-aa2a-3a49e92e2352 that if I do a :Louiselmhandoff from there then as it's a codex session im not proposed to hand it off to anything but codex, but that should be possible"

Relevant implementation evidence:
- lua/louiselm/routing/routing.lua:229-249 enumerates the current Agent as continue/model and other Agents as handoff candidates.
- lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3917-3921 explicitly excludes the source Agent from the manual Handoff picker, showing that same-Agent Handoff is not a valid target at that boundary.
- Existing routing tests at tests/routing/routing_spec.lua:141-148 assert handoff candidates for beta/gamma but do not assert that the current Agent can never appear as a handoff recommendation.

## Symptoms

- The operator is offered Codex as a Handoff target while already in a Codex Session.
- The proposed target does not satisfy the Handoff contract requiring another Agent.
- A manual Handoff should be able to target another configured Agent, but the recommendation does not surface that valid choice in this case.

## Root cause

The exact runtime cause of the Codex-only proposal is not yet confirmed. The candidate enumeration at lua/louiselm/routing/routing.lua:231-249 appears structurally correct, so the remaining hypotheses are the routing input inventory/current-agent identity or a later recommendation/presentation filter that mislabels the current Agent as a Handoff. Discriminate by capturing the RoutingRequest and ranked candidates at the failing Session, then tracing the recommendation label to the picker.

## Why it was not caught

Routing tests cover that non-current Agents are emitted as Handoff candidates, but do not assert the inverse invariant: no candidate with agent equal to request.current.agent may have action handoff. UI Handoff tests cover a Claude-to-Codex target and the manual picker exclusion, not a Codex-source recommendation.

## Fix direction

Preserve the invariant at the narrowest shared routing/presentation boundary: a Handoff candidate must have an Agent different from request.current.agent. Trace and correct the Codex recommendation input or classification rather than adding a UI-only alias or allowing same-Agent Handoffs.

## Acceptance

- Add a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after, using a current Codex Agent and at least one other configured Agent.
- No ranked/recommended Handoff candidate has agent equal to the current Session's Agent.
- From a Codex Session, the Handoff affordance proposes another configured Agent when one is available.

## Not covered

The report does not establish whether the issue occurs in the routing recommendation, the command's target picker, or both; the source code indicates the command picker already excludes the current Agent. No live routing payload or screenshot was available beyond the Session identifier and user report.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree: :LouiselmHandOff now includes the current Agent as a target while still creating a distinct target Session. Added same-Agent regression coverage and regenerated vimdoc. Tests: full MiniTest 728/728, focused chat 140/140, routing 33/33. Gates: stylua --check ., lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning, and generate-api-appendix --check passed.

title: skills-core group-death tests fail under ACP sessions: acp-proxy never reaps adopted orphans
description:
Full skills-core suite runs inside a LouiseLM ACP session fail three
bounded-system-runner tests deterministically: acp-proxy is a child subreaper
that never reaps adopted orphans, so killed descendants linger as zombies in
their process group and the group-death probes time out. Unrelated to any
source change; clean HEAD reproduces.

## Observed

2026-09-07, this machine, inside opencode Session
`opencode/ses_f841b1a05ffeaLc8MroaF2snhv` under acp-proxy PID 396272
(`acp-proxy -- opencode acp`).

`./scripts/test-skills-core` fails, 82 passed / 3 failed, deterministically
(two runs, plus one run at clean HEAD in a fresh detached worktree — no
source changes involved):

- `launcher_install::tests::bounded_system_runner_bounds_pipes_held_after_the_command_exits`
- `launcher_install::tests::bounded_system_runner_kills_a_timed_out_command_and_its_descendant`
  (both panic at `src/launcher_install.rs:3319`)
- `launcher_install::tests::bounded_system_runner_kills_a_daemonized_descendant_after_success`
  (panics at `src/launcher_install.rs:3222`:
  `the direct helper succeeds: Custom { kind: TimedOut, error: "command
  process group did not terminate" }`)

The same tests pass in GitHub Actions (run 34104827578 cargo job: 82 passed,
only the two identity deadline tests failed there, see louiselm-mbpc).

## Root cause

The tests SIGKILL a command's process group, then probe
`kill(-pgid, 0)` until it returns ESRCH (`wait_for_process_group_exit`,
`src/launcher_install.rs:726`). A zombie counts as an existing process, so
the group stays probeable until the zombie is reaped.

Observed directly: after one failing run, a `[tail] <defunct>` zombie (the
fixture's daemonized descendant) sits with PPID 396272 — the session's
acp-proxy. `sh` (the zombie's parent) died first, so the orphan reparented
to the nearest subreaper, acp-proxy, which never reaps adopted children.
A second acp-proxy instance (PID 387276, `claude-agent-acp`) shows the same
pattern with its own accumulated zombies (`nvim`, `git`, `find`, `sqlite3`),
so this is generic to acp-proxy, not one adapter.

On GitHub the nearest reaping ancestor is the runner's init; on a normal
local shell it is PID 1 / the user systemd; both reap, so CI and ordinary
local runs pass. Inside an ACP session the subreaper intercepts the orphans
and holds them as zombies indefinitely, so every group-death assertion that
relies on descendants being reaped by someone else fails after the 1-2s
cleanup deadline.

## Verification of the mechanism

- `systemd-run --user --scope` still fails: `--scope` keeps the process in
  its existing parent chain, still under acp-proxy's subreaper reach.
- `systemd-run --user --pipe --wait --collect` (transient service,
  double-forks under the user manager, outside the acp-proxy tree): the
  full suite passes, 85 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored.

## Impact

Any agent running the full skills-core gates inside a live LouiseLM ACP
session sees three phantom failures and may misattribute them to its own
uncommitted changes. They also mask real regressions in those three tests
during in-session runs.

## Fix direction

Root fix belongs to acp-llm-adapter (outside this repository): taking
`PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` carries the obligation to reap adopted orphans,
and acp-proxy should wait() its tree. Until then, in-session full-suite
runs can use `systemd-run --user --pipe --wait --collect` as the documented
escape, or the three group-death tests must be read as environment-blocked.
Not addressed by louiselm-mbpc, which is test-only and does not touch these
tests.

title: Grill-me needed: broker-authorized guarded warm Resume
description:
Do not resolve this in passing; the installed guarded launch needs a focused receipt and handoff ordering decision.

Question: When must the Control broker ACK the Sender guard listener relative to the signed Start-to-Running receipt, and what durable outcome records a failed handoff?

Context: skills-core/src/broker/provider_handoff.rs:193-204 requires a verified Start receipt to identify the runtime before accepting SenderGuardEnrolled. skills-core/src/launch_supervisor.rs:1297-1302 appends Start/Running before creating the lifecycle owner. Guard announce closes the channel on uncertain ACK. Issue louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4.5.1 calls for ACK before activation and keeps public Brokered launch disabled; its comment 2670 also says before Running. Existing post-Start cleanup gap is bug louiselm-adh86. docs/codex-kernel-guard-proof.md says the broker validates the signed runtime at handoff.

Threads to decide:
- Keep signed Start first, then make failed ACK a durable terminal outcome despite a closed broker channel; or allow provisional pre-Start listener custody with an independently authenticated runtime proof and no Provider service until Start is durable?
- What exactly does resulting_state Running mean before the guarded endpoint is active?
- How is a newer broker-authorized revision represented for warm Resume without re-enrolling the runtime?
- What negative VM control proves the chosen ordering cannot authorize a request early?
notes: Initial receipt/handoff ordering resolved by maintainer: signed Start first, terminal outcome on failed ACK, bounded fail-closed broker outage. On 2026-09-26 maintainer chose to deny guarded warm Resume until a later broker-authorized revision protocol. Remaining question is that protocol and its fit with Park vocabulary; it does not block initial listener wiring.

title: Grill-me needed: how do frozen project instructions coexist with editable workspace files?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; confirm the project-instruction lifetime contract before implementing native-source proofs.

louiselm-d6fv.3.3 requires every external instruction source measured or masked, including late-source mutation resistance. The input manifest binds a fixed per-Session snapshot. What should happen when an Agent edits an instruction file such as AGENTS.md during that Session?

Evidence: ConfinementPlan (skills-core/src/sandbox.rs:117) has a writable home and workspace, with no per-source snapshot/mask mount entries. Bubblewrap arguments (:1603) bind both writable; general FilesystemVisibility/FilesystemMutation evidence (:1902) cannot prove a specific native root was masked. The confirmed louiselm-5qzq decision covers read-only admitted Skill views at native skill roots, but does not decide the project-file editing contract. Searches including closed issues found no rediscovery decision.

Threads to settle:
- Whether project instruction paths remain editable, with edits affecting only a fresh Session, or become read-only for the Session lifetime.
- If editable, how each adapter is prevented from auto-reloading the mutable workspace copies while consuming the frozen snapshot.
- Which trusted pre-start confinement observation identifies each snapshot or empty mask, and how that evidence stays valid after workspace writes.
- Where the required snapshot/mask mount implementation lives: .3.3 explicitly excludes mount mechanics; .9 currently carries the read-only mount integration.

Do not count a host-side existence check or a caller-supplied masked boolean as proof. Resolve this before defining a successful native_supply producer; .3.4 depends on that producer. The .3.2 canonical manifest remains independently implementable.

title: Grill-me needed: how should louiselm expose Neovim diagnostics through ACP?
description:
Do not resolve this in passing — this question needs a deliberate design discussion before implementation.

## The question

Should louiselm collect Neovim diagnostics and send them to ACP agents as prompt context, and should the louiselm/acp-llm-adapter stack negotiate a custom capability or request for fresh diagnostics?

## Context and evidence

The user wants to fix diagnostics shown by Snacks (for example diagnostics on Cargo.toml) without making the model spend tokens rediscovering them. Snacks is only displaying Neovim’s diagnostic store; diagnostics may come from rust-analyzer, taplo, lua-language-server, or another LSP, so the client-side feature should be language- and adapter-agnostic.

The ACP client is louiselm.nvim and the agent is acp-llm-adapter. ACP has no standard diagnostics capability, but supports custom capabilities and methods through _meta and underscore-prefixed JSON-RPC extensions. The adapter currently advertises embeddedContext: true, so the client can already send diagnostics as text or embedded resource prompt content. The adapter records incoming client capabilities but does not currently advertise or implement a diagnostics extension.

## Threads worth pulling

- Decide whether initial diagnostics should simply be collected by louiselm on an explicit fix action and attached to session/prompt, with no protocol extension.
- Decide whether a custom client capability should advertise a semantic feature such as current editor diagnostics, without exposing the implementation detail vim.diagnostic.
- Decide whether the adapter needs an on-demand custom request for fresh diagnostics after edits, versus relying on terminal/LSP rechecks.
- Define scope and selection: current line, current buffer, workspace, or user-selected Snacks diagnostics; errors/warnings only by default.
- Define a compact, typed representation containing absolute URI/path, 1-based line/column, severity, source, code, message, and freshness/change context.
- Decide whether diagnostics belong in standard prompt content, prompt _meta, an embedded resource, or a custom request response.
- Account for stale diagnostics, noisy hints, external/untrusted diagnostic text, prompt size, and cross-editor interoperability.
- Keep the standard ACP path usable by other clients and agents; any custom extension must be optional and namespaced.

## Out of scope

Implementing the diagnostics collector, changing ACP protocol code, or choosing a final wire format before this design question is deliberately opened.
close_reason: Design confirmed by maintainer; diagnostics collection contract recorded in issue comment

comments.author: codex/01a037d9-bf57-7921-86bc-79ca8584c171
comments.text: Maintainer-confirmed design: expose an explicit :LouiselmDiagnostics action; collect current-buffer errors and warnings; queue compact text on the next prompt without auto-sending; use standard ACP with no custom capability/request in v1; include path, 1-based line/column, severity, source, code, and message; include observation time and buffer-change state without silently refreshing diagnostics; cap diagnostic count and message length with explicit truncation counts; report a clear error and make no changes when no LouiseLM Session is active; delimit diagnostic messages as untrusted data rather than Agent instructions. Implementation can now be decomposed separately.

title: QA round: AGENTS.md resource_link injection (louiselm-ce6.20)
description:
# Manual QA review — AGENTS.md resource_link injection

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `fde8c6a` (feat(context): attach project instructions as
an ACP resource_link, closes louiselm-ce6.20), repo now at `6b2a69f` (two
later commits are unrelated agent health-check work, not part of this
feature's scope). **Restart Neovim after any fix** — this is a plugin loaded
from source, there is no build step, but Lua modules are cached per-process.

Origin: on a brand-new ACP session's first prompt, louiselm now attaches a
`resource_link` content block (name + URI, not the file body) pointing at a
configured project-instructions file (e.g. `AGENTS.md`), when
`context.instructions_file` is set and the file exists at the project root.
The automated suite (251/251 mini.test cases, including one real-wire-bytes
test via a fake ACP process) proves the block is *sent* correctly. It cannot
prove a real agent *does anything* with it, and it cannot show you what the
chat buffer actually looks like — that's this round.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | A real agent actually reads the linked file | **passed** — session `claude/25ef1772-…`, log `20260820-082942-635200-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`: first action is a native `Read` tool call on `/home/lotso/code/louiselm/AGENTS.md`, answer cites AGENTS.md:229-239 verbatim-correct |
| 2 | Visible context chip on a brand-new session | **passed** — session `claude/8fe8fd28-…`, cursor lands after the chip |
| 3 | No duplicate/leaked link across two sibling new sessions | **passed** — user-confirmed, no duplication/leakage |
| 4 | Resumed session never gets the link | **passed** — session `claude/1dec0a6e-…` resumed, no `[context: ...]` chip |

## Setup

Add this to wherever you already call `require("louiselm").setup(...)` in
your Neovim config (I don't have that path — tell me if you want me to look):

```lua
require("louiselm").setup({
  -- ...your existing agents/skills/etc...
  context = { instructions_file = "AGENTS.md" },
})
```

Restart Neovim fully (`:qa` and relaunch) so the new commit's Lua is loaded
fresh, not the cached previous version. Confirm the running copy matches
source: `:lua print(require("louiselm.instructions") ~= nil)` should print
`true` with no error — that module didn't exist before this commit, so an
error here means you're still on stale Lua.

Run all cases from a project whose root already has `AGENTS.md` — this repo
(`/home/lotso/code/louiselm`) qualifies, since it has one. Open Neovim with
`cwd` set to this repo for that reason (`cd /home/lotso/code/louiselm && nvim`).

## Ground rules learned the hard way

(empty so far — append here whenever a case misses for an environmental
reason rather than a code reason)

## Cases

### 1. A real agent actually reads the linked file

Exercises the entire point of `fde8c6a` — a mock ACP process can prove the
bytes were sent, it cannot prove any real agent binary honors a
`resource_link`. Also worth knowing going in: louiselm's ACP client currently
advertises `fs = { readTextFile = false }` (`lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:195`,
predates this commit) — so a strictly spec-compliant agent should not even
attempt to fetch the link *through the ACP protocol*. The only way this can
work today is if the agent opens the local `file://` path directly off disk
itself. That's a real uncertainty this case is meant to settle, not a
predicted bug — some agents may ignore `resource_link` blocks entirely.

Steps:

> Open `:LouiselmChat` (or `:LouiselmNewSession`) against whichever real,
> responsive agent you normally dogfood with. As the very first prompt of
> the new session, type something that only makes sense if the agent has
> actually read this repo's `AGENTS.md`, e.g.:
>
> `> Without me telling you, name one thing this project's AGENTS.md says agents must do before finishing a code task.`

Expect: the agent's answer names something real from this repo's `AGENTS.md`
(e.g. "run stylua/lua-language-server/mini.test before handoff", "use
red-green-refactor", "don't add compatibility shims").

Failure signature: the agent says it doesn't have access to that file, asks
you to paste it, answers generically/incorrectly, or answers about a
*different* AGENTS.md-style convention it already knows from training rather
than this repo's actual content.

Evidence: if your agent is the default DeepSeek-backed
`acp-llm-adapter` wrapped by `acp-debug.sh`, its **stdout** (agent→client
direction) is logged to
`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/<timestamp>-<pid>-*-stdout-jsonrpc.log`
(newest file for this run — match by the timestamp printed at session start,
not "most recent," since old logs pile up). That log will *not* show the
`resource_link` louiselm sent (that's client→agent, unlogged by this script)
but it will show whether the agent issued an `fs/read_text_file` request back
— which it shouldn't, given the capability is off — and whatever `session/prompt`-adjacent
traffic it produces. For any other agent: there's no log, so this case rests
on what you read in its answer. Say so plainly when you report back.

### 2. Visible context chip on a brand-new session

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` `Chat:new_session` (queues
`instructions_context`) and `queue_context`'s `context_prefix` rendering.
Purely synchronous UI state — doesn't need the agent to ever respond.

Steps:

> Run `:LouiselmNewSession` (or `:LouiselmChat` for the first session). Look
> at the prompt line before typing anything.

Expect: the prompt line reads `> [context: AGENTS.md] ` — one clean chip,
cursor positioned right after it, ready to type. Type `hi` and look again:
`> [context: AGENTS.md] hi`, chip text not duplicated, not overwriting itself.

Failure signature: chip missing entirely, chip text garbled/duplicated,
cursor lands before the chip instead of after it, or typing overwrites part
of the `[context: AGENTS.md]` marker itself.

Evidence: what you see in the buffer. No file/log needed for this one.

### 3. No duplicate/leaked link across two sibling new sessions

Exercises the once-per-new-session gating in `Chat:new_session` — automated
coverage only exercises a single session per test process, never two created
back-to-back sharing one `Chat` instance.

Steps:

> With the chat UI already open from case 2, run `:LouiselmNewSession` again
> to create a second, sibling session (don't resume/switch to the first).
> Look at its prompt line. Then switch back to the first session
> (`:LouiselmSwitchSession`) and look at its prompt line again.

Expect: the second session's prompt line also shows exactly one
`[context: AGENTS.md]` chip. The first session's line is unaffected by the
second session's creation (still whatever you left it at in case 2 — one
chip, not two).

Failure signature: either session shows the chip twice concatenated, the
second session shows no chip at all, or the first session's chip
duplicates/changes after the second session is created.

Evidence: what you see in each session's buffer, switching between them.

### 4. Resumed session never gets the link

Exercises the `Chat:resume_session`/`load_session` path, which — unlike
`Chat:new_session` — never queues `instructions_context`. This is the
mechanism AC #4 relies on; automated coverage only asserts it for a directly
`attach`-ed fake session, never through the real discovery/picker UI.

Steps:

> Close the chat UI (`:LouiselmCloseSession` or just `:qa` and relaunch
> Neovim). Run `:LouiselmResume` (or `:LouiselmResume!` for all workspaces)
> and pick one of the sessions created in cases 2/3 from the picker.

Expect: the resumed session's prompt line shows no `[context: ...]` chip at
all — plain `> `.

Failure signature: a `[context: AGENTS.md]` chip appears on a resumed
session's prompt line before you've typed or queued anything yourself.

Evidence: what you see in the buffer right after resume, before typing.

## Evidence check

There's no single command that verifies all four cases — 2 through 4 are
pure UI-state observations (that's the point: things a mock-ACP unit test
cannot see), and case 1 has a log only if you're on the default DeepSeek
agent. Report what you saw for each; I'll flag anything that sounds like a
recipe issue (wrong cwd, stale Lua) versus a real product bug before we
record it.

## Cleanup when the round closes

No fixtures created outside your own Neovim session state (no files written,
no repo state changed). Nothing to revert beyond closing the chat sessions
you opened for cases 2–4.

## Reporting back

Tell me which case, what you saw, and anything surprising — especially for
case 1, since "the agent answered correctly" only proves the happy path;
tell me if it hedged, refused, or answered from training data instead of the
actual file. I'll pull whatever log evidence exists myself before we call a
case passed or failed.

## Findings this round

**F1 — cursor landed before the queued context chip, not after** (`louiselm-muo`,
closed, fixed in `e15a846`). `Chat:attach` sets the cursor once at
`ui/chat/init.lua:1441` before `Chat:new_session` queues any automatic context;
`queue_context` rewrote the prompt line to prepend the chip but never moved the
cursor, so it stayed at the pre-chip column regardless of chip length. Affects
skill-catalog inject mode too, not just this feature — pre-existing bug this
round's case 2 was the first thing to exercise. Fixed: `queue_context` now
repositions the cursor to just past the full `context_prefix` after rewriting
the line. Regression test: `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` "positions the cursor
after queued context, not before it" (failed `{6,1}` vs expected `{6,27}`
before the fix). Full suite 267/267, stylua/lua-language-server clean.
Confirmed live by user in session `claude/8fe8fd28-ac0c-4293-bc77-5fc605d432ea`.
close_reason: 4/4 cases passed. Case 1 (real agent honors the resource_link) and case 2 (visible chip) each got direct session-log/user evidence; 1 real bug found and fixed (louiselm-muo, cursor position). Cases 3 and 4 confirmed by direct user observation per the working file's own evidence design (no artifact for pure UI-state cases).

title: Launch supervisor
description: The privileged per-Session process created by the fixed louiselm-launch run entrypoint that confines, starts, relays, controls, and disposes exactly one Agent process tree.
design:
Established by the louiselm-ruxl grill-me and louiselm-ax-design-review, confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-09-03. Source Sessions: codex/01a067ef-6521-7ce2-8388-87f49972d615 and codex/01a0684c-d410-7292-97ff-4fdddeeff0e9.
Authority/startup refinement confirmed by the maintainer in louiselm-9onz on 2026-09-09; source Session codex/01a083f4-469e-7351-97fb-205f6aa39a6f.
notes:
A Launch supervisor is long-lived but not a root daemon: one fixed privileged invocation owns one Session. It executes mechanics but never chooses policy. Loss of broker or controller freezes or ends the Session according to the signed lifecycle contract; a later helper invocation never takes over an existing process tree.
The supervisor establishes and lifetime-pins the actual Agent runtime from trusted launch/kernel evidence, distinct from Bubblewrap's namespace reaper and the rest of the Session tree. Self-reported identity, first connection and Session membership are insufficient. It enforces the Agent/tool separation mechanics and Agent-exit revocation; the Control broker still chooses all grant policy. This does not authorize a runtime wrapper, altered Bubblewrap reaping or replacement-process takeover.

title: skills-core CI fails on stale control CLI usage assertion
description:
The skills-core CI test gate fails because the Control broker CLI usage diagnostic changed when skill-request verbs were added, while an existing invalid-invocation test still expects the old wording. This blocks the remaining gates in the job. Observed once in the linked run; no runtime broker failure is established.

## Observed

CI run 35117295825, job 104865846964 (cargo (skills-core)), 2026-09-16, commit 2a94e15b9001fba47abf92704bc17a6d4df743e6 (feat(broker): persist skill admission requests).
https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/35117295825/job/104865846964

Test step log at 15:46:13 UTC:
```
thread 'validates_verbs_confirmation_and_socket_activation' (12414) panicked at tests/control_binary.rs:27:9:
louiselm-control: expected 'serve', 'adopt-state --confirm', 'session inspect ID --json', or 'skill-request inspect|reject|cancel ID --json'
test result: FAILED. 4 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.01s
Process completed with exit code 101.
```
Format and Lint passed. Subsequent browser, documentation and privileged conformance steps were skipped.

## Symptoms

- cargo test exits 101 in the control_binary integration target.
- Invalid invocation is correctly refused, but its diagnostic fails the stale substring assertion.

## Root cause

Verified against source at the failing commit: skills-core/tests/control_binary.rs:27-32 expects "expected 'serve', 'adopt-state --confirm', or 'session inspect ID --json'". skills-core/src/bin/louiselm-control.rs:29-33 adds skill-request dispatch, and :47 lists that new command in the usage diagnostic. The old substring no longer matches because "or" now precedes the new final alternative. The first case (no arguments) already fails.

## Why it was not caught

The existing regression does catch this in CI. Its expectation duplicates the complete command-list wording, coupling invalid-invocation coverage to additions of valid verbs. Whether the full owning suite ran before the originating commit is unverified.

## Fix direction

Align the invalid-invocation diagnostic assertion with the current CLI contract while retaining all invalid-argument cases, failed exit status, empty stdout and the separate serve-without-socket-activation check. Keep typed inspection refusal coverage. Do not remove the new valid verbs to satisfy the stale test.

## Acceptance

- The existing validates_verbs_confirmation_and_socket_activation test reproduces the failure before the fix and passes afterward; preserve its refusal and socket-activation coverage.
- Focused reproduction from repo root, outside the ACP parent chain:
  systemd-run --user --pipe --wait --collect --working-directory="$PWD" --setenv PATH="$PATH" --setenv CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only ./scripts/test-skills-core --test control_binary
- The complete skills-core suite and applicable gates pass using docs/agent-testing.md; a fresh CI run passes the affected Test step and executes downstream gates.

## Not covered

Filed only at the maintainer's request; left open and unclaimed. No implementation or local test rerun performed. The CI log and exact-commit source establish the mismatch. No claim is made about later skipped gates or installed broker behavior.

title: Mixed-Agent Session picker separates matching effort and Fast mode columns
description:
Mixed Claude/Codex Sessions display corresponding effort and Fast mode options in different switch-picker columns, with large blank gaps.

## Observed
Maintainer screenshot /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260909_0422_1920x1200_1788920538.png, 2026-09-09. Sessions claude/3282c3df-a569-4d46-9b35-358157805c69 and codex/01a083f4-469e-7351-97fb-205f6aa39a6f. Read both /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/<ACP-id>/log.jsonl configOptions arrays: Claude advertises effort / Effort / thought_level and fast / Fast mode / model_config; Codex advertises reasoning_effort / Reasoning effort / thought_level and fast-mode / Fast mode / model_config, plus collaboration_mode. This records observed shapes, not event ordering.

## Symptoms
Effort and Fast mode appear in separate horizontal positions across the two rows. Context and identity starts appear aligned in the screenshot; viewport clipping is visible but its cause is unverified.

## Root cause
lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:499,528 keys cells and their union by raw option.id. Different Agent identifiers allocate different columns even for corresponding displayed controls. Original alignment task louiselm-pngu, commit c7b0278, closed after live acceptance on September 7.

## Why it was not caught
tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:6315 uses fabricated snapshots where both Agents share reasoning as the effort id. It verifies separator offsets and missing cells but does not represent the observed effort/reasoning_effort or fast/fast-mode pairs.

## Fix direction
Resolve presentation matching at session_formatter while retaining Agent option labels and distinct unrelated controls. Do not merge every model_config option indiscriminately: that category can contain unrelated settings.

## Acceptance
A public switch-picker regression derived from these observed option arrays fails before the fix. Corresponding effort and Fast mode controls share columns; Codex-only collaboration mode stays distinct; missing fields, Unicode widths, full identity, selection and cancellation remain correct.
