title: Permission picker treats Allow Once as Deny
description:
## Summary

After the fail-closed permission ordering fix, a user who selects the displayed second option, Allow Once, can still send the first option, Deny. Generic vim.ui.select providers may render numbered rows without interpreting a typed number as row selection.

## Reproduction

Session: claude/d0cb6393-4548-4533-937f-614160f5a2b5

1. Ask Claude to perform an operation requiring permission.
2. Deny the first request.
3. Ask Claude to retry and select displayed option 2, Allow Once.
4. Observe Claude receives User refused permission again.

The ACP trace advertised Deny as option 1 and Allow Once as option 2 on both requests.

## Expected

A deliberate Allow Once choice sends its exact ACP optionId. Rejecting, allowing, and cancelling must all be unambiguous regardless of the installed vim.ui provider.

## Actual

Typing the displayed option number can confirm the provider current row instead, so option 2 is interpreted as option 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The permission choice flow does not depend on provider-specific numbered-row key behavior.
2. Choosing Deny sends the deny optionId, and choosing Allow Once sends the allow optionId.
3. Invalid or dismissed choices cancel rather than approve.
4. Agent option labels and identifiers remain distinct and unmodified.
5. Scheduled UI handling and late-choice-after-disposal safety remain covered by headless tests.
close_reason: Replaced provider-dependent permission selection with explicit numbered input, preserving exact ACP option IDs. Added regression coverage for Claude's Deny/Allow Once options, invalid and dismissed input, distinct labels, scheduling, and disposal. Verification: 43 focused UI tests and 184 full MiniTest cases pass; installed Snacks input smoke returns typed 2; stylua --check and lua-language-server checks pass.

title: Session output taint
description: An immutable, transitive provenance condition on all externalized Session-authored content when emergency quarantine reaches the pinned Skill Generation of a Session.
design: Established by the louiselm-d6fv.6.5.3 grill-me and confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-09-25. Source Session codex/01a0d99e-129e-7423-ac29-1cbe603430f7.
notes: Use Session output taint for content provenance, not as a claim that trusted control-plane records are untrustworthy. It covers the full Session lifetime and propagates to derivatives. Clean independent verification plus exact operator acceptance may authorize one use but never remove taint. A newly admitted higher-sequence Skill Generation permits clean new Sessions; existing Sessions remain tainted.

title: Grill-me needed: what binds a package to a Provider view, and what is a materialized view?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; it needs a focused grill-me session
before any of `louiselm-d6fv.3` is implemented.

Two entangled questions block the first slice:

1. What binds an admitted package to a Provider's view, and does the
   Generation's signature cover that binding?
2. What is a materialized view physically — a published immutable tree, or a
   set of mount entries computed per launch?

## Context and evidence

`GenerationPayload.view_roots` (`generation.rs:53`) is a
`BTreeMap<String, String>` written at Admission (`admission.rs:56`, `:260`,
CLI `--view <provider>=<root>` at `cli.rs:536`) and bound into the signed
bytes. Nothing in `skills-core/src` or `skills-core/tests` ever reads it; the
tests that construct it pass an empty map (`tests/admission.rs:78`, `:743`).
Its value has no defined meaning: path, name, or digest are all consistent
with the current code.

`Member` (`generation.rs:24`) carries `package_digest`, `dossier_digest`, and
`review_depth` — no Provider scope. No `provider` field exists in
`manifest.rs`, `dossier.rs`, `inspect.rs`, or `store.rs`. On the Lua side the
only Provider-shaped convention is the OpenAI-specific `agents/openai.yaml`
lookup at `skills/discovery.lua:330`, which is a per-skill vendor extension,
not a scoping model. `AgentRegistration` (`registry.rs:50`) does know its
Provider, so scoping could equally live at deployment time.

`louiselm-d6fv.3` AC1 requires shared packages in every intended view and
Provider system packages only in their own view. If per-view membership is not
covered by the Admission signature, the signed set proves the total supply but
not the split, and re-scoping after Admission changes what an Agent reads
without invalidating anything.

## Threads worth pulling

- Where scoping is declared: the package declares its own Providers, the
  operator declares it at Admission, or the Agent registration decides at
  deployment. Each puts the authority in a different place.
- Whether the signed payload must commit to per-view membership. If it must,
  `louiselm.skills.generation/1` becomes `/2`: existing witnessed Generations
  stop parsing and a new physical YubiKey Admission ceremony is required. That
  cost is the reason this is not an implementation detail.
- What `view_roots`' value is meant to be, and whether an unread signed field
  should keep being written until it has a meaning.
- Whether a view is published once per Generation and bind-mounted, or
  computed per launch into `ConfinementPlan` (`sandbox.rs:113`), which today
  has `runtime_root` and `system_roots` but no instruction-view entry. This
  decides whether view publication mechanics exist at all.
- How Provider system and vendor skills are distinguished at Admission, given
  the epic requires them through the same Inspection and local Admission.
- Whether `skills=off` is an empty view or the absence of a view, and what
  happens to a package admitted for a Provider no registered Agent uses.
close_reason: Views keyed by Agent, membership signed at Admission, view published once and mounted read-only. Vocabulary promoted in louiselm-5txo and louiselm-ho14. inert:louiselm-d6fv.3.5

comments.author: claude/3282c3df-a569-4d46-9b35-358157805c69
comments.text:
Answered by grill-me, maintainer confirmed 2026-09-09.

1. Instruction views are keyed by Agent, not Provider: the harness decides skill compatibility, and one Agent may route through several Providers (lua/louiselm/agent/provider.lua resolves Provider before each prompt).
2. Provider is not a scoping axis. Disclosure stays in the provider_disclosure dimension; a per-Provider constraint is addable later without re-keying.
3. Membership is declared at Skill Admission and bound into the signed payload. generation/1 to /2, no migration: no store, no admitted Generation, no installed release exists yet.
4. A view is published once per (Generation, Agent) as an immutable store tree, mounted read-only at the Agent's native skill root inside the private home; inject-policy Agents read the same tree. view_roots deleted: a host path does not belong in a portable signed record and never had a reader.
5. No default membership. Every member carries an explicit literal Agent list; --all-agents expands at signing, so the record's meaning never depends on unsigned registry state.
6. skills=off binds and mounts the canonical empty view: an artifact with a digest, and a mask that stops vendor fallback discovery at the root it searches. Unregistered Agents named in a Generation are not an error.
7. provider_disclosure names the set of Providers a routed Agent can reach, fixed at launch; AgentRegistration.provider takes the Lua shape.

Derived and accepted: view digests are recomputed from members plus registry rather than stored as a claim, matching recomputed_member_root; views are published at Admission time.

Correction to this question as filed: I claimed the registry route left no proof of what a Session read. That was wrong. The receipt binds the input manifest, which binds the view digest, so the outcome is pinned either way. The real difference is that Admission signs the policy and the registry signs only the outcome, which is an error-model argument, not an attacker-model one. That is what decided it.

Vocabulary: created louiselm-5txo Instruction view; updated louiselm-ho14 Skill Generation from Provider-scoped to Agent-scoped. Routed to louiselm-d6fv.3.5 and louiselm-d6fv.3.6.

title: Investigate diff edit approval UX
description:
## Context

After asking LouiseLM to create a file, the plugin opened a `louiselm-diff` buffer. The latest screenshot (`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0457_1920x1200_1786244259.png`) shows the target path, `--- original`, `+++ proposed`, and an otherwise empty buffer. No visible accept/reject/close actions or instructions are presented, and Neovim is in insert mode.

## Investigation

Determine the intended lifecycle for an agent-proposed file edit and whether this diff view is currently incomplete, incorrectly rendered, or intentionally only a review surface. Trace the permission/edit/diff flow and document how a user should:

- understand what changed;
- accept/apply the proposed edit;
- reject it;
- cancel or return to the conversation;
- handle an empty/new-file diff;
- recover if the diff buffer is closed or the proposed edit becomes stale.

Assess the UX from a first-time user perspective, including discoverability of keymaps/commands, mode choice, statusline/help text, and whether approval belongs in the diff view, a permission prompt, or both.

## Exit criteria

- Reproduce the flow with a deterministic test or documented local scenario.
- Identify the root cause of the empty/unactionable presentation, if it is a bug.
- State the intended user-facing contract and recommended minimal UX changes.
- Add implementation follow-up beads tasks if the investigation finds separate fixes.
- Add or update headless UI behavior coverage for the confirmed contract where practical.
close_reason: Added discoverable diff approval instructions and normal-mode focus; verified full test and quality gates.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Investigation complete. The diff controller already had buffer-local normal-mode mappings: a accepts, d/q reject. The screenshot was unfriendly because the review buffer provided no instructions and inherited insert mode from the chat prompt, making those mappings undiscoverable/unusable. The diff is a permission review; accept sends the ACP allow response and the agent performs the write. Added an explicit instruction line and return to normal mode on focus. Existing behavior tests plus the new render assertion pass; no separate apply bug was reproduced.

title: Claude sessions show no [thinking] blocks with current ACP defaults
description:
Claude Sessions in LouiseLM show no `[thinking]` blocks even when Claude performs thinking and Codex ACP emits reasoning updates. The integration currently exposes no user-visible reasoning summaries for the current Claude ACP defaults.

## Observed

Seen on 2026-08-29 in `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`, commit `c1b293d584d88f6837a0da349b85bdbb7fb7dcfe`, using `acp-proxy -- claude-agent-acp`, `claude-agent-acp 0.70.0`, and `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.238`.

The latest Claude native transcript and matching ACP proxy log share session ID `ea8b846d-3700-44ed-aa39-ffb9e68c8973`:

- Native Claude JSONL: `/home/lotso/.claude/projects/-home-lotso-code-louiselm/ea8b846d-3700-44ed-aa39-ffb9e68c8973.jsonl` — 99 `thinking` blocks, 0 with non-empty `thinking` text (all signature-only).
- ACP log: `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ea8b846d-3700-44ed-aa39-ffb9e68c8973/log.jsonl` — 0 `agent_thought_chunk` updates and 183 `agent_message_chunk` updates.
- The same ACP path works when Claude supplies text: older Claude session `ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d` has 1 non-empty native thinking block and 5 `agent_thought_chunk` updates.
- Codex comparison: ACP session `01a04b3e-2755-7fd0-8256-2c58beb58b50` has 100 `agent_thought_chunk` updates.

## Symptoms

- The user sees Claude answers and tool rows, but no `[thinking]` fold/header between them.
- The wire has no non-empty Claude reasoning event for LouiseLM to render; this is not a renderer-only failure.

## Root cause

Claude native responses now contain signature-only blocks because the Claude SDK/provider is using `thinking.display = "omitted"`. The current adapter intentionally forwards a Claude thinking block only when its text is non-empty (`/home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp/src/acp-agent.ts:8380-8391`); an omitted block therefore produces no `agent_thought_chunk`.

The adapter leaves the thinking display at the SDK default unless an explicit thinking config is supplied (`/home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp/src/acp-agent.ts:6368-6369`, and the user-provided options are spread at `:6482-6486`). LouiseLM sends only `{ cwd, mcpServers }` in `session/new` (`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:521-522`), so its normal Claude configuration has no way to request `thinking: { type = "adaptive", display = "summarized" }`. LouiseLM itself already handles the event (`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:211-215`) and renders it (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2322-2341`).

Anthropic documents that `display = "omitted"` returns empty thinking text while retaining an opaque signature, and that `display = "summarized"` is required for readable summaries: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#controlling-thinking-display

## Why it was not caught

The LouiseLM tests cover synthetic non-empty `thought_chunk` events and the adapter tests cover both non-empty thinking and intentionally skipped empty thinking blocks. There is no live-shaped integration fixture asserting that the configured Claude path requests summarized display or that a current Claude session yields non-empty `agent_thought_chunk` updates.

## Fix direction

Expose an explicit, typed/configurable Claude thinking-display choice at the ACP boundary, or otherwise make the configured Claude Agent request summarized thinking. Keep omitted signature-only blocks non-rendering; do not synthesize user-visible text from opaque signatures. Decide and document whether summarized display is the default or an opt-in because omitted display trades visibility for lower streaming latency and matches the Claude SDK default.

## Acceptance

- A regression fixture derived from the captured Claude session proves that the configured LouiseLM Claude path emits at least one non-empty `agent_thought_chunk` for a reasoning-heavy turn when summarized display is selected.
- In a live Claude Session, the user sees a `[thinking]` fold/header with readable summarized text before the answer or tool activity, while Codex behavior remains unchanged.
- The default/opt-in latency and privacy behavior is documented.

## Not covered

No fix was attempted in this triage. The latest Claude transcript proves internal thinking occurred but does not expose readable text; raw chain-of-thought extraction is not requested or supported by this bug. The older Claude session demonstrates that the LouiseLM event and rendering path work when the adapter receives non-empty thinking text.
close_reason: Live acceptance confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-08-30 in Session claude/9f4fae89-a38b-4d73-be74-33cb34c9a4fc: the [thinking] fold is visible in a live Claude Session. Wire evidence in that session's proxy log: 2 agent_thought_chunk updates carrying non-empty readable text, where the bug's original capture had 0 chunks and 99 signature-only native thinking blocks. Fixed in commit 23c56bf by removing the transcript_layout gate so the summarized-thinking default reaches every Agent through ACP's _meta extensibility namespace; the earlier gated implementation (fb71613) was correct in shape but inert for every real configuration. A first prompt produced 0 chunks and was a false negative: type='adaptive' is documented in the Claude Agent SDK as 'Claude decides when and how much to think', so a conversational question legitimately yields no thinking, and confirming the default requires a prompt that warrants reasoning. Lesson routing: an AGENTS.md section 5 rule that a feature gated on optional configuration needs a test for the unset case and a check against the maintainer's real config, since testing both branches of a gate proves only that the gate works and never that it fires; plus louiselm-wh2l filed for acp-proxy never logging session/new, which is what made verifying this class of defect require source reading instead of wire reading.

comments.text:

Root cause verified by reading the pinned claude-agent-acp 0.70.0 source directly (committed code, not the maintainer's uncommitted local diff which is unrelated account-limits work): NewSessionMeta.claudeCode.options.thinking is read and spread over the env-derived thinking config at acp-agent.ts ~L6362/~L6483, confirming { type: "adaptive", display: "summarized" } is a real, already-shipped ThinkingConfig (sdk.d.ts ThinkingAdaptive). comments.text: Maintainer-authorized takeover in Session claude/004cc6f2-daa2-4bdf-b0b1-136c23318dc6 (2026-08-30). comments.author: claude/004cc6f2-daa2-4bdf-b0b1-136c23318dc6
comments.text:
Live verification result (2026-08-30, Session claude/004cc6f2-daa2-4bdf-b0b1-136c23318dc6): the fix committed as fb71613 is CORRECT but INERT for the maintainer's actual configuration. Live acceptance would have failed, so this stays open — the code change alone does not satisfy the acceptance criterion.

Evidence, from the live instance rather than reasoning:

1. session_meta (lifecycle.lua:129) returns early unless definition.transcript_layout == "claude".
2. The maintainer's claude agent entry (~/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua) sets no transcript_layout. A grep across the whole nvim config finds transcript_layout set for NO agent.
3. Therefore no _meta is built. Confirmed on the wire: this Session's own session/load params in ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/004cc6f2-daa2-4bdf-b0b1-136c23318dc6/log.jsonl are exactly {cwd, sessionId, mcpServers} — no _meta key at all.
4. Across every proxy log modified since the fix landed at 07:57, the structural pattern "thinking":{...} appears in zero requests. Earlier grep hits on the bare word 'summarized' were prose in session content, not configuration — worth recording because that false positive is easy to mistake for success.
5. The installed pack copy at ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim is current (819d392) and does contain the fix, so this is not a stale-plugin artifact.

The deeper problem is the choice of gate. session/locator.lua's configured_layouts treats an unset transcript_layout as a first-class supported state meaning 'search every known layout automatically' — it is genuinely optional for Provenance, which is the field's documented purpose (agent/config.lua:19). The thinking default reinterprets that same absence as 'this is not Claude'. So the common, documented-as-fine configuration silently disables the feature, with no diagnostic explaining why. Keying off the agent name was correctly rejected (louiselm-h00g: config keys are arbitrary labels), but transcript_layout is not a substitute for identity either — it is an optional Provenance hint.

Independently: the maintainer's claude agent should carry transcript_layout = "claude" regardless, because without it Provenance historical-session resolution for Claude is degraded. That was flagged in comment 542 and is confirmed here.

No code changed in this Session pending the maintainer's decision on the gate.

comments.author: claude/004cc6f2-daa2-4bdf-b0b1-136c23318dc6
comments.text:
Gate removed per maintainer decision (2026-08-30): the thinking default is now sent to every Agent rather than only a claude transcript_layout one.

Why this is safe rather than a gamble, verified in the pinned ACP SDK rather than assumed. schema/zod.gen.js types NewSessionRequest._meta and LoadSessionRequest._meta as z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()) wrapped in defaultOnError, so unknown keys are accepted by construction and even a malformed _meta degrades to undefined instead of failing the request. The generated type doc states the rule directly: '_meta is reserved by ACP to allow clients and agents to attach additional metadata to their interactions. Implementations MUST NOT make assumptions about values at these keys.' A vendor-namespaced claudeCode entry is therefore precisely what a non-Claude Agent is obliged to ignore, and sending it unconditionally is the protocol's intended extension mechanism rather than a workaround for the missing identity signal.

Test contract changes, recorded because coverage was intentionally displaced rather than merely updated. 'does not default thinking display for a non-claude-layout agent' inverted into 'sends the vendor-namespaced default to a non-Claude agent too'. 'sends no _meta key when the agent definition has no options._meta' became 'invents no _meta beyond the thinking default when the definition has none' — the no-_meta-at-all contract is obsolete, but the claim still worth holding is that nothing else is fabricated alongside the default, so that assertion was preserved in its new form. Added 'defaults thinking display without any configured transcript layout', which is the case that was silently broken and had no coverage. The shared start_ready_session helper asserted whole-params equality and was over-specified for what it tests; it now asserts cwd and mcpServers, which is what it is actually about. Explicit user thinking config is still respected verbatim and the shared agent Definition is still not mutated; both existing tests kept.

Full MiniTest 59/59 in api_spec and 0 fails suite-wide, LuaLS 0 problems, StyLua and API appendix clean.

STILL OPEN pending live acceptance (AGENTS.md section 5). Automated gates cannot close this one: the previous implementation also passed every gate while being inert on the wire. The maintainer must update the installed plugin copy, restart or reload, start a Claude Session, and confirm a readable [thinking] fold appears. The wire-level check is that session/new or session/load params in the new session's proxy log contain _meta.claudeCode.options.thinking — structurally, not the bare word 'summarized', which appears in ordinary prose and produced a false positive during this investigation.

title: Instruction view
description: The immutable per-Agent tree of admitted Skill packages that one verified Session may read.
design: Established by the louiselm-5qzq grill-me, confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-09-09. Source Session: claude/3282c3df-a569-4d46-9b35-358157805c69.
notes: Published once per (Skill Generation, Agent) and mounted read-only at the Agent's native skill root inside the Session's private home. Keyed by Agent, never by Provider: the harness decides skill compatibility, and one Agent may route through several Providers. Distinguish from Skill Generation, which is the signed root binding the whole approved supply and its per-Agent membership; the Generation is not the installed directory. An empty Instruction view is a mask, not an absence: it is mounted so a Provider's own discovery stops at the root it searches instead of falling back. skills=off binds that same empty view.

title: Namespace the LouiseLM caveman-commit skill fork
description:
## Goal
Bring caveman-commit in line with the other locally-modified skill forks
(louiselm-grill-me: louiselm-ce6.31, louiselm-to-beads*: louiselm-ce6.33),
which were renamed and provenance-tracked when they diverged from upstream.

## Evidence
caveman-commit was modified to generalize its reference rule to any id
(fork commit 5157ea1, "feat(caveman-commit): generalize reference rule to
any id" in JuliusBrussee/caveman) so it carries any named reference -
bead id, session id, ticket - as `Refs <id>`, matching the global CLAUDE.md
convention. This diverged the pinned skill from the tracked upstream ref:
/tmp/louiselm-skill-upstream-report.json records caveman-commit as
`"status": "diverged", "risk": "high"` (pinned 5157ea1 vs tracked
upstream 655b7d9), while every other skill in that report is "unchanged".
Unlike grill-me and to-beads, this divergence was never namespaced or
recorded as an owned fork.

## Scope
- Rename the locally owned caveman-commit fork to louiselm-caveman-commit
  (or the established owned-fork naming convention), following the
  louiselm-ce6.31 pattern.
- Update canonical skill frontmatter, catalog identities/paths, metadata,
  golden tasks, and any skill-chain references.
- Record provenance: upstream repo (JuliusBrussee/caveman), skill path,
  and the reviewed/pinned revision (5157ea1), so the catalog stops
  reporting it as an unexplained high-risk divergence.
- Rebuild the shared generated installation.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The fork is exposed under its namespaced identity and catalog state
   records owned-fork lifecycle plus upstream provenance.
2. /tmp/louiselm-skill-upstream-report.json (or its regenerated
   equivalent) no longer shows this skill as an unexplained "diverged"/
   "risk: high" entry.
3. Catalog inventory, lifecycle, metadata, build, unit, and golden-task
   checks pass across the shared installation.
close_reason: Renamed to louiselm-caveman-commit. Fork commit caveman-commit-fork@4743fbf (SKILL.md name/description); dotfiles commit de8f429 (symlink rename, catalog.json identity + pin via manage_lifecycle.py). Full verification suite green.

title: OpenCode Go limit response leaves Session stuck instead of surfacing ACP error
description:
An OpenCode Go Session appears to remain stuck after the provider reaches its 5-hour usage limit. The maintainer reports that this normally produces an ACP limit error, but this Session did not surface that error or become finishable. The 5-hour-limit explanation is still a hypothesis pending the raw ACP frame.

## Observed

Reported by the maintainer on 2026-08-30 for ACP Session `opencode/ses_fad10e00effea4Yk19LNe0CaAa`.

User report, verbatim: "is stuck i think i reach my 5h limit on opencode go and usually i get a acp limit error and im not stuck".

Live Neovim inspection in `/run/user/1000/nvim.566712.0` found an OpenCode view (`session-2`) with ACP id `ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney` (not the exact id reported), state `status = "prompting"`, `current_turn = 7`, buffer `38`. The exact reported ACP id was not present in the live registry, so the reproduction could not be independently confirmed from the running instance.

## Symptoms

- The maintainer sees the OpenCode Go Session as stuck after suspected 5-hour quota exhaustion.
- Expected behavior from prior OpenCode Go runs is a visible ACP limit error.
- The Session instead appears not to complete or transition to the expected error state.

## Root cause

Unknown. Hypotheses: an OpenCode Go quota error is delivered in an ACP error/notification shape that LouiseLM does not consume; the adapter emits a provider error without the terminal turn event; or the live Session is stuck for an unrelated transport/lifecycle reason. Discriminate by capturing the ACP frame sequence and checking whether the Session lifecycle receives a terminal error, `turn_end`, or equivalent after the provider limit response.

## Why it was not caught

Existing coverage exercises known Codex limit notifications and generic process/session failures, but no regression fixture captures an OpenCode Go 5-hour-limit response followed by the observed stuck state. The exact ACP payload and event ordering are missing.

## Fix direction

Capture the sanitized ACP log for the reported Session, identify the terminal signal and route it through the narrowest shared Session lifecycle boundary. Ensure a provider limit response always terminates the active turn, emits the normal structured error, and leaves the Session usable or explicitly errored; do not infer quota state from prose.

## Acceptance

- A regression test derived from the captured OpenCode Go ACP frame sequence fails before the fix and passes after it.
- When OpenCode Go reaches the 5-hour limit, the user sees the ACP limit error rather than a stuck Session.
- The Session does not remain in an active/prompting state after the terminal limit response.

## Not covered

- Whether the maintainer actually reached the 5-hour limit; this remains unverified until the provider/ACP evidence is captured.
- The exact reported ACP id could not be found in the inspected live Neovim registry.
- Other OpenCode provider errors or generic hangs without a quota response.
close_reason: Client-side prompt watchdog prevents indefinite stuck Sessions; upstream OpenCode ACP quota-error propagation remains outside LouiseLM.

title: QA: phone notification while another Session streams
description:
# Live QA — notification during another Session's output

Issue: louiselm-vi0kj. Prior round: louiselm-l0kp9.
Status: PASSED on 2026-09-17. The maintainer confirmed phone receipt during the
stream. Single-Session delivery passed in the prior round; this completes the
remaining live reproduction. Archive this report to Beads at round end.

## Setup

Use two Sessions in the same running Neovim, with the installed notification fix.
This conversation can be Session A. Do not use two separate editor instances.
Keep the phone reachable. No permission or service configuration changes needed.

## Steps

1. Send Session A:

   > For 90 seconds, post a short commentary update every 5 seconds, using sleep between updates. Keep the turn running until the 90 seconds are over. Do not change files.

2. While A is producing updates, create Session B with :LouiselmSessionNew.
   Send B:

   > Wait 10 seconds using sleep, then reply exactly READY. Do not change files.

3. Immediately switch to an ordinary file buffer inside Neovim, for example
   :edit QA_REVIEW.md. Leave Neovim untouched for 45 seconds after sending B.
   Do not type, navigate, change focus, or return to either chat during that wait.

4. Check the phone. Report whether the alert arrived while A was still producing
   updates. Do not wait for A to finish before deciding whether this case passed.

## Expected result and failure signature

B finishes after about 10 seconds. Its unseen completion becomes eligible about
30 seconds later, while A continues producing output. The phone should receive
the corresponding notification during A's turn; physical delivery can vary.

Failure signature: B remains ineligible because A's rendered output keeps
postponing the idle deadline. A delayed phone notification alone does not prove
that defect; distinguish eligibility, submission, and phone receipt.

## Evidence

The QA agent should start a bounded read-only receiver observer before A's first
update. Sample louiselm-capture attention list and the notifications field from
louiselm-capture status. Retain only subject IDs, kind, creation time,
eligibility, generation, submitted generation, retry count and sender health.
Match B's actual ACP Session ID, not whichever item is newest. Verify A remains
prompting and produces updates across B's idle interval.

Prior valid observer evidence: generation 861 ineligible after 06:16:19 UTC,
generation 862 eligible/submitted at 06:16:50, followed by phone confirmation.
That run had no second Session and is not evidence for this case.

## Observed result

- Streaming Session A: 01a0aded-8685-76d2-88c7-1c61d905f0ad.
- Unseen completed Session B: 01a0ae08-4195-7730-8a1d-c05bbc0e875e.
- B completed at 06:23:42 UTC (created_at_ms 1789626222000); generation 864
  was ineligible from the 06:23:43 sample through 06:24:08.
- At 06:24:13, generation 865 was eligible and submitted_generation was 865:
  approximately 31 seconds after B completed, consistent with the 30-second
  idle threshold at five-second sampling resolution.
- A was prompting and emitting commentary updates throughout that interval;
  B was ready and the current buffer was QA_REVIEW.md. A remained prompting
  through 06:25:13, so notification submission clearly preceded A completing.
- Sender health stayed ready, attempts 0. Generation 866 became empty by
  06:24:23 after navigation, while submitted_generation stayed 865. No duplicate
  submission appeared in the remaining samples through 06:25:23.
- Asked whether the phone alert arrived during the stream, the maintainer
  confirmed: “received the notif”.

The original streaming-related live acceptance now passes. The bounded observer
finished normally. No product finding or implementation change in this round.
Lesson stays in louiselm-vi0kj: rendered Agent output is not operator input;
eligibility, transport acceptance, and physical phone receipt are separate evidence.
Earlier tests missed the defect because the three UI Attention cases did not
exercise input-reset timing; the fix added real-renderer/timing regressions.

## Cleanup and outcome

No synthetic Attention items, product file edits, or configuration changes were
made. Both user-created Sessions remain available; no forced disposal needed.
The exact multiple-Session result is confirmed, so louiselm-vi0kj can close.
Archive this report to a qa-round Bead and remove this scratch copy at round end.
close_reason: Multiple-Session live QA passed: generation 865 submitted about 31s after B completed while A streamed; maintainer confirmed phone receipt. Bug louiselm-vi0kj closed; report archived. live:codex/01a0aded-8685-76d2-88c7-1c61d905f0ad

title: Restored chat crashes while rendering replayed history
description:
## Problem

Loading an existing ACP/Codex session works, but the chat UI crashes when replayed assistant history arrives. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:690` performs arithmetic on `view.transcript_tail`, which is nil for a newly attached restored session.

## Reproduction

1. Create a session with Codex ACP and exit Neovim.
2. Load the ACP session with `sessions:load_session(...)`.
3. Attach it to `Chat`.
4. Observe `vim.schedule callback ... chat/init.lua:690: attempt to perform arithmetic on a nil value`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Restored assistant history renders without an error.
- New-session streaming behavior remains unchanged.
- Add a focused regression test covering a replayed chunk on an attached restored session.
close_reason: Fixed restored assistant chunk rendering fallback and added regression coverage. Focused chat tests: 30 passed; full mini.test suite: 115 passed; stylua --check and lua-language-server diagnostics passed.

title: QA round: Handoff source retention acceptance
description:
# Manual QA review — Handoff source retention

Scratch follow-up to `louiselm-1orv`; do not commit. Archive the final report
in Beads and delete this file when the round ends.

**Build under test:** installed plugin `f7a2163`; Handoff owner extraction
`29f9fb1` includes the earlier takeover brief and typed-resource behavior.
No rebuild is needed. The human drives the UI; the assistant captures evidence.

The original round passed brief rendering, blank-task refusal, target focus,
transport, and receiver behavior. Only source retention was unverified because
the original source editor was closed before checking the switcher.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Establish a disposable source and record its identity/state | Passed — source `01a0a44d…`, local `session-3`, ready at turn 1; marker at buffer 53 line 13; one completed prompt and zero tool calls |
| 2 | Submit a real Handoff to a distinct target Session | Passed — distinct target `01a0a451…` received the filled task and source resource, completed one turn without tools, and rendered `HANDOFF-QA-TARGET` |
| 3 | Switch back to the unchanged source after target submission | Passed — human confirms source visible through the switcher; source identity/state/turn and buffer SHA-256 still match baseline; target remains ready |
| 4 | Close only the two QA Sessions | Passed — human reports done; full Registry contains only coordinator `session-1`; source/target chat buffers are gone |

## Setup and scope

- Keep this coordinating Session open:
  `codex/01a0a3e7-1523-74d2-b85f-ce98fd86fe51`, local `session-1`.
- Use a fresh `codex` source and a fresh `codex` target. Handoff to the same
  Agent is valid: the target must be a distinct Session (vocabulary
  `louiselm-7rjr`). Do not hand off the coordinating chat.
- The old errored Claude source is no longer open. This follow-up checks
  retention and unchanged state with a ready source; it does not claim to
  reproduce preservation of that historical error state.
- No tool use, file edits, tracker claims, Park, restart, or permission-policy
  changes are part of the fixture. Existing Agent approval settings stay intact.
- Source: `codex/01a0a44d-17c3-74b0-aa2d-dc065bbd7143`, local `session-3`.
  Buffer 53, URI `louiselm://session-3`, 17 lines, original marker at line 13;
  status `ready`, current turn 1.
- Target: `codex/01a0a451-d353-73e2-86a5-c52c91968be0`, local `session-4`.
  Buffer 66, URI `louiselm://session-4`, 44 lines, target marker at line 40;
  status `ready`, current turn 1.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Current command is `:LouiselmSessionSwitch`, not the old recipe's
  `:LouiselmSwitchSession`. `:LouiselmSessionNew` creates a separate Session.
- Keep the source open until after the target has received its Handoff and
  the source has been selected again through the normal switcher.
- Capture both exact ACP ids. Never identify a target from the newest log alone.
- Registry inventory must include errored Sessions: find the coordinator through
  `session.exit_verdict()`, then inspect its owner's complete `list_sessions()`.
  The exit verdict is an array and intentionally excludes errored Sessions.

## Cases

### 1. Prepare the source

Exercises the installed real Agent/UI path used by the later Handoff.

1. Run `:LouiselmSessionNew` and select `codex` if prompted.
2. Send exactly:

   > Reply only HANDOFF-QA-SOURCE. Do not run tools or change any files.

3. Wait for the reply and ready state, then tell the assistant. Do not start
   the Handoff yet; the assistant will pin the source identity and state.

Expect: a new ready Session containing `HANDOFF-QA-SOURCE`.

Failure signature: no reply, startup error, tool activity, or the prompt was
sent to the coordinating Session. Stop and report rather than retrying blindly.

### 2. Submit the Handoff

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:Chat:hand_off` and
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/handoff.lua:Handoffs:submit` (`29f9fb1`).

1. Run `:LouiselmSessionSwitch` and select the disposable source
   `01a0a44d-17c3-74b0-aa2d-dc065bbd7143`, with the `HANDOFF-QA-SOURCE` reply.
   Do not invoke Handoff from the coordinating chat.
2. Run `:LouiselmHandOff` and choose `codex` as target.
3. Replace only the placeholder after `- takeover task:` with:

   > Complete this Handoff QA checkpoint by replying only HANDOFF-QA-TARGET. Do not run tools, change files, or continue any task from the source context.

4. Submit the review buffer with Ctrl-S and wait for the target reply.
5. Report completion before closing either Session.

Expect: target is a new Session, receives the filled brief, and replies
`HANDOFF-QA-TARGET`. Focus lands in the target. The source remains available.

Failure signature: source gets the target prompt, source disappears, the target
never receives the brief, or submission fails. Record the exact notification.

### 3. Verify source retention

Exercises the Handoff retention contract through the normal Session switcher.

1. From the target, run `:LouiselmSessionSwitch`.
2. Select the pinned source Session, not this coordinating chat.
3. Confirm its original `HANDOFF-QA-SOURCE` reply is still visible and it is
   ready. Do not send it another prompt.
4. Tell the assistant that the source is visible, leaving it open for capture.

Expect: source is listed, switchable, and still has its original identity,
transcript, status, and turn count. The distinct target remains registered too.

Failure signature: source missing from the picker/Registry, wrong conversation
opens, transcript replaced, or source unexpectedly receives another turn.

### 4. Cleanup

After evidence acceptance, close each pinned QA Session with
`:LouiselmSessionClose`, using `:LouiselmSessionSwitch` to select the other.
Leave the coordinating Session open. The assistant verifies the full Registry.
Peer transcript records may remain as QA evidence; no history deletion is needed.

## Evidence check

Before Handoff, capture source state through the live Registry and its exact
chat buffer; after submission and switch-back, compare the same fields. Record
local id, ACP id, Agent, status, current turn, buffer id, and marker presence.
Both distinct Session ids must remain in the complete Registry until cleanup.

Pin the target's protocol log at
`/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/<TARGET_ACP>/log.jsonl`.
Project only `session/prompt` block types, expected marker/URI matches, and
completion/error metadata; do not dump source context or sensitive payloads.
The target should receive the filled takeover task and finish a normal turn.

The Registry proves retention and state, and buffer inspection proves the
original content survives. The human's normal switcher selection proves actual
UI reachability; inventory alone cannot substitute for that check.

## Findings

None yet. The historical errored-source variant is not reproduced by this
fresh ready-source fixture. Previously accepted transport and receiver cases
remain accepted; the new target is only needed to exercise source retention.

## Source baseline — 2026-09-15

Human reported ready. Exact source ACP log confirms one `session/prompt`,
completion `end_turn` at `2026-09-15T09:01:59.995Z`, zero `tool_call` updates,
and no JSON-RPC errors. Complete Registry contains coordinator `session-1`
and ready source `session-3`; no Handoff target has been created yet.

Source buffer SHA-256 before Handoff (newline-joined lines, no trailing newline):
`244b9dc1ed7be9dedb0b2e95ca677a7b18f96139cfddf871372d2091482f1f35`.
This is a supplementary comparison, not a substitute for checking the original
marker, state, identity, and human switcher reachability after submission.

## Target submission — 2026-09-15

Human reported finished. Exact target ACP log contains one prompt at
`2026-09-15T09:07:30.211Z`; its filled takeover instruction was present.
Actual block sequence: `resource_link`, `text`, `resource`. The embedded source
URI is `louiselm://handoff/codex/01a0a44d-17c3-74b0-aa2d-dc065bbd7143`.
Completion was `end_turn` at `2026-09-15T09:07:32.725Z`, with zero tool calls
and no JSON-RPC errors. Buffer 66 contains the exact target reply at line 40.

The complete Registry still contains coordinator, source, and target. Source
identity is unchanged; status remains ready/current turn 1. Buffer 53 is still
17 lines with its exact original reply at line 13, no target reply, and the
same SHA-256 as before Handoff. This proves retention and unchanged content;
normal switcher reachability still awaits the human check. At capture time
the visible chat was the coordinator, so no fresh focus-transition verdict
is inferred from that snapshot.

## Source switch-back acceptance — 2026-09-15

The maintainer followed the normal Session switcher step and reported
“visible,” confirming the original source reply is reachable after Handoff.
The follow-up live Registry still contains source `session-3` and target
`session-4`, both ready at current turn 1, with their pinned distinct ACP ids.
Source buffer 53 remains 17 lines with `HANDOFF-QA-SOURCE` at line 13, no
target reply, and the identical baseline SHA-256. Target buffer 66 still has
`HANDOFF-QA-TARGET` at line 40. The human returned to the coordinator to report,
so the source/target had no visible windows during the later RPC capture.

Source retention and normal switcher reachability pass. No new product
findings. Cleanup of the two disposable Sessions was subsequently verified.

Lesson for the round record: capture the source identity, turn, state, and
content before submission, then explicitly switch back before closing either
Session. A successful receiver turn alone does not prove source retention;
automated Registry tests do not prove the actual picker reaches that source.
No standing instruction change is needed.

## Cleanup and outcome — 2026-09-15

Human reported “done” after closing both QA Sessions. The complete Registry
now contains only coordinator `session-1`, ACP
`01a0a3e7-1523-74d2-b85f-ce98fd86fe51`. Neither source nor target chat buffer
remains. No permissions, files, or tracker work were changed by either fixture.
Their existing peer transcript records are retained as evidence; no history
was deleted. No disposable live Sessions or temporary fixture files remain.

The original round's prior passes plus this fresh ready-source retention
acceptance complete the scoped follow-up. The historical errored-source state
was not recreated; this report does not claim it was. No new finding or code
change resulted. This report becomes the sole durable follow-up record in
Beads; the scratch file is then removed.
close_reason: Handoff follow-up accepted: distinct target completes, ready source remains byte-identical and switchable, both QA Sessions cleanly closed. Earlier passes retained; historical errored-source state not recreated. Evidence and lesson archived in louiselm-61xhf. live:codex/01a0a3e7-1523-74d2-b85f-ce98fd86fe51

title: Exhausted trust sequence panics or wraps during rotation
description:
An exhausted or malformed trust sequence can panic a debug trusted tool or wrap a release tool instead of refusing the change. Normal enrollment will not realistically exhaust u64; this is a persisted-input validation edge case, not a reported live incident.

## Observed
Source inspection during louiselm-d6fv.11.1, 2026-09-06, codex/01a07753-51de-7733-bfeb-8a3f26fa907e.
skills-core/src/trust.rs:307: `sequence: self.sequence + 1,`
skills-core/src/trust.rs:340: `if change.sequence != trust.sequence + 1 {`
TrustStore derives Deserialize and stores sequence as u64; persistence::Directory::load deserializes without rejecting u64::MAX.

## Root cause
Unchecked successor arithmetic at the public rotation payload and apply boundaries. A well-formed roles.json with sequence=18446744073709551615 reaches addition. Default debug overflow checking panics; default release arithmetic wraps. Source-verified mechanism; no runtime reproduction claimed.

## Test gap
Existing rotation tests use small sequences and test stale signatures, not an exhausted persisted counter.

## Fix direction
Checked successor calculation with an explicit typed refusal shared by payload construction and apply. Propagate errors through callers; do not saturate, wrap, reset, or panic.

## Acceptance
RED/GREEN public API and CLI tests load an otherwise valid state with u64::MAX, refuse payload/apply with a useful non-panicking error, preserve every state byte, and cover the final valid increment. Debug and release tests, all skills-core gates.

## Deferral
Separate from serialization/atomic publication in .11.1; leave open for bounded numeric validation. Passkey/phrase recovery must also use checked counters. No hardware, live-store, or privileged reproduction performed.
close_reason: gate:skills-core/tests/trust.rs — shared checked successor refuses exhaustion without mutation; last increment and CLI/API refusal pass debug/release. Lessons in prior comment.

comments.text: RED: public CLI with sequence=u64::MAX exits 101 and reports src/trust.rs:307 attempt to add with overflow; regression expects typed refusal/exit 1. Shared checked successor used for existing and forthcoming paper changes. Agent Mail unavailable; scope trust.rs, its callers and tests.

comments.text: Lesson destination: this comment. Checked TrustStore::next_sequence at skills-core/src/trust.rs:373 is shared by rotation planning/apply and paper recovery; never wrap/saturate a persisted authority counter. RED CLI exited 101; GREEN typed SequenceExhausted/exit 1 preserves bytes. Final MAX-1 -> MAX succeeds; later planning/apply refuse in debug and release. Full Rust gates pass. No standing rule/design question warranted.

title: Completed tool fold is summarized as started
description:
A completed Codex tool call can render as a closed multi-line fold whose visible summary still says “started”. The defect affects long-running tools that emit repeated nonterminal ACP tool_call_update notifications; each update adds another row instead of updating the existing row.

## Observed

Seen live on 2026-08-27 in Neovim 0.12.5, Session codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee, buffer louiselm://session-1. Screenshot: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260827_0439_1920x1200_1787798371.png. Live RPC inspection found lines 12211-12228 all mapped to tool ID exec-eea9e929-fb56-4310-bb86-467944164daf. Lines 12211-12227 read “(started)”; line 12228 read “(completed) · text result — use :LouiselmInspectTool”. The recorded fold range is zero-based 12210-12227, so Neovim default foldtext exposes line 12211 and hides the only completed row.

## Symptoms

- The user sees one closed fold summarized as “(started)” after the tool completed.
- Opening it reveals many duplicate rows for the same tool ID and only the final row has completed status.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2301-2318 unconditionally inserts a new row for every tool_call_started event. lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:216-225 correctly classifies every nonterminal tool_call or tool_call_update as tool_call_started, so progress updates for an existing ID repeatedly enter that insertion path. Completion updates only the latest view.tool_lines[id] row. close_tool_fold_run then folds all duplicate rows because view.tool_statuses is keyed by the shared completed ID, and default foldtext displays the stale first row.

## Why it was not caught

Existing chat tests cover a single start followed by one finish, but not repeated nonterminal updates for one toolCallId before completion.

## Fix direction

At the chat rendering boundary, reuse and update view.tool_lines[id] for repeated started events, preserving the first title when later progress frames omit it. Append only when the ID has no live rendered row. Do not change ACP event classification or add custom foldtext.

## Acceptance

- A live-shaped regression fails before the fix and passes after it for repeated nonterminal updates followed by completion.
- One toolCallId produces one visible row whose final text says completed; no stale started duplicate fold remains.
- Session codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee no longer reproduces after reload/retest.

## Not covered

The existing reasoning folds visible in the same screenshot are separate and intentionally fold the [thinking] header with its content.
close_reason: done

comments.text: Raw-frame verification: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee/log.jsonl lines 33203-33221 contain one in_progress tool_call, seventeen tool_call_update frames with the same toolCallId and no status/title/content, then one completed tool_call_update. The UI turned the first 18 nonterminal frames into buffer lines 12211-12228; completion rewrote only the last. This confirms coalescing same-ID nonterminal updates at the chat rendering boundary is the narrow fix; no ACP classifier change is needed.

comments.text:

title: Uncapped grant-count test intermittently rejects allowed commands
description:
The uncapped grant-count integration test intermittently rejects a command its count policy permits, failing the full skills-core gate. Focused retry passed without source changes.

## Observed

2026-09-17, codex/01a0ad3a-e05a-7b10-a0b0-c7f89e0eef3c, commit preparation for louiselm-d6fv.12. Isolated source is HEAD ec1c72c plus the conformance inspection change; grant authority code/tests are unchanged.

Full suite through scripts/test-skills-core in a transient user service, with CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only and TMPDIR=/home/lotso/.cache/lm12t.4pf2DK, failed at tests/grant_authority.rs:95:

    uncapped_grants_require_uncapped_parents_and_explicit_delegation
    assertion `left == right` failed
      left: false
     right: true

The grant_authority target took 1.53s. Artifact: /home/lotso/.cache/louiselm-d6fv12.BuyFSA/tests-commit.log:715. Focused retry passed in 0.11s (systemd invocation c1f003bf86264f579fce39ca0456a08f); no implementation edits between runs.

## Root cause

Unknown. Hypothesis: tests/grant_authority.rs:64 gives each grant only 1000ms while the uncapped case executes and durably audits 65 operations (lines 93-109). A loaded runner may exhaust wall-clock grant validity before the count assertions finish. The assertion discards the actual error, so expiry is not yet proven.

## Why it was not caught

The count test uses real wall-clock expiry and asserts only is_ok(), hiding whether refusal came from expiry or count policy. Fast isolated runs pass.

## Fix direction

Expose the actual refusal in the assertion, then separate count-policy coverage from timing using existing deterministic facilities. Preserve independent expiry/refusal coverage; do not loosen production grant validity.

## Acceptance

- Confirm the failing error and reproduce the original refusal under controlled time/load.
- Count-policy coverage stays deterministic under representative load.
- Expired grants and over-budget finite grants still refuse.

## Not covered

Deferred because this commit only exposes conformance inspection. No evidence yet of a production authority defect; no grant code was changed.
close_reason: Expiry preempted count policy under load; test-only fix. Count case now uses 30_000ms grant validity and asserts BudgetExhausted by name. Lesson routed to docs/agent-testing.md (assert which refusal, size deadlines against load). gate:skills-core/tests/grant_authority.rs

comments.author: claude/35028f9f-a730-4136-b115-a8cddfcc69dc
comments.text:
Root cause confirmed, not a production defect.

src/broker/commands.rs:250 checks grant expiry before the budget check at :264,
so once a grant deadline passes mid-loop every refusal reads as Expired. The
count test grants 1000ms (tests/grant_authority.rs:73) and the uncapped case
runs 65 durably audited operations; only 1 of its 8 combinations does, which is
why the flake was rare.

Reproduced under controlled load: original 1000ms validity plus a 20ms sleep per
iteration refused at `sequence 49 refused with Expired`. The old assert_eq
rendered that as `left: false right: true`, matching the reported failure.

Fix is test-only. Grant validity for the count case is now the protocol maximum
30_000ms against a 2-minute policy deadline, and the loop asserts the refusal is
BudgetExhausted rather than just is_err. Re-ran with the same 20ms/op load: green
in 1.46s. Expiry keeps its own coverage in
expiry_and_audit_failure_never_reopen_reserved_authority, untouched.

Gates green from repo root: test-skills-core full suite, cargo clippy
--all-targets -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc.

title: Backticked Session IDs fail Provenance lookup
description:
Provenance Session lookup treats Markdown backticks around a Session id as part of the identifier, so a normal model-rendered reference fails unless the user manually removes formatting. This is a degraded but common UX path: models routinely emit IDs as inline code and the user does not control that formatting.

## Observed

QA round on 2026-08-30, louiselm commit e9386db, dotfiles Neovim config.

User entered the model-style inline-code reference with literal backticks:



Provenance opened successfully but rendered:

- unresolved (transcript not found for Session '' in supported layouts: claude, codex, copilot, openai-compatible)

Removing the backticks made the same Session resolve to /home/lotso/.codex/sessions/2026/08/30/rollout-2026-08-30T08-01-44-01a05142-72b8-73b0-9123-9fbef695a8cd.jsonl.

## Symptoms

- A user following a Session id copied from LLM output gets an unresolved transcript.
- The Provenance window includes the backticks in its displayed ID and lookup error.
- The workaround is to manually strip Markdown formatting.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:79 strips only trailing comma, semicolon, period, and closing parenthesis from detected Session candidates. It does not treat Markdown inline-code delimiters as presentation punctuation. The prompt path at lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:865 also trims whitespace only, so pasted backticked IDs fail there too.

## Why it was not caught

Existing UI fixtures use raw Session ids without Markdown delimiters. The automatic locator tests exercise filesystem matching after receiving a clean id; they do not cover the cursor detector or prompt input with model-formatted IDs.

## Fix direction

Normalize only the presentation delimiters at the UI input boundary: accept a matching pair of backticks around an otherwise valid Session id, while preserving backticks inside malformed IDs as invalid. Apply the same narrow normalization to cursor detection and prompted input. Do not weaken locator validation or strip arbitrary characters.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after for a cursor Session id wrapped in backticks.
- A prompted Session id wrapped in backticks resolves identically to the raw id.
- The displayed Provenance Session id and transcript path contain no backticks.
- Existing malformed-id and raw-ID behavior remains unchanged.

## Not covered

- Other Markdown links or prose wrappers around IDs.
- Backticks embedded inside an actual ACP Session id (not observed and should remain invalid).
close_reason: Fixed in the pending commit: normalize matching outer backticks for cursor and prompt Session IDs. Full suite: 751 tests; formatting, Lua diagnostics, API appendix, Vimdoc, and diff checks pass.

Provenance rendered the ID with those delimiters and reported: unresolved (transcript not found for Session '[backtick]codex/01a05142-72b8-73b0-9123-9fbef695a8cd[backtick]' in supported layouts: claude, codex, copilot, openai-compatible). Retyping the raw ID without delimiters resolved it to /home/lotso/.codex/sessions/2026/08/30/rollout-2026-08-30T08-01-44-01a05142-72b8-73b0-9123-9fbef695a8cd.jsonl.

title: Show newest cold Parks first
description:
The cold-Park picker makes operators identify the newest Park by Agent and ACP Session because durable Parks are returned in UUID order rather than recency order. With seven cold Parks in the 2026-08-31 QA run, the current Claude Park was not first and required manual matching.

## Observed

QA Session claude/803f0f3d-926a-45dc-baa9-c1bcd81bf4cb saw seven entries. The matching Run was 6df99a74-12f7-4c75-8484-cfb5874b88c7, but the operator had to compare Agent/ACP Session fields to choose it.

## Root cause

capture-service/src/runs.rs:838 sorts list_resumable summaries by UUID. Run stores parked_at_ms, but RunSummary and the CLI/UI projection do not expose it, so the UI cannot sort by actual Park time.

## Acceptance

- :LouiselmResumePark presents the newest cold Park first.
- Ordering uses durable Park creation time, not UUID or an expiry-time coincidence.
- Ties have deterministic ordering.
- Service and UI tests cover the ordering and preserve existing resume behavior.

## Not covered

No resume behavior defect was found in this observation; the selected Run resumed successfully and became active.
close_reason: Fixed in pending commit: RunSummary exposes parked_at_ms; list_resumable sorts newest Park first and Run ID on ties; Lua service preserves the timestamp. Tests: capture-service 54 tests and LouiseLM 801 cases. Gates: cargo fmt, stylua, LuaLS, API appendix passed.

title: CI intermittently stalls Session recording and replay
description:
The stable-Neovim CI gate fails on commit 7722b55c494e47be6c6e5d137c14aeadbe69e490 while the corresponding nightly-Neovim job passes. Session recording, replay, and transcript-export contracts do not settle, blocking a green CI result.

## Observed

GitHub Actions run 35579757728, job 106269642678 (`mini.test (nvim stable)`), 2026-09-21 08:47:59Z–08:50:53Z. The job ran 1129 cases and ended with 18 failures; the `mini.test (nvim nightly)` job in the same run passed.

`tests/session/recording_spec.lua:11: asynchronous recording did not finish`

`tests/session/usage_replay_spec.lua:18: replay did not settle`

`agent did not respond within 20000ms of starting`

Source log: https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/35579757728/job/106269642678

## Symptoms

- Stable CI fails after roughly 174 seconds.
- Ten recording cases time out, three replay cases do not settle, and four transcript-export cases report a 20-second Agent-start timeout.
- Two Session API expectations also fail (`tests/session/api_spec.lua:3243` and `:3362`).

## Root cause

Unknown. The common failure cluster points to Session asynchronous scheduling/recording/replay progress, but the job log does not identify a shared mechanism. Investigate without assuming that the passing nightly job proves the production behavior correct.

## Why it was not caught

The affected contracts exist and detect the regression, but they do not provide enough diagnostic state to distinguish a shared progress failure from independent test failures. The same run passed on nightly Neovim, so stable-specific coverage did not prevent the merge gate from failing.

## Fix direction

Reproduce on the CI stable Neovim version, capture the outstanding Session recording/replay state at the first timeout, then fix the narrowest shared progress boundary. Add a regression that deterministically proves the queued operation settles on stable Neovim; do not mask the failure by merely increasing timeouts.

## Acceptance

- The listed recording, replay, transcript-export, and API cases pass on the CI stable-Neovim job.
- A targeted regression test fails before the fix and proves the affected asynchronous Session work settles.
- The full stable and nightly mini.test CI jobs pass.

## Not covered

The run log does not establish whether this is deterministic, a Neovim-version compatibility issue, or a timing-sensitive race.

Two fault-injection regressions fail on bb9dc8e and pass after fix;1151 stable/nightly cases pass locally and in GitHub run35606662509. title: QA round: protected quit guard
description:
# Manual QA review — protect multiple chat sessions from last-window quit

Working file for the current round. Untracked on purpose; it is scratch, live
only for this round.

**Build under test:** `5146007` (`fix(chat): preserve window on protected
quit`). Re-run Setup after any fix.

Origin: the commit adds a `QuitPre` guard so quitting Neovim from the only
window displaying a LouiseLM chat does not silently abandon multiple attached
sessions. It warns the user and asks them to switch or close a session first.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Block quit from the only chat window with two live sessions | **passed** — `:q` leaves the chat open |
| 2 | Allow quit after reducing the chat to one live session | **passed** — idle session closed without prompt; remaining chat stayed visible and `:q` exited |
| 3 | Do not block quit when another window exists | **passed** — chat window closed without protection warning |
| 4 | Do not block quit from an ordinary buffer | **passed** — ordinary buffer quit without protection warning |

## Setup

From the repository root:

```sh
git rev-parse --short HEAD
nvim -u ./manual_init.lua
```

The first command must print `5146007` (or a later commit containing this
fix). The interactive checks require a
working configured ACP agent; `manual_init.lua` uses the project's default
DeepSeek adapter unless the environment is configured otherwise. If the agent
cannot start, report the case as blocked rather than treating it as a product
failure.

Inside Neovim, run `:LouiselmChat`, wait for the first chat buffer/session to
open, then run `:LouiselmNewSession` and wait for the second session to open.
Use `:LouiselmSwitchSession` to confirm both sessions are attached before each
relevant case. Do not use `:qa!`: the guard is intended to protect ordinary
quit commands, while force-quit deliberately bypasses safety checks.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Case 1 is not reached unless `:LouiselmNewSession` has produced a second
  attached session. With only one session, `:q` closing Neovim is expected.
- After `5146007`, a protected quit briefly creates a duplicate chat window;
  the pending `:q` should close that duplicate and leave the original chat
  window as the only window.
- For Case 3, run the first `:q` while the statusline/buffer visibly shows the
  chat session. After it closes, confirm the remaining window is the ordinary
  buffer before running the final `:q`.

## Cases

### 1. Block quit from the only chat window with two live sessions

Exercises `41fec85` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua` and
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Steps:

1. Run `:LouiselmNewSession`, then run `:LouiselmSwitchSession`. The picker
   must show two session rows; cancel the picker after confirming this.
2. Ensure the current chat buffer has two live attached sessions.
3. Ensure Neovim has exactly one window (`:only` if needed).
4. Run `:q` (or press the normal window quit mapping).

Expect: Neovim remains open in the same chat buffer. A warning appears saying
that multiple sessions are open and instructing you to use
`:LouiselmSwitchSession` or `:LouiselmCloseSession`. The current session,
buffer, and chat contents remain usable.

Failure signature: Neovim exits; the chat window closes; no actionable warning
appears; or the warning appears but the quit still completes.

Evidence check:

```sh
git show --format= --check 41fec85
```

This confirms the committed patch has no whitespace errors, but cannot prove
that the interactive `QuitPre` callback stopped the quit; the visible result
and the still-running Neovim process prove that part.

### 2. Allow quit after reducing the chat to one live session

Exercises the disposed-session count in `Chat:should_block_quit`.

Steps:

1. Recreate Setup so two sessions are attached in one chat window.
2. Run `:LouiselmSwitchSession`, select one session, then run
   `:LouiselmCloseSession` and confirm any prompt.
3. Confirm the remaining session is visible, then run `:q`.

Expect: the chat window closes and Neovim exits normally. No multiple-session
quit warning appears.

Failure signature: the warning still blocks quit after one session was closed;
the wrong session remains selected; or closing the session leaves a stale chat
buffer/window that prevents normal quit.

### 3. Do not block quit when another window exists

Exercises the `nvim_list_wins() ~= 1` boundary.

Steps:

1. Recreate Setup with two live sessions attached.
2. Split the editor (`:split`) so there are two windows.
3. In one split run `:enew`, then use `Ctrl-w w` until the other split visibly
   shows the chat session (for example `session-2`). Run `:q` in that chat
   window.
4. Confirm the remaining window is the ordinary `[No Name]` buffer, then run
   `:q` again.

Expect: the first `:q` closes only the current chat window without a
multiple-session warning. The second `:q` exits normally.

Failure signature: the warning blocks the first window close despite another
window existing, or the chat/session state is unexpectedly disposed while the
first window closes.

### 4. Do not block quit from an ordinary buffer

Exercises the current-buffer attachment check.

Steps:

1. Recreate Setup with two live sessions attached.
2. Open an ordinary buffer in the only window, for example with `:enew`.
3. Run `:q`.

Expect: Neovim exits normally without the multiple-session warning. This
confirms the protection applies only when the last window is displaying a chat
buffer attached to those sessions.

Failure signature: quit is blocked from the ordinary buffer, or a warning is
shown even though no chat buffer is current.

## Cleanup when the round closes

Close any running agent processes and remove this scratch file after the round
is recorded in beads. Do not commit `QA_REVIEW.md`.

## Reporting back

Send the case number, exact command/keystrokes, what remained visible after the
command, and any warning/error text. If the agent could not start, include that
startup error separately.

## Findings this round

**F1 — Ordinary `:q` exits with two live chat sessions** (`louiselm-yk67`,
fixed in `5146007`).

With two sessions visible in `:LouiselmSwitchSession` and one chat window,
ordinary `:q` originally closed Neovim instead of leaving it open with the
actionable warning. The fix uses a temporary duplicate window because
Neovim's `QuitPre` event has no cancellation API. A regression test now
exercises the registered callback, and all four manual cases pass against
`5146007`.
close_reason: QA complete: all four manual cases passed against 5146007; finding louiselm-yk67 was fixed and closed.

title: Launch completion can kill the Agent before ACP relay
description:
Launch completion can kill the live Agent: the thread that spawned Bubblewrap exits while another thread still owns the Session. GitHub CI exposes this as an intermittent five-second ACP-echo timeout after seven corrective commits for louiselm-23pb. P1: the same lifetime defect is in production launch; it also blocks the skills-core job and skips later privileged gates.

## Observed

Latest: 2026-09-05, main 3783f2b6582857f686acaedefe45a30153786adb, Actions run 33980286095, job 101344184997, step `Test privileged launch supervisor composition`.
https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/33980286095/job/101344184997

Ubuntu 24.04.4, runner image 20260831.293.1, Rust 1.97.1. CI invokes the integration test binary under sudo with UID/GID 60000, the unprivileged operator UID, `LOUISELM_REQUIRE_INITIAL_HOST_IDENTITY=1`, and umask 077; see .github/workflows/ci.yml:332.

Verified log, 17:15:06Z (job log lines 895-907):

```text
thread 'privileged_supervisor_launches_agent_under_the_assigned_outer_identity' (9512) panicked at tests/launch_supervisor.rs:8038:9:
the real Agent never echoed the ACP bytes
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 79 filtered out; finished in 5.03s
Process completed with exit code 101.
```

Read the exact evidence with:
`gh run view 33980286095 --repo euri10/louiselm --job 101344184997 --log`

Verified recurrence on 2026-09-05:

- 04:53Z: run 33945707560, job 101251266491, commit 27d04551d4878191eb4a55c0678759daa9e7b232: identical assertion, 5.04s. https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/33945707560/job/101251266491
- 10:57Z: run 33961974373, job 101295303829, commit 2ebea3dbed7b6a9b02db85199bcb025fd596f362: identical assertion, 5.07s. https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/33961974373/job/101295303829
- 14:26Z: run 33971769629, job 101321427879, commit d59fd391e2f2c5f29a11a56c483a95dfd65e86ca: privileged test PASSED in 0.04s; all later privileged gates passed. https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/33971769629/job/101321427879
- 17:15Z: latest failure above. `git diff d59fd39 3783f2b -- skills-core .github/workflows/ci.yml` is empty. The Lua refactor did not change the failing crate or workflow. The earlier 27d0455 demo commit likewise did not touch skills-core.

## Symptoms

- Format, Lint, ordinary Test, initial-host-identity and root-cgroup containment steps pass; the privileged composition step exits 101.
- Measured Bubblewrap rejection and root-owned registry acceptance steps are skipped after this failure.
- This is a bounded ACP-echo timeout. The original louiselm-23pb failure was an unbounded terminal-receipt deadlock; a common underlying cause for every historical failure is not established.

## Root cause

Confirmed by a kernel-signal regression and the real privileged fixture. sandbox.rs:1271 enables Bubblewrap --die-with-parent, implemented with PR_SET_PDEATHSIG. Linux binds that signal to the creating thread, not to the lifetime of the entire parent process: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/PR_SET_PDEATHSIG.2const.html

At 3783f2b, launch_supervisor.rs:518-525 spawns Bubblewrap through run_launch and exits after complete(result), while lifecycle.rs:138 hands ongoing Session ownership to a separate worker. The creator's exit sends SIGKILL to Bubblewrap; a very fast echo/cleanup can race that death. Increasing the echo timeout cannot repair this ownership error.

Verified locally before the fix:

- Standalone Rust/Bubblewrap probe /tmp/louiselm-parent-thread.vpyVJJ/repro.rs: echo succeeds while its spawning thread lives; joining that thread produces `signal: 9 (SIGKILL)` while the parent process remains alive.
- New ordinary-suite test `launch_keeps_parent_death_bound_children_alive_until_lifecycle_cleanup` fails in 0.01s: `launch completion killed the still-owned child: Ok(ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(9)))`. It arms the same kernel signal on /bin/cat from the documented coordinator callback, without root or another dependency, and always settles cleanup/reaps the probe.
- An isolated root Docker container with the initial user namespace, a private cgroup namespace and read-only binary mounts passed 10 immediate executions of the original privileged fixture. A temporary 100ms delay before ACP input reproduced the exact echo timeout in 5.17s. With the fix, that delayed case passed 10/10. The diagnostic delay was removed; the ordinary kernel-signal test preserves the regression.

The old fixture also discarded stderr, asserted before terminal cleanup, and ignored relay_stdio's numeric exit status; death after a fast echo could therefore look green. The updated fixture emits at most 4KiB of stderr, stops waiting when relay has already completed, and settles terminal cleanup before checking that the exact echo arrived before EOF and the Agent exited with status zero.

## Prior attempts / why it was not caught

louiselm-23pb records seven test-fix commits on 2026-09-04, all still present:

- f583c5f: service terminal receipts concurrently.
- 28b222a: send EOF and settle natural exit.
- 3271eaf: allow the Agent to be the sandbox leader.
- db5eba0: inspect the pinned sandbox leader.
- f8fdc28: observe identity before releasing the startup gate.
- 8628055: copy stdin and stdout concurrently.
- b7b191c: raise the privileged echo/terminal waits from 2s to the configured 5s.

The issue was repeatedly closed on a green run and reopened after code-identical failures (comments 862, 866, 870, 872, 875). Its final claim of deterministic acceptance is contradicted by this recurrence. Ordinary `cargo test` returns early from this test when LOUISELM_TEST_HOST_ID is unset (7932-7934), so an ordinary green suite does not exercise the privileged path. GitLab green results alone also do not prove this GitHub-only acceptance.

## Fix direction

Keep the spawning coordinator alive after publishing launch completion until the lifecycle worker has cleaned its resources. A private channel's disconnect carries that lifetime boundary, including unwinding. Keep --die-with-parent enabled; removing it would weaken launcher-loss protection. Public callback and Session APIs remain unchanged. The regression proves both survival before cleanup and parent-death termination after cleanup.

## Acceptance

- Establish the nondeterministic condition with captured failure evidence and a regression that fails before the fix.
- The real privileged composition preserves exact ACP bytes, assigned outer UID/GID/no supplementary groups, receipt ordering, and terminal cleanup.
- Early failure reports its bounded cause and cleans up; no generic echo timeout hiding an already-failed relay.
- Repeated executions of the exact privileged fixture pass on the affected runner, and both later privileged gates execute successfully.

## Not covered

Implemented in 7ccb05a; final exit-status assertion in 427c0ba. Local Rust formatting, clippy and full tests pass, as do all 844 Lua tests, StyLua, LuaLS and generated API/config checks. The privileged fixture passed 50 consecutive local runs, plus 10 delayed-input runs and 10 runs with the final zero-exit assertion.

Hosted acceptance: run 33992224895 attempts 1/2 (jobs 101376370174/101376641653), PR run 33992371910 (job 101376756636), and final-code PR run 33992558954 (job 101377256122) all passed privileged composition and both later privileged gates. The full workflows are green. Final-code evidence: https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/33992558954/job/101377256122

Draft PR https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/pull/3 contains the fix and remains unmerged. No installed launcher authority or real configured Agent was changed. Demo q58u.6 is outside this defect.

title: ACP discovery leaves Agent reverse requests unanswered
description:
An ACP connection created without an `on_request` callback silently drops every inbound Agent request. The Session path now owns and rejects unsupported methods, but registry discovery uses a raw client with no handler, so a reverse request there remains pending.

## Observed

Code inspection on 2026-09-03:

- `lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:52-64` returns after looking up the optional callback, whether or not one exists.
- `lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua:636-644` opens discovery clients without `on_request`.

## Symptoms

An Agent request emitted while LouiseLM is discovering Sessions receives no JSON-RPC response and can remain pending until the discovery process closes.

## Root cause

The optional-handler branch has no default `-32601 Method not found` response.

## Why it was not caught

ACP client tests cover request delivery when a callback exists, but not an inbound request with the callback omitted.

## Fix direction

When no request callback is installed, schedule exactly one `-32601` response through the existing `Client:respond` path. Do not change notification handling.

## Acceptance

- A valid inbound request on a client without `on_request` receives one `-32601` response.
- Notifications still receive no response.
- Session-owned delayed permission responses remain unchanged.

## Not covered

Callbacks that accept ownership and then fail to respond remain the callback owners responsibility. Deferred because the reported louiselm-01qt hang occurs on the normal Session path, which is fixed there.
