title: Grill-me needed: what evidence should a LouiseLM bug report snapshot collect, preserve, and safely share
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing — it wants full attention.**

Raised as a side idea during the 2026-08-21 grill of `louiselm-parallel-worker-tracker-substrate-6mtc`. The user explicitly asked to preserve the idea without interrupting or replacing the foreground grill.

## The question

When LouiseLM is being used to debug LouiseLM, what explicit evidence/forensics manifest should guide an agent toward the recurring useful sources, and should a `:LouiseLmReportBug` command create a bounded local snapshot of those sources for diagnosis?

## Evidence from the session that raised it

The user has referenced one faulty LouiseLM session from another session while debugging the plugin. Given that reference, the model was already intelligent enough to navigate the available records and locate the relevant logs. The recurring retrieval pattern suggests product knowledge that should be made explicit and durable: enumerate the evidence sources an agent usually needs, retain provenance and relationships between sessions, and make collection reproducible instead of depending on a model rediscovering the filesystem layout each time.

This idea arose immediately after accepting coordinator-managed recovery of a known-dead worker, including a snapshot of that worker worktree and inspection of commits and uncommitted changes. Bug-report evidence may overlap with recovery evidence, but this issue must not pre-decide that they are the same artifact.

## Threads worth pulling

- Inventory the evidence that has actually proved useful in real failures before defining a bundle: referenced session records/transcripts and lifecycle state, ACP/process diagnostics, relevant LouiseLM logs, configuration facts, version/capability information, worktree/commit state, and a concise reproduction narrative. Treat this as a candidate list to validate, not an authorization to collect everything.
- Decide how session references are represented so a report can preserve the relationship between the diagnosing session and the faulty session without silently expanding collection to unrelated sessions.
- Separate an evidence manifest (knowledge of where and how to inspect sources) from a snapshot command (copying bytes). A manifest may be useful to an agent even when no bundle is created.
- Separate local snapshot from export/share. Local collection must not imply consent to upload, paste, publish, or attach anything. Any export path needs an explicit review/redaction step and a clear inventory of what will leave the machine.
- Make privacy and security first-class. Logs, prompts, transcripts, tool payloads, process environments, configuration, filesystem paths, credentials/tokens, and referenced sessions can contain sensitive data. Collection must be bounded, avoid credentials and full environments by default, preserve neither secrets nor unrelated session content merely for convenience, and fail closed when safe sanitization is uncertain.
- Establish retention, permissions, size/time bounds, destination ownership, and cleanup behavior for local snapshots. Avoid an unbounded recursive archive or a long-lived secret cache.
- Decide whether `:LouiseLmReportBug` is the right user interface, what it reports before collecting, and whether it should produce a human-readable inventory alongside machine-readable evidence. Do not assume the command name or archive format is settled.
- Preserve forensic integrity without claiming more than the implementation can prove: record timestamps/source paths and collection failures, do not mutate source evidence, and distinguish absent evidence from evidence deliberately omitted for privacy.
- Coordinate rather than duplicate `louiselm-ufx.2` (on-demand raw ACP payload inspection), `louiselm-06yh` (session/commit/beads linkage), and the worker recovery design in `louiselm-parallel-worker-tracker-substrate-6mtc`. Those are adjacent inputs, not owners of this support-snapshot boundary.

## Out of scope for this grill

Implementing the command, choosing the final evidence list from speculation, collecting current session data, exporting or sharing a bundle, or changing the live parallel-worker grill. React to the recorded requirement when this issue is deliberately opened.
close_reason: Grill completed with maintainer-confirmed shared understanding; implementation tracked by louiselm-ce6.24.

comments.text: Grill decision 4: evidence/forensics collection is read-only with respect to source evidence—the crime-scene rule. It must not move, rename, rewrite, truncate, delete, normalize, or clean up logs, transcripts, worktrees, or other sources. An explicitly created durable record stores bounded typed observations at collection time: subject/provenance identity, versions, cwd, Git commit/branch and dirty filenames, evidence paths, availability, size/timestamps where applicable, failures, and deliberate omissions. It contains no file contents or diffs. Naturally live or externally retained sources are labeled as mutable and observed-at, not falsely described as frozen or preserved.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Storage/view design candidate pending confirmation: correct the earlier assumption that collection automatically opens a human-readable view. Persist one canonical, versioned, typed JSON record per explicit collection under a private stdpath(state)/louiselm/forensics directory; do not persist rendered views or duplicate the evidence. The canonical structured record is the Agent-facing representation and includes explicit source kinds, paths, availability/mutability/sensitivity, observed facts, and retrieval guidance. A human-facing Neovim view is an optional projection of that same record, emphasizing subject/provenance, missing or sensitive evidence, and deliberate actions. Collection should return/announce the record identity/path; viewing is a separate concern. Existing lua/louiselm/workflow/evidence.lua stores routing-quality history and should remain semantically distinct rather than being reused.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 5: storage is one private, versioned, typed JSON record per explicit collection under stdpath(state)/louiselm/forensics. That canonical record is the Agent-facing representation, with stable evidence kinds, pointers, observed facts, availability, mutability, sensitivity, and retrieval guidance. Human presentation is an optional Neovim projection generated from the same record, emphasizing identity, chronology, missing/sensitive evidence, and deliberate actions. Collection returns the record identity/path and does not inherently open UI. Do not persist a second Markdown/rendered copy or reuse workflow.evidence routing-quality storage.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 6: collection is a headless/core operation taking Agent + ACP Session ID and returning a canonical record path or structured error; it does not depend on an open chat. A chat caller queues that path as an ACP resource_link for the diagnosing Session’s next prompt. An Ex-command caller outside chat reports the created path through normal Neovim command feedback, and a headless caller can print it to stdout. No prompt or analysis starts automatically. Diagnosing-Session provenance is absent when no diagnosing Session exists and may be established later when the record is attached. This preserves forensics when the chat UI itself is broken.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 7: each canonical forensics JSON record is immutable after successful creation. Re-collection creates a new timestamped observation rather than rewriting an earlier record. Records have no automatic TTL because explicit collection keeps their volume bounded and expiry would erase durable incident context; deletion is an explicit user action. Referenced source artifacts retain their own independent lifecycles and retention policies—the pointer record neither copies them nor extends their retention.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 8: collection is partial-success by design. Each expected evidence source records a typed state such as present, absent, inaccessible, unsupported, or deliberately omitted, including a bounded failure reason where useful. Missing evidence does not erase the rest of the record. The operation fails without a record only when the subject cannot be validly identified or the canonical record cannot be durably written. Discovery follows explicit Agent/Session metadata and known pointers; it must not scan broadly through the filesystem to guess missing evidence locations.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 9: the immutable forensics record contains collected observations and source pointers, not later interpretations. Reproduction narrative, hypotheses, diagnosis, remediation, and fix verification belong in a separate human/Agent-authored report or Beads work item that references the forensics record ID. This preserves the distinction between original observed evidence and conclusions drawn from it.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 10: durable configuration evidence uses a fixed typed allowlist rather than sanitizing or copying arbitrary configuration. Record Agent identity and reported name/version; known normalized capability flags; selected ACP option IDs with their current string/boolean values; cwd; Neovim/LouiseLM versions; and the agreed Git facts. Do not store raw capability payloads, option descriptions/catalogues, environments, prompts, tool payloads, full Agent definitions, or raw command arguments. Opaque primary evidence remains available for in-place inspection when diagnosis requires it.

comments.author: codex/01a02fdb-a153-7832-9330-6b3fefe34864
comments.text: Grill decision 11: confirmed v1 surface. Provide a headless forensics.collect(Agent, ACP Session ID) operation; :LouiselmForensics defaults to the current Session or accepts Agent + ACP Session ID; collection reports the canonical JSON path and, when invoked with an attached diagnosing chat, queues it as resource_link context for the next prompt; :LouiselmForensicsView <record> renders the optional human projection. No bug-report workflow, snapshot/archive, export/share, record browser, or deletion UI in v1. Private immutable files may be explicitly removed through ordinary filesystem operations.

title: Usage signatures retain attached short-option values
description: New usage CLI normalizer retains -pVALUE as a flag, exposing a sensitive operand in its metadata-only index. Found during initial implementation, before any real-history indexing or installation. Repro: cd usage-cli && cargo test attached_short_option. Failing assertion in src/command.rs: test input 'git status -pPRIVATE_CREDENTIAL --token=PRIVATE_CREDENTIAL' leaves PRIVATE_CREDENTIAL in the signature. Root cause: arbitrary alphanumeric short-flag strings were treated as flag names. Existing e2e privacy fixture covered positional values, not attached option values. Acceptance: regression and full Rust gates pass; signatures preserve only unambiguous flag names while exact equality remains a private digest. Lesson belongs here and in the regression, not a new standing rule.

comments.author: c177a087-d429-49d7-96f9-c5a6957bae85
comments.text: Investigation evidence (2026-08-22): the exact persisted ACP session exists at the adapter state path and was last updated at 2026-08-22T01:45:45Z. It selected deepseek-v4-pro and contains 137 persisted history entries (5 user, 62 assistant, 70 tool); no billing-error marker is persisted. LouiseLM only receives ACP JSON-RPC error.message and deliberately suppresses arbitrary error.data. The adapter maps ChatError/provider failures through into_internal_error, yielding the generic message "Internal error". Therefore LouiseLM has no safe evidence to label this as insufficient balance, and it does not calculate or debit account balances. A user-actionable billing error requires the ACP adapter to classify provider billing rejections into a stable, sanitized public error before sending ACP.

title: Firebase bootstrap would create the insecure default VPC
description:
The first apply of the dedicated Firebase project would automatically create Google's default network and permissive default firewall rules, despite the composition requiring no VPC.

## Observed

Observed 2026-09-04 with Trivy 0.72.0:

`trivy config infra/firebase` reports `GCP-0010 (HIGH): Project has automatic network creation enabled` at `infra/firebase/main.tf:15-26`.

## Symptoms

- The security-policy CI job fails.
- A successful bootstrap would create unused network resources with a broader attack surface.

## Root cause

`google_project.notifications` omits `auto_create_network = false`.

## Why it was not caught

Format and OpenTofu validation check provider schema and syntax, not this security posture; Trivy had not been made green before deployment preparation.

## Fix direction

Disable default-network creation on the project resource. Do not add a replacement VPC because Hosting and FCM do not require one.

## Acceptance

- `google_project.notifications` explicitly disables automatic network creation.
- Trivy no longer reports GCP-0010.
- OpenTofu format and validation pass without cloud mutation.

## Not covered

Audit-log policy is a separate finding.
close_reason: Default VPC creation disabled. gate:tf-trivy

comments.author: codex/01a06a99-3443-7843-b88d-52c47007cd42
comments.text: Red: Trivy GCP-0010 found automatic default-network creation. Green: auto_create_network=false; Trivy 0.72.0 reports zero findings and OpenTofu validation passes. Lesson is encoded at the project resource and existing security gate; no AGENTS.md rule or design question warranted.

title: QA round: recovery replay, cold Park and claim restoration
description:
# Manual QA — recovery acceptance

Working record for this round. A human drives Neovim; the assistant collects
objective evidence and updates this file. Archive results in a Beads QA-round
chore when the round ends, then remove this scratch file. Do not commit it.

## Build and scope

- Tested and installed plugin: `9b893f3`.
- Installed checkout: `/home/lotso/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim`.
  It was clean, advanced by fast-forward, and all three changed runtime files
  match the source checkout byte-for-byte.
- Restart confirmed: socket `/run/user/1000/nvim.2435291.0`, changed from the
  previous editor. Runtime resolves to the installed `9b893f3` checkout;
  coordinator `codex/01a0a3e7-1523-74d2-b85f-ce98fd86fe51` is loaded as
  `session-1`. All six required Session/recovery commands are registered.
- Baseline before restart: only coordinator `session-1` is live; the capture
  CLI reports no resumable Parks. Re-resolve local IDs after every restart.
- Automated checks: 1044 Lua cases passed, including 180 Chat cases; StyLua,
  LuaLS, API/config-type/plugin-version/Vimdoc checks passed. Documentation-only
  follow-up passed all 13 Vimdoc/generator cases and regenerated help.
  Full-suite log: `/tmp/louiselm-recovery-tests.AJeqUC`.
- Operator permission settings remain unchanged. These cases require actual
  tool/replay behavior, not an approval dialog.

## Status

| Case | State | Evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0. Restart into installed build | Passed | User reports resumed; new socket, installed 9b893f3, matching runtime files, coordinator source=loaded |
| 1. Ordinary replay has one row per tool | Passed | User confirms replay, details and focus; real paired completed notifications at 07:33:31.231Z render once per ID in session-3/buffer72, rows21–23; one marker |
| 2. Loaded history Parks without a new prompt | Passed | User reports Park notification; session-3 still loaded/ready/current_turn=0, owner Run parked; durable ab132e7c-f642-4f67-9ec5-1781e3a1efd1 cold_parked/revision3 |
| 3. Cold resume restores history and Run accounting | Passed for empty claims | New editor2446803; exact Run active/revision5; reconstructed ceiling1/consumed0/reserved0 and claims[]; three titled rows once and one marker; user confirms |
| 4. Rejected cold load leaves no hidden Session | Passed | Actual active-writer rejection at07:43:09.703Z; complete Registry retains exactly session-1/2/3 and chat buffers11/39/49; no hidden error Session |
| 5. Nonempty claims round-trip | Passed; fixture cleanup verified | New editor2464255; same Run active/revision5; loaded/ready/current_turn0 owner claims=[louiselm-e80te], budget1/0/0; Beads assignee unchanged; durable pending/outputs empty; fixture subsequently closed by its owner |

Run one checkpoint at a time. Do not infer a pass from a notification alone.

Pinned case-1 fixture (2026-09-15):

- ACP Session: `01a0a3fa-350a-71c1-a496-668777837c8a`; configured Agent `codex`.
- Original tools: `exec-6e49507a-f127-4337-a69b-a2a516e2c83f` (`pwd`),
  `exec-8c7ea12c-b59f-47f0-a8a7-832a53c10351` (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`),
  `exec-ef73a7c3-41bc-48c3-8124-56dc2063575f` (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`).
- All three have observed in-progress starts and completed updates. Prompt
  request 4 finished with `end_turn` at 07:31:55.792Z. Final live state is
  ready/new/current_turn=1. Original buffer47 has tool rows26–28 exactly once
  each and one exact `RECOVERY-QA-READY` line.
- Proxy log: `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a0a3fa-350a-71c1-a496-668777837c8a/log.jsonl`.
  Validated envelope fields: `payload.params.update.sessionUpdate`,
  `toolCallId`, `status`, `title`; completion is `payload.result.stopReason`.
  First inventory happened while the final reply was still streaming; a second
  inventory confirmed ready before authorizing the close/reload checkpoint.
- Ordinary load request2 at 07:33:30.988Z completed at 07:33:31.232Z. Each
  original tool ID replayed as completed tool_call with title, immediately
  followed by completed tool_call_update without title at 07:33:31.231Z.
  Live inspection found exactly three titled rows21–23 in buffer72, one per
  original ID, and one marker. User confirmed tool details and focus return.
  The reloaded Session is local session-3, ready/loaded/current_turn=0, with
  loadSession support and no owner Run. No new QA prompt was sent.
- Case 2 saved Run `ab132e7c-f642-4f67-9ec5-1781e3a1efd1`, tied to that same
  ACP Session: durable state cold_parked, revision3, park_expires_at_ms
  `1789544118965`. The resumable summary has claims=[] and generated_work
  `{ceiling=1, consumed=0, reserved=0, pending=[], outputs=[]}`. Local owner Run
  has the same ID/status=parked/claims=[], while the Session remains
  ready/loaded/current_turn=0. Local pre-resume owner has no generated_work
  field; compare reconstruction against the authoritative durable budget.
  Record path: `/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm/workflow/runs/ab132e7c-f642-4f67-9ec5-1781e3a1efd1.json`.
  Validated summary expiry field is `park_expires_at_ms`, not `expires_at_ms`.
- Case 3 passed after a second editor restart: socket
  `/run/user/1000/nvim.2446803.0`. Cold load request2 at07:37:49.891Z completed
  at07:37:50.120Z. The real peer again emitted paired terminal updates for each
  of the three original tool IDs; buffer39 rows21–23 contain one titled row
  each and one marker. QA local session-2 is loaded/ready/current_turn=0.
  Its reconstructed owner retains the exact Run ID, status=active, claims=[],
  generated_work ceiling1/consumed0/reserved0. Durable Run is active/revision5,
  park expiry0, resume_attempt.result=active, with pending[] and outputs[].
  The user confirms the recovery worked. Nonempty claims remain case 5.

## 1. Ordinary replay

Exercises `louiselm-r141`, `ui/chat/buffer.lua`, and ordinary Session load.

1. After restart, create a fresh configured `codex` Session with
   `:LouiselmSessionNew`. Keep the coordinator separate.
2. Send this exact prompt:

   > Run exactly three separate exec_command tool calls with working directory
   > /home/lotso/code/louiselm: first pwd, then git rev-parse --show-toplevel,
   > then git rev-parse --short HEAD. Do not combine them. Do not change files
   > or Beads. Afterward reply RECOVERY-QA-READY.

3. Wait for completion, leave the QA Session open, switch back to the coordinator
   with `:LouiselmSessionSwitch`, and report ready. The assistant identifies the
   new Session against the one-Session baseline and pins its ACP/tool IDs. If
   several Sessions were created, use `:LouiselmSessionId` to disambiguate.
   Additional startup tools are a recipe difference to account for, not
   automatically a product failure. Wait for the evidence checkpoint before
   continuing to step 4.
4. Close only this idle QA Session with `:LouiselmSessionClose`, then resume
   that exact conversation with `:LouiselmResume`.
5. Send no prompt after loading. Check each recorded tool has one completed
   row, retains its title, and opens the correct details through the normal
   tool inspector. Close the inspector with `q` and confirm focus returns.

Failure signature: a titled completed row followed by another completed row
containing only the same tool ID; missing details; wrong inspector target.

Evidence: match stable IDs in the pinned Session's replay frames to buffer rows.
The assistant inspects only selected tool metadata, not whole logs. UI focus
and readability need the human report. Preserve this loaded Session for case 2.

## 2. Park loaded history without another prompt

Exercises `louiselm-s6xr`, `workflow/run.lua`.

1. Before any new prompt, let the assistant verify the QA Session is
   `source=loaded`, `status=ready`, `current_turn=0`, and supports `loadSession`.
2. Leave the input empty. Run `:LouiselmPark` in that QA Session.
3. Report the notification and leave the editor running for the evidence check.

Expect: Park succeeds without sending a marker prompt. One corresponding
durable Run appears, and its ACP Session identity matches the subject.

Failure signature: “cold Park requires a Session that has sent at least one
prompt”, an unexpected staged-context confirmation, or no durable Run after
the success notification.

Evidence: pin the Run ID from `louiselm-capture run list`; record its claims,
generated_work and expiry. Read no capability/token fields. An empty claims
array is valid but does not establish the nonempty-claim case.

## 3. Cold resume after editor exit

Exercises `louiselm-klm2` remaining recovery acceptance and `louiselm-r141`'s
cold replay path, including `workflow/recovery.lua`.

1. The pinned Run is `ab132e7c-f642-4f67-9ec5-1781e3a1efd1`. Wait until the coordinator is idle and exit
   Neovim normally. Do not dispose the parked QA Session first.
2. Reopen Neovim and resume this coordinator using `:LouiselmResume`.
3. Use `:LouiselmResumePark` and select the pinned QA Run. Do not ordinary-load
   its Session first; that would establish a competing active writer.
4. Wait for replay and the cold-resume result. Check the earlier marker and
   tools appear once. Report before sending a new prompt.

Expect: the Run becomes active, history remains readable, and the reconstructed
Session owner retains the same claims and generated-work accounting. Resume is
recoverable and lossy: staged context was never part of this promise.

Failure signature: resume hangs/errors, empty history, duplicate tool rows,
missing Run owner, a changed Run ID, or reset claims/budget.

Evidence: compare the pinned pre-Park summary to `session.owner_run` and the
durable Run's safe projection. ACP load completion alone does not establish
budget restoration or correct rendering.

## 4. Failed-load cleanup

Exercises existing `louiselm-rqqp` fix in `29f9fb1`, preserved by this batch.

Pinned negative fixture: configured codex ACP Session
`01a0a402-a05c-75d3-9ef5-c0b1866d7666`, local session-3. Its one prompt ended
with end_turn at07:40:36.555Z and its buffer contains one FAILURE-QA-READY marker.
It remains ready/new/current_turn=1, with an attached owner Run
`6cd3acf4-2756-4806-9538-aa6041c71eaa` locally parked and durably
cold_parked/revision3. Expiry1789544450135; budget1/0/0, pending/outputs empty,
summary claims[]. This is the only resumable Park in the CLI list.

Complete pre-attempt Registry on socket nvim.2446803.0:

- session-1: coordinator ACP01a0a3e7-1523-74d2-b85f-ce98fd86fe51.
- session-2: positive fixture ACP01a0a3fa-350a-71c1-a496-668777837c8a,
  ready/loaded, Runab132e7c-f642-4f67-9ec5-1781e3a1efd1 active.
- session-3: negative fixture above, ready/new with parked owner.

Evidence log for this case:
`/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a0a402-a05c-75d3-9ef5-c0b1866d7666/log.jsonl`.
Keep the original Session attached and the editor running for the rejection.

Result: user reported Park notice, one load error, then Park notice. Exact
load request2 at07:43:09.537Z failed at07:43:09.703Z with protocol details
`thread 01a0a402-a05c-75d3-9ef5-c0b1866d7666 already has an active writer`.
The failed adapter exited at07:43:09.721Z. Full Registry still has exactly
session-1/2/3 with their original ACP IDs and buffers11/39/49. Negative
source remains ready/new/current_turn1. Run returned cold_parked/revision5,
budget1/0/0 unchanged; failed-resume expiry is1789458488868 (five-minute
resume lease). No duplicate Session or load attempt was observed.

The repeated Park notices are consistent with initial revision3 observation
and the return-to-Park revision5 after failed resume. ParkObserver presents
each newer parked/cold_parked revision; these notices do not establish two
resume attempts. No separate product finding from those notices.

Create a separate fresh configured codex Session, send `Reply only FAILURE-QA-READY`,
and wait for completion so the peer has persisted history. Park only that
Session with `:LouiselmPark`, leave it open, and report parked. The assistant
pins its ACP and Run IDs and the complete Registry before attempting resume. This is
an explicit negative case: while its original writer remains live, attempt
`:LouiselmResumePark` for that exact disposable Run. The September 8 Codex peer
rejected this with “already has an active writer”. The assistant must confirm
the current peer produces that rejection before judging cleanup.

Expect: one error, original Session/history retained, no additional unattached
error Session remaining in the complete Registry. If the peer now permits the
load, stop and revise this recipe; that is not proof of cleanup on failure.

Evidence: complete Registry inventory before/after plus the exact failed load
response. `exit_verdict()` alone omits error Sessions and cannot prove cleanup.
Do not use the coordinator as the negative-case subject or delete peer history.

## 5. Nonempty claims and budget

Finish `louiselm-klm2`'s original acceptance with a fresh fixture. Before the
case, create one dedicated QA chore and have the QA Session resolve its own
identity and claim it normally. Record the fixture ID here before mutation.
Never borrow another task or another Agent's claim. Repeat Park, editor exit,
and cold resume, then compare the exact claim and all generated-work counters.
Release the dedicated QA claim using its attributable Session at cleanup.

Dedicated claim fixture created: `louiselm-e80te`, priority4 chore, qa-fixture,
external reference `codex/01a0a3e7-1523-74d2-b85f-ce98fd86fe51#qa-claim`.
It is open and unassigned at creation. No implementation or unrelated tracker
work belongs to it. Create a fresh codex Session and send:

> Follow AGENTS.md and docs/agent-workflow.md. Resolve your own CODEX_SESSION_ID
> with session.identity(). Claim only louiselm-e80te using br update --claim
> with that resolved actor. This is a QA fixture: do not edit files, implement
> anything, or close the issue. Reply CLAIM-QA-READY with the issue ID and actor.

After completion, report ready to the coordinator. Pin the new Session and
verify its claim before instructing Park. Do not use the negative-case Session.

Claim checkpoint passed: `louiselm-e80te` is in_progress, assignee
`codex/01a0a408-1ab3-7591-803d-07edec2c3c68`, updated07:46:56.445Z.
The exact Session resolves to that identity through session.identity(), local
session-5, source=new/current_turn=1, supports loadSession. Its prompt request4
ended at07:46:59.702Z; follow-up live inspection confirmed ready. No owner Run
exists yet. Park this Session, then capture the exact Run/claim/budget before
restarting. Its proxy log is
`/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a0a408-1ab3-7591-803d-07edec2c3c68/log.jsonl`.

Park checkpoint passed: saved Run `3dce5a40-25be-4bc8-9dcf-095391a17937`
is cold_parked and its resumable summary contains exactly `[louiselm-e80te]`.
Authoritative budget is ceiling1/consumed0/reserved0, pending[]/outputs[];
park expiry1789544875731. Beads still assigns the in_progress fixture to the
exact QA actor above. Local session-5 is ready/new/current_turn1 and owns
the same parked Run. Its pre-resume local owner claims remains[] and has no
generated_work field; verify reconstruction against the saved summary, not
that local pre-resume object. Durable record:
`/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm/workflow/runs/3dce5a40-25be-4bc8-9dcf-095391a17937.json`.

Cold-resume checkpoint passed: user reports resumed on new editor socket
`/run/user/1000/nvim.2464255.0`. Complete Registry contains only the coordinator
and QA local session-2, ACP `01a0a408-1ab3-7591-803d-07edec2c3c68`.
QA is loaded/ready/current_turn0: no post-resume prompt. Its reconstructed owner
is the same Run, active, claims exactly `[louiselm-e80te]`, generated_work
ceiling1/consumed0/reserved0. Durable record is active/revision5, park expiry0,
resume_attempt.result=active, pending[]/outputs[]. Beads retains the exact
in_progress fixture assignee. The resumable-Park list no longer contains this
active Run, as expected. This proves one nonempty claim and the recorded zero-use
budget survive editor exit and cold resume; it does not test a consumed budget.

Next: in the restored QA Session, ask its Agent to resolve its own identity
again and close only `louiselm-e80te` with that actor and reason
`live:codex/01a0a3e7-1523-74d2-b85f-ce98fd86fe51 recovery claim round-trip verified; disposable fixture complete`.
No implementation or unrelated edits. After the cleanup reply, close only
that QA Session through `:LouiselmSessionClose`, then report done here.
Cleanup verified after the user reported done: `louiselm-e80te` is closed with
the specified live verdict, and the complete Registry contains only coordinator
session-1. No QA Session remains attached. Durable records are retained:
positive Runs ab132e7c and 3dce5a40 remain active/revision5; negative Run6cd3acf4
is disposed/revision6. Session closure is not claimed to have deleted or
terminalized these durable records. No claim remains live on the closed fixture.

## Evidence access

Validated against the known-good coordinator before restart: find its exact ACP
ID through `require('louiselm.session').exit_verdict()`, then use
`verdict.session.owner:list_sessions()` and `owner:get_session(id):inspect()`
to enumerate the complete Registry. Project only local ID, ACP ID, source,
status, and current_turn. This includes error Sessions, unlike exit_verdict.
For the QA subject, also project owner_run.id, claims and generated_work.

The following read-only CLI check was validated against the empty baseline:

```sh
louiselm-capture run list | jq 'map({id,state,agent,acp_session_id,claims,generated_work})'
```

Pin actual Run/ACP IDs after fixture creation; never select “most recent”.
Validate event-check field names against the first observed positive replay
before using them to declare a failure. After restart, do not reuse old local
Session, buffer or window IDs.

## Findings and remaining order

- F1 `louiselm-s6xr`: fixed in `9b893f3`; full load/Park/editor-exit/cold-resume
  chain passed live with no intervening prompt. Closed with live evidence.

title: Show commit Provenance in a louiselm://provenance/commit buffer
description:
## Goal

Standing on a commit SHA, open `louiselm://provenance/commit/<sha>` and see the
issues it served and the Session that produced it, with a resolved transcript
path.

## Scope

- In scope: `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua`; a read-only buffer; cursor
  detection extended from issue ids to commit SHAs; wiring
  sources -> correlate -> locator into one answer.
- Out of scope: issue and Session views, bvr correlation, time travel.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `louiselm://provenance/commit/<sha>` renders the commit subject, the issue
   ids from its trailers, the Session id, and the resolved transcript path.
2. An unresolved Session renders as explicitly unresolved. Omitting the row is
   forbidden: a coverage gap that renders as absence of history is the failure
   this epic exists to prevent.
3. The buffer is read-only and mutates nothing in git, Beads or transcripts.
4. Presentation lives only in the UI module. Core modules return structured
   data and typed events.

## Testing

- Headless behavioural smoke test in the style of `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`, not
  pixel assertions.
- Queued work arriving after disposal does not revive closed state, and editor
  operations occur only after the required scheduling boundary.
- A commit with no trailer, and a trailer whose Session has no transcript, both
  render as legible partial answers.

## Notes

Model the module on the existing `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua`, whose cursor-id
detection, shell-out and read-only rendering are the same shape. Prefer
extending its patterns over inventing new ones.

This is the first user-visible slice of the epic: thin, but end to end through
every layer.
close_reason: Implemented read-only commit Provenance UI, command, tests, and generated documentation

Missing trailers and missing transcript roots remain explicit partial answers; late callbacks are ignored when the requesting view is inactive. Added headless behavior coverage and generated vimdoc. Lesson destination: this issue comment; no AGENTS.md rule or new design question is warranted.

title: CI: doc/api.md is stale, missing the thought_chunk EventType variant
description:
CI's required "lua-language-server" job fails at the "Verify generated API appendix" step because `doc/api.md` is out of date with the source it's generated from.

## Observed

GitHub Actions runs 32929697287 (commit 849f5dc) and 32932395090 (commit fd1d606), repo euri10/louiselm, job "lua-language-server", step "Verify generated API appendix":

```
doc/api.md is stale; run ./scripts/generate-api-appendix
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Reproduced locally on the same commit:

```
$ ./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check
doc/api.md is stale; run ./scripts/generate-api-appendix
```

Running it without `--check` regenerates `doc/api.md` with this diff:

```diff
 louiselm.session.EventType:
     | "chunk"
     | "user_chunk"
+    | "thought_chunk"
     | "tool_call_started"
     | "tool_call_finished"
     | "permission_requested"
@@ -390,9 +391,9 @@ louiselm.session.EventType:

 ### louiselm.session.GenericEvent

-- `data: unknown` -- Event-specific payload. For "chunk"/"user_chunk" this is the raw ACP
+- `data: unknown` -- Event-specific payload. For "chunk"/"user_chunk"/"thought_chunk" this is
 - `session_id: string` -- Local session identifier.
-- `type: "chunk"|"error"|"tool_call_finished"|"tool_call_started"|"turn_done"...(+1)`
+- `type: "chunk"|"error"|"thought_chunk"|"tool_call_finished"|"tool_call_started"...(+2)`
```

## Symptoms

- CI reports the required "lua-language-server" job red on every push, independent of what the push actually changed.
- Exact error text: "doc/api.md is stale; run ./scripts/generate-api-appendix".

## Root cause

`louiselm.session.EventType` gained a `"thought_chunk"` variant as part of the reasoning-fold feature (commit `c56805f`), but `doc/api.md` was never regenerated to match — `./scripts/generate-api-appendix` (which the "lua-language-server" CI job runs with `--check`) diffs the committed file against a freshly generated one and fails when they differ. The regeneration command was not run before that commit (or a later one) was pushed.

## Why it was not caught

AGENTS.md section 4 lists `stylua --check .`, `lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning`, and the `mini.test` run as the direct local quality gates; it does not call out `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check` as one of them, even though CI enforces it. Nothing in the documented pre-commit checklist would have caught this locally.

## Fix direction

Run `./scripts/generate-api-appendix` and commit the resulting `doc/api.md`. Separately, consider adding `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check` (and `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check`, see the related nightly-Vimdoc bug) to the documented local gates in AGENTS.md section 4, since both are already enforced in CI but currently only discoverable by reading `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Acceptance

- `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check` exits 0 on the fix commit.
- CI's "lua-language-server" job goes green on the next push.

## Not covered

- The `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua` CI failure and the nightly-only Vimdoc-staleness failure on the same CI runs are separate bugs with distinct root causes; filed separately.
- Whether other generated-doc drift exists elsewhere in the repo was not audited.
close_reason: fixed in 1395bfd. Regenerated doc/api.md via ./scripts/generate-api-appendix; --check now exits 0. Verified generate-vimdoc --check, stylua --check, and full mini.test suite unaffected (all green).

title: Codex reasoning chunks duplicate headers and fragment chat prose
description:
Codex reasoning updates corrupt the live chat after a tool call: the view renders one `[thinking]` header for each consecutive reasoning chunk instead of one collapsed reasoning paragraph, and the following assistant response is fragmented into one word/fragment per line with blank lines. This makes a normal Codex answer difficult to read. Reproduced in the currently attached Codex Session.

## Observed

Seen on 2026-08-26 in the live Neovim instance, Session `codex/01a03c4e-e214-7181-b31d-c59884d32810` (local view `session-3`, buffer 306), after its completed tool call and while the Session was `ready` at turn 1.

Live buffer evidence, lines 185-188, contains four consecutive `[thinking]` headers. Lines 190 onward contain the answer with every visible word/fragment separated by blank lines. The live state reports `thought_folds=1`, four visible headers, and six transcript blocks (`user`, `reasoning`, `assistant`, `tool_call`, `reasoning`, `assistant`), so the displayed structure is inconsistent with the recorded reasoning paragraphs.

Raw ACP evidence is retained at `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a03c4e-e214-7181-b31d-c59884d32810/log.jsonl` (156455 bytes, modified `2026-08-26 06:25:53.823794861 +0200`). Lines 60-63 are four adjacent `agent_to_client` `session/update` frames with `sessionUpdate="agent_thought_chunk"` and text lengths 2, 45, 2, and 50; they are followed by `agent_message_chunk` frames at lines 64-70. The log has six thought frames total (lines 15, 16, 60-63). No reasoning text is copied here because it may be sensitive; the local log is the primary artifact.

## Symptoms

- A Codex user sees four `[thinking]` labels rather than one collapsed reasoning section for contiguous thought updates.
- The assistant answer that follows is visually split into isolated words/fragments with blank lines, rather than streaming as readable prose.
- The Session's transcript structure says there is one second reasoning block, while the visible buffer presents four headers.

## Root cause

Unknown. `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:219-222` correctly maps ACP `agent_thought_chunk` to the typed `thought_chunk` event. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2232-2272` is responsible for maintaining `view.thought_run`, rendering its one header, and appending subsequent chunks. The observed four headers mean that run state is being closed or lost between adjacent Codex frames, or that the live loaded renderer differs from this checked-out path. The adjacent frame ordering above distinguishes this from an Agent emitting four separate reasoning paragraphs. The simultaneous fragmentation of later message chunks may share the same rendering/state-boundary failure, but that is unverified.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:674-719` directly emits two adjacent `thought_chunk` events through a synchronous fake session and asserts one header. It does not replay the captured Codex post-tool multi-frame sequence (four adjacent thought chunks followed by streamed message chunks) through the production ACP callback/scheduling boundary, nor assert that the rendered post-reasoning prose remains contiguous.

## Fix direction

Reproduce with a sanitized fixture preserving the observed event order from log lines 60-70. Trace the live event-to-render boundary to establish why `view.thought_run` does not persist. Fix the narrow shared rendering boundary so contiguous `thought_chunk` events produce exactly one header/fold and following `chunk` events append readable prose. Do not normalize or persist raw reasoning just to work around the presentation bug.

## Acceptance

- A regression test based on the observed Codex frame order fails before the fix and passes after it.
- Four contiguous `agent_thought_chunk` updates after a completed tool call render exactly one `[thinking]` header and one collapsed fold.
- The following streamed `agent_message_chunk` updates render as contiguous prose with no inserted blank line between ordinary word/fragments.
- The live Codex Session reproducer displays one collapsed reasoning section and a readable assistant answer.

## Not covered

- The exact mechanism that clears `view.thought_run` is not yet proven.
- Other Agents and Codex versions were not tested.
- Raw reasoning content remains only in the local ACP log and is intentionally not duplicated into this bead.
close_reason: Does not reproduce at HEAD; pinned with a characterization test in e538552 rather than repaired

description: The service supplying Model access whose quota or billing applies, recorded independently of the configured Agent and advertised Model.

title: Paste-only input bypasses Attention inactivity detection
description:
Direct Neovim paste API calls bypass the typed-input listener used by the Attention fix in louiselm-vi0kj. Paste-only activity can therefore allow an already-pending alert at the earlier idle deadline. This causes a premature alert, not missing notifications or data loss.

## Observed

2026-09-17, Neovim 0.12.5, codex/01a0ad4d-1be9-7c22-84a3-d5dd1320da1f. An isolated headless editor registered vim.on_key (counting nonempty typed strings) and TextChanged/TextChangedI counters, then called nvim_paste("fixture", true, -1) from vim.schedule. After returning to the normal editor event loop, the result was {changes=1, keys=0}. The unmodified observer sees the edit; the new keyboard observer does not.

## Root cause

Neovim's default vim.paste uses nvim_put for normal/insert pastes, bypassing key callbacks. Keyboard-driven paste commands and command-line pastes can still emit keys; the finding concerns direct nvim_paste input. Physical terminal/GUI clipboard behavior has not been reproduced.

## Fix direction and scope

Find a paste-input signal that distinguishes user pastes from Agent rendering. Neovim's documented vim.paste hook replaces a global function, conflicting with this project's no-global-monkey-patching contract; do not silently wrap it. Reintroducing unfiltered TextChanged/CursorMoved would restore the missed-alert defect. Keep the decision local to the input observation boundary.

Deferred from louiselm-vi0kj: the main defect is Agent output suppressing notifications. Ordinary keyboard/mouse input and focus changes restart the idle delay; paste-only input remains a known limitation. No generated text, keys or pasted content should be logged or retained to diagnose it.

## Acceptance

- An isolated controller has an unseen ready turn at t=0; direct nvim_paste at t=10s postpones eligibility from t=30s to t=40s.
- Streaming Agent output alone still leaves eligibility at t=30s.
- Preserve listener cleanup and the project's no-global-monkey-patching rule, or explicitly resolve that policy before adopting the paste hook.

title: Winbar clicks never work via real mouse click: v:lua.require(...) is not a valid click-function name
description:
## Symptom

No winbar click has ever worked through an actual mouse click in Neovim -
not the session-switch tabs, not the Limits click segment. Clicking produces
no error, no session switch, nothing. Discovered while manually QA'ing the
`437fbf0` cross-window click-routing fix (case 6) - that fix is itself
correct, but sits downstream of a click mechanism that was never wired up
correctly in the first place, so there was never a live click to route.

## Evidence

Isolated with two throwaway winbar click regions, independent of any
louiselm code, to bisect which part of the click wiring is at fault:

1. `vim.wo.winbar = "%0@v:lua.qa_click_test_handler@[CLICK ME]%X"` (a plain
   global function reference) - click worked, handler fired.
2. `vim.wo.winbar = "%0@v:lua.require('qa_click_mod').handler@[CLICK ME 2]%X"`
   (the exact same shape as this codebase's actual click target string) -
   click did nothing at all.

Confirms Vim's `%{N}@{Function}@` winbar/statusline click syntax requires
`{Function}` to be a plain dotted name it can resolve at click-dispatch
time, not an arbitrary Lua call expression like `require('mod')` embedded in
that field.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:306`:

```lua
local WINBAR_CLICK_HANDLER = "v:lua.require('louiselm.ui.chat.command').winbar_click"
```

This constant has existed since `7b31438` "feat(ui): show Session attention
in winbar" - the winbar-click feature has apparently never worked via a real
mouse click since it was introduced, only in unit tests that call
`M.winbar_click(...)` directly (bypassing Vim's actual click dispatch, so
the broken click-target string was never exercised).

## Fix

Expose a stable global Lua function (not a call expression) as the click
target, forwarding to the reassignable `M.winbar_click`:

```lua
-- command.lua
_G.__louiselm_winbar_click = function(...)
  return M.winbar_click(...)
end
```

```lua
-- init.lua
local WINBAR_CLICK_HANDLER = "v:lua.__louiselm_winbar_click"
```

title: Open current Session overview in a left sidebar with <leader>sO
description:
## Goal
Make Session Overview useful beside the current conversation: <leader>sO opens a left sidebar, similar in placement and feel to the Snacks explorer, containing the existing overview information for that Session only.

## Context
Maintainer likes the information in :LouiselmSessionOverview but finds the current UX poor. It opens side-by-side windows for all present Sessions (doc/louiselm.txt; lua/louiselm/ui/session_overview.lua). Requested change is presentation and Session scope.

## Scope
Replace the all-Session overview presentation with the current-Session sidebar and expose <leader>sO as Session Overview through the appropriate existing keymap mechanism. Make :LouiselmSessionOverview open the same view. Snacks explorer is the UX reference; no new runtime dependency is authorized.

## Acceptance criteria
1. From a Session chat, <leader>sO opens one sidebar on the left of the current tab, with the conversation still visible. It does not create an overview tab or one column per Session.
2. The sidebar clearly identifies the originating Session and shows its existing overview information: identity/status, working directory, modified files, edition line ranges, and change totals. Existing relevant conflict indications and file/line navigation remain usable.
3. With multiple Sessions present, only the Session from which overview was invoked supplies the displayed summary and file history. Invoking from another Session shows that Session; focusing the sidebar does not lose its subject.
4. Opening repeatedly reuses the sidebar. It has an obvious close action, supports normal window navigation, and leaves chat windows usable when closed.
5. Existing live refresh and manual refresh behavior works for the displayed Session; refresh does not inflate totals. A Session with no edits has a clear empty state. Missing/disposed Sessions are handled explicitly without showing another Session accidentally.
6. Closing/reopening and chat disposal leave no stale windows, buffers, or listeners.
7. Document the shortcut and new command behavior; update public LuaCATS and regenerate affected documentation from source as required.

## Testing and acceptance
Use behavioral headless UI coverage for left-sidebar placement, retained chat, invocation/Session selection with two Sessions, empty state, refresh, navigation, repeated opening and cleanup. Preserve real ACP edit-history regressions from louiselm-anuvy and louiselm-u5q2l; their lesson is that synthetic edits alone miss real multi-file diff events and status-only completion ordering.
Run focused checks and the complete affected suite per docs/agent-testing.md. Verify <leader>sO in the maintainer's effective keymap configuration and manually check the sidebar with two Sessions containing different edits. Ask the maintainer to confirm the requested UX before closure.

## Boundaries
This issue records the requested work only. No implementation or claim requested. Do not redesign Session history collection or introduce a file-tree feature.

title: Copilot Autopilot shows Your turn while continuing to execute
description:
Copilot Autopilot continues executing while LouiseLM shows Your turn. A completed ACP prompt is being treated as proof that the Session is idle, although Copilot can start another internally prompted interaction. Do not redefine every turn to mean whole-task completion.

## Original live evidence

2026-09-14, Session copilot/bfa01bbb-671a-4843-ad6a-a089bf256923, Neovim socket /run/user/1000/nvim.1575409.0. Live inspect: id=session-8, status=ready, activity=tool, current_turn=1, turn_done_turn=1, recording_turn.finished=true, exit_verdict.turn_active=false. Effective options: Mode=Autopilot, Model=Gemini 3.8 Flash, Reasoning Effort=high, Allow All=On. Native session.start confirms Copilot CLI 1.0.83. The original Session was no longer in the live registry during the follow-up investigation; it was not resumed or modified.

ACP log: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/bfa01bbb-671a-4843-ad6a-a089bf256923/log.jsonl. Only structural fields quoted; prompts/tool payloads remain local.

- Line 21, 15:48:39.454Z: client session/prompt id=10.
- Line 141, 15:50:23.489Z: response id=10, stopReason=end_turn.
- Line 145, 15:50:26.004Z: agent_thought_chunk.
- Lines 149/151, 15:50:29.985Z onward: new pending/completed tool.
- Lines 1478/1479, 16:09:43.289Z: final pending/completed task_complete.

Native log: /home/lotso/.copilot/session-state/bfa01bbb-671a-4843-ad6a-a089bf256923/events.jsonl.

- Line 144, 15:50:23.472Z: assistant.turn_end.
- Line 146, 15:50:23.508Z: system user.message, delivery=idle, agentMode=autopilot, isAutopilotContinuation=true, new interactionId; 19 ms after the ACP response.
- Line 581, 16:09:43.290Z: root session.task_complete, success=true.

Connection log: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/connections/17b1e699-94c8-4b0d-a183-21200c75dc20.jsonl identifies node /home/lotso/code/copilot-acp/src/index.js. Initialize did not subscribe to Copilot native events.

## Root boundary and corrected diagnosis

The local wrapper starts copilot --acp --stdio and forwards prompt responses/updates unchanged. lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:294 complete_turn sets ready and emits turn_done; handle_notification at :390 accepts later output without tracking independent agent liveness. ui/chat/status.lua:189 renders ready as Your turn. Session:cancel also rejects ready; registry exit protection uses this same status. This is not stale rendering.

The installed Copilot ACP handler awaits session.send({wait:true}) and returns end_turn. Its native Autopilot loop may then enqueue a continuation. Calling this necessarily a premature end_turn was too strong: the first interaction has completed. Copilot-native assistant.turn_start/end pairs are model iterations, not ACP prompt turns.

## Verified unmodified-runtime probes

Diagnostic script: /tmp/louiselm-copilot-events.u7L7cI/probe.mjs (temporary convenience, not the only evidence). Uses unchanged installed CLI 1.0.83, independent COPILOT_HOME, synthetic prompts, an in-process loopback OpenAI-compatible provider, and only task_complete exposed. No real model calls, installed-package edits, maintainer config changes, or live-user cancellation. ACP session/new defaults to Agent; the disposable session is explicitly switched to Autopilot through session/set_config_option.

Initialize subscription: clientCapabilities._meta["github.com/copilot"].events is an array of native event names. Notifications arrive as method github.com/copilot/sessionEvent, params={sessionId,type,timestamp,data,agentId?}. Thus no binary/package patch is needed to observe activity. For production minimize subscriptions to lifecycle signals, filter subagents, validate session attribution, and do not retain content-bearing raw events.

Observed timelines (relative milliseconds per probe):

1. Successful continuation, session 0d202688-b085-4eab-905e-439c55486f37: assistant.idle 2669; ACP end_turn 2671; continuation user.message 2677; assistant.turn_start 2679; task_complete 2698; session.idle 2699. No session.idle between the two interactions.
2. No task_complete, continuation limit, session 64dd2a77-8469-44a0-8746-f28e56cc09da: ACP end_turn 1945; five internal continuations; final session.idle 2067 with taskComplete=false. Waiting for task_complete would incorrectly remain busy forever.
3. Cancellation during initial prompt, session 9839d197-b5d4-4c00-abde-da186c270145: provider response held; cancel 2118; provider connection closed unfinished 2121; abort 2124; session.idle(aborted=true) 2126. No continuation. ACP response was nevertheless end_turn, not cancelled.
4. Cancellation during continuation, session ee38e3c5-1068-4662-8227-5648c375f67e: first end_turn 2053; continuation started 2063; second provider response held 2068; cancel 2169; response released 3569; task_complete still executed 3584; final idle 3585. Cancel had no effect, even with 1.4 seconds before any model output.

All probe sessions were closed; only their own child CLI processes were terminated. These are runtime diagnostic experiments, not a permanent test suite requiring a real agent binary.

## Fix direction / remaining work

Observe agent processing separately from an individual ACP prompt result. Normalize native lifecycle signals at the protocol boundary into shared Session behavior; do not change the meaning of turns for all Agents. session.idle is the relevant processing-completion signal; task_complete and assistant.turn_end are not substitutes. Preserve completed prompt callbacks/recording exactly once while accurately representing subsequent autonomous work and exit protection. Cancellation is a separately reproducible upstream defect and needs its own fix/acceptance, not a UI promise.

The opt-in raw extension was verified in installed 1.0.83; no public ACP subscription documentation was found. It has no explicit subscription acknowledgment, is ephemeral, and the implementation drops raw events beyond 256 in-flight notifications. Validate unsupported peers, lost events, ordering, replay, subagents, and error/disposal behavior before relying on it in production. ACP v2 state_update is a proposal, not a capability this v1 connection advertised.

The previous tasks.waitForPending installed-package patch is withdrawn and uninstalled. Fake source-transformation tests did not establish Autopilot lifecycle ordering. Do not resurrect that patch as a verified fix.

## Acceptance

- Deterministic fixture covers prompt response followed by autonomous start and final idle; include idle without task_complete.
- During active autonomous processing, Session status and exit protection do not claim idle; Your turn appears when processing actually stops.
- Preserve exactly-once completion for each client prompt; do not fabricate a second prompt response or wait indefinitely for optional task_complete.
- Handle subagent attribution, malformed/unsupported extension events, normal Agents, error/cancel/disposal, and legitimate late terminal-result rendering.
- Cancellation behavior is verified separately; no success claim from a UI state change alone.
- Maintainer confirms the exact live reproduction before closure.

## Sources / lesson

https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-sdk/features/agent-loop distinguishes model iterations, optional semantic task_complete, mechanical session.idle, and Autopilot-injected user messages.
https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/autopilot documents automatic continuations and stopping conditions.
https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/prompt-turn defines ACP prompt turns.
https://agentclientprotocol.com/rfds/v2/prompt explicitly discusses agent-initiated/out-of-turn work and proposes independent running/idle state.

Lesson lives here: prompt completion, model-iteration completion, agent idleness, and semantic task completion are different signals. Choose the signal matching the consumer; prove event order with the actual runtime.

Status: Deferred at maintainer request pending upstream github/copilot-cli#4743 and #4561. LouiseLM activity fix implemented and verified with deterministic tests and an isolated Neovim-to-unchanged-Copilot probe. Default initialize subscribes only to assistant.turn_start/session.idle; Session status running represents processing beyond the client prompt, preserving exactly-once prompt completion, queued input, exit protection, permission handling, and background unread attention. Real probe session d1b197b1-8c65-4459-ba18-e3dbbfaf84fc rendered Model responding after the callback and returned ready at final idle; callback_count=1, turn_done=1. No maintainer reload or live acceptance yet. Cancellation remains separately blocked by the installed-runtime guard (child louiselm-7mqy9.1). Maintainer explicitly declined installed-package patching; no approval request remains pending. Retest the exact continuation-cancellation case after upstream fixes reach the installed CLI: closure of the related upstream reports alone does not prove this defect fixed. Preserve local work and keep both bugs unclosed.
notes: Deferred at maintainer request on 2026-09-14 pending upstream github/copilot-cli#4743 (ACP completion versus autonomous activity) and #4561 (cancelled stop reason): https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4743 ; https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4561 . Local activity fix, regression coverage and generated docs are preserved on branch wip/copilot-autopilot-7mqy9 at commit 9123834f64c5ed6e7099726732d7687d977908fe and removed from the main working tree at maintainer request. Prior full-suite and isolated real-runtime verification is retained above; no maintainer live acceptance. Maintainer explicitly declined installed-package patching; no exception is pending. Revisit after upstream resolution and an installed version containing the fixes, then rerun both lifecycle and continuation-cancellation reproductions. Upstream closure alone is not sufficient to close this bug: the exact ignored-cancellation case was not found as a dedicated upstream report.

title: Copilot ACP cancellation ignores autonomous continuations
description:
Copilot CLI 1.0.83 ignores ACP session/cancel after an Autopilot continuation starts beyond the original session/prompt response. This is reproducible without LouiseLM and independently of the misleading Your turn label tracked by parent louiselm-7mqy9.

## Evidence

Unchanged installed CLI, isolated COPILOT_HOME, local synthetic OpenAI-compatible provider, only task_complete exposed. Probe /tmp/louiselm-copilot-events.u7L7cI/probe.mjs cancel_continuation creates a disposable ACP session and enables Autopilot. First synthetic model response ends without task_complete, causing an internal continuation. Hold the second HTTP response for 1500 ms and send session/cancel 100 ms into the hold.

Session ee38e3c5-1068-4662-8227-5648c375f67e: ACP end_turn at 2053 ms; continuation assistant.turn_start at 2063; second response held at 2068; session/cancel at 2169; response released at 3569; task_complete executed at 3584; session.idle at 3585. No abort event or connection cancellation. Cancellation preceded output by 1.4 seconds, ruling out a completed-work race.

Control: same probe with cancel_prompt holds the first response. Session 9839d197-b5d4-4c00-abde-da186c270145: cancel 2118; provider connection closed unfinished 2121; abort 2124; session.idle(aborted=true) 2126. No continuation. Note the returned stopReason was still end_turn, not cancelled; preserve this evidence when fixing cancellation outcome reporting.

All sessions closed and only their own CLI child processes terminated; no maintainer session or configuration changed. No real model calls or upstream writes.

## Cause

Installed bundle /home/lotso/.asdf/installs/nodejs/24.16.0/lib/node_modules/@github/copilot/node_modules/@github/copilot-linux-x64/app.js: ACP cancel retrieves the session and calls session.abort() only if pendingPrompt is true. The prompt handler has already cleared pendingPrompt before the autonomous continuation, so the cancel handler does nothing. The initial-prompt successful-send return path also returns end_turn without rechecking pendingPrompt.

LouiseLM currently rejects cancel from ready before it reaches this upstream handler. Fixing client activity tracking alone will not fix the upstream no-op. Do not silently switch modes, send synthetic user prompts, or close/dispose a session as a substitute for cancellation.

## Acceptance / deferred work

- A supported cancellation path stops active autonomous continuation, including while model output is delayed; emits authoritative abort/idle state and no subsequent tools or continuation.
- Original-prompt cancellation still stops processing and reports a correct cancelled outcome.
- Idle cancellation is safe and other sessions remain untouched.
- Add deterministic regression coverage using captured structural ordering; do not make the permanent suite depend on an installed real agent.
- Maintainer confirms user-facing cancellation on the original class of Autopilot reproduction before closure.

No fix implemented. Resolve through an authorized upstream change or supported runtime API, not a package monkey-patch or cosmetic client state. Lesson: ACP request-pending and agent-processing are not equivalent during internally scheduled Autopilot interactions.
notes: Deferred at maintainer request on 2026-09-14 alongside parent louiselm-7mqy9, pending related upstream issues https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4743 and https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4561 . Maintainer explicitly declined installed-package patching; no approval request remains pending and the installed runtime is unchanged. #4561 covers the wrong stopReason, not cancellation being ignored during an autonomous continuation; #4743 requests cancellation availability but does not reproduce this exact no-op. After upstream fixes reach the installed CLI, rerun the held-response continuation-cancel probe and original-prompt control, then obtain maintainer live acceptance. Do not infer this defect is fixed merely because the related upstream issues close. Client-side cancellation dispatch is preserved with the deferred activity patch on branch wip/copilot-autopilot-7mqy9 at commit 9123834f64c5ed6e7099726732d7687d977908fe, not shipped on main; upstream abort behavior remains unfixed.

title: Forensics records embedded_context from a nonexistent top-level ACP capability
description:
## Evidence

The Forensics collector records `embedded_context` from a field that does not exist in the ACP schema, so every Forensics record misreports the capability as `false`.

- ACP schema (agent-client-protocol-schema 1.5.0, `src/v1/agent.rs:4609`): `embedded_context` is a field of `PromptCapabilities` only — "Agent supports embedded context in `session/prompt` requests. When enabled, the Client is allowed to include `ContentBlock::Resource` in prompt requests." There is no top-level `AgentCapabilities.embeddedContext`.
- `lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua:333` (Forensics collection): `embedded_context = capabilities.embeddedContext == true`, where `capabilities = client.agent_capabilities`. That top-level key is never present, so the value is always `false` for every Session, for every Agent.
- `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:469` reads the same capability correctly: `prompt_capabilities.embeddedContext == true`. The Session's live state and the Forensics record therefore disagree by construction.
- Concrete on-disk record: `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/forensics/1787796219-1787796219-265777660586430.json` records `"embedded_context": false` for `deepseek/session-5d380d32-…`. The adapter serving that Session (acp-llm-adapter, `src/acp/mod.rs:764` `build_initialize_response`) advertises `promptCapabilities.embeddedContext: true`. False evidence on disk.

## Impact

- Anything gating on the Forensics `capabilities` table (diagnosis, routing evidence) treats deepseek Sessions as non-embedded-context.
- This session's handoff grill (louiselm-93wl) was briefly steered wrong by it: the record was cited as evidence that the deepseek adapter lacks embedded-context support, which is false — the adapter advertises and handles it.

## Fix direction

Read the nested field, mirroring the correct read at `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:469`. Do not add a top-level read as a second source.

## Acceptance

- A regression test builds a Forensics record for an Agent advertising `promptCapabilities.embeddedContext: true` and asserts `observations.capabilities.embedded_context == true`.
- A second case asserts `false` when the capability is absent.
- `registry.lua` no longer references a top-level `capabilities.embeddedContext`.
close_reason: done

comments.author: claude/b9144876-1764-4b20-a1c1-0d129f0a7105
comments.text: Fixed by reading subject.embedded_context (Session.state.embedded_context, already correctly derived from nested promptCapabilities.embeddedContext at lifecycle.lua:469 and exposed via inspect()) instead of re-deriving from client.agent_capabilities.embeddedContext. Single source of truth rather than mirroring the read in a second place. Regression test added in tests/session/api_spec.lua T[forensics]: one case for true (nested promptCapabilities.embeddedContext=true), one for false (capability absent). Full stylua/lua-language-server/mini.test/api-appendix gates pass.
