comments.text: Measured real recording picker/explorer readers on a private 2519-turn snapshot and deterministic 2518/25180/251800-turn fixtures (9 Agents, 10 Providers, 23 Models, 63 tuples; Sessions/days and sparse telemetry grow). Evidence and commands: docs/performance/usage-20260924/{README.md,benchmark.py,benchmark.lua,results.json}. Five API/CLI/fresh-connection repeats; four warmed-connection SQL samples; exact nested results and coverage agree across hosts. Current picker 12.32 ms, summary 50.31 ms; 100x summary 3945.78 ms (3921.62-4381.37), broad views 2196-2712 ms. Startup baseline 1.61 ms; median decode <=0.101 ms, headless render <=0.216 ms. Embedded SQL still takes seconds; SQLite builds differ (3.50.6 CLI vs 3.46.1 embedded), so no Rust speedup claimed. Cold means fresh SQLite cache, warm OS cache; no cold-disk or concurrent-writer claim. Recommendation: retain SQL/Lua and canonical aggregate semantics; tune broad SQL via filed follow-up louiselm-sawgo. No host, dependency, retention or production behavior changes. Checks: smoke/full fixtures pass; full Lua 1175 cases/89 groups, zero failures/notes; repository StyLua and LuaLS pass. Lesson destination: report plus this issue; bounded output does not bound cohort computation. Worktree changes remain uncommitted; unrelated work preserved.

title: Reflect on usage patterns with an advisory skill
description:
## Problem Statement

After factual collection and query tools exist, the operator wants to learn from patterns in option changes without mistaking correlation for motive or quality.

## Solution

Create a separate on-demand advisory skill that uses the completed factual tools to surface patterns and Sessions/turns worth reviewing.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want evidence-backed patterns in when options change and what consumption follows.
2. As an operator, I want tentative explanations identified as hypotheses and tied to inspectable records.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Depends on working collection and exploitation tools; consumes their structured queries rather than scanning raw logs interactively.
2. Reports the selected scope, counts, missing-data coverage, and source Session/turn/change references.
3. Distinguishes explicit requests from other Agent-reported changes and factual consumption from advisory interpretations of usefulness or intent.
4. Does not automatically change configuration, authorize actions, or claim that correlation proves an option helped.
5. Operates within the established private metadata scope. Any future need for transcript content or human labeling must be explicitly designed before adding that access.
6. Is discoverable through the maintainer's actual skill supply and demonstrated against a representative history with sparse and mixed-option cases.

## Implementation Notes

Keep this independent of the factual collector and explorer. Source: maintainer-confirmed collect -> exploit -> reflect sequence in louiselm-3x9p. Use the applicable skill-creation workflow when implementation starts.

## Testing Notes

Demonstrate correct source references and coverage handling on known data; reject unsupported causal claims. Record the real skill invocation and human acceptance.

## Out of Scope

Automatic optimization, quality scoring, price estimates, and silently adding prompt/tool data to the usage store.

title: Grill-me needed: may Attention use the documented vim.paste hook?
description:
Grill-me needed: preserve this policy decision for the maintainer; do not resolve it in passing.

May Attention use Neovim's documented vim.paste hook despite the repository's explicit prohibition on replacing global functions, or should direct-API paste remain a documented inactivity limitation?

Blocks louiselm-7hj6k. On 2026-09-24, delegated Luna investigation /root/paste_attention reproduced direct nvim_paste('fixture', true, -1) in an isolated Neovim 0.13-dev: TextChanged=1, on_key=0. The API serves UIs and scripts, so this classifies all direct paste calls as activity; it cannot prove human origin. Unfiltered TextChanged would count Agent-rendered output and reintroduce louiselm-vi0kj. Questions to resolve: allow a narrow documented-hook exception or retain the limitation; ownership with multiple Attention controllers; preservation of prior and subsequently installed handlers; exact return/error behavior; disposal without leaks or clobbering another plugin; whether long streaming pastes count once or throughout. Mutable ownership must remain explicit, not a hidden singleton. No general permission to patch globals follows from a paste-specific exception.

Acceptance remains: unseen turn at t=0, direct paste at t=10 moves eligibility t=30 to t=40; Agent output alone leaves t=30; disposal cleans observers. No production code changed while awaiting this decision.

title: Simultaneous ACP backup services still collide after bounded lock retry
description:
Hourly ACP backup and cloud-copy services can start together, contend for the local Restic repository, and emit a red failure notification even though a later retry succeeds. This is degraded but recoverable: the previous verified snapshot is retained and no data loss was observed.

## Observed

On the maintainer laptop, 2026-09-11 20:00 CEST, both timers activated together:

    2026-09-11T20:00:03+02:00 Starting louiselm-acp-backup.service
    2026-09-11T20:00:03+02:00 Starting louiselm-acp-cloud-copy.service
    2026-09-11T20:01:05+02:00 acp-log-backup: restic check failed: exit 11
    2026-09-11T20:01:05+02:00 acp-log-backup: restic cat failed: exit 11
    2026-09-11T20:01:05+02:00 louiselm-acp-backup-failure.service started

The next local run at 21:00 succeeded with a verified snapshot of 485 files / 759972003 bytes. Cloud-copy also succeeded at 21:00. Restic 0.19.1 is installed. The current wrapper passes --retry-lock 1m at scripts/acp-log-backup:129-134, but both operations can exhaust that bounded retry while competing.

## Symptoms

- The operator sees a red "LouiseLM backup failed" desktop notification.
- The local backup service exits failure with "restic check failed: exit 11".
- Cloud-copy can fail in the same overlap with "restic cat failed: exit 11".
- Previous verified snapshots remain retained; later scheduled retries recover.

## Root cause

The service templates have no ordering relationship: contrib/systemd/louiselm-acp-backup.service:1-3 and contrib/systemd/louiselm-acp-cloud-copy.service:1-3. Their timers both naturally activate at the same time: contrib/systemd/louiselm-acp-backup.timer:4-8 and contrib/systemd/louiselm-acp-cloud-copy.timer:4-8. The wrapper intentionally uses independent lock files at scripts/acp-log-backup:486-493 so offline cloud operations do not block local backup, while Restic still serializes access to the shared local repository. The native retry is bounded, so long contention remains user-visible.

## Why it was not caught

The prior fix d5a39bf added bounded native Restic lock retry and covered real overlap, but it does not guarantee ordering when both systemd services are activated together. The installed natural run reproduced the remaining edge after the retry window was exhausted.

## Fix direction

Add systemd ordering so louiselm-acp-backup.service runs before louiselm-acp-cloud-copy.service when both are activated together, while retaining --retry-lock 1m as a defense for catch-up/manual activation. Do not replace this with a shared global wrapper lock: a slow/offline cloud operation must not block local backup. Do not use schedule staggering as the sole fix because catch-up and manual activation can overlap again.

## Acceptance

- Add a regression/integration check that simultaneous service activation orders local backup before cloud-copy and preserves independent cloud retry behavior.
- With both timers firing at the same time, local backup succeeds, cloud-copy runs afterward, and no failure notification is triggered.
- An offline/failed cloud-copy does not prevent local backup from succeeding.
- Existing full backup tests and systemd verification pass.

## Not covered

No data corruption was demonstrated. Full cloud repository verification and desktop notification delivery are separate acceptance concerns. No manual unlock or destructive recovery action was performed.

Regression and full 31-test suite already passed.

title: Hardware signing withholds touch prompts until failure
description:
Installed C14 recovery setup withheld ssh-keygen's user-presence prompt until a Release signing failure. One observed failure; a second maintainer-started attempt subsequently committed successfully. This records the prompt-delivery defect; the native "invalid format" cause is not established.

## Observed

2026-09-08, codex/01a07d34-4adb-7491-8d0a-3f23cd0796e1; retained VM invocation c4a17aa6e8a941a3aba103e3a7758967, installed release sha256:4b37c7c25831c4fc1de7ded896d9bb0aa46493668085f0ca8bf9ba3e88b2e3dd/source af47989650e6f2e824901c92063ebf36d82f2831. Enter passphrase for "/home/vm/.ssh/id_louiselm_c14_primary_20260908_01a07d34":
Enter PIN for ED25519-SK key:
Enter passphrase for "/home/vm/.ssh/id_louiselm_c14_release_20260908_01a07d34":
Enter PIN for ED25519-SK key:
louiselm-skills: signing failed: Confirm user presence for key ED25519-SK SHA256:OmMZlGzi8rDzoA71wAl8LSUBcNQVxD3h9/uiY0rgEiI\u{a}Couldn't sign message: invalid format\u{d}\u{a}Signing /tmp/louiselm-sign-0DsYtN/payload failed: invalid format

## Symptoms

Passphrase/PIN prompts appear, but "Confirm user presence" appears only inside the final escaped error. Primary then Release is the observed order. Physical touch timing/count and the first failure's elapsed time were not reported.

## Root cause

Confirmed prompt transport: skills-core/src/launcher_install.rs:40 delegates signing to the shared runner; :436-437 pipes stdout/stderr even with a foreground terminal. :495 captures stderr with command_output_worker; :597-605 reads it into a buffer until EOF, not the operator TTY. skills-core/src/signer.rs:101-133 invokes ssh-keygen and surfaces escaped stderr only on failure; success discards it. Foreground ownership permits /dev/tty PIN/passphrase input but does not display piped stderr.

Native invalid-format root cause UNKNOWN. Missing/delayed touch, device/provider failure, or another native refusal need discriminating evidence. The recorded prompt-delivery defect is not proof which caused the refusal. Distinct from closed a2zc: that was overlong resident user ID during key creation, not signing existing keys.

## Why it was not caught

Existing process tests assert eventual captured output and foreground ownership, not that an interactive helper's stderr prompt reaches the private terminal BEFORE it exits. Ordinary software-key tests have no physical presence wait.

## Fix direction

At the narrow interactive-signing boundary, deliver required operator prompts live to the existing private TTY while preserving bounded deadlines, process-group cleanup, terminal restoration, diagnostic escaping and noninteractive capture. Do not weaken hardware/UP/UV policy, extend deadlines, auto-retry signing or broadcast raw output to Agent logs. Diagnose the native refusal separately if it recurs.

- Preserve noninteractive capture, cancellation/deadline cleanup and terminal foreground restoration tests; all affected Rust gates pass.
- Maintainer sees timely Primary and Release touch instructions and completes both without guessing when to touch; public setup/recovery status proves the intended atomic change.
- Record whether native invalid-format reproduces; do not claim its cause fixed solely from prompt visibility.

title: Operator-facing cold Park: :LouiselmPark and Run-reconstructing :LouiselmResumePark
description:
## Problem Statement

The only production path that creates a durable cold Park is the `louiselm-capture` CLI shelled directly from a terminal -- never from inside Neovim. `Run`, `Executor`, and `Service.admit`/`attach`/`park` (built by `louiselm-qbr.3.3`) are fully-tested library code with zero UI callers. During the `louiselm-t6mx` QA round, the CLI-synthesized Park bypassed `Run:park_cold`'s live ownership and Agent-capability checks, producing a Park the resuming Agent could not load -- invalid QA evidence, and cases 2-4 blocked.

## Solution

Give the operator a real, UI-native way to create and resume a cold Park, so manual QA of the Park lifecycle exercises the actual production path instead of a CLI shortcut.

`:LouiselmPark` transparently attaches the current chat session to a Run (creating one if the session is not already Run-backed -- no separate "start a Run" step, no ownership concept exposed to the operator) and cold-Parks it through the existing `Run:park_cold`/`cold_park_record` checks. `:LouiselmResumePark` is extended to reconstruct a live `Run` object around the resumed session, instead of leaving `claims`/`generated_work` stranded in the durable record with nothing on the Lua side to enforce them.

Settled design note: `louiselm-kdeg` (`Run` owns a supervision tree of Sessions) is unchanged by this feature. Forced cancel/dispose authority remains real for the automated Generator-bounded case (`louiselm-qbr.3.2.6`); for this manual operator-initiated path that authority is simply never exercised, since the human is the one requesting the Park.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want to cold-Park my current session with one command, so that I can safely walk away without losing durable state or exposing implementation concepts like "Run".
2. As an operator, I want to be warned if I have an unsent prompt or pending context before it is silently lost to cold Park, so Park remains a safe escape hatch rather than a silent data-loss trap.
3. As an operator, I want the issues I am actively working attached to the Park automatically, so I do not have to remember and retype them.
4. As an operator, I want a rejected Park to name the specific missing capability or precondition, not a raw ACP error, so I know what to fix or which Agent to switch to.
5. As an operator, I want `:LouiselmResumePark` to restore my claims and generated-work budget into a live, enforceable state, not just leave them inert in a durable record.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given an ordinary chat session with no existing Run, when the operator runs `:LouiselmPark`, then a Run is created, the session is attached as its sole worker, and it is cold-Parked -- with no separate prior command required.
2. Given a session with staged context (queued prompt, pending skill selection, context chips), when `:LouiselmPark` runs, then the operator is warned that this material will not survive cold Park and must confirm before it proceeds; Park is never silently lossy and never hard-blocked by staged context alone.
3. Given the session actor holds live `br` claims, when `:LouiselmPark` runs, then those claims are attached to the Park record automatically, with no picker or manual entry.
4. Given the Agent lacks `agent_capabilities.loadSession`, has no live ACP client, or has no `working_dir`, when `:LouiselmPark` runs, then the specific failing precondition is named to the operator, never a raw ACP error string.
5. Given a durable cold Park created through `:LouiselmPark`, when the operator runs `:LouiselmResumePark` and selects it, then a `Run` is reconstructed around the resumed session with `claims` and `generated_work` restored from the durable record into live state.
6. Warm Park is not exposed as a manual operator action anywhere in this feature; it remains internal to the existing automatic budget-exhaustion path (`louiselm-qbr.3.2.6`).

## Implementation Notes

- Reuses `Run:park_cold`/`cold_park_record` (`lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua`) and `Service.admit`/`attach`/`park` (`lua/louiselm/workflow/service.lua`) -- this feature is their first production caller.
- `:LouiselmResumePark` (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`) currently performs a bare ACP `session/load` with no Run reconstruction; needs a `Run.new()` + `accept_resume()`-style restoration path.
- Claims are sourced by querying live `br` state for the session actor (`<agent>/<acp-session-id>`), never typed by the operator.
- Does not add a `stage` field to the durable Run record -- see Out of Scope.

## Testing Notes

- End-to-end: a real Agent session, `:LouiselmPark`, Neovim restart, `:LouiselmResumePark`, assert the resumed session carries the original claims/budget in live state, not just in the durable record.
- A wedged/incapable Agent (no `loadSession`) must produce a named-precondition error, not a raw ACP failure.
- Staged context warning must be a headless-testable confirmation branch, not a manual-only check.
- Mutation-safety after resume (case 3 of the `louiselm-t6mx` QA round) becomes testable here for the first time, since only after this feature exists does a live Run object exist on the resumed side to assert against.

## Out of Scope

- Adding a `stage` field to the durable Run record (schema-v5 migration). `Executor` has zero UI callers today, so there is no live stage value to persist or validate against yet; file separately once something drives `Executor` from the UI.
- Exposing warm Park as a manual operator action.
- A picker or manual-entry UI for claims.
- Multi-Run selection UI -- this feature is scoped to the single active chat session having at most one Run.

## Rejected Alternatives

- Implicit Run-backing for every session from creation: rejected -- adds a per-session capture-service round-trip and couples `ui/chat` to `workflow/` unconditionally, for sessions that never Park.
- Fully cooperative Run/Session model with no override authority: rejected -- would defeat `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6`'s budget-exhaustion enforcement, which requires the Run to force-stop a Generator that will not cooperate.
- Hard-blocking Park when staged context is present: rejected -- Park must remain a safe escape hatch even mid-composition.
- Manual claims entry via picker or typed flag: rejected in favor of auto-query -- the data already lives in `br`, and manual entry is friction that gets skipped under time pressure.

title: :LouiselmResumePark fails for claude agent sessions: ACP session/load reports Resource not found
description:
`:LouiselmResumePark` fails unconditionally for `claude` agent sessions with "ACP session/load failed: Resource not found: <acp_session_id>". Reproduced twice in a row, including once in the exact same still-running Neovim process that created the Park (no restart involved) — this rules out "durability across an editor restart" as the cause. The underlying `session/load` call simply does not work for this agent in this environment, so cold Park's entire resume promise is currently non-functional.

## Observed

Manual QA round on `ab8e71c..HEAD` (session claude/5f934d18-b9b8-42b3-91cc-35fb293d14dc), 2026-08-28.

Session under test: `claude/6b80a87e-54dd-4f7b-ab9f-e2fb0ebc380d`, cwd `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`.

1. `:LouiselmPark` with no staged context succeeded -> run `72a8fa90-b11a-4dc7-a918-57f3c8fc5a64`:
   `{"id":"72a8fa90-b11a-4dc7-a918-57f3c8fc5a64","agent":"claude","acp_session_id":"6b80a87e-54dd-4f7b-ab9f-e2fb0ebc380d","working_dir":"/home/lotso/code/louiselm","state":"cold_parked","park_expires_at_ms":1788015591408,"generated_work":{"ceiling":1,"consumed":0,"reserved":0,"pending":[],"outputs":[]},"claims":[]}`
2. With issue `louiselm-8tzl` claimed to the same session (`br update louiselm-8tzl --claim --actor "claude/6b80a87e-54dd-4f7b-ab9f-e2fb0ebc380d"`, claimed only for this test and released afterward), `:LouiselmPark` succeeded again -> run `a998611f-bc18-414a-9a94-97c962b343b0`:
   `{"id":"a998611f-bc18-414a-9a94-97c962b343b0","agent":"claude","acp_session_id":"6b80a87e-54dd-4f7b-ab9f-e2fb0ebc380d","working_dir":"/home/lotso/code/louiselm","state":"cold_parked","park_expires_at_ms":1788016384189,"generated_work":{"ceiling":1,"consumed":0,"reserved":0,"pending":[],"outputs":[]},"claims":["louiselm-8tzl"]}`
   Both confirmed live via `louiselm-capture run list`.
3. `:LouiselmResumePark`, picking either run from the picker (`Chat:resume_park`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3993`), fails every time with: `Error: ACP session/load failed: Resource not found: 6b80a87e-54dd-4f7b-ab9f-e2fb0ebc380d`. Zero successes across two independent attempts, one of them same-process.
4. No on-disk trace of session id `6b80a87e-54dd-4f7b-ab9f-e2fb0ebc380d` exists anywhere on the filesystem (checked `~/.claude/projects/**` and a broader filesystem search) — the session was never durably persisted anywhere findable, despite the Agent having advertised `agentCapabilities.loadSession = true` (Park itself only succeeds because `cold_park_record`, `lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua:121-141`, checks exactly that capability and it passed).
5. No ACP protocol log exists for this session either; `lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua:338` reports `{ kind = "acp_log", state = "omitted", reason = "ACP adapter did not advertise a log path" }` for it, so the raw `session/load` JSON-RPC request/response could not be inspected directly.

## Symptoms

- User runs `:LouiselmResumePark`, picks a just-Parked run from the picker, and gets `louiselm: ACP session/load failed: Resource not found: <id>` instead of the expected `louiselm: cold Park resumed (recoverable, lossy)`.
- The system self-reports the session as simply not found by the freshly spawned `claude` ACP agent process, even immediately after that same session was live and cold-Parked successfully.

## Root cause

Unknown — not yet isolated to a specific file/line. The failing call is `Registry:load_session` (`lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua:450`) -> `start_session(self, agent_name, options, ready_callback, acp_session_id)`, which spawns a fresh `claude` ACP agent process and issues ACP `session/load` for that id. This registry code predates this QA round's diff (`ab8e71c..HEAD`) and is not one of the reviewed commits, but it was only reachable/user-visible for the first time through this round's new `:LouiselmPark`/`:LouiselmResumePark` commands (`71a6ae3`, `64523ac`), which is why it surfaced now.

Hypotheses, undiscriminated:
- The `claude` ACP agent process here does not actually persist session state to a location/keyed-form that a freshly spawned sibling process can rediscover via `session/load`, despite advertising `loadSession: true` in its capabilities — i.e. the capability advertisement over-promises.
- `start_session`'s invocation of the `claude` agent binary for a load is missing a required argument/env var (e.g. a working-directory or project-scope mismatch) that would let the agent locate the session on disk.
- Something in how the session id is threaded from the Park record (`selected.acp_session_id`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4018`) to the load call is subtly wrong (e.g. wrong id shape), though the id printed in the error matches the parked id exactly, which argues against this.

Distinguishing the first two needs an experiment outside Neovim: invoke the `claude` ACP agent binary directly (bypassing Registry/start_session) with a `session/load` request for a session id known to exist in `~/.claude/projects` for this repo, and see whether that succeeds. If it does, the bug is in how `start_session` invokes/targets the agent. If it still fails, the capability advertisement itself is wrong for this agent/config.

## Why it was not caught

The automated coverage for both `:LouiselmPark` (`louiselm-gc0z`) and `:LouiselmResumePark` (`louiselm-rili`) exercises `Registry:load_session` only through the mock ACP agent (`lua/louiselm/dev/mock_agent.lua`), which unconditionally advertises `loadSession = true` and always succeeds a load for any id it's given — it cannot express "advertises the capability but the load still fails," which is exactly this defect. There is no fixture derived from a real `claude` agent's `session/load` behavior (per `AGENTS.md` section 5, a real-peer fixture should be derived from a captured log frame, but no log path is advertised for this agent's sessions, so none exists to capture from).

## Fix direction

Not yet determined — needs the discriminating experiment above before a fix location can be named. If the capability advertisement over-promises, the fix is likely in whatever configures/reports `agentCapabilities.loadSession` for the `claude` agent adapter (outside this repo's Lua, in the ACP bridge process itself, unless louiselm controls that manifest). If it's an invocation gap in `start_session`, the fix is scoped to `lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua`.

## Acceptance

- A real (or accurately-captured-fixture) `claude` agent `session/load` round-trip succeeds for a session that was actually cold-Parked, end to end through `:LouiselmPark` then `:LouiselmResumePark`.
- A regression test using a mock agent variant that advertises `loadSession = true` but fails an actual load request, proving `:LouiselmResumePark` surfaces a clear, named error rather than a raw ACP string (this variant does not exist today, per "Why it was not caught").

## Not covered

- Whether this reproduces for other ACP agents (codex, glm, deepseek) — not tested; only `claude` was exercised this round.
- The secondary, lower-confidence observation that `Chat:park` (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3180`) hardcodes `load_session = true` when calling `WorkflowService.attach`, instead of reading the session's real advertised capability the way `cold_park_record` (`lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua:139`) does. This is not the cause of the reproduced failure here (the real capability was genuinely true, and `cold_park_record`'s own check passed both times) — but it means `WorkflowService.admit`/`attach` durably persist state before that capability gate gets a chance to reject, for any agent that genuinely lacks `loadSession` support. Worth a look while investigating this bug, but is a narrower, separate concern and not independently reproduced.
- Whether the two stale/expired Run records found in `~/.local/state/louiselm/workflow/runs/` at QA setup time (pre-dating this session, rejected by a since-superseded `louiselm-capture` binary build) are related — they are not; they were confirmed to be an unrelated stale-binary artifact, resolved by rebuilding `louiselm-capture` before this round's Park cases ran.
close_reason: Root cause fixed and tested: cold_park_record now rejects Parking a Session before its first prompt, which is what made session/load unresumable. Verified against the real claude-agent-sdk (resume succeeds after >=1 turn, fails identically to the report at 0 turns) and a new regression test. Full suite: 723/723 passing. Remaining acceptance item (clear error message on other session/load failures) intentionally split into open child louiselm-aaw0.1.1, not blocking this close.

Root cause isolated via the discriminating experiment this issue's description called for,
run against the real `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` (0.3.238, the version pinned in
`~/code/claude-agent-acp`) rather than inside Neovim:

- A session with at least one completed turn resumes successfully from a **freshly spawned**
  `query()` process — this rules out "invocation gap in `start_session`" and "capability
  advertisement over-promises" as general claims. `Registry:load_session` /

- A session that pre-assigns a `sessionId` (exactly how `claude-agent-acp`'s `createSession`
  mints one for a fresh, non-resume session — `options.sessionId = randomUUID()`,
  `src/acp-agent.ts:6603`) and never sends a prompt fails resume with exactly this issue's
  error: `No conversation found with session ID: <id>`, which the bridge maps to

  found" (`-32002`).

So: `loadSession: true` describes what the Agent *can* resume, not what a given Session has
*persisted yet*. The underlying `claude` CLI process only writes a durable transcript once a
prompt is actually sent; a Session that is cold-Parked before its first prompt has nothing on
disk for a later `session/load` to find. `cold_park_record` (`lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua`)
checked `capabilities.loadSession == true` but never checked whether the Session had sent
anything yet — which is exactly what happened in this issue's repro (`:LouiselmPark` "with no
staged context" on a just-initialized Session).

## Fix

Added a guard to `cold_park_record`: reject cold Park when `state.current_turn < 1`, using the
existing `current_turn` counter (incremented in `Session:prompt`, `lifecycle.lua:695`) as the
"has this Session ever sent a prompt" signal. Regression test added in
`tests/workflow/run_spec.lua` (`"rejects cold Park when the Session has never sent a prompt"`).
Updated the `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` cold-Park fixture, which previously relied on the
now-rejected zero-turn default.

## Not fixed here

The parent issue's second Acceptance item — a mock-agent variant that advertises
`loadSession: true` but fails an actual load, proving `:LouiselmResumePark` surfaces a clear
error instead of the raw ACP string — is a distinct, still-open gap: even with this guard,
`session/load` can fail for other legitimate reasons after a valid Park (eviction, Agent
reinstall, etc.), and today's mock agent can't model "advertises the capability but the load
still fails" at all. Split off as `louiselm-aaw0.1.1`.

The "Not covered" observation about `Chat:park` hardcoding `load_session = true` instead of
reading the Session's real advertised capability (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3180`) was not
touched — it wasn't the cause of the reproduced failure and remains a narrower, separate
concern per the parent issue's own note.

title: Surface a clear, named error when a valid cold Park's session/load still fails
description:
## Problem

`louiselm-aaw0.1` diagnosed the reproduced `:LouiselmResumePark` failure: `cold_park_record`
allowed cold-Parking a Session that had never sent a prompt, so the underlying `claude`
ACP agent (via `claude-agent-acp`, spawned as a fresh process per Session) had nothing durable
on disk for `session/load` to find, even though it correctly advertises `loadSession: true`.
That's fixed (guard added: cold Park now requires `state.current_turn >= 1`).

That fix only prevents the *reproduced* failure mode. It does not address the parent issue's
second acceptance item, which is a distinct, still-open gap:

> A regression test using a mock agent variant that advertises `loadSession = true` but fails
> an actual load request, proving `:LouiselmResumePark` surfaces a clear, named error rather
> than a raw ACP string (this variant does not exist today).

Even with the guard in place, `session/load` can still legitimately fail after a valid cold
Park — e.g. the Agent's session store evicted the transcript, the Agent process was
reinstalled/upgraded, or the `park_expires_at_ms` window lapsed in a way the Agent enforces
independently. Today those failures surface verbatim as `ACP session/load failed: Resource
not found: <id>` (`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua` `fail(self, "ACP session/" .. method ..
" failed: " .. error_message(session_error))`), which is not actionable to a user who doesn't
know what an ACP `session/load` is.

## Scope

- Add a mock-agent option (alongside the existing `crash_on` precedent in
  `lua/louiselm/dev/mock_agent.lua`) that makes `session/load` respond with a JSON-RPC error
  (mirroring the real bridge's `RequestError.resourceNotFound`, code -32002) instead of
  succeeding, while `initialize` still advertises `loadSession: true` — this is exactly the
  "advertises the capability but the load still fails" case the parent issue's "Why it was not
  caught" section says no fixture can express today.
- Surface a clear, named error from `:LouiselmResumePark` for this case instead of the raw ACP
  string — e.g. distinguish "the Agent no longer has this Park's session" from other ACP
  failures, at the UI layer (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`, `Chat:resume_park`) or in
  `Registry:load_session`.
- Add the regression test the parent's Acceptance section asks for.

## Evidence this is real and distinct from aaw0.1's root cause

Confirmed via a discriminating experiment against the real
`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` (0.3.238, the version pinned in `~/code/claude-agent-acp`):
a session that completes at least one turn resumes successfully from a freshly spawned
process (rules out "resume across process boundaries is broken"); a session with zero turns
fails resume with exactly `No conversation found with session ID: <id>`, which the bridge
maps to `RequestError.resourceNotFound` (`src/acp-agent.ts:6626`). The zero-turn case is what
`louiselm-aaw0.1`'s guard now prevents from ever being Parked — but the underlying
"session/load can fail after a superficially valid Park" scenario is broader than just that
one cause, and today's mock agent cannot model it at all.

Dependencies:
  -> louiselm-aaw0.1 (related)
close_reason: Implemented named error for resourceNotFound session/load failures, plus mock-agent fixture and regression tests. All gates pass.

title: Handoff prompt is missing from target Session transcript
description:
# A successful Handoff is sent to the target Agent but omitted from the target Session transcript. The target can act on the reviewed source transcript, while later transcript inspection cannot prove which source Session initiated it or recover the submitted Handoff prompt.

## Observed

Seen in the live Neovim instance on 2026-08-24 in `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`.

Live chat-controller introspection returned:

```
claude/8b826fbf-4771-4ab2-8231-e7aef6fe98ba | entries=246 | first-user=what is your next best task ?
codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374 | entries=10 | first-user=you were handed off claude/8b826fbf-4771-4ab2-8231-e7aef6fe98ba can you confirm ?
```

Both Sessions remained attached. The Codex target had already produced transcript entries, but its first recorded user entry was the later confirmation question rather than the reviewed Handoff transcript.

Code evidence:

- `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2437` sends the reviewed text with `handoff.target_session:prompt(text)`.
- `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1538` records ordinary submitted prompts with `view.transcript:record_user(text)` only inside `submit_prompt`.
- `Chat:submit_handoff` has no equivalent transcript recording step.

## Symptoms

- The operator cannot confirm a completed Handoff from the target Session transcript.
- Transcript export omits the reviewed source transcript injected during Handoff.
- The source and target Sessions can coexist in the UI without a durable causal link in the target transcript.

## Root cause

`Chat:submit_handoff` bypasses the ordinary `submit_prompt` capture boundary. It calls the target Session directly at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2437`, then closes the review buffer, without recording the accepted prompt in the target view transcript.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:175` asserts that the edited transcript reaches `target.prompts`, but does not inspect the target transcript or exported Markdown. The fixture therefore proves transport and buffer disposal while missing forensic completeness.

## Fix direction

Record an accepted Handoff prompt exactly once at the same narrow boundary that owns the target transcript, without recording failed sends. Preserve the reviewed text exactly as sent. Add source Session identity as structured provenance if transcript text alone cannot durably express the Handoff relationship; do not infer provenance later from view ordering.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix because a successfully submitted Handoff is absent from the target transcript, then passes with the exact reviewed prompt present once.
- A failed Handoff send leaves no user entry in the target transcript.
- Exporting the target Session after Handoff contains enough durable evidence to identify the source Session `claude/8b826fbf-4771-4ab2-8231-e7aef6fe98ba` and the reviewed prompt.
- The operator can confirm the Handoff after the review buffer is closed and after either Session view is switched.

## Not covered

Whether ACP Agent-side history independently persists the injected prompt is unverified. No behavior fix is included; this issue is intentionally deferred for later.
close_reason: Recorded successful Handoff prompts with source Session provenance in target transcript and UI; tests pass.

comments.author: copilot/21b608af-b244-4f7e-a013-681e0c1f8f97

Fixed by recording a separate Handoff user entry after a successful send, with source Session provenance, and rendering it in the target buffer/export. Failed sends leave no entry. Evidence: focused chat suite 114/114, full mini.test 499/499, lua-language-server zero diagnostics. No standing rule or design question warranted.

title: Account limits
description: Normalized Provider entitlement state — how much quota remains in an exact window — reaching LouiseLM only when an Agent advertises the provider-neutral ACP accountLimits extension.
design: Established by the louiselm-opencode-quota-runtime-ownership-blz13 grill-me, confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-09-16. Source Session: claude/7c202de1-9087-4c68-9c4a-7577d53221bc. Transport was settled earlier by louiselm-iexg (capability-advertised provider-neutral ACP extension owned by external Agent adapters); this record adds the authority half, which louiselm-iexg never reached: adapters own Provider access but are not thereby licensed to hold Provider credentials.
notes:
Use Account limits for Provider entitlement: remaining quota in an exact window, normalized by lua/louiselm/session/limits.lua into buckets of usedPercent, windowDurationMins and resetsAt.

Distinguish from Usage, the locally recorded turn facts LouiseLM collects itself (tokens, cost, spend) per louiselm-rdwb. An Agent's own spend report is not entitlement: opencode stats reports local token and cost history, and reading it as quota sent the OpenCode investigation down a dead end. Distinguish also from context usage (ctx %), which is per-Session window occupancy rather than account capacity.

unsupported is a correct terminal state, not a missing feature. LouiseLM and the adapters its maintainer maintains never read a Provider credential store or call a Provider API to obtain it; limits arrive only when an Agent advertises the extension over ACP. That restriction governs entitlement only and does not constrain local Usage collection.

title: Publish the accountLimits v1 wire contract so other adapters can implement it
description:
## Goal

Document the `io.github.euri10.louiselm` `accountLimits` v1 capability as a
public wire contract, so an adapter author other than the maintainer can
implement it.

## Why now

The contract is currently written down nowhere: zero hits across `docs/`,
`README.md` and `doc/`. It exists only as consumer code in
`lua/louiselm/session/limits.lua` and inside two fork patches. That makes the
forks the de facto specification, readable only by reading their source.

`~/.config/nvim/agent-runtimes/inventory.json` says the Codex patch retires
when "an upstream implementation passes LouiseLM negotiated read/update
snapshot acceptance". That exit condition is unreachable while the contract is
unpublished — upstreams are being asked to implement something they cannot
read.

Freezing v1 costs the freedom to reshape it silently. Alpha with no external
users is the cheapest moment to spend that.

## Scope

Specify, from `lua/louiselm/session/limits.lua` as the authority:

- Capability advertisement under `_meta["io.github.euri10.louiselm"].accountLimits`
  with `version`, `readMethod`, `updatedMethod`.
- The complete snapshot shape: buckets with `id`, optional `label`, `windows`
  of `usedPercent` / `windowDurationMins` / `resetsAt`, plus `reachedType`,
  `planType`, `credits`, `unlimited` and `resetCredits`.
- Validation rules the consumer enforces, including that `windowDurationMins`
  must be an exact positive integer — and that an adapter must not invent one
  to make a reset-only quota fit (the louiselm-ce6.27 failure).
- Which states are distinct: `unsupported`, `unavailable`, `empty`,
  `unlimited`, `stale`, `not_observed`.

Link `euri10/codex-acp` and `euri10/claude-agent-acp` as **unsupported
reference implementations, no compatibility promise**. Do not present them as
a distribution or an install path.

## Acceptance

1. A docs page specifies the capability and complete snapshot shape.
2. The spec matches what `limits.lua` actually accepts; a shape the doc
   permits but the code rejects is a defect in one of them.
3. Forks are described as reference only, with the no-promise wording.
4. `npm run site:test` and the full `npm run site:build` pass — this adds a
   public page, so the TOC and byte-checked artifact allowlist need deliberate
   updates per docs/agent-testing.md.

## Context

Decision: louiselm-opencode-quota-runtime-ownership-blz13.
Vocabulary: louiselm-account-limits-9n9st.
close_reason: Documented complete accountLimits v1 wire contract and linked public navigation; all site gates, four protocol examples and 94 Session API tests pass. Lesson and validation in comment2434. consumer:docs/index.md:11

title: Proposal-only diff has no review controls
description:
Agent-created proposal-only diffs open through Apply.preview followed by Buffer.open. They must be actionable reviews: accepting writes the reviewed proposal into the working tree without committing, while rejecting discards it.

## Observed

The resumed subject Session deepseek/session-5b4fb715-7267-4f09-848b-54e84fca2dfc reproduced the missing controls twice at history.jsonl lines 254-259 and 262-267 while repository and installed plugin were at 854a7bc. Both helpers called Buffer.open(preview, { focus = true }) directly. Ask Edits prompted for helper-file tool calls but did not create a diff decision responder.

## Root cause

Buffer.open was only a renderer. Interactive mappings existed exclusively in Diff:open for ACP permission requests, so proposal-only previews had no decision path.

## Fix direction

Make the existing standalone Buffer.open path a minimal proposal review. Reuse Apply.apply so acceptance refuses to overwrite a file changed since preview. Preserve the permission controller mappings, which override the standalone mappings for ACP decisions.

## Acceptance

- Standalone Buffer.open advertises and installs a, d, and q.
- a writes the proposed content only when the target still matches the reviewed original, then closes the review.
- d and q preserve the target and close the review.
- A stale target is preserved, the review remains open, and an actionable error is displayed.
- ACP permission review behavior remains unchanged.

## Not covered

Applying a proposal does not stage or commit it.
close_reason: Fixed in the working tree. Standalone Buffer.open now owns proposal apply/discard controls; acceptance reuses the stale-file guard in Apply.apply. Red: focused diff suite reproduced E21, unchanged target, and an unclosed review. Green: focused 14/14 and full mini.test 477/477. Gates: stylua --check ., lua-language-server at Warning, and git diff --check all passed.

comments.text: Corrected initial triage after inspecting the primary session log: the buffer was created directly through ui.diff.buffer.open, not through the permission controller. The missing mappings are expected for that low-level path; the defect is its unconditional controller-specific instruction line.

title: Back up ACP adapter logs hourly with verified restore
description:
## Problem Statement

On 2026-09-09 the maintainer accidentally removed ~/.local/state with rm -rf. ACP adapter logs were exceptionally valuable; recovery consumed most of a day, several scans, two small USB keys, and an offline boot. Recovery recovered useful material but did not establish complete restoration of the original logs. The maintainer explicitly requests a new DAILY backup capability at P0. The backup destination is intentionally undecided and must be discussed, not silently selected.

## Solution

Provide automatic, versioned daily backups of the maintainer's ACP adapter log data, with visible health and a verified restore procedure. A backup must survive deletion of the source state tree; increasing adapter retention or mirroring the latest directory is not this capability. Preserve at least one earlier good generation when the source becomes empty, disappears, or is accidentally deleted.

## User Stories

1. As the maintainer, I want daily backups without remembering a command or keeping Neovim open.
2. I want to restore a selected generation after deleting my local state, without overwriting newer logs unknowingly.
3. I want to know the last successful verified backup, its coverage, and any missed or failed run.
4. I want an explicit choice of destination, privacy, retention and storage budget before enabling backup.

## Decisions Required Before Implementation

- Discuss WHERE: independent local path/device, remote destination, or both; availability, encryption/key recovery, storage budget, and protection against source deletion versus whole-disk loss. Do not choose a cloud provider or purchase storage here.
- Confirm source inventory: adapter-owned state, Session logs AND proxy connection logs, required metadata and native transcripts if relevant. Respect effective state-root overrides. Discuss existing recovered-partial symlinks/external archives explicitly; do not follow arbitrary symlinks or claim those archives were backed up implicitly.
- Choose ownership/integration boundary (adapter, user-level OS job, separate backup tool, optional LouiseLM status surface). No existing parent epic is implied.
- Define daily scheduling, catch-up after shutdown/unavailable destinations, accepted data-loss window, generation retention and health notification. A daily cadence alone does not protect all activity since the last successful run; source eviction before backup also needs an explicit policy.
- Logs can contain prompts, tool arguments and credentials. Decide local permissions, encryption, and redaction/export boundaries; no automatic upload, public fixtures or content-bearing notifications.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The maintainer approves destination, scope, schedule/catch-up, retention, privacy and restore behavior before implementation is considered ready.
2. With backup enabled, a due run produces a separately stored, timestamped generation with an inventory and integrity checks; missing/unwritable/full destinations and interrupted runs report failure without claiming success or replacing the last good generation.
3. Deleting a disposable test source tree after a successful backup leaves that generation intact. Restoring into a fresh staging directory reproduces the declared backed-up bytes and reports exclusions or incomplete active-file coverage.
4. Source deletion/empty state does not propagate as destruction of prior generations. Active append, rotation and pruning races have a documented consistency contract and tested detection/handling.
5. Restore offers a preview and explicit conflict policy, preserves existing files by default, and never imports partial fragments as complete live logs silently.
6. Status exposes last successful verified backup, next due/missed run, coverage and actionable failure without sensitive content. If configuration is optional, unset/disabled behavior is tested; enabling it is verified in the maintainer's effective setup, including a scheduled run and actual restore drill.

## Testing Notes

Use isolated fixtures for source-tree deletion, concurrent append/rotation, offline/full destination, crash/cancel, bad checksums, retention and restore collisions. Never reproduce the accident against real state. A green copy operation alone is not acceptance: exercise the scheduler and restoration end to end.

## Prior Lessons / Boundary

louiselm-proxy-log-evidence-expiry-xxfu and its 2026-09-01 comment document earlier 100 MB aggregate eviction and a subsequent unlimited-retention setting/manual backup. That historical mitigation is not proof of current configuration, daily backup or protection from rm. README identifies raw ACP logs as adapter-owned. Canonical Forensics (louiselm-cvv3) indexes evidence in place and does not preserve the underlying files; this feature supplies a distinct backup capability, not a silent vocabulary change.

Out of scope: full-system backup, filesystem undelete, running another recovery scan, choosing the destination now, changing log disclosure defaults, or implementing anything as part of this filing. State: exploratory feature, needs-design, unclaimed; P0 by explicit maintainer request.
design:
Design checkpoint 2026-09-10 — partially agreed; not ready to enable.

CONFIRMED: Maintainer accepted hourly local backups after proposal of encrypted local snapshots and a private bucket in the louiselm cloud project. Hourly is the accepted local cadence; initial daily request is superseded. Maintainer suggested existing infra/booblin and louiselm buckets. No package install, production apply or log upload has occurred.

PROPOSED: Reuse Restic with a local encrypted repository outside ~/.local/state and copy completed snapshots to a dedicated private GCS bucket in project louiselm. Local snapshots continue offline; only successfully copied snapshots protect against laptop/disk loss. Use a user-level OS schedule independent of Neovim, with catch-up after wake and retries for cloud copy. Report local and cloud success/verification timestamps separately. An hourly schedule is not a guarantee during sleep or failed runs. Booblin need not relay laptop backups.

READ-ONLY EVIDENCE: infra/foundation already declares private gs://bartab-infra-backups/restic, a dedicated bucket-scoped identity and Restic 0.19.1 scripts (foundation/backup.tf; foundation/backup/README.md). The louiselm GCP project is ACTIVE, billing enabled, bucket inventory empty as of inspection. SSH to documented bartab.fr:2222 failed authentication; no server/job health verified. Existing foundation uses OpenTofu 1.12.x/google 8.0.0 and bartab-specific state. A LouiseLM stack must respect infra state/lifecycle boundaries, out-of-band secrets and reviewed saved-plan/manual-apply gates. Do not clone object retention/versioning settings without checking Restic delete/prune behavior.

CONFIRMED SOURCE SCOPE: Maintainer accepted all ordinary ACP adapter logs and metadata, including direct/proxy Session logs and connection logs. Native agent histories and recovered USB archives are excluded from this first version. Do not follow arbitrary symlinks; backing up a link is not preservation of its external target. Effective state-root overrides still require implementation-time verification.

IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARY: Prepare an opt-in Restic command and user-level systemd timer independent of Neovim. No installer auto-enables a timer. Restore only into a new empty staging directory, never into live ACP state. Keep local/cloud status distinct, with payload-free CLI/status and failure diagnostics. Retention will not run until cloud-copy acknowledgement and last-good safeguards are implemented and tested. Before live enablement, maintainer must confirm effective paths, restore behavior, failure notification and independent password recovery; cloud deployment follows the infra reviewed-plan gate.

VERIFICATION TO DESIGN: Restic incomplete snapshots and concurrent append/rotation must not be reported as complete coverage. Missing/empty source and failed runs must preserve prior good generations. Isolated deletion, offline/full destination, interruption, retention, corruption and restore-conflict tests, then actual scheduled run and restore drill before closure.

title: Investigate saved ACP fragments for better partial-log reconstruction
description:
## Goal

Investigate whether the saved recovery evidence can improve ACP adapter partial-log reconstruction, without another SSD scan or reboot. Requested for tomorrow morning, 2026-09-10; due time recorded as 09:00 Europe/Paris (07:00 UTC), a morning planning assumption. This Beads date does not launch an automatic job or notification.

## Scope / Inputs

- Ask the maintainer to reconnect the second USB when work begins. Identify General UDisk serial 1609011139261376675028 / filesystem UUID 72C2-CC8D, never a remembered /dev/sdX letter; read evidence without modifying it.
- Latest capture: acp-offline-results-bu27gn8m/scan/{target-spans.bin,target-spans.provenance.jsonl,SCAN-REPORT.json}; boot-kit tools, historical target plan and dedup baseline: offline-recovery-20260909/.
- Earlier evidence on the same key: state-recovery-backup-20260909/RECOVERY/, including adapter-coverage-report.gSomG8/, adapter-combined-partials.VzVhes/, journal/directory archives and saved extent maps. These copies allow this analysis without relying on the original recovery key's mount-dependent recovered-partials shortcut.
- Full incident ledger, output/manifest hashes, device identities and inspected photo evidence are in comment 1491 on louiselm-standalone-recovery-product-ah9s. This operational follow-up is independent of that exploratory product epic, not its implementation or a blocked child.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Verify the relevant manifests and acquisition identity before use. Select a safe scratch/output destination with sufficient space; keep evidence immutable and do not write analysis output onto the incident SSD. Obtain direction if no safe destination is available. No payloads or secrets in status output.
2. Compare the saved 191 ranges / 308,893,975 bytes against historical extent maps and existing partials, prioritizing the 14 targeted unresolved files. Investigate file-offset assembly only where mapping evidence supports it; do not join unrelated physical fragments based on textual resemblance. Preserve exact bytes, hashes, offsets, attribution and uncertain ordering/gaps.
3. Revisit the saved journal/directory evidence for unresolved mappings only within this bounded evidence-analysis pass. Record what was attempted and what remains, rather than starting an unbounded acquisition or unrelated recovery-product work.
4. Produce a per-file before/after report of any demonstrable gains (additional validated complete records, better mapped coverage, or more usable partial assembly), validation checks, unresolved gaps and a justified next action. Distinguish duplicate records, older snapshots, candidate reconstructions and verified original-file completeness. No improvement is a valid result.
5. Keep candidate files separate and clearly labelled partial/uncertain with byte-origin metadata. Preserve both original evidence and live ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/ unchanged; no restoration/import/overwrite without a separate maintainer instruction. If a USB was mounted for the work, finish with verified sync/unmount and tell the maintainer when it can be unplugged.

## Testing / Evidence Caveats

The completed offline scan recognized 151,477 valid records, all duplicates against its baseline, so it yielded zero new complete records. This does not exclude better reconstruction, and does not prove all original logs were recovered or remaining data irrecoverable. Compare candidate outputs to the existing baseline, validate record boundaries and mapped file ordering, and retain reproducible counts/hashes. Do not infer recovery percentages from overlapping output sizes or the historical 951,348,545-byte inventory. Use existing validated readers where practical; any necessary new analysis logic needs focused synthetic correctness checks before use on the saved evidence.

## Out of Scope

New raw SSD reads/scans or acquisition; repairs/fsck/TRIM; formatting; boot changes; automatic live-log imports; modifying evidence; uploading private data; implementing the separate recovery product or daily backups. This filing only records the task; it does not claim it, start analysis, install a scheduler, or grant new sudo access.
close_reason: Saved-evidence investigation complete: 14 mapped files, zero reconstruction gain; 3 unmapped files remain unresolved. 36 tests and evidence replay pass. Lesson/evidence: comment 1495 and USB report. gate:/media/lotso/72C2-CC8D/acp-fragment-analysis-20260910-mo4q/verify_results.py

title: Investigate adapter session-id exposure for the br --actor discipline
description:
Investigate how each adapter/Agent used against this repository exposes its session
identifier to a shell child, and fix the `--actor` discipline accordingly.

Evidence (2026-08-30, opencode session opencode/ses_fad76691affe5is0XoeZAMvtXH):

- opencode exports only `OPENCODE=1`, `OPENCODE_PID`, `OPENCODE_CLIENT=acp` to the
  shell. No session id. The ACP session id exists on the client side of the protocol
  but is not surfaced, so an opencode agent cannot construct an attributable
  `--actor` without asking the maintainer.
- Claude Code exports `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; attribution works unattended.
- Codex reportedly has no issue (maintainer observation); beads records show clean
  `codex/<uuid>` actors.
- One beads record shows a bare-uuid actor `ef5f2ba3-8f5c-4322-9c60-c49dcd1e48a2`
  (no adapter prefix), suggesting at least one other adapter also fails to expose a
  usable session identifier.

Scope: enumerate every adapter that appears as an actor in the .beads record
(claude, codex, opencode, deepseek, others as found); for each, determine from its
docs/source how a session id can be obtained from within a session (env var, state
file, RPC to the parent). This is AX work: AGENTS.md is an AX surface and the
`--actor` rule is unenforceable for adapters that hide their session id.

Outcome: either a documented per-adapter recipe added to AGENTS.md section 2, or
upstream feature requests filed with the offending adapters (tracked as deps or
external refs here), or both.
close_reason: Documented per-adapter actor lookup; ACP live Session is authoritative; no upstream request needed.

title: Redaction test fails when ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED is exported in the developer shell
description:
`logsink::tests::structured_payloads_share_one_redaction_policy` reads `ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED`
from the process environment at runtime. When that variable is exported in the developer's
shell -- which it is for anyone developing against LouiseLM, since the agent definitions set it
-- redaction is disabled and the test correctly finds the secret it asserts is absent, so it
fails.

The suite is green. The failure is the harness observing the developer's environment.

## Evidence

2026-09-01, `~/code/acp-llm-adapter`:

```
$ env | grep ACP_LOG
ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED=1

$ cargo test -q --lib
logsink::tests::structured_payloads_share_one_redaction_policy --- FAILED
test result: FAILED. 121 passed; 1 failed

$ env -u ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED cargo test -q --lib
test result: ok. 122 passed; 0 failed
```

Assertion is `src/logsink/tests.rs:117`.

## Why it matters

AGENTS.md section 1.5 makes the developer establish a baseline with `git stash` and treat any
new FAILED line as theirs to fix. A failure that depends on the shell rather than the tree
poisons that procedure: it is in the baseline, so it is dismissed as pre-existing, and a real
regression in the same test would be dismissed with it.

It also hides work. `cargo test` stops at the first failing target, so this failure prevented
the integration suite from running at all during a baseline -- concealing that
`acp_proxy_stdio::proxy_exits_when_the_wrapped_agent_dies_before_the_handshake` also fails.

## Fix direction

The redaction policy is resolved through `redaction_enabled_fn`, so the seam already exists.
Have the test drive the policy explicitly rather than inheriting the ambient environment.
Do not fix it by unsetting the variable in a test wrapper: `std::env::set_var` and friends are
unsafe under edition 2024 and race across parallel tests, which is the same class of bug.

Audit for siblings: any other test reading `std::env::var` directly has the same defect.

title: Post-Start refusal leaves Running receipt without terminal outcome
description:
The Launch supervisor can append a sequence-1 Start receipt with resulting_state Running, then discover revoked authority or lost Agent identity and dispose the process without a terminal receipt. The broker history can end at Running after the Session is gone; guarded ACK after Start would add another instance.

## Observed
2026-09-26 code inspection, no live Provider request. skills-core/src/launch_supervisor.rs:1297-1302 appends Start; lines 1306-1321 call cleanup_running after post-ACK failure. cleanup_running at lines 1527-1540 disposes process and identity but emits no terminal receipt.

## Root cause
The launch transaction still owns the process after durable Running; the lifecycle owner that records terminal outcomes is constructed only at lines 1323-1343. These failures bypass it.

## Why it was not caught
Existing tests assert refusal and cleanup, not receipt-head reconciliation after post-Start authority loss.

## Acceptance
- Inject a failure after exact Start ACK; history must not remain falsely Running after cleanup.
- Guard handoff/ACK failure obeys the same rule, with no successful launch.
- Cleanup uncertainty poisons identity and never forges terminal proof.

## Not covered
No live exposure demonstrated. Brokered is disabled; existing unguarded branches are affected.
close_reason: gate:skills-core/tests/launch_supervisor.rs:8915 post-Start failure is terminal-receipted; key withdrawal records containment

comments.author: codex/01a0d8f7-90be-7550-8f5b-c3e946cc0855
comments.text: Lesson: after Start ACK, transfer process/capability/identity to the lifecycle owner before post-ACK checks. Owner receipts terminal launch-finalization failure before reporting failure; revoked signing authority records local containment instead of producing a compromised signature. Focused 119/119, full skills-core suite and clippy passed before unrelated in-flight workspace/promotion compile change.

title: Adopt the Close verdict gate: .beads/policy.yaml plus the AGENTS.md rule
description:
Adopt the Close verdict gate: every `br close` on this project must carry exactly one typed
verdict naming what makes the close checkable by someone other than its author.

Ships the gate and its contract together. Landing `policy.yaml` without the AGENTS.md rule
leaves every agent hitting a rejection it cannot interpret.

## Why

Measured across 434 closed issues on 2026-09-01 (`louiselm-22h7` grill-me):

- 433 carry a close reason — compliance with the existing prose rule is total.
- 175 (40%) carry no anchor any other reader could check.
- 13 (3%) cite the `file:line` AGENTS.md section 2 already mandates.

The rule exists and is ignored 97% of the time, so it becomes a gate. Three confirmed
failures traced to act-shaped close reasons: `louiselm-ce6.1.4` -> `louiselm-5y8i` (25 days
inert), `louiselm-psz9` -> `louiselm-oaib.2` (maintainer live acceptance did not catch it),
and `louiselm-park-observer-inert-puha` (live).

## Scope

`.beads/policy.yaml` (new) and `AGENTS.md` section 2. No Lua, no `setup()` surface, no
user-facing config.

### policy.yaml

`close_policy.require_typed_references` with `required_kinds` set to exactly the five Close
verdict kinds, and `allow_bypass: true`.

The five kinds are a **partition, not a menu**: `required_kinds` is a logical OR, so a set
containing a built-in kind like `commit` would be satisfiable by a stray `commit:<sha>`
without ever naming a consumer — and 76 of the 433 existing reasons already cite a sha. Do
not add built-in kinds to the set.

| kind | means |
| --- | --- |
| `consumer:` | production code reaches this, e.g. `consumer:lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:11` |
| `gate:` | a check fails if it stops being true, e.g. `gate:scripts/generate-luacats` |
| `live:` | maintainer confirmed it running, e.g. `live:codex/01a050f8-93e9-7f00-847f-be08e6920e77` |
| `inert:` | not reachable yet — requires a filed follow-up issue |
| `none:` | nothing to verify, e.g. `none:mechanical` |

Values cannot contain whitespace (br's matcher requires a contiguous `kind:value` token).

### AGENTS.md section 2

Replace the "Write close reasons... cite `file:line`" bullet with the verdict rule, plus the
parent propagation convention: **a parent's verdict may be no stronger than its weakest
child's** — if any child closed `inert:`, the parent closes `inert:`. Convention, not a gate:
4 aggregate-laundering instances in 434 closes do not justify a graph-walking gate in `br`,
and a violation is a visible contradiction in the shared record. Note the existing chore
exemption is replaced by `none:` — one token, so "this is mechanical" becomes a claim rather
than an assumption.

## Sequencing

Blocked by the bypass-audit export. With `allow_bypass: true` and no exported audit, the gate
ships with an exit only the closing machine can see.

## Decisions taken, do not relitigate

- A repo-side script over `.beads/issues.jsonl` was rejected: AGENTS.md:70 forbids parsing
  `.beads/*.jsonl`, and it reimplements what `br` does natively.
- `forbid_self_close_after_in_progress`: declined. `louiselm-psz9` was live-confirmed by the
  maintainer and still wrong, so corroboration does not address a referent error.
- `require_acceptance_criteria_satisfied`: declined. House acceptance criteria are numbered
  lists, not `- [ ]` checkboxes, so it would not fire without a house-style change.

## Acceptance

1. `br close` on this project rejects a reason carrying none of the five kinds.
2. `br close` accepts a reason carrying exactly one, including `none:mechanical`.
3. A reason whose only typed reference is `commit:<sha>` is rejected.
4. AGENTS.md section 2 states the five kinds, the follow-up requirement on `inert:`, and the
   parent propagation convention.
5. Verified against the real binary, not by reading the policy schema.
close_reason: Shipped and verified live against br 0.5.7: gate:.beads/policy.yaml plus AGENTS.md section 2 verdict rule. See comment for the acceptance-criteria pass table.

comments.author: claude/ae23ad27-5122-4780-9c81-cbe9080fadba
comments.text:
Verified against the real binary (br 0.5.7) in a throwaway workspace with this repo's exact .beads/policy.yaml:

1. close_reason with no typed kind -> rejected, exit 4, 'Policy violation... requires at least one of: consumer, gate, live, inert, none'
2. close_reason whose only typed ref is commit:<sha> -> rejected, exit 4, same message (built-ins excluded since required_kinds is non-empty)
3. Each of the five kinds individually (consumer:, gate:, live:, inert:, none:) -> accepted, exit 0

Shipped: .beads/policy.yaml (close_policy.require_typed_references.required_kinds: [consumer, gate, live, inert, none], allow_bypass: true) and AGENTS.md section 2 -- replaced the file:line terseness bullet with the verdict-gate rule + parent propagation convention, and updated the routing bullet's chore exemption to point at none:mechanical. No Lua/setup() surface touched; full mini.test suite and stylua pass unaffected. --json

title: Cold Resume fails when prior command audit is unreadable
description:
Cold Resume with unavailable prior command accounting is authorized without commands, but the new launch-posture reader aborts the fresh Session before its final Start acknowledgement. This fails the privileged skills-core CI gate.

## Observed
https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/34875641969/job/104082023673, main 51dc51300f7278282f3406d166cc81a057de83e0, 2026-09-14.
17:53:02 UTC, installed_cold_resume_tests.rs:64:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Storage(Custom { kind: InvalidData, error: "audit entry is malformed" })
Controller at line 186: DurabilityUnavailable.
privileged_installed_cold_resume_unavailable_balance FAILED; exit 101. Finite, uncapped and failed_load scenarios passed.

## Root cause
installed_cold_resume_tests.rs:35 deliberately writes unreadable prior accounting. broker/cold_resume.rs:111 correctly withholds bounded command authority when audit cannot be read. broker/service.rs:568 then calls retain_launch_posture; broker/posture.rs:83 propagates start_receipt_stored_at failure from AuditLog::find, blocking base ACP launch even though command authority is absent. Signed receipt verification and current append durability have already succeeded.

## Why it was not caught
The ordinary cold_resume_uncapped_and_unavailable_accounting_keep_exact_scope test stops after allocation; it never launches the replacement. Prior louiselm-d6fv.6.10.1 covered the audit display bound, not malformed prior accounting.

## Fix direction
At posture evidence consumption, represent unavailable audit observation as missing freshness, hence failed/unverified Runtime posture. Preserve signed receipt verification, audit write durability, strict audit readers and command authority replay/accounting checks.

## Acceptance
Extend the ordinary cold-resume test through the real broker handshake and status response for unavailable bounded accounting; prove red before fixing, green afterward, commands remain absent and runtime evidence is missing. Run existing posture/reconnect/command gates and complete skills-core gates. Run exact failing installed test in disposable VM if available.

## Not covered
No audit repair, migration, relaxed command authorization, or real-Agent desktop acceptance. No hosted rerun without publishing a commit.

title: Declare agent capabilities in louiselm agent configuration
description:
## Goal
Let an agent definition declare what it can do, in typed configuration, so work
can be routed to a capable provider before any session is started.

## Scope
- In scope: a typed `capabilities` field on `louiselm.agent.Definition`,
  validated by the existing closed-schema path; LuaCATS annotation; README
  documentation alongside the existing `agents = { ... }` example; surfacing the
  declared value somewhere a human or script can read it (health output is the
  likely home -- confirm against `lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua` rather than
  assuming).
- Out of scope: reading beads, matching capabilities against issue labels,
  routing, any UI beyond making the declaration legible, and runtime discovery of
  what an agent can actually do.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `agents = { codex = { command = "codex-acp", capabilities = { "image-generation" } } }`
   validates and round-trips to the normalized definition.
2. A malformed value (not a list of non-empty strings) produces a
   `louiselm.agent.ConfigError` with a path, expected shape, and actionable
   message -- collected in the same single pass as other config errors, never
   silently dropped.
3. An absent `capabilities` field remains valid; declaring nothing is the
   default and is not an error.
4. The declared capabilities are readable without starting a session.
5. README documents the field next to the existing agents example, and states
   that capability strings are matched against `needs-capability:*` beads labels
   by the agent selecting work, not by louiselm.
6. No new dependency on beads is introduced anywhere in the plugin.

## Testing
Closed-schema validation coverage in the existing agent-config spec: accepted
shape, each rejected shape, absent-field default, and error-message content.
Whatever surfaces the value gets a headless assertion that the declaration
appears.

## Notes
The closed-schema rule in AGENTS.md section 9 applies: unknown keys are errors,
validate before defaults, collect all errors in one pass. This is a new key on an
existing closed schema, not a free-form stash in the existing `options` table --
`options` is agent-specific passthrough and would make the declaration invisible
to validation.

Reasoning and rejected alternatives are on the parent,
louiselm-capability-routing-m3sc. In particular: declared rather than discovered,
because routing must work before a session exists.
close_reason: Added typed capabilities string[] field to louiselm.agent.Definition (lua/louiselm/agent/config.lua) and to the top-level closed schema (lua/louiselm/config.lua), validated as a dense array of non-empty strings with per-item errors, collected in one pass alongside other config errors. Absent field defaults to nil/valid. Surfaced via :checkhealth louiselm (lua/louiselm/health/init.lua, synchronous, no session start needed). README documents the field next to the existing agents = {...} example and states capability strings are matched against needs-capability:* labels by the agent selecting work, not by louiselm. No beads dependency introduced. Covered by tests/agent/config_spec.lua, tests/schema/setup_spec.lua, tests/health_spec.lua; full mini.test suite (344 cases), stylua --check, and lua-language-server all pass.

title: Add work-tracking section to AGENTS.md and add CLAUDE.md pointer
description:
Add the work-tracking conventions to `AGENTS.md` and make it the loaded entrypoint for every adapter.

`AGENTS.md` is currently 214 lines across 11 sections and never mentions beads, so an agent entering the repo cold cannot learn that beads is the task graph. It is also not auto-loaded by Claude Code, which reads a root `CLAUDE.md` that does not exist here.

## What to do

Insert a new **section 2**, immediately after Project Scope, and renumber the existing sections 2-11 to 3-12. Reading order should be *what this project is* → *how work is found and tracked* → *how code must be written*.

Write it by hand in the file's existing register: terse, imperative, opinionated. Around 15 lines. It must state:

- beads is the task graph for this project; `.beads/` is tracked in git
- file findings as beads before fixing them, including work deliberately deferred
- use `br` and `bv` rather than reading `.beads/*.jsonl` directly
- prefer draining in-progress work before starting new work, even when `bv` scores an unstarted item higher
- never run bare `bv` (it opens a blocking TUI); use the `--robot-*` flags

Point at `br robot-docs` for command syntax instead of duplicating a cheatsheet.

Add one line linking the example workflow document (from the sibling task) and stating plainly that it is **not binding**.

Then add a root `CLAUDE.md` containing only a pointer to `AGENTS.md`. It must stay a pointer — instruction content in both files guarantees silent drift.

## Do not use `br agents --add`

It emits roughly 60 lines of generic beads tutorial inside a `<!-- br-agent-instructions-v1 -->` block. The register clashes with `AGENTS.md`; it teaches syntax already available from `br --help` while saying nothing about this project's conventions; and `br agents --update` overwrites that block, so hand-written conventions placed inside it are destroyed on the next update.

## Acceptance criteria

- `AGENTS.md` has a work-tracking section at position 2, in the file's own voice, and later sections are renumbered consistently with no duplicate or skipped numbers.
- The section references `br robot-docs` rather than inlining command syntax.
- The link to the example workflow document states it is non-binding.
- Root `CLAUDE.md` exists and contains a pointer only, with no instruction content of its own.
- No `<!-- br-agent-instructions-v1 -->` block is present.
close_reason: AGENTS.md section 2 added (sections renumbered 3-12), CLAUDE.md pointer added, docs/example-workflow.md written, triage requirement commented onto qbr.3/qbr.5, all seven memory notes migrated to repo or user-level instructions

title: Sender guard drops pin lease before retained sockets
description: Found while implementing louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4.3. No installed-host exposure claimed because Brokered remains refused.

title: Usage paging drops previous-page input during refresh
description:
Previous-page input is silently discarded while the usage explorer is loading a next page. A quick n then p leaves the user on the next page instead of returning. P2: waiting for each query is a workaround.

## Observed
September 21 desktop QA, coordinator codex/01a0c433-de8c-79d0-9d88-eea2e81235da, installed build 5151b9d, test editor /run/user/1000/nvim.1104584.0, usage buffer 4. Maintainer reported "bs yes, np no". The live snapshot was turns, Codex filter, rows 51-75 of 1669, cursor on aggregate line 9, with n/p mappings present and no query error. That snapshot proves pagination occurred, not the user's exact key timing.

Independent production-history reproduction in clean headless Neovim, through actual mapped keys:
- initial offset0: Rows 1-25 of 1670.
- n, wait for result: offset25, Rows 26-50.
- p, wait: offset0, Rows 1-25.
- feed mapped np without waiting between keys: offset25, Rows 26-50. The p input is lost.
No primary histories or live editor keys changed by the reproduction.

## Root cause
lua/louiselm/ui/usage.lua:243 View:previous_page returns when self.page is nil. View:refresh clears self.page immediately while a read is pending, so the known requested offset cannot be reversed until the result arrives. Cancellation and generation guards already support replacement reads.

## Why not caught
tests/ui/usage_spec.lua delivers the next-page result before calling previous_page. It never reverses an in-flight page request.

## Fix and acceptance
Allow previous_page to use the requested offset during a pending read, preserving disposal and first-page boundaries and existing cancellation/generation guards. Add a regression through the mapped n/p keys: pending next reader is cancelled, offset returns to the prior page, late next-page response cannot overwrite the returned page. Run focused and full Lua/static/generated gates. Live acceptance: maintainer sees the row range return after n then immediate p, without needing to wait between keys. Do not claim this independently reproduced timing defect explains the original report until the maintainer confirms.

## Boundaries
Do not redesign paging or queue speculative forward input. Cursor placement and clarity of the totals/page indicator remain separate observations, not diagnosed defects. Keep open for exact live retest.
