title: Beads refuses live tracker reads with header-only WAL
description:
# Beads read-only recovery refusal — 2026-09-18

Incident report for `louiselm-n897n`. Authorized live recovery applied;
normal committed-write/export verification is in progress. No binary upgrade.
Actor: `codex/01a0b350-de3e-7020-9ac9-615b56e88bb6`, verified through
`session.identity()`.

## Observed

The installed `/home/lotso/.cargo/bin/br` is 0.6.0 at
`0dcd837098e922c71f8f53bc1fda13e8b1aa9b25`, linked to FrankenSQLite 0.4.0.
Database-backed reads and tracker writes refuse the LouiseLM database:

```text
Database error: database is busy (recovery in progress)
```

Mutations additionally refuse because pending sync-merge state cannot be
inspected under database-family authority. Reproduce without automatic sync:

```sh
br show louiselm-n897n --no-auto-import --no-auto-flush --json
br doctor --quick --json
```

The doctor errors are `sync.merge_pending` and
`db.read_only_open_observational`. Namespace identity and database integrity
checks pass. No live database file holder was reported by `lsof`.
`br show --no-db` remains usable for reading the existing export; it is not
permission to bypass the mutation gate or rewrite that export.

## Retained evidence

- Verified pre-sync backup:
  `/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-sync-backup.20260918.zeOpC2/`.
  Its `SHA256SUMS` covers the online SQLite backup, dirty export, and five
  untracked CI evidence files.
- Private diagnostic directory:
  `/var/tmp/louiselm-beads-diagnosis.7RL0nG/`.
  `family/` retains byte copies of the live database, WAL, SHM, certificates,
  namespace records, and migration-state sidecar. The other directories hold
  isolated test cases; no tracker initialization was performed.
- Live database SHA-256, unchanged throughout this investigation:
  `2e802a48f4361343538cced0ef9c32674f96fe5b5499a0d57b2c267b0c4f352d`.
- Live export SHA-256, unchanged throughout this investigation:
  `5fbf5e5a903a9360a31c73822c1cbbfb8539cebc6ad70cfad5823d566ecf07f0`.
- Live WAL: exactly 32 bytes, a header with no room for a WAL frame; SHA-256
  `f2752eb82e540a14ed6eefa88a0de05616d7818d40b5e0cb158781a3c316559d`.

## Discriminating checks

Each read used the same installed binary and the same copied main database.
Initial minimal variants omitted namespace records; the complete-family case
then reproduced the failure with those records and migration state included.

| Copied state | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Main database only | Read succeeds |
| Main database plus 32-byte WAL | Busy recovery |
| Main database, WAL, and certificates | Busy recovery |
| Main database, WAL, and SHM | Busy recovery |
| Complete database family | Busy recovery |
| Main database and certificates, without WAL | Read succeeds |
| Complete family, only WAL moved into private quarantine | Three repeated reads and rollback-only write probe succeed; doctor flags orphan SHM |
| Same copy, SHM also moved into private quarantine | Full doctor exits 0, `ok: true`, no failed checks |

The final copied-family doctor confirms both integrity checks, all 1,194 issue
records matching the export, zero dirty issues, no pending import/export, and a
successful rollback-only write probe. Main database and export hashes remain
exactly those above. No committed-write/flush cycle has been tested, so this
rehearsal is not proof that the installed engine cannot recur after later writes.

Running the original SQLite online-backup command against the readable
main-only copy created a zero-byte WAL and an SHM, but subsequent `br` reads
still succeeded. Thus the backup command alone did not reproduce this failure.
The precise event that made the live family unreadable is not established.

## Diagnosis and related prior work

The failure is isolated to the installed engine's admission of this header-only
WAL, not evidence of damaged issue rows or an active writer. SHM and certificate
removal are not required to reproduce the read failure.

Local engine source has the read-only bootstrap calling
`set_journal_mode(Wal)` in `fsqlite-core-0.4.0/src/connection.rs:77975`; the pager's
implementation at `fsqlite-pager-0.4.0/src/pager.rs:14533` enters maintenance
admission. The adjacent beads_rust checkout documents a related published fix
under `beads_rust-otrgz` / `beads_rust-nx2sh` in
`docs/reliability/ENGINE_OPERATING_MODEL.md` and `UPGRADE_LOG.md`. Its newer
0.4.4 qualification does not prove that a replacement binary fixes this exact
snapshot; no such binary was tested or installed here.

## Reviewed recovery procedure

The maintainer explicitly approved applying this reversible recovery:

1. Recheck live holders, current hashes, and the WAL's exact 32-byte size.
   Any new WAL frame or intervening write invalidates this rehearsal.
2. Retain the complete live family and move only `beads.db-wal` and
   `beads.db-shm` into a new recoverable quarantine under exclusive tracker
   access. Keep the main database, certificates, namespace and migration state.
3. Require a green full doctor and unchanged main/export bytes. Then record this
   defect and the backup in Beads, flush normally, and repeat fresh-process
   reads and doctor after that actual committed write/export.
4. If refusal recurs, stop and validate a build containing the published engine
   fix on the retained failing copy before considering installation.

Do not rebuild from JSONL, force-import, delete sidecars, replace the live
database, or run a broad repair. Those actions are unnecessary for the
demonstrated recovery and risk losing audit history or local-only records.

## Live recovery receipt

At `2026-09-18T13:51:48Z`, with the existing workspace writer,
database-family writer, and database-opener locks held exclusively and
non-blocking, the exact rehearsed database/export/WAL hashes and 32-byte WAL
size were checked again. No database file holder was reported. The complete
family plus exports/configuration was copied and byte-compared under the locks.

Recovery directory:
`/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-beads-recovery.20260918.9RWlMK/`.
`family/` preserves the pre-recovery files; `quarantine/` holds the original
`beads.db-wal` and `beads.db-shm`, moved without overwriting anything. No file was
deleted. Main database and export were byte-identical immediately after the move.

The first live full doctor returned `ok: true`, zero failures/warnings, both
integrity checks passing, all 1,194 records matching the export, and a successful
rollback-only write probe. Repeated fresh-process reads and a subsequent quick
doctor passed. Later normal diagnostics/coordination changed database bytes and
recreated engine sidecars; the export and issue timestamp remained unchanged.
Do not claim that the physical database hash stays fixed across normal tracker
operations. The retained pre-recovery family remains available for comparison.

## Tracking and acceptance

P1: database-backed tracker operations are unavailable. This report is the
pending bug description because the same access gate blocks issue creation.
An attributable `br create --description-file` attempt using this report exited
6 with `SYNC_CONFLICT`; no bug ID was created and no flush was attempted.
Duplicate searches through `br --no-db search -a` found no matching LouiseLM
issue; `louiselm-br-tracker-divergence-0tjz0` concerns a different database/export
divergence and is not this failure.

Acceptance: restore the maintainer's actual read/update/flush workflow without
losing issue records, comments, dependencies or audit history; verify repeated
fresh-process reads and doctor after a committed update; retain the failure and
recovery evidence. Keep the live defect open until maintainer confirmation.

Neither PR #11 nor GitHub, GitLab or local main was changed by this diagnosis.
The maintainer reserves merging PR #11. Synchronization remains unfinished.

title: Cold Park resume leaves durable Run cold_parked
description:
A cold-Parked Run can be loaded and reported as resumed in the UI while the capture-service record remains cold_parked. The durable state is not finalized, so the same Run remains resumable and its expiry lease can still reap claims while the reconstructed Session is active.

## Observed

Manual QA round on 2026-08-31, current HEAD cd66b47, Session claude/769df194-9e9c-4604-8370-3f0b2bde9c53.

The user observed the cold Park resume notification and the resumed Session accepted work. The durable record remained at:

Path: /tmp/louiselm-qa-state.CqS0UQ/louiselm/workflow/runs/98a5046c-5dd3-4c70-8eda-e7b872f4da72.json

Structural record: state=cold_parked, revision=3, load_session=true, resume_attempt=null, session_id=claude/769df194-9e9c-4604-8370-3f0b2bde9c53.

The matching command XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/louiselm-qa-state.CqS0UQ capture-service run list still returned state=cold_parked after the UI resume. The ACP log for the Session contains three completed prompts.

## Symptoms

- UI reports cold Park resumed and the loaded Session is usable.
- The durable Run remains listed as a cold Park and retains its expiry lease.
- A second operator can potentially resume the same Run, or expiry can release claims for the already resumed local Run.

## Root cause

Chat:resume_park in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4181-4230 lists the Run, loads the ACP Session, reconstructs a local Workflow Run, calls Run:accept_resume, and reports success. It never calls RunClient:resume or RunClient:finalize_resume.

The intended service mutation path already exists in lua/louiselm/workflow/resume_controller.lua:94-158 and routes to capture-service/src/run_socket.rs:208-230; capture-service/src/runs.rs:704-790 transitions cold_parked to resuming and then active.

## Why it was not caught

tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:329-379 stubs WorkflowService.list and API load_session, then asserts only that the local owner_run claims, generated_work, and status are reconstructed. It does not assert a capture-service resume/finalize mutation or that a parked Run disappears from run list. The existing resume_controller tests cover the unused controller in isolation.

## Fix direction

Wire Chat:resume_park through the existing ResumeController and its RunClient, or make an equivalent narrow service resume/finalize call around the existing load path. Preserve the two-phase behavior: mark resuming before ACP session/load, finalize active only after successful reconstruction, and finalize cold_parked on failure.

## Acceptance

- A real cold Park resume changes the durable capture-service Run from cold_parked to active after successful session/load.
- The Run is not returned by the cold Park list after successful resume and cannot be resumed twice.
- Failed session/load finalizes back to cold_parked with its lease and claims intact.
- A regression test covers Chat:resume_park through the service mutation boundary, not only local Run reconstruction.

## Not covered

The Run record observed in this round reported claims=[]; claim restoration itself was therefore not independently proven. The durable-state defect is independent of claim count.

title: Permission pickers from two sessions can still collide
description:
The permission queue added in c639f95 (louiselm-4wx) is per session. vim.ui.select is a process-wide resource: two attached chat sessions that each reach a permission request at the same time still open two pickers, and an async provider such as the Snacks picker tears the first one down. That reproduces the louiselm-4wx failure across sessions - one request answered cancelled without the user acting, the other left unanswered and blocking its agent.

Not fixed with louiselm-4wx because the narrowest boundary for the reported single-session deadlock was the session, and a process-wide picker queue means module-level mutable state, which AGENTS.md section 7 warns against.

Repro sketch: attach two sessions, prompt both so each hits an ask-human permission in the same window, and observe both pickers.

Options to weigh:
- Serialize decision UI in louiselm.ui.chat across views (the chat controller already owns every view and the diff review, so it has a clear owner and lifecycle for the queue).
- Or serialize in louiselm.ui.picker, which also covers the session, skill, and agent pickers, but introduces a module singleton.

Whatever the layer, the invariant is the same as louiselm-4wx: at most one decision UI open at a time, and every ACP permission request answered exactly once.
close_reason: Fixed in 0ed18d0. Chose the chat controller over louiselm.ui.picker: it already owns every view and the diff review, so the queue has a clear owner and lifecycle instead of a module singleton (AGENTS.md section 7), and it covers reviews as well as pickers. lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua now queues decisions across all views (queue_decision/pump_decisions/open_decision), releases the slot exactly once per decision, and cancels what it cannot host: chat disposal, an event delivered to a torn-down view, and a select provider that throws. lua/louiselm/ui/diff/init.lua adds a BufWipeout handler because review buffers are bufhidden=wipe - navigating away used to abandon the request unanswered, which would have stalled the queue. Tests: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'opens one permission decision at a time across sessions', 'cancels permission decisions still queued when the chat is disposed', 'cancels a permission request delivered after disposal'; tests/ui/diff_spec.lua 'cancels the permission request when its review buffer is wiped'. chat_spec now restores vim.schedule/vim.ui.select in post_case, because a failing expectation skipped a test's own restore and broke MiniTest itself. Full suite 196 cases, stylua --check, lua-language-server all clean. Not covered: pickers louiselm opens for its own commands (session options, skills, agents) are still unqueued and can collide with a permission decision.

Tracks `u5no`; current `skills-core/README.md` manual ceremony and C14 setup apply.

two-token/SSH-Recovery wording. Activation/witness fixes: `7da0254`, `df353e3`,

1. Prepare one harmless complete Skill candidate, read its trusted Dossier,
   and record exact package digest in the disposable protected store.
2. Admit using the installed tool and current Primary; observe touch/PIN.
3. Witness to a dedicated protected test remote/branch; verify the exact remote
   bytes/readback before activation. Activate and inspect Generation status.
4. Repeat activation of that exact current digest; confirm its original pin
   timestamp/lineage does not acquire another entry. Verify with the token absent.
5. Against only the disposable witness setup, make the remote unavailable and
   attempt witnessing a new Generation: failure must leave the old active
   Generation unchanged. Retired-Primary refusal is checked after C14 rotation.

Expect: actual physical authority, remote witness and active digest agree;
retry is idempotent and a witness failure cannot authorize local activation.
Failure: no required touch, activation without remote evidence, changed pin time
on same-digest retry, or loss of prior active state.
Evidence: public `generation status`/`list`, exact digests, protected remote
commit/readback and observed token interaction. Validate current installed CLI
syntax via `--help` before filling fixture paths. Crash-boundary rollback and

title: Grok x_search fetch exhausts quota and ends Session in Error
description:
A simple LouiseLM prompt asking Grok to fetch publicly searchable posts with x_search can expand into unrelated skill/file/web research, exhaust the Grok free usage allowance, and leave the Session showing Error instead of a clear bounded rate-limit outcome. This blocks the planned Grok-based tweet-fetch workflow.

## Observed

- Session: grok/01a05666-bf8c-7c02-b6f5-e14e3f6c8726
- Date: 2026-08-31
- Proxy session log: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a05666-bf8c-7c02-b6f5-e14e3f6c8726/log.jsonl
- Prompt frame: line 6 requested only x_search, JSONL output, and @doodlestein.
- Grok then read local tweet-fetch/tweet-corpus skills (lines 93-99), searched the repository for x_search (lines 273-292), and made multiple web/API fallback calls.
- The turn completed with stop_reason=rate_limit, modelCalls=7, totalTokens=272915, at line 602.
- The exact terminal error at line 605 was: {"code":-32003,"message":"Rate limited","data":{"message":"API error (status 429 Too Many Requests): subscription:free-usage-exhausted ... tokens (actual/limit): 518216/500000 ...","promptUsage":{"modelCalls":7,"numTurns":7}}}.
- The proxy then recorded exit code 137 at line 606.

## Symptoms

- User sees the Grok Session enter Error while attempting the x_search fetch.
- No JSONL tweet result is produced.
- A small fetch request consumes the remaining free Grok allowance through repeated model/tool calls.
- Exit 137 obscures the primary rate-limit cause as a secondary cleanup effect.

## Root cause

The upstream Grok run hit its free-usage limit after seven model calls; this is confirmed by the structured -32003 Rate limited response and stop_reason=rate_limit. The later exit 137 is cleanup after the failed turn, not evidence of an independent Grok crash.

The reason Grok broadened the narrow x_search request into skills, repository, and web/API research is not yet established. The prompt included the repository AGENTS.md resource, and Grok chose to inspect related skills and fallback sources; whether that is expected Grok behavior, an instruction/context interaction, or an ACP presentation issue needs a controlled reproduction.

## Why it was not caught

Previous Grok QA exercised ordinary prompts and unsolicited skills-reload responses, not a tool-heavy x_search request with a free-usage boundary. Automated ACP tests do not model Grok model-call budgeting, tool fallback behavior, rate-limit responses, or post-rate-limit process cleanup.

## Fix direction

- Reproduce with a minimal prompt/context and a deliberately bounded x_search request; record the first tool call and model-call count.
- Ensure rate-limit responses remain visible as an actionable rate-limited Session outcome, without presenting cleanup exit 137 as the primary failure.
- Define a safe, bounded x_search fetch recipe that forbids unrelated skill/repository/web fallback work and caps windows/results before requesting output.
- Determine whether LouiseLM should avoid injecting repository guidance for this data-only request, or whether Grok must honor the narrow task despite that context.

## Acceptance

- A narrow x_search fetch either returns the requested JSONL or stops at a visible, actionable rate-limit state without runaway retries/fallbacks.
- The user-facing diagnostic identifies the upstream quota exhaustion and does not misattribute the failure to exit 137.
- Regression coverage records the observed ordering: tool/model calls -> rate-limit -> prompt completion/error -> process cleanup.

## Not covered

- The free-usage allowance cannot be restored by LouiseLM and was not independently verified outside the ACP response.
- No fix is included in this filing.
- Whether the same expansion occurs for other Grok tools or other ACP Agents is untested.

title: Support Grok interactive ACP reverse requests
description:
Support Grok Build’s vendor-specific blocking agent-to-client extension requests `x.ai/ask_user_question` and `x.ai/exit_plan_mode`, including their ACP wrapped wire forms `_x.ai/ask_user_question` and `_x.ai/exit_plan_mode`.

title: Disposal during preparing poisons the shared turn recorder
description:
A synchronous state_changed observer disposing a Session during preparing queues an outcome before its initial turn row. SQLite rejects the foreign key, and the immutable failed queue blocks later prompts for every Session in that registry.

Observed 2026-09-07 in the uncommitted lus3 implementation, actor codex/01a07bb4-c41e-7010-8332-d9a6ff731e2c. Reproduction script: /tmp/lus3-verify.xTbnCN95/preparing_disposal.lua. Run nvim --headless --noplugin -u ./tests/minimal_init.lua -c "luafile /tmp/lus3-verify.xTbnCN95/preparing_disposal.lua" -c "qa!". Neovim reports E5113 despite process exit 0; assert output is the verdict.

Exact output: recording_error.code=storage, recording_pending=true, disposed=disposed; assertion: Disposal observer poisoned the shared recorder.

Reproduce through public Session APIs: create two ready mock Sessions in one registry with a temporary usage_directory. Subscribe the first to state_changed and call dispose immediately when status is preparing. Subscribe the second to recording_changed, then submit the first prompt and wait for a terminal recording notification. Expect no error and no pending writes; observed storage failure with pending writes. Initial attempt incorrectly inspected pending before scheduled work began; corrected reproduction waits for recording_changed.

Root cause: lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:953 emits preparing before append(prepared) at :956. The observer calls dispose, which appends its outcome immediately. Queue drain inserts outcome first under foreign_keys=ON.

Acceptance: a deterministic public-API regression proves initial attribution precedes every observer-triggered Cancellation/Disposal observation, no ACP prompt dispatches after Disposal, and another Session can record/dispatch normally afterward. Also preserve callback-at-most-once and main-loop behavior.

Fix direction: establish the initial queued fact before publishing the reentrant preparing event; check cancellation as the sibling path. Do not weaken foreign keys or drop failed records.

Not fixed by this execution because another execution under the same Session actor is actively editing lifecycle/recording/tests. Coordinate ownership before editing those files.
close_reason: gate:tests/session/recording_spec.lua Queue prepared row before preparing observers; Cancellation/Disposal and next-Session regressions pass. Lesson in comment.

comments.text: Red: public preparing observers calling cancel or dispose both produce storage failure and poison witness Session. Green: queue PreparedTurn before publishing preparing; both regressions preserve zero dispatch for the first attempt and successful next Session. Lesson destination: this comment; establish owned durable-write order before invoking reentrant lifecycle observers. Tests: tests/session/recording_spec.lua (3 pass).

title: QA: Park observer wiring
description:
# Manual QA review — Park observer wiring

Working file for the current round. You run the steps; I update this file from
the evidence. Untracked on purpose.

**Build under test:** `43f61fb` (`fix(workflow): wire budget Park observer`) and
`009e945` (`fix(workflow): normalize null Run fields`).
**Origin:** `louiselm-park-observer-inert-puha` found that the production chat
never constructed `ParkObserver`, so a durable service Park could not reach the
editor. The automated test covers the scheduled socket callback; this round
checks the real installed plugin, capture service, and editor presentation.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Durable Park snapshot reaches the running editor and shows bounded accounting | **passed** — `:LouiselmResumePark` resumed Run `8981f800-c2ea-457f-8238-13e561246679` after `009e945`; `run list` no longer contains it |
| 2 | A budget-exhaustion Park cancels its matching live Run | blocked — no public workflow-runner path creates a live budgeted Run |

## Setup

1. Refresh the installed `louiselm.nvim` from this checkout by your normal
   plugin-manager/install workflow, then start a **new Neovim process**. The
   currently running editor resolves the plugin at
   `~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim`, so it cannot test
   `43f61fb` until refreshed.
2. In that new editor, run `:checkhealth louiselm` if available. The capture
   service must be running; from a terminal, `systemctl --user is-active
   louiselm-capture` must print `active`.
3. Use a fresh disposable LouiseLM Session. Do not Park a Session containing
   work you need to preserve: cold Park is recoverable but lossy.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- `:LouiselmResumePark` is what establishes the Run-socket client and therefore
  constructs the observer. `:LouiselmPark` alone does not exercise this fix.
- Case 1 verifies the real socket-to-editor boundary, but a manually requested
  cold Park is not a budget-exhaustion Park. It cannot close Case 2.

## Cases

### 1. Durable Park snapshot reaches the running editor and shows bounded accounting

Exercises `43f61fb` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4363` and the service Run
socket. This is a single ordered sequence; do not reset between its steps.

Steps:

1. Open a fresh chat with `:LouiselmChat`, create a disposable Session with
   `:LouiselmSessionNew`, and send a short prompt such as `Reply READY only.`
   Wait for the reply so the Session has an ACP Session id.
2. Run `:LouiselmPark` while that disposable Session is current. Wait for
   `louiselm: Session cold-Parked`.
3. Run `:LouiselmResumePark`. At the cold-Park picker, select the disposable
   Run created in step 2. Wait for the resume attempt to finish.
4. Inspect `:messages` and note the exact `louiselm: budget Park:` notice. Do
   not paste its content into a prompt.

Expect: before the picker finishes, the editor receives the durable Run
snapshot and shows one bounded notice of the form
`louiselm: budget Park: generated work 0/1, reserved 0, pending 0, mutation none`.
The picker then resumes the disposable Session and reports
`cold Park resumed (recoverable, lossy)`.

Failure signature: no bounded Park notice; an error beginning `could not
connect to Run service`; a notice containing prompt, token, argument, or raw
payload content; or the resumed Session fails to attach.

## Evidence check

After step 2, and again after step 3, run:

```sh
louiselm-capture run list
```

Pass evidence after step 2 is a record for the disposable Run with
`"state":"cold_parked"` and `"generated_work":{"ceiling":1,"consumed":0,"reserved":0}`.
After a successful resume, that record is absent from `run list`. The command
proves durable service state; the bounded notice in `:messages` is the only
evidence of editor presentation.

### Retest after F1

Refresh the installed plugin with `009e945`, start a new Neovim process, then
run `:LouiselmResumePark` and select Run
`8981f800-c2ea-457f-8238-13e561246679`. Expect the picker to open with no
`Park snapshot is malformed` message, followed by the bounded Park notice and
the normal cold-Park resume result. This reuses the durable record from the
failed attempt; do not create a second disposable Park first.

## Cleanup when the round closes

The disposable Session is intentionally cold-Parked/resumed. Do not use it for
real work. If resume fails, leave the durable Park intact for evidence and tell
me its Run id.

## Reporting back

Send the case number, the relevant `:messages` lines, the redacted `run list`
record (Run id is fine; never include capability data), and anything surprising.
I will inspect the evidence, update this file, and route any finding before
asking for a retest.

## Findings this round

**F1 — JSON `null` optional Run fields reject the real service snapshot** (`louiselm-y39u`, fixed in `009e945`, retest passed).
Case 1 Session `codex/01a05d64-ece8-77a0-998c-5e44f3be40f1` initially reported `louiselm: Park snapshot is malformed`. The authoritative snapshot for Run `8981f800-c2ea-457f-8238-13e561246679` contains `"triggering_mutation_id":null`; `vim.json.decode` turns it into `vim.NIL`. `009e945` normalizes it at the Run-socket boundary. The maintainer then resumed the exact durable Park successfully; `louiselm-capture run list` confirms the Run is no longer resumable.

## Round summary

Case 1 passed after the regression fix. The original test suite missed F1 because
its Run snapshots were hand-built Lua tables with omitted optional fields rather
than a decoded real service payload. Case 2 remains blocked: the product has no
public workflow-runner path that creates a live budgeted Run to exhaust.
close_reason: QA passed: live durable and budget Park cases

title: Design persistent ACP permission UX
description:
## Goal

Decide and implement how louiselm should remember ACP permission choices such as Allow for Session and Allow Commands Starting With a command prefix.

## Current state

The chat UI displays permission options supplied by the ACP adapter and forwards the selected optionId. louiselm does not persist those choices itself. ACP defines allow_always as remembering the choice but does not prescribe the storage mechanism.

## Scope

- Grill and document the desired UX and trust model for once, session, workspace, command-prefix, and permanent approvals.
- Decide whether louiselm, the ACP adapter, or both own persistence and enforcement.
- Define storage location, scope/keying, revocation/editing UX, and behavior across sessions, adapters, workspaces, and restarts.
- Implement the agreed behavior with tests and documentation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Permission choices have clear, truthful lifetime/scope semantics.
- Persisted rules cannot silently broaden command or file scopes.
- Users can inspect and revoke remembered rules.
- Behavior is covered by deterministic tests and documented for headless and chat consumers.

## Out of scope

- Changing ACP protocol semantics or adding adapter-specific compatibility shims before the UX decision.
close_reason: Implemented exact workspace-and-adapter permission memory, atomic persistent state, option-kind replay, headless list/revoke APIs, file lifetime selection, and :LouiselmPermissions

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
Agreed UX direction from grill session:

- louiselm owns remembered permission decisions; no user-configurable rule object initially.
- Default scope is current workspace + current ACP adapter.
- Command rules match exact argv prefixes; no shell strings, regexes, or substring matching.
- Persist state in a user-level file under Neovim stdpath("state"), never the project repo.
- Add :LouiseLmPermissions to inspect and revoke remembered rules.
- allow_once/reject_once are not saved; allow_session is memory-only for the ACP session; allow_always/reject_always are persisted.
- Commands and file edits have separate rule types.
- If a later adapter request lacks a compatible option kind, fail closed and ask the user again; never infer from labels.

title: Grill-me needed: what proves durable ACP recovery to the Control broker?
description:
Do not resolve this architecture question in passing; confirm the trusted recovery-evidence source with the maintainer before implementing controller-loss disposal in louiselm-qbr.5.1.2.2.

Question: what authenticated, durable record proves ACP recovery exists for one broker-owned Session, and what must the broker retain or verify before permitting disposal of the old tree?

Evidence: skills-core/src/broker/authorization.rs persists launch authorization and command scope only. skills-core/src/broker/installed.rs owns the supervisor connection but has no ACP recovery registration or lookup. capture-service/src/runs.rs RunSession/Run hold ACP identity, working directory and loadSession support, but no binding to the broker launch authorization or signed receipt head. launch_protocol::ControllerLossDisposition::Recoverable accepts an opaque reference; inventing a reference alone cannot establish recoverability. The parent requires projection compromise not to change authorization, so an Attention acknowledgement cannot serve as recovery proof.

Decision threads: broker-retained authenticated recovery record versus verified reference to existing durable Run data; exact Session/Run/Agent/ACP identity binding; which trusted controller registers evidence and how; retained native Agent state and workspace lifetime; controller loss before registration; replay/restart and stale evidence; capture-service outage or compromise; preserving capture-service ownership of Run projections while broker retains lifecycle authority.

The implementation can continue independently on lifecycle authorization and ordered Attention delivery. Record the confirmed source and route the resulting recovery integration work before closing this question.
design:
Confirmed by the maintainer in codex/01a0916a-ecfb-7030-9af3-f41a17b4bbab: final shared-understanding summary accepted with "yes i confirm". This resolves the architecture question, not implementation or live recovery acceptance.

1. Ownership: the Control broker durably owns recovery evidence. Capture-service continues owning Run records and Attention, without recovery authority.
2. Registration: only the controller authorized for that launch submits ACP identity and recovery metadata. The broker validates the exact authorized launch, Session, Run, configured Agent and ACP identity binding. Trusted launch-supervisor evidence proves storage retention; a controller assertion alone is insufficient. Agents, tools and capture-service cannot register or replace the evidence.
3. Threshold: a durable recovery point must exist. An ACP identifier or advertised loadSession alone is insufficient. Recovery is potentially lossy, need not include in-flight work, and a later load may fail.
4. Startup: ordinary work may begin before recovery is ready, with recovery visibly unavailable until valid evidence is durably acknowledged. Runs explicitly requiring cold recovery must satisfy it at admission. Agents without loadSession remain usable outside that requirement.
5. Retention: preserve explicitly identified Agent recovery files and required workspace, not unrestricted private-home contents, credentials or live capability grants. Each supported Agent needs a verified recovery layout; unknown layouts cannot claim cold recovery. Retained data must be protected against reuse of the old Session host identity. Follow existing Park expiry and Disposal/Forensics rules.
6. Failure handling: without valid evidence, record abnormal loss rather than recoverable cold Park. Restart/replay cannot revive stale evidence or transfer authority. Capture-service outage or compromise cannot alter the decision; delivery retries from the broker durable Attention outbox. Preserve freeze/revoke -> durable recovery decision and Attention enqueue -> authenticated disposal settlement ordering. Resume remains operator-only through a fresh authorized Session and cannot widen the original envelope.

Vocabulary delta: No change. Implementation refinement only; no vocabulary promotion authorized or required.
close_reason: inert:louiselm-qbr.5.1.2.2 Maintainer-confirmed broker-owned recovery evidence design recorded; retention .5 and registration .6 filed, settlement/status updated. Vocabulary unchanged; implementation remains open.

comments.author: codex/01a0916a-ecfb-7030-9af3-f41a17b4bbab
comments.text: Maintainer confirmed the complete summary in codex/01a0916a-ecfb-7030-9af3-f41a17b4bbab. Decision preserved in this issue design; vocabulary unchanged. Routed retention to louiselm-qbr.5.1.2.5, registration/admission to .6, settlement to .2, readiness presentation to .4, and broader retention integration to louiselm-d6fv.5.5. Lesson: recovery locators and advertised protocol support are not durable recovery proof; preserve the separate controller/broker/supervisor/projection trust boundaries. No standing instruction change warranted. Closing design only, not implementation or live acceptance.

title: Clarify transcript configuration as optional Provenance integration
description:
## Goal

Make the transcript UX match the actual ownership model.

Live chat transcripts are already captured by louiselm for every Session without configuration. The existing agent-level transcript_layout setting is only used to locate Agent-owned historical transcript files for Provenance/session inspection. Calling that setting transcript configuration makes it appear to enable or control the main transcript feature, which is confusing when users see transcripts working with no setting.

## Scope

- Clarify user-facing documentation and schema descriptions that live transcript capture is automatic.
- Reframe transcript_layout as an optional historical transcript locator / Provenance integration.
- Keep the explicit layout mapping and no-implicit-filesystem-discovery safety boundary.
- Do not add compatibility aliases or change transcript capture behavior.

## Acceptance

1. A user can understand from the config schema/docs that no transcript setting is needed for normal live chat.
2. The purpose and limitation of transcript_layout are explicit: it enables best-effort lookup of Agent-owned historical Session transcripts for Provenance.
3. Existing live transcript capture and explicit configured-layout lookup tests remain passing.
4. Any public LuaCATS/schema annotation changes regenerate doc/api.md.

## Evidence

- lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua creates an in-memory Transcript for every attached ChatView and exports it independently.
- lua/louiselm/session/locator.lua only resolves on-disk Agent transcripts when a layout is explicitly configured.
- lua/louiselm/config.lua currently describes transcript_layout as resolving historical Sessions, but the setting remains easy to misread as the switch for transcripts generally.
close_reason: Clarified transcript ownership and optional Provenance lookup in schema/help/API docs; 747 MiniTest cases and all quality gates pass.

comments.text: Implemented by updating the schema description, Definition LuaCATS field, generated doc/api.md, and generated doc/louiselm.txt. The key lesson is that transcript_layout is a historical Agent-owned transcript locator for Provenance, not a switch for louiselm's always-on live transcript capture. No standing AGENTS.md rule or unresolved design question warranted.

title: Grill-me needed: should qbr.3's workflow execution engine be undeferred to unblock qbr.3.2.6.5, or should its acceptance criteria drop runtime enforcement until qbr.3 lands?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; run a focused louiselm-grill-me session before implementation of qbr.3.2.6.5 continues.

Question: qbr.3.2.6.5's acceptance criteria require a runtime that walks workflow stage transitions and recognizes back-edges and work-producing skill invocations as they happen, so it can charge the per-Run generated-work budget at the moment they fire. That runtime does not exist anywhere in the codebase, and the feature that owns it — louiselm-qbr.3 ("the full workflow execution engine") — is status: deferred. Should qbr.3 be undeferred now so this task can build the stage-transition executor properly, or should qbr.3.2.6.5's acceptance criteria be rewritten to drop back-edge/skill-runtime enforcement (AC1 and AC4) until qbr.3 lands on its own schedule?

Context/evidence:
- qbr.3.2's own scope notes name "the full workflow execution engine" as explicitly out of scope, owned by qbr.3.
- qbr.3's closed child (comment 265) already settled representation: workflows persist as graphs of discovered SKILL.md documents, frontmatter declares named outcomes mapped to next-skill transitions, the model selects an outcome, LouiseLM validates/records/follows it. That is a real design decision, just never implemented as running code.
- lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua only supervises ACP Sessions (create/cancel/park/dispose/emergency_stop) — it has no notion of "current stage", "outcome taken", or "next stage".
- lua/louiselm/workflow/validate.lua and schema.lua fully parse and validate Generator shape (generates.max, back-edge + max-iterations + automatic resolver) at document-validation time, but nothing downstream ever reads those fields again — confirmed by grep across the non-test, non-.deps Lua tree.
- capture-service's ledger (capture-service/src/runs.rs) is otherwise close to Generator-shape-agnostic (GeneratedWorkBudget/PendingGeneration/GeneratedOutput are generic over kind/units) but validate_reservation (runs.rs:1003-1013) hardcodes kind == "beads_issue" and units == 1, which is the one place today that forbids a multi-unit skill-level reservation.
- The dead codex session (codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee) filed 3.2.6.5 as the task that "closes the parent only after all preceding slices are green" without flagging this gap; its claim went abandoned (486m, past the 480m threshold) before this was discovered.

Threads worth pulling:
1. Is "walk stage transitions and detect a taken outcome" small enough to build as a narrow, qbr.3.2.6.5-scoped primitive without it becoming qbr.3's engine by another name — or is that a distinction without a difference once written?
2. If qbr.3 is undeferred: does that pull in qbr.3.1 and qbr.3.4 (still-deferred siblings) too, or can the transition-walking piece be built without their unresolved questions (grill-me support for challenger passes, Assessment)?
3. If AC1/AC4 are dropped from 3.2.6.5: does the parent (qbr.3.2.6) get to close on a ledger that only ever enforces the br-create Generator, with back-edge/skill Generators left as a named, tracked gap — or does the parent's own acceptance criterion ("every automatic Generator consumes the same Run budget") block closing it either way?
4. Is there a cheaper interim enforcement — e.g. rejecting/Parking at Validation or admission time if a workflow declares a back-edge or generates Generator at all, until the runtime exists — that would make the safety contract honest (no silent gap) without building the executor?
close_reason: Resolved by maintainer confirmation: implement the narrow outcome-follower child louiselm-qbr.3.6 under qbr.3; keep qbr.3.2.6.5 runtime enforcement acceptance criteria.

comments.author: claude/70be7a6a-8674-45f2-ae6e-37ab67c8eac9
comments.text:
Refining, not resolving: the maintainer explicitly declined to pick a door in the chat that surfaced this and asked for a dedicated grill-me session instead. No option below is chosen.

New evidence that sharpens the question: there is no code anywhere in this tree that walks "Agent took outcome X -> follow it to the next stage." Stage-chaining in this project's own grill -> beads -> execute -> qa-review -> retrospect loop works entirely by convention today — a skill's prose tells the Agent what to invoke next, and the Agent cooperates. LouiseLM tracks no current-stage or outcome-taken state anywhere (confirmed: lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua is Session-supervision only; lua/louiselm/workflow/validate.lua and schema.lua only reason about document shape at validation time). The line in qbr.3's closed comments ("the model selects an outcome, LouiseLM validates, records, and follows it") is a decision about what to build, not a description of anything running today.

That changes the shape of the fork from two doors to three:

A. Undefer all of qbr.3. Pulls the whole remaining feature back onto the board — evidence links, canonical decisions, supersessions, session-replacement handoffs — plus two still-open grill-me questions under it (qbr.3.1: challenger-pass support; qbr.3.4: Assessment of workflow documents for unbounded effects), none of which budget-charging needs.

B. Drop AC1/AC4 from qbr.3.2.6.5 and close what's achievable now (loosen capture-service/src/runs.rs's validate_reservation past its current kind=="beads_issue"/units==1 restriction, add partial-confirm/release-remainder, ship that). Concrete residual risk: a workflow can declare `back-edge: true, max-iterations: 5, resolver: agent` today and it validates cleanly, but nothing in the runtime ledger ever sees that loop fire — only the br create calls it happens to produce. If a workflow author ever gets max-iterations wrong, there is no second gate. This is the "acyclicity is not termination" scenario qbr.3.2 exists to prevent, left open on 2 of 3 Generator kinds while the parent issue is marked closed.

C. Charter a narrowly-scoped, separately-named child of qbr.3 (NOT bundled inside qbr.3.2.6.5) that builds only the minimal outcome-follower needed to detect a taken back-edge/skill-Generator outcome and call the existing ledger — explicitly excluding evidence links, canonical decisions, supersession, session-replacement handoff, challenger passes, and Assessment. Caveat that makes this not a small tuck-in: since no stage-transition-walking code exists anywhere today, this is literally the first piece of the execution engine to get built, under any name. It sets real precedent for how the rest of qbr.3 eventually gets implemented. That foundational weight is exactly why this deserves its own session rather than an inline call.

Threads worth pulling, updated:
1. Same as original thread 1: can "detect a taken outcome" be scoped narrowly enough to stay clear of qbr.3.1/qbr.3.4's unresolved questions, or does building any of it force an implicit answer to those too?
2. If C is chosen: what does the minimal outcome-follower's public surface look like, and who owns it going forward — does it become qbr.3's first merged child, or a permanent resident of qbr.3.2 with qbr.3 rescoped around it?
3. Original threads 3-4 (parent-closing semantics under B; cheaper interim enforcement via Validation/admission-time rejection of any workflow declaring a back-edge/generates Generator at all) still stand and are cheaper fallbacks worth ruling in/out before committing to A or C.

title: Send bounded hidden skill catalogs in inject mode
description:
## Goal

Provide natural-language skill discovery to injected agents without visible context markers, unbounded prompts, or duplicate delivery.

## Scope

- In scope: serialize implicit skills using the Agent Skills `<available_skills><skill>...` XML shape with escaped name, description, and absolute configured-alias location.
- In scope: prepend the fixed agreed behavioral instructions and cap the complete serialized hidden block at 8,000 UTF-8 bytes, including preamble and wrappers.
- In scope: preserve the preamble and all possible names/paths, shorten descriptions fairly and codepoint-safely first, then omit the deterministic name/path-sorted tail if minimum metadata still cannot fit.
- In scope: exclude explicit-only skills from the model catalog while retaining them in the picker; expose omitted/truncated diagnostics.
- In scope: build the catalog only for a new session, hold it locally, and attach it as a separate hidden first text block to the first accepted non-slash model prompt.
- In scope: defer catalog and ordinary attached contexts across user-authored slash prompts; consume the catalog when prompt submission returns a valid ACP request id. Do not resend after accepted cancellation, crash, or uncertain failure.
- In scope: explicit picker activation attaches the exact complete SKILL.md once for that activation; a selected-file read failure blocks submission and preserves the prompt/selection.
- Out of scope: resumed-session reinjection, synthetic catalog turns, recursive resource embedding, native command invocation, and transcript persistence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No `[context: skill-index]` or catalog text is rendered before submission.
2. The entire hidden block never exceeds 8,000 bytes and is validly truncated at UTF-8 boundaries.
3. Natural-language prompts receive one catalog per new injected session; explicit-only skills never appear in it.
4. Slash commands defer rather than consume attached skill context.
5. Synchronous local failure retains the catalog, while any accepted request consumes it exactly once.
6. A deliberate re-selection may attach the same skill on a later turn, but one activation never sends it twice.
7. Resumed or external sessions do not receive a guessed catalog; documentation directs users to start a new session when provenance is uncertain.
8. MiniTest and mock ACP coverage assert block ordering, budgeting, XML escaping, slash deferral, request-id consumption, failure/cancel behavior, picker reads, and no-double-send invariants.

## Testing

Use byte-counting and multibyte fixtures for the budget. Assert exact ACP prompt block arrays through the mock agent.

## Notes

The 8,000-byte rule is a conservative adaptation of Codex fallback behavior, not an ACP or Agent Skills specification requirement.
close_reason: Completed bounded hidden skill catalogs, exact picker bodies, one-shot accepted delivery, and mock ACP coverage (306 tests green)

- Catalog uses <skills_instructions>/<available_skills> XML, escapes metadata, excludes explicit-only skills, and stays <= 8000 bytes by fair codepoint-safe description truncation before deterministic tail omission. Public catalog.truncated/catalog.omitted fields expose diagnostics.
- New inject sessions hold the catalog invisibly and prepend it only to the first accepted non-slash model prompt. Slash prompts defer all attached context; local write/read failures preserve it; accepted requests consume it once; attached/resumed sessions never receive guessed catalogs.
- Explicit picker activation captures the exact SKILL.md body once. Failed reads preserve the chip and prompt and retry safely.
- Focused skills/context/chat/command/mock-agent tests pass. Full MiniTest: 306 cases, 0 failures. stylua --check lua tests passes. Repository-wide stylua and lua-language-server remain blocked only by pre-existing blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua findings tracked as louiselm-d7l.

title: Route work to agents by declared capability
description:
## Problem Statement

A session that cannot complete work has no machine-readable way to say so. On
2026-08-21 a Claude session picked up louiselm-qbr.1.10 (generate Android logo
proposals), found it had no image-generation tool, and recorded that fact as a
prose comment: "leaving open/unclaimed for a codex session". No `br` query can
act on that sentence. The issue stayed in `br ready` for every agent, including
the ones that also cannot do it, and its routing depended entirely on the
maintainer remembering.

`docs/example-workflow.md` already documents this hole from a different
direction: a QA round surfaces a process question, "there is no route for that
finding... it survives by attention, and attention is exactly the resource the
loop is supposed to protect." Two independent instances is the point where a
hole stops being a hole and becomes a missing primitive.

## Solution

Make "what this work requires" and "what this agent can do" both machine-readable,
and make emitting the first one a contract obligation rather than a habit.

Work declares requirements as namespaced beads labels (`needs-capability:*`).
Agents declare what they can do in louiselm's agent configuration. Selection
happens through `br ready --label-any`, which already filters on labels and
already returns them.

## Implementation Decisions

Settled in a grill-me session on 2026-08-21 (see louiselm-provider-switch-ypqs
for the full reasoning and rejected alternatives):

- A standing requirement is a **label**, not a `blocks` dependency. The
  distinguishing test: *does something have to change before anyone can do this?*
  If yes it is a genuine blocker and beads already handles it. If no, and merely
  not every agent qualifies, it is a property of the work. Modelling
  "needs image generation" as `blocks` would remove the issue from `br ready`
  for the very agent that could do it immediately -- the exact opposite of the
  intent.
- Labels name the **capability**, not the agent. Agent names are user-chosen
  config keys (`agents = { codex = ..., claude = ... }`, README.md:527-535);
  `.beads/` is committed and cross-adapter, so `agent:codex` is only meaningful
  to someone whose config happens to use that key. A capability is a fact about
  the work; an agent name is a fact about one machine.
- Capability truth is **declared** in configuration, not discovered at runtime.
  The entire point is routing work before a session exists; if an agent must be
  spawned to learn it cannot do the job, the cost the mechanism exists to avoid
  has already been paid. A wrong declaration is wrong once and then corrected;
  no declaration is wrong every time.
- The emission obligation lives in **AGENTS.md**, not only in a skill. AGENTS.md
  is the sole artifact every adapter reads. During the grill the acting session
  had no `grill-me` skill available and had to read SKILL.md off disk, while it
  had already read AGENTS.md unprompted. A discipline that lives only in a skill
  reproduces the defect AGENTS.md section 2 names: context one adapter cannot
  read. A skill on top is optional ergonomics and must not block this.
- **One emission rule, two destinations**, not two rules. Both the
  capability-block case and the sideways-finding case already have working
  destinations -- `needs-capability:*` labels and the existing
  `needs-design` / "Grill-me needed:" question route, which louiselm-iyy proves
  has been used successfully. The missing piece in both cases is identical: no
  trigger. Two rules would address one defect twice.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. AGENTS.md states when a session must emit a record, naming both triggers
   concretely: it could not complete the work, or it noticed something outside
   the work.
2. AGENTS.md states the label-versus-blocker test in one line, so the choice is
   settled at writing time rather than left to judgment.
3. `needs-capability:*` is documented as a namespaced label vocabulary, greppable
   via `br label list-all`.
4. An agent definition can declare its capabilities in typed configuration, and
   an undeclared or malformed value is a validation error rather than silent
   acceptance.
5. AGENTS.md's existing preference for `br scheduler` carries an explicit
   carve-out for capability-aware selection, because `br scheduler` cannot filter
   by label and returns empty labels (louiselm-scheduler-labels-xw1i). The
   carve-out is deleted when that bug is fixed.
6. louiselm-qbr.1.10 carries the capability label that would have routed it, as
   the first real use.

## Testing Notes

Agent-configuration validation is ordinary closed-schema coverage: accepted
shape, rejected shape, error message. The AGENTS.md and label-vocabulary halves
are documentation and convention; they are verified by using them on
louiselm-qbr.1.10 and confirming `br ready --label-any` selects and deselects it
as expected, not by a test suite.

## Out of Scope

- Any louiselm dependency on beads. The louiselm-qbr epic states beads is "the
  tracker in the reference preset, not a core dependency or a second
  implementation inside LouiseLM". louiselm declares capabilities; it does not
  read issues or route work.
- Automatic matching of declared capabilities against issue labels. The agent
  selecting work does the matching; nothing in the plugin does it.
- Fixing `br scheduler` (upstream, louiselm-scheduler-labels-xw1i).
- Provider handoff of a live session, which is a separate mechanism with a
  separate failure mode.
close_reason: Both children delivered the full feature: louiselm-emission-rule-yc4b added the emission rule, label-vs-blocker test, needs-capability:* vocabulary, and br-scheduler carve-out to AGENTS.md; louiselm-agent-capabilities-pk5z added the typed capabilities field to agent configuration (closed schema, LuaCATS, README, :checkhealth surfacing). qbr.1.10 already carries the label. See comments on both children and on this issue for the AC6 verification caveat.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: AC6 verification note: louiselm-qbr.1.10 already carried needs-capability:image-generation from a prior session before this feature's children were worked, and was closed before this session ran -- confirmed via 'br label list louiselm-qbr.1.10'. 'br ready --label-any needs-capability:image-generation' now returns nothing because br ready only surfaces open work and that issue is done; the label and the routing mechanism both work as designed, the AC's specific verification command is just unsatisfiable post hoc. See the same note on louiselm-emission-rule-yc4b.

title: Capture receiver binds loopback by default and its pairing is address-bound, so LAN and off-LAN sync both fail
description:
Capture from Android did not reach the receiver during a working session on
2026-08-21. The maintainer expected to sync over a LAN address and found it
was not working.

## What the code actually does

The lifecycle half of this is already decided and shipped, and the answer is
"not session-scoped":

- `capture-service/contrib/systemd/louiselm-capture.service` is a user service
  with `WantedBy=default.target` and `Restart=on-failure`. It runs independently
  of Neovim, which is what the `louiselm-qbr` epic requires — the Rust service
  "owns durable capture ingestion and transcription **while the editor is
  closed**". Tying the receiver's lifecycle to a louiselm session would break
  that requirement, so the shipped design is correct and the open work is not
  "start it with a session".

The reachability half is the actual defect:

- The unit hardcodes `Environment=LOUISELM_CAPTURE_BIND=127.0.0.1:7391`
  — loopback. A phone on the LAN cannot reach it at all.
- `capture-service/README.md:20-21` states the default binds TLS on
  `127.0.0.1:7391` and that `LOUISELM_CAPTURE_BIND` must be set "explicitly to a
  LAN address before pairing a phone". The only override path is the unit's
  `EnvironmentFile=-%h/.config/louiselm/capture.env`, which is optional (`-`)
  and undocumented in the README.
- So the documented happy path requires an out-of-band manual step whose absence
  produces exactly the observed silent failure. Nothing in `status` or the
  pairing flow says "you are bound to loopback and no phone will ever reach
  you".

## The structural problem underneath

`pair` prints a QR payload "containing the receiver URL, **exact certificate
fingerprint**, and pairing token" (README:22-24). The pairing is therefore
**bound to the address it was created at**.

That makes the off-LAN case more than a firewall question. On mobile data the
LAN address is unroutable, and re-pairing at a different address is not a
transparent fallback — it is a new receiver URL and potentially a new
certificate fingerprint. A capture taken away from home has nowhere to go and
no second address to try.

## Threads worth pulling

- Does the device credential need to be address-independent, with the receiver
  URL a mutable field the phone can be told about, rather than baked into the
  paired identity? That is the difference between "re-pair when you leave the
  house" and "it just syncs".
- Overlay network (WireGuard/Tailscale) gives one stable address that is valid
  on LAN and on mobile data, which would make the address-binding harmless
  without changing the pairing model. `RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6`
  in the unit already permits it. This is probably the cheap correct answer, and
  it should be priced against exposing the receiver to the public internet,
  which the current threat model (one-use pairing tokens, hashed credentials,
  20 MiB cap) was not designed for.
- Should the phone queue captures durably while unreachable and drain on next
  contact, making reachability a latency question instead of a loss question?
  If yes, that weakens the urgency of everything above.
- `status` should probably refuse to look healthy while bound to loopback with
  paired devices registered.

Refs louiselm-qbr.1
close_reason: Defect already fixed and physically verified; this session verified the three original symptoms are gone (unit no longer hardcodes loopback, README documents configure-network, cli.rs:371 warns), confirmed the regressions pass, and closed the real remaining hole: those tests ran in no CI. Blocking chain complete — louiselm-1chb.2 recorded the overlay evidence comment 144 required.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 1 — delivery contract: LouiseLM guarantees capture anywhere without loss, not immediate synchronization everywhere. The phone must queue recordings durably while the receiver is unreachable and drain automatically when contact returns. Near-immediate off-LAN delivery through a stable private overlay such as Tailscale/WireGuard is an optional enhancement. Publicly exposing the receiver is not justified merely to remove delivery latency.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 2 — safe setup and pairing: loopback remains the unconfigured security default. Phone pairing must refuse to generate a plausible but unreachable QR while the advertised receiver is loopback-only. It must explain the problem and require an explicit reachable profile: LAN address, preferably a private-overlay address, or an advanced explicit override. Do not silently bind every interface merely to make pairing appear convenient.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 3 — pairing identity: pairing establishes a durable receiver identity rather than permanently binding a device credential to the current URL. Enrollment conveys the stable receiver trust identity, a one-use token, and the initial endpoint. The device credential survives endpoint changes; authenticated endpoint reconfiguration changes reachability without full re-pairing. Re-pair only when the receiver identity/trust key changes.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 4 — endpoint resolution: a paired phone stores a small ordered endpoint set, such as private-overlay hostname then home-LAN address. It tries local failover and accepts an endpoint only when the peer proves the pinned receiver identity; if none respond, delivery remains queued. Endpoint changes are explicit through manual entry or a lightweight update QR and do not mint a new device credential. Do not build a LouiseLM cloud discovery or relay service.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 5 — durable queue semantics: persist audio and metadata locally before upload, assign an immutable capture ID, and retry idempotently across application/device restarts. Delete the phone copy only after the receiver confirms durable storage for that ID; a lost response may safely cause a deduplicated retry. Never auto-evict queued captures. If a new capture cannot be persisted, fail visibly before representing it as saved.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 6 — two-sided health: receiver status reports configured bind and advertised endpoints, loopback-only state, paired-device count, last successful delivery per device, and an explicit warning when paired devices exist but no phone-reachable endpoint is configured. Phone status reports pending count and oldest age, last successful sync, active endpoint, latest failure, and manual retry. A running receiver process must not be represented as healthy delivery.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 7 — v1 network scope: configure exactly one profile. Preferred private-overlay mode provides one stable address at home and away; LAN-only mode uses an explicitly selected local address and queues captures while away; loopback is an unconfigured/development state and cannot pair a phone. The phone endpoint representation may hold an ordered set, but v1 setup supplies one reachable endpoint. Defer simultaneous LAN-plus-overlay listeners and automatic failover until evidence requires them.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 8 — supported exposure boundary: v1 supports selected LAN addresses, detected private-overlay addresses, and explicit advanced binds for unusual private setups. It does not support public-internet exposure, port-forwarding guidance, or public-reachability claims; refuse obvious wildcard/public configurations when classification is reliable. Overlay software is externally owned: LouiseLM may detect and explain Tailscale/WireGuard addresses but does not install or manage those products.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 9 — receiver trust anchor: pairing pins a long-lived receiver identity key, not the entire current TLS certificate. TLS certificates and endpoint hostnames may change only with proof of continuity to that pinned identity. Rotating or losing the receiver identity key requires explicit recovery or re-pairing; routine certificate renewal must not invalidate device pairing.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 10 — Android delivery execution: attempt upload immediately after capture, retry on connectivity restoration, and use Android's scheduled background-work mechanism with bounded exponential backoff plus manual retry. Do not keep a permanent foreground service or wake lock solely for synchronization. The product guarantees eventual delivery from the durable queue, not a delivery deadline.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 11 — recovery and queued-data ownership: each queued capture remains associated with the receiver identity for which it was recorded. Pairing a new receiver identity neither deletes nor silently redirects old queued captures. The phone shows the retained count and requires explicit user confirmation to migrate those captures to the new receiver, preventing re-pairing from becoming an unnoticed disclosure.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Clarification to decision 5 from android/AGENTS.md: the existing product invariant is stronger than the grill wording—original recordings are never automatically deleted, including after upload. Therefore durable receiver acknowledgement controls only the transition to delivered/uploaded state and retry cessation. The immutable local original remains retained; no implementation task may weaken that invariant.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 12 — completion evidence: require deterministic coverage for loopback pairing refusal, private profile pairing, restart-safe queued upload, acknowledgement-loss deduplication, stable-key acceptance across TLS certificate renewal, receiver-identity mismatch rejection, and non-redirecting re-pair recovery. Require a focused physical Android/network QA round for LAN departure/return, overlay delivery across Wi-Fi/mobile data, process restart, and two-sided degraded-state reporting. Automated tests use fakes, never live networks or credentials.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Grill decision 13 — pre-pair captures: recordings created before any receiver is paired initially have no receiver owner. First successful pairing explicitly assigns all unassigned captures to that receiver and queues them, while the pairing UI states the affected count. Later pairing to a different receiver is not equivalent: already assigned queued captures remain with the old identity unless the user confirms migration.

comments.text: Design complete; implementation is now represented by blocking tracer-bullet tasks, so release the design-session claim while retaining the open defect.

title: Android CI dependency downloads fail with Maven HTTP 429
description:
An unchanged full-CI baseline fails before Android tests because Maven Central refuses dependency downloads. This blocks the authorized cache experiment, not an observed app-runtime regression.

Observed: 2026-09-21, run 35563239473, job 106219976493, exact revision c4c12245d9b753817549313bc14745e52be88a4f, Ubuntu 24.04. https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/35563239473/job/106219976493

Evidence: at 05:06:13Z, "Could not resolve all artifacts for configuration classpath" and Maven POM requests for Gson 2.11.0, ASM 9.9, Kotlin Gradle plugin 2.2.10 and many others report "Received status code 429 from server: Too Many Requests". "BUILD FAILED in 20s"; exit 1. Exact excerpts: docs/performance/skills-cache-20260921/android-baseline-failure.log on experiment branch codex/skills-cache-ab-20260921.

Root cause: dependency endpoint rate limiting is observed. Why this runner was limited is unknown; three parallel benchmark workflows may increase requests but that causal link is unproved. The unchanged job at .github/workflows/ci.yml:172-190 resolves dependencies on the hosted runner; it has no Gradle cache step. Other completed main/PR runs passed, so source correctness is not disproved.

Test gap: the gate correctly fails, but dependency provisioning is an external prerequisite not covered by deterministic application tests.

Fix direction: diagnose cold dependency acquisition and evaluate existing-action caching or bounded transient-download handling without swallowing build/test failures, changing repositories blindly, adding dependencies, or weakening gates.

Acceptance: preserve all Android gates; distinguish dependency acquisition from test failures; demonstrate controlled transient-dependency behavior if changing retry logic; obtain complete hosted baseline success with retained logs before resuming performance candidates.

Not covered: no Android repair, retry-until-green, mirrors, dependency upgrades, or cache-policy changes were authorized in the cache experiment. The remaining benchmark runs were cancelled; no cache candidate was applied. Deferred for separate reliability authorization.
