title: Investigate unexpected repeated browser opening of external issue URL
description:
## Observation

On 2026-08-29, the maintainer reported that a live Session `codex/01a04b63-d5b5-7fc0-8456-06c6281c7744` appeared to open `https://github.com/org/repo/issues/42` four times in Chrome without an intentional user action.

## Evidence collected

- The Session is live in Neovim and owns `louiselm-f8r1`, the beads_viewer_rust/bvr custom-status and historical-load bug.
- Its ACP log is `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a04b63-d5b5-7fc0-8456-06c6281c7744/log.jsonl`. The log contains no browser, URL-open, `xdg-open`, Playwright, or web-search tool call.
- Around the relevant event it was running `cargo test --tests`, not a bvr TUI process.
- Chrome Profile 5 history recorded visits to the URL at `04:49:56` and `04:49:57` local time on 2026-08-29; the copied read-only History database reported three visits in that interval.
- Chrome session file `/home/lotso/.config/google-chrome/Profile 5/Sessions/Session_13432442774644676` contains the URL repeatedly. These repetitions are serialized tab-state data and do not establish 18 openings.
- Chrome renderer processes were created at approximately `04:49:55`, consistent with Chrome reusing/opening tabs.
- beads_viewer_rust has an explicit external-link action: `src/tui.rs:5336` handles `o` when an external reference is available, and `src/tui.rs:14218` invokes `xdg-open` (with fallbacks).
- Repository tests and fixtures intentionally contain this placeholder URL as an external reference, but no evidence showed test rendering itself opening it.

## Assessment

The target Codex Session did not open the URL according to its durable ACP log. The strongest hypothesis is that a bvr TUI received `o` while an external issue link was selected, possibly repeated input; this is not proven. The browser history/session files cannot attribute the opener to a process.

No code change was made. Preserve this issue as the evidence record unless a reproducible trigger is found.

title: All-workspace session discovery sends empty params as a JSON array and every Agent rejects it
description:
`:LouiselmResume!` (all-workspace discovery) sends `session/list` with `"params": []` — an empty JSON
array — and every strict ACP Agent rejects it with `-32602 Invalid params`. The user gets a warning
naming each Agent and a silently truncated session list: 30 sessions instead of the 238 the
cwd-filtered path returns. This is the same defect class as louiselm-ce6.25.4 / de04317, which fixed
empty-object encoding for `account_limits/read` but not for `session/list`.

## Observed

Manual QA round 2026-08-25, build acb65c7, case 7, run against the real state root
(~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy), Agents claude, codex, copilot — all via acp-proxy.

Tester saw:

    louiselm: session discovery: claude: ACP session/list failed: Invalid params; codex: ACP
    session/list failed: Invalid params; copilot: ACP session/list failed: Invalid params

`:LouiselmResume!` then listed 30 sessions. `:LouiselmResume` (cwd-filtered) listed 238 with no
warning. So the bang, which is supposed to widen the search to every workspace, returns an order of
magnitude FEWER sessions than the narrow form.

Wire evidence, six independent connection logs under
/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/connections/ (6718d38b, f3183b4f, e61ced5f, 7f40d206,
01aa06f2, 32511725), all identical:

    request  {"method": "session/list", "params": [], "id": ...}
    response {"code": -32602, "message": "Invalid params",
              "data": {"_errors": ["Invalid input: expected object, received array"]}}

The cwd-filtered path is unaffected and works, including cursor pagination — connection fba1d164
shows `{"params": {"cwd": "/home/lotso/code/louiselm"}}` succeeding and paginating through
`{"cwd": ..., "cursor": "2026-08-23T12:31:10.449Z"}` and onwards, returning real session titles.

## Symptoms

- `:LouiselmResume!` warns once naming every configured strict Agent, then shows a partial list.
- The partial list is not marked as partial; the count simply looks small.
- A user comparing the two commands sees the broader query return fewer results, which reads as data
  loss rather than as a failed request.

## Root cause

`vim.json.encode({})` produces `[]`, not `{}`. Lua cannot distinguish an empty table from an empty
array, so an empty params table serializes as a JSON array and strict ACP Agents reject it.

Two sites build that empty table:

- lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua:379 — `local params = {}`, then `cwd` and `cursor` are added only
  when non-nil. With `:LouiselmResume!` there is no cwd, and the first page has no cursor, so the
  first request goes out with an empty table. This is the site that fires in practice.
- lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:273 — `self:request("session/list", params or {}, callback)` has the same
  hazard for any caller passing nil.

The already-fixed comparison is in the same file: `Registry:refresh_agent_limits` passes
`nvim.empty_dict()` to `client:request(capability.read_method, ...)`, which is exactly why
`account_limits/read` goes out as `{}` and works.

## Why it was not caught

lua/louiselm/dev/mock_agent.lua:196 handles `session/list` without validating the params shape, so
the mock accepts `[]` where every real Agent refuses it. The discovery tests therefore exercise a
peer more permissive than any production peer, and the all-workspace path — the only one that
produces empty params — is precisely the case the mock cannot fail.

This is the third finding in two QA rounds where an invented fixture stood in for observed wire
behavior; see louiselm-4tum (snake_case vs camelCase usage keys) and louiselm-zufj (assumed
tool-update-before-turn_done ordering).

## Fix direction

Send `nvim.empty_dict()` rather than a bare table whenever the params object may end up empty, at
both sites above. Match `refresh_agent_limits`, which already does this.

Worth considering at the same time, but not required by this bug: an audit of every
`client:request(...)` call for the same hazard, and a mock-agent params-shape check so `[]` fails
there too. Filed as fix direction rather than acceptance because widening scope silently is how this
recurred after de04317 fixed one instance.

## Acceptance

- A regression test that fails while empty params serialize as `[]` and passes once they serialize as
  `{}`, asserting the encoded JSON rather than the Lua table.
- `:LouiselmResume!` against a strict Agent produces no `Invalid params` warning and returns at least
  as many sessions as `:LouiselmResume` for the same Agent.
- The mock agent rejects array-shaped params for `session/list`, so this cannot regress unnoticed.

## Not covered

- Which Agent supplied the 30 sessions that did appear under `:LouiselmResume!` was not confirmed;
  the warning named claude, codex and copilot, so the remainder presumably came from an
  acp-llm-adapter Agent that tolerates `[]`. Not verified.
- Other `client:request` call sites were surveyed but not individually tested for empty params.
close_reason: Fixed empty session/list params and passed live acceptance: 235 cwd-scoped sessions, 517 all-workspace sessions, no errors

title: Forensics
description: Read-only collection and inspection of bounded observations and pointers for exactly one subject Session. A durable Forensics record indexes primary evidence in place and preserves its own observations and pointers; it does not copy, normalize, interpret, or make that evidence safe to share. Record durability does not guarantee primary-evidence availability.
acceptance_criteria: Use Forensics for the collection capability, its immutable record, and views derived from that record. On inspection, report the current availability of indexed evidence by property; do not rewrite the record when a referent is absent. Raw ACP logs and other primary sources remain inspectable by the diagnosing Agent for the selected subject Session. Distinguish from Evidence export, the explicit bounded redacted sharing artifact.

title: Add explicit per-agent Agent Skills profiles
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM currently injects one global skill index into every session, including adapters such as Codex and Claude that already provide native Agent Skills support. This exposes an implementation marker in chat, wastes context, can send a skill twice, and leaves users unable to understand which component discovers or invokes a skill.

## Solution

Add explicit per-agent Agent Skills profiles. Global skill paths remain shared, the default policy is `native`, and an agent may override only `skills.policy` with `native`, `inject`, or `off`. Native mode delegates discovery and invocation to the adapter. Inject mode provides a hidden, bounded Agent Skills catalog and attaches a selected full SKILL.md only once per activation. Off disables LouiseLM skill automation and the picker. Never infer or switch policy at runtime.

## User Stories

1. As a Codex or Claude user, I want native skills used without LouiseLM reinjecting them, so that skills are not duplicated.
2. As a custom-adapter user, I want to opt one agent into injected discovery, so that natural-language skill matching still works.
3. As a user, I want a picker that invokes a known local skill safely in both native and injected profiles, so that explicit activation is predictable.
4. As a user, I want skill context hidden before submission but inspectable afterward, so that chat stays clean without concealing what was sent.
5. As a skill author, I want malformed, shadowed, explicit-only, truncated, or inaccessible skills diagnosed clearly, so that configuration failures are understandable.
6. As a user configuring an unfamiliar ACP adapter, I want documentation explaining Agent Skills, ACP transport, host responsibilities, and filesystem assumptions, so that I can choose the correct policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Global `skills.policy` defaults to `native`; agent definitions may override only the policy, while paths remain global and session-static.
2. `native` sends no automatic catalog or skill body. Picker activation resolves against the adapter's latest advertised command list and sends exactly one advertised command plus task.
3. `inject` sends one hidden catalog only on the first accepted non-slash prompt of a new session, then sends a selected complete SKILL.md once per deliberate activation. It never falls back to native or reinjects after uncertain accepted requests.
4. `off` sends no skill automation and disables the skill picker without intercepting user-authored slash commands.
5. The old `full_content` setting and dormant automatic-native-fallback API are removed with clear migration errors and documentation.
6. Agent Skills core metadata is parsed with `lyaml` and semantically validated; Codex and Claude invocation-control extensions are recognized without treating them as ACP requirements.
7. Missing `lyaml` blocks injected sessions and local native picker/validation, but does not block native sessions themselves or off sessions.
8. The injected catalog uses the agreed Agent Skills XML shape, fixed behavioral preamble, XML escaping, and an 8,000-byte UTF-8-safe total budget with deterministic diagnostics.
9. Submitted prompt contexts are represented as one closed Neovim fold containing exact sent content in order; automatic hidden catalog text never appears as a pre-send marker.
10. README, generated configuration help/annotations, checkhealth, and migration guidance explain policy selection, no-double-send behavior, dependency installation, trust/path rules, filesystem limits, and live-only fold persistence.
11. Automated tests cover configuration, discovery, YAML, invocation metadata, native command correlation, injection lifecycle, slash deferral, failures/cancellation, no-double-send invariants, and context folds. Installed Codex/Claude checks remain documented manual smoke tests.

## Implementation Notes

- Agent Skills defines the skill format; ACP transports prompts and command updates; LouiseLM is the host responsible for policy and injected discovery.
- Explicit-only wins when `disable-model-invocation: true` or OpenAI's `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` is present. Such skills remain picker-visible but are excluded from injected catalogs.
- Root order defines duplicate precedence; path handling is deterministic, symlink-aware, and diagnostic without adding a trust database.
- The 8,000-byte mechanism intentionally mimics Codex's conservative fallback behavior; it is not part of ACP or the Agent Skills specification.
- Use native Neovim folds and existing context transport. Do not introduce a generic fold framework.

## Testing Notes

Use MiniTest for module behavior and a mock ACP agent for command updates and prompt transport. Test public behavior and exact no-double-send invariants. Do not require authenticated live adapters in automated tests.

## Out of Scope

- Runtime policy switching or inference.
- A general UI for every ACP advertised command.
- A LouiseLM ACP filesystem service.
- Recursive embedding of skill resources.
- Persistent transcript reconstruction.
- Automatic dependency installation.
- Generic adapter-native skill implementation.
- Tool-call fold rendering; track that as a separate design question.
close_reason: All Agent Skills profile children and feature acceptance criteria are complete.

title: Diagnose installed lyaml outside Neovim search paths
description:
## Problem

Local skill discovery reports:

```
louiselm: lyaml is required for local skill discovery; install it with `luarocks --lua-version 5.1 install lyaml`
```

However, LuaRocks confirms that lyaml is already installed for Lua 5.1. The actual failure is that the active Neovim process does not search the LuaRocks tree, so the message sends the user toward an installation command that will not fix the search-path mismatch.

## Reproduction evidence

- `luarocks --lua-version 5.1 show lyaml` succeeds with lyaml 6.2.9-2 under `$HOME/.asdf/installs/lua/5.1.5/luarocks`.
- Neovim 0.12.2 embeds LuaJIT 2.1.
- In `nvim --headless -u NONE`, `pcall(require, "lyaml")` returns `module 'lyaml' not found`.
- Neovim's `package.path` and `package.cpath` contain system paths, but not the asdf LuaRocks share/lib paths reported by `luarocks path --lua-version 5.1`.

## Expected behavior

When lyaml cannot be loaded, LouiseLM should preserve enough of the loader failure to distinguish an absent installation from an installed-but-unreachable LuaRocks tree (and from native module load failures), then give a corrective action that matches the failure.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The user-facing/checkhealth diagnostic distinguishes at least package-not-found/search-path mismatch from a native loader failure instead of always saying to install lyaml.
2. Documentation gives a supported way to make a Lua 5.1 LuaRocks tree visible to Neovim, including non-system/asdf installs.
3. Tests cover the generic `require("lyaml")` failure mapping without depending on a real LuaRocks installation.
4. Diagnostics do not expose unrelated environment values or sensitive data.
close_reason: Shortened interactive lyaml failures to point at checkhealth, added detailed persistent zsh/asdf guidance to health and README, and covered both surfaces. Verified 181 MiniTest cases, StyLua, and LuaLS.

title: Abandonment
description: Loss of a live Session because Neovim exited without disposing it.
design: Established by the louiselm-ce6.28 grill-me session on 2026-08-26, from a reproduction in which ordinary :q from a louiselm://limits detail buffer exited Neovim while a Session remained alive.
notes: Avoid: using Abandonment for a deliberate lifecycle end. Distinguish from Disposal, which deliberately ends a Session, and from Cancellation, which ends a turn but leaves the Session alive. All three appear in the quit-safety contract; conflating them changes lifecycle behavior.

title: Add Session edges from Beads actor fields to issue Provenance
description:
## Goal

Show which Sessions worked an issue, using the Session ids that the claim
convention already writes into Beads.

## Scope

- In scope: issue -> Session edges from `assignee` and `created_by`; those rows
  in the issue Provenance view; transcript resolution through the locator.
- Out of scope: time travel, Session-rooted views.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The issue view lists Sessions from Beads actor fields, deduplicated against
   Sessions already found through commit trailers.
2. Actor values that are not Session ids (`assistant`, `lotso`) are shown as
   non-Session actors rather than being resolved or silently dropped. 169 of the
   backlog's issues predate the convention, so this is the common case for older
   work, not an edge case.
3. Edges are read through `br`, never by parsing `.beads/*.jsonl`.

## Testing

- Fixtures covering a Session-id actor, a bare-name actor, an empty assignee,
  and an issue whose commit trailer and assignee name the same Session, which
  must appear once.

## Notes

Coverage is uneven by construction and the view must not imply otherwise:
Beads actors are codex-heavy (codex 123, claude 34, copilot 14) while commit
trailers are claude-heavy (claude 25, deepseek 7). An issue can therefore have
a Session on one edge and nothing on the other.
close_reason: Completed: issue Provenance reads actors through br, classifies legacy actors, resolves and deduplicates Session edges, with 682-case suite and all quality gates passing.

comments.author: codex/01a0428e-6b0e-7fa3-a088-c03e6b235bf4
comments.text: Lesson: the issue view needed two independent read paths: BVR history for commit correlations and br show --json for authoritative assignee/created_by actors. Preserving BVR commit messages let the pure correlation layer derive trailer Sessions, while the merge boundary deduplicates those against actor-derived Sessions. No standing AGENTS.md rule or unresolved design question is warranted.

title: Pairing QR is oversized, clipped, and exposes payload
description:
The Neovim pairing screen renders a terminal QR nearly twice as wide as it is tall, and it is clipped in a normal split. This makes the core phone-pairing flow difficult to photograph and can leave the user believing pairing succeeded when the receiver still has no registered device. The same screen also prints the raw one-time pairing JSON above the QR, unnecessarily exposing the token as selectable text.

## Observed

Physical QA round `louiselm-qbr.1.9` on 2026-08-21, 1920x1200 terminal.

- `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260821_0612_1920x1200_1787285559.png`: in a two-column split, the QR extends beyond the right window edge and its right side is clipped.
- `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260821_0612_1920x1200_1787285570.png`: even full-screen, the rendered QR is about twice as wide as tall and occupies almost the whole editor.
- Both screenshots show a serialized pairing object above the QR, including a `token` field. The token value is intentionally omitted from this issue.
- Immediately after the reported scan, `louiselm-capture status` returned `devices: []`; no pairing completed.

## Symptoms

- The user must maximize the editor and carefully frame a distorted, oversized code.
- A split clips QR modules, preventing reliable scanning.
- The raw short-lived credential is displayed as ordinary text in addition to being encoded in the QR.

## Root cause

`capture-service/src/cli.rs:191-196` renders `unicode::Dense1x2` with `module_dimensions(2, 1)`. `Dense1x2` already packs two vertical modules per terminal row; doubling only the horizontal module width produces roughly four character columns per row and the observed wide code. Line 196 prints `{payload}` before `{rendered}`, so the Neovim buffer exposes the serialized token.

## Why it was not caught

Pairing tests cover offer validation, credential issuance, persistence, and HTTP authentication, but no test constrains the CLI pairing output's geometry or asserts that the raw offer is absent. The Neovim command smoke test only asserts command registration.

## Fix direction

At the CLI output boundary, render `Dense1x2` at its native module width and print only the QR. Keep the pairing protocol and Neovim buffer mechanism unchanged.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and proves terminal QR character geometry is approximately 2 columns per row rather than 4.
- A regression test proves the CLI-visible rendering does not contain the serialized token or raw JSON payload.
- In the same Neovim split used in the screenshot, the complete QR fits and a physical phone scan registers the device on the receiver.

## Not covered

Terminal font aspect ratios and color-scheme contrast outside the reported Ghostty/Neovim environment are not evaluated.
close_reason: Fixed in 456031b, 13dfe23, and f7d85fc. Root causes: redundant horizontal QR scaling, raw offer output, colorscheme-dependent inverted polarity, and listchars corruption of the quiet zone. Tests: pairing_outputs_a_compact_qr_without_the_raw_offer and pairing QR is black on white independently of the colorscheme were red before their fixes and green after. Gates: full Rust suite/format, StyLua, lua-language-server zero diagnostics, mini.test 316/316. Physical verification: fresh Neovim QR paired successfully; receiver registered device 62e8883e-2f0d-47f0-84dd-832879ad1453 and subsequently accepted the previously rejected 7c7353dc-1c2c-474a-a4c8-a39d102f82e8 capture.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Automated fix landed in 456031b: Dense1x2 now uses native width and CLI prints only rendered QR. Public CLI regression pairing_outputs_a_compact_qr_without_the_raw_offer was red on both raw-offer and geometry assertions, then green. Gates passed: cargo fmt/check + full Rust suite; stylua; lua-language-server zero diagnostics; mini.test 315/315. Release binary installed at /home/lotso/.local/bin/louiselm-capture without modifying TLS/pairing state. Physical same-split scan remains required before closure.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Physical retest partial: user reports the corrected QR screen in the same environment seems okay, so layout/raw-line presentation is provisionally passed. However objective receiver status remains devices: []; scan/registration is not yet proven, so bug remains open and Case 8 has not started.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Physical scan still fails after 456031b. User tried repeated portrait/landscape photos; Android reports exactly: No QR code was found. Move closer. Receiver remains devices: []. Inspection confirms Dense1x2 represents dark modules as foreground glyphs; under the reported dark colorscheme the screenshot is light-on-dark/inverted. Android uses ML Kit 17.3.0 photo scanning and returns no barcode. Follow-up must force black foreground/white background on the QR region independent of colorscheme; first fix remains valid for size and raw-payload removal.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Follow-up fix committed in 13dfe23: :LouiselmCapturePair highlights only QR lines with explicit black foreground/white background, independent of colorscheme. UI regression test pairing QR is black on white independently of the colorscheme failed before the fix (no highlight) and passes after. Gates: stylua, lua-language-server zero diagnostics, mini.test 316/316. Physical scan/receiver registration still required before closure.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Third physical attempt: QR is visibly black-on-white after 13dfe23, but Android pairing error persists and receiver remains devices: []. Exact environment check via a fresh configured Neovim: vim.wo.list=true and listchars={trail="·", tab="» ", nbsp="␣"}. The CLI QR quiet zone is made of leading/trailing spaces; listchars replaces every trailing quiet-zone space with dots and turns fully blank top/bottom quiet rows into dotted rows, corrupting the barcode despite correct contrast. Next regression/fix: :LouiselmCapturePair must set the pairing window list=false.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Quiet-zone fix committed in f7d85fc: pairing window sets list=false, preventing listchars.trail=· from replacing QR border spaces. The existing public UI test was extended to start with list=true; assertion was red before the fix and green after. Gates: stylua, lua-language-server zero diagnostics, mini.test 316/316. Fresh-Neovim physical scan remains required before closure.

title: Resumed-session export silently drops nested/subagent tool calls
description:
`:LouiselmResume`'s replay of a prior ACP session silently drops nested/child
tool calls (a tool call made *by* a Task subagent, i.e. one carrying a
`parentToolUseId`), while still replaying the parent Task call's own summary
text. Anyone exporting a resumed session — including the blog publishing
pipeline, which exports whatever the agent replays on `session/load` — gets a
transcript that is missing subagent-internal tool-call detail, with no error
or signal that anything is missing.

## Observed

QA round for the transcript-export/blog-publishing features
(`4e4a58b`, `674939b`), case 4 ("resumed-session export vs live export"),
session `21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384`, 2026-08-18.

Prompt that produced the nested call (case 1 of the same round):
"Do these three things in order, in this one turn. (1) Run the Bash tool on
the absolute path: `wc -l .../transcript.lua`. (2) Use the Task tool to
launch one general-purpose subagent whose prompt is exactly: 'List the
top-level directories of /home/lotso/code/louiselm as one comma-separated
line.' (3) Write me a two-sentence summary of what you found."

Original live export, captured right after that turn ended:
`louiselm-session-1-20260818-150448.md` (repo root at the time). Contains 3
tool-call blocks — Bash (`wc -l`), Task (`List top-level directories`), and a
nested Bash call made by the Task subagent:
```
toolCallId = "toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr"
parentToolUseId = "toolu_018NnXLu4qGQc7e4bei8C52a"  (the Task call)
title = "ls -d /home/lotso/code/louiselm/*/ | xargs -n1 basename | paste -sd, -"
rawOutput = "android,assets,blog,capture-service,configured,lua,scripts,tests"
status = "completed"
```

Resumed export (`:LouiselmResume` on the same session, immediate
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` → `/tmp/qa-resumed.md`, no other prompt sent first):
same acp session id (session/load reconnects rather than creating a new
session). Contains the parent `## Tool: List top-level directories
(completed)` block with its rawOutput summary intact, but grepping the full
573KB resumed export for the toolCallId `toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr`, the
literal command text `paste -sd`, and `xargs -n1 basename` finds zero
tool-call blocks — those strings appear exactly once, incidentally, inside
unrelated later text content (a grep-output dump quoted in a much later
turn), not as a `## Tool:` entry.

Raw jsonrpc log:
`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260818-150022-1160867-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`
(818 lines). The nested `tool_call` event for
`toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr` appears exactly once, at line 19, during the
original live turn:
```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{"sessionId":"21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384","update":{"_meta":{"claudeCode":{"toolName":"Bash","parentToolUseId":"toolu_018NnXLu4qGQc7e4bei8C52a"}},"toolCallId":"toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr","sessionUpdate":"tool_call","rawInput":{"command":"ls -d /home/lotso/code/louiselm/*/ | xargs -n1 basename | paste -sd, -"},"status":"pending", ...}}}
```
No second occurrence appears later in the log during the replay burst
triggered by `session/load` — the agent process itself never re-emits this
event on replay.

Everything else about the resumed export checked out clean: 65 of the 66
total tool calls in the session (by then spanning many turns) present and in
correct relative order, and the case-1 `## User` block matches the typed
prompt verbatim. Only this one nested call is missing.

## Symptoms

- User sees: a resumed-session export (or a blog post built from one) that
  looks complete — full assistant text, the parent Task call's own summary —
  but is silently missing the detail of what the subagent actually did
  internally.
- System reports: nothing. No error, warning, or count mismatch anywhere;
  `Chat:to_markdown` and `create-blog.sh` both report success normally.

## Root cause

Unknown, and outside this repo (`louiselm.nvim`). `louiselm`'s own
`Transcript:record`/`Transcript.render` (lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua)
only records whatever `session/update` events it receives over ACP — the
live stream sent the nested tool_call event and louiselm recorded it
correctly (see the original export above); on replay, the same event simply
never arrives, so there is nothing to fix on this side.

Hypothesis (unverified): `claude-agent-acp`
(`/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter`, a sibling project) or the underlying
Claude Code SDK reconstructs the Task/subagent call tree differently when
replaying a resumed session's history than when streaming it live — possibly
only replaying top-level tool calls and treating subagent-internal calls as
already-summarized by the parent's own output. Nothing in this investigation
confirms which layer (adapter vs. upstream SDK) is responsible; that needs a
look at the adapter/SDK's own session/load implementation, not louiselm's.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/session/transcript_export_spec.lua` and
`tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` exercise `Transcript` against synthetic,
hand-built event fixtures for both the live and "loaded" replay paths — no
fixture in the suite includes a nested/subagent tool call in a replay
scenario, because nobody had a real payload to model one on. This QA round
was the first time a resumed session containing a Task-subagent call was
actually exported and diffed against its own live-captured original.

## Fix direction

Not in this repo. If the root cause is confirmed to be in
`claude-agent-acp`, the fix belongs there (ensure `session/load` replay
re-emits every historical `tool_call`/`tool_call_update`, including nested
ones with `parentToolUseId` set, not just top-level calls). If it turns out
to be inherent to how the upstream Claude Code SDK exposes subagent history
on resume, this may not be fixable without a scope change to what
`session/load` guarantees — in which case the practical mitigation is
documentation: warn blog-pipeline users that `create-blog.sh` on a resumed
session may omit subagent-internal tool-call detail, and recommend exporting
live when that detail matters.

## Acceptance

- A regression test in whichever repo owns the fix: replay a session
  containing a Task call with a nested tool call, and assert the replayed
  event stream includes the nested `tool_call`/`tool_call_update` events,
  not just the parent's.
- Re-run this round's case 4 comparison
  (`louiselm-session-1-20260818-150448.md` vs. a fresh `:LouiselmResume` +
  immediate `:LouiselmToMarkdown` export of the same session) and confirm
  `toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr` (or an equivalent nested call in a new
  repro) is present in the resumed export.

## Not covered

- Which of `claude-agent-acp` vs. the upstream Claude Code SDK is actually
  responsible — unverified, needs investigation in that repo, not this one.
- Whether the same gap exists for other nested-call shapes (e.g. a tool call
  made by a tool call, rather than by a Task subagent specifically) — only
  one nested-call example existed in the session under test.
- Whether `create-blog.sh` (case 5, not yet run at time of filing) actually
  reproduces the same gap end-to-end through the headless path — this bug is
  filed from the interactive `:LouiselmResume` path only; case 5 should
  re-check this once it runs.
close_reason: Fixed in owner repo /home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp commit 041da5b; exact historical session headless export restores the missing nested tool call and parent attribution; full owner-repo gates pass.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
Confirmed reproducing through the headless path too (case 5 of the same QA
round). `./blog/scripts/create-blog.sh qa-round claude/21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384`
succeeded (exit 0, expected messages, scaffold created), and the exported
`blog/post-qa-round/conversations/claude-21a0ede3-....md` (664KB, 87 tool
calls by then) has no `## Tool: ls -d ...` block for the nested call either
— checked precisely for a genuine top-level `## Tool:` header, not just a
text match, since by this point the session transcript also contains this
bug's own filing (which quotes the missing toolCallId and command verbatim),
so a plain grep for those strings alone would false-positive. Confirms the
gap is in the shared `session/load` replay path itself, not specific to the
interactive `:LouiselmResume` UI flow.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Claimed for root-cause investigation in /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter. Intended source scope: session/load replay and its tests only; LouiseLM code remains unchanged unless adapter evidence disproves ownership. Existing sibling .beads schema-migration artifacts will be preserved.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Root cause confirmed in official claude-agent-acp replay. getSessionMessages reads only the main JSONL; the missing call is stored in the SDK-managed subagents/agent-a37d72065ac3f3d29.jsonl and is returned by listSubagents plus getSubagentMessages. Upstream main commit 8663170 preserved nested messages only when already supplied, so its split-storage unit assumption did not cover the real session. Implemented local owner-repo fix at /home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp commit 041da5b: load all persisted subagent histories, recursively interleave them after their parent tool-use messages, then reuse the existing replay converter. TDD: new test failed with only parent-agent-call and passed with parent-agent-call then child-tool. Gates: 811 passed, 20 skipped; ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript build, and diff check pass. Exact headless acceptance passed against session 21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384: exported child toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr with parentToolUseId toolu_018NnXLu4qGQc7e4bei8C52a and original output.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Manual acceptance passed on 2026-08-20 with the local owner-repo build 041da5b. User visually confirmed the resumed first turn rendered the parent Agent/Task call, nested Bash call, then assistant response in order. Pinned stderr proves the configured process was node /home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp/dist/index.js. ACP log 20260820-183053-1060915-node-stdout-jsonrpc.log emitted child toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr with parent toolu_018NnXLu4qGQc7e4bei8C52a. Fresh Markdown export /tmp/louiselm-d2o-local.md preserved parent at line 89, child at line 124, and assistant heading at line 130 with the original command and output. No QA findings.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Published the owner-repo fix to fork https://github.com/euri10/claude-agent-acp on branch fix/replay-persisted-subagents. Review history is explicitly test-first: fece865 adds the split-storage regression and fails with expected parent-agent-call plus child-tool but actual parent-agent-call only; e8f2df4 adds the implementation and makes that same focused test pass. Final gates on the pushed tip: npm run check passed, npm run build passed, full Vitest 811 passed and 20 skipped. Upstream agentclientprotocol remote was not pushed.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Upstream review reference: PR https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp/pull/1020 (fix: replay persisted subagent histories). The PR contains the red/green regression history, real-session evidence, and the owner-repo implementation that closes this out-of-repo finding.

title: QA round: accept Copilot terminal completion and exact echo suppression
description:
# Manual QA — Copilot terminal completion (`louiselm-zufj`)

Completed QA round, accepted by the maintainer on 2026-09-11 in
`codex/01a08f74-e392-7463-bc93-0e0c269a53a5` ("i confirm"). This record is
archived in a `qa-round` Bead; its temporary working file is removed afterward.

Build under test: installed LouiseLM `bf36c37`. The installed
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` is byte-identical to workspace `ce0ae05`:
SHA-256 `54f71e0c1f539c0417eb0356f85c9463fddcf022f3c40fefa4b106db3d42ddb8`.
The fix is `d351821`, already present in the installed copy. No reload or
code change is needed for this round.

The original failure hid a distinct final answer whenever Copilot had already
streamed progress text. Earlier fixes also missed `task_complete` updates that
arrived after the prompt response. Current regression coverage addresses both.

## Status

| Case | State |
| --- | --- |
| Automated chat coverage | Passed: 174 cases, 0 failures, 0 notes on workspace `ce0ae05` |
| 1. Distinct final result after progress | Passed and maintainer-confirmed: `copilot/34b099ae-9767-4002-9a24-ed4184bc69dd`, final text inline once at buffer 227 line 17. Tool completion preceded `end_turn` by 8 ms, so late arrival remains unexercised live. |
| 2. Exact duplicate suppression | Passed and maintainer-confirmed: `copilot/e37fa54f-ece3-4297-b700-b3cabf262353`, identical assistant/tool text rendered once at buffer 9 line 18 in QA Neovim socket `/run/user/1000/nvim.1194962.0`. |

## Setup

1. Run `:LouiselmSessionNew` and choose `copilot`.
2. In `:LouiselmSessionOptions`, select Autopilot. The original reproduction used
   GPT-5.6 Terra with medium reasoning; select it if available, otherwise report
   the selected Model. Existing permission preferences can stay as configured.
3. Run `:LouiselmSessionId` and retain the copied `copilot/<uuid>` identity.
4. If Copilot reports unavailable quota or cannot start, report that error;
   neither case has then exercised the completion fix.

The running editor initially had two Codex Sessions and no Copilot Session.
Configured Copilot uses `acp-proxy -- node /home/lotso/code/copilot-acp/src/index.js`.
The configuration enables unredacted local proxy logging. Keep raw payloads local;
the QA record needs only this synthetic result, timestamps, IDs, and counts.

## Cases

### 1. A distinct terminal answer survives earlier progress

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2004` and the late-result branch at
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2764`.

Send this exact prompt in the fresh Copilot Session:

> This is a presentation QA check. First send one ordinary progress message:
> "QA_ZUFJ_PROGRESS_A: checking the multiplication." Then calculate 17 × 19
> and finish using your task_complete tool with the result text exactly
> "QA_ZUFJ_FINAL_A: 323." Put that final text only in task_complete, not in an
> ordinary assistant message. Do not read or change files or call other tools.

Wait for completion and a further five seconds to include late tool updates.
Do not submit a second prompt yet.

Expect: the progress message is visible, and the final result is readable inline
exactly once without opening the tool inspector.

Failure: a completed `task_complete` row exists and its inspector contains the
final result, but the result is absent from the timeline or appears twice.

If no `task_complete` event occurs, the prompt missed the required path; report
the miss, not a pass. Whether it arrived after `end_turn` must be established
from the log; the five-second wait does not prove that ordering.

### 2. An exact terminal echo is suppressed

Use a second fresh Copilot Session with the same options; retain its Session ID.
This exercises the exact-text containment guard at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2005`.

> This is a presentation QA check. First send one ordinary progress message:
> "QA_ZUFJ_PROGRESS_B: checking duplicate suppression." Then calculate 23 × 19
> silently. Finish using your task_complete tool, deliberately repeating exactly
> "QA_ZUFJ_PROGRESS_B: checking duplicate suppression." as its result text.
> The repeated progress sentence is intentional; this checks whether the UI
> suppresses an exact echo. Do not read or change files or call other tools.

Wait for completion and another five seconds without submitting another prompt.

Expect: the response shows `QA_ZUFJ_PROGRESS_B: checking duplicate suppression.`
once, though both the assistant stream and the completed tool payload contain it.
Ignore its occurrences in the user's prompt or tool inspector when counting
rendered responses.

Failure: two copies appear in the response. Without both wire sources, this case
has not exercised duplicate suppression.

### Case 2 first attempt: recipe miss

Session `copilot/f9fab884-9501-403b-9e7c-dd5d11d20376` sent prompt request 6
at `2026-09-11T08:13:04.261Z`. Tool `call_cEROTb6Ms9jHi2n58WwXBlRv`

title: Grill-me needed: when does a launch receipt claim Running?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; use a focused grill-me session.

The Launcher receipt vocabulary says each receipt records a completed privileged outcome and its resulting state. d6fv.4.4 requires sequence 0 to be durable before the capability channel is enabled or the gated Agent starts. The current /1 receipt schema nevertheless makes Launch sequence 0 result in Running, so a later enable/start failure leaves a durable false Running head.

Choose and confirm the v1 transaction semantics: (A) sequence 0 records Launch/Starting, then a linked mechanical Start/Running receipt is durably acknowledged after the gate releases; or (B) Running means a durable authorization-to-run rather than actual post-action state, requiring a vocabulary/schema change and terminal correction semantics. Pull on success timing, broker head truth, start failure, reconnect, and whether Start is a receipt-only action.

title: Verified skill supply and contained Agent Sessions
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM currently loads instructions from shared mutable directories and launches Agents with the operator's ambient filesystem, credentials, network, and host privileges. Provider-managed skills, repository-local skills, project instructions, plugins, native configuration, mutable symlinks, and self-updating runtimes can bypass LouiseLM's skill discovery.

A rogue or compromised Agent can therefore persist instructions, influence later Agents, alter the code enforcing checks, reach root-equivalent capabilities such as Docker, or write directly to shared repositories and Beads state. Human review is not a boundary when the Agent can modify either the reviewed bytes or the verifier.

LouiseLM needs one end-to-end outcome covering managed instruction supply, every Provider-visible file-based instruction source, and runtime containment. Partial delivery must never be reported as a Verified posture.

## Solution

Build a Linux-first verified Session pipeline.

Untrusted Skill candidates are normalized into immutable packages, deterministically inspected, presented in a canonical Dossier, and admitted into a complete signed Skill Generation through a local YubiKey ceremony. A protected remote Git branch witnesses each Generation before activation.

A root-owned launcher starts each verified Session under a distinct host identity with a private source snapshot, private home and Git metadata, measured Provider runtime, masked native instruction and configuration sources, and explicit capability channels. A separate unprivileged control service brokers Provider egress, credentials, dependency retrieval, canonical Beads mutations, and receipts. Agents may prepare candidates, request authority, collaborate, test, and export changes, but cannot alter trusted supply, the operator checkout, or canonical coordination state directly.

Every verification dimension is reported independently. Interactive operators may grant narrow expiring waivers; unattended Runs always fail closed.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want every Provider-visible file-based instruction source measured or masked, so native and repository-local instructions cannot bypass the managed gate.
2. As an operator, I want Agents to submit Skill candidates without installing them, so autonomous skill creation remains useful without granting persistence.
3. As a reviewer, I want a trusted tool to reconstruct the exact package and Dossier immediately before signing, so an Agent cannot substitute bytes or analysis.
4. As a reviewer, I want hidden characters, binaries, scripts, URLs, images, SVG content, source links, and update diffs exposed before approval.
5. As an operator, I want one YubiKey touch to admit a complete Skill Generation, while normal skill use remains prompt-free.
6. As an operator, I want a physically separate recovery key and explicit trust-reset procedure without a seed phrase or extractable master secret.
7. As an operator, I want vendor and LouiseLM skills governed by the same local Skill Admission policy, with publisher identity only evidence.
8. As an operator, I want Provider-specific views so one vendor's system instructions do not silently steer another vendor's Agent.
9. As an operator, I want new Generations activated only after remote witnessing and any integrity failure to block skill-enabled verified Sessions.
10. As an operator, I want emergency quarantine to narrow authority immediately for already-running Sessions.
11. As a user, I want each verified Session isolated from the operator checkout, credentials, Docker, privileged IPC, and other Sessions.
12. As a user, I want Provider binaries and adapters pinned as measured runtime packages rather than selected through live PATH or self-update.
13. As a user, I want project instructions captured from the Session's starting snapshot so Agent edits affect only future reviewed Sessions.
14. As a user, I want reusable Provider credentials kept outside Session files, environment, arguments, and prompts.
15. As an operator, I want network, commands, and child tools governed by attenuated Run capabilities.
16. As an Agent, I want lockfile dependencies fetched automatically and new dependencies handled as typed requests rather than unrestricted network traffic.
17. As an Agent, I want native br and bvr reads against local snapshots and brokered canonical mutations, preserving fast collaboration without direct canonical writes.
18. As an operator, I want Agent changes exported as normalized bundles and independently tested in a fresh confined Session before promotion.
19. As an operator, I want Sessions safely Parked when the control service disappears and retained under an explicit Forensics expiry.
20. As an Agent, I want stable robot-readable status, findings, requests, and receipts so I can organize all work except the human Admission act.
21. As an operator, I want verification reported by dimension with named expiring interactive waivers, so one debugging exception does not discard every protection.
22. As a reviewer, I want portable expiring Endorsements, so review evidence can be shared without admitting supply on another machine.

## Implementation Decisions

- Deliver managed skill integrity, Provider-visible instruction control, and runtime containment as one program. Slices may be developed independently, but the Verified posture claim requires the full chain.
- Build louiselm-skills as the sole Rust writer for Skill candidate ingest, immutable packaging, Inspection, Dossier generation, Skill Admission, Skill Generation construction, witnessing, installed views, Supply lineage, and robot status. Replace the legacy Python management scripts.
- Normalize packages to regular files. Resolve and copy allowed symlink content once; reject live links, hardlinks, special files, escaping paths, undeclared binary/executable content, races, and policy size violations.
- Keep local origins, URLs, commits, pins, rationale, and source-link history in Supply lineage; exclude them from portable package digests and Endorsements.
- Keep Inspection deterministic and model-free with a small fatal class and mandatory Dossier findings. Assessment remains isolated, digest-bound, model-generated, and advisory.
- Version and bind the Unicode allowlist, confusable checks, Inspection rules, Dossier, package manifests, Provider views, sequence, and predecessor into the Skill Generation.
- Recompute the exact package, Inspection, diff, Dossier, and set root inside the trusted local approval command; never sign Agent-supplied digests.
- Use a primary FIDO key for routine Skill Admission, a physically separate recovery key for key-policy change, and a separate logical release-signing role. Enforce user-presence and user-verification flags. Treat hardware-attestation data as optional evidence unless its manufacturer chain is actually validated.
- Trust the local kernel, root-owned approval binary, and local terminal during the v1 ceremony. Do not claim offline-host protection or proof that the human understood the Dossier.
- Keep a signed Generation pending until its exact record is present on the protected Git remote. Keep the prior Generation active during an outage. Do not require a redundant hardware signature on the containing Git commit.
- Fail closed on package or root mismatch. Permit an explicit isolated skills=off Session, but never silently drop content, load-and-label, downgrade, or fall back.
- Let authenticated emergency quarantine narrow authority without hardware; require a new hardware-authorized policy Generation to re-enable or persistently widen signers, endpoints, runtimes, Inspection, or isolation policy.
- Build louiselm-launch as a root-owned daemonless launcher reached through a narrow fixed privilege rule. It accepts a closed request and no caller-defined command, environment, mount, identity, or service property.
- Give each verified Session a distinct host identity, private home, stable private source snapshot including intentional dirty changes, private Git metadata, measured read-only cache base, and disposable overlay. Never share-write the live operator checkout or its Git metadata.
- Define a versioned isolation contract with hostile conformance tests. Linux mechanisms such as systemd, Landlock, and a pinned sandbox helper are replaceable implementations, not authority by name.
- Package Provider executables, adapters, origin, versions, hashes, relevant system-library baseline, and isolation evidence as immutable runtime identities. Stage updates explicitly.
- Mask or replace all external file-based Provider instruction/configuration sources, including native and repository skills, project instruction files, plugins, and native MCP configuration. Embedded instructions remain part of the measured Provider runtime and Provider disclosure.
- Expose no MCP servers in verified v1. Failure to prove native MCP and uncontrolled instruction sources absent blocks verified launch.
- Bind each Session to the Skill Generation, Provider view, measured runtime, project-instruction snapshot, tool/plugin schemas, isolation evidence, capability envelope, and disclosure posture through a Session input manifest.
- Put control authority in a separate local-only service under a dedicated unprivileged UID. Capture-service owns Attention state and delivery but no signing, launch, or approval authority.
- Use launcher-created per-Session Unix capability channels bound to Session, Run, policy revision, envelope, and peer identity. Store no reusable bearer token in files, environment, arguments, or prompts.
- Broker Provider authentication and destination-limited egress outside the sandbox; attenuate capabilities again for child commands and tools.
- Auto-fetch only exact starting-lockfile dependencies. Treat new coordinates as typed candidate requests; interactive approval may batch them and unattended Runs require a pre-authorized scope. Arbitrary URLs and Git dependencies require explicit approval.
- Let Sessions use local Beads replicas for native br and bvr reads. Route canonical mutations through a broker that invokes upstream br, derives actor identity, enforces revision/idempotency and budgets, returns receipts, and refreshes replicas.
- Preserve worker autonomy to request tracker actions while the broker remains the sole canonical byte writer and the coordinator retains dispatch, blocker promotion, integration, gate, and closure authority.
- Export changes through a trusted byte-only base-to-final bundle. Ignore Agent Git objects as authority, disable hooks, apply to a fresh snapshot, and run tests in a fresh confined verification Session before explicit promotion.
- On bounded control-service loss, revoke brokered capabilities and freeze the Session; record Park and Attention when control returns.
- Retain manifests, identities, hashes, receipts, and exported bundles durably. Retain private workspaces only for a configurable TTL or explicit pin; never retain reusable credentials.
- Apply ordinary updates to future Sessions. Emergency quarantine closes affected capabilities, Parks matching Sessions, and marks later outputs tainted.
- Report managed_supply, native_supply, runtime, isolation, network, and provider_disclosure separately. Allow only interactive named expiring waivers; unattended Runs never degrade.
- Provide stable human and robot interfaces for candidates, Inspection, Dossier, Admission, witnessing, posture, capabilities, dependencies, receipts, quarantine, and recovery. Extend Attention with skill_approval_pending and skill_unverified.
- Define portable Endorsement import/export, expiry, signer roles, signature-algorithm versioning, and local trust-policy evaluation. Endorsement never installs or admits anything.
- Treat the existing installation as untrusted input at cutover. Do not grandfather mutable links, compiled artifacts, Provider-managed system skills, or legacy typed reasons.
- Supersede the shared writable worktree, direct canonical Beads-write, and environment bearer-token assumptions in existing capability and parallel-worker work.

## Testing Decisions

- Use red-green-refactor for meaningful behavior and test public contracts rather than internal structure.
- Give canonicalization and Inspection deterministic vectors plus property/fuzz coverage for ordering, path normalization, traversal, links, special files, mutation races, modes, Unicode, binary declarations, SVG/assets, executable inventory, and stable hashes.
- Test trusted approval recomputation, stale/substituted Dossiers and Assessments, required FIDO flags, signer roles, sequence/predecessor chains, corruption, rollback, quarantine, recovery, and remote-witness failure with deterministic doubles plus a manual YubiKey acceptance procedure.
- Build hostile launcher conformance tests for filesystem and process escape, live host writes, Docker/privileged sockets, D-Bus/user-service escape, ptrace, cross-Session access, credential discovery, network bypass, native instruction/config leaks, uncontrolled MCP, cache poisoning, and sandbox-helper regressions.
- Test Provider adapters against every declared discovery source and prove unknown/unmasked sources fail closed. Verify measured runtime pinning, native-source masking, project-instruction capture, MCP absence, and truthful disclosure.
- Test capability attenuation, peer authentication, revision/replay, revocation, secret absence, egress destinations/costs, dependency request channels, and Beads mutation identity/idempotency/concurrency.
- Test trusted export, special-file/path rejection, ignored Agent Git metadata, disabled hooks, fresh verification Sessions, failed tests, and explicit promotion.
- Test service-loss grace, revoke/freeze/Park/recovery, Forensics expiry, Attention, taint propagation, per-dimension posture, named waiver expiry, and unattended fail-closed behavior.
- Add an end-to-end tracer: Skill candidate -> Inspection -> Dossier -> Skill Admission -> remote witness -> verified Session -> brokered work -> trusted bundle -> fresh verification -> promotion.
- Keep normal tests deterministic and offline with fake Providers, registries, witnesses, signers, and services. Use isolated Linux/manual acceptance for real kernel, Provider, Git remote, and YubiKey behavior.
- Verify clean-source release construction, dedicated release signature, root-owned installed bytes, dependency lock, policy digest, development-build rejection, and tamper detection.
- Add performance guards for realistic skill closures, Session materialization, manifest verification, and robot output without weakening policy limits.

## Out of Scope

- Compromise of the kernel, root account, root-owned trusted binaries, or local approval terminal.
- Cryptographically proving that a human read or understood a Dossier.
- Hiding plaintext intentionally sent to the selected cloud Provider.
- Treating a vendor signature or Endorsement as local Skill Admission.
- Windows support.
- MCP support in verified v1.
- Public Endorsement aggregation, anonymous or zero-knowledge reviewer membership, blockchains, tokens, OpenTimestamps, and offline approval on another machine.
- Automatic semantic proof that instructions or scripts are benevolent.
- Claiming direct vendor CLI launches outside louiselm-launch as verified.
- Compatibility shims or grandfathering for the legacy installation.

## Further Notes

This epic resolves louiselm-sooa. It must amend louiselm-qbr.5.1 and louiselm-qbr.6 rather than duplicating their capability and coordination semantics. beads_rust issue 436 shows native br can run in a narrow Landlock workspace; it does not authorize hostile Sessions to write canonical state. Any sandbox helper must be pinned and pass LouiseLM's contract because prior version-specific escapes make its name insufficient evidence.

Rollout is an atomic posture cutover: install trusted binaries, establish confinement and Provider adapters, inspect and admit the first complete Generation, witness it, then enable verified launches. Legacy Sessions remain unmanaged and Handoff into fresh verified Sessions.

Design provenance: claude/04517c0f-b217-423b-9433-7233027e6a78 and codex/01a0635e-ae82-71d3-b910-66377e02bd07.

## Success Criteria

1. The complete hostile tracer reaches an exact promoted bundle through a witnessed Skill Generation, verified Session, brokered effects, and fresh verification without an uncontrolled instruction, credential, network, host-write, or canonical-Beads path.
2. A Session is reported verified only when every required posture dimension has trusted evidence; partial components and waivers cannot produce the full claim.
3. Agents cannot modify trusted release bytes, admitted skill packages, the operator checkout, canonical Beads bytes, reusable credentials, or another Session.
4. Quarantine, service loss, recovery-key rotation, witness outage, and legacy Handoff have tested fail-closed operator procedures.
5. Human and robot interfaces agree on state, authority, evidence, failures, and next actions.

title: Package Skill candidates and render canonical Dossiers
description:
## Problem Statement

Skills remain connected to mutable directories, symlink targets, generated binaries, and Provider-managed files. A reviewer cannot know that the bytes shown are the bytes later loaded.

## Solution

Build the daemonless Rust `louiselm-skills` core that ingests a Skill candidate into an immutable content-addressed package, runs deterministic Inspection over its complete resolved closure, and produces the canonical Dossier. The trusted tool resolves, snapshots, hashes, and safely renders every input; Agent-produced hashes or reports are evidence only.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want mutable sources converted into immutable packages so later changes cannot alter reviewed instructions.
2. As a reviewer, I want suspicious text, scripts, URLs, binaries, assets, source links, and diffs exposed clearly before approval.
3. As an Agent, I want stable robot output for candidate state and next actions without loading candidate instructions into my working Session.
4. As an auditor, I want Supply lineage retained separately from portable package contents.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Equivalent trees with different source locations, traversal order, timestamps, and ownership produce the same canonical manifest and digest.
2. Declared symlink content is copied once as regular immutable files; later source or link mutation cannot alter the package. Local link origins remain only in Supply lineage.
3. Cycles, hardlink ambiguity, devices, sockets, FIFOs, escaping paths, duplicate normalized paths, mutation during capture, and policy size violations fail closed without publishing a package.
4. Inspection rejects its small fatal class and emits typed mandatory Dossier findings for Unicode/confusables, URLs, credential references, encoded payloads, network/process imports, SVG behavior, declared binaries, executables, and images.
5. The Unicode profile and Inspection policy are versioned and content-addressed; external feeds cannot silently widen or weaken them.
6. Assessment is isolated, has an empty capability envelope, is keyed to package digest + Model + prompt version, and remains advisory. A mismatch is treated as no current Assessment.
7. Before approval, the trusted command independently recomputes package, Inspection, diff, and Dossier from captured bytes; it never accepts an Agent-provided digest as authority.
8. Human and `--robot-*` views derive from one normalized state. Hostile content is escaped and robot output has versioned fields, typed findings, stable identifiers, and explicit next actions.
9. The immutable store prevents replacing an existing digest with different bytes.

## Implementation Notes

- This Rust tool becomes the only writer for immutable packages and generated skill views and replaces the legacy Python management scripts.
- Keep portable package bytes separate from local Supply lineage.
- Define one canonical path, mode, hashing, and serialization contract shared by later signing and verification.

## Testing Notes

- Use golden vectors for manifests, digests, Unicode findings, decoded content, SVG extraction, and Dossier rendering.
- Add hostile traversal, symlink-cycle, hardlink, special-file, normalization collision, race/TOCTOU, and source-removal tests.
- Fuzz path normalization and manifest parsing; assert robot output never carries unsanitized control sequences.
- Use an isolated fake for Assessment; normal tests require no model, network, or hardware.

## Out of Scope

- FIDO signing, recovery, and remote witnessing.
- Provider-specific views and Session launch.
- Runtime containment of package scripts.
- Public Endorsement aggregation.

comments.text:
Canonical contract decisions, for the issues that bind to it (d6fv.2 signs it, d6fv.3 views it, d6fv.8 endorses it).

Package digest = sha256 of the canonical manifest bytes; manifest is the Merkle root. Pinned byte-for-byte in skills-core/tests/canonical.rs — changing it changes what a Skill Generation signature means.

Manifest carries path, executable, size, sha256, sorted by path. Excluded deliberately: mtime, ownership, permission bits beyond executable, inode, source location, empty directories, symlinks. Everything excluded is either local (goes to Supply lineage) or uncheckable by a reviewer.

Symlinks materialize as regular files. TOCTOU and source-removal are exercised through a crate-private probe seam (capture::stage_with_probe), not a racing writer thread. A guard whose failure path was only ever raced is a guard nobody has seen fail.

Fatal class is three cases on purpose: no SKILL.md, unusable frontmatter, text that is not UTF-8. Everything else is a mandatory finding. Growing the fatal class moves judgement from the reviewer to a scanner that cannot read prose.

title: Generated skill installation silently diverges from its catalog source
description:
The skill directory consumed by LouiseLM can be rewritten independently of the catalog source and already contains undeclared generated binary content. A later Agent may therefore read bytes that catalog ownership, source, and review metadata do not describe.

## Observed

Verified locally on 2026-09-03 during Session `codex/01a0635e-ae82-71d3-b910-66377e02bd07`.

The Codex system-skill marker differs between the consumed view and the catalog's claimed source:

```text
84972c9eed7562a1cbb564bf4ff714e33f5e5c40ebd0b201f0fbb572251b04c6  ~/.config/agentskills/generated/.system/.codex-system-skills.marker
bc2f559db2500f4ab635caca0f90f210bded879faa81b6569e74f8b42960b9f0  ~/dotfiles/agentskills/.config/agentskills/.system/.codex-system-skills.marker
```

`diff -qr` also reports differing consumed/source bytes in at least:

```text
.system/imagegen/SKILL.md
.system/imagegen/references/{cli,image-api,prompting,sample-prompts}.md
.system/skill-creator/SKILL.md
.system/skill-creator/agents/openai.yaml
.system/skill-creator/scripts/{init_skill,quick_validate}.py
```

The catalog still labels `.system--imagegen`, `.system--skill-creator`, and `.system--skill-installer` as `lifecycle=owned`, `ownership=owned`, with their source under `~/dotfiles/agentskills/.config/agentskills/.system/...`.

An undeclared compiled artifact is also inside the consumed tree:

```text
~/.config/agentskills/generated/tweet-fetch/scripts/__pycache__/fetch_tweets.cpython-313.pyc
```

## Symptoms

- Catalog output can say a Provider system skill is owned while LouiseLM consumes different runtime-managed bytes.
- An accidental Python cache becomes instruction-supply content without a catalog transition or review.
- No load-time error or posture downgrade identifies either mismatch.

## Root Cause

`generated/` is both a catalog build output and a Provider-writable native skill directory. Provider refresh and ordinary script execution can mutate it after inventory/build. LouiseLM discovery scans directories directly and does not enforce catalog identity or an immutable admitted package at Session construction.

## Why It Was Not Caught

The current scripts check consistency only when explicitly run. There is no sole writer, immutable package, signed set, continuous source mediation, or test in which a Provider refreshes `.system` after a successful build.

## Fix Direction

Do not teach the catalog to bless the changed bytes. Route every current entry through Skill candidate packaging/Inspection and replace the shared mutable directory with Provider-scoped witnessed views under `louiselm-d6fv.1`, `.3`, and the atomic cutover `.9`. Remove compiled/cache artifacts and the Provider installer from admitted views.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A captured regression reproduces Provider mutation after inventory and fails Verified posture before the fix.
2. Provider refresh cannot alter the immutable package or active witnessed view; unknown bytes fail closed with a typed source/digest error.
3. The `.pyc` is rejected as undeclared binary content and cannot enter the first Skill Generation.
4. Catalog/Supply-lineage metadata is never presented as Skill Admission authority.
5. The end-to-end cutover proves no native or runtime-managed path can add content to a verified Session.

## Not Covered

Embedded instructions inside a measured Provider executable remain part of Provider runtime trust. No current files are deleted or changed by filing this bug.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Hash `generated/.system/.codex-system-skills.marker` and the catalog source `.system/.codex-system-skills.marker`; observe different digests.
2. Run a recursive file comparison between those two `.system` directories; observe differing skill, reference, metadata, and script bytes.
3. Inspect `catalog.json`; observe the affected `.system` skills still claim `owned` source entries under the separate catalog tree.
4. Search the consumed generated tree for compiled Python files; observe `tweet-fetch/scripts/__pycache__/fetch_tweets.cpython-313.pyc`.
5. Start ordinary LouiseLM discovery; observe no source/digest failure before those bytes become available as skill supply.

title: Recover signing access with Android passkeys and paper phrases
description:
## Problem Statement
An operator with one physical YubiKey cannot complete the current first-time recovery setup, even with an Android phone and the ability to keep a paper backup.

## Solution
Enroll a password-manager-backed Android passkey and a paper recovery phrase alongside one physical YubiKey. Either recovery method independently authorizes replacement signing keys; the YubiKey continues to sign ordinary Skill Admissions and trusted releases.

## User Stories
1. As an operator, I want first setup to work with my existing YubiKey, Android phone, and paper.
2. As an operator who lost a YubiKey, I want either recovery method to enroll replacement hardware keys.
3. As an operator who also lost a phone, I want the paper phrase to work independently.
4. As an operator, I want exact changes shown before approval and a durable result afterward.
5. As an auditor, I want replaced keys refused for new approvals while already-approved history remains verifiable.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Initial setup enrolls normal hardware-backed Admission/release credentials plus both recovery methods. Incomplete setup cannot report recovery-ready.
2. Android passkeys may be backed up by the operator's password manager. Passkey recovery is reusable; no claim that a synced credential is confined to one physical device.
3. Either passkey OR paper phrase alone authorizes replacement keys. Neither directly authorizes ordinary Admissions or release signatures.
4. Replacement confirms possession of the new hardware credentials and the exact proposed change. Replaced keys cannot authorize future approvals; existing approved history remains verifiable.
5. Paper phrases are generated and entered through a trusted local tool, never Agent/chat/log/argv payloads. A successful use consumes the phrase and confirms a new written replacement in the same durable transition.
6. Changing recovery methods requires an existing YubiKey or working recovery method and explicit confirmation of the exact change. Paper authorization consumes and replaces its phrase.
7. Concurrent, stale, replayed, malformed, wrong-domain, wrong-origin, missing-verification, and interrupted requests fail closed; partial failure does not strand the operator or revive retired credentials.
8. Losing every usable signing/recovery method requires explicit trust reset and re-enrollment.
9. Production enrollment/recovery verifies the installed authority and protected trust store; development tests cannot confer Verified posture.
10. Real Android/password-manager, paper-recovery, and root-owned-install acceptance is recorded before claiming the installed workflow works. lm70 owns the subsequent genuine release acceptance.

## Implementation Notes
Confirmed by maintainer in codex/01a07753-51de-7733-bfeb-8a3f26fa907e after louiselm-nksh. This supersedes the two-physical-token prerequisite and exclusion of paper/software recovery for this supported policy. Preserve distinct signing purposes and the existing local trusted-tool/kernel/TTY boundary. Vocabulary delta: No change.
Use standard browser passkey facilities where they provide the requested Android behavior; do not add a native Android layer merely to duplicate them. Use established WebAuthn and mnemonic implementations, with dependency rationale recorded; no custom cryptography or vendored wordlist.
Serialize and atomically publish trust mutations before implementing single-use recovery.

## Testing Notes
Red-green coverage through the trusted CLI and public APIs; deterministic credentials and browser doubles for automated tests; real competing processes and failure/interruption boundaries. Existing Rust gates and relevant browser tests. Hardware and actual installed acceptance remain separate evidence.

## Out of Scope
Normal release/Admission signing by passkey or phrase; generic account login; recovery of project files; host conformance/Verified cutover decisions in ucj1; automatic reset or authority widening; native Android capture changes unless the selected passkey flow demonstrates a concrete gap.

title: Serialize and atomically publish trust changes
description:
## Goal
A concurrent or interrupted trust mutation cannot lose an acknowledged change or apply one authorization twice.

## Scope
Existing TrustStore bootstrap, rotation, and reset plus their production CLI paths; preserve existing signing behavior. No new recovery UI or cryptography.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Mutations share one cross-process lock and re-read current trust while holding it.
2. Competing/stale rotations fail explicitly; at most one applies.
3. Publish complete validated state atomically with file and directory durability; never overwrite unrelated/symlink targets.
4. Reset coordinates with bootstrap/rotation; malformed existing state is not replaced silently.
5. Public CLI/API results preserve causes and do not report durable success prematurely.

## Testing
Demonstrate RED/GREEN with real competing CLI processes or an externally held storage lock and preservation/failure-path tests. Run all skills-core Rust gates. Use existing rustix/std facilities; no new dependency for locking or atomic files.

## Notes
Prerequisite for single-use paper recovery under d6fv.11. Keep lock ownership explicit and bounded; no broad transaction framework.

title: Recover hardware signing keys with a single-use paper phrase
description:
## Goal
The trusted tool accepts a locally generated paper phrase to authorize exact replacement hardware signing keys and atomically issues a replacement phrase.

## Scope
Closed recovery policy/state, typed changes, paper enrollment/recovery through CLI and public API. Passkey proof integration and complete two-method onboarding follow separately.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Use cryptographically random, checksummed human-readable phrases and store only their verifier/public authority, never plaintext.
2. A successful paper authorization changes only the reviewed keys/methods and consumes/replaces the phrase in the same serialized durable state change.
3. Wrong/malformed/reused phrases, stale plans and failed new-phrase confirmation leave authority unchanged.
4. Replaced keys cannot issue new approvals; already-approved history remains verifiable. Recovery cannot directly sign releases/Admissions.
5. Phrase generation/entry uses a trusted local TTY, with no secret in argv, robot output, Agent transcripts, logs or durable plaintext files.
6. Normal signing remains hardware-required; assert replacement-key possession and reject a software replacement in production.
7. Interrupted/competing requests cannot revive a phrase or lock out the operator.

## Testing
Behavior-first CLI/public API tests with deterministic fixture secrets, preservation/replay/role/retirement/failure/concurrency coverage; full Rust gates. No real secrets or hardware in automated tests.

## Notes
Use a maintained mnemonic implementation rather than inventing encoding or vendoring a wordlist. Full production recovery-ready status waits for passkey enrollment and the integrated onboarding task.

title: Authorize recovery with a password-manager-backed Android passkey
description:
## Goal
The operator can approve exact recovery changes using an Android passkey backed up by their password manager.

## Scope
Passkey registration/authentication and their trusted CLI/browser path into the shared recovery transaction. Reuse browser cross-device passkey support when it meets the Android requirement; no native app changes without a demonstrated gap.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Use a maintained WebAuthn verifier; verify RP/origin, unpredictable challenge, credential identity, user verification, and the exact pending change.
2. Bind short-lived challenge state to the protected authority snapshot and transaction; altered, expired, replayed and cross-origin assertions fail without mutation.
3. Accept backed-up passkeys as confirmed policy without claiming device-bound hardware.
4. A passkey independently authorizes replacement keys or recovery-method changes; it never directly signs ordinary releases/Admissions.
5. Prompt cancellation, browser/transport loss and late responses dispose pending work without changing authority.
6. Browser UI displays the exact action and result; capture-service and pairing credentials gain no recovery authority.
7. Avoid exposing secrets, accepting attacker-selected trust roots, or leaving a network service running after the ceremony.

## Testing
Deterministic WebAuthn fixtures with real verifier checks and browser virtual authenticators, including negative origin/challenge/UV/credential/replay cases; behavioral UI tests; all affected gates. Real Android/password-manager behavior belongs to the manual acceptance task.

title: Accept both recovery methods against the installed release
description:
## Goal
Prove the actual installed one-YubiKey workflow with Android/password-manager and paper recovery after the genuine release ceremony.

## Scope
Maintainer-assisted installed acceptance in the disposable Linux VM, with host-side signing/passkey interaction and explicit public-artifact transfer. Preserve resettable guest state and stop the VM afterward.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Record installed release ID, root-owned authority and successful initial enrollment of both methods.
2. Maintainer observes real Android passkey user verification and password-manager availability.
3. Exercise each independent recovery route using distinct replacement credentials on the available physical YubiKey; do not claim a second physical device was tested.
4. Prove the old paper phrase fails after successful use, a replacement phrase works, old signing credentials refuse new approval, and approved history remains verifiable.
5. Exercise method replacement, wrong/replayed inputs, cancellation and reset boundaries without mutating unrelated user credentials.
6. Record maintainer acceptance, separate remaining limitations, and the exact evidence before closing the feature.

## Testing
No fake/software credential result substitutes for hardware/passkey acceptance. Fixtures and gate results are supporting evidence only. No host sudo, silent USB passthrough, production credential deletion or secret capture. Use isolated recovery credentials and protected local TTYs.
