title: Gate Verified Sessions on current host conformance
description:
## Problem Statement

The hostile launcher suite establishes component/host behavior in disposable environments, but production admission does not consume a current host-conformance result. Mechanism records and registration labels cannot establish that the actual host, installed launch implementation and active policy passed the required probes.

The maintainer confirmed the complete policy in louiselm-ucj1 on 2026-09-11, Source Session codex/01a09171-93e0-7b53-9c29-ce2a0465bb92. This feature implements that decision and gates the end-to-end Verified cutover.

## Solution

Require current, host-specific conformance evidence for Verified admission; keep it current through supervisor-owned validity checks; expose precisely scoped interactive waivers and fail-closed suspension/recovery. Use the existing privileged launcher authority, Control broker, Launcher receipts and lifecycle ownership. This is one capability under the Verified skill supply and contained Agent Sessions epic.

## User Stories

1. As the operator, I can explicitly certify my actual host without disturbing unrelated workloads, and learn exactly why evidence is current, missing, stale, incomplete or failed.
2. As the operator, I can knowingly waive unavailable evidence for one interactive Session while unattended Runs and demonstrated containment failures remain blocked.
3. As the operator, I retain control when evidence becomes invalid: affected work stops, its actual state remains inspectable, and recovery never resumes work automatically.
4. As an auditor, I can retrieve the exact report and waiver bound to a launch and distinguish observed results, measured inputs and the policy actually enforced.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An explicit installed maintenance command invokes trusted conformance code on the actual host. Installation/update automation may invoke it; ordinary launch does not initiate testing. Use test-owned files, identities, processes and isolated endpoints, harmless sentinels, bounded operation deadlines and owned cleanup. Unrelated workloads and host-wide settings remain untouched. A required check that cannot run yields incomplete certification, never a silent skip or pass.
2. Retain the existing hostile matrix's positive-control and observed-denial contract, required inventory and rejection of missing, contradictory, duplicate or unexpected observations. Reuse production launcher mechanics. Fixture success is not proof for untested real Agent integrations or the installed end-to-end workflow.
3. Bind reports to the actual host/current boot, relevant running-host measurements, exact launcher/backend/probe/policy artifacts and an explicit bounded list of required runtime libraries and loader configuration. Required inputs must be measurable. Enumerate the supported measurement surface and its limits. A changed relevant input or reboot invalidates the corresponding certificate; version labels alone cannot establish unchanged bytes.
4. Admission revalidates report identity, integrity, applicability, result, currency and unresolved-failure state before allowing Verified execution, together with existing mandatory launch checks. Current passing evidence is eligibility, not a substitute for the other Verified dimensions.
5. Missing, stale or incomplete evidence allows an explicit interactive waiver scoped to the Session and the waived condition, with isolation displayed as unverified and the actual waiver recorded. Unattended Runs cannot waive it. Missing mandatory containment controls still refuse launch. A cancelled/incomplete test cannot produce a passing result or erase known failure; unreadable failure history cannot be treated as empty.
6. An observed containment failure is non-waivable, blocks affected launches and remains recorded across reboot, upgrade and certificate expiry. Only successful recertification covering the failed boundary clears it. Retain failure state independently of the current passing-report reference.
7. Each active Session uses its existing Launch supervisor for validity checks every second. A detected relevant mismatch triggers suspension; five seconds without a successful check also triggers suspension of a Verified Session. Bound work and validate cadence/freshness handling under load, including stalled checks. Sampling is not a hard real-time guarantee, instantaneous drift detection or continuous containment attestation.
8. On lost/invalid evidence, revoke affected brokered capabilities and freeze the actual process tree. If freeze cannot be confirmed, attempt full termination. Preserve unconfirmed cleanup as an unresolved failure; never report successful containment/disposal or release reusable identity without proof. Existing waivers cover only their approved condition and cannot hide new containment failure.
9. Recovery is operator-directed and requires fresh checks/authorization. Successful recertification never automatically resumes processes or restores capabilities. Evidence-only suspension can resume after revalidation; actual containment failure requires bounded diagnostic-evidence preservation, disposal and fresh Sessions after recertification.
10. A new release requires its own certification. Existing Sessions can continue only while their pinned implementation/dependencies, host state and governing policy remain valid and their old release remains approved. Mere installation of a new release must not invalidate unaffected pinned Sessions. Revocation or an actual relevant change does affect them.
11. The signed launch receipt binds the exact admission report digest. The launcher protects the report; the Control broker retains the exact bytes for inspection. Waived launches bind the actual evidence status and waiver. Lifecycle evidence records the cause and actual resulting state without rewriting historical launch evidence or manufacturing a pass.
12. Consume the correction tracked by louiselm-etth: remove library_baseline and isolation_policy_version from registration and RuntimeMeasurement; bind the policy actually enforced and concrete measurement/conformance evidence. Do not duplicate the bug or treat its currently declared strings as measured inputs.
13. Integrate the installed admission, supervisor, broker, receipt and operator-posture consumers. Preserve unrelated user-selected Agent approval policies. Reuse the existing posture/quarantine work where applicable. The maintained end-to-end acceptance in louiselm-d6fv.9 is the only route to activating the user-visible Verified claim; closing this feature must state its actual production consumer/gate and cannot claim that cutover happened.

## Implementation Notes

- Existing boundaries: isolation contract and evidence validation; launcher runtime registry, release identity and sandbox backend; launch-supervisor admission/lifecycle; launch receipts; Control broker canonical evidence storage and capability revocation; existing posture/waiver presentation.
- The approved policy is authoritative on louiselm-ucj1. Keep caller-selected identifiers separate from trusted measurements; caller input cannot choose arbitrary privileged test commands or omit mandatory checks.
- Reports and validity work require bounded input validation, explicit expected errors, safe ownership and shutdown handling. Apply existing protocol, privacy, cleanup-proof and scheduling invariants.
- Do not silently expand a measurement claim beyond the supported inputs or confuse conformance observations with proof against unknown kernel flaws or trusted-root compromise.
- The existing louiselm-etth bug owns removal of misleading metadata. This feature depends on that correction rather than duplicating it.
- Coordinate integration with existing Verified posture/emergency-quarantine work and the real broker lifecycle. No takeover of another Agent's live claim.

## Testing Notes

Use red-green-refactor and existing deterministic test tools. Cover real report production/consumption, receipt-to-report integrity, wrong host/boot/artifacts/policy/dependencies, missing and malformed inputs, positive-control failure, cancellation and cleanup, persistent failure across reboot/upgrade/expiry, waived versus unattended admission, per-Session waiver scope, monitored mismatches and stalled checks, capability revocation/process-tree suspension, disposal failure, manual recovery and unaffected pinned-release Sessions. Use controllable time for deadline behavior plus representative-load verification; do not claim a hard real-time bound. Preserve real privileged-boundary coverage through disposable environments and the existing required hostile matrix. Run complete affected Rust and, if touched, Lua suites and gates. Installed host-safe certification and the genuine consumer path require maintainer acceptance before declaring the corresponding live behavior proven.

## Out of Scope

Automatic launch-triggered conformance runs; tests against live credentials or desktop services; modifying host-wide settings to make tests pass; a new privileged daemon or signing-role system; root/kernel-compromise attestation; treating CI or fixture success as installed Verified proof; automatic recovery; preserving unsafe process trees after observed failure; implementing the end-to-end cutover itself.

Vocabulary delta: No change.

Desktop /usr/local/lib/louiselm absent. Full isolated Rust and strict/browser gates plus disposable actual-daemon/certification/hostile gates green; evidence on .12.5/.12.7. No installed Verified claim or .9 cutover. Self-claim released; implementation is included in the requested scoped commit, unrelated edits preserved.

title: Optional host measurements conflate absence with literal bytes
description:

title: Report absent conformance evidence as unverified in canonical status
description:
## Goal
Make absent conformance admission observable in every canonical Session status without confusing admission history with current isolation posture.

## Confirmed scope
Maintainer decision louiselm-nj0g6 supersedes original AC2/AC3. Add separate bounded immutable admission history derived from authenticated retained LaunchEvidence. Preserve current six-dimension posture and its existing pure evaluator.

## Acceptance
1. Every canonical status includes conformance admission: Unevaluated, Certified with exact report digest, or Waived with exact Condition and optional report digest.
2. Unevaluated remains isolation unverified/evidence_missing with a safe next action and no invented success timestamp.
3. Historical Certified or Waived admission alone never promotes current isolation to verified or waived; missing current evidence remains unverified. Waiver history is not renewed or treated as current authority.
4. Derive admission only from authenticated retained launch facts, preserving report validation. Status reads run no probes, renew nothing, and leave receipts, audit and authority unchanged.
5. Operator and self-scoped Agent responses agree on admission and posture. Fields are closed/validated and bounded: no paths, process identities or raw producer text.
6. Default/unset, all admission variants, redaction, restart and operator/Agent parity have regression coverage. Preserve historical-report rejection tests, update public protocol docs/schema, run full affected gates.

## Boundaries
No admission gate activation, currentness monitor, waiver policy or user-visible Verified cutover. .12.4 owns currentness; .6.3 current waivers; .6.9 ordered Attention projection; .9 complete cutover. Consumes .12.3 retained evidence and .6.10 canonical posture. Lessons/design: oi5an, rn38 and nj0g6.

title: Retain exact conformance report bytes for broker inspection
description:
## Goal
Retain the exact conformance observation report bytes in the Control broker, so
an auditor can fetch the evidence a launch was admitted under rather than only
its digest.

## Why this is separate
Parent AC11 has two halves. The receipt half landed in louiselm-d6fv.12.3:
`LaunchEvidence.conformance` binds the exact report digest, and
`BrokerInspection.launch_evidence` already carries the recorded status through
the existing inspection surface, so certified, waived and unevaluated Sessions
are already distinguishable.

The byte-retention half has no producer yet. Under the louiselm-oi5an decision
the production launch path records `Unevaluated`: the admission gate is not in
force before the louiselm-d6fv.9 cutover, so no report is read and no bytes
exist to retain. Building the store and its mismatch rejection now would be an
extension point for a consumer that does not exist, which project scope
forbids, and would be a third inert slice in this area.

## Scope
In: broker retention of the exact report bytes bound to the Session and to the
digest already in the receipt; refusal of bytes that do not match that digest;
bounded inspection access.
Out: running the admission gate, attendance/waiver protocol, re-measuring or
re-evaluating evidence on a status read, and the cutover itself.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Bytes retained for a Session hash to the exact `conformance_report_digest`
   already bound in its sequence-zero receipt; a mismatch is refused, not
   stored.
2. Retention is bound to the exact Session, Run and authorization; foreign or
   replayed report bytes cannot be attached.
3. Inspection returns the retained bytes within existing bounds and redaction
   rules; absence is reported as absence, never as an empty success.
4. A launch recording `Unevaluated` or a waiver over absent evidence retains no
   bytes and says so, rather than storing a placeholder.
5. Reading retained bytes runs no probes, renews nothing and changes no
   authority.

## Testing
Red-green through the broker inspection APIs: matching bytes accepted, mismatched
and foreign/replayed bytes refused, absent-evidence cases reported as absent,
redaction, and a read leaving receipts and authority unchanged. Run complete
affected crate gates.

## Notes
Confirmed design: louiselm-oi5an. Receipt half and the digest it must match:
louiselm-d6fv.12.3. Cannot start until the admission gate actually reads host
evidence, which louiselm-d6fv.9 carries as part of the cutover.

title: Preserve receipt trust across launcher key changes
description:
## Problem Statement
Launcher receipt chains must survive routine key rotation and release upgrades without losing their evidentiary value. Today the broker pins historical chains to current installed release/key identity. Compromised or unreadable history also needs an explicit failure boundary.

## Solution
Preserve trusted historical release/key bindings and exact receipt bytes; separate routine key retirement from compromise revocation; quarantine individual untrusted chains without disabling unrelated Sessions. Confirmed decision and provenance: louiselm-b68f, codex/01a0a13a-d078-7662-aecf-e0d916c9b262.

## User Stories
1. Operators rotate keys and upgrade releases without invalidating ordinary historical receipts.
2. Existing Sessions finish under their original key while new Sessions use the active key.
3. Operators contain compromised-key effects and see precise Session-local versus shared-authority failure.
4. Retired private keys cease being retained when no live Session needs them; public verification history remains.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Normal rotation preserves existing-chain verification/continuation and rejects new chains under retired keys. Release upgrades preserve historical verification against originally trusted identities without reapproval or rewriting receipts.
2. Root-controlled historical authority remains distinct from current launch authority; unknown/revoked keys, unregistered identities, forged/backdated new history, and chain splicing are rejected.
3. Explicit key-compromise handling disables affected capabilities, freezes affected Sessions, blocks their continuation/recovery from compromised evidence, and retains receipts marked untrusted. Unaffected Sessions remain usable.
4. Individual unreadable/unverifiable chains are preserved and isolated with typed errors. Shared registry or broker identity trust failure blocks the broker.
5. Historical public keys survive retirement; private-key cleanup requires trusted proof that no live Session can still need the key and cannot race with launch, signing, Park/resume, disposal, or rotation.
6. Installed tests exercise restart, rotation, cross-release historical verification, compromised/unreadable chains, unaffected Sessions, and cleanup. Report automated versus maintainer/live acceptance separately.

## Implementation Notes
Reuse installed launcher trust, receipt-chain verification, supervisor lifecycle controls, and canonical broker status. Do not build a second grant, receipt, or quarantine system. Existing emergency Skill Generation quarantine stays owned by louiselm-d6fv.6.5; this feature handles launcher signing-key trust.
Prior lesson louiselm-9xza: retired keys verify protected admitted history, not any old-key signature or unsigned timestamp. Launcher keys may continue an already admitted live chain after retirement.

## Testing Notes
Red-green behavioral coverage plus complete affected Rust and privileged disposable-host gates per docs/agent-testing.md. Use temporary authorities and mock Agents; no production key mutation or live workload changes during implementation testing.

## Out of Scope

title: Verify admitted receipt history across rotation and upgrades
description:
## Goal
Existing Launcher receipt chains stay verifiable after routine rotation or release upgrade, and live Sessions continue under their original key.

## Scope
Installed historical authority, new-chain admission, ReceiptStore anchors, installed public verification, and their production consumers. Excludes compromise propagation, failure isolation, and retired-private-key cleanup.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Enroll durable trusted release/key and Session-chain bindings at the existing trusted installation/admission boundary. Historical identity never comes solely from an untrusted receipt or self-declared timestamp.
2. A chain admitted before routine rotation verifies and can append valid lifecycle receipts under its original key. New Session admission uses the current active key; retired keys cannot start new chains.
3. After ordinary release upgrade and broker reopen, original exact receipts verify against original trusted authority; current release authority still governs new launches. No receipt rewriting, re-signing, manual reapproval, or permission widening.
4. Preserve exact Session/Run/revision, sequence, previous digest, signature, and per-chain release/key checks. Reject unknown identity, fabricated/backdated historical genesis, foreign prefix and splicing.
5. Enrollment/rotation/restart cannot partially publish authority or admit a stale new chain. Replay has a bounded deterministic outcome and no duplicate identity.
6. Wire changes into installed broker/verifier and publish required operator/API documentation; a helper-only implementation cannot close this task as consumed.

## Testing
Red-green regressions through real ReceiptStore and installed verifier consumers: rotate live chain, stale/new admission race, release change with old history, failed durable enrollment, restart/replay, tampered genesis and suffix. Run full affected crate gates and relevant installed disposable-VM tests.

## Notes
Starting points: skills-core/src/broker/receipts.rs, broker/installed.rs, launcher_install.rs and launcher_install/broker.rs. Source decision louiselm-b68f. Prior lesson louiselm-9xza concerns protected history, not blanket acceptance of retired keys. Do not change Skill Admission retirement semantics or claim seamless live release upgrades.

title: Isolate unverifiable Session chains in broker recovery
description:
## Goal
A damaged or untrusted Session receipt chain does not prevent unrelated Sessions from using a trustworthy broker.

## Scope
Installed broker startup/reconciliation, per-Session history trust state, canonical inspection and safe Attention/error projection. Shared authority validation remains a broker-wide prerequisite. Excludes signing-key revocation commands and general Skill Generation quarantine.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Malformed, missing/unreadable, bad-signature, unknown-identity, or contradictory chain evidence is preserved without truncation, splice, automatic repair, or replacement.
2. Quarantine the affected Session: deny continuation, recovery, Resume and capability enablement based on that chain; expose a stable typed cause and safe next action. Inspection never grants authority.
3. Trustworthy unaffected Sessions remain inspectable and usable. An invalid key registry or broker identity marker refuses broker-wide operation because Session-level separation cannot establish trust.
4. Restart and retries preserve the quarantine decision; later stale status or receipt input cannot silently reclassify the chain as trusted.
5. Durable normalized reporting uses existing canonical status and outbox boundaries; avoid prompts, raw payloads, private keys or sensitive paths in diagnostics.

## Testing
Two-Session installed/recovery tests: corrupt or make one chain unreadable, restart, prove isolated refusal and unaffected operation; corrupt shared authority and prove global refusal. Include malformed genesis, unknown key, stale retry, disk/reporting failure and byte preservation. Run complete affected gates.

## Notes
Source decision louiselm-b68f. Reuse broker lifecycle/reconciliation and existing receipt/status consumers. Relate to louiselm-qbr.5.1.2.4 without taking over its work. Do not treat every failure as whole-host corruption, nor continue when the shared trust boundary is uncertain.

title: Revoke compromised launcher keys across affected Sessions
description:
## Goal
Explicit revocation of a compromised launcher key disables its live authority and marks its history untrusted while unaffected Sessions continue.

## Scope
Trusted operator/admin key-revocation mutation through existing launcher authority, installed signer/verifier enforcement, affected-Session lifecycle/capability control, and broker status. Excludes root-compromise recovery, re-attestation, and private-key garbage collection.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Persist a clear compromised/revoked state distinct from routine retirement. Agent actions, broker projections and receipt text cannot authorize this administrative trust change or undo it.
2. Prevent signing/admission/continuation using a revoked key, including already-open signer/verifier snapshots, concurrent signing, pending launch and resumed Sessions. Restart or retry cannot resurrect revoked authority.
3. Revoke affected Session capabilities and request freeze through existing authenticated lifecycle boundaries; required control failures remain fail-closed and visible. Preserve existing narrowed-authority ordering.
4. Block affected continuation/recovery based on compromised evidence. Keep original receipt bytes and mark them untrusted, including older receipts: no exemption based only on claimed signing time.
5. Unaffected-key Sessions remain usable. Do not relabel a receipt newly signed by the compromised key as proof that containment succeeded; report controller/supervisor outcomes with their actual trust limits.
6. Trusted inspection reports revoked key, affected Sessions, containment failures and safe next actions without secrets. No auto re-trust, automatic replacement launch, or rollback claim.

## Testing
Disposable two-key/two-Session tests cover explicit revocation, unaffected continuation, live and paused Sessions, old signer snapshots, signing/revocation races, late replies, controller loss, persisted restart and retry. Use existing lifecycle tests with production callback shapes; run complete affected gates and installed checks.

## Notes
Source decision louiselm-b68f. Reuse established capability revocation and freeze controls. louiselm-d6fv.6.5 owns Skill Generation quarantine and remains separate; do not create another general grant/quarantine engine. Root compromise is outside the trusted-host model and must not be called repaired by key rotation.

title: Remove retired private keys after their final live Session
description:
## Goal
Retired launcher private keys stop being retained once no live Session needs them, while historical public verification remains available.

## Scope
Root-owned installed key lifecycle/cleanup, authoritative live-Session key references, and existing signer validation. Excludes history deletion, unrelated state cleanup and any weakening of revocation.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. An active key remains available. A routinely retired key remains available while any live Session still needs lifecycle signatures, including a retained Session that can resume or still requires terminal/disposal evidence.
2. Remove only the exact retired private key after trusted lifecycle state proves no live Session can use it and no signing operation is in flight. An age threshold, Agent claim, empty/unreadable inventory, or uncertain cleanup is insufficient proof.
3. Serialize retirement/cleanup with admission, signing, lifecycle completion and rotation. Crash/retry is idempotent; uncertainty preserves needed private material and exposes an actionable failure.
4. Retain public keys and trusted historical bindings so unchanged receipts continue verifying after cleanup and release upgrade. Installed validation no longer requires a deleted historical private key.
5. Cleanup never restores a revoked key or enables old-key signing; compromise remains distinct from ordinary retirement. No secrets appear in output and no broad recursive deletion is used.
6. Add installed integration coverage spanning two Sessions, rotation, final disposal, private-key removal, broker restart and historical verification; document the maintenance behavior and acceptance limits.

## Testing
Prove first Session disposal cannot delete a key still needed by the second; prove final authoritative disposal allows removal and old receipts still verify. Cover Park/resume, signing races, stale references, revoked key, failed deletion/fsync, restart and missing authority. Run full affected Rust and disposable privileged gates.

## Notes
Source decision louiselm-b68f. Reuse installed keyring, lifecycle and locking mechanisms; do not add a separate scheduler or speculative key-management service. Test solely with disposable keys. Production key cleanup requires the applicable operator maintenance workflow, not an implementation test.

title: Admit and witness hardware-signed Skill Generations
description:
## Problem Statement

Immutable packages do not prove operator approval, bind the approved set as a whole, prevent rollback, or define recovery after loss of the routine key.

## Solution

Implement Skill Admission as a trusted local ceremony. `louiselm-skills` recomputes the canonical Dossier and complete set root, then uses a FIDO2 YubiKey to authorize a new Skill Generation. The Generation binds all package membership, Provider view roots, governing policies, review claims, predecessor, and sequence, and becomes current only after remote witnessing.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want one physical touch to approve an exact complete set, not one touch per file or invocation.
2. As an auditor, I want additions, deletion, replacement, policy weakening, and rollback visible in the signed chain.
3. As an operator, I want quarantine to narrow authority immediately without requiring the token.
4. As an operator, I want a physically separate recovery path without a seed phrase or extractable master key.
5. As an Agent, I want typed lifecycle and failure status for every Generation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Skill Admission signs a canonical versioned payload binding package and Provider-view roots, policy and Dossier digests, review depth, signer role, trust domain, sequence, and predecessor.
2. The trusted tool recomputes the complete payload and ignores Agent-supplied roots as authority.
3. Verification accepts only the enrolled role and enforces FIDO user-presence and user-verification flags; missing flags, wrong role/key/domain, malformed or altered records, sequence gaps, and wrong predecessors fail closed.
4. A newly signed Generation remains `pending_witness` until the exact record is confirmed on the protected Git remote; the previous Generation remains current during an outage.
5. Restoring an older signed Generation after a higher witnessed sequence is rejected. Intentional rollback requires a newly admitted higher sequence.
6. Pin advancement and Skill Admission are one transaction; Supply lineage records prior pins but has no approval authority.
7. Authenticated emergency quarantine may only narrow authority. Re-enable and persistent widening require a new hardware-authorized policy Generation.
8. The primary key signs routine Admissions. The separate recovery key may replace key policy or the primary but cannot silently act as an ordinary signer. Loss of both requires explicit trust reset and re-Admission.
9. OpenSSH hardware-attestation bytes are recorded only as optional evidence unless their manufacturer chain is actually validated. The v1 ceremony states that kernel, root-owned binary, and local TTY are trusted.
10. The signed Generation is committed normally to the witness branch without a redundant second hardware signature.
11. Robot status reports candidate/current/quarantined/superseded/invalid state, sequence, predecessor, signer role, witness evidence, failure reason, and safe next action.

## Implementation Notes

- Keep local Admission, recovery, and LouiseLM release-signing roles distinct.
- Use a dedicated SSH signature namespace and one shared verifier implementation for skill management and launch.
- Activation must consume the exact signed bytes confirmed by the witness.

## Testing Notes

- Use deterministic signer and witness doubles for automated state-machine tests.
- Maintain vectors for signatures, FIDO flags, roles, domain separation, sequence/predecessor chains, corruption, replay, and rollback.
- Prove failures between sign, store, witness, and activate leave the prior Generation current.
- Add a manual Linux ceremony for primary signing, verification without a token, recovery rotation, and primary replacement.

## Out of Scope

- Offline approval on a second computer.
- Seed phrases or software recovery keys.
- Public transparency logs, chains, tokens, and OpenTimestamps.
- Session isolation.
close_reason:
Skill Admission ceremony, signed Generation chain, git witnessing, and narrowing-only quarantine in skills-core. 93 crate tests; rollback and witness-mismatch refusals each verified red with the guard disabled. Signatures are real ssh-keygen crypto with software keys; FIDO assertion flags are enforced from parsed SSHSIG bytes and covered by crafted vectors.

Acceptance criteria 1-8, 10, and 11 met. AC9 met as written — attestation is recorded as evidence with validated:false — but nothing populates the field yet (louiselm-ye2v). The physical touch is untested by construction: louiselm-u5no holds the manual ceremony, which needs hardware no agent here can reach. Trust data is not root-owned until d6fv.7.

Lessons routed: namespace separation, retired-key verification, append-only witnessing, and portable Dossier digests to a br comment on this issue; the ceremony and what v1 trusts to skills-core/README.md.

comments.author: claude/4e301c59-b296-4ef8-af9d-c13cd7d3e840
comments.text:
Decisions the rest of the epic inherits.

Signature layer: SSHSIG parsed in-crate (skills-core/src/sshsig.rs), crypto delegated to ssh-keygen. No ed25519 implementation here. The FIDO user-presence/user-verification flags live in the signature blob and ssh-keygen -Y verify does not report them, so the parser extracts them and the flag check runs BEFORE the crypto check — that ordering is what lets a crafted blob be refused for the right reason, and it is what makes the flag path testable without hardware.

Namespaces are the domain separation: louiselm.skills.admission/1 and louiselm.skills.trust/1. A release or Endorsement signature must never verify as an Admission; d6fv.7 and d6fv.8 need their own.

Retired keys: rotating the primary would otherwise invalidate every Generation that key signed — an outage dressed as a security improvement. TrustStore keeps retired primaries; they may verify history, never sign. Ordinary Admission is checked against the current primary only.

Recovery cannot rotate recovery. Allowing it would let one surviving token quietly become the only token. That path is trust reset, which is explicit and destructive.

Witness is append-only per Generation: fetch first, publish only if absent, then read back and compare bytes. Publishing over an existing record would have let a mismatched remote be repaired instead of reported.

Dossier digests bound in the payload are portable digests (Dossier::portable_bytes drops Supply lineage). Lineage holds absolute paths and capture timestamps; leaving it in would make a Generation stop verifying the moment it left the machine that signed it.

Deferred and filed: louiselm-u5no (manual ceremony with real tokens — no agent here can touch a YubiKey), louiselm-ye2v (no path to record attestation evidence). The trust store is not yet root-owned; d6fv.7 owns that.

title: Materialize Agent-scoped verified Instruction views
description:
## Problem Statement

Providers discover instructions from global, repository-local, plugin, system-skill, and native configuration sources. The shared installation lets Provider-managed content cross Agent boundaries and lets instructions outside the approved set bypass verification.

## Solution

Materialize one immutable instruction view per configured Agent from the current witnessed Skill Generation. Bind it to a Session input manifest containing the measured Provider runtime, exact project-instruction snapshot, masked native roots, tool/plugin schemas, empty MCP state for verified v1, and policy identifiers. Each adapter must prove every external file-based source is measured or masked.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want shared approved skills available to the Agents I named at Admission, while harness-specific skills stay with the Agent they target.
2. As an operator, I want repository-local and native Provider instructions measured rather than silently auto-loaded.
3. As an operator, I want verified launch refused when an adapter cannot prove control of every source.
4. As an Agent, I want robot status naming the exact Generation, view, runtime, project instructions, and Provider disclosure for my Session.
5. As an operator, I want a safe `skills=off` launch when verified skill supply is unavailable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every admitted package appears in exactly the Instruction views its signed Agent list names, and in no others. Membership is explicit; nothing enters a view by default.
2. Content absent from the witnessed Generation cannot enter through native/global/repository skill roots, plugins, old installations, or runtime-managed system directories.
3. Global instructions, project instructions, Provider files, plugin/tool schemas, native skills, and native MCP configuration are either bound by digest in the input manifest or demonstrably masked.
4. Verified v1 supplies an empty ACP MCP list and masks native MCP configuration. Incomplete proof blocks verified launch.
5. The input manifest deterministically binds Agent configuration, runtime identity, Skill Generation and view, project-instruction snapshot, tool schemas, policy, isolation evidence, capability envelope, and Provider disclosure.
6. Unmeasured runtimes, live executable lookup, self-update, unknown instruction sources, or incomplete masking fail closed with dimension-specific codes.
7. Embedded instructions inside a measured Provider executable remain part of runtime trust and are reported as Provider disclosure, not mislabeled as managed skills.
8. Generation mismatch rejects the complete skill-enabled view without per-skill dropping or older fallback; `skills=off` exposes no candidate or unverified content.
9. Human and robot status report `managed_supply`, `native_supply`, `runtime`, and `provider_disclosure` independently with evidence and next actions.

## Implementation Notes

- Provider adapters own versioned discovery-source inventories and masking proofs; unknown sources fail closed.
- Project instruction files are per-Session measured inputs, not reusable hardware-admitted skills.
- Provider system skills follow the same Inspection and local Skill Admission as all other skills, and are scoped by the same explicit Agent list. Exclude the Provider skill installer from verified views.
- Package Provider executables/adapters as staged immutable runtime identities; never use live PATH or self-update.
- Views are keyed by Agent, never by Provider, and membership is bound into the signed Generation payload. Decided in louiselm-5qzq, confirmed 2026-09-09.

## Testing Notes

- Use fake Providers attempting every known global, repository, plugin, system-skill, instruction-file, and MCP path.
- Prove Instruction view isolation across Agents, late-source mutation resistance, runtime refresh rejection, native fallback denial, and deterministic input manifests.
- Test all adapters without real Provider credentials, network, or hardware.

## Out of Scope

- Session UID/filesystem isolation and capability brokering.
- Public Endorsement aggregation.
- MCP support in verified v1.
- Windows support.
close_reason: Agent view, input binding, discovery verification and independent supply status components complete; full gates pass. Lessons: child records and README. End-to-end enforcement remains inert:louiselm-d6fv.9

title: Materialize one immutable instruction view per Agent
description:
## Goal

Materialize one immutable instruction view per configured Agent from the
current witnessed Skill Generation, so a verified Session reads instructions
only from bytes the Generation admits.

## Scope

In: reading the current `GenerationRecord` and its members from the `Store`,
selecting the packages whose signed Agent list names that Agent, and publishing
an immutable view tree in the store with a view digest over its canonical
description, mounted read-only at the Agent's native skill root inside the
Session's private home. Also the `skills=off` view, which is the empty view.

Out: the Session input manifest (`louiselm-d6fv.3.2`), adapter source
inventories and masking proofs (`louiselm-d6fv.3.3`), status rendering
(`louiselm-d6fv.3.4`), mounting the view into `ConfinementPlan`, Neovim UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A package appears in exactly the Instruction views its signed Agent list
   names. An Agent named by no package gets the empty view; an Agent named by a
   package but absent from the registry yields no view here and is not an error.
2. Content absent from the witnessed Generation cannot enter a view through a
   native, global, repository, plugin, or previously installed root. A view is
   built from `Store` package bytes alone.
3. A Generation whose witnessed state is not current refuses the whole view.
   No per-skill dropping, no fallback to an older Generation.
4. `skills=off` binds and mounts the canonical empty view, which exposes no
   candidate, unadmitted, or partially admitted content and masks the native
   root so a Provider's own discovery stops there. A failure yields no view at
   all, which is how the two are distinguished.
5. A published view is immutable and content-addressed: the same Generation and
   Agent yield the same view digest on every host, and republishing differing
   content is detected rather than silently overwriting.
6. Failures name the dimension and the exact refusal cause; unknown states fail
   closed.

## Testing Notes

Red-green through the public API with deterministic fixture packages and a
temporary `Store`. Cover: shared/system package routing across two Providers,
a foreign package injected at the view root before and after publication,
non-current Generation refusal, empty `skills=off` view, digest determinism
across two roots, and republication of a differing view.
close_reason: Agent-scoped immutable views and canonical empty mask published/reverified by CLI; 12 regression cases and full crate gates pass. Lessons in issue comment and README. Session mount remains follow-up. consumer:skills-core/src/cli.rs:899

CLI escapes hostile path diagnostics.

Green: 12 public API/CLI cases; full parallel skills-core 529 pass/3 existing ignored, Rustfmt/Clippy/Rustdoc and Node 13 pass. First full run reproduced h157; reproduction and passing rerun recorded there.

title: Bind the Session input manifest
description:
## Goal

Bind one deterministic Session input manifest whose digest is the
`session_input_manifest_id` that `LaunchRequest` already carries, so the
launcher's receipt names inputs that were actually measured.

## Scope

In: a canonical versioned record binding Agent registration identity, runtime
measurement, Skill Generation id and materialized view digest, the measured
project-instruction snapshot, tool and plugin schemas, governing policy
identifiers, isolation evidence reference, capability envelope identity, and
the Provider disclosure statement; plus its canonical bytes and digest.

Out: view materialization (`louiselm-d6fv.3.1`), masking proofs
(`louiselm-d6fv.3.3`), status rendering (`louiselm-d6fv.3.4`), changes to
`launch.rs` digest validation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The manifest binds every input named above; a missing or empty required
   input is a refusal, never a default.
2. Canonical bytes are deterministic: identical inputs yield an identical
   digest across hosts and orderings; any changed input changes the digest.
3. Project instruction files are bound as per-Session measured inputs, distinct
   from admitted packages, and never presented as hardware-admitted skills.
4. Verified v1 binds an empty ACP MCP list; a non-empty one is refused.
5. An unmeasured runtime, an unresolved Generation, or an unresolved view
   refuses the manifest with a dimension-specific code.
6. The digest satisfies the shape `LaunchRequest::validate` already enforces.

## Testing Notes

Red-green through the public API. Cover: determinism across two constructions
and shuffled input order, each required input missing, project-instruction
snapshot mutation changing the digest, non-empty MCP refusal, and a round trip
whose digest is accepted by `LaunchRequest` validation.

title: Prove every Provider discovery source is measured or masked
description:
## Goal

Make every Provider adapter prove that each of its file-based discovery
sources is measured or masked, so a verified launch is refused when an adapter
cannot account for a source.

## Scope

In: a versioned per-adapter inventory of discovery sources (global, repository
local, plugin, native skill roots, instruction files, native MCP config), a
typed proof per source that it is either bound by digest in the input manifest
or masked in the confinement, refusal on any unknown or unproven source, and
reporting instructions embedded in a measured Provider executable as Provider
disclosure rather than managed supply.

Out: view materialization (`louiselm-d6fv.3.1`), manifest binding
(`louiselm-d6fv.3.2`), status rendering (`louiselm-d6fv.3.4`), the sandbox
mount mechanics themselves.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each adapter declares a versioned source inventory; a source outside the
   declared set refuses the launch rather than being ignored.
2. Every declared source resolves to exactly one typed proof: measured with a
   digest bound in the input manifest, or masked with the confinement evidence
   that masks it.
3. Native MCP configuration is masked and the ACP MCP list is empty for
   verified v1; an unmasked native MCP config refuses the launch.
4. Instructions embedded inside a measured Provider executable are reported as
   Provider disclosure and are never labelled managed skills.
5. Incomplete masking, a live executable lookup, self-update, or an unmeasured
   runtime fails closed with a dimension-specific code.
6. A source added after the inventory was written is detected, not silently
   accepted.

## Testing Notes

Red-green through the public API with fake Providers that attempt every known
global, repository, plugin, system-skill, instruction-file, and MCP path.
Cover late source mutation, an undeclared source appearing at launch time, a
runtime refresh attempt, and native fallback denial. No real Provider
credentials, network, or hardware.
notes: Confirmed louiselm-2gvo: workspace project instruction files stay editable; automatic instruction loading uses the fixed per-Session snapshot. Require adapter evidence that mutable discovery and reload are disabled. Do not satisfy this by read-only mounting the workspace instruction paths.

title: Report supply and disclosure dimensions in status
description:
## Goal

Report `managed_supply`, `native_supply`, `runtime`, and `provider_disclosure`
independently from the materialized view, the input manifest, and the adapter
proofs, so humans and Agents read the same supply state with evidence and a
next action.

## Scope

In: deriving the four `posture::DimensionInput` values from this feature's
artifacts, their evidence references and failure codes, and the human and
robot status surfaces `skills-core` already owns.

Out: the Neovim health and launch-preview projection, which is
`louiselm-d6fv.6.2`; waiver mutation (`louiselm-d6fv.6.3`); Attention
projection (`louiselm-d6fv.6.4`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each of the four dimensions reports its own state, requirement, evidence,
   failure code, and narrow next action; one failing dimension does not
   collapse the others.
2. States derive only from trusted component evidence: a materialized view
   digest, a bound manifest, or an adapter proof. Agent claims, prompt text,
   tool labels, and Provider branding cannot mark a dimension verified.
3. Human and robot outputs derive from the same state and agree; robot output
   needs no prose parsing and carries a versioned schema.
4. Provider disclosure states plainly that plaintext intentionally sent to a
   cloud Provider is visible to it despite local containment.
5. An absent artifact reports the dimension as unverified with its next action,
   never as verified by default.

## Testing Notes

Red-green through the public API. Cover each dimension failing alone, all four
verified, missing artifacts, human/robot agreement on identical state, and the
absence of hostile or sensitive content in robot output.

title: Bind per-Agent view membership into the signed Generation
description:
## Goal

Bind per-Agent Instruction view membership into the signed Generation payload,
so the split of who reads what is covered by the Admission signature instead of
by mutable deployment state.

## Scope

In: `generation.rs` (`Member` gains an explicit Agent list folded into the
recomputed member root; `view_roots` removed; `GENERATION_SCHEMA` becomes
`louiselm.skills.generation/2`), `admission.rs` (`AdmissionRequest` carries
per-member Agent lists in place of `view_roots`), and `cli.rs` (member syntax
gains the Agent list, `--all-agents` expands to the literal registered Agent
names at signing time, `--view` removed).

Out: materializing the view itself (`louiselm-d6fv.3.1`), the input manifest
(`louiselm-d6fv.3.2`), and any migration path — no Generation has ever been
admitted, so `/1` is deleted rather than supported.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each `Member` carries an explicit, non-empty list of Agent names, and that
   list is covered by `recomputed_member_root`, so a payload cannot claim a
   root that omits its own scoping.
2. `--all-agents` expands to the literal Agent names known at signing time. No
   payload ever stores a wildcard, and the record's meaning never depends on
   the registry's later contents.
3. A member with an empty Agent list is refused at Admission.
4. An Agent name in a member that no registry entry matches is accepted: it
   yields no view on this host and a view on another. Portability is the point.
5. `view_roots` no longer exists in the payload, the request, or the CLI, and
   no host path appears anywhere in the signed bytes.
6. A `louiselm.skills.generation/1` payload is refused as an unsupported
   schema, not silently upgraded.

## Testing Notes

Red-green through the public API. Cover: member root changing when only the
Agent list changes, empty list refusal, `--all-agents` expansion recorded
literally, an unregistered Agent name accepted, a `/1` payload refused, and a
round trip through sign and verify with two Agents scoped differently.
close_reason: Per-Agent membership is in the signed payload and covered by the recomputed root; view_roots and --view are gone; /1 is refused. gate:skills-core/tests/admission.rs

AdmissionRequest.members became Vec<AdmissionMember> {package, depth, agents}; an empty list is refused as NotReviewable rather than through a new variant. GENERATION_SCHEMA is louiselm.skills.generation/2 and verify_record's existing schema check refuses /1 unchanged. view_roots is gone from payload, request and CLI; --view is now an unknown option.

CLI: --member <digest>[:<depth>][=<agent>,...]. The = separator avoids the existing digest-versus-depth colon ambiguity entirely, since neither digests nor depths contain =. --all-agents expands through --registry at signing time into literal sorted names; without --registry it refuses, and an empty registry refuses rather than admitting an empty scope.

title: Give AgentRegistration the real Provider shape
description:
## Goal

title: Launch verified Sessions inside a Linux security boundary
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM starts Agent processes with the operator identity, mutable home, ambient credentials, live executable paths, and root-equivalent host capabilities. ACP permission handling cannot contain an Agent that omits requests or invokes subprocesses directly.

## Solution

Introduce root-owned daemonless `louiselm-launch` as the only path to a verified Session. It accepts a closed request of trusted identifiers, creates a distinct per-Session host identity and private filesystem/process view, starts a measured runtime, and emits evidence against a versioned Provider-neutral isolation contract. Linux mechanisms and a pinned sandbox helper are replaceable implementations that must pass the same hostile conformance suite.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want every verified Session isolated from my account and other Sessions.
2. As an operator, I want exact runtime and instruction inputs measured so self-update and native configuration cannot silently change them.
3. As an adapter author, I want one isolation contract rather than Provider-specific security meanings.
4. As an operator, I want Cancellation, Park, quarantine, and Disposal to govern the complete process tree.
5. As an Agent, I want precise failure evidence and safe next actions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Verified launch uses only the root-owned signed-release installation; development or operator-writable launchers are reported unverified.
2. The versioned request references registered Agent, runtime, Skill Generation, Session-input manifest, Run, and envelope identities. It accepts no caller-selected command, environment, mount, path, host identity, backend flag, or systemd property.
3. Each Session has a distinct host identity, private home, process/cgroup lifecycle, measured inputs, private workspace/cache overlay, and launcher-created capability channels.
4. It cannot ptrace/signal the operator, launcher, control service, or another Session, and cannot access the operator checkout/home, credentials, Docker, privileged or user-service sockets, native Provider configuration, or ambient network.
5. The runtime package records executable and adapter digests, versions, origins, relevant library baseline, and isolation-policy version. Live PATH lookup and self-update are unavailable.
6. The isolation contract covers filesystem visibility/mutation, process separation and inheritance, IPC/socket access, network denial, identity, lifecycle, and evidence. Missing or contradictory evidence fails closed.
7. Conformance attempts `/proc` and ptrace escape, inherited descriptors, symlink traversal, Unix sockets, user D-Bus/systemd, Docker, child survival, writable runtime/config, cross-Session access, and the known sandbox D-Bus escape class.
8. Cancellation, quarantine, Park, Disposal, and failure act on the whole Session process tree. Park freezes preserved work; Disposal terminates descendants and releases the identity.
9. Successful launch returns an integrity-protected receipt binding Session, Run, runtime, Skill Generation, input manifest, isolation contract/backend, kernel prerequisites, and capability-channel identities without credentials, prompts, environments, or hostile text.
10. Direct vendor CLI execution remains possible but produces no LouiseLM Verified posture; PATH wrappers are UX only.

## Implementation Notes

- Keep the launcher narrow: validate, materialize confinement, execute, supervise, and report evidence. Policy, egress, credentials, dependencies, and Beads belong to the control broker.
- Use one narrow fixed privilege entrypoint; reject setuid and a root daemon.
- Systemd, Landlock, and a pinned `nono` build are candidates, not trusted names.

## Testing Notes

- Use a deterministic fake Agent for ordinary tests; separate pure schema, unprivileged lifecycle, and privileged Linux conformance suites.
- Prove operator-writable launcher, caller-selected policy, native MCP, runtime mutation, escape attempts, and surviving children all prevent verified status.
- Exercise async startup/failure/lifecycle through production callback boundaries.

## Out of Scope

- Capability classification and egress.
- Skill Inspection and Admission.
- macOS and Windows.
- Trusting any sandbox backend without conformance evidence.

title: Define the launcher protocol and signed receipt chain
description:
## Goal

Give the Launch supervisor and Control broker one closed v1 contract for lifecycle commands, canonical status, stable errors, and machine-signed Launcher receipts.

## Scope

- In scope: pure request/response types; public states starting, running, parked, and terminal; lifecycle actions Park, resume, interrupt, Disposal, and status; request id, expected receipt sequence, expected state, and envelope revision; canonical receipt payload bytes and chain verification.
- Out of scope: sockets, filesystem persistence, key installation, process launch, broker policy, and UI presentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every message has an explicit protocol version and closed schema; unknown, malformed, contradictory, or oversized values fail with stable typed errors before state changes.
2. Launch produces sequence 0. Every later Launcher receipt binds Session and Run identity, authorization or cause, action, resulting state, release ID, signing-key ID, sequence, and previous receipt digest.
3. Canonical bytes are deterministic. Verification rejects mutation, reordering, gaps, duplicate sequence numbers, foreign Session prefixes, and chain splicing.
4. Lifecycle requests are serialized compare-and-swap operations. An identical request-id retry returns the original receipt; a conflicting reuse or stale expected state, sequence, or envelope revision is rejected.
5. Canonical status exposes state, posture, broker connection, envelope revision, channel state, receipt head, pending operation, allowed actions, and last failure. Errors expose code, message, retryable, current state, expected sequence, and next action.
6. The contract has no transport, policy, presentation, or generalized networking abstraction.

## Testing

- Red-green pure Rust tests cover valid transitions, every malformed branch, replay/conflict/staleness, deterministic serialization, complete chain verification, and stable status/error serialization.
- Run all skills-core Rust gates.

## Notes

Prefer narrow launch_protocol.rs and launch_receipt.rs modules. Define an async-shaped signing/persistence seam, but keep the implementation dependency-free. Canonical terms: Launch supervisor (louiselm-2jxz), Control broker (louiselm-vogp), Launcher receipt (louiselm-1d5r).

title: Install the launcher key, identity pool, and sudo boundary
description:
## Goal

Install the minimum persistent root-owned material needed to invoke one measured Launch supervisor and prove its signing and host-identity authority.

## Scope

- In scope: persistent Ed25519 launcher keyring; explicit key rotation and retired-key verification; SSHSIG signing with namespace louiselm.launch.receipt/1; fixed sudoers entry; pinned release digest; reserved non-overlapping subuid/subgid pool; root-only configuration, locks, and diagnostics.
- Out of scope: launch protocol semantics, broker policy, Session process supervision, hardware signing, and a new cryptography library.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Installation creates a root-only persistent software Ed25519 key with stable key ID and public verification record. Rotation is explicit; retired public keys remain verifiable, and a retired private key remains available while any live receipt chain still uses it.
2. Signing invokes a measured absolute ssh-keygen path with SSHSIG namespace louiselm.launch.receipt/1 and root-private scratch. Human, Admission, recovery, and release keys are never reused.
3. Sudo policy permits only the configured operator to run root-owned current/bin/louiselm-launch run with the pinned release digest. Callers use sudo -n; prompts, mutable paths, extra arguments, and digest mismatch fail closed.
4. Installation reserves bounded non-overlapping /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid ranges without login accounts. The broker may assign only a configured slot; the supervisor validates the range and owns an exclusive per-ID file lock.
5. Install/status output reports active key ID, retained keys, release digest, operator, pool bounds, occupied slots, and actionable failures without exposing private key bytes.
6. Reinstall and rotation are idempotent and do not silently replace a key, widen sudo authority, overlap an identity range, or release an occupied slot.

## Testing

- Deterministic tests use temporary filesystem and command-runner seams for permissions, rotation, sudoers rendering/validation, range overlap, reinstallation, and failures.
- A documented privileged Linux acceptance check proves root ownership, sudo -n behavior, ssh-keygen verification, and identity-range reservation.
- Run all skills-core Rust gates.

## Notes

Use existing release identity and installer boundaries. Keep root-key mechanics separate from receipt semantics. No runtime wrapper and no new crypto dependency.
close_reason: Installed dedicated measured launcher authority, exact sudo digest, reserved and leased identity pool, crash-safe rotation, and actionable status; full skills-core gates pass. Runtime reachability awaits inert:louiselm-d6fv.4.4

title: Bootstrap retry generates a second launcher key
description:
A root installer retry after private-key durability but before keyring publication enrolls a new key and leaves the first durable key orphaned.

## Observed

On 2026-09-04 in skills-core, `cargo test --test launcher_install retry_after_keyring_publication_failure_reuses_the_generated_key` failed:

```
left: Some("sha256:7285a0b700b490449657f4da94792a42957c47118bdda9bdaafb98e0aa8ba58a")
right: Some("sha256:0dd7c591e02273cb71da75276cad0153bac28df9bf5b9f7c33c78656652556b8")
```

## Symptoms

- Reinstall silently replaces the first generated launcher authority before enrollment.
- `private/keys` retains an unreferenced private key.

## Root cause

`skills-core/src/launcher_install.rs:493-510` calls `generate_key`, which finalizes `private/keys/<id>/key`, before atomically writing `keyring.json`. The no-keyring retry path never recovers that durable key.

## Why it was not caught

The retry test covered ssh-keygen failure before durable key material, not keyring publication failure after durability.

## Fix direction

Recover and validate exactly one un-enrolled durable key when config exists without keyring; refuse ambiguous/unsafe contents instead of generating again.

## Acceptance

- The failing fault-injection test passes.
- Retry performs one keygen total, enrolls the original key, and leaves one private key directory.

## Not covered

Rotation uses its separate durable journal and is tracked independently.
close_reason: Recovered the sole validated bootstrap key across pre-move and pre-keyring crashes; ambiguous contents fail closed. Full skills-core gates pass. gate:skills-core/tests/launcher_install.rs

comments.text: Lesson routed here: bootstrap key generation needs a deterministic durable pending name and both rename parents synced before keyring publication. No standing AGENTS.md rule is warranted.

title: Rotation retry rejects its durable empty key directory
description:
A crash after creating the final digest directory but before moving the pending launcher private key makes the exact rotation retry permanently fail.

## Observed

On 2026-09-04 in skills-core, `cargo test --test launcher_install rotation_reuses_an_empty_destination_after_a_crash_before_key_move` failed:

```
retry completes through the durable empty destination directory: Malformed("pending launcher key destination already exists without its key")
```

## Symptoms

- The documented exact rotation replay cannot finish.
- Status remains `rotation_incomplete` with a durable key and journal that no normal retry can publish.

## Root cause

`skills-core/src/launcher_install.rs:1603-1614` creates `private/keys/<digest>` before renaming the pending key, but retry rejects any pre-existing destination directory even when it is the secure empty directory left by that step.

## Why it was not caught

Fault injection covered failure before journal key metadata publication, not the later mkdir-before-rename crash window.

## Fix direction

Validate and reuse only the exact empty private destination directory, while refusing symlinks, unsafe metadata, or unexpected entries.

## Acceptance

- The failing crash-state regression passes.
- Retry publishes the original pending key without a third key generation.

## Not covered

Initial bootstrap keyring publication has a separate bug bead.
close_reason: Exact rotation replay now reuses only a safe empty destination and retains the original generated key. Full skills-core gates pass. gate:skills-core/tests/launcher_install.rs

comments.author: codex/01a068c6-2ca1-7be3-88ff-96c887e50df0
comments.text: Lesson routed here: crash-idempotent rotation must accept its exact safe intermediate state while rejecting unexpected destination contents. No standing AGENTS.md rule is warranted.

title: Bootstrap failure reports an impossible rotation action
description:
After initial launcher key generation fails, status labels the durable pending bootstrap directory as an unfinished rotation and tells the maintainer to replay a rotation identity that does not exist.

## Observed

On 2026-09-04, `cargo test --test launcher_install retry_after_key_generation_failure_recovers_without_duplicate_reservations` failed because no `bootstrap_incomplete` failure with an installer recovery action was present. The current status emitted `rotation_incomplete` for `private/pending-key`.

## Symptoms

- The maintainer receives a non-actionable recovery instruction after first install failure.
- The diagnostic conflates bootstrap and explicit rotation authority.

## Root cause

`skills-core/src/launcher_install.rs:830-844` groups any pending-key path with a pending-rotation journal and always renders the rotation code/action.

## Why it was not caught

The prior keygen-failure test checked persistent intent and retry only, not the interim status action.

## Fix direction

Distinguish pending-key-without-rotation-journal as bootstrap state and direct the maintainer to rerun the same installer request.

## Acceptance

- The failing status regression passes.
- A real pending rotation retains its rotation-specific diagnostic.

## Not covered

Bootstrap and rotation crash recovery mechanics have separate bug beads.
close_reason: Status now distinguishes bootstrap retry from rotation replay and tests both recovery actions. Full skills-core gates pass. gate:skills-core/tests/launcher_install.rs

title: Authenticate launcher packets with Unix credentials
description:
## Goal

Provide the smallest Linux transport that lets a Launch supervisor and Control broker exchange one authenticated closed message per packet without a stream framing layer.

## Scope

- In scope: fixed local AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET rendezvous; bounded versioned JSON packets; peer credentials; SO_PASSCRED and SCM_CREDENTIALS per message; connection/reconnection primitives; structured transport errors.
- Out of scope: lifecycle policy, receipt persistence, process launch, egress, and a reusable networking framework.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The transport uses AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET and preserves exactly one protocol message per packet.
2. Sender and receiver enforce one documented maximum packet size. Truncation, empty packets, malformed JSON, unknown message variants, and trailing data are rejected before dispatch.
3. The receiver exposes kernel peer credentials and SCM_CREDENTIALS from every message; supplied JSON identity fields never substitute for host UID, GID, or PID.
4. Callers can pin an expected broker identity or top-level Agent host PID and reject a connection or message whose kernel credentials differ.
5. Disconnect, credential mismatch, oversize input, and protocol-version mismatch have stable typed errors and close the affected channel.
6. The I/O seam is asynchronous from callers and uses bounded background work; Neovim or policy code is absent.

## Testing

- Linux socket-pair/integration tests cover packet boundaries, maximum size, truncation, malformed messages, peer and per-message credentials, PID mismatch, disconnect, and reconnect.
- Prove credentials come from the kernel by sending contradictory claimed identity fields.
- Run all skills-core Rust gates.

## Notes

Use the explicitly approved rustix dependency only for the required transport and credential APIs. stdx was inspected and does not provide seqpacket or credential passing; do not wrap rustix in a generalized network abstraction. Prefer launch_transport.rs with a narrow API.
close_reason: Authenticated seqpacket transport and Linux regressions complete; inert:louiselm-d6fv.4.4

comments.text: Claimed for skills-core launch_transport.rs, its Linux integration tests, the approved rustix dependency/lockfile change, narrow lib.rs export, and release schema inventory only. No lifecycle policy, persistence, launch orchestration, or unrelated sandbox work.

comments.text: Lesson: SO_PEERCRED is the connection peer; SCM_CREDENTIALS is the actual packet sender. Process pins require both exact; Identity pins intentionally allow a same-UID/GID descendant. d6fv.4.4 comments 698/713 retain capability-channel cgroup/descendance checks. Linux empty seqpackets differ from EOF only by attached credentials; full backlogs return ConnectBusy without blocking workers.

title: Launch one authorized Session against a fake broker
description:
## Goal

Make the fixed louiselm-launch run entrypoint start exactly one measured, confined Agent process tree and report success only after its launch receipt is durable at a fake Control broker.

## Scope

- In scope: one bounded stdin launch document; release identity validation; fixed broker rendezvous; durable pending-authorization consumption; assigned identity lease; Bubblewrap launch; host child PID capture; opaque ACP stdio relay; capability-channel creation; sequence-0 receipt signing and durable acknowledgement.
- Out of scope: later lifecycle operations, real broker policy, egress, dependency installation, Beads mutation, and Neovim presentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. louiselm-launch run is the only privileged invocation. It accepts one bounded closed document and no caller-selected command, environment, mount, path, identity, backend, policy, or systemd flag.
2. The fake broker authorizes one short-lived single-use record binding exact request digest, controller identity, Session and Run, envelope revision, authorization ID, and assigned identity. Missing, expired, replayed, or mismatched authorization fails before spawn.
3. The supervisor validates that the assigned UID/GID is inside the installed pool, takes its exclusive file lock, clears supplementary groups for the child, and proves the Bubblewrap child actually runs under that host identity.
4. Historical implementation scope: Bubblewrap --json-status-fd supplies the host-view namespace reaper PID. The delivered capability connection gate uses assigned UID/GID plus Session membership and retains a connection without dispatching capability effects; this is not actual Agent-process authentication. Confirmed louiselm-9onz replaces the original top-level-PID assumption: louiselm-qbr.5.1.1.2 must establish the actual Agent principal and .3-.5 enforce tool isolation and real enablement. Identifiers are not bearer secrets.
5. ACP stdio is relayed opaquely. No prompt, environment, credential, or tool payload is logged or copied into the receipt.
6. Delivered receipt discipline after louiselm-yvof/d3ix: exact sequence-0 Launch/Starting durable ACK gates startup; exact sequence-1 Start/Running durable ACK gates success. Confirmed louiselm-9onz adds restricted initialization and identity/tool-isolation verification before capability enablement and Running, implemented by louiselm-qbr.5.1.1.2-.5 rather than claimed by this historical close.
7. Every failure disposes the spawned process tree, releases the identity and sockets, and completes at most once.

## Testing

- Red-green integration tests use a deterministic fake broker and fake ACP Agent for authorization mismatch, replay, UID exhaustion, spawn failure, hostile JSON, PID binding, broker fsync rejection, cleanup, and success ordering.
- The privileged Linux fixture proves the outer host UID/GID differs from root and the operator while the supervisor remains root.
- Run all skills-core Rust gates.

## Notes

Reuse launch.rs request resolution and the existing Bubblewrap backend. Prefer a small launch_supervisor.rs plus binary wiring. This task consumes the fix from louiselm-i03a; it must not infer host identity from namespace-local --uid output.
notes: 2026-09-09 louiselm-9onz reconciliation: comments 698/713 correctly identify Bubblewrap child-pid as reaper, but their Session-membership policy does not authorize direct tool effects. Historical closed evidence remains unchanged; new authority requirements are tracked by qbr.5.1.1.2-.5.

title: Operator-owned cgroup can eject a launched Agent
description:
Evidence: Cgroup::delegated_parent at skills-core/src/sandbox.rs:218 selects the sudo launcher current cgroup after only write-access checks at :360. On the live host, that scope and cgroup.procs are owned by operator UID 1000 (755/644). Linux cgroup-v2 delegation permits the delegatee to migrate processes anywhere inside that writable subtree. An operator can move the assigned-UID Agent from the Session child into the parent; dispose then observes an empty child and can release/reuse the identity while the Agent survives.

Acceptance: production launcher Sessions use a fixed root-owned, non-group/world-writable cgroup parent outside the operator-delegated subtree; the operator cannot migrate the Agent out; capability membership and zero-survivor cleanup remain anchored there. Generic unprivileged sandbox conformance may retain its delegated-parent path.

title: Supervise Session lifecycle and loss against a fake broker
description:
## Goal

Keep one Launch supervisor authoritative for its Session process tree through Running, Park, Resume, interrupt, broker/controller loss, and terminal Disposal while every Launcher receipt remains truthful.

## Scope

- In scope: a serialized lifecycle owner; authenticated fake-broker commands; whole-tree mechanics; truthful receipt ordering and replay; signed broker-loss grace; exact-head reconciliation; controller-loss recovery handoff; identity lifetime; canonical supervisor status; production-facing async seams needed by these mechanics.
- Out of scope: Control broker policy/persistence implementation, operator UI, Attention presentation, capture-service storage, egress, supervisor crash takeover, and launching a replacement Session.

## Confirmed design

- One serialized supervisor event loop owns mutable Session state. Broker requests, process/relay exits, timers, signing, durable acknowledgements, and reconnect results arrive as typed epoch-tagged events. Stale events have no effects.
- Resume uses durable broker authorization, not a predictive success receipt, to gate thaw. After successful thaw the supervisor signs a truthful Resume-to-Running receipt and waits for its exact durable acknowledgement. Signing or acknowledgement failure immediately re-Parks; reconciliation later records Park(AcknowledgementFailed).
- Unacknowledged receipt intents and exact signed bytes remain in a bounded in-memory supervisor backlog. Audit failure revokes command/capability channels and forbids widening, while narrowing safety mechanics still run.
- Supervisor status separates actual mechanics from launcher_head, broker_head, pending operation, and bounded pending-receipt count.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Only the authenticated Control broker can request Park, Resume, interrupt, Disposal, or status. Agent capability channels and later stateless helpers have no lifecycle authority.
2. Park, interrupt, Disposal, confirmed process exit, controller-loss freeze, and broker-loss freeze execute their narrowing mechanic before receipt signing. An identical retry replays the same result/bytes without repeating mechanics.
3. Resume stays Parked until durable authorization; thaw runs once; only successful thaw produces Resume-to-Running. Signing/ACK failure re-Parks immediately and cannot enable channels until exact reconciliation.
4. Launch authorization binds broker_loss_grace_ms in the inclusive range 0..5000, and sequence-zero signed evidence commits to it. Broker loss revokes channels immediately and starts one monotonic deadline that reconnect attempts never reset.
5. Automatic channel restoration during grace requires the same authenticated broker, an exact current receipt head, and unchanged authorization envelope. Expiry, suffix repair, conflict, or identity/envelope change leaves the Session Parked for explicit Resume.
6. Reconnect exchanges {session_id, run_id, sequence, receipt_digest}. Equal heads attach; a matching older broker head accepts only the exact continuous launcher-held suffix. Gaps, conflicts, foreign subjects, unknown/broker-ahead sequences, invalid signatures, or invalid ACKs remain/fall Parked and return receipt_chain_invalid.
7. Controller loss revokes and freezes immediately. With an ACP recovery reference, the old Session stays frozen until one broker acknowledgement proves both the recovery reference and Attention projection durable; then its tree is disposed, identity released, and truthful terminal Disposal recorded. Failure retains the frozen Session and identity. Without recovery capability, abnormal Disposal is terminal and never called cold Park.
8. Warm Park retains its identity. Cold/terminal completion releases it. Exhaustion returns session_identity_exhausted without eviction; a bounded sorted {session_id,state,slot} list is visible only on the authenticated operator path. Invalid occupied/poisoned assignments return identity_assignment_invalid.
9. Status reports actual process state independently from launcher_head and broker_head; callers never infer mechanics from receipt sequence. Confirmed process-tree exit is terminal and exposes only a sanitized exit classification.
10. Racing terminal causes and late callbacks cannot revive a Session, duplicate receipts, touch released resources, reset grace, or complete an operation twice.

## Testing

- Deterministic fake-broker/fake-Agent tests cover each transition, authorization boundary, pending/stale/concurrent commands, exact retry, thaw/sign/ACK failures, grace expiry and reconnect races, all prefix cases, recovery/no-recovery controller loss, identity retention/release and privacy, process exit, terminal idempotency, backlog behavior, and late callbacks.
- Async doubles deliver callbacks from production-equivalent worker contexts; grace uses a manually released monotonic clock, never sleeps.
- Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test in skills-core.

## Notes

The supervisor executes mechanics only; authorization and canonical broker composition belong to the Control broker. Raw ACP stdio is not reconnectable. A cold Park is lossy reconstruction through ACP session/load. Vocabulary remains unchanged: a Launcher receipt records an outcome actually reached.
notes: Confirmed louiselm-9onz (2026-09-09): whole-tree lifecycle proof is not Agent-principal lifetime proof. New qbr.5.1.1.2/.4 revoke the Agent channel and every delegated grant on actual Agent exit even when tools remain. Reconciliation/Resume cannot transfer authority to a helper, replacement or recycled PID; qbr.5.1.2 preserves this invariant. Historical close evidence does not claim these new grants are implemented.

title: Serialize broker Park and truthful supervisor status
description:
## Goal

Create the long-lived per-Session supervisor owner and prove an authenticated broker can Park the whole process tree while status remains mechanically truthful.

## Scope

- In scope: one serialized event loop; epoch-tagged broker/mechanic/sign/ACK events; reversible capability revocation; Park and side-effect-free status; actual state plus launcher_head, broker_head, pending operation, and bounded pending count; warm identity retention.

3. One pending operation rejects concurrent/stale requests; an exact retry replays identical completion/receipt bytes without repeating mechanics.
4. All external callbacks enter one owner queue with connection/operation epochs; status reads have no side effects.
5. The installed run path reaches the long-lived supervisor seam without introducing a second mutable owner.

## Testing
