Enter should clear the phrase and request hidden re-entry of all 24 words.

title: CI mini.test fails on nvim nightly only, on two unrelated specs
description:
CI's `mini.test (nvim nightly)` job fails on every push to main while `mini.test (nvim stable)` passes in the same run, so the nightly canary is permanently red and no longer signals anything. Two unrelated specs fail; both pass locally on v0.12.5 and on CI stable.

## Observed

2026-09-17, claude/36dc56d6-d466-4f8e-952a-113b9cd6a053. Reproduced on three consecutive runs, always nightly, never stable:

- https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/35197802093/job/105125115578 (ef178ba)
- run 35197451660 (2ccf61c), job conclusion failure
- run 35198885130 (aec9ee2), job conclusion failure

Nightly is `NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1651+gcb76690546`, installed by `rhysd/action-setup-vim@v1`. Stable in the same runs is green. Local `nvim --version` is `NVIM v0.12.5`; `MiniTest.run_file` on both spec files reports `Fails (0) and Notes (0)`.

Failure 1, `tests/session/api_spec.lua:2434`, case `new | does not mistake terminal warnings or unsupported failure extensions for turn failure`:

```
Failed expectation for equality
Cause: different values at key "error", left = "turn recording database is locked; retry after the writer finishes", right = nil
Left:  { error = "turn recording database is locked; retry after the writer finishes" }
Right: { result = { _meta = { jetbrains = { air = { sessionFailure = { id = "warning", revision = 1, severity = "warning", title = "Recovered" }, version = 1 } } }, stopReason = "end_turn" } }
```

Failure 2, `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:6280`, case `chat | mouse hover reveals the winbar Session identity without taking focus`:

```
Failed expectation for equality
Cause: different types
Left:  nil
Right: { "codex/acp-first" }
```

The first CI run to carry both specs' current content was 35197451660; the immediately preceding run, 35195218562 at 85e232d, was a full success. The changes in between are 5427c1e `fix(session): retain sessions after turn errors` and 539b96f `feat(ui): show Session ID on winbar hover`, both from codex/01a0ae34-ae0f-7221-b0b4-61385c11e46f.

## Symptoms

- Every push to main shows a red CI check, so a real regression will be indistinguishable from the standing failure.
- Failure 1: a submitted prompt completes with a turn-recording lock error instead of its ACP result, and the recorded status stays out of sync with what the Agent actually returned.
- Failure 2: hovering the winbar Agent name shows no Session ID tooltip.

## Root cause

Unknown. Two candidate mechanisms, one per failure, and they are probably independent.

Failure 1: the turn recorder's SQLite writer still holds the database when the next prompt is submitted, and that lock error is surfaced as the turn's completion error rather than retried or kept out of the turn result. Whether nightly changes the timing (faster event-loop scheduling, different `vim.uv` ordering) or merely exposes an existing race is not established. Discriminator: run the case under stable with an artificial delay in the recorder writer; if it fails there too, this is a latent race and not a nightly regression.

Failure 2: the test drives the tooltip with `nvim_input_mouse("move", ...)` then `getchar(0)` and `nvim.wait(30)` at tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:6266-6270, with `mousemoveevent` set at :6256. Nightly may deliver or coalesce mouse-move events differently, so the hover handler never runs inside the 30 ms window. Discriminator: raise the wait and re-run on nightly; if it passes, this is a test-timing assumption rather than a product defect. Checking Neovim's changelog between v0.12.5 and v0.13.0-dev-1651 for mouse-move or `getchar` changes would settle it.

Neither mechanism has been traced to a line in `lua/`, so do not treat either as established.

## Why it was not caught

Both cases pass on stable locally and in CI, so the pre-push gate documented in docs/agent-testing.md cannot see them: it names one Neovim, and nightly is only exercised after the push. Nothing in the suite asserts either behavior in a version-independent way, and the hover case encodes a timing assumption (30 ms) as if it were a contract.

## Fix direction

Diagnose before fixing; the two failures likely need different answers.

For failure 1, the narrowest fix is wherever the recorder's lock error is allowed to become the turn's completion error — that error belongs to recording, not to the turn, and a locked database should not change what the Agent returned.

For failure 2, prefer waiting on the observable condition (the tooltip window existing) over a fixed 30 ms sleep, rather than raising the constant.

Rejected: marking the nightly job `continue-on-error`. That converts a signal into silence, which is the failure this bug is about.

## Acceptance

- Both cases pass on `NVIM v0.13.0-dev` and on stable, in CI, for three consecutive runs.
- A regression that fails before the fix and passes after, for whichever of the two turns out to be a product defect rather than a test-timing assumption.
- Prompt completion never carries a turn-recording storage error in its `error` field.

## Not covered

- Whether either failure is user-visible on nvim nightly outside the test harness. If failure 1 reproduces in a real Session on nightly, prompts fail there and this becomes P1.
- The `cargo (skills-core)` job in run 35197802093 also shows a red X. That is cancellation from the concurrency group when aec9ee2 was pushed, not a test failure; its steps were still green when it was cancelled.
- No bisect against individual Neovim nightly builds.
close_reason: gate:tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:6264 Neovim 0.13 stopped invoking vim.on_key() for keys getchar() consumes, so the test's own input pump hid the hover observer; lua/ unchanged. Full mini.test suite green on both NVIM v0.12.5 and v0.13.0-dev-1651+gcb76690546, plus stylua and both generator --check gates. Turn-recording symptom split out as louiselm-gajsq; rule recorded in docs/agent-testing.md.

comments.author: claude/36dc56d6-d466-4f8e-952a-113b9cd6a053
comments.text:
Correction to the filed record: this was two defects, not one. Split the turn-recording failure out as louiselm-gajsq. That one is intermittent (1 of 3 CI runs), not nightly-specific, and passes locally on the exact nightly build. This issue is now only the hover failure, which is deterministic and nightly-only: 3 of 3 CI runs, and reproduced locally on NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1651+gcb76690546.

Root cause, established rather than hypothesised. Neovim 0.13 news.txt, EVENTS: 'vim.on_key() callbacks are not invoked for keys consumed by getchar().' The test pumped its queued mouse move with nvim.fn.getchar(0) at tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:6268, so on 0.13 the chat's on_key observer at lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1561 never saw <MouseMove> and update_winbar_hover never ran. Measured with a probe on both builds: nvim_input_mouse plus getchar(0) yields 1 on_key event on v0.12.5 and 0 on nightly, while getmousepos() reports the same position on both.

So this is a test-harness defect, not a product defect. The hover feature itself is untouched: real editing does not consume keys through getchar(), and lua/ is unchanged by the fix.

Second trap found while fixing it, worth the line: feeding the key with nvim_feedkeys(move, 'nx', false) still failed. 'x' completes the pending command with a trailing <Esc>, that <Esc> reaches the same observer after the move, takes the close branch and bumps hover_revision, so the hover work the move had just queued was superseded. Instrumented the observer to see it: saw=["<80><fd>d", "\27"]. 'nx!' orders the ESC first and leaves the move last, identically on both builds.

Fix: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua only, three getchar(0) pumps replaced by one deliver_move() helper. Lesson routed to docs/agent-testing.md so the next mouse or on_key test does not rediscover either half.

title: Stack LouieLM transcript content in chronological order
description:
## Problem

In the latest screenshot of a LouieLM session, the transcript content feels split by type: the conversation text appears above while tool activity/status lines are grouped at the bottom near the prompt. This makes the sequence of the session awkward to follow.

## Desired behavior

Render each printed item in one chronological vertical stack, including model text, user text, tool calls, tool results, and status messages. New items should appear after the preceding item in the same transcript flow, with the composer/input area remaining at the bottom.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Model text, user text, tool activity, tool results, and status messages appear in a single chronological transcript order.
2. Tool output is positioned next to or directly after the event that produced it rather than in a separate bottom group.
3. The input/composer remains clearly separated from transcript history at the bottom.
4. Existing session header and chat behavior remain unchanged.

Source report: /tmp/nvim-wtu.md
close_reason: Reset streamed response cursor after tool and error transcript items so interleaved chat content remains chronological; added regression coverage. Verified focused and full mini.test suites, StyLua, LuaLS, and git diff --check.

title: LouiselmToMarkdown crashes with uncaught E482 instead of a clean write error
description:
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` crashes with an uncaught Lua/Vimscript error instead of
the clean "could not write markdown file: ..." message when the destination's
parent directory does not exist.

## Observed

Manual QA round on commits 674939b (blog publishing pipeline) and 4e4a58b
(session transcript export), case 2.2/2.3 in QA_REVIEW.md. User ran
`:LouiselmToMarkdown`, typed `~/tmp/qa-export.md` (nonexistent dir):

```
louiselm markdown path (blank for default): ~/tmp/qa-export.md
Lua :command callback: Vim:E482
: Can't open file ~/tmp/qa-export.md for writing: no such file or directory
stack traceback:
        [C]: in function 'writefile'
        ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1561: in function 'to_markdown'
        .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:276: in function 'on_confirm'
        ...installs/neovim/0.12.2/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/ui.lua:114: in function 'input'
        .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:272: in function <.../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:266>
```

Reproduced identically with the absolute path `/tmp/nope/qa-export.md`
(missing dir), ruling out `~`-expansion as the sole cause — the real trigger
is any nonexistent parent directory.

## Symptoms

- User sees a raw `E482` Lua stack trace in `:messages`, not a `louiselm:`
  notification.
- The chat UI's own error path (`report_error`) never fires for this failure.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1561`:

```lua
if nvim.fn.writefile(split_lines(markdown), destination) ~= 0 then
  return nil, "could not write markdown file: " .. destination
end
```

This assumes `writefile()` reports failure via a nonzero return. In Neovim,
when the destination cannot be opened at all (missing parent directory, no
permission), `writefile()` throws `E482` as a Lua error instead of returning
a value — so the `~= 0` check is dead code for this failure mode and the
error propagates uncaught through `Chat:to_markdown` ->
`command.lua:276 on_confirm` -> `vim.ui.input`.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` covers the success path, "no chat
session", "not attached", and "disposed" errors, but has no case where
`writefile` itself fails (e.g. destination inside a nonexistent directory).
The suite never exercises the real `writefile()` call against an unwritable
path.

## Fix direction

Wrap the `writefile` call in `pcall` in `Chat:to_markdown` (init.lua:1561) so
any thrown error is caught and converted into the existing
`"could not write markdown file: " .. destination` return.

## Acceptance

- A regression test in tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua that calls
  `to_markdown` with a path inside a nonexistent directory and asserts a
  clean `(nil, "could not write markdown file: " .. path)` return with no
  thrown error.
- Manually confirmed: `:LouiselmToMarkdown` against a missing directory shows
  a `louiselm: could not write markdown file: ...` notification, no stack
  trace in `:messages`.

## Not covered

`~` is not expanded by `vim.fn.writefile` either (a second, separate
usability issue: paths starting with `~` will still fail even inside an
existing directory tree, just with a clean error now instead of a crash).
Not filing separately since the pcall fix already turns it into the correct
clean-error path; only worth a follow-up if users expect `~` to expand.
close_reason: Fixed in 6167df0. Root cause: nvim.fn.writefile throws E482 (Lua error) instead of returning nonzero when the destination directory doesn't exist, so Chat:to_markdown's `~= 0` check never caught the failure. Fix: wrapped the writefile call in pcall (init.lua:1561), converting any thrown error into the existing clean 'could not write markdown file: ...' return. Tests: added 'reports a clean error instead of crashing when the destination directory does not exist' to tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua -- failed with the exact E482 traceback before the fix, passes after. Gates: full mini.test suite (235/235 cases) and stylua --check on both changed files pass. No deviation from filed acceptance criteria.

title: Selecting a Provenance Decision takes about 11 seconds
description:
Selecting a row in the Provenance Decision index eventually opens the correct evidence popup, but the interaction takes about 11 seconds before the second window appears.

## Observed

Manual QA on 2026-08-28 after fix commit d6851c6, in the maintainer environment. The user reported: "it takes 11s to see the 2nd window...but it loads". Screenshot evidence: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260828_0551_1920x1200_1787889089.png. The screenshot shows the selected Decision evidence popup populated for issue louiselm-c274, proving the result eventually loads. No timing trace or pinned process log was captured, so the 11-second duration is a user measurement.

## Symptoms

- Decision index buffer appears quickly.
- Pressing CR on a row waits about 11 seconds.
- The second Provenance window then appears and contains the expected Decision evidence.
- There is no duplicate-buffer error after d6851c6.

## Root cause

Unknown. The selection path runs asynchronous bvr history and br issue lookups before rendering in lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:514-565. Measure each subprocess and callback boundary before choosing a fix; do not assume the delay is Neovim window creation.

## Why it was not caught

Automated tests stub process execution and invoke callbacks immediately, so they cover ordering and rendering but not real bvr/br latency or user-visible time-to-popup.

## Fix direction

Capture timings for the bvr history call, br issue lookup, and popup render in a real Session. Optimize only the measured bottleneck while preserving explicit partial-error behavior.

## Acceptance

- Selecting a Decision row displays the evidence popup without the duplicate-buffer error.
- The measured time from row selection to popup is reduced to an acceptable interactive delay, with the target agreed from the captured baseline.
- Regression coverage or a deterministic timing boundary prevents reintroducing unnecessary serial work.

## Not covered

- The screenshot does not prove the exact duration independently.
- The previous duplicate-buffer failure is tracked separately by louiselm-g2ya.
close_reason: Fixed in 7efbc44 by opening the Decision Provenance popup immediately with a loading state, then refreshing the same named buffer with final evidence. Regression asserts the loading view before the BVR callback; full MiniTest 703/703, stylua, lua-language-server, and API appendix checks pass. Manual QA confirmed the popup appears immediately and final Decision content loads successfully. BVR latency remains tracked in louiselm-cvlc.

comments.text: Lesson: when enrichment is materially slower than view creation, render a truthful loading state at the UI boundary and refresh the same Provenance buffer when data arrives. The expensive BVR subprocess remains a separate performance concern; no design question is warranted.

title: Attention item
description: A durable, typed, unresolved condition requiring operator awareness. An Attention item is current state owned by capture-service, keyed to a Session or Run, and is independent of whether or how that state is delivered.
design: Established by the louiselm-qbr.9 grill-me session on 2026-08-31 with explicit maintainer confirmation. The distinction prevents delivery mechanisms such as FCM notifications from becoming the source of truth and prevents Agents from composing arbitrary phone-facing text. Extended with skill_approval_pending and skill_unverified after the maintainer confirmed the skill-supply integrity grill-me on 2026-09-03, Sessions claude/04517c0f-b217-423b-9433-7233027e6a78 and codex/01a0635e-ae82-71d3-b910-66377e02bd07.
notes: Use Attention item for unresolved normalized state. Distinguish it from an event, which causes a state transition; from a notification, which is one delivery attempt; and from history, which v1 does not retain. V1 kinds are turn_ready, permission_required, run_parked, session_failed, skill_approval_pending, and skill_unverified. Only trusted local controllers create or clear items; Agents and Android are read-only. Capture-service owns current Attention state and delivery but has no skill-approval or cryptographic authority.

title: Recovery admission test fails without a host br
description:
The stable and nightly Lua CI jobs fail at the same recovery admission regression introduced in 9b893f3. The unit test accidentally depends on the developer-installed Beads executable and live checkout.

Observed: GitHub run 34953331670, commit c0af8335f28e365f4e66bf2ca9e3faf0f5b6c8ef. Stable job104329304641 and nightly job104329304507 both report: FAIL in tests/workflow/recovery_spec.lua | failed asynchronous admission preserves its error and never attaches: tests/workflow/recovery_spec.lua:243: could not start Beads claim query. Evidence https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/34953331670/job/104329304641 and https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/34953331670/job/104329304507.

Root cause: recovery_spec.lua:216 mocks Service.admit and Service.attach, but Recovery:park invokes recovery.lua:108 live_claims first through vim.system(br list --assignee ... --status in_progress --json). CI does not install br. The fake Session uses the real working directory. The fixture fails before its intended admission callback/assertions.

Verified reproduction: run the focused recovery_spec.lua through tests/minimal_init.lua; normal developer PATH gives 8/8 passing. In the separate test Neovim, set vim.env.PATH to /usr/bin:/bin and assert vim.fn.executable("br")==0 before MiniTest.run_file: 7/8 pass and the exact CI failure occurs. No production file was edited to reproduce.

Why missed: local gates found ~/.cargo/bin/br and queried the real Beads checkout; a passing developer environment concealed the missing fixture boundary.

Fix direction: isolate this test with a temporary executable br fixture and a scoped PATH, retaining real asynchronous process/callback delivery. Restore PATH and remove only its temporary fixture in MiniTest.finally. Do not add a production injection abstraction, weaken the assertion, or install a new CI dependency.

Acceptance: the existing admission-error assertion passes with host br absent; claims query cannot consume the real workspace; original PATH restored even on assertion failure; focused and complete Lua suite, formatting/typecheck and generated checks pass. Stable CI no longer fails this test.

Scope: test harness only; no runtime behavior change or manual application QA required. Own regression from current Session.
close_reason: gate:tests/workflow/recovery_spec.lua c5d281e; isolated executable/cwd preserves async failure coverage;1044 local cases and hosted stable/nightly pass run34954752663; lesson comment1835.

title: Resolve a Session id to its transcript with a layout-keyed locator
description:
## Goal

Given a Session id such as `codex/01a0343a-...`, return the path to that
Session's transcript on disk, for every Agent the maintainer actually uses.

## Scope

- In scope: `lua/louiselm/session/locator.lua`; a config surface mapping an
  Agent entry to a transcript layout; layouts for claude, codex, deepseek and
  copilot; a `nil, err` result when no transcript exists.
- Out of scope: reading, parsing or rendering transcript contents. This task
  returns a path and nothing more. No UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `locator.resolve("<agent>/<session-id>")` returns an absolute path, or
   `nil, err` with an actionable message.
2. Resolution keys on transcript LAYOUT, never on Agent name. `config.agents`
   is a `map-of` with default `{}`, so Agent names are arbitrary user labels;
   two Agents configured with different names but the same CLI must resolve
   through one layout implementation.
3. An Agent renamed in config after its Sessions were recorded still resolves
   those Sessions.
4. A malformed id, an unknown layout, and a well-formed id whose transcript
   file is absent are each distinguishable failures, not one generic error.
5. Public API is LuaCATS-typed; no editor or UI calls anywhere in the module.

## Testing

- Temporary directory trees, one per layout, asserting resolution and the
  missing-file path.
- Two differently-named Agents sharing one layout both resolve.
- An Agent renamed between recording and lookup still resolves.
- No network, no real Agent binaries, no reliance on the maintainer's home
  directory.

## Notes

First slice of louiselm-h00g deliberately: self-contained, unblocked by the
bvr defect (louiselm-f8r1), and independently wanted by louiselm-3x9p, so it
retains value even if the rest of the epic is reshaped.

glm is expected to resolve through the OpenAI-compatible layout shared with
deepseek. There are no glm Session ids in the record yet, so do not claim glm
support until a real glm Session resolves; leave it unverified rather than
asserted.
close_reason: Implemented layout-keyed transcript resolution for all four observed layouts; live acceptance and 557-test suite pass.

title: Read git commit trailers into structured Provenance edges
description:
## Goal

Turn `Refs <id>` commit trailers into structured Provenance edges, so a commit
can name the issues and Sessions it belongs to.

## Scope

- In scope: the git half of `lua/louiselm/provenance/sources.lua`; the trailer
  parsing and edge construction in `lua/louiselm/provenance/correlate.lua`.
- Out of scope: bvr correlation, time travel, and any UI. Beads actor fields
  are a separate slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a commit range, produce edges of commit -> issue id and
   commit -> Session id derived from `Refs` trailers.
2. `correlate` performs no I/O at all. It takes already-collected input and
   returns edges, so the whole join is fixture-testable.
3. `sources` spawns git with `vim.system()` and an argument array, never a
   built command string, and passes cwd explicitly.
4. Commits with no trailer, several trailers, and a trailer naming an id that
   no longer exists are each handled without error.
5. Both are LuaCATS-typed and return structured errors rather than notifying,
   printing or opening UI.

## Testing

- `correlate` against captured real `git log` output from this repository,
  cited in the test per AGENTS.md section 5 so observed shapes stay
  distinguishable from invented ones.
- The pre-convention era, where commits carry no trailers at all, yields
  partial edges rather than failure.
- `sources` callbacks are exercised in the production callback context, and the
  test proves no editor API is touched before a scheduling boundary.

## Notes

The trailer convention is already established: of the last 200 commits every
one carries a `Refs` line, and they already mix both node types.
close_reason: Implemented typed git Refs parsing/correlation and scheduled git source; focused and full 571-case MiniTest, StyLua, LuaLS, and diff checks pass.

comments.author: codex/01a03df9-6992-71e2-9050-1d4dd466011c
comments.text: Implemented with git's NUL/record-separated log format: sources parses bounded commit records and schedules all completion work out of vim.system's fast event; correlate remains pure and preserves unknown/stale Refs as typed issue or Session edges. Tests cite the captured repository log and prove no-trailer partial output plus callback scheduling. Lesson destination: this issue comment; no standing AGENTS.md rule or design question is warranted.

title: Open every UI selector outside insert mode
description:
## Problem

Commit 1eb309a fixed permission selection by leaving insert mode immediately before vim.ui.select. That diagnosis is correct: Chat:attach enters insert mode, and list-focused select providers can otherwise receive the wrong mode and confirm or edit the wrong picker state.

The same bug remains in session configuration. Chat:attach schedules open_session_options after entering insert mode, while both the options overview and its nested model/value picker call vim.ui.select without normalizing mode. This affects the automatic first-session overview and can also affect :LouiselmSessionOptions when invoked from an insert-mode mapping.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Attach a ready session that advertises a model or boolean configuration option.
2. Let Chat:attach focus the prompt and enter insert mode.
3. Wait for the scheduled initial options overview, or invoke :LouiselmSessionOptions from an insert-mode mapping.
4. Observe that vim.ui.select is called while the inherited mode is insert; with a list-focused provider, navigation or confirmation targets the wrong picker state.
5. Select an option such as Model and observe the nested value picker has the same unnormalized boundary.

## Investigation

There are 12 vim.ui.select call sites across chat, context, and diff UI. In addition to session options, selectors that are asynchronous, nested, or exposed through public Chat methods can inherit insert mode: resumed-session selection, remembered-permission selection and confirmation, session switch/close, agent selection, and file/skill context selection. The permission picker is now protected. The diff-review selector is currently protected indirectly because the focused diff buffer exits insert mode before its normal-mode actions run.

## Scope

- Normalize mode at the narrowest shared LouiseLM selection boundary immediately before opening every vim.ui.select picker.
- Cover both stages of the session-options flow, especially the model/value picker opened by :LouiselmSessionOptions and the automatic picker scheduled by Chat:attach.
- Migrate or audit every raw vim.ui.select call in lua/louiselm/ui so no insert-mode-sensitive sibling remains.
- Preserve provider ownership of picker layout and interaction; do not detect or configure Snacks or another provider.
- Preserve selection values, cancellation behavior, asynchronous scheduling, and disposal guards.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The automatically opened session-options overview is invoked outside insert mode after Chat:attach starts the prompt in insert mode.
2. The nested model/boolean value picker is also invoked outside insert mode.
3. Every LouiseLM vim.ui.select call either uses the shared normalization boundary or has a tested invariant proving insert mode cannot reach it.
4. The existing permission-picker mode regression remains green, and diff review remains in normal mode.
5. Headless behavioral tests cover the session-options regression and at least one representative shared/public or asynchronous selector path without relying on provider internals.
6. The focused UI tests, full MiniTest suite, StyLua check, and lua-language-server check pass.
close_reason: Normalized all 12 vim.ui.select call sites through one normal-mode picker boundary. Added red-green regressions for automatic/nested session options and file context selection. Verification: focused chat 44/44, context 5/5, diff 5/5; full MiniTest 185/185; StyLua and LuaLS passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Usage refresh strands the cursor above result rows
description:
Usage paging changes the data but leaves the cursor in unchanged aggregate totals, making n/p appear ineffective and making Enter a no-op after navigation.

## Observed
September21 manual QA, coordinator codex/01a0c433-de8c-79d0-9d88-eea2e81235da. Maintainer after loading timing fix992162f: "i press p and n and it reloads soething but the view stays the same".
Pinned new test editor /run/user/1000/nvim.1126797.0, buffer4/window1000: installed992162f, turns header, Rows101-125 of2071 at line18; first turn line20, cursor13 in totals. Viewport1-42, width92, height50. Original test editor was replaced; this is the fixed build.

Independent actual-history/mapped-key reproduction on992162f:
- Before n: offset0, rows1-25, cursor20 on first result, turn c804e4c28c67c6f0fa94f9550bd46859.
- During read: offset25, cursor9, no result rows.
- After read: rows26-50, first resultline20 and new turn12beac2a72983fc29aed7b18f0bf82f9, cursor still9.
- Press mapped Enter: view remains turns, selected=false.
No query error. Data actually changes; lost result focus plus unchanged whole-cohort totals explains the stationary presentation. Earlier F1/louiselm-ahamh independently fixed dropped p during loading but did not solve this focus problem.

## Root cause
lua/louiselm/ui/usage.lua render replaces all lines with the short Loading display when refresh clears self.page. Neovim clamps a result cursor into that short header. Completion replaces the lines again without selecting a result. This shared render path serves opening, grouping, drilldown, paging and back navigation.

## Test gap
Existing UI tests assert rendered data and call enter(index) directly. They do not require Enter at the post-refresh cursor to reach the returned row. Async cancellation tests preserve data but do not assert cursor usability.

## Fix and acceptance
After a successful render with rows, position the cursor on the first returned row only when this usage buffer is the current buffer. Do not focus another window or move its cursor on an async completion; empty/error/loading views retain their status display. No new state/config/dependency.
Add mapped-key regression: n loads another turn, cursor selects it, Enter opens its observations; Backspace/p preserve a usable selected result. Add asynchronous other-buffer focus protection. Run full Lua/static/generated gates.
Live acceptance: after n/p the cursor visibly lands on a dated turn from the returned page and Enter opens that turn; the maintainer can distinguish the page change. Keep open until confirmed.

## Boundaries
No totals aggregation, SQL ordering, history mutation or global keymap change. Improving the overall page layout is not part of this narrow fix.
close_reason: Maintainer accepted paging focus and immediate Enter on b61d922; pinned events view verified. Lesson retained in issue comments. live:codex/01a0c433-de8c-79d0-9d88-eea2e81235da

comments.text:
## Confirmed recurrence and diagnosis — 2026-09-17

Subject: codex/01a0ae17-2bfd-7562-8afb-cc965aedc72b. Investigator: codex/01a0ae34-ae0f-7221-b0b4-61385c11e46f, resolved through the live session.identity() API. User requested filing and investigation only; no implementation or live retry was performed. This supersedes the original root-cause-unknown statement. Reuse this P2 bug because the original September 15 occurrence has the same upstream error and downstream termination sequence.

## Observed

Primary Codex transcript:
/home/lotso/.codex/sessions/2026/09/17/rollout-2026-09-17T08-39-09-01a0ae17-2bfd-7562-8afb-cc965aedc72b.jsonl

- Line 426: final turn uses model gpt-6-astra, effort xhigh.
- Line 439, 2026-09-17T07:10:14.320Z: task_complete for turn 01a0ae33-4c09-7ee3-a4d1-46cf6f0bd6a8 after 21,792 ms, with exact error {"message":"Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.","codex_error_info":"server_overloaded"}.
- Line 438: reported weekly usage 28%, rate_limit_reached_type null. This is a model-capacity error, not an observed exhausted-account-limit error.
- Lines 130 and 423: two preceding turns completed without errors. The failed turn had already produced successful tool results; it failed during continuation.

ACP log:
/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a0ae17-2bfd-7562-8afb-cc965aedc72b/log.jsonl

- Line 1511, 07:09:52.491Z: session/prompt request id 8.
- Line 1571, 07:10:14.320Z: {"sessionUpdate":"session_info_update","_meta":{"codex":{"threadStatus":{"type":"systemError"}}}}.
- Line 1572, 07:10:14.352Z: internal exit {"code":137}, only 32 ms later.
- No response to prompt id 8 and no typed sessionFailure notification arrived before exit. The detailed capacity message exists in the Codex transcript, not this ACP stream.

Construction log:
/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/connections/1f620c85-33cc-4729-9949-a08bdc800ca9.jsonl

- Line 1: launch via python3 /home/lotso/.config/nvim/agent-runtimes/runtime.py launch codex.
- Line 2: client advertised jetbrains.air version 1 capabilities ["sessionFailure"].
- Line 6 binds this connection to the subject ACP id.

Original occurrence independently checked:
/home/lotso/.codex/sessions/2026/09/15/rollout-2026-09-15T10-17-01-01a0a424-0de4-70d2-a27e-ab915b83af5e.jsonl:10 contains the identical server_overloaded/capacity error at 08:17:07.987Z, turn 01a0a424-215a-7cc3-a3ce-96bf40c7986e. Its ACP systemError and exit137 sequence was already recorded in this issue. This establishes a shared trigger for both incidents.

## Root cause

There are two distinct boundaries: upstream capacity ends the turn; LouiseLM's failure handling then makes the Session unusable and hides the actionable cause.

1. lua/louiselm/session/validation.lua:316 recognizes any Codex threadStatus.type=systemError, without distinguishing capacity, authentication, or transport failure.
2. lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:534-540 immediately calls fail("Codex agent reported a system error for this turn"). That happens before processing later typed failure metadata or the prompt response.
3. fail(), lifecycle.lua:257-268, records failed, clears session_failure, sets status=error, and closes the ACP client. lua/louiselm/acp/transport.lua:207-216 closes stdin and sends SIGTERM to the proxy.
4. /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/src/proxy/lifecycle.rs:50-63 handles termination by killing the child; src/proxy.rs:308-318 maps signal termination to 128+signal. This code path explains the observed exit137. No signal-delivery trace was captured; exit137 alone is not evidence of OOM.

The active Neovim runtime path points to /home/lotso/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim, revision b65de573024d21cdb7e287d918096be70035e2c0. Its lifecycle.lua, validation.lua and transport.lua byte hashes exactly match the investigated checkout, revision 68581b7bcd7f72fbec814c4c13e2c976e47b0f1c.

The current managed Codex adapter source at /home/lotso/.local/share/louiselm/agent-runtimes/codex/builds/46b2f984f61a887c also explains the lost diagnostic: src/CodexEventHandler.ts:499 forwards thread/status/changed immediately, while src/CodexAcpServer.ts:3019-3032 waits for notifications before handleFailedTurn processes the detailed terminal error. That later result never reached the captured ACP stream. The historical process is gone, so no independent in-memory adapter-build or signal-source inspection is possible.

The overbroad fatal handler originated in b60706a6c0577cdd9813d7af8194140856cf9fd8, intended to prevent revoked-auth failures followed by end_turn from appearing successful. Preserve that protection when correcting the Session lifecycle.

## Why it was not caught

tests/session/api_spec.lua:2183 explicitly expects a Codex systemError to put the entire Session in error and discard a later normal-looking end_turn. It omits the captured capacity-error ordering, preservation of typed failure details, and successful continuation after a recoverable turn failure. The existing focused case was executed unchanged: 1 case, 0 failures. That confirms the implemented assumption; it is not a regression fix or live acceptance.

## Fix direction and acceptance

- Separate a failed turn from an unusable ACP transport at the shared Session lifecycle boundary. Keep a capacity failure marked failed without immediately killing the healthy adapter.
- Consume the negotiated structured failure/result and display a bounded actionable capacity cause. Do not introduce automatic model fallback or claim to repair upstream capacity.
- Add a regression derived from the observed systemError-before-terminal-diagnostic order: callback/outcome fires once, no false successful turn, detailed failure remains visible, and retry/model selection can continue on the same Session.
- Preserve the revoked-auth false-success regression, malformed-protocol handling, disposal and genuine process/transport failure coverage. Run applicable Lua gates.
- Live acceptance: the maintainer sees the capacity diagnostic and can continue the retained Session when capacity returns or after choosing another model. Keep open until that behavior is confirmed.

## Scope and remaining uncertainty

P2: there is a reload/retry or operator-selected alternate-model recovery path, but this incident did not test it. Upstream scheduling details are unavailable; louiselm-xd91 separately tracks provider capacity behavior. No proof of OOM, context exhaustion, a failing tool command, or bad user configuration. No code/configuration changes, no claims, no commits, and no full-suite or live-fix acceptance in this diagnostic task.

title: Keep the chat header compact instead of dumping session metadata
description:
## Problem

The chat buffer header expands into a long Markdown heading containing every session option and context field. At normal split widths it wraps across visual rows, dominates the top of the conversation, and is difficult to scan.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat session whose agent reports several configuration options plus context or cost telemetry.
2. Display the chat in a typical narrow vertical split.
3. Observe that the level-one Markdown heading includes all metadata and wraps across multiple visual rows.

## Observed

A Codex session currently renders a heading such as:

`# codex · session-1 · ready · Mode=agent-full-access · Collaboration mode=default · Model=gpt-5.6-sol · Reasoning effort=xhigh · Fast mode=off · context=62585/258400 (24% normal) · Your turn`

The screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0534_1920x1200_1786246460.png` shows this heading wrapping in the chat split.

## Expected

The transcript heading remains a compact, stable summary of session identity and current turn state, for example `# codex · session-1 · ready · Your turn`. Detailed configuration and telemetry remain discoverable through session options or a separate secondary status surface instead of being concatenated into an unbounded Markdown heading.

## Likely Root Cause

`session_summary()` appends every `config_options` entry plus context and cost telemetry, and `session_header()` uses the complete summary as the level-one Markdown heading. The heading length therefore scales with agent capabilities and enabled metadata.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The level-one chat heading contains only concise session identity/lifecycle/turn information and stays readable at a typical vertical split width.
2. Static/default fields such as mode, collaboration mode, model, reasoning effort, and fast mode are not dumped into the transcript heading.
3. Detailed configuration remains accessible through the existing session-options flow or another clearly defined secondary surface; do not silently remove the ability to inspect or change supported options.
4. Useful dynamic telemetry such as context pressure or cost, if retained in the UI, is presented outside the primary Markdown heading and does not make that heading grow without bound.
5. Header updates for state changes, renamed sessions, loaded sessions, and turn transitions continue to work.
6. Add or update headless UI behavior tests using a session with several config options and context telemetry. Assert the compact buffer heading and continued access to configuration; use a manual narrow-split smoke check for wrapping rather than a pixel assertion.

## Scope

- In scope: chat header/status presentation and its behavioral tests.
- Out of scope: changing ACP session metadata, removing configuration controls, or redesigning the rest of the transcript.
close_reason: Split compact session identity from the detailed switcher summary so chat headings contain only name/agent/id/lifecycle/turn while options and telemetry remain accessible. Verification: focused chat suite 27/27 passed; full mini.test suite 112/112 passed; stylua --check . passed; lua-language-server reported zero diagnostics; 48-column headless smoke passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Production guarded launch rejects configured stock Codex chain
description:
Configured stock Codex cannot reach the production guarded Brokered launch path. The installed positive fixture uses louiselm-tool-test-agent, while the real ACP chain needs configured arguments/environment and Codex sends from a descendant app-server. This blocks louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.13 real API acceptance.

## Observed
2026-09-26 source inspection in this checkout (HEAD c371bf2):
- skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/system.rs:1334 calls validate_registration for every SystemLaunchPlatform launch.
- skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/tool_integration.rs:130-139 rejects any nonempty Agent arguments or environment with ToolIsolationUnproven.
- skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/installed_tests.rs:216-329 measures only louiselm-tool-test-agent and registers arguments=[] and environment={}.
- skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/installed_guard_tests.rs:287-545 runs this test Agent and synthetic Provider traffic; no stock Codex process is launched.
- docs/codex-kernel-guard-proof.md:335-460 shows stock Codex only in a separate experimental Python guard fixture.

## Impact
The current production fixture cannot establish the stock Codex plus acp-proxy plus codex-acp.js chain required for a real brokered OpenAI turn. The API key and live network would not repair the registration refusal.

## Why missed
The installed positive fixture verifies production guard and broker plumbing with a synthetic Agent. The earlier stock ACP proof uses a separate experimental guard, so no gate composes stock Codex with SystemLaunchPlatform.

## Fix direction
Extend the measured installed Agent registration and sender enrollment to the exact stock ACP chain, preserving adapter/tool isolation and immutable runtime identity. Add a disposable VM regression that starts that chain through the production launcher before any real API request. Do not loosen validation to arbitrary arguments/environment or enroll an adapter instead of the actual sending Codex runtime.

## Acceptance
A configured stock Codex chain launches through SystemLaunchPlatform with the exact measured ACP ancestry and kernel sender enrollment, reaches the local broker listener, and a helper cannot reach it. Wrong arguments, environment, process ancestry or executable identity refuse before Provider effects. Existing synthetic installed guard cases remain green.

## Not covered
Real paid OpenAI requests and maintainer-host Verified acceptance remain louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.13 and .14.

description:
# Manual QA — OpenCode approval details

Final QA record for louiselm-16sc; archived into Beads when the round closes.

Build under test: d9ed958. Installed checkout verified at d9ed958 at acceptance.

## Status

| Case | State |
|---|---|
| OpenCode command and scope are readable before approval | PASS — maintainer reports "it worked" after the corrected recipe. Installed d9ed958 verified. Initial attempt was a recipe miss (zero permission requests). |

## Setup

1. Update the installed plugin to include d9ed958 and restart Neovim. Verify
   `git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim merge-base --is-ancestor d9ed958 HEAD`
   exits zero before restarting.
2. For this test, temporarily replace the global `permission` value in
   `/home/lotso/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` with:
   `{"*":"allow","external_directory":"ask"}`.
   Original value was `"allow"`. No setting was changed by the diagnosing Agent.
3. Start a fresh OpenCode Session; use Allow once, not Always allow.

## Case

Paste: Use your bash tool to run exactly `cd /var/tmp && pwd`. Report the output.
Do not change any files.

Expect the approval picker to show the command, with View request details
available. Select it: full command and directory/pattern scope must be readable
and scrollable. Press q/Esc: return to choices without approving. Select Allow
once: command completes. Failure: unknown/details unavailable despite a supplied
title, inaccessible/truncated details, premature approval, or stuck Session.

## Evidence

Prior attempt: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ses_f7b8b7cd3ffelUtF6fc0zX2p6f/log.jsonl:15-18
shows tool chatcmpl-tool-9ac4a91592752434 running and completing
`ls -ld /tmp\nls -ld /var/tmp`; zero session/request_permission frames.
Connection 1d5af039-6100-4be0-ab31-f427a744db1e launched opencode acp, version 1.18.29.

For the next Session, count frames with:
`jq -s '[.[] | select(.payload.method == "session/request_permission")] | length' <pinned-session-log>`.
This check returns 0 for the missed attempt. A nonzero count proves the request
reached LouiseLM; picker readability/focus requires the maintainer's observation.

## Cleanup

The maintainer's temporary external_directory=ask remains enabled at closure;
restore permission to "allow" when finished. The diagnosing Agent did not change
the operator's permission configuration. No fixture files were created.

## Acceptance and lessons

2026-09-09, maintainer in codex/01a0845c-2920-7af2-9bc7-f55683ca6f80:
"it worked". This accepts the corrected manual case. Reference Session: opencode/ses_f7b871336ffeKhV5y8XOSOUR8E, subsequently supplied
by the maintainer. Its proxy session log:86 requests permission for
`cd /var/tmp && pwd` with kind=other and command/directories/patterns metadata;
:87 selects once; :90 completes the tool call. Protocol evidence corroborates
the completed approval; readability and focus remain the maintainer's observation.
Installed checkout d9ed958 independently verified.

No additional product findings. louiselm-16sc is fixed by d9ed958 and accepted.
The regression suite covers captured OpenCode shape, async scheduling, exact
response IDs and details-window lifecycle; all 932 Lua tests and required Lua
gates passed. Only live QA could prove the operator could use the actual picker.

Recipe lesson: verify both installed build and upstream permission settings

title: Beads inspector cannot locate workspace from session
description:
The Beads issue inspector fails to locate the workspace when invoked with `<leader>lB` on a Beads issue in a LouiseLM chat session, reporting `louiselm: could not locate Beads workspace`. This prevents inspecting the issue under the cursor from the session buffer.

## Observed

Reported 2026-08-28 in session `codex/01a04621-223a-7c83-982e-94c88435ed5b`, with the cursor on line 281. Reproduction: press `<leader>lB`.

Observed error:

> louiselm: could not locate Beads workspace

The keymap routes `<leader>lB` to `:LouiselmInspectBead` (`lua/louiselm/ui/keymaps.lua:35`). The command invokes `Beads.inspect` (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:398-426`). Workspace discovery runs `br where --json` with `cwd = options.cwd or nvim.fn.getcwd()` (`lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:215-226`). Any nonzero `br where` exit is collapsed into the reported error at `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:225-227`.

## Symptoms

- Pressing `<leader>lB` on a line containing a Beads issue does not open the issue inspector.
- LouiseLM reports that it could not locate a Beads workspace.
- The session and line context are not enough to make the lookup succeed.

## Root cause

Unknown. The reported message does not preserve `br where`'s stderr, exit status, or resolved cwd, so it is not yet possible to distinguish an incorrect cwd, a missing/unavailable workspace, or another `br` failure. Capture the command result and working directory for this reproduction before assigning the mechanism.

## Why it was not caught

Existing tests cover successful workspace discovery and issue inspection with explicit test cwd values, but do not cover a real Session buffer invoking the keymap with the session's actual cwd and a failing `br where` result.

## Fix direction

Reproduce using the supplied session and capture the actual cwd plus `br where --json` stderr/exit status. Then make the inspector use the requesting Session's workspace cwd, or report the underlying lookup failure if the workspace genuinely is absent. Preserve actionable command diagnostics instead of reducing every nonzero exit to the same message.

## Acceptance

- `<leader>lB` on the supplied session's line 281 successfully resolves and opens the Beads issue when the session belongs to a Beads workspace.
- If lookup genuinely cannot run, the user-visible error identifies the actual cause and cwd.
- A regression test covers the Session/keymap path and the relevant workspace lookup failure or cwd behavior.

## Not covered

The issue ID under the cursor and the exact `br where` stderr/exit code were not captured in the report. No root cause is asserted yet.
close_reason: Fixed in the current working tree (not committed because the repository contains pre-existing user changes). Root cause: inspect_bead omitted the active Session's working_dir, causing Beads discovery to use the unrelated current editor cwd. The command now forwards state.working_dir. Regression: tests/ui/command_spec.lua 'inspects Beads from the active Session workspace'. Verification: focused command tests 32/32 pass; beads tests 10/10 pass; full suite 701/701 pass; stylua --check passes; lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning passes. No deviation from acceptance criteria.

Fixed in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua by forwarding that cwd. Added tests/ui/command_spec.lua regression that changes editor cwd after session creation and verifies Beads receives the Session workspace. No standing AGENTS.md rule is warranted; this is an issue-local ownership bug.

title: Agents exposing no session id must interrupt the maintainer to get an actor
description:
`session.identity()` (louiselm-hmmc) resolves a caller's actor from the ACP
session id the caller already knows about itself. An Agent whose adapter
exposes no id of its own therefore has nothing to pass, and AGENTS.md sends it
to the maintainer before every Beads mutation.

## Observed
2026-09-07. AGENTS.md records that OpenCode inside LouiseLM exports only
`OPENCODE=1`, `OPENCODE_PID`, and `OPENCODE_CLIENT=acp` — process markers, not a
session id. Codex and Claude Code both expose an id and are unaffected.

## Cost
Every Beads mutation from such a Session becomes a blocking question. The
previous focused-Chat recipe answered without asking, which is exactly why it
returned the wrong Session (louiselm-hmmc).

## Options, none chosen
- Map the calling process back to its Session through process ancestry: a tool
  call runs in a descendant of the Agent process LouiseLM spawned, and the
  registry knows each Session's process. Linux-specific, and it must not
  resolve a child-agent task to its parent Session.
- Give the Agent its own identity at spawn. The ACP session id does not exist
  until `session/new` returns, so this needs a LouiseLM-assigned handle the
  Agent can read and hand back.
- Accept the ask. The maintainer answers once per Session, not per mutation.

## Acceptance
Either a Session whose adapter exposes no id resolves its own actor without
asking, or this issue closes recording that asking is the accepted cost.

title: Measure source-sensitive skills-core Cargo cache reuse

Evidence: louiselm-8nblj; docs/performance/skills-ci-20260918/ci-timings.json. All four Sep18 runs restored the same 1,243,187,453-byte archive created Sep17. This does not explain the 8-minute runtime variation; prioritize the isolated-job split independently.

Scope: evaluate a source/manifest-aware suffix with a toolchain/profile/lock-compatible restore prefix, retaining Cargo's exact-source fingerprint validation. Preserve public/fork/PR cache scope and do not treat caches as trusted release artifacts. No production optimization, test skipping, new dependencies, full target upload on every matrix job, or release guard changes.

Acceptance: capture identical-source warm rerun, changed-source warm rerun and cold-cache measurements including restore, compile, save, cache bytes and total job time. Preserve all current gates and exact release commit coverage. Use existing dependencies and validate the cache-key/restore behavior against the actual installed Actions versions. Keep a candidate only if total time and storage/runner cost show a useful measured tradeoff; report a rejected candidate just as explicitly. The theoretical recoverable build work is about a minute, not the privileged step's 14–23 minutes.

title: Attention socket test mistakes invalidation for mutation reply
description:
Observed GitHub run34954752663 on c5d281e, job104334069049 cargo(capture-service): attention_socket_requires_capability_and_retries_without_new_generation panicked at tests/attention.rs:507: assertion failed: store.snapshot().expect("session cleared").items.is_empty(). https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/34954752663/job/104334069049 . Previous run passed this job; stable/nightly Lua now pass.

Root cause: tests/attention.rs:476 consumes one untyped line for replay, then accepts any MutationResult for clear without matching request_id. attention_socket.rs:207-239 multiplexes AttentionChanged invalidations every50ms with correlated replies. An invalidation consumed as replay response leaves request-2 ACK to be consumed as request-3 ACK; state can be checked before clear completes.

Why missed: fast local runs usually finish before the periodic notification; test assumed one frame per request, unlike the actual wire protocol.

Fix direction: test-only bounded reply reader, skip only AttentionChanged and assert exact correlation. Deterministically queue invalidation ahead of reply over a real UnixStream pair to reproduce without arbitrary sleeps. Preserve real socket authorization/idempotency/clear assertions and no production changes.

Acceptance: deterministic mixed-frame regression fails for first-frame reading, passes for correlated reader; all89 existing capture cases plus added regression pass; fmt/clippy/rustdoc gates pass; hosted capture-service test passes. Scope is test synchronization, not installed service behavior.

title: Sender guard
description: The kernel-enforced checks owned by a Session's Launch supervisor that authenticate its enrolled Agent runtime at the Session's broker endpoint and enforce the enrolled Control broker's authority on that Session's upstream Provider sockets.
design: Established by louiselm-80yzp, maintainer-confirmed 2026-09-24 in claude/d7834ce3-9555-4d81-ad34-eb0aed935af8. Extended by louiselm-8a8id, maintainer-confirmed 2026-09-25 in codex/01a0d6a5-8a3f-7e52-a20c-ff6a3db36d4f, to include per-Session upstream socket enforcement. Built on docs/codex-kernel-guard-proof.md; production acceptance remains required.
notes: Use Sender guard for runtime-to-broker sender authentication and Session-bound broker-to-Provider socket enforcement. It never authorizes a request: per-request admission, Run limits, destination and Model policy belong to the Control broker. The Launch supervisor loads/owns enforcement and creates guarded upstream sockets before authenticated handoff. Process enrollment is immutable; additional sockets may be registered while authority remains live. Socket bindings cannot move between Sessions/Runs/revisions. Loss is enforced in the kernel at send; recovery never re-enrolls a runtime. Broker replacement requires fresh Sessions for Provider networking. Distinguish from Control broker policy and Launch supervisor lifecycle mechanics.

GitLab job https://gitlab.bartab.fr/oss-public/louiselm/-/jobs/145166, pipeline 39282, commit d303588b997e8ba84e4ab04e6bdd331bb597a009 ("feat(preflight): inspect proposed launch inputs"), 2026-09-11T04:17:52Z.

Job trace (MyST build succeeds, then the publication guard fails):

    2026-09-11T04:18:27.964084Z 01E public artifact rejected: Markdown export does not match a curated source: build/README-ddfda54b8253b48146ed77e9025c5590.md
    ERROR: Job failed: exit code 1

Still failing on every subsequent site-build job through current HEAD: 145173 (ce0ae058), 145192 (c024ec0d), 145205 (66f6d219), 145212 (39eb1355), 145225 (9a02feea), 145232 (8f19cae1), 145239 (46cacc75). Last known-good site-build was 145159 (95510881), before d303588b landed.

Reproduced locally via `./scripts/build-site` (myst build phase only, prior to the unrelated build-demo.mjs CI-token requirement). Two hashed README exports appear under `_build/html/build/`:

- `README-91d8fe403b9fc53bae481e60e633ee43.md` — `cmp` matches root `README.md` (accepted).
- `README-35d41122f2cd6bbe5eb7ec999594c04f.md` — `cmp` differs at byte 11; its content is actually `skills-core/README.md` ("# LouiseLM skills core..."), not the root README (rejected).

## Symptoms

- Maintainer sees: GitLab pipeline red on `main`, `site-build` job, no site publish possible.
- System reports: `public artifact rejected: Markdown export does not match a curated source: build/README-<hash>.md`, exit code 1.

## Root cause

Commit d303588b added a relative Markdown link in `README.md`:

    [artifact preflight](skills-core/README.md#prospective-artifact-preflight)

MyST follows relative Markdown links from public pages and exports the linked file as a hashed Markdown artifact under `build/`, using only the linked file's own basename (here colliding with root `README.md`, disambiguated solely by the content hash). `scripts/check-public-artifact`'s `public_markdown_sources` allowlist (check-public-artifact:13-26) does not include `skills-core/README.md`, so the export fails the byte-identity check at check-public-artifact:108-121 and is rejected as "does not match a curated source".

## Why it was not caught

Same test gap as the prior occurrence: `npm run site:test` (demo config + artifact policy unit tests) does not run the actual MyST build, so a new relative link added in a feature commit isn't exercised against the real export/allowlist path before it reaches CI. This is the exact same defect class as the already-closed louiselm-o7v6 ("Site CI rejects README-linked backup operator guide", root-caused to a relative link to docs/acp-log-backups.md, fixed in commit 89fa1ef1 by switching to a repository URL, gate:gitlab-job-145056) and louiselm-ermp (README-linked turn recording doc, same mechanism). The lesson recorded on o7v6 — "relative Markdown links from public MyST pages also opt sources into downloadable exports; operator-only/non-curated docs must use repository URLs, and README link changes require the full site build, not only feature tests" — was written as a closed-issue comment, not promoted to a standing instruction or a pre-merge gate, so it recurred one day later on a different link.

## Fix direction

Two options, not mutually exclusive:
1. Route the README link through a repository URL (`https://gitlab.bartab.fr/oss-public/louiselm/-/blob/main/skills-core/README.md#...`) instead of a relative Markdown link, matching the o7v6 fix pattern — appropriate if skills-core/README.md is not meant to be a curated public site page.
2. If skills-core/README.md is meant to be public site content, add it to `public_markdown_sources` in scripts/check-public-artifact.
Either way, consider promoting the recurring lesson into something CI actually checks (e.g. run the full `./scripts/build-site` + `check-public-artifact` locally as part of any README-touching change, or a lint that flags new relative Markdown links from public pages to non-allowlisted sources) so a third recurrence doesn't need a human to notice red CI again.

## Acceptance

- `./scripts/build-site` run end-to-end produces a `public artifact accepted` result (currently blocked locally by an unrelated `LOUISELM_DEMO_PACKAGE_TOKEN` requirement in `build-demo.mjs`, not part of this defect).
- New GitLab `site-build` job on `main` succeeds.
- A regression fixture in `scripts/test-public-artifact.sh` covering a relative link from a public page to a non-curated source, analogous to the `build/acp-log-backups-...md` fixture added for o7v6.

## Not covered

- The unrelated local repro blocker in build-demo.mjs (needs CI_JOB_TOKEN/LOUISELM_DEMO_PACKAGE_TOKEN) — not investigated further here, does not affect the CI failure since CI supplies that token.
- Whether skills-core/README.md's content is otherwise appropriate for public consumption — only its export mechanism was investigated.
- No fix has been applied; this bug is filed per the "file before fixing" workflow rule, at the reporter's explicit request to investigate and file only.
close_reason: Fixed in <pending commit>. Root cause: README.md:83 linked skills-core/README.md relatively; MyST exported it under build/README-<hash>.md, colliding with the root README's own curated basename, and check-public-artifact correctly rejected it as non-curated. Fix: switched the link to the absolute GitLab blob URL (matches louiselm-o7v6's fix pattern), removing it from MyST's crawl. Verified: rebuilt the MyST site locally after the fix — only one build/README-<hash>.md export remains and it byte-matches root README.md; ./scripts/check-public-artifact no longer reports the curated-source rejection (only the pre-existing, unrelated, CI-only demo/ route failure remains, caused by build-demo.mjs needing a CI_JOB_TOKEN not available locally). Added a named regression fixture in scripts/test-public-artifact.sh reproducing the exact README-basename collision; npm run site:test passes. gate:npm-run-site-test

title: State the emission rule and needs-capability vocabulary in AGENTS.md
description:
## Goal
Add the emission obligation and the label vocabulary to AGENTS.md, so a session
that cannot finish its work, or that notices something outside it, records that
as data instead of prose.

## Scope
- In scope: one rule in AGENTS.md section 2 naming both triggers concretely
  ("you could not complete the work" / "you noticed something outside it"); the
  label-versus-blocker test in one line; the `needs-capability:*` namespaced
  vocabulary; an explicit carve-out on the existing `br scheduler` preference.
- In scope: applying the resulting label to louiselm-qbr.1.10 as the first real
  use, and replacing its prose comment's role (the comment stays as history).
- Out of scope: the louiselm agent `capabilities` config field (sibling task),
  any skill, documenting the other 90 undocumented labels, and fixing
  `br scheduler`.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. AGENTS.md names both emission triggers in concrete terms, not as "facts worth
   keeping" -- vagueness is what produced the original prose comment.
2. The label-versus-blocker test appears as one line: does something have to
   change before anyone can do this?
3. `needs-capability:*` is documented as the namespace for standing requirements.
4. The `br scheduler` preference in section 2 carries a carve-out stating that
   capability-aware selection must use `br ready --label-any`, referencing
   louiselm-scheduler-labels-xw1i, and stating the carve-out is removed when that
   bug closes.
5. louiselm-qbr.1.10 carries `needs-capability:image-generation`, and
   `br ready --label-any needs-capability:image-generation` returns it.
6. The rule is stated so an agent with no skills available can comply from
   AGENTS.md alone.

## Testing
Documentation change; no automated test applies. Verify by running
`br ready --label-any needs-capability:image-generation` and confirming
louiselm-qbr.1.10 is selected, and that a plain `br ready` still lists it (a
label is not a blocker).

## Notes
Reasoning and rejected alternatives are on the parent, louiselm-capability-routing-m3sc.
Keep the addition short. Section 2 is already dense, and a rule nobody finishes
reading is the failure mode being fixed.
close_reason: Added emission rule, label-vs-blocker test, and needs-capability:* vocabulary to AGENTS.md section 2, plus the br scheduler carve-out for capability-aware routing. qbr.1.10 already carries the label; see comment on AC5.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: AC5 verification note: louiselm-qbr.1.10 already carries needs-capability:image-generation (confirmed via 'br label list louiselm-qbr.1.10'), but a codex session closed it before this task ran, so 'br ready --label-any needs-capability:image-generation' now returns nothing -- br ready only surfaces open work, and the issue it would have surfaced is done. The label and the routing mechanism both work as designed; the specific verification command in the AC is unsatisfiable post hoc because the target issue completed in the interim.

title: Preview bounded historical ACP usage imports
description:
## Goal
Produce a usable explicit dry-run report identifying historical turns and proposed attribution batches without writing usage facts.
## Scope
Timestamped ACP wire JSONL, paired connection/Session streams, explicit source/time bounds; native-only sources reported unsupported. No apply or live-store mutation.
## Acceptance
Parse actual configOptions, prompt dispatch/response and reported costs/usage in observed stream order. Correlate connection identity, Session binding and request IDs; repeated IDs across resumes never collide. Require full starting options and known ordering; missing completion/metrics stay absent. Preserve supported confirmed option changes without inferred source/causality. Human Agent/Provider proposals must be explicitly marked unconfirmed. Show exact Sessions/time/source selection, normalized candidate facts, counts, exclusions with bounded reasons, source evidence references and a stable selection digest for confirmation. Sensitive payloads are omitted. File/time/byte limits make work bounded; missing/changed/unreadable/unsupported sources are visible. Public async entrypoint and runnable explicit command/report consumer.
## Testing
Sanitized captured fixture from proxy Session 62b4d897-b815-47ec-865a-764225cf98c5 on 2026-08-31 (paths in 4lh8); test initial options, changes, mixed turns, missing completion/telemetry, malformed ordering, reused request IDs, currency clearing/reset, absent source and privacy. Lua gates.
## Notes
Confirmed parent contract louiselm-b1uo and design louiselm-4lh8. Read recording.lua, validation.lua, docs/turn-recording.md; reuse existing validators where strict enough. Native source parsers are outside v1.

title: Assistant fails to recognize available OpenCode session ID
description:
## Problem

The assistant sometimes claims that no attributable OpenCode session ID is available and refuses to perform a Beads mutation, even when the session ID is present in the interaction context.

## Observed

On 2026-08-30, while processing the shared ChatGPT URL https://chatgpt.com/share/6a943166-c51c-83eb-ba80-9d8a79830de8, the assistant repeatedly said it could not file a Beads issue because no actor/session ID was exposed. The maintainer then supplied the valid actor: opencode/ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney.

The assistant had also discovered related OpenCode session identifiers in tool results and existing Beads records, but did not reliably distinguish the current session identifier from missing environment variables.

## Impact

The assistant unnecessarily blocks requested issue filing and asks the maintainer for information that may already be available, adding friction and risking untracked work.

## Expected behavior

Before declaring the actor unavailable, inspect the complete interaction/tool context for the current OpenCode session ID. If a valid opencode/<session-id> is available and points to an open transcript, use it as the Beads --actor value. Only ask the maintainer when no current attributable ID can be established.

## Acceptance

- A reproducible test or documented harness check demonstrates that the current OpenCode session ID is discovered when present outside the environment-variable list.
- The assistant does not substitute a stale session ID from another Beads record or a child-agent task ID.
- When no current ID exists, the assistant still asks rather than inventing one.

## Related

- louiselm-adapter-session-id-exposure-fq4k tracks the upstream adapter problem where session IDs are absent from shell environment variables. This bug concerns assistant-side failure to recognize an ID that is available in context.
close_reason: Document live OpenCode actor lookup and cover it

comments.author: codex/01a053d7-4308-76c0-9eac-a9e424812c48
comments.text: Completion evidence: AGENTS.md:291 now requires using the live Chat:session_id() result verbatim, including opencode/<ACP-session-id>, and rejecting stale Beads/child-task IDs. tests/ui/command_spec.lua covers an OpenCode Session ID with no environment variable. Existing :LouiselmSessionId and Chat:session_id() already provide the value; no runtime code change was needed. Lesson: adapter environment variables are not the authority when live Session state is available; related adapter exposure gaps remain in louiselm-adapter-session-id-exposure-fq4k.

title: Site CI rejects README-linked turn recording documentation
description:
GitLab site-build fails after rendering the public site.

## Observed
Job https://gitlab.bartab.fr/oss-public/louiselm/-/jobs/144625, pipeline 39091, commit 5751ddbf4dcb0c9039ff8338ac8d4f0fa3c248da:
2026-09-07T14:54:08.518890Z public artifact rejected: forbidden source or state file: build/turn-recording-840b754e466242c5f0cfea9d9c3ae604.md

## Root cause
README.md:45 links docs/turn-recording.md. MyST copies the linked Markdown into its artifact, but myst.yml omits the page from its TOC and scripts/check-public-artifact:14 and :85 omit it from the curated source/basename allowlists. The publication gate correctly rejects an uncurated source.

## Why it was not caught
scripts/test-public-artifact.sh covers tutorial exports but not the newly linked recording guide.

## Fix direction
Review the guide as public documentation, add it to the explicit TOC and curated export allowlist; preserve byte-identity enforcement and private-source rejection.

## Acceptance
Regression accepts the exact curated recording export and rejects modified bytes; fails before the fix. npm run site:test and npm run site:build pass, producing docs/turn-recording/index.html.

## Not covered
No deployment or GitLab PR; unrelated skills-core work is untouched.
close_reason: Curated recording guide; regression red→green and full site build pass. gate:scripts/test-public-artifact.sh
