title: Site favicon is the MyST theme default, not LouiseLM
description:
The published site serves the book-theme's stock MyST/Jupyter favicon, so every
browser tab, bookmark and history entry for louiselm.com carries someone else's
mark instead of the LouiseLM logo that the header already shows.

## Observed

Maintainer screenshot 2026-09-07 (~/Pictures/scrot/20260907_1933_1920x1200_1788802395.png):
louiselm.com loaded in Chrome, header logo is the LouiseLM mark, tab icon is not.

In the current build tree:

- `_build/html/index.html` emits `<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico"/>`.
- `_build/html/favicon.ico` (41662 bytes, md5 672666b145a7dc27a4cadf957b18d2ac)
  is the theme default, not a project asset; nothing under `assets/` matches it.
  The theme ships that route as
  `_build/templates/site/<hash>/public/build/routes/[favicon.ico]-MH4XVVZI.js`
  alongside `_assets/jupyter-favicon-*.svg`.
- `myst.yml` `site.options` sets `logo`, `logo_alt`, `folders` and `style`, and
  no `favicon`.

## Symptoms

- Browser tab, bookmark and history icon for louiselm.com is the MyST mark.
- Site build succeeds and reports nothing: the default is a silent fallback,
  not an error.

## Root cause

`myst.yml` never sets `site.options.favicon`. The pinned book-theme
(`template.yml` in the downloaded template, option id `favicon`, type `file`)
falls back to its bundled icon when the option is absent. `assets/` holds
`louiselm-logo.png`, `louiselm-hero.webp` and `louiselm-chat-demo.webp` — no
favicon asset exists to point at yet.

## Why it was not caught

`scripts/check-public-artifact` audits the published tree for origin leakage and
TOC residue; it asserts nothing about branding assets. `myst build --strict`
treats an unset theme option as valid. Nothing compares a served asset against
a project-owned file, which is exactly the shape of this defect: correct build,
wrong bytes.

## Fix direction

Add a site-owned favicon asset and reference it from `myst.yml`
`site.options.favicon`, the same way louiselm-fb2t made the header logo
site-owned. Prefer a square source derived from the existing launcher mark over
a new drawing. Rejected: overriding `_build/html/favicon.ico` in
`scripts/build-site` after the fact — that hides the config gap and breaks on
the next theme bump.

## Acceptance

- `myst.yml` sets `site.options.favicon` to a committed asset under `assets/`.
- After `scripts/build-site`, `_build/html/favicon.ico` (or the emitted
  `rel="icon"` target) is byte-identical to that asset's rendered output and no
  longer matches md5 672666b145a7dc27a4cadf957b18d2ac.
- A gate in `scripts/check-public-artifact` fails if the served icon is the
  theme default again.

## Not covered

- Apple touch icon, PWA manifest icons and the demo subsite's own icons are not
  checked here.
- Whether the 48px header PNG is an acceptable favicon source at 16px is
  untested; it may need a dedicated square crop.
close_reason: myst.yml:58 sets site.options.favicon to assets/louiselm-favicon.ico, a 48/32/16 ico cut from the launcher mark. Built /favicon.ico is now byte-identical to the asset (md5 104e4c82…), no longer MyST's 672666b1…. gate:scripts/check-public-artifact rejects a favicon that is not that asset; scripts/test-public-artifact.sh covers wrong-bytes and missing cases. Reaches louiselm.com only on the next build and deploy.

comments.author: claude/31dfad97-cb83-4198-972f-1b98857d40b4
comments.text: The theme's favicon fallback is a network fetch, not a bundled file: the route loader does fetch(options.favicon || "https://mystmd.org/favicon.ico"). Two consequences - the stock icon was MyST's own, served from their domain at build time, and a build with no favicon configured and no network yields a 404 route rather than any icon. With site.options.favicon set, the route serves our bytes verbatim and the static export writes them to /favicon.ico unchanged.

title: CI: nvim-nightly-only Vimdoc-staleness check fails while stable passes on the same commit
description:
The advisory "mini.test (nvim nightly)" CI job's "Verify generated Vimdoc" step fails, but `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` passes cleanly when run locally against nvim stable on the same commit — suggesting the check's result differs between nvim stable and nvim nightly rather than the doc actually being stale.

## Observed

GitHub Actions runs 32929697287 (commit 849f5dc) and 32932395090 (commit fd1d606), repo euri10/louiselm, job "mini.test (nvim nightly)", step "Verify generated Vimdoc":

```
louiselm Vimdoc is stale; run ./scripts/generate-vimdoc
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

This step runs identically in the "mini.test (nvim stable)" job (per `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, both `stable` and `nightly` are the same matrix job differing only in `neovim: ${{ matrix.neovim }}`), and it passes there — only the nightly leg fails.

Reproduced (partially) locally: `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` exits 0 with nvim stable installed locally, on the same commit (fd1d606) where the nightly CI leg reports it stale. Nightly was not installed locally to cross-check directly.

## Symptoms

- The nightly matrix leg of "mini.test" reports failure on "Verify generated Vimdoc", though this job has `continue-on-error: true` for `matrix.neovim == 'nightly'` (per `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), so it does not fail the overall required checks — it only shows as a red/crossed-out leg in the Actions UI.

## Root cause

Unknown — not yet isolated. Hypotheses:

1. `./scripts/generate-vimdoc` (or the `:helptags`/doc-generation machinery it drives) produces byte-for-byte different output between nvim stable and nvim nightly (e.g. a changed `:h` formatting default, a Lua stdlib behavior change nightly introduced), so the committed `doc/*.txt` matches stable's output but not nightly's.
2. The nightly Neovim build used by `rhysd/action-setup-vim@v1` in that run had a transient/unrelated regression unconnected to the actual doc content.

What would discriminate: install nvim nightly locally (or in a disposable container) and run `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` directly against it, then compare its regenerated output to the committed doc file to see the actual diff.

## Why it was not caught

The documented local gates (AGENTS.md section 4) run against local/stable Neovim only; there is no local nightly Neovim in the loop, so a stable-vs-nightly divergence in generated-doc output is invisible until CI's nightly leg runs. Because that leg is advisory (`continue-on-error`), a failure there produces no blocking signal and is easy to miss entirely — this was only noticed because of an unrelated report about the required jobs failing on the same run.

## Fix direction

Not yet chosen — depends on which hypothesis above holds. If it's genuine stable/nightly output drift in the doc generator, the fix likely lives in `./scripts/generate-vimdoc` (make its output version-independent, or gate the `--check` comparison on stable only). If it's a nightly build flake, no code fix is needed, just noting it as expected nightly noise.

## Acceptance

- Root cause identified with a reproduced diff (or confirmed flake) rather than a hypothesis.
- `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` passes on nvim nightly in CI, or the check is explicitly scoped to stable only with a documented reason.

## Not covered

- The `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua` CI failure and the stale-`doc/api.md` failure on the same CI runs are separate bugs with distinct root causes (both on the *required* stable/lua-language-server jobs); filed separately. This bug is lower priority since the affected job is advisory and does not block merges.
close_reason: fixed in 8e4a427. nvim_get_commands() changed the user-command description field from definition on stable to desc on nightly; documented_commands() now prefers non-empty desc and falls back to definition. Added regression coverage for both shapes. Exact CI stable 0.12.5 and nightly 0.13.0-dev-1418+gf97bcbdf77 pass the Vimdoc check and all 546 tests with VIM/VIMRUNTIME unset.

title: Kimi as a configured Agent
description:
## Problem Statement

Kimi is not yet available as a LouiseLM Agent: docs/onboarding.md carries verified profiles only for Codex, Claude, and DeepSeek, and the maintainer dotfiles Agent map has no kimi entry. Moonshot ships a native ACP server in the Kimi Code CLI (`kimi acp`), so no bridge or plugin code is needed — the gap is a documented recipe, a configured Agent entry, and live verification of the capability claims, which so far come only from a conversation held with Kimi outside the project (https://www.kimi.ai/share/1a065c95-8942-8679-8000-00001c004e2d) and Moonshot docs (https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/reference/kimi-acp.html).

That outside conversation ended with a proposed config shape (`providers.kimi = { command = "kimi", args = { "acp" }, env = {} }` plus an OpenAI fallback) that does not match LouiseLM: Agents are entries of the `agents` map in setup() (lua/louiselm/config.lua schema), not a `providers` table.

## Solution

Kimi becomes a configured, documented, live-verified Agent: an onboarding profile in docs/onboarding.md following the existing Claude/DeepSeek pattern, and a `kimi` entry in the maintainer dotfiles following the acp-proxy pattern used for grok/opencode. No plugin code changes — agent configuration is an established extension boundary (AGENTS.md section 1).

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want a Kimi profile in onboarding.md, so I can install, log in, and configure the Agent from one recipe.
2. As the maintainer, I want a `kimi` entry routed through acp-proxy in my dotfiles, so Sessions get wire logs like every other Agent.
3. As a user, I want a not-logged-in Kimi to surface its auth error loudly, so the fix (terminal login first) is obvious.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given an installed, logged-in `kimi`, a fresh Kimi Session completes a prompt turn and returns to ready.
2. The options picker lists and applies Kimi standard `configOptions[]` (Kimi advertises standard options plus modes on session/new, unlike Grok vendor metadata louiselm-yyvx).
3. Given `loadSession: true`, session/load replays history (cold-Park resume works).
4. Given no login, Session creation fails with a specific actionable error; the recipe states the terminal-login prerequisite (LouiseLM advertises no ACP terminal-auth client capability, same stance as the Claude profile).
5. docs/onboarding.md gains a Kimi recipe with its verification date.
6. The maintainer confirms the live acceptance; the feature stays open until then (AGENTS.md Live acceptance).

## Implementation Notes

- Agent entry: `command = "kimi", args = { "acp" }`, env empty — the CLI reuses its login state. Sources for the shape: Kimi IDE guide (Zed/JetBrains configs) and the share conversation.
- Login prerequisite: run `kimi` once and `/login`, or `kimi login`; ACP returns AUTH_REQUIRED (-32000) while unauthenticated.
- Advertised matrix (docs; verify against the live initialize frame before trusting any entry): loadSession true; promptCapabilities image true, audio false, embeddedContext true; sessionCapabilities list/resume/close/delete/fork/additionalDirectories; mcpCapabilities http+sse; auth.logout {}. Terminal methods not implemented. fs/read_text_file and fs/write_text_file are client-routed only when the client advertises fsCapabilities — LouiseLM advertises fs.readTextFile=false/writeTextFile=false (lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua), so Kimi should execute locally; confirm live.
- Per AGENTS.md section 5: the live initialize/session-new frames captured through the proxy log are the authority over any doc matrix; cite log path and Session ID for any fixture derived from them.
- Decide the skills policy entry (native vs inject) from observed behavior; maintainer config uses inject for codex/deepseek/glm and native for opencode.
- Issue reporting channels for defects found in Kimi: MoonshotAI/kimi-code GitHub Issues, code@moonshot.ai, in-CLI /feedback.

## Testing Notes

- Documentation plus configuration: no red test applies; the checkable outcome is the maintainer live acceptance.
- If any regression fixture is derived from the live Session, encode the observed event order and cite the proxy log path and Session ID.

## Out of Scope

- A `kimi` transcript_layout for Provenance over historical Kimi transcripts; live Sessions need no layout. File separately if wanted.
- A Kimi backend for acp-llm-adapter (the OpenAI-compatible fallback path discussed in the share conversation).
- ACP terminal-auth client capability in LouiseLM.

title: Cgroup delegation detection accepts read-only hierarchies
description:
`Cgroup::delegated_parent()` treats any existing `cgroup.procs` as delegated, although cgroup v2 delegation requires write access to the cgroup directory and membership file.

Observed while adding the privileged HostIdentity CI gate: on an ordinary GitHub runner, `/proc/self/cgroup` can resolve to a real cgroup whose files are readable but whose subtree is not delegated to the runner. `skills-core/src/sandbox.rs:189-198` returns it anyway, so every Bubblewrap spawn attempts `Cgroup::create` and fails before the backend runs.

Acceptance: return a parent only when the current process can create children and write membership there; ordinary no-delegation runs omit cgroup lifecycle evidence instead of failing unrelated sandbox launches; delegated and initial-root paths remain covered.
close_reason: Delegation now requires effective write authority; inert:louiselm-d6fv.4.4

comments.text: Lessons: delegation discovery now requires effective W+X access to the current cgroup and W access to cgroup.procs; file existence alone is not authority (skills-core/src/sandbox.rs). The read-only regression fails under the old predicate and passes under the access check. No standing rule warranted.

title: Show attached Session attention in the chat winbar
description:
## Problem Statement

When several Sessions are attached, the user can see only the current Session status without opening the Session picker. Permission requests, completed background responses, and failures can therefore wait unnoticed.

## Solution

Show a right-aligned, clickable strip for attached background Sessions in every LouiseLM Session winbar. Keep all Sessions visible when space permits, make attention states visually prominent, and preserve the existing picker as keyboard and overflow navigation.

The strip is always enabled when at least two Sessions are attached and absent with one. Entries use the renamed Session title when present, otherwise the Agent name. ACP Session IDs are not shown.

A completed response becomes attention-worthy only when its turn_done event occurred while the Session was not focused. Focusing that Session acknowledges the response. Permission and error attention persist until resolved or disposed.

## User Stories

1. As a user working in one Session, I want to see all other attached Sessions so I know their state without opening a picker.
2. As a user, I want permission requests, unseen completed responses, and errors to stand out so I notice required action.
3. As a user, I want to click a Session entry to switch directly to it.
4. As a user in a narrow window, I want attention-needed Sessions protected from overflow.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given one attached Session, its winbar remains the existing single-Session presentation with no background strip.
2. Given two or more attached Sessions, every Session is represented by the current Session segment or a clickable background entry when width permits.
3. Clicking a background entry switches the window to that Session; keyboard users can continue to use :LouiselmSwitchSession.
4. A renamed Session uses its name; otherwise its Agent name is shown; ACP Session IDs are omitted.
5. Ready and seen Sessions use a green dot, active Sessions use a blue ellipsis, unseen completed responses use a yellow dot, permission requests use a yellow exclamation, and errors use a red cross.
6. A background turn_done marks that Session unseen; focusing it clears only that completed-turn attention.
7. Permission attention remains until answered and error attention remains until resolved or disposed.
8. Under width pressure, labelled attention entries remain visible, quiet entries collapse into a neutral clickable +N entry, and +N opens the Session picker.
9. Repeated setup, Session changes, window changes, and disposal do not leak handlers or mutate unrelated winbars.

## Implementation Notes

- Reuse the existing Session event stream, status highlights, winbar renderer, Session picker, and rename state.
- Track unread completion state in the Chat UI owner, not the core Session lifecycle: attention is presentation-specific and depends on window focus.
- Use stable Neovim APIs and marshal editor operations through existing scheduling boundaries.
- Add no configuration option, dependency, compatibility shim, or speculative extension point.

## Testing Notes

- Extend behavioral headless chat tests.
- Cover background turn completion versus initial ready state, focus acknowledgement, persistent permission/error attention, direct click routing, overflow priority, disposal, and scheduled UI rendering.
- Preserve existing single-Session winbar behavior.

## Out of Scope

- Global tabline or statusline integration.
- ACP protocol changes.
- Desktop notifications, animation, sound, or user-configurable visual themes.
- Replacing the existing Session picker.
close_reason: Implemented and verified clickable multi-Session attention winbar

Verified focused chat and command suites; full 470-case mini.test suite; stylua --check .; lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning; git diff --check.

title: Resume picker hides last-updated time at line end
description:
In the session picker opened by `:LouiselmResume`, the last-updated timestamp is placed after the session title and cwd, so long titles consume the available width and hide the timestamp. Users cannot quickly tell which resumable Session is newest without moving to the far end of the picker line, which is especially painful in a narrow picker.

## Observed

Screenshot evidence captured 2026-08-24 at 09:31 local time after running `:LouiselmResume`:

`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_0931_1920x1200_1787556713.png`

The selected row visibly contains:

`is your next best task · cwd=/home/lotso/code/louiselm · updated=2026-08-24T06:54:07.000Z`

and the `updated=` portion is at the far right, beyond the useful visible width for long rows. The lower row shows the same layout with `updated=2026-08-23T19:09:52.000Z` after the title and cwd.

Source path inspected: `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:378-389`, where `discovered_session_summary()` appends the cwd and then the updated timestamp after the title.

## Symptoms

- The resume picker shows session identity/title first, then cwd, then `updated=`.
- Long titles push the recency information out of view.
- The user must navigate to the end of each picker line to compare when Sessions were last updated.

## Root cause

Confirmed in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:378-389`: `discovered_session_summary()` builds the display parts in the order agent/session id, title, cwd, updated timestamp. The timestamp is therefore the least likely field to remain visible when the picker width is scarce.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:1980` asserts a full summary string but does not exercise display behavior with a constrained picker width or a long title that obscures the trailing metadata.

## Fix direction

Change the summary ordering at `discovered_session_summary()` so the last-updated information appears before the long title/cwd fields, while preserving enough session identity to distinguish rows. Keep the result compact; do not solve this by requiring horizontal navigation to inspect recency.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after, asserting that `updated=` precedes the title and cwd in the discovered-session summary.
- In a picker with scarce width and a long session title, the last-updated value is visible near the beginning of the row without navigating to the line end.
- Session identity remains visible and existing resume selection behavior is unchanged.

## Not covered

The exact compact timestamp format and final ordering of title versus cwd are implementation choices. This report does not require changing picker width, truncation behavior, or the underlying persisted timestamp.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree. Reordered discovered_session_summary() in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua so updated= appears immediately after the session identity, before title and cwd, keeping recency visible in scarce picker width. Regression updated in tests/ui/chat_spec.lua and failed before the implementation change. Focused chat suite: 105/105. Full MiniTest suite: 469/469. Gates: stylua --check . and lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning pass. Existing test-environment warnings about a missing temporary grill-me skill and clipboard/write output remain unrelated.

title: Grill-me needed: Forensics indexes evidence in place, but ACP logs are not durable
description:
Do not resolve this in passing — it needs a full grill-me session, not a quick take folded into
other work.

## The question

Forensics is defined (louiselm-cvv3) as a durable, immutable record that "indexes primary
evidence in place; it does not copy, normalize, interpret, or make that evidence safe to
share." The louiselm-proxy-log-evidence-expiry-xxfu episode showed that the primary evidence
for ACP defects is evictable, so an index into it is not durable regardless of how durable the
index itself is.

Does Forensics need to copy the frames it depends on, or does its definition overstate what a
durable record guarantees?

## Context / evidence that raised this

2026-09-01, session claude/b2f2f248-deef-4d75-95cd-07972ebc9c26. ACP proxy logs were being
evicted by a 100MB aggregate size cap in acp-llm-adapter's logsink. Of 95 Sessions that
provably did work, 8 still had a log. louiselm-gf9a cited
`sessions/ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney/log.jsonl` lines 1527-1623 in its description; by the
time the maintainer retested, the file was gone and the recorded ordering could not be checked
against the wire.

The immediate cause is fixed: retention can now be disabled and is
(acp-llm-adapter 8ec536c). That removes the pressure but not the structural point. Eviction was
only one way to lose the referent. A log can also be lost to a wiped state directory, a
different machine, a container, or a Session that predates a proxy reinstall.

Note this is the same class of failure as the Close verdict work (louiselm-yx1g): a record that
names something it does not control, and cannot tell you when that thing stops being true. A
Forensics record indexing a deleted file reports success and points at nothing.

## Threads worth pulling

- Is "index in place" load-bearing for a stated safety property, or was it a simplicity
  choice? The vocabulary record's design note says Forensics derives its safety from being
  scoped to exactly one subject Session, which does not obviously require indexing over
  copying.
- If Forensics copies, what does it copy? Whole logs are large (two Sessions held 66MB of the
  old 100MB budget) and unredacted ones carry prompts, tool arguments, and file contents.
  Copying everything reintroduces the size problem inside the repository, where it is worse.
- Is the narrower answer at file time rather than record time — a bug citing a proxy log inlines
  the specific frames it relies on, since those are small and are what the argument actually
  rests on? That needs no Forensics change at all.
- Should a Forensics record verify its referents on read and report absence, rather than
  silently pointing at nothing? "No evidence available" is a legitimate answer; a dead path
  presented as evidence is not.
- Does the same critique apply to Provenance (louiselm-tsxh), which is derived on demand from
  git trailers and Beads actors and stores nothing? Git history is durable in a way proxy logs
  are not, so possibly not — worth stating explicitly either way.
close_reason: none: design resolved; availability and export routed

comments.author: claude/b2f2f248-deef-4d75-95cd-07972ebc9c26
comments.text:
Material input for this grill, 2026-09-01: the Agents' own stores are a second, independent copy of most of what a proxy log holds, and they survived the eviction entirely. ~/.claude/projects (224 transcripts back to 2026-08-03), ~/.codex/sessions rollouts (1.8GB), ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db (session/message/part tables), and ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*-stdout-jsonrpc.log (516 files back to 2026-06-17, outside proxy/ so never pruned).

That reframes the question. Forensics indexing evidence in place is not wrong so much as under-specified: it indexes ONE copy and treats it as the evidence. A record that indexed the Agent-side transcript as well would have survived this incident with its conversational content intact.

But the two copies are not equivalent and the difference is exactly what defects need. Agent stores hold the conversation; only the wire trace holds JSON-RPC ids, response outcomes, and frame ordering. louiselm-gf9a needed the ordering and no Agent store could supply it. So 'copy vs index' is the wrong axis -- the real question is which properties of the evidence a Forensics record claims to preserve, and whether it can say 'content available, wire ordering lost' rather than pointing at a path and being silent about what is behind it.

comments.author: codex/01a05d39-f54f-7052-96f9-f69339f2a1dc
comments.text: Resolved: Forensics stays an index with current availability inspection; Evidence export is explicit and redacted. Routed to vocabulary louiselm-cvv3/louiselm-euxk and feature louiselm-ucl1 with tasks .1/.2.

title: Enter does nothing with a visible draft in a ready resumed chat
description:
A resumed louiselm chat can display an intact non-empty draft under a ready session while buffer-local Enter produces no ACP prompt and no visible error. The affected user cannot continue that session through the primary chat path, although the agent process remains healthy and the draft is recoverable.

## Observed

Seen 2026-08-21 in live Codex ACP session `01a01fd3-bcf8-74d2-bf0c-edc7b9329101`, Neovim 0.12.2, louiselm buffer on `/run/user/1000/nvim.1020915.0`.

Read-only live probes returned: `name=louiselm://session-1`, `mode=i`, `modifiable=1`, `line=598`, `line_count=598`, `last_len=181`, `last_prefix=> can you ch`, and insert `<CR>` mapping description `Submit louiselm prompt` with a buffer-local callback. `undotree()` reported `seq_cur=268`, `seq_last=268`; the user reported using normal-mode `U` and `Ctrl-r` before the failure.

The Codex rollout `/home/lotso/.codex/sessions/2026/08/20/rollout-2026-08-20T17-39-25-01a01fd3-bcf8-74d2-bf0c-edc7b9329101.jsonl` ends with `task_complete` at `2026-08-20T16:55:34.216Z` and contains no later user turn. The adapter log `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260820-173923-1021245-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log` contains no later `session/prompt`; the live `codex-acp` and Codex app-server processes remain running. `v:errmsg` is empty and `:messages` contains no louiselm submission error.

## Symptoms

- Header says `Your turn`; typing works, but pressing Enter appears to do nothing.
- Draft remains visible and no prompt reaches ACP/Codex.
- No error explains why submission was rejected or skipped.

## Root cause

Unknown. The failure is below Codex and after louiselm rendered the ready state, but it has not yet been discriminated between (a) the key callback not executing despite the installed mapping, and (b) `Chat:submit()` reading an empty or wrong range because `view.prompt_line` is plain Lua state while normal-mode undo/redo mutates only the buffer. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:722` reads from `view.prompt_line`; `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1637` installs the Enter callback; `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1910` silently returns for an empty prompt.

## Why it was not caught

Chat tests call `chat:submit()` directly and exercise buffer edits, but there is no behavioral test that drives the installed Enter mapping after real normal-mode undo/redo in an attached/resumed transcript. Empty-prompt rejection is also silent at the keymapping boundary.

## Fix direction

First capture the failure in a headless UI test that feeds the actual mapping after transcript changes and undo/redo. At the narrowest boundary, make the prompt location track buffer edits (for example, an extmark owned by the view) or explicitly prevent transcript undo from invalidating UI state. The Enter callback must surface any returned submission error instead of silently appearing dead. Do not patch Codex or restart the adapter as the evidence shows no request reaches it.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and proves Enter submits the visible draft after `U`/undo and redo on a ready attached or resumed chat.
- The prompt sent to the fake ACP session exactly matches the visible draft and prior transcript text is never included.
- If the draft cannot be resolved, Enter emits one actionable louiselm error rather than doing nothing.
- Existing queueing, multiline prompt, and resume tests remain green.

## Not covered

The exact key event has not been injected into the live user session because that would submit their draft. A clean synthetic 1:1 undo/redo probe did not reproduce the defect, so the live undo branch and callback-vs-boundary hypotheses remain unverified. No code fix is included in this diagnostic.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree. Root cause: the prompt boundary was a Lua row number, so undoing streamed transcript lines left submission reading past the visible draft; a left-gravity extmark now tracks the boundary and the real Enter mapping test passes after :undo. Tests: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 75/75; full mini.test 315/315. Formatting: changed files pass. Project-wide StyLua/LuaLS remain blocked only by pre-existing blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua issues.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Recovery follow-up, 2026-08-21: `:LouiselmResume` (without bang) correctly discovered the same-workspace session. `:LouiselmResume!` means all workspaces and was unnecessary here. The load then failed independently because the original live Neovim/ACP chain still owns the Codex thread. Exact JSON-RPC error in `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260821-040016-1245805-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log:2`: `{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"details":"thread 01a01fd3-bcf8-74d2-bf0c-edc7b9329101 already has an active writer"}}`. Original writer processes remain live under Neovim PIDs 1020909/1020915 and codex-acp PID 1021253. Safe recovery requires exiting the original stuck Neovim to release the writer before loading from the fresh instance; do not kill or restart Codex while preserving the draft.

title: Codex edit permissions are answered with a -32602 protocol error
description:
codex-acp sends edit permission requests with no reviewable payload at all:

  {"toolCall":{"toolCallId":"call_SObIFxWtTS90EE6K7JbBTfgX","kind":"edit","status":"pending"},"options":[...]}

(from ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260717-163626-2991539-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log)

No rawInput, no content, no path. lua/louiselm/permission/gates.lua from_acp therefore returns {kind = "file_edit", path = nil}, gates.check rejects it with "permission file edit must have a non-empty path", and lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua handle_request answers the agent with JSON-RPC error -32602 instead of asking the user anything. The user never sees a prompt and codex sees a protocol error.

Separate from the claude case: there is nothing to review here, so the fix is not a better diff. A file-edit request that carries no path or reviewable text should fall back to the generic permission picker (allow/reject options are present in the payload) rather than being answered with a protocol error.

Found while fixing the claude payload bug; not verified live with codex, only from the logged payload and reading the code.
close_reason: Completed: pathless edit requests now reach the generic permission decision flow; regression and full suite pass

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Reproduced with the logged Codex shape: edit toolCall with no rawInput/path caused no permission_requested event and an immediate -32602. Regression test now proves it is normalized to {kind=unknown}, enters waiting_permission, and returns the selected advertised option. Focused session/permission tests pass; isolated full suite passes 312/312.

title: Activated daemon restart loses queryable Session under CPU throttling
description:
The activated-daemon lifecycle fixture failed to regain a queryable Session after broker restart in a CPU-limited disposable VM. Observed once on unchanged 0d13d84 at CPUQuota45%; the same binary passed at CPUQuota200%. This is distinct from w841i's final 240-second upgrade/adoption timeout. Production impact and repeatability are unknown.

## Observed

2026-09-17, Rust1.97.1, Debian13 disposable launcher VM, host-built current binaries with CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only. Evidence: /var/tmp/louiselm-w841i-recurrence.rZHuWo/baseline-daemon-measured.log; harness /var/tmp/louiselm-w841i-recurrence.rZHuWo/run-daemon.sh. Guest artifacts retained for this VM lifetime under /tmp/louiselm-w841i-recurrence.X7Fr5i; original executable debug/deps/louiselm_skills-30d700aec22bdf5f. Run via scripts/launcher-vm only. title: Grill-me needed: should manual QA rounds use a native louiselm://qa-review workspace
description:
Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this question in passing.

Should manual QA rounds use a native `louiselm://qa-review` workspace instead of making a long `QA_REVIEW.md` file the tester's primary interface?

## Context and evidence

During the 2026-08-24 manual QA round, Case 5 required different setup from earlier cases. A shared Setup section forced the tester to navigate backward and reconstruct which commands applied. The screenshot at `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_0708_1920x1200_1787548138.png` shows the practical cost: separate panes for the QA recipe, LouiseLM Session under test, setup terminal, and conversation/evidence, with the current case detached from the setup it needs.

The immediate process improvement is clear: every case should be self-contained and repeat its exact launch, reset, action, and evidence-capture steps. A small global constants section may hold the build and scratch-state path, but completing a case should never require scrolling elsewhere to reconstruct its apparatus.

## Threads to pull

- Is the native buffer a transient controller/view while Beads remains the durable round and finding record?
- Which case-local actions belong in the buffer: launch recipe, pass, fail, blocked, retest, next, cleanup?
- How should keyboard navigation and commands work for a human tester without turning the interface into a second test framework?
- How should Agent Session IDs and Forensics pointers be captured without copying, rewriting, or exposing raw evidence?
- When and how should findings be created and parented to the QA round?
- What survives editor restart, and who owns cleanup of scratch state and test Sessions?
- Does `QA_REVIEW.md` remain as a generated/exportable view, or disappear?
- How does the same structure remain legible to an Agent performing analysis and a human intervening at the keyboard?

Process failures owned by coordinator: enormous cases concealed serial setup/credential/recovery/negative-path work; in-session repair/build/sign/install/retest loops consumed the human QA budget; recipe mistakes and ambiguous phone/key instructions added retries; frequent tiny acknowledgements/preflights and append-only CURRENT NEXT history increased reconstruction cost. Example docs/example-workflow.md:73 normalizes hours/several rebuilds. Those defaults need review, not merely fewer case labels.

- What is a small behavior case versus an entire hardware workflow? Which risk/novelty criteria select a bounded batch while retaining prior passes and accurately recording untested/deferred coverage?
- On finding F, when does QA stop/retry once/defer versus authorize an inline fix or a separate repair Session? Who owns shared fixtures and the single human/device, and when are fixes batched into one build/retest window?
- What compact current-state record survives compaction/restart without copying the evidence timeline? Must include exact build, pass/fail/unrun, current fixture/authority state, pending operation, owner, cleanup and ONE next step.
- Is a selected turn range sufficient for a repair takeover, or only an evidence pointer accompanying expected/actual, repro, build, constraints and acceptance? How do we exclude private keys, paper/PINs and ceremony proof while preserving relevant evidence?

No workflow/skill implementation, vocabulary promotion, agent delegation or destructive QA authorized by these proposals. Local run paused; isolated-copy reset approval is recorded separately on C14, not executed.

title: Beads inspector hard-codes louiselm prefix for other workspaces
description:
LouiseLM's Beads inspector cannot inspect issues from a different Beads workspace when the issue uses that workspace's prefix. In a Neovim terminal working in /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter, placing the cursor on daa-nk1l and pressing <leader>lB invokes br in that cwd but looks up louiselm-daa-nk1l, which does not exist.

## Observed

Seen in the maintainer's other Neovim terminal / Codex Session codex/01a03ed8-9e9f-77d0-b771-a8b18f97ba81 on 2026-08-26.

Verified workspace prefixes:
- /home/lotso/code/louiselm: br where --json => {"path":"/home/lotso/code/louiselm/.beads","prefix":"louiselm",...}
- /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter: br where --json => {"path":"/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/.beads","prefix":"daa",...}

Verified target:
- cd /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter && br show daa-nk1l --json succeeds and returns the issue "Migrate agent-client-protocol to 2.x".
- LouiseLM reports: "louiselm: could not read Beads issue louiselm-daa-nk1l".

## Symptoms

- Pressing <leader>lB on daa-nk1l in a chat buffer rooted in acp-llm-adapter fails.
- The command attempts the wrong ID, with louiselm- prepended to the adapter-local ID.
- The same inspector is currently coupled to the louiselm Beads prefix even though its br cwd is configurable/current-working-directory based.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:23 hard-codes the louiselm- prefix in valid_issue_id(). Line 34 only recognizes louiselm- IDs under the cursor. Lines 237-241 prepend louiselm- to bare prompted IDs and reject IDs without that prefix. The lookup at lines 173-176 correctly runs br with options.cwd or the current working directory, but the ID validation/normalization does not derive the prefix from that workspace.

## Why it was not caught

tests/ui/beads_spec.lua:78-268 use only louiselm-kpod, louiselm-zmab, and other louiselm-prefixed fixtures. There is no fixture for a workspace whose br where prefix differs from louiselm, and no assertion that the inspector derives the prefix from the same cwd used for br.

## Fix direction

Resolve the Beads prefix from the selected cwd using br where (or an equivalent br-supported machine-readable lookup), then use that prefix for cursor extraction, prompted-ID normalization, and validation. Keep the existing br show cwd identical to the prefix-discovery cwd. Do not infer a prefix from the issue text or silently fall back to louiselm- when the workspace reports another prefix.

## Acceptance

- A regression test with a br workspace prefix daa and issue daa-nk1l fails before the fix and passes after it.
- From a chat buffer using cwd /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter, <leader>lB on daa-nk1l invokes br show daa-nk1l --json and displays the issue.
- Manual entry of a bare issue suffix uses the discovered workspace prefix.
- A LouiseLM workspace continues to inspect louiselm-prefixed issues.
- Missing or malformed br where output produces a specific actionable error without starting an incorrect br show lookup.

## Not covered

The live Neovim instance was not modified and the bug was not fixed in this report. Prefix discovery behavior for nested Beads workspaces, if br where resolves a different workspace than cwd, remains unverified.
close_reason: Fixed prefix-scoped Beads inspection in lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua: the inspector asynchronously runs br where --json in the lookup cwd, derives and validates the workspace prefix, then uses it for cursor parsing, prompts, and br show. Added daa cross-workspace cursor and manual-entry regressions; focused tests pass (11/11), full suite passes for the changed behavior, lua-language-server reports no diagnostics, and git diff --check passes. Full suite has one unrelated pre-existing failure in tests/docs/vimdoc_spec.lua because committed generated help is already out of sync with user-modified sources; stylua --check . likewise reports unrelated existing differences in lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua, both left untouched.

comments.author: codex/01a03ed8-9e9f-77d0-b771-a8b18f97ba81
comments.text: Lesson: Beads issue IDs are workspace-scoped; derive the prefix from br where in the exact lookup cwd before parsing cursor text or prompting. The regression models the production async ordering (where callback schedules show), which was the relevant test gap. No AGENTS.md rule or design question is warranted.

title: Selecting a Provenance Decision fails with duplicate buffer name
description:
Selecting a row in the Provenance Decision index opens a popup window but fails to populate the selected evidence view because Neovim rejects the buffer name as already in use.

## Observed

Manual QA on 2026-08-28 in resumed Session codex/01a0461a-382d-7fb0-b46e-0a552b0bb40b. The Decision index buffer appeared quickly. Pressing CR on a row was very slow, then another window appeared and LouiseLM reported:

louiselm: could not display Provenance: .../louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:290: Vim:E95: Buffer with this name already exists

The relevant code at lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:287-290 creates a new buffer and calls nvim_buf_set_name(buffer, name). No raw log artifact was available; the exact user-visible error and source location are preserved here.

## Symptoms

- Decision index loads.
- Selecting a Decision row opens another window after a delay.
- The selected Provenance view is not displayed.
- The user receives Vim:E95 about a duplicate buffer name.

## Root cause

Likely duplicate URI buffer ownership in open_provenance at lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:287-290. The function always creates a fresh buffer and assigns the requested URI without handling an existing buffer with that name. Confirm whether the existing buffer is the index, an already-open selected view, or a stale hidden buffer before fixing.

## Why it was not caught

Automated tests assert the first Decision index buffer and mocked navigation output, but do not exercise a real Neovim window sequence with an existing named Provenance buffer and the actual asynchronous Beads callback.

## Fix direction

Handle an existing Provenance URI at the shared open_provenance boundary while preserving read-only behavior and avoiding stale content. Add a headless behavioral regression that opens the Decision index, selects a row, and verifies the selected URI view is displayed.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.
- Selecting a Decision row displays its Provenance content without Vim:E95.
- Reopening an already-open Provenance view does not create duplicate named buffers or stale windows.

## Not covered

- The perceived slowness is not independently attributed yet; isolate it after the duplicate-buffer failure is fixed.
close_reason: Fixed in d6851c6 by reusing existing named Provenance buffers and windows at open_provenance; added regression coverage. Focused Provenance suite 14/14 and full MiniTest suite 703/703 pass; stylua and lua-language-server pass. Manual QA screenshot /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260828_0551_1920x1200_1787889089.png confirms the selected Decision evidence popup renders without Vim:E95. The separate approximately 11-second latency remains open as louiselm-dkga.

comments.author: 01a0465c-762f-73f3-90ff-b096b27607fc
comments.text: Lesson: Provenance URI buffers are reusable view identities. The shared open_provenance boundary must look up an existing named buffer, make it writable while refreshing content, then restore read-only state and reuse an existing window when present. The regression must keep a valid URI buffer alive; a test that lets the popup be wiped does not reproduce E95. No AGENTS.md rule or design question is warranted.

title: Malformed ACP file-edit permission request terminates session
description:
## Reproduction

In session codex/019ff53a-629d-71a3-a1de-1a2506b42912, the agent sent an ACP session/request_permission file-edit request without a non-empty path. louiselm reported:

`Error: invalid ACP permission request: permission file edit must have a non-empty path`

The invalid request currently calls the session fatal-error path, closes the ACP client, and prevents the grilling session from continuing.

## Expected

Reject only the malformed permission request with a JSON-RPC invalid-params error. Keep the ACP session alive so the agent can continue or retry with a valid request.

## Acceptance criteria

- A file-edit permission request with a missing or empty path receives an error response with code -32602 and the validation message.
- The session remains ready/waiting for subsequent work and does not emit a fatal session error.
- Existing valid permission requests and malformed fatal startup/update handling remain unchanged.
- Add deterministic regression coverage.
close_reason: Changed malformed ACP permission requests to receive JSON-RPC -32602 errors without terminating the session; added regression coverage. Verification: focused api_spec 17/17, full MiniTest 132/132, stylua --check ., lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning.

title: Android CI lint fails when a newer Gradle release appears
description:
Observed: GitHub Actions CI run 36146971765, job 108110445707, 2026-09-25. :app:lintDebug fails: android/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties:4: Error: A newer version of Gradle than 9.7.1 is available: 9.8.0 [AndroidGradlePluginVersion]. Tests and APK assembly had passed before lint failed. Same finding occurred in runs 36103837046 and 36096300065.

Root cause: android/app/build.gradle.kts:45 sets warningsAsErrors=true, promoting the moving latest-version advisory to a CI failure even though the Gradle wrapper is intentionally pinned at 9.7.1. The previous successful run 36008899704 predates the 9.8.0 release.

Acceptance: exclude only AndroidGradlePluginVersion with an explanation tied to intentional toolchain pinning; keep abortOnError and warningsAsErrors; ./gradlew test lint assembleDebug passes and an unrelated lint warning remains fatal. No Gradle upgrade or broad lint baseline. Hosted Android CI success remains unverified until a new Actions run.

title: Turn-recording lock error replaces a successful turn result
description:
A submitted prompt intermittently completes with a turn-recording storage error instead of the result the Agent actually returned. Seen once in CI; not reproducible locally on either Neovim version. Split out of louiselm-dhqgv, which turned out to be a different, deterministic defect.

## Observed

2026-09-17, claude/36dc56d6-d466-4f8e-952a-113b9cd6a053, GitHub Actions run 35197802093, job 105125115578 (`mini.test (nvim nightly)`, commit ef178ba), case `tests/session/api_spec.lua | new | does not mistake terminal warnings or unsupported failure extensions for turn failure` at tests/session/api_spec.lua:2434:

```
Failed expectation for equality
Cause: different values at key "error", left = "turn recording database is locked; retry after the writer finishes", right = nil
Left:  { error = "turn recording database is locked; retry after the writer finishes" }
Right: { result = { _meta = { jetbrains = { air = { sessionFailure = { id = "warning", revision = 1, severity = "warning", title = "Recovered" }, version = 1 } } }, stopReason = "end_turn" } }
```

Frequency: 1 of 3 nightly CI runs on 2026-09-17 (failed in 35197802093; passed in 35197451660 and 35198885130, which failed only the unrelated hover case). Not observed on any stable run.

Not reproducible locally: `MiniTest.run_file('tests/session/api_spec.lua')` reports `Fails (0) and Notes (0)` on both `NVIM v0.12.5` and `NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1651+gcb76690546`, the exact nightly build CI used.

## Symptoms

- The caller's completion callback receives an `error` naming the turn-recording database instead of the Agent's `result`.
- A storage-layer condition is reported to the user as if the turn itself had failed.

## Root cause

Unknown. The lock message is reached while another writer holds the turn-recording database, but what holds it, and why the caller sees it as the turn's error rather than a recording failure, is not established. The CI runner is slower and more contended than a local machine, which fits a race that only widens there.

Discriminators, cheapest first:
- Grep the exact message to find the producing call site, then check whether that error can propagate into the turn completion path at all, or only into recording.
- Force the race locally: hold the recorder's database open across a submit and assert what the caller receives.
- If the error is genuinely confined to recording, the defect is that recording failures are allowed to become turn errors, and it is reproducible without any timing at all.

## Why it was not caught

The case asserts the happy path for two `_meta` shapes and never exercises a busy recorder, so nothing in the suite states what a caller should receive when recording is unavailable. Whether recording failures may surface as turn failures is not written down anywhere as a contract.

## Fix direction

Decide the contract first: a turn that the Agent completed successfully should not report a storage error as its outcome. Recording unavailability is worth reporting, but through the recording path, not by replacing the turn result.

Rejected: retrying or widening the lock timeout. That hides the contract question behind a longer wait and leaves the same failure at higher load.

## Acceptance

- A test that makes the turn-recording database unavailable during a submit and asserts the caller still receives the Agent's result, failing before the fix.
- Three consecutive green CI runs, both Neovim versions.

## Not covered

- Whether this is reachable in a real Session or only under the test's fake process harness.
- The nvim-nightly hover defect that shared the original report; that is louiselm-dhqgv, a separate cause with its own fix.

title: :LouiselmPark command: lazy Run attach, staged-context warning, auto-claims, named-precondition errors
description:
## Goal

An operator can cold-Park the current chat session with one Neovim command, exercising the real `Run:park_cold` ownership and capability checks instead of a CLI-only shortcut.

## Scope

- In scope: new `:LouiselmPark` command; lazy `Run.new()` + attach-as-sole-worker when the session is not already Run-backed; Staged-context warn-and-confirm; auto-queried `br` claims attached to the Park record; named-precondition error surfacing (loadSession capability, live client, working_dir) instead of raw ACP errors; wiring the existing `Service.admit`/`attach`/`park` calls as production callers.
- Out of scope: `:LouiselmResumePark` changes (separate task, see dependent), warm Park exposure, a `stage` schema field, multi-Run selection UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given an ordinary chat session with no existing Run, when the operator runs `:LouiselmPark`, then a Run is created, the session is attached as its sole worker, and it is cold-Parked, with no separate prior command required.
2. Given a session with staged context (queued prompt, pending skill selection, context chips), when `:LouiselmPark` runs, then the operator is warned it will not survive cold Park and must confirm before it proceeds.
3. Given the session actor holds live `br` claims, when `:LouiselmPark` runs, then those claims are attached to the Park record automatically, with no picker or manual entry.
4. Given the Agent lacks `agent_capabilities.loadSession`, has no live ACP client, or has no `working_dir`, when `:LouiselmPark` runs, then the specific failing precondition is named to the operator, never a raw ACP error string.
5. Warm Park is not exposed as a manual action anywhere in this command.

## Testing

- Headless test: session with staged context triggers the warning branch; confirming proceeds, declining does not Park.
- Headless test: session actor with live `br` claims produces a Park record carrying exactly those claims.
- Headless test: each of the three `cold_park_record` precondition failures produces a distinct, named error message (use the mock ACP agent, degrading its advertised capabilities per case).
- Full StyLua, LuaLS, and MiniTest gates.

## Notes

Parent feature: louiselm-aaw0. Reuses `Run:park_cold`/`cold_park_record` (`lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua`) and `Service.admit`/`attach`/`park` (`lua/louiselm/workflow/service.lua`), which exist today with zero production callers.
close_reason: Implemented :LouiselmPark with staged-context confirmation, live Beads claim capture, Run admission/attachment, named cold-Park errors, and generated docs/tests.

title: OpenCode Session stays prompting after permission handling
description:
An OpenCode Go Session can remain in status prompting after the user interacts with permission choices, leaving the chat unable to accept another prompt. The maintainer reports: "im stuck in opencode/ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney after i think i choose allow always". The exact lifetime choice is not verified by the transport trace: no allow_always option was recorded as selected.

## Observed

Reported on 2026-08-30 for ACP Session ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney, OpenCode Go with model opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna in the captured run.

Live Neovim inspection via /run/user/1000/nvim.566712.0 found Chat view session-3 attached to this ACP Session with status = "prompting", current_turn = 1, permission_active = nil, permission_queue = 0, and one pending local ACP client callback (request id 5).

The authoritative ACP proxy trace is /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney/log.jsonl. It records session/prompt id 13 at line 1527, then permission requests at lines 1610, 1612, 1615, and 1622. The recorded client responses are: id 7 selected optionId once (line 1611), id 8 cancelled (line 1614), id 9 cancelled (line 1621), and id 10 selected optionId once (line 1623). No allow_always selection appears. The trace also contains an ACP session/prompt response id 13 with stopReason = end_turn at line 1620, interleaved before the final permission responses.

OpenCode diagnostics at /home/lotso/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log:1750-1762 show the gpt-5.6-luna turn starting, then four external_directory permission checks being asked.

## Symptoms

- Chat remains in "prompting" / Model responding state.
- A new prompt cannot be submitted because the Session is not ready.
- Permission requests appear to have been answered, but the Session does not visibly reach a stable ready state.

## Root cause

Unknown. Candidate causes are a client-side response-correlation/lifecycle race around a session/prompt terminal response arriving while permission requests remain outstanding, reuse of an ACP Session through a new local client with stale pending state, or an OpenCode/proxy ordering defect. The exact live local request-to-proxy frame mapping still needs to be discriminated.

## Why it was not caught

Existing permission coverage tests synchronous selection and ordinary serialized requests. Existing prompt-timeout coverage models a missing terminal response but does not model a terminal session/prompt response interleaved with outstanding permission requests or a reattached OpenCode Session.

## Fix direction

Reproduce from the captured ACP frame ordering through the lifecycle boundary. Ensure each permission response and the session/prompt response is correlated exactly once, terminal prompt completion cannot be overwritten by late permission callbacks, and a reattached Session cannot retain stale pending request state. Preserve the client-side watchdog from louiselm-5zhl as a last-resort bound.

## Acceptance

- A regression fixture derived from the proxy trace covers the observed permission and terminal-response ordering.
- The Session reaches a correct terminal state after all observed permission responses, without leaving a stale pending prompt callback.
- The user can submit a subsequent prompt or receives a specific actionable error.
- The test distinguishes an actual allow_always selection from once/cancelled outcomes.

## Related

- louiselm-4wx fixed the earlier concurrent permission-picker deadlock.
- louiselm-5zhl added a generic watchdog for an ACP prompt that never resolves. This report is separate because the captured trace includes a terminal session/prompt response and the live Session still reports prompting.
close_reason: live:opencode/ses_fa3bdf1f9ffeNAfrX0FxUvWUzi maintainer-retested 2026-09-01 on a c5a7046 build: Session settles and accepts subsequent prompts, no stuck prompting. Scope limit stated plainly -- the original race was NOT reproduced. OpenCode serializes permissions and its terminal response lands ~200ms AFTER the last permission reply (inverse of the original ordering), reject ends the turn rather than producing outcome:cancelled, and :LouiselmCancel clears the queue before status change, so the c5a7046 guard at lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:255 was never entered in any producible flow. That guard rests on the regression fixture alone. Original trace ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney is deleted (proxy logs expire ~24h; this waited 2340 min) so the recorded ordering cannot be re-read -- louiselm-proxy-log-evidence-expiry-xxfu. Reopen if a stuck prompting Session recurs.

comments.author: codex/01a05303-3f5b-7291-82ec-bd7f1efc9522
comments.text: Fix evidence (2026-08-30): session/lifecycle.lua now keeps a completed turn in waiting_permission while permission_active or permission_queue is non-empty. Once the terminal session/prompt response has been observed, the final permission response transitions to ready instead of prompting; late permission requests are still answered through the existing serialized queue. Regression coverage reproduces proxy Session ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney ordering from ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney/log.jsonl: permission IDs 7-9, terminal prompt response, request 10, then all responses. The old behavior fails at the terminal response because it reports ready before permission 9; the fixed behavior ends ready with one prompt completion and all four permission responses. Focused session suite: 58 cases; full MiniTest: 786 cases; StyLua, LuaLS, and API appendix checks pass. Lesson: terminal ACP completion and permission draining are separate lifecycle boundaries; a terminal response must not erase the active permission phase. No AGENTS.md change is warranted. Live acceptance remains pending maintainer retest.

comments.author: claude/b2f2f248-deef-4d75-95cd-07972ebc9c26
comments.text:
Live acceptance recipe for the maintainer, 2026-09-01. Fix is c5a7046 ("fix(session): drain
permissions after turn"); the guard is live at lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:255 --
complete_turn now sets waiting_permission instead of ready when permission_active is set or
permission_queue is non-empty, so a terminal turn cannot be reopened as prompting by a late
permission callback.

## 0. Confirm the running build, not this worktree

louiselm-wi0y was diagnosed against a stale vim.pack clone. From inside the running Neovim:

    :lua print(vim.fn.system({"git","-C",vim.fn.fnamemodify(vim.api.nvim_get_runtime_file("lua/louiselm/init.lua",false)[1],":h:h:h"),"log","--oneline","-1","--","lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua"}))

Must show c5a7046 or later in that file's history. If it does not, the retest is invalid.

## 1. Reproduce the original conditions

Original trace: OpenCode Go, model opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna, ACP Session
ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney. Four external_directory permission checks (ids 7-10), answered
once / cancelled / cancelled / once, with the terminal session/prompt response (id 13,
stopReason end_turn) arriving BEFORE the final permission response.

Start an OpenCode Session in the louiselm repo and send one prompt that must touch several
directories outside the repository, so OpenCode raises multiple external_directory checks in a
single turn. Reading a few unrelated files under $HOME works.

The ordering is what matters, not the count: at least one permission decision must still be
outstanding when the turn's terminal response lands. Answer the first two or three promptly,
mixing allow-once and cancel as the original did, then leave the last picker open for several
seconds before answering it.

## 2. Pass criteria

1. After the last permission decision the Session settles in a stable ready state -- not
   "Model responding" / prompting.
2. A second prompt can be submitted and produces a normal turn.
3. No stale pending prompt callback: the internal check below reports status ready,
   permission_active false, queue 0.

## 3. Internal state check

Run from a shell that is a child of the Neovim instance, when NOT mid-turn (an in-flight turn
legitimately reports prompting):

    nvim --server "$NVIM" --remote-expr 'luaeval("dofile(\"/tmp/probe.lua\")")'

with /tmp/probe.lua:

```lua
local cmd = require("louiselm.ui.chat.command")
local chat
local i = 1
while true do
  local n, v = debug.getupvalue(cmd.winbar_click, i)
  if n == nil then break end
  if n == "chat" and v ~= nil then chat = v break end
  i = i + 1
end
if not chat then return "chat upvalue not found" end
local out = {}
for id, view in pairs(chat.views or {}) do
  local s = view.session
  if s and s.inspect then
    local d = s:inspect()
    out[#out+1] = ("%s  status=%-18s turn=%-3s permission_active=%-6s queue=%s")
      :format(tostring(id), tostring(d.status), tostring(d.current_turn),
              tostring(d.permission_active ~= nil), tostring(d.permission_queue and #d.permission_queue or 0))
  end
end
if #out == 0 then return "no views open" end
return table.concat(out, "\n")
```

Verified working 2026-09-01 against a live instance; returns e.g.
`session-3  status=prompting  turn=15  permission_active=false  queue=0`, the same shape the
original diagnosis used.

## 4. If it fails

Capture the ACP Session id from the winbar and keep the proxy log before retrying:
`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/<session-id>/log.jsonl`. Per AGENTS.md, the
session/new frame is in `proxy/connections/<connection-id>.jsonl` instead; resolve it with
`grep -l <session-id> ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/connections/*.jsonl`. Record the
permission request ids, their responses, and the line number of the session/prompt terminal
response relative to them -- that interleaving is the whole defect.

## 5. On pass

Close with a live: Close verdict naming the ACP Session id retested, per
louiselm-adopt-close-verdict-gate-xfoj. The issue's remaining acceptance bullets (regression
fixture from the proxy trace, allow_always distinguished from once/cancelled) are already
covered by c5a7046's tests; only the live retest is outstanding.

comments.author: claude/b2f2f248-deef-4d75-95cd-07972ebc9c26
comments.text:
Maintainer live acceptance 2026-09-01, Session opencode/ses_fa3bdf1f9ffeNAfrX0FxUvWUzi, on a
build carrying c5a7046.

## What was retested

Prompt "create 10 files in /tmp under the name 1.txt to 10.txt", twice, with permission
decisions mixed allow-once and reject. Wire trace
`proxy/sessions/ses_fa3bdf1f9ffeNAfrX0FxUvWUzi/log.jsonl`:

```
09:18:36.706  PROMPT id=5
09:18:43.030  REQ  perm id=0                       /tmp/1.txt
09:18:49.046  RESP id=0 -> selected "once"
09:18:49.059  REQ  perm id=1                       /tmp/2.txt
09:18:49.976  RESP id=1 -> selected "reject"
09:18:50.172  TURN-END id=5 stopReason=end_turn
09:19:06.677  PROMPT id=6   (accepted normally)
09:19:19.367  PROMPT id=7
09:19:21.350  REQ  perm id=2 -> once
09:19:22.739  REQ  perm id=3 -> once
09:19:23.570  REQ  perm id=4 -> reject
09:19:33.361  TURN-END id=7 stopReason=end_turn
```

Result: the Session settled and accepted two subsequent prompts. No stuck `prompting` state.
Acceptance bullets 2 and 3 hold for every flow that could be produced.

## What could NOT be reproduced, and why

The original defect needs a terminal `session/prompt` response arriving while a permission
request is still outstanding. That state was never reached:

- Permission requests are strictly serialized by the agent: `REQ id=1` is sent only after
  `RESP id=0`. Never more than one outstanding.
- The terminal response consistently lands ~200 ms AFTER the last permission response (196 ms
  round one, 195 ms round two) -- the inverse of the original ordering.
- Selecting "reject" does not produce the original `outcome: cancelled` frames. OpenCode simply
  ends the turn on a rejection (confirmed: reject at 09:18:49.976, end_turn at 09:18:50.172),
  so requests 3-10 are never issued. That is agent behaviour, not a LouiseLM defect.
- `outcome: "cancelled"` is emitted only by `cancel_permissions` (lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:483),
  reachable solely through `Session:cancel()` / `:LouiselmCancel`. Checked: that path clears
  `permission_queue` and `permission_active` before the status change, so `complete_turn` still
  observes an empty queue and the c5a7046 guard is not exercised by it either.

So `complete_turn` took the `ready` branch in every observed flow -- the same branch it took
before the fix. The guard at `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:255` was never entered.

Only the agent can create the outstanding-permission-at-turn-end state, by ending a turn while
a picker is open. Attempts to induce it by leaving a picker unanswered did not get OpenCode to
end the turn.

## Evidence that no longer exists

The original trace `proxy/sessions/ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney/log.jsonl` is gone; the
directory is empty. Proxy logs survive about 24 hours and this issue waited 2340 minutes for
retest. The recorded line ordering in the description cannot be re-read against the wire.
Filed as louiselm-proxy-log-evidence-expiry-xxfu.

## Standing conclusion

The regression fixture added by c5a7046 encodes the original ordering and is the only thing
holding this behaviour. Live retest confirms the Session does not get stuck in the flows that
can be produced today; it does not confirm the original race was hit and survived.

comments.author: claude/b2f2f248-deef-4d75-95cd-07972ebc9c26
comments.text: Correction 2026-09-01: the close reason and the prior comment attribute the lost trace to a ~24h retention window. That was wrong. ACP proxy logs are evicted by a 100MB aggregate size cap in acp-llm-adapter/src/logsink.rs (DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES); max_age is 30 days and never fires here. prune() runs on every write, oldest-first. The workspace measured 98.8MB of 100MB, with two Sessions holding 66MB of it. ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney's log existed with 1600+ lines on 08-30 as the description records; its directory mtime 2026-08-31 09:01 is the eviction moment. Nothing about this changes the retest conclusion or the close -- the evidence was gone either way -- but the cause is a configurable cap, not time. Root cause and mitigation: louiselm-proxy-log-evidence-expiry-xxfu (now P1).

comments.author: claude/b2f2f248-deef-4d75-95cd-07972ebc9c26
comments.text:
Recovery check 2026-09-01: the lost evidence is largely recoverable from the Agents' own stores, which the proxy retention cap never touched.

Of 87 working Sessions with no proxy log: 30 have a native transcript in ~/.claude/projects, 45 have a codex rollout in ~/.codex/sessions (e.g. rollout-2026-08-21T16-11-47-01a024a9-....jsonl, 33MB), 3 are in OpenCode's SQLite store, 2 appear in ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*-copilot-stdout-jsonrpc.log, and 4 were not Session ids at all but actor-string parsing noise. Effectively all of them.

This issue's own Session survives: ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney is in ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db, title 'Create Agent Skill from Shared Chat and File Beads', created 2026-08-30 13:34:46, 24 messages and 103 parts (20 text, 30 tool, 16 reasoning, 2 patch). A sibling Session ses_fad10e00effea4Yk19LNe0CaAa is titled 'Stuck in opencode session after allow al...', 15 messages -- that is this defect's symptom captured from the Agent side.

What is NOT recoverable is the part this bug turned on. OpenCode's store holds the conversation, not the ACP wire: no session/request_permission ids, no client response outcomes, no interleaving of the terminal session/prompt response against outstanding permissions. Reconstructing the 1610/1612/1615/1620/1622/1623 ordering from these stores is not possible. The close stands.

Also durable and worth knowing: ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*-stdout-jsonrpc.log (516 files, back to 2026-06-17) are real JSON-RPC dumps for adapter-run Agents and sit outside proxy/, so logsink's prune() never collected them.

title: Acceptance VM cannot compile current OpenSSL tests offline
description:
The prepared launcher VM cannot compile the current skills-core conformance suite offline.

## Observed
2026-09-09, codex/01a083f4-469e-7351-97fb-205f6aa39a6f. In guest /home/vm/qbr-identity.JmKF84, scripts/launcher-conformance --disposable-guest fails compiling openssl-sys v0.9.117: "Package openssl was not found in the pkg-config search path". dpkg-query -W libssl-dev: "no packages found matching libssl-dev". Runtime libssl3t64 is 3.5.7-1~deb13u2; libc6 2.41. Restricted guest has no cached libssl-dev package.

## Root cause
scripts/launcher-vm provisioning installs build-essential/pkg-config but not libssl-dev; skills-core/Cargo.toml now declares the openssl development dependency. Guest package prerequisite drift is not covered by the wrapper argv/SSH safety tests.

## Fix direction / acceptance
Provision the existing declared dependency in the trusted prepared guest baseline, without desktop package/security changes or silently opening restricted guest egress. Prove offline current-source conformance compilation in the prepared VM; retain provenance and rollback for baseline refresh.

## Not covered
Deferred while qbr.5.1.1.2 validates explicitly transferred host-built binaries in the existing guest. No guest/host package changes made.

title: QA round: OpenCode Go quota propagation
description:
# Manual QA review — OpenCode quota error propagation

Build under test: local OpenCode 1.18.29 + commit 343bd71; upstream equivalent
7a6ef21 (PR anomalyco/opencode#47805). Installed binary SHA256:
1f65b0fc3f358ed7a67982b4bd1cf8044a798393a60f6a3fe5f009d302d55c13.

## Status

| Case | State |
| --- | --- |
| Real Go quota rejection reaches LouiseLM | Passed: prompt 4 receives error in 1.230s; maintainer confirms visible Error state and quota/reset message |

## Setup and case
