title: Beads inspector: cross-workspace sibling sweep + beads.sibling_roots config
description:
## Goal

`<leader>lB` opens an issue from a sibling repo's Beads workspace when the
cursor is on a full `<foreign-prefix>-<suffix>` ID that does not resolve
locally, using a new user-configured list of sibling roots.

## Scope

- In scope: add a `beads` table to the config schema in
  `lua/louiselm/config.lua`, following the existing `Schema.define` DSL
  already used there (see e.g. the `capture` or `context` entries for the
  pattern). Add `beads.sibling_roots`: `type = "array-of"`, `items =
  "string"`, `default = {}`. No custom validator function is needed beyond
  what `array-of`/`string` already enforces; do not hand-roll extra checks.
- In scope: in `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua`, when the cursor token already
  looks like a full `<prefix>-<suffix>` ID (i.e. it failed the *local*
  workspace lookup, both the existing exact-prefix path and the sibling
  bare-suffix task's local lookup if that task has landed first -- check
  before assuming either exists yet) but has the general Beads ID shape, glob
  one level under each configured `sibling_roots` entry for a `.beads/beads.db`
  and try `br --db <that path> show <token>` against each, in the order
  configured, stopping at the first hit. Fall through to the existing manual
  prompt if none hit or if `sibling_roots` is empty/unset.
- Out of scope: bare-suffix matching against siblings (rejected in the
  parent design -- bare tokens stay local-only, see `louiselm-r98e` and the
  closed `louiselm-qmmk` grill for why).
- Out of scope: caching the glob result, persisting a registry, or any UI to
  configure `sibling_roots` -- it is a plain config-table value the user sets
  in their own `setup()` call (see the reference file at
  `~/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua` for what a
  real user config call looks like, if you need an example of the shape).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given `beads.sibling_roots` is unset (default empty list), when
   `<leader>lB` is pressed on any token, then no sibling sweep happens at
   all -- behavior is byte-identical to before this task.
2. Given `beads.sibling_roots` contains one or more paths and the cursor is
   on a full `<foreign-prefix>-<suffix>` ID that exists in the second
   configured sibling's workspace but not the first, when `<leader>lB` is
   pressed, then the first sibling is tried and misses, the second is tried
   and hits, and that issue opens (proves ordering and short-circuit, not
   just "some sibling matched").
3. Given `beads.sibling_roots` is configured but the ID exists in none of
   them (and not locally either), when `<leader>lB` is pressed, then the
   existing manual `Beads issue id:` prompt appears, unchanged.
4. Given a `sibling_roots` entry whose value is not a table of strings
   (e.g. a bare string or a number in the list), when the config is loaded,
   then validation rejects it with a clear error, consistent with how other
   `array-of` fields in this schema already fail on bad input.

## Testing

- Add cases to `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua` following its existing fake-`br`
  pattern (no real subprocesses, per AGENTS.md determinism rules): the
  unset-default no-op case, the ordering/short-circuit case across two fake
  siblings, the exhausted-sweep-falls-to-prompt case.
- Add a config-schema test (wherever `lua/louiselm/config.lua`'s existing
  schema fields are tested -- find that spec file first) covering the new
  `beads.sibling_roots` field: valid list of strings accepted, invalid entry
  type rejected, default is an empty list when omitted.

## Notes

- Full design context and rejected alternatives (no persisted registry, no
  hardcoded `~/code/*`, no piggybacking on beads_rust's own user config) live
  in the parent feature `louiselm-r98e` and the closed grill question
  `louiselm-qmmk` -- read those before starting, do not re-derive or
  re-litigate the design.
- Live-measured cost (2026-08-28): a `--db`-pointed `br show` call costs
  ~25-60ms regardless of hit/miss, dominated by process startup. A full
  sweep of a handful of siblings is well under 500ms -- acceptable for an
  explicit per-keypress action.
- Config addition and sweep logic are folded into one task rather than split,
  since the config addition alone is too small (a few lines following an
  existing DSL pattern) to be independently worth grabbing on its own.
close_reason: done

comments.author: claude/b59dc4cb-7c9d-4efc-908a-2cca0884acca
comments.text:
Implemented:

- lua/louiselm/config.lua: new `beads.sibling_roots` schema field (array-of string, default {}), following the existing capture/skills.paths DSL pattern exactly.
- lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua: candidate_token_at_cursor() (renamed/refactored from the bare-suffix tasks helper) now feeds a branch in inspect_with_prefix() -- a token containing a hyphen is treated as a foreign-workspace-shaped ID and handed to the new try_sibling_ids(), which globs each configured sibling_roots entry one level for `.beads/beads.db` (sibling_db_paths()) and tries `br --db <path> show <token> --json` against each in order, stopping at the first hit. A hyphen-free token still goes through the existing local bare-suffix path. Exhausting all siblings (or having none configured) falls through to the manual prompt, matching the local bare-suffix path's speculative-miss behavior.
- decode_issue()/run_show() prefix parameter is now optional: sibling calls pass no prefix (a sibling's own prefix is unknown without an extra round trip) and instead rely on the exact `issue.id == token` equality check already performed by callers.
- lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua: threads `configured.beads.sibling_roots` into the Beads.inspect() call.

Caught by the new tests before merging: the hyphen-shape branch check used `token:find("%-", 1, true)` -- with plain=true, `%-` is a literal 3-char search string, not an escaped hyphen, so it never matched and every foreign-looking token silently fell into the bare-suffix path instead (producing a broken double-prefixed guess like "louiselm-codex-acp-a1b2"). Fixed to `token:find("-", 1, true)`. This is exactly the kind of thing the acceptance-criteria tests exist to catch.

Tests added: tests/ui/beads_spec.lua (sibling-sweep hit proving order/short-circuit across two fake siblings, sweep-exhausted falls to prompt, sibling_roots-unset produces zero sibling calls / identical pre-feature behavior); tests/schema/setup_spec.lua (valid sibling_roots accepted, default empty list, non-string entry rejected without mutating caller config).

doc/louiselm.txt and doc/tags regenerated via scripts/generate-vimdoc for the new config option (generate-api-appendix --check stayed clean -- no public LuaCATS surface changed). Full suite green (709 -> 715 cases across both tasks under this feature), stylua clean, lua-language-server zero diagnostics. --json

title: Claude scheduled wakeup shows Your turn while responding
description:
Claude resumes after ScheduleWakeup while the LouiseLM winbar still says "Your turn". Reported by the maintainer on 2026-09-16 in the sslc Session. Implementation authorized by the maintainer and prepared on 2026-09-16; activation and exact maintainer acceptance remain pending.

## Observed

Screenshots: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260916_0618_1920x1200_1789532298.png and /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260916_0618_1920x1200_1789532300.png. Both show "Your turn"; new Claude output appears between them after ScheduleWakeup.

Subject Session: claude/f995461f-3871-4cd4-81d9-330b5a697424, local session-6, cwd /home/lotso/code/sslc, editor socket /run/user/1000/nvim.2484254.0. Read-only inspection during diagnosis returned status=ready, current_turn=29, turn_done_turn=29, recording_turn.finished=true, exit_verdict.turn_active=false. This later snapshot alone does not prove the Agent was still processing at inspection time; the screenshots and timestamped log establish the mismatch.

ACP log: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/f995461f-3871-4cd4-81d9-330b5a697424/log.jsonl. Structural evidence only (UTC; local screenshots are UTC+2):
- Line 26237, 04:16:58.728Z: client session/prompt id=269.
- Line 26343, 04:17:26.302Z: pending ScheduleWakeup; line 26349 completed.
- Line 26362, 04:17:29.367Z: response id=269, stopReason=end_turn.
- Line 26367, 04:17:54.862Z: new pending Bash tool without another session/prompt.
- Lines 26382-26395, 04:18:00.260-265Z: agent_thought_chunk after completion.
- From 04:17:29.368Z through 04:20:00Z: 563 session/update frames (30 usage_update, 14 tool_call, 56 tool_call_update, 387 agent_thought_chunk, 76 agent_message_chunk), no session/prompt, no subsequent prompt response, and no explicit busy/idle notification. Account-limit traffic is unrelated.

Connection log /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/connections/c902a2d8-c678-4917-822c-9c5d57c69975.jsonl records launch through python3 /home/lotso/.config/nvim/agent-runtimes/runtime.py launch claude. Current managed target inspected: /home/lotso/.local/share/louiselm/agent-runtimes/claude/builds/dfce48a70b9fd7a1. No runtime was changed or restarted.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:294 complete_turn sets ready at :302. handle_notification at :409-428 forwards subsequent progress without tracking independent Agent activity. lua/louiselm/ui/chat/status.lua:189 renders ready as Your turn. Session:cancel at :1185 also rejects ready, and registry.lua:284 derives exit protection from prompt-related states. This is a shared lifecycle gap, not stale rendering. Actual cancellation of this Claude wakeup was not attempted or verified.

The current managed Claude adapter src/acp-agent.ts:4260 handles SDK session_state_changed with idle/running/requires_action, stores lastSessionState, and uses idle for internal lifecycle handling; the case ends at :4406 without forwarding the activity state. Its persistent consumer explicitly forwards between-turn/background output. Thus native activity can be available at the adapter boundary even though LouiseLM only receives content/tool/usage updates. Native event ordering for this exact scheduled wakeup still needs captured verification.

Related prior art: louiselm-7mqy9 (Copilot Autopilot). Its independent activity implementation is preserved on wip/copilot-autopilot-7mqy9, commit 9123834f64c5ed6e7099726732d7687d977908fe, and deliberately absent from main at maintainer request. Do not restore it wholesale or change the deferred Copilot work implicitly.

## Why it was not caught

Existing Session tests cover client prompt/response and prolonged silence inside a prompt. The live sequence here is completed prompt -> autonomous work -> independent idle, which has no activity contract in main. Initial diagnosis had no automated regression. Implementation added a failing scheduled-work regression (ready instead of running), then made it pass.

## Fix direction

Expose validated, Session-scoped native activity from the Claude adapter through an explicit extension; consume it in LouiseLM's shared Session lifecycle independently of client prompt completion. Preserve prompt callback/recording exactly once. Use the activity state for winbar, queued input and exit protection; verify cancellation separately. Review reusable parts of the preserved Copilot implementation without reviving that deferred integration.

Do not infer completion from tool completion, usage_update, silence, or ScheduleWakeup's name. Switching to prompting on arbitrary chunks lacks a reliable idle transition and can mistake replay or late terminal results for new work.

## Acceptance

- Captured structural fixture proves native running/idle ordering during a scheduled wakeup; regression fails before the fix.
- Schedule a CI check, finish the originating prompt, let Claude wake autonomously: show Model responding while processing, then Your turn on authoritative idle.
- Completed client prompt callbacks and recorded outcomes remain exactly once; autonomous work does not fabricate another user prompt.
- Cover replay, late terminal output, permissions, queued input, normal peers without the extension, malformed state events, cancellation, error and disposal.
- Inspect effective managed runtime and run affected suites in each changed repository.
- Keep open until the maintainer confirms this exact live reproduction.

## Not covered

The initial diagnosis changed no runtime or code. The maintainer subsequently authorized implementation, local commits and deployment. Implementation and activation are recorded below. Existing live Sessions remain untouched; Copilot issues remain deferred. Lesson: prompt completion and Agent idleness are distinct; use authoritative lifecycle signals rather than output timing.


## Implementation and verification (2026-09-16)

LouiseLM: opt-in initialize capability io.github.euri10.louiselm.sessionActivity v1; validated session_info_update metadata drives independent running state. Native idle does not resolve a prompt or clear pending permissions. Queued input, admission/configuration overlap, background unread status, cancellation dispatch and Run/editor-exit protection consume the activity state. Public help/API generated; extension documented in docs/acp-session-activity.md.

Adapter topic: /home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp-activity, branch fix/session-activity, based on upstream 8823ea6fcb6743d37c1aad91ccd44725164b8927. Opt-in native state forwarding in src/acp-agent.ts, src/tests/session-activity.test.ts and session_activity_protocol.md. Committed as a2326b8ac9e7afd0c23afba38ab15d6b4b65483b. Separate combined verification worktree /home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp-activity-verify starts at the currently deployed 0510c91 and applies the same patch, retaining account limits. This initial verification did not modify an installed package/build; subsequent authorized activation is recorded below.

Gates: full LouiseLM suite 1067/1067; full adapter topic suite 1328 passed / 27 opt-in skipped; combined deployed-patches suite 1371 passed / 27 skipped. Lua static analysis, StyLua and API/LuaCATS/plugin-version/Vimdoc generator checks pass. Adapter TypeScript build and lint/Prettier checks pass on topic; combined static checks recorded separately below when complete.

Real unchanged SDK 0.3.270 / CLI 2.1.270 with synthetic loopback Anthropic responses, isolated home/workspace, ScheduleWakeup only, no paid model requests or maintainer Session controls. Temporary scripts /tmp/louiselm-claude-wakeup.ft5NG0/probe.mjs and probe.lua. Evidence:

- e2e.log, Session d038c7cd-3cac-4119-9396-3e1c089a2fa7: real headless LouiseLM -> built adapter -> native Claude -> local simulated provider. Prompt callback count=1 and turn_done=1; callback status running then initial ready; autonomous running at 97718 ms rendered Model responding with turn_active=true; ready at 97754 ms rendered Your turn with turn_active=false. Native wakeup is independent of another client prompt.
- cancel.log, Session 1c6bd613-f084-452b-911e-1acd6af614c9: autonomous provider request held at 96416 ms; session/cancel at 96516 ms; provider connection closed unfinished at 96521 ms; native idle/extension idle at 96526 ms. No response was released. Unlike the deferred Copilot case, native Claude cancellation works in this reproduction.

Probe lesson: ScheduleWakeup requires noop and clamps delaySeconds to at least 60, then rounds to a minute boundary; a 75-second diagnostic deadline can expire before a healthy wakeup. First probes were recipe corrections, not product failures. Unit comments distinguish captured lifecycle order from synthetic malformed/replay/permission/race cases. title: Pin chat immunity to codecompanion #913-style malformed-markdown parse-back
description:
External: olimorris/codecompanion.nvim#913 (closed as not planned, PR #3355). Model-emitted nested triple-backtick fences break the codecompanion chat parse: their buffer is the conversation source of truth, split on ## headings per request, so the heading separator stops being recognized and every later user turn silently never reaches the model.

Verdict: louiselm is immune.
- State is the structured Transcript (record_user, lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1914) plus agent-owned ACP history; session:prompt (init.lua:1904) sends only the new turn.
- The buffer is a one-way render target; the prompt region is extmark-delimited (prompt_text init.lua:1400, mark_prompt init.lua:1363), never derived from markdown structure, so model bytes cannot move or disguise the boundary.
- The chat buffer is filetype=louiselm-session, deliberately not markdown (init.lua:2952), so no fence or heading parsing exists even visually.
- The one structural buffer read-back, split_handoff_brief (init.lua:3197), is a plain literal find over an operator-authored brief whose ## Context header we generate first; fence nesting cannot hide it, and an edited-out header degrades to the flattened form (init.lua:3205). Narrow edge: if the operator deletes our header AND compacted model text contains a literal ## Context line, the split lands on the model line instead of degrading — a mis-partitioned prompt, not corruption.

Residual already tracked as louiselm-yvdf: navigation_targets (init.lua:2778) classifies any > -prefixed rendered line as a prompt, so model blockquotes create spurious [u/]u jump targets — the same prefix-classification-over-rendered-text mistake at cosmetic blast radius. codecompanion #913 is that mistake at full strength; the yvdf fix direction (render-time metadata over text parsing) is corroborated.

Work: pin the immunity with one spec — after an assistant reply containing nested fences and ## headings, submit a prompt and assert session:prompt receives exactly the extmark-region text and the transcript records it verbatim.
close_reason: gate:tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:1440 pins malformed-Markdown prompt isolation and verbatim transcript recording; 1164 tests pass.

Characterization only: existing behavior passes, no production change or artificial red phase. Lesson stays here: prompt extraction uses extmark boundaries, never rendered Markdown structure. Gates: 194 chat cases and all 1164 Lua cases pass; StyLua, LuaLS and four generated-artifact checks pass.

title: Closing an adopted listener must preserve the service manager socket
description: During 96pv.1 handoff inspection: ListenerCore::close_locked in skills-core/src/launch_transport.rs calls shutdown(control, Both). title: Reconnected guard closure can ACK while old owner lives
description: A reconnected BrokerSession starts with provider_listener=None (broker/reconnect.rs), while close_provider_listener accepts matching SenderGuardClosing when provider_listener is None (broker/provider_handoff.rs:101-108) and sends SenderGuardClosed. The original Session worker can still own handed-off listener/stream descriptors after its channel is closed; reconnect runs concurrently. Thus a new Session can ACK closure before old owners release descriptors, allowing the supervisor to mistake uncertain handoff cleanup for proof and release its identity. Reproduction gate: keep the original Session listener/stream owner alive, reconnect the same signed head, send SenderGuardClosing on the new channel; it must not ACK until every prior descriptor owner is gone. No recovery re-enrollment or permissive fallback.
close_reason: gate:skills-core/tests/broker/provider_handoff.rs:136 rejects false closure ACK until old owner drops

comments.author: codex/01a0d8f7-90be-7550-8f5b-c3e946cc0855
comments.text: Lesson: a reconnected BrokerSession starting with provider_listener=None says nothing about descriptors held by another live worker. Track listener and upstream descriptor lifetimes in the shared BrokerService; closure ACK requires all exact Session/revision leases gone. Re-enrollment of the same revision remains forbidden. Regression red before fix, green after; broker 191/191, full skills-core and clippy green.

title: Grill-me needed: should Control broker Provider egress be proven on a Provider with a supported credential contract before Codex?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; it needs a focused louiselm-grill-me session and maintainer confirmation before any scope or dependency changes.

## Question
The Control broker's Provider egress and credential custody (louiselm-qbr.5.1.3) is modelled around Codex subscription authentication. Should the first enforced egress path instead target a Provider whose credential contract is already documented, so broker enforcement and Verified posture can proceed while the Codex path waits?

## Evidence
- louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.11 (deferred): as of 2026-09-18 no supported broker-originated Codex subscription contract exists (docs/codex-auth-proof.md). louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.10 closed requiring a documented production transport; legacy token export stays research-only.
- Chain: qbr.5.1.3.4 -> .3.2 -> .3.3 all wait on .3.11. louiselm-d6fv.6.13 and louiselm-d6fv.6.5 wait on qbr.5.1, so the Verified posture branch (d6fv.6) is stalled too. br scheduler still ranks qbr.5.1 and d6fv.6 first (score 64, 13-14 dependents) with no workable child.
- Surfaced 2026-09-24 triage in claude/d7834ce3-9555-4d81-ad34-eb0aed935af8; maintainer agreed the question is worth a grill.

## Threads to pull
- Is the broker's value enforcement itself, or Codex-subscription custody specifically? Which acceptance criteria of qbr.5.1 are Provider-neutral?
- Candidates: Anthropic API key, OpenCode, API-key egress for OpenAI (per-token cost vs subscription). Which satisfy broker-only custody as defined in qbr.5.1.3.10?
- Does a Provider-neutral first path change the Verified posture network dimension (d6fv.6.13), or only its first producer?
- What happens to Codex Sessions under Verified launch meanwhile: unavailable (current rule) or explicitly unverified?
- Cost and lock-in: how long can the flagship security boundary depend on one vendor's roadmap?

title: Provenance: queryable commit/issue/Session lineage with backlog time travel
description:
## Problem Statement

Starting from a commit, there is no way to answer "which issue was this for"
and "which Session produced it" without hand-archaeology. The same holds in
reverse: an issue does not say which commits implemented it, and a closed
design question does not say what the backlog looked like when it was decided.

The maintainer works across several Agents, and the record of what happened is
already split three ways -- git commits, Beads issues, Session transcripts --
with no join between them. When a past decision needs revisiting, the context
it was made in has to be reconstructed by hand every time. This has already
happened: louiselm-ce6.27 revisited the boundary accepted on louiselm-iexg two
days earlier and re-derived the surrounding context from scratch.

## Solution

Make Provenance a first-class, queryable thing inside LouiseLM.

Nothing new is stored. All three edges already exist as data:

- issue <-> commit: bvr already correlates these from git history, with a
  method and confidence per correlation and a curation loop for the inferences.
- commit <-> Session: the maintainer's `Refs <id>` commit trailer convention
  already carries both issue ids and Session ids.
- issue <-> Session: the `br update --claim --actor "<session id>"` rule in
  AGENTS.md section 2 already puts Session ids in `assignee`/`created_by`.

What is missing is a query surface and one resolver: Session id -> transcript
on disk, which is per-Agent, local-machine, and the only part that actually
evaporates.

On top of that, time travel. `.beads/issues.jsonl` is committed, so git holds a
snapshot of the whole backlog at every commit. Combining the closed question,
the backlog state at its closing commit, the diff since, and the Session
transcript makes a past decision re-interrogable on evidence rather than on
memory: here is what we knew then, here is what has drifted, does the decision
still hold.

## User Stories

1. As a maintainer reading a commit, I want to see which issue(s) it served and
   which Session produced it, so that I can recover intent without guessing.
2. As a maintainer reading an issue, I want to see every commit that touched it
   and every Session that worked it, so that I can find the reasoning behind a
   change.
3. As a maintainer revisiting a closed design question, I want the backlog state
   as of its closing commit plus everything that changed since, so that I can
   judge whether the decision still holds.
4. As a maintainer, I want to jump from a Session id to that Session's
   transcript, so that the reasoning is one keystroke away rather than a
   filesystem hunt.
5. As an Agent picking up related work, I want machine-readable Provenance for
   an issue, so that I can load prior context without re-reading the repository.
6. As a maintainer, I want an unresolved Session to be shown as unresolved, so
   that a gap in coverage never reads as an absence of history.
7. As a maintainer whose commits predate the trailer convention, I want partial
   Provenance rather than an error, so that old work still yields what it can.
8. As a maintainer, I want Provenance to be read-only, so that inspecting the
   past can never mutate the record.
9. As an Agent, I want correlation confidence surfaced rather than hidden, so
   that an inferred edge is never presented as a recorded fact.

## Implementation Decisions

Vocabulary: this work introduces the term Provenance (louiselm-tsxh), agreed
with the maintainer on 2026-08-26. It is deliberately distinct from Forensics
(louiselm-cvv3): Forensics is a durable immutable record indexing evidence for
exactly one subject Session, while Provenance is recomputed per query, spans
entities, and persists nothing. Forensics is not being widened.

Modules:

- `provenance/correlate.lua` -- pure join over already-collected inputs,
  producing the edge set. No I/O whatsoever, so the entire graph logic is
  fixture-testable. This is the deep module of the epic.
- `provenance/sources.lua` -- bounded `vim.system` calls to `bvr --robot-*` and
  `git`, returning structured data or `nil, err`. Isolates process and
  fast-event discipline from logic.
- `provenance/vintage.lua` -- time travel: resolve a git ref to the historical
  `.beads/issues.jsonl` and diff it. Encapsulates a live upstream defect
  (louiselm-f8r1) behind a stable interface so it can be deleted when upstream
  lands, without touching callers.
- `session/locator.lua` -- per-Agent registry mapping `<agent>/<session-id>` to
  a transcript path. Independently valuable beyond this epic; louiselm-3x9p
  wants the same capability.
- `ui/provenance.lua` -- read-only `louiselm://provenance/<kind>/<id>` buffer,
  modelled directly on the existing `ui/beads.lua`, whose cursor-id detection,
  `br` shell-out and read-only buffer rendering are the same shape. Extends id
  detection to commit SHAs and Session ids.

Agent coverage: every Agent that appears in the record is supported on day
one -- claude, codex, deepseek and copilot -- by maintainer decision on
2026-08-26. Staging them was considered and rejected as false economy.

The reason it is cheap is that the resolver must not key on Agent name in the
first place. `config.agents` is a `map-of` with default `{}` (lua/louiselm/
config.lua): Agent names are arbitrary user labels, not a known enum. Two
setups can call the same CLI different things, and renaming a config entry
would silently break Provenance for every historical Session under the old
name. So `session/locator.lua` keys on transcript LAYOUT, with configuration
mapping an Agent entry to a layout. Layouts are shared -- the OpenAI-compatible
CLIs (deepseek, glm) resolve the same way -- so once the registry exists the
marginal cost of an Agent is a layout entry, not a module. glm is expected to
work through the OpenAI-compatible layout without separate work, but this is
unverified and must not be claimed until a real glm Session resolves.

Measured coverage at the time of writing, which is why no single Agent could
have been treated as the default: the two edges disagree, so name-keyed or
partial support would leave holes whose shape depends on which direction the
graph is queried.

| Agent    | Beads actors | commit trailers |
|----------|--------------|-----------------|
| codex    | 123          | 1               |
| claude   | 34           | 25              |
| copilot  | 14           | 1               |
| deepseek | 0            | 7               |

Contracts:

- Provenance is strictly read-only. It never writes to Beads, git, or a
  transcript.
- Correlation confidence and method from bvr are carried through to the surface,
  never flattened into an assertion.
- An unresolved Session renders as explicitly unresolved. Omitting the row is
  forbidden, because a coverage gap that looks like data is worse than a
  visible hole.
- Core modules return structured errors and typed events; only the UI module
  presents them (AGENTS.md section 8).

## Testing Decisions

- `correlate` is tested against captured real `bvr --robot-history` and
  `git log` output, cited per AGENTS.md section 5 so observed shapes stay
  distinguishable from invented ones. Cover: explicit-id and co-committed
  methods, an issue with no commits, a commit with no trailer, a Session id that
  resolves to nothing, and the pre-convention era where trailers are absent.
- `vintage` is tested against a temporary git repository fixture with a
  committed `.beads/issues.jsonl`, including the custom-status case that
  currently breaks upstream, so the workaround has a red test proving why it
  exists and a signal for when it can be removed.
- `session/locator` is tested against a temporary directory tree per transcript
  layout, plus the missing-transcript path, an Agent renamed in config after the
  Session was recorded, and two differently-named Agents sharing one layout.
- `sources` is tested for the fast-event boundary: process callbacks must not
  touch editor APIs directly, per AGENTS.md section 10.
- `ui/provenance` gets a headless behavioural smoke test in the style of the
  existing chat UI specs, not pixel assertions, plus the queued-work-after-
  disposal case.
- Prior art to follow: `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` for UI behaviour, and the
  existing Beads inspector for the shell-out-and-render shape.

## Out of Scope

- Writing or mutating any Provenance data. Derived only.
- Visualisation beyond a text buffer. No graph rendering in this epic.
- Fixing the upstream bvr defect (louiselm-f8r1). Encapsulated, not fixed. The
  maintainer has explicitly deferred upstream action.
- Widening or redefining Forensics.
- Analytics over Session option changes (louiselm-3x9p), which will consume
  `session/locator` but is separate work.

## Further Notes

Direction settled with the maintainer on 2026-08-26 as "door B", chosen over a
shell-and-skill join that would have delivered lookup only. Full evidence,
including the measured state of every edge and the bvr capability audit, is on
the louiselm-06yh comment.

louiselm-06yh is resolved as a design gate by explicit maintainer decision.
Door B answers "build it, derive rather than store, LouiseLM owns the surface";
transcript-resolution semantics are settled as local, adapter-specific,
best-effort lookup with explicit unresolved states. The agreed
Decision/Provenance model and implementation slices are recorded in this epic.

Known blocker: louiselm-f8r1. bvr drops every custom-status record and
hard-fails all time travel on this backlog, so `vintage` cannot work through
bvr's git-ref path until that is resolved or worked around. The workaround is
recorded on that bead.

Refs louiselm-06yh
Refs claude/ce71a8b9-3415-4247-a8a5-9e1ecf6ff943
close_reason: All 11 descendants closed; epic delivered. Housekeeping close, no remaining work.

comments.text:
Adapter scope changed before any implementation started: all Agents supported on day one (claude, codex, deepseek, copilot), not the staged claude+codex split originally drafted. Maintainer decision 2026-08-26, on the grounds that glm is OpenAI-compatible and therefore shares deepseek's shape.

Recording the design consequence, since it is the part that would be expensive to discover late: this only stays cheap if session/locator keys on transcript LAYOUT rather than Agent name. config.agents is a map-of with default {} — names are arbitrary user labels, so a name-keyed resolver breaks on a config rename and cannot share one implementation between two Agents that use the same CLI. If a future change reintroduces name keying, the day-one-all-Agents decision stops being cheap and this comment is the reason why.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Design resolved through louiselm-06yh on 2026-08-26. End state: LouiseLM owns a derived, read-only Provenance/Decision browser over git, Beads/bvr, and local adapter-specific transcript locators; no graph database or persisted Decision entity. Decisions are question-issue anchors. Current and historical views share one perspective-aware model. Recorded and inferred edges remain distinct; Session links require attributable evidence; explicit QA acceptance is part of the evidence lifecycle; explicit supersession/reconsideration is shown, while drift is never judged automatically. Implementation is split into small slices: existing core/current/history slices plus Decision-anchor, Decision-index, current-timeline, and historical-drift tasks.

title: Admission lock-release test intermittently stays busy
description:
A full parallel skills-core gate intermittently reports Trust::Busy after the fixture drops its deliberately held trust lock.

## Observed
2026-09-08 during C14 fixes, codex/01a07d34-4adb-7491-8d0a-3f23cd0796e1. User service run-p541680-i554028 / invocationaa5aa14aab1f4641a363eeb5492624bc, scripts/test-skills-core with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 (isolating louiselm-8zdb), outside ACP subreaper (2fb5 workaround). Library106 PASS/2 existing ignored; admission18 PASS/1 FAIL.
tests/admission.rs:423 a_held_trust_lock_refuses_activation_readers_and_other_writers: called Result::unwrap() on Err Trust(Busy("/tmp/.tmpzWrESZ/store/trust")).
Previous same-code parallel run passed this case (failed unrelated GPG witness case).

## Symptoms
The post-drop unlocked assertion intermittently fails, blocking the full gate.

## Root cause
UNKNOWN. tests/admission.rs:422 drops a raw fixture flock immediately before current(&store). Parallel fork may transiently retain that lock descriptor; related production protection explicitly unlocks in trust/persistence.rs. Prior browser descriptor fixture lesson louiselm-b7us suggests this hypothesis but is not proof. No production trust/locking code changed by current passkey fixes.

## Why it was not caught
Fixture assumes last descriptor closes synchronously in a parallel process-spawning test suite. Need captured ownership/timing evidence or deterministic fork-equivalent fixture before assigning cause.

## Fix direction
Diagnose raw fixture lock lifetime without weakening production Busy refusal or hiding concurrency regressions. Do not fix unrelated admission code during C14 work.

## Acceptance
- Deterministic reproduction establishes cause before correction.
- Parallel full suite passes with original lock-held refusal coverage and unlocked-after-release acceptance.
- No test skip, weakened security assertion, or production locking change without root-cause evidence.

## Not covered
Deferred outside two authorized passkey fixes; only diagnostic reruns now. Raw fixture data is disposable, no production trust mutation. Actual inherited descriptor holder not inspected/proved.

title: Investigate duplicate allow_always permission options
description:
## Observation

Screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260810_0558_1920x1200_1786334287.png` shows the LouiseLM command permission picker with four entries:

1. `allow_once`
2. `allow_always`
3. `allow_always`
4. `reject_once`

This appeared while running the commit/sync workflow in the Codex session.

## Question

Determine whether the two `allow_always` entries are intentional because they represent distinct permission scopes/operations, or whether the renderer is duplicating/collapsing distinct option labels.

## Acceptance criteria

- Trace the ACP permission options from the agent response through normalization and chat picker rendering.
- Identify the semantic difference between the two `allow_always` options, if any.
- If distinct, make the picker labels explain their scopes; if duplicate rendering is a bug, fix it.
- Add focused regression coverage for the resolved behavior.
- Preserve the existing allow/reject semantics.
close_reason: Confirmed duplicate allow_always entries are intentional: Codex uses distinct names and option IDs for session-scoped versus persistent permission grants. Fixed chat rendering to prefer ACP option names over generic kinds; added regression coverage. Verification: focused chat 31 passed; full mini.test suite 116 passed; stylua and lua-language-server passed.

title: :LouiselmForensicsView refuses a bare invocation with a raw E471
description:
`:LouiselmForensicsView` cannot be invoked the way a human reaches it -- immediately
after `:LouiselmForensics`, to read the record just written. It is declared
`nargs = 1`, so a bare call aborts with Neovim's own `E471: Argument required`, and
the only place the generated record path is ever shown is a transient INFO
notification from the collect command. The user must recover a 40-character
generated filename from a toast that has already faded, or list the state
directory by hand, to use the command at all.

## Observed

Manual QA round 2026-08-27, session `deepseek/session-5d380d32-0e8d-4396-afa4-82cc1ee5c4fb`,
HEAD `e0d27d8`, Neovim 0.12.5. Maintainer at the keyboard.

`:LouiselmForensics` succeeded and notified:

```
louiselm: Forensics record written to /home/lotso/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/forensics/1787796219-1787796219-265777660586430.json
```

The resource link was staged into the chat (`[context: forensics...]` visible).
`:LouiselmForensicsView` typed with no argument then failed with `E471: Argument
required`. The record itself is well-formed: 841 bytes, mode `0600`,
`schema_version: 1`, correct `subject.acp_session_id`, and truthful
`evidence_sources` (the `acp_log` source is honestly marked `omitted` with reason
"ACP adapter did not advertise a log path" -- verified correct, deepseek does not
route through the acp-llm-adapter proxy, so no log exists to point at).

## Symptoms

- Collect a Forensics record, try to read it, and the viewer refuses to open.
- The error is Neovim's raw `E471`, with no mention of Forensics, the expected
  argument, or where records live.
- The one command that names the path prints it to a notification; in a
  `snacks.notifier` configuration that toast is transient and is not recoverable
  from `:messages`.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:540-560`. The command is registered with
`{ nargs = 1, complete = "file" }`, so Neovim rejects a bare invocation before the
callback runs. The callback's own guard at `command.lua:541-545`:

```lua
local path = arguments.args
if path == "" then
  report_error("Forensics record path is required")
  return
end
```

is therefore unreachable dead code -- `nargs = 1` guarantees `args` is non-empty.
The intended friendly error can never be delivered.

`:LouiselmForensics` (`command.lua:523-538`) holds the path only long enough to
pass it to `nvim.notify`; nothing records a "last record" the viewer could default
to.

## Why it was not caught

The prior QA round (`louiselm-wnpd`, case 5) exercised collect + view + resource
link and passed, because the reviewer supplied the path explicitly. No test or
manual step covers the bare invocation, which is the way the command is actually
first reached. The unreachable `path == ""` branch also reads, to anyone skimming,
as though the no-argument case is handled.

## Fix direction

Narrowest correct fix: make the argument optional (`nargs = "?"`) and default to
the most recently written record for the current Session, which `:LouiselmForensics`
already knows. That makes the existing `path == ""` branch live and turns it into
a real fallback rather than dead code.

Rejected: keeping `nargs = 1` and only improving the error text -- it leaves the
common path (view what I just collected) requiring a copied 40-character filename.
Rejected: a picker over the state directory -- more surface than the problem needs;
revisit only if multi-record browsing is wanted.

## Acceptance

- A regression test that fails before the fix and passes after, invoking the
  command with no argument and asserting the most recent record opens.
- Live: `:LouiselmForensics` then `:LouiselmForensicsView` with no argument opens
  the record just written, with no `E471`.
- Invoking with no record ever collected reports a LouiseLM-worded error, not a
  raw Neovim one.

## Not covered

Whether the rendered buffer should be a readable human projection rather than the
raw JSON it currently shows (`readfile` + `buf_set_lines` + `filetype = "json"`,
`command.lua:546-560`) is deliberately out of scope here: that is louiselm-ce6.24's
own outstanding acceptance item, recorded as a comment there rather than duplicated
as a bug. Multi-record selection, records from a different Session than the current
one, and the behaviour when the state directory is unreadable are untested.
close_reason: done

title: Generation activation can report persistence failure after changing current supply
description:
Observed by source inspection while fixing louiselm-kcys, 2026-09-07; no live store mutation attempted. skills-core/src/admission.rs:411-418 writes the old Generation as Superseded, writes the new Generation as Current, then calls record_pin. A lineage write failure therefore returns AdmissionError::Io after changing current supply; retrying the same activation returns Rollback at :402. Failure writing the new record can also leave the previous record superseded with no current Generation. Module documentation :3-4 promises failures leave the prior Generation in force.

Reproduction for implementation: prepare two admitted and witnessed Generations through the public API; activate the first; replace pins.jsonl with a directory to force a deterministic lineage write error; activate the second and compare current/load state before and after. Exercise the second record write failure separately. Existing admission tests cover witness/rollback failures but not activation persistence failures.

Acceptance: a failed activation preserves the prior current Generation and supports retry after the I/O fault is removed; lineage never claims an uncommitted activation. Define and test crash durability and partial-write recovery using the existing persistence facilities. Deferred from kcys, whose scope is distinguishing NotFound from lineage read errors and preserving unreadable pin bytes; that guard alone does not make activation transactional.
close_reason: gate:skills-core/tests/admission.rs:267 — failed activation preserves prior supply and retries; journal rollback/restart tests and full Rust gates pass. Post-commit durability uncertainty is explicit and idempotently retryable.

comments.author: codex/01a07c87-f528-7231-9186-47431397275b
comments.text: Implementation scope: shared trust lock serializes Admission state readers/writers; a durable rollback journal covers prior/current Generation records and pins.jsonl. Recover interrupted writes before exposing state; remove and sync the journal only after all new files are durable. Ordinary pre-commit failure restores prior supply; rollback failure blocks reads until recovery succeeds. A post-commit directory-sync failure must explicitly report uncertain durability, following d6fv.11.1 comment 1057; retrying the same current digest confirms durability without adding another pin. No storage migration, new dependency, or activation authority change. Prior lessons: d6fv.11.1 comments 1056-1057; kcys regression retained. References: fsync(2) requires parent-directory sync; tempfile persist alone does not sync file/directory.

No real store touched.

title: Render a session transcript into an editable handoff prompt buffer
description:
## Goal
Render a live session's transcript into an editable buffer that becomes the first
prompt of another session, with nothing sent until the user submits.

## Scope
- In scope: turning `Transcript:snapshot()` entries into buffer text; opening it
  for editing; submitting the edited buffer as a prompt to a target session;
  abandoning it without sending.
- Out of scope: choosing the provider, creating the target session, and the
  user command -- all in the sibling task. This task is the payload half only.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given a session with recorded entries, a buffer is produced containing the
   transcript with full tool commands and results, not one-line summaries.
2. Nothing is sent to any session while the buffer is open.
3. Submitting sends exactly the buffer's current contents, so edits are honoured.
4. Abandoning the buffer sends nothing and leaves both sessions untouched.
5. An empty buffer refuses to send with an actionable message rather than
   prompting with nothing.

## Testing
Headless: entries in, buffer text out; edit-then-submit sends the edited text;
abandon sends nothing; empty refuses. Assert on the payload actually handed to
the session, not on buffer appearance.

## Notes
`lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua` (`snapshot`, `render`) and
`lua/louiselm/session/transcript_export.lua` already turn entries into markdown
untruncated; reuse rather than write a third renderer. Check whether
`Transcript.render` is directly usable before adding anything.

Reasoning is on the parent, louiselm-provider-handoff-3e2p. The review step is a
hard requirement, not a convenience: it is both the disclosure gate and the way a
wrong frame gets cut before it contaminates the second provider.
close_reason: Completed: added editable transcript handoff buffers with edit-and-submit, abandon, empty-input rejection, and cleanup; focused and full mini.test suites pass

title: Wire the provider handoff command and keep the source session attached
description:
## Goal
Wire the handoff command: pick a target provider, open a session on it, feed it
the reviewed transcript buffer, and leave the source session attached.

## Scope
- In scope: the user command and its error paths; the provider picker excluding
  the current agent; creating the target session through the existing
  `new_session` seeding path; handing the buffer from the sibling task to it;
  keeping the source session attached and switchable.
- Out of scope: rendering the buffer (sibling task), capability routing, and any
  automatic or policy-driven switching.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The command opens a picker of configured providers excluding the current one,
   and does nothing on dismissal.
2. The target session is created through the same path as `new_session`, so
   initial contexts, skill catalog, and instructions context are seeded, and the
   target provider's own `skills_policy` is applied rather than the source's.
3. The source session stays attached and reachable through the existing session
   switcher after the handoff.
4. Errors are distinct and actionable for: no chat session, an open permission
   decision, a non-idle source session, fewer than two configured providers, and
   target session creation failure.
5. A test proves a permission remembered for the source agent does not apply to
   the target agent.
6. No command, option, or user-facing string uses "model" to mean provider.
7. README documents the command in the interactive-controls list.

## Testing
Headless with the mock ACP agent configured twice under different names. Cover
each error branch, the dismissal path, source-session survival, and permission
isolation. Async paths must exercise the production callback context.

## Notes
Depends on the buffer task; wire against its interface rather than reimplementing
rendering.

Naming: the maintainer's earlier phrasing was `:LouiselmModelChange`, which was
the wrong word and cost a reverted implementation (louiselm-model-change-cl59,
db39f96). Repository convention is verb-first --- `LouiselmSwitchSession`,
`LouiselmRenameSession`, `LouiselmPickSkill` --- so something like
`:LouiselmSwitchProvider` or `:LouiselmHandOff` fits. Confirm the name with the
maintainer before implementing; do not infer it.

Reasoning is on the parent, louiselm-provider-handoff-3e2p.
close_reason: Wired :LouiselmHandOff end to end: picker excluding the current agent, target session created via the existing new_session seeding path, source stays attached/switchable, distinct errors for every listed case, permission isolation proven by test, README updated. See implementation-notes comment for file-level detail.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Command name confirmed with maintainer: :LouiselmHandOff. Rejected :LouiselmSwitchProvider -- the picker is over named agent config entries, not vendors; two entries can share a provider/binary and differ only in model (e.g. codex/Luna vs codex/Sol), so 'provider' would misdescribe what's being picked. 'Handoff' names the mechanic (hand the conversation to another configured entry) without asserting what changed underneath. PascalCase per repo convention (LouiselmSwitchSession, LouiselmPickSkill).

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Implementation notes: wired :LouiselmHandOff (chat:hand_off()) in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua and lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua. Reuses chat:new_session(agent_name) for target creation (same seeding path, target's own skills_policy applied) after resolving the target via a Picker.select excluding the source agent. Errors: disposed, open permission decision (DECISION_OPEN_ERROR), no chat session attached, non-idle source (status ~= ready or a queued prompt), fewer than two configured agents, and target creation failure (notified async in the picker callback, source untouched). Permission isolation across agents proven in tests/permission_spec.lua (store-level, per the parent's implementation decision that this needs no new mechanism, only a test). README documents the command. No 'model' wording anywhere. Full mini.test suite (351 cases), stylua --check, and lua-language-server all pass.

title: Improve :help louiselm: table of contents, working cross-links, code blocks, mappings
description:
`:help louiselm` is a flat wall of prose. It has no table of contents, one
cross-reference (which is broken), no code examples, no mappings section, and
74 lines wider than 78 columns. Neovim's help syntax and the vimdoc treesitter
parser give navigation and colour for free when the conventions are followed;
LouiseLM currently uses almost none of them.

The file is generated: `lua/louiselm/docs/vimdoc.lua` holds the prose in Lua
string literals and emits the Commands section from `nvim_get_commands`;
`lua/louiselm/schema/gen_vimdoc.lua` emits the Configuration section from the
normalized schema. All work lands in the emitters, never in `doc/louiselm.txt`
by hand. `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` already gates staleness in CI
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml:295`).

## Observed

- `doc/louiselm.txt:0` — no table of contents; a reader entering at `:help
  louiselm` cannot see that Sessions, Permissions, Commands or Configuration
  exist, or jump to them.
- `lua/louiselm/docs/vimdoc.lua:74` — the only `|link|` in 462 lines is
  ``|require('louiselm').setup()|``, and no such tag exists in `doc/tags` (79
  entries). It renders as a link and goes nowhere: `E149`.
- Prose names `:LouiselmChat`, `:LouiselmCancel`, `:LouiselmSessionNew`,
  `:LouiselmSessionSwitch`, `:LouiselmSessionId`, `:LouiselmPreflight` and
  `:checkhealth louiselm` as bare text. Every one of those has a tag already,
  or is a Neovim builtin tag; none is linked, so none is followable with
  `CTRL-]`.
- No code block anywhere. The Overview tells the reader to call
  `require('louiselm').setup()` and never shows a single working call. `>lua`
  fenced blocks are the thing the vimdoc parser injects real Lua highlighting
  into, so this is the same omission for colour and for usefulness.
- `lua/louiselm/docs/vimdoc.lua:12` — `heading()` pads the tag to a fixed
  start column of 62 instead of right-aligning its closing `*` at column 78.
  74 lines exceed 78 columns, the longest is 109
  (`*louiselm-config-context-instructions-file*`). In an 80-column window they
  wrap, which breaks both the alignment and the highlight run.
- No modeline. Every praised plugin doc ends with
  `vim:tw=78:ts=8:noet:ft=help:norl:` (see `.deps/mini.nvim/doc/mini-pick.txt`)
  so the file is highlighted when opened as a file, not only through `:help`.
- The 28 default keymaps in `lua/louiselm/ui/keymaps.lua:13` are undocumented.
  `louiselm-config-keymaps` says they can be turned off without ever saying
  what they are.

## Wanted

Reference docs worth imitating, all readable locally or from the runtime:
`.deps/mini.nvim/doc/mini-pick.txt` (echasnovski's generated docs — TOC,
dense `|links|`, `~` subheaders), `:help lua-guide` and `:help news` (Neovim
core's own `>lua` blocks and TOC), telescope.nvim (`*telescope.setup()*`
function-tag style), lazy.nvim.

1. **Table of contents.** A `louiselm-contents` section after the title,
   listing every section as a `|tag|` with a right-aligned label. Emitted from
   the same section list the body is emitted from, so it cannot drift.
2. **Dense cross-linking.** Every command, config key, and Neovim builtin
   named in prose becomes a `|link|`. Mechanically: the emitter knows the full
   tag set it just produced, so linking can be a pass over the prose against
   that set rather than hand-marked strings — that also makes a dangling link
   impossible to emit.
3. **A real `setup()` tag and anchor.** Add `*louiselm.setup()*` and make the
   existing reference point at it. Fix or delete the broken link either way.
4. **`>lua` examples.** Minimum: a complete `setup()` call with one Agent
   configured, in the Overview; a headless Session API example in its own
   section. These are what turn `:help louiselm` from a description into
   something a reader can paste.
5. **Use the colour conventions.** `~` subheaders inside long sections,
   `{arg}` for command and function parameters, `'option'` for Neovim options,
   `CTRL-]` for keys. These are free highlight groups that the file currently
   forfeits.
6. **Column discipline.** Right-align tags to 78, wrap at 78, and gate it: no
   emitted line may exceed 78 columns.
7. **Mappings section.** Emit `louiselm-mappings` from
   `lua/louiselm/ui/keymaps.lua`'s `DEFAULTS` table the same way Commands is
   emitted from `nvim_get_commands` — needs a read-only accessor, `DEFAULTS` is
   currently a file-local. Each row links to the command it invokes.
8. **Modeline** as the last line.

## Acceptance

- `:help louiselm` opens on a table of contents; `CTRL-]` on any entry lands on
  that section.
- Every `|link|` in the file resolves: a test asserts every `|...|` target
  appears as a `*...*` tag in the same file or is a known Neovim tag. This is
  the regression gate for the `E149` above.
- No emitted line exceeds 78 columns, asserted in the emitter tests.
- Commands, config keys and mappings are each reachable by their own tag:
  `:help :LouiselmChat`, `:help louiselm-config-skills-policy`,
  `:help louiselm-mappings`.
- At least one `>lua` block renders with Lua syntax highlighting (treesitter
  vimdoc injection) on the maintainer's Neovim.
- `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` passes with the regenerated file
  committed.

## Out of scope

`doc/api.md` and the LuaCATS appendix. This issue is the human-facing help
file only.
close_reason: live:claude/5eca63a9-a90c-4c2b-beae-009f373b0a1d maintainer confirmed :help louiselm renders after 2a166f8. Lesson routed to this issue's comment: the width assertion in tests/schema/gen_vimdoc_spec.lua exempted lines containing '*', which is every heading, so 74 overlong lines shipped past a green gate; exemption removed, gate now real. No instruction change warranted - agent-testing.md already says green tests are not evidence a gate fires.

comments.author: claude/5eca63a9-a90c-4c2b-beae-009f373b0a1d
comments.text:
Implemented. Evidence, all from a clean tree:

- `doc/louiselm.txt`: 0 lines over 78 columns (was 74, longest 109); `doc/tags`
  grew 79 -> 83 (`louiselm-contents`, `louiselm.setup()`, `louiselm-mappings`,
  `louiselm-api`).
- Links: 1 -> 60, all resolving. `lua/louiselm/docs/vimdoc.lua:M.generate`
  errors on any `|link|` that is neither a tag it emitted nor a declared
  external tag, so the `E149` class is unreachable, not just fixed.
  `M.EXTERNAL_TAGS` (`:checkhealth`, `mapleader`) is itself checked against
  `$VIMRUNTIME/doc/tags` in the suite.
- `>lua` blocks: headless treesitter parse of the rendered help reports
  injected languages `vimdoc,lua,lua`, so both examples get real Lua
  highlighting.
- The Overview example is `M.setup_example()`, a table the suite runs through
  `Schema.validate(Config.schema, ...)` and then renders to Lua source. A
  documented configuration `setup()` would reject now fails the suite.
- Mappings are emitted from `louiselm.ui.keymaps.defaults()` (new accessor,
  returns a copy), each row linking to the command it runs.
- `lua/louiselm/docs/vimdoc_text.lua` is new: the width, heading-alignment,
  wrapping and link primitives both generators now share. It fixes the root
  cause of the overflow, which was two copies of a `heading()` that padded to
  a fixed start column instead of right-aligning to 78.
- `tests/schema/gen_vimdoc_spec.lua` had a width assertion that skipped any
  line containing `*` - i.e. every heading. That exemption is removed; it is
  what let all 74 overlong lines through.

Gates: full MiniTest suite 0 fails, `stylua --check .`,
`lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning` (no problems),
`generate-vimdoc --check`, `generate-api-appendix --check`,
`generate-luacats --check` all pass.

Open acceptance: the maintainer confirming the `>lua` block renders coloured
in their own Neovim and colourscheme.

comments.text: Correction to the comment above: the link count is 55, not 60. Counted with the emitter's own pattern over the committed file; the 60 was unverified.

title: Beads inspector opens too short to read long descriptions
description:
Pressing <leader>lB opens a shallow Beads inspector that leaves most of a long description out of view despite substantial available editor height. The maintainer wants a broader view on opening, comparable in readability to br show. P2: degraded inspection with a CLI workaround.

## Observed

Maintainer screenshot, 2026-09-07 10:28 Europe/Paris:
 /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260907_1028_1920x1200_1788769708.png

Inspected directly during Session codex/01a07753-51de-7733-bfeb-8a3f26fa907e. Left: <leader>lB on louiselm-b1sk, eight content rows showing title, metadata, and only the beginning of the description. Right: br show louiselm-b1sk presents the readable paragraph and further issue context. Most editor height below the float is unused.

Reproduce: in a LouiseLM chat buffer, place the cursor on louiselm-b1sk and press <leader>lB; compare with br show louiselm-b1sk in an adjacent terminal. Its description is one long stored line. At filing time the live editor reports 93 columns, 48 rows, and no remaining float; screenshot dimensions are 1920x1200, not Neovim cell dimensions.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:111-122 constructs seven heading/metadata rows plus newline-split description rows.
lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:139-140 sets width to at most 100 columns and height to math.min(#lines, math.max(1, nvim.o.lines - 4)).
Thus a one-paragraph description gets an eight-row float regardless of paragraph length. Height counts logical lines, not displayed rows. open_issue does not explicitly choose wrapping; the exact screenshot wrap setting was not captured.

## Why it was not caught

tests/ui/beads_spec.lua:101-145 uses the short description "Add blank lines." and verifies buffer text, scheduling and close mapping. No height/width/wrapping regression covers a long single-paragraph description.

## Fix direction

Adjust sizing and text presentation at open_issue so existing description content is readable on opening and available editor space is used when needed. Bound the float to the editor; retain scrolling for overflow and q/<Esc> dismissal. Do not require users to insert newlines into issue descriptions.

## Acceptance

- In the screenshot scenario, opening louiselm-b1sk shows its complete description without immediate scrolling when sufficient space exists, using a substantially taller readable view.
- Long paragraphs wrap readably; small editors remain bounded with overflow accessible.
- A headless behavioral regression uses a long single-line paragraph and fails against the current layout; also cover short content and constrained editor sizes.
- Preserve asynchronous lookup, read-only content and dismissal; maintainer confirms the original live reproduction before closure.

## Not covered

Missing comments, dependents and other fields are already tracked by louiselm-beads-inspector-drops-comments-atrv; height alone will not restore them. These are related defects with separate causes, not blockers for one another.

Tracking only at maintainer request. Implementation and live acceptance are deferred; no code changed or tests run.

title: Publish curated LouiseLM docs and blog at louiselm.com
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM's source repository is private, GitHub Pages is unavailable for it, and the self-hosted GitLab Pages path is not operational. The existing MyST blog also uses private full-session transcripts as authoring inputs, so publishing the wrong directory could expose prompts, tool payloads, paths, or credentials.

## Solution

Publish one curated static site at louiselm.com with documentation under /docs and posts under /blog. Build an explicit public artifact from the private repository, deploy only that artifact to Firebase Hosting from protected GitLab CI through Workload Identity Federation, and keep the dedicated LouiseLM application project separate from the bartab-dns DNS control project.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want current installation, tutorial, workflow, and API documentation at a stable public URL.
2. As a reader, I want curated posts without access to raw Session transcripts or repository-only evidence.
3. As the maintainer, I want previewable, repeatable deployments from the private GitLab repository without stored Google credentials.
4. As the operator, I want a staged custom-domain cutover with managed TLS and a tested rollback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A strict MyST build produces a single artifact with a landing page, /docs routes, and /blog routes from canonical repository sources.
2. The artifact contains no raw transcript directories, JSONL, OpenTofu state or plan files, environment files, or unlisted authoring source; MyST may expose Markdown copies of the same explicitly curated pages it renders as HTML.
3. A reviewed OpenTofu plan provisions Firebase Hosting and narrowly scoped protected-main deployment identity in the dedicated deletion-protected LouiseLM project, using locked remote state.
4. Protected GitLab CI validates every site change and deploys only the built artifact to the generated Firebase hostname without a stored Google key.
5. louiselm.com serves the verified artifact over managed TLS after a separately approved DNS change; rollback can restore the previous Hosting release without changing state.
6. A second OpenTofu plan after bootstrap reports no infrastructure changes.

## Implementation Notes

- Keep generated Hosting releases and site objects out of OpenTofu state; OpenTofu owns durable cloud configuration and IAM, while CI owns content releases.
- Keep bartab-dns-20260802 limited to DNS. Adding Firebase to the DNS control project is explicitly rejected because it creates irreversible project-level coupling.
- Reuse the existing pinned MyST and GitLab WIF patterns.
- Raw Session exports remain private authoring inputs. Only deliberately selected excerpts may appear in rendered pages.

## Testing Notes

- Run strict MyST builds and inspect the deploy artifact structurally.

title: MyST cache republishes documents removed from the public TOC
description:
The public-site build cleaned only `_build/html`, leaving MyST's intermediate `_build/site` graph intact. A document removed from the public table of contents therefore remained in the next supposedly clean deploy artifact.

## Observed

During the 2026-09-04 site implementation, `CONTRIBUTING.md` stopped linking to the private `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md` was explicitly excluded in `myst.yml`, and a new strict build no longer exposed an AGENTS route. Nevertheless `_build/html/build/AGENTS-<hash>.md` was copied again and the artifact gate rejected it. `_build/site` still existed because `scripts/build-site` ran `myst clean --html --yes`.

## Symptoms

- A source removed from public navigation/dependencies can remain directly downloadable.
- A build can publish stale content that no longer exists in the reviewed public source graph.
- Raw internal/operator documentation can cross the intended artifact boundary.

## Root cause

MyST keeps the parsed site content graph separately from final HTML. `myst clean --html` removes only the latter; rebuilding reused stale `_build/site` content.

## Fix direction

Clean both MyST site content and final HTML before every production build, while retaining downloaded templates to avoid network-only cold builds. Keep the artifact allowlist as the independent final gate.

## Acceptance

- Build once with a linked private fixture, remove its link, build again, and prove the private export is absent.
- The real build contains no AGENTS export, Session ID, or conversation directory.
- The strict MyST build and artifact gate pass.

## Not covered

Content review of intentionally public pages remains a human/code-review responsibility.
close_reason: Stale MyST content is purged and independently rejected. gate:scripts/check-public-artifact

Green: build-site cleans --site and --html; the rebuilt 11-page artifact has no AGENTS export or Session IDs, and the final gate byte-compares every Markdown export with a curated source. Lesson routed to scripts/build-site, scripts/check-public-artifact, and CONTRIBUTING.md; no new AGENTS.md rule or design question warranted.

title: Custom-domain import crashes OpenTofu tests
description:
Adding a declarative import block for the already-created Firebase custom domain makes every native mock-provider test crash OpenTofu 1.12.3 instead of producing a test result.

## Observed

Session `codex/01a06a99-3443-7843-b88d-52c47007cd42`, 2026-09-04, OpenTofu 1.12.3, google/google-beta 7.40.0. `tofu validate` passes, then `tofu test -no-color -filter=tests/project_parent.tftest.hcl` exits 1 with:

> OpenTofu crashed!
> Importing is not supported in testing context. providerForTest must not be used to call ImportResourceState

The stack enters `NodePlannableResourceInstance.importState` for the new custom-domain import block.

## Symptoms

- All 17 static infrastructure tests become unusable.
- CI would crash before validating the custom-domain boundary.

## Root cause

OpenTofu 1.12.3 test execution cannot evaluate a root import block against mocked providers.

## Why it was not caught

The existing configuration had no import blocks, so the credential-free mock test path never exercised this OpenTofu limitation.

## Fix direction

Keep the managed custom-domain resource and remove the declarative import block. Perform the single reviewed state import after merge, then require a zero-diff plan. Avoid disabling mock tests.

## Acceptance

- The custom-domain test fails before the resource exists and passes with it.
- The full native suite completes without a crash.
- The live domain association is imported once after merge and a fresh plan is empty.

## Not covered

This does not change DNS records, Hosting content, or the OpenTofu runtime version.
close_reason: gate:infra/firebase/tests/project_parent.tftest.hcl:164 — 17 tests pass; live import is managed and final plan exits 0.

Fix: remove import block; keep managed resource and perform one reviewed CLI import after merge. Green: fmt/validate, 17/17 native tests, tflint, Trivy 0, diff-check. Live state import and zero-diff plan remain before close.

Import advanced state without resource mutation; deletion policy normalized to PREVENT. Final plan at main 3786246 returns detailed-exitcode 0, state serial 17/generation 1788536524021554, no live lock. Lesson routing: issue-local—OpenTofu 1.12.3 import blocks cannot coexist with mock-provider tests; use reviewed one-time CLI import.

title: Custom-domain timestamp keeps plans dirty
description:
The new custom-domain output exports Firebase's computed DNS check timestamp, so every refresh produces an output-only diff and the required zero-drift plan can never return 0.

## Observed

Session `codex/01a06a99-3443-7843-b88d-52c47007cd42`, 2026-09-04, OpenTofu 1.12.3, google-beta 7.40.0, after importing and protecting `google_firebase_hosting_custom_domain.public`.

A fresh `tofu plan -detailed-exitcode` exits 2 with no resource changes:

> hosting_custom_domain_dns_updates.check_time = "2026-09-04T15:34:54.261437344Z" -> "2026-09-04T15:36:24.478848295Z"
> You can apply this plan to save these new output values ... without changing any real infrastructure.

No apply followed.

## Symptoms

- Every operator plan appears dirty despite zero infrastructure drift.
- Idempotence acceptance is blocked by a polling timestamp.

## Root cause

`infra/firebase/outputs.tf` exposes the provider's full `required_dns_updates` object, including volatile `check_time`.

## Why it was not caught

Mock tests cannot know computed DNS updates, and the pre-import plan did not have the resource state needed to expose the timestamp churn.

## Fix direction

Delete the unneeded aggregate output. Operators can inspect the managed resource when DNS records are needed; do not persist volatile provider observations as root outputs.

## Acceptance

- Fresh plan contains only removal of the stale output and no resource actions.
- After exact state-only apply, another detailed-exitcode plan returns 0.

## Not covered

No Firebase custom-domain or DNS record mutation is needed for this fix.
close_reason: live:codex/01a06a99-3443-7843-b88d-52c47007cd42 — output-only cleanup applied; fresh plan exits 0.

comments.text: Red: post-import detailed-exitcode plan returned 2 solely because required_dns_updates.check_time advanced. Fix: delete volatile root output; managed custom-domain resource remains. Green plan has zero resource actions and exactly one output deletion. Gates: 17/17 tests, validate, tflint, Trivy 0, diff-check. Keep open until merged state-only apply and exit-0 plan.

Fresh plan returns detailed-exitcode 0; state serial 17/generation 1788536524021554, no live lock. Lesson routing: issue-local—do not expose provider polling timestamps as durable root outputs.

title: TFLint cold cache hits GitHub rate limit
description:
The mandatory `tf-tflint` MR gate can fail before linting because the pinned component installs plugins anonymously from GitHub on a branch-specific cold cache and exhausts the runner's shared-IP API rate limit.

## Observed

GitLab pipeline 38903, job 143941, commit 09147fa, 2026-09-04:

> GITHUB_TOKEN is not provided: anonymously access to API. Beware of rate limits
> Failed to download artifact attestations ... 403 API rate limit exceeded for 92.88.75.50

The job saved its partially populated branch cache after failing. Local tflint and all other CI gates pass.

## Symptoms

- Unrelated merge requests turn red without running TFLint.
- Retrying may pass from runner-local cache but does not remove the cold-cache failure.

## Root cause

The TBC default config downloads AWS, Azure, and Google TFLint plugins from GitHub with no authenticated token. Cache keys are branch-specific and the shared runner IP consumes GitHub's anonymous quota.

## Why it was not caught

Warm prior branch caches hid the remote bootstrap dependency; CI does not test cold-cache behavior.

## Fix direction

Configure only the Google ruleset used by this GCP stack and provide an authenticated, least-privilege download path or immutable prebuilt lint image. Do not weaken the mandatory lint gate.

## Acceptance

- A cold-cache `tf-tflint` run installs only required pinned plugins without anonymous rate-limit failure.
- The lint result remains mandatory.

## Not covered

Retrying job 143941 is a delivery workaround, not the fix.
close_reason: gate:GitLab job 143961 cold-cache install and lint passed without GITHUB_TOKEN; lesson routed to issue comment 826.

comments.author: codex/01a06a99-3443-7843-b88d-52c47007cd42
comments.text: Root fix: pin TFLint 0.64.0 image and Google ruleset 0.39.0; install the attestation-verified linux_amd64 archive from its immutable release URL with committed SHA-256 e5034d2c. Cold install passed checksum; tflint --init and recursive lint passed with --network none and no GITHUB_TOKEN. Avoids exposing the local gh token (repo/read:org/admin:public_key/gist) to the shared runner.

title: Beads actor lookup follows focused chat instead of requesting Agent
description:
Concurrent Sessions can be attributed to the wrong Agent if they follow the AGENTS.md live Chat recipe after the maintainer switches the visible chat.

## Observed
2026-09-07, current codex/01a07753-51de-7733-bfeb-8a3f26fa907e. CODEX_THREAD_ID and CODEX_SESSION_ID both explicitly expose 01a07753-51de-7733-bfeb-8a3f26fa907e. The documented controller session_id() query initially matched, then returned codex/01a07a69-570c-76f3-a70c-611df3c03f1a while the same task kept running. A read-only lookup of chat.views matching the current adapter ID returned {actor:codex/01a07753-51de-7733-bfeb-8a3f26fa907e,status:prompting,focused_actor:codex/01a07a70-6a45-7930-a5bd-ae78def5c53a}. No historical inventory or old Beads actor was used to choose the current identity.

## Root cause
lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3709 session_id() reads self.current_id and is correct for the visible UI, not caller identity. AGENTS.md recommends that focus-dependent value as authoritative for every running ACP Agent. Focus can change independently of a requesting Agent.

## Why not caught
The recipe assumes a single focused Session. Tests of the UI accessor do not establish caller attribution during concurrent Sessions.

## Acceptance
A documented or tested lookup resolves the requesting Agent from current interaction identity and its matching live Session without changing focus. Switching the visible chat cannot change the actor. No stable caller ID or ambiguous match must require clarification, never selection of an arbitrary Session.

## Deferral
Outside d6fv.11.4. Existing workaround in this run: current explicit CODEX_THREAD_ID/CODEX_SESSION_ID plus exact matching live Chat view, still prompting. No runtime or AGENTS.md fix made; no claim transfer needed or performed.
notes: 2026-09-07 confirmed claim collision on louiselm-lus3: current CODEX_THREAD_ID/CODEX_SESSION_ID=01a07bb4-738e-7ad1-bd47-f351e01a2d3f; documented live Chat lookup returned codex/01a07bb4-c41e-7010-8332-d9a6ff731e2c. This Session then claimed the open issue at 11:51:42Z using that wrong actor and authored comment 1200. The other Session resumed as the same actor (comment 1201) and both implemented concurrently. Current Session discovered its identity mismatch when the other SQLite module appeared; lus3 comments 1202/1203 confirm the other execution paused. Maintainer explicitly requests a bug report and selects 738e to continue. Claim protection cannot distinguish two executions presenting the same actor; no evidence yet of br accepting a different live assignee. Acceptance must include two Sessions attempting the same task: focus changes must not alias actors, and a second distinct actor must be refused by claim. Existing UI lookup is lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3782; AGENTS.md incorrectly elevates focused Chat over caller identity. Deferred implementation while completing lus3; current actor cross-checked against its matching live view.
close_reason: consumer:lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua identity() resolves the caller, not the focused chat; live:claude/19710d4e-99bd-4e2e-9f24-8eb6059ee9b5 maintainer confirmed both focus directions with two concurrent Sessions

title: QA round: automatic Provenance transcript lookup
description:
