title: Grill-me needed: How should Agent account limits cross the pure-ACP boundary?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; run a focused design decision before implementing account-limit transport.

Question:
How should structured Provider account-limit state reach LouiseLM while preserving the core pure-ACP boundary and enabling both Codex and, where possible, Claude?

Context and evidence:
- The accepted human UX contract is recorded on louiselm-u56l.
- The core epic louiselm-ce6 says LouiseLM is a pure ACP client and that non-ACP capabilities arrive through external bridges, never in-plugin Provider adapters.
- Codex App Server provides account/rateLimits/read and account/rateLimits/updated with the required structured data.
- Installed @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.2 receives and caches that structured data but exposes it only as rendered /status text, not as a structured ACP event.
- Parsing /status would bind behavior to prose and is rejected.
- Starting a Codex App Server sidecar inside LouiseLM would provide data quickly but introduces a Provider protocol into the pure ACP client and does not generalize to Claude.
- A provider-neutral structured ACP extension emitted by external Agent adapters would preserve the boundary and give Codex and Claude a shared normalized contract, but requires adapter work and a clear capability negotiation/fallback rule.

Threads worth pulling:
- Standard ACP extension mechanism versus a LouiseLM-namespaced method or session update.
- Capability advertisement and behavior for Agents that do not implement account limits.
- Whether the external adapter normalizes Provider data or forwards a lossless Provider payload.
- Ownership and deduplication when several Sessions share one Agent or account.
- Versioning, validation, sparse updates, and compatibility with other ACP clients.
- Which repository owns the codex-acp and Claude adapter changes and how LouiseLM tests them deterministically.

Decision boundary:
Choose the cross-process contract and ownership. Human UX is already decided. AX and automated switching policy remain separate follow-up work.
close_reason: Maintainer accepted a capability-advertised, provider-neutral ACP custom extension owned by external Agent adapters.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: 2026-08-24 protocol finding: ACP v1 officially supports extension methods. Custom request and notification names must start with underscore, unrecognized notifications are ignored, and extensions should advertise support in agentCapabilities._meta. Source: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/extensibility. LouiseLM already preserves the agentCapabilities table and its ACP transport can send arbitrary request methods and receive arbitrary notifications; session lifecycle currently ignores non-session/update notifications. codex-acp uses the ACP SDK custom-handler path already for other extensions, and its schema preserves _meta, so adding a limits extension is structurally supported. Recommended boundary: external Agent adapters advertise a versioned provider-neutral account-limits capability, answer an underscore-prefixed read request, and emit an underscore-prefixed updated notification. The adapter owns Provider-specific parsing and sparse-update merging, and sends a complete normalized snapshot. LouiseLM validates snapshots and owns Agent-level freshness, UI, notification deduplication and source failover across live Sessions. This preserves the pure-ACP core, avoids /status parsing and sidecars, and lets a Claude adapter implement the same contract. Stock codex-acp 1.6.2 must be changed before the live Codex slice can work.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: Decision accepted by maintainer: use the official ACP custom-extension mechanism. External Agent adapters advertise a versioned Provider-neutral account-limits capability in agentCapabilities._meta, answer an underscore-prefixed read request and emit an underscore-prefixed update notification. Adapters own Provider parsing and sparse-patch merging and emit complete normalized snapshots. LouiseLM remains a pure ACP client and owns validation, Agent-level source selection/state, freshness, UX and notification deduplication. Incubate under a collision-resistant LouiseLM namespace; pursue ACP standardization separately only if broader adoption warrants it. No sidecar and no rendered-text parsing. Lesson routing: this decision is already enforced by parent epic louiselm-ce6 pure-ACP boundary and the child feature; no duplicate AGENTS.md rule is warranted now.

title: Start louiselm chat input in insert mode
description:
## Goal

When opening a `louiselmchat`, place the cursor directly after the `>` prompt and enter insert mode so the user can start typing immediately.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Opening a `louiselmchat` positions the cursor immediately after the visible `>` prompt.
2. The chat buffer enters insert mode automatically.
3. The user can type and submit a message without manually moving the cursor or entering insert mode.
4. Existing chat rendering, prompt behavior, and non-chat buffers are unchanged.
5. Add or update a headless behavioral test for the initial mode and cursor position, if the current test harness supports it.
close_reason: Implemented prompt cursor placement and automatic insert mode when a chat UI is opened. Added headless cursor coverage; full MiniTest suite, StyLua, and lua-language-server checks pass.

title: QA round: session filetype, collapsed tool blocks, blog wiring
description:
# Manual QA review — session filetype, collapsed tool blocks, blog wiring

**Round closed 2026-08-20.** All ten cases (0–9) run. Six findings, two fixed
and verified during the round, four filed and deliberately left open. This is
the round's sole durable record; the working file it was written in has been
deleted, per `louiselm-ri1`.

**Build under test:** `ec19281..HEAD` (15 commits). The ones with testable
behaviour:

| Commit    | What changed                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `6167df0` | writefile errors in `Chat:to_markdown` (re-verify, `louiselm-dim`)   |
| `14dbab6` | tool-call blocks collapse to `<details>` in the markdown export      |
| `f0b4d9c` | blog fragments wired into built pages (re-verify, `louiselm-xrf`)    |
| `cd37ab2` | chat buffer filetype `markdown` → `louiselm-session` + explicit TS   |

Doc/bookkeeping only, nothing to test: `ec86d89`, `a515c01`, `e9d801a`,
`3140b93`, `b1f2781`, `a8af349`, `10ba83c`, `e0c6269`, `0d53644`, `9856288`,
`cd47617`.

**Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: the last round (`louiselm-vj0`) closed on build `4e4a58b`/`674939b` and
produced two fixes that were never re-driven by hand. Since then the chat
buffer's filetype changed under every filetype-keyed plugin the user has
installed, and the export format grew raw HTML — both changes whose real
consequences live entirely outside the test process.

## Status

| #   | Case                                                        | State                          |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| 0   | `stylua --check .` on a clean tree                          | **found a defect** — see F1    |
| 1   | image.nvim no longer attaches to the transcript             | **PASS** — 1.1/1.2/1.3 all confirmed, see below |
| 2   | Markdown highlighting survived the filetype change          | **PASS** — `:Inspect` shows `markdown` + `markdown_inline` captures |
| 3   | What else was keyed on `filetype=markdown`                  | **PASS** — options identical in both buffers, nothing lost |
| 4   | `:LouiselmToMarkdown` into a missing directory (re-verify)  | **PASS** — clean notification, no E482; `louiselm-euj` reconfirmed |
| 5   | Collapsed tool blocks in a real export                      | **2 defects, both fixed and re-verified** (`a6484ea`, `3d6557d`) — F4, F5 |
| 6   | `:lines: 1` placeholder fails loudly                        | **PASS** — exit 1 naming `blog.md:5`, nothing written, `myst.yml` untouched |
| 7   | Fragment reaches the built page, in a browser (re-verify)   | **PASS** — wiring verified, page looks right; width prediction refuted |
| 8   | Same under `myst start`, not just `myst build`              | **PASS** — excerpt renders in the dev server too |
| 9   | Re-run idempotency in the real repo                         | **found a defect** — see F6 (`louiselm-qcq`); `blog.md`/`myst.yml` stable, fragment is not |

## What the test suite already covers — skip these

- `render_entry`'s exact `<sub>`/`<details>` output and block ordering
  (`tests/session/transcript_spec.lua`), and the same assertions end-to-end
  through the file (`tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua`).
- `Chat:to_markdown` returning `nil, "could not write markdown file: ..."` for a
  missing destination directory — the new test added by `6167df0`. Case 4 only
  covers what the *command* shows the user, which no test reaches.
- Buffer filetype is not the literal `markdown`, and a treesitter highlighter is
  active on the chat buffer (`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`, both added by `cd37ab2`).
  They prove the two assertions in isolation; they cannot see any third-party
  plugin, which is the entire point of the change.
- Fragment bytes matching an independent TOhtml capture, three-way idempotency
  (fragments/blog.md/myst.yml), excerpt removal cleanup, and a real
  `myst build --html --strict` producing a page that references the fragment
  (`blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh`, parts 1–3). Cases 7–9 are what that
  suite structurally cannot reach: a browser, the dev server, and this repo's
  own `myst.yml` rather than a synthetic fixture root.
- Scaffold shape and marker-comment stubbing (`test-create-blog.sh`).

Baseline for this round: the full `mini.test` suite is green (0 fails, 0 notes)
at `cd37ab2`. `stylua --check .` is not — see F1.

## Setup

The installed plugin clone is already at `cd37ab2`, same as the repo, so there
is nothing to update before starting. Confirm and restart nvim:

```bash
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim log --oneline -1
git -C ~/code/louiselm log --oneline -1
```

After any fix I commit mid-round:

```vim
:lua vim.pack.update({ 'louiselm.nvim' })
```

then `:write` the buffer it opens, restart nvim, and re-confirm both commits
match.

Cases 7–9 need `nvim`, `node` (v24.16.0 here, CI pins node:24) and `myst`
(v1.10.1) on PATH — all three confirmed present.

Throughout, `<bufnr>` means the transcript buffer's number. Get it with
`:lua =vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()` while the transcript window is focused.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Carried from `louiselm-vj0` / `docs/example-workflow.md`: when the round runs
  inside louiselm's own session, the ACP log covers the whole conversation, not
  the turn being examined. Restrict the log's tool-call ids to the prefix ending
  at the last id that also appears in the export before diffing.
- Cases 1–3 share one open session on purpose (a fresh transcript has too
  little content for the perf question). Cases 4 and 5 are independent; run
  them in whatever order suits.
- Case 7 writes into `blog/` and `blog/myst.yml` in the real repo. That is
  deliberate — a fixture root is what the automated test already does — but see
  Cleanup, and do not commit any of it.
- **`:messages` is the wrong place to look for any louiselm notification on this
  machine.** louiselm surfaces user-facing errors and successes through
  `vim.notify`; snacks.nvim replaces `vim.notify` with `Snacks.notifier`, which
  renders floating windows and keeps its own history. Nothing it shows lands in
  `:messages`. Use `:lua Snacks.notifier.show_history()` (`<leader>n`) for every
  case in this file that expects a notification — 4, 5 and 6 all do. Cost of
  learning this the hard way: one round of case 4 where the expected evidence
  could not have appeared no matter what the code did.

## Cases

### 0. `stylua --check .` on a clean tree

Already run by me, before handing this over. Recorded here so the round's record
is complete.

```bash
git status --porcelain    # was empty at the time
stylua --check .; echo "exit=$?"
```

Result: `exit=1`, one diff, in `blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua`. See F1. The
tree is no longer clean after this — filing F1 wrote `.beads/issues.jsonl`, and
this file is untracked. Neither affects any case below.

### 1. image.nvim no longer attaches to the transcript

Exercises `cd37ab2` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1366`.

This is the whole reason the commit exists, and nothing in-process can assert
it. Parts 1.1–1.3 share one session; do not restart between them.

**1.1** "Transcript" here just means the conversation text that accumulates in
the louiselm window — header, then every user turn, assistant reply and tool
call, then the `> ` input line at the bottom. It is all **one buffer** (see
`Chat:attach`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1376-1378`), so the input line is
part of it too and you do not have to aim at a particular window: anywhere in
the louiselm window is the right place to stand.

So there is nothing to set up. Just use louiselm normally for a few turns —
ideally ones where the agent runs tools, since tool payloads are what make the
buffer grow fast — until it is long enough to scroll through. Length is the
whole point: a per-keystroke rescan costs nothing on a three-line buffer, which
is why a fresh session cannot show this bug.

Then, with the cursor anywhere in that louiselm window:

```vim
:lua =vim.bo[vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()].filetype
```

Expect: `louiselm-session`.

Failure signature: `markdown` — the fix did not reach the running copy, stop and
redo Setup.

**1.2** With the transcript window still focused (nothing to substitute — the
command reads the current buffer itself):

```vim
:lua =vim.iter(vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds({ buffer = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf() })):map(function(a) return a.event .. " / " .. (a.group_name or "-") end):totable()
```

Expect: no entry whose group name mentions `image`.

Failure signature: an `image.nvim`-ish group is still bound to the buffer, which
would mean it keys off something other than filetype and the fix targeted the
wrong mechanism.

**1.3** Type a sentence into the input line at a normal speed, in a session with
that long transcript loaded.

Expect: no perceptible per-keystroke lag.

Failure signature: the stutter you originally reported. If it is still there,
say so before we theorise — the mechanism check in 1.2 passing while 1.3 fails
would mean the cause was never image.nvim.

Optional, only if 1.3 is ambiguous — the A/B that settles it:

```bash
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim stash list   # expect empty
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim checkout 14dbab6
```

restart, reproduce the same transcript, type, then
`git -C ... checkout cd37ab2` and restart again. Tell me if you do this so I
know which build a later case ran against.

### 2. Markdown highlighting survived the filetype change

Exercises `cd37ab2` / the `nvim.treesitter.start(buffer, "markdown")` line.

`vim.treesitter.start` is called unprotected, so a missing parser would throw
inside `Chat:attach` and take the whole attach down. Your nvim (0.12.2) bundles
the markdown parser — I confirmed that outside the test — so this case is about
appearance, not availability.

With the transcript focused:

```vim
:lua =vim.treesitter.highlighter.active[vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()] ~= nil
```

Expect: `true`.

Then put the cursor on a word *inside* a fenced code block in the transcript and:

```vim
:Inspect
```

Expect: treesitter captures listed, sourced from the `markdown` (and, inside
inline spans, `markdown_inline`) parser.

Also just look at it: headings distinct, fences distinct, inline code distinct —
the same as before the change.

Failure signature: `:Inspect` reports no treesitter captures, or the transcript
renders as flat, uncoloured text — highlighting was lost along with the
filetype, and the explicit `treesitter.start` did not take.

**Result: PASS.** `:Inspect` returned captures under a `Treesitter` heading from
both parsers — `@spell.markdown` (language `markdown`) and
`@markup.raw.markdown_inline` / `@nospell.markdown_inline` (language
`markdown_inline`). Both matter: the second shows the markdown parser's
injections are running, not just the outer parser, so fenced and inline code
still highlight. `cd37ab2`'s explicit `nvim.treesitter.start(buffer, "markdown")`
fully replaces what `filetype=markdown` used to provide here.

**Result for case 1: PASS on all three parts**, with raw evidence from
`:messages`:

```
"louiselm-session"     <- 1.1, filetype
{}                     <- 1.2, buffer-local autocmds
true                   <- case 2, treesitter highlighter active
```

1.2 is stronger than the case asked for. The list is **empty**, not merely free
of an image.nvim group: the transcript buffer has no buffer-local autocmds
bound to it at all. Since attaching to a buffer is how image.nvim registers its
per-buffer work, that is a categorical negative rather than a name-matching one.
1.3 (no perceptible lag on a long buffer) is the tester's own observation, which
is the only way that part can be judged.

### 3. What else was keyed on `filetype=markdown`

Exercises `cd37ab2`'s blast radius. No test can see your config; this is the
case most likely to find a real regression.

First, list what a *real* markdown buffer gets:

```vim
:enew
:setfiletype markdown
:lua =vim.iter(vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds({ event = "FileType", pattern = "markdown" })):map(function(a) return (a.group_name or "-") .. ": " .. (a.desc or "(no desc)") end):totable()
```

Then compare the options that actually landed, real markdown buffer vs
transcript buffer:

```vim
:lua =vim.tbl_map(function(o) return o .. "=" .. tostring(vim.opt_local[o]:get()) end, { "wrap", "linebreak", "conceallevel", "spell", "textwidth", "foldmethod" })
```

Run that once in the scratch markdown buffer, once with the transcript focused,
and send me both.

Expect: the differences are things you do not want in a live transcript.

Failure signature: something you *do* want is now missing — soft wrap, conceal,
spell, a keymap, a rendering plugin. Any such item is a finding: the fix traded
one plugin's cost for another's absence, and the trade needs to be deliberate.

**Partial result.** The blast radius is far smaller than assumed. Exactly one
autocmd is registered against `FileType markdown`:

```
MystMarkdownFiletype: Override markdown filetype if MyST content detected
```

from `myst-markdown-tree-sitter.nvim` (`~/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/myst-markdown.lua`).
Nothing else keys on the filetype — the config's own treesitter autocmd uses
`pattern = "*"` and so still fires on `louiselm-session`, which is why case 2
passed. render-markdown.nvim is **not** active: it appears in
`nvim-pack-lock.json` pointing at a local checkout, but no config loads it, and
it registered no autocmd. (An earlier note in this file claiming otherwise was
wrong — it was inferred from a stale `render-markdown.log` dated Aug 3.)

**Result: PASS.** The two readings are byte-identical:

```
markdown scratch buffer:  wrap=true linebreak=false conceallevel=0 spell=false textwidth=0 foldmethod=manual
louiselm transcript:      wrap=true linebreak=false conceallevel=0 spell=false textwidth=0 foldmethod=manual
```

The `FileType markdown` path sets no options at all, so the transcript lost
nothing by leaving that filetype. Combined with the single-autocmd finding
above, `cd37ab2`'s blast radius on this config is empty: one plugin detached
(image.nvim, intended), one autocmd no longer firing (`MystMarkdownFiletype`,
beneficial), and no option, keymap or highlight difference.

This is the case I expected to find a regression in. It found none, and the
reason is worth keeping: the transcript never depended on `filetype=markdown`
for anything except treesitter, which `cd37ab2` re-attaches explicitly.

Worth recording as an incidental benefit, not a defect: under the old
`filetype=markdown`, `MystMarkdownFiletype` could fire on the transcript and
override its filetype whenever the conversation contained MyST content — which,
in this repo, it routinely does. `cd37ab2` makes that impossible.

### 4. `:LouiselmToMarkdown` into a missing directory — re-verify `louiselm-dim`

Exercises `6167df0` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1570`.

The test added by that commit already asserts the return value. What it cannot
see is what the command puts in front of you.

With a session attached and at least one turn in it:

```vim
:LouiselmToMarkdown
```

At the prompt, enter a path under a directory that does not exist:

```
/tmp/louiselm-qa-nope/export.md
```

Expect: a single clean `louiselm: could not write markdown file:
/tmp/louiselm-qa-nope/export.md` notification. Editor usable, cursor back where
it was.

Failure signature: a raw `E482: Can't create file` and/or a Lua stack trace, or
a hit-enter prompt you have to dismiss — the regression `louiselm-dim` was.

Evidence, run right after:

```vim
:lua Snacks.notifier.show_history()
```

(bound to `<leader>n` in your config). **Not `:messages`** — see the ground rule
below; louiselm calls `vim.notify` (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:278`),
snacks replaces `vim.notify`, and snacks notifications never reach `:messages`.

Send me the tail of that history. Also re-check `louiselm-euj` while you are here (the
deferred P3): the prompt appears *before* an explicit bad session id is
validated. Try `:LouiselmToMarkdown nosuchsession` and tell me whether it still
asks for a path first — I only want to know if it changed, not to fix it.

**`louiselm-euj` result: unchanged, still reproducible on `cd37ab2`.**
`:LouiselmToMarkdown nosuchsession` still prompts for a path before rejecting
the session id. Second round in a row it has been reconfirmed and deliberately
left open; that is a decision, not neglect, but a third reconfirmation should
probably come with either a fix or a downgrade to wontfix.

**Main part of case 4 (missing destination directory) still outstanding.**

### 5. Collapsed tool blocks in a real export

Exercises `14dbab6` / `lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua:182`.

Export a real session that contains at least two tool calls, one of them
completed and one that failed or was cancelled if you can arrange it:

```vim
:LouiselmToMarkdown
```

Accept the default path, then tell me the path. I will run:

```bash
grep -c '^## Tool$' <export>
grep -c '^<details>$' <export>
grep -c '^</details>$' <export>
grep -n '^<sub>' <export>
```

Pass: the first three counts are equal and non-zero, and every `<sub>` line
reads `<sub>**<title>** — <status></sub>` with a real title, not a raw tool-call
id, for the calls that had one.

Failure signature: unequal counts (an unbalanced `<details>` breaks every
downstream markdown renderer), or `<sub>**toolu_01...** — unknown</sub>` for a
call that plainly had a title and status on screen — meaning the real agent's
payload does not carry `raw.title`/`raw.status` where the synthetic fixtures put
them. That is exactly the class of bug fixtures cannot catch.

Then look at the file in something that renders GFM (`:GBrowse`-style paste into
a gist, `glow`, or the GitHub preview of a scratch commit) and tell me:

- do the tool blocks actually collapse, and
- is the transcript readable now, i.e. did collapsing the payloads do what it
  was supposed to do?

The second question is a judgement call and it is yours, not mine.

### 6. `:lines: 1` placeholder fails loudly

Exercises `f0b4d9c` / `render-post.mjs:63`, in the real authoring order — the
first thing that happens after a scaffold.

Pick a real session id you are happy to publish an excerpt of, then:

```bash
cd ~/code/louiselm
blog/scripts/create-blog.sh qa-round claude/<session-id>
blog/scripts/render-post.sh blog/post-qa-round
```

The session id must be the full `<agent>/<session-id>` form. If the export step
fails, that is a case-6 result too — send it to me rather than working around
it, since `create-blog.sh` drives the same headless export path as case 5 but
through a separate process.

Expect: exit 1 with a message naming `blog.md:<line>` and the unsupported
`:lines:` value `"1"`, telling you to replace the placeholder.

Failure signature: it renders something anyway (a one-line excerpt, or an
empty fragment), or it fails with a stack trace instead of that message. Note
that on failure the fragment-deletion step has not run yet, so nothing should
have been written into the post directory — confirm with `ls blog/post-qa-round`.

### 7. Fragment reaches the built page, in a browser — re-verify `louiselm-xrf`

Exercises `f0b4d9c` end to end. The automated test builds and greps HTML; it
never renders a pixel, and the bug it closed was precisely "the wiring exists
but nothing shows up".

The range is already set for you: `:lines: 1481-1522` in
`blog/post-qa-round/blog.md`, 42 lines chosen to span a `## User` turn, the
`## Assistant` reply, and one complete `## Tool` block whose caption is
truncated — so this case answers, in one shot, what both the `<details>` markup
and F5's ellipsis look like once they are a published excerpt. Content is the
Ghostty crash investigation, which reads as a real post rather than filler.

```bash
blog/scripts/render-post.sh blog/post-qa-round
```

Then I will pull:

```bash

grep -n 'iframe' blog/post-qa-round/blog.md
sed -n '/static_files/,/^[a-z]/p' blog/myst.yml
```

Then build and look at it:

```bash

```

Then **serve the built output** — do not open `_build/html/index.html` over
`file://`. The book theme uses client-side routing and the fragment is
referenced by a site-root absolute path (`/post-qa-round--….html`), neither of
which resolves from a `file://` URL, so a `file://` attempt fails for reasons
that have nothing to do with the code under test.

```bash
cd ~/code/louiselm/blog/_build/html && python3 -m http.server 8000
```

then open `http://localhost:8000/post-qa-round/blog/`. Serving `_build/html` as
the document root is what makes the absolute src resolve, and it keeps this
case about the **built** artifact — `myst start` is case 8, deliberately
separate.

Expect, and this is the part only you can answer:

- the excerpt is visible on the page, not a blank box or a broken-frame icon;
- it has the real Catppuccin colours and Tree-sitter highlighting, not MyST's
  generic hljs grey;
- the excerpt is longer than the iframe box, and **scrolls inside it** rather
  than being clipped — `render-post.sh`'s header admits the theme fixes the
  iframe's aspect ratio and does not expose height, so this is the known rough
  edge. Tell me whether the result is publishable or merely technically wired;
- the `## Tool` block inside the excerpt: six lines of raw `<details>` /
  `<summary>` / `</details>` markup are now visible as literal text in the
  rendered excerpt (the excerpt is a picture of the markdown *source*, taken by
  TOhtml — MyST never parses it). **Prediction to confirm or refute:** this
  looks like noise and eats vertical space in a box that cannot grow. If
  confirmed it is a finding against `14dbab6`, not against the blog pipeline.

Failure signature for the wiring itself: an empty iframe, a 404 in the browser
console for `/post-qa-round--...nvim-transcript.html`, or the page falling back
to plain hljs highlighting — `louiselm-xrf` reopened.

**Result: PASS. `louiselm-xrf` stays fixed.**

Wiring, pulled rather than eyeballed:

```
fragment generated       15200 bytes
myst.yml static_files    one entry, scoped to this post
copied to site root      _build/html/post-qa-round--….nvim-transcript.html
post page built          _build/html/post-qa-round/blog/index.html
iframe src               /post-qa-round--….nvim-transcript.html  -> resolves
```

Colour check settled without the tester: the fragment carries 9 distinct
colours (`#303446` base, `#c6d0f5` text, `#8caaee`, `#a6d189`, `#e78284`,
`#ef9f76`, `#f4b8e4`, `#81c8be`, `#51576d`) — Catppuccin Frappé, not MyST's
generic hljs grey.

Tester's verdict on the rendered page at
`http://localhost:8000/post-qa-round/blog/`: looks good.

**Prediction refuted, and worth keeping as a correction.** I predicted the
`<details>` markup and long payload lines would make the excerpt unpublishable.
The widths are real — of 45 rendered lines, two are ~5600 characters (the
escaped `rawOutput` and `text` values) and four exceed 200 — but they sit
behind a horizontal scrollbar instead of breaking the box, and 41 of 45 lines
are ordinary width. The fragment's own `overflow: auto` absorbs it. Reasoning
from file line lengths overestimated the visual damage; the person who decides
what is publishable looked at it and disagreed. No finding filed.

### 8. Same under `myst start`, not just `myst build`

Exercises `f0b4d9c` / the absolute `/<basename>` iframe src, which the automated
test only ever exercises through `myst build`.

### 9. Re-run idempotency in the real repo

Exercises `f0b4d9c`'s "running twice against unchanged input is byte-identical"

`git diff blog/myst.yml` so I can see the merge result against the committed

One command that summarises the blog half of the round once cases 6–9 are done:

Send me the case number, what you saw, and the raw output of any command in it.

## How the round closed

**The commits under test came out clean.** `cd37ab2` (cases 1–3) did exactly
what it claimed with an empty blast radius. `f0b4d9c` (cases 6–8) is correctly
wired end to end, browser included, so `louiselm-xrf` stays fixed. `6167df0`
(case 4) holds. Only `14dbab6` had a defect behind it, and that defect predated
it.

**Every finding came from somewhere other than the commit it was filed
against**, which is the round's most useful pattern:

| Finding | Surfaced by |
| ------- | ----------- |
| F1 `louiselm-d7l` | running the documented gate before starting, on a clean tree |
| F2 `louiselm-tcb` | the editor vanishing mid-round |
| F3 `louiselm-msg` | a stray notification in the history opened for case 4 |
| F4 `louiselm-cmr` | a real payload where every fixture was well-behaved |
| F5 `louiselm-u1r` | measuring the artifact *after* F4's fix instead of trusting the assertion |
| F6 `louiselm-qcq` | a real excerpt where the test fixture was too small |

**Why the suite missed each — the transferable part.**

Three of the six (F3, F4, F6) are the *same* gap: **fixtures are well-behaved
in exactly the dimension real data is not.** `skills_spec.lua` builds symlinks
inside a temp root, so it never sees a symlink to a Rust repo with a 2839-
directory `target/`. `transcript_spec.lua` used titles like `"Run tests"`, so
it never saw a title containing a newline — and asserted with substring
searches that cannot detect an unclosed element even in principle.
`test-render-post.sh` part 2 runs exactly the right `diff -rq` check against a
fixture too small to produce enough CSS rules for the ordering to move. In all
three the assertion was sound and the fixture was the defect. A fixture
captured from real traffic, rather than invented, would have caught all three.

F1 is different and simpler: the gate exists, is documented, and nothing runs
it. CI does not yet enforce the gates, and the previous round had `674939b` in
scope but tested behaviour rather than running the formatter. Behavioural QA
does not substitute for a gate.

F5 is the one worth internalising. F4's fix made every assertion pass — counts
balanced, no fabricated headings, elements closed. The export was still not fit
for the pipeline that consumes it, because nothing had *measured* the result.
Verifying the assertion a fix targets is not the same as inspecting what the
fix produced.

F2 was not ours at all. Worth recording anyway: the reported symptom
("neovim crashed") was wrong, and taking it at face value would have sent the
round after a `vim.treesitter.start` call that the user's own config had
already been making for months.

**Recipe bugs, mine, all corrected in place:** `<bufnr>` left as a literal
placeholder in case 1.2; `:messages` named as the evidence channel when snacks
replaces `vim.notify` and keeps its own history; repo-root-relative paths in
case 9 given to someone standing in `blog/`; "open the built page" with no
usable way to open it. The snacks one was the expensive one — it made a passing
case look like it produced no evidence.

## Findings this round

**F2 — Ghostty dies and takes every Neovim window with it** (`louiselm-tcb`,
P1, open investigation, likely not ours). Reported mid-round as "neovim simply
crashed". It did not. `journalctl --user` shows all three
`app-ghostty-surface-transient-*.scope` units ending within one second at
05:14:18-19, then a fresh ghostty process at 05:14:27 — eleven seconds before
Neovim was relaunched at 05:14:38. Ghostty is single-process/multi-surface, so
one death closes every window; Neovim was hung up, which is why there was no
deadly-signal banner. Ruled out: Neovim crash (no `ERR` in `nvim.log`), OOM
(`oom_kill 0` in the user slice), a Ghostty panic (no trace in a journal that
holds its full lifecycle), and `cd37ab2`'s `vim.treesitter.start` — the user's
config already ran `vim.treesitter.start()` on `FileType *`, so treesitter load
on that buffer is unchanged by the commit. Still open: the kernel log for an
AMDGPU reset, and whether image.nvim's kitty-graphics traffic is involved —
**which makes case 1.2 the discriminator, so run it.** Found by the tester when
the editor vanished, not by any case in this plan.

**F6 — `render-post` fragments are not byte-identical across runs**
(`louiselm-qcq`, P3, not fixed). `render-post.sh`'s header promises fragment
output is "a pure function of the current input" and that "running twice
against unchanged input is byte-identical". Ten consecutive runs on identical
input in an identical environment produced **four distinct fragments**; holding
`TERM` fixed still flips it, so it is run-to-run nondeterminism, not
environment sensitivity. The entire diff is CSS rule order and property order
within a rule (`.-conceal {}` moving position;
`.-markup-strong {color: …; font-weight: bold}` vs the reverse) — the `<pre>`
is identical every time and every variant renders the same, which is why case 7
looked fine. Origin is upstream: `:TOhtml` emits its `<style>` block from an
unordered table, and this pipeline preserves it verbatim by design.
`test-render-post.sh` part 2 runs precisely the right check (`diff -rq` across
two runs) and passes anyway, because its fixture excerpts are 4–5 lines of
prose and a three-line Lua snippet — too few highlight groups for the order to
move. The real excerpt produces 11 rules. Not fixed because the obvious fix
(sort the CSS in `render-post.mjs`) collides with part 1's assertion that the
fragment matches an *independent* TOhtml capture byte-for-byte; that is a
design decision, written up in the bead.

**F5 — Single-line captions run to thousands of characters** (`louiselm-u1r`,
P2, **fixed in `3d6557d`**, closed). Exposed by F4's own fix: once captions
were one line, the longest in the verified export was **7319 characters** (then
6963, 6490) — whole `br create --description` invocations with the bead body
inlined. Correct but useless as a label, and a live risk to case 7, which
renders these exports through `:TOhtml` into an iframe whose width the theme
fixes and does not expose. Bounded at 120 characters via
`strchars`/`strcharpart` rather than `string.sub`, since real titles carry em
dashes and a byte-wise cut would emit invalid UTF-8 mid-character; the full
title is untouched in the `<details>` payload. Worth noting how this was found:
not by a case, but by measuring the artifact after a fix instead of declaring
victory on the assertion that the fix targeted.

**F4 — Multi-line tool titles break the export's `<sub>` caption and inject
fake `##` sections** (`louiselm-cmr`, P1, **fixed in `a6484ea`**, closed,
**verified** by re-export: 156 `## Tool` / 56 `## Assistant` / 17 `## User` and
no other `##`; 156 of 156 captions closing on their own line; zero multi-line
spans). Found by
case 5, and exactly the failure class the case was written for: fixtures use
short single-line titles, real payloads carry whole shell commands. In a 120
tool-call export, 12 captions span more than one line — the worst runs 150
lines — because `transcript.lua:182` interpolates `raw.title` into a
single-line string and `split_lines` then turns its embedded newlines into real
breaks. Everything between the unclosed `<sub>` and its `</sub>` lands in the
document as raw markdown, which added 28 fabricated `##` headings
(`## Observed`, `## Root cause`, …) leaked out of heredoc bead descriptions.
Older than `14dbab6` — the previous `## Tool: <title>` format split the heading
the same way — but the round found it while testing that commit. What passed:
the block counts balance exactly (120 `## Tool` / `<details>` / `<summary>` /
`</details>`), no title fell back to a raw tool id, and all statuses are real
(`completed` ×104, `failed` ×4).

**F3 — Skill discovery warns per symlinked subdirectory and scans whole source
repos** (`louiselm-msg`, P2, not fixed — out of scope). Surfaced by accident:
the snacks notifier history opened for case 4 also held
`louiselm: skill discovery found 31 issue(s)`. Thirty of those 31 are the same
"symlink resolves outside configured root" warning, fired once per symlinked
subdirectory on a stow layout where every skill is a symlink by design. The
check at `lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua:209` warns and then queues the
directory anyway, so it prevents nothing — and because `bvr`'s skill directory
symlinks to a whole Rust repo, discovery walks 3133 directories of which 2839
are `target/`. Measured in-process against the real config: `discover()` takes
381 ms, of which the `bvr` subtree alone accounts for 376 ms. `skills_spec.lua`
misses it because its fixtures build symlinks inside a temp root, so no case
models a symlink to a large real repository. Not fixed: nothing in
`ec19281..HEAD` touches skills, and the fix is a behavioural decision about
what "outside the root" should mean.

**F1 — `stylua --check .` fails on a clean tree** (`louiselm-d7l`, not fixed).
`blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua` is not StyLua-formatted (single-quoted strings
where the repo config sets `quote_style = "AutoPreferDouble"`), so the gate
AGENTS.md §4 declares — `stylua --check .`, unscoped, whole repo — has exited 1
since `674939b`. Introduced by the blog pipeline commit, which the previous
round (`louiselm-vj0`) had in scope and did not catch, because that round tested
the pipeline's behaviour and never ran the formatter gate. Not fixed during the
round: it is a one-command fix, but it is out of scope for the cases below and
touching the tree mid-round invalidates case 0's clean-tree premise.

title: Firebase bootstrap omits project audit logging
description:
The dedicated Firebase project has no explicit project-wide Data Access audit configuration, leaving access events unavailable and keeping the security-policy CI job red.

## Observed

Observed 2026-09-04 with Trivy 0.72.0:

`trivy config infra/firebase` reports `GCP-0079 (LOW): Project should have audit logging configured for security compliance` at `infra/firebase/main.tf:15-26`.

## Symptoms

- The security-policy CI job fails.
- The new project's data reads and writes lack the intended audit trail.

## Root cause

The composition creates `google_project.notifications` without a corresponding project IAM audit configuration.

## Why it was not caught

OpenTofu validation does not enforce security policy; the failing Trivy result was outside the earlier backend-selection bug.

## Fix direction

Configure all-services ADMIN_READ, DATA_READ, and DATA_WRITE audit logging at the project boundary. Keep exclusions empty unless a measured cost or volume problem justifies one.

## Acceptance

- Project-wide audit logging covers ADMIN_READ, DATA_READ, and DATA_WRITE.
- Trivy no longer reports GCP-0079.
- OpenTofu format and validation pass without cloud mutation.

## Not covered

Log retention, export sinks, and alerting are not required for the initial static site and notification project.
close_reason: Project-wide audit logging declared. gate:tf-trivy

title: Receipt store hides later records after a gap
description: Observed in restart work louiselm-qbr.5.1.2.2.1, 2026-09-12, deterministic local Rust fixture. ReceiptStore::stored_bytes in skills-core/src/broker/receipts.rs stops at the first missing sequence without checking later files, so a corrupted store can silently shorten the prefix presented for broker restart. Reproduction: store valid receipts 0/1, add a record at sequence 3 while 2 is absent; stored_bytes returns Ok with 0/1. Red test: reconnect::stored_receipt_gap_cannot_silently_shorten_the_verified_prefix, tests/broker/reconnect.rs:154, assertion failed: service.receipts().stored_bytes(&authorization.session_id).is_err(). Command: scripts/test-skills-core --test broker stored_receipt_gap --quiet via systemd-run; exit 101. Existing tests did not model a hole with a later file. Fix at bounded shared reader: reject gaps/unexpected entries, never truncate, repair or splice. Acceptance: regression green, ordinary empty/continuous stores unchanged, full skills-core gates. No live desktop reproduction or vendor recovery claim.
close_reason: Reject gaps and unexpected receipt records without shortening history. gate:skills-core/tests/broker/reconnect.rs

comments.text: Fixed shared bounded reader: count directory records and require every contiguous sequence; a later entry cannot disappear behind a missing predecessor. Regression failed before and passes after. Full skills-core suite, Clippy, fmt, Rustdoc and 13 browser tests pass. Lesson destination: this issue; never discover a durable chain by stopping silently at the first absent file.

title: Grill-me needed: how should qa-review rounds be archived, and does beads belong in the loop
description:
Not actionable as-is — this is a seed for a future grill-me session, not a
spec to implement from. Surfaced at the close of the transcript-export/
blog-publishing QA round (2026-08-18), when a process question came up that
didn't fit anywhere in the existing skill chain.

## The open questions

- **Archiving authority.** Once a qa-review round closes, does the working
  file (`QA_REVIEW.md`-style) become the durable record of what was tested
  and found, or is it disposable scratch once findings are filed to beads?
  Right now nothing says either way, so rounds just accumulate as loose
  untracked files.
- **Where archiving sits in the qa-review process.** Should the qa-review
  skill itself have a defined "closing" step that decides what happens to
  the file (commit it, summarize it into beads, delete it), or is that
  always a manual call by whoever's running the round?
- **Could beads be leveraged more directly.** Instead of (or alongside) a
  markdown working file, could a qa-review round's cases/results live in
  beads itself — e.g. as a parent issue with the plan, sub-issues per case?
  Unclear if that's better or just adds ceremony to something that works
  fine as a file today.

## Why this doesn't fit the usual chain

Their standing workflow is grill-me -> to-beads -> tasks executed across
sessions ("skill chaining"). Within a qa-review round, a code bug correctly
triggers to-beads-bug — that chain already works. But this round produced a
different kind of finding: not a bug, a question about the skills/workflow
itself. There's currently no formalized way for a skill to route that kind
of self-reflective finding anywhere — it only survived this time because the
user happened to notice and say it was worth a grill-me session. Whether
findings like this should sometimes get folded directly into a skill's own
instructions (when concrete enough) versus always deferred to a grill-me
session (when still vague) is itself part of what's open here.

## A concrete proposal already on record

This question isn't new — the user raised it explicitly at the *start* of
this same QA round, in an earlier session (`claude/85f97534-8fa6-4d95-a05a-7c0851bec937`):
"while we do this i want you to think if those reviews conversation or
document you produce as part of the review could leverage beads for
historical / archiving purposes." That session's assistant answered with a
concrete sketch the user liked and wants preserved verbatim here for the
grill-me session to react to, not re-derive:

1. **One bead per round**, type `chore`, label `qa-round`, created with
   `--description-file QA_REVIEW.md`. The whole plan lands in
   `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which is committed — so the round becomes
   greppable history instead of an untracked file you have to decide about
   at the end. That's the exact question that ended the *previous* round
   (the permissions round) unresolved too: "commit it as a record, or
   delete it."
2. **Findings hang off it as children.** `br create -t bug --parent
   <round-id>` — the graph then answers "which round found this?" and `br
   graph` shows a round's blast radius. This round's findings
   (`louiselm-dim`, `louiselm-euj`, `louiselm-d2o`, `louiselm-xrf`) are
   already beads but orphaned from the round that produced them — exactly
   the gap this proposal closes.
3. **Round-by-round narration goes in `br comments add`** — append-only and
   timestamped, matching the loop shape (plan, run, learn, edit). The
   markdown file stays the live scratchpad *during* the round since it
   churns every round; beads takes the final state on close.
4. **`--external-ref` holds the session id** (e.g.
   `claude/21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384` for this round), which
   dovetails with the user's global commit-message rule (`Refs <id>` for
   named sessions/issues), and `br orphans` catches anything referenced in a
   commit but still open.

The convergence the prior session flagged as the nice part: the
transcript-export feature this very round was testing turns a session into
a publishable artifact. So under this proposal the bead becomes the index,
the exported transcript is the evidence, and a blog post (via the same
publishing pipeline, once `louiselm-xrf` is fixed) is the human-readable
version of the same round — three layers of the same feature set reused for
QA's own record-keeping instead of a fourth bespoke mechanism.

## Bigger context

Connects to a broader, previously-discussed wish: the user's own workflow
(grill-me/beads/session-chaining) eventually being expressible as a
configurable part of louiselm itself, not just a convention they follow by
hand. Not fully re-litigated here — worth pulling that thread in the
grill-me session too.

## Not covered

No decision on the concrete proposal above — it was well-received when
sketched, but never evaluated against the three open questions or actually
tried on a round (this round still used a plain `QA_REVIEW.md`). Left for
the grill-me session: whether to adopt it as-is, adapt it, or reject it in
favor of something else.
close_reason: Resolved via grill-me. Routed to feature louiselm-ri1 (Give qa-review rounds a mandatory archiving/closing step backed by beads), with child tasks louiselm-ri1.1 (skill closing step) and louiselm-ri1.2 (retroactive close of QA_REVIEW.md and QA_REVIEW-permissions-round.md, blocked on ri1.1). Adopted the concrete proposal on record as-is: one chore/qa-round bead per round via --description-file + --external-ref, findings as children via the existing to-beads-bug chain, cases stay flat (never beaded), narration via br comments, working file deleted on close. Bigger workflow-config-engine thread explicitly left out of scope per agreement.

title: Supply lineage
description: Persistent origin, upstream, pin, transition, and local-source history for instruction supply, with no approval authority.

title: Show Session Provenance: every commit and issue a Session produced
description:
## Goal

From a Session id, see everything that Session produced: its commits and the
issues it worked.

## Scope

- In scope: `louiselm://provenance/session/<id>`; the reverse traversal;
  cursor detection for Session ids.
- Out of scope: reading or rendering transcript contents.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `louiselm://provenance/session/<id>` lists commits carrying that Session in a
   trailer and issues carrying it as actor.
2. The view offers the resolved transcript path, or states plainly that it could
   not be resolved.
3. A Session id with no commits and no issues renders as an empty result, not an
   error.

## Testing

- Headless behavioural smoke test.
- A Session appearing on only one of the two edges renders the populated side
  and marks the other empty.

## Notes

Completes the third traversal direction. With commit-rooted and issue-rooted
views already in place, this is the slice that makes Provenance navigable from
whichever end the maintainer happens to be holding.
close_reason: Completed: added reverse Session Provenance over git trailers and br actor fields, with transcript resolution and empty-side rendering; 688 MiniTest cases and all quality gates pass.

comments.author: codex/01a0428e-6b0e-7fa3-a088-c03e6b235bf4
comments.text: Lesson: reverse Provenance can stay derived and read-only by joining git log --all trailer edges with br list --status all actor edges. Session IDs must be detected before issue IDs because the trailing session component can otherwise be mistaken for a Beads issue. No standing AGENTS.md rule or unresolved design question is warranted.

title: Beads inspector hides database errors behind generic lookup failure
description:
During fresh-Codex QA, the Beads inspector concealed an actionable database error behind "louiselm: could not read Beads issue louiselm-dtwil". Database access subsequently recovered outside this Session; the UI still discards the cause.

## Observed

2026-09-15, codex/01a0a4c3-d513-7363-acd2-ce29762dfa73, Neovim /run/user/1000/nvim.2516148.0, source ee86142.
Installed br 0.6.0 (release), main@0dcd837, /home/lotso/.cargo/bin/br.
br show louiselm-dtwil --json returned nonzero with DATABASE_ERROR and message "Database error: database is busy (recovery in progress)".
br --no-db show louiselm-dtwil --json returned the expected open P2 issue.
br doctor reported sync.merge_pending and db.read_only_open_observational errors with the same cause; Frankensqlite 0.4.0. Integrity checks and 1032/1032 record counts were OK. Neither old recovery artifacts nor a sampled absence of a live lock establishes the underlying database cause.
After the maintainer reported recovery, normal br show succeeded and both read/merge checks became OK. No database repair or sidecar deletion was performed by this Session. Overall doctor still reports other findings; this is specific read-access recovery, not an all-clear.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua, run_show: every nonzero CLI result becomes miss_reason=not_found. show_issue then displays the generic read failure, losing structured error classification and remediation. The source of the separate database failure remains unknown.

## Why it was not caught

tests/ui/beads_spec.lua explicitly expects the generic could-not-read message for nonzero exits. The test does not require actionable, sanitized structured CLI errors to reach the human.

## Fix direction

Decode and validate bounded structured br errors at the shared lookup boundary. Distinguish database/process failure from missing issues while preserving existing sibling lookup behavior, scheduling, disposed-view guards and issue validation. Never display arbitrary raw stderr or sensitive payloads. Do not introduce automatic database repair or silently read potentially stale exports.

## Acceptance

- Regression uses the observed DATABASE_ERROR shape, expects an actionable cause, and fails on the current generic-only message before the fix.
- True missing issues and malformed CLI output retain specific safe failures.
- Successful lookup still opens the exact selected issue.
- Human sees a bounded actionable diagnostic when the CLI fails; required Lua and generated-doc gates pass.

## Not covered

Database-engine repair belongs to the owning tool. Earlier louiselm-kk27 fixed omitted-description decoding; this is a different failure.
Deferred from Codex startup QA; no inspector implementation or live failure-message acceptance has occurred.

title: Firebase service agent inherits access to in-project state

The HCL, bootstrap runbook, tests, and recovery model match that choice before any project creation.

title: Preserve option changes and observed request attribution
description:
## Goal

Retain confirmed Session option transitions, their observed source, and their relationship to recorded turns.

## Scope

In: shared option-change boundaries, persistence, source/request metadata, full starting options plus mid-turn timeline, and recording-failure behavior. Out: causal inference, failed requests falsely represented as changes, or analytics UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Medium -> High -> Medium retains both confirmed transitions even if no prompt follows, with Session identity, timestamp, old/new typed values, and stable event identity.
2. Distinguish the explicitly requested option/value from additional Agent-reported changes. Attach request linkage only where established; timing alone does not prove a cause or human intent.
3. Repeated advertisement of unchanged values and history replay do not mint new change events. Preserve actual ordering from event payloads rather than later mutable snapshots.
4. A started turn keeps its initial full option tuple; active-value transitions are associated with its timeline and mark it unsuitable for a fixed-combination comparison. Never split measured consumption by guesswork.
5. Provider attribution remains resolved under the agreed collection contract. An unresolvable configuration or failed event write surfaces a recording failure and holds subsequent prompt admission; accepted Agent state must not be misreported as an unchanged/rejected option.
6. The same behavior works for Chat and headless API callers, including late notifications after Disposal and fast-event callbacks.

## Testing

Use public Session methods and captured structural ACP fixtures for explicit request responses and unsolicited updates. Cover no-prompt changes, actual mid-turn value changes, unchanged advertisements, Agent confirmation changing multiple options, replay, duplicate delivery/retry, source linkage, and storage errors. State any unobserved event order in fixtures. Run full Lua gates and event/API-doc generation.

## Notes

Current config_options_changed carries only the complete replacement list (session/events.lua:28); both set_config_option responses and config_option_update notifications emit it. Persist differences at the shared boundary and retain immutable observations. Source: louiselm-3x9p decisions 4-5 and 15.
close_reason: Confirmed typed option history, response-only request linkage, immutable starting tuple and fixed-cohort exclusion; schema 2 upgrade/retry tested. 914 tests and all Lua/doc gates pass. Lessons: comment 1209 and docs/turn-recording.md. consumer:lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:369

comments.author: codex/01a07bb4-c41e-7010-8332-d9a6ff731e2c
comments.text: Plan: immutable option_events in the existing SQLite writer; per-observer order, old/new typed tuples, response-only request linkage, active-turn association. Shared option acceptance queues facts before publishing state; replay establishes baseline only. Unresolved Provider remains a visible Session-local recording error until corrected. Preserve concurrent hmmc identity changes in tests/session/api_spec.lua and registry/init. Prior lessons: 3x9p decisions 4/5/15 and bznu observer ordering.

comments.author: codex/01a07bb4-c41e-7010-8332-d9a6ff731e2c
comments.text: Implemented at lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:369: snapshot and queue confirmed values before publishing events; response-only requested id/option/value, no retrospective notification causality. Schema 2 adds option_events without rewriting turns; observer_id/sequence orders each live stream. Active changes retain initial tuples and set turn_options_changed. Keep unresolved Provider separate from writer errors so a successful flush cannot erase attribution failure (registry.lua:224). Lesson destination: docs/turn-recording.md for consumer/retry/cohort contract; this comment for test evidence. No new standing rule warranted. Red: initial option tests failed missing table/flag; green: 11 focused cases and 914 full Lua cases, zero LLS diagnostics, Stylua and API/LuaCATS/vimdoc checks. Fixed future-schema fixture from 2 to 999 because 2 is now supported. Real peer structures cited in option_recording_spec.lua:13; interleavings explicitly adversarial, not claimed observed. Verification also found/fixed separately tracked 3gen and 3vi2. Legacy replay/UI writer retirement remains lc32.

title: Migrate CI and release Actions to Node 24
description:
Goal: Remove Node.js 20 deprecation warnings from GitHub Actions CI and plugin releases by upgrading Actions to supported Node 24 releases.

Evidence:
- Maintainer reports the release job warning: "Node.js 20 is deprecated".
- GitHub announcement, updated August 25, 2026, schedules Node 20 removal for September 23, 2026: https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/
- .github/workflows/release-please.yml:62,88 pins googleapis/release-please-action to 5c625bfb5d1ff62eadeeb3772007f7f66fdcf071 (v4.4.1), whose action.yml declares node20.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml uses checkout@v4, cache@v4, setup-node@v4, stylua-action@v4, and action-setup-vim@v1.

Scope:
- Audit all workflow Action references and upgrade those needing Node 24 support. Verified Node 24 releases on 2026-09-18: release-please-action v5.0.0, checkout v7.0.1, cache v6.1.0, setup-node v7.0.0, stylua-action v5.0.0, action-setup-vim v1.6.1. Check whether floating refs already resolve to migrated releases; review breaking changes and runner requirements before selecting replacements.
- Preserve immutable Release Please SHA pinning and update both release steps plus the matching checkout in the plugin-release-contract CI job.
- Align scripts/test-release-please.cjs and docs/releases.md with the selected pin. Release Please action v5.0.0 upgrades the underlying library from 17.3.0 to 17.6.0.
- Preserve release permissions, reviewed-main checkout, checked-commit publication and draft recovery behavior.
- Project Node versions selected by setup-node are separate from Action runtimes; do not change them solely to silence this warning. Evaluate running release fixtures under Node 24 to match the Action.
- No release redesign, credential changes, new tooling dependencies, or insecure Node 20 opt-out. Do not force publication solely to exercise the fix.

Acceptance:
1. Affected Action metadata declares Node 24; pin, fixture library version and documentation agree.
2. Existing release contract checks pass against the selected upstream version without weakening assertions.
3. Hosted CI and the next authorized release workflow execution succeed without Node 20 deprecation warnings; record run URLs and annotation evidence. Local tests alone do not prove hosted acceptance.

Testing:
- Follow docs/agent-testing.md; run python3 scripts/check-release-commits.py, python3 scripts/test-plugin-release.py, and scripts/test-release-please.cjs using the temporary pinned-tool setup in the plugin-release-contract CI job.
- Validate workflow changes with available existing checks, then inspect hosted CI and release annotations.
- Mechanical version updates need no artificial failing unit test; preserve existing release security and behavior coverage.

Priority P1: announced runtime removal is five days after filing. This is one standalone CI maintenance task, with no dependency on unfinished component-release features.

title: Skill/file/buffer/selection context pickers are unreachable through the documented :LouiselmChat setup path
description:
The chat context-queuing API (`pick_skill`, `pick_file`, `mention_buffer`, `send_selection`) documented in README.md under "Chat context" is completely unreachable through the plugin's own documented setup path, so no user who follows the README can ever attach a file, skill, buffer mention, or visual selection to a prompt.

## Observed

Found 2026-08-20 while setting up a manual QA round for louiselm-2w4 (native ACP skill invocation): asked the user to invoke the skill picker to test it, and they had never wired anything for it -- because there is nothing to wire it to.

`grep -rn "pick_skill\|pick_file\|mention_buffer\|send_selection" lua/ --include="*.lua" | grep -v chat/init.lua` returns nothing: these four `Chat` methods are defined in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua and never called anywhere else in the tree -- not in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua (which backs `:LouiselmChat` and every other registered `:Louiselm*` command), not anywhere.

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua` registers 12 `:Louiselm*` ex commands (LouiselmChat, LouiselmNewSession, LouiselmResume, LouiselmSwitchSession, LouiselmRenameSession, LouiselmSessionId, LouiselmToMarkdown, LouiselmCloseSession, LouiselmCancel, LouiselmSessionOptions, LouiselmPermissions, LouiselmInline) -- none of them calls pick_skill/pick_file/mention_buffer/send_selection.

The `chat` object these methods live on is a local upvalue private to `Command.register()`'s closure (command.lua:194 `local chat`); nothing exposes it, and `Louiselm.setup()` (lua/louiselm/init.lua) returns only a boolean. So even a user willing to write their own keymap has no object to call these methods on unless they bypass `Louiselm.setup()`/`:LouiselmChat` entirely and hand-construct a second, parallel `Chat` instance via the low-level `require("louiselm.ui.chat").new(sessions, {...})` constructor -- which would not be attached to the same session as their real chat buffer.

README.md documents these four methods under "## Chat context" (around line 438) as plain Lua snippets (`chat:mention_buffer()`, `chat:send_selection()`, `chat:pick_file()`, `chat:pick_skill()`) with no indication that `chat` here is a user-constructed low-level object, not the one `:LouiselmChat` creates -- reading the README top to bottom gives no working path to ever call them.

## Symptoms

- Following the README exactly (`Louiselm.setup(config)` + `:LouiselmChat`), there is no command, keymap, or other UI affordance to pick a skill, pick a file, mention the source buffer, or send a visual selection.
- The entire native/inject skill-invocation feature (including the just-shipped louiselm-2w4) is unreachable in practice for the documented setup path.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua never registers commands for these four `Chat` methods, and never exposes the `chat` instance it privately constructs.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` and `tests/ui/context_spec.lua` call `chat:pick_skill()` etc. directly on a `Chat` object constructed in the test, which is exactly the low-level path the README also (accidentally) documents -- so the tests exercise the methods correctly but never assert that the *shipped, documented, high-level setup path* (`:LouiselmChat`) can reach them. No test covers `command.lua`'s command surface for context actions because there was never a command to cover.

## Fix direction

Add `:LouiselmPickSkill`, `:LouiselmPickFile` (optional root arg, `nargs = "?"`, mirroring `:LouiselmToMarkdown`'s optional-arg pattern), `:LouiselmMentionBuffer`, and `:LouiselmSendSelection` to command.lua, following the existing `if chat == nil then report_error("no chat session is open") ... end` pattern used by `:LouiselmCancel`/`:LouiselmSessionOptions`/`:LouiselmCloseSession` (these need an already-open session to queue context onto, unlike `:LouiselmChat`/`:LouiselmPermissions` which use `ensure_chat()` to open one on demand). Update README's command list (around line 269) and the "Chat context" section to stop implying the low-level constructor snippet is reachable from the documented setup path.

## Acceptance

- New `:Louiselm*` commands registered and covered by a test in tests/ui/command_spec.lua that drives them through the real `:LouiselmChat` + `Command.register()` path (matching the file's existing "through the normal chat path" test style), not just calling the Chat method directly.
- README updated to list the new commands and no longer implies the raw snippets are usable from a documented setup.

## Not covered

- Whether default keymaps (not just ex commands) are also warranted -- left as a separate decision; this bug is about there being no path at all, not about ergonomics beyond a command existing.
close_reason: Fixed in 9e553a1. Added :LouiselmPickSkill, :LouiselmPickFile [root], :LouiselmMentionBuffer, :LouiselmSendSelection to lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua, matching the existing chat==nil guard pattern used by :LouiselmCancel/:LouiselmSessionOptions. Tests: command existence check, a combined 'no chat session is open' case for all four, and a real end-to-end test driving :LouiselmMentionBuffer through :LouiselmChat + a fake ACP process, asserting the chip renders and the queued context is sent in the next session/prompt. Updated README's command list and Chat context section. Gates: full mini.test suite green, stylua and lua-language-server clean repo-wide (excluding a pre-existing unrelated blog/ script). Deferred: default keymaps beyond the ex commands, per the bead's own 'Not covered' note.

title: QA round: exact option usage cohorts
description:
# Manual QA — Astra option history

Build: f7804df. Issue: louiselm-rvu8. Working scratch file; results will be
recorded in Beads when the round closes, then this file removed.

| Case | State |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Real Astra reasoning picker | Maintainer accepted: "ok it seems ok"; exact row text not supplied |
| 2. Recompute after Model/mode changes | Not individually reported; automated regression passes |
| 3. Real completed turn appears | Not individually reported; automated regression passes |

## Setup

Use a fresh Neovim launched after the installed checkout update. Open a Codex
Session and wait until it is idle. These checks change real Session options;
note the original Model, Reasoning effort and Mode so you can restore them.
Run `:LouiselmSessionId` and keep the displayed identity for reporting.

The installed checkout was verified at f7804df. The maintainer can verify the
loaded Session method after opening a Session:

```vim
:lua for _, v in ipairs(require("louiselm.session").exit_verdict()) do print(v.agent, v.acp_session_id, type(v.session.option_usage)) end
```

Expect `function` for the subject Session. This establishes that the new API
is loaded, not that the visual picker or its cohort is correct.

## 1. Real Astra reasoning picker

Exercises f7804df, lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2164.

1. Run `:LouiselmSessionOptions`, choose Model, select GPT-6-Astra.
2. From the options overview choose Reasoning effort.
3. Inspect the candidate rows before changing anything.

Expect: `No matching history` for combinations with no recorded turns; otherwise
`observed: N turns` with a mean and `token data for M`. Existing exact Astra
history is legitimate. The original hundreds of cross-Model `samples` must not
be reused. Missing total-token telemetry is explicitly labelled.

Failure: old `... samples` labels, inherited large historical counts, History
unavailable, an error, or the picker closing before a choice.

Evidence: report the Session identity and the text of one or two rows. The agent
will read that Session's confirmed tuple and query its exact SQLite cohort;
the user's observation establishes the displayed text and focus behavior.

## 2. Recompute after confirmed Model/mode changes

Exercises f7804df, lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:1026 and picker reopening.

1. Dismiss the reasoning values to return to the overview.
2. Change Model to GPT-5.6-Terra, then reopen Reasoning effort.
3. Return to Astra. Change Mode to Ask for approval and reopen Reasoning effort.
4. Restore the original Mode.

Expect: each picker uses the now-confirmed other options. An unused combination
shows `No matching history`. Different configurations can legitimately both
show no history, or equal counts; numerical difference alone is not proof.
The header/overview must reflect the Agent-confirmed configuration.

Failure: stale prior configuration or unchanged inherited measurements despite
the exact database cohort being different. The agent checks reported rows
against each confirmed tuple; do not guess from counts alone.

## 3. One real completed turn

Exercises the installed Session recorder -> SQL query -> visible picker path.

1. Select Astra and the desired reasoning value; record that candidate's count.
2. Close the picker and submit: `Reply with exactly OK. Do not use tools.`
3. Wait for completion, then reopen `:LouiselmSessionOptions` -> Reasoning effort.

Expect: the exact chosen combination includes the completed turn. If token
telemetry was reported, token coverage includes it. Other reasoning values do
not inherit that turn. Concurrent Sessions can add matching turns, so an
increase greater than one is not by itself a failure. If the Agent changed an
option during the turn, exclusion is intentional; report it for inspection.

Failure: completed unchanged-tuple turn remains absent, another reasoning value
inherits it, missing telemetry appears as zero, or errors interrupt normal use.

Evidence: Session identity, selected options and before/after row text. The agent
will check committed dispatch/outcome/option observations for that Session.

## Automated coverage not repeated manually

924 tests already cover exact typed equality, Agent/Provider isolation, legacy
exclusion, mixed turns, missing telemetry, separate currencies, invalid cost
sequences, query failures and callbacks after Disposal. This round checks the
real installed peer, visible results, focus and picker navigation.

## Cleanup and results

Restore your original Model, Reasoning effort and Mode. The small test turn
remains normal recorded history; no database deletion or reset is needed.
Report cases 1–3 as pass/fail with the Session identity and any surprising row.
Round closed: maintainer accepted the visible fix, then asked about missing Luna
history. Read-only verification found 697 Codex/Luna and 13 OpenCode/Luna legacy
samples still present in usage.json, plus 3 new Codex/Luna dispatched turns in
turns.sqlite3. Legacy aggregates lack complete option attribution and are
intentionally excluded from the new picker. Maintainer acknowledged this
explanation. Historical import is separate existing task louiselm-b1uo.

No product defect filed this round. Do not interpret general acceptance as
separate manual execution of every case. Automated gates: 924 cases/72 groups,
LuaLS zero diagnostics, StyLua and generated API/LuaCATS/vimdoc checks passed.
Evidence and acceptance conversation: codex/01a07cf9-eb38-7ed2-91d4-26a3cb1f4c7a.
Pre-fix tests accepted marginal buckets; new regressions enforce full tuples.
Lesson: disclose that fixing cohort contamination excludes legacy aggregates;
absence from the picker does not mean stored history was deleted.

title: Grill-me needed: who owns trusted skill Attention operations?
description:
Do not resolve this architecture question in passing; confirm the trusted producer contract with the maintainer before implementing louiselm-d6fv.6.6.

Question: which trusted controller owns the durable Admission/posture operation, binds it to a real Session or Run, and emits the exact create/resolve transitions consumed by Attention?

Evidence:
- lua/louiselm/ui/attention.lua:53 requires subject_kind, subject_id and a canonical source_operation_id UUID. Its four skill projection methods have no production callers.
- skills-core/src/admission.rs:63 and :216 accept packages, signer and timestamp and return a signed Generation. There is no Session/Run association, pending operation identity, or create/resolve event stream. generation admit/witness/activate are separate global CLI operations (skills-core/src/cli.rs:824).
- skills-core/src/preflight.rs:24 and :193 explicitly produce prospective artifact snapshots, not authorization or live Session state. Request identities are proposed input. The maintainer confirmed this scope in closed louiselm-9b14; d6fv.6.2 therefore does not supply the authoritative transitions d6fv.6.6 assumed.
- skills-core/src/broker/service.rs:89 exposes initial receipt inspection, without normalized live posture transitions. Open louiselm-qbr.5.1.2 owns canonical lifecycle status and a durable Attention outbox.

Decision threads:
1. Which existing controller owns each operation and its durable replay record? What work belongs in qbr.5.1.2 versus a separate Admission producer?
2. Admission is Agent-scoped global supply; Attention subjects are Session or Run. How does a trusted operator bind an Admission request to its affected subjects, including requests originating outside a Session?
3. What starts and resolves approval pending: candidate registration, beginning the ceremony, signature completion, rejection/cancellation, witness or activation? How do errors/restarts preserve unresolved conditions?
4. Does posture project per dimension or per check operation, and how do simultaneous failures, retries and later trusted resolution retain exact identities and codes?
5. How are event authenticity, observed ordering and replay preserved across the controller/Neovim boundary? Preflight cannot silently gain live authority or turn caller-proposed identities into trusted subjects.

Completion: maintainer-confirmed source ownership, subject binding, operation identity/lifecycle and replay contract, then route independently completable producer/integration work and actual dependencies before resuming d6fv.6.6. No executable changes made.
design:
Maintainer confirmed the complete summary on 2026-09-11: "i confirm we reached shared understanding". Source Session: codex/01a08f40-ff3a-7700-853d-18444f0b78d4. This confirmation authorizes recording this contract and its resulting work items.

1. Scope: skill Attention belongs to a Session or Run actually waiting. Standalone Skill Admission remains in the skills CLI; no global Attention subject or synthetic Session.
2. Ownership: the Control broker owns durable waiting records, operation IDs and replay. The trusted skills tool performs Skill Admission and proves its outcome. Capture-service owns Attention state/delivery; Neovim presents that state.
3. Start: skill_approval_pending begins only when the broker accepts an explicit, policy-permitted request binding exact packaged bytes and intended Agent scope. Candidate discovery alone creates no alert. Changing bytes or Agent scope requires a new request.
4. Initiation: an Agent may request Admission only when its current capability envelope explicitly permits it. The broker derives the subject from its authenticated channel and validates scope. Agent text cannot authorize approval or choose another subject.
5. Approval: clear pending only after exact Admission is signed, verified and durably recorded. Failed signing or uncertain persistence leaves pending. Witness/activation failures remain separate skill_unverified conditions with accurate closed codes; approval is not usable supply by itself.
6. Rejection/cancellation: explicit operator rejection/cancellation records a terminal outcome, clears pending and reports the result to the waiting subject. Resubmission has a new operation ID; delivery retries return the original outcome and never reopen it.
7. Posture: each failed dimension has a separate durable condition and exact failure code. Repeated checks update the same unresolved condition; trusted resolution clears it. A later failure starts a new operation ID.
8. Waivers: a valid Session-scoped operator waiver clears the matching dimension condition while posture remains waived. Expiry or revocation recreates the condition if failure persists. Other dimensions remain unchanged; unattended Runs cannot waive.
9. Continuation: approval records/reports its outcome only. Existing Sessions retain immutable Instruction views. Fresh launch after witnessing/activation and operator Resume retain their existing authorization paths; approval never replaces a Session or resumes a Parked Run.
10. Delivery: reuse the Control broker durable ordered outbox planned in louiselm-qbr.5.1.2, publishing directly to capture-service independently of Neovim. Delivery outages do not change the authoritative outcome. Restart/retries preserve order; stale updates cannot recreate resolved conditions.
11. Subject end: Session Disposal or terminal Run cancels its outstanding requests and clears its skill conditions; retain outcomes and ignore late callbacks for that subject. Park retains its requests. Cancellation neither undoes completed Admission nor cancels another subject.

Vocabulary delta: No change. Existing canonical definitions remain valid; this specifies producer ownership and operation behavior.

Implementation routing: create separate Admission-request, verified-outcome and dimension-posture producer tasks under louiselm-d6fv.6. Keep louiselm-d6fv.6.6 as end-to-end integration. Reuse qbr.5.1.2 for canonical lifecycle/status and the outbox, and d6fv.6.3 for waiver authority. d6fv.6.2 is prospective preflight only, per confirmed louiselm-9b14, and is not an authoritative event producer.
close_reason: Maintainer-confirmed contract recorded in design and routed to d6fv.6.7/.8/.9, integration .6.6, broker outbox and waiver acceptance. Vocabulary unchanged; implementation remains tracked. none:design-decision

Routed P1 tasks d6fv.6.7 request acceptance/terminal outcomes, d6fv.6.8 verified Admission completion, d6fv.6.9 dimension/waiver projection. d6fv.6.6 now integrates .8/.9; removed obsolete .6.2 live-producer dependency.
