title: QA: installed usage skill ranking and trace acceptance
description:
# Manual QA review — installed louiselm-usage

Date: 2026-09-17. Source snapshot: 43e4d34, with a clean worktree before this
review. The test used the installed helper and generated skill; its transcript
does not fingerprint the binary. Index generation: 3255.

Acceptance Session: codex/01a0af06-6722-7623-a3c1-df6541f79867.
Review actor: codex/01a0ae77-ff80-7f92-82c7-989d3557a351.
The maintainer reported “it worked” and supplied that Session.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Installed skill ranks cross-project commands | Passed — record 23, successful bounded JSON; 126200 canonical calls |
| 2 | Ranking traces to a real call and historical evidence | Passed — records 30/37; selected git status call, source records 30/33, 31 retained bytes |
| 3 | Historical option comparison | Partial — missing Claude options handled honestly; durable comparisons used native-only option keys, see F2 |
| 4 | Claude infra project-filter regression | Not exercised by this Session — louiselm-f2ou8 remains open for exact live acceptance |

## Setup and scope

The acceptance Session originated in louiselm.nvim with cwd
/home/lotso/code/louiselm. It read the installed SKILL.md and measurement
reference, then queried the existing index without refreshing it. This round
does not establish a second human invocation from another cwd; implementation
smoke checks for that are already recorded on louiselm-ylo32.

No permission-prompt behavior is under test. No new fixtures, configuration,
hooks, source-history edits, or replays were needed. Automated parser/count
tests were not repeated: this round checks actual Agent use of the installed
skill, not unit behavior already covered by the implementation gates.

## Cases and failure signatures

1. Ask the installed skill to rank most-used commands. Expect bounded rows,
   source coverage and retained-byte units. Failure: missing helper, raw
   transcript dumps, fabricated completeness or equating bytes with billing.
2. Select git status through calls, then show call. Expect a namespaced Session,
   source pointers and explicit missing configuration. Failure: untraceable
   aggregate or inferred Provider/options. The actual selected Claude child
   had options={}, options_complete=false and no durable turn; the final answer
   correctly preserved that uncertainty.
3. Discover options, then compare fixed durable turns. Expect option IDs from
   that subject and known/unknown coverage, with mixed turns excluded. This run
   selected codex.effort and codex.approval_policy from global discovery; all
   1685 fixed turns had null values. That does not prove settings were absent
   from the durable history. A separate read-only reviewer control using
   reasoning_effort returned OpenAI/gpt-6-astra xhigh=656 turns (648 measured)
   and high=362 (355 measured), excluding one mixed turn. That control is not
   maintainer acceptance of the corrected recipe.
4. Pending reproduction: louiselm-usage stats commands --project
   /home/lotso/code/infra --fields family,calls --limit 3, followed by a selected
   native Claude call showing the same project. Failure: omitted calls whose
   later source records explicitly supply cwd. The prior automated/live smoke
   fix is recorded on louiselm-f2ou8; this Session did not run the filter.

## Evidence check

Pinned artifact:
/home/lotso/.codex/sessions/2026/09/17/rollout-2026-09-17T13-00-27-01a0af06-6722-7623-a3c1-df6541f79867.jsonl

```sh
jq -c 'select(.type == "event_msg" and .payload.item.type == "CommandExecution") | {line:input_line_number,exit_code:.payload.item.exit_code,command:.payload.item.command[2]}' /home/lotso/.codex/sessions/2026/09/17/rollout-2026-09-17T13-00-27-01a0af06-6722-7623-a3c1-df6541f79867.jsonl
```

Validated against this run: records 23/30 succeed; record 37 contains successful
show-call output followed by an invalid projection (exit 2); record 51 repairs
that projection; records 58/72 expose the all-null native-option cohorts;
record 65 rejects a second invalid projection; record 93 measures the unknown
executable bucket. The artifact proves recorded commands/results, not binary
identity, every discovered history, or human inspection of each row.

## Findings and lessons

F1 — Existing safe-normalization limitation, louiselm-7p7n0, not fixed here.
The unknown-executable bucket contains 14507 calls and 27121223 retained bytes;
14499 calls have an output measurement and 8 do not. Its signature is null and
normalization is opaque. This is not one missing OS executable. Parser tests
exercise deliberate conservative fallback; only the real corpus establishes

F2 — Subject-specific schema guidance, louiselm-0mv0o, newly filed AX follow-up.
Global option discovery omits query-subject scope; generic field discovery and
diagnostics also required guessing. The run hit two correctly rejected field

accounting defect is established. CLI validation tests passed; the recorded

scope separation and improve the query-specific discovery/recipe.

Determine whether the new `:LouiselmResume` command is available for a normal louiselm.nvim installation using the user configuration in `~/.config/nvim`, and make it available by default if it is not.

title: Submitted context folds disappear in configured editor
description:
The submitted-context outer fold disappears in the maintainer's configured editor, exposing the skill catalog and making fold toggles fail.

## Observed

2026-09-21, installed d344926, editor /run/user/1000/nvim.1229105.0, buffer17, DeepSeek Session deepseek/session-7801c332-5e18-4a3b-a144-da8d49082c22. Before manual interaction, read-only RPC proved outer fold6–205 (level1), nested catalog11–201 (level2), AGENTS.md202–205 and prompt206 outside the folds. After Escape / 6G / reported zo: cursor6:0, Normal mode, foldmethod=manual, foldenable=true, foldlevel99, outer line6 has level0, catalog11–201 level1 and all folds open. Text structure remains intact.

Maintainer traceback: E5108: Lua: nvim_exec2(), line 1: Vim(normal):E490: No fold found; buffer.lua:233 toggle_chat_fold; buffer.lua:1078 mapping callback. The traceback is the za mapping, although the reported key was zo; exact key sequence unverified.

Read-only ufo inspection: attached=true, Fold Status=start, main=treesitter, fallback=indent, selected=indent. Personal provider_selector selects both providers for every filetype, including louiselm-session.

## Root cause

Not yet proven. Likely competing fold ownership: nvim-ufo's asynchronous indent provider replaces LouiseLM's semantic manual folds. apply_incremental_folds (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/buffer.lua:136) trusts installed counts; toggle_chat_fold:227 invokes native za without a fold except for a streaming thought header. Prior louiselm-9wjm comment510 explicitly could not prove the external fold-loss mechanism; do not repeat that hypothesis as established fact.

## Why it was not caught

Existing nested-context coverage runs with no user plugins and verifies immediate native fold operations. It does not reproduce installed automatic fold-provider recomputation.

## Fix direction

Reproduce using already-installed ufo in an isolated editor, then fix the actual ownership boundary. Do not mask missing folds by swallowing E490 or repeatedly recreating folds over the user's open/closed choices. If only personal configuration must change, request authorization for that scope.

## Acceptance

- Reproduction fails before and passes after the narrow fix.
- In the maintainer's normal editor, outer contexts open to resource metadata with catalog body still folded; body independently opens/closes; outer fold remains usable after idle/repeated toggles.
- AGENTS.md order and submitted prompt remain intact; no model credits required to test.

## Not covered

DeepSeek prompt returned only generic Internal error; credit exhaustion is unconfirmed and unrelated to this fold defect. No changes to credentials, permissions, model requests, or the user's live editor are authorized by this investigation.

title: Running identity reports verified from a prefix its own Agent can rewrite
description:
`release::running_identity()` checks that the executable sits inside an installed release, that `current` points at that release, that the executable's hash matches the manifest, and that the compiled policy matches. It does not check who owns the prefix.

## Observed

2026-09-03, smoke test of the louiselm-d6fv.7 pipeline as uid 1000:

```text
$ louiselm-skills release status --prefix /tmp/louiselm-smoke/prefix
  ownership  uid 1000, NOT root-owned, writable beyond root
  trusted    no
  failure    prefix_not_root_owned
exit: 2

$ /tmp/louiselm-smoke/prefix/current/bin/louiselm-skills release identity
verified — The running executable belongs to the current installed release.
exit: 0
```

Two commands disagree about the same prefix. `status` is right.

## Why it matters

`Store::record_provenance` marks a store trusted from `running_identity().verified`, once, at creation. An Agent that copies a legitimately signed release into a directory it can write, runs the installed binary once to create a store marked trusted, and then swaps the binary, gets a trusted store backed by bytes it controls. Signing does not stop this: the bundle was signed by the real release role, it is just installed somewhere that is not a boundary.

## Fix

`verify_installed` must fail when the prefix chain is not root-owned or is writable beyond root, with the same evidence `install::status` already computes. Share one ownership function rather than a second implementation that can drift.

Found by running the pipeline end to end after the automated tests passed; every automated install runs as an ordinary user, so no test could have distinguished the two answers.
close_reason:
running_identity now fails with prefix_not_root_owned or prefix_world_writable when the install prefix is not a boundary, reusing install::ownership_of rather than a second implementation that could drift. Regression test asserts the ordinary-user install reports unverified, which is what every automated run is.

Lesson routed to the d6fv.7 comment: automated installs all run as an ordinary user, so no test could distinguish 'bytes match' from 'bytes are fixed'. Running the pipeline end to end after green tests is what found it.

title: Inline human-readable rendering for jsonl log lines
description:
Idea from conversation, not yet designed: for jsonl files, render each line's *display* as a compact human-readable string (e.g. "14:23:05 WRN nvim.175374 server_start:197 Failed to start server...") via conceal/virtual-text, without touching the underlying buffer content — the file stays true jsonl on disk (greppable/diffable/pipeable).

Context: jsonl.nvim already renders jsonl nicely via treesitter formatting. jsonlogs.nvim takes a different approach — splitting into an expanded pretty-printed panel/view — which trades away the one-line-per-record structure that makes jsonl useful in the first place. That's judged as doing too much for the goal here.

Closer prior art: render-markdown.nvim's approach of decorating a buffer's *display* without mutating its content. Worth checking whether treesitter's line-level virtual text/decoration hooks, or the same conceal machinery jsonl.nvim already uses, can drive this before reaching for a new plugin/dependency.

Not yet scoped as an implementation task — needs design: what subset of jsonl schemas to target (arbitrary vs known log formats), how much configurability, conflict with existing jsonl.nvim formatting.
notes: Deferred by maintainer after live feedback: :LouiselmJsonl works mechanically but feels useless. Compact alphabetical fields and hidden nested values have not established useful readability. Do not continue redesign or request more QA until maintainer resumes it. Current opt-in implementation remains unchanged; usability acceptance was not granted.

comments.author: claude-code/01e02390-3c65-4332-a93e-a9f1a4ff9bef
comments.text:
Implemented as lua/louiselm/forensics/{log_view.lua,command.lua} + :LouiselmForensicsLogView.

Confirmed target: acp-llm-adapter/acp-proxy stdout-jsonrpc.log files under
~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter -- real JSON-RPC 2.0 ACP traffic, one message
per line. Design landed on Neovim's native fold machinery instead of extmark
overlay: foldexpr forces one fold per line, foldtext renders a compact human
summary (dispatches on session/update's sessionUpdate kind, reusing the same
kind vocabulary session/lifecycle.lua already handles), buffer content is
never touched, zo/zO reveals the exact raw line. Reuses acp/protocol.lua's
decode/validate rather than re-parsing JSON-RPC.

Verified live against a real 1051-line log: all lines fold/render, widths
stay bounded, zero errors.

Known limitation, not fixed here: streamed text arrives as one JSON-RPC line
per small delta, so a paragraph of agent_message_chunk/agent_thought_chunk
becomes many one-or-two-word folds rather than one merged block. Fixing that
means multi-line folds keyed on messageId -- a materially bigger feature than
this one-line-to-one-fold v1. Left as a possible follow-up, not filed as a
separate issue yet pending user reaction to v1.

comments.author: claude-code/01e02390-3c65-4332-a93e-a9f1a4ff9bef
comments.text:
Follow-up from live testing: za felt sluggish, and a request to keep this
free of regex.

Regex removed: the only pattern-matching in the file was single_line's gsub
collapsing embedded newlines for display; replaced with plain (non-pattern)
vim.split/table.concat/vim.trim. JSON parsing itself was never regex -- it
already went through vim.json.decode via acp/protocol.lua.

Investigated delegating fold *boundaries* to the already-installed jsonl/json
treesitter fold query instead of the hand-rolled foldexpr, per the instinct
that hand-rolling is redundant when a treesitter parser is already there.
Tested directly: wired foldexpr to vim.treesitter.foldexpr() against a real
log and foldlevel() came back 0 for every line. Root cause: every ACP
JSON-RPC record is exactly one physical line, and Neovim's/Vim's fold model
only ever folds a node whose start and end line differ -- a same-line node
never registers as a fold, treesitter or not. There's no existing
one-fold-per-line building block to delegate to for this shape; forcing a
fold boundary at every line via a custom foldexpr remains the only way to
get it. Documented this finding in the module's doc comment so it isn't
re-litigated later.

Real fix for the sluggishness: foldtext had zero caching -- it re-decoded
and re-summarized the raw line from scratch on every redraw of every visible
closed fold. Added a per-buffer, per-line cache keyed against the exact raw
line text (self-invalidating on edit, no changedtick bookkeeping needed).
Added a test that spies on render_line to prove a repeated foldtextresult()
call for an unchanged line hits the cache instead of re-rendering.

Caveat: benchmarked the fix against the real 1051-line log used earlier
(lines up to 55KB) and could not reproduce dramatic sluggishness even before
this fix -- full-buffer foldtextresult sweep ~26ms, 50x za ~1ms in headless
timing. So either this fix already resolves what was felt live, or the
tested file differs from what's slow, or the slowness is in real terminal
redraw rather than computation. Asked the user to re-test and report back
with which file if still slow.

comments.author: claude-code/01e02390-3c65-4332-a93e-a9f1a4ff9bef
comments.text:
Reverted (commits a531705, 771484a): the ACP-only forensics implementation
did not satisfy after two rounds of live testing, even after the caching
fix -- za still didn't feel right in practice.

Redirecting scope back to the original framing: fast and generic, not
ACP-log-specific. It must work on arbitrary jsonl, including this project's
own .beads/issues.jsonl -- the ACP-only implementation didn't (it only
understood JSON-RPC envelopes via acp/protocol.lua).

New technical direction to explore: jsonlogs.nvim's split-panel approach is
still judged as doing too much (see original description), but its
rendering logic might be replicable faster and more generically by building
on an actual jsonl treesitter parser (jsonl.nvim's tree-sitter-jsonl grammar
is already installed) rather than hand-decoding each line with
vim.json.decode + hand-written per-field-shape summarizers in Lua. Worth
investigating before the next attempt: whether treesitter's own incremental
parse/query caching (as opposed to this repo's foldtext-per-redraw
recompute) is what actually gets the performance and genericness right, and
whether fold boundaries still need the hand-rolled one-line-forces-a-fold
trick (still true per the prior finding: same-line nodes never register as
a Vim fold) or whether a non-fold display mechanism reads better anyway.

Deferred pending a redesign; not closing since the underlying need (some
of these logs are unreadable one-line JSON) is still real.

comments.author: codex/01a0d3a0-9c6d-73f0-be4d-df2e421f9b47

title: Explore code-contracts as a LouiseLM verification aid
description:
Evaluate whether spolu/code-contracts or a minimal equivalent improves LouiseLM agent workflow verification beyond existing AGENTS.md, Beads acceptance criteria, and executable tests.

Hypothesis: colocated contracts could make cross-cutting invariants easier for agents to discover and review, especially around broker authority, Session disposal, launcher receipts, and Verified posture.

Constraints: do not add a dependency or adopt the format broadly before evidence; current checker appears focused on TypeScript/Python/Go/Rust and LouiseLM is primarily Lua plus Rust.

Experiment: choose one Rust security boundary already covered by existing work, write a compact contract or equivalent, seed a plausible violation, and determine whether the contract catches anything existing tests/review do not. Record false positives, maintenance cost, and whether it improves agent-generated verification evidence. If it only duplicates current instructions/tests, close as not useful.

title: Grill-me needed: broker trust access for Admission outcomes
description:
Do not resolve this trust-boundary question in passing; confirm the authority and access contract with the maintainer before implementing louiselm-d6fv.6.8.

Question: how does the dedicated Control broker obtain independently trusted Admission evidence from the operator-owned skills store, including current enrollment/rotation state and exact package bytes, without gaining signing or supply-write authority?

Evidence:
- skills-core/src/cli.rs:443 and :1259 let the skills CLI select a store via --store/environment/operator home. No broker-pinned skills store exists in LauncherConfig (skills-core/src/launcher_install.rs:194).
- skills-core/src/admission.rs:216 signs/verifies, writes a PendingWitness Generation, then persists approved_admissions in trust. A returned Generation or client success alone cannot prove both writes are durable.
- admission::load_verified acquires transaction::lock. That read path can recover an interrupted activation and therefore writes supply. It is not a read-only broker verifier.
- skills-core/src/trust/persistence.rs creates trust directories mode0700 and roles/lock files mode0600. A separately installed broker UID has no existing access contract to the operator store.
- Existing operator IPC pins operator UID but cannot turn caller-supplied keys, store provenance or claimed success into an independently anchored verification root.

Decision threads:
1. Which protected configuration pins the authoritative skills store/trust domain for linked requests? May a linked CLI invocation select another store?
2. Should the broker receive narrowly provisioned read-only access to the existing protected store, or verify a proof through a separate already-trusted producer? Who owns rotations/revocation freshness and recovery of interrupted writes?
3. How is durable ceremony linkage established before signing so process death after Admission persistence can be reconciled without repeating signing?
4. Keep standalone Admission unchanged, operator signing access private, existing Instruction views immutable, and no activation/Resume authority in this integration.

Completion: confirm the trust/access contract, record it, then implement the smallest integrated CLI/broker slice and its cross-identity/restart tests. No executable changes yet.
design: Maintainer confirmed 2026-09-16: explicitly configured, read-only broker access to Admission evidence in the existing trusted skills store; signing and all supply/recovery writes remain in the skills tool. Pin source and trust domain through protected installed configuration; linked CLI requests cannot supply a new trust root. Unset stays disabled; standalone Admission unchanged. Reuse current trust/enrollment and exact package records, refusing unsettled recovery rather than repairing it from the broker. No activation, Instruction-view replacement or Resume authority.
close_reason: none:design — maintainer confirmed explicitly configured read-only broker evidence access; signing and writes remain in skills tool.

title: Park
description: Non-destructive suspension of a Run: every in-flight turn is Cancelled, Sessions are retained where possible, and the Run waits for an operator decision under a declared expiry. Warm Park stays within one Neovim lifetime and resumes exactly. Cold Park has survived an editor exit, so its Sessions are gone and resume is lossy reconstruction via ACP loadSession.
design: Established by the louiselm-qbr.8 grill-me session on 2026-08-26, with explicit maintainer confirmation of the final summary. Chosen over killing an over-budget Run, because an attention control plane whose response to 'this needs a decision' is to destroy the work has inverted its own thesis. The warm/cold split follows from Agents being vim.system children of Neovim (lua/louiselm/acp/transport.lua:164).
notes: Distinguish from the existing triad: Park is not Disposal (a deliberate end) and not Abandonment (loss). Park expiry converts a Park into a Disposal, releasing claims and retaining Forensics. Per the Staged context record, cold-Park resume is recoverable, NOT lossless. An Agent that does not advertise loadSession cannot be cold-Parked at all, and admission must say so up front. Resuming a Park is an operator act, never an Agent act, and cannot exceed the original envelope on any axis.

title: Systemd broker startup rejects its redundant primary group
description: Observed 2026-09-14 in disposable Debian 13 VM, systemd 257: systemd-run --pipe --wait --collect --property=User=nobody --property=Group=nogroup /usr/bin/python3 -c "import os; print(os.getgroups())" prints [65534]. skills-core/src/broker/installed.rs:237 rejects every nonempty getgroups result, including the already-effective primary GID, so the requested User=/Group= system service cannot start. Existing installed_daemon_tests.rs uses setpriv --clear-groups and misses the actual manager shape. Fix at installed broker validation: accept an empty list or entries equal to configured primary GID; reject every additional GID. No new group authority is granted. Acceptance: installed daemon gate starts with the primary supplementary GID, refuses an unrelated supplementary GID, and existing wrong-identity refusals remain. Discovered while implementing louiselm-96pv.5; real vendor/live editor acceptance is out of scope.
close_reason: Accept redundant primary GID; reject every extra group. Lesson and red/green evidence in issue. gate:skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/installed_daemon_tests.rs

title: Admission pin append can discard unreadable lineage
description:
Observed during lint adoption, source inspection only; no live data loss reproduced. skills-core/src/admission.rs:624 record_pin uses read_to_string(pins.jsonl).unwrap_or_default() before rewriting the entire file. Invalid UTF-8 or a transient read failure is indistinguishable from absence and can erase prior lineage when the subsequent write succeeds. Existing tests do not cover an unreadable existing pin log.

Fix direction: treat only NotFound as an empty log; preserve other read errors and leave bytes untouched. Keep lineage append ordering/durability explicit.

Acceptance: regression through Admission activation with an invalid-UTF-8 existing pins.jsonl returns an error without replacing its bytes; absent and valid logs still append correctly. Record observed failure before implementation. Deferred from louiselm-xhgy; lint checks do not detect semantic error swallowing.
close_reason: Preserve unreadable pin bytes and propagate non-NotFound I/O errors. Missing and valid logs still append. Rust gates pass via documented ACP test workaround; activation transaction defect tracked in louiselm-had9. gate:skills-core/tests/admission.rs:224

title: Analyse DDD and AI-coding lessons for the LouiseLM workflow
description:
## Goal

Analyse Miłosz Smółka's article, Domain-Driven Design matters more when AI writes your code, and translate its findings into concrete improvements or deliberate non-changes for the LouiseLM agent workflow.

Source: https://threedots.tech/post/ddd-and-ai-coding/

## Scope

- In scope: the article claims about domain modeling as shared understanding, design before code generation, ubiquitous language and bounded contexts, developer accountability, and not delegating thinking.
- In scope: map those claims against LouiseLM concepts and practices including canonical vocabulary, grill-me design sessions, Beads work tracking, AGENTS.md contracts, Sessions, Runs, Handoffs, Validation, Assessment, Forensics, and tracer-bullet tasks.
- In scope: recommend a small set of actionable workflow changes, with expected benefit and tradeoff.
- Out of scope: adopting tactical DDD patterns in the Lua implementation, introducing ceremony for simple CRUD-like work, or treating the article as authoritative evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Summarize the authors findings accurately and distinguish direct claims from interpretation.
2. Produce an application map showing which LouiseLM workflow surfaces already embody each idea and where gaps remain.
3. Recommend no more than five concrete changes, each with rationale, scope, and a way to test whether it helps.
4. Explicitly identify practices to avoid because they would add ceremony without improving domain clarity.
5. Record unresolved product or architecture choices as separate needs-design questions rather than silently deciding them.

## Testing

- Verify each article-derived claim against the source URL.
- Check proposed terminology against the repository vocabulary reference records.
- Ensure recommendations preserve the project contract: correctness and safety first, explicit lifecycle ownership, bounded work generation, and no unnecessary abstractions.

## Notes

The article is an opinion piece about complex, long-lived software rather than a universal process prescription. The analysis should treat LouiseLM itself as the domain under discussion and focus on improving how humans and Agents build shared understanding before implementation.
close_reason: Analysis complete, posted as a comment on this issue. Summary: LouiseLM's existing loop (Grill, vocabulary/reference records, Live acceptance discipline) already embodies nearly every claim in the article -- likely because both were independently designed around the same values (shared understanding over artifacts, human accountability, explicit reasoning capture). 3 recommendations (not padded to 5): R1 write down the already-practiced but unstated grill-proportionality rule; R2 filed separately as louiselm-n83s since it changes the vocabulary contract; R3 confirmed the existing close-discipline already satisfies the article's 'don't delegate thinking' concern, no new mechanism needed. 4 practices explicitly flagged to avoid as ceremony. Full AC-by-AC mapping and verbatim article verification in the comment.

comments.author: claude/ea8b846d-3700-44ed-aa39-ffb9e68c8973
comments.text:
## 1. Summary: direct claims vs. interpretation

Source verified directly (https://threedots.tech/post/ddd-and-ai-coding/, Miłosz Smółka,
2026-08-20).

**Direct claims** (the author states these as the article's thesis, not hedged):

1. Eric Evans' 2003 claim still holds: "the hard part of software engineering is understanding
   the problem domain and modeling it well in code" -- AI changes *what* is hard to produce, not
   *what* is hard to understand.
2. A domain model's value is the team's shared understanding built while making it, not the
   artifact itself; letting AI generate a domain model from documents skips the part that
   mattered.
3. Design and team discussion should happen *before* code generation, not be reconstructed
   afterward through PR review -- otherwise review becomes "the start of a discussion" instead of
   "a double-check."
4. Ubiquitous language matters *more* with agents because "they'll look for the names you give
   them" and may naively unify entities that are legitimately distinct (bounded contexts).
5. Trusting AI output requires someone accountable who understands the domain well enough to
   catch it when the output is wrong.
6. Much of engineering is thinking, not typing; delegating the thinking erodes the mental models
   needed to judge future AI output, so working problems by hand still has value.

**Interpretation / more contestable** (author's own framing, illustrative rather than argued):

- The "agentic setup optimization" trap as a direct successor to framework-obsession -- an
  analogy, not demonstrated.
- The $1/month anecdote is one illustrative failure, not a controlled finding.
- "Keep documentation in Markdown near code" is a specific tooling preference, not a general law.
- The closing "mix old-school and new" stance is explicitly hedged by the author as uncertain.

## 2. Application map

LouiseLM's own working loop (`docs/example-workflow.md`) and vocabulary system
(`br list --type vocabulary --status all`) were designed independently of this article, before it
existed, but converge on nearly every one of its claims -- which is itself the most useful finding
here.

| Article idea | LouiseLM surface | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Domain model's value is team understanding, not the artifact | **Grill** stage: "The stage ends when both sides can state the same plan. Not before." Vocabulary records carry a `design` field citing *which grill session* produced them, not just a definition. | Strong match |
| Design before code generation | **Grill -> Route to beads**: reasoning and rejected alternatives are captured in the issue *before* Execute. | Match, but heavier by default than the article's "sticky notes" framing -- see gap below |
| Ubiquitous language; agents will naively unify distinct entities | 15 `vocabulary/reference` Beads records, each with an explicit `notes` field naming what to **avoid** and what to **distinguish**. `louiselm-7bm3` (Provider) exists *because* Provider/Agent got conflated once already -- the exact failure mode the article warns about, already caught. `AGENTS.md` requires loading this vocabulary before any semantic work. | Strong match, arguably exceeds the article -- it's a durable, queryable glossary with negative space, not just a team agreement |
| Bounded contexts: same concept, different valid names per subsystem | Not present. Current convention is one canonical name, enforced project-wide, with everything else listed as "avoid." | Gap, but arguably correct at this scale -- see Avoid-list below |
| Developers (or the maintainer) stay accountable, domain-expert-trusted | "the decisions, and only the decisions, belong to the human" (Grill). `AGENTS.md` section 5.2, Live acceptance: automated gates cannot close a defect while a live reproduction exists -- "keep it open until the maintainer confirms." | Strong match -- LouiseLM structurally refuses to let an agent self-certify domain-level correctness |
| Don't delegate thinking | Grill's one-question-at-a-time-with-a-recommended-answer protocol is a *structural* answer to this: the human reacts and corrects rather than generating from a blank page, which keeps judgment engaged without maximal friction. This is a genuine LouiseLM-specific mechanism the article doesn't describe -- the article's own remedy is individual (spend time thinking), LouiseLM's is procedural. | Strong match, and a real point of originality worth naming, not just a mapping |

One structural point the article doesn't address at all, because it doesn't apply to a human
team: every LouiseLM agent session starts with *zero* memory of prior sessions. `AGENTS.md` plus
the vocabulary records are the mechanism by which a domain-illiterate newcomer (every session, by
construction) becomes domain-literate fast enough to be trusted with real decisions. This
session's own bootstrap -- reading `AGENTS.md` cold, loading vocabulary, following the
close-discipline correctly across four issue closes today -- is itself evidence the mechanism
works, not just a claim that it should.

## 3. Recommendations (3, not padded to 5)

**R1 -- Write down the grill-proportionality rule that is already being practiced but never
stated.**
Today's session closed `louiselm-7tvl`, `louiselm-qbr.3.2.5`, and `louiselm-nwrv` on evidence
alone, no grill; `kd2b` (this one) and prior architecture work (Park, Run, Generator) went through
full grill-me sessions. The size-matching already happens correctly, but there's no written
criterion an agent or the maintainer could consult to check a borderline case, or teach it to a
new contributor. *Scope:* a short addition to `docs/example-workflow.md`'s Grill section, not a
new mechanism. *Test:* take five recently-closed issues, hide their actual resolution path, and
check whether the written criterion predicts which ones needed a grill and which didn't.

**R2 -- Decide whether the vocabulary schema should ever support a bounded-context-style
surface-specific name, before it's forced under time pressure.**
Today's vocabulary already contains one near-miss: AX and UX are a deliberate split of what is
largely the same underlying state into two audience-facing names. As AX surfaces grow relative to
UX, LouiseLM may need the same concept to legitimately read differently in an agent-facing surface
vs. a human-facing one -- exactly what DDD bounded contexts exist for. Today's convention (one
canonical name, everything else is "avoid") would fight that if it happens. This changes a
project-wide contract (the vocabulary schema and its consumption rule in `AGENTS.md`), so per the
project's own vocabulary-conflict rule ("If competing meanings would materially change
architecture... stop and ask"), **I filed this as a needs-design question
(`louiselm-n83s`) instead of deciding it here.**

**R3 -- Nothing further to build; the existing close-discipline already does what the article asks
for.**
I looked for a gap in "does an agent's solo decision get checked for real understanding, not just
pattern-matching" (the sharpest form of "don't delegate thinking" applied to an agent instead of a
human). `AGENTS.md`'s close-discipline already requires routing what the work taught -- evidence,
false starts, or a named destination -- before closing a bug/task/feature, which is exactly the
"write down why, not just what" mechanism the article recommends. This session's own closes today
complied with it every time. No new rule needed; recorded here so the "don't delegate thinking"
claim was actually checked against a mechanism rather than assumed satisfied.

## 4. Practices to avoid (ceremony without domain-clarity benefit)

- **A full grill-me session for every closeable issue.** Today's evidence-based closes (`7tvl`,
  `qbr.3.2.5`, `nwrv`) would have been pure overhead if forced through interrogation; the decision
  was already unambiguous from the code and tests.
- **Adopting DDD's bounded-context tooling wholesale** (context maps, anti-corruption layers,
  per-subsystem glossaries). LouiseLM is one small codebase without the multi-team integration
  costs that justify bounded-context pluralism. The current single-canonical-name-with-explicit-
  avoid-list is stricter and correct at this scale; loosening it without the underlying problem
  (R2 aside, which is a narrow, deliberate exception, not a wholesale adoption) would just
  reintroduce naming drift.
- **A mandatory domain-model diagram or UML artifact as a Grill deliverable.** The article's own
  central warning is that an AI-generated domain model fails because it substitutes an artifact
  for the understanding that was supposed to produce it. Adding a required diagram step would risk
  exactly that trap inside the mechanism meant to prevent it.
- **A formal prompt-precision style guide for Beads issue descriptions**, modeled on the article's
  vague-vs-precise prompting example. Today's issue descriptions (including several read closely
  this session) are already precise by convention. Formalizing an already-solved problem is
  ceremony, not improvement.

## 5. Unresolved question filed separately

`louiselm-n83s` -- "Grill-me needed: should the vocabulary schema support a bounded-context-style
surface-specific name, and if so, what's the rule for when it's allowed vs. drift?" -- labeled
`needs-design`, per R2 above. Not resolved here.

title: Enable strict Rust gates in capture-service
description:
Adopt the strict Rust policy requested in codex/01a07354-d702-77b2-a532-dbd96f279510 and recorded by louiselm-klkw.

title: Run
description: One execution instance of a workflow definition. A Run owns a supervision tree of Sessions, a bounded budget for generated work, a capability envelope, and a durable record held by capture-service that outlives the Neovim process.
design: Established by the louiselm-qbr.8 grill-me session on 2026-08-26, with explicit maintainer confirmation of the final summary. Established because Validation (definition-scoped, static) and admission (Run-scoped, live) are provably different contracts: an open skill graph makes recursion undecidable from any single document.
notes: Use Run for the execution instance and for anything scoped to it (Run budget, Run ancestry, Run record). Distinguish from the workflow definition, which is a static SKILL.md graph shared by many Runs. Avoid: execution, job, invocation. A Run owns Sessions; it is not itself a Session.

title: Launcher broker waits have no cleanup deadline
description: SeqpacketChannel::receive and connector/accept workers can block indefinitely (skills-core/src/launch_transport.rs:457-470,539-551). Add a bounded cancellable wait used by launch authorization and ACK; timeout closes the channel and completes cleanup exactly once. Test both phases with a silent peer.

title: Launcher VM preparation omits compile-time test inputs
description:
Fresh launcher-VM preparation cannot compile all current skills-core tests because its source archive omits five compile-time inputs outside the crate.

## Observed

2026-09-24, source c6e49ff, Session codex/01a0d1f7-c72b-7691-955e-b76f481e9aac, while accepting louiselm-e8en.

The preparation command at scripts/launcher-vm:189 archives only skills-core and tests/fixtures/verified_posture_v1.json. Running that exact git archive selection through tar -t and filtering tests/fixtures or docs produces only:

    tests/fixtures/
    tests/fixtures/verified_posture_v1.json

Current committed Rust tests consume these missing inputs with include_str!:

- tests/fixtures/provider_config.json (skills-core/tests/registry.rs:33)
- tests/fixtures/preflight_v1.json and preflight_request_v2.json (skills-core/tests/preflight_cli.rs:126,130)
- tests/fixtures/broker_attention_projection.json (skills-core/tests/broker/attention.rs:104)
- docs/recovery-ceremony.md (skills-core/tests/onboarding.rs:22)

## Root cause and test gap

The preparation source bundle was not kept current with external compile-time fixtures. Host Cargo sees the full checkout, while launcher-vm safety tests exercise command boundaries without preparing/building a real guest. Fixing OpenSSL headers alone cannot make this archive compile.

## Fix direction

Add the five exact committed inputs to the existing archive selection and update its documentation. Preserve source pinning, offline guest builds, and the existing isolation settings; do not transfer the host checkout or unrelated operator data.

## Acceptance

- The recipe archive includes all six external include_str inputs (existing posture fixture plus these five files).
- Fresh preparation compiles all current tests with the fetched locked cache.
- The conformance entrypoint builds/runs with Cargo offline in the restricted guest, recorded on louiselm-e8en.

The archive inventory is the red evidence. The path-list correction is mechanical; verify it through actual preparation/compilation instead of adding a source-spelling assertion. No desktop installation or Verified-cutover claim.
close_reason: gate:scripts/launcher-vm fresh prepare compiled all current test targets offline after including five missing files; source/digests and guest conformance in comment2568. Lesson routed to corrected recipe and docs/launcher-vm.md.

title: Beads inspector rejects installed br issue data
description:
Louiselm’s Beads inspector repeatedly reports errors instead of opening the selected issue. The failure is visible in the notification history and is reproducible from the captured session screenshot; the exact cause of the mismatch between the installed br output and the inspector parser is not yet established.

## Observed

Screenshot: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260901_1500_1920x1200_1788267612.png
Captured 2026-09-01 at 15:00 in the maintainer’s louiselm Neovim session. Notification history contains four errors:

> ERROR louiselm: br returned malformed issue data
> ERROR louiselm: br returned malformed issue data
> ERROR louiselm: br returned malformed issue data
> ERROR louiselm: could not read Beads issue louiselm-df70

The buffer behind the popup shows Beads inspection/triage output, and the command line identifies a Beads issue id (`d7f0`).

## Symptoms

- Selecting/inspecting a Beads issue does not open the issue view.
- The user sees repeated malformed-data and could-not-read notifications.

## Root cause

Unknown. The UI path runs `br show <id> --json` in `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:230-253`, decodes stdout, and rejects a nil decoded issue at `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:260-269`. A possible cause is that the installed br emits a valid JSON shape not accepted by `decode_issue`, but this must be confirmed from the live command output before fixing.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/beads_spec.lua:490-510` covers invalid JSON, while `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua:512-535` covers a nonzero br exit. There is no regression fixture for the actual successful `br show --json` output produced by the maintainer’s installed br version.

## Fix direction

Capture the non-sensitive stdout and exit status from the failing `br show --json` invocation, then align the parser and error classification at the shared Beads lookup boundary. Preserve rejection of malformed JSON and mismatched issue ids.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails against the observed output before the fix and passes after it.
- Inspecting the issue under the cursor opens the correct Beads issue without an error notification.

## Not covered

The screenshot does not establish whether `louiselm-df70` or `louiselm-d7f0` is the selected id, nor whether the br process returned malformed JSON, a different issue, or a nonzero exit. No code or configuration was changed in this report.
close_reason: Fixed: decode_issue treated a missing description key as malformed; now defaults to empty string like labels does. See comment for root cause and test.

comments.author: claude/ae23ad27-5122-4780-9c81-cbe9080fadba
comments.text:
Root cause: br show --json omits the description key entirely (not "") when an issue has none, e.g. closed fixture louiselm-qced. decode_issue at lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:77 required type(issue.description) == "string", rejecting the whole payload as malformed -- same class of bug as the labels omission fixed for louiselm-t6j2, just not applied to description. The df70/d7f0 not_found symptom in the original report is a separate cursor-token mismatch, not this decode bug; left unaddressed per the issue's own 'Not covered' note.

Fix: lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:77,94 -- allow issue.description == nil, default to "" (mirrors the labels ~= nil handling one line above). Regression test: tests/ui/beads_spec.lua, 'opens an issue whose JSON omits the description key entirely (louiselm-kk27)', reproduces with the exact louiselm-qced shape, failed before the fix (assert nil) and passes after. Full mini.test suite, stylua, lua-language-server, and both --check generators all pass. --json

title: QA round: cold Park command + tool inspector close + onboarding Tutor (ab8e71c..HEAD)
description:
# Manual QA review — cold Park feature + tool inspector close + onboarding Tutor

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `ab8e71c..HEAD` (7 commits, 2026-08-28 14:53–16:21):
`44b7cdd` close tool inspector with `q`, `71a6ae3` add cold Park command,
`64523ac` restore Park Run state, `097bcd6` add first-run onboarding Tutor.
(`f092fec`, `862fd1e`, `8782442` are README/CI-only — no manual case.)
**Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: last QA round closed at `ab8e71c`. Everything since is untested by a
human. The headline change is `:LouiselmPark`/`:LouiselmResumePark` growing
real state: zero-claim Park is now allowed (previously rejected), and resume
now reconstructs `claims`/`generated_work` instead of discarding them.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Tool inspector closes with `q` / `<Esc>` | **passed** — both keys close the floating window and return focus, per user report |
| 2 | `:LouiselmTutor` opens read-only Tutor | **passed** — well-formatted content, resolved from runtime path not cwd, edits blocked, per user report |
| 3 | `:LouiselmPark` succeeds with zero live claims | **passed (partial)** — proven via case 4's run record (`claims:[]`, `state:cold_parked`); the "no picker when nothing staged" half wasn't separately exercised |
| 4 | `:LouiselmPark` with staged context asks to confirm; Cancel aborts | **passed** — `claude/6b80a87e-…380d`: Cancel produced no notification and no run; Park produced run `72a8fa90-b11a-4dc7-a918-57f3c8fc5a64`, `state:"cold_parked"`, `claims:[]` |
| 5 | `:LouiselmResumePark` restores claims + generated-work budget | **blocked on F1** — resume never completes, so restoration can't be observed |

## Setup

The nvim plugin checkout at `~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim`
is a separate git worktree tracking this repo (`origin` = `file:///home/lotso/code/louiselm`),
currently at `097bcd6` — already matches HEAD, no reinstall needed for the Lua
side.

**`louiselm-capture` is stale and will block cases 3–5.** The binary on `PATH`
at `~/.local/bin/louiselm-capture` is dated 2026-08-26 20:46 — built *before*
`run admit`/`run attach` existed and before the Run schema moved to version 4
(commit `c65ca9f`, 2026-08-27). Confirmed by hand: it rejects `run admit`/`run
attach` outright ("run supports only list and park") and fails `run list`
against any schema-v4 file with `invalid run: stored Run is invalid` — that is
what's currently happening against your own `~/.local/state/louiselm/workflow/runs/`
(two already-expired parked runs from earlier today trip the same stale
check; they're harmless leftovers that a rebuilt binary will just filter out
as expired, no cleanup needed).

Rebuild and install before cases 3–5:

```bash
cd /home/lotso/code/louiselm/capture-service && cargo build --release
cp target/release/louiselm-capture ~/.local/bin/louiselm-capture
louiselm-capture run list   # expect: [] (not an error) — proves the binary is current
```

I already ran the `cargo build --release` — it succeeded and `target/release/louiselm-capture`
is current. I have **not** copied it over `~/.local/bin/louiselm-capture` yet:
that file also backs your running `louiselm-capture.service` (systemd
`ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/louiselm-capture serve`), so say go-ahead before I
overwrite it. You don't need to restart the service — the CLI subcommands used
by Park (`run admit`/`attach`/`park`/`list`) touch the filesystem directly,
never the daemon.

**Do not run `:LouiselmPark` from the session you're reading this in.** I
checked the live instance (`$NVIM`): your current chat view's session *is*
this Claude Code session (`claude/5f934d18-b9b8-42b3-91cc-35fb293d14dc`).
Cold-Parking it would suspend the session you're driving me from. For cases
3–5, open a **second**, disposable chat session in the same Neovim instance
(`:Louiselm` → new session, any agent) and drive Park/Resume from that one.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- A `louiselm-capture` binary on `PATH` that predates the Run schema it's
  asked to read fails closed with a generic "stored Run is invalid" — no
  version number in the message. If case 3/4/5 fails with exactly that text,
  suspect a stale binary before suspecting the Lua change; re-run the `run
  list` sanity check in Setup.
- `br list --assignee <session_id> --status in_progress` is what `:LouiselmPark`
  queries for live claims — it needs `session_id` to be `<agent>/<acp_session_id>`
  exactly, and needs the `br` binary in the shim'd `PATH` `service.lua` builds
  (see `Run tools require the br shim, br, and louiselm-capture executables`).
  If claims come back empty when you expected one, confirm the issue is really
  claimed by that exact session id: `br list --assignee <id> --status in_progress --json`.

## Cases

### 1. Tool inspector closes with `q` and `<Esc>`

Exercises `44b7cdd` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1230-1237`.

The automated test only asserts the inspector *buffer* becomes invalid after
calling the keymap callback directly — it never asserts what happens to the
*floating window* on a real close, which is the part a human notices.

Steps:

> In your live chat buffer, trigger any tool call (e.g. ask the agent to read
> a file). Move the cursor onto the tool-call summary line and inspect it
> (however you normally open the tool inspector — winbar click or its mapped
> keymap). With the floating inspector window focused, press `q`.

Expect: the floating window disappears entirely and focus returns to the chat
buffer/window you were in before opening the inspector. Repeat, but press
`<Esc>` instead of `q`, from a fresh tool inspection — same result.

Failure signature: the window stays open but goes blank/empty (buffer deleted
but window not closed — Neovim can replace a deleted buffer's window with an
alternate buffer instead of closing it), or focus lands somewhere unexpected
(e.g. a different existing window) rather than back on the chat.

### 2. `:LouiselmTutor` opens a read-only onboarding Tutor

Exercises `097bcd6` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:295-310`.

Steps:

> Run `:LouiselmTutor`.

Expect: opens `docs/tutorial.md` (resolved from the plugin's `runtimepath`,
not your cwd) in the current window, `filetype=markdown`, and the buffer is
non-modifiable — try `i` + type a character, or `:normal! ihello`, and confirm
Neovim refuses the edit (`E21: Cannot make changes, 'modifiable' is off`).

Failure signature: command errors with "could not find the bundled Tutor"
(runtime-file resolution broken — check `nvim_get_runtime_file("docs/tutorial.md", false)`
directly), or the buffer opens editable.

### 3. `:LouiselmPark` succeeds with zero live Beads claims

Exercises `71a6ae3` (`service.lua` dense-array validation, no longer requires
`#claims > 0`) + the `capture-service` CLI fix filtering empty `--claims`
entries. This is the actual behavior change in this round: before, Park
*required* at least one `in_progress`-claimed issue for the parking session or
it errored; now zero is fine.

Needs: Setup done (rebuilt `louiselm-capture` installed), a **second** chat
session (see Setup), and that session's `<agent>/<acp_session_id>` must have
**no** Beads issue currently claimed to it — sanity-check with
`br list --assignee <agent>/<acp_session_id> --status in_progress --json` and
expect `{"issues":[]}` before you start.

Steps:

> In the second session, with no staged context (no queued prompt, no pending
> skill, no staged file), run `:LouiselmPark`.

Expect: a single `louiselm: Session cold-Parked` notification, no error. No
confirmation picker (there's nothing staged to warn about).

Failure signature: `louiselm: Park record claims must be a non-empty array`
(old validation still active — binary not actually rebuilt) or any other
`louiselm: ...` error notification.

Evidence: `louiselm-capture run list` should show the new run, `cold_parked`,
with `"claims":[]`.

### 4. `:LouiselmPark` with staged context asks to confirm first

Exercises `71a6ae3` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` — the `has_staged`
branch of `Chat:park`, entirely new UI-interaction code with no automated
coverage (the existing test only exercises the no-staged-context path).

Steps:

> In a second, disposable session (same rule as case 3), stage something —
> easiest is typing a prompt into the input and *not* sending it (a queued
> prompt), or stage a file/context item the way you normally do. Then run
> `:LouiselmPark`.

Expect: a picker appears with prompt text naming what will be lost, e.g.
`louiselm: queued prompt will not survive cold Park; proceed? ` with options
`Park` / `Cancel`. Choosing **Cancel** leaves the session open and unparked —
your queued prompt/staged item is still there afterward. Re-run `:LouiselmPark`
and choose **Park** this time: it proceeds and cold-Parks (same notification
as case 3), and the staged item is gone (Park doesn't survive it — that's the
whole point of the warning).

Failure signature: no picker shown (staged context silently discarded or
silently blocks Park with no explanation), or `Cancel` still parks the
session, or the reasons text doesn't match what was actually staged (e.g. says
"pending skill selection" when you only queued a prompt).

### 5. `:LouiselmResumePark` restores claims and generated-work budget

Exercises `64523ac` end to end — this is the one case that needs a *real*
claimed issue threaded all the way through `br` → cold Park → durable storage
→ resume, which the mocked unit tests (fake `nvim.system`, fake picker)
cannot prove.

Needs: Setup done, a second disposable session, and one Beads issue actually
claimed to that session — e.g.
`br update <some-ready-issue-id> --claim --actor "<agent>/<acp_session_id>"`
(pick a low-stakes issue you don't mind claimed-then-released; unclaim it in
Cleanup below regardless of outcome).

Steps:

> With the issue claimed, run `:LouiselmPark` in that second session (expect
> `louiselm: Session cold-Parked`, same as case 3 but now with one live
> claim). Then close/detach that chat view (however you normally dismiss a
> session without disposing the plugin), and run `:LouiselmResumePark`. Pick
> the just-parked run from the picker.

Expect: `louiselm: cold Park resumed (recoverable, lossy)`. Tell me when
you're at this point and I'll pull `owner_run.claims` / `owner_run.generated_work`
off the live resumed session through the `$NVIM` socket to confirm the claim
id round-tripped and the budget numbers match what `run admit` set
(`ceiling=1`, since `PARK_GENERATED_WORK_MAX = 1` in `init.lua`).

Failure signature: resume notification never fires / fires with an error
instead, or (only checkable via the evidence pull) `owner_run.claims` is `{}`
or missing the claimed issue id, or `generated_work` is `nil`/zeroed instead
of the admitted ceiling.

## Evidence check

`louiselm-capture run list` after each Park (case 3, 4-Park-branch, 5) prints
the durable run JSON including `claims` — this is the one thing that proves
Park actually persisted rather than just showing an optimistic UI
notification. It does *not* prove the UI-side `owner_run` object matches;
for case 5 I'll pull that separately through the `$NVIM` socket once you
confirm the resume notification appeared.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- Unclaim the Beads issue used in case 5:
  `br update <issue-id> --status open --actor "<agent>/<acp_session_id>"` (or
  whatever its prior status/assignee was — check before you claimed it).
- Dispose the second chat session(s) opened for cases 3–5.
- Any leftover `cold_parked` run records from these cases self-expire
  (`PARK_TTL_MS` = 24h) — no manual deletion needed unless you want
  `run list` clean immediately: `rm ~/.local/state/louiselm/workflow/runs/<id>.json`.

## Reporting back

Send me the run id, which case, what you saw, and anything surprising. I pull
the evidence myself. If something is wrong I will fix it, and you will need to
redo Setup before retesting.

## Findings this round

**F1 — `:LouiselmResumePark` fails unconditionally for `claude` sessions** (`louiselm-aaw0.1`, open,
not fixed). `ACP session/load failed: Resource not found: <acp_session_id>` on every resume
attempt, including one in the same still-running Neovim process that created the Park — rules out
"lost on editor restart" as the cause; `session/load` itself doesn't work here. Reproduced twice
(runs `72a8fa90-b11a-4dc7-a918-57f3c8fc5a64` and `a998611f-bc18-414a-9a94-97c962b343b0`, both
`claude/6b80a87e-54dd-4f7b-ab9f-e2fb0ebc380d`). Root cause not yet isolated — see the bead for the
discriminating experiment needed. Blocks case 5 entirely. Full evidence and reproduction in the
bead description.

  permissions, and loaded Chat close_view calls Attention session_disposed.

- Live Claude command: `acp-proxy -- node /home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp/dist/index.js`.
- Live Grok command: `acp-proxy -- grok agent --always-approve stdio`.
- Watchdog interval is 300000 ms. Hold permission for 10 minutes 15 seconds:
  this exceeds the old two-window renewal path without changing production timing.
- Test files contain only harmless marker text under
  `/tmp/louiselm-live-acceptance.DowG3j/`, outside the project workspace.
- This round's coordinating Session is in Neovim PID 3145175. The maintainer
  opened the OpenCode test in another Neovim: PID 3155407, RPC socket
  `/run/user/1000/nvim.3155407.0`. Query the test's socket, not the coordinating

  and pins ACP evidence to each test's exact Session ID. No broad raw-log export.

Automated revision validation, ordinary silence timeout, malformed AIR metadata,
and asynchronous cleanup unit cases are already covered by the recorded fixes.
This round tests real peer behavior and the installed UI instead of repeating them.

## Case 1 — permission survives the watchdog

Exercises commit `08825f8`, session/lifecycle.lua pending-permission suspension.

1. Run `:LouiselmSessionNew` and select `opencode`.
2. Send exactly:

   > Use your read tool to read /tmp/louiselm-live-acceptance.DowG3j/watchdog.txt and reply with its single line. Do not use shell or search tools, and do not change any files.

3. Leave the permission picker unanswered. Tell the assistant "picker open".
   The assistant obtains the Session ID and request timestamp through live state/logs.
4. Wait until the assistant has verified 10 minutes 15 seconds from the request.
5. Choose allow once. The turn must finish with the marker line, with the Session usable.

Expect: picker remains available, no timeout or transport-closed error, then
normal completion after permission is granted.

Failure signature: picker vanishes without an answer; Session fails, exits, or
reports a watchdog/transport error; granting permission fails to resume the turn.

Evidence: the pinned ACP log has an unanswered session/request_permission for
at least 615 seconds, followed by the answer and successful prompt result;
live state remains waiting_permission before the answer and ready afterward.
Use `:LouiselmSessionId` if the assistant cannot identify the test view.

Observed apparatus: opencode/ses_f8afddf40ffe0R236fD2tGkzpe, local session-1,
Neovim PID 3155407. Prompt id 4 at 04:38:24.520Z; permission request id 0 at
04:38:30.136Z; both match the exact watchdog.txt fixture. At 04:39Z the live
Session was waiting_permission, permission_active=true, with the picker open.
Attention generation 356 contains permission_required for this Session,
source_operation_id 51467877-678e-48bb-a780-c57542cb7239.
Pinned log: `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ses_f8afddf40ffe0R236fD2tGkzpe/log.jsonl`.

Hold result: monitor polled the exact test socket every 30 seconds through
04:48:53Z (reported age 623 seconds). Every poll showed waiting_permission,
active request 0, and picker_open=true. Monitor exited successfully after the
required hold. At 04:48:54Z the pinned ACP log still ended at the original
permission request: zero permission answers and zero prompt results. This
proves survival through Agent silence, not merely continued background progress.
Final acceptance: permission id 0 answered with selected/once at
04:49:03.639Z, after 633.503 seconds. Prompt id 4 returned stopReason=end_turn
at 04:49:08.140Z. Its two assistant text chunks join exactly to
"watchdog permission acceptance reached". RPC then showed ready, no active
permission, and no picker. Attention generation 357 has no item for this
Session. Maintainer confirmed normal completion in the coordinating Session.
Issue closed with its typed live verdict; evidence/lesson recorded in comments
962, 963, and the final acceptance comment.

Evidence-check lesson: join streamed assistant chunks before comparing output;
searching for the whole marker inside each individual chunk falsely reported
absence. This was corrected internally before interpreting the test result.

If no picker appears, report that immediately: the permission path was not reached.
Do not revoke broad remembered permissions or alter global OpenCode policy.

## Case 3 — Claude retry warning

## Case 4 — offline Android pending count

title: QA: isolated installed recovery reset
description:
# Prepared QA — isolated recovery reset

## Final result — scoped reset PASS, 2026-09-22

Human reported: "Trust reset. Run recovery setup to enroll everything anew,
then re-admit supply." Independent public postcheck: QA domain/snapshot/keys are
null; paper/passkey unenrolled; recovery_ready=false; next_action=recovery_setup.
Original store retains exact e4df45cb snapshot, both role4 fingerprints and
recovery_ready=true. No re-enrollment performed. No product findings.

Human warning readability was requested but not separately confirmed; do not
claim that subjective check passed. Actual destructive reset of this isolated
enrolled store is proven. Retired Primary/Admission, nonempty approval-history
reset and post-reset re-enrollment are NOT established by this round.

VM stopped after postchecks; no USB was attached. The QA store's enrollment is
removed and is not to be restored by copying old authority. Separate QA paper
and passkey no longer authorize this store. Physical signing credentials, original
store, installed release and retained artifacts remain untouched. Password-manager
entries/papers were not deleted; cleanup would require a separately scoped request.

Lessons: exact target/snapshot preflight and original-store comparison distinguish
a scoped reset from collateral authority loss. Status proves reset postconditions,
not warning readability or recovery-route acceptance. Routed to d6fv.11.5 and
this round. Sections below preserve the executed recipe, not queued actions.

Scope: one remaining boundary of louiselm-d6fv.11.5. Maintainer explicitly
authorized the exact isolated reset and asked to start. VM started WITHOUT USB,
invocation5261cf52743f4e80b2ea77590dd5f885. No reset executed by Agent.

## Current human step

Fresh public checks match both recorded snapshots and verified installed cf5c3344.
All checked target ancestors/provenance/trust paths are root-owned, non-writable
by others and not symlinks; QA/original directories and roles files have distinct
device/inode identities. QA ready, original ready.

In a private host terminal:

```sh
cd /home/lotso/code/louiselm
./scripts/launcher-vm terminal
```

In that guest terminal ONLY:

```sh
sudo /usr/local/lib/louiselm/current/bin/louiselm-skills recovery reset \
  --store /var/lib/louiselm/a6xc-20260922-01a0c512
```

Read warning: domain must be louiselm/a6xc-qa and snapshot exactly
sha256:322fa747cd9657a40c4999a60c709b9e0190e1aea79c1f2aaf452cbda8f37efc.
If matched, type reset then Enter (input hidden). Otherwise Ctrl-C and report.
Report final message and whether the warning clearly identified what was removed.
Do not follow the generic setup-again suggestion; stop for independent postchecks.

## Proposed target and exclusions

Only `/var/lib/louiselm/a6xc-20260922-01a0c512`, domain `louiselm/a6xc-qa`.
It is the separate QA store created today, not the older recovery fixture.
Last verified snapshot:
`sha256:322fa747cd9657a40c4999a60c709b9e0190e1aea79c1f2aaf452cbda8f37efc`.
Fresh public preflight is required; recorded state is not current live evidence.

Never target `/var/lib/louiselm/skills`. Its last verified snapshot is
`sha256:e4df45cb907559f12a3777032803950308439b1b56f7b7dc7a87eb5171cb4c48`.
Never reset the physical token or delete hardware credentials, passkeys or papers.
No new key generation. Retired-Primary/Admission/witness tests are OUT OF SCOPE.
This proposed isolated-store scope replaces, only after explicit approval, the
older deferred original-VM-copy/reset recipe; that old approval is not reused.

## Build

Installed release cf5c33446e41e1c7aa2a278adacbb5eb41b3aed04613b75c0aba50f12926cceb,
source c2d6024. Read-only identity/status must confirm it before acceptance.
Reset path: skills-core/src/cli/recovery/setup.rs and trust/onboarding.rs.

## Status

| Case | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh protected QA/original-store baselines | Passed: exact recorded snapshots and verified installed identity; distinct protected paths |
| Explicit QA-only reset and public postcondition | Passed: human reset success and independent unenrolled public status |
| Original recovery store unchanged | Passed: exact e4df45cb snapshot, original keys and readiness preserved |

## Intended manual case (not a queued command)

1. After approval, start retained VM without USB; reset needs no hardware signing.
2. Agent reads installed identity and both public recovery statuses; stop on a
   changed target, unrecognized domain or unexpected baseline. Confirm distinct
   protected paths and no symlink alias before human execution.
3. Human uses private unrecorded VM terminal. Run installed recovery reset with
   ONLY the exact QA path above. Agent supplies command after fresh checks.
4. Read the displayed domain/snapshot. Confirm only if louiselm/a6xc-qa and the
   freshly verified target match. Human types reset; do not expose private data.
5. Agent checks QA status has no enrolled keys/methods, recovery_ready=false,
   next_action=recovery_setup; original store snapshot/roles/readiness unchanged.
6. Stop VM. No repeat enrollment or further ceremony is queued.

Failure signature: reset reports success but QA authority remains enrolled,
unexpected original-store changes, or domain/snapshot mismatch at confirmation.
On failure inspect public status before any retry; no automatic repair/reset.

Evidence: human warning/confirmation observation plus exact before/after public
status and installed identity. Successful reset is destructive to QA authorization
and must not be described as undoable by copying old trust back. It does not
delete the physical signing credentials or password-manager entry. Keep artifacts
until a separately authorized cleanup; QA paper/passkey cease authorizing this store.

## Acceptance limits and remaining work

This tests an actual reset of an enrolled installed QA store, not reset with
nonempty approved history, retired-Primary refusal, or fresh post-reset enrollment.
Do not close the aggregate automatically. Prior September8 passes remain in
louiselm-bvdb; retired Primary/Admission work remains deferred under
louiselm-d6fv.11.5/louiselm-u5no. u5no's old two-token recipe is obsolete: follow
the current one-token recovery contract when separately planning that round.
dtwil remains open pending natural capacity failure/recovery.

## Cleanup and findings

No findings or changes during preparation. Keep this scratch while the approved
round is active; archive to a qa-round Bead and delete when it ends. No secrets
belong in the archive. Neither reset nor cleanup is authorized by preparation.

title: Usage telemetry is unreadable when flush against transcript content
description:
The chat transcript renders the `[usage] ...` line without a blank line above or below it, making usage telemetry hard to read when it is adjacent to prose or tool output. Add vertical spacing around the usage line, following the existing transcript block-spacing precedent used for tools and terminal completion.

## Observed

Seen in the maintainer screenshot on 2026-08-25 at 17:13 local time (Europe/Paris), Neovim chat buffer in `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`:

`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260825_1713_1920x1200_1787670818.png`

The visible transcript contains:

```text
Recorded all of this as a comment on **louiselm-exw0** and committed (`5dd00ba`). Ready to tackle the implementation when you are.
[usage] total_tokens=3468175 · input_tokens=...
> i just asked in codex for reason but it showed nothing ...
```

The usage row is directly adjacent to the preceding and following transcript content, with no empty line separating it.

## Symptoms

- Human-facing chat transcript usage telemetry is difficult to scan.
- Usage should be presented as its own block with one newline above and below.

## Root cause

Likely in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2250-2263`: the `turn_done` handler calls `insert_transcript(self, view, { line })` for the usage line, but does not surround it with empty lines. The neighboring terminal-completion path explicitly inserts blank lines, which suggests the usage path omitted equivalent block spacing. This mechanism is a hypothesis based on the current source and screenshot; verify with a focused UI regression test.

## Why it was not caught

Existing tests cover usage formatting and transcript ordering/data, but no headless UI assertion currently requires blank lines around the rendered usage line in the live chat transcript.

## Fix direction

At the transcript presentation boundary in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`, insert one empty line before and after the usage line while preserving existing behavior for turns without usage and avoiding duplicate blank lines where the preceding/following block already supplies spacing. Add a behavioral headless regression test for the rendered transcript.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.
- In the chat buffer, `[usage] ...` has exactly one blank line above and below it, including when adjacent to prose or tool output.
- Usage formatting and persistence remain unchanged.

## Not covered

The screenshot does not establish whether every usage-producing agent or replay path has the same spacing issue. Verify live and replay rendering when implementing the fix.
close_reason: Fixed in the current working tree. Root cause was usage presentation inserting only the usage line, unlike neighboring transcript blocks with explicit separators. Added neighbor-aware spacing for live and replay usage. Tests: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 117/117; full MiniTest suite 517/517. Gates: stylua --check passed; lua-language-server reported no problems. Acceptance met: usage is separated from surrounding transcript content.

Implemented neighbor-aware insert_usage() at lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1904, used by both restore_turn_usage() and turn_done. Focused chat_spec: 117/117 passed; full suite: 517/517 passed; lua-language-server: no problems; stylua --check: passed.

title: Show whose turn it is in LouieLM chat
description:
## Problem

During a LouieLM chat session, the top red header shows the session option, but it does not indicate whether the model is currently sending text or whether it is the user's turn to respond.

## Desired behavior

Add a visible status indicator in the chat header that distinguishes at least:

- Model is responding/sending text
- Your turn / waiting for user input

The indicator should update as the conversation state changes and remain consistent with the actual session state. Preserve the existing red session-option header.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A LouieLM chat session visibly shows whether the model is currently responding or it is the user's turn.
2. The status changes promptly when model output starts, finishes, or the session becomes ready for user input.
3. The indicator is understandable without relying on color alone (for example, include text or an icon with accessible labeling).
4. Existing session-option header behavior remains intact.
close_reason: Already implemented by commit 106aa9c: the window-local winbar persists Your turn and Model responding while scrolling, updates on lifecycle changes, and restores the previous winbar. Current chat coverage also exercises Waiting for permission, Starting, Stopping, Error, and Unavailable labels; the latest full MiniTest run passed 185/185.

title: Correlate issues to commits through bvr history with confidence intact
description:
## Goal

From an issue, see every commit that implemented it, with bvr's correlation
method and confidence carried through rather than flattened into a claim.

## Scope

- In scope: the bvr half of `provenance/sources.lua`; issue -> commit edges in
  `correlate`; `louiselm://provenance/issue/<id>`.
- Out of scope: Session edges from actor fields, and time travel.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `louiselm://provenance/issue/<id>` lists correlated commits with their
   created and closed milestones.
2. Correlation method (`explicit_id`, `co_committed`) and confidence reach the
   surface. An inferred edge is never presented as a recorded fact.
3. The default git range is set explicitly. A bare `bvr --robot-history` reports
   zero correlations on this repository because it only scans the last N
   commits, which reads as "unimplemented" and is a trap worth encoding once.
4. An issue with no correlated commits renders as such, not as an error.

## Testing

- `correlate` against captured real `bvr --robot-history` output, cited per
  AGENTS.md section 5.
- A regression proving the history window is passed explicitly, since the
  default silently returns nothing.
- Fixtures encode observed event order as well as field shape.

## Notes

Prior art proving this works: `bvr --robot-history --bead-history louiselm-w726
--history-since 2026-08-10 --history-limit 500` returns real SHAs, authors and
milestones for that issue.
close_reason: Implemented bvr-backed issue Provenance with explicit history range, issue-to-commit correlation edges, method/confidence display, milestones, empty-history handling, and issue lookup from the existing Provenance command. Tests and quality gates pass.

comments.text: Implemented the bvr-backed issue Provenance slice. Evidence: focused provenance tests and full MiniTest suite pass (671 cases); stylua, lua-language-server, API appendix check, and git diff --check pass; live bvr_history lookup returned louiselm-kwp6 with one commit. The already-closed louiselm-06yh design decision was sufficient; no new design question was needed. The view preserves bvr's explicit_id/co_committed method, confidence, and created/closed milestones without adding a graph store.

title: Gemini setup recommends retired consumer Google login
description:
The new Gemini recipe directs consumer users to a retired Google-account authentication path, so following the documented setup cannot produce a working Gemini Session.

## Observed
User in codex/01a0a866-b00d-7cb2-9567-39ceb3bc56cd reports: "Failed to sign in. Message: This client is no longer supported for Gemini Code Assist for individuals. To continue using Gemini, please migrate to the Antigravity suite of products: https://antigravity.google".
Installed CLI is now 0.60.0; local settings select oauth-personal.
https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/code-assist-individuals confirms consumer Gemini CLI access stopped June 18, 2026. Standard/Enterprise is unaffected. https://developers.googleblog.com/an-important-update-transitioning-gemini-cli-to-antigravity-cli/ confirms paid API-key access remains.

## Root cause
docs/onboarding.md:154, examples/quickstart.lua:37 and the dotfiles louiselm.lua Gemini comment recommend unqualified Google login. README.md advertises that recipe. The implementation used https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/, which still recommends personal Google accounts despite the specific deprecation announcement.

## Why it was not caught
Local tests validate configuration and protocol behavior. A real Session reached ready before a prompt failed with 401; this was prematurely attributed to missing credentials without checking service eligibility.

## Fix direction
Correct the public recipe to supported API-key authentication with separate billing clearly stated; qualify Google login as Standard/Enterprise only. Correct the dotfiles comment without silently changing the user's selected service or installing a different adapter. Record consumer login as the current blocker in louiselm-ce6.36. Antigravity ACP is separate scope; upstream request https://github.com/google-antigravity/antigravity-cli/issues/31 is open.

## Acceptance
No unconditional consumer Google-login recommendation remains in the new Gemini docs/config comments; deprecation and supported routes are cited. Run affected documentation/config checks; no artificial red test for prose corrections. Main Gemini task remains open until user chooses a supported route and live acceptance passes.

## Not covered
No credentials or billing setup, Antigravity install, service restriction workaround, or claim of authenticated live success.

Lesson routed to this issue and cited onboarding notice: consult service deprecations when general authentication docs conflict; handshake success does not prove eligibility. Prose/config-comment correction needs no artificial red test. site:test, StyLua, luac parsing, diff checks pass.
