title: Grill-me needed: what does a pre-cutover launch record when conformance evidence is absent
description:
Do not resolve this in passing: the answer decides whether louiselm-d6fv.12.3
delivers the Verified cutover it was explicitly told not to deliver.

## Question

Before the louiselm-d6fv.9 cutover, what does a launch on a host with no
current conformance evidence record in its receipt?

## Evidence

- louiselm-d6fv.12.3 slice 3 makes `LaunchEvidence.conformance` a required
  nested field (`ConformanceEvidence::Certified | Waived`). Every construction
  site compiles except the production path,
  `skills-core/src/launch_supervisor.rs:1163`, which has no honest value.
- Populating it means running the admission gate. The gate needs attendance
  (interactive vs unattended) and a Session-scoped waiver, and `LaunchRequest`
  (`skills-core/src/launch.rs:55`) carries neither. Both would be additions to
  a closed `deny_unknown_fields` wire type.
- Parent AC4 gates "Verified execution"; AC13 assigns the user-visible cutover
  to louiselm-d6fv.9 and forbids claiming it here.

## Rejected in passing

- Fabricating `Certified` at the call site: louiselm-d6fv.6.10 AC2 bans a
  caller-supplied conformance verdict, and louiselm-rn38 decided posture is
  derived from retained facts, never manufactured.
- Treating every launch as unattended and requiring current evidence: safe and
  fail-closed, but no launch proceeds without certification, which is the
  cutover AC13 puts out of scope.
- Making the field optional with a serde default: a receipt with no conformance
  evidence would validate, the fail-open shape AC11 exists to prevent.

## Threads worth pulling

- Is there a third `ConformanceEvidence` variant for "no evidence, not claimed",
  making the receipt truthful without gating anything? If so, what stops it
  becoming a permanent excuse rather than a pre-cutover state?
- If the gate is advisory before cutover, what consumes the recorded status,
  and does an uncertified Session differ observably from a certified one?
- Where do attendance and waiver enter: `LaunchRequest`, the broker
  authorization, or supervisor construction? Each puts the operator decision in
  a different trust boundary.
- Does louiselm-d6fv.12.4 (suspend/recover on invalid evidence) presuppose an
  answer here?
design:
Maintainer-confirmed oi5an design, 2026-09-14.
Source Session: claude/25d50255-06ea-4824-a0a2-b431a08aa093. The maintainer
chose the truthful-receipt option and delegated the forcing function.

1. Pre-cutover state: a launch that consulted no host conformance evidence
   records `ConformanceEvidence::Unevaluated`. It asserts nothing. Any other
   value would claim a property nothing checked.
2. The admission gate is NOT put in force here. louiselm-d6fv.9 retains the
   user-visible Verified cutover, as parent AC13 requires.
3. Attendance and Session-scoped waiver do not enter `LaunchRequest` now. The
   question of which trust boundary carries them reopens when the gate is
   actually wired; the decision vocabulary already exists unused and typed.
4. Forcing function, delegated to and chosen by this Session: visibility in
   canonical status, not a timer or a lint. A Session recording `Unevaluated`
   reports its conformance dimension unverified with a typed reason and a safe
   next action in every default status response. Filed louiselm-d6fv.12.6;
   louiselm-d6fv.9 now depends on it, so its cutover acceptance becomes the
   observable condition "no Session on the maintainer's host reports
   conformance unverified".
5. Wire format: the launch payload shape changed, so RECEIPT_SCHEMA and
   SIGNED_RECEIPT_SCHEMA move to /5. No compatibility shim; existing receipts
   from the /4 era do not parse, which the project scope accepts.
6. Nesting: `conformance` is a named field on `LaunchEvidence`, never
   `serde(flatten)`. `deny_unknown_fields` and `flatten` cannot be combined, a
   round trip that breaks only at runtime (broker audit entries, 2026-09-10).

Vocabulary delta: No change.
close_reason: consumer:louiselm-d6fv.12.3 implements this decision in slice 3; forcing function consumer:louiselm-d6fv.12.6 with d6fv.9 depending on it

comments.author: claude/25d50255-06ea-4824-a0a2-b431a08aa093
comments.text: Maintainer confirmed door A in this Session and delegated the forcing function choice. Canonical decision and provenance stored in this issue design. Implementation landed in louiselm-d6fv.12.3 slice 3: ConformanceEvidence{Certified|Waived|Unevaluated} as a required nested field on LaunchEvidence, digest validation on both digest-bearing variants, receipt schema bumped to /5, production launch path records Unevaluated with a test asserting that default so it cannot be silently upgraded. Forcing function filed as louiselm-d6fv.12.6 with d6fv.9 depending on it; zero active dependency cycles. Gates: cargo test full suite green, clippy -D warnings exit 0, rustdoc -D warnings exit 0, fmt clean. Lesson retained here: an inert honest state needs a consumer that makes it visible, or it becomes the permanent normal - d6fv.6.2 and louiselm-5tuq are the precedents. Existing standing rules suffice. This resolves design only; the gate and the cutover remain open in their own work items.

title: Split skills CI can bypass its branch-required status
description:
The proposed CI split can leave the branch-required skills status successful
when its new lifecycle sibling fails. This is a regression in candidate
5fb6f6f, not a demonstrated failure on main; no failing code was merged.

## Observed

2026-09-18, current session codex/01a0b350-de3e-7020-9ac9-615b56e88bb6.
`gh api repos/euri10/louiselm/branches/main` reports `protected:true` and
`protection.required_status_checks.checks` contains
`{"app_id":15368,"context":"cargo (skills-core)"}` but no
`cargo (skills-core lifecycle)`. Effective rules API returns `[]`.
Candidate `.github/workflows/ci.yml:378` assigns the required name only to
matrix group core; lifecycle is independent with `fail-fast:false`.

## Symptoms and root cause

A lifecycle failure makes overall CI fail, and the existing release guard
correctly refuses that run, but does not fail the required core context.
The dispatcher tests cover invocation/failure preservation, not the actual
branch-required status topology. A green sample cannot prove this refusal.

## Fix direction

Keep parallel matrix execution, give its core group a distinct check name,
and retain `cargo (skills-core)` as an always-run aggregate requiring matrix
success. Do not mutate branch protection or broaden token permissions.

## Acceptance

- Regression fails against the candidate and passes after repair.
- Aggregate covers both groups and rejects failure, cancellation and skip.
- Every original gate remains; full hosted CI passes on the repaired revision.
- Release guard still refuses any failed overall CI run.

## Not covered

No intentionally failing PR or merge is created. Repository settings stay
unchanged. Performance acceptance restarts on the repaired candidate.

title: Collapse tool-call blocks in LouiselmToMarkdown transcript rendering
description:
## Goal
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` / `Chat:to_markdown` tool-call blocks take up huge vertical space (full `vim.inspect` dump always expanded) and visually compete with `## User`/`## Assistant` at the same heading weight. Make tool-call blocks compact and collapsed by default, without dropping any information.

## Scope
- In scope: `lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua` — `render_entry()` and its module doc comment (the "M.render turns a snapshot..." section describing tool block format).
- In scope: `tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` — update the four assertions that do `markdown:find("## Tool: ...", 1, true)` to match the new multi-line shape.
- Out of scope: `Chat:to_markdown` (init.lua:1549) and `transcript_export.lua` — both just call `Transcript.render`, no changes needed, no API change.
- Out of scope: fixing any blog-pipeline (`blog/scripts/render-post.sh`, MyST `:lines:` literalinclude ranges) friction this causes — explicitly deferred, see Notes.

## Agreed format (discussed with user)
Replace the current single line:
```
## Tool: <title> (<status>)

```
<vim.inspect dump>
```
```
with:
```
## Tool

<sub>**<title>** — <status></sub>

<details>
<summary>payload</summary>

```
<vim.inspect dump, unchanged>
```

</details>
```
- `## Tool` stays its own heading, same weight as `## User`/`## Assistant`.
- Title/status move to a `<sub>` line — smaller, one line, no expansion needed to see what ran.
- The full raw payload dump is unchanged in content, just wrapped in `<details><summary>payload</summary>...</details>` so it renders collapsed by default in GitHub/VS Code/Obsidian (falls back to expanded, not lost, in renderers without HTML passthrough).
- Fallback cases (`raw.title` absent → id, `raw.status` absent → "unknown") keep working the same way, just placed in the `<sub>` line instead of the heading.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `render_entry()` for a `tool_call` entry produces the new `## Tool` / `<sub>` / `<details>` shape described above, with the full `vim.inspect(raw)` dump byte-for-byte unchanged inside the `<details>` block.
2. `## User` and `## Assistant` blocks are unchanged.
3. `tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` assertions updated to match (still checking title/status and full raw dump presence, just via the new shape — e.g. assert the `<sub>` line and `<details>`/`<summary>` markers appear, and the dump content is still present).
4. `busted`/test suite passes (`make test` or repo's standard Lua test runner).
5. Module doc comment in `transcript.lua` (lines ~19-24) updated to describe the new tool-block format instead of the old one-line heading.

## Testing
- Run existing Lua test suite for `tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` (and `tests/session/transcript_export_spec.lua`, `tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` as regression checks — they should not need format-specific changes since they likely just check the file was written, but verify).

## Notes
- Risk, explicitly accepted by user: `transcript.lua's doc comment says this markdown format is a dependency of the blog-publishing pipeline (`blog/scripts/render-post.sh`, feature `louiselm-mia`), which uses MyST `{literalinclude}` with `:lines: N-M` ranges against these exported files. Adding multi-line `<sub>`/`<details>` markup shifts line numbers for any existing blog post literalinclude ranges pointed at old-format transcripts. User: "happy with both, it's alpha software so I'll fix it after if that creates friction with louiselm-mia." Do not attempt to fix the blog pipeline as part of this task — file a separate bug if/when it actually breaks something.
close_reason: Implemented: render_entry() in lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua now emits ## Tool heading + <sub> title/status line + collapsed <details><summary>payload</summary> block, exactly per the agreed spec. Updated tests/session/transcript_spec.lua and tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua assertions. All 3 quality gates pass: stylua --check clean, lua-language-server --check clean, full mini.test suite 235/235 (0 fails). Blog-pipeline (louiselm-mia) line-number friction risk left as accepted/deferred per prior discussion.

title: Add tweet-fetch agent skill (twitterapi.io ingestion into tweets.jsonl)
description:
## Summary

Added the `tweet-fetch` skill in the owned skill catalog
(`~/.config/agentskills/tweet-fetch/`), the fetch-side companion to
tweet-corpus (louiselm-vg72).

## What it does

Wraps two verified twitterapi.io REST endpoints directly (no dependency on
the unverified third-party `kaitoInfra/twitterapi-io` package the original
opencode session had floated):

- `GET /twitter/user/last_tweets` (timeline, ~3200-tweet cap, X's own limit)
- `GET /twitter/tweet/advanced_search` (date-windowed `from:user
  since_time:/until_time:` search, for going further back)

`scripts/fetch_tweets.py` normalizes results into the exact schema
tweet-corpus/scripts/build_corpus.py ingests and appends to a shared
`tweets.jsonl`. Duplicate lines across overlapping fetch windows are
harmless — corpus build upserts by tweet id.

Cost guard: defaults `--max-tweets` to 200 since twitterapi.io bills per
tweet returned; SKILL.md instructs the agent to quote an estimate and get
explicit confirmation before a larger pull.

## Verification

- Offline smoke test of `normalize()` (Twitter date format -> ISO,
  entities.urls -> links list, retweet/reply detection), `build_search_query()`
  (since/until -> since_time:/until_time: unix timestamps), and CLI arg
  validation (missing env var, missing user, mutually exclusive
  --timeline/--search) — all correct. No live API call made (no
  TWITTERAPI_IO_KEY available in this environment; the endpoint shapes were
  confirmed against docs.twitterapi.io, not guessed).
- Catalog entry seeded (with a golden task: confirm-before-large-fetch),
  `inventory_skills.py`, `manage_lifecycle.py check`, `build_installation.py`,
  `generate_openai_metadata.py --check`, the unittest suite, and
  `run_golden_tasks.py` all pass. `generated/tweet-fetch` present.

## Related

louiselm-vg72 (tweet-corpus, the storage/query side this feeds).

title: Exploit usage facts through shared queries and Neovim views
description:
## Problem Statement

The operator needs factual comparisons over complete usage history rather than the existing independent-option buckets.

## Solution

After collection is complete, expose shared SQL queries through the corrected picker and a Neovim :LouiselmUsage explorer, then measure the complete query path.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want picker samples matching the configuration I am comparing.
2. As an operator, I want time ranges, hourly/daily buckets, dimension filters/grouping, and turn/change details.
3. As an Agent, I want structured results with the same factual semantics as the human UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The picker matches Agent, all other active options, and the candidate's resolved Provider. Empty cohorts say No matching history; no marginal or legacy fallback.
2. Explorer filters/grouping support Agent, Provider, advertised Model, and active option dimensions, with drill-down to the underlying recorded turns and changes.
3. Total turns, outcomes, and per-metric sample coverage remain distinct. Preserve absent measurements; separate currencies; no estimated prices or usage splits.
4. Changed-during-turn records remain inspectable and in appropriate totals but are excluded from fixed-combination comparisons. A filter/group must not invent attribution for dimensions that changed during a turn.
5. SQL performs aggregation; Lua handles query orchestration and presentation. Public query errors and result types are documented.
6. Reproducible measurements separate SQL execution, CLI/process overhead, and rendering before recommending an owned Rust query host.
7. Maintainer confirms the existing Astra picker reproduction after a behavior-changing build.

## Implementation Notes

Reuse louiselm-rvu8 for the first query consumer and picker repair. Extend the same query boundary for the explorer; do not duplicate calculations in UI code. Preserve source timestamps; make displayed timezone/bucket boundaries explicit. Raw ACP logs are never the interactive query path.

## Testing Notes

Use deterministic datasets spanning Agents, Providers, Models, typed option values, partial telemetry, outcomes, currencies, and mid-turn changes. Cover async rendering/disposal, pagination, empty results, and query errors. Run full Lua gates, public-doc generation checks, and live picker acceptance.

## Out of Scope

Reflection, automatic Model selection, speculative Rust implementation, or historical import. Source: confirmed louiselm-3x9p summary.

title: Expose normalized account limits for OpenCode
description:
## Goal

A live OpenCode connection exposes normalized account-limit snapshots through
the existing provider-neutral ACP account-limits extension, so the winbar and
`:LouiselmLimits opencode` show real OpenCode capacity instead of
`unsupported`.

## Why now

OpenCode is the one configured Agent whose quota is invisible from inside
LouiseLM, and that invisibility costs real diagnosis time. louiselm-5zhl made
"OpenCode reached its 5-hour limit" the standing hypothesis for a stalled
OpenCode Session. When louiselm-watchdog-kills-pending-permission-lg95 was
diagnosed on 2026-09-03 the maintainer had to leave the editor and check
OpenCode usage out-of-band just to rule quota out. Codex, Claude and Copilot
all answer that question in the winbar; OpenCode does not.

## Evidence

- The LouiseLM consumer side is done and provider-neutral:
  `lua/louiselm/session/limits.lua` normalizes any Agent advertising
  `_meta["io.github.euri10.louiselm"].accountLimits` (v1: `read_method` +
  `updated_method`, exact-window snapshots). No LouiseLM UI work is implied.
- The Agent is configured as stock `acp-proxy -- opencode acp` with no local
  adapter, exactly as Copilot was before louiselm-ce6.27. Grepping the full
  session log
  `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ses_f9a93a9f9ffeXz1SXPE1DLPAg3/log.jsonl`
  (3380 frames) returns zero `accountLimits` occurrences, so the capability is
  never advertised and limits resolve to `unsupported`.
- OpenCode CLI 1.18.25 ships `opencode stats`, which reports *local* token and
  cost history from the session database. That is spend, not account quota,
  and is not the source.
- The account in use is an `opencode-go/*` plan (models `glm-5.3`,
  `gpt-5.6-luna` observed), so the authoritative quota is account-side. The
  exact surface — server route, SDK method, or plugin hook — is not yet
  identified and finding it is part of this task.

## Scope

- In scope: identify the authoritative OpenCode quota surface; normalize it to
  the v1 extension; advertise the capability; serve read and, if OpenCode
  emits them, structured updates; deterministic adapter tests; docs; live
  LouiseLM acceptance.
- Out of scope: parsing rendered `/usage` or TUI output, scraping a billing
  page, LouiseLM UX changes, AX, automatic Agent switching, account mutations,
  and starting an Agent solely to fetch limits.

## Runtime ownership

The accepted pure-ACP boundary from louiselm-iexg still binds: LouiseLM must
not learn OpenCode internals. Pick one and state why — upstream capability in
`opencode acp`, an independent wrapper as louiselm-ce6.27 chose for Copilot,
or an `opencode` plugin — and prefer whichever reuses the already-authenticated
runtime instead of spawning a second process.

## Acceptance

1. The adapter advertises version 1 of `io.github.euri10.louiselm.accountLimits`
   with the same read and update method names and complete snapshot shape as
   codex-acp.
2. Read reuses an existing live connection and never creates a Session or
   provider process solely for account limits.
3. Real OpenCode quota data normalizes without invented values; unsupported
   plans, empty data, malformed data, and provider failures stay distinct
   states.
4. Standard ACP clients that ignore the extension see no behavior change.
5. A live LouiseLM run shows fresh OpenCode limits in the winbar and
   `:LouiselmLimits opencode`, without printing or persisting credentials.

## Stop condition

If the discovered OpenCode quota shape cannot be expressed truthfully in v1 —
the Copilot failure mode in louiselm-ce6.27, where a reset-only quota had no
exact `windowDurationMins` — stop, file a `needs-design` question, and do not
invent a duration to make it fit.
close_reason: Won't-do: OpenCode exposes no containment-preserving path to Account limits, and reading a Provider credential is now forbidden (louiselm-opencode-quota-runtime-ownership-blz13, louiselm-account-limits-9n9st). consumer:lua/louiselm/session/limits.lua already normalizes the extension provider-neutrally, so limits appear with zero new code if opencode acp ever advertises it.

comments.author: claude/7c202de1-9087-4c68-9c4a-7577d53221bc
comments.text:
Probe 2026-09-16, opencode CLI 1.18.30 (issue cited 1.18.25). Rules out one of the three candidate surfaces.

'opencode serve' is a real structured surface the issue had not checked. Started it on 127.0.0.1:47823 and fetched its OpenAPI document from /doc (478968 bytes). Route groups: agent, api, auth, command, config, event, experimental, file, find, formatter, global, instance, log, lsp, mcp, path, permission, project, provider, pty, question, session, skill, sync, tui, vcs.

No route matches usage, quota, billing, limit, balance, credit, plan or subscription. The only account-adjacent routes are credential flows: /auth/{providerID}, /provider/auth, /provider/{providerID}/oauth/authorize, /provider/{providerID}/oauth/callback.

GET /config/providers confirms both plans are live and keyed the same way:
- opencode-go 'OpenCode Go', source=api, 27 models, env=[OPENCODE_API_KEY]
- opencode 'OpenCode Zen', source=custom, 7 models, env=[OPENCODE_API_KEY]
Neither payload carries a quota, limit or balance field; keys are env, id, key, models, name, options, source. No baseURL is set, so the gateway endpoint is a provider default rather than local configuration.

Conclusion: the local server does not hold account quota. It is gateway-side behind OPENCODE_API_KEY. The two candidate surfaces still open are (a) an account/quota endpoint on the OpenCode gateway for that key, and (b) rate-limit response headers observable by a wrapper or plugin, which is the louiselm-ce6.27 Copilot pattern. Probing (a) means an authenticated request to a third-party account API and was not attempted without the maintainer's go-ahead.

Separately: the maintainer already runs OpenCode daily (acp-proxy -- opencode acp, provider prefix map for opencode-go/ and opencode/), so acceptance 5's live run needs no new account access. What blocks this issue is the unidentified surface and the runtime-ownership choice, not credentials.

comments.text:
FOUND THE SURFACE. Undocumented but live: GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage with Authorization: Bearer <OPENCODE_API_KEY>. 200, 250 bytes. Not in https://opencode.ai/docs/zen, which documents only /responses, /messages, /chat/completions, /models.

Key is in ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json (opencode-go, owner-only); OPENCODE_API_KEY is not exported in the shell. /usage answered only on the go base; the Zen base was 404 with a Go key, which does not by itself prove Zen lacks the route.

Payload (2026-09-16T08:55Z):
{"usage":{"rolling":{"status":"ok","percent":0,"resetsAt":"2026-09-16T13:55:20.270Z"},"weekly":{"status":"ok","percent":0,"resetsAt":"2026-09-21T00:00:00.270Z"},"monthly":{"status":"rate-limited","percent":100,"resetsAt":"2026-09-30T08:49:16.270Z"}}}

Three buckets, each with status + percent + resetsAt. No window length is stated, so durations must be established by observation, not assumed.

Two samples 53s apart (08:55:20Z and 08:56:13Z) decide it:
- rolling resetsAt advanced 13:55:20.270 -> 13:56:14.426, tracking wall clock. PROVEN rolling 5h window. windowDurationMins = 300, exact.

LIVE OPERATIONAL FINDING, independent of this issue: the monthly bucket is at percent 100, status rate-limited, until 2026-09-30T08:49:16Z. The maintainer's OpenCode Go monthly quota is exhausted for the next two weeks. This is exactly the invisible-quota diagnosis cost louiselm-5zhl and louiselm-watchdog-kills-pending-permission-lg95 paid for out-of-band.

comments.text:
Closing won't-do per the louiselm-opencode-quota-runtime-ownership-blz13 grill, confirmed by the maintainer 2026-09-16.

The stop condition this issue wrote for itself was never reached, because the blocker turned out to be authority rather than shape. The quota exists and is expressible: GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage returns rolling/weekly/monthly with status, percent and resetsAt, and two samples 53s apart proved rolling = 300 min and weekly = 10080 min (calendar Monday 00:00 UTC). Only the monthly anchor stayed undetermined.

What stopped it: reaching that data requires reading OPENCODE_API_KEY out of ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json and calling the Provider gateway directly. OpenCode's plugin API exposes no hook for HTTP, provider requests, response headers, quota or auth, so there is no way to read it from inside the process that already holds the key. Upstreaming the extension was rejected as presumptuous and unbounded: it would oblige the same push for every ACP adapter ever configured.

The decision binds beyond OpenCode: neither LouiseLM nor an adapter its maintainer maintains reads a Provider credential store or calls a Provider API. unsupported is a correct terminal state. See vocabulary louiselm-account-limits-9n9st.

Nothing is lost if OpenCode changes its mind. lua/louiselm/session/limits.lua is provider-neutral and already normalizes the extension; if opencode acp ever advertises accountLimits, limits appear with zero new code in this repository.

Consistent with louiselm-5zhl, which already closed with 'upstream OpenCode ACP quota-error propagation remains outside LouiseLM'.

title: Measure the OpenCode monthly quota window across its 2026-09-30 reset
description:
## Goal

Establish the exact `windowDurationMins` for the OpenCode `monthly` quota
bucket by observation, so louiselm-opencode-account-limits-9350 can emit a
truthful v1 snapshot instead of a guessed month length.

## Why this blocks implementation

`GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage` returns three buckets but never
states a window length (evidence on louiselm-opencode-account-limits-9350,
2026-09-16). Two samples 53s apart already settled two of them:

- `rolling` resetsAt tracks wall clock -> rolling 5h, `windowDurationMins` 300.
- `weekly` resetsAt fixed at Monday 00:00 UTC -> calendar week, 10080.
- `monthly` resetsAt fixed at 2026-09-30T08:49:16Z -> anchored, duration
  undetermined. A 30-day window (43200) and a calendar month (40320-44640)
  both fit one observation.

louiselm-opencode-account-limits-9350's stop condition forbids inventing a
duration to make the shape fit v1. That is what killed the Copilot attempt in
louiselm-ce6.27. Measuring is the alternative to guessing.

## Method

Sample the endpoint shortly before and shortly after 2026-09-30T08:49:16Z and
record `monthly.resetsAt` both times. The new anchor decides it:

- next anchor 2026-10-30T08:49:16Z -> fixed 30-day window, 43200 exact.
- next anchor 2026-10-31T08:49:16Z (or another month-length offset) ->
  calendar month, not expressible as an exact `windowDurationMins` in v1.

Record both raw payloads on this issue. If the result is calendar-month, do
not force it: file the `needs-design` question the stop condition calls for.

## Cost of waiting

Zero today. The monthly bucket is already at percent 100 / `rate-limited`
until that same reset, so no quota display would be usable before it anyway.

## Out of scope

Implementing the adapter, choosing runtime ownership, or deciding whether the
adapter may read `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` rather than reuse the
authenticated runtime. Those stay on
louiselm-opencode-account-limits-9350.
close_reason: Moot: existed only to fill a v1 snapshot nobody will build, now that louiselm-opencode-account-limits-9350 closes won't-do. The two proven durations (rolling 300, weekly 10080) and the undetermined monthly anchor stay recorded on that issue as evidence. none:superseded-by-decision in louiselm-opencode-quota-runtime-ownership-blz13.

title: Grill-me needed: may LouiseLM hold a Provider credential to read quota off-protocol?
description:
Do not resolve this in passing. It is the standing rule for every Provider
whose quota lives outside ACP, not a detail of one adapter, and answering it
cheaply inside an implementation task is how it gets decided by accident.

## The question

When a Provider's account quota is not advertised over ACP, who is allowed to
go and get it, and with whose credential?

## What raised it

A probe on 2026-09-16 (evidence on louiselm-opencode-account-limits-9350)
found a live, undocumented account endpoint:
`GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage`, returning rolling, weekly and
monthly buckets. It is absent from https://opencode.ai/docs/zen, which
documents only `/responses`, `/messages`, `/chat/completions` and `/models`.

The way it was reached is the problem. The key was read from
`~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` — another tool's credential file — and the
request went straight to the Provider's gateway. That works today and is by far
the cheapest thing to build. It also means LouiseLM would hold a Provider
credential and talk to a service outside the ACP boundary.

Three constraints already in the record pull against each other here:

- louiselm-iexg drew a pure-ACP boundary: LouiseLM must not learn an Agent's
  internals.
- louiselm-ce6.27 answered the same problem for Copilot with an independent
  wrapper, not by reaching around the protocol.
- louiselm-opencode-account-limits-9350's own runtime-ownership note prefers
  reusing the already-authenticated runtime over spawning a second process.

None of them says whether reading another tool's credential file is permitted.

## Threads worth pulling

- Does "must not learn Agent internals" govern knowledge, credentials, or
  both? They come apart here: the endpoint is an internal, the key is a
  credential, and a design can take one without the other.
- An undocumented endpoint carries no compatibility promise. When it changes
  shape or disappears, what does the winbar show — `unsupported`, stale, or a
  confidently wrong number? Which of those is acceptable for a quota display
  whose whole purpose is diagnosis?
- Does the existing security policy already answer this, or is reading a
  sibling tool's credential file a class of action the policy has never had to
  rule on?
- Codex, Claude and Copilot all report quota today. Did each arrive by a
  bespoke path, or is there a pattern here that generalises? If they are all
  bespoke, that is itself the answer to whether a standing rule exists.
- Is this a LouiseLM concern at all? `acp-proxy` already sits in the path of
  every configured Agent and already holds the runtime.
- If a wrapper "reuses the authenticated runtime", what does reuse mean
  concretely: the same process, the same token in memory, or merely the same
  file on disk? The third is the credential-reading option wearing a hat.
- What happens for someone who is not the maintainer — a Zen plan rather than
  Go, a key supplied by environment rather than file, or no key at all?
- Does the answer bind only OpenCode, or every future Provider whose quota
  lives off-protocol? If the latter, it belongs in AGENTS.md or a required
  reference rather than in one issue.
close_reason: Decided: the pure-ACP boundary protects distribution AND blast radius separably; an external adapter satisfies the first and launders nothing of the second. Neither LouiseLM nor an adapter its maintainer maintains may read a Provider credential store or call a Provider API. Vocabulary promoted: louiselm-account-limits-9n9st. inert:rule not yet written to AGENTS.md — follow-up filed for the Security line and the public wire contract.

title: Make optional capabilities explicit and discoverable in checkhealth
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM should provide useful ACP chat after configuring one installed, authenticated Agent, without requiring the operator to adopt Attention, Beads, skill management, speech capture, or workflow automation. Today chat constructs a durable Attention controller unconditionally, health reports capture prerequisites even when capture was never requested, and the capture service combines Attention/Run sockets, a phone receiver, and credential-triggered transcription in one startup path. Installed tools, environment credentials, and workspace files must not silently activate these capabilities.

The maintainer requested explicit opt-ins with minimal configuration and installation guidance only, following the existing Agent executable/upgrade approach. The maintainer accepted the four implementation slices and specifically replaced the proposed feature screen with :checkhealth louiselm. There must be no separate :LouiselmFeatures command or preferences UI.

## Solution

Keep ordinary chat complete by default. Optional integrations start only after an explicit configuration choice. :checkhealth louiselm is the single discovery/readiness surface: it describes disabled capabilities, gives their opt-in settings and setup references, and checks prerequisites for enabled capabilities. LouiseLM never downloads, installs, upgrades, builds, provisions, pairs, enrolls, or initializes dependencies as a consequence of setup, checking health, or enabling a feature.

Normal prerequisite reuse is automatic after consent; consent itself is never inferred from availability. An enabled but unavailable optional feature is reported as blocked without making unrelated chat unusable.

## User Stories

1. As a new user, I configure one Agent and Provider and can chat without br, bvr, lyaml, a recorder, or louiselm-capture installed.
2. As an operator, I can discover optional capabilities and copy their exact configuration/settings from checkhealth without learning the repository's component layout.
3. As an operator, I can enable Attention without recording audio, exposing a phone receiver, starting transcription, or enabling push delivery.
4. As a Beads user, I can inspect an existing workspace without opting into Run automation; an absent workspace is never initialized for me.
5. As a skill user, I can invoke configured local skills independently of trusted skill packaging/Admission, and manage packages without automatically injecting or admitting them.
6. As an operator, I receive a bounded, actionable diagnosis of a missing prerequisite, perform installation myself, and rerun checkhealth to verify readiness.
7. As an operator with existing Sessions or Runs, changing configuration preserves records, claims, pending lifecycle obligations, and truthful security status.
8. As a headless consumer, I get the same effective policy and explicit errors as the UI at the relevant runtime boundaries.

## Implementation Decisions

### Core default

- Keep streaming chat, multiple Sessions, editor context, cancellation, existing permission handling and diff review, local Session status/account limits, ordinary ACP history/resume, Handoff, and explicit transcript export/Forensics commands available.
- Preserve operator-selected Agent YOLO/auto-approval. Optional-feature consent does not redefine ACP/tool permission policy.
- Preserve mandatory durable turn metadata and its sqlite3 >= 3.38 with JSON prerequisite; this epic does not introduce a recording opt-out or claim zero external dependencies.
- Core default mappings remain available and respect existing user mappings. Optional integrations add their mappings only when enabled; keymaps=false still suppresses plugin mappings.
- Configuring no Agent should continue to allow Tutor/health guidance; never install or select an Agent implicitly.

### Explicit configuration and scope

- Add disabled-by-default gates for attention.enabled, beads.enabled, capture.enabled, and workflows.enabled.
- Reuse skills.policy as the skill-invocation switch, changing its default from native to off. Keep native/inject as deliberate choices and retain explicit per-Agent overrides as scoped opt-ins; effective policy remains fixed when a Session is created. skills.paths stays empty by default.
- Keep trusted skill-management activation separate from invocation policy; the agreed proposed shape is skills.management.enabled=false. Enabling management exposes relevant installed-tool operations, not automatic packaging, trust enrollment, Skill Admission, witnessing, or verified launch. Integrate only operations that actually exist; missing integration must be diagnosed truthfully.
- Finding an executable, credential, .beads directory, skill root, or previous installation is not opt-in. Settings such as paths or recorder commands do not imply an enabled flag. An explicit per-Agent skill policy does convey its documented scoped choice.
- These gates govern LouiseLM integrations, not the ordinary Agent's independent skill discovery or shell access. Enforcing restrictions on Agent behavior belongs to the execution policy/containment work.
- Validate the untouched complete configuration against the closed schema, including disabled sections. Resolve effective settings once for their owners; never mutate the caller's table. No compatibility aliases, permissive merges, duplicate persistent preference store, or automatic rewriting of user Lua.
- Use a small fixed set of supported feature descriptions/checks and plain functions. Do not add a plugin framework or configurable dependency graph.

### checkhealth contract

- checkhealth is the only new discovery/readiness surface. Tutor links to it; disabled feature commands explain the required setting and point there. Invoking a disabled command never enables it.
- Disabled: informational purpose, opt-in setting, prerequisite description, and setup/help reference. No optional dependency probes, service connections, skill scans, or missing-dependency warnings.
- Enabled: perform relevant bounded, asynchronous/read-only checks and report ready, blocked, or degraded with the precise next action. Core failures are errors; optional failures are warnings scoped to the affected operation. Requested configuration and observed readiness remain distinct.
- Show installation/setup instructions or copyable commands; execute none. Re-running checkhealth after manual setup is the recheck mechanism. Reuse the existing Agent guidance convention.
- Keep runtime failure notifications deduplicated and actionable. Disabled features cause no recurring suggestions. Health describes data stored, relevant outbound services, and client/service ownership where those affect the user's decision.

### Independent service capabilities

- Keep the existing service binary, but separate startup choices for durable Attention, Run support, the phone receiver, and transcription. Disabled components must not construct stores/listeners/workers or consume credentials for their operation.
- Attention-only startup requires the local store and authenticated socket, not a recorder, TLS receiver, transcription credentials, or a paired phone. Local editor status remains core and does not require durable Attention.
- Desktop recording, phone connectivity/pairing, transcription, and future push delivery are distinct opt-ins. Credentials alone must not start a transcription worker or authorize external delivery.
- The service's configuration owns service behavior; Neovim configuration owns its client integrations. Health reports discrepancies and next steps without pretending a client flag can stop a daemon used by another editor. Supply explicit manual setup instructions; never restart or reconfigure the shared service from setup/health.
- Do not enable the service's Beads cleanup solely from ambient configuration while Run support is disabled. Retain cleanup obligations for already admitted work as described below.
- Existing operator-invoked installer tooling is not an automatic plugin action. This epic must make documented setup choices explicit; it must not invoke that tooling itself.

### Dependencies belong to operations

- Basic Beads issue inspection requires br and an existing workspace. Cross-workspace lookup remains explicitly scoped by sibling_roots. bvr is required only for operations that actually use its correlations; Git-only Provenance remains usable where sufficient.
- Current cold Park queries Beads claims and uses the durable service and Agent session/load capability. Report those prerequisites before admission/effects. Never silently turn on Beads or Attention to satisfy a composite operation.
- Distinguish internal parsing/storage dependencies from user-facing features. Workflow-definition discovery may reuse skill parsing without implicitly enabling chat skill injection; do not create false dependencies from module names or code reuse. Core Handoff/routing must remain usable when optional workflow Runs are off.
- Preserve Run budgets, capability checks, expiry, and durable-record requirements. User-requested verified execution must never fall back silently to ordinary execution. Installing or enabling the skills tool never establishes Verified posture.

### Lifecycle

- Disabled integrations are inert on a fresh lifecycle: no optional observers, timers, connections, child processes, scans, or writes.
- Disabling prevents new use and disposes owned resources safely. Retain durable data; never delete captures, Attention state, skill stores, or Beads state as a toggle side effect.
- Already admitted Runs retain required cleanup/expiry/claim obligations until settled. Refuse a transition that cannot safely preserve them and report the necessary next action. Do not claim that disconnecting resolves an Attention condition.
- Preserve pending writes, scheduling boundaries, cancellation, and late-callback disposal. Never retrofit an existing Session into a new skill policy or verified posture.

### Four agreed implementation slices

1. Make the default chat path independent of durable Attention and capture prerequisites, gating their construction, health checks, and mappings. Establish shared effective settings through a complete end-to-end default/opt-in slice.
2. Consolidate feature discovery/readiness in checkhealth and extend the same contract to Beads, skill invocation, and available trusted skill-management operations. No separate feature screen.
3. Separate service startup choices for Attention, Runs, receiver, and transcription, with explicit manual setup guidance and reported service/client state.
4. Apply operation-specific prerequisite reports to Park/Run and verified-launch integration points, preserving safety and lifecycle obligations. Compose with existing projects instead of reimplementing their deliverables.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With only an authenticated configured ACP Agent and required SQLite available, ordinary chat and its core controls work while br, bvr, lyaml, pw-record, and louiselm-capture are absent. Health contains no errors/warnings for disabled optional capabilities.
2. Repeat with optional binaries installed, Beads/skill directories present, and credentials configured: disabled integrations remain inactive. Availability never grants consent.
3. Each explicit opt-in reaches a real consumer when ready and produces a scoped actionable health/runtime result when prerequisites are absent. Per-Agent skill overrides are reflected accurately rather than hidden behind the global off default.
4. Attention-only service startup exposes only its required local functionality and initiates no recording, phone receiver, transcription, or push. Enabling one of those additional capabilities does not enable the others.
5. Basic Beads inspection does not require bvr; no tracker is initialized implicitly. Composite operations report missing prerequisites before partial admission or mutation.
6. checkhealth and runtime owners agree on effective settings and readiness; checks/install guidance do not install, activate, pair, enroll, or change configuration. Disabled commands point to the same instructions.
7. Configuration reload, disposal, disabled transitions, and late asynchronous callbacks leave no leaked owners or lost lifecycle obligations. Durable records and claims are preserved correctly.
8. No optional flag weakens core permission handling, turn recording, Run limits, trusted Admission, or required verified-launch controls. No component-only success is described as a fully verified Session.
9. Public configuration/types/help, quickstart/Tutor, and service setup documentation describe the same defaults and operation boundaries, with generated outputs consumed and checked in CI.

## Testing Decisions

- Use red-green-refactor for changed behavior and extend existing setup/schema, health, chat/Attention, keymap, skill policy, workflow/Park, and service integration coverage.
- Explicitly test unset configuration, false, true-ready, true-missing-prerequisite, and deliberate per-Agent skill overrides. Unset is a first-class acceptance case.
- Test both absent dependencies and present-but-disabled dependencies/credentials; prove lack of optional effects, not just absent UI buttons. Observe real production ownership boundaries without introducing global/package monkey-patching.
- Exercise independent service startup with temporary private stores, local sockets, and fake external transports. No tests contact cloud services, run installers, require real Agent credentials, or enroll trust hardware.
- Preserve asynchronous/main-loop scheduling, disposal/late-callback, protocol/authentication, security, and durable-state coverage. Include existing Runs/pending records when testing disable transitions.
- Run focused checks while implementing, then the complete affected Lua and/or Rust suites and required format, type, lint, and generated-doc gates. Rust crates have separate suites; do not conflate them.
- Verify the maintainer's actual effective configuration and the exact default/opt-in experience before reporting conditional features as working. Live defects remain open until their exact reproduction is accepted; this epic is not itself a claim that fixes are already live.

## Out of Scope

- Automatic dependency installation/upgrades, downloads/builds, service provisioning, tracker initialization, pairing, credential enrollment, or skill Admission.
- A second feature UI/command, runtime preferences database, general plugin framework, or speculative dependency resolver.
- Disabling mandatory turn recording, changing operator-selected permission policy, or sandboxing ordinary Agent behavior through a feature flag.
- Rebuilding the trusted skill-supply/verified-Session pipeline, implementing the control broker, or delivering FCM as part of this epic. Their own work items own those implementations and acceptance.
- Broad architecture rewrites, service renaming, new external dependencies, platform expansion, or new Android functionality.

## Further Notes

- Related existing work: louiselm-d6fv.9 (P1, verified-Session cutover), louiselm-qbr.5.1 (P1, control broker), and louiselm-qbr.9.6 (P2, optional FCM delivery). These are related integration contracts, not blanket blockers on making default chat minimal. Add blockers only to later concrete slices that actually need those implementations.
- Prior skills behavior/documentation is recorded in louiselm-5fv; this epic intentionally changes LouiseLM's default invocation policy from native to off while preserving explicit choices and ordinary Agent independence.
- This is the accepted design from codex/01a089e3-3bde-77b3-ac6c-e42a0788b501. The maintainer agreed to slices 1, 3, and 4, directed slice 2 into checkhealth, and accepted that revision. No new vocabulary or unconfirmed semantic promotion is included. A full grill-me is unnecessary; a newly discovered material product/security conflict should become a narrow needs-design blocker for the affected slice only.
notes: Implementation of slices .1-.4 is ready, uncommitted, with 1058 Lua tests and 93 capture-service tests passing; LuaLS, StyLua, Rust fmt/clippy/docs and all generated artifact checks pass. Site fixtures pass; full site build reaches demo packaging but requires CI_JOB_TOKEN or LOUISELM_DEMO_PACKAGE_TOKEN. Installed plugin remains separate older checkout e8c06d05186512a1d462c6be8b04c61a9cdb3b1e; active Sessions were not reconfigured. No installer/service restart/config activation performed. Personal all-feature rollout remains dotfiles-louiselm-all-features-787 after authorized landing/update and safe reload. Keep implementation issues in progress pending landing; do not describe flags as active in the maintainer editor.
close_reason: gate:tests/schema/setup_spec.lua Four implementation slices complete; Lua/Rust suites and static/generated gates pass. Personal activation and live acceptance remain dotfiles-louiselm-all-features-787.

title: Session Overview shows the same diff for different hunk selections
description:
Session Overview opens the same latest per-file diff when the operator presses d on different historical hunk rows.

## Observed
Maintainer screenshots, inspected directly on 2026-09-17:
- /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260917_0659_1920x1200_1789621193.png: selected skills-core/src/dependency_fetch.rs L295-301 (+1 -0).
- /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260917_0700_1920x1200_1789621204.png: selected same file L173-181 (+3 -0).
Both popups show identical headers @@ -1,6 +1,6 @@ and @@ -180,6 +180,7 @@.
Subject shown: louiselm-qbr.5.1.4 (codex), local session-9. Diagnosing actor resolved through live session.identity(): codex/01a0adbc-9b9f-76d1-b9fa-cf5b0d60ac76.
Read-only live buffer inventory found no remaining louiselm_overview buffer; original live row targets were unavailable.

## Symptoms
Selecting different changes to one file yields the same latest patch, including hunks unrelated to either selected historical change.

## Root cause
lua/louiselm/ui/session_overview.lua:359 merge_file_edits appends all incoming hunks, but line 372 overwrites existing.diff with incoming.diff.
At line 548 every rendered hunk target receives file.diff rather than its source patch/hunk.
At line 776 the d callback consumes target.path/target.diff only; target.line does not select or focus a hunk.
The original relation between historical hunks and their source patches is lost before rendering.

## Reproduction evidence
Read-only headless Neovim using tests/minimal_init.lua called public collect_session_summary and render_session_buffer with two session.edits for the same path:
earlier = "@@ -295,1 +295,2 @@\n context\n+earlier"
latest = "@@ -173,1 +173,2 @@\n context\n+latest"
Actual row projections:
{"target_line":173,"diff_header":"@@ -173,1 +173,2 @@","equals_latest":true,"row":"    • L173-174 (+1 -0)"}
{"target_line":295,"diff_header":"@@ -173,1 +173,2 @@","equals_latest":true,"row":"    • L295-296 (+1 -0)"}
No file writes or live keypresses were performed.

## Why it was not caught
tests/ui/session_overview_spec.lua:836 uses one edit and presses d on a file header. It asserts float/sidebar/chat lifecycle but never compares contents selected from two different hunk rows.
Prior QA louiselm-upbn6 exercised a one-line fixture and navigation; it did not cover multiple edits to the same file.

## Fix direction
Preserve each hunk's association with its source patch during extraction/merge and carry the selected hunk through the preview boundary. A hunk-row preview should display that selected change; changing only the popup cursor cannot recover patches already overwritten. Preserve file-header preview behavior deliberately, and distinguish historical line coordinates from current-file coordinates.

## Acceptance
- Add a regression with multiple completed edits to one file; pressing d on distinct hunk rows displays the corresponding distinct changes.
- Cover multiple hunks within one patch, including repeated/overlapping historical line ranges.
- Preserve sidebar/chat lifecycle and file navigation.
- Run applicable focused checks and complete Lua suite.
- Maintainer repeats the two screenshot selections and confirms the correct corresponding changes before closure.

## Not covered
Diagnosis/tracking only, as requested; no implementation or live retest performed. Synthetic reproduction establishes the mapping defect, not captured ACP event ordering. Capture structural event ordering before implementing a real-peer regression.

title: Grill-me needed: which Provider operation and cost contract should the broker enforce first?
description:
Do not resolve the contract in passing; confirm the supported request and cost boundary with the maintainer before implementing louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.

Confirmed parent decision: the broker performs typed Provider calls; Sessions never supply destinations. Each new Provider API shape is broker-side work. The task does not select an API/operation, supported payload, or trusted pre-call cost bound.

Evidence: registry.rs Provider contains service attribution only; broker/provider_credentials.rs provides custody and handles, not request authority; GrantRequest has no Provider request permission; no concrete Provider transport exists. Existing authenticated status/dependency relay and HTTPS dependency transport provide reuse points. All 16 credential custody tests pass through the documented systemd test wrapper.

Decide the first supported API and operation, then its bounded input/output and cost reservation contract (trusted pricing/configuration, budget owner/lifetime, unknown outcomes and retries). Alternatively explicitly scope this slice to provider-neutral enforcement with a concrete adapter follow-up; that cannot claim real Provider calls are complete. The separate Verified-launch gate remains louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.3.

Source: codex/01a0b244-e023-7762-bdbf-19baf015da98. No executable changes made.
design:
Confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-09-18 in codex/01a0b244-e023-7762-bdbf-19baf015da98, after the final summary and explicit "yes i confirm".

1. Codex/OpenAI is the first integration. Preserve the subscription through a separate, explicit broker-owned sign-in to the same account. Ordinary Codex login remains untouched.
2. Investigate a narrow local Codex Responses endpoint using the existing routing hook. Preserve the LouiseLM -> acp-proxy -> codex-acp -> Codex chain. No Codex runtime patch is assumed or approved by this decision. This permits investigation of specific HTTP operation mediation, revising the blanket rejection in parent comment2097; no generic forwarding proxy or Session-selected upstream destination is authorized.
3. Authentication/login/refresh and isolation that prevents tools from acquiring Codex endpoint authority must be proven before production request implementation. Offline routing alone is proven (comment2236); it is not subscription compatibility or Verified acceptance.
4. Operator-approved Model allowlist, finite upstream model-request budget and expiry are the v1 limits. No exact dollar ceiling or subscription-quota guarantee. Account limits remain an Agent-advertised ACP extension; do not read another tool credential store or query Provider limits.
5. Every Session and child in a Run shares one durable budget. Atomically reserve one unit before each upstream model-request attempt, including retries. A child limit also consumes the Run total; restarting/replacing a Session or broker never resets spent authority.
6. Exhaustion stops new calls, Parks the Run and creates an Attention item. Resume requires an explicit operator-approved extension.
7. Expiry cancels in-flight requests locally and Parks the Run. Preserve output already received and spent request units. Cancellation cannot prove upstream work stopped. Unknown outcomes receive no refund or automatic retry; completed effects are never described as rolled back.
8. Until authentication, isolation and enforcement are proven, do not claim this integration supplies Verified protection. Existing launch-gate and network-posture tasks retain their responsibilities.

Vocabulary delta: No change.

Reopened sender-authority decision confirmed on 2026-09-18 in codex/01a0b2b8-3e82-7b02-ab50-9b40601ac7da, after the maintainer chose "stock", authorized "investigate", and accepted the final summary with "ok i confirm".
1. Keep stock Codex. Select an external Linux BPF-LSM sender guard plus independent Control broker authorization for every complete request as the candidate to prove. Preserve the ACP chain and the existing exact-process authority contract.
2. The disposable VM evidence in docs/codex-kernel-guard-proof.md establishes only the primitive: stock streaming succeeds, actual tools/siblings and inherited-socket helpers are denied; next sends fail after revocation/expiry. Batched requests can share a kernel check, and detachment restores access.
3. Require exact lifetime/endpoint binding (louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.6), fail-closed guard survival and host prerequisites (louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.7), independent admission of queued/partial/batched requests (louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.8), and the full hostile ACP composition (louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.9). The existing production request task remains blocked by the complete proof and independent subscription authentication. Unsupported hosts/integrations must refuse Verified launch; ordinary Sessions and configured auto-approval remain supported.
4. Keep Model allowlist, shared durable Run request count, expiry, Park/Attention and unknown-outcome accounting from the earlier confirmed design. No generic forwarding, runtime patch, desktop installation, real sign-in or production cutover is authorized by the proof decision.
5. Concurrent authentication findings do not establish a supported broker-owned subscription bridge. Route that still-unresolved architecture to louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.10, which blocks .3.4; this confirmation does not approve a helper/legacy-token API or upstream subscription transport.
Vocabulary delta: No change.

Existing confirmed operation/cost/authentication decisions remain historical accepted context. Decide how the local HTTP endpoint can authenticate the exact lifetime-pinned Codex app-server on every request while denying tools/helpers, without a runtime patch or weaker authority implicitly assumed. docs/codex-endpoint-proof.md and scripts/probe-codex-endpoint.py reproduce actual Codex-tool replay, sibling replay, inherited TCP descriptor use and post-runtime-exit acceptance in an empty network namespace. These reject base_url alone as authority, not every possible stock integration. Existing .3.2 dependency on this question keeps the implementation blocked.

title: Grill-me needed: guarded Provider worker ownership
description:
Do not resolve this in passing; a focused design decision is needed before production Provider activation.

Question: How should a per-Session Control broker serialize each complete request admission with Park/disposal/revision while a supervisor-created upstream socket is connecting, awaiting authenticated ACK, or streaming a long HTTPS response?

Evidence: skills-core/src/bin/control/inspection.rs:416-458 owns BrokerSession and operator queries on one worker. skills-core/src/broker/provider_handoff.rs:246-292 serves an entire accepted connection synchronously on that worker. skills-core/src/broker/provider_service.rs:62-151 reserves the durable Run unit and starts the transport before returning. skills-core/src/broker/provider_transport.rs:54-67 still uses an ambient DefaultConnector. skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/sender_guard/handoff.rs:26-90 blocks through connect/send/ACK, while lifecycle Park must revoke without waiting; louiselm-raay2 remains open. No typed broker-to-supervisor upstream-create request exists yet.

Threads: owner state machine versus split admission/relay worker; what exact event linearizes the admitted upstream effect without handing out a stale permit; how the Session channel single reader routes upstream descriptor and ACK while lifecycle messages continue; how Park can revoke during every wait and a retained TLS stream; what installed VM controls prove this without a paid Provider call.

title: QA round: Provenance, resumed folds, and recovery
description:
# Manual QA review — recent UI and Provenance changes

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; it becomes the round bead when the review closes.

**Build under test:** `ca9b72b..ded81aa` (last five commits). **Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: recent Provenance UI work, recovery-warning fixes, and the live report
that resumed reasoning paragraphs are recorded but not installed as Neovim
folds.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Resumed reasoning paragraphs fold and toggle | **passed** — maintainer confirmed folds in Session `codex/01a0461a-382d-7fb0-b46e-0a552b0bb40b` |
| 2 | Decision index renders and navigates | **passed** — screenshot shows selected Decision `louiselm-c274` in a populated Provenance popup after fix `d6851c6`; latency recorded as F2 |
| 3 | Decision evidence timeline separates history and drift | **blocked** — historical snapshot/drift is the separate open task `louiselm-97qw`, blocked by `louiselm-8tzl` |
| 4 | Missing Provenance sources remain explicit | **passed** — Decision `louiselm-parallel-worker-tracker-substrate-6mtc` retained implementation/Session evidence and explicitly rendered unresolved QA acceptance and Forensics |
| 5 | Recovery warning reflects actual recoverability | **passed** — first restart identified one abandoned Session and offered `:LouiselmResume`; next restart emitted no warning |

## Setup

Start a fresh Neovim instance from the repository root with the plugin loaded.
The running instance must be restarted after any Lua change. Confirm the source
tree is the build under test with:

```vim
:lua print(vim.inspect(require("louiselm.ui.provenance")))
```

For Case 1, resume a Session that has multiple historical reasoning paragraphs
separated by prose or tool output. The known live reproduction was
`codex/01a04635-f2b8-7e70-9485-7a931923ec99`; use a fresh equivalent if it is
not available. Do not use a synchronous test fixture for this case.

For Provenance cases, use the repository's existing closed Decision issues and
open them through the normal LouiseLM commands. Record the Session id or issue
id used so evidence can be pinned to it.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- `:LouiselmInspectProvenance` is the cursor/object inspector and prompts for
  Beads/Session identifiers when the cursor is not on a supported object. The
  Decision index is `:LouiselmProvenanceDecisions` or `<leader>lP` in chat.
- The shipped Decision view (`ca9b72b`) shows current correlations and explicit
  unresolved evidence. Historical backlog state and later drift are not part of
  that slice; they belong to `louiselm-97qw` and its `louiselm-8tzl` dependency.

## Cases

### 1. Resumed reasoning paragraphs fold and toggle

Exercises `ded81aa` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` and the resumed Session
rendering path.

Steps:

1. Resume the prepared Session.
2. Wait until replay completes and the chat view is interactive.
3. Find at least two historical `[thinking]` headers and one reasoning block
   produced after resume.
4. Place the cursor on each header and press `za` twice.

Expect: every historical and post-resume reasoning block has a real manual fold;
each closes and opens with `za`, and the view remains interactive after replay.

Failure signature: a historical header has `foldlevel=0`, `foldclosed=-1`, or
`za` does nothing while a post-resume block folds normally.

### 2. Decision index renders and navigates

Exercises `90f3ca1` / `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua`.

Steps:

1. Run the normal command for the Provenance Decision index.
2. Confirm the buffer opens and wait for source collection to finish.
3. Select a Decision row and follow its issue Provenance link.

Expect: the index is readable, shows Decision state and recent activity, and
navigation lands on the selected issue rather than a different row or the
source chat.

Failure signature: empty output despite known Decisions, rows reorder while
selecting, navigation opens the wrong issue, or a source error closes the view.

### 3. Decision evidence timeline separates history and drift

Exercises `ca9b72b` / `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua`.

From the Decision index, open a Decision with a closing commit.

Expect: the view identifies the Decision anchor and historical reference, then
shows later changes as separate evidence. It does not present current state as
if it were historical state.

Failure signature: historical and current issue state are conflated, or later
changes appear without an explicit drift/reconsideration relationship.

### 4. Missing Provenance sources remain explicit

Exercises `ca9b72b` / `lua/louiselm/provenance/sources.lua`.

Open a Decision or issue whose commit, Beads snapshot, or Session evidence is
unavailable.

Expect: the available sections still render and the missing source is named as
unavailable; one missing source does not erase the rest of the answer.

Failure signature: a blank buffer, generic success with omitted evidence, or a
single missing source preventing unrelated evidence from appearing.

### 5. Recovery warning reflects actual recoverability

Exercises `5b2312f` / `lua/louiselm/ui/abandonment.lua`.

Trigger the normal startup recovery path once with a known abandoned Session,
then repeat startup after the breadcrumb has been consumed.

Expect: the first startup reports the truthful recovery state once; the second
startup does not repeat a stale warning or claim a recoverable Session when it
cannot be resumed.

Failure signature: stale warning repeats, recovery claims success without a
Session, or the warning disappears before the operator can act.

## Evidence check

For Case 1, report the Session id and inspect the live buffer through the
maintainer's Neovim instance; the verdict is that historical and new headers
have equivalent fold behavior. This proves UI behavior, not just recorded fold
ranges.

For Cases 2–5, report the exact `louiselm://` buffer name and capture the
rendered buffer text or the relevant session/log artifact. Pin logs by Session
id, never by newest-file order.

## Cleanup when the round closes

Close temporary Sessions if desired, remove any temporary fixtures, and delete
this scratch file only after its contents have been transferred to the round
bead.

## Reporting back

Send me the case number, what you saw, the Session or buffer id, and any exact
failure signature. I will inspect objective evidence, update this file, and
file any product finding before changing code.

## Findings this round

**F1 — Selecting a Provenance Decision fails with duplicate buffer name**
(`louiselm-g2ya`, fixed in `d6851c6`).

The Decision index loads, but selecting a row reports `Vim:E95: Buffer with this
name already exists` at `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:290`. The likely shared
boundary is `open_provenance`, which always assigned a requested URI to a new
buffer without handling an existing named buffer. The fix reuses an existing
named buffer and window, with regression coverage. Focused Provenance tests
(14/14), full suite (703/703), and manual QA passed. The perceived slowness is
tracked separately as F2.

**F2 — Selecting a Provenance Decision takes about 11 seconds**
(`louiselm-dkga`, fixed in `7efbc44`).

The selected Decision eventually renders, but the user measured approximately
11 seconds from `<CR>` to the second window. The screenshot
`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260828_0551_1920x1200_1787889089.png` proves the
eventual populated result. The fix shows a loading view immediately; the BVR
latency investigation is tracked separately as `louiselm-cvlc`.

**F3 — Loaded Provenance content keeps the loading popup height**
(`louiselm-7tvl`, not fixed).

Screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260828_0600_1920x1200_1787889613.png`
shows the completed Decision content in a 3–4-line popup. The loading-state
height is not recalculated after the buffer refresh.

title: Large resumed Sessions remain Starting while replay renders
description:
A large resumed Session visibly remains Starting for about 20 seconds before its chat view reaches ready, even though the Agent completes session/load almost immediately.

## Observed

Manual retest on 2026-08-24 with deepseek/session-5b4fb715-7267-4f09-848b-54e84fca2dfc and build ee9e541. The current replay connection is /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/connections/57902114-99cf-42b6-ae4c-d88b46a85b04.jsonl. session/load request id=2 is line 3 at 11:54:40.491Z and its response is line 172 at 11:54:40.506Z: 15ms. Between them the Agent emits 12 user chunks, 11 assistant chunks, and 145 completed tool updates. The user observed the winbar on Starting for roughly 20 seconds.

## Symptoms

- Resume appears stuck on Starting for a large Session.
- The ACP wire has already completed load, so the visible delay is client-side replay presentation.

## Root cause

Unknown. The chat schedules each replay event separately and performs incremental buffer, header, fold, and Treesitter work. A main-loop replay backlog is the leading hypothesis; measure it before choosing a fix.

## Why it was not caught

Resume tests replay only a handful of tiny events and assert ordering, not bounded readiness/render latency for a large history.

## Fix direction

Benchmark a captured structural replay fixture without payload contents, identify the dominant UI work, and batch or defer that work at the narrowest presentation boundary.

## Acceptance

- A deterministic regression models a large replay and fails before the fix.
- Ready state becomes visible promptly after the load response.
- The full replay remains ordered and complete without blocking normal editing for tens of seconds.

## Not covered

The missing restored usage annotation is tracked by reopened louiselm-hxvc and has a separate event-state root cause.

title: [thinking] folds dropped by a mid-session session/load are never restored
description:
After a mid-conversation `session/load`, every pre-reload `[thinking]` paragraph in the live chat buffer displays unfolded forever. The louiselm-9wjm recovery (`apply_thought_folds` rescans all recorded ranges on each close, lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1214) demonstrably runs after the reload — new paragraphs keep folding — yet never reinstalls the dropped ranges, although the identical `:fold` command issued manually works immediately.

## Observed

2026-09-02, live Neovim instance, Session `opencode/ses_f9ef11742ffeKkE7eI95In2iVx`, buffer `louiselm://session-5` (buf 149, win 1000). Environment: `foldmethod=manual foldenable=true foldlevel=99` (global and window; the chat fold code sets only foldmethod/foldenable, init.lua:1218-1219 — folds close when created, so foldlevel is not the blocker).

Live introspection through `$NVIM` (10:00 local): 11 recorded `view.thought_folds`, 11 `[thinking]` headers, 6 closed, 5 with no fold at all:

- deleted (foldlevel=0, foldclosed=-1 across the range): recorded [622,841], [847,881], [889,914], [921,1098], [1493,1494] — headers at 1-based lines 623, 848, 890, 922, 1494
- intact (foldlevel=1, closed): e.g. [1129,1206] -> closed 1130..1207

At 10:05, after three more paragraphs had closed (14 recorded folds, each triggering the full rescan), the same five ranges were still foldlevel=0 — the rescan executes and does not restore them.

Probe (10:01): `nvim.api.nvim_cmd({cmd="fold",range={623,842}},{})` inside `nvim_win_call(win 1000)` — the exact command the rescan would issue — succeeded and closed the fold instantly. Probe side effect: fold [622,841] is now manually restored; 848/890/922/1494 remain unfolded.

ACP log timeline (local +0200): session created 09:39:22 (connection 23dfef02, initialize+session/new); re-initialization at 09:50:36 (connection 253203ac, initialize+session/list) and 09:50:43 (connection 5d2c7741, initialize) followed by `session/load` for this session at 07:50:45.404Z — `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ses_f9ef11742ffeKkE7eI95In2iVx/log.jsonl:18201`. Every dead fold covers a pre-reload reasoning paragraph; every fold recorded after the reload is intact.

## Symptoms

- Pre-reload `[thinking]` blocks display fully expanded; `za` does nothing on them (no fold exists).
- Post-reload blocks in the same buffer fold and toggle normally.

## Root cause

Unknown. Hypotheses:

- H1: in the real reload path the rescan guard `nvim.fn.foldclosed(fold.first + 1)` (init.lua:1222) reads as already-closed at its execution point, so the re-issue is skipped. The 9wjm regression's comment attributes the original live drop to a global nvim-ufo fold provider; an external provider's interaction with the apply context is not modeled.
- H2: the re-issued `:fold` runs but a later operation in the same event cascade deletes exactly those folds again.
- H3 (contributing): window re-entry re-application is asymmetric — init.lua:3520-3521 re-applies context and tool folds but not thought folds.

Discriminators: log `foldclosed` per recorded range per `apply_thought_folds` invocation, or reproduce with the mock agent's `replay_reasoning` (lua/louiselm/dev/mock_agent.lua:9) driven through a real `session/load` in the chat UI.

## Why it was not caught

The 9wjm regression (tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:1603) simulates the external drop with `normal! zE` mid-replay and asserts rescan recovery — that simulation recovers; the real `session/load` path does not. No UI test drives a real session/load replay and then asserts recorded thought folds are closed in the live window.

## Fix direction

Discriminate H1/H2 first (instrument the rescan to log its per-range view). Likely then: re-apply thought folds at the window re-entry boundary like context/tool folds (init.lua:3520), and/or verify the post-condition (`foldlevel(first+1) > 0`) after re-issue and escalate instead of silently proceeding.

## Acceptance

- A UI regression that drives a real `session/load` replay through the chat (mock agent `replay_reasoning`), then asserts every recorded `thought_folds` range is a closed fold in the live window after subsequent paragraph closes; fails before the fix.
- Live acceptance (AGENTS §5): the maintainer confirms pre-reload `[thinking]` blocks render folded in a live session after a mid-session reload. Keep open until then.

## Not covered

- Whether nvim-ufo (or another fold provider) is active in the maintainer's live config — unverified.
- A second live session (`louiselm://session-1`, 43 recorded folds, no window displayed) was not examined.
- louiselm-6ze7 (duplicated `[thinking]` headers after tool calls) is a different rendering defect, checked and excluded.
