title: Validation
description: Pure, total, side-effect-free structural checking of one workflow definition from its frontmatter alone. Binary: a definition is accepted or rejected. Cacheable on hash(document) + hash(skill manifest).
design: Established by the louiselm-qbr.8 grill-me session on 2026-08-26, with explicit maintainer confirmation of the final summary. Kept binary with no warn tier and no override flag, on the grounds that a warn tier trains users to ignore the validator and an override degrades every rejection to a warning with extra steps.
notes: Use Validation only for the structural, frontmatter-only, model-free check. Distinguish from Assessment, which reads prose with a model and has no authority. Avoid 'lint' -- lint warns, Validation rejects. Validation never activates a skill, never enters a context window, and never resolves ambiguity by inference: ambiguity is a rejection.

title: Grill-me needed: what tracker state does an isolated parallel worker own, and how does it reconcile
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing — it wants full attention.**

## The question

`louiselm-qbr.6` commits to running parallel workers in **isolated workspaces**.
Every worker in that design needs to read and write the beads graph — claim a
task, comment, close, file findings. But the beads graph is not a service: it is
a per-checkout SQLite database plus one tracked export file. Isolating the
workspaces necessarily isolates the tracker state along with them.

So: **what does a parallel worker own, and what does it borrow?** Does each
worker get its own `beads.db` and reconcile on integration, or do workers never
own tracker state at all and instead report to a single coordinator that holds
the only writable graph?

That fork is not a detail. It decides whether beads is a shared substrate the
workers contend on, or a coordinator-only resource the workers never touch.

## Evidence (2026-08-21)

Today two Claude Code sessions ran concurrently in this repository. Both wrote
the tracker; the second landed `ee7f254` cleanly. It worked — and the reason it
worked is the property `qbr.6` proposes to remove:

- **One checkout, one database.** `.beads/beads.db` (SQLite, WAL) is the source
  of truth; `.beads/issues.jsonl` is a tracked export. The db is gitignored, so
  it is never shared through git.
- **Same-process contention is already solved.** `.beads/` carries live lock
  files — `.br-db-write-<hash>.lock`, `.br-jsonl-write-<hash>.lock`,
  `.write.lock`, `.sync.lock`. Concurrent writers in one checkout serialize.
  None of that machinery spans two checkouts.
- **Git-level merging is unconfigured.** The repository has no `.gitattributes`,
  so `issues.jsonl` merges as plain lines. `br sync` has a real three-way merge
  (`--merge`, using `beads.base.jsonl` + db + jsonl, with `--force-db` /
  `--force-jsonl` / `--force` for semantic conflicts) — but nothing routes git's
  merge through it.
- **The two paths actively disagree.** `br sync --import-only` names an
  unbypassable guard: *"Conflict markers: Rejects files with git merge conflict
  markers."* So a naive git merge produces exactly the artifact beads refuses to
  import. The failure is not a silent corruption; it is a hard stop that needs a
  human, which is the one thing an unattended worker pool cannot supply.
- **Beads already anticipates some of this.** `.beads/.gitignore` reserves a
  `redirect` file described as "Worktree redirect file", and ignores daemon
  runtime files (`daemon.lock`, `daemon.pid`, `bd.sock`). Both suggest upstream
  has thought about multi-checkout and about a single-writer daemon. Whether
  either is a fit here is unexamined.

## Why file it separately from qbr.6

`louiselm-101q` solves *who claims what* — session identity on a claim. It
assumes one graph that all agents can see. This issue is the layer underneath:
whether a shared graph still exists once workers are isolated. Solve 101q
perfectly and this is untouched.

`qbr.6` says "isolated workspaces" and "coordinate integration" but scopes
integration to the **work product** — branches, conflicts, rerouting. It never
says what happens to the **tracker state** the workers generate. Filing here so
`qbr.6` inherits the constraint instead of discovering it mid-implementation,
when the isolation model is already built.

## Threads worth pulling

- A merge driver in `.gitattributes` routing `issues.jsonl` through
  `br sync --merge` is the cheap answer. Does it actually resolve semantic
  conflicts unattended, or does it just relocate the human gate — given that
  semantic conflicts explicitly require a `--force*` flag, i.e. a decision?
- The coordinator-only model kills the merge problem by construction: workers
  emit structured results, one process writes the graph. Cost is that a worker
  can no longer file a finding while it works, which AGENTS.md section 2 requires
  ("File before the fix, while the failing evidence still exists"). Is that
  requirement compatible with isolation at all, or does it need a per-worker
  append-only journal that reconciles later?
- Reversibility framing from `louiselm-autonomy-authorization-question-grt`
  applies directly: a tracker write is trivially reversible, a bad merge across
  N workers' graphs is not. The two issues probably want to be grilled in that
  order.
- Does `br`'s `redirect` / daemon machinery already implement one of these
  models? Read before designing — this may be a configuration question wearing
  an architecture question's clothes.

## Out of scope for the grill

Re-deriving the evidence above. React to it, and settle the ownership fork.
close_reason: Design resolved by the continued grill and routed into louiselm-qbr.6; user explicitly confirmed the convergence readback.

comments.text: Takeover provenance: the user explicitly asked this Codex session to continue the grill after Claude session claude/d2856b79-aa3e-4d36-a1e2-bbfaec7aae74 hit its model limit, then explicitly confirmed the final convergence readback. This is a human-authorized continuation, not a stale-claim reclaim. The complete Claude transcript was used as continuity evidence.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Settled design routed into feature louiselm-qbr.6. Decisions: shared canonical tracker with isolated first-class ACP worker worktrees; br-authorized candidate set plus bvr ranking; coordinator-only blocker promotion, integration, gates, closure, and .beads Git ownership; graph-based blocking with preserved-work resumption; strict ready_for_integration/rework workflow; bounded recovery manifests; integration-aligned tracker checkpoints. Explicitly rejected per-worker tracker reconciliation, coordinator-only tracker writes, opaque subagents as primary workers, worker self-promotion/closure, labels as lifecycle states, and per-worker .beads commits.

title: Budget Park observer is never constructed, so budget Parks never reach the editor
description:
`lua/louiselm/workflow/park_observer.lua` is never constructed in production, so a
service-originated budget Park never cancels a live Run and never presents accounting to
the operator. The capability `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.4.2` closed on is inert.

## Observed

Found 2026-09-01 during the `louiselm-22h7` grill-me session while measuring whether
agent-authored close reasons describe delivered effects. Detected mechanically by scanning
all 89 Lua modules for the `louiselm-ce6.1.4` signature: a production-namespace module whose
only consumer is its own spec.

## Evidence

- `lua/louiselm/workflow/park_observer.lua` is required by exactly one file:
  `tests/workflow/park_observer_spec.lua:2`. `grep -rn "park_observer\|ParkObserver"` over
  the repo returns no other reference outside the module itself.
- `park_observer.lua:116` is the **only** production caller of `Run:accept_park`
  (`lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua`). Every other `accept_park` call site is a test:
  `tests/workflow/run_spec.lua:125,153,357` and `tests/workflow/resume_controller_spec.lua:24`.
- Nothing calls `ParkObserver`'s constructor (`park_observer.lua:74`), so `observe()` never
  runs against a live editor.
- This is not a whole-subtree deferral: the sibling from `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.4.3`,
  `lua/louiselm/workflow/resume_controller.lua`, **is** wired at
  `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:11` and constructed at `init.lua:4320`.
- No follow-up bead tracks the wiring. `br search -a "park observer"` returns 0 issues.

## Why it was not caught

`louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.4.2` closed with "Revision-idempotent Park reconciliation cancels live
work after scheduling and presents only bounded non-sensitive state; all gates pass." Every
clause is true of the module and false of the running editor. Its gates passed because the
spec exercises the module directly. Its parent `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.4` then closed on "All
children closed... Acceptance criteria met and verified under full Rust + Neovim gates", and
the feature `louiselm-qbr.3.2` closed on "all child slices closed" above that — so one
unwired module reads as a delivered feature three levels up.

Added 98f6ac4 on 2026-08-27, inert since.

## Acceptance

1. A service-originated budget Park arriving over the Run socket cancels the matching live
   Run on Neovim's main loop, from a real editor process.
2. The operator sees the bounded accounting presentation (ceiling, consumed, reserved,
   triggering mutation id) with no token, argument, prompt, or payload content.
3. A `consumer:<file:line>` exists naming the production construction site.
4. `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.4.2`'s stated acceptance criteria 1-5 hold against the wired path,
   not only against the module in isolation.

## Not covered

Whether `.4.1`'s socket streaming delivers Run snapshots to the editor at all was not
verified; if it does not, wiring the observer is necessary but not sufficient. Check before
assuming the observer is the only gap.

the exact compaction ID. That was evidence-query scope, not a product finding.

lifecycle. Classify this as a recipe error; apologize and combine reopening,
task editing and submission in one human step. Do not infer lost source data

remains unused and will need normal UI cleanup after the round.

ready state. Real source history includes the seed, compaction, and eu-west turn.

### Submitted Handoff checkpoint

Human supplied target codex/01a0c536-0ff0-78d0-b296-b7d5505847de, local session-6,
buffer192. Its sole prompt request3 contains resource_link,text,resource blocks;

### Fallback capture and final acceptance

Human reports done after reopening, leaving visible and cancelling. The bounded
observer captured visible buffer238 named louiselm://handoff-session-7-session-9:
source_matches=true,has_transcript=true,has_marker=true,has_reply=true,

claude/96d93a8d-6e68-4007-a369-4b9abef17cc8 is ready/current_turn0 and its exact
ACP log has zero prompts. MINT source remains ready/current_turn1/zero compactions,
with the identical baseline SHA256. Original ORCHID source also retains its exact
baseline hash and ready/current_turn3. Intermediate empty Claude target
a8a263ee-0865-4ec4-9324-888209fd9b55 is no longer in the live snapshot; its precise
disposal was not observed. Case4 fallback/cancel and the scoped round are complete.

## Cases after the prerequisite

### 1. Retained summary

Create one fresh Session using the verified supporting adapter. Pin its ACP ID,
exact runtime, negotiated capability and advertised compaction command before
issuing that command. Seed a small synthetic task with a distinctive fact and
ask the Agent to retain it without tools. If the peer refuses compaction because
the conversation is too short, record that limitation; do not repeatedly spend
turns to fill context.

Run the advertised compaction command once. Expect one lifecycle row that reaches
completed. Inspect it with LouiselmInspectTool and confirm a nonempty summary.
Failure: generic events arrive but no usable row/summary is retained, the row
duplicates, or the Session becomes stuck. Legacy tool events do not pass this case.

### 2. Review with later context

After successful compaction, submit one distinct synthetic fact. Then invoke
LouiselmHandOff and choose a configured target. Expect an editable takeover brief
with Retained compaction summary, Recent conversation (including boundary overlap),
the new fact, and correct source identity. Fill the takeover task explicitly.
Inspect before submitting. Failure: missing recent context, wrong source,
unexpected extra source prompt, or inaccessible review controls.

### 3. Submission and source preservation

Submit the brief with Normal-mode Ctrl-S. Ask the target to report the two
synthetic facts without tools. Expect a distinct ready target Session and a usable
source retaining its transcript. Pin both identities and compare source transcript
and prompt count before/after Handoff. Failure: source disappears/changes, an extra
source prompt is sent, or the target receives the wrong reviewed content.

### 4. Fallback

Use a separate fresh source with one synthetic exchange and no retained summary.
Open Handoff review. Expect the filtered transcript and source identity, without
claiming a retained summary. Abandon the review after inspecting it. Failure:
missing context or Handoff incorrectly requiring compaction support.

## Evidence

Read-only Session projections print identity, status, turn count, command names,
and compaction IDs/status/summary size, never whole Session objects. This probe
has been validated against the coordinator's known empty compaction collection.
Summary content may be structured: use the production Compaction.text helper
when checking usability rather than assuming a string.

Pin protocol files by exact ACP ID. Inspect initialize in the linked connection
log; inspect compaction event ordering in that Session's log. Compaction and
Handoff checkers were validated against the exact real fixtures above. No
synthetic check certifies live peer support.
Human observation establishes readability, focus and intermediate interactions;
state/log evidence establishes event delivery, identities and source preservation.

## Round result and lessons

Four scoped cases passed: real generic compaction and inspection, summary plus
recent context in reviewed Handoff, completed distinct target with unchanged
source/no extra source prompt, and actual no-summary fallback with cancellation.
No product bug was found or fixed, so no claim that an automated test missed a
new defect. No repeated Lua gates for this evidence-only round. The runtime
candidate's1429-test/build/static/startup gates are recorded above.

Manual evidence closes the prior gap left by synthetic compaction fixtures:
Claude0.79.0 delivered a summary then a metadata-only completed patch; LouiseLM
retained it, and a real Codex target received both old and new facts through
the embedded-context Handoff path. Scope does not certify every model, adapter,
summary coverage, permissions, or other unrelated runtime behavior. Human
confirmed summary inspection and review contents; protocol/state evidence proves
the exact target reply and source preservation, not separate visual target styling.

Lessons stay in this round record: inspect ephemeral reviews while visible;
switching back to the coordinator wipes them. Match the actual response contract
(separator whitespace was unspecified). Distinguish omitted JSON fields from
null and structured summary blocks from strings. Existing generic tests cover
these semantics; no new standing rule or unresolved design question is warranted.

## Final cleanup and retained state

Four QA Sessions remain ready and may be closed through normal UI; no automatic
disposal is performed and the coordinator must remain open:

- ORCHID source: claude/a11d1b78-1ca2-48ba-939b-022a9b899d90, three turns.
- Successful target: codex/01a0c536-0ff0-78d0-b296-b7d5505847de, one turn.
- MINT fallback source: codex/01a0c539-a959-7113-bece-3820651f8f89, one turn.
- Final empty target: claude/96d93a8d-6e68-4007-a369-4b9abef17cc8, zero turns.

Earlier empty targets01a0c532 and a8a263ee are no longer live. Their exact disposal
was not observed. Source histories, protocol logs and fallback snapshot remain
as evidence; the temporary snapshot/verification logs may disappear on reboot.
The observer has exited. No review is open; no extra source prompts were sent.

Runtime0.79.0 remains selected, previous0.77.0 retained for rollback. Dotfiles
inventory/tracker commit0de210c is local; no push occurred. Unrelated dotfiles
config/lockfile and pre-existing LouiseLM Beads changes were preserved.
Archive the complete record into one qa-round Bead, verify identical contents,
then remove this untracked scratch. No findings need parenting; runtime
preparation/activation is already recorded in dotfiles-it8 and louiselm-muckf.

title: louiselm-capture serve crash-loops: RestrictAddressFamilies blocks the new Run socket
description:
## Observed

Found live while scoping louiselm-y8vj (Case 4 needs the `serve` daemon running for reaping). The
`louiselm-capture.service` systemd --user unit is crash-looping right now:

```
$ systemctl --user status louiselm-capture
Active: activating (auto-restart) (Result: exit-code)
Main PID: 196178 (code=exited, status=1/FAILURE)
```

```
$ journalctl --user -u louiselm-capture.service -n 8 --no-pager
louiselm-capture[196178]: louiselm-capture: Run socket I/O failed: Address family not supported by protocol (os error 97)
systemd[3173]: louiselm-capture.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
systemd[3173]: louiselm-capture.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
```

Restart counter was at 2154 and climbing (RestartSec=5), i.e. crash-looping roughly every 5s.

## Root cause

`capture-service/src/cli.rs`'s `serve` command calls `RunSocket::bind(...)` (`run_socket.rs:82-114`),
which does `UnixListener::bind(path)` (`run_socket.rs:106`) -- a Unix-domain socket, added by the Run
socket feature (louiselm-qbr.3, commit 731b381 and neighbors, landed 2026-08-26).

Both the repository's reference unit (`capture-service/contrib/systemd/louiselm-capture.service`) and
the maintainer's locally installed unit (`~/.config/systemd/user/louiselm-capture.service`, mtime
2026-08-26 20:46, one minute before 731b381 landed) set:

```
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6
```

This systemd hardening directive was written before the Run socket existed, when `serve` only needed
a TCP/TLS listener for the capture receiver. It was never updated when `RunSocket::bind` added a
`UnixListener::bind` call. Under `RestrictAddressFamilies`, the kernel rejects any `socket()` call for
an address family not in the allow-list with `EAFNOSUPPORT` (os error 97) -- exactly the observed
error. `RunSocket::bind` runs (and fails) *before* the TLS network server binds
(`cli.rs:425-463`), so the entire `serve` process exits before the audio-capture HTTP receiver ever
starts either -- this is not just blocking Run reaping, the whole capture-service daemon has been
nonfunctional since 2026-08-26.

## Impact

- The background reaper (`RunStore::reap_expired`, only invoked from inside `serve`,
  `cli.rs:437-448`) has never run since the unit was last (re)started under this config: expired
  cold-Parked Runs are not reaped and their Beads claims are never released.
- The paired-phone audio-capture receiver (`Receiver`/axum TLS server, `cli.rs:425,457-463`) has not
  been listening at all -- durable speech capture from Android during this window depends on the
  phone's local durable queue (per louiselm-capture-receiver-reachability-rnjc's design) rather than
  ever reaching the receiver.
- Continuous restart-loop (~every 5s) has been consuming systemd journal space and CPU/log churn
  since 2026-08-26.

## Fix direction

Add `AF_UNIX` to `RestrictAddressFamilies` in both places:
- `capture-service/contrib/systemd/louiselm-capture.service` (tracked reference template -- fix so
  future installs/copies don't repeat this).
- `~/.config/systemd/user/louiselm-capture.service` (the maintainer's live instance -- needs
  `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user restart louiselm-capture` after editing).

## Acceptance

- `RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_UNIX` in both files.
- `systemctl --user status louiselm-capture` shows `active (running)` with a stable PID (no restart
  loop) after reload+restart.
- `journalctl --user -u louiselm-capture.service -n 5` shows no further "Run socket I/O failed"
  errors after the fix.
close_reason: Fixed by adding AF_UNIX to RestrictAddressFamilies; service confirmed stable

comments.author: claude/d4b23fbe-32a3-4c77-8802-687f31119e64
comments.text: Fixed: added AF_UNIX to RestrictAddressFamilies in capture-service/contrib/systemd/louiselm-capture.service and ~/.config/systemd/user/louiselm-capture.service, then systemctl --user daemon-reload && restart louiselm-capture. Confirmed active (running), stable PID 201220, no further 'Run socket I/O failed' errors, no restart past the RestartSec=5 threshold (verified at +3s and +15s).

title: Normalize bounded current-buffer diagnostics
description:
## Goal
Produce a bounded, typed snapshot of the current Neovim buffer's diagnostics for later prompt attachment.

## Scope
- In scope: collect `vim.diagnostic` entries for the current buffer; include errors and warnings only.
- In scope: normalize path, 1-based line/column, severity, source, code, and message.
- In scope: include observation time and buffer-change state without triggering an LSP refresh.
- In scope: cap total diagnostics and message length, reporting explicit truncation counts.
- In scope: format diagnostic messages as delimited untrusted data, never as instructions.
- Out of scope: ACP transport, prompt queueing, automatic collection, workspace-wide diagnostics, and custom protocol capabilities.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A public/internal collector returns a deterministic typed snapshot for the current buffer.
2. Error and warning diagnostics are included; hints/info are excluded.
3. Locations are 1-based and paths are represented consistently for named and unnamed buffers.
4. Source, code, and message are preserved when present; raw `user_data` and arbitrary diagnostic payloads are excluded.
5. The snapshot contains observation time and a buffer-change marker captured without refreshing diagnostics.
6. Per-message and total caps are enforced and the output reports what was truncated or omitted.
7. Diagnostic text is clearly delimited as untrusted data.

## Testing
- Start with a failing behavioral test using `vim.diagnostic.set`.
- Cover severity filtering, 1-based positions, optional fields, named/unnamed buffers, caps/truncation, freshness metadata, and untrusted-text framing.
- Run focused tests plus the full project gates.
close_reason: Implemented lua/louiselm/ui/context/diagnostics.lua: M.snapshot(buffer, opts) returns a deterministic, capped, typed snapshot (path/lnum/col/severity/source/code/message + observed_at/changedtick/truncated_count/truncated_messages) of a buffer's ERROR/WARN diagnostics, reading vim.diagnostic's cache without refreshing it. Wired into ui/context as Context.diagnostics alongside its sibling collectors. TDD: tests/ui/diagnostics_spec.lua red-green (6 cases covering positions, severity filtering, named/unnamed paths, both caps, and changedtick/no-mutation). Full suite green, StyLua clean, LuaLS zero diagnostics.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: vim.diagnostic.get's severity={min=,max=} filter is inverted from the naive reading: the predicate is severity <= min AND severity >= max. So min sets the LEAST severe level to include (min=WARN includes WARN+ERROR, excludes INFO/HINT) and max sets the MOST severe floor (rarely needed, defaults to ERROR). Reaching for max=WARN (as 'most severe I want is warn-level') silently drops ERROR diagnostics instead. Verified against neovim/runtime/lua/vim/diagnostic.lua:504-522 (0.12.2). Used min=WARN in lua/louiselm/ui/context/diagnostics.lua.

title: Grill-me needed: how should louiselm show at-a-glance status for every attached session from inside one session's buffer?
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing -- it wants full attention.**

## The question

When multiple sessions are attached at once, `:LouiselmSwitchSession` already
shows a compact status/telemetry row per session (`session_summary`,
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:338-360`), but only inside that picker. What is
the right way to surface an at-a-glance indicator of *every* attached
session's status while looking at just one of them, and does that belong in
the winbar, the tabline, somewhere else entirely, or not as ambient UI at
all?

## Context

Raised 2026-08-22 as a "what would be nice" question, not a committed
design. The session's own status is already rendered per-window in the
winbar (`session_winbar`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:539-568`), built
from `STATUS_HIGHLIGHTS` (`init.lua:244-252`) mapped to highlight groups
(`init.lua:258-261`) and a `winbar_segment(group, text)` helper
(`init.lua:533`). None of that currently shows anything about sessions other
than the one in the current window.

A sketch was floated in conversation (not committed to): right-align a
compact multi-session strip onto the existing winbar, one glyph+label per
*other* attached session, reusing the same status-to-highlight-group
mapping (`●` ready/green, `…` starting/configuring/prompting/blue,
`!` waiting_permission/cancelling/yellow, `✗` error/red), label from
`rename_session` if set else the agent name, omitted entirely when there are
zero other attached sessions, truncated/collapsed to `+N` when too many fit.
The alternative floated was the tabline instead of the winbar: global rather
than per-window, so it survives even when a chat buffer isn't the active
window, but it is a single global option that would fight any bufferline/
tabline plugin already claiming that space, whereas the winbar is currently
owned entirely by louiselm's chat buffers.

## Threads worth pulling

- Winbar vs. tabline vs. something else (statusline component, floating
  indicator, none of the above) -- the tradeoff above is a first pass, not a
  decision.
- Whether clicking a glyph should switch to that session. Neovim's winbar
  supports click handlers (`%@Func@...%X`), so this could fold
  `:LouiselmSwitchSession` into a direct click instead of picker-only, or
  that could be scope creep for what starts as a passive indicator.
- Label source: renamed name only (compact, but sessions rarely get renamed
  today) vs. agent name vs. including the ACP session id like
  `session_summary` does in the picker.
- Ordering and truncation policy when many sessions are attached: the floated
  idea was to prioritize non-ready sessions (the ones needing attention) over
  ready ones when space runs out, but that is untested against how the
  maintainer actually uses multiple sessions.
- Whether this wants to be always-on ambient UI at all, or opt-in (a config
  flag, a command that toggles it), given the winbar is otherwise fairly
  quiet today.

## Out of scope for the grill

Re-deriving the sketch above from scratch. React to it, keep what holds up,
replace what doesn't.
close_reason: Design resolved through grill; implementation tracked by louiselm-fni7

comments.author: codex/01a02fe7-7c23-7082-aac7-8d54e2bdfc24
comments.text: Grill decision 1: place the multi-Session indicator in the winbar. LouiseLM already owns the winbar in Session buffers, so this keeps the UI local to relevant buffers and avoids competing with global tabline/bufferline plugins.

comments.author: codex/01a02fe7-7c23-7082-aac7-8d54e2bdfc24
comments.text: Grill decision 2: each background Session entry in the winbar is clickable and switches directly to that Session. :LouiselmSwitchSession remains the keyboard-accessible picker and overflow path.

comments.author: codex/01a02fe7-7c23-7082-aac7-8d54e2bdfc24
comments.text: Grill decision 3: show every background Session while space permits. When the winbar is constrained, retain attention-needed Sessions ahead of ready Sessions. The current Session keeps its existing separate winbar segment.

comments.author: codex/01a02fe7-7c23-7082-aac7-8d54e2bdfc24
comments.text: Grill correction to decision 3: the winbar is an attention indicator, not a list of all attached Sessions. Show only background Sessions that require the user's attention, such as an unresolved permission request or a completed response awaiting acknowledgement. Label choice delegated to implementation judgment: use the renamed Session title when present, otherwise the Agent name; omit ACP Session IDs from ambient UI.

comments.author: codex/01a02fe7-7c23-7082-aac7-8d54e2bdfc24
comments.text: Grill correction to visibility policy: every attached Session must appear in the winbar. The current Session remains represented by its existing segment; every other Session appears in the clickable background strip. Ordinary Sessions use a quiet neutral treatment, while Sessions requiring attention use a distinct color and glyph that stand out. This supersedes the attention-only interpretation in the prior comment.

comments.author: codex/01a02fe7-7c23-7082-aac7-8d54e2bdfc24
comments.text: Grill decision 4: an unseen completed response highlights its background Session until the user focuses that Session, then clears like an unread notification. A permission request remains urgent until answered; an error remains urgent until the Session is disposed or otherwise resolved.

comments.author: codex/01a02fe7-7c23-7082-aac7-8d54e2bdfc24
comments.text: Grill decision 5: the multi-Session strip is always enabled when at least two Sessions are attached and omitted when only one is attached. Do not add a config flag or toggle.

comments.author: codex/01a02fe7-7c23-7082-aac7-8d54e2bdfc24
comments.text: Grill decision 6: under width pressure, preserve every attention-needed Session as a labelled entry, then show as many quiet Sessions as fit and collapse the remaining quiet Sessions into a clickable +N entry. Clicking +N opens the existing Session picker. Attention-needed Sessions must never be hidden in overflow.

comments.author: codex/01a02fe7-7c23-7082-aac7-8d54e2bdfc24
comments.text: Grill decision 7: background entries are right-aligned and use the existing status color language: green dot for seen/ready, blue ellipsis for starting/configuring/working, yellow dot for an unseen completed response, yellow exclamation for permission required, and red cross for error. Quiet overflow uses neutral +N. Attention entries are ordered last for visual prominence.

title: Migrate louiselm.com authority to Cloud DNS
description:
## Goal
Move louiselm.com authoritative DNS from Squarespace to the bartab-dns-20260802 control project after the Firebase site is already stable.

## Scope
- In scope: a lifecycle-separated OpenTofu state, Cloud DNS zone and records, parity checks, staged DNSSEC migration, registrar nameserver/DS changes, and rollback.
- Out of scope: Hosting resources, content deployments, and unrelated bartab.fr zones.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The new root has a distinct remote-state key and owns no existing foundation resources.
2. Cloud DNS answers match the current authoritative zone before delegation.
3. DNSSEC follows Google's migration sequence; DS and nameserver changes are separately approved.
4. Public resolvers converge without a validation outage and Firebase TLS remains healthy.
5. Old authority is retained through delegation-cache expiry and rollback is documented.

## Testing
- OpenTofu format, init, validate, security scan, reviewed plan, and idempotent second plan.
- Compare SOA, NS, DNSKEY/DS, A/AAAA, CNAME, TXT, MX, and CAA answers before and after delegation.

## Notes
This later migration is not required to launch the Firebase site and must not be combined with the first content release.

This round tests the explicit command outside a displayed chat and the human

or certify operation after actual UI corruption. No genuine faulty subject is
currently established. Automated no-chat-owner/headless API cases are separate
coverage; hiding a view does not prove the UI owner was never constructed.

Existing approval/YOLO policy stays as configured. No permission UI, model turn,
runtime upgrade, credentials, export or sharing is required. Forensics writes a
private metadata/pointer record; it does not copy or sanitize its raw sources.

Exercises lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:656 and the process-wide
session.collect_forensics API, introduced in4867092.

path; :messages can recover it if the notification disappears. Failure:
requires an open chat, diagnoses the coordinator/wrong subject, produces no
actionable completion, freezes the editor, or mutates the subject's evidence.
The explicit path deliberately has no diagnosing-Session provenance or automatic
resource-link queueing; those are supplied by the bare chat form only.

raw sensitive contents, editable canonical record, or a command error.

select a file by recency. A Session being healthy is not faulty-Session acceptance.
No raw prompt, log, environment, credential or tool payload belongs in this report.
Checkers must distinguish schema validity from human readability and from actual

copied, exported, sanitized or shared. Retain the canonical private record and
source log under their own retention policies; no automatic deletion or TTL.

Lessons: pin exact record paths and subject IDs; distinguish record observation
from later live events; preserve honest unsupported/omitted evidence states; arm
the observer before opening ephemeral views. No standing instruction or design
question is warranted.

Existing .beads/issues.jsonl changes predate this round and are preserved. The
human may close the disposable subject through normal UI; no automatic disposal
or editor restart is performed.

title: Resumed sessions drop the user's own messages from the transcript
description:
After :LouiselmResume the chat shows the agent replies and tool calls from the prior conversation but none of the user prompts, so a resumed session reads as one-sided and anything the user wrote — a session id, a decision, a constraint — is invisible.

## Observed

Session claude/fa72dc03-6c22-41c8-be19-9274bea75695, resumed 2026-08-17 08:50.

~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260817-085040-286753-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log replays both prompts before the session/load result:

  line 1  user_message_chunk  "commit and sync, those skills addition have been performed in claude/71c82ed5-9db8-44a3-9e64-e610a51b6cea"
  line 24 user_message_chunk  "sorry redo it i miscliked"
  line 37 session result for fa72dc03-6c22-41c8-be19-9274bea75695

Neither line appeared in the resumed chat buffer. The text is intact in ~/.claude/projects/-home-lotso-dotfiles-nvim--config-nvim/fa72dc03-....jsonl, so nothing is lost upstream; only the client drops it.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua handle_notification dispatches update types at lines 184-209: agent_message_chunk, tool_call, tool_call_update, config_option_update, usage_update. user_message_chunk matches nothing and falls through silently.

claude-agent-acp is launched with --replay-user-messages, so the replay is expected behavior of the agent, not a quirk.

## Why it was not caught

tests/ui/chat_spec.lua "renders replayed assistant chunks before a new prompt" covers the resume path but only asserts the agent side, so the missing half of the conversation is invisible to it.

## Fix direction

Handle user_message_chunk and render it as a user prompt line in the transcript.

Check whether the chunk arrives outside replay before deciding where to render. Evidence so far: across every stored adapter log, user_message_chunk appears only in logs that include a session/load replay - claude, codex and the deepseek adapter all behave this way, and live turns in the same logs never emit it. If an agent does echo the prompt during a live turn, the chat would double-render it, because the chat writes the submitted prompt into the buffer itself.

## Acceptance

- A resumed session shows the user prompts interleaved with the agent replies in their original order.
- Submitting a prompt in a live turn still renders it exactly once.
- A chat_spec case asserts a replayed user chunk reaches the buffer.

## Not covered

Whether replayed prompts should be visually distinguished from newly typed ones, and whether replayed tool calls should be folded, are UX questions left open.
close_reason: Resumed user prompts now render in original order before replayed assistant replies; red-green UI regression coverage and full suite pass.

title: Refactor Chat UI around explicit state owners
description:
## Problem Statement

Chat combines Session coordination, streaming buffer geometry, Staged context, permission presentation, status displays and Run recovery in one module. At the 2026-09-11 exploration baseline it held 5,036 of 10,005 UI lines and appeared in 60 of the last 100 UI commits. Its growing shared mutable state makes independent changes and lifecycle review expensive.

## Solution

Keep Chat as the coordinator for attached Sessions and explicit UI owners. Extract six complete, consumed slices: status presentation; permission decisions; buffer rendering and coordinates; staged drafts; Park/resume integration; Handoff review. Each slice leaves the application working and carries its existing behavior coverage.

## User Stories

1. As a maintainer, I can change status presentation without understanding permission or Run recovery state.
2. As an operator, I retain chronological streaming, editable drafts, folds, navigation and replay while implementation boundaries change.
3. As an operator, overlapping permission requests, cancellation and Session close preserve their established behavior.
4. As a maintainer, I can identify which owner creates and disposes every buffer, listener, picker slot, timer and pending operation.
5. As an operator, Handoff and cold Park/resume keep their existing context, recovery and authority contracts.

## Implementation Decisions

- Each component owns specific state or consumes explicit snapshots. Extracted modules must not accept the entire mutable Chat object or introduce a generic UI framework.
- Chat retains Session/view membership, command coordination and the event ingress boundary: record transcript data and capture completion state before scheduled editor work. Preserve replay buffering and stale-view/disposal checks.
- One buffer owner manages prompt coordinates, extmarks, streaming positions and fold ranges. Draft content is a distinct responsibility.
- One decision owner spans all attached Sessions. Answered authority and a provider-owned picker awaiting its callback remain distinct states.
- Reuse Transcript, Gates, Diff, Limits and the existing workflow clients/controllers. Keep capability, policy and validation semantics at their existing domain boundaries.
- Status output supplies the buffer renderer; draft uses the buffer boundary; Handoff uses draft assembly and accepted-submission rendering. These are actual prerequisites. Decisions and Park/resume need no artificial ordering dependency.
- Suggested execution order is status, decisions, buffer, draft, Park/resume, Handoff. Paths and private API names may be adjusted to the smallest cohesive implementation.
- No vocabulary, configuration, Session/Agent/Model meaning, or intentional public behavior change is required. No grill-me is needed for the agreed structural work.

## Testing Decisions

- The exploration baseline passed all 311 UI cases. Re-establish focused characterization coverage before each implementation slice; this is not a substitute for that slice's gates.
- Move related cases alongside their extracted owner while retaining Chat integration coverage. Preserve observable assertions, recorded event ordering, async scheduling, cancellation, replay, disposal and error paths.
- Run focused checks during work and the complete affected Lua suite and required format/static/generated-document gates before handoff, per repository testing policy.
- A pure refactor does not require an artificial failing test. Any behavioral defect discovered during implementation needs its own recorded evidence and regression.
- Regenerate the API appendix when exported LuaCATS changes; no new dependencies or numeric file-size target.

## Out of Scope

Fixing the staged skill-marker defect (louiselm-8i35), redesigning context-removal UX, changing upstream/policy auto-approval, protocol rewrites, replacing incremental streaming with whole-transcript rerenders, broad command-framework work, and feature removal.

Provenance lookup/render separation is a separate lower-priority follow-up. Command registration and Attention are later candidates only where a concrete responsibility split justifies the work; their size alone does not make them required deliverables.

## Further Notes

Prior lessons: louiselm-4wx (overlapping permission requests), louiselm-wnu (competing command pickers), louiselm-8qk (fast-event UI access), and louiselm-lua-ponytail-simplifications-662a (already-completed command/fold simplifications and preserved recovery distinctions).

The user authorized turning the explored plan into Beads in codex/01a09041-dba2-7351-8a4b-1c0a6da8296b. This epic authorizes planning records; no implementation was performed or claimed during filing. Aggregate completion follows the child tasks; do not add reciprocal blocking edges from this epic to its parent-linked children.
acceptance_criteria: All six child extractions are consumed by the application and satisfy their behavior/lifecycle gates. Chat coordinates explicit owners without retaining their internal mutable bookkeeping. Existing regression contracts and generated API documentation remain current; linked behavior bugs are not closed by mechanical refactoring.

Separate behavior follow-ups: rqqp implementation tested but live acceptance pending; wtee records pre-existing ignored admission failure, deferred. Neither is silently closed by this structural epic.

title: Give Chat permission decisions one lifecycle owner
description:
## Goal

Make permission presentation and cancellation reviewable independently of Chat rendering and Session navigation.

## Scope

Extract the decision queue and responder/picker lifecycle from lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua into an explicit Chat-owned component, suggested chat/decisions.lua. Own the pending queue, active decision, provider-owned picker awaiting its callback, request-details window and the decision-related Diff instance/lifecycle.

Route permission_requested, permission_cancelled, Session close and Chat disposal through a small API. Supply narrow callbacks/data for view liveness, transcript error presentation and Attention updates; never pass the whole mutable Chat object. Retain other raw-tool inspectors with their current owner.

Consume existing Gates and Diff behavior. Permission policy and upstream Agent settings, including YOLO/auto-approval, remain supported. Preserve the distinction between retired authority and a selector whose provider callback has not yet returned. Do not introduce a shared queue for every UI picker.

## Testing

Preserve the Chat and Diff cases for overlapping requests across Sessions, request-details return/cancellation, picker exceptions, exact selected options, remembered decisions, nested Diff lifetimes, Session-close confirmation/survivor selection, queued fast events and callbacks after disposal. Exercise exactly-once responses and ensure a late callback cannot release another decision's slot or grant authority.

Start from passing characterization coverage; run focused Chat/Diff/command tests and the complete required Lua gates. Move relevant cases without deleting their integration assertions.

## Notes

Current entry points: permission_prompt, prompt_permission, decision_responder, open_decision, pump_decisions, cancel_decisions, queue_decision and close_view. The component must be explicitly constructed and disposed.

Read prior lessons louiselm-4wx and louiselm-wnu. Ordinary command pickers retain their current refusal behavior; close/cancel remain reachable and nested decision-owned pickers remain usable. No dependency on status or buffer extraction is required: adapt the current transcript writer through a narrow callback.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Decision queue, active authority and outstanding selector state have one explicit owner across attached Sessions.
2. Chat event, close and dispose paths use that owner's API and do not modify its private fields.
3. Cancellation, details, Diff review, late callbacks and competing pickers preserve established behavior; responses remain at most once.
4. Policy/auto-approval behavior is unchanged and focused plus full Lua gates pass.

title: Unify Chat buffer rendering and coordinate ownership
description:
## Goal

Keep every position affected by streaming, editing, undo, folding or replay under one buffer owner.

## Scope

Extract the incremental rendering, prompt-coordinate and fold/navigation responsibilities from lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua into chat/buffer.lua or the smallest equivalent cohesive module. Consume the completed status-presentation result for headers.

Own buffer creation/deletion and buffer-local subscriptions/keymaps, prompt extmarks, transcript/response tails, tool row indexes, context/tool/reasoning fold ranges and per-window application state, submitted prompt markers and transcript navigation. Keep context/tool incremental application shared while retaining reasoning-fold recovery/rescan behavior.

Route buffer writes from live events, accepted prompts, replay, diagnostics and usage rows through this owner. It may remain substantial in size when cohesive. Chat retains Session/view membership, transport subscription coordination, permission/Attention/workflow decisions and replay/history ordering. Staged semantic context remains caller-owned until the draft extraction.

Preserve the existing event-ingress boundary: Transcript recording and immutable turn-completion snapshot happen before scheduled UI work. A renderer consumes scheduled work; it does not add an independent event queue or rebuild the whole transcript on each chunk.

## Testing

Port relevant tests/ui/chat_spec.lua assertions for multiline chunks, interleaved tool/reasoning/prose, repeated tool IDs, tool completion before/after turn_done with exact echo suppression, undo-shifted prompt extmarks, fold recovery, hidden views and navigation origins. Retain public Chat integration for replay/history buffering, completion snapshots, queued-prompt release and fast events after disposal.

Use real headless buffers and production callback context where the scheduling boundary is under test. Run focused tests, full Lua suite and required static/format/generated-doc gates.

## Notes

Key current functions: mark_prompt/current_prompt_line, reconcile_prompt_boundary, replace_submitted_prompt, insert_transcript, handle_event, navigation_targets/navigate_transcript and attach_session. This slice consumes the status output shape, which is its prerequisite. It must not redefine Session history or replace Transcript's immutable data record.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Prompt markers, streaming positions, tool indexes, fold ranges and buffer lifecycle are owned and mutated through one coherent API.
2. Chat orchestrates rendered operations without directly maintaining those positions.
3. Streaming chronology, undo, replay, exact completion echo suppression, folds and navigation remain covered through observable behavior.
4. Main-loop scheduling, immutable completion snapshots and disposal behavior are preserved; all required Lua gates pass.

title: Separate staged Chat drafts from buffer geometry
description:
## Goal

Make staged prompt content and its consumption independent of rendering coordinates.

## Scope

Extract ownership of queued contexts, pending native skill, hidden first-prompt catalog, context presentation metadata and the one queued next-turn prompt from lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua into chat/draft.lua or an equivalent narrow component.

Build ACP prompt content from explicit current Session inputs and resolved skill content. Keep filesystem reads, Session prompt dispatch and operator notification at their appropriate existing I/O boundaries; do not hide I/O inside pure content transformations. Use the completed buffer API for reading/editing the visible draft, queued indicators and accepted-submission rendering; draft state must not write extmarks or stream positions.

Wire ordinary submit, busy-turn queuing, queue release, context/skill staging and staged_context reporting to this owner. Preserve late native-command resolution, slash-command passthrough, first-prompt context rules, exact context order and failed-submission retention. Expose only operations consumed in this change; no speculative removal API or generic prompt framework.

## Testing

Preserve existing Chat cases for native/inject/off skills, command-cache changes before release, hidden catalogs, embedded context, multiline prompt submission, local failures, queued prompt editing and per-Session context isolation. Preserve error/disposal cancellation and the established acceptance boundary for clearing staged content.

Use real buffer edits and Chat:submit() with omitted text when exercising the editor-to-draft boundary. Do not encode louiselm-8i35's marker-deletion defect as intended behavior. If its fix lands first, carry its regression through this refactor.

Start with characterization coverage and run focused tests and the complete required Lua gates. Any behavior fix needs its own red-green evidence.

## Notes

Current entry points: render_chip/queue_context/queue_native_skill/queue_injected_skill, build_context_content/build_content, submit_prompt, queue_prompt/release_queued_prompt, Chat:submit and Chat:staged_context.

The buffer owner is a real prerequisite so semantic state does not share coordinate ownership. louiselm-8i35 remains a separately tracked behavioral defect and is related, not a completion prerequisite; this refactor must not silently close it or redesign context-removal UX.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Staged context, pending skill, catalog and queued prompt have a clear owner separate from buffer coordinates.
2. Production stage/submit/queue/release paths consume its narrow API; pure assembly consumes explicit resolved inputs.
3. Prompt content/order, slash handling, native resolution timing, failure retention and one-time consumption preserve established contracts.

title: Write the political statement document
description:
Write the political statement document.

The licence deliberately carries no politics — that was the whole point of choosing MIT for reach. Which means this document carries all of it. Without it the position is invisible.

## What it should say

- Why the licence is permissive: reach is the mechanism. A harness's effect comes from being everywhere and shaping how human-agent work happens — local-first, legible, owned by the operator. Every install is a small decommodification of the means of producing software.
- What is retained and why: trademark, patents, and the right to relicense. Not granted away, and named as deliberate.
- What is refused: the named class, enforced through the trademark policy.
- The community position: AI removed the need to depend on other people for code, which is what used to create open-source community. The scarce contribution now is workflows, evidence, and judgment — which is what `CONTRIBUTING.md` already asks for. Community here forms around decisions, not patches.
- Honest about the limit: no licence ends anything. What a licence decides is who captures the surplus, and whether the tool spreads. Claiming more would be flattery.

## Acceptance criteria

- Document exists, linked from README.
- Nothing in it reads as a licence term or a condition of use. It is a statement, not an obligation — that separation is the point.
- The reasoning is legible to someone who did not sit through the original session.

title: QA round: cold Park ordering
description:
# Manual QA review — cold-Park ordering

**Build under test:** `2d9dacd..HEAD` (`dcf87d0 fix(park): show newest Parks first`; current HEAD `f974301`).

## Scope

Only `dcf87d0` needs a new manual case. The other behavior change in this range,
`31bd9d7`, changed the Grok empty-options diagnostic and was already accepted
live in `grok/01a0568f-0b1b-72b1-a84e-64a3abdfc5ff`. Beads-only commits are not
manual-test cases.

## Setup

Build the capture service from the source checkout, update the installed
LouiseLM plugin if it is a separate clone, then restart Neovim:

```bash
cargo install --path capture-service --locked --force
git -C /home/lotso/code/louiselm rev-parse HEAD
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim rev-parse HEAD
command -v louiselm-capture
louiselm-capture run list | jq 'if length == 0 then "no Parks" else .[0] | has("parked_at_ms") end'
```

Both plugin and capture-service must contain the current source. The final
command must print `true` for any existing Park; if it prints `false`, the shell
is still running an old capture binary and the case has not started. Do not run
this case from an unnamed buffer: open a named project file before starting the
chat.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Newest cold Park appears first | **passed** — screenshot/service order agree; picker dismissed cleanly |

### Setup miss

The first attempt used four successfully created Parks, but
`louiselm-capture run list` returned summaries without `parked_at_ms`. This is
the pre-fix capture binary, not a product result: the current LouiseLM service
parser intentionally rejects that older JSON as malformed. No finding is filed.

**Retest passed (2026-08-31).** Screenshot
`~/Pictures/scrot/20260831_0910_1920x1200_1788160225.png` shows the picker order
`01a056a2`, `01a056a1`, `01a056a0`, then `01a0560a`. The service output confirms
the corresponding `parked_at_ms` values descend: `1788159935111`,
`1788159926884`, `1788159806994`, `1788149950567`. The visible order therefore
matches the authoritative timestamps, not UUID order.

The tester pressed `Esc`; the picker closed and focus returned normally. No
Park was resumed by dismissal.

## Case 1 — newest cold Park appears first

Exercises `dcf87d0`, `capture-service/src/runs.rs:797-845`, and the
`LouiselmResumePark` picker path in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Create at least three cold Parks in order, with a pause of a few seconds between
them so their timestamps differ:

1. Start a fresh LouiseLM session.
2. Send a trivial prompt such as `Reply with only: ok` and wait for completion.
3. Run `:LouiselmPark` and confirm the session is parked.
4. Repeat steps 1–3 two more times, waiting a few seconds between Parks.
5. Run `:LouiselmResumePark`.

Expect: the picker’s first row is the Park created most recently, regardless of
the Run UUID. The remaining rows descend by Park time. Dismiss the picker with
`Esc` without resuming anything.

Failure signature: rows appear in UUID order, the oldest Park is first, the
order changes between repeated openings, or dismissing the picker resumes a
Run.

Tie check: if two Parks have the same millisecond timestamp in the evidence,
the lower Run UUID must appear first. This is a deterministic tie-breaker, not a
recency claim.

## Evidence

Capture the exact picker order and the service’s authoritative timestamps. Run:

```bash
louiselm-capture run list | jq -c '.[] | {id, parked_at_ms, park_expires_at_ms}'
```

The JSON output proves the service order and timestamps. The visible picker
proves the UI presents that order; the command cannot prove picker focus or
dismissal behavior.

## Cleanup

Resume or dispose the temporary Parks after testing. Leave no intentionally
created cold Parks behind.

## Reporting back

Reply with `case 1`, what the first three rows showed, whether `Esc` dismissed
the picker, and the output of the evidence command. Include the current Neovim
and capture-service commit/binary versions if setup was unusual.

## Findings this round

None. The first attempt was a QA setup miss caused by an old
`louiselm-capture` binary; after `cargo install --path capture-service --locked
--force`, the intended case passed.
close_reason: QA passed: newest cold Park appeared first by parked_at_ms, UUID tie order remained deterministic, and Esc dismissed without resuming. Initial malformed-data attempt was a stale capture binary setup miss; no product finding.

title: Grill-me needed: authenticate Run lifecycle for broker skill requests
description:

4. Install the newer release; prove current changes atomically and the older
   directory remains. Older-bundle installation must refuse with current intact.

- Host original artifacts `/home/lotso/.cache/louiselm-lm70.NQCeob` and fixed

  `/var/lib/louiselm-lm70-fix-91qF9s`; provenance stays untrusted/development.

  directories under `/usr/local/lib/louiselm/releases`.

recovery enrollment or production-store promotion. F3 required runtime
fix816563d and fresh signatures; original failures remain preserved evidence.
Only this scratch checklist is removed after its exact contents are archived
in the qa-round bead. No acceptance artifact, backup or key is deleted.

## Final result and remaining scope

lm70 genuine release acceptance passed: distinct credentials, real strict Release
signatures, root-owned installed identity/status, upgrade, retained releases,
downgrade refusal, component tamper refusal, restoration and clean shutdown.
F1–F3 are resolved, each with maintainer acceptance and preserved evidence.
Lessons live in the findings below and their issue comments; no new standing
rule or unresolved design question emerged from the final two cases.

This release-only acceptance does not establish overall Verified posture or
production recovery readiness. Installed launcher authority remains
`louiselm-d6fv.4.9`; actual Android passkey and paper-phrase recovery acceptance
remains `louiselm-d6fv.11.5`. The Verified cutover question `louiselm-ucj1` is
separate. No follow-on work was claimed or started.

## Findings

**F1 — resident-key identity collision** (`louiselm-cjy6`, recipe corrected in `fad6e85`;
live acceptance passed 2026-09-07: corrected Release enrollment and both signing
roles proved possession). My original key-generation recipe supplied distinct
comments/paths but omitted distinct resident user IDs. Primary creation
succeeded; Release requested token overwrite. Directed maintainer to decline
and preserve Primary; corrected Release adds `-O user=louiselm-release`.
Official OpenSSH manual confirms that option supports multiple resident keys
for one application: https://man.openbsd.org/ssh-keygen.1#FIDO_AUTHENTICATOR .
Software-key tests never exercised two actual resident enrollments; the
bootstrap recipe regression deliberately skips hardware key generation.
Original Primary proves possession (case 2a); new Release signed the first bundle
with strict policy and recorded approval (case 2b).
Public-file fingerprints alone do not prove that token credentials survived.

**F2 — Primary proof routed through refusing desktop SSH agent**
(`louiselm-qbb5`, corrected retry passed live acceptance 2026-09-07). Maintainer observed
`agent refused operation` without a token PIN prompt. The inherited socket
`/run/user/1000/gcr/ssh` advertises the original Primary; the failed first attempt
created no signature. OpenSSH selects a matching agent key even with `-f` naming the local
handle. Case 2a now unsets `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` for that command only. The desktop
agent's internal refusal cause remains unproven. Existing release signing
already clears its environment (`skills-core/src/launcher_install.rs:435`), so
this corrects the diagnostic recipe only; no runtime change or rebuild.
Evidence: https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_10_0_P2/ssh-keygen.c#L2627 .
The corrected retry produced the pinned valid signature in case 2a. Software
fixtures do not exercise the maintainer's desktop SSH agent. Recipe-only
correction lives here until the round is archived; tracking evidence is in qbb5.

**F3 — installed current symlink misclassified as writable content**
(`louiselm-se9g`, P1 product bug; fixed816563d, live acceptance passed2026-09-07).
Original `install::ownership_of`
(`skills-core/src/install.rs:357`) tests mode022 on every entry. `walk` uses
`DirEntry::metadata`, which reports the link itself; the legitimate Linux
`current` symlink's mode0777 therefore rejects an otherwise root-owned protected
installation. Both status and running identity share that ownership check.
Official semantics: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fs/struct.DirEntry.html#method.metadata
and https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/symlink.7.html .

Why green tests missed it: `tests/release.rs:453` expects a non-root install to
be untrusted via `prefix_not_root_owned`, never asserting the independent
world-writability field. The earlier denial masks this false positive; the suite
had no positive real root-owned installed-identity case. Fix exempts only the
validated current link, preserving real owner/mode/target refusals. Standard Rust
gates, frozen release-mode tests, both initial-namespace root regressions and
genuine newly signed installed identity/status now pass. No permission workaround.

title: Skill instruction paths advertised by runtime are unavailable
description:
## Evidence

- /home/lotso/dotfiles/agentskills/.config/agentskills/generated/.system/bvr/SKILL.md
- /home/lotso/dotfiles/agentskills/.config/agentskills/generated/.system/to-beads-bug/SKILL.md

Each path returned: No such file or directory.

The assistant therefore could not read the required skill instructions and had to fall back to direct repository commands. The skill catalog advertises these paths as available, so the runtime's skill metadata and filesystem installation are inconsistent.

## Impact

Skill-triggered tasks cannot reliably load their instructions. This weakens required workflow compliance and may cause incorrect fallbacks.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every advertised filesystem-backed skill locator resolves to its SKILL.md, or the catalog omits unavailable skills.
- At minimum, the bvr, br, and to-beads-bug locators used in this session resolve successfully.
- A fresh session can read a selected skill before taking task actions.

title: Bind LouiseLM and maintained adapters against reading Provider credentials
description:
## Goal

Write the confirmed rule into `AGENTS.md` so it binds every future session,
including ones that rediscover the OpenCode quota endpoint and treat it as a
gift.

## Why AGENTS.md and not a reference

The failure mode is concrete and near-certain. The undocumented endpoint
`GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage` was found from a standing start in
under thirty minutes, and it returns exactly the data a filed issue asked for.
Any competent session will find it and wire it up as an obvious win. Only the
always-loaded contract stops that before review.

## Exact change

Add to the `## Security` list in `AGENTS.md`:

```
- Never read another tool's credential store or call a Provider API. Account
  limits reach LouiseLM only when an Agent advertises them over ACP; absence
  is a correct answer, not a gap to fill (louiselm-opencode-quota-runtime-ownership-blz13).
```

The rule binds this plugin **and any ACP adapter the maintainer maintains**.
State that scope in the line; a rule that binds only `lua/` loses the
blast-radius half of the decision.

## Acceptance

1. The line is present in the `## Security` section.
2. `./scripts/check-agent-instructions` passes. The rule measured 246 bytes
   against 374 bytes of headroom; if the file has grown since, trim elsewhere
   rather than dropping the rule.
3. The scope covers maintained adapters explicitly, not just the plugin.

## Verified free today

No existing adapter violates it: the codex-acp patch uses Codex's own
`account/rateLimits/read`, the claude-agent-acp patch uses the SDK, and
`copilot-acp` calls `client.rpc.account.getQuota({})`. None reads a credential
file. This writes down a property the adapters already have.

## Context

Decision: louiselm-opencode-quota-runtime-ownership-blz13.
Vocabulary: louiselm-account-limits-9n9st.
close_reason: consumer:AGENTS.md:176 Always-loaded Account limits credential rule covers plugin and maintained ACP adapters; instruction-size and whitespace checks pass.

Scoped to entitlement per louiselm-account-limits-9n9st; unsupported is correct. Instruction gate passes (11918/12000 bytes); git diff --check passes.
