title: Hand off a live session to another provider with a reviewed transcript
description:
## Problem Statement

Comparing two providers on the same problem currently means re-typing the
problem. `:LouiselmNewSession` already picks an agent and seeds initial contexts,
the skill catalog, and the AGENTS.md instructions context
(`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2191-2212`), but it starts the conversation from
zero. When a session is going in circles and the question is "would Codex do
better with this", the friction of restating everything is exactly what stops
the comparison happening.

## Solution

A handoff: pick another provider, open a new session on it, render the current
session's transcript into a buffer the user edits, and send the edited result as
the first prompt. The original session stays attached and switchable, which the
chat UI already supports.

## User Stories

1. As the maintainer, I want to move a stuck conversation to another provider
   without restating the problem, so comparing providers costs a keystroke rather
   than a retype.
2. As the maintainer, I want to see and cut down what is sent before it is sent,
   so I control both what a second vendor receives and how much of a wrong frame
   the new provider inherits.
3. As the maintainer, I want the original session to stay open, so I can compare
   the two answers and go back.

## Implementation Decisions

Settled in a grill-me session on 2026-08-21 (full reasoning on
louiselm-provider-switch-ypqs):

- The live session cannot survive the switch. Each provider is a separately
  configured agent definition with its own process, connection, and session ids;
  `Api:load_session` is same-agent only and gated on
  `agentCapabilities.loadSession` (`lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:252`).
- The transcript can only arrive as **content in a prompt**. ACP offers no way to
  seed a fabricated history into another agent: `session/prompt` with content
  blocks is the sole input channel (`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:664-686`).
  "Replay as conversation history" was not rejected on taste; it is not
  expressible.
- The review step is **not optional**, for two independent reasons. A transcript
  carries file contents, full command output, and tool results, so forwarding it
  is a publication event to a second vendor that the user asked for only
  implicitly -- the permission model is the existing precedent for gating that.
  Separately, for comparison the whole transcript is often the wrong payload: if
  the first provider went in circles, replaying those turns hands the second
  provider the same wrong frame and contaminates the experiment. The edit step is
  where that gets cut back.
- Remembered permissions do not cross. They are already agent-scoped by
  construction -- `rule.agent ~= context.agent` fails the match
  (`lua/louiselm/permission/store.lua:391`) -- so this needs no new work, only a
  test proving it.
- The command name must not contain "model". That word already cost one wrong
  implementation (louiselm-model-change-cl59, reverted in db39f96); see
  louiselm-slo.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A command hands the current session off to a chosen other configured provider,
   opening a new session on it.
2. The current session's transcript is rendered into an editable buffer before
   anything is sent, and nothing reaches the new provider until the user submits.
3. Editing that buffer down changes what is sent; the transcript is a starting
   point, not a fixed payload.
4. Abandoning the buffer sends nothing and leaves both sessions untouched.
5. The original session remains attached and reachable via the existing session
   switcher.
6. The new session receives the initial contexts, skill catalog, and instructions
   context that `new_session` already seeds, with the new provider's own
   `skills_policy` respected rather than the old session's.
7. Remembered permissions from the source provider do not apply to the target,
   proven by test.
8. No command, option, or user-facing string introduced by this feature uses the
   word "model" for what is a provider.

## Testing Notes

Headless coverage for: the buffer appearing before any prompt is sent, abandoning
it sending nothing, an edited payload being what arrives, both sessions being
live afterwards, and permission isolation across the two agents. The mock ACP
agent covers the two-provider case without real binaries. Async work must
exercise the production callback context per AGENTS.md section 5.

## Out of Scope

- Capability-based routing, which is a separate mechanism
  (louiselm-capability-routing-m3sc).
- Automatic or policy-driven switching. This is manual and human-initiated.
- Any attempt to migrate ACP session state, which the protocol does not support.
- Diffing or evaluating the two providers' answers.
close_reason: Both children delivered the full feature: louiselm-handoff-buffer-gk9i rendered the editable transcript review buffer; louiselm-handoff-command-d15l wired :LouiselmHandOff (agent picker excluding current, session creation via the existing new_session path, source stays attached, distinct errors, permission isolation, README). All 8 acceptance criteria on this issue are satisfied.

title: Grill-me needed: what should switching provider mid-session do to the live session
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing -- it wants full attention.**

## The question

The maintainer wants to switch *provider* mid-flight: sitting in a live Claude
session and moving to Codex, without losing the thread of work. What should
that actually do to the session they are in?

This is a live want, stated on 2026-08-21, not a hypothetical. What is
undecided is the semantics, not the desire.

## Why it is not a small command

A model change is one `session/set_config_option` call against a live ACP
session: the agent stays, the connection stays, the session id stays, and the
only recorded consequence is that context-usage telemetry goes stale
(`Session:set_config_option` in `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua`).

A provider change shares none of that. Each provider is a separately
configured agent definition with its own process, its own ACP connection, and
its own session ids. The current session cannot survive the switch. So the
question is not "how do we add a picker" but "what, if anything, crosses the
boundary".

## Threads worth pulling

- What carries across: nothing (clean new session), the rendered transcript,
  the structured transcript replayed as context, queued context items,
  pending permission decisions, the session title, or some subset. Each has a
  different price and a different failure mode when the new provider rejects
  or truncates it.
- Whether the old session is disposed, kept attached, or kept as a
  read-only buffer the user can switch back to. `:LouiselmNewSession` already
  runs sessions side by side; is provider switch just "new session, seeded"
  plus a focus change, or is it genuinely a different operation?
- Whether a replayed transcript should be presented to the new provider as
  conversation history or as a single context injection, and whether the user
  has to see and approve what gets replayed. Sending prior tool output to a
  second vendor is a disclosure decision, not only a fidelity decision.
- Whether permissions remembered for the old provider apply to the new one.
  They almost certainly must not, but the rule should be explicit.
- How this interacts with the logical-thread idea in the louiselm-qbr epic,
  which already asserts that workflow threads outlive replaceable ACP
  sessions. Provider switch may be the first concrete instance of that, in
  which case the grill should decide whether it is built on that abstraction
  or ships before it.
- Naming: this is the term that just cost a wrong implementation
  (louiselm-model-change-cl59, reverted in db39f96). Whatever the command ends
  up called, "model" must not appear in it. See louiselm-slo.

## Out of scope for the grill

Re-deriving the above. React to it. Also out of scope: changing how a single
agent advertises or applies its own model options, which already works through
`:LouiselmSessionOptions`.
close_reason: grill complete; decisions recorded, routed to louiselm-capability-routing-m3sc and louiselm-provider-handoff-3e2p

comments.author: claude/cca6e4b5-ff23-495e-a84c-6a69b4c18c99
comments.text:
Grill complete, 2026-08-21. Ten questions, shared understanding reached, routed to beads.

DECISIONS

Q1 Motivation: comparison primary ('this one is stuck, would the other do better'), continuation second. The triggering incident was neither -- it was capability: a Claude session could not generate images for louiselm-qbr.1.10 and recorded the fact as prose.
Q2 Two mechanisms, not one. Comparison needs a live session and a human; capability routing needs a record that outlives every session and works with no human present. They fail in opposite directions.
Q3 Scope is the general known-gap primitive, not a capability-only fix. Two independent instances existed already (this one, and the QA-process-question gap documented in docs/example-workflow.md).
Q4 A standing requirement is a label; a genuine blocker is a 'blocks' dependency. Test: does something have to change before anyone can do this? Modelling capability as 'blocks' would hide the work from the agent that could do it.
Q5 Labels name the capability, not the agent. Agent names are user-chosen config keys; .beads is committed and cross-adapter.
Q6 Capability truth is declared in config, not discovered at runtime. Routing must work before a session exists.
Q7 The emission obligation goes in AGENTS.md, not only a skill. AGENTS.md is the only artifact every adapter reads -- demonstrated during this grill, where the acting session had no grill-me skill and read SKILL.md off disk.
Q8 One emission rule with two destinations, not two rules. Both destinations already existed and had been used (louiselm-iyy proves the sideways-finding route works); the missing piece in both cases was identical -- no trigger.
Q9 Ship on 'br ready' and amend the AGENTS.md scheduler preference with an expiring carve-out. Do not block on upstream beads.
Q10 The handoff carries the transcript as a reviewed prompt injection. ACP offers no other channel: session/load is same-agent only, session/prompt is the sole input. Review is mandatory -- it is both the disclosure gate to a second vendor and the way a wrong frame gets cut before contaminating the comparison.

REJECTED

- A provider switch that carries nothing: fails the comparison motivation, and is already :LouiselmNewSession.
- Replaying the transcript as structured conversation history: not expressible in ACP.
- Automatic transcript injection: publication to a second vendor the user requested only implicitly.
- 'agent:codex' style labels: bind committed beads to one machine's config keys.
- Runtime capability discovery: requires spawning the agent to learn it cannot help, which is the failure being fixed.
- Blocking the design on upstream beads changes: swarm selection is not live, so it buys an option that cannot be exercised.

PRODUCED

louiselm-capability-routing-m3sc (feature) with louiselm-emission-rule-yc4b and louiselm-agent-capabilities-pk5z.
louiselm-provider-handoff-3e2p (feature) with louiselm-handoff-buffer-gk9i and louiselm-handoff-command-d15l.
louiselm-scheduler-labels-xw1i (bug, out-of-repo) filed mid-grill from live evidence.
louiselm-slo updated with the needs-capability namespace as a second vocabulary entry.
louiselm-qbr.1.10 labelled needs-capability:image-generation, verified selectable by 'br ready --label-any' and still present in plain 'br ready'.

title: ACP proxy logs are evicted by a 100MB size cap, not age; workspace is at 98.8MB now
description:
ACP proxy logs are evicted by a 100 MB aggregate size cap, not by age. Two long Sessions can
consume the entire budget and evict every other Session's log, including evidence a filed bug
cites by line number.

The workspace sits at **98.8 MB of the 100 MB cap right now**, so every write is evicting
something.

## Root cause

`~/code/acp-llm-adapter/src/logsink.rs`:

- `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES = 100 * 1024 * 1024` — aggregate across `connections/` **and**
  `sessions/`, overridable with `ACP_LOG_MAX_BYTES`.
- `DEFAULT_MAX_AGE = 30 days`, overridable with `ACP_LOG_MAX_AGE_DAYS`. Logs here span ~10
  days, so the age bound never fires. Size is the only active bound.
- `prune()` (logsink.rs:502) runs on **every write**: it sorts by mtime and removes
  oldest-first until the total is under the cap. It deletes the file and leaves the directory,
  which is why empty session directories remain.

## Evidence

Measured 2026-09-01 in `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/`:

- Total 98.8 MB — `sessions/` 90 MB, `connections/` 11 MB. At the cap.
- Two Sessions hold 66 MB of it: `01a0561f-…` at 35 MB and `01a057e5-…` at 31 MB.
- 347 session directories, 312 with no `log.jsonl`.
- Of 95 Sessions that provably did work (they appear as Beads actors, assignees, or comment
  authors), **only 8 still have a log**; 83 have an empty directory and 4 have no directory.
- Retained logs begin `2026-08-31 06:41` — that is simply where the surviving 100 MB starts,
  not a time boundary.
- No external deleter exists: no cron, no user timers, no `tmpfiles.d` rule touching
  `~/.local/state`.

A separate and benign population explains most empty directories: 208 of the 312 are session
ids that only ever appeared in a `session/list` result, i.e. enumerated by the resume picker
and never used. Those never had traffic to log.

The `louiselm-gf9a` loss is the size cap, confirmed: its description cites lines 1527-1623 of
`sessions/ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney/log.jsonl` on 2026-08-30, so the file existed with
1600+ lines. Its directory mtime is 2026-08-31 09:01, the moment the file was evicted.

## Contributing factor

The louiselm agent definitions set `env = { ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED = "1" }`
(`~/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua:34,52`). Unredacted logs carry
full prompts, messages, and tool arguments, which is the point — but it multiplies log volume
and shortens the retention window proportionally. The cap was presumably sized for redacted
logs.

## Immediate mitigation

`ACP_LOG_MAX_BYTES` goes in the same per-agent `env` table that already sets
`ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED`. Raising it to e.g. 2 GB restores roughly 20x the history at current
volume. Verify with `du -sb ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy` staying below the new bound.

## Threads worth pulling

- What is the right cap for unredacted logging, and should louiselm's agent definitions set it
  rather than relying on an adapter default sized for redacted logs?
- Should eviction be per-Session rather than global? Two runaway Sessions currently evict
  everyone else's evidence, which is the opposite of what a debugging log should prioritise.
- Should a Session whose log a Beads issue cites be exempt from eviction? That is the
  Forensics question: Forensics is defined as indexing primary evidence *in place*
  (louiselm-cvv3), and an index into an evictable file is not durable. Either Forensics copies
  the frames it depends on, or its definition overstates what it guarantees.
- Should filing a bug that cites a proxy log inline the frames it relies on at file time? That
  is the narrowest fix and needs no retention change.
- AGENTS.md section 5 requires deriving fixtures from captured frames and keeping
  live-reproducible defects open for maintainer acceptance. Acceptance is asynchronous and the
  evidence is evictable, so the rules compose into a trap regardless of the cap's value.

Root cause was the aggregate size cap in logsink.rs, not age; retention now has an explicit off switch instead of a sentinel-large number. title: Proxy logs now grow unbounded at ~51MB/day against a 94%-full disk
description:
ACP proxy log retention is now unlimited (louiselm-proxy-log-evidence-expiry-xxfu), which is
the intended setting: the logs are primary evidence for filed defects and must not be evicted.
The consequence is unbounded growth on a disk that is already nearly full.

Measured 2026-09-01:

- ~51 MB/day of proxy logs (102.8 MB across the two days currently on disk)
- ~18.3 GB/year at that rate, unbounded
- `/` is 910G with **54G free (94% used)**

That is roughly a third of the remaining free space per year, from one subsystem. Not urgent,
and not a reason to re-enable eviction — deletion is explicitly rejected, since losing the
evidence is what this whole thread was about.

The volume is driven by `ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED=1`, which is also deliberate: redacted logs cannot
answer the questions these logs exist to answer.

## Options that delete nothing

- Compress logs at rest. JSONL frames compress hard, plausibly 10-20x. A closed Session's
  `log.jsonl` is append-only and never rewritten, so it is a natural compression target once
  its Session ends. Needs the readers (`grep`, the Forensics path, the fixture-derivation
  workflow in AGENTS.md section 5) to handle compressed input, or a transparent decompress
  helper.
- Move the state root to a larger or dedicated volume, leaving retention untouched.
- Archive Sessions older than N days to a separate location that is not on the hot disk, still
  without deleting.

## Not options

Re-enabling the size or age bound in any form. The bound is what destroyed the evidence for
louiselm-gf9a.

## Note

Unredacted logs hold full prompts, tool arguments, shell commands, and file contents. A scan on
2026-09-01 found no live credential values in the current set (matches for `API_KEY` were all
prose such as `required_env` and placeholder text), but the directory should be treated as
sensitive by default, and any archive location inherits that.

title: Production cold Park reports Run was not found
description:
The production `:LouiselmPark` path fails after the Session has sent a prompt and after a Beads issue was claimed to the exact live Session. The operator sees `louiselm: louiselm-capture: invalid run: Run was not found`, so Case 4 cannot reach Parked-Run mutation or expiry testing.

## Observed

Manual QA Case 4 on 2026-08-30 in `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`. Live Session: `codex/01a050d8-1fe2-7d22-a7c2-6146807a3c6a`.

Setup had previously reported `louiselm-capture run list` as `[]`. The operator then claimed a ready Beads issue to the Session, sent a first prompt as required by `e2fd0c2`, waited for completion, and invoked `:LouiselmPark`. The exact visible error was:

`louiselm: louiselm-capture: invalid run: Run was not found`

No Parked Run was produced, so `louiselm-capture run list` cannot provide a Run record for the case.

## Symptoms

- A valid live Session with at least one completed prompt cannot be cold-Parked through the production UI path.
- The error is emitted by the capture-service Run store while trying to persist the Park.
- Parked-Run mutation-safety and expiry/reaping acceptance is blocked.

## Root cause

Unknown. The UI path at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3192-3242` generates a Run id, calls `WorkflowService.admit`, then calls `WorkflowService.attach`, adopts the Session, and calls `Run:park_cold`. The service then reports `Run was not found` from `capture-service/src/runs.rs:593`, meaning the Park command cannot find the id it was given in the Run store. Possible causes include a state-directory mismatch between the admit and park subprocesses, a stale/mismatched executable or environment in the live Neovim process, or an id not surviving the asynchronous admit/attach chain. The exact Run id and admit/attach outputs were not captured before the error, so these hypotheses are not yet discriminated.

## Why it was not caught

The automated Park tests replace `vim.system` with a fake and assert callbacks, while the workflow service tests use a fake process boundary. They do not run the real `:LouiselmPark` sequence through the installed capture binary and its durable Run store.

## Fix direction

Capture and correlate the generated Run id across the real `admit`, `attach`, and `park` subprocess commands, and verify all three use the same state root and executable. Fix the narrowest shared process/store boundary; do not make Park retry blindly or hide the missing Run error.

## Acceptance

- From a fresh real Neovim process, after one completed prompt, `:LouiselmPark` creates a durable `cold_parked` record visible in `louiselm-capture run list`.
- The Park command and its preceding admit/attach commands use one identical Run id and state root.
- Existing missing-Run validation remains an actionable error for genuinely unknown ids.

## Not covered

No mutation-safety or expiry result was obtained because Park failed before creating a durable Run. The Beads claim's original state and the exact issue id were not recorded in this report and must be recovered before cleanup.
close_reason: Fixed at Run:park_cold's park_record restore timing; live acceptance confirmed by maintainer 2026-08-30

comments.author: claude/d4b23fbe-32a3-4c77-8802-687f31119e64
comments.text:
Root cause found, distinct from the state-root/executable hypotheses already ruled out by the prior comment: lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua:409-428 (Run:park_cold) set self.park_record = record, called the async self:park(callback) (which only starts the louiselm-capture run park subprocess and returns immediately), then unconditionally restored self.park_record = previous_record on the very next line -- synchronously, before the subprocess's completion callback ever fires. So run.park_record was always nil again by the time park_cold returned, regardless of whether the park later succeeded.

That matters because lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3192 reuses run.park_record.id to avoid re-admitting an already cold-Parked Run: `run_id = run and run.park_record and run.park_record.id or park_run_id()`. Once owner_run is set (adopt_session runs unconditionally during attach, before cold_park is even attempted) but park_record reads back nil, any later Park attempt on that same Session takes the owner_run~=nil branch at chat/init.lua:3210, mints a brand-new park_run_id() that was never passed to admit/attach, and calls park_cold with it -- which the capture-service Run store correctly reports as "Run was not found", because that id was never admitted. This matches the reported sequence: admit/attach created 63a87d73-5cc4-498b-ad1d-b53cdd6cbf92 successfully, but the retry after that used a different, never-admitted id.

Fix: Run:park_cold now only rolls park_record back to its previous value if the service call fails to start or its async callback reports failure; on success (or while pending) the record persists. Confirmed the existing tests hid this because they used synchronous fake park_service callbacks (calls back before returning), masking the ordering bug -- AGENTS.md section 5 flags exactly this pattern. Added two regression tests in tests/workflow/run_spec.lua using an async fake service (callback captured, invoked later): "retains the cold Park record while the async service confirms persistence" (red before the fix, green after) and "rolls back the cold Park record when the async service reports failure".

Full mini.test suite, stylua --check, and lua-language-server --checklevel=Warning all pass.

Per AGENTS.md Live Acceptance: this was reproduced live, so automated gates alone do not close it. Needs the maintainer to confirm from a fresh real Neovim process (vim.pack clone updated, per the sibling stale-clone issue hit on louiselm-wi0y): after one completed prompt, :LouiselmPark creates a durable cold_parked record visible in `louiselm-capture run list`, and a second :LouiselmPark on the same already-Parked Session does not error.

Not addressed here (per the issue's own "Not covered" section): the Beads claim left on the live Session during this QA round was not identified in the report and still needs manual recovery/cleanup; that is unrelated to the Run-id bug and out of scope for this fix.

title: Resume Park crashes while creating operation id
description:
Cold Park resume aborts before any durable mutation when the UI generates the resume operation UUID. The operator is left in an empty buffer and cannot resume the selected Run.

## Observed

Manual QA on 2026-08-31, build ca30c28, Session codex/01a0560a-40aa-75d3-bd30-eb978b8052df, selected Run a1dff263-9874-4332-8f8a-77e586a739a5.

The UI reported:

vim.schedule callback: ...louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/workflow/resume_controller.lua:27: bad argument #2 to 'random' (expected nil, integer, or table)

The stack is resume_controller.lua:27 operation_id -> resume_controller.lua:101 resume -> ui/chat/init.lua:4414 on_choice. The capture-service Run remained cold_parked because the failure occurred while creating operation_id, before RunClient:resume.

## Symptoms

- Selecting a valid cold Park leaves an empty buffer.
- No resume notification appears and no ACP session/load starts.
- The selected durable Run remains cold_parked.

## Root cause

vim.uv.random uses the signature random(length, buffer?, callback). resume_controller.lua:27 calls random(16, callback), so the callback is interpreted as argument 2, which must be nil, an integer, or a buffer table. The corrected call is random(16, nil, callback). A direct check with nvim --headless confirmed random(16, nil, callback) returns 16 bytes.

## Why it was not caught

The controller unit tests inject operation_id, and the UI regression also replaced nvim.uv.random with a two-argument fake matching the incorrect call. No test exercised the real libuv signature.

## Fix direction

Use the real three-argument vim.uv.random signature and update the test seam to match it. Keep UUID conversion and scheduling unchanged.

## Acceptance

- A regression test reaches the real callback shape or a faithful three-argument fake and passes.
- Selecting the saved Run resumes it without an exception and finalizes the durable Run active.

## Not covered

This QA attempt stopped before ACP session/load, so no Agent-side failure was observed.
close_reason: Fixed in a983ea4: use vim.uv.random(16, nil, callback). The faithful three-argument regression failed before the fix and passed after it; manual resume then succeeded for Run 6df99a74-12f7-4c75-8484-cfb5874b88c7. Full 798-case suite and all quality gates pass.

title: Offer a progressive LouiseLM browser demo
description:
## Problem Statement

Installing Neovim, LouiseLM, an ACP Agent, and Provider authentication hides LouiseLM's distinctive UX behind substantial setup. Static documentation cannot let a prospective user feel Session continuity, operator-controlled Handoff, limits, permissions, or configuration-driven picker UX before installing anything.

## Solution

Publish the LouiseLM Interactive Demo as a standalone browser experience. It runs an exact pinned Neovim WebAssembly build and the real LouiseLM UI against a clearly disclosed in-browser demo double; no Agent or Provider is connected. A bilingual web guide leads the visitor through one action-verified six-stage journey over a disposable sample project. The visitor can compare Core LouiseLM with a curated Enhanced configuration using Snacks for vim.ui.select and which-key for mappings.

## User Stories

1. As a prospective user, I want to operate LouiseLM in a browser so I can understand its interaction model before installing it.
2. As a user evaluating multiple Agents, I want to experience prior-Session Resume, Session switching, limits, and Handoff without supplying credentials.
3. As a cautious visitor, I want prompts and sample-project edits to remain inside my browser tab.
4. As a Neovim user, I want to compare LouiseLM's dependency-free fallback UX with an enhanced user configuration.
5. As an English- or Chinese-speaking visitor, I want the guided journey in a language I understand.
6. As a visitor whose browser cannot run the demo, I want a useful static walkthrough instead of a broken editor.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A primary homepage action and secondary Tutor/onboarding links open a standalone `/demo/` experience; the installed Tutor remains a separate product surface.
2. The interactive path runs real Neovim and real LouiseLM UI from self-hosted assets pinned to exact commits and SHA-256 digests. It is labelled experimental and continuously discloses that lifecycle behavior is scripted and no Agent or Provider is connected.
3. The journey completes in at most eight minutes and teaches, in order: first prompt; context plus permission/diff review; Resume of a pre-seeded prior Session; creation and switching of Sessions; a simulated Agent limit followed by the real Handoff review ceremony; and return to the retained source Session.
4. Progress advances only from observed Neovim/LouiseLM state. The guide offers assisted command entry, Skip, and Reset; arbitrary non-empty prompts are accepted but receive an explicit scripted response.
5. Permission acceptance applies a real edit to the browser-local sample project through LouiseLM's diff-review UI; rejection leaves the project unchanged and permits retry.
6. Entry offers Core and Enhanced profiles, with Enhanced preselected. Enhanced enables only Snacks' in-memory vim.ui.select path and which-key over existing mapping descriptions. Changing profile restarts the journey, and completion offers replay in the other profile.
7. Guide content, disclosures, scripted responses, fallback, and completion are available in English and Simplified Chinese. Authentic Neovim commands and LouiseLM UI remain unchanged.
8. After static assets load, prompts, keystrokes, progress, and project contents never leave the tab. The demo uses no credentials, runtime CDN/package fetches, persistence, or client analytics; refresh begins from known state while normal browser caching may retain immutable assets.
9. Modern desktop browsers with physical keyboards receive the interactive path. Mobile and unsupported or non-isolated browsers receive an accessible static walkthrough and installation links.
10. Completion summarizes the exercised behaviors and presents local installation through onboarding as the sole primary conversion action.
11. Exact Neovim, Snacks, and which-key updates are promoted manually only after both profiles complete the full deployed browser journey in English and Chinese.

## Implementation Notes

- Treat the browser target as experimental and fail visibly when boot or cross-origin isolation fails.
- Keep the web guide outside the Neovim canvas so recovery, Skip, Reset, language, and accessibility controls remain reachable when editor state is confusing.
- Reuse the existing mock ACP Agent as a behavioral reference, not as the runtime: it is a stdio process and WebAssembly cannot launch it.
- The Enhanced profile is a narrow demo-only dependency exception. LouiseLM itself remains dependency-free; do not copy maintainer dotfiles or enable modules that require processes, Git, terminals, native parsers, or host tools.
- Use sanitized observed event shapes where Provider or ACP extension payload fidelity matters; never invent a payload and present it as observed.
- Keep public artifact inputs explicitly allowlisted so the browser bundle cannot absorb Beads state, Sessions, transcripts, environment data, or private authoring material.

## Testing Notes

- Use browser automation against the built public artifact to prove boot, cross-origin isolation, real Lua execution, action-verified progression, reset, failure fallback, and the full journey in both profiles and languages.
- Prove the interactive route performs no post-load network requests carrying visitor input and that no demo state survives refresh.
- Exercise permission rejection and acceptance, Handoff review, source-Session retention, arbitrary prompt labelling, profile restart, mobile fallback, and unsupported-browser fallback.
- Keep deterministic tests free of real Agents, Providers, credentials, and external network calls.

## Out of Scope

- Live Agents or LLM calls.
- Skill management; it may become a separate advanced track only after the feature is reviewed and tested outside this work.
- Park, workflow Runs, Provenance, capture/Android, real shell commands, LSP, Git, search executables, terminals, and host filesystem access.
- Mobile interactive editing, progress persistence, analytics, automatic dependency updates, or a general-purpose browser transport extension.

title: Boot pinned Neovim and LouiseLM at /demo/
description:
Goal
Deliver the smallest end-to-end browser artifact: /demo/ boots an exact pinned Neovim WASM build and the real LouiseLM UI in the Core profile.

Scope
- Pin the Neovim WASM artifact to an exact upstream commit, checksum, and license provenance.
- Self-host the runtime and a strict allowlist of LouiseLM/demo files; load nothing from a CDN at runtime.
- Initialize a disposable browser-local MEMFS sample project and open LouiseLM's real UI.
- Apply COOP/COEP headers to the demo route and present actionable startup failures.
- Extend public-artifact validation for required WASM companion files and prevent private/local state from entering the artifact.
- Do not add the scripted conversation, lifecycle course, or Enhanced profile in this slice.

Acceptance criteria
- The built /demo/ route reaches an attached Neovim UI in a supported desktop browser with crossOriginIsolated=true.
- Lua can require LouiseLM and open the demo welcome surface against the three-file sample project.
- The runtime performs no external network request after static assets are loaded.
- The Neovim source identity and SHA256 digest are reproducible and checked.
- Missing isolation or corrupt assets fail visibly instead of leaving a blank canvas.
- Public-artifact checks admit required .wasm/.data assets while rejecting non-allowlisted repository and user-state files.

Testing
- Browser smoke test for boot, isolation, require("louiselm"), and sample files.
- Artifact allowlist regression tests, including a forbidden-state fixture.
- Existing site build and quality gates.

title: Fit the demo into one viewport with a compact guide row
description:
## Goal
Fit the interactive desktop demo into the browser content viewport with a much more compact first row and no vertical page scrolling.

## Evidence
Maintainer screenshot: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260907_0534_1920x1200_1788752043.png, captured 2026-09-07 at https://louiselm.com/demo/. The updated guide-above-editor layout is visible; this screenshot does not demonstrate a cache problem. On the 1920x1200 screen, browser/desktop chrome leaves approximately 1030px of page height. The guide occupies roughly 512px and Neovim extends below the visible page.
Follow-up to closed louiselm-0x9g (commit 2ebea3d), whose acceptance required only a useful portion of Neovim to remain visible, not a scroll-free page.
Source constraints: demo/demo.css:143 gives the heading up to 3.5rem; :214 reserves 17.5rem for the step; :381 gives the editor grid nearly a whole viewport of minimum height in addition to the guide.

## Scope
- Compact the top row: intro and Enhanced/Core choices on the left; current tutorial instruction, actions, and status on the right.
- Keep full-width Neovim below; size its container and actual rendered grid to the remaining viewport height, including after browser resize.
- Reduce oversized heading, spacing, and unnecessary reserved height while keeping text legible and controls accessible.
- Preserve language/profile switching, tutorial progression, assisted entry, Skip, Reset, completion, focus, and scripted-demo disclosure.
- Out of scope: cache/deployment changes without evidence, new tutorial behavior, runtime dependency changes, and mobile interactive support.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. At the screenshot-equivalent browser content viewport (approximately 1920x1030), the complete guide row and Neovim panel fit at once; the document has no vertical scroll range.
2. Verify the same desktop contract at 1440x900 and 1280x720. Use content viewport dimensions rather than monitor dimensions.
3. Neovim receives the majority of the available vertical space. The top row is visibly more compact than the reference; the terminal bottom and status line remain visible and usable.
4. No clipping, overlapping controls, inaccessible instructions, or nested scrolling guide is used to disguise overflow. Neovim's own buffer scrolling remains normal.
5. English and Simplified Chinese, both profiles, every guide step, completion, loading/error status, and viewport resizing preserve the fit and usable controls.
6. Unsupported/mobile static fallback remains readable and accessible; it is outside the desktop interactive no-scroll contract.
7. Maintainer confirms the live page fits their browser without vertical scrolling before closure.

## Testing
- Add browser layout regression coverage against the built artifact: assert document scrollHeight <= clientHeight (allow at most 1px rounding), guide above editor, editor bottom within viewport, no horizontal overflow, and actual Neovim grid/status line visible.
- Cover representative desktop sizes, both languages/profiles, longest guide content, completion, and resize. Confirm the layout regression fails against the current page before changing it.
- Run npm run site:test and npm run site:build; smoke-test the full tutorial interactions.
- Record before/after guide and editor bounds and screenshots. Preserve evidence in this issue; no new dependency without approval.
close_reason: Compact guide and complete Neovim viewport confirmed by maintainer; live:codex/01a079e9-4e91-7eb3-9599-f7b26a4a2076

title: Drive a browser-local LouiseLM prompt and diff
description:
Goal
Let a visitor complete a genuine LouiseLM prompt, permission, and diff-review interaction entirely inside the browser.

Scope
- Add a browser-safe deterministic Session/API double, using the existing mock Agent only as a behavioral reference.
- Configure the visible placeholder Agent as your-codex-here.
- Accept any nonempty prompt and label every generated response as scripted.
- Exercise real LouiseLM context, permission, and diff-review UI against the MEMFS sample.
- Accepting the diff updates the sample file; rejecting it leaves the file unchanged and permits a retry.
- Do not spawn a process, contact an Agent or Provider, or introduce a general browser transport.

Acceptance criteria
- A visitor can submit an arbitrary nonempty prompt through the real Chat UI.
- The response carries a persistent, accessible "scripted demo—no Agent/Provider connected" disclosure.
- The implementation attempt raises LouiseLM's real permission and diff-review flow.
- Accept and reject produce the specified observable file outcomes, including retry after reject.
- Refresh starts from a clean sample and no prompt or project data leaves the tab.

Testing
- Deterministic headless tests for the browser Session double and its terminal/cancellation behavior.
- Browser tests for arbitrary prompt, disclosure, context, accept, reject, retry, and fresh reload.
- Assert that no prompt-dependent network request occurs.
close_reason: Browser prompt drives real context, permission, and diff UI with accept/reject semantics. consumer:demo/bootstrap.js:55

title: Teach Resume, Session switching, limits, and Handoff
description:
Goal
Expose LouiseLM's most distinctive Session lifecycle in one coherent simulated scenario.

Scope
- Seed a prior Session that the visitor can Resume.
- Let the visitor create and switch among Sessions.
- At the scripted implementation attempt, surface a simulated Agent limit based on a sanitized observed event shape.
- Run the real Handoff review ceremony to your-claude-here: compact reviewed transcript, editable takeover task, explicit confirmation, and a distinct destination Session.
- Retain the source Session and let the visitor switch back to review the result.
- Preserve production Session and Handoff semantics; do not make Sessions change Agents.

Acceptance criteria
- Resume restores the seeded prior Session through LouiseLM's actual lifecycle surface.
- Creating and switching Sessions visibly changes the active Session.
- The limit is unambiguously labeled simulated.
- Handoff opens the actual review buffer and requires visitor confirmation after editing or accepting the takeover task.
- The destination is a new your-claude-here Session and the source remains available.
- Switching back demonstrates that the source Session was retained.

Testing
- Derive limit/Handoff fixtures from sanitized captured shapes and record provenance without sensitive payloads.
- Behavioral tests cover ordering, source retention, destination creation, cancellation, and late events.
- Browser journey covers Resume through return to the source Session.
close_reason: Browser lifecycle teaches Resume, switching, limits, and reviewed Handoff. consumer:lua/louiselm/dev/demo.lua:446

description:

Scope

- Offer Type it for me, while requiring the visitor to press Enter, plus Skip and Reset.

- Type it for me never submits on the visitor's behalf.
- Skip and Reset are keyboard accessible and Reset returns to the initial disposable state.
- Both languages cover all guide, response, disclosure, error, and completion strings.
- Focus order, announcements, contrast, and keyboard operation support the full journey.
- A normal first run fits the intended six-to-eight-minute envelope.

Testing
- State-machine tests for each completion predicate, skip, reset, and invalid/out-of-order actions.
- Browser journeys in English and Simplified Chinese.
- Accessibility checks for focus, keyboard use, names, and live announcements.

title: Offer Core and Enhanced browser profiles
description:
Goal

Scope

- Enhanced self-hosts exact pinned Snacks and which-key sources: Snacks overrides vim.ui.select only where needed, and which-key exposes existing mapping descriptions.

- Enhanced is preselected and the entry choice clearly explains the distinction.
- Core loads neither Snacks nor which-key.
- Enhanced performs no process/native-tool lookup and makes no runtime CDN request.
- Plugin source commits, SHA256 digests, and licenses are recorded and checked.
- Selecting another profile discards current demo state and cleanly restarts; replay does the same after completion.

Testing
- Browser journey for both profiles.
- Assertions that Core excludes optional plugin code and Enhanced enables only approved modules.
- Network/process-capability checks and restart/replay state-isolation tests.

title: Disposed Attention still mutates queued state
description:
Attention event methods can still append queued actions or clear retained entries after Attention:dispose(), so the disposed controller is not a terminal state.

## Observed

Observed 2026-09-04 while reducing the pinned WASM demo hang. The original reconnect hypothesis was disproven by a focused test: `ensure_connection` already guards `self.disposed`. Calling `seen`/`prompt_started` after disposal nevertheless appends actions through `enqueue`, while clearing methods can still mutate `entries`.

The WASM hang that led here occurs while Attention is live: browser cursor activity attempts a Unix socket that the demo intentionally does not have. Disposing the observer before chat attach keeps subsequent `{ mode = "n", blocking = false }` RPC responsive; it does not require this bug fix.

## Symptoms

- A disposed controller accumulates unreachable queue entries after later public calls.
- Later clearing calls mutate retained state even though lifecycle teardown completed.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/attention.lua` guards transport connection and several producers after disposal, but `enqueue`, `seen`, `permission_resolved`, `permission_cancelled`, `run_resumed`, and `session_disposed` do not consistently short-circuit before mutation.

## Why it was not caught

Tests covered transport disposal and scheduled callbacks, but did not snapshot internal state and invoke the whole public event surface after disposal.

## Fix direction

Make the narrow shared queue boundary and public clearing methods no-op once disposed.

## Acceptance

- A regression calls the public event surface after dispose and proves transport count, queue length, and entry count are unchanged.

## Not covered

Native Attention sockets are intentionally unavailable in the WASM demo; demo startup disposes that observer before attaching chat.
close_reason: Disposed Attention is terminal for transport and state. gate:tests/ui/attention_spec.lua

comments.author: codex/01a06d85-2ee2-7863-898b-f68a140beed2
comments.text: Lesson: lifecycle disposal must guard both I/O and state mutation at the shared queue/clear boundaries; transport-only assertions miss unreachable work retained after teardown. tests/ui/attention_spec.lua now exercises every public event method post-dispose.

title: Enhanced demo logs an RPC timeout during the guided journey
description:
The deployed Enhanced journey completes, but one guide setup request can remain pending for 30 seconds and then warn in the browser console. The visitor can continue, yet the delayed response becomes an unknown RPC message and deployed promotion cannot claim a clean console.

## Observed

Observed 2026-09-05 on `https://louiselm.com/demo/`, Firebase Hosting version `9b17434364745d3d`, Enhanced/English, Chromium through Playwright session `hiex-demo`.

`.playwright-cli/console-2026-09-05T03-25-18-484Z.log` records:

`LouiseLM demo step setup failed Error: Request 514 (nvim_exec_lua) timed out after 30s`

followed by:

`[RpcClient] unknown msgid 514 pending: []`

The same journey still reached guide step 10, returned to `louiselm://demo-1`, and showed one primary completion action.

## Symptoms

- The browser console reports one guide setup timeout and one late-response warning.
- The visible journey eventually completes; no wrong edit or Session loss was observed.

## Root cause

Unknown. `demo/bootstrap.js:541` awaits the optional step `enter` request, and `runtime/rpc.js` expires the pending `nvim_exec_lua` call after 30 seconds. Hypotheses are an inspection/setup request overlapping a picker or an editor operation that temporarily blocks the WASM RPC loop. Reproduce while recording the guide step and request source to discriminate; do not assume the transport itself is defective.

## Why it was not caught

Local browser acceptance checked visible progression and console errors, but did not fail on console warnings or attribute each guide setup RPC request.

## Fix direction

First identify which step setup owns the timed-out request. Keep setup idempotent, serialize it against picker input if necessary, and make deployed browser acceptance fail on unexpected warnings. Do not lengthen the RPC timeout to hide the late response.

## Acceptance

- A deterministic browser regression fails on the current overlap and passes after the narrow fix.
- Enhanced and Core complete the deployed journey with zero unexpected console warnings or errors.
- No unknown late RPC message appears after completion.

## Not covered

The three remaining profile/language rows have not yet been run against this release. The current warning did not prevent the Enhanced/English completion.
close_reason: Production Enhanced/Core journeys complete without timeout or late RPC warning. live:codex/01a06d85-2ee2-7863-898b-f68a140beed2

title: Site build fails because pinned Neovim asset returns 404
description:
Every `npm run site:build` attempt currently stops before assembling `/demo/` because the exact pinned Neovim WASM release asset cannot be downloaded.

## Observed

Seen 2026-09-05 from `/home/lotso/code/louiselm` while verifying louiselm-0x9g.

Command: `npm run site:build`

Error: `Error: build-demo: could not download https://api.github.com/repos/neovim/neovim/releases/assets/543842099: Error: 404 Not Found`

Independent reproduction: `curl -L -H "User-Agent: louiselm-site-build" https://api.github.com/repos/neovim/neovim/releases/assets/543842099` reports `status=404`.

## Symptoms

- Maintainers cannot produce a fresh site artifact.
- `scripts/build-demo.mjs:57` aborts after three failed download attempts.

## Root cause

`demo/assets.lock.json:5-6` pins GitHub release asset ID 543842099, and that exact GitHub API endpoint now returns HTTP 404. Whether the asset was removed or its access path changed is unverified.

## Why it was not caught

`scripts/test-demo-config.mjs` validates the pin format and checksums but does not prove that the remote asset remains reachable. The build has no checked local copy or alternate source.

## Fix direction

Identify a currently published, reproducible Neovim WASM artifact and update its exact commit, source URL, SHA256, and license provenance together. Preserve the self-hosted runtime and integrity checks; do not weaken the pin to make the download pass.

## Acceptance

- `npm run site:build` completes from a clean cache.
- The replacement Neovim artifact is reachable and matches its committed SHA256 and source identity.
- Existing demo configuration and public-artifact tests pass.

## Not covered

The currently deployed `/demo/` artifact was not tested, so this record does not claim that the live demo is down. Deferred because the active task is the demo layout, not runtime provenance.

title: LouiseLM attention control plane: ideas into reality
description:
## Problem Statement

Ideas arrive faster than sustained human attention can evaluate and realize them. Existing agent tools automate isolated conversations and coding turns but do not make the whole workflow, its authority boundaries, or its human-attention gates observable.

## Solution

Build LouiseLM as an attention control plane that turns ideas into reality. It makes workflow topology explicit, automates work agents can safely perform, and surfaces only decisions where human judgment materially improves or unblocks the outcome. LouiseLM ships an explicit software-delivery reference preset while allowing other workflows to configure different stages and resolvers.

The first active vertical slice is durable speech capture from Android and Neovim into one local Linux inbox. Later idea modelling, triage, workflow history, attention visualization, sequential orchestration, and parallel workers remain dependency-shaped deferred features.

## Implementation Decisions

- Human attention is assigned per transition, never by one global human-or-agent rule.
- Declarative validated topology describes stages, transitions, triggers, and resolvers; typed providers perform effects.
- Raw capture is immutable and local-first. Android and Neovim speech are the first bundled capture providers.
- Neovim is the cockpit; a narrow Rust user service owns durable capture ingestion and transcription while the editor is closed.
- The reference workflow is triage -> human/agent grill -> automatic plan and critique -> tracker DAG -> policy-controlled execution -> automated evidence -> human outcome acceptance.
- Logical workflow threads outlive replaceable ACP sessions and preserve decisions, supersessions, questions, evidence, and handoffs.
- The live idea journey and its expanding task DAG are the primary visualization. Human gates are visually distinct.
- Beads is the tracker in the reference preset, not a core dependency or a second implementation inside LouiseLM.
- Sequential execution precedes the committed parallel-worker milestone.

## Testing Decisions

Each executable boundary has deterministic tests. The capture milestone additionally requires a physical Android-to-Linux-to-Neovim dogfood test and explicit human outcome acceptance.

## Out of Scope

The first slice does not implement semantic idea segmentation, triage actions, workflow orchestration, graph UI, or parallel workers. Those remain visible deferred children with evidence-based entry criteria.

title: Durable speech capture from Android and Neovim
description:
## Problem Statement

Ideas arising away from the keyboard are currently kept in memory or Gmail drafts and can be lost. Capture must be faster than classification and must not require Neovim to remain open.

## Solution

Record short speech streams from Android and Neovim, preserve the original audio in a local Linux inbox, transcribe asynchronously, and expose quiet durable status in Neovim. Android saves first and syncs later; no project, title, or priority is requested during capture.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Multiple rapid Android recordings survive offline use, app exit, restart, upload retry, and duplicate delivery.
2. Android pairs to a Linux receiver using pinned TLS and a scoped revocable device credential.
3. Neovim records through a validated external command and ingests through the same capture contract.
4. Original audio and successful transcript are retained indefinitely by default and are never silently rewritten or deleted.
5. The Linux service transcribes with an explicitly configured provider while Neovim is closed.
6. A physical-phone gardening journey reaches the Neovim inbox without loss and receives human outcome acceptance.

## Out of Scope

Semantic idea extraction, triage, workflow topology, task planning, agent orchestration, graph UI, hosted sync, and local Whisper tuning.

## Goal
Generate five genuinely distinct logo proposals for the LouiseLM Android capture app, exploring a recognizable Louise Michel portrait/head motif while leaving room for stronger imaginative directions.

## Scope
- In scope: one image-generation pass producing five clearly differentiated visual concepts; each should remain legible at Android launcher-icon size and communicate some combination of Louise Michel, voice/microphone, capture, or private/local-first recording.

5. A labeled contact sheet and five individual full-resolution raster files are saved in a clearly named design/proposals location in the repository.

title: Successful manual sync leaves Android status stuck on queued
description:
After a user taps Sync now while the Android activity remains visible, completed upload work does not refresh the queue status. The user keeps seeing “Upload work queued.” until leaving and returning to the app, even though app-private state and receiver ingestion have already completed.

## Observed
Physical QA bead louiselm-1chb on 2026-08-21, commit efe6a15, Xiaomi 21081111RG, Android 14/API 34, build V816.0.19.0.UKWEUXM.

Exact user observation: “it says upload work queued, i have to press Home then back into app to see pending 0”.

At that moment both queued UUIDs (4deb4e34-4b17-4545-a1ee-3558a6dbc300 and b5bf51ad-79ef-448a-86c7-e28bba2b2a10) had phone upload status `uploaded`, uploaded markers, one receiver directory each, matching audio SHA-256 values, and receiver last_delivery_at_ms 1787314849471. Thus upload completion preceded the lifecycle round-trip that changed the display.

## Symptoms
- The visible status remains “Upload work queued.” after successful completion.
- Pending 0 becomes visible only after Home then returning to LouiseLM triggers onResume.
- The durable queue and receiver state are correct; this defect is stale operator feedback, not data loss or duplicate ingestion.

## Root cause
`android/app/src/main/java/dev/louiselm/capture/MainActivity.kt:102-107` enqueues manual work and replaces the status text with `sync_queued`, but registers no WorkManager completion observation or callback. `MainActivity.kt:57-59` refreshes only on activity resume, which explains why Home then return reveals pending 0. `UploadWorker.kt:15-45` changes durable state on a background worker with no foreground status notification.

## Why it was not caught
Existing tests cover queue/upload behavior and lifecycle refresh separately but the physical round exposed the missing asynchronous UI boundary: no test keeps MainActivity resumed while WorkManager transitions a manual upload to terminal success.

## Fix direction
At the narrowest UI/WorkManager boundary, observe the uniquely named manual upload while the activity is active and call `refreshStatus()` after terminal completion. Keep worker/storage layers presentation-free and remove observers during activity teardown. Do not add polling or refresh timers.

## Acceptance
- A behavioral Android test fails before the fix and proves that a resumed MainActivity changes from queued to pending 0 after manual work completes, without an onPause/onResume cycle.
- Failure/retry terminal information refreshes through the same lifecycle-safe boundary.
- Repeated setup/resume does not accumulate observers or update a destroyed activity.
- Existing Android unit, lint, and assemble gates remain green.

## Not covered
Visual redesign of the status panel, periodic age updates, notifications while the activity is backgrounded, and the separately blocked overlay QA case are out of scope.
close_reason: Completed lifecycle-safe WorkManager completion observation; Android tests, lint, and assembleDebug pass

title: QR pairing hides progress behind stale queue status
description:
During QR pairing, returning from the camera leaves the previous multiline receiver/queue status on screen while barcode decoding and network work occur, then replaces that entire status with a lone error. Users cannot tell whether the captured photo was accepted, whether pairing is still running, or how the error relates to the prior endpoint and pending queue.

## Observed
Physical QA bead louiselm-1chb on 2026-08-21, Xiaomi 21081111RG, Android 14/API 34, commit efe6a15. During a same-identity endpoint update from port 7391 to 7392, the user photographed and confirmed a pairing QR three or four times without a successful update. Exact observation: “after you take the photo and press ok button then you see the previous status lines then only the error message”. The exact terminal error text for these attempts was not captured and remains to be added; a QR delayed by the separate Neovim image-rendering defect may have expired, so repeated pairing failure itself is not yet attributed to this UI defect.

## Symptoms
- Immediately after camera confirmation, old endpoint/queue lines remain with no indication that decoding or pairing is in progress.
- A later failure replaces the whole durable status with a standalone error, removing the context needed to understand or retry it.
- Repeated attempts are ambiguous: the user cannot distinguish photo decoding, expired QR, endpoint verification, and pairing rejection phases.

## Root cause
`android/app/src/main/java/dev/louiselm/capture/MainActivity.kt:228-262` returns from the camera and starts asynchronous ML Kit decoding without changing `statusView`. Only after a payload is found does `pair()` set `pairing_in_progress` at lines 264-267. Decode failures directly replace `statusView` at lines 250-260, and parse/network failures also replace it at lines 288-290 and 339-347. The same single view owns both durable `status_format` output (`MainActivity.kt:364-387`) and transient operation messages, so progress and terminal context cannot coexist.

## Why it was not caught
Automated tests cover pairing transition logic and protocol behavior, but no UI lifecycle test models camera RESULT_OK, asynchronous barcode completion, and terminal pairing failure while asserting what the user sees at each phase.

## Fix direction
Make the camera-return/decode phase explicit immediately and present terminal pairing outcomes without erasing the durable receiver/queue context. Keep barcode and network work off the main thread and ignore late results after destruction. Preserve one small programmatic-Views screen; no UI framework dependency is warranted.

## Acceptance
- A behavioral test fails before the fix and proves RESULT_OK immediately exposes a pairing/decode-in-progress state instead of stale queue lines.
- Decode, expiry, endpoint-verification, and receiver errors remain specific and visible alongside enough current endpoint/queue context to retry safely.
- A successful same-identity endpoint update visibly settles on the new endpoint and current queue state without an ambiguous intermediate screen.
- Late camera/scanner/network callbacks cannot update a destroyed activity, and Android test/lint/assemble gates remain green.

## Not covered
The root cause of the current failed QR attempts remains unverified until the exact error is captured. Camera-app UX, QR delivery in Neovim, and live WorkManager status refresh are tracked separately.

title: Pairing QR is unreadable from a dark terminal
description:
`louiselm-capture pair` renders its only pairing QR using terminal-default foreground/background colors. In a dark Neovim terminal this produces a light-on-dark inverted code that the LouiseLM Android ML Kit scanner repeatedly fails to detect; forcing black foreground on white background makes the same flow decode and update the endpoint.

## Observed
Physical QA bead louiselm-1chb on 2026-08-21, commit efe6a15, Xiaomi 21081111RG Android 14/API 34, Neovim terminal using a dark color scheme.

The receiver native QR from `:tabnew | terminal /home/lotso/.local/bin/louiselm-capture pair` produced the exact app error `No LouiseLM pairing QR was found. Move closer and try again.` A fresh QR generated in a terminal with explicit ANSI black foreground/white background decoded: the app changed its displayed endpoint from `https://192.168.10.121:7391` to `https://192.168.10.121:7392` under the same receiver identity and without creating another device enrollment.

## Symptoms
- The default QR looks plausible to the user but camera confirmation ends in QR-not-found.
- Repeating or moving closer does not explain that terminal contrast is the boundary.
- Pairing succeeds only after an undocumented manual terminal-color override.

## Root cause
`capture-service/src/cli.rs:235-237` renders `qrcode::render::unicode::Dense1x2` and prints it without explicit colors or a machine-renderable alternative. The renderer uses block glyphs and spaces whose effective dark/light values depend on terminal foreground/background. On the tested dark terminal the code is inverted relative to the scanner-compatible black-on-white form.

## Why it was not caught
CLI tests assert pairing behavior/payload issuance but do not photograph or decode the rendered artifact under terminal color schemes. The first physical QA path did not record terminal contrast as evidence.

## Fix direction
Give `pair` a deterministic scanner-readable presentation independent of the user’s terminal theme, while keeping credentials short-lived and out of logs/files by default. Evaluate explicit terminal contrast versus an intentional image/output option; redirected/non-TTY behavior and cleanup must remain safe.

## Acceptance
- A regression check proves the generated visual has deterministic dark modules on a light quiet zone rather than inheriting terminal colors.
- The Android app decodes a fresh QR displayed in the maintainer’s normal dark Neovim terminal without a manual ANSI wrapper.
- Light-terminal behavior remains readable, QR expiry/one-use semantics are unchanged, and no raw payload or token is logged.
- Rust tests and formatting/lint gates remain green.

## Not covered
Neovim ACP image-result rendering (`louiselm-ce6.21`) and Android pairing progress/status composition (`louiselm-qbr.1.12`) are separate defects.

title: Tightly packed Android actions cause accidental recordings
description:
The Android screen places Start Capture, Pair Receiver QR, and Sync Now as consecutive full-width buttons with no separation or grouping. While repeatedly trying to pair, the user mispressed Start Capture twice, creating real immutable recordings that then entered and uploaded through the durable queue.

## Observed
Physical QA bead louiselm-1chb on 2026-08-21, commit efe6a15, Xiaomi 21081111RG Android 14/API 34. The user explicitly confirmed: “i mispressed buttons are too tightly spaced”. App-private inventory proves two unintended recordings created during pairing attempts: `ab3f5431-4d9c-4878-b8a9-9d2bf5bed6c6` (1377 ms, 21,464 bytes) and `67ffeb3d-1e1d-4a61-b9d4-44f7a514834d` (605 ms, 10,121 bytes). Both were assigned to the current receiver and later uploaded exactly once when the user synced. They are preserved; no automatic deletion is authorized.

## Symptoms
- A user aiming for Pair Receiver can accidentally begin recording.
- A second mistaken tap stops and publishes the recording, so accidental audio becomes durable queue content rather than a harmless transient state.
- The unintended items are indistinguishable from intended thoughts downstream and cannot be silently removed under the immutable-capture contract.

## Root cause
`android/app/src/main/java/dev/louiselm/capture/MainActivity.kt:90-108` adds the capture, pairing, and sync buttons consecutively with the same `matchWidth()` layout parameters. `matchWidth()` at lines 112-115 supplies no margins, and there is no grouping or visual separation between the fast primary recording action and administrative pairing/sync actions.

## Why it was not caught
Headless tests verify action behavior but not physical mis-target risk on the actual device. The manual QA plan exercised each action but did not include rapid repeated pairing attempts adjacent to the capture control.

## Fix direction
Create a clear spatial/hierarchical boundary between the primary capture action and receiver-management actions using the existing programmatic Views. Preserve one-tap capture and avoid a confirmation dialog that would undermine fast thought capture. Do not introduce Compose or another UI dependency.

## Acceptance
- On the physical reference phone, repeated Pair Receiver and Sync interactions can be performed without touching the capture target or creating a recording.
- Start Capture remains a single deliberate tap with a visibly distinct recording state.
- Pairing/sync controls are visibly grouped apart from capture across supported display/font scaling.
- A behavioral smoke test proves pairing and sync actions never invoke capture state transitions, and Android test/lint/assemble gates remain green.

## Not covered
Deleting or suppressing the two already-uploaded accidental recordings, redesigning the full screen, and the separate stale-status/pairing-progress defects are out of scope.

title: Offline capture leaves pending count stale until app resume
description:
After a recording is finalized, the Android app replaces the status panel with `Capture <UUID> is durable and queued.` and never refreshes the queue summary. While offline, the user must leave and reopen the app before seeing that pending increased to 1.

## Observed
Physical QA bead louiselm-1chb on 2026-08-21, commit efe6a15, Xiaomi 21081111RG Android 14/API 34. With Wi-Fi disabled, the user recorded `c30cc720-e07a-44e1-9338-19289e568ddd` and saw `Capture c30... is durable and queued`, then reported: “i have to go back home then start the app to see pending 1, annoying”. App-private evidence confirms the capture was pending, receiver-owned, unmarked, and absent from the receiver throughout; only the activity lifecycle round-trip changed the display.

## Symptoms
- The useful durable-capture acknowledgement replaces rather than updates the queue summary.
- Pending count remains visually stale after a successful offline capture.
- The user must navigate Home and back to learn whether the queued count changed.

## Root cause
`android/app/src/main/java/dev/louiselm/capture/MainActivity.kt:180-194` completes storage on the executor, then success line 190 assigns `saved_status` directly to the same `statusView` used for the durable queue summary. It enqueues upload but does not call or compose with `refreshStatus()`. `MainActivity.kt:57-59` refreshes only on a later `onResume`, explaining the workaround. This is separate from `louiselm-qbr.1.11`, where a background WorkManager completion occurs after manual Sync now.

## Why it was not caught
Capture tests prove durable file/state creation, but no behavioral UI test keeps MainActivity resumed after offline finalization and asserts both the capture acknowledgement and updated pending summary.

## Fix direction
Reconcile the durable-capture acknowledgement with current queue status immediately after finalization at the existing UI scheduling boundary. Preserve the UUID acknowledgement and keep filesystem/network work off the main thread; avoid polling and a second status model.

## Acceptance
- A behavioral test fails before the fix and proves an offline capture changes the visible pending count to 1 without an onPause/onResume cycle.
- The user still sees an unambiguous durable acknowledgement containing the capture UUID.
- Fast online upload completion composes correctly with the same status path and does not regress `louiselm-qbr.1.11` handling.
- Late completion after activity destruction cannot mutate UI, and Android test/lint/assemble gates remain green.

## Not covered
Live WorkManager terminal refresh, pairing progress composition, and control spacing are tracked in separate bugs.

title: Make command invocation limits opt-in
description:
## Problem Statement

The broker currently requires a finite invocation count for each authorized command. The maintainer confirmed in louiselm-zqk9 that ordinary coding and unattended Runs must not have a default command-count quota. Counts are useful for explicitly bounded operations; the number of shell commands is not a reliable measure of work or effect size.

## Solution

Support command grants with either an explicit finite invocation limit or no invocation quota. Preserve every other authorization boundary. This is the command-policy prerequisite for the existing cold Resume task, which must carry either policy through a fresh authorized Session.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I can authorize ordinary or unattended work without choosing an arbitrary command count.
2. As an operator, I can explicitly bound a particular command grant and rely on that bound across delegation, failure, and restart.
3. As an operator, I retain my chosen Agent and LouiseLM permission/auto-approval policy while count limits remain an independent choice.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An explicitly authorized command grant with no count limit is accepted and executes within its existing capability scope and deadlines without acquiring a default invocation quota. Cover ordinary and unattended policy inputs.
2. No command grant still means no command authority. An omitted invocation quota must not imply a broader command scope, permission to delegate, extra capabilities, a new expiry, or bypass of Agent/upstream settings and LouiseLM permission policy.
3. An explicit finite limit remains validated and enforced. Admitted uncertain effects remain spent; delegated reservations remain non-refundable and cannot amplify a finite parent allowance. A finite parent cannot produce an uncapped child grant.
4. Persist and round-trip finite versus uncapped count policy distinctly. Do not represent uncapped behavior with a large integer, turn invalid counts into uncapped authority, or retain obsolete compatibility shims.
5. Preserve the distinction between command-count limits and existing Run generated-work budgets. Existing scope, expiry, timeout, revocation, identity, and delegation checks remain enforced in either count mode.
6. Make the policy available through the existing broker authorization and installed command consumer, with focused acceptance for the unset/default case and explicitly counted grants. Expose the selected mode to the existing policy/presentation boundary; do not introduce mandatory repeated approval prompts.
7. Provide the finite/uncapped policy and accounting contract needed by louiselm-qbr.5.1.2.2.3 without reconstructing spent old lifetimes. Cold Resume allocation and recovery activation remain that task's deliverable.

## Implementation Notes

- Confirmed by the maintainer in codex/01a09931-7f28-7e22-b94d-ea6edf438c8e on 2026-09-13; full decision in louiselm-zqk9.

title: Enforce the approved Provider metadata disclosure profile
description:
## Problem Statement

Brokered requests currently forward reviewed headers and the request body unchanged, including stable installation and Session/thread/turn identifiers. Operators need an explicit, enforceable disclosure contract; Agent updates must not silently expand it.

## Solution

Use a versioned metadata disclosure profile. Forward profile-permitted metadata unchanged, bind the exact profile to the existing Provider permission, and report it in Verified posture and the existing authorization surface. Unknown or malformed metadata fails closed.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I can see which metadata the approved Provider receives, including identifiers that permit cross-Run linkage, without an anonymity claim.
2. As an operator, I can authorize the exact disclosure profile through the existing Provider permission and selected approval policy.
3. As a workflow author, I know an Agent update cannot add unreviewed metadata to an authorized request.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The supported versioned profile explicitly defines permitted metadata fields and valid structure in both headers and body. Derive the initial profile from observed offline request evidence, not invented optional fields.
2. Accepted reviewed metadata, including stable installation and Session/thread/turn identifiers, is forwarded unchanged. Do not strip, synthesize, rotate, or rewrite identifiers.
3. Unknown metadata fields or malformed structure refuse the request before upstream forwarding with a typed, safe, actionable failure. No silent pass-through or sanitization fallback.
4. The existing Provider permission binds the exact profile. A changed profile cannot reuse authorization for the previous profile and requires fresh authorization through the existing policy.
5. Existing operator-selected auto-approval remains supported; no separate mandatory metadata prompt is added.
6. Existing permission presentation and Verified posture report the authorized disclosure profile and safe summary. State that the Provider receives reviewed metadata and stable identifiers; make no anonymity claim. Do not expose actual identifier values, prompts, credentials, or raw metadata in diagnostics.
7. Missing or mismatched profile evidence must not produce a verified disclosure claim or permit the brokered request. Ordinary Sessions and unset Provider permission retain their existing behavior.
8. Brokered activation consumes this enforcement and authorization evidence. Closing the design question alone never enables networking.

## Implementation Notes

Reuse the existing Provider request parser, broker transport, permission authorization, and normalized provider_disclosure posture dimension. Keep policy validation separate from I/O. A top-level body-key allowlist alone does not establish the permitted structure inside client_metadata. The initial observed capture is recorded on louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.1; the confirmed decision is louiselm-hp733. Do not assume that removing identifiers would preserve caching or provide anonymity.

## Testing Notes

Red-green regressions cover unchanged accepted metadata; unknown header/body metadata; malformed metadata structure; missing/stale/mismatched profile authorization; profile change and fresh authorization; existing auto-approval; ordinary/unset behavior; and agreement between safe human/robot disclosure summaries. Verify refused requests never reach the upstream transport. Use offline fixtures and the existing affected suites; paid Provider calls and host installation are not authorized.

## Out of Scope

Metadata anonymization, identifier rewriting, a new approval system, mandatory human prompting, paid requests, installed-host acceptance, and enabling Brokered networking in this feature alone.

## Provenance

Maintainer confirmed the final grill-me summary in codex/01a0d6e6-d484-7f53-8c08-f58fd0df0b1e on 2026-09-25. Vocabulary delta: No change.
close_reason: Closed profile enforcement, exact durable permission binding, unchanged metadata and safe disclosure components tested. No mandatory prompt, dependency or activation added. Both child lessons recorded; production wiring and privileged activation acceptance remain inert:louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4.5

title: Persist declarative workflows and grill history
description: Define validated stages, transitions, granular resolvers, backward transitions, logical threads, canonical decisions, supersessions, session replacement handoffs, and evidence links. Depends on evidence from capture and triage.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
**Candidate requirement for this issue's design — not a settled decision.**

When a workflow engine sequences beads work on the operator's behalf, it should
default to draining in-progress or claimed work before opening new work, even
when a scoring pass ranks an unstarted item higher. That is what a human
operator does by hand, and it is the behaviour the current tooling cannot
express.

**Evidence.** `bv`'s triage score is a weighted sum over eight components.
Urgency (weight 0.1) already rewards in-progress work — raw 1.0 for
`in_progress` against 0.8 for `open` — but it is one component among eight. A
fresh `open` task carrying a real `blocks` edge (BlockerRatio, weight 0.13) plus
a deeper unlock chain (TimeToImpact, weight 0.1) out-scores an in-progress epic
comfortably. Measured in this repo: a two-paragraph policy doc scored ~0.459
against ~0.405 for an in-progress epic covering an entire ACP client.

None of the five built-in weight presets fix this. `priority-first` raises
Urgency only to ~0.146, still not a gate, and there is no custom-weights file.
So the preference cannot be extracted from `bv` by configuration. It has to be
applied on top of its output — which is why it belongs in the engine that
consumes that output rather than in the scorer.

The sequencing policy is this issue's to define. This comment records why the
question exists and what the evidence was, so the design conversation does not
have to re-derive it.

Refs louiselm-repo-context-substrate-09r
