title: Grill-me needed: how should grill-me support challenger passes and non-interrupting side capture
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing — it wants full attention.**

Raised as an explicit meta-idea during the 2026-08-21 grill of `louiselm-parallel-worker-tracker-substrate-6mtc`. The user did not ask to redesign grill-me now; they asked to preserve the improvement opportunity while the foreground grill continued without losing its thread.

## The question

Should the grill-me workflow gain two cooperating capabilities:

1. a distinct challenger skill or role, possibly run by another model, that stress-tests the primary grill's framing, assumptions, and conclusions; and
2. an isolated side-capture worker that can inspect beads, deduplicate or file an interjected idea, and return control without making the foreground facilitator stop grilling?

The product requirement behind both is continuity of human attention: useful meta-ideas should survive, but recording or challenging them should not silently replace the conversation the user was having.

## Evidence from the session that raised it

A Claude grill hit its model limit immediately after the user's answer. A different model could read the transcript and resume at a clean boundary, which exposed a broader possibility: model diversity may be useful not only for handoff but as an intentional challenge pass.

While discussing that possibility, the user interjected this improvement idea but explicitly said they did not want to take on a new grill. They proposed that a background subagent could search beads and preserve the side idea while the foreground agent resumed the live question “as if nothing happened.” This issue is the durable result of that experiment.

## Threads worth pulling

- When should a challenge pass run: during a grill, at explicit checkpoints, only after convergence, or on request? It must add scrutiny without repeatedly reopening settled decisions.
- What context should the challenger inherit? Full transcript continuity preserves nuance; an intentionally fresh model may expose anchoring. The workflow may need both a settled-decision ledger and a bounded challenge brief.
- Is this best expressed as a skill, a declarative workflow stage, a model/role policy, or some combination? Do not assume “another skill” is automatically the right implementation boundary.
- Define the side-capture worker's narrow contract: search via `br`, choose comment versus issue, preserve provenance and nuance, avoid changing the live issue's claim/status, sync the mutation, and report back asynchronously.
- Preserve foreground UX: one-question cadence and conversation ownership stay with the grilling agent; a recorder must not become the facilitator or force the user to context-switch.
- Evaluate the improvement empirically. Compare ordinary grills, handoff grills, and challenger-assisted grills for missed assumptions, needless re-litigation, time to convergence, and quality of the resulting beads.
- Coordinate with `louiselm-parallel-worker-tracker-substrate-6mtc` before implementing a writable background worker: that live question owns tracker-state isolation and reconciliation, not this one.

## Why this is separate from its parent

`louiselm-qbr.3` broadly owns persisted workflows and grill history. This is a narrower unresolved product/design fork about adversarial review and side-channel capture. It is substantial enough for its own grill, while remaining deferred with the parent rather than interrupting current work.

## Out of scope for this grill

Reconstructing the 2026-08-21 conversation, taking over its live tracker-ownership question, or treating the user's interjection as authorization to implement workflow machinery now. React to the recorded requirement and design the improvement when this issue is deliberately opened.

title: Validate workflow definitions and admit Runs against safety contracts
description:
## Problem Statement

A workflow that can invoke Agents can grow work without bound, and the growth is invisible until
Agents have already started. The motivating failure is not a cycle: a qa-review stage whose Agent
invokes `louiselm-to-beads-bug` files a new issue, which becomes ready work, which re-enters
execute, which re-enters qa-review. `br dep cycles` reports no cycles the whole way down, correctly,
because every iteration mints a new issue id. Acyclicity is not termination.

## Solution

Two contracts over workflow definitions and Runs, settled by the louiselm-qbr.8 grill-me session.

**Validation** is a pure, total function over one workflow definition, using frontmatter only. It is
binary: accept or reject. There is no warn tier and no run-it-anyway override. The escape valve for
a disagreement is editing the SKILL.md, which is versioned, reviewable and attributable.

**Admission** checks live Run state at every stage entry and every spawn. It cannot reject
retroactively; it stops or escalates. Recursion, fan-out and budget are only knowable here, because
the skill graph is open and an Agent is a nondeterministic edge-generator.

The bounding unit is the Generator: a back edge, a work-filing stage, or an Agent invoking a
work-producing skill. Automatic Generators declare a literal integer bound. Human-resolved
Generators need no number, because the human is the bound.

## User Stories

1. As a workflow author, I want a malformed workflow rejected at discovery time, so that I find out
   before any Agent starts rather than at 3am on the sixth iteration.
2. As a workflow author, I want the bound to appear only on edges no human ever sees, so that review
   cycles do not acquire fake numbers nobody believes.
3. As an operator, I want a workflow's generated-work budget enforced against my Run before the
   `br create`, so runaway work never reaches the backlog.
4. As an operator, I want to intervene in any stage without destroying the work in flight.
5. As an operator, I want cancellation to actually reach every worker the Run owns.

## Acceptance Criteria

Validation rejects, with a message naming the offending transition:

1. A transition targeting an ancestor stage without `back-edge: true`.
2. An automatic Generator with no literal iteration bound.
3. A bounded loop whose exhaustion outcome transitions back inside the loop it exits.
4. A named stage outcome with no mapped transition.
5. A transition whose target skill does not resolve against the discovered skill manifest.
6. A stage from which no terminal stage is reachable.
7. A stage unreachable from the entry stage.
8. A stage declaring a detached or fire-and-forget worker the Run does not own.

Validation is pure:

9. Given any workflow document, when Validation runs, then no Agent is started, no `br` command is
   run, no git or network access occurs, and no document content enters a context window.
10. Given ambiguity in a document, Validation rejects rather than inferring — no model in the loop.
11. Given an unchanged document and manifest, Validation returns a cached result keyed on
    `hash(document) + hash(manifest)`. Adding an unrelated skill invalidates the cache.

Escape and cancellation:

12. Every stage has a synthesized, non-destructive human escape transition the author does not write
    and cannot remove; taking it Parks the Run.
13. The escape is takeable unilaterally by the operator, with no Agent outcome required and no Agent
    cooperation needed — verified against a deliberately wedged mock agent.
14. A global emergency stop exists, is destructive (Disposal), and is not the ordinary intervention.
15. Cancellation walks the Run's supervision tree; the wait for acknowledgment is bounded and a
    silent worker escalates to Disposal.

Budget:

16. Generated work is attributed to the Run through the `--actor "<session id>"` provenance already
    required by AGENTS.md, and the budget is per-Run, so a human filing bugs by hand is unaffected.
17. Exceeding the budget Parks the Run rather than killing it or silently degrading it.

## Implementation Notes

- Frontmatter parsing reuses the existing lyaml path (`lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua`); this is
  the reason `louiselm-4gif` refused a hand-rolled parser, so parser correctness is now load-bearing
  beyond skills.
- Topology comes from structured frontmatter only, never prose — the settled `louiselm-uqip` ruling.
- Which skills a stage's Agent may invoke is a capability question and belongs to
  `louiselm-qbr.5.1`'s envelope, not to a second authority mechanism here. This feature depends on
  that boundary but must not reimplement it.
- Accepted coupling: "who resolves this transition" becomes a safety-relevant field. Changing a
  resolver from human to agent can turn a valid workflow invalid, so the attention model and the
  validator cannot be edited independently.
- Stated limit to write into the contract: cancellation reaches every worker LouiseLM can address,
  not every process. An ACP Agent ignoring both cancel and dispose is the outer harness's problem.

## Testing Notes

- Validation is a pure function and should be tested as one: a table of malformed documents against
  expected rejection identifiers, no fixtures beyond the document and a manifest.
- The wedged-agent escape test needs `lua/louiselm/dev/mock_agent.lua` extended to ignore
  cancellation.
- The generative-growth case deserves an explicit regression test asserting that budget, not cycle
  detection, is what stops it — the failure mode is a design that passes a DAG check forever.

## Out of Scope

- Durable Run state and Park expiry reaping — see the capture-service feature.
- Assessment (model reading prose) — separate feature, advisory, never gates.
- Capability envelopes themselves — `louiselm-qbr.5.1`.
- The full workflow execution engine — `louiselm-qbr.3` owns schema and runtime mechanics.

title: Rename louiselm.workflow to louiselm.routing to free the workflow namespace
description:
## Goal

Free the `louiselm.workflow` namespace for workflow definitions by renaming the existing
Agent-routing coordinator to `louiselm.routing`.

## Scope

- In scope: rename `lua/louiselm/workflow/` to `lua/louiselm/routing/` (approval, evidence, init,
  phase, routing, usage), rename `tests/workflow/` to `tests/routing/`, update every

  update the require sites in `lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua`,
  `lua/louiselm/skills/metadata.lua`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua`,
  `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`, `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`.
- Out of scope: any behaviour change, any new module, any file split. `routing.lua` staying inside
  `louiselm.routing` (giving `louiselm.routing.routing`) is acceptable for this task; renaming it is
  a separate judgement call, not part of a mechanical move.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No reference to `louiselm.workflow` remains anywhere outside `.git` — 223 references across 17
   files at the time of filing.
2. The full test suite passes with no behavioural diff; this is a pure rename.
3. `lua/louiselm/workflow/` does not exist, leaving the namespace free for `louiselm-qbr.3.2`'s
   validator.
4. Generated docs regenerate cleanly if `louiselm.schema.gen_luacats` / `gen_vimdoc` cover these
   types.

## Testing

- The existing `tests/workflow/*_spec.lua` suite, moved to `tests/routing/`, is the regression
  check. It must pass unchanged apart from the renamed requires.
- No new tests. If a test needs changing beyond its require line and type names, the rename has
  stopped being mechanical — stop and say so rather than adjusting the test.

## Notes

- Why: `louiselm.workflow` currently means *Agent routing* — `Coordinator:recommend(phase, state)`
  ranks Agents and Models, with approval and observed-reliability evidence. It has no stages, no
  transitions, no topology. The promoted vocabulary from the `louiselm-qbr.8` grill-me (Run,
  Generator, Validation, Assessment, Park) is entirely about workflows-as-stage-machines, which is
  also how `louiselm-qbr` uses the word throughout. The existing module is the misnamed one.
- Caught before either meaning has many callers. The cost is monotonically increasing, which is the
  whole argument for doing it now.
- Maintainer decision, 2026-08-26: "rename first, way more appropriate naming."

title: Define the workflow frontmatter schema and pure Validation rejection table
description:
## Goal

A pure function that accepts or rejects one workflow definition from its frontmatter, where the set
of rejections *is* the schema's specification.

## Scope

- In scope: the minimal workflow frontmatter schema (only the fields the eight rejections require,
  nothing speculative), a pure `validate(document, manifest)` in the freed `louiselm.workflow`
  namespace, and the rejection table with a stable identifier and message per case.
- Out of scope: purity enforcement and caching (own task), escape synthesis, cancellation,
  budgets, and any execution. No runtime, no Run, no Agent.

## Acceptance Criteria

Validation rejects, naming the offending stage or transition:

1. A transition targeting an ancestor stage without `back-edge: true`.
2. An automatic Generator (resolver is trigger, resolver, or agent) with no literal integer bound.
3. A bounded loop whose exhaustion outcome transitions back inside the loop it exits.
4. A named stage outcome with no mapped transition.
5. A transition whose target does not resolve against the discovered skill manifest.
6. A stage from which no terminal stage is reachable.
7. A stage unreachable from the entry stage.
8. A stage declaring a detached or fire-and-forget worker.

And:

9. A human-resolved back edge with no bound is ACCEPTED. This is the case a universal-bound rule
   would get wrong, and it must have an explicit passing test.
10. The result is binary. There is no warning severity, no `severity` field, and no option,
    flag, environment variable, or config key that permits a rejected definition to run.
11. Topology is read from structured frontmatter fields only. No prose is parsed, and no field is
    inferred from the document body.
12. The rejection identifier is stable and machine-readable, so callers can assert on the reason
    rather than on message text.

## Testing

- This is a pure function: test it as a table of `(document, manifest) -> expected identifier`,
  with no fixtures beyond those two inputs. No Neovim state, no filesystem, no mock agent.
- One accepting document per shape that is legal but looks suspicious: a human-resolved back edge
  with no bound, and a bounded automatic loop whose exhaustion exits correctly.
- A regression test asserting that a *generative* workflow (a stage that files tracker issues,
  minting a new id each pass) is not rejected by any cycle or reachability rule. It is legal
  topology; only a Run budget stops it. This test exists to prevent a future contributor from
  "fixing" unbounded growth with a graph check that cannot see it.

## Notes

- Blocked on the namespace rename; land that first.
- Parse frontmatter through the existing `lyaml` path used by `lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua`,
  as a data read. Do not route through skill activation: nothing here may enter a context window.
  `louiselm-4gif` kept lyaml deliberately, so parser correctness is now load-bearing beyond skills.
- `lua/louiselm/schema/` already provides a field/validator DSL (`louiselm.schema.Field`,
  `array-of`, `one-of`). Prefer expressing the frontmatter schema in it over a second hand-rolled
  shape checker.
- Design the schema from the rejections outward. Each rejection forces exactly one field into
  existence and no more; `louiselm-qbr.3` owns the eventual full schema and should inherit this
  minimum rather than a guess at it.
- The Generator is the bounding unit, not the back edge: a work-filing stage and an Agent invoking
  a work-producing skill are Generators too. Rejection 2 must be written against the Generator
  concept so the other two cases fall under it rather than needing new rules later.
close_reason: Completed: lua/louiselm/workflow/{init,schema,validate}.lua with tests/workflow/validate_spec.lua, 22 cases, all green. All eight rejections implemented with stable identifiers: undeclared_back_edge, unbounded_generator, exhaustion_inside_loop, unmapped_outcome, unresolved_target, no_reachable_terminal, unreachable_stage, unknown_field; plus duplicate_outcome, unnamed_outcome, missing_exhaustion_outcome, wrong_field_type, missing_entry, ambiguous_entry. Criterion 9 covered by an explicit ACCEPTING test for a human-resolved back edge with no bound. Criterion 10 covered by a test asserting no severity field and no override argument -- lua-language-server proves both statically, and the two diagnostics are suppressed with the justification that the warning is the assertion. Criterion 11 covered by a test that an unrecognized prose-carrying field rejects. Criterion 12 covered by asserting reason and message are distinct strings. The generative-growth regression asserts a work-filing workflow that grows without forming a cycle is ACCEPTED, so no future contributor can 'fix' unbounded growth with a graph check that cannot see it. Gates: MiniTest 46 spec files Fails (0) Notes (0); stylua --check clean; lua-language-server --check --checklevel=Warning no problems.

comments.author: claude/0929f4e1-c8f2-4717-998f-1902618ce5f8
comments.text:
Two design refinements made while implementing, both worth carrying into louiselm-qbr.3's full schema.

1. Rejection 8 (detached worker) is satisfied by OMISSION, not by a check. The schema gives no way to declare a detached or fire-and-forget worker, so the attempt surfaces as unknown_field. This is the same move as the synthesized escape in qbr.3.2.4: an obligation met by construction cannot be forgotten by a later contributor, and it costs a field nobody can write rather than a rule someone can delete. Consequence: the schema is closed -- any unrecognized key rejects.

2. Validation is rooted at a WORKFLOW NAME, not handed a single document. louiselm-uqip settled that a workflow is a set of discovered SKILL.md files with named outcomes mapping to next-skill transitions, so the graph is the transitive closure over the manifest, not one file's contents. Each stage block declares 'workflow: <name>' for membership and one declares 'entry: true'. Signature is validate(workflow, manifest) where manifest maps skill name to its parsed workflow block. This is what makes rejection 7 (unreachable stage) meaningful: without membership, everything reachable is reachable by construction and the rule could never fire. It also catches the real authoring error -- a typo in a 'to' silently orphaning a stage.

Implementation note worth keeping: back edges are classified by ANCESTRY from the entry via DFS, not by mutual reachability. The first attempt used 'target can reach source', which is symmetric -- in any cycle it marks the forward edge as a back edge too, and rejected the reference workflow. Caught by the accepting test for the reference loop, which is the argument for having written it.

title: Enforce and test Validation purity, and cache on document plus manifest
description:
## Goal

Make Validation's purity an enforced, tested property rather than a convention, and cache its result
on a correct key.

## Scope

- In scope: purity enforcement and its tests, the cache keyed on `hash(document) + hash(skill
  manifest)`, and manifest-change invalidation.
- Out of scope: the rejection rules themselves, anything runtime-scoped.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given any workflow document, when Validation runs, then no Agent process is started, no `br`
   command is run, no git or network access occurs, and no filesystem access happens beyond skill
   discovery.
2. No document content — frontmatter or prose — enters any context window.
3. Given an ambiguous or unparseable document, Validation rejects. It never resolves ambiguity by
   asking a model; there is no inference path.
4. Given an unchanged document and manifest, a second Validation returns the cached result without
   re-parsing.
5. Given an unrelated skill added to the manifest, the cache is invalidated. This is correct, not a
   bug: transition-target resolution depends on which skills exist.
6. A changed document invalidates only its own entry.

## Testing

- Purity is asserted by the test harness observing that the forbidden calls did not happen, not by
  reading the implementation. Stub or intercept the process, `br`, and network paths and assert
  zero invocations.
- Cache-key behaviour is deterministic: same inputs, one parse; manifest delta, two.
- An explicit test that adding an unrelated skill invalidates a cached result, so the coupling is
  documented as intentional rather than discovered later as a stale-cache bug.

## Notes

- The manifest dependency is the non-obvious part and belongs in the contract, not in a comment.
- Ambiguity-rejects is the same rule as no-override at a different level: an inference escape hatch
  would recreate "run it anyway" one layer down.
close_reason: Implemented document and manifest keyed Validation cache

title: Synthesize an unremovable human escape into every stage
description:
## Goal

Every stage carries a human escape the author never writes and cannot remove, and taking it Parks
the Run without destroying work.

## Scope

- In scope: runtime synthesis of a non-destructive human escape transition into every stage,
  Validation checking the synthesized graph, the destructive global emergency stop, and optional
  author-declared domain escapes.
- Out of scope: the Park record's durability and expiry (`louiselm-qbr.3.3`), budget accounting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every stage has a synthesized human escape transition; the author writes nothing and cannot
   suppress it.
2. Validation runs against the synthesized graph, so the reachable-human-override obligation is
   satisfied by construction and cannot fail.
3. The escape is takeable unilaterally by the operator: no Agent outcome is required and no Agent
   cooperation is needed. Verified against a mock agent that ignores everything.
4. Taking the escape Parks the Run — turns Cancelled, Sessions retained — and does not Dispose.
5. A global emergency stop exists, is destructive (Disposal of the whole Run), and is separate from
   the escape.
6. An author-declared escape with domain semantics is accepted and is optional; its absence is
   never a rejection.

## Testing

- The wedged-agent test is the important one. `lua/louiselm/dev/mock_agent.lua` needs a variant that
  ignores cancellation, so that "reachable in the graph but unreachable in fact" is actually
  exercised.
- Assert the escape is enforced at the runtime's transition boundary, not delivered to the Agent as
  a request it may decline.

## Notes

- Graph reachability of a human gate is NOT the property wanted: a gate two hops away behind an
  Agent-only edge is reachable on paper and unreachable behind a hung Agent. Synthesis is what makes
  the correct property trivially true, which is most of why it was chosen over an authoring rule.
- A global stop alone does not satisfy the invariant, because it is destructive. The property is
  "a human can intervene without losing the work", not "a human can end this".
close_reason: Implemented synthesized human Park escape and emergency stop

comments.text: Implemented and verified: Workflow.validate now validates a copied graph with a reserved human __louiselm_park terminal outcome synthesized on every stage; Run:park requests cooperative cancellation without waiting or disposing, and Run:emergency_stop remains destructive. Tests cover graph immutability, synthesized validation, wedged-agent Park retention, emergency stop, cooperative cancellation, bounded escalation, and ownership. Full suite: 604 cases, 0 failures; stylua, lua-language-server, and git diff --check pass. Lesson: keep the human escape as a runtime-synthesized reserved outcome and keep Park separate from bounded Cancellation, because Park must remain available when an Agent ignores cancellation. No further destination warranted.

title: Enforce Run ownership and bounded-ack Cancellation escalating to Disposal
description:
## Goal

Cancellation reaches every worker a Run owns, because no worker can exist outside the Run's
supervision tree.

## Scope

- In scope: the ownership invariant and its Validation rejection, the supervision tree, broadcast
  Cancellation with bounded acknowledgment, and escalation to Disposal for a silent worker.
- Out of scope: durable Run state, Park expiry, budgets.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A Run owns a supervision tree of Sessions; no Session created during a Run exists outside it.
2. A workflow declaring a detached or fire-and-forget worker is rejected by Validation.
3. A skill invoked by a stage's Agent inherits Run ownership by construction, because the
   invocation happened inside a Run-owned Session. This needs an explicit test, since it is the
   case that motivated the whole contract.
4. Cancellation walks the tree and reaches every owned worker.
5. The wait for acknowledgment is bounded by a declared value; it is not open-ended.
6. A worker that has not acknowledged within the bound is escalated to Disposal.
7. Cooperative cancellation is attempted first as the fast path but is never the guarantee.
8. The contract states its limit explicitly in code documentation: propagation reaches every worker
   LouiseLM can address, not every process. An ACP Agent ignoring both cancel and dispose is the
   outer harness's problem.

## Testing

- A wedged mock agent that acknowledges nothing must end Disposed within the bound, not hang.
- An ordinary agent must Cancel cooperatively without ever reaching the Disposal escalation.
- The invoked-skill inheritance test should mirror the motivating scenario: a stage Agent invoking
  a work-producing skill, then the Run cancelled, then the invoked work stopped.

## Notes

- An unbounded wait-for-ack is exactly the "cancellation path that does not reach every active
  worker" the design set out to prevent: it reaches them and then hangs, which is indistinguishable
  from not reaching them.
- Cooperative cancel is unreliable precisely in the case being cancelled — the wedged Agent — which
  is why it is the fast path and not the mechanism.
close_reason: All acceptance criteria satisfied. Most of the ownership/bounded-cancellation contract was already implemented and tested by prior work in this tree; audit details and what was actually added (the invoked-skill-inherits-ownership test) are in the preceding comment. Full suite (742 cases) and stylua clean.

comments.author: claude/ea8b846d-3700-44ed-aa39-ffb9e68c8973
comments.text:
## Audit

Before implementing anything, checked each acceptance criterion against the current codebase.
Almost the entire contract was already implemented and tested by prior work on this tree
(`qbr.3.2.1`-`.4`):

1. "No Session created during a Run exists outside it" -- satisfied by construction:
   `Run:create_session` is the only Run-aware session-creation path and always calls
   `adopt_session`, which is the only way into `self.workers`. Tested:
   `tests/workflow/run_spec.lua` "creates stage Sessions through the Run owner".
2. "A detached/fire-and-forget worker declaration is rejected" -- already done via the schema's
   closed-world unknown-field rejection (`lua/louiselm/workflow/schema.lua`'s own comment:
   "There is no way to declare a detached or fire-and-forget worker, so a document that tries
   produces an unknown field"). Tested by name in `tests/workflow/validate_spec.lua`: "a stage
   declaring a detached worker" and "a stage declaring a fire-and-forget worker".
4-7. Bounded-ack Cancellation with Disposal escalation -- already fully implemented in
   `Run:cancel` (`lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua`) and tested in the `T["cancellation"]` group:
   cooperative cancel without disposal, disposal after the bound for a non-acknowledging worker,
   and Cancellation reaching every owned worker.
8. The contract's limit is already stated in `Run:cancel`'s docstring almost verbatim to this
   criterion's wording ("covers every worker LouiseLM can address, not every process...").

The only gap was criterion 3 and its matching Testing bullet: an explicit test for "a skill
invoked by a stage's Agent inherits Run ownership by construction... since it is the case that
motivated the whole contract." `Executor` (`lua/louiselm/workflow/executor.lua`) is a pure stage
state machine with zero Session/ACP coupling today (no live wiring from a stage's Agent to a
skill invocation exists yet -- that's `qbr.3`'s still-deferred workflow execution engine, out of
this issue's scope), so there is no real end-to-end path to test this against yet. Added the
most faithful test buildable at the current architectural layer: a stage Session already owned
by a Run, whose Agent invokes a skill that reaches the Run through the same
`Run:create_session` every other stage worker uses (mid-flight, after the Run already has one
worker) -- proving it is owned the moment it exists and that cancelling the Run reaches it too,
with no special-casing for how or when it was created. This test passed against the existing
implementation with no code change required; it fills a documentation/coverage gap, not a bug.

Full suite (742 cases) and `stylua --check .` clean.

title: Bound generated work per Run and Park on exhaustion
description:
## Goal

A Run that generates more work than its budget allows Parks for an operator decision, before the
work reaches the backlog.

## Scope

- In scope: per-Run accounting of generated work, attribution through the `--actor "<session id>"`
  provenance, admission checks at stage entry and spawn, and Park on exhaustion.
- Out of scope: the durable Park record and the expiry reaper (`louiselm-qbr.3.3`), capability
  envelopes (`louiselm-qbr.5.1`), Assessment.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Work generated during a Run is attributed to that Run through the `--actor` session id already
   required by `AGENTS.md:30`.
2. The budget is checked BEFORE the mutation, not reconciled after: an over-budget `br create` never
   happens.
3. The budget is per-Run. A human filing issues by hand, or a second concurrent Run, is unaffected.
4. Exceeding the budget Parks the Run. It does not Dispose it, and it does not silently remove the
   generating capability.
5. Resuming a Parked Run with a raised budget is an operator act. A request originating from an
   Agent is refused.
6. A resumed Run may not exceed the original envelope on any axis other than the raised budget.
7. Admission surfaces the budget and its consumption to the operator at the Park.

## Testing

- The motivating scenario end to end: a qa-review stage whose Agent invokes a work-producing skill
  repeatedly, Parking at the bound with the expected number of issues created and no more.
- A regression test asserting that the beads graph in that scenario contains NO cycle — `br dep
  cycles` is clean throughout — proving the budget, not cycle detection, is what stopped it.
- Attribution is verifiable through `br` actor fields; assert on the actor string, not on counts
  alone.
- A concurrent-Run test showing budgets do not pool.

## Notes

- Blocked on `louiselm-qbr.3.3`: a budget that Parks needs somewhere durable to Park into, and an
  expiry that fires while Neovim is closed.
- Degrading instead of Parking was rejected: an Agent that cannot file issues writes them into its
  transcript, which is unbounded growth somewhere with no schema, no provenance and no actor.
  Removing the mechanism does not remove the pressure.
- `br policy.yaml` capacities were investigated and rejected as the bound: workspace-global, no Run
  concept, and they fire after the work exists.
close_reason: Completed: all seven acceptance criteria proven by the closed child slices and current Lua/Rust gates.
