title: Workflow documents cannot become stage manifests: no frontmatter path exists
description:
## Observed

Found on 2026-08-30 while scoping `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5.3`, which had been written on the assumption that a workflow fixture could be authored as real `SKILL.md` documents and fed through the existing discovery path.

There is no such path. The workflow validator and executor consume a stage manifest — a table keyed by stage name whose blocks carry `workflow`, `entry`, `outcomes`, `generates`, `back-edge`, `max-iterations`, `on-exhausted`, `generated-work`, and `park-expiry` — and **nothing in the codebase constructs one from a document**.

Evidence:

- `lua/louiselm/skills/metadata.lua:132` (`M.skill`) is the only SKILL.md frontmatter parser. It extracts exactly `name`, `description`, `metadata.short-description`, `disable-model-invocation`, and `phase`. Grepping it for any workflow stage key returns zero hits.
- Every workflow stage key (`outcomes`, `generates`, `back-edge`, `max-iterations`, `on-exhausted`, `generated-work`, `park-expiry`) appears nowhere in the non-test Lua tree outside `lua/louiselm/workflow/` itself.
- Every manifest that exists is a hand-built Lua table inside a spec: `tests/workflow/{executor,validate,cache,run}_spec.lua`.

## Why this matters

`louiselm-qbr.8` settled that workflows persist as graphs of discovered `SKILL.md` documents whose frontmatter declares named outcomes and transitions. `lua/louiselm/workflow/validate.lua` implements the full structural contract for that shape — bounded back-edges, Generator maxima, exhaustion-outcome reachability — and it is thorough. But it validates a shape that only tests ever produce.

The practical consequence is the same class of gap `louiselm-qbr.3.6` closed for stage execution and `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5.2` closed for the ledger: a fully specified contract with no production path reaching it. A workflow author cannot today write a workflow document at all.

## Deliberately not folded into the slice that found it

`louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5.3` was rescoped to a hand-built looping manifest rather than absorbing this work. Building the document-to-manifest parser is the next piece of `louiselm-qbr.3`'s execution engine, which remains deferred, and quietly building it inside a mock-Agent test-double slice is exactly the scope reallocation that the 2026-08-27 pause on `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5` correctly refused to make.

This is also not a blocker for `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5`'s acceptance. AC4 is a claim about budget enforcement — that a generating loop Parks at its ceiling having created exactly that many issues. A manifest bounds the loop identically whether it was parsed from YAML or written as a table, so the budget contract is provable without this. What is not provable without it is that a *workflow author's document* produces the manifest the budget then bounds.

## Fix direction

Parse the workflow stage block out of SKILL.md frontmatter and assemble the per-workflow manifest that `Workflow.validate` and `Workflow.new_executor` already accept. Reuse `skills/discovery.lua`'s traversal and `lyaml` rather than adding a second frontmatter reader. Keep it structural and total, matching the Validation vocabulary record (`louiselm-p5h0`): parsing decides shape, never prose.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A discovered `SKILL.md` declaring workflow stage frontmatter yields a manifest block that `Workflow.validate` accepts, without any hand-built table.
- A document set spanning several files assembles into one manifest keyed by stage name, and stages belonging to other workflows are excluded.
- Malformed or contradictory stage frontmatter is rejected with an actionable diagnostic rather than silently dropped, and a document with no workflow frontmatter is simply not a stage.
- The existing hand-built manifests in specs can be replaced by parsed fixtures for at least one end-to-end case.

## Not covered

Executing the parsed workflow (owned by `louiselm-qbr.3.6`), Assessment of document prose, and the remainder of `louiselm-qbr.3`.
close_reason: Parse workflow stage frontmatter into validated manifests

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
**Candidate requirement for this issue's design — not a settled decision.**

When a workflow engine sequences beads work on the operator's behalf, it should
default to draining in-progress or claimed work before opening new work, even
when a scoring pass ranks an unstarted item higher. That is what a human
operator does by hand, and it is the behaviour the current tooling cannot
express.

**Evidence.** `bv`'s triage score is a weighted sum over eight components.
Urgency (weight 0.1) already rewards in-progress work — raw 1.0 for
`in_progress` against 0.8 for `open` — but it is one component among eight. A
fresh `open` task carrying a real `blocks` edge (BlockerRatio, weight 0.13) plus
a deeper unlock chain (TimeToImpact, weight 0.1) out-scores an in-progress epic
comfortably. Measured in this repo: a two-paragraph policy doc scored ~0.459
against ~0.405 for an in-progress epic covering an entire ACP client.

None of the five built-in weight presets fix this. `priority-first` raises
Urgency only to ~0.146, still not a gate, and there is no custom-weights file.
So the preference cannot be extracted from `bv` by configuration. It has to be
applied on top of its output — which is why it belongs in the engine that
consumes that output rather than in the scorer.

The sequencing policy is this issue's to define. This comment records why the
question exists and what the evidence was, so the design conversation does not
have to re-derive it.

title: Enforce Run capabilities through a local control broker
description:
## Problem Statement

A Run capability envelope has no security value unless every governed effect reaches an enforcement boundary. ACP permission requests are cooperative, the current reusable Run token can leak through environment state, and direct networking, credentials, package fetching, and canonical Beads writes bypass policy.

## Solution

Create a local-only control service under a dedicated unprivileged identity. The trusted launcher gives each Session a unique Unix capability channel bound to its Session, Run, envelope revision, and peer identity. The broker enforces attenuating capabilities and mediates Provider egress, credentials, dependencies, privileged tool effects, and canonical Beads mutations.

Agents retain fast native `br`/`bvr` reads against disposable local replicas. The broker invokes the real pinned `br` for typed canonical mutations and returns revisioned receipts.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want one inspectable Run envelope enforced outside the Agent.
2. As a coordinator, I want child authority to attenuate rather than inherit every Session capability.
3. As an operator, I want reusable Provider credentials kept outside every Session.
4. As an Agent, I want ordinary locked dependencies and tracker operations to work through typed requests.
5. As a coordinator, I want workers to initiate claims, comments, findings, and transitions while preserving one canonical graph.
6. As an operator, I want broker loss to preserve work without silently degrading enforcement.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Effective authority is the intersection of launcher ceiling, operator-approved Run, stage, parent, task/worker, child command, revision, expiry, and Verified posture. Workflow or Agent prose may propose but never grant authority.
2. The launcher binds the full Agent channel to exactly one supervisor-authenticated, lifetime-pinned Agent-runtime process plus Session, Run and envelope revision. Per-message kernel credentials must match. Bubblewrap reaper identity, assigned UID/GID, Session membership, ancestry, self-reported PID and first connection alone confer no authority. No reusable secret appears in arguments, environment, prompts, files, or Agent-visible logs.
3. Tools and internal helpers require explicit narrower grants across an enforced isolation boundary, not voluntary child restraint. Automatic delegation requires existing operator approval explicitly permitting it; a subset alone is insufficient. Scope, revision, expiry and delegation permission are broker-enforced; descendants gain no authority by ancestry.
4. The broker exposes local authenticated IPC only, runs under a stable dedicated non-root identity with exact state/Beads ACLs, and shares neither operator nor capture-service identity.
5. Typed policy covers filesystem and destructive effects, process execution, network destination, disclosure, credentials, external mutation, dependencies, cost, delegation, and expiry. Unknown or contradictory effects fail closed.
6. Reusable Provider credentials remain broker-side. Provider requests reach only the configured endpoint within operation and cost limits. A runtime that cannot use brokered or ephemeral authentication cannot launch verified.
7. Sessions have no ambient network. Additional destinations remain inside exact grants across DNS resolution, redirects, protocol, and operation.
8. Starting-lockfile dependencies may be fetched automatically only by exact coordinate and integrity value. The broker downloads without executing package code and writes only the Session cache overlay.
9. New dependency coordinates are typed candidates. Interactive approval may batch them; unattended Runs require pre-authorized scope. Git dependencies, arbitrary URLs, missing integrity, and non-registry sources require explicit approval; Agent-chosen names are not sent externally first.
10. Native `br` and `bvr --robot-*` read refreshed local replicas. Canonical mutations are typed requests: the broker derives the attributable Session actor, enforces role/envelope/revision/idempotency/budget, invokes pinned upstream `br` with controlled temporary storage, returns a receipt, and refreshes the replica.
11. Workers may initiate ordinary tracker mutations. Only the coordinator may dispatch, promote blockers, satisfy integration gates, publish canonical state, and close work. No Session can write canonical `.beads` or JSONL directly.
12. Optional out-of-envelope actions are denied. Required actions create one deduplicated escalation naming the missing capability and narrowest expansion; prose cannot grant it.
13. Revocation closes channels before cleanup, removes egress/credentials, stops children that cannot continue, and preserves workspace state. Authenticated Agent exit revokes its channel and all delegated grants; helpers, replacement processes and recycled PIDs cannot inherit authority. Replacement requires a fresh authorized launch. Completed external effects are reported, never called rolled back.
14. Broker or durable-receipt failure stops new privileged effects. After bounded grace, the launcher freezes the Session; the controller records Park and Attention. Recovery never silently broadens authority.
15. Durable records contain normalized envelope revisions, decisions, effects, identities, and references—not prompts, full commands/diffs, environments, credentials, or raw payloads.
16. Remembered interactive permissions may narrow an active envelope but cannot expand it. ACP permissions and Agent promises remain evidence only.
17. Refuse Verified launch if the exact integration cannot enforce Agent/tool authority separation. Ordinary Sessions may remain usable without claiming that protection. After sequence-0 durable ACK, restricted initialization has no brokered effects until actual Agent identity and tool isolation verify; then enable capabilities, record Start/Running, and wait for sequence-1 durable ACK before launch success. Failure ends launch.
18. Effects requested by the Agent on a tool's behalf remain Agent actions subject to its permissions, approval requirements and audit. Tool isolation does not imply immunity to hostile tool output influencing the Agent.

## Implementation Notes

- This replaces the former cooperative supported-path model; do not build a parallel capability system.
- Separate pure envelope/policy rules from IPC and effect adapters.
- Capture-service owns Attention delivery and durable projections but never authorization.
- Invoke upstream `br`; do not reimplement its graph/workflow/storage semantics.
- Delete the `LOUISELM_RUN_TOKEN` path rather than retaining a fallback.

## Testing Notes

- Use fake launcher channels and external adapters for deterministic tests.

title: Broker one authorized launch through a durable receipt
description:
## Goal

Make the unprivileged Control broker authorize one exact verified launch, persist the exact signed Launcher receipt, and enable the Session capability channel only after durability.

## Scope

- In scope: durable pending launch authorization; bounded identity-slot assignment; supervisor authentication; exact receipt append and fsync acknowledgement; operator authorization audit; initial canonical Session status; actual Agent identity and lifetime proof; enforced tool isolation; one explicit narrower delegated grant; fail-closed launch integration.
- Out of scope: later lifecycle recovery, Provider egress, credentials, dependencies, Beads mutation, and capture-service authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The broker stores a short-lived single-use pending authorization binding exact launch-request digest, controller identity, Session and Run, envelope revision, authorization ID, and one slot from the installed UID/GID pool.
2. Authorization is consumed atomically. Restart, duplicate delivery, expiry, mismatched controller, request digest, revision, Session, or assigned identity cannot produce a second launch.
3. The broker authenticates the supervisor through kernel credentials at the fixed rendezvous and validates the sequence-0 signature, release ID, key ID, authorization, state, and chain prefix before storage.
4. The broker stores the exact signed receipt bytes as canonical data and fsyncs them before acknowledging. It cannot rewrite, reserialize, or sign a launcher outcome.
5. Enforce exact sequence-0 Launch/Starting durable ACK -> restricted Agent initialization with brokered effects disabled -> actual Agent identity and tool-isolation verification -> capability enablement -> sequence-1 Start/Running durable ACK -> launch success. Verification or durability failure ends launch with a stable error and existing cleanup-proof discipline.
6. Full Agent authority binds exactly one supervisor-authenticated, lifetime-pinned Agent-runtime process plus Session, Run, channel, envelope revision and assigned identity. Per-message kernel credentials must match; reaper PID, membership, ancestry, self-claims and first connection are insufficient. Tools/helpers require explicitly narrower grants with operator-permitted delegation, scope/revision/expiry checks and enforced isolation. Agent exit revokes its channel and all delegated grants; replacement requires fresh launch authorization. Agent requests on a tool's behalf remain Agent actions under its permissions/approvals/audit, not prompt-injection immunity.
7. Initial session inspect state and the operator audit identify bounded normalized IDs and outcomes without prompts, environments, credentials, or hostile text.

## Testing

- Red-green broker tests with a fake supervisor cover restart, expiry, replay, concurrent consume, pool exhaustion, credential mismatch, receipt mutation/signature failure, fsync failure, ACK ordering, capability enablement, hostile Agent identity claims, child denial, and parent proxying.
- Run the owning crate gates and protocol compatibility fixtures.

## Notes

This is the launch aggregate. Independently completable children: .1 durable broker transaction; .2 actual Agent identity; .3 zero-authority tool isolation; .4 explicit delegation and revocation; .5 real launch integration. Child parent-child edges alone model aggregate completion; do not add reverse aggregate-blocks-child edges. Component test success cannot close the aggregate before the integration child or establish installed-release Verified posture.

The broker decides policy and owns canonical bytes; the Launch supervisor signs outcomes; capture-service is not part of the authority path.

title: Authenticate and lifetime-pin the actual Agent process
description:
## Goal

Let only the one supervisor-authenticated Agent runtime use its full capability channel, without mistaking the Bubblewrap reaper or another Session member for that runtime.

## Scope

In: supervisor-side actual Agent identity proof, process-lifetime pin, capability packet authentication, bounded restricted-startup gate, revocation on Agent exit. Out: real broker persistence, granting tools authority, full tool confinement, runtime wrappers and installed-release cutover.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Derive the actual Agent process from trusted launch/kernel evidence and pin its lifetime. Session UID/GID, cgroup membership, ancestry, a caller-supplied PID, or being the first connector is never sufficient to select the principal. Verify the intended measured runtime; reject unsupported startup shapes with a stable error.
2. Preserve Bubblewrap PID1 reaping. Do not introduce a runtime wrapper, --as-pid-1, a root daemon, or stateless supervisor takeover. Document the chosen identity proof, rejected alternatives and races; if existing constraints cannot support a sound proof, file a concrete blocking design question rather than weakening them.
3. Bind Session, Run, channel, envelope revision, assigned identity and pinned Agent lifetime; enforce kernel per-message credentials. Passed/inherited descriptors, helpers and tools cannot impersonate the Agent.
4. After sequence-0 durable ACK, restricted runtime initialization may establish identity but performs no brokered effects. Keep capability access disabled until both identity and tool-isolation evidence validate. This slice can use a fake isolation verifier; production missing evidence remains denied.
5. Agent exit revokes its channel before cleanup and emits the terminal authority event consumed by delegation. A recycled PID, exec/startup mismatch, stale callback or replacement cannot inherit authority; replacement requires a fresh authorized launch.

## Testing

Red-green real local process fixtures plus deterministic supervisor doubles: reaper mistaken for Agent, sibling/child connects first, hostile self-reported PID, descriptor passing, UID/GID mismatch, exit during observation, lifetime reuse/stale event, missing isolation evidence, bounded startup failure and cleanup. Production async callback contexts; all skills-core gates.

## Notes

Entry points: skills-core/src/sandbox/host_identity.rs, sandbox.rs, launch_supervisor.rs, launch_supervisor/system.rs, launch_transport.rs. Current sandbox_leader_pid is the reaper anchor, not packet identity; SystemCapabilityGate currently admits Session members and retains a connection without dispatch. Source: confirmed louiselm-9onz. A PID filter alone is not tool isolation.

title: Confine a zero-authority tool outside the Agent runtime
description:
## Goal

Run a repository-controlled tool without allowing it to acquire or modify the authenticated Agent runtime's authority.

## Scope

In: one production tool-execution boundary owned by the existing per-Session supervisor, a measured integration contract, zero-authority command execution, protected Agent state and deterministic hostile-tool tracer. Out: nonzero tool grants, real Provider/vendor integration rollout, generic effect mediation and installed-release cutover.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Use the existing per-Session supervisor for confinement mechanics and broker policy for authorization; expose a bounded typed tool-execution path rather than accepting Agent-selected privileged commands/mounts/identities. The Agent remains unprivileged.
2. Keep repository tool code outside the trusted Agent process, including in-process plugins. The tool cannot read/control Agent private memory or authority-bearing runtime state, alter its measured executable/configuration, impersonate it, or obtain its capability channel. Intentional workspace access and returned tool output remain distinct from trusted runtime state.
3. Tool descendants acquire no implicit broker authority. Prove denial through inherited/passed descriptors, direct socket attempts and available cross-process control paths; ordinary Session UID/cgroup isolation is insufficient.
4. Produce checkable compatibility evidence for the exact measured integration; missing or mismatched evidence denies capability enablement and Verified launch. A cooperative promise or toy fixture is not evidence that an arbitrary installed Agent is supported.
5. Support a deterministic measured test integration without adding a runtime wrapper or changing Bubblewrap reaping. Unsupported integrations remain refused. Record a blocking design question if a necessary new mechanism exceeds these confirmed constraints.

## Testing

Red-green hostile repository command attempts broker access, Agent-state mutation, cross-process control and descendant bypass; a permitted workspace-only command succeeds. Include unset/unsupported integration and post-disposal callbacks. Use deterministic fixtures, no real Agent binaries/network/credentials; skills-core gates.

## Notes

title: Broker one explicit attenuated tool grant and revoke it
description:
## Goal

Allow an isolated tool to perform only an explicitly delegated effect and lose that authority when its Agent exits.

## Scope

In: a bounded typed grant for one isolated tool, operator-approved delegation permission, scope/revision/expiry checks, attributable requests, revocation on parent Agent exit. Out: Provider credentials/egress, dependency/Beads adapters, lifecycle recovery, UI approval collection and broad automatic delegation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Only the authenticated Agent may request a narrower tool grant. Existing operator authorization must explicitly permit delegation; a subset alone is insufficient. Reject new power, unapproved delegation, stale revisions, expiry and amplification without silently expanding authority.
2. Bind each grant/channel to its intended authenticated tool and Session/Run/envelope context. Internal helpers also need narrower explicit grants; tool descendants cannot inherit or redelegate by ancestry.
3. Check identity, scope, expiry, revision and live parent authority on each request. Exercise a bounded existing effect or deterministic effect adapter without inventing a new product effect API. Audit normalized attribution and outcome, not prompts/full commands/secrets.
4. Revoke the Agent channel and all its delegated grants on authenticated Agent exit; queued, in-flight-not-yet-committed and late requests cannot start new effects after revocation. Report already completed external effects honestly, never promise rollback.
5. A request the Agent makes itself on a tool's behalf is attributed to the Agent and subject to its permissions and approval requirements. This is not a guarantee against hostile tool output influencing Agent decisions.

## Testing

Red-green one granted effect succeeds; ungranted test/helper/descendant denied; subset-without-delegation denied; approved automatic attenuation succeeds; expiry/revision/replay/identity mismatch denied; Agent exit cascades to all grants, including race/late callbacks. Owning-crate gates; effect doubles remain deterministic.

## Notes

Source: confirmed louiselm-9onz. Reuse the durable broker, authenticated Agent and isolated tool boundary. No extra operator prompt is required only when delegation is already explicitly approved; approval UI and broader effect adapters remain separate.

title: Gate real broker launch on Agent and tool authority proofs
description:
## Goal

Make the real broker launch path fail closed unless authenticated Agent identity and enforced tool isolation are both established.

## Scope

In: integrate production broker/supervisor initial launch, compatibility preflight, restricted startup, authenticated channel enablement, truthful initial receipts/status and hostile launch tracer. Out: later recovery/status expansion and installed-release or real-vendor Verified cutover.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Wire the real Control broker, installed identity configuration and per-Session supervisor; retain exact request authorization and receipt ownership. Reject known unsupported integrations before launch; discovery failures during restricted startup dispose the attempted Session.
2. Enforce the full order: exact sequence-0 Launch/Starting durable ACK; restricted Agent initialization without brokered effects; actual Agent identity plus tool-isolation verification; capability enablement; sequence-1 Start/Running durable ACK; launch success. Neither first connector nor reaper identity can satisfy the gate.
3. Initial status distinguishes Starting, verified prerequisites, disabled/enabled channel and durable receipt head without claiming Running early. Failed identity/isolation/ACK leaves no successful authorized launch and a stable bounded diagnostic; clean up or retain poisoned identity according to existing cleanup-proof rules.
4. Through production request paths, the intended Agent can use its authorized channel, an ungranted repository tool cannot, an explicitly granted tool is constrained, and Agent exit revokes all grants. Prove ordinary/unsupported Sessions are not mislabeled.
5. Update production-facing fixtures/docs and preserve existing launch/lifecycle boundaries. End-to-end installed release and every real supported Agent still require louiselm-d6fv.9; do not enable the user-visible fully Verified claim from component tests.

## Testing

A deterministic fake measured Agent/tool runs against real broker/supervisor paths and injected signer/receipt failures; capture exact async event order. Gate early effects, unauthorized child/first connector, missing proof, failed seq0/seq1 fsync, Agent exit, late callbacks and truthful status. All affected Rust/browser gates.

## Notes

Source: confirmed louiselm-9onz; final integration child of louiselm-qbr.5.1.1. Later lifecycle recovery remains louiselm-qbr.5.1.2. No runtime wrapper or Bubblewrap reaping change is authorized.

description:

title: Authorize one Agent command across broker and supervisor
description:
## Goal
Execute one intended Agent command through the real authenticated capability path using a single-use broker decision and supervisor-local identity/commit checks.

## Scope
In: replace the delegation component's in-process commit assumption, bounded typed supervisor attribution/authorization/result records, authenticated Agent dispatch, durable broker intent/budget, supervisor final start checks, Agent-policy revocation and uncertain outcomes. Out: delegated helper creation (next sibling), reconnect/recovery, installation and user-visible Verified cutover.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The supervisor owns actual Agent process pins and capability sockets; forwards only per-packet authenticated Session/Run/principal attribution. The broker cannot manufacture authority from a peer-claimed PID. Unknown fields and contradictory subjects are rejected at this closed boundary.
2. The broker evaluates existing approved policy, validates exact command/scope/revision/expiry and spends one authorization/budget before dispatch. No extra mandatory human prompt. Supervisor-local final checks reject wrong/replaced/dead principal, expired/revoked policy and stale/replayed authorization immediately before actual start.
3. Agent command requests round-trip through SystemCapabilityGate, real broker policy and existing isolated tool mechanics. An ungranted child/first connector cannot execute through the Agent's channel. Preserve the separate principal-local and supervisor Session-wide sequences.
4. Broker revocation stops approvals immediately; supervisor prevents queued starts and cancels the affected running command before successful acknowledgement. Local deadlines enforce expiry with the same stop semantics. Failed cleanup stays explicit and follows existing poison rules.
5. Lost/uncertain execution keeps authorization spent, returns unknown without automatic retry, and accepts a late authenticated actual outcome after revocation. Commands/output/prompts/secrets stay out of normalized audit.
6. Port unchanged delegation scope/replay/budget/lifetime/audit/late-outcome coverage. Before replacing tests, record that only the old same-process commit assumption and start-only expiry behavior are superseded by the confirmed contract.

## Testing
Deterministic measured Agent and actual seqpacket paths; barriers around queued/start/revoke/expiry races, malformed/cross-Session attribution, replay, dead/replaced Agent, audit failure, lost reply and late outcome. Focused plus full affected Rust/browser gates. No new dependencies, unsafe operations, runtime wrapper or root policy owner.

## Notes
Primary seams: broker/delegation*, launch_protocol/tool.rs, launch_supervisor/system.rs, tool_dispatch.rs and tool_execution.rs. Full contract and provenance: louiselm-cross-process-tool-commit-z288. Retained connection is a prerequisite. Delegated tools remain denied until the next sibling.

title: Exercise an explicit tool grant through isolated production channels
description:
## Goal
Let one supervisor-authenticated isolated tool use an explicitly attenuated grant through the real broker and prove revocation/expiry cancels only the authority it owns.

## Scope
In: measured deterministic helper integration, trusted tool process/channel proof, explicit Agent-requested delegation, per-grant execution and cancellation. Out: automatic descendant authority, generic helper plugins, vendor Agent integration, later lifecycle recovery and installed Verified cutover.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Supervisor creates and authenticates an isolated tool principal and its own channel using trusted launch/kernel evidence. It cannot access Agent-private material or inherit the Agent capability channel. Membership, ancestry and first connection never suffice.
2. Only the authenticated Agent may request a narrower grant, and only existing operator approval permitting delegation authorizes it. Broker owns scope/expiry/revision checks and non-refundable aggregate budget reservation.
3. Each granted tool command uses the preceding single-use authorization path. Requests outside scope, revision, budget, lifetime or expiry fail closed; a tool cannot redelegate or amplify authority by cloning/reconnecting.
4. Revocation immediately stops broker approvals; supervisor rejects queued starts, terminates affected running tool command trees, and acknowledges only confirmed enforcement/termination. Grant expiry behaves identically without waiting for broker notification; earlier command timeouts apply.
5. Agent exit invalidates every delegated grant locally before late events can admit effects. Replacement requires fresh launch. Failed termination is explicit, never successful revocation; preserve cleanup/identity poison and already-performed outcomes.
6. Unknown outcomes never refund/replay authorization. Late authenticated completion remains recordable after revocation. Preserve unchanged component security coverage and document the replacement contract before removing obsolete local-handle tests.

## Testing
Positive granted helper versus ungranted sibling/child, parent-only delegation, scope/budget/deadline/replay races, queued/running revocation, local expiry, Agent exit, failed cleanup and late results. Actual seqpacket plus measured helper; privileged mechanisms in the disposable launcher VM when required. Full affected Rust/browser gates.

## Notes
Uses existing zero-authority tool isolation and the preceding Agent command bridge. Canonical decision: louiselm-cross-process-tool-commit-z288. No new executable/mount/network authority selected by an untrusted peer; no runtime wrapper or altered Bubblewrap reaping.

title: Broker lifecycle recovery and canonical Session status
description:
## Goal

Complete the Control brokers lifecycle authority, reconciliation, Attention projection, and machine-readable status across normal control, broker restart, and controller loss.

## Scope

- In scope: authorization matrix; serialized lifecycle CAS; exact receipt reconciliation; operator/coordinator actions; quarantine ordering; durable Attention outbox; operator CLI inspection; read-only Agent self status.
- Out of scope: Provider egress, credentials, dependencies, canonical Beads mutation, Android delivery, and human UI rendering.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Operators may Park, interrupt, and Dispose; only operators may resume. Coordinators may act only on descendant Sessions within the current envelope. The Agent capability channel has no lifecycle authority.
2. Every request carries request ID, expected receipt sequence, expected state, and envelope revision. Identical retry returns the same receipt; conflicting reuse and stale expectations fail closed with the canonical typed error.
3. Quarantine first revokes broker capabilities and then requests Park. Narrowing actions may complete before receipt durability; resume and capability enablement require durable receipt acknowledgement.
4. On broker restart, equal receipt prefixes reattach and a continuous valid supervisor-ahead suffix is appended exactly. Gap, conflict, non-prefix, invalid signature, or broker-ahead state stays frozen, disables capabilities, and creates an Attention projection; no receipt is discarded or spliced and no Session auto-resumes.
5. Controller loss follows the confirmed contract: freeze/revoke; if durable ACP recovery exists, record cold Park, durably enqueue its Attention projection, then authorize supervisor Disposal and identity release. Otherwise record abnormal Disposal and Attention without claiming recovery.
6. The broker uses a durable outbox to project bounded normalized Attention items into capture-service. Projection failure never changes authorization or canonical receipt state; capture-service cannot authorize, sign, clear broker policy, or rewrite receipts.
7. louiselm-control session inspect ID --json returns state, posture, broker connection, envelope revision, channel state, receipt head, pending operation, allowed actions, and last failure. Agent session.status returns the same normalized self-scoped subset read-only.
8. Error objects expose code, message, retryable, current_state, expected_sequence, and next_action; neither humans nor Agents must parse logs or prose to recover safely.
9. Preserve louiselm-9onz Agent-lifetime authority: Agent exit revokes its channel and all delegated grants even while tools survive. Restart/reconciliation/Resume may not transfer authority to another process or recycled PID. Replacement needs a fresh authorized launch; existing cold-Park recovery creates a new Session. Consume the launch/delegation revocation path rather than implementing a parallel grant system.

## Testing

- Broker/supervisor integration tests cover the full authority matrix, CAS races, retries, quarantine order, all prefix-reconciliation cases, restart, cold-Park ordering, no-recovery loss, outbox retry/deduplication, projection compromise, CLI JSON, Agent scoping, and redaction.
- Use fake ACP/controller and capture-service seams with production asynchronous signatures.
- Run all owning-crate gates.

## Notes

This is the broker-side lifecycle slice. The existing end-to-end task louiselm-d6fv.9 remains responsible for complete Verified Session cutover; existing posture UX work remains responsible for human presentation.

title: Reconcile broker restart and settle controller loss
description:
## Goal
Reconcile broker restart and settle controller loss without widening authority or claiming unproven recovery.

## Scope
Authenticated reconnect against exact verified receipt prefixes; controller-loss recovery decision and ordered durable Attention outbox; authenticated supervisor settlement. Evidence registration/retention are owned by louiselm-qbr.5.1.2.6 and .5. Follow confirmed louiselm-c0vs; reuse supervisor mechanics and existing grant revocation.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Equal verified prefixes reattach. Append only a continuous valid supervisor-ahead suffix exactly; gaps, conflicts, non-prefix, invalid signatures and broker-ahead state stay frozen with capabilities disabled and Attention. No discarded/spliced receipts, widening or automatic Resume.
2. On controller loss, freeze/revoke first. Use only valid broker-owned recovery evidence bound to the exact authorized launch/Session/Run/Agent/ACP identity and trusted retained storage. Capture-service Run metadata, a reference string and loadSession advertisement cannot establish recoverability.
3. With valid evidence, record cold Park and durably enqueue Attention before acknowledging supervisor Disposal/identity release. Without valid evidence, record abnormal Disposal and Attention without claiming recovery.
4. Missing or failed broker settlement/durability retains the unresolved loss latch, frozen tree and safe identity ownership. Already-Parked Sessions settle the existing truthful head; no invalid Parked-to-Parked receipt.
5. Capture-service outage/compromise never changes authorization or receipts. Durable local enqueue, not remote projection delivery, gates settlement; retries deliver later.
6. Restart/retry/stale callbacks cannot revive expired or superseded evidence, transfer old Agent authority or release twice. Operator Resume uses a fresh authorized Session within the original envelope; recovery can be lossy and a failed reconstruction must not be reported active.

## Testing
Red-green broker/supervisor integration for all prefix cases, recovery/no-recovery, loss before registration, wrong or stale evidence, ordering, store/outbox failures, capture outage/compromise, broker loss during settlement, already-Parked loss, identity reuse and late callbacks. Use production asynchronous doubles and run complete owning-crate gates.

## Notes
Source: confirmed louiselm-c0vs. Prior lessons: louiselm-d6fv.4.5.5 requires an unresolved loss latch independent of transport callbacks; louiselm-brp7 requires durable resume/finalize state, not UI/local success alone. Full installed vendor acceptance remains louiselm-d6fv.9.
notes: Retention handoff from .5: only the measured synthetic counter Agent is supported. Source Session root is sealed mode 0700 before successful disposal, so operator reconstruction must use a trusted supervisor-owned restore path into a fresh authorized Session; neither Neovim nor capture-service may directly copy from protected storage. The .5 VM gate deliberately performs fixture restoration under root to prove the bytes are usable; that is NOT the production operator restore consumer. Implement/verify that consumer here, preserving durable resume/finalize ordering and the original envelope.

design:
Policy confirmed in louiselm-zqk9 by the maintainer in codex/01a09931-7f28-7e22-b94d-ea6edf438c8e on 2026-09-13. This supplements the existing protected-restore work and louiselm-c0vs; it does not claim implementation or live acceptance.

Prerequisite: louiselm-qbr.10 supplies explicit finite versus uncapped command policy. Counts are opt-in for ordinary and unattended Runs. Preserve capability scope, generated-work budgets, expiry, delegation restrictions, and configured permission/auto-approval policy.

Cold Resume is operator-only and constructs a distinct Session through fresh authorization. Choosing Resume authorizes the remaining original authority: retain uncapped count policy, or allocate only verified unspent finite allowance. Do not reuse live grants, widen scope, reset counts, or extend expiry. Direct admitted/uncertain command intents and non-refundable delegated reservations remain spent; do not subtract delegated executions twice. Persist a single-use allocation bound to the source recovery and new authorization so concurrent resumes, crash/restart, replay, and retry cannot duplicate the allowance.

If valid recovery succeeds but the balance of one bounded permission cannot be established, withhold that permission and expose the reason. Work covered by independently valid permissions may continue; dependent steps wait for an operator decision. This partial-continuation policy is limited to unavailable grant accounting: it does not excuse invalid overall authorization, required recovery evidence, unsupported layout, expired launch authority, failed ACP load, or other existing admission failures.

Required acceptance additions: finite and uncapped count modes; remaining/zero/expired allowance; uncertain outcomes and delegated-reservation accounting; unavailable-balance partial continuation with unaffected work and a blocked dependent step; concurrent Resume, crash boundaries and retry without duplicated authority; failed ACP load never active; late callbacks after failure/disposal. Preserve the original installed synthetic restoration and identity/retention tests, and its vendor/desktop acceptance exclusion.

title: Serve operator Session inspection through an authenticated broker endpoint
description:
## Goal

Give the operator `louiselm-control session inspect ID --json`, reading the same
canonical `SessionStatus` the broker composes for every other consumer.

## Why this is its own slice

`louiselm-control` is reserved in `release::ALLOWED_COMPONENTS`
(`skills-core/src/release.rs:51`) but **no binary exists**. More importantly the
broker has no operator query transport: `/run/louiselm/control.sock` is the
launch rendezvous a supervisor connects to, not an endpoint an operator CLI can
ask about an arbitrary Session. This slice adds a new authenticated trust
boundary, which deserves its own evidence rather than riding along.

## Scope

- In scope: the `louiselm-control` binary; an authenticated local operator
  endpoint on the broker; kernel-UID authentication against the installed
  operator; `session inspect ID --json` emitting canonical `SessionStatus`
  bytes; stable typed errors and distinct exit codes; installation provisioning
  for the endpoint.
- Out of scope: lifecycle mutation verbs, posture sourcing (`louiselm-rn38`),
  and Agent-facing status (its own sibling).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `session inspect ID --json` writes exactly `SessionStatus::canonical_bytes`
   and parses back through `parse_canonical`, with no prose on stdout.
2. Only the installed operator UID is served; every other peer is refused
   before any Session state is read.
3. Unknown Session, unavailable broker, and refused authentication each get a
   distinct stable exit code and a typed error naming the next safe action.
4. Output carries no `assigned_uid`, `assigned_gid`, `pid`, path, environment
   or prompt content, asserted the way `tests/launch_protocol.rs` already
   asserts operator-evidence redaction.
5. The binary is covered by the crate gates and by the release component check.

## Testing Notes

`BrokerService::session_status` and `LifecycleCaller::allowed_actions` already
exist and are covered in `tests/broker/lifecycle.rs`; this slice tests the
transport, authentication and CLI surface, not the composition again.
notes: rn38 is maintainer-confirmed. louiselm-d6fv.6.10 owns replacing caller-supplied posture with evidence-derived default six-dimension SessionStatus (state, typed reason, freshness, safe next action); louiselm-d6fv.6.12 owns lifetime validity. This operator transport consumes the same canonical composition and retains authentication/exit codes/redaction. Missing source implementations report unverified/evidence_missing; Pending is genuine initialization only. Transport work remains separate from evidence producers; component completion must identify any still-missing louiselm-d6fv.6.10 or production broker consumer rather than claim installed Verified status.
close_reason: gate:skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/installed_daemon_inspection_tests.rs Installed authenticated CLI returns exact canonical status; UID refusal precedes lookup, typed exits/redaction/deadlines/restart verified. Full crate, Node and real systemd gates pass. Lesson in issue/docs.

title: Operator inspection can outlive its total deadline
description: Found during pre-handoff inspection of new uncommitted .4.1 code, 2026-09-16. Observed source: broker/operator.rs serve_once establishes Instant::now()+TIMEOUT before reading frames, but calls lookup(session_id) without forwarding that deadline; bin/control/inspection.rs inspect starts a fresh QUERY_TIMEOUT (30s). An authorized peer spending 34s on its request can hold the single listener another 30s despite the documented 35s total budget. Only the client deadline was tested; malformed-frame and normal installed tests pass. Fix: pass the original deadline into routing, clamp the worker budget to it, and refuse elapsed budgets without Session lookup. Acceptance: regression proving an already elapsed exchange cannot renew the worker wait; total request deadline reaches routing; full owning gates. No authority mutation or unauthenticated Session access observed. Not a live desktop defect; caught before this slice shipped.
close_reason: gate:skills-core/src/bin/control/inspection.rs Expired query never reaches worker; remaining exchange deadline bounds queue expiry and wait. Red/green regression and all crate/installed VM gates pass. Lesson in issue; no acceptance deviation.

Fix forwards original accept deadline into routing, refuses expired requests before queue admission, and clamps expiry plus wait to min(exchange deadline, now+30s). Two focused deadline tests now cover expiry and remaining-budget exhaustion. Lesson: socket framing and worker queues share one absolute request deadline; per-stage timeouts renew an already exhausted budget.

title: Answer read-only Agent self status on the capability channel
description:
## Goal

Let a Session's own Agent read its own `SessionStatus`, and nothing else, over
the existing authenticated capability channel.

## Why this is its own slice

The Agent capability channel is not a separate socket: it is the retained
supervisor connection carrying `ProtocolMessage::Command` packets, served by
`BrokerSession::handle_command` (`skills-core/src/broker/command_service.rs`).
Answering status there means extending the command protocol and its supervisor
relay — independent of the operator CLI, which needs a new socket instead.

## Scope

- In scope: a read-only status operation on the capability channel; self-scope
  enforcement; empty `allowed_actions` for `LifecycleCaller::Agent`; the
  supervisor relay; redaction of operator-only evidence.
- Out of scope: any lifecycle authority for the Agent, operator surfaces, and
  posture sourcing (`louiselm-rn38`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An Agent asking for its own Session gets canonical `SessionStatus` bytes with
   `allowed_actions` empty, because `LifecycleCaller::Agent` has no lifecycle
   authority.
2. An Agent naming any other Session is refused with a typed error, and the
   refusal does not disclose whether that Session exists.
3. The answer is byte-identical to what the operator surface composes for the
   same Session, except for the caller-scoped `allowed_actions`.
4. The reply carries no operator-only evidence: no occupancy list, no slot, no
   `assigned_uid`/`assigned_gid`/`pid`/path, matching the existing self-status
   redaction assertions in `tests/launch_protocol.rs:1624`.
5. A status read never resets a budget, revives a grant, or counts as admission.
6. Status remains answerable after Park, Resume, broker restart and recovery,
   reporting the state those transitions actually left behind.
notes: rn38 is maintainer-confirmed. Consume louiselm-d6fv.6.10's evidence-derived canonical six-dimension status and louiselm-d6fv.6.12's validity handling; remove externally supplied posture through that shared implementation. Agent posture facts match operator facts, with self-scope, forbidden-field redaction and empty allowed_actions preserved. Reads grant/renew nothing. Missing sources are unverified/evidence_missing; Pending is genuine initialization only. The Park-disabled Agent channel and existing serialized receive constraints still apply. Remaining Resume/recovery coverage stays .4.2.1; production transport/evidence limitations retain explicit follow-ups.

title: Retain verified ACP recovery material across Session disposal
description:
## Goal
Prove that explicitly identified ACP recovery material survives old-Session disposal without becoming accessible through a recycled host identity.

## Scope
Recovery-specific launch-supervisor retention mechanics and authenticated retention evidence for the broker. Follow confirmed louiselm-c0vs. Reuse existing private Session storage, process/identity ownership and protocol boundaries. Broader source/cache/export/Forensics lifecycle integration stays in louiselm-d6fv.5.5; broker registration and eligibility are a separate dependent task.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Retention accepts only the authorized Session's explicitly identified Agent recovery files and required workspace. A verified per-Agent recovery layout is required; unknown or unsupported layouts return unavailable, never a generic whole-home fallback.
2. No reusable credentials or live capability grants are carried into recovery material. Do not infer a valid layout from directory names or loadSession advertisement alone.
3. A trusted supervisor result binds retained material to the exact authorized launch and its Session/Run, and proves a durable usable recovery point under the supported Agent contract. A path string, controller assertion or fixture-only provider claim is not proof of real Agent support.
4. Retained material remains isolated across tree termination and host-identity reuse; partial failure never releases unsafe ownership or reports retention success.
5. Repeated operations and restart do not substitute or revive stale retained material. Respect existing Park expiry and Disposal/Forensics ownership; operator Resume restores only into a fresh authorized Session, without transferring process authority.
6. Expose expected failures explicitly through the existing asynchronous supervisor boundary. Do not add a parallel privileged service or policy owner.

## Testing
Red-green coverage for valid retained state, unsupported layout, excluded secret/capability material, path substitution/symlink escape, interrupted persistence, identity reuse, retry/restart and expiry ownership. Include an installed/mechanical consumer test with a deterministic recovery-capable Agent fixture; explicitly distinguish fixture proof from real configured-Agent support. Run full owning-crate gates. Real vendor/desktop cutover remains louiselm-d6fv.9.

## Notes

title: Register trusted recovery evidence and enforce recovery admission
description:
## Goal
Let the launch-authorized controller establish broker-owned cold-recovery readiness only from verified, durably retained recovery evidence.

## Scope
Authenticated controller submission, broker validation/persistence, and headless admission/readiness behavior using the retention proof from louiselm-qbr.5.1.2.5. Follow confirmed louiselm-c0vs. Reuse existing launch authorization and controller identity boundaries; do not create a second grant system. Controller-loss settlement remains .2; operator CLI/Agent status presentation remains .4.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The controller authorized for the exact launch may submit ACP identity/recovery metadata; untrusted role strings, Agent/helper channels and capture-service cannot register, replace or mint evidence.
2. Bind the configured Agent and ACP identity to the exact authorized launch, Session, Run and applicable canonical lifecycle/envelope state. Validate trusted supervisor retention evidence; a reference string, advertised loadSession, or controller assertion alone is insufficient.
3. Persist accepted evidence before acknowledging readiness. Identical retries return the original result; conflicting reuse, cross-Session substitution, expired/stale evidence and restart replay fail closed without transferring or renewing authority.
4. Wire the actual controller submission path, with asynchronous callbacks and lifecycle disposal handling. Tests must reach broker registration from that caller, not only construct trusted records in a unit test.
5. Ordinary admission stays usable with evidence unset/unavailable, including Agents without loadSession. Runs explicitly requiring cold recovery cannot pass that admission requirement without valid durable evidence; initialization needed to obtain evidence must not enable prohibited work.
6. Broker-owned readiness and a typed reason for unavailability are available to the existing canonical status composer. Recovery means a retained recovery point, not lossless continuation or guaranteed future load success.
7. Capture-service remains the Run/Attention projection owner, not a source of recovery authorization. Outage, forged projection acknowledgements and tampering with Run metadata cannot establish readiness.

## Testing
Red-green controller-to-broker integration with production asynchronous shapes; unauthorized submitters, exact binding, retention failures, replay/restart, torn writes, evidence invalidation, late callbacks, required-vs-optional admission, unset effective configuration and normalized/redacted readiness. Run complete affected Lua/Rust gates and update public protocol/docs/types where changed.

## Notes
Source: confirmed louiselm-c0vs. Initial code entry points are broker authorization/service/installed boundaries and workflow recovery/admission. Unknown Agent recovery layouts remain unavailable. Do not describe fixture recovery as installed vendor support.
notes: Retention mechanics are implemented by .5 in RunningAgent::retain_recovery(RetentionRequest, RecoveryCompletion). Installed SystemRunningAgent binds SessionStorage to the already-authorized LaunchRequest and measured test integration. Requests are path-free (operation ID, ACP ID, absolute expiry); response carries exact launch/operation/integration/material bindings. Call only through the authenticated, serialized supervisor owner and validate canonical state/receipt binding before broker readiness. Current contract requires an idle frozen tree and retains one immutable point per Session: identical retries work, replacement/expiry renewal conflicts. Coordinate required-cold-recovery admission without enabling work early or auto-Resuming a canonical Park. No vendor layout is supported; ordinary SystemRunningAgent::new returns Unsupported. .5 closure must remain inert until this production broker/controller consumer is wired and verified.

title: Mediate Provider egress and credential custody through the broker
description:
## Problem Statement

louiselm-qbr.5.1 requires that Sessions have no ambient network and that reusable
Provider credentials never reach a Session, but nothing broker-side enforces
either property yet. louiselm-qbr.5.1.1 and louiselm-qbr.5.1.2 explicitly scoped
Provider egress and credentials out ("Out of scope: ... Provider egress,
credentials..."), and louiselm-d6fv.6.13 (network posture evidence) explicitly
defers enforcement itself here: "Out: implementing Provider proxying,
credentials or egress enforcement itself; those remain louiselm-qbr.5.1."

## Scope

In scope: broker-side credential custody for configured Providers; a network
mediation point every Session must go through for any destination; per-grant
scoping across DNS resolution, redirects, protocol, and operation; a
"cannot launch verified" gate when a runtime cannot use brokered/ephemeral
Provider authentication.

Out of scope: dependency/package-registry fetches (sibling task, filed
separately under this same parent); deriving or reporting network posture
evidence for display (louiselm-d6fv.6.13, which consumes this task's
enforcement, not the other way round); typed canonical Beads mutation
(sibling task).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Reusable Provider credentials are stored and used only broker-side; no
   Session process, environment, argument, file, or log ever contains one.
2. Provider requests reach only the configured endpoint(s) for that Provider,
   within the confirmed Model allowlist (v1: stock Codex via a broker-held OpenAI API key; gpt-6-astra and gpt-5.6-luna, effort <= high; louiselm-gy165), shared Run request budget
   (including retries) and expiry. Exact monetary/subscription-quota ceilings are
   not promised in v1; see louiselm-ow3ok. Requests outside the approved limits
   are denied, exhaustion Parks with Attention, and expiry cancels locally
   without refunding unknown outcomes.
3. A runtime that cannot authenticate through brokered or ephemeral
   broker-issued credentials cannot complete a Verified launch (extends the
   louiselm-qbr.5.1.1 AC5 launch gate to also check this).
4. Sessions have no ambient network by default. Any additional destination
   requires an exact grant, enforced across DNS resolution, redirects,
   protocol, and operation — not just the initial hostname.
5. Denied network/credential requests return the typed error shape from
   louiselm-qbr.5.1.2 AC8 (code, message, retryable, current_state,
   expected_sequence, next_action).

## Testing Notes

- Fake Provider/network adapters; no live network in tests.
- Cover: credential never observable outside the broker process; redirect to
  a non-granted destination denied; DNS rebind to a non-granted IP denied;
  shared Run request-limit exceeded denied before any external effect; Verified launch refused when brokered auth is
  unavailable.

## Notes

Establishes or extends the broker's typed effect-policy schema (filesystem,
process, network, credentials, cost, ... — parent AC5) for the network and
credential effect categories. Do not build a general policy engine ahead of
this concrete need; the dependency-fetch sibling task extends the same
schema for its own category rather than inventing a second one.
notes:
Confirmed refinement in louiselm-ow3ok (codex/01a0b244-e023-7762-bdbf-19baf015da98, 2026-09-18): Codex/OpenAI subscription first, separate broker-owned sign-in; narrow local Responses endpoint investigation is permitted, revising the blanket HTTP-mediator rejection in comment2097. Generic proxying, Session-selected upstream destinations and assumed runtime forks remain out of scope. Model allowlist/shared Run request-count/expiry replace exact monetary or quota claims for v1. louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.4 and louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.5 must establish authentication and caller-isolation feasibility before .3.2 implementation. Confirmed full contract and provenance live in ow3ok design. Vocabulary delta: No change.
Current confirmed sender candidate: stock Codex + external BPF-LSM guard + broker admission per request (ow3ok, codex/01a0b2b8-3e82-7b02-ab50-9b40601ac7da, 2026-09-18). .3.5 is the completed negative routing-only result, not positive isolation proof. Follow-up .3.6-.3.9 now establish that proof; .3.2 blocks on .3.9 and .3.4. Concurrent subscription transport/helper question is louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.10, blocking .3.4. No production or Verified acceptance inferred from primitive passes.

comments.text:
Design decision (maintainer, 2026-09-17): broker PERFORMS the Provider call. The Session sends a typed request; the broker holds the reusable credential, calls the configured endpoint and returns the response. The Session never names a destination.

Rejected alternative: a broker-side mediating HTTP proxy the Session connects through. It is the more general shape and would cover AC4 "any additional destination" directly, but it makes the broker a parser of someone else the protocol and injects credentials in flight, which is a much larger surface to get wrong. Chosen door buys the security property now; the generic destination-grant path is deferred to whatever the dependency-fetch sibling louiselm-qbr.5.1.4 actually needs, extending the same typed effect schema rather than inventing a second one.

Consequence accepted: a new Provider API shape is broker-side work, not Session configuration.

Existing seams this builds on, verified 2026-09-17: skills-core/src/registry.rs:200 NetworkPolicy::Brokered is already declared and documented as owned by this feature, with Denied the only value a verified launch accepts in v1 -- this task makes Brokered real. skills-core/src/isolation.rs:96 NetworkDenial already enforces AC4 default (no network, no route out). skills-core/src/launch_protocol.rs:283 ProtocolError/NextAction already supply the AC5 typed error shape; do not define a second one.

title: Keep reusable Provider credentials broker-side only
description:
## Goal

Reusable Provider credentials live only inside the Control broker, so no Session
process, environment, argument, file, or log can ever contain one.

## Scope

- In scope: broker-side storage, loading and in-memory handling of configured
  Provider credentials under the broker's own dedicated non-root identity;
  state ACLs consistent with the existing broker store; a typed credential
  handle a Session may reference by Provider id without ever receiving the
  secret; redaction guarantees on every durable record and Agent-visible log.
- Out of scope: performing Provider requests (sibling task); the Verified-launch
  gate (sibling task); dependency/package-registry credentials
  (louiselm-qbr.5.1.4); operator or capture-service credential custody, which
  parent louiselm-qbr.5.1 explicitly keeps out.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Configured Provider credentials are readable only by the broker identity,
   with the same exact state ACLs the broker already asserts for its stores.
2. A Session references a Provider by configured id and receives a handle, never
   a secret. No secret appears in any argument, environment variable, file the
   Session can read, prompt, receipt, audit record, or Agent-visible log.
3. Credential material is not written into durable records: parent AC15 forbids
   credentials in durable records, and the existing receipt/audit redaction
   contract is extended to cover this category rather than duplicated.
4. A missing, unreadable or malformed credential is a typed failure using the
   existing `ProtocolError` shape in `skills-core/src/launch_protocol.rs`, never
   a panic and never a silent empty credential.

## Testing

- A test asserts the secret's absence across the full Session-visible surface:
  process environment, arguments, readable files, receipts, audit records.
- Malformed and unreadable credential stores produce the typed error, not a
  panic or a default.
- No live network and no real Provider credential in any fixture.

## Notes

- Rust in the `skills-core` crate; `docs/agent-rust.md` and
  `docs/agent-testing.md` are binding. No production `unwrap`/`expect`.
- Reuse `ProtocolError`/`NextAction` from `skills-core/src/launch_protocol.rs:283`.
  Do not define a second error shape.
- First slice of the maintainer's door-A decision recorded on the parent: the
  broker performs Provider calls, so custody is the foundation the request path
  builds on.

title: Grill-me needed: which stock Codex subscription bridge can the broker support?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; confirm the authentication-helper and supported subscription-transport contract with the maintainer before implementing it.

## Question
Can the Control broker use one separately owned stock Codex authentication helper and its legacy token-export method for subscription requests, and what supported upstream operation contract makes that safe and maintainable?

## Evidence
louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.4 remains open with BLOCKED_SUBSCRIPTION_BRIDGE. docs/codex-auth-proof.md and scripts/probe-codex-auth.py show that external-token mode delivers the reusable bearer into the confined app-server, violating the accepted broker-only custody contract. The installed getAuthStatus(includeToken=true) does export synthetic managed access material, but current primary auth documentation does not establish it as a supported broker subscription interface or establish a supported raw subscription Responses transport. Real sign-in, refresh-token rotation/expiry/revocation, concurrent refresh ownership, entitlement and billing were not proven.

## Decisions to resolve
- Whether a pinned, broker-owned stock app-server used solely for fresh managed sign-in/refresh is acceptable, including reliance on the legacy export API.
- Which supported subscription service and reviewed operation permit broker-originated calls; do not infer this from fake HTTP success, planType or API-key endpoints.
- Single refresh-owner lifecycle across restart and overlapping broker processes, private credential storage and secret-free private IPC. Existing ACP frame logging must never capture authentication material.
- What to do if no supported bridge can be established while preserving stock Codex and the existing subscription.

## Boundaries
The BPF-LSM sender-guard direction confirmed in louiselm-ow3ok is independent and does not select this authentication proposal. Keep .3.4 and production .3.2 blocked until this decision and its actual acceptance succeed. Preserve ordinary login; no existing credential-store reads/imports, API-key billing migration, runtime fork, real sign-in, external request or deployment is authorized by filing this question. Explicit operator acceptance comes only after a concrete candidate is reviewable.
The separate full-VM-disk defect louiselm-eze4t concerns rerunning custody gates; it does not explain away the unsupported transport.

## Provenance
Split from concurrent .3.4 findings routed to ow3ok comment2254, preserving them while closing only the confirmed sender-guard decision. Session codex/01a0b2b8-3e82-7b02-ab50-9b40601ac7da, 2026-09-18.
design:
Confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-09-18 in codex/01a0b2ba-3709-7f22-b9eb-f0285afb3444, including explicit confirmation of the final shared-understanding summary.

1. Production requires documented support for login, refresh, and broker-originated Codex/OpenAI subscription requests. A working undocumented API or synthetic successful request is insufficient.
2. Legacy getAuthStatus token export remains research-only. Pinning a version and adding regression gates do not authorize production reliance on it.
3. Reusable credentials stay under Control broker ownership, outside every confined Session. Preserve the ordinary Codex login and existing subscription; no credential-store import or implicit API-key billing migration.
4. Without a supported bridge, Verified Codex remains unavailable while ordinary Codex continues working. This is the accepted fallback, not permission to weaken custody or patch the runtime.
5. .3.4 remains open to establish the documented boundary and its actual authentication/custody/lifecycle acceptance. Production .3.2 remains blocked on that proof and the independent full guarded-composition proof .3.9. This decision selects requirements and fallback; it does not establish that a supported bridge exists.
6. Fresh broker-owned sign-in and live upstream acceptance remain explicit operator steps only after a concrete candidate is reviewable. No sign-in, external Provider request, installed cutover or runtime fork is authorized by this confirmation.

Vocabulary delta: No change.

title: Authenticate stock Codex broker requests with a broker-held OpenAI API key
description:
## Goal
The Control broker authenticates stock Codex Provider requests with an OpenAI API key it holds, so louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2 no longer waits on subscription support (louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.11).

## Scope
- In scope: API-key authentication on the broker's upstream side of the proven narrow local Responses endpoint (louiselm-ow3ok, .3.5-.3.9); loading the key through existing custody (skills-core/src/broker/provider_credentials.rs, installed.rs:395); typed failure when the key is absent, malformed or rejected; confirming from current OpenAI primary documentation that gpt-6-astra and gpt-5.6-luna are offered through the API under those names and that the Responses operation Codex sends is supported with API-key auth.
- Out of scope: subscription login/refresh (louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.4, deferred, optional second method); request limits, allowlist enforcement and Park (louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2); the Verified launch gate (.3.3); any real key or network in automated suites.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The broker adds the API key only on its own upstream request; the confined Session sends no Authorization and never observes the key (argv, environment, files, logs, receipts, ACP messages).
2. Missing, unreadable, malformed or upstream-rejected keys fail closed with the existing ProtocolError/NextAction shape and zero retries that bypass the Run budget.
3. Model availability is recorded with primary-source citations and date. If either allowlisted Model is not offered through the API, stop and file a needs-design question to the maintainer; never substitute another Model silently.
4. A key has no refresh lifecycle; key rotation is an explicit operator re-provisioning, documented next to the existing custody procedure.

## Testing
Red-green through authenticated public request handling with a fake upstream asserting the Authorization header is added broker-side only. Reuse the 16 provider_credentials tests and the distinct-UID custody fixture pattern. Run skills-core through ./scripts/test-skills-core under systemd-run (docs/agent-testing.md).

## Notes
Decided in louiselm-gy165 (maintainer confirmation, claude/d7834ce3-9555-4d81-ad34-eb0aed935af8, 2026-09-24): OpenAI API key first, few-USD budget, spend cap set on the OpenAI project because v1 limits request count, not money. .3.11 notes OpenAI's documented Responses proxy path uses API keys.
close_reason: Feasibility confirmed from primary sources (official responses-api-proxy; both Models on Responses API); code ACs moved to .3.2 first slice. none:research

comments.author: claude/d7834ce3-9555-4d81-ad34-eb0aed935af8
comments.text: Research 2026-09-24. (1) API-key custody outside Codex is officially supported: openai/codex codex-responses-api-proxy reads key from stdin, mlock+zeroize, forwards only POST /v1/responses with its own bearer, drops incoming Authorization; Codex uses it via model_providers base_url (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/responses-api-proxy/README.md). (2) Both Models on API with Responses: gpt-6-astra (effort low..max, no ultra; 10/1/50 USD per M in/cached/out) https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra ; gpt-5.6-luna (effort none..max; 0.2/0.02/1.2) https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna . (3) Cost from usage index: astra high ~2.10 USD/turn (cached re-reads ~1.44M tokens/turn dominate), luna medium ~0.015. Maintainer chose luna default, astra opt-in, ~20 USD cap. (4) Broker has no Provider request path yet; with_secret is dead code, so code ACs A1-A3 moved into .3.2 as its first slice rather than shipping an unreachable adapter.

title: Accept real capped OpenAI API requests through the broker in the launcher VM
description:
## Goal
Prove the broker request path against the real OpenAI endpoint, cheaply and disposably, before any host installation.

## Scope
- In scope: a documented operator procedure in a fresh scripts/launcher-vm overlay: maintainer creates a dedicated OpenAI API project with a hard spend limit of a few USD and provisions its key through the custody procedure; a confined stock Codex Session completes real turns on gpt-5.6-luna at effort <= high, plus at most one gpt-6-astra turn to prove the second allowlisted Model.
- Out of scope: host installation (louiselm-d6fv.12.5); daily-work use; monetary enforcement inside the broker.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Real turns succeed through broker-selected endpoints only; the Session has no ambient network.
2. Effort above high and a non-allowlisted Model are refused with the typed denial before any upstream call.
3. Run request-count exhaustion Parks with Attention; recorded evidence shows zero extra upstream attempts.
4. The key is absent from the Session's process state, files and logs, checked with the existing custody fixture's probes.
5. Evidence (commands, versions, counts, redacted) recorded on this issue; the key and response content never enter Beads. VM stopped and discarded afterwards.

## Notes
Needs the maintainer's key and live network, so it is a maintainer-driven step, not an automated gate. Decided in louiselm-gy165, step 1 of 3.

Cost decision (maintainer, claude/d7834ce3-9555-4d81-ad34-eb0aed935af8, 2026-09-24): run on gpt-5.6-luna (~0.015 USD/turn) by default; gpt-6-astra (~2 USD/turn at high) only when the maintainer explicitly chooses it. OpenAI project spend cap about 20 USD.

description:

## Scope

2. Verified launch was refused before key provisioning and admitted after (louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.3 observed live).
