title: Serve brokered Codex requests within shared Run limits
description:
## Goal
A confined Codex Session uses OpenAI through the Control broker with brokered authentication (API key first, louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.12), which keeps reusable credentials broker-side and enforces operator-approved Model, request-count and expiry limits.

## Scope
Implement only after louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.12 establishes broker-held API-key authentication and louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.9 establishes exact runtime authority through the complete guarded ACP integration. louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.5 is historical negative routing-only evidence. The confirmed candidate is stock Codex using a narrow local Responses endpoint, external BPF-LSM sender enforcement and broker authorization for every complete request. No runtime patch or generic HTTP forwarding is authorized. The ACP proxy/adapter chain stays intact. The broker owns upstream destinations and validates supported operations; its typed policy failures reuse ProtocolError/NextAction.

The first integration is stock Codex/OpenAI authenticated by a broker-held OpenAI API key (louiselm-gy165). Subscription sign-in (louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.4) is a deferred, optional second method and blocks nothing. Ordinary subscription login remains untouched. Unknown authentication or isolation is a blocker, not a reason to pass a reusable credential into a Session.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Exact configured Provider operations reach only broker-selected endpoints. The Session cannot choose an upstream host, URL or address, including through redirects or alternate protocol fields. Unsupported operations and Models fail closed before any external effect.
2. The approved Model allowlist (v1: gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-luna) with a reasoning-effort ceiling (v1: high; xhigh/ultra/max refused with the typed denial before any upstream call; raised via Run policy, not code), finite request count and expiry are Run-scoped. Every Session and child shares the same durable count. Atomically reserve one unit before each upstream model-request attempt, including retries; narrower child allowances also consume the common total.
3. Concurrent calls cannot overspend. Broker/Session restart, Session replacement, child creation or request replay cannot reset the allowance. Distinguish response replay from a new upstream attempt; transport ambiguity never silently grants another attempt.
4. Count or expiry denials return validated ProtocolError metadata. Exhaustion stops new requests, Parks the Run and creates an Attention item using existing lifecycle/Attention owners. Resume needs an explicit operator-approved extension, never an automatic reset.
5. At expiry, cancel in-flight requests locally and Park the Run. Preserve already received output and spent units. Unknown outcomes receive no refund or automatic retry. A local cancellation is not proof that the Provider stopped; completed external effects are never described as rolled back.
6. Make NetworkPolicy::Brokered an enforced value under the proven integration. Preserve Denied and absence-of-Provider-permission refusal; never enable ambient Session networking. Wrong process/Session/Run/revision, revoked authority and late results after disposal fail at the existing shared authorization/lifecycle boundary.
7. Reusable credentials and refresh material remain in broker-owned trusted state, never in Session process state, argv, environment, prompt, Agent-readable files, receipts or logs. Existing credential-storage ACL and redaction contracts remain intact.
8. This v1 makes no exact monetary or subscription-quota guarantee; the money ceiling is the operator's spend limit on the OpenAI API project (about 20 USD for acceptance). Estimated API cost per turn from the maintainer's usage index, 2026-09-24: gpt-6-astra high ~2.10 USD, medium ~1.35 USD; gpt-5.6-luna medium ~0.015 USD. Default Verified Model is gpt-5.6-luna; gpt-6-astra stays allowlisted for explicit per-Session choice. Account-limit reporting remains the existing Agent-advertised ACP extension; neither broker nor adapter reads another tool store or queries Provider limits for this work.
9. Kernel send checks never authorize a complete HTTP request by themselves. Reuse the .3.8 admission proof to validate each batched, partial or buffered request at the current lifecycle/revision/expiry boundary before reserving and performing an upstream attempt. Guard-loss or unsupported-host refusal must preserve ordinary Sessions without claiming Verified protection.
10. Update public types/docs and real consumer wiring. The Verified-launch gate remains louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.3; network-posture display remains louiselm-d6fv.6.13. Fake transport success alone is not installed or subscription acceptance.

## Authentication slice (moved from louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.12)
First slice of this task: the broker authenticates its own upstream request with the custody-held API key through ProviderCredentialStore::with_secret (skills-core/src/broker/provider_credentials.rs:283, currently dead code awaiting this consumer).
A1. The broker sets Authorization: Bearer <key> only on its own upstream request and strips any incoming Authorization; the confined Session sends none and never observes the key (argv, environment, files, logs, receipts, ACP messages).
A2. Missing, unreadable, malformed or upstream-rejected (401/403) keys fail closed with ProtocolError/NextAction and no retry outside the Run budget.
A3. Keys have no refresh lifecycle; rotation is explicit operator re-provisioning, documented next to the custody procedure in docs/broker-launch-acceptance.md.
Reference behaviour: OpenAI's official codex-responses-api-proxy (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/responses-api-proxy/README.md) forwards only POST /v1/responses to https://api.openai.com/v1/responses, sets the bearer itself and drops incoming Authorization; Codex reaches it via a documented model_providers base_url. The broker keeps per-request admission (.3.8) on top; no generic forwarding.

## Testing
Red-green tests through authenticated public request handling, using fake Provider adapters and no live network/credentials in automated suites. Cover unknown Provider/Model/operation; unset permissions; limit denial with zero upstream calls; atomic last-unit races across Sessions/children; retries/replays and restart persistence; expiry during a stream; disconnect with unknown outcome; partial output retention; Park/Attention and explicit extension; redirects/alternate destination denial; validated ProtocolError shape; secret absence and revoked-process denial. Follow docs/agent-rust.md and docs/agent-testing.md; run complete affected gates.

## Notes
Confirmed by the maintainer in louiselm-ow3ok, codex/01a0b244-e023-7762-bdbf-19baf015da98, 2026-09-18. This replaces this task's former exact cost-limit expectation with the agreed bounded-work contract and permits investigation of narrowly scoped HTTP operation mediation. It does not authorize a generic proxy or guarantee every Codex feature works. Keep API-specific operations and supported feature coverage explicit once feasibility evidence identifies them. Split further independently completable implementation slices if the proven integration requires them; do not hide them as serial progress notes.

## Out of Scope
Other Providers; moving everyday Sessions to API-key billing (Verified stays opt-in, louiselm-gy165); exact dollar/quota ceilings; generic destination proxying; unsupported runtime forks; replacing acp-proxy; dependency fetches; network posture presentation; bypassing authentication/isolation or installed acceptance.

Re-scoped by louiselm-gy165 (maintainer confirmation, claude/d7834ce3-9555-4d81-ad34-eb0aed935af8, 2026-09-24): API key first, subscription optional later.
notes:
ow3ok confirmed 2026-09-18. Implementation now waits on louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.4 and louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.5; earlier missing-contract comment2230 is resolved. No request-path executable changes yet. Scope and limits are replaced by the current description.
Releasing my implementation claim after the confirmed design split; no executable edits are pending. .3.4 and .3.5 remain required feasibility blockers. Next claimant must not interpret the closed design question as proof of authentication or isolation.
Current prerequisites supersede historical .3.5-as-positive-proof wording: louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.9 must prove the complete guarded stock ACP composition, and .3.4 must prove subscription authentication (it is blocked by louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.10). ow3ok confirmation/closure is only a design decision; .3.2 remains blocked.
Authentication decision .3.10 is confirmed: documented production login/refresh/subscription-request support is mandatory; legacy token export is research-only. Without a supported bridge, Verified Codex remains unavailable while ordinary Codex continues. Closing that design question does not unblock implementation: .3.4 must still establish the supported boundary and actual acceptance, alongside .3.9 guarded composition.

title: Serve one brokered Responses request end to end against a fake upstream
description:
## Goal
Thin tracer slice of louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2: a production broker endpoint accepts a stock-Codex POST /v1/responses, admits the complete request, reserves one Run request unit, authenticates upstream with the broker-held API key and streams the SSE response back, proven against a fake upstream.

## Scope
- In scope: production local endpoint (promote the louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.8 fixture skills-core/tests/broker/buffered_requests.rs framing/owner logic into src, keeping its header/body limits and fail-closed parsing); per-request admission at the current lifecycle/revision/expiry boundary; a durable Run-scoped request counter with atomic reserve-before-attempt (count only); upstream POST to the broker-selected endpoint via the existing ureq client (dependency_fetch/transport.rs pattern: pinned resolver, no redirects, HTTPS only), streaming relay; auth slice A1-A3 from the parent (bearer set broker-side via ProviderCredentialStore::with_secret, incoming Authorization stripped, 401/403 and missing key fail closed).
- Out of scope: Model/effort allowlist (sibling S2); Park/Attention on exhaustion, expiry cancellation and restart/replay guarantees (S3); kernel sender guard and enabling NetworkPolicy::Brokered in the sandbox (S4, stays refused at sandbox.rs:1670).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A request from an admitted Session reaches only the configured upstream URL; Session-supplied Host/URL/redirects cannot change the destination.
2. Exactly one durable unit is reserved before each upstream attempt; a denied or unadmitted request makes zero upstream calls.
3. The key appears only on the upstream request; tests assert its absence from the downstream response, receipts, audit and logs.
4. Missing/unusable key and upstream 401/403 return typed ProtocolError with no retry.
5. SSE chunks are relayed as they arrive (test observes the first chunk before the upstream finishes).

## Testing
Red-green through the public endpoint with a fake HTTPS upstream (no live network, synthetic key). Run skills-core via systemd-run ./scripts/test-skills-core per docs/agent-testing.md; strict clippy/doc gates.

## Notes
Reference: official codex-responses-api-proxy (see louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.12 comment). Production enablement waits for S4.
close_reason: Request path built and gated offline (skills-core/tests/broker/provider_requests.rs, src/broker/provider_transport_tests.rs). Lesson: ureq returns 3xx as Ok under http_status_as_error(false); refused in provider_transport.rs exchange; issue comment. inert:louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4

title: Enforce the Provider Model and reasoning-effort allowlist per Run
description:
## Goal
Grants carry a typed Provider permission (Model allowlist, reasoning-effort ceiling) and the brokered request path refuses anything outside it before any upstream effect.

## Scope
- In scope: Provider/Model permission in GrantRequest (authorization.rs:83) with v1 defaults gpt-5.6-luna (default) and gpt-6-astra, effort <= high; parse model and reasoning.effort from the admitted request body; a Provider-neutral denial (CapabilityDenied's fixed message at launch_protocol.rs:~2320 says "Beads capability is unavailable" - generalise or add a code).
- Out of scope: budgets (S1/S3); guard (S4).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Non-allowlisted Model, effort above the ceiling, or missing/contradictory fields are refused with a typed error and zero upstream calls.
2. Unset Provider permission denies (fail closed); unset-case test required.
3. Ceiling raised only through grant/Run policy, never by the request.

## Notes
Depends on S1 for the request path it guards. Decided in louiselm-gy165.
close_reason: Grant carries sorted models + max_effort (ReasoningEffort order none..max; unknown e.g. ultra and missing effort refused); admission denies with CapabilityDenied before spend (provider_service.rs); endpoint answers 403; CapabilityDenied message now Provider-neutral. Gates: full skills-core 1138/0/13, strict clippy, rustdoc. Lesson: none beyond code docs. inert:louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4

title: Park Runs on Provider budget exhaustion or expiry with restart-safe accounting
description:
## Goal
Parent ACs 3-5: the Run request budget survives restart/replay/concurrency, and exhaustion or expiry Parks the Run with an Attention item.

## Scope
- In scope: concurrency (last-unit races across Sessions/children), restart persistence, replay vs new attempt, ambiguous transport never grants another attempt; exhaustion -> Park + AttentionReason::RunParked via existing owners (pattern: broker/controller_loss.rs:276-321, lifecycle_service.rs); expiry cancels in-flight locally, keeps received output and spent units, no refund; explicit operator extension to resume.
- Out of scope: allowlist (S2); guard (S4).

## Acceptance Criteria
Parent louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2 AC2-AC5 in full.

## Notes
Depends on S1.
close_reason: Park/extend on Provider budget exhaustion or expiry via children .1-.3; concurrency/restart/no-refund already in S1 ledger. inert:louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4 (request path not served in production until the listener lands; weakest child .2 inert). Lessons: none.

title: Hold, Park and raise Attention when a Run's Provider budget runs out
description:
## Goal
Parent AC4 core: exhaustion or expiry of the Run's Provider budget writes a durable Run-wide hold, refuses with typed ProtocolError metadata, Parks every Session of the Run and raises one RunParked Attention item.

## Design (maintainer-confirmed, claude/f1ec2cf3-7b27-4e2b-970d-41ce196b5bb8, 2026-09-25)
- Durable Run-scoped hold marker in the provider ledger (quarantine-marker pattern); written on first exhaustion/expiry observation, idempotent.
- New broker-internal lifecycle authority permitted only Park, only for Sessions of its own Run.
- Each Session worker parks its own Session when it observes the hold: on its next Provider request and on the 1 s idle tick (posture_attention pattern). No cross-worker signalling.
- One Attention item per Run (AttentionReason::RunParked, linked_run_id).
- Budget/expiry refusals map to validated ProtocolError (CapabilityDenied + NextAction), not a generic 403.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Exhaustion: zero upstream calls, hold written, Session Parked via signed receipt, Attention enqueued once per Run.
2. Sibling Session of the same Run Parks on its next request/idle tick; other Runs unaffected.
3. Hold survives restart; Resume stays refused while held (extension is louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.3 child 3).
4. Refusal body is a validated ProtocolError.
close_reason: Hold+Park+Attention on Provider exhaustion/expiry. consumer:skills-core/src/bin/control/inspection.rs:338. Lessons: none beyond comment.

comments.author: claude/f1ec2cf3-7b27-4e2b-970d-41ce196b5bb8
comments.text: Hold: provider-requests/holds/<run digest>.json, first writer wins (provider_requests.rs). Park via LifecycleCaller::ProviderBudget (Park-only, own Run) from settle_provider_hold on the 1 s worker tick (inspection.rs:338); Resume refused + withheld from status while held (lifecycle_service.rs). Attention: one RunParked per Run for UUID Run ids; legacy non-UUID Run ids fall back to a per-Session subject. Sibling Park relies on each worker's tick reading the shared Run hold; covered at ledger level, not with two live Sessions. Gates: fmt/clippy/doc clean; broker 167 pass; lib 8 + sandbox 2 failures are pre-existing env (reproduced on clean HEAD, louiselm-2fb5).

title: Cut in-flight Provider streams locally at permission expiry
description:
## Goal
Parent AC5: at Provider permission expiry, cancel the in-flight upstream attempt locally and Park the Run.

## Design (maintainer-confirmed 2026-09-25)
Upstream body read is bounded by the remaining permission lifetime (per-request transport deadline). On deadline the relay closes without the terminating chunk; bytes already relayed stay with the runtime; the unit stays spent; no refund or retry; the Run hold (child 1) is written with an expiry reason. Docs state local cancellation is not proof the Provider stopped.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A stream still open at expiry is cut locally; the client sees received chunks and no terminating chunk.
2. Spent count unchanged by the cut; no second attempt.
3. Hold + Park + Attention follow as in child 1.
close_reason: Stream cut at expiry: transport timeout_global + ExpiringBody (provider_service.rs); red-checked. inert:louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4 (endpoint not served in production until the listener lands). Lessons: none.

title: Lift a Provider budget hold only by operator-approved extension
description:
## Goal
Parent AC4 resume half: only an explicit operator-approved extension lifts a Run's budget hold; nothing resets automatically.

## Design (maintainer-confirmed 2026-09-25)
Operator command on the existing operator socket, modelled on waiver_control: controller UID only, interactive Sessions only. Records a durable, append-only extension (extra units and/or later expiry, never past the launch authorization expiry). Ledger total = grant + extensions. Clears the hold but does not Resume; the operator Resumes separately.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Resume refused while held and no covering extension exists.
2. Extension from a non-controller UID or unattended Session refused.
3. After extension, new requests spend from the raised total; restart preserves it; replayed extension request is idempotent.
4. Expiry extension beyond launch authorization expiry refused.
close_reason: Operator extension lifts Provider hold. consumer:skills-core/src/bin/control/inspection.rs:370. Lessons: none.

comments.author: claude/f1ec2cf3-7b27-4e2b-970d-41ce196b5bb8
comments.text: Holds/extensions are numbered generations (provider_requests.rs); extension n lifts hold n, bound by record equality so a missing/rewritten hold fails closed. Total = grant + extensions (<= MAX_RUN_REQUESTS); latest extended expiry replaces the grant's, capped by launch expiry. Policy check runs under the ledger lock with spent count (service extend_provider_budget). Wire: louiselm.operator-provider-extension/1; CLI provider-extend. Tests: broker provider_requests 17, operator 15, control_binary 7, ledger unit. Pre-existing env failures unchanged (louiselm-2fb5).

title: Load the production Codex sender guard and enable brokered network
description:
## Goal
Implement the confirmed supervisor-owned Sender guard and accept NetworkPolicy::Brokered only while production sender enforcement, broker admission and current host conformance are valid.

## Scope
The maintainer confirmed louiselm-80yzp in claude/d7834ce3-9555-4d81-ad34-eb0aed935af8 on 2026-09-24: root per-Session Launch supervisor owns the guard; explicitly approved libbpf-rs links system libbpf.so.1 without bundling; build.rs compiles C with clang and embeds the object in the measured launcher. The Control broker stays non-root. No new privileged service.

## Implementation slices
- louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4.1: compile and embed the reviewed guard.
- louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4.2: supervisor loader, protected pins/maps, enrollment and kernel loss lifecycle.
- louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4.3: listener placement in the Session namespace and authenticated descriptor handoff.
- louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4.4: measured support through the existing host conformance gate, non-waivable.
- louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4.5: final Brokered activation after all enforcement and the disclosure decision.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every slice meets its own acceptance and privileged VM gate. Missing or unloadable enforcement refuses Verified launch; ordinary Sessions remain usable without a Verified claim.
2. Keep the guard protected while any endpoint/connection is usable; supervisor death/exec latches kernel loss, including at the actual upstream write. Recovery never re-enrolls a runtime.
3. Enablement follows exact runtime/broker enrollment and an authenticated post-enrollment supervisor response. Per-request admission remains independent of kernel send checks.
4. Final activation consumes the S2 Model/effort policy and S3 shared Run limits, expiry, Park and Attention, and implements the confirmed outcome of louiselm-hp733 before any enablement.
5. Preserve Denied and unset-config behavior, stock ACP chain, no ambient Session network and no credential disclosure.

## Testing
Each child extends the existing disposable launcher-VM/conformance machinery with production-boundary coverage and specific refusals. No paid calls or desktop installation. Run complete affected skills-core gates. Guest proof does not close .3.3 Verified authentication gating or .3.13/.3.14 real acceptance.

## Notes
Canonical vocabulary: louiselm-eglwd. Proof obligations: docs/codex-kernel-guard-proof.md (Existing consumers and remaining integration).
Use the parent-child links for aggregate completion; do not add reverse parent-blocked-by-child edges. Disclosure blocks only activation so independent preparatory work remains ready.

title: Own Sender guard enrollment and lifetime in the Launch supervisor
description:
## Goal
The root per-Session Launch supervisor owns the production Sender guard without granting BPF authority to the Control broker.

## Scope
In: a narrow libbpf-rs loader, supervisor enrollment/pinning/disposal, and the ownership/loss contract in docs/codex-kernel-guard-proof.md.
Out: new privileged daemons, policy decisions in the supervisor, subscription authentication and Brokered activation.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Use the explicitly approved libbpf-rs/libbpf-sys dependency with system libbpf.so.1, no bundled libbpf. Verify linking/features before implementation; inability to meet this constraint needs a maintainer decision.
2. Load only the embedded object. Preserve protected link pins/maps and namespace references while any endpoint or accepted connection remains usable.
3. Enroll the exact measured Agent runtime and authorized broker before freezing enrollment. Retain the post-enrollment authenticated supervisor response as an enablement prerequisite.
4. Supervisor death or exec latches loss in the kernel; recovery never re-enrolls a runtime. Runtime exit/replacement and stale Session/Run/revision cannot regain authority.
5. Loss blocks the actual upstream write, including a decision made before owner loss. Do not substitute a userspace preflight check. Dispose endpoints/descendants before releasing enforcement or identities; ambiguous cleanup refuses reuse.
6. Return typed sanitized failures. Any added unsafe platform boundary requires the alternatives/evidence and precise safety arguments in docs/agent-rust.md.

## Testing
Privileged disposable-VM gate using production loader code and deterministic runtime/upstream fixtures: protected pins/frozen maps, helper denials, death/exec between admission and upstream write, broker crash, no recovery re-enrollment and complete cleanup. Retain positive controls and existing ownership negative controls. Run complete skills-core gates.

## Notes
Maintainer approval and source: louiselm-80yzp, claude/d7834ce3-9555-4d81-ad34-eb0aed935af8. Sender guard authenticates the sender; request admission remains broker policy.

title: Hand the guarded Session listener to the unprivileged broker
description:
## Goal
Stock Codex reaches the broker request path through a listener in its Session network namespace, with no ambient Session networking.

## Scope
In: privileged listener placement, authenticated descriptor handoff through existing launcher/broker ownership boundaries, and connection cleanup.
Out: guard-policy redesign, generic proxying, host cutover and enabling Brokered before final integration.

1. The Launch supervisor creates the narrow endpoint in the exact Session namespace and hands its descriptor to the dedicated non-root Control broker. No broker BPF privilege or new root service.

4. Preserve the ACP proxy/adapter chain, broker-owned upstream destination/authentication and absence of credentials in Session state. No external route is introduced into the Session.
5. Failed/partial handoff, broker restart/crash and disposal close owned descriptors and fail closed; no endpoint reuse while ownership or cleanup is uncertain.

## Testing
Add a privileged disposable-VM gate with distinct kernel UIDs/namespaces and offline runtime/upstream doubles through the production handoff: successful request, inherited-socket helper and cross-Session denials, invalid handoff, broker crash, stale connection and zero-survivor disposal. Run focused and complete skills-core gates.

title: Gate Sender guard support through existing host conformance
description:
## Goal
The existing host conformance gate refuses Verified launch when the Sender guard is missing, unloadable or no longer matches its measured inputs; this control cannot be waived.

## Scope
In: installed measurement/probes, admission and conformance invalidation using the existing report/certificate contract.
Out: a parallel certificate/gate, weakened waivers, host installation or declaring a guest pass installed acceptance.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Bind the embedded guard through the measured launcher and measure the actual system loader/library and required kernel/BTF/LSM inputs through the existing profile.
2. Exercise production load/attach/ownership behavior; an advertised kernel flag or the old proof alone cannot certify support. Missing hooks, failed load and uncertain cleanup fail specifically.
3. Changed/stale measured inputs or lost enforcement invalidate the applicable evidence. The launch path reports a typed actionable guard-unavailable reason via existing conformance admission.
4. Missing/broken Sender guard enforcement is not waivable, for interactive or unattended Verified launch.
5. Ordinary Sessions remain usable without claiming Verified protection, including the unset/default configuration and operator-selected auto-approval.

## Testing
Extend the privileged disposable launcher-VM/conformance gate with positive control, unsupported host/load failure, changed inputs, stale evidence, attempted waiver and ordinary-Session cases. Keep guest reports unable to certify an installed host. Run focused conformance tests and complete skills-core gates.

## Notes

title: Enable Brokered networking only with complete Sender guard enforcement
description:
## Goal
Enable NetworkPolicy::Brokered only after the production Sender guard, broker admission and current host conformance jointly enforce the confirmed contract.

## Scope
In: replacing sandbox.rs unconditional Brokered refusal with checked production wiring, plus end-to-end privileged offline acceptance and public docs.
Out: real API requests/host acceptance (.3.13/.3.14), subscription support, posture UI and the separate Verified authentication launch gate (.3.3).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Enable only after exact runtime/broker enrollment, immutable guard state, authenticated post-enrollment supervisor response, correct listener handoff and current non-waivable conformance evidence. Any failure refuses Brokered.
2. Consume S1 request mediation, S2 Model/effort policy and S3 durable shared Run limits/expiry/Park. Each complete buffered/batched HTTP request receives current admission; sendmmsg kernel checks are never request-count authorization.
3. Preserve loss enforcement at the actual upstream write and through reused/streaming connections, including owner death/exec after admission. No recovery re-enrollment or stale authority reuse.
4. Consume the confirmed disclosure contract from louiselm-hp733 and its implementation in louiselm-qbr.11 before activation: forward reviewed metadata unchanged under a versioned closed profile, reject unknown/malformed metadata, bind the exact profile to Provider permission, require fresh authorization for profile changes through existing policy (including selected auto-approval), and report disclosure without an anonymity claim. No separate mandatory prompt or silent stripping/rewriting. Acceptance must prove the profile enforcement and authorization boundary are reached.
5. Denied networking, unset Provider permission and ordinary subscription Sessions preserve their behavior; no ambient network or credential leakage. Keep Verified opt-in and operator-selected auto-approval supported.
6. Update consumed public docs/types. Guarded fake-upstream success does not close the separate Verified launch gate or real VM/host acceptance.

## Testing
A mandatory disposable-VM gate reaches production sandbox, supervisor, non-root broker and HTTPS request transport with deterministic runtime/upstream doubles. Cover positive streaming request, unauthorized sender, per-request budget denial, expiry, unsupported host, owner-loss race at actual upstream write and disposal. title: Serve Provider traffic only through guarded sockets
description:

title: Refuse Verified launch without brokered Provider authentication
description:
## Goal

A runtime that cannot authenticate through brokered or ephemeral broker-issued
credentials cannot complete a Verified launch, so Verified never implies a
protection the integration does not actually provide.

## Scope

- In scope: extending the existing louiselm-qbr.5.1.1 AC5 launch authority gate
  to also check brokered/ephemeral Provider authentication; refusing Verified
  launch when that check fails; keeping ordinary non-Verified Sessions usable
  without claiming the protection.
- Out of scope: credential custody and the request path (blocking sibling
  tasks); host conformance gating, owned by louiselm-d6fv.12; network posture
  evidence and display, owned by louiselm-d6fv.6.13, which consumes this
  enforcement rather than the other way round.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Verified launch is refused when the exact runtime cannot use brokered or
   ephemeral broker-issued Provider credentials. Refusal ends launch, consistent
   with parent louiselm-qbr.5.1 AC17.
2. The check extends the existing launch authority gate rather than adding a
   second gate with its own ordering. For the confirmed stock Codex candidate,
   consume the measured BPF-LSM guard/lifetime evidence and current host
   prerequisites from .3.6-.3.9 and existing host conformance; missing or lost
   enforcement refuses Verified launch. Do not duplicate host probing here.
3. An ordinary Session may still launch without brokered authentication, and
   does not report or imply Verified posture. Per AGENTS.md, operator-selected
   YOLO/auto-approval stays a supported choice.
4. Refusal is a typed failure using the existing `ProtocolError` shape, naming
   the missing capability, and is recorded in durable records without
   credentials or raw payloads.

## Testing

- A runtime double that cannot use brokered auth is refused Verified launch; one
  that can is admitted.
- The unset/default case: no configured Provider credential leaves ordinary
  launch working and Verified unclaimed.
- Gate ordering is asserted against the existing louiselm-qbr.5.1.1 acceptance,
  so this check cannot be satisfied after the effects it is meant to guard.
- Verify the maintainer's effective configuration, per AGENTS.md's rule for a
  feature behind optional config.

## Notes

- Rust in the `skills-core` crate; `docs/agent-rust.md` and
  `docs/agent-testing.md` are binding.
- Blocked by both siblings: the gate can only check a capability that exists.
- Brokered authentication means the broker-held OpenAI API key first (louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.12); subscription sign-in (.3.4) is optional and deferred (louiselm-gy165).
- This is the slice that makes the other two honest. Without it, Verified can be
  claimed while Provider credentials still sit inside a Session.

title: Prove broker-owned Codex subscription authentication and refresh
description:
## Goal
Establish a supported way for the Control broker to make Codex/OpenAI subscription requests while reusable credentials remain outside every confined Session.

## Scope
Investigate and prove authentication custody, the separate operator sign-in and refresh lifecycle for the exact installed Codex integration. Preserve the existing account/subscription and ordinary Codex login. Prefer supported Codex authentication machinery; do not assume that managed login exports tokens to the broker or that external-token login provides confinement.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Identify a supported login/refresh and request-authentication boundary with current primary documentation and exact executable/API versions. Demonstrate how an authenticated request reaches the intended subscription service rather than API-key billing.
2. Dedicated broker-owned credential state is provisioned through explicit operator sign-in; no import of the operator's existing credential stores, no secrets in ACP messages, Session files, argv, environment, logs or durable decision records.
3. Reproducible disposable evidence covers login success/failure, refresh/expiry/revocation, restart, concurrent refresh ownership and absence of credentials from the confined Session. Preserve existing private credential storage validation.
4. Record actual integration limitations and a precise pass/fail verdict. If supported custody or subscription use cannot be established, keep the implementation blocked and route the unresolved architecture back to ow3ok; an offline fake is not proof of real subscription support.
5. No runtime fork, current-login change or installed cutover is implicit. Real sign-in and upstream acceptance happen through a concrete operator-driven procedure after the candidate is reviewable; automated suites use synthetic credentials and no external network.

## Testing
Reuse credential custody tests and distinct-UID acceptance patterns. Separate deterministic protocol/refresh tests from explicitly recorded installed/live acceptance. Keep all credential contents out of Beads.

## Notes
Confirmed contract: louiselm-ow3ok design, codex/01a0b244-e023-7762-bdbf-19baf015da98. Existing broker/provider_credentials.rs is static UTF-8 custody and has no OAuth lifecycle. Local codex-acp generated GetAccountParams supports managed refresh; account/read returns account metadata, not an exported credential. Primary docs: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server#auth-endpoints and https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth. This is a feasibility prerequisite, not a declaration that a viable bridge already exists.
notes:
Investigation artifacts: docs/codex-auth-proof.md and scripts/probe-codex-auth.py. BLOCKED_SUBSCRIPTION_BRIDGE: external-token custody fails; legacy managed token export exists but supported broker subscription transport and real lifecycle/custody acceptance remain unproven. Existing real-sign-in/custody/lifecycle acceptance remains required.
Confirmed .3.10 contract supersedes the pending-design notes above: require documented support for login, refresh and broker-originated subscription calls; legacy getAuthStatus export is research-only even when pinned/tested. If no supported bridge can be established, Verified Codex stays unavailable and ordinary Codex keeps working. .3.10 closes as a decision, not a passing proof. This task remains open for documented support plus explicit operator sign-in, lifecycle/concurrent-refresh/custody and real subscription acceptance; existing tests do not satisfy those missing gates.

title: Prove Codex local endpoint authority cannot pass to tools
description:
## Goal
Prove that a local Responses endpoint can serve the exact authorized Codex runtime without granting its Provider authority to tools, helpers or other Sessions.

## Scope
One reproducible offline integration proof for the installed Codex runtime, existing local endpoint hook and LouiseLM launcher/broker boundary. Keep upstream destinations broker-owned and the Session without ambient network. No real Provider credentials or internet requests.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Exercise an exact pinned Codex app-server request through the candidate boundary to a fake endpoint, including streaming completion. Identify the authoritative runtime process across acp-proxy, codex-acp and app-server; wrapper membership or ancestry is not authentication.
2. Demonstrate denials for a tool/helper in the same Session, another Session, inherited connections/descriptors, stale envelope revision, revoked or expired authority, runtime exit/replacement and late responses after disposal. No shared Session bearer token, loopback address, UID membership or first connection alone may grant full Agent authority.
3. Explain and test how endpoint placement works with the empty network namespace and how any bridge authenticates each request against the exact Session/Run/revision/lifetime. Preserve the existing lifetime-pinned per-message credential requirement; explicitly account for any translation boundary.
4. Only reviewed Codex operations reach a broker-selected upstream; malformed or alternate-destination attempts cause no external effect. Existing ACP logging/proxy behavior is preserved.
5. Record a concrete pass/fail and runnable evidence. If stock Codex cannot meet the boundary, report the exact missing hook and return the architecture decision to ow3ok. Do not silently add a runtime patch, generic proxy, broader networking or weaker authority.

## Testing
Disposable real processes/namespaces plus fake endpoint; no real Agent account, Provider network or current Neovim changes. Include concurrent sibling/tool attempts and lifecycle ordering, not only happy-path HTTP.

## Notes
Confirmed contract: louiselm-ow3ok design, codex/01a0b244-e023-7762-bdbf-19baf015da98. title: Bind stock Codex endpoint sends to its exact runtime lifetime
description:
## Goal
Prove that a guarded local model endpoint accepts bytes only from the exact authorized stock Codex runtime throughout its lifetime.

## Scope
Extend the disposable BPF-LSM proof into a measured sender/endpoint binding using existing launcher identity and isolation facilities. This slice owns the binding, not guard-loss recovery, full broker request policy, subscription authentication or installed cutover.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Preserve successful synthetic streaming from the pinned stock app-server while denying actual tools and concurrent siblings. Kernel evidence binds Session, Run, envelope revision and runtime lifetime; a port number, UID, ancestor, first connection or reusable bearer alone grants nothing.
2. Prove denial for another Session/network namespace, PID reuse, exec/replacement, inherited and explicitly passed TCP descriptors, endpoint address/port reuse, IPv4/IPv6 and stale bindings. No pidfd or procfs snapshot is presented as per-send sender identity by itself.
3. Protect the authoritative binding against tools changing it. Explain the exact production sender-to-broker association and test it; keep policy authorization in the unprivileged Control broker and privileged mechanics in the Launch supervisor.
4. Define and test atomic publication/revision of the binding, with a denied initial state and no mixed-old/new policy during concurrent sends. Unsupported exact integration fails closed.
5. Retain the primitive report as limited historical evidence. Deliver a reproducible assigned-identity VM proof with both positive controls and specific denials; a missing prerequisite or timeout is not a pass.

## Testing
Use offline fake upstreams and bounded real processes in an independently owned disposable VM; run applicable complete Rust/launcher gates for executable changes. title: Keep the Codex endpoint closed across kernel-guard failures
description:
## Goal
Ensure a reachable Codex model endpoint never accepts unauthenticated traffic when its kernel guard is absent, lost or being replaced.

## Scope
Own startup, protected attachment/map lifetime, loss, recovery and teardown around the sender binding. Reuse existing launch sequencing and host-conformance ownership. Request-content policy and authentication remain sibling work.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Start with the endpoint inaccessible. Enable effects only after measured guard attachment and runtime/tool authority checks satisfy the existing sequence-0/sequence-1 launch ordering.
2. Reproduce the prototype's detachment counterexample, then prove fail-closed behavior for loader/supervisor death, link/map loss, broker loss, replacement and concurrent connection/sends during each transition. Protect guard links, maps and attachment ownership from Sessions.
3. Revoke authority before releasing endpoints/identities; deny inherited open sockets and buffered work after revocation. Disposal must prove descendants and owned enforcement resources are cleaned without detaching protection too early.
4. Missing/disabled BPF LSM or BTF, unsupported kernel behavior, failed verification and stale host conformance refuse Verified launch. Feed existing host conformance and launch-gate consumers; do not create a parallel posture system.
5. Ordinary Sessions, including operator-selected auto-approval, remain supported without claiming this protection. No silent fallback from Verified to ordinary authority.
6. Recovery restores only still-authorized identity/revision/expiry and never broadens grants. Provide bounded positive and hostile VM evidence plus an explicit cleanup result.

## Testing
Existing launcher and host-conformance seams, deterministic fault injection, and disposable assigned-UID VM composition. Exercise failures during startup and active streaming, concurrent policy changes and teardown. Keep destructive or privileged changes inside the private guest.

title: Prove broker admission for each buffered Codex request
description:
## Goal
Prove every complete local model request is authorized independently even when several requests share one authenticated kernel send.

## Scope
An offline feasibility slice at existing broker authorization/lifecycle seams with a fake upstream. Own framing-to-admission evidence; do not implement live subscription transport or duplicate the full shared-budget implementation in louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Reproduce two same-destination sendmmsg requests receiving one kernel hook check, then show two separate broker admission decisions. Also cover multiple requests in one write and one request split across writes.
2. Before each fake upstream effect validate the trusted sender binding, Session/Run/revision, current authority, expiry, reviewed operation, Model allowlist and available request reservation. Socket acceptance or a previous request cannot cache permission for the next.
3. Revoke/change revision/expire between queued or partial requests and prove no later unauthorized upstream call occurs. Serialize authority/reservation decisions with the existing broker owner; explain and exercise the race boundary.
4. Reject malformed/contradictory framing, unsupported operations, alternative destinations and redirect requests with zero unauthorized effects. Define the reviewed operation fixture explicitly; do not claim coverage for untested Codex operations.
5. Cancel locally at expiry/disposal, preserve received output and spent units, discard late results, and never refund/retry an unknown outcome automatically. Reuse typed ProtocolError/NextAction and existing lifecycle ownership.
6. Return reusable validation/fixture evidence for .3.2 and the complete ACP proof. If the current seams cannot support the contract, file a focused needs-design blocker rather than inventing a general proxy.

## Testing
Deterministic fake-upstream tests for batch/partial/queued framing and concurrent lifecycle changes, plus the opt-in sendmmsg counterexample. No Provider network, real credentials or runtime patch.

title: Prove the complete stock Codex guarded ACP integration
description:
## Goal
Establish whether the exact stock Codex ACP composition can satisfy endpoint authority and enforced tool separation before production Provider requests are implemented.

## Scope
Integrate the three kernel-guard proof slices through LouiseLM -> acp-proxy -> codex-acp -> the measured Codex app-server, using synthetic model replies and a fake upstream. This replaces the missing positive integration proof; louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.5 remains the routing-only negative result.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Pin all relevant executable/adapter and host-policy identities and prove a streaming tool-call turn through the complete chain with no account credentials or ambient Session network.
2. The actual runtime succeeds while real tools/helpers, concurrent siblings, other Sessions and replacement runtimes fail without fresh authorization. Prove inherited descriptors and SCM_RIGHTS transfer, IPv4/IPv6/namespace crossings and runtime exit/exec/PID reuse.
3. Exercise asynchronous I/O/io_uring and alternative send paths. Every supported path preserves actual-sender authority; explicitly refuse unsupported paths and prove stock Codex remains functional under those restrictions.
4. Compose stale revisions, batched/partial/buffered requests, expiry, guard/loader/broker loss, revocation, recovery and late responses after disposal. No unauthorized fake upstream effect and no fail-open interval may occur.
5. Prove tool separation beyond network sends: process-memory access, descriptor theft and untrusted code inside the runtime cannot bypass the accepted boundary. Agent actions influenced by tool output remain Agent actions; no prompt-injection immunity is claimed.
6. Unsupported host/integration refuses Verified launch, with ordinary Sessions and operator-selected auto-approval still available. Preserve ACP logging behavior and prohibit sensitive request/auth material in new evidence or logs.
7. Publish an exact pass/fail matrix, runnable reproduction, measured artifacts and cleanup evidence. Negative or incomplete results keep .3.2 blocked and return unresolved architecture to a needs-design question. Subscription authentication remains the independent .3.4 prerequisite; a synthetic pass cannot satisfy it.

title: Same-UID helper can control the guarded Codex runtime
description:
The complete stock-Codex guard candidate admits only the enrolled app-server’s network sends, but a concurrent process under the Session UID can attach to that app-server and modify its memory. That process can make the enrolled app-server perform an otherwise-denied effect.

## Observed

2026-09-21, disposable Debian 13 KVM guest 6.12.107+deb13-cloud-amd64, task louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.9. The full LouiseLM -> acp-proxy -> codex-acp -> stock Codex chain ran under scripts/probes/codex-kernel-guard/integration_probe.py with no ambient network or credentials.

The hostile concurrent same-UID probe reported:

```
AssertionError: {'ptrace': {'denied': False}, 'process_memory': {'denied': False}, 'descriptor_theft': {'denied': True, 'errno': 13}, 'endpoint': {'denied': True, 'errno': 1}}
```

The guest has `/proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope=0`. The direct endpoint send was correctly rejected with EPERM while ptrace attach and `/proc/<runtime>/mem` open succeeded.

## Symptoms

- The kernel socket guard says the helper has no endpoint authority.
- The helper can instead modify the authorized app-server and cause that process to send.
- A positive Verified integration claim would therefore be false.

## Root cause

`scripts/probes/codex-kernel-guard/binding.bpf.c:90` authenticates the sender at `socket_sendmsg` but does not protect the enrolled task from cross-process control. `scripts/probes/codex-kernel-guard/integration_tool.py:23` supplies the observed ptrace and process-memory probes.

## Why it was not caught

The binding proof covered sender identity, exec/PID reuse, SCM_RIGHTS and endpoint effects. The tool-isolation suite covers tools inside the production namespace boundary. Neither composed an unsandboxed adapter/helper sharing the exact stock app-server UID with the guarded full ACP chain.

## Fix direction

At the same protected BPF-LSM ownership boundary, deny ptrace access to an enrolled runtime from every other task. Preserve self access and pre-enrollment supervisor measurement. Re-run loader-loss/read-only-pin cleanup with the additional hook; do not rely on host Yama configuration or weaken the exact-process authority contract.

## Acceptance

- The recorded same-UID ptrace and `/proc/<runtime>/mem` probes fail while the app-server remains functional.
- The complete guarded ACP streaming tool-call turn still passes.
- Existing binding, ownership, request-admission and hostile tool gates remain green.
- Removing only the runtime-protection hook reproduces the bypass.

## Not covered

Kernel/root compromise, actual Provider credentials, installed host certification and subscription authentication remain outside this defect.

title: Mediate locked-dependency fetches through the broker without executing code
description:
## Problem Statement

Direct package fetching is called out in louiselm-qbr.5.1's problem statement
as an effect that currently bypasses policy. Nothing broker-side yet fetches
or authorizes dependency coordinates; louiselm-qbr.5.1.1 and
louiselm-qbr.5.1.2 explicitly scoped dependencies out.

## Scope

In scope: broker-mediated fetch of starting-lockfile dependencies by exact
coordinate and integrity value, writing only to a Session's cache overlay;
typed-candidate handling for new dependency coordinates encountered after
start; interactive batched approval; pre-authorized scope for unattended
Runs; explicit-approval requirement for git dependencies, arbitrary URLs,
missing integrity, and non-registry sources.

Out of scope: executing any fetched package's code (never in scope for the
broker, at any point); Provider network egress (sibling task, filed
separately under this same parent); general filesystem effect policy beyond
the Session's cache overlay.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Starting-lockfile dependencies are fetched automatically only by exact
   coordinate and integrity value; the broker never executes fetched package
   code and writes only to the Session's cache overlay.
2. A dependency coordinate not present in the starting lockfile is a typed
   candidate, not an automatic fetch.
3. Interactive Sessions may batch-approve typed candidates; unattended Runs
   require the scope to be pre-authorized before the Run starts — an
   unattended Run cannot prompt mid-flight.
4. Git dependencies, arbitrary URLs, missing integrity values, and
   non-registry sources always require explicit approval, regardless of Run
   mode.
5. A dependency name chosen by the Agent is never sent to any external
   service before it is an approved, typed candidate (no speculative
   resolution against an untrusted registry).

## Testing Notes

- No live network in tests: fake registry/transport.
- Cover: dependency-name exfiltration attempt, redirect during fetch, altered
  lockfile, missing integrity, malicious archive contents, package
  install/post-install scripts never executed, unattended Run without
  pre-authorization denied.

## Notes

Extends the broker's typed effect-policy schema (see the Provider-egress
sibling task filed under this same parent) for the dependency-fetch effect

title: Broker typed canonical Beads mutations for a Session
description:
## Problem Statement

Every Session today invokes `br`/`bvr` directly against the canonical
`.beads` database and JSONL. louiselm-qbr.5.1 AC10-11 require the broker to
be the sole path for canonical Beads mutation, deriving the attributable
actor and enforcing role/envelope/revision/idempotency/budget, with only a
coordinator permitted to dispatch, promote blockers, satisfy integration
gates, publish, and close. louiselm-qbr.6 already assumes this primitive
exists ("Only the control broker invokes canonical `br` ... Workers and
coordinators request typed operations") but louiselm-qbr.6 is deferred and
scoped to the parallel-worker case specifically — it does not implement the
primitive itself, and nothing implements it for the ordinary single-Session
case either.

## Scope

In scope: a typed request/receipt path from a Session to the broker for
ordinary canonical Beads mutations (claim, comment, update status/labels,
dependency edits, close with verdict); broker-derived attributable Session
actor; role/envelope/revision/idempotency/budget enforcement; invocation of
the pinned upstream `br` with controlled temporary storage; a receipt back to
the Session; refresh of the Session's local read replica.

Out of scope: coordinator-only role restrictions for dispatch, blocker
promotion, integration gates, publish, and close, and the parallel-worker
replica model — both remain louiselm-qbr.6, which consumes this task's
primitive. Any UI/CLI presentation of receipts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A Session cannot open or write the canonical `.beads` database or JSONL
   directly; the broker is the only process with that access.
2. Canonical mutations are typed requests (claim, comment, update, dep edit,
   close-with-verdict); the broker derives the actor from the authenticated
   Session/channel binding established in louiselm-qbr.5.1.1 — a
   client-supplied actor string is never trusted verbatim.
3. The broker enforces revision and idempotency: identical retries return the
   same receipt; a stale expected-revision fails closed with the typed error
   shape from louiselm-qbr.5.1.2 AC8.
4. The broker invokes the pinned upstream `br` binary for the actual
   mutation, using controlled temporary storage, and never reimplements
   `br`'s graph/workflow/storage semantics.
5. A successful mutation returns a receipt and triggers a refresh of the
   Session's local read replica; native `br`/`bvr --robot-*` reads continue
   to work unchanged against that replica.
6. An action outside the Session's granted role (e.g. attempting the
   coordinator-only actions reserved by louiselm-qbr.6) is denied with one
   deduplicated escalation naming the missing capability, per parent AC12 —
   not a silent no-op and not a duplicate escalation per retry.

## Testing Notes

- Disposable real Beads workspace (per parent Testing Notes) for actor
  attribution, replica refresh, idempotency, and denied direct canonical
  writes.
- Cover: concurrent requests from two Sessions, stale revision, duplicate
  idempotency key, attempted direct file open denied, escalation
  deduplication.

## Notes

This is the primitive louiselm-qbr.6 AC2/AC11 assumes already exists.
Extends the broker's typed effect-policy schema for the "external mutation"
effect category (parent AC5).

title: Run isolated parallel workers and coordinate integration
description:
## Problem Statement

Parallel workers need to execute independent Beads concurrently without colliding on code, fragmenting tracker truth, broadening authority, or closing work before integration is proven. Shared writable worktrees and direct access to one canonical `.beads` database let a hostile Session bypass both isolation and typed authorization.

## Solution

Run each worker as a first-class contained Session with a stable private source snapshot, private Git metadata, and a local disposable Beads replica. Workers use native `br`/`bvr` robot reads and may immediately request claims, comments, findings, updates, and transitions through the local control broker. The broker is the sole writer of canonical Beads bytes and invokes upstream `br` with derived Session identity, capability/revision checks, and receipts.

The coordinator remains the semantic authority for candidate selection, dispatch, blocker promotion, integration, gates, and closure. Worker code leaves confinement as a normalized bundle, is applied to a fresh integration snapshot, and is independently verified before promotion.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want parallel workers isolated from one another and the live checkout while seeing a current task graph.
2. As a coordinator, I want graph eligibility separated from ranking and exact work dispatched under attenuated authority.
3. As a worker, I want to record findings immediately and hand off verifiable work without direct canonical writes.
4. As a coordinator, I want to validate blocker requests and integrate exact independently verified bundles.
5. As an operator, I want dead-worker recovery and bounded quarantine without copying sensitive logs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each worker is an attributable Session with its own identity, private stable source snapshot/workspace, private Git state, capability channel, input manifest, and atomic brokered Beads claim.
2. Worker startup receives a revisioned local Beads replica from the broker. Native `br`/`bvr --robot-*` read and may experiment there, but canonical-path discovery and direct canonical writes are denied. Replica changes are disposable and never reconciled as authority.
3. The coordinator obtains the authorized ready set from broker-backed `br` state, intersects it with advisory `bvr` ranking/tracks, and dispatches one exact Bead. Ranking cannot authorize or claim.
4. Workers may request claims, comments, findings, ordinary updates, and transitions immediately within their envelope. Discoveries do not expand code scope automatically.
5. A worker cannot promote its own discovery to a blocker. It files evidence and a structured request; the coordinator validates before changing a `blocks` edge.
6. On blocker promotion, the coordinator records the edge and state transition through the broker, stops/Parks the worker as policy requires, and preserves its Session/workspace. Closing the blocker may resume the preserved work when safe.
7. Workflow policy retains `open -> in_progress -> ready_for_integration -> closed` and `ready_for_integration -> rework -> in_progress`; handoff requires evidence and only the coordinator satisfies `integration_verified` and closes.
8. Worker handoff exports a deterministic normalized bundle and evidence identifying its digest, originating Session/input, checks, and risks. Agent branches/commits remain evidence only.
9. The coordinator applies the exact bundle to a fresh integration snapshot, runs combined verification in a fresh contained Session, and promotes/closes only the verified digest.
10. Known-dead worker lifecycle evidence permits immediate recovery: freeze/terminate as appropriate, retain a bounded quarantine manifest and workspace under TTL, record a brokered recovery comment, and release only its claim. Stale thresholds remain fallback for external unmanaged actors.
11. Only the control broker invokes canonical `br`, publishes canonical JSONL, and performs control-checkout tracker checkpoints. Workers and coordinators request typed operations; role policy reserves dispatch, blocker promotion, integration gates, publication, and closure to the coordinator.
12. Tracker and integration tests prove attributable concurrent requests, revision/idempotency handling, coherent publication, direct-write denial, rework readiness, blocker suppression/restoration, exact bundle promotion, and recovery without unrelated mutation or sensitive evidence copying.

## Implementation Notes

- Treat the coordinator as semantic authority and the broker as canonical byte writer; these roles are complementary.
- Use upstream `br` for graph/workflow/storage semantics. A broker-owned TMPDIR stays inside its allowed storage or fails closed.
- Treat `bvr` as advisory and intersect its output by Bead identity with authorized `br` state.
- Preserve local replicas for fast Agent-native robot workflows; never merge their database/JSONL bytes.
- This supersedes the earlier shared linked-worktree and shared SQLite writer design.

## Testing Notes

- Use fake ACP workers, private temporary source snapshots, and disposable Beads replicas.
- Exercise death before/after claim, edits, handoff, blocker discovery, and broker receipt.
- Test concurrent requests, stale revisions, retries, coordinator-only operations, publication checkpoints, and attempts to open canonical paths.
- Reuse the trusted exporter/verifier tests rather than accepting Agent Git output.

## Out of Scope

- Per-worker semantic database reconciliation.
- Direct canonical Beads access from any Session.
- Workers selecting arbitrary work, promoting blockers, integrating, satisfying gates, publishing, or closing.
- Opaque subagents as primary workers.
- Automatic copying of raw logs, prompts, tool payloads, environments, or credentials.

title: Grill-me needed: how should LouiseLM validate workflow safety?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; it needs a focused design session.

## Question
How should LouiseLM validate a workflow before allowing it to run, especially when the workflow can invoke Agents that may create or trigger more work?

## Context
The attention-control-plane design is intentionally moving from informal loops toward declarative workflows with stages, transitions, triggers, resolvers, Agent execution, and human attention gates. A workflow validator should catch unsafe topology before execution rather than discovering it after Agents have started.

The motivating risks are:
- recursive or unbounded Agent spawning when a workflow triggers itself indirectly;
- cycles that continually re-enter stages or regenerate work;
- no reachable human or operator escape hatch;
- cancellation and disposal paths that do not reach every active worker;
- a workflow that is structurally valid but has no terminating path;
- a workflow whose automatic transitions bypass the intended human-attention gate.

## Threads worth pulling
- Should validation be static topology analysis, a runtime budget, or both?
- What must be proven before execution: acyclicity, bounded repetition, reachable termination, reachable human override, cancellation propagation, and ownership of spawned work?
- How should intentional loops (polling, retries, review cycles) be expressed and bounded without making ordinary workflows impossible to describe?
- Is an explicit escape transition required for every workflow, or can a global emergency stop satisfy the invariant?
- How should nested Agent-created workflows be scoped, budgeted, and prevented from recursively spawning indefinitely?
- Which failures reject a workflow, which produce warnings, and which require explicit human approval?
- How can validation itself remain side-effect free and avoid starting Agents?

## Desired outcome
A small, testable validation contract for workflow definitions, including safety invariants, bounded-loop semantics, escape-hatch requirements, and the boundary between static validation and runtime enforcement.

## Out of scope
Do not implement workflow execution, spawn Agents, or settle the contract in this issue without a dedicated grill-me session.
close_reason: Resolved by maintainer in the 2026-08-26 grill-me session. Settled: two contracts (Validation, pure/frontmatter/binary/no-override, may reject; admission, Run-scoped, stops or escalates). Bounding unit is the Generator, not the back edge -- automatic Generators declare a literal bound, human-resolved ones are bounded by the human, exhaustion must exit its loop. Generated work is bounded per Run via --actor provenance, NOT by br policy.yaml: a generative loop keeps the beads graph a DAG forever, so acyclicity is not termination. Skill-invocation permission routes to louiselm-qbr.5.1 envelopes, not a second authority mechanism. Bound exhaustion Parks (Cancellation, Sessions retained) with a declared expiry that Disposes; kill and degrade rejected. Escape hatches: synthesized per-stage non-destructive human escape (reachable unilaterally, no Agent cooperation) + destructive global stop + optional authored escapes; global stop alone insufficient because it is destructive. Cancellation propagates by ownership invariant (no stage may create a worker the Run does not own) with bounded ack escalating to Disposal; limit stated -- reaches every worker LouiseLM can address, not every process. Run state lives in capture-service (ambitious and narrow: durable Run record + expiry reaper only), because Agents are vim.system children and a Park expiry enforced in Neovim is unenforceable while the editor is closed; Runs-as-beads-issues rejected. Warm/cold Park tiers, cold gated on loadSession. Assessment (model reads prose, advisory, empty envelope, never gates, stored verdicts) added at maintainer's request alongside Validation. Vocabulary promoted: Run louiselm-kdeg, Generator louiselm-4wtn, Validation louiselm-p5h0, Assessment louiselm-x29k, Park louiselm-k1fv. Work: louiselm-qbr.3.2, louiselm-qbr.3.3, louiselm-qbr.3.4.

title: Wake paired Android for typed Attention items
description:
## Problem Statement

When the operator leaves Neovim, a Session or Run can finish a turn, request permission, Park, or fail without a bounded real-time signal. Agent-authored prose must never become phone notification content, and Android must not gain workflow authority.

## Solution

Capture-service owns a durable current snapshot of typed Attention items for Session and Run subjects. Neovim is the only writer through the owner-only operator socket. Paired Android devices read deterministic cards over pinned HTTPS on Tailscale. After 30 seconds without Neovim input, an unseen item advances delivery through an optional FCM adapter whose collapsible payload contains only fixed generic text and an opaque inbox generation.

## User Stories

1. As an operator away from Neovim, I want a prompt phone signal when an Agent turn is ready, so I know it is my turn to inspect the Session.
2. As an operator, I want explicit permission, Park, and failure conditions surfaced without exposing work content to Google.
3. As an operator with multiple paired devices, I want each active device notified independently and revoked devices excluded immediately.
4. As a maintainer, I want one inspectable durable source of truth so retries and restarts cannot duplicate or lose unresolved attention.
5. As a public user, I want the inbox to work without Firebase configuration and make no provider call unless push is explicitly configured.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a recognized typed lifecycle event, when Neovim upserts it, then capture-service persists one Attention item keyed by subject kind, subject ID, attention kind, and source operation ID.
2. Given a duplicate upsert or retry, when no semantic state changes, then the item and inbox generation do not duplicate or advance.
3. Given a turn_ready item that remains unseen, when Neovim has received no user input for 30 seconds, then delivery becomes eligible; viewing the source Session before that cancels delivery.
4. Given permission_required, run_parked, session_failed, or turn_ready, when the underlying condition ends, then the trusted controller clears the corresponding item and advances the generation once.
5. Given a paired non-revoked Android device, when it fetches the inbox over pinned HTTPS, then it receives only deterministic typed cards and has no endpoint that can create, clear, resolve, approve, resume, or otherwise control work.
6. Given multiple paired devices with registered FCM tokens, when a new generation becomes eligible, then each device is submitted independently once; unchanged unresolved state produces no reminders.
7. Given an FCM submission, then the payload contains only fixed generic notification text and opaque collapsible generation metadata, with no event kind, Session or Run ID, Beads ID, prompt, transcript, path, command, issue title, or Agent-authored text.
8. Given FCM is unconfigured, when Attention items change, then the authenticated inbox remains usable and no Google endpoint is contacted.
9. Given service, editor, or network restart, then unresolved items, monotonic generation, and pending per-device delivery remain deterministic and inspectable.
10. Given a revoked device or invalid credential, then inbox and token-registration requests are rejected and future pushes stop.
11. Given the OpenTofu composition, then a reviewed plan provisions a dedicated deletion-protected Firebase project, Android app, narrowly scoped sender identity, and GitLab Workload Identity Federation without placing private keys in source, plan artifacts, or state.
12. Given the deployed composition and a physical paired Android device away from Neovim, then all four v1 transitions produce the expected generic wake-up and read-only Tailscale inbox behavior.

## Implementation Notes

- Keep Attention storage and delivery modules separate from capture ingestion and Run reaping.
- Extend the local operator socket with typed upsert, clear, snapshot, and status operations; Run tokens and Android credentials cannot write Attention items.
- Extend paired-device HTTPS authentication for current inbox reads and registration or rotation of only that device's FCM token.
- Persist only unresolved state, one monotonic generation, and per-device submitted generation. Opening Android marks seen locally and never resolves server state.
- Deliver all paired non-revoked devices without FCM topics or a primary-device abstraction. Transient failures retry the latest generation; invalid tokens are disabled; permanent auth or configuration failures are surfaced without retry storms.
- Keep the FCM adapter optional. Our deployed acceptance requires it; public installations may omit it.
- Put OpenTofu under infra/firebase with OpenTofu >= 1.12, pinned Google providers, a committed lockfile, GitLab-managed HTTP state, and pinned to-be-continuous Terraform plus GCP components 9.4.0.
- Run credential-free checks on all changes. Restrict authenticated plans to protected main and apply only the exact reviewed plan manually.
- Bootstrap once with operator ADC, then use GitLab OIDC Workload Identity Federation. OpenTofu creates the runtime service account and least-privilege role but never creates its private key; generate and install that one key out of band.
- Preserve project deletion protection. Roll back by disabling delivery, revoking runtime and device credentials, reverting configuration, and applying a reviewed plan rather than destroying the project.

## Testing Notes

- Derive pure model and protocol tests for validation, identity, idempotency, generation, clear transitions, payload redaction, retry classification, and per-device delivery.
- Exercise the real Unix-socket callback and Neovim scheduling boundaries; synchronous fakes alone are insufficient.
- Use authenticated receiver integration tests and fake FCM transport only; automated tests use no network, Firebase credential, or physical device.
- Android tests cover bounded parsing, read-only presentation, token rotation, notification tap, offline retry, Keystore ownership, and revoked credentials.
- Infrastructure checks include tofu fmt -check -recursive, tofu init, tofu validate, a saved reviewed plan, provider lock verification, and CI lint.
- Final closure requires physical Android plus Tailscale acceptance; automated gates alone do not prove background wake-up.

## Out of Scope

- Remote Agent control, approval, rejection, resume, or arbitrary Android actions.
- Agent-authored notification text or inference from Agent prose.
- Periodic reminder notifications, FCM topics, or a primary-device setting.
- A globally shared LouiseLM Firebase project.
- workflow_decision_required until the executor emits a dedicated typed lifecycle event.
- Replacing Neovim as the full workflow cockpit.

title: Persist and expose the current Attention snapshot
description:
## Goal
Make capture-service the inspectable durable owner of current typed Attention items.

## Scope
- In scope: a cohesive Rust Attention model/store; strict validation for Session and Run subjects and the four v1 kinds; idempotent upsert, eligibility update, and clear over the owner-only operator socket; atomic owner-only persistence; monotonic generation; paired-device authenticated read-only snapshot; structured local list/status output.
- Out of scope: Neovim event production, Android presentation, Firebase, and real push delivery.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The key is subject kind plus subject ID plus attention kind plus source operation ID; duplicate semantic writes are no-ops.
2. Only turn_ready, permission_required, run_parked, and session_failed plus bounded deterministic fields are accepted; arbitrary text and unknown fields are rejected before state changes.
3. Effective add, eligibility update, or clear advances generation exactly once and survives process restart; only unresolved state is retained.
4. Operator-socket mutation requires the operator capability. Paired HTTPS exposes only an authenticated snapshot and no Attention mutation route.
5. Revoked or invalid device credentials cannot read the snapshot.
6. louiselm-capture exposes concise machine-readable Attention state including generation, unresolved count, kinds, and sanitized storage errors.

## Testing
- Pure model/store tests cover bounds, idempotency, generation, crash-safe persistence, malformed state, and deterministic ordering with a fake clock.
- Unix-socket tests cover real framed messages, capability rejection, retry identity, and structured errors.
- Receiver tests prove authentication and absence of write routes or sensitive fields.

## Notes
Keep the module separate from capture ingestion and Run reaping. Reuse existing filesystem locking, private-permission, socket, and receiver patterns rather than introducing a database or generic event bus.
close_reason: Implemented durable typed Attention store, owner socket, authenticated read-only inbox, CLI status, and Rust regressions; cargo fmt/clippy/test pass.

title: Show a read-only Attention inbox on paired Android
description:
## Goal
Let a paired Android device inspect current Attention items privately over the existing Tailscale HTTPS channel.

## Scope
- In scope: bounded snapshot parsing in PinnedHttps; deterministic Android card models and platform-View presentation; refresh, empty, unavailable, revoked, and retry states; receiver identity pinning and the existing Keystore-owned pairing credential.
- Out of scope: Firebase SDK, background wake-ups, workflow mutation, transcript or prompt display, and a local Android database.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A paired device fetches the authenticated snapshot over its pinned receiver endpoint and presents attention kind, Session or Run identifier, optional linked identifier or stage, fixed reason label, and age.
2. No server- or Agent-authored display text, transcript, prompt, path, command, Beads title, or issue title is accepted or rendered.
3. Android offers no approve, reject, resume, clear, resolve, or arbitrary action.
4. Opening the inbox records the seen generation only in app-private local state and does not mutate server Attention state.
5. Offline or tailnet-unavailable fetches keep the last safely parsed screen state and expose a bounded retry action; authentication or pin failures require operator action.

## Testing
- JVM protocol tests cover bounded parsing, unknown fields, malformed identifiers, deterministic labels, generation ordering, and receiver errors.
- Headless/instrumented smoke coverage verifies read-only presentation and lifecycle-safe background network work.
- No live receiver, credential, or network is used.

## Notes
Keep networking in PinnedHttps, pairing secrets in PairingStore, and presentation in the Activity. Use platform Views and existing dependencies.
close_reason: Implemented pinned authenticated Attention fetch, strict bounded models, generation-safe read-only Views inbox, retry/operator states, and JVM coverage; Gradle test/lint/assembleDebug pass.

title: First Firebase apply bills the bootstrap project
description:
The first approved Firebase OpenTofu apply partially completes, then stops before Firebase/Hosting/Android creation because the provider charges its Firebase Management API request to the bootstrap quota project, where that unrelated API is intentionally disabled.

## Observed

OpenTofu 1.12.3 with google/google-beta 7.40.0, local operator ADC, GCS production backend, approved plan SHA-256 `fb6c07e738e1f89096014b7b487dd05059ce9a64fa55732053e21d8e1b2cd5b2`.

`infra/firebase/.terraform/apply.log:93-106`:

> Error checking if Firebase is already enabled: googleapi: Error 403: Firebase Management API has not been used in project bartab-dns-20260802 before or it is disabled.
>
> consumer: projects/bartab-dns-20260802
> service: firebase.googleapis.com
> reason: SERVICE_DISABLED

The command exited 1. GCS state safely advanced from serial 9 to serial 13 at generation `1788532026856091`, with no live lock. Firebase project, Hosting site, Android app/key, app audit config, and three project IAM grants are absent. The consumed plan was not retried.

## Symptoms

- The explicitly approved first apply cannot complete.
- The apply is partial but state-consistent, requiring a new plan rather than replaying the old binary.

## Root cause

`infra/firebase/README.md:163-173` directs `GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT=bartab-dns-20260802` through the first apply. The google-beta Firebase client consequently sends its service-usage quota check to that project. The runbook enabled Cloud Billing there for bootstrap but deliberately did not enable Firebase Management.

## Why it was not caught

The saved plan did not execute the create-time Firebase preflight, and static/native tests cannot observe provider quota attribution. Pre-apply validation proved the quota project's billing/API prerequisites but not each provider client's request consumer.

## Fix direction

Keep the GCS/backend bootstrap quota on `bartab-dns-20260802`, but give the Google provider an app-project quota override for post-import plan/apply. Do not enable Firebase Management in the unrelated DNS project. Generate and review a fresh plan from serial 13; never reuse the consumed binary.

## Acceptance

- A documented, version-accurate provider-only quota setting leaves backend access working and charges Firebase Management to `louiselm`.
- A fresh saved plan from serial 13 has no deletes/replacements and contains only unfinished or normalization actions.
- Exact approved apply succeeds; the subsequent live access proofs and detailed-exitcode plan return clean.

## Not covered

The planned resource graph and IAM design remain unchanged. No retry, deploy, DNS change, or state surgery is authorized by this bug filing.
