title: State-bucket acceptance reads the wrong gcloud schema
description:
The post-apply state-bucket acceptance stops even when every live hardening property is correct because it compares raw Cloud Storage API field names against gcloud's flattened presentation schema.

## Observed

Session `codex/01a06a99-3443-7843-b88d-52c47007cd42`, 2026-09-04, gcloud 582.0.0, immediately after exact OpenTofu apply plan SHA-256 `4b543f0c5e5c7c7967a348819b7e8b3d6d848f5d6a10dc76d43c631df96cd68a`.

`infra/firebase/README.md` post-apply bucket check invokes:

> gcloud storage buckets describe gs://louiselm-tfstate --billing-project=bartab-dns-20260802 --format=json

The following jq sees `projectNumber`, `storageClass`, `iamConfiguration`, `versioning`, and `softDeletePolicy` as null and exits 1. The same command with `--raw` returns owner project 729973359575 plus EU, STANDARD, UBLA enabled, PAP enforced, versioning enabled, 604800-second soft delete, and no retention policy.

## Symptoms

- A correct first bootstrap cannot complete its documented live acceptance.
- The fail-closed script stops directly after the project/network milestone without identifying a cloud drift.

## Root cause

The runbook assertion expects Cloud Storage JSON API camelCase fields, but `gcloud storage buckets describe --format=json` emits the command's flattened presentation schema unless `--raw` is supplied.

## Why it was not caught

Static Bash/HCL gates do not execute the live bucket-describe assertion, and earlier reviews validated expected fields without exercising the exact command output mode against the created bucket.

## Fix direction

Add `--raw` to the bucket describe used for machine assertions. Keep human-facing describe commands unchanged where raw API fields are not consumed.

## Acceptance

- The exact post-apply bucket jq fails without `--raw` against the live hardened bucket.
- It passes with `--raw` and asserts the correct owning project and every documented bucket hardening property.
- The remainder of post-apply effective-access and empty-plan acceptance completes.

## Not covered

No infrastructure resource, state, IAM, site content, GitLab variable, deployment, or DNS change is authorized by this documentation/check fix.

title: Absent Firebase service agent stops state-access proof
description:
The first live state-isolation acceptance cannot finish because it unconditionally asks Policy Troubleshooter about the Firebase Rules service agent before that optional identity exists. The preceding six real identities all return exact CANNOT_ACCESS, then gcloud exits NOT_FOUND rather than returning an access state.

## Observed

Session `codex/01a06a99-3443-7843-b88d-52c47007cd42`, 2026-09-04, gcloud 582.0.0, after successful exact apply plan SHA-256 `4b543f0c5e5c7c7967a348819b7e8b3d6d848f5d6a10dc76d43c631df96cd68a`.

The checked-in post-apply block constructs `service-560968636189@firebase-rules.iam.gserviceaccount.com` even though it is absent from both `gcloud iam service-accounts list` and the app project IAM policy. The loop completes 54 checks for principals 1–6, then:

> ERROR: (gcloud.policy-intelligence.troubleshoot-policy.iam) NOT_FOUND: Requested entity was not found.

No cloud mutation or retry followed.

## Symptoms

- Correct live access denials cannot reach the empty-plan acceptance gate.
- `set -e` stops on an optional Firebase identity that has not been provisioned.

## Root cause

`infra/firebase/README.md` adds the known Firebase Rules address to `app_principals` without first proving that the principal exists. Policy Troubleshooter requires an existing principal and reports NOT_FOUND for this absent service agent.

## Why it was not caught

Static gates and command-help validation cannot model which Firebase service agents a first project activation creates. The exact loop was not executed against a newly bootstrapped project before this apply.

## Fix direction

Troubleshoot concrete identities proven present by the app service-account inventory or IAM policy. For known optional service agents, separately prove either absence or include them when present. Preserve the fail-closed direct state-project/bucket IAM scans for explicit app-account, app principal-set, and WIF grants so a future identity cannot silently gain state access.

## Acceptance

- The live newly bootstrapped project no longer stops on the absent Firebase Rules agent.
- Every present app/service identity still returns literal CANNOT_ACCESS for all nine state permissions.
- Optional known identities are either proven absent or checked when present; UNKNOWN and command errors still fail.
- The fresh OpenTofu detailed-exitcode plan returns 0.

## Not covered

No resource, IAM, state, GitLab variable, Hosting deployment, content, or DNS mutation is authorized by this runbook correction.

title: Emit turn-ready Attention after Neovim inactivity
description:
## Goal
Notify the durable Attention system when an Agent turn is ready and the operator has actually left Neovim.

## Scope
- In scope: one typed Neovim Attention client over the local operator socket; immediate turn_ready upsert on authoritative Session turn completion; source-operation identity; user-activity tracking; 30-second idle eligibility; clear when the source Session is viewed or its condition ends; lifecycle disposal and reconnect behavior.
- Out of scope: parsing Agent prose, other Attention kinds, Android, and FCM transport.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Authoritative turn completion immediately creates one unresolved turn_ready item without inspecting response prose.
2. No push eligibility is emitted until the item remains unseen and Neovim has observed no user input for 30 seconds.
3. Continued input anywhere in Neovim delays eligibility; FocusLost may contribute but cannot be the sole presence signal.
4. Viewing the source Session before eligibility cancels pending delivery and clears the item; retries reuse the same operation identity.
5. Late timers, socket callbacks, or Session events after disposal cannot recreate cleared state or call editor APIs from a fast event.
6. Socket failure is visible and retryable without blocking Neovim or losing the local Session state.

## Testing
- Start red with public Session/UI behavior tests for immediate upsert, timer reset, seen clear, reconnect, and disposal.
- Async tests exercise production scheduling and fake time rather than directly invoking callbacks synchronously.
- Existing full Lua quality gates remain green.

## Notes
Use one small shared Attention client and existing Session lifecycle events. Do not create a generic desktop-presence subsystem or infer questions from text.
close_reason: Implemented turn_ready emission, activity-reset idle eligibility, view/prompt clearing, reconnect/disposal handling, and typed client tests; Lua gates pass.

title: Declare the Firebase notification foundation with OpenTofu
description:
## Goal
Define a reviewable, public-safe OpenTofu composition for LouiseLM Android notifications.

## Scope
- In scope: infra/firebase; OpenTofu and pinned Google provider constraints; committed provider lockfile; dedicated deletion-protected Google project; billing input; required APIs; Firebase project; Android app registration; restricted Android Firebase key/config; dedicated runtime sender service account; least-privilege custom role containing only the supported message-create permission; outputs and bootstrap/rotation documentation.
- Out of scope: generating private service-account keys, applying unreviewed plans, GitLab CI federation, application code, and destroying the project.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. OpenTofu >= 1.12 and exact compatible provider constraints are declared; tofu init produces a committed lockfile from trusted registries.
2. The project is dedicated, billing is explicit, deletion is prevented, APIs are enumerated, and provider/resource upgrades cannot silently replace identities.
3. Android configuration is reproducible and its API key is restricted to the application identity and required Firebase APIs.
4. OpenTofu creates no service-account private key, FCM server secret, device token, or other secret-bearing resource.
5. Variables, outputs, state-sensitive values, generated files, plans, and local credentials have explicit public-repository boundaries.
6. tofu fmt -check -recursive, tofu init, tofu validate, and a saved plan can be run in the documented order; apply is explicitly limited to the reviewed saved plan.

## Testing
- Run formatting, initialization, validation, provider lock verification, and a plan with operator-supplied non-secret inputs.
- Inspect tofu show output for deletion, IAM, API, and replacement behavior.
- Add static assertions or OpenTofu tests only where they catch a demonstrated invariant better than plan inspection.

## Notes
Risk category: secret exposure, identity churn, blast radius, state drift, and provider drift. Rollback disables sender IAM or APIs through a reviewed plan; project deletion stays prevented. The one runtime JSON key is generated and installed out of band with restricted permissions and documented rotation.
close_reason: Added pinned OpenTofu Firebase foundation with dedicated protected project, APIs, Android registration/key, sensitive config output, sender account, least-privilege role, lockfile, docs, and validated saved plan; no apply.

title: Run protected keyless OpenTofu plans in self-hosted GitLab
description:
## Goal

1. State is locked, versioned, encrypted by the self-hosted GitLab backend and never committed or mirrored to GitHub.

title: Deliver opaque Attention generations through optional FCM
description:
## Goal
Wake every active paired Android device for new eligible Attention generations without disclosing work content.

## Scope
- In scope: per-device FCM token registration or rotation over paired HTTPS; private token persistence and revocation; an optional delivery adapter; FCM HTTP v1 OAuth from GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS; fixed generic notification plus opaque collapsible generation; per-device submitted generation; transient backoff, latest-generation collapse, invalid-token disabling, permanent configuration health, and structured status.
- Out of scope: FCM topics, primary-device selection, notification reminders, Agent-authored payloads, Android receiving code, and OpenTofu key generation.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. An authenticated device can register or rotate only its own token; revocation removes inbox and future delivery authority together.
2. Every eligible generation is independently submitted once to each active token; newer state supersedes unsent older generations.
3. Unchanged unresolved state never creates a periodic reminder.
4. The serialized FCM payload has an explicit allowlist containing only fixed generic title/body and opaque collapse/generation metadata.
5. No configured credential means no Google request while inbox behavior remains intact.
6. Transient network, rate-limit, and server failures back off durably; invalid tokens disable only that token; auth/config failures stop retry storms and appear in sanitized status.
7. OAuth access tokens are short-lived and never persisted or logged; the service-account key path is external configuration.

## Testing
- Fake transport tests inspect exact HTTP method, endpoint, OAuth boundary, payload allowlist, collapse behavior, retry classes, and per-device state.
- Restart tests prove pending latest-generation delivery resumes without duplicates.
- Receiver tests cover token ownership, bounds, rotation, revocation, and redacted errors.
- No automated test contacts Google or uses real credentials.

## Notes
Reuse reqwest and existing worker patterns. Any new Rust authentication/crypto dependency must demonstrate the standard library and current dependencies cannot safely mint Google OAuth tokens, be narrowly pinned, and avoid a Firebase Admin dependency if plain HTTP v1 is sufficient.

title: Wake Android through FCM and refresh the private inbox
description:
## Goal
Turn an opaque FCM wake-up into a reliable generic notification and read-only Tailscale inbox refresh.

## Scope
- In scope: pinned Firebase Messaging and Google services Gradle dependencies; generated Android Firebase configuration; notification permission/channel behavior; token registration and rotation using existing pairing; opaque generation validation; generic background notification; tap-to-open inbox; WorkManager retry when the receiver is unavailable; local seen generation.
- Out of scope: notification work content, direct Agent or Run control, foreground permanent services, polling sockets, topics, and a new Android architecture stack.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Installation obtains an FCM token and registers it only after pairing; token refresh updates the same paired device without exposing another device.
2. A valid wake-up shows only the fixed generic LouiseLM notification and never trusts provider-supplied display text.
3. Tapping opens the inbox and fetches the authoritative snapshot through pinned HTTPS over Tailscale.
4. If Tailscale is unavailable, the generic notification remains useful and the inbox presents a retryable unavailable state without resolving anything.
5. Duplicate or older generations do not create duplicate visible notifications; a newer generation can notify again.
6. Revoking or replacing pairing prevents future registration and fetch; local credentials remain Android Keystore-owned.
7. Android lifecycle, background-execution, notification permission, and process-restart behavior are explicit and testable on minSdk 28 plus the configured target SDK.

## Testing
- JVM tests cover payload allowlisting, generation ordering, token transitions, and notification DTOs.
- Instrumented or headless smoke tests cover channel/permission behavior and tap routing where framework APIs require it.
- Run ./gradlew test lint assembleDebug with no live Firebase or receiver dependency.

## Notes
The Firebase Messaging SDK is the approved new Android runtime dependency. Keep platform Views, WorkManager, PinnedHttps, PairingStore, and existing ownership boundaries.

title: Bridge permission, Park, and failure into Attention
description:
## Goal
Complete the v1 Attention taxonomy from authoritative LouiseLM lifecycle transitions.

## Scope
- In scope: permission_required from explicit ACP permission requests; run_parked from authoritative durable Run state; session_failed from terminal Session error while work remains; stable source-operation identities; exact clear transitions on response, cancellation, resume, retry, disposal, or end; shared 30-second inactivity eligibility policy.
- Out of scope: parsing Agent prose, workflow_decision_required, generic plugin event subscriptions, and new notification kinds.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Each kind is emitted only from its named typed lifecycle source and carries deterministic bounded fields.
2. Repeated observations reuse the same source operation and do not duplicate Attention items.
3. Permission response or cancellation clears permission_required; Run resume/end clears run_parked; Session retry/disposal/end clears session_failed.
4. Session items may include a linked Run ID without changing their Session subject identity.
5. All kinds use the same inactivity/seen delivery policy and cannot bypass Neovim-only authority.
6. Disposal and late callback races cannot leave a false unresolved item or recreate cleared state.

## Testing
- Public lifecycle tests cover every create/clear transition, duplicate observation, Run linkage, cancellation, disposal, and fast-event scheduling.
- Derive ACP permission fixtures from observed protocol frames rather than invented payloads.
- Full Lua and focused Rust socket integration gates remain green.

## Notes
Keep the taxonomy closed. Add workflow_decision_required only when the workflow executor owns a dedicated typed transition.
close_reason: Implemented typed permission, failure, and Run Park Attention bridges with deterministic deduplication and clear transitions; focused Lua tests pass.

## Goal
Prove the complete private real-time path in the maintainer's deployed environment.

## Scope
- In scope: review and apply the saved OpenTofu bootstrap plan; verify GitLab state and WIF; generate and install the narrowly scoped runtime key out of band; configure the systemd user service; build/install Android; pair over Tailscale; exercise all four Attention kinds; verify inactivity, seen cancellation, collapse, multi-device behavior where available, offline recovery, restart recovery, invalid-token handling, and revocation.
- Out of scope: automated cloud mutation without review, destructive project teardown, remote workflow control, and claiming automated gates substitute for physical background behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The operator reviews tofu show for the saved bootstrap plan before its explicit apply; subsequent protected-main CI plans authenticate without a stored Google key.
2. GitLab state is locked/versioned and no state, plan, Google key, FCM token, or private credential appears in Git, GitHub, public artifacts, or public logs.
3. With Neovim active, Attention remains in-editor and the phone is quiet; after 30 seconds away, a generic notification arrives near real time.
4. Tapping fetches deterministic current state over Tailscale for turn_ready, permission_required, run_parked, and session_failed without exposing content through FCM.
5. Seeing the source before the grace cancels delivery; unchanged state does not remind; multiple changes collapse to the latest generation.
6. Service/editor/phone restart and temporary tailnet or Google outage preserve unresolved state and recover delivery safely.
7. Revoking the paired device rejects inbox/token requests and prevents later pushes.
8. Status commands identify generation, unresolved kinds, configuration, and sanitized per-device delivery failure without reading raw state files.

## Testing
- Run all repository Lua, Rust, Android, formatting, static-analysis, API-generation, and OpenTofu gates before the physical recipe.
- Record exact device/OS, Tailscale path, observed transition order, plan identity, and sanitized outcomes in the issue.
- Keep the feature open until the maintainer confirms the physical acceptance.

## Notes
Rollback disables the sender, revokes runtime and device credentials, and applies reverted configuration from a reviewed plan. Project deletion protection remains enabled.

title: Firebase rejects QA notification registration

QA notification registration fails on the physical phone because the QA APK consumes the normal app API key.

Observed 2026-09-16, device ba5hfqzhvgiru4ai, Android14/API34, package dev.louiselm.capture.qa, installed/local APK SHA256 c1fa5ac95ab92fed1adc9bd97d1c07558617cb5daf7a44d418f0a70f191f45a3. Scoped QA PID8655 logs, allowlisted codes only: epoch1789544422.845 PERMISSION_DENIED + API_KEY_ANDROID_APP_BLOCKED; 1789544422.849 Failed to get FIS auth token; 1789544423.085 Worker result RETRY; retries at1789544453.359 and1789544513.764. WorkManager connectivity satisfied with retry backoff.

Root cause confirmed: infra/firebase/outputs.tf:30 forwards raw Firebase SDK config. Actual SDK config contains both Android clients, each with api_key order [normal key, QA key]. Packaged google_api_key matches state resource google_apikeys_key.android (normal key UID91c1dcaf-27ae-495c-9b28-8fc96132832a), not android_qa[0]. The receiver independently has generation **11**, one eligible unresolved
turn-ready item for that same Session, and enabled device

not replay of the denied generation. Human observation proves physical display

Case 3 and the three-case smoke round pass. Tailscale and the temporary
notification-permission change are restored. No ADB permission mutation,
re-pair, data clear, service restart, cloud apply or commit was performed.

## Evidence

Run against the chosen receiver's actual state directory (use its configured
`LOUISELM_CAPTURE_STATE_DIR` if nondefault):

```sh
louiselm-capture status | jq '.notifications | {health, next_action, devices}'

```

Both projections were run against the installed CLI: status reported
`unconfigured` with no devices; Attention reported generation 617 with no items.
This validates the current empty-state checks, not a successful delivery. Pin evidence to the
test Session/device, never “the newest” global log. `submitted_generation`
proves Google accepted a send, not that Android displayed it. Phone observation
or a screenshot settles display/tap behavior. Never dump token/credential files
or unrestricted phone logs.

## Report and cleanup

appeared. Case 0 pairing/private inbox and F1 registration retest passed,
and case 1 physical push display, generic wording and tap-to-inbox passed.
Case 2 outage/cache retention and recovery passed; phone Tailscale is restored.
Case 3 permission denial/manual inbox and restoration/fresh delivery passed.
Later Park, failure,
restart, collapse and revocation coverage belongs to the full `.9.9` acceptance
round after this smoke test works. Revoke only disposable test registrations
when finished; preserve original app data and restore temporary permission and
Tailscale changes. This round updated the pre-existing QA app in place and
started the isolated QA receiver; neither app's data may be cleared as cleanup.

## Findings

- **F1 — Firebase rejects QA notification registration**
  (`louiselm-qbr.9.9.2`, in progress; no fix commit). The original QA APK consumed the normal
  app's restricted API key from a multi-key SDK config. Firebase Installations

  End-to-end notification display/generic wording/tap also passed in case 1.
  Outage/recovery and notification denial/restoration also passed. Only the

`5455a9c64a58ec8f2c7932eff08a4222baa2a01d4b07df7d39e9584d71ff39e7`.

# Manual QA — Attention timing and cancellation

Completed timing round for `louiselm-qbr.9.9`. Owner:
`codex/01a0a9b4-7dcc-7bb3-9c02-6af9345717c8`.
The human drives the QA editor and phone; the Agent records scoped evidence.
This round continues the completed smoke round `louiselm-qbr.9.9.3`.

## Status

| Case | State |
| --- | --- |
| Setup | Passed: human reports source visible; receiver generation 12 has zero items, submitted generation remains 11, sender ready with no retries |
| 1. Viewed completion | Passed: human saw reply and no notification; exact fresh Session ready, receiver remains empty at generation 12, submitted generation stays 11 |
| 2. Active editor, then idle delivery and no reminders | Passed: activity held the item; idle delivery reached generation 14; human confirms exactly one alert after two unchanged minutes; receiver/submission remain 14 |
| 3. See the source before the grace expires | Passed: human reports no alert after source viewing; generation 17 is empty and submitted generation remains 14 |

Permission-required, Park, failure, collapse, restart recovery, Google outage,
invalid tokens, revocation, optional multiple devices and normal-service rollout
remain on the parent. They are outside this bounded timing round.

## Verified setup — 2026-09-16

- QA receiver: `louiselm-capture-notifications-qa.service`, PID 151623,
  active/running, zero restarts; sender ready with no attempts or retries.
- QA endpoint: `https://100.90.156.114:17391`.
- Device registration: `10ff90e9-69ff-4ad2-81b7-636d8b05ea2e`, enabled.
- USB phone: `ba5hfqzhvgiru4ai`, model 21081111RG; prior smoke record identifies
  Android 14/API 34. User-0 QA notification permission is currently granted.
- Retained corrected QA APK SHA256:
  `5455a9c64a58ec8f2c7932eff08a4222baa2a01d4b07df7d39e9584d71ff39e7`.
  Installed version is `0.1.0-qa`, code 1, last update 2026-09-16 10:06:21.
  The previous round verified the installed bytes; this handoff checked the
  retained APK hash and installed package metadata, without reinstalling.
- Receiver binary SHA256:
  `aadd4e0c87134519aa54717890cfebb2fc7012278ecb86e9f7089664ebfc2b72`.
- Receiver baseline: generation 11, submitted generation 11, one eligible
  `turn_ready` for prior QA Session
  `01a0a978-b269-70f1-869c-3540f42b532f`.
- The previous QA editor closed. Its retained init and read-only socket probe
  work: generation 11, one item, zero active Sessions, editor state beneath
  `/tmp/louiselm-attention-editor.xoFfgJ/state/louiselm`, and the isolated
  receiver socket beneath `louiselm-notifications-qa/state/louiselm/workflow`.
- After the maintainer reported the prior source visible, the receiver advanced
  to generation 12 with no items. Submitted generation remains 11, the paired
  device remains enabled, and the sender has no retry. This establishes an
  empty baseline without sending another notification or erasing state.

The prior round records Android and Rust suites and the infrastructure gates.
This handoff made no application change and does not claim a fresh full gate
run. The consumer socket smoke check passed. Current Attention, capture-service
and Android executable sources are unchanged from the previous smoke build;
other Lua changes since then concern Forensics. Recheck applicable gates before
the final broad acceptance, and after any implementation fix.

## Setup the human completes first

1. Use only the window titled **LouiseLM notification QA**. Keep phone Tailscale
   connected and notifications enabled for **LouiseLM QA**. Background that app.
2. In the QA editor, run `:LouiselmResume` and choose the previous QA Session
   `01a0a978-b269-70f1-869c-3540f42b532f`. Viewing its source should clear its
   old turn-ready condition. Do not submit another prompt to it.
3. Report that the source is visible. The Agent checks the isolated receiver
   is empty before any timing case. If the Session cannot be resumed, stop at
   this setup step; do not reset pairing or erase state to get an empty inbox.
4. Dismiss the already-delivered QA notification, if one remains. Create a fresh
   Session with `:LouiselmSessionNew` for each case below.

Upstream Agent permission settings remain as configured. If the harmless sleep
command asks permission, allow that command only. These cases do not test
permission-required Attention; that later case needs a deliberately configured
test Agent that actually emits an ACP request.

## 1. Viewed completion stays in the editor

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/attention.lua` (`turn_done` and `seen`) and the chat's
source-visibility wiring.

In a fresh QA Session, submit:

> Use your shell tool to run exactly `sleep 10`, then reply exactly
> `NOTIFY-QA-VIEWED`. Do not modify files.

Keep the source chat current until the reply appears. Continue viewing it for
one minute. Expect the reply in the chat and no new phone notification.

Report completion and the phone observation. The Agent pins the new Session
and verifies no unresolved turn-ready item exists for it. Silence without a
completed real turn is not a pass.

Failure signature: a new QA alert for the viewed completion, or its turn-ready
condition remaining unresolved while its source is visible.

### Case 1 result — passed

The maintainer reports the reply appeared and no notification arrived during
the requested observation. Read-only QA-editor inspection identifies the fresh
Session as `01a0a9c1-5c41-7710-8c0d-4f7da408a954`, status `ready`, no active
turn, with its source `louiselm://session-2` still current. The receiver remains
at generation 12 with zero items. The enabled phone registration remains at
submitted generation 11, attempts 0, retry 0; sender health is ready.
Human observation establishes the visible reply and phone silence; server
evidence independently confirms no unresolved condition or new submission.

## 2. Unseen completion waits for editor inactivity

Exercises the same controller's activity observer and eligibility timer, then
the existing push sender and Android notification path.

1. Create a fresh QA Session. Submit the same prompt with final text
   `NOTIFY-QA-ACTIVE`.
2. Before it completes, use `:edit /home/lotso/code/louiselm/QA_REVIEW_ATTENTION_TIMING.md`
   in the QA editor. Keep moving the cursor every few seconds for one minute;
   do not return to the source chat. Expect no new phone notification.
3. Report the active interval while continuing cursor movement. The Agent must
   capture the new unresolved item with `eligible=false` before you stop.
4. Once that checkpoint is confirmed, stop touching the QA editor. Record the
   last activity time and notification arrival time. Expect a generic alert
   after the 30-second inactivity grace; the observation window is one minute,
   not a guarantee of Google's delivery time. Do not open the source chat.
5. Leave state unchanged for two further minutes. Expect no repeated alert.
   Report whether one arrived and whether it repeated.

The Agent compares the exact subject, eligibility and submitted generation at
each checkpoint. Human observation establishes display timing and silence;
an accepted Google submission alone cannot establish either.

Failure signature: early delivery while the editor is active, no eligibility
transition after inactivity, failed submission, or another notification for
the unchanged generation. Distinguish these outcomes before diagnosing.

After recording this case, use `:LouiselmSessionSwitch` to view its source and
clear its condition. The Agent checks that this previous subject is absent at
the next case's checkpoint.

### Case 2 active-editor checkpoint — passed

The maintainer reports cursor movement and no notification. The exact fresh
QA Session `01a0a9c4-341e-71b1-8210-dd5385a8e2f2` is ready with no active turn;
the recipe buffer is current. Receiver generation 13 contains its sole
`turn_ready` item with `eligible=false`. The enabled phone registration still
has submitted generation 11, attempts 0 and retry 0; sender health is ready.
This proves a completed unseen reply is being held while the editor is active.
The subsequent idle-delivery and no-repeat observations are recorded below.

### Case 2 idle delivery — passed

After the instruction to stop editor activity, the maintainer reports receiving
one notification. The receiver advanced from generation 13 to 14; the exact
same Session `01a0a9c4-341e-71b1-8210-dd5385a8e2f2` now has `eligible=true`.
The enabled device has submitted generation 14, attempts 0 and retry 0; sender
health remains ready. This links physical delivery to the condition previously
held during activity. Exact last-activity and arrival times were not supplied,
so this does not establish precise delivery latency. The later two-minute
no-repeat confirmation is recorded below.

### Case 2 no-repeat interval — passed

The maintainer explicitly confirms exactly one notification after two minutes
with unchanged state. The receiver still has generation 14 and the same single
eligible Session item. Device submitted generation remains 14, with attempts 0,
retry 0 and sender ready. The recipe buffer remains current and the test turn
is inactive. Case 2 passes activity suppression, subsequent idle delivery and
the bounded two-minute no-repeat observation; precise arrival latency remains
unmeasured.

## 3. Seeing the source cancels before delivery

Exercises `Attention:seen` and cancellation of queued eligibility callbacks.

First use `:LouiselmSessionSwitch` to view the case-2 reply `NOTIFY-QA-ACTIVE`
(Session `01a0a9c4-341e-71b1-8210-dd5385a8e2f2`), clearing its old condition.
Dismiss its already-delivered phone notification. The next checkpoint must
show that this previous subject is absent, with only the new ineligible item.

1. Create a fresh QA Session. Submit the same sleep prompt with final text
   `NOTIFY-QA-SEEN`.
2. Before completion, open this recipe in the QA editor. Keep moving the cursor
   every few seconds until the Agent has verified the exact new item exists
   with `eligible=false`. Do not start the idle interval yet.
3. Stop interacting for about ten seconds, then use `:LouiselmSessionSwitch`
   and select that source Session. Read its completed reply before the
   30-second inactivity grace expires.
4. Wait one minute. Expect no new phone alert. Report what appeared.

The Agent verifies the item disappears and the phone's submitted generation
does not advance for this cancelled condition. This checkpoints a real unseen
condition; returning to the source before the reply completed would miss it.

Failure signature: source viewing leaves the item unresolved, a stale timer
makes it eligible afterward, or a new notification arrives for that condition.

### Case 3 pre-cancellation checkpoint — verified

After the maintainer reports ready, read-only checks find the fresh QA Session
`01a0a9ca-8986-7603-8b6c-c8ee741ce892` ready with no active turn, while the recipe
buffer is current. Receiver generation 16 contains only this Session's
`turn_ready` item, `eligible=false`; the previous case's subject is absent.
The enabled device remains at submitted generation 14, attempts 0, retry 0,
sender ready. This established a real completed unseen reply before the human
viewed its source; the cancellation result follows.

### Case 3 cancellation — passed

The maintainer reports no phone notification after viewing the source and the
requested one-minute observation. The exact Session
`01a0a9ca-8986-7603-8b6c-c8ee741ce892` remains ready and inactive; its source
`louiselm://session-4` is current. Receiver generation 17 has zero items,
where generation 16 previously held this ineligible condition. The device
remains enabled at submitted generation 14, attempts 0 and retry 0; sender
health is ready. Viewing the source cleared the real pending condition without
a new submission, and the human confirms no physical alert followed.

## Evidence commands

Run against the retained QA receiver, never the normal receiver:

```sh
export LOUISELM_CAPTURE_CONFIG_DIR=/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-notifications-qa/config
export LOUISELM_CAPTURE_DATA_DIR=/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-notifications-qa/data
export LOUISELM_CAPTURE_STATE_DIR=/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-notifications-qa/state
/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-notifications-qa/bin/louiselm-capture attention list |
  jq '{generation,items:[.items[] | {subject_id,kind,eligible}]}'
/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-notifications-qa/bin/louiselm-capture status |
  jq '{attention,notifications}'
```

These exact projections were validated against generation 11 during takeover.
They exclude credentials and content. Pin every later observation to its case's
Session; do not select a globally newest log or infer display from submission.

## Findings, lesson and closing

All three cases passed. No product defect or source fix was found in this
round; there is no test-suite miss to explain. Automated coverage cannot prove
real desktop focus, human-visible phone alerts or silence, so the human reports
and exact receiver/Session checkpoints supply complementary evidence.

Issue-local lesson: verify a completed unseen item with `eligible=false` before
accepting suppression or cancellation as a pass. Silence alone could otherwise
mean the turn never completed or the source was viewed too early. Global sender
status alone cannot identify the tested Session or prove Android display.

Retained for subsequent parent acceptance: QA editor PID 400288 with four idle
Sessions, temporary init/check/workspace/state, running isolated receiver,
installed QA app, pairing, sender credential and protected artifacts. Final QA
Attention state is empty at generation 17; last submitted generation is 14.
No phone settings were changed this round. Nothing was uninstalled, re-paired,
revoked or deleted from app/receiver storage. Normal setup remains unchanged.

Remaining parent work: permission-required, Park, failure, collapse, restart
recovery, Google outage, invalid-token handling, revocation, multiple devices
where available, full final gate evidence and normal-service rollout. Exact
delivery latency was not measured. This bounded round does not close the parent.

Archive this file verbatim as a `qa-round` Beads record under
`louiselm-qbr.9.9`, verify the description matches, then remove this scratch
file. The round issue is the sole durable record; no duplicate is committed.

# Manual QA — collapse multiple Attention changes

Completed collapse round for `louiselm-qbr.9.9`, owned by
`codex/01a0a9b4-7dcc-7bb3-9c02-6af9345717c8`. Previous timing results are
archived in closed round `louiselm-qbr.9.9.4`; do not repeat them.

## Status

| Checkpoint | State |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | Empty QA inbox at generation 17, submitted generation 14; sender ready, device enabled, no retries |
| Two completed unseen replies held during activity | Verified: generation 19 holds exactly two ineligible items, both Sessions ready; submitted generation remains 14 |
| Latest generation delivered as one current notification entry | Passed: human reports one notification; receiver/device/phone notified generation 21 |
| Tap fetches both current unresolved items | Passed: human reports two items; phone cached/seen generation 21 contains both exact test Sessions |

## Setup and scope

Reuse the same QA receiver, editor and corrected QA APK recorded in `.9.9.4`.
No rebuild, configuration change, reinstall or new pairing is needed. Keep
phone Tailscale connected and LouiseLM QA notifications allowed; background
the app. Dismiss any old QA notification before this case.

This case exercises the Attention controller, the sender's latest-generation
behavior and collapse key, Android's fixed notification tag, and tap-to-inbox
fetch. It does not establish Google's offline message-queue behavior or an
exactly-once delivery guarantee. Sender submissions and visible notification
entries are separate facts: more than one accepted generation may be replaced
by one current notification entry.

## Human steps — create two pending replies

1. In the isolated QA editor, create a fresh Session and submit:

   > Use your shell tool to run exactly `sleep 10`, then reply exactly
   > `NOTIFY-QA-COLLAPSE-A`. Do not modify files.

2. Before the reply completes, hide its source by opening this file:

   ```vim
   :edit /home/lotso/code/louiselm/QA_REVIEW_ATTENTION_COLLAPSE.md
   ```

3. From the recipe buffer, create another fresh Session. Submit the same prompt
   with `NOTIFY-QA-COLLAPSE-B`, then immediately return to this recipe. Do not
   revisit A's source while creating B.
4. Keep moving the cursor in this nonempty recipe every few seconds for one
   minute. Report ready and continue moving until the Agent checks both exact
   Sessions have completed, both items exist with `eligible=false`, and the
   device still has submitted generation 14. A missing item or earlier push
   means this checkpoint was missed; do not infer collapse from an empty test.

## Human steps — deliver and inspect

Only after the two-item checkpoint is verified:

1. Stop interacting with the QA editor and leave both source chats hidden.
   Allow about one minute for delivery. Report how many alerts occurred and how
   many current LouiseLM QA notification entries appear. Expect one current
   generic entry, without reply text or Session identities.
2. Count the current QA notification entries before tapping. Do not open either
   source chat. The Agent can verify the latest submitted generation after your
   report; phone inbox fetching does not clear the source conditions.
3. Tap the QA notification. Expect the private inbox to show both current
   turn-ready items, corresponding to the two Session IDs the Agent recorded.
   Report the item count and whether they match. Fetching the inbox does not
   itself clear their underlying Session conditions.

Failure signatures: separate persistent QA notification entries, stale private
inbox after a successful fetch, missing/extra source items, content leaked into
notification wording, or sender stuck behind the current eligible generation.
Record multiple audible alerts separately; the Agent will trace their timing
instead of assuming every accepted generation is a distinct current entry.

### Two-item checkpoint — verified

The maintainer reports ready. Read-only receiver checks show generation 19 with
exactly two `turn_ready` items, both `eligible=false`, for fresh Sessions
`01a0a9e1-ef55-7822-8b1e-4604700642bc` and
`01a0a9e2-6ce3-7a02-886d-32b887709843`. Both Sessions are ready with no active
turn; this recipe is the current QA-editor buffer. The enabled phone remains
at submitted generation 14, attempts 0, retry 0, with sender health ready.
No prior-case item remains. Delivery and tap results follow.

### Collapse and latest-inbox result — passed

The maintainer reports one notification and two inbox items after tapping.
Receiver generation 21 contains exactly the two checkpoint Sessions above,
both now eligible. The device is enabled with submitted generation 21,
attempts 0 and retry 0; sender health is ready. Both QA turns are inactive and
their source chats remain hidden behind this recipe.

A read-only projection of only the QA app's Attention preferences confirms
cached generation 21, snapshot generation 21, seen generation 21 and notified
generation 21. Its two cached turn-ready items match the exact test Session
IDs above. No credential, pairing token, reply text or unrelated phone state
was printed. Human observation proves one physical notification and successful
tap; the matching private cache establishes which current items were fetched.

This passes the bounded live collapse/latest-inbox case. It does not establish
an exactly-once Google submission count, disconnected FCM queue behavior or
precise arrival latency.

## Evidence

The Agent runs the same validated status/list projections against only:

```sh
export LOUISELM_CAPTURE_CONFIG_DIR=/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-notifications-qa/config
export LOUISELM_CAPTURE_DATA_DIR=/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-notifications-qa/data
export LOUISELM_CAPTURE_STATE_DIR=/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-notifications-qa/state
/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-notifications-qa/bin/louiselm-capture attention list |
  jq '{generation,items:[.items[] | {subject_id,kind,eligible}]}'
/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-notifications-qa/bin/louiselm-capture status |
  jq '{attention,notifications}'
```

Record both exact fresh Session IDs and checkpoint generations. Project only
these IDs, counts and delivery fields if inspecting the phone's cached inbox.
Do not dump tokens, pairing credentials, unrelated notifications or raw logs.
Human reports prove physical display and tap; server acceptance alone does not.

## Findings, lesson and cleanup

No product defect or source change was found. Automated tests alone cannot
establish the physical notification count or tap navigation; the human result
and exact phone cache supplied that evidence. Issue-local lesson: compare both
Session IDs and generation across receiver, submission and phone cache, and
distinguish one current notification entry from an exactly-once send claim.

# Manual QA — Attention recovery

Completed recovery round for `louiselm-qbr.9.9`, owner
`codex/01a0a9b4-7dcc-7bb3-9c02-6af9345717c8`.
Completed timing and collapse evidence is archived in `.9.9.4` and `.9.9.5`.

## Status

| Case | State |
| --- | --- |
| QA receiver restart preserves unresolved inbox and delivery state | Passed: human reports Refresh/observation works fine; receiver and phone retain exact two subjects at generation 21 with no newer submission/notification |
| Fresh reply delivers after receiver restart | Passed: human confirms all steps; fresh Session only, receiver/submitted/phone generations 25 |
| QA editor restart preserves the unresolved item | Passed: human confirms Refresh and one-minute no-extra-alert checks; receiver/phone still match exact subject at generation 25 |

| Phone restart preserves pairing and unresolved inbox | Passed: human confirms correct QA app shows the item and no duplicate; receiver/phone generations remain 28 with the exact subject |
| Fresh notification delivers after phone restart | Passed: human confirms one notification and tap to one new item; receiver/submitted/phone generations 34 match the sole fresh turn-ready Session |

This recovery round now covers the isolated receiver, QA editor and physical
phone. Other parent acceptance remains outstanding. No normal service or normal
editor restart is part of it. The human controls the phone restart.

## Baseline and scope

Reuse the retained QA receiver and phone installation without changing any
credential, pairing, permission, Agent approval mode or network configuration.
The read-only preflight and restart target exactly
`louiselm-capture-notifications-qa.service`.

Build under test: Android/capture-service source baseline
`37de434f6f4410712fcce4cda0644bced1c278c1`, with the corrected QA Firebase export
from `louiselm-qbr.9.9.2`. Retained APK
`android/app/build/outputs/apk/qa/app-qa.apk` SHA256
`5455a9c64a58ec8f2c7932eff08a4222baa2a01d4b07df7d39e9584d71ff39e7`;
installed QA version `0.1.0-qa`, code 1, last update 2026-09-16 10:06:21.
Phone `ba5hfqzhvgiru4ai`, model 21081111RG, Android 14/API 34; QA receiver
`https://100.90.156.114:17391` over Tailscale. Dedicated QA binary and live
`/proc/449362/exe` both SHA256
`aadd4e0c87134519aa54717890cfebb2fc7012278ecb86e9f7089664ebfc2b72`.
No rebuild or reinstall occurred during this recovery round.

The previous collapse round intentionally retained two eligible turn-ready
items at receiver generation 21:

- `01a0a9e1-ef55-7822-8b1e-4604700642bc`
- `01a0a9e2-6ce3-7a02-886d-32b887709843`

The enabled device `10ff90e9-69ff-4ad2-81b7-636d8b05ea2e` has submitted generation
21, attempts 0 and retry 0; sender health is ready. The phone's cached, seen,
notified and snapshot generations are all 21 with these exact two subjects.
Viewing their source chats would clear the fixture, so leave them hidden until
the restart checks below are complete.

## 1. Receiver restart

Exercises durable Attention and pairing/delivery state, the real systemd QA
service lifecycle, TLS continuity and the paired Android inbox consumer.

Agent actions:

1. Record QA and normal service IDs/PIDs/start times, QA readiness and current
   inbox/device projections. Verify the exact QA service is the retained one.
2. Restart only `louiselm-capture-notifications-qa.service` using the user service
   manager. Do not modify the transient unit or erase any state.
3. Confirm a new QA PID/start time and an unchanged normal PID/start time.
   Verify generation 21, the same two unresolved eligible subjects, one paired
   device, submitted generation 21, enabled registration and no retries.

Human steps after the Agent reports the restart finished:

1. Keep Tailscale connected. Open LouiseLM QA and tap Refresh inbox.
2. Expect the same two Attention items without an unreachable, authentication
   or certificate error, and without another pairing step.
3. Leave the QA editor's two source chats hidden and observe one minute for an
   unsolicited duplicate notification. Report whether refresh worked and
   whether any extra alert appeared.

The Agent projects the phone cache to confirm the exact subjects/generation.
Server status proves persisted state; the human proves the live fetch and
physical observation. Failure signatures: lost items or pairing, receiver
startup failure, mismatched TLS identity, retry/error on refresh, or unexpected
duplicate alert. A clean restart is not a simulated crash/power-loss test.

### Receiver restart checkpoint — server state preserved

Before restart, the exact QA service was active with PID 151623 and start time
08:38:41 CEST, running its dedicated QA binary. The normal service was active
with PID 116944 and start time 08:07:02 CEST.

`systemctl --user restart louiselm-capture-notifications-qa.service` succeeded.
The QA service is active/running with PID 449362, start time 13:10:32 CEST on
2026-09-16, and no automatic restart attempts. The normal receiver still has
PID 116944 and the same start time. No unit/configuration was changed.

Post-restart QA state remains generation 21, exactly the two eligible subjects
above, one paired device, enabled registration, submitted generation 21,
attempts 0 and retry 0, with sender ready. This proves persisted state across
the controlled QA restart; the subsequent human result follows.

### Receiver restart physical result — passed

The maintainer reports "works fine" in response to the Refresh/no-extra-alert
recipe. Follow-up projections show receiver generation 21 with the same two
eligible subjects, one enabled paired device and submitted generation 21 with
attempts 0/retry 0. Phone cached, snapshot, seen and notified generations remain
21 with both exact subjects. The successful human-observed Refresh supplements
the persisted-state evidence; the unchanged cache alone would not prove a fresh
network fetch. The fresh-delivery result is recorded below.

## 2. Fresh delivery after restart

Only after case 1 passes:

1. View each retained source Session with `:LouiselmSessionSwitch` to clear the
   two old items (`NOTIFY-QA-COLLAPSE-A` and `NOTIFY-QA-COLLAPSE-B`). On the phone,
   Refresh inbox and confirm no items remain; if it is not empty, stop and
   report that before submitting the new prompt. Dismiss any old QA alert.
   The Agent also verifies both old subjects are absent at the next checkpoint.
2. Background LouiseLM QA on the phone. Create a fresh QA Session and submit:

   > Use your shell tool to run exactly `sleep 10`, then reply exactly
   > `NOTIFY-QA-RESTART`. Do not modify files.

3. Before completion, open this recipe in the QA editor, then leave that editor
   idle for about one minute with the source chat hidden.
4. Expect a fresh generic notification. Tap it and expect one current item for
   the new Session. Report notification and inbox results.

The Agent pins the exact new subject and compares current, submitted and phone
cache generations. This reaches the restarted sender and the retained editor's
connection recovery. Merely preserving a previously cached inbox does not
prove new delivery after restart.

### Fresh delivery after receiver restart — passed

The maintainer confirms all steps worked: old items cleared, the refreshed
inbox was empty, a fresh notification arrived and tapping showed one new item.
Receiver generation 25 contains only eligible turn-ready Session
`01a0a9ee-2a03-7d40-a94e-411c63af2561`; both prior collapse subjects are absent.
The enabled device has submitted generation 25, attempts 0, retry 0 and sender
ready. Phone cached, snapshot, seen and notified generations are all 25 with
exactly that Session. The retained QA editor is on this recipe, and all seven
Sessions are idle. This proves new work reached the restarted receiver and
physical phone through the retained editor connection.

## 3. QA editor restart preserves the unresolved item

Exercises editor exit/start, receiver-owned Attention durability and the
retained paired phone's current inbox. Keep the fresh Session above unseen.

1. In the window titled **LouiseLM notification QA**, run `:qa` to close that
   editor. Do not close the normal editor hosting this conversation. If Neovim
   reports unsaved changes or asks a question, report it rather than forcing
   the exit. All seven QA turns are currently idle.
2. Report that the QA window closed. The Agent verifies its socket/process
   ended and receiver generation 25 still contains the same one eligible item,
   with submitted generation 25. The normal editor and QA receiver stay up.
3. The Agent reopens the same isolated QA init, workspace and state roots on
   this recipe, without loading any Session automatically. Record the new PID,
   correct QA socket/state roots and zero loaded Sessions.
4. On the phone, Refresh inbox. Expect the same single item without an error or
   another pairing step. Observe one minute without a fresh duplicate alert.
   Report what happened. The Agent matches the exact cached Session/generation.

Failure signatures: unresolved item lost during editor exit/start, stale or
unavailable private inbox, wrong receiver/state root after reopening, or an
unexpected new alert. This is a normal controlled exit, not a crash test.

### Editor restart checkpoint — pending state preserved

The maintainer reports the QA editor closed. Old PID 400288 is absent; its
remaining socket path refused a connection. Only that verified stale socket
was removed before reusing its address; no Session or receiver storage was
deleted. Receiver generation 25 still held the exact eligible Session
`01a0a9ee-2a03-7d40-a94e-411c63af2561`, with submitted generation 25, one enabled
paired device, attempts 0 and retry 0. QA receiver PID 449362 and normal receiver
PID 116944 retained their start times.

Reopened the same private init/workspace/state configuration in the window
**LouiseLM notification QA**, PID 462177, one attached UI, this recipe current,
and zero loaded Sessions. Its state root remains
`/tmp/louiselm-attention-editor.xoFfgJ/state/louiselm`; receiver state remains
`/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-notifications-qa/state`. Post-start receiver
generation/submission remain 25 with one unresolved item and sender ready.
No Agent Session was loaded or prompted automatically. The human Refresh result
follows; fresh work from the reopened editor remains to test.

### Editor restart physical result — passed

The maintainer confirms both checks passed: Refresh still showed the same one
item without error, and no extra alert appeared during the requested minute.
Receiver generation 25 and submitted generation 25 are unchanged; the only
item is the exact eligible Session `01a0a9ee-2a03-7d40-a94e-411c63af2561`, with
attempts 0, retry 0 and sender ready. Phone cached, snapshot, seen and notified
generations are all 25 with that same subject. The reopened QA editor remains
PID 462177 on this recipe, with zero loaded Sessions. The item survived without
reloading its source or re-pairing the phone.

## 4. New editor resumes and sends fresh work

Only after case 3 passes:

1. In the reopened QA editor, use `:LouiselmResume` to load Session
   `01a0a9ee-2a03-7d40-a94e-411c63af2561`. View its `NOTIFY-QA-RESTART` reply.
   On the phone, Refresh must show no Attention items; stop and report if not.
2. Background the phone app. Create a fresh QA Session and submit:

   > Use your shell tool to run exactly `sleep 10`, then reply exactly
   > `NOTIFY-QA-EDITOR-RESTART`. Do not modify files.

3. Before completion, open this recipe and leave the QA editor idle for about
   one minute. Expect one fresh generic notification; tap and expect one item
   for the new Session. Report the results.

The Agent checks the old source is absent and matches the exact new subject
across receiver, submitted generation and phone cache. This exercises the newly
started editor's Attention connection rather than just previously saved state.

### Fresh delivery after editor restart — passed

The maintainer confirms all steps passed. Receiver generation 28 contains only
eligible turn-ready Session `01a0a9fe-22e8-7642-845f-f541576b4f0c`; the previous
source is absent. The enabled device has submitted generation 28, attempts 0,
retry 0 and sender ready. Phone cached, snapshot, seen and notified generations
are all 28 with the exact same fresh subject. Reopened QA editor PID 462177 is
on this recipe and contains the resumed old Session plus this fresh Session,
both inactive. This proves source resumption/clearing and new physical delivery
through the reopened editor.

## 5. Phone restart preserves pairing and pending state

Exercises physical Android restart, persisted pairing/Keystore access after
unlock, Tailscale reachability and the real private inbox. Leave the new source
above hidden so its condition stays unresolved.

Pre-restart receiver/submitted/phone baseline is generation 28, one eligible
turn-ready item for `01a0a9fe-22e8-7642-845f-f541576b4f0c`, enabled pairing,
attempts 0/retry 0. Read-only Android boot ID is
`29342d98-0656-4bad-be3e-664ef6bdb3dd`.

1. Restart the Android phone using its normal restart control. The Agent does
   not issue an ADB reboot, clear app data, force-stop the app or re-pair it.
2. Unlock the phone. Ensure Tailscale is connected again; then open LouiseLM QA
   and tap Refresh inbox. Expect the same single pending item without an
   authentication, certificate or unreachable error, and no new pairing step.
3. Background LouiseLM QA for one minute. Expect no new duplicate notification
   for the already-seen generation. Report whether both checks passed.

The Agent verifies the changed boot ID when ADB reconnects, unchanged receiver
subject and submitted generation, and the exact phone cached subject/generation.
If the phone is not reachable by ADB yet, keep objective verification pending
rather than treating elapsed time as proof. Failures include lost pairing,
inaccessible Keystore state after unlock, missing inbox item or duplicate alert.

### Phone reboot checkpoint — initial wrong-app observation

The maintainer reports "nothing needs attention" after reboot. The Android boot
ID changed from `29342d98-0656-4bad-be3e-664ef6bdb3dd` to
`24362eed-e56f-425a-9f99-ca6d892a535d`, establishing an actual restart.

The isolated receiver still has generation 28 and its one eligible Session
`01a0a9fe-22e8-7642-845f-f541576b4f0c`; the enabled device remains submitted 28,
attempts 0/retry 0 and sender ready. The QA app's cached, snapshot, seen and
notified generations are all 28 with that exact item. QA notification permission
remains granted for user 0. The QA editor still shows the recipe; the source
Session is ready and inactive. No pending item was lost at those boundaries.

Read-only window/activity inspection identifies the regular package
`dev.louiselm.capture/.MainActivity` beneath the notification shade, rather than
the QA package `dev.louiselm.capture.qa`. This explains the likely mismatch;
the QA app's actual refreshed display had not yet been observed at that
checkpoint. No product bug was established; the recipe was corrected to name
the **LouiseLM QA** launcher entry explicitly. Neither app was reset or re-paired.

Recipe lesson: after a phone restart, distinguish the two installed launcher
entries before interpreting an empty inbox as lost QA state.

### Phone restart persistence — passed

The maintainer confirms the corrected QA-app checks passed: one item after
Refresh and no duplicate notification during the requested background minute.
Follow-up receiver generation 28 still has the exact eligible Session
`01a0a9fe-22e8-7642-845f-f541576b4f0c`, one enabled paired device, submitted 28,
attempts 0/retry 0 and sender ready. Phone cached, snapshot, seen and notified
generations remain 28 with that same subject. Combined with the changed boot ID
above, this proves pairing and the unresolved inbox survived the actual phone
restart. Fresh push delivery after boot remains to test.

## 6. Fresh delivery after phone restart

Only after case 5 passes:

1. In the QA editor, use `:LouiselmSessionSwitch` to view the already-attached
   Session `01a0a9fe-22e8-7642-845f-f541576b4f0c`
   (`NOTIFY-QA-EDITOR-RESTART`). Do not use `:LouiselmResume` for this step:
   it would attempt a second client while the original is still open.
   Refresh the phone inbox and confirm it is empty;
   if not, stop and report. Dismiss any old QA alert, then background the app.
2. Create a fresh QA Session and submit:

   > Use your shell tool to run exactly `sleep 10`, then reply exactly
   > `NOTIFY-QA-PHONE-RESTART`. Do not modify files.

3. Before completion, open this recipe in the QA editor and leave it idle for
   about one minute. Expect a fresh generic notification; tap and expect one
   item for the new Session. Report the results.

The Agent matches the new exact subject across receiver, accepted generation
and phone cache. This tests actual push delivery after boot, beyond access to
an already-cached inbox. Do not change the phone's permission or pairing to
make a failed attempt pass without first recording the failure.

### Recipe correction — return to the attached Session

The maintainer reports `ACP session/load failed: session is already open in
another client; close it there before resuming` for the retained source.
Read-only `session.identity` resolves that exact ACP ID in QA editor PID 462177;
its original Session is still ready and inactive. It does not resolve in the
normal editor hosting this conversation. This is the established active-writer
rejection documented by `louiselm-zdq0`, not evidence of reboot data loss.

A QA-buffer-only projection identifies the original reply marker in buffer 4,
`louiselm://session-2`, without a conflict error. A distinct failed attempt is
current in buffer 6, `louiselm://session-3`, and contains the conflict error.
At the first check the receiver had generation 30 with a single ineligible
`session_failed` condition for that ACP ID, submitted generation still 28,
enabled device and no retry. This changed the test baseline; fresh post-boot
delivery has not been exercised. No product fix or state reset was performed.

Correction: while the failed-attempt error buffer is visible, use
`:LouiselmSessionClose` to dispose only that rejected attempt. Then use
`:LouiselmSessionSwitch` to select the original ready Session and view its
`NOTIFY-QA-EDITOR-RESTART` reply. Refresh LouiseLM QA and report when the inbox
is empty before proceeding with a fresh Session. Preserve the original live
Session and its transcript. The instruction to "view" the reply was ambiguous;
the recipe now names Switch explicitly for an already-attached Session.

### Clean post-reboot baseline — confirmed

The maintainer confirms the QA inbox is empty after closing the rejected attempt
and switching to the original source. Receiver generation 32 has zero unresolved
items; phone cached, seen and snapshot generations are 32 with an empty item list.
The enabled paired device has submitted generation 31, attempts 0/retry 0 and
sender health ready; the phone's notified generation is 31. That intermediate
notified generation is not the fresh post-reboot test; dismiss any prior alert.
The QA editor remains PID 462177 with the original `01a0a9fe-22e8-7642-845f-f541576b4f0c`
Session ready/inactive in the current `louiselm://session-2` view. Its older
`01a0a9ee-2a03-7d40-a94e-411c63af2561` Session is also ready/inactive.
No failure condition remains. Proceed with case 6 steps 2–3 from this clean
baseline; fresh delivery remains unverified.

### Fresh delivery after phone restart — passed

The maintainer confirms all four final steps passed: clean baseline, fresh
hidden completion, one physical notification and tap to one new inbox item.
Receiver generation 34 contains exactly one eligible `turn_ready` subject,
`01a0aa10-9237-70d1-8f39-81a42da87e39`. The enabled paired device has submitted
generation 34, attempts 0/retry 0 and sender health ready. Phone cached,
snapshot, seen and notified generations are all 34 with the same exact new
Session. The QA editor remains PID 462177 on this recipe, with the new Session
ready/inactive and the two older ready Sessions retained. No older subject or
failed-resume condition remains in the receiver inbox. This proves fresh
end-to-end delivery after the phone reboot, not merely a retained cache.

## Evidence and closing

Use the validated QA-only environment roots under
`/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm-notifications-qa/{config,data,state}` and its
dedicated `bin/louiselm-capture` for `status` and `attention list`. Project only
generation, subjects, kinds, eligibility, pairing count and sanitized delivery
fields. Never dump credentials, token files, service environments or broad logs.

All six recovery cases passed. Receiver and phone projections prove persisted
state and matching delivered generations; the maintainer's observations prove
physical notification display, tap behavior and absence of extra alerts during
the requested observation windows. These are controlled restarts, not crash or
power-loss tests. Exact delivery latency and exactly-once FCM submission are not
established. No new product defect or implementation change arose in this round.

Two recipe misses were corrected: explicitly select LouiseLM QA after reboot,
and use SessionSwitch for an already-attached Session, closing only a rejected
duplicate attempt. Automated tests do not cover which installed launcher entry
or manual command the operator selects; neither miss establishes a product bug.
The complete evidence and those lessons stay in this round's Beads description.

Retain the approved QA receiver, pairing, sender credential, installed QA app
and isolated editor for subsequent parent acceptance. Dedicated roots remain

`/tmp/louiselm-attention-editor.xoFfgJ` (init, workspace, editor state and socket).
The QA service is transient, not a normal-service rollout or host-boot service.
Final check: QA PID 449362/start 13:10:32 CEST and normal PID 116944/start
08:07:02 CEST on 2026-09-16 are active/running with zero automatic restarts.
The phone still reports post-reboot boot ID
`24362eed-e56f-425a-9f99-ca6d892a535d`.
The final unresolved turn-ready fixture above and three idle QA Sessions remain.
No credentials, pairing, app data or source transcripts were erased. Normal
receiver configuration was not changed, and this round did not restart the
normal receiver or normal editor.

No executable files changed, so no new automated gate run is claimed. Preserve
prior gate/build evidence in the parent; final aggregate gates and remaining
physical acceptance still govern its close. Outstanding scope includes the
other Attention kinds, Google outage/recovery, invalid-token handling,
revocation and multi-device coverage where available. The accidental failed

Archive this exact record as one `qa-round` child, verify byte equality, then

Isolated the failure class, not the lost diff. Two prior hypotheses tested and dead: no ordering tie at (file,line) in either HEAD or the failing tree 960c3de (75 included entries, 0 ties), and no multi-file/unsorted field provenance. CI Neovim version, flagged uninspected in the description, recovered from job 104941880259: NVIM v0.12.5, identical to local.

Evidence of the actual mechanism, from step timings: failing job ran generate-api-appendix --check in 2.5s (19:21:21.36-19:21:23.90); passing job 104946584384 took 6.0s (19:35:20.12-19:35:26.09). Gate is strengthened, not weakened, and no source or generated content changed.

Limits, stated: this catches a section lost wholesale, not a partially loaded section, and does not prove the 2026-09-16 diff. A partial loss still relies on the unified diff added in f111c52. Per-file coverage is deliberately not asserted: permission/init.lua and agent/init.lua legitimately export zero entries.

Lesson routed to docs/agent-testing.md (validate an external exporter before trusting its exit code). title: render-post fragments are not byte-identical across runs; CSS rule order varies
description:
`render-post.sh` documents its output as "a pure function of the current input"
and promises that "running twice against unchanged input is byte-identical".
It is not. Ten consecutive runs against identical input, in an identical
environment, produced four distinct fragment files. The difference is CSS rule
ordering, so the rendered page is unaffected — but the contract is false and
the test that claims to check it passes anyway.

## Observed

Found by QA case 9 of the round covering `ec19281..HEAD`, on build `daf3dfc`,
2026-08-20. Real post, real conversation excerpt (`:lines: 1481-1522`).

`blog.md` and `myst.yml` are byte-identical across runs. The fragment is not:

```
run  1  942aeb6aa0d2bbc13473e42d635ea066
run  2  b357a62c877f12da018565305d648c68
run  3  b357a62c877f12da018565305d648c68
run  4  07d64a69bd68ef675f020bcacd527080
run  5  5e4da75d9e1bbcd9942792ffa7a53d1e
...
```

Four distinct outputs across ten runs. Not environment-dependent — holding
`TERM` fixed still flips it:

```
TERM=dumb run 1  5e4da75d
TERM=dumb run 2  942aeb6a
TERM=dumb run 3  5e4da75d
```

The whole diff between two variants:

```
10d9
< .-conceal {}
12a12
> .-conceal {}
16a17
> .-markup-strong {color: #e78284; font-weight: bold}
18d18
< .-markup-strong {font-weight: bold; color: #e78284}
```

Rule order within the `<style>` block, and property order within a rule. The
`<pre>` markup is identical every time; the CSS is semantically identical every
time.

## Symptoms

- Re-rendering an unchanged post rewrites its fragment with different bytes.
- Fragments are written into the post directory and referenced from
  `myst.yml` `static_files`, so they are committed alongside a post — every
  re-render therefore dirties the working tree with a semantically null diff.
- No visual difference. The published page is correct in every variant.

## Root cause

Neovim's `:TOhtml` builds its `<style>` block by iterating the highlight groups
it collected with `pairs()`, whose order is unspecified in Lua and varies
between processes. `render-post.mjs` extracts that block verbatim
(`extractTagBlock`, then `buildFragmentDoc`), by design — `render-post.sh`'s
header states the style and `<pre>` are taken "unmodified (no selector
rewriting)".

So the non-determinism originates upstream in `tohtml.lua`, and this pipeline
faithfully preserves it. The real excerpt produces 11 rules
(`.-spell .-conceal .-nospell .-none .-markup-raw .rainbow2 .Whitespace
.Special .-tag-delimiter .-markup-strong .-tag`), which is enough for the
ordering to vary.

## Why it was not caught

`blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh` part 2 does exactly the right check —
`diff -rq "$run1_dir" "$run2_dir"` over fragments, `blog.md` and `myst.yml`.
It passes because its fixture is too small to expose the bug: the excerpts are
`:lines: 9-12` and `:lines: 16-20` of a hand-written fixture transcript that is
plain prose plus a two-line shell block and a three-line Lua snippet. That
yields a handful of highlight groups, and with few enough rules the iteration
order does not visibly change. The assertion is sound; the fixture is not
representative.

This is the same fixture-scale gap as louiselm-msg (skills discovery) and
louiselm-cmr (single-line tool titles): invented fixtures are well-behaved in
exactly the dimension the real data is not.

## Fix direction

There is a genuine conflict here, which is why this is filed rather than
patched.

Sorting the CSS is the obvious fix — normalise rule order and property order in
`render-post.mjs` before `buildFragmentDoc`. But `test-render-post.sh` part 1
asserts that the fragment's embedded `<style>`/`<pre>` match an *independent*
TOhtml capture byte-for-byte, and that capture would be unsorted. Sorting
therefore breaks part 1 unless part 1 normalises identically — at which point
"byte-for-byte against a real TOhtml capture", the property part 1 exists to
protect, is weakened to "byte-for-byte after our own normalisation".

Options, none free:

1. Sort in `render-post.mjs`, and normalise part 1's comparison the same way.
   Deterministic output; part 1 becomes a slightly weaker guarantee.
2. Sort in `tohtml-driver.lua` before the raw capture is written, so both the
   pipeline and part 1's independent capture see sorted input. Keeps part 1
   byte-exact against what the driver produces, but the driver is then no
   longer a transparent TOhtml wrapper.
3. Weaken the documented contract to semantic rather than byte equality, and
   compare parsed rule sets in part 2. Honest, but gives up the cheap
   `diff -rq` check and the "pure function of input" claim.
4. Fix upstream in Neovim's `tohtml.lua` and pin a version. Correct, slowest,
   outside this repo.

Recommend 1: it puts the normalisation where the pipeline already takes
responsibility for assembling the document, and the weakening of part 1 is
small and explicit. Whatever is chosen, `render-post.sh`'s header must stop
claiming byte-identical output until it is true.

## Acceptance

- Ten consecutive runs against unchanged input produce ten identical
  fragments.
- `test-render-post.sh` part 2's fixture is enlarged until it produces enough
  highlight groups to have caught this — otherwise the same gap remains.
- `render-post.sh`'s header contract matches the implemented behaviour.

## Not covered

- Whether `.rainbow2` and similar plugin-provided groups make the group set
  itself vary between runs (as opposed to only its order) is unverified; every
  observed variant had the same 11 rules, but that is 10 samples.
- Neovim's `tohtml.lua` has not been read to confirm `pairs()` specifically;
  the unspecified-order conclusion is inferred from the symptom.
close_reason:
Fixed by canonicalising the TOhtml <style> block inside buildFragmentDoc (blog/scripts/render-post.mjs): rules sorted by selector, declarations sorted within each rule, code-unit comparison so the output does not depend on locale. <pre> is still passed through verbatim.

Root cause verified at source rather than inferred: Neovim 0.12.2 tohtml.lua has TWO pairs() loops, line 1004 over highlight groups (rule order) and line 1032 over a group's attributes (declaration order). Sorting only rule order left 5 distinct blocks out of 10 runs; sorting both collapses to 1.

Boundary is better than the issue proposed. The issue expected part 1 of test-render-post.sh to need a matching normalisation and to be weakened by it. It does not: part 1 builds its expected fragment by calling buildFragmentDoc itself, so normalising inside that function keeps part 1 byte-exact against an independent real TOhtml capture with no change and no loss of guarantee. The filed conflict does not exist at that boundary.

All three acceptance criteria met:
- Ten consecutive runs against unchanged input are byte-identical (new part 2 check; two runs used to pass by luck).
- Part 2's fixture enlarged until it would have caught this: the excerpts now carry bold, italic, inline code, a link, a blockquote, a list and two fenced languages, producing 30 CSS rules against the old fixture's handful. Proof it is now representative: with the enlarged fixture and the fix reverted, the suite fails 4 checks (part 1, part 2 two-run, part 2 ten-run, part 2b) where it previously passed 20/20 -- the old fixture was masking this in three more places than the one it was filed against.
- render-post.sh's header contract and render-post.mjs's overview no longer claim the CSS is unmodified, and state what the canonicalisation is and why.

Independent verification outside the fixture: the 10 real TOhtml captures used to reproduce the bug (7 distinct raw style blocks) produce exactly 1 distinct fragment after buildFragmentDoc.

Gates: blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh 21 passed 0 failed; stylua --check . exit 0; lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning no problems found; MiniTest full suite Fails (0) Notes (0); git diff --check clean.

Not done, deliberately: option 4 from the issue, fixing pairs() ordering upstream in Neovim's tohtml.lua. It is still the root-cause fix, but it now has no user-visible effect on this pipeline.

comments.text:
Both 'Not covered' items resolved during the fix.

1. The group SET is stable; only ordering varies. Ten captures of a rich markdown buffer (bold, italic, inline code, link, blockquote, list, bash fence, lua fence -> 30 rules) gave 7 distinct raw style blocks, but parsing them into {selector -> sorted declarations} maps yielded exactly 1 distinct map, and 1 distinct selector set. 2. pairs() confirmed at source, not inferred. Neovim 0.12.2, runtime/pack/dist/opt/nvim.tohtml/lua/tohtml.lua: line 1004 'for hlid, name in pairs(state.highlights_name)' emits one rule per highlight group (rule order), and line 1032 'for attr, val in pairs(c)' emits the declarations inside a rule (property order). The issue assumed normalising in render-post.mjs *before* buildFragmentDoc, which would have forced test-render-post.sh part 1 to normalise separately and weakened it. But part 1 builds its expected fragment BY CALLING buildFragmentDoc itself, so putting normalizeStyleBlock inside buildFragmentDoc makes part 1 normalise identically for free. Part 1 keeps its exact property: 'fragment == the same builder applied to an independent real TOhtml capture'. Nothing was weakened, and the conflict that got this filed rather than patched does not exist at that boundary.

The <pre> block was verified deterministic across all 10 captures and is still passed through verbatim.
