title: Grill-me needed: should <leader>lB recognize bare-suffix and cross-workspace Beads IDs under the cursor?
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this question in passing — it wants full attention.**

## The question

Should `:LouiselmInspectBead`/`<leader>lB` recognize a Beads issue under the cursor beyond a full `<current-workspace-prefix>-xxx` ID -- specifically (1) a bare suffix with no prefix at all, assumed to belong to the current workspace, and (2) a full ID belonging to a different workspace's prefix, referenced while working in an unrelated repo? If so, how?

## Context/evidence

Raised while fixing `louiselm-04cy` (ambiguous-count false positives from ordinary hyphenated English words). That fix restores prefix-scoped cursor matching against the *current* workspace's own prefix (via `br where`), which only covers the maintainer's case 1 below.

The maintainer's stated use case, verbatim: while working in `~/code/louiselm` (workspace prefix `louiselm`), `<leader>lB` should open the issue whether the cursor is on:

1. `louiselm-xxx` -- an ID with the current workspace's own prefix. Solved by the `04cy` fix.
2. `xxx` -- a bare suffix with no prefix, implicitly meaning `louiselm-xxx`.
3. `another-repo-xxx` -- a full ID belonging to a *different* workspace's prefix (e.g. `daa-nk1l`, the acp-llm-adapter workspace's prefix, referenced in chat prose while sitting in the louiselm repo).

Checked and confirmed during triage: `br` has no cross-workspace registry or global index -- `br where`, `br info`, and `br config` are all scoped to the single workspace resolved from `--db`/cwd auto-discovery. There is no `br workspaces list` or equivalent. Case 3 cannot be solved by asking `br` for the answer; LouiseLM would have to build and maintain its own prefix-to-path mapping across sibling repos, which does not exist today.

## Threads worth pulling

- Case 2's false-positive surface: matching bare, unhyphenated tokens means virtually any English word in prose becomes a candidate lookup attempt. Is there a reliable cheap signal to scope this down? One candidate raised during triage: in this project's own chat rendering, genuine issue references are consistently backtick-wrapped (`` `louiselm-f8r1` ``) while ordinary prose is not -- but that only helps once a message is rendered as markdown, not on a raw compose line still being typed, and couples cursor detection to markdown code-span boundaries.
- If bare-suffix matching ships, what is the ambiguity behavior when a bare token happens to coincidentally also be a real word AND a real issue suffix in some other workspace? Does the existing "prompt if count != 1 on the line" contract still make sense once bare tokens are candidates, given how much more often they'll appear?
- Case 3's registry: is a prefix-to-path map worth building at all, or is cross-repo Beads reference resolution out of scope for a Neovim plugin whose `br` interactions are otherwise cwd-scoped by design? If it is built, where does it live (LouiseLM config, a cache file, scanned from known sibling directories under e.g. `~/code`), how is it kept fresh, and what happens on collision (two sibling repos sharing a prefix)?
- Is there a simpler alternative to full auto-detection for case 3 -- e.g. requiring the operator to explicitly pass a workspace hint, or leaving cross-repo IDs to the existing manual-entry prompt (which already accepts a full `<prefix>-<suffix>` typed by hand) rather than trying to make cursor-based detection omniscient?
- Should cases 2 and 3 ship together, or does case 2 (in-workspace bare suffix) stand alone as a smaller, safer increment while case 3 (cross-repo) waits on a registry decision?

## Not covered

Redesigning case 1 (already fixed via `louiselm-04cy`'s prefix-scoped matching restoration), or treating the maintainer's use case as authorization to implement any of this now.
close_reason: done

comments.author: claude/b59dc4cb-7c9d-4efc-908a-2cca0884acca
comments.text:
Resolved via a louiselm-grill-me session on 2026-08-28.

Decision:
- Case 2 (bare suffix, e.g. "04cy" alone): match against the LOCAL workspace prefix only, via `br show <local-prefix>-<token>`. No sibling sweep for this case — an unprefixed token has no disambiguating signal, so sweeping N sibling workspaces for a bare word is a far worse false-positive surface than a fully-formed foreign ID would be.
- Case 3 (foreign-prefix ID, e.g. codex-acp-xxxx while sitting in louiselm): on local miss, sweep `br --db <sibling>/.beads/beads.db show <token>` against a NEW louiselm config option `beads.sibling_roots` (user-supplied directory list, globbed one level for `.beads/beads.db`), first hit wins. No caching, no persisted registry.

Rejected alternatives (recorded so they are not re-litigated):
- A persisted prefix-to-path registry file. `br --db <path>` already lets any command target an arbitrary workspace explicitly, and beads_rust has NO global workspace registry to source one from -- confirmed by reading its source: prefix is derived from the directory name (or --prefix) at `br init` and stored in the workspace's own SQLite config table; no ~/.local/state or ~/.config file anywhere lists known workspaces. A registry would be redundant, staleness-prone infrastructure for something a cheap live glob+try already solves.
- Hardcoding a sibling-roots glob (e.g. ~/code/*) in louiselm Lua source. Bakes in one user's personal directory convention; belongs in louiselm's own closed-schema config instead.
- Storing sibling_roots inside beads_rust's own user config file (~/.config/beads/config.yaml). Layering violation: br has no concept of "sibling workspaces for cursor lookup" and should not be taught one for this.
- Sweeping siblings for the bare-suffix case the same way as the prefixed case. Rejected for the false-positive reason above; bare-suffix stays local-only.

Live-measured evidence backing "just try it, br is cheap": a `br show` call, hit or miss, costs ~25-60ms (dominated by process startup); a `--db`-pointed cross-repo call costs the same. A full sweep of a handful of sibling workspaces is well under 500ms.

Routed to louiselm-r98e (feature) for implementation. --json

title: Beads inspector wrongly depends on workspace prefix discovery
description:
The Beads inspector performs workspace discovery before inspecting an issue and constrains issue IDs to the discovered workspace prefix. This breaks valid issue inspection when a LouiseLM Session is in a directory without `.beads`, or when the transcript contains a Beads issue belonging to another workspace. Prompted IDs are also rewritten with the discovered prefix instead of accepting full IDs as entered.

## Observed

The behavior was introduced by commit `36d4125` (`fix(ui): use workspace Beads prefix`). Current flow in `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua`:

- `inspect()` runs `br where --json` before looking at the cursor (`discover_prefix`, lines 213-245).
- It extracts `prefix` and passes it to cursor parsing and JSON validation.
- `show_issue()` runs `br show` only after that discovery.
- A prompted bare ID is automatically rewritten as `<discovered-prefix>-<id>` (`inspect_with_prefix`, lines 258-274).

## Symptoms

- `<leader>lB` fails with `could not locate Beads workspace` when the active Session cwd is not itself a Beads workspace, even if the cursor line contains a full Beads issue ID.
- Issue IDs from another Beads workspace/prefix are ignored or treated as absent.
- A full issue ID entered at the prompt is subject to prefix-dependent behavior.

## Root cause

The inspector treats the current workspace prefix as the authority for identifying issue IDs. A Session transcript can contain IDs from any Beads workspace, while `br show` only needs the appropriate workspace cwd; prefix discovery is therefore an unnecessary and blocking prerequisite.

## Why it was not caught

Tests added with `36d4125` asserted successful `br where --json` discovery and same-prefix lookup, but did not cover a non-Beads cwd, a transcript containing another workspace prefix, or prompt entry of a complete cross-workspace ID.

## Fix direction

Remove `br where --json` from the inspection path. Parse a syntactically valid full Beads ID under the cursor without a workspace prefix, then run `br show <id> --json` in the active Session workspace cwd. When prompting, accept a complete Beads ID as entered; do not synthesize a prefix. Keep workspace lookup and prefix discovery out of the critical inspection path.

## Acceptance

- A full issue ID under the cursor is sent directly to `br show`, regardless of its prefix.
- `<leader>lB` does not require `br where` when a full issue ID is under the cursor.
- A full prompted ID is sent unchanged to `br show`.
- A non-Beads cwd produces the underlying `br show` result rather than a prefix-discovery error.
- Regression tests cover foreign prefixes, no workspace discovery, and full prompt IDs.

## Not covered

The exact Beads ID grammar beyond the existing prefix/suffix shape remains to be preserved or clarified. This change should not make bare prompted fragments valid; Beads IDs should be entered in full.
close_reason: Fixed in the current working tree (not committed because the repository contains pre-existing user changes). Removed br where --json and all automatic prefix detection. Beads inspection now identifies full IDs independent of prefix, runs br show directly in the active Session workspace, accepts full prompted IDs unchanged, and reports br availability at the synchronous boundary. Regression coverage updated in tests/ui/beads_spec.lua for foreign prefixes, no workspace discovery, unchanged full prompt IDs, and invalid input. Verification: full MiniTest suite 701/701 pass; focused Beads tests 10/10 pass; focused command tests 32/32 pass; stylua --check passes; lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning passes; git diff --check passes. No deviation from acceptance criteria.

comments.author: codex/01a04621-223a-7c83-982e-94c88435ed5b
comments.text: Root cause confirmed from 36d4125: workspace prefix discovery became a prerequisite and prefix was threaded through cursor parsing, JSON validation, and prompt rewriting. Fixed by removing discover_prefix entirely; full IDs are parsed/validated without a workspace prefix, prompts require a full ID and preserve it, and br show is the first Beads subprocess in the active Session cwd. No standing project rule is warranted; this is an inspector flow correction.

title: Beads reconciliation fixture fails on uncertain-result replay
description:
A complete hosted skills-core suite fails when the reconciliation fixture repeats a request after an intended lost tracker result. This blocks the CI optimization retry; no Beads mutation source was changed by that candidate.

## Observed
2026-09-18 09:48 UTC, codex/01a0b350-de3e-7020-9ac9-615b56e88bb6. Full GitHub CI run35331251883, core job105555865674, candidate77533b86b2af9acd7ccea13324faf55216ca0c3e. Failing step Test invokes bash ../scripts/test-skills-core-git-isolation 142</dev/null with line-tables-only profile, Rust1.97.1, all features/locked.
https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/35331251883/job/105555865674
Exact failure: broker::beads_mutation::tests::control::operator_attestation_never_replays_unknown_writes_or_refunds_the_attempt panicked at src/broker/beads_mutation_control_tests.rs:55:14: called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: TrackerInvocation(Custom { kind: Other, error: "lost result after mutation" }).
Result: FAILED. 334 passed; 1 failed; 3 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in13.73s. Cargo exit101.
The same repaired Rust tree cb21e42b65614d728f0fb046bba6c2ef04388aeb passed three full local parallel suites, all21 privileged guest invocations and three complete hosted unsplit workflows immediately before this candidate. Test file blob4b40fe81a867528cc32faed5a1e8b75d325e3ffc is unchanged. Workspace mutation regressions pass in the failing run.

## Symptoms
The second accept call at logical time2 returns the fake LostResult runner error instead of the expected retained Unknown receipt.

## Root cause
UNKNOWN. The first accept at logical time1 asserts only is_err(), not the exact TrackerInvocation variant or runner invocation count. A pre-invocation refusal can therefore masquerade as the intended lost-result event. Shared permission fixture expires_at_ms=100 (beads_mutation_tests.rs:274); production accept rechecks now_ms plus real elapsed time before persisting intent/invoking the runner (beads_mutation.rs:177-184). Hypothesis: host scheduling/storage consumes the ~99ms setup allowance, first call expires before intent, second performs the first actual invocation. The first error was not retained by the fixture, so this remains a hypothesis. No duplicate real mutation or production replay violation has been established.

## Why it was not caught
The generic first-error assertion does not prove the test entered the uncertain-effect state. The final runner-count assertion cannot diagnose it because the second unwrap fails first. Prior all-green runs do not establish deterministic setup.

## Fix direction
First prove/capture the original error class and invocation count, then make uncertain-result setup deterministic without weakening production expiry, at-most-once, spent-budget, operator-authentication or reconciliation assertions. Preserve genuine expiry tests; do not blanket-extend deadlines or rerun until green. Inspect sibling lost-result fixtures that share permission setup if the mechanism is confirmed.

## Acceptance
- Deterministic red evidence distinguishes pre-invocation refusal from lost result after invocation.
- Original result remains Unknown on retry; reconciliation never replays the write, rewrites original bytes or refunds spent authority.
- Expiry still refuses before invocation; focused and complete parallel/hosted gates pass.

## Not covered
Separate defect outside the three authorized fixes. Filed before any fix; no production or fixture repair made. Optimization pass2 will be withdrawn under the failing-gate stop rule. Original three fixes remain verified; this failure is excluded from timing acceptance.

The exact historical first error remains unavailable. Fix 84524b4 is test-only: explicit non-expiry fixture, exact runner-error/call-count assertions in both uncertain-result tests, finite expiry boundary refusal and exact spent-budget refusal. Three full local parallel suites and complete hosted CI 35335645097 (13/13 jobs) pass. Production expiry/replay/permission code unchanged. title: Queued prompt can remain stuck after active turn becomes ready
description:
Observed during live LouiseLM chat QA on 2026-08-22: while the model was responding, pressing Enter queued a prompt. After the agent finished, the status remained Model responding instead of returning to Your turn / advancing the queued prompt.

Root cause: lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua releases queued prompts only from the turn_done handler. The session lifecycle publishes state_changed ready as the authoritative idle transition separately; if the terminal turn event is lost or delivered out of order, the queued prompt and its marker remain indefinitely. The UI currently has no ready-state fallback.

Acceptance:
- A queued prompt is released when its session emits state_changed with status ready, even if no turn_done event is delivered.
- The normal state_changed + turn_done sequence submits the queued prompt at most once.
- Existing queued prompt, error, cancellation, disposal, and status rendering behavior remains green.
close_reason: Fixed queued prompt release on ready state transition; focused and full suites pass.

title: Private blog-publishing pipeline for louiselm session transcripts
description:
## Problem Statement

Turning an interesting agent conversation into a blog post currently requires manual, repetitive steps: copying chat buffer text by hand into a markdown file (lossy — collapses tool calls to one-line summaries, truncates commands and output), hand-building a MyST project from scratch, and no way to render a quoted excerpt with the same Neovim/Catppuccin/Tree-sitter styling the author actually saw, while keeping the rest of the post in a separate blog theme.

## Solution

A private, louiselm-adjacent publishing pipeline for turning louiselm session transcripts into blog posts. One real plugin command (LouiselmToMarkdown) exports a session's full structured transcript (not a lossy buffer scrape) to markdown. A blog/ directory at the repo root (sibling to android/ and capture-service/, not documented as a plugin feature) holds a multi-post MyST site plus two private scripts: one scaffolds a new post (optionally auto-exporting named sessions into it), the other batch-renders every excerpt a finished post quotes through the author's real Neovim config into scoped, dual-theme-safe HTML fragments, ready for a plain myst build with zero Neovim dependency in CI.

## User Stories

1. As the author, I want to export any louiselm session's full transcript to markdown from its structured JSONL data (not the truncated chat buffer), so quoting a conversation in a post does not require re-digging through raw logs.
2. As the author, I want to scaffold a new post directory in one command, so starting a post from "I want to blog about lines X-Y in session A and lines Z-W in session B" does not require manually creating folders.
3. As the author, I want that scaffold command to optionally take session ids and auto-export plus auto-stub a literalinclude block for each, so the moment scaffolding finishes, every source I named is already present and ready to quote from.
4. As the author, I want a single batch step that renders every nvim-transcript-tagged excerpt in a finished post through my real Neovim config (Catppuccin, Tree-sitter) into namespaced HTML+CSS, so the published transcript looks exactly like what I saw on screen, without polluting the blog's own theme.
5. As the author, I want the rendered output committed and CI to just run myst build with no Neovim dependency, so publishing does not require reproducing my personal editor setup inside a CI container.
6. As the author, I want the finished site published at blog.bartab.fr via GitLab Pages from this same repo, so there is no second repo to maintain for a workflow that is fundamentally "I am already in louiselm."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a louiselm session id, running LouiselmToMarkdown produces a markdown file containing the full transcript reconstructed from the session's structured JSONL (full tool commands and results, not one-line summaries).
2. Given blog/scripts/create-blog.sh <name>, a blog/post-<name>/ directory is created containing an empty blog.md and an empty conversations/ folder.
3. Given blog/scripts/create-blog.sh <name> <session-id>..., the same scaffold is created, conversations/<session-id>.md exists for each session id (via the same export path as LouiselmToMarkdown), and blog.md contains one literalinclude block per session pointing at its exported file.
4. Given a blog.md with one or more code blocks tagged :class: nvim-transcript, running the batch render script produces fragment HTML for each block plus one shared, namespaced CSS file, using the author's real Neovim config — and running it again is idempotent (safe to re-run after editing line ranges).
5. Given the rendered fragments are committed, myst build --html succeeds using only MyST and Node — no Neovim process is spawned during the build.
6. The GitLab CI pipeline in this repo builds and deploys blog/ to blog.bartab.fr via GitLab Pages on push, without requiring Neovim in the CI image.

## Implementation Notes

- LouiselmToMarkdown follows the existing Louiselm* command registration pattern (alongside LouiselmResume, LouiselmSessionId, etc. in the chat command module) and reads from the same structured session/transcript data those commands already have access to, not the rendered chat buffer.
- blog/ is a new top-level directory, siblings android/ and capture-service/ — precedent already exists in this repo for non-Neovim-plugin material living alongside lua/.
- The scaffold and render scripts are plain shell/Node scripts under blog/scripts/, not Neovim commands — this tooling is intentionally not part of the plugin's discoverable command surface.
- The render script needs to invoke the author's real Neovim configuration headlessly (not nvim --clean) to get accurate Catppuccin/Tree-sitter output — reusing whatever TOhtml/tohtml.tohtml() wrapper already exists or building a minimal one.
- CSS namespacing (scoping generated Neovim highlight-group classes under a wrapper class) is required so the blog's own theme and the Neovim theme cannot collide on the same page.
- MyST config (blog/myst.yml, blog/blog.css) should be structured as a real multi-post project from the start, not a single-page site — a second post is expected.

## Testing Notes

- LouiselmToMarkdown output should be tested against a fixture session JSONL, asserting full tool commands/results appear (not truncated).
- The scaffold script's directory-creation and auto-stub behavior can be tested as a plain shell/script test (given a fake session export, assert the resulting blog.md contents).
- The render script's CSS-namespacing step is the highest-risk piece — worth a focused test asserting generated selectors are correctly prefixed and that two renders of the same input are byte-identical (supports the idempotency acceptance criterion).
- No UI/Neovim-buffer testing needed — this is headless tooling.

## Out of Scope

- Writing the first post's prose, choosing excerpt line ranges, and designing blog.css's actual visual theme — tracked separately, not part of this feature.
- Any interactive/visual-selection tool for previewing excerpts while authoring (considered and explicitly rejected — plain Neovim navigation is sufficient for picking line ranges).
- Any MyST build-time JS plugin that renders excerpts live during myst build/myst start — rendering is a separate, explicit, pre-build step by design, to avoid needing Neovim in CI.
- Deploying/configuring anything at the bartab.fr root domain — this feature only concerns the blog.bartab.fr subdomain.

Do not close on child count or recreate old deployment. Remaining work is to link maintainer-approved scope changes and certify the intended current publishing path against this parent. title: Grill-me needed: How should oversized submitted prompts be presented?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; use a focused grill-me session.

How should oversized submitted prompts be presented while retaining exact text for copying and keeping the next editable prompt easy to reach?

Evidence from louiselm-zvap: docs/performance/markdown-20260921/probe.lua reproduces a synthetic 64-KiB single-line command occupying 820 screen rows in an 80-column LouiseLM window, despite the accepted-turn buffer containing only eight logical lines. This is display expansion, not transcript line-count growth. A 16-KiB raw command is also slower through md-render's document builder than through the native chat renderer; renderer adoption is not justified by these measurements.

Discuss editable draft versus submitted-turn behavior; exact-copy and navigation expectations; optional versus automatic compact display; what should trigger it (bytes, lines, or visible rows); explicit inspection and expansion; and how a single logical line can be compacted without changing transport content. Existing native folds need more than one buffer line. Window-local nowrap is available now but affects ordinary prose too.

The investigation recommends keeping native rendering. It does not authorize a threshold, default fold policy, renderer dependency, or implementation. Markdown table layout remains louiselm-sm41.

title: Extend <leader>lB cursor detection to bare-suffix and cross-workspace Beads IDs
description:
## Problem Statement

`<leader>lB` / `:LouiselmInspectBead` only recognizes a fully-formed
`<workspace-prefix>-<suffix>` issue ID under the cursor (fixed for false
positives in louiselm-04cy). It does not recognize a bare suffix with no
prefix (e.g. cursor on `04cy` alone, implicitly meaning the local workspace's
`louiselm-04cy`), and it cannot resolve an ID that belongs to a *different*
workspace's prefix while sitting in an unrelated repo (e.g. a `codex-acp-xxxx`
ID referenced in chat prose while working in `~/code/louiselm`). Both gaps
were raised and resolved in the louiselm-grill-me session that closed
louiselm-qmmk.

## Solution

Extend the cursor-based Beads ID resolution in `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua`
with two additional, independently-shippable lookup attempts before falling
back to the existing manual `Beads issue id:` prompt:

1. **Bare suffix (local only):** if no prefixed match is found under the
   cursor, try resolving `<local-workspace-prefix>-<token>` against the local
   workspace (the same `br where`-derived prefix the 04cy fix already wires
   up). Mirrors the bare-id handling louiselm-y8y1 already added to the
   manual-entry prompt path (prepend the local prefix before validating).
2. **Cross-workspace ID (sibling sweep):** if the token already looks like a
   full `<prefix>-<suffix>` ID but doesn't resolve locally, sweep
   `br --db <sibling>/.beads/beads.db show <token>` against each path in a new
   `beads.sibling_roots` louiselm config option (a user-supplied list of
   directories globbed one level for a `.beads/beads.db`), stopping at the
   first hit. No caching and no persisted registry: each attempt is
   recomputed live, so there is no staleness or collision bookkeeping to
   maintain. Defaults to an empty list (feature off) until the user opts in.

## User Stories

1. As the maintainer, I want `<leader>lB` to open the local issue when my
   cursor is on a bare suffix like `04cy`, so that I don't have to type the
   full `louiselm-` prefix by hand or hit the manual prompt for something
   already visible on the line.
2. As the maintainer, I want `<leader>lB` to open an issue that belongs to a
   sibling repo's Beads workspace when I reference it by its full ID while
   working elsewhere, so that cross-repo issue mentions in chat prose are
   navigable without switching directories or typing IDs into another
   terminal.
3. As a user who has not configured `beads.sibling_roots`, I want the
   existing behavior (local-prefix-only resolution, then the manual prompt)
   to be unchanged, so that this feature is strictly additive.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given the cursor is on a bare token (e.g. `04cy`) with no configured
   ambiguity on the line, when `<leader>lB` is pressed, then the local
   workspace's `<prefix>-04cy` opens directly if it exists, or falls through
   to the manual prompt if it does not.
2. Given `beads.sibling_roots` is configured and the cursor is on a full
   `<foreign-prefix>-<suffix>` ID that does not exist in the local workspace,
   when `<leader>lB` is pressed, then the plugin tries each configured
   sibling's `.beads/beads.db` in order via `br --db` and opens the first
   match.
3. Given `beads.sibling_roots` is unset or empty (the default), when
   `<leader>lB` is pressed on any token, then behavior is identical to
   pre-feature: only the local-prefix exact match (louiselm-04cy) and now the
   local bare-suffix attempt are tried, no sibling sweep happens.
4. Given no sibling and no local match resolves, when `<leader>lB` is
   pressed, then the existing manual `Beads issue id:` prompt appears
   unchanged.

## Implementation Notes

- Primary file: `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua` (`issue_id_at_cursor`,
  `current_issue_id`, `inspect_with_prefix`/`show_issue` — exact function
  names may have shifted since this was written; re-read the file first).
- New config surface: `lua/louiselm/config.lua`, likely under a `beads =
  { sibling_roots = {...} }` table with closed-schema validation consistent
  with the rest of the module (reject non-table/non-string entries, do not
  silently coerce).
- Sibling glob: one level under each configured root looking for
  `*/.beads/beads.db`; do not recurse further and do not cache the glob
  result between invocations.
- Reuse the existing `vim.system`-based async `br` invocation pattern already
  used for `br where`/`br show` in this file; do not introduce a new process
  abstraction.
- Rejected alternatives (do not re-litigate without new evidence):
  - A persisted prefix-to-path registry file: unnecessary — `br --db <path>`
    already lets any command target an arbitrary workspace explicitly, and
    `beads_rust` itself has no global workspace registry to source one from
    (confirmed by reading its source: prefix comes from the directory name or
    `--prefix` at `br init` time, stored in the workspace's own SQLite config
    table; no `~/.local/state` or `~/.config` file lists known workspaces).
  - Hardcoding a sibling-roots glob (e.g. `~/code/*`) in Lua source: bakes in
    one user's personal directory convention instead of living in louiselm's
    own config.
  - Storing `sibling_roots` inside `beads_rust`'s own user config file
    (`~/.config/beads/config.yaml`): a layering violation — `br` has no
    concept of "sibling workspaces for cursor lookup" and should not be
    taught one for this.
  - Sweeping siblings for the bare-suffix case (case 2) the same way as the
    prefixed case (case 3): rejected — an unprefixed token has no
    disambiguating signal, so sweeping N sibling workspaces for a bare word
    is a far worse false-positive surface than a fully-formed foreign ID.
    Bare-suffix stays local-only.
- Live-measured costs (2026-08-28): a `br show` call (hit or miss) costs
  ~25-60ms, dominated by process startup, not data size; a `--db`-pointed
  cross-repo call costs the same. A full sweep of a handful of sibling
  workspaces is well under 500ms — acceptable for an explicit per-keypress
  action, not a hot path.

## Testing Notes

- Follow the existing `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua` pattern (fake/mock `br`
  invocations, not real subprocesses, per AGENTS.md determinism rules).
- Cover: bare-suffix hit, bare-suffix miss (falls to prompt), sibling-sweep
  hit on the second configured sibling (proves ordering/short-circuit),
  sibling-sweep exhausted (falls to prompt), and the `sibling_roots`-unset
  case producing byte-identical behavior to pre-feature.
- Cover config validation: non-table `sibling_roots`, non-string entries.

## Out of Scope

- Case 1 (full local-prefix ID) — already shipped in louiselm-04cy /
  commit 729c3f2.
- Any UI to configure `sibling_roots` interactively (`:LouiselmSetup` or
  similar) — this is a plain config-table option like any other, set in the
  user's own `setup()` call.
- Caching, persisting, or auto-discovering sibling roots beyond the
  user-supplied list.
close_reason: done

title: Make skill discovery deterministic and symlink-aware
description:
## Goal

Discover local skills predictably across configured roots while preserving useful paths and diagnosing duplicates or unsafe-looking topology.

## Scope

- In scope: process global skill roots in configuration order; within each root sort deterministically by skill name and configured path.
- In scope: first valid duplicate skill name wins, later names are reported as shadowed, and the same canonical file is deduplicated.
- In scope: expand absolute paths and `~`; resolve relative roots against the session working directory. Health checks resolve them against Neovim's current working directory and say so.
- In scope: support symlinked roots and skill directories, detect canonical cycles/duplicates, preserve the configured-root alias in advertised absolute locations, and warn when a symlink resolves outside its root.
- In scope: continue past unreadable or invalid individual skills with one deduplicated user warning and full details available to diagnostics.
- In scope: refresh discovery whenever the picker opens and read the selected file at selection time.
- Out of scope: automatic project-local roots, a trust database, policy transport, and catalog budgeting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Root order, not global absolute sorting, decides duplicate-name precedence.
2. Discovery order and diagnostics are stable across runs.
3. Canonical aliases do not create duplicate skills or traversal loops.
4. Catalog/picker locations preserve the user-configured alias rather than exposing a canonical dotfiles target.
5. Escapes outside a configured root remain usable but produce a source-to-target warning.
6. Relative-root behavior is covered for both sessions and checkhealth.
7. MiniTest covers duplicate names, identical canonical files, symlinked roots/directories, cycles, outside-root targets, unreadable files, and picker refresh behavior.

## Testing

Use temporary directory fixtures with real symlinks where supported. Keep path-policy tests separate from YAML semantic fixtures.

## Notes

Configured skill roots are trusted prompt/plugin-like input. Diagnostics inform the user; they do not create a new authorization system.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic root-order discovery, canonical symlink traversal and diagnostics, session-relative picker refresh, selection-time reads, and checkhealth coverage

title: Guard handoff can delay lifecycle revocation
description:
Brokered activation is still disabled, so this is an inert integration defect, not an observed production exposure. A future production caller cannot safely run sender_guard::handoff_upstream on the Session owner: it synchronously waits for descriptor-send completion and a broker ACK while borrowing the whole SenderGuard, delaying the lifecycle owner from processing Park/disposal/revision. A naive worker that locks the guard across the same wait has the same problem. An already accepted upstream stream may remain writable while revocation is queued.

## Observed
2026-09-25 code inspection, no live Provider request. skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/sender_guard/handoff.rs:18-76: handoff_upstream takes &mut self; lines 43-64 wait on completion.recv_timeout and receive_ack; receive_ack at 195-223 waits for a broker packet. skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/sender_guard.rs:340-364: revoke needs &mut self to delete policy and shut down retained sockets. skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/lifecycle.rs:800-812, 818-883: one owner consumes broker lifecycle messages and rearms receive after handling each message. skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/system.rs:1639-1660: disposal invokes guard revoke first. No active production Brokered caller exists yet; the safety failure is a pending activation race, not a reproduced upstream leak.

## Root cause
Descriptor handoff combines blocking protocol I/O and exclusive guard mutation in one method. The current API has no independent, immediate revocation path while a handoff waits. Reusing the original authenticated channel also requires exclusive receive ordering, so spawning a worker alone does not solve it.

## Why it was not caught
Existing component VM handoff tests exercise success, rejection, and cleanup serially. They do not race Park/disposal/revision against connect, descriptor send, broker ACK, and an existing upstream write. Brokered launch remains fail-closed, hiding the integration race.

## Fix direction
Before production activation, split handoff waiting from a revocation mechanism that can close policy and active sockets without waiting for the ACK or the handoff lock; preserve exact channel ordering and epoch/revision checks. Do not enable Brokered or use a mutex held through the blocking ACK.

## Acceptance
- A deterministic barrier test parks/disposes/revises during each handoff stage and proves revocation can complete without waiting for the broker ACK.
- An existing guarded stream cannot write after the completed revocation/receipt; stale ACKs cannot reactivate it.
- The disposable VM gate repeats the owner-loss and actual-upstream-write controls.

## Not covered
Park-to-guard mapping and same-revision Resume policy need to be wired by the activation issue; no live exploit or paid Provider request was attempted.
close_reason: Independent revoker and single-reader ACK route pass VM connect/queue/ACK races and installed guard suite; inert:louiselm-qbr.5.1.3.2.4.5

Red: the initial 16-bit policy-key implementation failed the VM revision gate; corrected to the BPF map's u32 key. title: Grill-me needed: How should Normal-mode navigation work in louiselm://session buffers?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; decide the normal-mode navigation contract for louiselm://session buffers before implementation.

Question:
When a louiselm://session buffer is not in Insert mode, how should an operator navigate its transcript efficiently? The desired destinations include the previous prompt, the latest usage entry, previous/next usage entries, tool calls, reasoning/thinking blocks, and assistant answers.

Context/evidence:
Session buffers currently put the operator in Insert mode by default, which is appropriate for continuing the conversation but makes transcript inspection awkward. In Normal mode the operator should be able to jump among semantic transcript objects without manually searching or relying on fragile line counts. This is a navigation idea, not a reported defect; no behavior is chosen yet.

Threads worth pulling:
- Which targets deserve dedicated motions or commands: previous/next prompt, usage, tool, thinking, assistant answer, turn boundaries, and errors/permissions?
- Should navigation move to the object header, first content line, or the nearest visible line, and what happens when the target type is absent?
- Should repeated motions cycle backward/forward, and should counts work?
- How should folded reasoning, tools, and submitted context interact with jumps?
- Should Normal mode use explicit <Plug>/commands, default keymaps, or existing Neovim search/fold motions?
- How does the operator return to prompt editing, and should Insert mode remain the default after each completed turn?
- What observable headless tests and manual checks prove cursor placement, fold behavior, and no interference with prompt submission?

Decision boundary:
Choose the smallest coherent Normal-mode navigation surface for transcript inspection and its interaction with Insert-mode prompt editing. Do not implement until the key targets, motion semantics, and default-keymap policy are agreed.
close_reason: done

title: Add primary Normal-mode navigation motions to session buffers
description:
Implement the confirmed Normal-mode navigation contract for `louiselm://` session
buffers (decided in the louiselm-rcuv grill-me session, 2026-08-30).

## Contract

- `]u` / `[u` — next/prev **submitted** user prompt (a `> ` prompt line in
  history). The live prompt line is NOT a target (Normal `<CR>` covers it).
- `]r` / `[r` — next/prev **assistant reply**, defined as the first prose line
  of a turn's response: the first line after a user prompt that is not blank,
  not a `[…` marker line (`[thinking]`, `[tool]`, `[usage]`, `[context:`,
  `[workflow]`), and not `Error:`/`Warning:`. A tool-only turn (no prose) is
  not a target and is skipped.
- Normal `<CR>` — jump to the live prompt line, column 2 (past `> `), and
  `startinsert`. Idempotent when already on the prompt.
- Semantics: land on the target's first line at the first non-blank column;
  honor `v:count1` (`3]u` = third-next target); stop at first/last target with
  a **silent no-op** (no error, cursor unmoved); no cycling; motions keep the
  editor in Normal mode.
- Keymap policy: default-on **buffer-local** maps in session buffers only. No
  config option, no `<Plug>` layer, no global maps.
- No fold interaction is needed for these targets: prompt lines sit above
  context folds and reply prose is never folded. Motions must not disturb
  fold state (do not open/close folds) or the in-flight `[thinking]` guard.

## Keymap safety (evidence)

Neovim 0.12 default-occupied `[`/`]` space (checked empirically, clean
instance, 2026-08-30): `[a/[b/[d/[l/[q/[t` (+ uppercase) are default mappings;
`[[ ]], [m ]m [M ]M, [s ]s (spell), [c ]c (diff), [p ]p (put-with-indent),
[(, {, #, *, /` are hardcoded motions. `u`, `r`, `e`, `E` are free; the chosen
keys avoid all of the above.

## Implementation notes

- Primary file: `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`. Register the buffer-local
  Normal maps alongside the existing `n za` fold toggle (init.lua:2816-2818)
  in the buffer setup path used by `Chat:attach` and re-checked by
  `Chat:switch`.
- Submitted-prompt detection: `> `-prefixed lines above the prompt boundary
  extmark (`prompt_mark` / `current_prompt_line`, init.lua:1341-1359). Exclude
  the live prompt and the `> [contexts: …]` block header lines from `]u`
  targets (target the `> <text>` line of each prompt, i.e. the first `> `
  line of the prompt block).
- The transcript is append-only with a stable header line count, so a
  scan-at-keypress (parse buffer lines from the cursor) is acceptable and
  avoids maintaining another line-index table like `tool_lines`; do not add
  persistent tracking state.
- Use `nvim_feedkeys`-equivalent callback maps (Lua callbacks, not Ex-command
  strings).

## Acceptance criteria (headless behavioral tests, no manual gate)

Fixture transcript: multiple turns, one tool-only turn, one turn with
submitted context, a `[thinking]` block, a `[usage]` line.

1. `]u`/`[u` land on submitted prompt lines in order; the live prompt line is
   never a target; `> [contexts: …]` headers are not targets.
2. `]r`/`[r` land on each turn's first prose line; the tool-only turn is
   skipped.
3. `3]u` honors the count; motion at the first/last target is a silent no-op
   (cursor unmoved, no error raised or echoed).
4. Normal `<CR>` from mid-transcript lands at the prompt line at column 2 in
   Insert mode; pressing `<CR>` while already on the prompt line still enters
   Insert.
5. A motion issued while a turn is streaming leaves fold state, the
   `[thinking]` guard, and tool-line tracking untouched.
6. Mode is Normal after every motion.

Run the standard gates (stylua, lua-language-server, full mini.test suite;
`generate-api-appendix` only if public annotations change).

## Out of scope

- Secondary navigation family (usage, errors, tool/thinking targets) —
  tracked as a sibling task.
- Any config surface or `<Plug>` remap layer.
- Insert-mode-default-after-turn behavior (unchanged).
close_reason: done

title: Usage history: collect, exploit, then reflect
description:
## Problem Statement

Usage history currently pools option values independently, loses the combinations and timestamps needed for honest comparisons, and misses headless and unmeasured turns. Changing a Model can therefore display another Model's samples. Option-change sequences cannot be analyzed later.

## Solution

Deliver in the maintainer-confirmed order: collect durable facts; exploit them through factual queries, Neovim history, and the options picker; then reflect using a separate advisory skill.

## User Stories

1. As the operator, I want every started turn and confirmed option change retained so history survives Sessions and editor restarts.
2. As the operator, I want Provider to identify the access/quota service so a Model used through different services stays correctly attributed.
3. As the operator, I want missing attribution or recording failures to prevent new prompts so collection cannot silently stop.
4. As the operator, I want matching option combinations, time filters, and metric coverage so comparisons describe observed usage.
5. As an Agent using headless Sessions, I want the same recording and query contracts as the chat UI.
6. As the operator, I want reflection after the factual tools work, with hypotheses clearly separated from evidence.

## Implementation Decisions

- Provider is required, explicitly resolved, and historically snapshotted. Never store an unknown/null/guessed Provider. Preserve Agent, advertised Model, full active options, identity, timestamps, outcomes, reported token fields, and costs by currency.
- Record every started Chat/headless turn, including failure, Cancellation, and absent telemetry. Record confirmed option transitions even without a following prompt; retain old/new values, observed source, and established request links without inferred intent/causality.
- Preserve starting options and any mid-turn changes. Changed turns remain in history and totals but cannot represent one fixed option combination; never estimate usage splits.
- Private local SQLite through asynchronous sqlite3 CLI calls; runtime/test dependency explicitly approved. Initial record must be durable before prompt dispatch. Recording failure blocks new prompts; an active turn continues with a visible error.
- Preserve all facts/events indefinitely; no expiry, truncation, or lossy rollups. No prompt/tool content. New analytics starts at rollout; retain old replay annotations. Evidence-complete historical import is a separate optional deliverable.
- SQL calculates factual cohorts/aggregates; Lua collects, orchestrates, and presents. Reconsider an owned Rust query host only after separating database, subprocess, and rendering costs or demonstrating another concrete consumer need.
- Neovim explorer and picker share queries. Picker varies one candidate option, holds the other options and Agent fixed, and resolves Provider for the candidate. Empty cohorts say No matching history; wider comparisons require explicit explorer filters.
- Keep total turns separate from each metric's sample coverage. Missing measurements are absent, currencies stay separate, and prices/tokens are never estimated.

## Testing Decisions

Use repository TDD and Lua gates. Cover real async scheduling, headless/UI parity, durable-before-send ordering, concurrent editors, storage errors, late callbacks/disposal, replay identity/deduplication, sparse telemetry, mixed options, currency boundaries, and the maintainer's live Astra picker reproduction. Keep deterministic fixtures; capture real ACP structures/order for peer-dependent cases. Profile the functioning query path before considering Rust.

## Success Criteria

1. The collection feature is complete and all configured Chat/headless Sessions reach its production recording boundary with required Provider attribution.
2. The exploitation feature is complete: exact joint picker cohorts, a usable Neovim history explorer, explicit metric coverage, and measured query-host tradeoffs.
3. The advisory reflection skill works through those factual tools and identifies evidence separately from hypotheses.
4. All required gates and relevant live acceptances pass; no aggregate closes stronger than its weakest deliverable. Optional historical import does not gate completion.

## Out of Scope

Automatic configuration changes, inferred quality/intent verdicts, price tables, raw prompt/tool logging, cloud analytics, new Rust components without evidence, and making historical import a prerequisite for current collection.

## Further Notes

Confirmed source: louiselm-3x9p, final summary approved on 2026-09-07 in codex/01a07a70-6a45-7930-a5bd-ae78def5c53a. Provider vocabulary: louiselm-7bm3. Existing defect: louiselm-rvu8. Model aggregate completion only with explicit prerequisite edges; do not add reverse parent-child edges.

title: Add README licence section framing the choice as serving reach
description:
Add a licence section to `README.md` that states the choice and the reasoning behind it.

## Content

- LouiseLM is MIT licensed.
- The licence is chosen to serve reach: the project's usefulness depends on being installable anywhere with no friction.
- If reach stops being the binding constraint, the choice will be revisited.
- Link to the trademark policy and the political statement.

## Why the last point matters

Publishing the expiry condition is what makes a future relicense a disclosed term rather than a rug-pull. It costs nothing now and is the difference between a relicense that is legitimate and one that is radioactive.

## Acceptance criteria

- README has a licence section containing all four points.
- Wording does not promise perpetuity, and does not read as a threat either.
- Links resolve.

title: README advertises account limits no public user can obtain
description:
## Problem

The project is public and the README advertises a feature no reader can get.

- `README.md:139` lists "cost or account limits when the Agent reports them"
  as a shipped feature.
- `README.md:194` shows a sample winbar reading `limits 98%/7d ↻7d`.
- `README.md:61` hands the quickstart `codex = { command = "codex-acp" }` —
  the stock build, which does not emit the extension.

Every Agent that reports limits does so through a build the maintainer
maintains:

| Agent | source of limits | public user gets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | `feat/account-limits` patch on fork `euri10/codex-acp` | nothing |
| Claude | `feat/account-limits` patch on fork `euri10/claude-agent-acp` | nothing |
| Copilot | `~/code/copilot-acp`, no git remote at all | nothing |
| OpenCode | won't-do, louiselm-opencode-account-limits-9350 | nothing |

Evidence: `~/.config/nvim/agent-runtimes/inventory.json`, whose Codex
`retire_when` already concedes upstream is not there — "PRs #334/#426 alone
are not equivalent".

The defect is not that the feature is unavailable. It is that the docs promise
it and never say so.

## Fix

- State in the feature bullet that Account limits are adapter-dependent, and
  that stock adapters generally do not advertise the extension.
- Add a column or note to the Agent table recording which adapters emit it.
- Link the published wire contract so a reader can see what an adapter must
  do, and the forks as unsupported reference implementations with no
  compatibility promise.

Do **not** publish the forks as a supported distribution. That is the
unbounded maintenance commitment rejected in
louiselm-opencode-quota-runtime-ownership-blz13, and it is worse than the
upstream version: it carries other people's codebases in public rather than
asking them to carry one extension.

## Acceptance

1. No README claim implies a stock adapter reports Account limits.
2. The Agent table says which adapters emit the extension.
3. Fork links, where present, carry the unsupported/no-promise wording.
4. `npm run site:test` and full `npm run site:build` pass.

## Context

Decision: louiselm-opencode-quota-runtime-ownership-blz13.
Vocabulary: louiselm-account-limits-9n9st.

title: Make the repo the substrate for cross-adapter agent context
description:
## Problem Statement

louiselm is an interface to ACP adapters, not a Claude-only tool. But the durable context an agent accumulates while working on this repo — conventions, design decisions, the maintainer's workflow — has been landing in Claude Code's private per-project memory store. Any other adapter reading this repo sees none of it.

The inverse failure exists too. `AGENTS.md` is the adapter-neutral instruction file, and it is not auto-loaded by Claude Code: there is no root `CLAUDE.md` and no setting pointing at it. So the repo currently has one context store that only Claude reads and one that Claude ignores, and neither is a shared substrate.

Concretely: `AGENTS.md` is 214 lines across 11 sections and does not mention beads once, even though beads is the task graph the whole project runs on. An agent entering this repo cold has no way to learn that findings should be filed as beads. Meanwhile five of seven notes in Claude's project memory are repo content that was misfiled there purely because it was the path of least resistance.

## Solution

Make the repository the substrate for durable agent context, and reduce per-adapter memory to only what is genuinely adapter-specific.

The routing rule, by two axes:

- **About louiselm, adapter-independent** → the repo.
- **About the maintainer, cross-project** → that adapter's own user-level instructions.
- **About one adapter's harness quirks** → that adapter's project memory. Applied honestly this is nearly empty, which is the correct outcome and not evidence the rule is wrong.

Within the repo, placement follows the anchor:

- Anchored to a specific work item → a `br` comment on that issue, so it travels with the issue and needs no separate discovery mechanism.
- A standing convention true for every session → `AGENTS.md`.
- The maintainer's own workflow loop → an explicitly non-binding example document.

`AGENTS.md` becomes the single entrypoint. Every adapter is pointed at it rather than given its own parallel instruction file, because parallel instruction files diverge silently and the divergence surfaces at the worst possible moment.

## User Stories

1. As an agent entering this repo through any ACP adapter, I want the work-tracking conventions stated in the file I already read on entry, so that I file findings as beads instead of inventing my own process.
2. As the maintainer, I want a decision recorded during a session to survive regardless of which adapter recorded it, so that switching adapters does not silently lose context.
3. As a contributor or agent, I want the maintainer's personal workflow clearly marked as an example rather than a requirement, so that I can invent my own loop without believing I am violating a contract.
4. As the maintainer, I want my own loop written down as prose now, so that the future workflow-config feature has a spec to implement against rather than being reconstructed from memory.
5. As an agent picking up a deferred issue months later, I want design context attached to that issue, so that I do not need the conversation that produced it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a fresh clone opened by any adapter that reads `AGENTS.md`, when the agent reads it, then the beads work-tracking conventions are present and stated in the file's own imperative register.
2. Given Claude Code opening this repo, when it auto-loads project instructions, then it is directed to `AGENTS.md` and no instruction content exists outside it.
3. Given the example workflow document, when any reader reaches it, then it self-identifies as a non-binding example, and `AGENTS.md` says the same where it links out.
4. Given the deferred workflow-engine issues, when someone opens them, then the in-progress-first triage requirement is attached as a comment.
5. Given Claude's project memory folder, when it is inspected after migration, then it contains only genuinely Claude-specific harness notes, and every repo fact previously held there exists in the repo.
6. Given `AGENTS.md`, when the workflow section is read, then it references `br robot-docs` for command syntax rather than duplicating a command cheatsheet.

## Implementation Notes

- Affected: `AGENTS.md` (new section, renumbering), a new root `CLAUDE.md` pointer, a new example workflow document under `docs/`, `br` comments on the deferred workflow-engine issues, and Claude's project memory store.
- **Do not use `br agents --add`.** It emits roughly 60 lines of generic beads tutorial in a `<!-- br-agent-instructions-v1 -->` block. Three problems: the register clashes with `AGENTS.md`, which is terse and imperative; it teaches command syntax discoverable from `br --help` while saying nothing about this project's actual conventions; and hand-edits inside a versioned generated block are destroyed by `br agents --update`, so the conventions would live in the one place designed to be overwritten.
- The workflow section is inserted as section 2, immediately after Project Scope, not appended at the end. Reading order should be *what this project is* → *how work is found and tracked* → *how code must be written*, because an agent finds work before it writes any. Renumbering the existing sections is mechanical churn and acceptable; section 1 already states breaking changes are fine and there are no external users.
- The example document lives at a `docs/` path rather than root. A root-level uppercase filename reads as normative regardless of any disclaimer it carries, which is the precise misreading to avoid.
- The `CLAUDE.md` pointer must stay a pointer. Real content in it beside a real `AGENTS.md` guarantees drift.
- The example workflow document is the first draft of the workflow-config that louiselm intends to ship as an example. It should be written knowing that, without over-committing to a config schema that does not exist yet.

## Testing Notes

- No automated tests. Verification is documentary: read `AGENTS.md` top to bottom as if entering cold and confirm the work-tracking conventions are learnable; confirm the example document is unambiguously non-binding on first read.
- Confirm no instruction content is duplicated between `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`.
- Confirm nothing was lost in the memory migration by checking each migrated note has a repo destination.

## Out of Scope

- Cross-adapter portability of *session/conversation history*. That is a much larger problem already implied by the attention-control-plane roadmap, and is not solved as a side effect of relocating notes.
- Any wrapper script around `br`/`bv`, and any project-scoped skill override for them. Both were considered and rejected: they relocate a personal preference into the repo without it becoming a real louiselm capability.
- Building the workflow-config engine itself. This feature produces the prose spec, not the implementation.
- Resolving how completed QA review rounds get archived. Tracked separately; it wants full attention rather than being decided in passing.
- Rewriting the existing 11 sections of `AGENTS.md`. Purely additive apart from renumbering.
close_reason: All four children complete: AGENTS.md work-tracking section, CLAUDE.md pointer, docs/example-workflow.md, br comments on qbr.3/qbr.5, memory migration

title: Give qa-review rounds a mandatory archiving/closing step backed by beads
description:
## Problem Statement

A `qa-review` round produces a working file (`QA_REVIEW.md`-style) that
accumulates the plan, case-by-case results, and narration for the round. When
the round ends, nothing decides what happens to that file — commit it, fold
it into beads, or delete it. This has now happened twice in a row
(transcript-export/blog-publishing round, then the permissions round), each
time ending with the same unresolved question and an untracked markdown file
left sitting in the repo root. Findings filed during a round (via
`to-beads-bug`, which already works correctly) also end up orphaned from the
round that produced them — nothing records which round found which bug.

Resolved via grill-me session against `louiselm-iyy`, which had a concrete
proposal already on record from an earlier session; this feature adopts that
proposal.

## Solution

A `qa-review` round closes into exactly one bead, which becomes the round's
sole durable record:

1. **One bead per round.** Type `chore`, label `qa-round`, created with
   `--description-file <working-file>` so the round's plan/results become the
   bead description, and `--external-ref <session-id>` so the round is tied
   to the session that ran it.
2. **Findings hang off it as children.** Continues using the existing,
   already-working `to-beads-bug` chain: `br create -t bug --parent
   <round-id>`. This makes "which round found this?" answerable from the
   graph.
3. **Cases stay flat.** Individual test cases inside the round are never
   promoted to their own beads — they aren't independently actionable, have
   no lifecycle of their own, and beading them would add ceremony for no
   graph benefit. Only findings (bugs) get promoted.
4. **Narration goes in `br comments add`** on the round bead as the round
   progresses, matching the loop shape (plan, run, learn, edit).
5. **On close, the round bead is authoritative.** The working markdown file
   is deleted, never committed — a second, uncommitted-but-lingering copy of
   the same round is exactly the failure this feature removes.
6. **The closing step is mandatory**, built into the `qa-review` skill
   itself as a defined step, not a manual call left to whoever is running the
   round. Two rounds in a row already skipped it by default; an optional step
   is not a fix.

## User Stories

1. As the maintainer running a qa-review round, I want the round to close
   into a bead automatically, so that I don't have to remember to decide the
   working file's fate every time.
2. As an agent picking up a bug found during a past round, I want to see
   which round produced it, so that I have the round's full context without
   reconstructing it from a conversation.
3. As an agent or maintainer looking at repo history, I want closed rounds to
   be greppable via `br`/`bv`, so that "what did we test and find in round
   N" doesn't require finding an untracked file that may not exist anymore.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a qa-review round following the (updated) skill's closing step, when
   the round ends, then exactly one `chore`/`qa-round` bead exists with the
   round's plan/results as its description, `--external-ref` set to the
   session id, and the working markdown file is gone (not committed,
   deleted).
2. Given findings filed during a round, when the round closes, then each
   finding bead is a child of that round's bead (`--parent <round-id>`).
3. Given the `qa-review` skill's own instructions, when an agent reads them
   top to bottom, then the closing step reads as mandatory, not optional or
   merely suggested.
4. Given the two rounds currently sitting as untracked files in this repo
   (`QA_REVIEW.md`, `QA_REVIEW-permissions-round.md`), when this feature
   ships, then both have been retroactively closed under the new rule: round
   beads created, their already-filed findings re-parented under the correct
   round bead, and the two files deleted.

## Implementation Notes

- Skill file: `/home/lotso/dotfiles/agentskills/.config/agentskills/qa-review/SKILL.md`
  (and its `TEMPLATE.md`) — add the closing step here.
- `--external-ref` dovetails with the maintainer's existing global commit rule
  (`Refs <id>` for named sessions/issues in commit messages).
- The transcript-export/blog-publishing round's findings are:
  `louiselm-dim` (closed), `louiselm-euj` (open), `louiselm-d2o` (open),
  `louiselm-xrf` (open) — all currently un-parented, all belong under that
  round's bead.
- The permissions round (working file: `QA_REVIEW-permissions-round.md`,
  origin `louiselm-4wx`) reports "all six cases passed" with three
  in-round fixes (commits `a57cee2`, `348c6fc`, `c0ae0aa`) — check whether
  those fixes have their own bead IDs to re-parent, or whether the round bead
  is created with no open children if they were fixed without being filed
  separately.
- Convergence noted during the grill: the round bead becomes the index, an
  exported transcript (once the export pipeline is wired up) is the
  evidence, and a blog post is the human-readable version — reusing the
  transcript-export/blog-pipeline feature set for QA's own record-keeping.

## Testing Notes

- No automated test surface (this is a documentation/process change to a
  skill plus one-time data migration). Verification is documentary: read the
  updated `qa-review` skill cold and confirm the closing step is
  unambiguous, then confirm via `br show` that both retroactively-closed
  rounds have the right shape (round bead, parented findings, no stray file).

## Out of Scope

- The "maintainer's workflow as louiselm configuration" thread
  (workflow-config engine) — raised as bigger context during the grill but
  deliberately not pulled in here; it's a separate, much larger question.
- Rejected: keeping the working markdown file committed alongside the round
  bead as a second durable copy (two sources of truth for one round drift
  silently).
- Rejected: leaving the closing step optional/manual (the exact failure mode
  that produced this feature).
- Rejected: giving individual test cases their own child beads (not
  independently actionable, adds ceremony for no graph benefit).
close_reason: Both children complete. louiselm-ri1.1: qa-review skill now has a mandatory closing step (dotfiles commit 29e76e0). louiselm-ri1.2: both stray rounds retroactively closed into louiselm-vj0 and louiselm-aib, findings reparented, working files deleted.

title: Add mandatory closing step to the qa-review skill
description:
## What

Add a mandatory closing step to the `qa-review` skill
(`/home/lotso/dotfiles/agentskills/.config/agentskills/qa-review/SKILL.md`,
alongside `TEMPLATE.md`) that runs at the end of every round:

1. Create one bead: `br create -t chore --labels qa-round --description-file
   <working-file> --external-ref <session-id>`.
2. Re-parent (or newly create, if not yet filed) any findings from the round
   under that bead: `br create -t bug --parent <round-id>` for new findings;
   `br update <finding-id> --parent <round-id>` for findings already filed
   during the round.
3. Append round narration to the round bead via `br comments add` as the
   round progresses (not just at the end).
4. On close: delete the working markdown file. Never commit it.
5. State explicitly that individual test cases are never beaded — only
   findings are.

This step must read as required, not optional — the skill has twice let
rounds end without deciding the working file's fate.

## Why

Parent feature: louiselm-ri1. Full rationale, rejected alternatives, and
acceptance criteria live there — this task is the skill-file change only.

## Acceptance

- The `qa-review` skill's closing step is unambiguous on a cold read: an
  agent running a round for the first time reaches it and cannot mistake it
  for optional.
- `TEMPLATE.md` (if it currently ships a working-file template) reflects
  that the file is scratch, not a committed artifact.

TEMPLATE.md's opening note updated to match. Explicit fallback stated for projects without beads. Committed in dotfiles 29e76e0 (Refs louiselm-ri1.1).

**Round B — permissions** (`QA_REVIEW-permissions-round.md`, origin

title: :LouiselmResumePark reconstructs a live Run with restored claims and generated-work budget
description:
## Goal

`:LouiselmResumePark` reconstructs a live `Run` around the resumed session, so `claims` and `generated_work` budget are enforceable state after resume, not just fields sitting inert in the durable capture-service record.

## Scope

- In scope: extending `Chat:resume_park` (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`) to call `Run.new()` plus an `accept_resume()`-style restoration of `claims`/`generated_work` from the durable record, after the existing `session/load` succeeds.
- Out of scope: the `:LouiselmPark` creation command (separate task, this depends on it existing for end-to-end fixtures), a `stage` schema field, warm Park.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a durable cold Park record, when the operator runs `:LouiselmResumePark` and selects it, then a `Run` object exists in live Lua state around the resumed session, not just an attached bare ACP session.
2. The reconstructed `Run` carries the original `claims` and `generated_work` (ceiling/consumed/reserved) from the durable record.
3. A resumed Run does not silently widen any envelope axis beyond what the durable record held.
4. Existing `resume_park` behavior (picker, lossy-resume notification, chat attachment) is preserved; this only adds the Run-reconstruction step after successful load.

## Testing

- Headless test: resume a durable Park fixture (built via the mock ACP agent and a temporary Beads workspace) and assert the live Run's claims/budget match the durable record.
- Regression test for mutation-safety after resume: attempting to exceed the restored budget or add an unrelated claim through the resumed Run is rejected the same way it would be for a never-parked Run.
- Full StyLua, LuaLS, and MiniTest gates.

## Notes

Parent feature: louiselm-aaw0. This is what makes QA case 3 from louiselm-t6mx ("Parked Run is visible, bounded, and rejects unsafe mutations") testable at all, since today nothing on the Lua side exists after resume to enforce anything against.

title: Report receiver reachability and per-device delivery health
description:
## Goal
Make receiver status distinguish a running process from a phone-reachable and recently used delivery path.

## Scope
- In scope: configured bind and advertised endpoint in status; loopback-only/unconfigured classification; paired-device count; durable last successful delivery per device; warning when paired devices exist without a phone-reachable endpoint; health response semantics needed by the Android endpoint check.
- Out of scope: phone queue contents on the receiver, cloud monitoring, notifications, public availability probing, transcription-health redesign, and installation of network software.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. status reports the configured profile, bind, advertised endpoint, loopback-only state, and paired-device count without exposing credentials, tokens, environments, or capture contents.
2. Successful new and idempotent duplicate uploads durably update the authenticated device last-delivery time only after the capture is present in the canonical store.
3. Device status reports last successful delivery, or clearly reports none, and survives receiver restart.
4. A loopback-only receiver with paired devices reports a degraded actionable warning rather than healthy delivery.
5. The HTTP health response supplies only the bounded identity/reachability evidence required for safe same-receiver endpoint validation.
6. Authentication failures, interrupted uploads, digest conflicts, and storage failures do not advance last-delivery state.

## Testing
- Start with failing Rust pairing, receiver, and CLI status tests.
- Cover successful create, duplicate retry after acknowledgement loss, rejected identity/credential, failed ingest, restart persistence, and sanitized status output.
- Run cargo fmt, clippy under the repository policy, and the complete capture-service test suite.

## Notes
Keep delivery health separate from transcription health. The server cannot know the phone queue depth and must not pretend otherwise.
close_reason: Implemented receiver reachability and durable per-device delivery health

title: Compact Session winbar with inspectable options
description:
## Problem Statement

The single-line winbar must answer which Session, Agent, Model and effort are active without hiding turn state or background attention. The existing full ACP identity and raw telemetry consume space; session options currently require opening details.

## Confirmed Solution

User confirmed the reviewed shared understanding in codex/01a09e3b-3b0c-75c3-a910-7f9d2514bc46, following the original grill in opencode/ses_f63e6b614ffeNB9HFKXd8CAkCL.

- Status-only, always-on options block when supported options exist. No new configuration toggle.
- Show current Model and thought_level using advertised semantic categories. Model value is unlabeled; effort uses e=. Preserve distinguishing model/version information; do not reduce different models to the same nickname.
- Other options appear behind +N, meaning the number of currently hidden options, not changed settings. As effort/model collapse, their hidden controls contribute to that count. A fully collapsed block reads opts.
- No delta tracking, default inference, or config_options_baseline. Identical current options have the same presentation regardless of creation, mutation, or resume history.
- Retain options after limits in visual order. Prioritize human Session name and Agent over full ACP identity; use compact context percentage with stale indication. Full identity and raw telemetry remain available in details.
- One click target for the entire options block opens the complete options overview. Keep keyboard access. Inspection works during an active turn; mutation remains available only when idle and otherwise permitted by existing lifecycle/decision guards.
- Explicit whole-line width allocation governs collapse. Optional detail collapses before critical turn state and background permission/error attention. Inside the options block, hide extra detail first, then effort, then model, leaving opts when space permits. Reserve room for this affordance; extreme widths must favor critical state rather than promise that every field can always survive.
- No arbitrary 30% budget. Neovim %< is a final truncation location, not a field-priority system.
- Agents with no supported options render no options block.
- No vocabulary change.

Illustrative progression (not fixed pixel layouts):
Wide: Your turn · Review · codex · [limits] · model-name e=high +2 · ctx 53%
Compact: Your turn · Review · codex · [limits] · model-name +3
Narrow: Your turn · Review · opts
Background attention participates in the same allocation and takes priority over optional detail.

## User Stories

1. Identify current Model and effort without opening a picker.
2. Inspect every hidden setting by mouse or keyboard while the Agent is responding.
3. Resize a split without losing critical turn state or background permission/error awareness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Current model/effort values render from supported advertised options, preserving meaningful model distinctions.
- Equivalent current option lists render equivalently across new, changed, and loaded Sessions; no baseline field is introduced.
- Hidden option counts are accurate at each collapse level; zero-option Sessions have no block or dangling separators.
- Wide, compact, and narrow layouts use explicit deterministic collapse and restore on resize; critical attention wins over optional detail.
- The options block remains a single overview target, including its compact/folded forms; keyboard access reaches the same overview.
- During an active response the overview shows current settings without allowing mutation; when idle, existing validated option changes still work.
- Full option values, including false booleans, remain inspectable. Long names, percent signs, and multi-column text do not corrupt rendering or click targets.
- Session name/Agent remain useful identity cues; compact context preserves stale information and full details stay accessible.
- Maintainer checks actual wide/narrow splits, busy inspection, keyboard access, and physical clicks before UX acceptance.

## Implementation Notes

Reuse existing status rendering, option display-value resolution, Session options overview, and winbar click routing. Keep presentation derived from current Session snapshots; no lifecycle baseline storage. Update applicable public documentation and generated API output if public annotations change, even though no configuration key is added.

## Testing Notes

Use red-green behavioral coverage for collapse, option counts, busy inspection versus idle mutation, option-less Agents, resize restoration and click dispatch. Preserve protocol, lifecycle and background-attention coverage. Run focused checks and the complete affected suite per docs/agent-testing.md; distinguish automated evidence from live UX acceptance.

## Out of Scope

Multi-line/floating winbar replacement, direct per-token toggles, baseline/default comparison, new configuration gates, vocabulary changes, and implementation in this tracking-only operation.
