title: Grill-me needed: where does broker-owned Verified posture come from for live Session status
description:
Do not resolve this in passing: pick the source of truth deliberately, because
every consumer of `SessionStatus` inherits the answer.

## Question

`SessionStatus.posture` is a `PostureSummary` the broker is supposed to own, but
the broker holds no posture record for a live Session. Where does it come from?

## Evidence

- `crate::posture::Posture` is constructed in exactly one place,
  `skills-core/src/preflight.rs:231`, on the artifact-only pre-launch path.
  `louiselm-d6fv.6.2` closed that slice `inert`.
- `LaunchAuthorization` and `LaunchEvidence` (`skills-core/src/launch_receipt.rs:105`)
  carry runtime, isolation, Generation and manifest identities, but no posture
  and no waiver.
- So `BrokerService::session_status` currently takes `PostureSummary` as a
  caller-supplied parameter. That is honest about the gap, but it means the one
  field the parent feature exists for is supplied by whoever asks.

## Threads worth pulling

- Does the broker persist the preflight `Posture` at authorization time, so
  status reports the posture the launch was actually authorized under?
- Or is posture re-evaluated live, in which case what evidence is current
  enough to re-check without turning a status read into an enforcement action?
- How do the Session-scoped expiring waivers of `louiselm-d6fv.6.3` reach the
  record, given `.6.3` is blocked behind the broker that would hold them?
- `PostureSummary::Pending` exists. Is "pending until a later slice" an
  acceptable shipped state, or does it advertise a safety property that has not
  been checked?
design:
Maintainer-confirmed rn38 design, 2026-09-14.
Source Session: codex/01a09fee-0c4d-70e0-8970-978088adc56c. The maintainer confirmed the complete shared-understanding summary and authorized the resulting Beads work.

1. Meaning: SessionStatus.posture describes the broker's current assessment. Retain the exact original admission decision/evidence separately as immutable history; later failures or waivers do not rewrite it.
2. Ownership: the Control broker retains validated, Session-bound evidence and policy/waiver decisions and derives posture through the existing evaluator. Preflight remains a prospective artifact preview. Neither status callers, Agent claims nor deserialized status manufacture evidence; remove the caller-supplied posture verdict.
3. Freshness: required evidence that is missing, expired or invalidated makes only its affected dimension unverified, with a typed reason and the last successful check retained for inspection. A never-checked source has no invented success timestamp. Apply each source's actual validity rule; invent no common timeout. Existing conformance deadlines and Broker loss grace retain their meanings.
4. Reads: posture evaluation consumes retained validated facts and their current validity. A status read does not run evidence probes, renew evidence/waivers, make an admission decision, or change authority. Existing authenticated mechanical-status transport remains separate from evidence probing.
5. Partial delivery: ship truthful partial posture before every producer is connected. Missing producers report unverified/evidence_missing. Pending means actual initialization in progress, not an indefinite missing implementation. Fully verified requires valid evidence in every required dimension; waived dimensions remain waived.
6. Presentation: every canonical status response carries the compact six-dimension breakdown by default: state, typed reason, freshness and safe next action. Preserve bounded evidence references and redaction; never expose raw evidence, paths, process identities, prompts, environments or arbitrary producer text. Operator and Agent responses agree on posture facts; Agent requests remain self-scoped and carry no lifecycle authority.
7. Integration: reuse existing trusted admission/launcher evidence, broker policy, conformance, waiver, quarantine and Attention owners. Sources validate and retain facts at admission/lifecycle/update boundaries; presentation derives from those facts. Existing source-specific revocation, freeze, reconnect and recovery policy still governs effects. Partial status does not enable user-visible Verified cutover or override operator-selected Agent approval policy.

Implementation routing: extend the existing posture feature louiselm-d6fv.6 with focused tasks for evidence-derived status, supply/disclosure evidence, freshness/recovery and network evidence. Existing louiselm-d6fv.12.3/.12.4 own conformance evidence and validity; .6.3 owns waiver decisions; .6.5 owns quarantine mechanics; .6.9 owns ordered Attention projection. Existing status transports consume the shared record; their claims remain with their owners. louiselm-d6fv.9 retains complete installed Verified cutover.

Vocabulary delta: No change.
close_reason: none:design-confirmed Maintainer-approved contract is in rn38 design; implementation routed to louiselm-d6fv.6.10-.6.13 and existing source/consumer issues. No executable change or live Verified claim.

title: Failed cold-Park loads leave hidden Sessions live
description:
An asynchronous ACP session/load failure leaves its local Session registered but unattached, so the operator cannot see or dispose it through Chat.

## Observed

Code inspection on 2026-09-03. `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:227-232` reports startup failure as `callback(nil, message)`. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4338-4344` can therefore dispose only `loaded_session`, which is nil on failure. The actual Session returned earlier by `api:load_session` is not placed in `pending_resume_sessions` until successful Run reconstruction at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4366-4367`. `Session:fail` closes ACP but does not remove the error Session from Registry; only `Session:dispose` does that at `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:1017-1033`.

## Symptoms

- A failed cold resume leaves an error Session in the Registry with no chat buffer.
- Chat disposal cannot reach the hidden Session through `pending_resume_sessions`.

## Root cause

The cold-resume path records ownership of the returned starting Session only after successful loading, while the failure callback deliberately returns nil instead of that Session.

## Why it was not caught

Existing tests assert the error message and Run state, not Registry/session disposal after an asynchronous cold-load failure.

## Fix direction

Track the returned starting Session for the whole cold-load attempt and dispose it on failure or Chat/controller disposal, without removing Agent-side history.

## Acceptance

- An asynchronous session/load failure removes the local Session from Registry.
- Disposing Chat during an in-flight cold load disposes that Session and late callbacks do not revive it.

## Not covered

Deferred while louiselm-waa0 fixes successful replay delivery; Agent-owned replay history remains untouched.

title: Named explicit-only workflow skill is reported unavailable in injected Sessions
description:
An injected LouiseLM Session cannot load the installed `louiselm-grill-me` workflow skill when the operator names it in the prompt. The skill is discoverable on disk and picker-visible, but it is removed from the only catalog the Agent is instructed to treat as available, so Codex reports that the dedicated skill is unavailable and proceeds without its workflow contract.

## Observed

Seen in Session `codex/01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926` on 2026-08-28, cwd `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`. Transcript: `/home/lotso/.codex/sessions/2026/08/28/rollout-2026-08-28T15-05-12-01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926.jsonl`.

At transcript lines 126-127 Codex says: `The dedicated louiselm-grill-me skill is not available in this session`. Extracting `<name>` entries from the `louiselm://skills/index` context lists the other `louiselm-to-beads*` skills but no `louiselm-grill-me`. The file exists at `/home/lotso/.config/agentskills/generated/louiselm-grill-me/SKILL.md`.

## Symptoms

- The operator asks for the project-standard grill workflow, but the Agent says the skill is unavailable.
- The Agent imitates part of the protocol from AGENTS.md instead of loading the complete SKILL.md, so required one-question sequencing, confirmation, vocabulary promotion, and to-beads routing are not guaranteed.

## Root cause

`/home/lotso/.config/agentskills/generated/louiselm-grill-me/SKILL.md:4` sets `disable-model-invocation: true`; `agents/openai.yaml:5` also sets `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false`. Discovery correctly maps those controls to `skill.explicit_only = true` in `lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua:329-355`. `lua/louiselm/skills/inject.lua:120-129` then omits every explicit-only skill from the injected catalog. The Agent instructions say available skills are the catalog entries, so exact user naming cannot recover a skill that is absent.

This omission was intentional in the closed feature `louiselm-cxh`, whose implementation notes say explicit-only skills remain picker-visible but are excluded from injected catalogs. The observed workflow requirement now demonstrates that picker-only reachability is insufficient: explicit operator naming in text must remain distinguishable from implicit model activation.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/skills_spec.lua:779-805` positively asserts that explicit-only skills are absent from the catalog. `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:2332-2355` covers explicit picker injection, but there is no end-to-end contract for a named explicit-only workflow skill in an injected Session. The tests therefore preserve the mechanism that produces the live failure while proving only the UI-picker workaround.

## Fix direction

At the narrow shared boundary, preserve discoverability for explicit operator invocation without making explicit-only skills eligible for ordinary description matching. Likely options are an invocation-mode field plus catalog instructions that permit exact-name requests only, or an explicit command/context transport that the text path can resolve before the Agent claims availability. Do not simply erase explicit-only semantics globally. If `louiselm-grill-me` is intended to auto-trigger on ordinary “grill me” phrases, its contradictory invocation metadata should instead be changed in the canonical agentskills source and the generated installation rebuilt. Settle that product distinction before implementation.

## Acceptance

- A regression reproduces an injected Session where `louiselm-grill-me` is explicit-only and the operator names it; the exact installed SKILL.md is loaded before the workflow begins.
- Unrelated prompts do not implicitly activate the explicit-only skill.
- The live acceptance is that a fresh injected Codex Session no longer says `louiselm-grill-me` is unavailable when the operator explicitly requests it, and its response follows the skill contract.

## Not covered

Whether bare trigger wording such as `grill me` counts as explicit invocation or only the canonical skill name/selection does; this product distinction is not established by the failing Session alone. Native-policy adapter command behavior is also out of scope.

title: Resumed session picker row exposes raw prompt text before ready status
description:
The attached-session picker exposes the resumed session's raw initial prompt before its normal status metadata, making that row visually inconsistent and harder to scan. In the picker, an existing session appears as a compact identity/status/metadata row, while a session resumed from persisted state starts with a long `[AGENTS.md](file:///...)` prompt fragment and only then shows `ready`; the prompt content should not be the primary identity shown in this picker.

## Observed

Screenshot: `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260823_0543_1920x1200_1787456626.png` (1920x1200, captured 2026-08-23 05:43 local time).

The picker shows two attached sessions. The first row is compact:

`session-1 · ready · skills: native · codex/01a02c74-a9f9-7222-9378-059083ea6f87 · Mode=Agent (full access) · Collaboration mode=Default · Model=GPT-5.6-Luna · Reasoning effort...`

The resumed second row begins with prompt text:

`session-3 · [@AGENTS.md](file:///home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/AGENTS.md)can you takeover this PR, it fails, fix it ready · loaded · skills: native · codex/...`

The relevant picker path is `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2117-2121`, where attached sessions use `session_summary(session:inspect())`; `session_identity` at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:313-334` concatenates the session name, status, loaded marker, skills policy, and agent/acp id. The screenshot demonstrates that the resumed session's inspected identity/name (or equivalent state field) contains unsanitized prompt content, unlike the normal session row.

## Symptoms

- A resumed session has a radically different row shape from a freshly created session.
- Long prompt content consumes the picker row and can obscure the stable status and session identity.
- The row is misleadingly centered on prompt text even though the user is choosing an attached session, not reviewing prompt history.

## Root cause

Not fully confirmed. The picker formatter is shared and deterministic; it delegates the displayed identity to inspected session state. The likely defect is that resumed-session restoration populates a display identity/name field from the persisted initial prompt, or fails to provide a bounded title, and the picker does not sanitize or bound that field before rendering. Confirm by tracing the loaded-session state construction and comparing it with fresh-session state.

## Why it was not caught

Current picker coverage appears to exercise the formatter/state path without a realistic persisted session whose initial prompt contains a Markdown file link and a long takeover request. No regression fixture captures the visual/row-shape difference between fresh and resumed sessions.

## Fix direction

Keep the picker’s stable identity first: use a bounded, single-line display name/title derived from the persisted session title when available, otherwise the session id or agent/session id. Do not use raw prompt content as the primary picker label. Sanitize and bound any user/session-provided display text at the shared picker formatting boundary, while preserving the full prompt in the session transcript.

## Acceptance

- A regression test covers a resumed/persisted session with a long Markdown/file-link prompt.
- The attached-session picker row remains compact and starts with a stable session name/id and status (for example `session-3 · ready · loaded ...`), with no raw initial prompt preceding those fields.
- Fresh and resumed sessions use the same picker row shape, subject only to their legitimate metadata differences.

## Not covered

This report does not claim that loading or session readiness is functionally broken. It also does not prescribe whether the final label should be a persisted title, session id, or agent/session id; that choice should follow the existing session identity contract.
close_reason: Fixed at lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2651 by using the stable discovered session_id as the attached session name instead of the ACP-provided title, which may contain the initial prompt. Updated tests/ui/chat_spec.lua with a Markdown/file-link prompt title and asserted the load options use prior-acp. Focused chat suite: 94 passed. Full MiniTest suite: 351 passed. stylua --check . passed. lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning passed. Full suite emitted existing skill-discovery/write warnings but had 0 failures.

title: Grill-me needed: how does louiselm-launch's control surface and receipt signing fit the not-yet-built control broker?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing — it needs a focused grill-me session.

## The question

Two related design gaps in louiselm-d6fv.4 ("Launch verified Sessions inside
a Linux security boundary") that I do not think a single implementing agent
should decide unilaterally, because both cross into louiselm-qbr.5.1's
("Enforce Run capabilities through a local control broker") declared
territory and into signing-role conventions this project has previously
settled only through a grill-me (primary/recovery/release in trust.rs):

1. **Invocation and control protocol.** `louiselm-launch` is specified as
   "root-owned daemonless" (d6fv.4's Solution section). A single invocation
   can straightforwardly: check `release::running_identity()`, resolve a
   `LaunchRequest` (now built, skills-core/src/launch.rs), spawn via
   `BubblewrapBackend`, and relay stdio for the life of the process — that
   part needs no further design input. What is NOT decided: how does a
   *separate*, later invocation reach an *already-running* Session to Park,
   interrupt, quarantine, or Dispose it (AC8)? `SandboxedSession::park` /
   `interrupt` / `dispose` (skills-core/src/sandbox.rs) already work against
   a cgroup keyed by session_id, so the mechanics exist — what is missing is
   who calls them and how: a `louiselm-launch control --session <id> --park`
   re-invocation? A control broker (qbr.5.1) that itself never runs as root,
   so it cannot touch the cgroup directly — does it shell out to
   `louiselm-launch` for every lifecycle action, or does something else hold
   a privileged handle for the Session's whole life? The epic's own
   Implementation Decisions say "Put control authority in a separate
   local-only service under a dedicated unprivileged UID" — an unprivileged
   service cannot itself freeze/kill a cgroup, so *some* privileged relay is
   required, and its shape affects both issues' acceptance criteria.

2. **Receipt signing role.** AC9 asks for an "integrity-protected receipt."
   This project already treats "which role signs what" as consequential
   enough to gate through a grill-me and a physically separate hardware key
   per role (trust.rs: primary signs Skill Admission, recovery only replaces
   key policy, release authorizes trusted builds — RELEASE_NAMESPACE is
   explicitly kept distinct from the Admission namespace "even on one
   physical token"). A launch receipt is a distinct claim from all three of
   those. Does it get a fourth role and hardware key (real operational cost:
   another YubiKey touch, or another physically separate token), reuse the
   release key (blurs "authorizes trusted builds" into "attests every
   Session launch," a much higher signing volume with different risk), or
   use a softer integrity mechanism that isn't a human-touched signature at
   all (e.g., HMAC'd by a machine-held key the root launcher owns, since a
   receipt is generated automatically per-Session and cannot practically
   require a YubiKey touch per launch)? The last option seems likely right
   to me but changes what "integrity-protected" can mean for AC9, and I do
   not think that's mine to decide by picking an implementation.

## Context / evidence

- louiselm-d6fv.4 (this issue) is otherwise substantially built: isolation
  contract (src/isolation.rs), launch registries (src/registry.rs),
  bubblewrap backend with real cgroup lifecycle (src/sandbox.rs), and the
  closed LaunchRequest + resolution into a ConfinementPlan (src/launch.rs)
  are committed, gated, and tested against a real bwrap (not mocked) —
  commits 8fb3bb9 and 7c2ca56.
- release.rs's ALLOWED_COMPONENTS already names "louiselm-launch" as an
  expected release component, and running_identity()/identity_of() already
  implement exactly the "development build vs root-owned trusted install"
  check AC1 needs — that part of the entrypoint has no open design question,
  only implementation work.
- louiselm-qbr.5.1 (open, unclaimed) is the sibling issue that owns "Run
  capabilities through a local control broker" — I did not want to
  prejudge its wire protocol from inside d6fv.4.

## Threads worth pulling

- Does the control broker hold a long-lived privileged file descriptor /
  socket to each live Session, or does every lifecycle action re-invoke a
  root-owned helper fresh (matching "daemonless")?
- If receipts are machine-signed rather than hardware-signed, what does
  "integrity-protected" mean for AC9's purposes — tamper-evidence against a
  compromised unprivileged broker, not against a compromised root launcher?
- Should this question block d6fv.4's close, or can d6fv.4 close with an
  unsigned/placeholder receipt and a follow-up once qbr.5.1 exists?
close_reason: Confirmed supervisor, broker, signed-receipt, recovery, and AX contracts; routed to launcher and broker tracer tasks. inert:louiselm-d6fv.4.1

title: Astra reasoning picker inherits other Models usage samples
description:
The Reasoning effort picker shows historical Codex samples while GPT-6-Astra is selected during the maintainer's first uses of that Model. Observations from other Models/options appear applicable to the current combination.

## Observed
2026-09-07 screenshot inspected directly: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260907_0531_1920x1200_1788751860.png.
Subject Session in screenshot: codex/01a079ea-f12a-7a70-aac3-de374ae041a9 (session-10).
Header: Model=GPT-6-Astra; Reasoning effort=Medium; Fast mode=Off; Collaboration mode=Default; Mode=Full access.
Reasoning effort picker:
- Low: 38187.666666667 tokens/turn; 15 samples.
- Medium: 108034.18738739 tokens/turn; 555 samples.
- High: 126175.65187713 tokens/turn; 293 samples.
- Xhigh: 138724.69483568 tokens/turn; 213 samples.
- Max: 123320.04545455 tokens/turn; 44 samples.
- Ultra: 129289.76023392 tokens/turn; 171 samples.
Maintainer reports Astra has just become available and these counts cannot represent their Astra use. Release timing is user context, not independently verified.
Filing Session (live Chat lookup): codex/01a079e9-4e91-7eb3-9599-f7b26a4a2076.

## Root cause
lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2036 queries self.usage:summary(state.agent, option_id, value), omitting selected Model and all other active options. lua/louiselm/routing/usage.lua aggregates individual option buckets, so Codex reasoning-effort counts pool Models. This is verified query behavior; the screenshot alone does not establish which historical Models contributed.
Prior audit in louiselm-3x9p comment 700 already identifies marginal aggregation and missing complete option tuples.

## Why it was not caught
Existing picker/usage coverage validates individual option summaries. It does not establish that selecting a previously unused Model removes samples from other Models. Full test-gap audit deferred.

## Fix direction
Use the shared usage recording/query boundary to preserve and query matching option combinations. Do not relabel unidentifiable historical aggregates as Astra evidence. Resolve the remaining schema/history decisions in louiselm-3x9p before implementing joint analytics.

## Acceptance
- With old Codex Model history and no matching Astra history, Astra reasoning choices show no inherited sample count or token estimate.
- After measured Astra turns, only matching Model/option combinations contribute; changing Model or mode recomputes the cohort.
- Regression covers two Models sharing reasoning values, mode changes, and legacy records missing joint attribution.
- Maintainer confirms the original picker reproduction after a behavior-changing build.

## Not covered
Tracking only, as requested; no fix or test execution. Exact historical contributors, mode-specific contamination, and live telemetry ordering remain unverified. Related design question: louiselm-3x9p.
design: Confirmed implementation contract from louiselm-3x9p; prerequisite collection feature louiselm-houv. Implement the first shared typed SQL usage query and consume it in the Session options picker. Hold Agent and every other current option value fixed; resolve Provider for the candidate value, which may select another service. Exclude changed-during-turn records from fixed-tuple summaries. Never use legacy marginal samples or silently widen an empty cohort. Show No matching history when appropriate; distinguish total turns from each token/currency measurement denominator, and never sum currencies or estimate prices. Lua submits SQLite queries asynchronously and renders results; it does not duplicate SQL aggregation. Recompute from confirmed replacement options after selecting a value. Extend this same query boundary in explorer task louiselm-fbcs.

- [ ] Shared typed SQL query returns exact candidate cohorts with metric-specific coverage; source fields and filters are validated, and empty/legacy/mixed-turn cohorts never inherit unrelated measurements.
- [ ] Regression exercises two Agents/Providers and Models sharing reasoning values, typed option changes, candidate-specific Provider resolution, absent telemetry and separate currencies, query failures, and queued UI work after disposal.
- [ ] Maintainer confirms the original Astra picker reproduction after a behavior-changing build; automated gates alone do not close this live defect.

QA record: louiselm-j9t2. 924 tests and Lua/doc gates passed; individual manual cases 2/3 were not separately reported. Eligible historical import is separate louiselm-b1uo. No remaining work in this defect.

title: QA round: durable cold-Park resume
description:
# Manual QA review — durable cold-Park resume

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; its final content becomes the round Beads record
when the round closes.

**Build under test:** `ecb7b46..a983ea4` (`a983ea4` pushed to `origin/main`).
Re-run Setup after any fix.

Origin: `louiselm-brp7` found that `:LouiselmResumePark` loaded an ACP Session
and reported success while the capture-service Run stayed `cold_parked`. The
fix routes the UI through the authoritative revisioned `resume` → ACP
`session/load` → `finalize_resume(active)` sequence before attaching the
Session.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Successful cold Park resume finalizes the durable Run | **passed** — Run `6df99a74-...` active after resume; follow-up accepted |
| 2 | A finalized Run cannot be resumed a second time | **passed** — saved Run absent from second picker; six unrelated cold Parks remained |

## Setup

From `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`:

```sh
git rev-parse --short HEAD                 # expect a983ea4
cargo build --release --manifest-path capture-service/Cargo.toml
systemctl --user is-active louiselm-capture.service
PATH="$PWD/capture-service/target/release:$PATH" nvim -u ./manual_init.lua
```

Use the same state-root environment as the already-running capture service.
Do not start a second service. If the service was started with
`LOUISELM_CAPTURE_STATE_DIR` or a non-default `XDG_STATE_HOME`, export that
same value before launching Neovim. Inside Neovim verify the CLI path:

```vim
:lua print(vim.fn.exepath("louiselm-capture"))
```

It must point at `capture-service/target/release/louiselm-capture`. Use a fresh
real Session in its normal Agent mode; do not use a skip-approval/yolo mode.
The Agent must advertise ACP `loadSession`; the prior Claude QA setup did.
Record the Session id with `:LouiselmSessionId`.

Do not use the capture-service CLI to create the Run. The Park must be created
by `:LouiselmPark` from a live Session that has completed at least one prompt.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- The CLI list and the UI Run socket must use the same state root as the
  service. A mismatched `XDG_STATE_HOME` makes the picker or evidence look
  empty without testing the product path.
- Restart Neovim between Park and resume. `Chat:dispose()` closes the original
  Session; a fresh process proves the picker reconstructs the cold Run instead
  of reusing a local owner.
- Pin the selected Run id and Session id. Never inspect whichever JSON file or
  ACP log happens to be newest.
- Automated tests already cover failed `session/load` finalization and late
  disposal. This manual round focuses on the real Agent/service boundary,
  durable state, and UI timing.

## Cases

### 1. Successful cold Park resume finalizes the durable Run

Exercises `ca30c28`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4365`,
`lua/louiselm/workflow/resume_controller.lua:94`, and the real
`louiselm-capture` Run socket.

Steps:

1. Start a fresh real Session and send a harmless prompt such as: “Reply
   exactly `park-qa-ready`; do not modify files.” Wait for it to finish.
2. Run `:LouiselmPark`. Expect `Session cold-Parked`.
3. Run `louiselm-capture run list` in a shell using the same state root. Save
   the new Run id; it must be listed as a cold Park. Also save the ACP Session
   id from `:LouiselmSessionId`.
4. Quit Neovim completely. Start it again with the Setup command.
5. Run `:LouiselmResumePark`, select the saved Run, and wait. Expect
   `cold Park resumed (recoverable, lossy)` and a focused loaded chat buffer.
6. Send a follow-up: “Reply exactly `park-qa-followup`; do not modify files.”
   It must complete normally.

Current retest attempt: select Run
`6df99a74-12f7-4c75-8484-cfb5874b88c7`, paired with ACP Session
`claude/803f0f3d-926a-45dc-baa9-c1bcd81bf4cb`. The prior failed-test Run is
`a1dff263-9874-4332-8f8a-77e586a739a5`; the remaining listed Runs pair with
older Session `01a050f8-93e9-7f00-847f-be08e6920e77`.

Observed pass: the user selected the matching Run, saw `cold Park resumed
(recoverable, lossy)`, and Claude accepted `park-qa-followup`. The durable
record is `state=active`, `revision=5`, `park_expires_at_ms=0`, and
`resume_attempt.result=active`; the Run is absent from `louiselm-capture run
list`.

Expect: the loaded Session is usable, and the Run is no longer a resumable
cold Park. The success notification must occur only after the ACP Session has
loaded and the durable service has finalized the Run active.

Failure signature: the old bug — the notification appears and the follow-up
works, but the Run remains `cold_parked`, retains a nonzero expiry, or appears
again in the cold-Park picker; the picker has no Run; ACP `session/load` fails;
or the loaded chat cannot accept the follow-up.

### 2. A finalized Run cannot be resumed a second time

Exercises the same durable boundary and the operator’s post-resume view.

Steps:

1. After Case 1 succeeds, run `:LouiselmResumePark` again.
2. If the picker opens, do not select anything; dismiss it and mark the case
   failed. A successfully finalized Run must not be offered as a cold Park.

Expect: LouiseLM reports `no durable cold Parks found` (or shows only other,
unrelated cold Parks), and the saved Run id is absent from
`louiselm-capture run list`.

Failure signature: the same Run is offered again, a second ACP Session is
loaded, or the service list still reports it as `cold_parked`.

Observed pass: the second picker showed `6/6` remaining entries, all older
Runs from unrelated Codex Sessions; saved Run `6df99a74-12f7-4c75-8484-cfb5874b88c7`
was absent. The Claude Session remained ready with the successful follow-up
visible.

## Evidence check

Set `RUN_ID` to the saved id and use the same state root as Setup:

```sh
STATE_ROOT="${LOUISELM_CAPTURE_STATE_DIR:-${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}}"
RUN_FILE="$STATE_ROOT/louiselm/workflow/runs/$RUN_ID.json"
jq '{id,state,revision,park_expires_at_ms,resume_attempt}' "$RUN_FILE"
louiselm-capture run list
```

Case 1 passes when the JSON says `state: "active"`,
`park_expires_at_ms: 0`, and `resume_attempt.result: "active"`; the saved Run
id must not be in `run list`. Case 2 passes when the same absence remains.
The JSON and CLI prove durable service state and the socket/session evidence
proves the local UI reached the loaded Session; neither command proves focus or
what the user saw, so report that observation separately.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- Remove any disposable Beads claim created for QA and restore its exact prior
  status/assignee.
- Dispose the disposable Session and close extra Neovim windows.
- Do not delete the finalized Run JSON; record its id and outcome first, then
  remove only deliberately created test artifacts if needed.
- Delete this scratch file only after its final content becomes the round bead.

## Reporting back

Send the case number, what you saw, the Run id, the ACP Session id, and any
surprising detail. I will inspect the durable evidence before classifying it.

## Findings this round

**F1 — Resume Park crashes while creating operation id** (`louiselm-q2hp`,
fixed in `a983ea4`, live retest passed).
`resume_controller.lua:27` called `vim.uv.random(16, callback)` although the
local API requires `random(length, buffer?, callback)`. The valid Run
`a1dff263-9874-4332-8f8a-77e586a739a5` in Session
`codex/01a0560a-40aa-75d3-bd30-eb978b8052df` therefore left the user in an
empty buffer before any durable `resume` mutation. The UI regression failed
with a faithful three-argument fake before the fix and passes after changing
the call to `random(16, nil, callback)`.

**F2 — Cold Park picker does not show newest Parks first**
(`louiselm-6d2b`, open task).
The picker made the operator identify the current Session among seven Parks.
`capture-service/src/runs.rs:838` sorts `list_resumable` by UUID, while the
summary does not expose Park creation time. The current retest succeeded after
manual Session matching, but the ordering is avoidable UX friction.
close_reason: Cases 1-2 passed; q2hp fixed and retested; 6d2b filed for picker ordering.

title: Switching sessions leaves chat input in Normal mode
description:
Switching between attached LouiseLM chat sessions leaves the selected chat buffer in Normal mode, so typing and pressing Enter does not submit a prompt. The session appears idle and its ACP process remains alive, but no new prompt reaches the agent until the user manually presses i.

## Observed

Seen 2026-08-22 in the same Neovim instance with Codex sessions codex/01a02a74-274c-79d2-967e-597c37d997ed and the current session. The old session transcript stopped at its previous task completion; no new user turn was recorded after switching to it and pressing Enter. The associated ACP processes were alive.

## Symptoms

- Switching sessions succeeds, but the selected chat does not accept a prompt normally.
- Text typed after switching is handled as Normal-mode input; Enter does not submit.
- Manually pressing i restores the expected behavior.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2027` (`Chat:switch`) changes the current buffer and renders it, but does not restore insert mode or move the cursor to the prompt. `lua/louiselm/ui/picker.lua` stops insert mode before opening the session picker. Initial attachment calls `startinsert` at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1837`, but switching does not.

## Why it was not caught

Existing switch tests assert buffer/session selection and queued prompt behavior, but do not assert the editor mode or cursor state after switching through the picker.

## Fix direction

Make `Chat:switch` restore the selected view prompt cursor and insert mode, using the same narrow behavior as initial attachment. Add a headless regression assertion for switching to a session and submitting through the restored prompt.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.
- After `:LouiselmSwitchSession` selects a session, the cursor is on that session prompt and Neovim is in Insert mode.
- Pressing Enter submits a prompt to the selected session without requiring a manual i.

## Not covered

No changes to ACP process lifecycle or persisted Codex sessions are required.
close_reason: Fixed in the working tree: Chat:switch now restores the selected prompt cursor and Insert mode. Regression test tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'restores prompt input after switching sessions' failed before the fix and passes after it. Verification: focused chat_spec.lua 87/87; full MiniTest suite 334/334; stylua --check . passed; lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning passed; git diff --check passed. The full test output still emits pre-existing skill-discovery/write warnings, but no test failures.

title: Site CI rejects README-linked Evidence export guide
description:
Public site publication is blocked on main.

## Observed
GitLab site-build job https://gitlab.bartab.fr/oss-public/louiselm/-/jobs/145586 at commit 3d37a574f96d6baa561b5aeb91de3f71de40ea33, 2026-09-13:
2026-09-13T09:41:04.658549Z public artifact rejected: forbidden source or state file: build/evidence-export-71a3375ea259fd96a3576bc51651b9e9.md
ERROR: Job failed: exit code 1

## Root cause
README.md:149 links docs/evidence-export.md relatively. MyST copies the linked guide into build/ despite its absence from myst.yml public TOC and scripts/check-public-artifact curated source allowlist. The publication guard correctly rejects it.

## Why it was not caught
site:test checks synthetic artifacts, not actual README exports. Prior lessons louiselm-o7v6 and louiselm-ejbu document the same mechanism; full site build is needed for public Markdown link changes.

## Fix direction
Use the repository-hosted guide URL, matching the existing non-curated operator-guide pattern. Add explicit Evidence export source rejection coverage and record the recurring full-build requirement in docs/agent-testing.md. Preserve the publication allowlist.

## Acceptance

title: Replace unsafe spawn hooks with trusted bootstrap
description:
Replace the two remaining unsafe pre_exec hooks with a trusted exec bootstrap in the existing louiselm-launch binary. User explicitly authorizes redesign while preserving functionality (codex/01a074b2-a152-70b1-81eb-21ed37d04e7d).

Decision: launch a fresh, single-threaded bootstrap under the final UID/GID with a private socket on stdin. It blocks before any descendant/exec. Parent admits its unreaped PID to the Session cgroup, then sends exactly three CLOEXEC-owned descriptors via SCM_RIGHTS: workload stdin, Bubblewrap JSON status, and the blocking datagram. The helper changes only its own gate descriptor flags and safely execs Bubblewrap, preserving PID, stdio APIs and parent-death behavior. Require a bounded ready/exec-error handshake; post-spawn failure must kill/reap and prove zero survivors or return CleanupUnproven. Production selects the exact pinned release binary; development explicitly supplies its bootstrap path. No dependency or sudoers authority expansion.

Evidence: sandbox.rs:1527 currently writes cgroup.procs in pre_exec; sandbox/host_identity.rs:204 clears CLOEXEC in pre_exec. A trusted process blocked before release permits parent-side cgroup admission without the descendant race of directly moving Bubblewrap. Prior lessons: louiselm-xhgy.1, louiselm-wzy5, louiselm-6f7q. The last fix is implemented on fix/6f7q-launch-thread but unmerged; do not remove --die-with-parent or hide its known baseline lifetime failure.

Contract replacement: descriptors move into an owned IPC transfer instead of Command pre_exec closures. Port Gate-drop ownership and parent EOF coverage to that boundary. run remains the only privileged operator verb; the private bootstrap accepts only inherited capabilities and grants no additional authority.

Acceptance: real bootstrap regressions for inheritance, CLOEXEC isolation, malformed/truncated/missing/extra rights, lost parent, readiness/exec errors and deadlines; preserve blocking prepare/start/dispose, exact stdio, UID/GID/maps, parent/namespace PIDs, cgroup membership and descendant cleanup. Zero unsafe blocks with package forbid(unsafe_code). All skills-core Rust gates plus isolated privileged host conformance. Record any baseline limitation separately; no installed authority mutation.

title: Agent process stderr is captured by the transport but never surfaced on failure
description:
When the ACP agent process exits (crashes, fails to start, misconfigured
command) before or without completing the handshake, the user only sees a
generic "agent process exited with code N" — the process's own stderr, which
usually names the actual problem, is captured by the transport layer and then
discarded.

## Observed

Code reading, 2026-08-30 (louiselm.nvim main, related to session investigated
in louiselm-8hau).

`lua/louiselm/acp/transport.lua:94-108` defines and wires `on_stderr`:

```lua
local function on_stderr(self, err, data)
  if err ~= nil then
    report_error(self, err)
    return
  end
  if data ~= nil and data ~= "" then
    local callback = self.options.on_stderr
    if callback ~= nil then
      callback(data)
    end
  end
end
```

`M.start` (transport.lua:147-154) registers this as the `stderr` handler
passed to `vim.system`, so stderr chunks do reach `on_stderr` — but
`self.options.on_stderr` is only ever populated if the *caller* of
`Acp.connect`/`Transport.start` sets it.

`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:661-676`, the only production call site
(`Session:start`), builds the options table with `on_notification`,
`on_request`, `on_error`, and `on_exit`, but no `on_stderr` key. So every
stderr chunk hits `if callback ~= nil then callback(data) end` with
`callback == nil` and is silently dropped.

## Symptoms

- A failing agent process (bad command, missing dependency, broken install,
  crash) only ever surfaces `"agent process exited with code N"` in the
  transcript (via `handle_exit`, lifecycle.lua:475-484 -> `fail`).
- The actual diagnostic text the process printed — e.g. an npm CLI's own
  human-readable error message explaining exactly what's wrong — never
  reaches the user, and is not logged anywhere in this code path either.

## Root cause

`Session:start` (lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:661-676) omits an
`on_stderr` callback in the options table passed to `Acp.connect`, even
though `lua/louiselm/acp/transport.lua` fully supports one
(on_stderr defined at lines 97-108, wired at lines 152-154).

## Why it was not caught

No test asserts that stderr output from the agent process becomes visible to
the user or reaches any log. Existing lifecycle tests presumably only cover
the `on_exit`/`handle_exit` path with an exit code, not process output.

## Fix direction

Wire an `on_stderr` callback in `Session:start`'s options table that appends
the captured text to the failure context — e.g. buffer recent stderr lines on
`self.state` and include them in the message `fail()` emits when `handle_exit`
subsequently fires, or surface them as a distinct transcript event. Keep
consistent with AGENTS.md's redaction requirements (`ACP_LOG`/
`ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED` already governs sensitive wire content for the ACP
protocol layer; stderr here is process-level output rather than protocol
payload, but should not be assumed automatically safe to display verbatim —
review before implementation whether it needs the same redaction gate).

## Acceptance

- A regression test that starts a session against a transport double which
  emits stderr output and then exits nonzero, and asserts the resulting error
  event/message includes the emitted stderr text.
- Live: an agent command that prints a diagnostic to stderr before failing
  (e.g. the postinstall-not-run npm error reproduced in louiselm-8hau) shows
  that diagnostic text in the transcript, not just a bare exit code.

## Not covered

- Whether stderr should be shown unconditionally or gated behind
  ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED-style redaction — left as an open question for
  implementation, flagged above.
- The louiselm-8hau startup-timeout gap (a session whose process neither exits
  nor completes the handshake) — separate defect, filed separately.
close_reason:
Fixed. Session:start() (lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua) now wires
`on_stderr` into the Acp.connect options table; a new buffer_stderr() helper
appends incoming chunks to self.stderr_buffer, capped to the most recent
STDERR_BUFFER_LIMIT = 4096 bytes so a chatty process can't grow it unbounded.
handle_exit() now appends the trimmed buffered stderr text to the failure
message ("agent process exited with code N: <stderr>") instead of emitting a
bare exit code.

Tests added in tests/session/api_spec.lua ("new" set):
- "appends buffered agent stderr to the exit error message" - reproduces the
  exact scenario from louiselm-8hau's evidence (the opencode postinstall
  error text), asserts it now reaches the error event message.
- "caps buffered agent stderr to the most recent output" - asserts the
  STDERR_BUFFER_LIMIT truncation keeps the tail.

Gates: full mini.test suite (all files) - 0 fails, 0 notes. `stylua --check` -
clean. `lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning` - no problems
found. `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check` - clean after regenerating
doc/api.md alongside louiselm-8hau's LuaCATS changes (same commit scope).

Not covered, as filed: whether stderr should be gated behind an
ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED-style redaction switch was left open in the original bug
and is still open - stderr is shown unconditionally in this fix. Flagging for
a follow-up if that turns out to matter (e.g. an agent CLI that echoes secrets
to stderr on failure).

Deviation: same as louiselm-8hau - implementation preceded the regression
tests rather than witnessed red-green-refactor; tests are behavioral and
verified green against the fix, not proven red against the pre-fix code.

title: A loaded Session cannot Park until it sends another prompt
description:
The Park eligibility check uses prompts sent by this local Session instance as proof of persisted history. A successful session/load already proves history exists, but its local current_turn is zero, so Park rejects it until another prompt is sent.

## Observed
Code-proven preflight finding during C8 recovery, installed195460b, 2026-09-08, socket /run/user/1000/nvim.97179.0. Exact Codex Session01a07efc-1094-7873-9c89-91e31c3e6f52 is local session-1, source=loaded/status=ready/current_turn=0, loadSession=true, owner_run=nil.
Pinned proxy/sessions/01a07efc-1094-7873-9c89-91e31c3e6f52/log.jsonl line184 request2 at03:34:00.389Z; line207 success03:34:00.711Z. Buffer11 contains the two historical answers and usage42401/42432, with clean prompt228. SQLite holds both completed turns fb49d0de8bf2b6b28dd70891f185c628 and273e2797d0df104f0bca3ca9df4f7c45.
Park has NOT been invoked on this freshly loaded instance: this is live-state plus exact-guard evidence, not a captured user-facing refusal.

## Root cause
lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua:147 cold_park_record rejects state.current_turn<1 with cold Park requires a Session that has sent at least one prompt. The adjacent comment explains the intent as refusing a never-persisted new Session (aaw0.1), but the check ignores source=loaded and successful ACP load. Replay belongs to historical UI turns and does not increment the live prompt counter.

## Why it was not caught
The original aaw0.1 guard concerns a fresh Session with no persisted prompt. That scenario is not equivalent to successfully loaded history with no new local prompt; current code uses the same counter for both.

## Fix direction
Use actual evidence of persisted history at the eligibility boundary without weakening the never-prompted new-Session refusal. Do not manufacture a live turn count from UI replay or send a prompt solely to satisfy the check.

## Acceptance
Characterize successful load with current_turn0, then prove Park admits that persisted Session without a new prompt. Preserve rejection of a new never-prompted Session and Agents lacking loadSession. Maintainer verifies load -> Park -> editor exit -> cold resume with no intervening prompt.

## Not covered
F6 in current QA round; no fix/claim or Park mutation now. Workaround for continuing C8: one explicit harmless marker prompt, acknowledged as a workaround and not acceptance of this defect. Keep the original persisted turns; do not synthesize a CLI Run.

title: Native skill picker never resolves against the real Claude ACP adapter (exact description match rejects its scope-annotation suffix)
description:
Native skill invocation via the picker never resolves against the real Claude Code ACP adapter, because Claude appends a scope annotation to every advertised command description and the correlation code requires exact equality.

## Observed

Found 2026-08-20 during a qa-review round for louiselm-2w4 (native ACP command invocation, commit 763ba78), before any human test case was run -- by inspecting a pre-existing real ACP debug log on this machine (louiselm.nvim itself is run through claude-agent-acp for this very session).

Log: ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260820-100019-702281-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log, line 3 (session/update, sessionUpdate=available_commands_update). The "grill-me" entry:

  "name":"grill-me","description":"Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases. (user)","input":null

The local SKILL.md at ~/.config/agentskills/generated/grill-me/SKILL.md has description:

  Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

-- identical text, but the advertised one carries a trailing " (user)" that the local one does not.

Checked systematically: parsed all 76 entries in that available_commands_update payload. Every command whose name matches a configured local skill path (br, bvr, caveman, caveman-commit, caveman-help, caveman-review, grill-me, htmx, karpathy-guidelines, lightweight-charts, playwright-cli, playwright-qa-review, ponytail*, qa-review, rscss, rtk, rust-architecture, terraform-skill, to-beads*, write-a-skill -- 27 total) ends with " (user)". Claude's own built-in/plugin commands in the same payload (compact, config, model, doctor, mcp, loop, schedule, security-review, etc.) do not have this suffix.

## Symptoms

- User picks a configured skill via the native picker, types a task, submits.
- louiselm silently notifies "louiselm: advertised command '"'"'<skill>'"'"' description does not match the skill" and does not send the prompt; typed text and the skill chip are preserved (per louiselm-2w4 AC7), so it looks like a transient hiccup rather than a permanent break.
- This happens for every skill, every time, against the real Claude adapter -- native mode is a no-op for Claude in practice, despite ~40 unit/mock tests passing.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/skills/native_command.lua, description_matches() (around line 45): compares the whitespace-normalized advertised description to the whitespace-normalized local skill.description (or skill.short_description) with `==`. Real claude-agent-acp always appends " (user)" (or, presumably, another scope word for project/plugin-scoped commands) to the description of any command sourced from a user-configured skill path, so the strings are never equal even though the command is a correct, unambiguous match. The $-prefixed (Codex-style) tier is unaffected since it never checks description.

## Why it was not caught

Every existing test (tests/skills_spec.lua resolve_command cases, tests/ui/chat_spec.lua native-picker cases, tests/mock/agent_spec.lua) constructs its own advertised-command fixtures with hand-typed descriptions that exactly echo the local skill's description -- none of them models the real adapter's annotation behavior, because that behavior was never observed before this bead was implemented. The acceptance criteria for louiselm-2w4 specified "the whitespace-normalized advertised description matches the local SKILL.md description" without anticipating an adapter-appended suffix.

## Fix direction

In description_matches(), treat the advertised (normalized) description as matching when it *starts with* the local skill's normalized description or short_description, not only on exact equality -- tolerating a trailing annotation without weakening the $-tier or the ambiguity/duplicate rules (those are untouched). Reject anything where the local description is not a prefix of the advertised one, so an unrelated built-in that merely shares a name still fails to match.

## Acceptance

- A regression test in tests/skills_spec.lua using the real captured pair (grill-me description with and without the trailing " (user)") that fails before the fix and passes after.
- Existing exact-match cases keep passing (equality is the size-27-prefix special case of starts-with).

## Not covered

- Whether Codex's $-tier ever needs a similar tolerance -- not verified; no codex-acp session in the available debug logs got far enough to emit available_commands_update. Left as a follow-up if codex turns out to need it too.
- Whether Claude ever uses a different annotation word (e.g. "(project)", "(plugin)") for non-user-scope local skills -- not directly observed, but the starts-with fix is annotation-word-agnostic so it should not matter.
close_reason: Fixed in c230f8c. Root cause: description_matches() in lua/louiselm/skills/native_command.lua required exact whitespace-normalized equality; real claude-agent-acp appends a scope annotation (" (user)") to every command sourced from a user-configured skill path. Changed to starts-with matching against the local description/short_description. Tests: new resolve_command case using the real captured grill-me description pair (tests/skills_spec.lua), plus full existing resolve_command suite re-verified green. Gates: full mini.test suite green (287 cases), stylua and lua-language-server clean. No deviation from filed acceptance criteria. Codex's $-tier tolerance remains unverified (no codex-acp session reached available_commands_update in available logs) -- left as a known gap, not blocking this fix.

title: Resuming a Session dies with 'malformed ACP usage_update notification' when used > size
description:
A `usage_update` reporting `used > size` — which the real Claude agent emits on
the first mid-turn frame after `session/load` — is rejected as malformed, and
the rejection tears down the whole Session: status goes to `error`, the ACP
client is closed, and the in-flight prompt is aborted. The user sees only
`Error: malformed ACP usage_update notification` and loses the resumed
conversation.

## Observed

Reported live by the maintainer on 2026-08-28 against build `bbe82e7`: resumed
`claude/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d`, typed `ok`, session died.

Log: `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d/log.jsonl`
Session ID: `claude/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d`

Observed frame order at the end of that log:

```
07:33:39.017 client_to_agent  session/load
07:33:40.646 agent_to_client  result                     (replay complete)
07:34:21.836 client_to_agent  session/prompt             ("ok")
07:34:21.874 agent_to_client  session/update available_commands_update
07:34:25.340 agent_to_client  session/update usage_update {"used": 237031, "size": 200000}
07:34:25.349 internal         (connection torn down; log ends here)
```

The log's own earlier frames, from the same Session before the editor exit,
carry `{"used": 233011, "size": 1000000}` — i.e. the Session really is running
on a 1M-context model, and 237031 tokens is a perfectly ordinary occupancy for
it. The `size: 200000` in the fatal frame is the agent's pre-correction
default, not a real window.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/session/validation.lua:283-291` rejects any update where
`value.used > value.size`, returning `nil` context.
`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:239-243` maps that `nil` to
`fail(self, "malformed ACP usage_update notification")`, and `fail`
(`lifecycle.lua:136-161`) sets status `error`, closes the ACP client, drops the
permission queue, and completes the pending prompt callback with the error.

`used > size` is not a malformed frame. It is an over-full context window,
which is precisely the condition the `pressure` ladder exists to report. The
guard treats a representable state as a protocol violation.

The agent-side reason it happens on resume is documented in the agent's own
source, `/home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp/src/acp-agent.ts:6800-6813`: a model
alias resolving to an extended-context model with no `1m` token in its id
"stream[s] `usage_update.size: 200000` until the first result's modelUsage
corrects it". So the wrong `size` is transient and self-correcting — the client
only has to survive it.

## Symptoms

- Resuming a Session on a 1M-context model whose accumulated context exceeds
  200k kills the Session on the first prompt after resume.
- The failure is not recoverable in place: the ACP client is already closed by
  the time the error is displayed.
- The error message names a protocol fault, pointing debugging at the agent
  rather than at louiselm's own validation.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/session/api_spec.lua:1084` covers only the `used = -1, size = 0` case,
where every guard in the condition fires at once. No test isolates
`used > size` with otherwise valid values, and no resume test drives a
`usage_update` whose `size` is smaller than the already-accumulated `used`.

## Fix direction

Accept `used > size` as valid over-full occupancy: clamp `percentage` at 100
and report `pressure = "critical"`. Keep rejecting genuinely unrepresentable
input (`used < 0`, `size <= 0`, malformed `cost`).

## Acceptance

- A regression test feeds `{used = 237031, size = 200000}` (the observed live
  values) and asserts the Session stays `ready` with `pressure = "critical"`.
- Maintainer resumes `claude/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d`, sends a
  prompt, and the turn runs.

## Not covered

Whether *any* malformed `usage_update` should be fatal to a Session at all —
telemetry that cannot be parsed is not a reason to close a working ACP
connection. Filed separately.
close_reason: Live acceptance confirmed via louiselm-rlu7: maintainer resumed claude/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d and sent a prompt; the session survived and the turn completed normally (see rlu7's close reason for log evidence).

title: LouiseLM reports stale codex-acp version after terminal upgrade
description:
LouiseLM reports the configured codex Agent as outdated even though the same terminal environment reports codex-acp 1.7.0. The notification claims 1.6.2 is installed and 1.7.0 is upstream, so the health check appears to resolve a different executable/environment or stale process state than the user-facing shell.

## Observed

Reported by the maintainer on 2026-08-28 in the louiselm.nvim session. The exact notification was:

louiselm: codex is outdated (@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.2 installed, 1.7.0 upstream)

In the terminal, the same user ran:

 ~/code/louiselm  main *1 !1 ?1  ❯ codex-acp --version
@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.7.0

## Symptoms

- LouiseLM shows an outdated warning for codex.
- The terminal command reports the current installed version as 1.7.0.
- The warning reports an installed 1.6.2, which conflicts with the terminal result.

## Root cause

Unknown. The health path invokes the configured version command through vim.system() in lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:150-162 and compares its output with the configured latest check in lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:194-197. A likely cause is that the running Neovim process has a different PATH/environment or executable resolution than the terminal, but this is unverified.

## Why it was not caught

Existing tests cover parsing and comparison of mocked version outputs, but do not verify executable/environment parity between a running Neovim instance and the terminal after an agent upgrade.

## Fix direction

Trace the exact argv, cwd, PATH, and resolved executable used by the running Neovim health check without logging sensitive environment contents. Ensure the check observes the same installed codex-acp as the configured Agent, or make the discrepancy actionable if Neovim must be restarted.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails for the displaced version-resolution behavior and passes after the fix.
- When codex-acp --version returns 1.7.0 in the active LouiseLM environment, the notification must not report 1.6.2 installed or mark codex outdated against upstream 1.7.0.

## Not covered

- No reproduction was performed in the maintainer live Neovim instance during filing.
- The upstream version source and configured agent definition were not changed.
close_reason: Ignore superseded asynchronous version results; regression covered

Added a generation guard so superseded callbacks are ignored. Regression test failed before the fix and passes now; live shell and Neovim checks both currently report 1.7.0. No separate lesson warranted beyond this issue-local evidence.

title: br scheduler --json returns empty labels, hiding label-based routing from the command AGENTS.md prefers
description:
`br scheduler --json` emits `labels: []` for every recommendation, even when the
issue demonstrably carries labels. The field exists in the `br.scheduler.v1`
envelope and is always empty, so it reads as authoritative absence rather than
as missing data.

## Evidence (br 0.3.2, 2026-08-21)

`br scheduler --limit 6 --json`, labels as reported by the scheduler versus the
same issues via `br label list`:

| issue | scheduler | `br label list` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| louiselm-ce6.21 | `[]` | acp, chat, multimodal, qa-finding, ready-for-agent, ui |
| louiselm-ufx | `[]` | ui |
| louiselm-qbr.1.11 | `[]` | android, capture, qa-finding, ready-for-agent, ui |
| louiselm-qbr.1.12 | `[]` | android, capture, pairing, qa-finding, ready-for-agent, ui |
| louiselm-qbr.1.14 | `[]` | android, capture, privacy, qa-finding, ready-for-agent, ui, usability |
| louiselm-qbr.1.15 | `[]` | android, capture, qa-finding, ready-for-agent, status, ui |

`br list --json` and `br show --json` both populate `labels` correctly for the
same issues, so this is specific to the scheduler envelope.

## Why it matters here

AGENTS.md section 2 tells agents to prefer `br scheduler` over hand-scanning,
because it excludes claimed work and explains its ranking. An agent that follows
that instruction receives issues stripped of their labels.

That closes both routes for label-aware work selection at once. `br scheduler`
has no `--label`/`--label-any` filter of its own (unlike `br ready`), so
server-side filtering is unavailable; and because the returned labels are empty,
client-side filtering on the scheduler's own output is unavailable too. Any
convention that routes work by label is invisible to the command the contract
tells agents to use.

This was found while designing capability-based work routing
(`needs-capability:*` labels). It is not blocking that design -- `br ready`
carries labels and supports `-l` and `--label-any` -- but it does mean the
documented preference for `br scheduler` and label-based routing are mutually
exclusive until one of them changes.

## Not this repository

This is a defect in `br` (beads), not in louiselm. Filed here because it
constrains a louiselm workflow decision and would otherwise be lost. Upstream
report still to be raised.

## Suggested resolution

Populate `labels` in the `br.scheduler.v1` issue envelope from the same source
`br list --json` uses. A `--label`/`--label-any` filter matching `br ready`
would be a separate, larger ask.

title: Root-owned release fails trust check on current symlink mode
description:
lm70 manual QA F3, 2026-09-07, codex/01a07753-51de-7733-bfeb-8a3f26fa907e. First genuine release installs successfully but installed release identity and release status exit 2 with prefix_world_writable. This blocks actual installed acceptance; no workaround applied.

Observed: disposable VM invocation 10d850567c734ab88265d975e9cc8199, source f5983004aebfe7e8020159270792584991f63bad, release sha256:5042a209762b71e0d94be27add2754149ce375941bc1a9bbc6856abe27b3bf24. Installed at /usr/local/lib/louiselm. Root and vm status both show root_owned=true, world_writable=true, trusted=false. vm uid1000 writable_by_invoker=false. Root identity shows verified=false, failure_code=prefix_world_writable. find lists only root:root dirs0755, executables0555, data0444, state.json0644; current is root:root symlink0777 to exact first release. No regular file/directory has mode022 write bits and vm cannot write any installed path. Installed bundle signature still verifies under the protected provisional trust. Evidence /home/lotso/.cache/louiselm-lm70.NQCeob/ceremony.TBjRcG/installed-first-failure.json contains exact command outputs. Pre-install backup lm70-before.qdjO4T retained; no chmod, link removal, upgrade or tamper attempted.

Root cause: skills-core/src/install.rs:357-364 applies metadata.mode() & 0o022 to every entry; walk at :374 uses DirEntry::metadata, which returns symlink metadata rather than target metadata. The required current symlink therefore always contributes Linux symlink mode0777. Both install status and release::identity_of consume this shared ownership boundary (release.rs:647). Official API semantics: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fs/struct.DirEntry.html#method.metadata ; symlink mode is not access permission on Linux: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/symlink.7.html .

Test gap: tests/release.rs:453 only asserts non-root prefix rejection and never asserts world_writable=false for a normal installation; that earlier failure masks the symlink false positive. Suite intentionally omits real root-owned positive installed identity.

Fix direction: correct the narrow shared ownership check without weakening genuine ownership/writability or symlink-target integrity checks. Do not chmod current, remove it, follow arbitrary links recursively, or blanket-accept all symlink targets. Add failing regression for a legitimate current link plus negative real-writable-path coverage, and an enforceable root-owned installed positive control. Fresh built bytes will require real maintainer release signatures and installed retest; old frozen bundles cannot prove the correction.

Scope: record/diagnosis now; await maintainer direction before changing signed runtime and restarting the release ceremony. Associate F3 under the qa-round bead when this ongoing round is archived.

title: Analyze tool and command usage across local sessions
description:
## Problem Statement

The operator wants to rank tools and commands across all their local agent histories, including projects outside LouiseLM, and trace each usage to its Session and historical Provider/Model/options. Existing durable turn facts do not record tools or commands; the planned option-reflection skill has a narrower metadata scope. Raw transcript scans in an Agent's context would make the analysis itself expensive and difficult to verify.

## Solution

Proposed louiselm-usage skill backed by a standalone Rust/Clap CLI and a private derived SQLite index. Import recognized histories locally, preserve evidence links, then expose bounded sortable/filterable aggregates and drill-down. Keep recorded output size, estimated text tokens and provider-reported consumption separate. Recommend local workflow improvements without installing hooks or changing configuration.

Design artifact: docs/session-usage-skill.md. This is a reviewable design proposal; no CLI or skill is implemented or installed, and implementation is not claimed.

## User Stories

1. Rank tools and commands across all local projects, or restrict by project, source, time, Session, operation or result.
2. Trace an aggregate to real calls, Sessions, turns and source records.
3. Compare historical Agent/Provider/Model/typed option cohorts with explicit unknowns and measurement coverage.
4. Identify frequent, noisy, repeated, truncated or failing operations where a local query, cache, recipe or output formatter might help.
5. Query the corpus cheaply through structured, bounded CLI responses without repeatedly loading transcripts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Account for discovered Codex, Claude/child, OpenCode, Copilot, Gemini and ACP adapter/proxy histories, plus read-only LouiseLM turn enrichment. Report unsupported, absent, inaccessible, stale and partial sources; never claim a complete census from incomplete history.
2. Index incrementally and idempotently. Handle incomplete tails, rewritten/rotated files, patch journals, mutable SQLite rows, resumed histories and child/ancestor duplication. Do not mutate source histories or the durable turn database.
3. Preserve namespaced IDs and checkable source references. Merge native/ACP representations only with established identity; show unresolved overlap separately. Distinguish tool lifecycles, orchestration, command executions and polls. Observe commands inside wrappers through execution evidence, without evaluating script text.
4. Support validated filtering, grouping, sorting, field projection and pagination. Queries return bounded valid JSON with applied scope, freshness, coverage and actionable diagnostics. Discover fields through the CLI schema command.
5. Keep retained/produced/delivered output boundaries distinct. Never allocate turn tokens to tools, sum cumulative counters, substitute zero for missing usage, infer Provider from Model, or claim that historical output reduction proves billing savings. Exclude mixed-option turns from fixed-option comparisons.
6. Default index and responses contain metadata, sanitized signatures, sizes, private fingerprints and pointers, not copied raw prompts/results/operands or credentials. Explicit content drill-down is bounded. No replay of historical commands, hook installation or automatic option changes.
7. Install through the maintainer's owned skill catalog with a prebuilt Rust helper. Demonstrate a real invocation from LouiseLM and another project, producing usage rankings, traceable calls and a historical configuration comparison.

## Implementation Notes

Use concrete parser modules and SQL aggregation; no new daemon, generic adapter framework or coupling to trusted skills-core. Canonical commands are sources, index, stats, calls, show and schema. Implementation slices and intended SKILL.md are in the design artifact.

Related: louiselm-rdwb, louiselm-a1a9, louiselm-fbcs and louiselm-9ytn. This proposal does not change their accepted scope or create a dependency on the Neovim explorer. The independent cross-project consumer and explicit Rust preference justify proposing a separate CLI, not replacing existing query hosting on presumed performance grounds.

## Testing Notes

Use sanitized observed-format fixtures and behavior-first Rust tests. Cover exact counts and evidence links, sparse telemetry, option changes, cumulative usage, source overlap, command normalization gaps, malformed input and private content. Add the repository's locked fmt/Clippy/test/Rustdoc CI gates with the first implementation. Measure import, refresh and query performance on the actual corpus; no benchmark results are claimed by the design. Maintainer acceptance verifies a ranked command against its real Session.

## Out of Scope

Hooks, automatic rewrites/optimization, cloud analytics, command replay, a new Neovim dashboard, prices/quality scoring, causal provider rankings and adding tool content to the durable usage store.

CLI, source catalog and installed helper exist; implementation prerequisites closed. ylo32 retains installation/ranking/trace evidence; f2ou8 and0mv0o now closed with exact maintainer acceptance. Aggregate remains open for ylo32 maintainer requeue and explicit decision on final human historical-comparison acceptance; do not schedule a new implementation of the existing CLI.

title: Command cleanup failure panics before typed quarantine
description:
Found in the uncommitted qbr.5.1.1.5.2 implementation, not an installed-user regression.

## Observed
The new regression launch_supervisor::lifecycle::tool_dispatch::tests::failed_revocation_cleanup_is_not_acknowledged_and_poisons_identity failed on 2026-09-11: src/launch_supervisor/lifecycle.rs:2155 panicked: "an ambiguous mechanic failure has a pending operation". Six sibling command integration tests passed.

## Root cause
New command dispatch called quarantine_pending_mechanic after cancellation failure, but a command need not have a pending lifecycle receipt operation. The wrapper asserts that one exists. The common quarantine_mechanic already accepts an optional operation.

## Why not caught
Normal cancellation and repeated executor cleanup failure were covered separately; their Session-owner failure composition was not.

## Fix direction
Pass the actual optional lifecycle operation to common quarantine from command failures. Do not weaken the invariant for existing lifecycle-only callers.

## Acceptance
The named regression gets enforced:false, keeps broker revocation incomplete, and observes identity poison rather than release, without a panic. Full affected tests and lints stay green.

## Not covered
No real privileged cleanup failure is injected; the typed mechanics fault and lease disposition are deterministic doubles around real capability/broker transports.
