comments.text: Lesson routed here: command cancellation is not a pending lifecycle operation. Command failure paths now take the optional operation and call common quarantine_mechanic; the lifecycle-only assertion remains intact. The regression first reproduced the panic, then proved enforced:false, incomplete broker revocation, and identity poison (never release). Full Rust suite, fmt, strict Clippy, Rustdoc and browser gates pass. Fault injection is a deterministic mechanics/lease double, not a live privileged cleanup failure.

title: QA round: quit guard acceptance, Forensics viewer, Codex reasoning repro
description:
# Manual QA review — Neovim acceptance queue (2026-08-27)

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; it becomes a `qa-round` bead and gets deleted when
we close.

**Build under test:** `f44e0fd` (main, clean tree). Relevant commits:
`32665fd` (quit guard, ce6.34), `faf8cbf` (za fold, already accepted),
forensics slice (ce6.24). **Restart nvim after any fix.**

Origin: four Neovim-side issues sat `in_progress` not because the code was
unfinished but because AGENTS.md requires live maintainer acceptance and nobody
sat down to give it. This round converts "agent says done" into closed or into
a filed bug.

## Scope

In: **ce6.34** (quit guard, P1 — cases 1–5), **ce6.24** (Session Forensics,
P3 — case 6), **6ze7** (Codex reasoning fragmentation, P1 — case 7, *repro
only*, the fix was never written).

Out: **zufj** — dropped, not deferred. Its acceptance needs a live Copilot
Autopilot `task_complete`, and the 2026-08-26 comment records GitHub billing
showing premium quota unavailable for ~6 more days (≈2026-09-01). No amount of
keyboard time reaches it today.

Also out: Android (`1chb.1`, `qbr.1.15`, `1chb.2`) — needs a device, and
`1chb.2` is separately blocked on no tailscale/wireguard binary on the receiver.

Not tested because unit tests already cover it: **refusal clause 1** (Agent does
not advertise ACP `loadSession`). Reaching it live needs an agent that lacks
`loadSession`; codex advertises it (`recoverable: true` in the breadcrumb
below). `tests/ui/command_spec.lua` covers all three clauses together.

## Status

| # | Case | Issue | State |
|---|------|-------|-------|
| 1 | Breadcrumb from the fold session surfaces once at startup | ce6.34 | **passed** — 1a delivered the message, 1b `false`, 1c silent, file unlinked |
| 2 | Clause 2 — turn in flight refuses `:q`, message names `:qa` | ce6.34 | **passed** — refused, message names `:qa`; layout unconfirmed |
| 3 | Clause 3 — staged context refuses `:q`; `:q!` refused identically | ce6.34 | **passed** — both `:q` and `:q!` refused, counts truthful |
| 4 | Accepted residual — idle + recoverable + unstaged exits freely | ce6.34 | **passed** — exited freely, breadcrumb `recoverable:true, turn_active:false, contexts:0` |
| 5 | `:qa` escape exits and still records the breadcrumb | ce6.34 | **passed** (via `:qa!`) — exited, breadcrumb recorded `contexts: 2` |
| 6 | `:LouiselmForensics` collection + human projection | ce6.24 | **partial** — collect + resource link passed; view fails (F1), projection absent (F2) |
| 7 | Codex reasoning after a tool call — repro for the unfixed bug | 6ze7 | **does not reproduce** — trigger shape matched on the wire, renders correctly |

## Setup

Run every case in a **separate Neovim instance** from the one you are reading
this in, exactly as you did for the fold test. Cases 2–5 deliberately quit the
editor.

Confirm the running copy matches source before starting:

```
git log --oneline -1   # expect f44e0fd
```

The breadcrumb is a **single overwritten file** at
`~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/abandoned.json`. It is not append-only, so never
identify a run by "most recent file" — pin on `acp_session_id` and
`recorded_at`. Tell me the ACP session id of each instance you test with.

**Important ordering:** a breadcrumb from your fold-test session is sitting
there right now, unconsumed. Case 1 must run first or it will pollute the
later cases.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- **A concurrent agent is live in the worktree.** Between writing the scope
  section and writing the cases, uncommitted changes appeared in
  `capture-service/tests/runs.rs` and four `tests/workflow/*_spec.lua` files —
  Park-expiry work, matching `f045008` and the open question
  `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.3.1`. **None of them touch any file this round exercises**
  (`ui/chat/*`, `ui/abandonment.lua`, `session/*`), so the round is safe to run.
  But do not `git stash`, and if a case fails, check whether that agent has
  landed something before blaming the build. This is the same collision that
  blocked 6ze7 in the first place.
- **R1 — there is no `:LouiselmSetup` command.** Setup is the Lua entry point
  `require("louiselm").setup(config)`, invoked by the plugin manager at startup;
  the full registered command list is 32 `Louiselm*` commands and Setup is not
  among them. Any case that wants to re-run setup must either restart nvim or
  call the module function directly. My error, case 1 rewritten.
- **R2 — `:messages` is the wrong channel; notifications go to snacks.** Your
  config loads `snacks.nvim` at `config/plugins/init.lua:6`, before louiselm at
  line 19, and `snacks.notifier` replaces `vim.notify` with a transient float
  that keeps its **own** history and writes nothing to `:messages`. Every
  louiselm notification in this round — the breadcrumb message, the quit-guard
  refusal — arrives that way. Read them with `<leader>n`
  (`Snacks.notifier.show_history()`), never `:messages`. Applies to cases 1, 2,
  3 and 5.
- Append here every time a case misses for an environmental reason rather than a
  code reason.

## Cases

### 1. Breadcrumb from the fold session surfaces once at startup

Exercises `32665fd` — `lua/louiselm/ui/abandonment.lua:131` (`M.consume`) and
the setup consumption path.

There is already an un-consumed breadcrumb on disk, written at 03:15 today when
you quit the fold-test Neovim:

```json
{"version":1,"recorded_at":1787793346,"sessions":[{"agent":"codex",
"acp_session_id":"01a040c5-40ae-7891-b5a5-a39ea279e6f7",
"recoverable":true,"turn_active":false,
"staged":{"contexts":0,"pending_skill":false,"queued_prompt":false}}]}
```

Mode is `0600` — private permissions already confirmed from here, no keyboard
needed for that part.

There is no `:LouiselmSetup` Ex command — setup is
`require("louiselm").setup(config)`, which your plugin manager calls at startup,
and `surface_abandonment()` runs inside it (`lua/louiselm/init.lua:60`). So the
trigger is simply **starting nvim**.

**Attempt 1 (2026-08-27) did not reach the code as intended.** The breadcrumb
was consumed and unlinked — the file is gone, so `surface_abandonment` ran — but
I sent you to `:messages`, which snacks.notifier never writes to (ground rule
R2). I have recreated the identical breadcrumb on disk (same session id, same
`recorded_at`, mode `600`) so this is a clean rerun.

Steps:

> **1a.** Start a fresh nvim. Do not open a chat. Watch the top-right corner
> during startup, then immediately press `<leader>n` for the snacks
> notification history.
>
> **1b.** Still in that instance, run:
> `:lua print(require("louiselm.ui.chat.command").surface_abandonment())`
>
> **1c.** Quit with `:q`. You opened no chat, so there is no live Session and
> nothing should be written. Start nvim again and check `<leader>n`.

Expect: **1a** — one entry in the notification history, approximately
`louiselm: previous exit ended 1 live Session; resume codex with :LouiselmResume`.
**1b** prints `false` and adds no new entry — the breadcrumb is consumed once
and deleted. **1c** — no louiselm entry at all.

Failure signature: 1b prints `true` or re-notifies (consume did not delete);
codex reported as unrecoverable when the breadcrumb says `recoverable: true`;
1c nags from a breadcrumb a chatless exit should never have written; or **1a's
history is empty**, which is the interesting one — see the prediction below.

**Result (2026-08-27): passed.** 1a delivered
`louiselm: previous exit ended 1 live Session; resume codex with :LouiselmResume`
— truthful: recoverable codex, named, with the resume command. 1b printed
`false` and added no entry. 1c was silent. I confirmed the file is unlinked. All
three of consume-once, truthful classification, and no-write-on-chatless-exit
hold end to end.

**Prediction REFUTED — the delivery question.** `M.consume`
(`abandonment.lua:151`) unlinks the file *unconditionally*, before it has any
idea whether the message was seen, and before it even validates the record. The
delivery surface is a single transient WARN toast during startup churn. On
attempt 1 you were deliberately looking for that message, knowing exactly what
it should say, and did not see it — and the record was deleted anyway. If 1a's
history is empty too, then the guard's whole second half ("leaves a breadcrumb
that reaches the maintainer at the next session") does not reach the maintainer,
and fails silently and irreversibly.

Refuted: the toast rendered and was legible on a fresh start. Attempt 1's miss
was entirely my wrong observation channel (R2) — it was never evidence of
non-delivery. **No finding filed.** The unconditional unlink stays a
theoretical sharp edge, not an observed defect; it is not worth a bead on this
evidence.

Evidence: I check the file is gone after the first setup.

### 2. Clause 2 — turn in flight refuses `:q`

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:347-368`.

Steps:

> Open a chat, send a prompt that takes a while (e.g. *"read AGENTS.md and
> summarise every rule in it"*), and **while the turn is still streaming** type
> `:q` and hit enter.

Expect: nvim does **not** exit. A warning appears **as a snacks toast** (check
`<leader>n` if it flashes past) naming the session and the reason, ending
`. :qa to exit anyway.` The chat window is still there and the editor looks
unchanged.

Failure signature: nvim exits; or it refuses but the message omits `:qa` (the
design record calls a guard that hides its escape hatch "a trap"); or you are
left sitting in a stray extra split that did not clean itself up.

**Result (2026-08-27): passed.** Session
`deepseek/session-af10ba94-1b6f-4bb1-8829-12ef35c0187e`, `:q` during a live turn
was refused with:

```
louiselm: 1 live Session (deepseek: turn in flight). :qa to exit anyway.
```

Correct singular agreement, correct clause attribution, and the escape hatch is
named — the guard is not a trap. Count and parenthetical agree at n=1, so the
second prediction below is still untested.

Outstanding: window layout after the refusal was not reported. Folded into
case 3, which reuses the same instance.

**Prediction to confirm or refute:** the refusal works by opening a temporary
split of the *current* buffer and letting `:q` close that instead. Watch where
the cursor and window layout end up. If the current buffer was a normal file
rather than the chat, you should still end up net-zero windows.

**Second prediction:** the message counts `#sessions` (all live sessions) but
lists reasons only for `blocked` ones. With one blocked and one free session
you would read `2 live Sessions (codex: turn in flight)` — a count that does not
match its own parenthetical. Only observable with two sessions attached; note it
if you happen to see it.

### 3. Clause 3 — staged context refuses `:q`, and so does `:q!`

Exercises the same handler via the Staged-context clause
(`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:40-56`).

Steps — **reuse the case 2 instance**, so the layout check carries over:

> **3a.** First, before anything else: `:echo winnr('$')` and tell me the
> number, plus whether the chat window still looks the way it did before you
> pressed `:q`. This closes out case 2's untested half — the refusal works by
> opening a temporary split, and a leftover window is the failure.
>
> **3b.** Let the turn finish, or `:LouiselmCancel` it. Confirm the Session is
> idle — a still-running turn masks clause 3 behind clause 2 and the case
> proves nothing.
>
> **3c.** Attach a context (file/selection, your normal staging keymap) but
> **do not send**. Confirm the chat shows the staged item. Then `:q`. Then `:q!`.

**Result (2026-08-27): `:q` leg passed.** Session
`deepseek/session-9673cfd7-a022-474c-9fc0-2ce1d5d00d10`, two contexts staged:

```
louiselm: 1 live Session (deepseek: 2 queued contexts). :qa to exit anyway.
```

Staged count is truthful and matches the breadcrumb's `contexts: 2`.

**Still untested: `:q!`.** The run used `:qa!`, which is case 5's escape hatch,
not this case's bang. `:q!` is the one that matters — it is refused *identically*
to `:q` by design, which is backwards from muscle memory, so it is the single
most trap-shaped keystroke in the feature. One keystroke closes it; see the
retry step below.

Expect: **both** are refused, with the staged count in the message.

Failure signature: `:q!` exits. Per the design probe, `:q!` is refused
identically to `:q` — this is intentional and backwards from muscle memory, so
the *message* is the only thing that rescues it. If `:q!` exits, the guard has a
hole; if it refuses silently, it is a trap.

### 3b. Retry — the `:q!` leg only

> Fresh nvim, open a chat, stage **one** context, do not send. Then `:q!`.

Expect: refused, exactly like `:q`, message naming `:qa`.

Failure signature: nvim exits. That is a hole in the guard — `:q!` reads as
"force" to every Vim user alive, and clause 3 losses are unrecoverable.

**Result (2026-08-27): passed.** Session
`deepseek/session-5af6ecbd-af8c-4e75-8eea-9b810a31eb30`, one context staged:

```
louiselm: 1 live Session (deepseek: 1 queued context). :qa to exit anyway.
```

Refused, and singular agreement is correct at n=1 where case 3 showed the plural
at n=2. **ce6.34 is fully accepted and closed.**

### 4. Accepted residual — a clean idle session exits freely

Steps:

> Fresh instance. Open a chat with codex, send nothing (or let a turn fully
> finish), stage nothing. `:q`.

Expect: nvim exits immediately, no refusal. This is the deliberate residual —
you pay one `session/load` replay and nothing else.

Failure signature: it refuses anyway. That would be the blanket-refusal
behaviour the design explicitly rejected as "high-and-decaying coverage".

**Result (2026-08-27): passed**, reached accidentally via case 3 step 3b. Session
`deepseek/session-af10ba94-1b6f-4bb1-8829-12ef35c0187e` went idle and `:q` exited
immediately with no refusal. Breadcrumb confirms all three clauses were false:
`recoverable: true`, `turn_active: false`, `staged.contexts: 0`. Also confirms
deepseek advertises ACP `loadSession`, so clause 1 stays unreachable live.

**Prediction CONFIRMED, but by design — no finding.** `VimLeavePre` writes
the breadcrumb whenever `#sessions > 0`, *not* only when the exit was blocked
(`command.lua:370-378`). So this free, blessed exit should still leave a
breadcrumb, and your **next** nvim start will greet you with
`previous exit ended 1 live Session; resume codex with :LouiselmResume` — after
an exit that was entirely correct and lost nothing. That is exactly how the
`:qa` reflex forms, one rung down. The breadcrumb already on disk from your fold
session is this case, unblocked and pre-confirmed. If it nags you on the next
start, I file it.

### 5. `:qa` escape with a blocked session

Steps:

> Fresh instance. Reproduce case 2 or 3 (get a refusal). Then `:qa`.

**Result (2026-08-27): passed**, via `:qa!` from the case 3 instance. nvim
exited immediately despite an active clause-3 refusal, and `VimLeavePre` still
recorded the loss: breadcrumb at 03:45:49, mode `600`, session
`session-9673cfd7-a022-474c-9fc0-2ce1d5d00d10`, `staged.contexts: 2` matching the
refusal message exactly. Escape hatch and trail both intact. `:qa` without the
bang is not separately tested; `:qa!` is the strictly harder case.

Expect: nvim exits immediately. On the next start you get the breadcrumb
message naming the abandoned session.

Failure signature: `:qa` is also refused (the escape hatch is gone, the guard is
now unescapable), or it exits but writes no breadcrumb (you lost the session
*and* the trail).

### 6. `:LouiselmForensics` collection and human projection

Exercises the ce6.24 first slice. Its own comment says collection is verified;
what is *not* verified is "explicit human projection / resource-link /
targeting coverage" — so that is all this case tests.

Steps:

> With a live chat session, run `:LouiselmForensics`. Then `:LouiselmForensicsView`.
> (Both are real Ex commands — verified against the registered command list.)

Expect: a record is written under `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/forensics/`, a
resource link is queued into the chat's next prompt, and the view renders a
readable projection showing session identity, chronology, and which evidence
sources are missing or sensitive.

Failure signature: the view is raw JSON (the projection is the whole point), or
the queued resource link points at a path that does not exist, or the record
targets the wrong session.

**Result (2026-08-27): two of three legs pass.** Session
`deepseek/session-5d380d32-0e8d-4396-afa4-82cc1ee5c4fb`, from an empty baseline
directory.

- Leg 1 **passed**: record written, 841 bytes, mode `0600`, `schema_version: 1`,
  correct `subject.acp_session_id`. `evidence_sources` honestly marks `acp_log`
  as `omitted` with reason "ACP adapter did not advertise a log path" — verified
  correct, deepseek does not route through the acp-llm-adapter proxy, so there is
  genuinely no log to point at. Truthful, not merely populated.
- Leg 2 **passed**: `[context: forensics...]` staged into the next prompt.
- Leg 3 **failed twice over**: see F1 and F2.

Evidence: I diffed the forensics directory before/after and read the record.

### 7. Codex reasoning after a tool call — repro only

**This is not acceptance.** 6ze7 was never fixed: the assigned agent stopped
before editing because uncommitted changes had appeared in its target files.
Those changes are now committed and the tree is clean, so the blocker is gone —
and its claim is 1244m old, well past the 480m abandoned threshold, so it is
takeable. I want fresh evidence at current HEAD before anyone writes the fix,
because `faf8cbf` since touched the same renderer.

Steps:

> Fresh instance, codex session. Send a prompt that forces a tool call followed
> by reasoning and prose — e.g. *"read /home/lotso/code/louiselm/AGENTS.md and
> then explain in three paragraphs what its actor rules are for"* (absolute path
> on purpose, so it does not burn a search first).
> When the answer lands, look at the reasoning region and the prose after it.

Expect (if it has silently healed): one `[thinking]` header for the contiguous
reasoning run, and the answer streaming as normal prose.

Failure signature (the filed bug): several consecutive `[thinking]` headers
where there should be one, and the answer split one word/fragment per line with
blank lines between.

**Result (2026-08-27): does not reproduce.**

Attempt 1, `codex/01a040fc-493c-75e1-89a5-9c494fc67d39`, missed the trigger — my
prompt gave codex nothing to reason about after the tool result, so the only
thought frames arrived *before* the tool call. Useful negative only: 203 post-tool
message chunks with no fragmentation.

Attempt 2, `codex/01a04106-62aa-71e1-a127-82a02a8be68f`, hit it exactly:

```
tool_call             lines 34-35  (completed)
agent_thought_chunk   x2  lines 38-39
tool_call             lines 40-41  (completed)
agent_thought_chunk   x4  lines 44-47   <- the recorded trigger
agent_message_chunk   x183 lines 48-230
```

Thought-chunk text lengths at 44-47 are **2, 43, 2, 40**; the bug's own recorded
frames at its lines 60-63 were **2, 45, 2, 50** — same count, same alternating
2/N pattern, same position immediately after a completed tool call. The buffer
showed one `[thinking]` header and readable prose.

Caveat kept deliberately: one non-reproduction at HEAD is not a proven fix, and
**no regression test pins this shape**. Recorded on the issue; the close/pin
decision is the maintainer's.

## Evidence check

Breadcrumb state, pinned by session id rather than mtime:

```
stat -c '%a %s %y' ~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/abandoned.json 2>&1
python3 -m json.tool < ~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/abandoned.json 2>&1
```

Pass conditions: mode `600`; `acp_session_id` matches the instance you just
quit; `turn_active`/`staged` match what you actually had open. Absence of the
file after a setup is the pass condition for case 1.

Codex reasoning frames for case 7 (substitute your session id):

```
grep -c '"sessionUpdate":"agent_thought_chunk"' \
  ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/<ID>/log.jsonl
```

What this cannot prove: the frame count tells me what the *peer sent*, not how
the buffer rendered it. The rendering half of case 7 rests on what you see, so
describe the buffer, or tell me the buffer number and I will read it live.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/abandoned.json` — delete if a case leaves a
  stale one behind.
- Forensics records written by case 6 under
  `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/forensics/`.
- This file: becomes a `qa-round` bead, then deleted. Never committed.

## Reporting back

Tell me the case number, the ACP session id, what you saw, and anything
surprising. I pull the evidence myself before agreeing or disagreeing with your
reading. If I commit a fix, you re-run Setup before retesting and I will say
which cases to redo.

## Findings this round

**F1 — `:LouiselmForensicsView` refuses a bare invocation with a raw `E471`**
(`louiselm-h65x`, filed, not fixed).
Registered `nargs = 1` (`ui/chat/command.lua:560`), so Neovim rejects the bare
call before the callback runs — which makes the callback's own
`if path == "" then report_error("Forensics record path is required")` guard
(`command.lua:541-545`) unreachable dead code that can never deliver its friendly
error. The only place the 40-char generated path appears is a transient INFO
toast from `:LouiselmForensics`, unrecoverable under snacks.notifier. Fix
direction: `nargs = "?"` defaulting to the last record, which makes the existing
branch live. Missed because the prior round (`louiselm-wnpd` case 5) supplied the
path explicitly and never tried the bare form.

**F2 — the "human projection" is a JSON pager** (recorded on `louiselm-ce6.24`,
not filed separately).
`:LouiselmForensicsView` is `readfile` + `nvim_buf_set_lines` + `filetype="json"`
(`command.lua:546-560`): no rendered identity, no chronology, no marking of
missing or sensitive sources. ce6.24 user story 4 is unimplemented. Deliberately
**not** a new bead — it is ce6.24's own declared remaining acceptance, and a
duplicate would be noise. Also flagged there that `wnpd` case 5's "view passed"
covered readability, not projection, so it should not be read as prior
acceptance.


## Round summary (closed 2026-08-27)

Seven cases run, six behaviours accepted, two findings, one non-reproduction.

**Accepted and closed: louiselm-ce6.34** (P1). All three reachable refusal
clauses, the accepted residual, the `:qa` escape and the breadcrumb trail
verified live. Clause 1 (Agent without ACP `loadSession`) was unreachable — every
agent exercised advertises it — and stays unit-tested. Closed in `e0d27d8`.

**Still open: louiselm-ce6.24** (P3). Collection, targeting and resource-link
queueing accepted; the human projection is not implemented (F2). Comment added,
issue left open and unclaimed.

**Filed: louiselm-h65x** (P3, F1). Not fixed this round.

**Not reproducing: louiselm-6ze7** (P1). Trigger matched on the wire, symptoms
absent, but no code change was ever made against it and no regression test pins
the shape. Evidence recorded; close-or-pin left to the maintainer.

**Dropped, not deferred: louiselm-zufj.** Acceptance needs a live Copilot
Autopilot `task_complete` and premium quota is unavailable until ≈2026-09-01.

### Why the suite missed each finding

- **F1** — the prior round (`louiselm-wnpd` case 5) supplied the record path
  explicitly, so the bare invocation was never exercised. The unreachable
  `path == ""` branch also makes the code *read* as though the no-argument case
  is handled, which is how it survived review. Nothing in the suite invokes an Ex
  command the way a user first types it.
- **F2** — no test asserts what the view buffer *contains*, only that it opens.
  A JSON pager and a rendered projection are indistinguishable to a test that
  checks for a non-empty buffer.

### Leftovers

- `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/forensics/1787796219-1787796219-265777660586430.json`
  — the record from case 6, left in place as F1/F2 evidence.
- One breadcrumb may exist at `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/abandoned.json` from
  the final case; harmless, consumed on next start.
- Two predictions refuted (breadcrumb non-delivery; stray split after refusal)
  and one confirmed-but-by-design (breadcrumb on a clean exit). None filed.
close_reason: Round complete: 7 cases, ce6.34 accepted and closed, 2 findings routed, 6ze7 non-reproduction evidenced

comments.author: claude/65abe0a6-1362-47b6-aed7-cebbc8f60a11
comments.text:
Closed with --force: child louiselm-h65x is still open and deliberately so. A qa-round bead records that a round happened and what it found; it is not a tracking parent that should wait on its findings being fixed, or no round would ever close. h65x stays open on its own merits with its evidence intact and this round as its parent.

Final state of the four issues this round covered:
- louiselm-ce6.34 (P1): accepted live and closed (e0d27d8).
- louiselm-ce6.24 (P3): open. Collection, targeting, resource-link queueing accepted; human projection unimplemented, recorded in comment.
- louiselm-h65x (P3): open, filed this round, unfixed.
- louiselm-6ze7 (P1): open, does not reproduce at HEAD, evidence recorded; close-or-pin decision left to the maintainer.
- louiselm-zufj: not attempted, Copilot premium quota unavailable until approximately 2026-09-01.

Unfiled observation left for the maintainer: notifications in this configuration are delivered by snacks.notifier, which replaces vim.notify and writes nothing to :messages. Any future live-acceptance step concerning notification behaviour must name the notifier's own history instead. Proposed as an AGENTS.md rule and not added without agreement.

title: Skill locator includes nonexistent .system path
description:
Codex skill resolution advertises an incorrect filesystem locator for the karpathy-guidelines skill.

Reproduction and evidence:
- Session ID: codex/01a02e9a-7870-71b0-a820-c37f696a05d3
- Available-skills metadata reported: /home/lotso/dotfiles/agentskills/.config/agentskills/generated/.system/karpathy-guidelines/SKILL.md
- Reading that path failed with ENOENT.
- In the user's Neovim session, gf on the advertised file produces E447: Can't find file ... in path.
- The actual skill path is the corresponding path without the .system component: /home/lotso/dotfiles/agentskills/.config/agentskills/generated/karpathy-guidelines/SKILL.md

Expected behavior:
- Skill metadata and generated file/location references resolve to the real SKILL.md path.
- If unavailable, Codex reports it as unavailable rather than asserting that it loaded.

Observed behavior:
- Codex attempted the advertised path, could not read it, and the location is not navigable from Neovim.

Scope:
- Investigate skill locator generation/resolution, especially the erroneous .system path segment.
- Reproducer session: codex/01a02e9a-7870-71b0-a820-c37f696a05d3.
close_reason: Local workaround applied and parses: Codex now uses LouiseLM injected skill discovery; upstream openai/codex#24189 remains the root-cause fix.

comments.author: codex/01a02e9a-7870-71b0-a820-c37f696a05d3
comments.text:
Investigation 2026-08-23:
- LouiseLM config runs the Codex Agent with the default skills policy native; therefore LouiseLM does not discover or inject its catalog for this Agent.
- Installed @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp version 1.6.2 refreshes Codex-native skills by forwarding skills/list with forceReload=true. It does not construct or rewrite individual skill locations.
- On disk, generated/.system exists but contains only imagegen, openai-docs, plugin-creator, review-agent, skill-creator, and skill-installer. karpathy-guidelines exists at generated/karpathy-guidelines/SKILL.md, not below .system.
- Therefore the invalid location was produced downstream by the Codex native skill runtime, outside LouiseLM's catalog/discovery code.

No LouiseLM code change is safe: native mode intentionally delegates discovery to the Agent. A local workaround is to set agents.codex.skills.policy = "inject", which makes LouiseLM emit its independently discovered, correct paths, but changes Codex from native skill handling to injected catalog handling and requires maintainer approval.

It reports the same category/path reconstruction bug: a normal installed skill is emitted below /skills/.system instead of its discovered path. The proposed upstream fix is to preserve the actual discovered path and validate it exists. codex-acp's open issue list has no matching path-location report; this belongs to openai/codex.

A pre-existing br/references symlink-layout warning was observed but does not affect catalog generation.

title: Privileged skills-core host-identity test panics after executable pinning
description:
The skills-core job on main fails its privileged host-identity acceptance while ordinary local runs skip that test. P0 requested by maintainer.

Observed: https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/34583247534/job/103211452538 at commit 66f6d219f339eb0dbaba503c55bcf754d9326c01, 2026-09-11. tests/sandbox.rs:714: host_identity_changes_outer_credentials_and_owns_private_directories panics: a privileged launcher applies the assigned identity: SpawnFailed { backend: "bubblewrap", reason: "Agent identity verification failed: Agent process or executable changed" }. Five tests passed, one failed, exit 101. Ordinary cargo Test step had passed.

Root cause under investigation: fixture plan creates a shebang script, whereas new lifetime pinning compares the planned executable inode with /proc/PID/exe at exec stop, which refers to the interpreter. Need verify production runtime contract before changing fixture or identity checks. This is distinct from earlier bootstrap ancestry, inherited FD, Git-config, and orphan-reaping CI incidents.

Acceptance: reproduce the failed privileged scenario locally or an equivalent deterministic kernel-boundary regression; preserve fail-closed identity checks; make the existing identity/permissions assertions pass with a valid runtime fixture; provide one reusable local privileged test recipe and useful bounded diagnostics if unavailable. Run focused and complete affected gates. No GitHub PR or CI trial-and-error.

Limits: local sudo currently requires a password. Existing launch_protocol and launch_supervisor/lifecycle changes belong to another session.
close_reason: Kernel executable fixture corrected; unprivileged regression and exact local privileged reproduction red→green. All affected Rust gates and VM conformance pass using host-built artifacts (gg5r); lesson and limits in comment 1566. gate:scripts/launcher-conformance

Exact inode pin introduced by 69045c7; sandbox shared plan() still supplies shebang script, whereas kernel exe is interpreter. Other privileged fixtures audited: native binaries, NamespaceOnly, or no start(); no further fixture changes warranted. VM build lacked OpenSSL development headers; transferred host-built artifacts instead, no package/host changes. Local regression will guard shared fixture executable identity without root; local launcher-conformance will include these six cases so CI has no exclusive recipe.

comments.author: codex/01a08fc9-01a5-76f0-878b-14b7c95578ce
comments.text:
Fixed shared sandbox runtime fixture: copied native /bin/sh is the planned executable; scenario script is its fixed argument. New unprivileged kernel-executable probe red exit=1 before fix, green afterward. Production exact executable checks remain fail-closed. Diagnostics now distinguish process exit/missing executable from mismatch and include PID + expected/observed device/inode without paths or payloads; two existing assertions went red then green.

Green: host full skills-core suite (outside ACP via transient user service), cargo fmt --check, strict all-target/all-feature Clippy, warning-denied Rustdoc, 13 Node browser tests, shell syntax, CI YAML parse and git diff --check. Gates used isolated committed 66f6d219 + only our three Rust paths at /var/tmp/louiselm-boke.tiby5Z; live shared-tree fmt currently fails in another sessions command/broker work, left untouched.

Exact VM host_identity selection: 6 passed with assigned UID/GID 60000 and umask 077 (unprivileged-only guard legitimately returns early under root). Because existing VM provisioning bug gg5r blocks compilation, tests use host-built actual Cargo artifacts copied to identical guest paths; run-prebuilt-conformance substitutes only Cargo no-run artifact discovery, executes unchanged conformance script and real privileged binaries. title: Grill-me needed: should louiselm formalize a persisted project vocabulary from grill-me sessions
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing -- it wants full attention.**

Raised as explicit "food for thought" on 2026-08-20. Originally noted only in
an agent's private memory; migrated into beads on 2026-08-20 alongside
louiselm-3od once it was pointed out that louiselm is cross-adapter by
design, so a note only one adapter can see is exactly the kind of context
AGENTS.md says does not belong there.

## The question

Should louiselm (or its workflow) formalize a persisted "project vocabulary" --
a working glossary that accumulates meaning from `grill-me` sessions over
time, so each term embeds context that would otherwise need re-explaining --
and if so, what does that mechanism look like here?

## Context

The user referenced a video by mattpocock (the original author of the
`grill-me` skill/pattern) describing that a grill-me session's real product
is shared understanding, and that over time this naturally produces a working
vocabulary for a project. The user recalled mattpocock built this into one of
his own skills: a mechanism that persists the accumulated vocabulary to a
markdown file rather than letting it live only in conversation history. The
user wants something equivalent for their own workflow here, and floated
possibly integrating it with beads -- the local issue tracker this project
already leans on heavily (`br`/`bvr` triage, the `to-beads-*` skill family).

## Threads worth pulling

- Whether this lives as its own artifact (a `VOCABULARY.md` or similar) or as
  structured beads content (e.g. a dedicated issue type, or metadata on
  existing issues).
- How it interacts with the `to-beads-*` skill family, which already turns
  grill-me sessions into beads work -- is vocabulary a byproduct of that
  same pipeline, or a separate one?
- Two concrete instances of the problem this would solve already exist in
  this project. First, "chat" vs. "session" naming drift (caught and
  corrected once, but only recorded in an agent's private memory before this
  migration). Second, and far more expensive, "model" vs. "provider" on
  2026-08-21 -- see the worked example below. A persisted vocabulary
  mechanism would presumably have caught or prevented both on its own.
- Worth checking mattpocock's public work (skills, videos, blog) for the
  specific mechanism he built, if the user references it again, rather than
  reinventing it blind.
- Related, separately filed thread: louiselm-3od (documentation strategy) --
  not the same question, but a persisted vocabulary could plausibly feed or
  overlap with an agent-legible documentation artifact. Worth deciding during
  either grill whether they should be one session or two.

## Worked example: "model" vs. "provider" (2026-08-21)

The maintainer asked whether `:LouiselmModelChange` should exist, then said
"file it as a priority beads task and implement it asap". An agent filed
louiselm-model-change-cl59, implemented it test-first, passed all three gates,
and committed it (1e7e560). The maintainer then clarified that by "model" they
had meant *provider*: switching a live Claude session to Codex, not switching
between the models one agent advertises. The commit was reverted (db39f96) and
the bead closed as not planned.

What makes this the strongest available argument for the mechanism:

- The ambiguity was invisible to both parties. The agent checked the code,
  confirmed the capability already existed, cited the tests covering it, and
  was told to proceed. Nothing in the exchange surfaced that the two sides
  were pointing at different referents.
- The cost was not an argument about naming. It was a wrong feature built,
  reviewed, gated, committed to main, and reverted.
- The two referents are not near-synonyms wearing different labels. A model
  change is one `session/set_config_option` call inside a live ACP session; a
  provider change needs a different agent process, a different connection,
  and a different session, so the current session cannot survive it. A
  glossary entry binding each term to its definition would have made the
  mismatch visible at the moment the command was proposed.
- ACP already supplies the disambiguating vocabulary: the option carries
  `category = "model"`, while the agent is a separately configured definition.
  A project vocabulary would have had a wire-level authority to anchor to
  rather than inventing a house convention.

Note for the grill: this example argues the vocabulary has to be legible at
*proposal* time, not only at review time. A VOCABULARY.md that nobody reads
before implementing would not have prevented this. That is a constraint on the
mechanism, not just on the artifact.

## Out of scope for the grill

Re-deriving the above. React to it.
close_reason: Resolved through grill-me: confirmed a Beads-native vocabulary lifecycle, promoted Agent/Model/Session/Handoff/Provider reference records, and created feature louiselm-ce6.22 with implementation tasks louiselm-ce6.22.1 and louiselm-ce6.22.2.

comments.author: claude/cca6e4b5-ff23-495e-a84c-6a69b4c18c99
comments.text: Cross-reference: louiselm-provider-switch-ypqs is the real want that the model/provider slip was hiding. If the vocabulary grill runs first, 'provider' vs 'model' is a ready-made first entry with a wire-level authority (ACP category) to anchor to.

comments.author: claude/cca6e4b5-ff23-495e-a84c-6a69b4c18c99
comments.text: Second vocabulary candidate, from the 2026-08-21 grill on louiselm-provider-switch-ypqs: the `needs-capability:*` label namespace agreed in louiselm-capability-routing-m3sc is a controlled vocabulary by construction, and it already has a live drift risk -- `multimodal` exists on louiselm-ce6.21 and overlaps semantically with an image-generation capability name. Two properties make it a useful test case for whatever this grill decides. It is greppable (`br label list-all | grep needs-capability:`), so the vocabulary has a mechanical inventory rather than a prose one; and `br label rename` rewrites a label across every issue, so a bad entry is repairable rather than permanent. If the vocabulary mechanism cannot express 'these two names mean the same thing, prefer this one', it will not survive contact with this namespace.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 1 — ambiguity handling is consequence-based. If competing meanings imply materially different architecture, lifecycle, protocol behavior, authority, or user-visible behavior, stop before implementation and require explicit confirmation. Harmless naming drift may be silently normalized to the canonical term. The gate is therefore not every unknown word; it is ambiguity whose interpretations would produce meaningfully different work.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text:
Research note — upstream and Beads capabilities (2026-08-23). Matt Pocock's current upstream separates plain grill-me (delegates only to grilling) from grill-with-docs (composes grilling + domain-modeling). domain-modeling updates CONTEXT.md inline as terms crystallize, keeps it glossary-only and implementation-free, lists avoided synonyms, checks ambiguous terms against code, and relies on repo instructions to make later skills read/use it. Upstream to-tickets consumes that glossary but the tracker is not its canonical vocabulary store. Sources: https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/main/README.md; /skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md; /skills/engineering/domain-modeling/SKILL.md; /skills/engineering/domain-modeling/CONTEXT-FORMAT.md.

Local divergence: this repo's grill-me waits for shared understanding and then invokes to-beads; local to-beads requires project vocabulary in outputs but does not create or maintain a vocabulary artifact.

Beads 0.4.0 can support a Beads-native glossary: custom issue types are accepted (a dry-run with type=vocabulary succeeded); list/search filter by type/status/label; search covers title, description, id, and comments; descriptions are replaceable; comments retain rationale; saved queries and git-backed JSONL provide discovery/history. A closed vocabulary reference is excluded from ready work. Important limits: Beads does not ambiently inject the glossary before proposal work; AGENTS/skills must explicitly load it. One bead per term would inflate issue/closure/velocity metrics and fragment the glossary. agent_context inheritance follows parent hierarchy, so using it project-wide would corrupt product hierarchy. Strong candidate: one closed custom-type vocabulary bead per bounded context, with canonical current definitions in its description, rationale/history in comments, and separate open question beads for disputed changes; AGENTS and grill/to-beads load it before proposing work.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 2 — use Beads as the canonical vocabulary store. The storage unit is one closed custom-type  bead per bounded context, starting with one project-wide LouiseLM vocabulary bead. Its description is the current concise glossary; comments preserve rationale/history; open question beads carry disputed or proposed changes. Do not create one bead per term, which would fragment consumption and distort tracker metrics.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Correction to comment 169: the omitted custom issue type is vocabulary. Agreement 2 is unchanged: use one closed vocabulary bead per bounded context, starting with one project-wide LouiseLM vocabulary bead. Its description is the current concise glossary; comments preserve rationale/history; open question beads carry disputed or proposed changes. Do not create one bead per term.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 3 — load vocabulary at grill start, keep term decisions provisional on the source question during discussion, and promote resolved terms to the canonical vocabulary bead only after the user confirms shared understanding. Promotion happens even when no implementation work results. Adoption constraint still to settle: the first run and later grills must not trigger a retroactive vocabulary audit or flood the workflow with terminology disputes.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 4 — vocabulary adoption is an incremental ratchet, not a migration. Do not scan repository history or the backlog for terms, do not treat missing entries as debt or warnings, and do not pursue completeness. Seed only proven high-cost distinctions. A grill proposes vocabulary changes only when ambiguity materially affects its current decision; harmless synonyms do not trigger discussion. A comprehensive vocabulary audit requires an explicit user request.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Tradeoff analysis for universal loading. Costs: a small process and context tax on every applicable session; irrelevant vocabulary if bounded contexts multiply; stale definitions can steer agents confidently away from current code; custom vocabulary issues still appear in aggregate tracker metrics; a Beads JSONL issue is one record, so concurrent edits to one vocabulary description have coarser merge behavior than line-oriented Markdown; and two sessions that both read then replace the description can produce a semantic last-writer-wins loss even though SQLite serializes each write. Guardrails: load once only for sessions that plan, implement, review, or file work, not pure housekeeping; keep definitions conceptual, short, and free of countable implementation facts; load only relevant contexts once multiple contexts exist; keep canonical vocabulary beads closed so they never enter ready scheduling; re-read immediately before promotion and refuse or reconcile when updated_at changed; route disagreements through question beads rather than reopening the vocabulary reference.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 5 — vocabulary loading is mandatory once per semantic work session: planning, implementation, review, or filing work. Pure housekeeping and mechanical changes may skip it. Load only relevant bounded contexts, keep entries concise and conceptual, keep canonical vocabulary beads closed, and re-read updated_at immediately before promotion to detect concurrent change. Expected context cost is intentionally small because the vocabulary is not expected or encouraged to become exhaustive.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 6 — semantic freshness is conflict-driven, not periodically audited. SQLite and JSONL provide durable current storage but cannot determine whether a definition still matches product intent or code. When vocabulary, code, a work item, or user intent materially contradict one another, neither source automatically wins. Stop, create or reuse a vocabulary question bead, resolve the conflict with the user, then promote the agreed definition to the canonical vocabulary bead.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 7 — implement vocabulary as workflow infrastructure first, not as a louiselm.nvim runtime subsystem. Initial scope is a canonical Beads vocabulary bead, project instructions for loading and conflicts, and local grill-me/to-beads integration for consumption and end-of-grill promotion. Dogfood several real grills before considering any plugin command or UI; productize only from observed workflow friction.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 8 — seed only the proven high-value language from the model/provider failure and shipped handoff. Canonical concepts: Agent is a named configured ACP entry LouiseLM can start sessions with; Model is an agent-advertised option that can change within the same session; Session is a conversation bound to one agent and cannot change agents; Handoff creates a session with another agent, injects a reviewed transcript, and retains the source session. Provider is reserved for the underlying vendor or service and is avoided when referring to a configured agent entry.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Format investigation revises the earlier storage recommendation. In an isolated Beads workspace, a custom type vocabulary bead with custom status reference was accepted. br list filtered by type/status with TOON exposed title, description, design, and notes as distinct fields; normal br show rendered the same fields readably. BVR ignored the reference-status bead entirely: it was absent from total/type/status counts, recommendations, and actionable work. A single vocabulary bead using agent_context was less suitable because br emits agent_context as a JSON-encoded string and a human view would require a duplicated rendering. Strong revised candidate: one reference-status vocabulary bead per canonical term; title=term, description=one or two sentence definition, notes=Avoid and Distinguish-from guidance, design=provenance/source question. Query all terms in one TOON call. This is genuinely Beads-structured, avoids one opaque multi-term description, isolates concurrent updates per term, remains human-readable, and does not pollute BVR work metrics.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 9 supersedes agreement 2 storage granularity. Use one Beads record per canonical term, with issue_type=vocabulary and status=reference. Title is the canonical term; description is its tight conceptual definition; notes carry Avoid and Distinguish-from guidance; design carries current provenance/source questions. Agents load all applicable terms with br list filtered by vocabulary/reference in TOON format; humans inspect the same records with br show. Add context labels only when multiple bounded contexts actually emerge. Isolated verification proved reference records are excluded from br ready and from BVR project counts, recommendations, and graph analysis.

comments.author: codex/01a02cf7-4dcd-7e33-a7e9-a8f8cca2b9c5
comments.text: Grill agreement 10 — the final shared-understanding summary must include an explicit compact vocabulary delta: terms to create, terms to update with the semantic change, or no vocabulary changes. The user confirmation of that single final summary authorizes both vocabulary promotion and creation/update of resulting work items. Do not mutate vocabulary silently, and do not add a second confirmation ceremony after shared understanding.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Agreement 11 — grill-me behavior replacement and bootstrap: supersedes the proposed opt-in-by-existing-vocabulary-record behavior discussed in the transcript. Do not introduce a separately named grill-me-vocabulary command. Keep the grill-me name and change its standard behavior so every grill-me session performs the vocabulary workflow: load any existing vocabulary/reference records, treat an empty result as a valid first-session state, surface a vocabulary delta in the shared-understanding summary, and create the first vocabulary records after confirmation. Existing vocabulary records are not an activation flag.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Agreement 12 — projects without Beads: grill-me remains usable when the current project has no Beads database, but explicitly reports that the vocabulary delta cannot be persisted. It must not silently initialize Beads. In a Beads-enabled project, zero vocabulary/reference records is a valid bootstrap state and does not disable the vocabulary workflow.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Implementation refinement from the confirmed bootstrap: br list rejects an undeclared custom status when no reference record exists, while br list --type vocabulary --status all --format toon returns a structured empty result. Therefore discovery must query vocabulary across statuses and consume only records whose status is reference. This preserves the agreed vocabulary/reference invariant without silently editing project policy or breaking first use.

title: Render Markdown pipe tables legibly in Session buffers without plugins
description:
Valid Markdown pipe tables in a live Session are syntax-highlighted but remain literal pipe-delimited text. Long cells wrap independently of the column structure, making comparisons difficult to scan. The requested UX must not require a Markdown rendering plugin.

## Observed

Screenshot: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260903_2225_1920x1200_1788467145.png, Session codex/01a068e8-fde0-7830-afe0-8ca2a66482de, 2026-09-03. Lines 503-510 show a valid three-column table as raw pipes and delimiter dashes.

Live inspection of that buffer found:
- filetype: `louiselm-session`
- active Tree-sitter highlighter language: `markdown`
- explicit Markdown parser nodes: `pipe_table_header`, `pipe_table_delimiter_row`, and `pipe_table_row`
- default `vim.treesitter.get_parser(buf)`: nil; explicit `get_parser(buf, "markdown")`: markdown

Thus `:InspectTree` without an argument reports no language because it derives the parser language from the custom filetype. `:InspectTree markdown` can inspect the already-active parser.

## Cause and constraint

Tree-sitter parses and highlights Markdown; it does not lay out a terminal table. Setting the Session buffer filetype to literal `markdown` would not add table rendering.

Keep the custom filetype boundary. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2983-2992` deliberately uses `louiselm-session` and starts the Markdown parser explicitly. Closed bug `louiselm-ff8` established why: literal `markdown` caused image.nvim and similar filetype-keyed integrations to treat the growing transcript as an editable Markdown document and rescan it on every keystroke.

## Direction

Find the smallest LouiseLM-owned, native-Neovim presentation that makes parsed pipe tables legible without a third-party Markdown renderer. Preserve the underlying Markdown for copying/export, streaming updates, prompt editing, and Session navigation. Register `markdown` as the Tree-sitter language for `louiselm-session` if safe so no-argument diagnostic tooling sees the parser without changing the filetype.

Adjacent but not duplicate: open task `louiselm-zvap` evaluates md-render.nvim and is plugin-centric; this task records the explicit no-plugin requirement.

## Acceptance

- A valid `pipe_table` in a Session is visually legible as rows and aligned columns without installing a Markdown plugin.
- Long cell content has deliberate wrap, truncation, or inspection behavior rather than destroying column readability.
- Malformed Markdown and ordinary prose containing `|` remain untouched.
- The buffer remains `filetype=louiselm-session`; filetype-keyed Markdown integrations stay detached.
- Source Markdown remains copyable and export output is unchanged.
- Bare `:InspectTree` resolves the active Markdown language, or the remaining diagnostic limitation is explicitly justified.
- Normal streamed prose, prompt editing, navigation, and disposal retain behavioral coverage.

## Not covered

Full rich-Markdown rendering, images, Mermaid, media, and adoption of md-render.nvim remain under `louiselm-zvap`.

comments.author: claude/2249525d-9f65-4c29-991e-bc3b0e2c80b7
comments.text:
Investigated the "this is a treesitter-markdown problem" hypothesis. It is not. Evidence, Neovim 0.12.5:

Parser is correct. The screenshot's own table (lines 503-510, em dash, curly quotes, ragged cell spacing) reparses to one `pipe_table` spanning rows 2..8 with `pipe_table_header`, `pipe_table_delimiter_row`, and 4 `pipe_table_row` nodes. Live buffer 1043 (`louiselm://session-14`) currently holds 2 `pipe_table` nodes.

Queries are complete and applied. `runtime/queries/markdown/highlights.scm` shipped with Neovim 0.12.5 and the copy from nvim-treesitter rev 41416e81 (`~/.local/share/nvim/site/queries/markdown/` symlinks into the pack) are byte-identical. Both give tables highlight groups only: `@markup.heading` on header cells, `@punctuation.special` on `|` and on `pipe_table_delimiter_cell`. That is exactly what the screenshot shows -- bold header, dim pipes. Nothing is missing or unapplied.

The query layer cannot express alignment even in principle. Highlight queries set only `conceal`, `conceal_lines`, `priority`, `url`, `spell` (`:h treesitter-highlight-conceal`). There is no virtual-text or padding directive, and `conceal` uses only the first character of its string, so a query can hide a range or swap one character -- never widen a cell. Alignment means adding display cells. No upstream change to tree-sitter-markdown or to Neovim's runtime queries could deliver it without a new Neovim capability (query-driven virtual text). Ceiling of a pure-query fix: `|` redrawn as a box-drawing character, still unaligned.

Not louiselm-specific. No Markdown renderer is active: `render-markdown.nvim` sits in `pack/core/opt` and in `nvim-pack-lock.json` (src `file:///home/lotso/code/render-markdown.nvim`, local commit c918864 on 8.13.0) but is off `runtimepath` and unloaded in the live instance, and nothing in `~/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/` requires it. A plain `filetype=markdown` buffer in this config shows the same raw pipes.

One acceptance bullet IS a treesitter-layer one-liner: `vim.treesitter.language.register("markdown", "louiselm-session")` makes bare `vim.treesitter.get_parser(buf)` resolve markdown with the filetype unchanged. Verified.

Measurements from prototyping, so the next attempt does not rediscover them:
- Extmark `conceal` over a range does not reclaim the screen rows a long line wraps into. A 64-column line in a 40-column window still occupies 2 screen rows when fully concealed; `nvim_win_text_height` returns `all = 2` before and after. Conceal-based column truncation therefore leaves a blank phantom row under every source line wider than the window -- exactly the rows that need truncating.
- `conceal_lines` does reclaim those rows, but `virt_lines` on a concealed line are hidden too, on any extmark, not just the one carrying `conceal_lines`. Replacement lines must anchor to a visible line outside the table, so a table scrolled half out of view disappears entirely unless rendering is skipped when its anchor leaves the viewport.
- `vim.wo[win][0].conceallevel` scopes to the buffer within that window and reverts for other buffers, so the option can be set without leaking into the user's other files.

Conclusion: everything upstream behaves as designed. Any fix is louiselm-side extmarks, or the plugin route under louiselm-zvap.

title: Grill-me needed: should louiselm adopt or integrate a sandboxed execution environment such as nono?
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing -- it wants full attention.**

## Question

How should louiselm think about sandboxed execution environments for agents, and should it evaluate or integrate a provider such as nono rather than treating sandboxing only as an abstract capability in its own policy model?

## Trigger and sources

A pull request discussion mentioned [nono](https://nono.sh/docs/core/overview), whose Rust core library exposes capability-based filesystem/network controls, OS-level enforcement via Landlock on Linux and Seatbelt on macOS, and C FFI. The project homepage describes it as created by the team behind Sigstore; the relationship should be verified rather than assumed to mean that nono has Sigstore project governance or guarantees.

- nono core overview: https://nono.sh/docs/core/overview
- nono project: https://nono.sh/
- nono source: https://github.com/nolabs-ai/nono
- Existing louiselm security feature: `louiselm-qbr.5.1` (capability envelopes and verified isolation)

## Threads worth pulling

- Compare nono with the existing generic isolation model: what can be represented as an attested enforcement boundary, and what remains provider-specific?
- Decide whether louiselm should integrate a Rust/FFI sandbox, launch agents through an external sandbox, define a provider-neutral adapter, or keep sandboxing outside louiselm. Do not add an abstraction merely because one implementation exists.
- Examine whether process-level Landlock/Seatbelt confinement is sufficient for louiselm’s threat model, especially network mediation, credentials/phantom-token patterns, subprocess inheritance, writable workspaces, `/tmp`, symlinks, and host-side tools.
- Determine the minimum evidence required before trusting a sandbox provider: kernel/OS prerequisites, fail-closed behavior, policy coverage, escape resistance, lifecycle/cancellation behavior, auditability, version/provenance, and tests against adversarial agents.
- Clarify whether a sandbox should narrow capability authorization only, or also be required before unattended execution; preserve the principle that a sandbox is not authority by itself.
- Check project maturity, governance, security history, and maintenance before making a dependency or product commitment.

## Desired outcome

A short design decision recorded in beads answering whether sandboxed environments belong in louiselm’s trusted enforcement boundary, whether nono is a candidate worth a spike, and what concrete evidence or follow-up issue is required.

## Out of scope

Do not add a runtime dependency, Rust code, FFI, or provider integration as part of this reflection. Do not treat the “team behind Sigstore” wording as a security certification.
close_reason: live:codex/01a0635e-ae82-71d3-b910-66377e02bd07 maintainer confirmed launcher-owned confinement; routed to louiselm-d6fv.4

comments.text: Resolved by the maintainer-confirmed security design. Sandboxing is required for Verified posture and belongs behind the root-owned, Provider-neutral louiselm-launch contract. Linux system facilities, Landlock, and a pinned nono build are replaceable mechanisms; every backend/version must pass hostile conformance, including the historical user-D-Bus escape. beads_rust#436 proves native br can run inside a narrow workspace but does not authorize hostile canonical writes. Implementation is routed to louiselm-d6fv.4; the full program is louiselm-d6fv. No AGENTS.md rule is warranted before the launcher exists.
