title: QA: Codex capacity-recovery bounded probe
description:
# Manual QA — Codex capacity-error recovery (louiselm-dtwil)

Completed bounded probe, 2026-09-22. Smoke passed; capacity acceptance unavailable.
Archive into a qa-round Bead and delete scratch. No further probe queued.

## Scope and setup

Fix: 5427c1e. Active Neovim runtime resolves lifecycle.lua to the installed
package at c2d6024. Its SHA-256 matches checkout and the recorded fix:
`1a69374d91a67caea81310430a6b6dff77b5958598fa375cb8f26c5543cbee5d`.
This is installed-file evidence, not proof of a newly loaded Lua closure.
Current coordinator is the sole live Session returned by exit_verdict; no
session_failure reported. Errored/disposed Sessions are excluded by that API.
Prior normal-turn smoke is recorded in louiselm-452fq and does not close this bug.

## Status

| Case | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Installed fix available | Passed: source hash matches fixed version |
| One fresh real Codex turn | Passed: exact DTWIL-QA-READY, end_turn, remains ready |
| Real capacity error shown and Session retained | Awaiting real occurrence |
| Same Session succeeds after retry/model selection | Not run |

## One bounded manual probe

Open one fresh Codex chat using normal configured permissions. Send:
`Reply only DTWIL-QA-READY. Do not use tools.`
Report its Session ID (:LouiselmSessionId) and whether it replied or showed an
error. Do not send repeated requests to induce overload. A successful reply is
only a smoke result; it leaves capacity acceptance pending.

If a real capacity error occurs, keep that exact chat open. Expect an actionable
capacity cause and a usable Session; after inspecting the pinned error evidence,
retry once when capacity clears or select an available model in that same Session.
Send `Reply only DTWIL-QA-RECOVERED. Do not use tools.`
Human checks visible error and retained interaction. Agent checks pinned ACP
event ordering and inspect state before and after recovery.

Failure signature: generic system error hides capacity cause, adapter connection
is closed, chat becomes unusable, or a failed turn is recorded as successful.

## Evidence

Pin protocol evidence by supplied ACP ID, never by latest log. Project only
session/prompt IDs, systemError, terminal sessionFailure fields, stop reason and
exit metadata; don't dump prompts/tool payloads. Confirm schema/event order before
trusting the checker. Retained ready state plus a subsequent successful end_turn
on the same ACP Session is the recovery evidence; ordinary success alone is not.
No fault injection, forced overload, or provider traffic loop authorized.

## Cleanup and findings

No product changes or new findings. Do not close dtwil without exact live evidence;
leave it unclaimed as recorded. Dispose only the QA Session when the human is done.

## Observed result

Subject: codex/01a0c756-2d3f-7cf3-a76d-49d68e44aae7. User supplied identity.
Pinned log:
`/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a0c756-2d3f-7cf3-a76d-49d68e44aae7/log.jsonl`.
One prompt, request3 at04:18:32.634Z; concatenated agent message chunks equal
DTWIL-QA-READY; response3 end_turn at04:18:34.603Z. No RPC errors, tool calls,
systemError/sessionFailure fields, or exit records observed in this run. Live
inspect: ready,current_turn=1,no session_failure. No UI success report beyond
the supplied ID; backend/protocol smoke evidence only.

No capacity failure occurred, so neither error presentation nor same-Session
recovery was exercised. dtwil stays open/unclaimed. No repeated prompts to force
overload. QA Session retained for normal human disposal; no fixture files or
product/config changes. Lesson: normal success cannot substitute for the exact
recoverable-failure path; prior normal smoke already established the same limit.
close_reason: Bounded probe ended: normal-turn smoke passed, no capacity failure; dtwil remains open/unclaimed. live:codex/01a0c756-2d3f-7cf3-a76d-49d68e44aae7

title: Single-line tool captions run to thousands of characters and overflow rendered excerpts
description:
Once louiselm-cmr made the `<sub>` caption a single line, that line could be
enormous: the longest in a real 156-tool-call export was 7319 characters, with
6963 and 6490 behind it. Correct, and useless as a label — and actively harmful
downstream, since the blog pipeline renders excerpts of these exports through
`:TOhtml` into an iframe whose width the theme fixes and does not expose.

Filed during the QA round covering `ec19281..HEAD` rather than before the fix:
louiselm-cmr's close reason recorded this as deliberately deferred presentation
work, and the tester elected to take it immediately when the measured caption
lengths arrived. The evidence below is from the verified post-fix export.

## Observed

`/home/lotso/code/louiselm/louiselm-session-1-20260820-062145.md`, exported on
build `a6484ea`, 6384 lines, 156 tool calls:

```
longest <sub> caption lengths, characters: 7319, 6963, 6490
```

Captions of that length are whole `br create --description "$(cat <<'EOF' ...`
invocations with the entire bead body inlined.

## Symptoms

- A caption that is a wall of text rather than a label.
- In a `<pre>` rendered by TOhtml, one physical line 7319 characters wide,
  overflowing horizontally inside a fixed-width iframe.

## Root cause

Not a defect in the collapsing itself. `render_entry`
(`lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua`) interpolated the full normalized title
into the caption with no length bound, because the title's natural size is the
size of a shell command.

## Fix direction

Bound the caption; keep the payload whole. The untruncated title is already a
few lines below inside `<details>`, which is what that block is for.

Rejected: wrapping the caption across lines. That re-creates exactly the
multi-line `<sub>` element louiselm-cmr just removed.

## Acceptance

- Caption truncated at a fixed character count with an ellipsis.
- Truncation counts characters, not bytes: real titles contain em dashes and
  other multi-byte characters, and a byte-wise cut would emit invalid UTF-8.
- The full title still appears in the `<details>` payload dump.
- A title exactly at the limit is left untouched.

## Not covered

- The limit is a judgement, not a measurement; 120 characters is chosen to fit
  a conventional terminal width, not derived from the theme's iframe width.
close_reason: Fixed in 3d6557d. render_entry now passes the normalized title through truncate(), which cuts at CAPTION_TITLE_LIMIT=120 using vim.fn.strchars/strcharpart so multi-byte characters are never split, and appends an ellipsis. Tests: 'truncates an overlong title in the caption but keeps it whole in the payload' (400 x's -> 120 + ellipsis in the caption, full 400 still present in the <details> dump), 'truncates on character boundaries, not bytes' (400 e-acutes), 'leaves a title at the limit untouched' (exactly 120, no ellipsis). First two confirmed red before the fix; the third was green already and is a boundary guard against an off-by-one. Gates: mini.test 0 fails/0 notes across the full suite, stylua clean on both changed files, lua-language-server unchanged at 9 pre-existing problems all in blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua. No deviation from the filed acceptance criteria. Tester re-export verification still pending.

title: Clicking winbar limits replaces chat with normal buffer
description:
Clicking the account-limits segment in the chat winbar opens `louiselm://limits/<agent>` as the current normal buffer instead of a disposable floating inspector, so it replaces the chat view and has no `q` close mapping.

## Observed

Seen in the live louiselm.nvim workspace on 2026-09-07. The existing winbar regression in `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` calls `chat:winbar_click(99)` and observes the limits buffer become the current buffer.

Relevant implementation:
- `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4004-4010` calls `Limits.open()` from `Chat:show_limits()`.
- `lua/louiselm/ui/limits.lua:326-342` creates a scratch buffer and calls `nvim.api.nvim_set_current_buf(buffer)`; it does not call `nvim_open_win` or map `q`/`<Esc>`.
- The sibling tool inspector at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1351-1368` opens a rounded floating window and maps `q`/`<Esc>`.

## Symptoms

- Clicking limits visibly replaces the chat buffer in the current window.
- There is no floating border and no `q` close behavior.
- The requested inspector interaction is unavailable.

## Root cause

`Limits.open()` implements a normal-buffer view rather than the established floating inspector boundary.

## Why it was not caught

The existing test only checks the limits buffer name and rendered content after the click; it does not assert the containing window is floating or that `q` closes it.

## Fix direction

Make `Limits.open()` create and focus a rounded editor-relative floating window using the existing tool-inspector dimensions, and install buffer-local `q`/`<Esc>` mappings that delete the scratch buffer. Keep the existing limits refresh/update lifecycle intact.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.
- Clicking the winbar limits target leaves the chat window in place and opens the details in a floating window.
- Pressing `q` closes the limits inspector and returns to the chat window.

## Not covered

The command-based `:LouiselmLimits` entry point should use the same floating presentation because it shares `Chat:show_limits()`, but broader layout styling is out of scope.
close_reason: Fixed. Limits.open now uses the shared editor-relative rounded float pattern and q/Esc cleanup. Tests: focused chat winbar regression, ui/limits_spec.lua, command limits case. Checks: stylua and lua-language-server clean. consumer:lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4008

description:
The skills-core CI Test step fails three bootstrap integration tests, skipping documentation and privileged conformance.

Observed: 2026-09-06, main 1e2c822ff4ca8e41a4e1c76ae1dab206e8025899, Ubuntu 24.04.4, Rust 1.97.1. Run 34051565904/job 101536008049: https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/34051565904/job/101536008049
Retrieve: gh run view 34051565904 --repo euri10/louiselm --job 101536008049 --log-failed

Evidence: tests/bootstrap.rs:165 bootstrap_preserves_stdio_and_gate_descriptors_across_exec: left [2, 0, 0, 0, 22], right [1], Ready must precede exec channel close. At :243 bootstrap_reports_exec_failure_and_closes_transferred_channels: left [2, 0, 0, 0, 22], right [1, 2, 0, 0, 0, 2]. At :215 bootstrap_waits_for_complete_parent_release_before_exec: left [2, 0, 0, 0, 22], right [1]. Result: 5 passed; 3 failed; exit 101.

Why missed: prior local/guest validation did not reproduce hosted bootstrap environment.

Acceptance: reproduce exact failure; retain rejection of undeclared file/socket authority and declared-channel/exec-error coverage; all skills-core fmt, strict Clippy, complete tests, Rustdoc and applicable conformance gates pass. Fix directly in checkout, no PR.

Not covered: installed runtime/hardware acceptance; preserve concurrent trust/recovery edits.

title: Unicode path collisions are undetected once non-ASCII package paths are admitted
description:
`CanonicalPath::collision_key` folds ASCII case only, so it detects `SKILL.md` versus `skill.md` and nothing else. That is sufficient today because `policy_default.json` sets `paths.allow_non_ascii: false` and capture refuses any non-ASCII path outright (skills-core/src/canonical.rs, skills-core/src/policy.rs).

The moment a pinned policy sets `allow_non_ascii: true`, two distinct paths that normalize to the same NFC/NFKC form — `café.md` composed versus decomposed — enter one manifest and materialize as one file on a normalizing filesystem. Capture would publish a package whose manifest describes bytes the filesystem cannot hold.

## Fix

Fold paths through Unicode normalization before comparing collision keys. This needs a normalization table; `unicode-normalization` is the obvious crate and needs the AGENTS.md section 3 dependency approval, or an embedded table content-addressed alongside the Unicode profile.

## Until then

The default policy is the guard. Do not ship a policy with `allow_non_ascii: true` while this is open.
close_reason: Unicode normalization collisions refused before publication; original manifest bytes preserved. Lesson recorded in issue and canonical API docs. gate:skills-core/tests/capture.rs:235

comments.author: codex/01a0d1d7-884f-7af0-b55e-afd2ff22c762
comments.text: Red: canonical regression accepts café.md + cafe U+0301.md; capture regression publishes both. Shared collision_key will use NFKD then ASCII folding, preserving manifest path bytes. Runtime dependency unicode-normalization 0.1.25 supplies normalization tables (stdlib has none); exact version pinned. Full Unicode case folding remains outside this normalization fix.

comments.author: codex/01a0d1d7-884f-7af0-b55e-afd2ff22c762
comments.text: Lesson: compare NFKD + ASCII-folded keys at CanonicalPath, never rewrite signed manifest paths. Docs: skills-core/README.md and canonical.rs. Red-green proves manifest construction/parsing and capture refusal with empty store; original Unicode bytes and ASCII golden digest preserved. Passed focused tests, full skills-core suite via systemd service (existing opt-in tests ignored), fmt, strict Clippy, Rustdoc, and 13 browser tests. No installed/privileged acceptance claimed. Changes uncommitted.

title: Grill-me needed: How should LouiseLM show Codex usage limits to users?
description:
Do not resolve this design question in passing. Facilitate a dedicated decision about how LouiseLM presents Codex usage limits to users.

Question:
What user-facing representation should LouiseLM use for Codex usage limits, including multiple windows/buckets, remaining percentage, reset timing, plan information, credits, stale/loading/error states, and change notifications?

Evidence from shared conversation:
- Source: https://chatgpt.com/share/6a8bde60-0154-83eb-bea8-9389d85a2149
- The supported integration surface identified is the Codex App Server JSON-RPC method `account/rateLimits/read`, with `account/rateLimits/updated` notifications.
- The result exposes `usedPercent`, `windowDurationMins`, `resetsAt`, `planType`, and possibly `rateLimitResetCredits` and additional/model-specific buckets.
- `usedPercent` is consumed usage, while the UI needs to decide whether to show remaining usage (`100 - usedPercent`), consumed usage, or both.
- Window meaning must come from `windowDurationMins`; do not assume primary means five hours or secondary means weekly.
- The private `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/usage` endpoint exists behind the ChatGPT UI, but should not be used as LouiseLM’s integration contract; HTML scraping is overkill and brittle.

Threads worth pulling:
- Which buckets belong in the default view, and how should arbitrary/additional buckets be labeled?
- Should the primary metric be remaining percentage, used percentage, absolute counts/credits, reset-at time, or a combination?
- How should weekly and shorter windows be made understandable without hard-coded names?
- Where should this appear in the Neovim UI, and should it be on-demand, persistent, or both?
- How should live updates, sparse/partial notifications, stale data, unavailable auth, malformed data, and app-server errors be communicated?
- What behavior is safe when no limits are returned or when credits are present?
- Which exact observable contract should tests and typed events enforce?

Decision boundary:
Choose the presentation and state semantics only. Keep the supported App Server transport and protocol choice as established evidence unless new evidence shows it cannot support the chosen UX.
close_reason: Human UX presentation and state semantics decided with maintainer confirmation; implementation boundary routed separately.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: 2026-08-24 investigation: Official Codex App Server docs define account/rateLimits/read plus account/rateLimits/updated. The result can carry a legacy rateLimits bucket and rateLimitsByLimitId; buckets may have absent labels, optional primary/secondary windows, plan type, credits, and reset-credit metadata. Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server. A sanitized probe against installed codex-cli 0.144.3 returned both legacy data and one codex multi-bucket entry: unlabeled, primary 10080-minute window, no secondary window, with plan/credits and reset-credit metadata. No percentages, timestamps, or account identity were retained. Architectural boundary: installed @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.2 receives account/rateLimits/updated and caches structured buckets internally, but exposes them only as rendered /status text; it does not emit a structured ACP session update. Therefore limits are account/Agent state, not LouiseLM Session telemetry, and implementation needs a structured adapter boundary rather than parsing /status text or duplicating a direct provider process inside every Session.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: Grill direction from maintainer: treat human UX and agent experience (AX, including AGENTS.md conventions) as two distinct formats/contracts. Resolve UX first; revisit AX later. Primary human motivation is deciding whether to continue/cancel work as limits approach. Design implication under canonical vocabulary: a user cancels a running turn or refrains from the next prompt; the Session remains resumable. Moving work to another Agent is a Handoff that creates another Session. Current UX recommendation: an always-visible compact decision signal plus an on-demand detailed view, rather than warning-only display. Human questions to answer: whether it is safe to start/continue a task; which Agent to choose or hand off to; when work can resume after reset; whether a failure is quota-related; and whether a reset credit or workspace-owner action is available. Do not estimate remaining prompts because usage cost varies by task/model and the protocol does not provide that forecast.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: UX decision accepted: emit at most one human notification per quota window/reset cycle when remaining capacity crosses 20 percent, then 10 percent, then when the server classifies the limit as reached. Each notification identifies the Agent, affected window, remaining capacity, and reset timing. The UX must not automatically cancel a turn or initiate a Handoff.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: UX state policy accepted: initial fetch is loading; fresh data renders normally; refresh failure preserves the last good snapshot with visible staleness age; passing a reset timestamp without a confirmed refresh also makes the snapshot stale rather than synthesizing a reset. Initial failure is unavailable with details. A successful empty result is no limit data, never unlimited; unlimited is displayed only from an explicit upstream value. Valid sparse updates merge into the snapshot. Malformed updates are rejected, the last good snapshot is preserved and marked stale. Stale data never triggers threshold notifications. Agents without the capability omit the compact segment and explain unsupported in the detailed view; unexpected failures from supporting Agents remain visible.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: UX bucket/window policy accepted: deduplicate the legacy bucket against rateLimitsByLimitId by limitId and treat its matching entry as the default bucket. Prefer non-empty upstream limitName; otherwise render the exact limitId without invented semantics. Derive window labels from exact windowDurationMins and never expose primary/secondary as meanings. Sort windows shortest to longest. The normal winbar shows default-bucket windows; a low, critical, or reached additional bucket takes precedence. Show at most two windows plus +N in the winbar; detailed view shows all. Winbar reset timing is relative; detail includes relative and local absolute time. Render whole remaining percentages, except positive values below one percent render as <1%.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: UX interaction scope accepted: :LouiselmLimits shows the active Agent, :LouiselmLimits <agent> inspects another configured Agent, and clicking the winbar segment opens the same detail view. Opening refreshes only through an already-live Agent connection; it never starts an Agent merely to fetch limits. Otherwise show last-known or not observed. Detail shows reset-credit count and expiry, and reached state advertises reset availability. The first UX is read-only: no credit consumption, owner email, turn cancellation, or Handoff.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: Final UX contract: account limits are shared Agent-level state with two human formats: an always-visible decision-oriented winbar segment and a read-only :LouiselmLimits [agent] detail view. Remaining capacity is primary; detail also shows used capacity, exact-duration window labels, relative and absolute reset timing, plan, credits, freshness and errors. Notifications occur once per reset cycle at 20 percent, 10 percent and reached. The accepted state, bucket, ordering and interaction semantics are recorded in comments 268-271. AX is explicitly deferred and now has canonical vocabulary record louiselm-y3f3. Lesson routing: issue-local protocol and adapter evidence stays on this issue; the pure-ACP integration conflict is routed to a separate needs-design question. No additional standing AGENTS.md rule is warranted.

title: Run the manual Skill Admission ceremony with the real YubiKeys
description:
Automated tests cover the Generation chain, the state machine, the git witness protocol, and signature verification, all with software keys and real `ssh-keygen` crypto. They cannot cover a physical touch, so the FIDO assertion path — `--require-hardware`, resident `ed25519-sk` keys, `verify-required`, and the user-presence/user-verification flags the verifier enforces — has never run against hardware.

## What to run

skills-core/README.md, section 'The manual ceremony'. Five steps: enrol two resident keys on two physically separate tokens, admit and witness a Generation, verify without a token, rotate the primary with the recovery key, and confirm the replaced primary is dead.

## What to watch

Each signing step must make the token blink. A step that completes without a touch means `--require-hardware` did not reach the enrolled key: the assertion flags carried in the signature are what verification actually checks, and a software key silently satisfying a hardware role is the failure this ceremony exists to catch.

## Why it is filed rather than done

No agent in this project can touch a YubiKey.

title: LouiselmInbox crashes when a capture has a null transcript
description:
Opening `:LouiselmInbox` crashes instead of showing the durable capture inbox when a listed capture has a null transcript. This blocks operators from inspecting captures through the inbox command.

## Observed

Reported 2026-08-21 in a Neovim runtime loading `louiselm.nvim`; no reproducible capture-service payload or session identifier was available.

```text
vim.schedule callback: .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:74: attempt to index field 'transcript' (a userdata value)
stack traceback:
        .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:74: in function 'inbox_lines'
        .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:132: in function 'callback'
        ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/capture/init.lua:108: in function 'complete'
        ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/capture/init.lua:137: in function <...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/capture/init.lua:123>
```

## Symptoms

- Running `:LouiselmInbox` raises a scheduled-callback error rather than opening the inbox.
- Neovim reports `attempt to index field 'transcript' (a userdata value)`.

## Root cause

Confirmed at `lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:74`: `inbox_lines` checks only `capture.transcript ~= nil` before indexing `.text`. The traceback proves that this field can instead be userdata, which cannot be indexed. The source representation that produces that userdata (likely a decoded null) is unverified without the capture-service response.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/capture_spec.lua:171` checks only that `LouiselmInbox` is registered. It does not exercise inbox rendering with a capture whose `transcript` is a non-table null/userdata value.

## Fix direction

At the narrowest validated capture-service boundary, normalize or reject a non-table `transcript`; preserve the inbox renderer's absent-transcript behavior. Add a renderer/command regression test using the actual Neovim decoded-null representation. A simple non-nil guard is insufficient because userdata is truthy.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after for a listed capture whose `transcript` is the decoded-null/userdata value.
- `:LouiselmInbox` opens and renders that capture without a Lua error; it omits transcript text and may show the existing transcription error when present.

## Not covered

- The exact capture-service JSON payload and whether every null-capable field needs the same boundary validation are unverified.
- No fix is included in this report.
close_reason: Fixed in 35e7927. Inbox rendering now requires a table transcript with string text, so Neovim JSON null (userdata) follows the existing absent-transcript path. Regression: tests/capture_spec.lua commands opens inbox when a capture transcript is null. Gates: full MiniTest suite (322 cases), stylua --check ., lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning.

title: Physical mouse click on Session winbar source does nothing
description:
## Observed

During manual QA of build `60724f3`, in Agent Session `claude/9efb19db-aa0b-4f45-8cab-18eab9d86937`, the winbar rendered an attention source entry:

`%#LouiselmStatusReady#Your turn%*%=%1@v:lua.require('louiselm.ui.chat.command').winbar_click@%#LouiselmStatusWarning#● source%*%X`

After `:set mouse=a`, physically clicking `● source` did nothing: the active Session did not change, the cursor did not move, and `:messages` remained empty. Physical clicks on ordinary buffer lines also did not move the cursor in that environment.

Calling `require('louiselm.ui.chat.command').winbar_click(1, 1, 'l', '')` directly selected the source Session correctly, so the Session target and handler path worked while physical mouse-event delivery did not.

## Impact and disposition

Low impact and non-blocking: keyboard/direct selection remains available. Do not fix as part of the current QA round; retain this finding for reproduction in a terminal/TUI environment where the physical input path can be isolated.

## Evidence

- Agent Session: `claude/9efb19db-aa0b-4f45-8cab-18eab9d86937`
- ACP log: `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/9efb19db-aa0b-4f45-8cab-18eab9d86937/log.jsonl`
- Manual QA Case 4
- No error or notification appeared
- Root cause remains unknown; evidence is consistent with terminal/TUI mouse delivery rather than the LouiseLM click handler itself
acceptance_criteria: With mouse support enabled in a supported terminal, physically clicking a Session entry in the winbar selects that Session exactly as keyboard selection and direct winbar_click invocation do; behavioral coverage distinguishes click-event delivery from direct handler invocation, or the unsupported environment is detected and communicated.
close_reason: Completed: routes clicked Winbar window correctly; live environment has no generic mouse delivery and is documented as unsupported.

Regression coverage fails against current-window lookup and passes for a click originating in another window; command-level coverage verifies forwarding the mouse window. Full mini.test: 505/505; Stylua and lua-language-server pass. Live Ghostty acceptance remains pending a physical click, so this bug intentionally stays in_progress.

description:
# Manual QA — fresh Codex startup

Completed bounded round, 2026-09-15. Human drove Neovim; assistant collected

## Scope and build

- Subject: louiselm-dtwil, P2, fresh Codex Session errors before its first reply.

  reproduced; no repeated-run reliability claim or root-cause fix follows.
- No permission-policy change is needed for this reply-only case.
- Database read access is restored. F1 is filed as louiselm-j5meh.
  Normal br show reads louiselm-dtwil again. Startup bug remains open with this
  coordinator's QA claim released after recording the result.

## Status

| Case | State |
| --- | --- |
| Evidence checker against recorded successful and failed Sessions | Passed: true/true for success; false/false for original failure |
| 1. Fresh Codex first reply | Passed protocol/state check: exact marker, end_turn, ready; original failure not reproduced |
| F1. Beads issue inspection | CLI access restored; hidden error cause filed as louiselm-j5meh; UI fix deferred |

## Current Session baseline

Live API snapshot before the new fixture:
- Claude session-5 / 467c4e1a-0583-4cc1-96d7-df1797b263b7: ready, new, current_turn 2.
- This Codex session-6 / 01a0a4c3-d513-7363-acd2-ce29762dfa73: prompting, new, current_turn 2.

This snapshot uses session.exit_verdict(), which excludes errored and disposed
Sessions. It is a baseline of live Sessions, not an inventory of failed ones.
For a failed new fixture, the human supplies its exact :LouiselmSessionId.

## Case 1 — first reply in a fresh Codex Session

Exercises the real configured Codex Agent, ACP process/protocol lifecycle and
chat error presentation; tests using the mock Agent cannot establish this.

1. Run :LouiselmSessionNew and select codex.
2. Send exactly: Reply only ATTENTION-QA-READY
3. Wait for completion or an error. Leave that new Session open.
4. Run :LouiselmSessionId in that new Session; return here with the copied ID
   and whether the marker appeared, an error appeared, or it kept waiting.

Expected: assistant displays ATTENTION-QA-READY, the prompt completes with
end_turn, and the Session becomes ready.

Failure signature: "Codex agent reported a system error for this turn",
a missing completed assistant marker, or a Session that remains busy.

The assistant pins the returned ACP ID and inspects only that Session's log
and state. Do not Park, load, close, or submit another prompt in the fixture
until its first-turn evidence is collected.

### Result

User identified codex/01a0a4d0-d492-7ee3-9c86-f42843f5041b.
Pinned log: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a0a4d0-d492-7ee3-9c86-f42843f5041b/log.jsonl.
First and only prompt request 4 at 2026-09-15T11:26:27.395Z; response at
11:26:30.927Z (3.532 seconds), stopReason=end_turn, no response error.
Assistant chunks concatenate to the exact ATTENTION-QA-READY marker.
Live state: local session-7, agent codex, source new, ready, current_turn 1,
loadSession supported. Human supplied the Session ID without a separate visual
report; protocol/state success does not assert focus or layout acceptance.
Chat buffer 231 (louiselm://session-7) contains one exact marker line and zero
lines matching the previously reported Codex system error.

No Codex code or configuration changed. The original exit137 source remains
unknown. One earlier retry plus this run passing does not close louiselm-dtwil.

the same failure recurs and retain its exact Session evidence.

## Evidence checker

Run the following with the exact Session log path as its final argument.
It selects the first prompt and matching response, concatenates assistant text
chunks only within that turn, and excludes later loadSession replay.

```sh
jq -s --arg marker ATTENTION-QA-READY '
  ([.[] | select(.direction == "client_to_agent" and .payload.method == "session/prompt")][0]) as $p |
  ([.[] | select(.direction == "agent_to_client" and .payload.id == $p.payload.id and (.payload.result != null or .payload.error != null))][0]) as $r |
  {session_id:$p.session_id, request_id:$p.payload.id, completed:($r.payload.result.stopReason == "end_turn"),
   marker_matches: (([.[] | select(.direction == "agent_to_client" and .timestamp >= $p.timestamp and ($r == null or .timestamp <= $r.timestamp) and .payload.method == "session/update" and .payload.params.update.sessionUpdate == "agent_message_chunk") | .payload.params.update.content.text // ""] | join("") | gsub("^\\s+|\\s+$"; "")) == $marker)}
' /absolute/path/to/exact/session/log.jsonl
```

log establishes protocol completion and assistant output, not focus or layout.

title: Grill-me needed: how should host conformance evidence gate Verified launch?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; use a focused grill-me session before designing admission evidence.

The d6fv.4.8 hostile suite establishes reproducible build/host conformance, but how does a production launch prove that its exact backend, kernel and policy passed it? sandbox.rs:1304 currently claims launches without a passing conformance report are refused; the actual evidence method records mechanism booleans and no report is read. isolation.rs checks dimension completeness, not provenance of a host conformance run. The old acceptance audit already warned against treating those booleans as hostile observations; the new suite and CI gate do not silently create a runtime attestation protocol.

Threads: authority that runs and accepts conformance; binding to release/backend/kernel/configuration; rerun/invalidation triggers; failure and stale/missing report behavior; integrity/storage and launch-receipt linkage; separation of component CI from installed authority and end-to-end Verified posture. d6fv.9 is the only consumer allowed to activate the user-visible claim. No new daemon, report format, signing role or per-Session hostile test execution is authorized by the test implementation alone.
design:
Confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-09-11 after a focused louiselm-grill-me interview.
Source Session: codex/01a09171-93e0-7b53-9c29-ce2a0465bb92.
The maintainer explicitly confirmed the final design summary and Beads routing.

## Confirmed design

1. Host certification is an explicit maintenance command under the installed launcher's existing privileged authority. It tests the actual host. It may be automated by an installation/update workflow, but a Session launch never automatically starts certification.
2. Exercise the installed launcher with test-owned files, identities, processes and isolated endpoints. Leave unrelated workloads and host-wide settings untouched. Harmless sentinels stand in for forbidden resources. Required checks cannot silently skip; inability to run within these limits yields incomplete certification.
3. Evidence is bound to the current boot, relevant host measurements and exact launcher, sandbox backend, conformance suite, policy, required runtime-library and loader-configuration inputs. Use a bounded explicit dependency list; required inputs must be measurable. Changed relevant inputs invalidate certification. Version strings alone are insufficient.
4. The existing Launch supervisor checks validity every second. A detected mismatch triggers suspension; five seconds without a successful validity check also triggers suspension. Validate these deadlines under load. Sampling is not instantaneous detection, continuous proof of containment or a hard real-time guarantee.
5. Current passing evidence makes a Session eligible for Verified launch, subject to every other required check. Missing, stale or incomplete evidence allows only an explicit Session-scoped interactive waiver, displaying isolation as unverified; unattended Runs remain blocked. Mandatory launch checks still apply.
6. Observed containment failure is non-waivable and blocks affected launches. An interrupted run or unavailable test tool does not itself prove broken containment and cannot erase an earlier failure. Missing mandatory containment capability still blocks launch.
7. Recorded containment failures persist across reboot, upgrade and report expiry until successful recertification covers the failed boundary. Failure state is independent of certificate currency; stale evidence must not convert a known failure into a waivable absence.
8. If a running Verified Session loses valid/readable evidence, revoke brokered capabilities and freeze the affected process tree. If freezing cannot be confirmed, attempt full termination. Unconfirmed cleanup remains an unresolved failure. Existing interactive waivers cover only their approved condition, never a new containment failure.
9. Recovery always requires an explicit operator action; recertification alone never resumes work or restores capabilities. Evidence-only suspension permits resume after revalidation and fresh authorization. Actual containment failure requires diagnostic-evidence preservation, disposal of affected process trees and fresh Sessions after recertification.
10. Installing a new release need not interrupt existing Sessions whose pinned software, host measurements and governing policy remain valid and whose old release remains approved. The new release needs its own certification. Invalidated evidence or release revocation suspends affected Sessions.
11. Each signed launch receipt binds the exact conformance report used for admission. The launcher protects the report and the Control broker retains its exact bytes for inspection. A waived Session records the actual evidence status and its explicit waiver, never an invented passing result.
12. Remove library_baseline and isolation_policy_version from both registration and RuntimeMeasurement. Receipts identify the policy actually enforced and bind actual measurement/conformance evidence. The existing louiselm-etth bug owns that correction.

## Routing and acceptance boundary

Create a P1 implementation feature under louiselm-d6fv and make it block louiselm-d6fv.9. Keep louiselm-etth open with the chosen fix. The feature carries implementation acceptance; the design decision alone enables no Verified claim. Existing required gates and installed maintainer acceptance still apply; louiselm-d6fv.9 remains the only end-to-end cutover consumer.

Lesson destination: this design record, the implementing feature's acceptance, and the selected fix on louiselm-etth. No additional standing instruction is warranted.

Vocabulary delta: No change.

title: Inspectable and exportable Forensics
description:
## Problem Statement
Forensics persists bounded pointers, but an operator cannot tell which primary evidence remains available or intentionally prepare safe evidence for external sharing.

## Solution
Show current availability for indexed evidence and support an explicit Evidence export artifact without changing Forensics into a raw-evidence store.

## User Stories
1. As an operator, I can see which Forensics evidence properties remain available before relying on them.
2. As an operator, I can explicitly create a bounded redacted artifact for an external issue without publishing raw ACP data by default.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Inspecting a Forensics record reports current evidence availability without mutating its immutable record.
2. Export is an explicit bounded redaction step and is distinct from Forensics collection.

## Out of Scope
Copying whole ACP logs into Forensics or automatically publishing evidence.

title: Grill fold-based tool-call rendering UX
description:
## Question

Would native Neovim folds make LouiseLM's chronological tool-call timeline less cluttered without hiding active work, failures, or permission decisions?

## Scope

- Explore fold behavior separately for active versus completed calls.
- Decide whether adjacent calls should be grouped and what summary information remains visible.
- Cover failed calls, cancelled calls, permission prompts, nested/repeated calls, default open/closed state, discoverability, keyboard behavior, and mobile/narrow-window equivalents where relevant.
- Compare the proposal against the current one-line started-to-completed renderer.
- Prefer native Neovim behavior and the smallest viable design; do not assume a generic fold framework shared with prompt contexts.

## Desired Outcome

A grill-tested UX decision with concrete states, examples, accessibility/discoverability considerations, and—only if implementation is justified—small follow-up beads with acceptance criteria.

## Out of Scope

Implementing tool folds as part of the Agent Skills profile feature. This question has no dependency on that feature.
close_reason: Completed: grill decision recorded; louiselm-ufx.1 and louiselm-ufx.2 are closed and shipped.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
Grill-me session reached full agreement. Decision: fold-based rendering, scoped to within-turn clutter only.

- Fold unit = contiguous run of `completed` tool-call lines; any active, failed, or cancelled call breaks the run and is always rendered as a standalone visible line (never folded, never flagged-then-hidden).
- Trigger = superseded, mid-turn: a run folds the moment something follows it (new tool-call run, resumed assistant text, or `turn_done` as a force-close catch-all for a trailing run).
- Foldtext = Neovim default (first line + native line count), no custom renderer.
- Discoverability/keyboard = fully native (za/zo/zc/zR/zM), no new keymaps or foldcolumn.
- New fold state is separate from `context_folds` (different trigger/lifecycle) but mirrors its pattern (manual foldmethod, per-window tracking).
- Permission decisions are out of scope: they never render inline in the transcript today.
- Separately decided: live raw ACP payload access becomes on-demand only (not inline/folded) -- a new command/keymap on a `[tool]` line, decoupled from the fold mechanism.

Implementation split into louiselm-ufx.1 (fold rendering) and louiselm-ufx.2 (on-demand raw-payload inspector). Leaving this question open until both land -- br policy blocks closing a parent with open children, and that's the right call here since the decision is made but the work is not done.

title: Fold completed tool-call runs in the chat transcript
description:
## Goal
Reduce transcript clutter from many tool calls within one turn by folding contiguous runs of completed tool-call lines, using native Neovim folds.

## Scope
- In scope: new fold-tracking state in `louiselm.ui.chat` (separate from `context_folds`/`fold_counts`, same pattern: `foldmethod=manual`, `foldenable=true`, per-window fold-count tracking), applied in `handle_event`.
- A "run" is a contiguous stretch of tool-call lines whose terminal status is `completed` (see `lifecycle.lua:197`: `tool_call_finished` is only ever `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`).
- An active (started, not yet finished) or `failed`/`cancelled` call breaks the run and is never itself folded -- always a standalone visible line.
- Fold trigger is "superseded": a completed run folds the moment something follows it -- a new `tool_call_started` begins a new run, an assistant `chunk` resumes text, or `turn_done` fires (force-close catch-all so a trailing run is never left open across a turn boundary).
- Foldtext: Neovim's default only (first line of range + native line count). No custom `foldtext`.
- No new keymaps, no `foldcolumn` changes -- native `za`/`zo`/`zc`/`zR`/`zM` only.
- Out of scope: cross-session/history folding beyond one turn, folding or flagging failed/cancelled calls, any change to permission-decision UI, any inline raw-payload rendering (separate task).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A turn with 3+ consecutive `completed` tool calls followed by assistant text: the calls collapse into one native fold as soon as the text starts.
2. A turn ending on tool calls (no trailing text) still has the trailing run folded once `turn_done` fires.
3. A `failed` or `cancelled` call in the middle of an otherwise-successful sequence is never folded and splits the sequence into separate runs around it.
4. An active (not-yet-finished) call is never included in a fold.
5. Resuming/loading a session replays through the same `handle_event` path and produces the same fold behavior with no special-casing.
6. No custom foldtext or keymap is added; behavior relies entirely on Neovim defaults and existing fold commands.
7. Fold state is tracked per-window, mirroring `context_folds`/`fold_counts`'s existing per-window tracking, but in its own separate table (not reusing `context_folds`).

## Testing
- Headless `mini.test` coverage: run-to-fold assertions (e.g. via `foldclosed()`/`nvim_buf_call`), covering: multi-call successful run + supersede-by-text, trailing run + turn_done, failure-breaks-run, active-call-not-folded, resume/replay parity.

## Notes
- Decision reached via a grill-me session recorded on louiselm-ufx; this task implements the fold-rendering half of that decision.
- Related, decoupled work: on-demand raw payload inspection is a separate task -- do not couple its implementation to this one.
close_reason: Implemented native folding for contiguous completed tool-call runs with turn-end and failure/active boundary tests

title: On-demand raw ACP payload inspector for a tool-call line
description:
## Goal
Let the user inspect a tool call's full raw ACP payload live, on demand, without adding it to the always-visible transcript.

## Scope
- In scope: a command and/or keymap, invoked with the cursor on a `[tool] ...` line, that resolves that line's tool-call id and opens its merged raw fields (everything `session/transcript.lua`'s `merge_tool_call` already accumulates for markdown export -- title, status, and whatever else the agent sent) in a scratch or floating buffer.
- `handle_event` in `ui/chat/init.lua` currently only reads `status`/`title` off each event and discards the rest live; this task needs the merged raw payload available live, not just at export time -- reuse or adapt the accumulation approach already used by `louiselm.session.transcript`'s `merge_tool_call`/`open_tool_calls`, without duplicating the export pipeline.
- Out of scope: any inline/always-visible rendering, any change to the one-line tool-call renderer, any change to `:LouiselmToMarkdown` or `session/transcript_export.lua`.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Invoking the new command/keymap with the cursor on a finished tool-call's line shows that call's full merged raw payload (not just title/status).
2. Invoking it on an active (not-yet-finished) call's line shows whatever fields have arrived so far (partial payload), not an error.
3. Invoking it off a `[tool]` line is a no-op or clear error, not a crash.
4. Nothing changes about the default transcript rendering -- no new lines appear until the command is explicitly invoked.
5. The scratch/float buffer is disposable (closes without side effects on the session).

## Testing
- Headless `mini.test` coverage: invoke the command against a view with a known tool-call id and assert the opened buffer's content matches the merged raw payload; cover both a finished and a still-active call.

## Notes
- Decision reached via a grill-me session recorded on louiselm-ufx; this task implements the on-demand-inspection half of that decision, deliberately decoupled from the fold-rendering task (louiselm-ufx.1).
close_reason: Added LouiselmInspectTool raw-payload float with finished/active/off-line coverage

title: Allow handoff from Error sessions
description:
## Evidence

A Session whose ACP turn fails enters status=error. LouiselmHandoff calls Chat:hand_off(), which currently rejects every status other than ready with the active-turn error. LouiselmCancel cannot clear an error Session because Session:cancel() only accepts prompting, waiting_permission, or cancelling. The resulting Session is stranded: it cannot be cancelled and its transcript cannot be handed off.

## Acceptance

- A terminal error Session can open a reviewed Handoff to another Agent.
- Prompting, waiting_permission, cancelling, and queued prompts remain rejected.
- Add regression coverage for the error-state handoff path.
- Preserve the source Session and its transcript.
close_reason: Implemented terminal error-state handoff and regression coverage; focused and full suites pass.

comments.author: claude/0929f4e1-c8f2-4717-998f-1902618ce5f8
comments.text: Lesson: handoff eligibility must distinguish terminal Session states from active-turn states. `error` is terminal and retains the source transcript, while `prompting`, `waiting_permission`, and `cancelling` still require cancellation/completion. The fix belongs in Chat:hand_off(), the shared UI boundary, and does not change Session:cancel().

title: Unsupported account limits vanish silently from the winbar
description:
## Problem

`lua/louiselm/ui/limits.lua:110` returns `nil, nil` for both `unsupported` and
`not_observed`, so the limits block is simply absent from the winbar. Absence
is indistinguishable from "this Agent has limits and they are fine".

That matters more now that `unsupported` is a **correct terminal state** for
some Agents rather than a temporary gap
(louiselm-account-limits-9n9st, louiselm-opencode-account-limits-9350). A user
on OpenCode or a stock adapter sees nothing and has no way to learn why.

Silent absence is also what invites the mistake the new AGENTS.md rule exists
to prevent: an invisible gap reads as a bug, and the next session goes looking
for an endpoint to fill it.

## Fix direction, not prescription

Make the state legible without adding noise to every Agent that has no limits
concept. Open questions the implementer should settle with evidence, not
assumption:

- Should `unsupported` differ visually from `not_observed`? They mean
  different things: the Agent cannot report, versus nothing observed yet.
- Does this belong in the winbar at every width, or does it fold early like
  cost and context already do? Reserved space for background attention is
  already a constraint there.
- `:LouiselmLimits` and `:checkhealth louiselm` are the places a user asks
  deliberately. A brief winbar marker plus a real explanation in those may
  beat a verbose winbar.

## Acceptance

1. A user on an Agent that does not advertise the extension can tell that
   limits are unavailable rather than fine.
2. `unsupported` and `not_observed` remain distinguishable somewhere a user
   can reach.
3. Agents that do report limits are unchanged.
4. Narrow-width folding behavior stays correct; no regression in the existing
   winbar width tests.

## Context

Decision: louiselm-opencode-quota-runtime-ownership-blz13.

title: QA: Session overview sidebar focus and navigation
description:
# Manual QA — Session overview sidebar

Scratch working record; archive final results in a Beads QA-round chore and
remove this file afterward. Do not commit it as a second source of truth.

## Build and scope

- Original tested plugin: `e81229f`, including sidebar change `41c3422`.
- Fix under retest: `0c674ff`, closes the sidebar on another Session's focus.
  Installed checkout advanced to this build and chat code matches tested bytes;
  the existing Neovim keeps
  its old loaded modules until restart. Resume this coordinator conversation
  with `:LouiselmResume` after restart, then resume QA-Overview for the retest.
- Installed `lua/louiselm/ui/session_overview.lua` matches workspace bytes.
  Live `:LouiselmSessionOverview` and `<leader>sO` mapping are present.
- Implementation issue `louiselm-7km1j` awaits live acceptance. This independent
  QA round does not reclaim or alter its existing assignment. Liveness check
  classified its prior claim abandoned_likely, expired reservation, no unresolved
  holder; no takeover is needed to inspect the committed installed behavior.
- Prior round `louiselm-u5q2l` covered file counts before the sidebar change.
  This round targets layout, focus, reuse, navigation and invoking-Session scope.
- Baseline: one tab, one ordinary chat window 1000, width 190, coordinator
  `codex/01a0a37b-8369-7211-b930-d4082a8f035a`. No overview window is open.
- Isolated fixture directory created: `/tmp/louiselm-overview-qa.rxFCcB`.
  `probe.txt` does not exist yet. Only the fresh QA Agent should create it.

Keep existing permission settings; an approval dialog is not required. Restart
Neovim once to load fix `0c674ff`, then resume this conversation and QA-Overview.
Do not hot-patch loaded modules or dispose Sessions programmatically. No new
dependencies or Android/service changes are involved.

## Status

| Case | State | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Open/reuse empty sidebar in current tab | Passed | User confirms command opening and reuse without a second sidebar. Live snapshot confirmed one tab, a left overview window and retained chat. QA-Overview `codex/01a0a3c4-ebde-73c1-a165-9e1b5543bf63`. |
| 2. Live file update, diff preview and file navigation | Passed | User confirms the live update, diff/file navigation and that the file remains open. Fixture `probe.txt` contains `sidebar-one` plus newline; sidebar showed [new] (+1 -0). Keeping the file open is expected; only switching Sessions closes the sidebar. |
| 3. Invoking Session, focus and clean closure | Passed live on `0c674ff` | Sidebar appears only in QA-Overview and closes on switching to another Session. Ordinary file navigation leaves the file open. |

## 1. Open/reuse empty sidebar

Goal: current Session's overview opens as a sidebar without moving its chat
into a new tab. Exercises `41c3422`, `session_overview.open` and command wiring.

1. Run `:LouiselmSessionNew`, choose `codex`, wait until ready, and rename the
   new Session **QA-Overview**. Do not send a prompt yet.
2. From that chat press Escape explicitly, then run `:LouiselmSessionOverview`.
   Test the shortcut separately after command success: in Normal mode press
   Space, s, Shift+o without pausing beyond the configured 300 ms mapping timeout.
3. Expect one narrow left sidebar for QA-Overview, zero modified files, the
   chat still visible, and no new tab. Report this checkpoint; leave it open.
4. After evidence is collected, run `:LouiselmSessionOverview` once more while
   the sidebar is focused. Expect reuse of the same sidebar, not another
   window or tab, and the same subject. Report before moving on.

Failure: a new tab appears, multiple sidebars accumulate, the chat disappears,
older Sessions' edits appear in the fresh overview, or the focused sidebar
changes its subject unexpectedly.

Evidence: compare tab/window IDs before and after, sidebar filetype
`louiselm_overview`, width and position, subject header and zero-file summary.
Human observation establishes readability and intended focus. API inventory
alone does not establish visual quality.

## 2. Live update, preview and navigation

Goal: a real ACP edit reaches the open sidebar and navigation preserves chat.
Exercises history collection, scheduled refresh, preview and jump-to-file.

1. From the sidebar press `s` to focus its Session chat. Send exactly:

   > Use apply_patch to create /tmp/louiselm-overview-qa.rxFCcB/probe.txt containing exactly sidebar-one followed by one newline. Do not edit any other files or run other commands.

2. After completion, inspect the still-open sidebar. Expect that one fixture,
   marked new, and +1/-0. Report before navigation; the assistant verifies the
   actual edit tool and bytes. Shell redirection instead of apply_patch is a
   recipe deviation to inspect, not proof of an overview defect.
3. Focus the fixture row in the sidebar and press `d`. Expect a floating diff
   preview, with sidebar and chat preserved underneath. Close the preview with
   `:close` in its floating window; do not close the chat.
4. In the sidebar, press Enter on the fixture row. Expect the file at line 1
   in an ordinary editing window, with chat and sidebar still available.
5. Return to the sidebar and press `r` twice. Counts must remain unchanged.

Failure: no edit row, wrong file or counts, blank/wrong diff, preview replaces
chat, Enter replaces chat, wrong line, or refresh increases accumulated counts.

Evidence: pin the QA ACP ID, verify completed diff content for the fixture,
and compare exact file bytes via `od -An -tc` or `wc -l`. Inspect window types,
buffer identity and cursor position before/after navigation. Current disk
contents do not independently prove attribution or displayed diff history.

## 3. Invoking Session, focus and closure

Goal: sidebar closes when another Session gains focus, without affecting its
ordinary file/diff navigation. Exercises shared view entry and window disposal.

1. With QA-Overview and its sidebar still available, use
   `:LouiselmSessionSwitch` to return to this coordinator conversation.
2. The QA-Overview sidebar should close as soon as the coordinator is focused.
   Report that checkpoint before invoking any overview command here.
3. Switch back to QA-Overview. Its sidebar must remain closed until explicitly
   reopened. Run `:LouiselmSessionOverview`; expect its own file history.
4. Press `s` to focus QA-Overview's own chat; its sidebar must remain open.
   Complete case 2's preview/file navigation on this build as well. If both
   chats are visible in separate windows, focusing the other chat should close
   the sidebar just as using the Session switcher does.
5. Focus the sidebar and press `q`. Expect it to disappear without closing the
   Session or file window. Reopen it once, verify the same subject/history,
   then close it with `:close` and report any error.

Failure: previous Session's sidebar survives another Session gaining focus,
file/diff navigation closes it, returning auto-reopens it, `s` focuses another
Session, queued callbacks revive it, or reopening throws an error.

Evidence: pin local/ACP IDs; match `louiselm://<local-id>` chat buffers to the
invoking window, inspect sidebar headers, window reuse and eventual absence.
Check the known fixture belongs only to QA-Overview's edit history. Human
confirmation establishes focus and layout. Unit lifecycle tests already cover
synthetic late callbacks; do not claim that exact race occurred here.

## Evidence access

Validated live window inventory returns only layout metadata: tab count and
each window's ID, buffer, filetype, width and relative configuration. At setup
it returned tab 1/window 1000, `louiselm-session`, width 190, no floats.

Resolve the fresh Session through `require('louiselm.session').exit_verdict()`
and its `session:inspect()` projection, then pin the ACP/local IDs. Inspect only
the QA fixture tool frames and bounded sidebar lines; do not dump unrelated
conversation text. Preserve the distinction between the test subject and the
coordinator's attributable actor.

## Findings and cleanup

F1 — Overview remained beside another Session (`louiselm-wf9wf`, fixed in

Confirmed behavior: close on focus/switch to another Session; preserve ordinary

StyLua, LuaLS, API appendix, config types, plugin version and Vimdoc checks pass.
Full-suite log: `/tmp/louiselm-wf9wf-tests.HLyHg2`; LuaLS log:

Initial recipe ambiguity: the chat can open in Insert mode, but the first chat

The only planned filesystem fixture is the named temporary

Archive final results with the unique external reference

Session already use the base reference and `#qa-chat`. Keep the same Session
