title: Grill-me needed: should a persisted workflow be a SKILL.md-shaped document discovered by the existing skill mechanism?
description:
Do not resolve this design question in passing. Facilitate a dedicated decision about the substrate and location of a persisted, declarative workflow. This is the representation half of louiselm-qbr.3, raised as a maintainer self-reflection on 2026-08-24.

Question:
When LouiseLM persists a declarative workflow, what document is it? Candidates raised: a dedicated `WORKFLOW.md`, or a `SKILL.md` at a path like `/generated/louiselm-workflow/SKILL.md` that the existing skill discovery mechanism already finds. And where does that document live -- is it tied to a project, and what makes its placement agent-friendly?

Context/evidence:
- docs/example-workflow.md already anticipates this in its own words: "louiselm intends to make workflows configurable rather than conventional, and when that lands this document is the thing it should be able to express. Treat it as a description that wants to become a specification." The maintainer now proposes taking that literally -- the example document becomes, or seeds, the actual spec.
- The maintainer's stated lean is toward SKILL.md over WORKFLOW.md, on the grounds that a skill discovery mechanism already exists and a second discovery path for a second document type is duplicated machinery.
- Skill discovery already parses frontmatter through lyaml (lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua) and already supports standard nested metadata (louiselm-m8a). A workflow spec needing structured fields -- stages, transitions, resolvers, envelopes -- would land on parsing that already exists rather than new parsing.
- This decision is why louiselm-4gif was resolved in favour of keeping lyaml and refusing a hand-rolled parser: if workflows are frontmatter documents, parser correctness stops being a skills-only concern.
- louiselm-qbr.3 owns declarative representation and lists what the format must express: validated stages, transitions, granular resolvers, backward transitions, logical threads, canonical decisions, supersessions, session replacement handoffs, evidence links. Its settled boundary with louiselm-qbr.5.1 also applies -- a persisted workflow may PROPOSE autonomy envelopes but never authorizes them.

Threads worth pulling:
- Does reusing SKILL.md conflate two things a user should be able to reason about separately? A skill is an instruction set offered to an agent; a workflow is a stage machine that sequences work. Sharing a file shape may be economy, or may be a category error that gets expensive once workflows need fields skills never have.
- If a workflow IS a skill, does it become injectable into agent context by the existing skill path, and is that desirable or a footgun -- does an agent get handed the workflow spec as instructions when it should merely be executing under it?
- "Probably tied to a project" was flagged as uncertain. Per-project in the repo (discoverable, versioned, cross-adapter, matching the repo-as-substrate posture in louiselm-repo-context-substrate-09r), or user-global, or both with precedence? Skill discovery already has root ordering and shadowing semantics that would answer this if reused.
- The `/generated/` path in the maintainer's sketch implies the document may be produced rather than authored. If it is generated, what is the source of truth, and does a human ever hand-edit it?
- Does docs/example-workflow.md become the spec, seed it, or stay a non-binding description alongside it? It currently declares itself binding on nobody; a spec binds by definition, so the relationship needs stating rather than assuming.
close_reason: Resolved by maintainer: persist workflows as discovered SKILL.md graphs with explicit named outcomes mapped to validated next-skill transitions; never infer topology from prose. Exact schema and runtime mechanics remain with louiselm-qbr.3.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Maintainer hints, 2026-08-24, materially advancing this question.

The stated model: a note / idea / self-reflection triggers questions; questions get answered; the workflow becomes more precise. Skill chaining already embodies it -- grill-me chains to to-beads, to-beads DECIDES epic/feature/task/bug, and that decision triggers the corresponding to-beads-xxxx skill. The maintainer's position: that chain IS the workflow, improving the workflow is itself a skill, and those skills ARE the louiselm workflow config.

This largely dissolves the 'category error' thread. If skills already encode their own handoffs, a workflow is not a different kind of object that happens to share a file format -- it is the graph induced by the skills' declared handoffs. There is no separate WORKFLOW.md object to describe. docs/example-workflow.md already states this in its own words: 'A workflow is not a list of stages; it is a set of stages plus the rules about what each one hands to the next, and the second half is where all the value is.'

Proposed resolution of the injection thread: a SKILL.md has TWO audiences, and that is the distinction, not skill-vs-workflow.
- body prose -> injected into the agent; what the agent reads and acts on.
- frontmatter -> read by the engine; how the workflow sequences.
Same file, two consumers. This is a second, independent argument for the louiselm-4gif decision: frontmatter is the machine-readable control plane, so parser correctness is structural rather than cosmetic.

The tension that SURVIVES, and is probably this issue's real content: today every handoff is prose, and it works because a model reads the prose and exercises judgment. Making it config means moving handoffs from prose into declarative frontmatter. That is a dial, not a binary:
- all prose -> flexible, but unverifiable; louiselm-qbr.3 explicitly wants VALIDATED stages and transitions, which prose cannot support.
- all declarative -> verifiable and sequenceable without model judgment, but rigid, and it destroys the thing that makes the current loop work. to-beads choosing epic vs feature vs task vs bug is a genuine situational judgment, not a lookup.

Candidate sweet spot: frontmatter declares the CHOICE SET of outgoing edges (enumerable, validatable), while the model resolves which edge is taken. That yields validation without rigidity and maps directly onto qbr.3's existing requirement for 'granular resolvers' -- a resolver is precisely a conditional edge whose decision procedure is a model rather than a predicate.

On self-modification: 'improving the workflow is a skill' makes the config a fixed point -- the workflow contains a skill that edits the workflow. The safety pattern for this is already settled one level up, in the qbr.3/louiselm-qbr.5.1 boundary: a persisted workflow may PROPOSE but never AUTHORIZE. Self-evolution should inherit that shape -- the workflow proposes its own revision, the operator authorizes it. That also answers the '/generated/ implies produced, is it ever hand-edited' thread: both, with the operator as an explicit stage rather than an implicit gap.

Precedent already in the tree: AGENTS.md is injected as an ACP resource_link on new-session start, gated by config.context.instructions_file (louiselm-ce6.20). So 'instruction documents are workflow config' is not speculative here -- it already ships, with AGENTS.md as the always-on member and skills as the conditionally-chained ones.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text:
Maintainer decision, 2026-08-24.

Accepted representation contract:

- A persisted workflow is the graph formed by discovered `SKILL.md` documents; there is no separate `WORKFLOW.md` substrate or second discovery mechanism.
- Each `SKILL.md` has two consumers: body prose instructs the Agent, while frontmatter supplies engine-readable workflow metadata.
- Frontmatter declares explicit named outcomes and the permitted next skill for each outcome. The model exercises judgment by selecting an outcome; LouiseLM validates the choice against that finite declaration, records it, and follows the declared transition.
- LouiseLM must not infer workflow topology or a next skill from prose, skill descriptions, or naming conventions. Existing phase-name inference is classification for routing and is not workflow-edge inference.
- These graph edges are transitions. Handoff retains its canonical narrower meaning: creation of a Session with another Agent, including injection of a reviewed transcript while retaining the source Session.
- Existing skill-root ordering and shadowing semantics govern project/global precedence rather than adding workflow-specific placement rules.
- `docs/example-workflow.md` remains a non-binding human-readable example that may seed the initial skill graph; it is not executable source of truth.
- Workflow self-improvement may propose edits to the selected `SKILL.md` graph, but operator authorization remains required under the settled qbr.3/qbr.5.1 boundary.

The earlier `workflow.outcomes` YAML was illustrative, not a frozen field name. Exact schema spelling, typed outcome reporting, validation, history, backward transitions, and execution belong to `louiselm-qbr.3`.

No standing AGENTS.md or vocabulary promotion is warranted: this is a feature-specific representation decision, and the existing canonical meanings of Handoff, Session, Agent, Model, and Provider remain unchanged.

title: QA round: skill discovery and pathless Codex permissions
description:
# Manual QA review — skill discovery and Codex pathless edit permissions

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; when the round closes its final content becomes a
QA-round bead and this file is deleted.

**Build under test:** `467a32e..2fa70dc` (five commits, beginning with
`a8b5730`). **Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: the previous round (`louiselm-yik`) closed at `467a32e`. Since then one
runtime change pruned expensive skill-tree traversal and another changed real
Codex edit requests with no path from protocol errors into generic permission
decisions. The three other commits are licensing/publication documentation or
tracker state and add no interactive behavior.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Real symlink-heavy skill discovery stays complete and fast | **passed** — 35 skills, 2 diagnostics, 21.8 ms; `bvr` present in picker and native catalog |
| 2 | Real pathless Codex edit reaches the generic permission picker | **passed** — real pathless request accepted; edit completed with no protocol error |

## Setup

The source checkout and installed plugin were both confirmed at `2fa70dc` at
the start of this round. Confirm again, then restart Neovim so no Lua module
from the previous build remains loaded:

```bash
git -C ~/code/louiselm log --oneline -1
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim log --oneline -1
```

Both must print `2fa70dc fix(permissions): ask on pathless edits`.

Case 2 requires a fresh **Codex** session using LouiseLM's normal default
`ask-human` permission policy **and Codex's `read-only` ACP mode**. In the new
session overview, change `Mode` from `agent` to `read-only`; if the overview was
dismissed, use `:LouiselmSessionOptions`. Confirm the header says
`Mode=read-only` before submitting. Codex 1.6.0's ordinary `agent` mode permits
workspace writes without an approval request, while `read-only` requires
approval for edits. The fixture path is new, so a remembered file rule cannot
short-circuit it.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Use a fresh session for the permission case. A previous denial or remembered
  rule can make the model detour or bypass the picker.
- A Codex edit may carry a full diff in `session/update` while its separate
  `session/request_permission` payload carries no path. Case 2 is specifically
  about the permission request, not the update shown in the transcript.
- Pin protocol evidence by the session id shown in the chat header. Never use
  the newest log by filename; other sessions may write newer logs.

## What does not need a manual case

- `a8b5730` and `56b9b42` change README/licence/policy prose only.
- `83fae1d` records completed GitLab publication work in beads only.
- Automated tests already prove pruning each named build directory, preserving
  a directly configured skill inside one, limiting layout warnings to one per
  root, and routing a synthetic pathless request through the session. The two
  cases below cover what those fixtures cannot: the real stow/symlink tree and
  the real Codex ACP payload/UI.

## Cases

### 1. Real symlink-heavy skill discovery stays complete and fast

Exercises `1c83964` / `lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua`.

In the restarted Neovim, run:

```vim
:lua local S=require("louiselm.skills"); local t=vim.uv.hrtime(); local s,d=S.discover({vim.fn.expand("~/.config/agentskills/generated/")}); print(string.format("skills=%d diagnostics=%d elapsed_ms=%.1f",#s,#d,(vim.uv.hrtime()-t)/1e6)); print(vim.inspect(vim.tbl_map(function(x) return x.name end,s)))
```

Then open a fresh chat, choose Codex, and invoke `:LouiselmPickSkill`. Search
for `bvr`, confirm it is offered, then dismiss the picker without selecting it.

Expect: the command returns promptly with `skills=35 diagnostics=2`; the names
include `bvr` and the other configured skills; the picker opens promptly and
offers `bvr`. The validated pre-round reading was `31.0 ms` on this machine, so
the exact timing may vary, but it should be tens of milliseconds rather than
the previous roughly 380 ms pause.

Failure signature: materially fewer than 35 skills, `bvr` missing, a flood of
roughly 31 diagnostics, or a visible several-hundred-millisecond pause before
the command/picker appears.

Evidence: send the two printed lines. They objectively prove the discovered
count, diagnostic count, names, and elapsed time. Whether the picker visibly
hesitated is observational and rests on what you saw.

**Result: PASS.** Direct discovery passed with `skills=35 diagnostics=2
elapsed_ms=21.8`; all expected names, including `bvr`, were present. The first
picker attempt did not exercise this case: screenshot
`~/Pictures/scrot/20260820_1556_948x1123_1787234213.png` shows the prompt
`louiselm file`, 27,230 workspace-file candidates, and paths matching `bvr`.
That is categorically `:LouiselmPickFile`, whose prompt is distinct from the
required `louiselm skill`. Command wiring in the build maps
`:LouiselmPickSkill` to `chat:pick_skill()` and the file command separately to
`chat:pick_file()`, so there is no code evidence of a wiring defect. The exact
skill-picker rerun passed in `codex/01a01f7a-b5ce-7e62-9ebe-83650123c8e1`:
the tester confirmed `bvr` was offered, and the pinned ACP log independently
shows Codex advertised `$bvr` in that session's native command catalog. The log
does not prove picker appearance or responsiveness; those remain the tester's
observation.

### 2. Real pathless Codex edit reaches the generic permission picker

Exercises `2fa70dc` / `lua/louiselm/permission/gates.lua`.

Create the fixture from Neovim:

```vim
:call writefile(['before'], '/tmp/louiselm-qa-pathless.txt')
```

Open a **fresh Codex session**, set its ACP `Mode` option to `read-only`, confirm
the header says `Mode=read-only`, and submit exactly:

> Use the edit/apply-patch tool, not a shell command, to replace the entire contents of /tmp/louiselm-qa-pathless.txt from `before` to `after`. Do not use sed, perl, Python, or shell redirection.

Expect: a normal select picker opens with the prompt
`louiselm permission (unknown, details unavailable):`. It is a generic picker,
not a `louiselm-diff://` review buffer. Rejection should be listed first. Choose
the adapter's once-only allow option. The turn should continue normally and the
file should contain `after`.

Failure signature: no picker; Codex reports a JSON-RPC `-32602` error; a diff
review opens despite the permission request having no path; the picker vanishes
without a choice; or approval succeeds but the turn remains stuck in
`waiting_permission`.

Report the `codex/<session-id>` from the chat header. I will pin and inspect its
protocol log. You can verify the file immediately with:

```vim
:lua =vim.fn.readfile('/tmp/louiselm-qa-pathless.txt')
```

Expect `{ "after" }`.

**First attempt: RECIPE MISS, not a product result.** Session
`codex/01a01f7d-55e4-7b60-8d16-f3503f027403` stayed in the default `agent`
mode. Its pinned log contains zero `session/request_permission` messages: Codex
sent one `edit` tool call, completed it, and changed the fixture to `after`.
LouiseLM therefore had no decision to display and could not reach the branch
changed by `2fa70dc`. The installed codex-acp 1.6.0 source confirms why:
`agent` uses an `on-request` policy with workspace-write sandboxing, so this
in-workspace-capable write needed no request; `read-only` explicitly requires
approval to edit. The recipe now sets `Mode=read-only` and requires the header
as proof before the prompt.

**Result: PASS.** Retest session
`codex/01a01f9c-15dc-7db1-a84d-56c1973fc210` emitted one real
`session/request_permission` request. Its `toolCall` was exactly the pathless
shape under test: `{ kind = "edit", status = "pending", toolCallId = ... }`
with no `rawInput`, content, or path. It advertised `allow_once`,
`allow_always`, and `reject_once`. The tester observed the decision UI and
allowed it; the same tool call then moved through `in_progress` to `completed`,
the fixture contains `after`, and the pinned agent output contains no protocol
error. The log and fixture prove the real payload reached the fixed path and
the response released the agent; exact picker appearance remains the tester's
observation.

## Evidence check

After case 2, substitute the ACP id without the `codex/` prefix:

```bash
S=<session-id>
L=$(rg -l --fixed-strings "\"sessionId\":\"$S\"" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log | tail -1)
jq -c --arg sid "$S" 'select(.method == "session/request_permission" and .params.sessionId == $sid) | {id,toolCall:.params.toolCall,options:.params.options}' "$L"
printf 'fixture='; cat /tmp/louiselm-qa-pathless.txt
```

Pass condition: one request shows `toolCall.kind` as `edit`, no path/raw input
in that request, advertised allow/reject options, and `fixture=after`. The log
proves the real peer sent the pathless shape; the fixture proves the selected
response released the agent and the edit completed. The exact picker appearance
and focus rest on what you saw.

## Cleanup when the round closes

```vim
:call delete('/tmp/louiselm-qa-pathless.txt')
```

No permission rule should be created when the once-only option is used. If a
persistent option was selected accidentally, revoke it with
`:LouiselmPermissions` before closing the round.

## Reporting back

Send me the case number, its printed output or session id, what you saw, and
anything surprising. I pull the objective evidence myself before classifying
the result. If a case did not reach the intended code path, I will correct the
recipe; if it found a product bug, I will file it before fixing it.

## Findings this round

None. Both runtime changes passed against the real environment and peer.

## How the round closed

Both manual cases passed. `1c83964` reduced discovery on the real symlink-heavy
skill root from the previously measured roughly 380 ms to 21.8 ms while
preserving all 35 skills and reducing diagnostics from roughly 31 to 2.
`2fa70dc` handled Codex 1.6.0's real pathless edit-permission payload through a
human decision and completed the edit instead of returning `-32602`.

The automated tests already asserted both normalized behaviors, but they could
not establish that the production stow layout still retained every skill or
that the current Codex peer still emitted the historical payload shape. Those
were the useful manual checks; both assumptions held.

Two recipe misses were corrected during the round. The first picker attempt
opened `:LouiselmPickFile`; its `louiselm file` title and 27,230 path candidates
made the missed code path objective. The first permission attempt used Codex's
default `agent` mode, which completed the workspace-capable edit without ever
sending a permission request. Requiring the picker title and `Mode=read-only`
made both cases reach their intended paths.

No product finding, persistent permission rule, or unverified adjacent defect
remains. The temporary fixture and this scratch file are removed as the round
is archived into beads.
close_reason: Completed: both real-environment QA cases passed with no product findings

title: Project input can diverge from the fixed state backend
description: The GCS backend and bootstrap runbook are fixed to project ID louiselm, but variables.tf accepts any syntactically valid project_id and terraform.tfvars.example presents it as editable. A stale or mistyped value can make the resource graph target another project while state remains in louiselm-tfstate. Found during pre-merge review; no LouiseLM project or bucket exists.
acceptance_criteria: The composition accepts only project ID louiselm, its example and runbook do not invite another value, and a native test rejects a different project ID before any cloud action.
close_reason: gate:reject_other_project_id — native plans reject alternate fixed project identities.

comments.author: codex/01a06b50-598b-7d32-86e1-818ef27ea658
comments.text: Lesson: a fixed backend anchor requires fixed, tested project and bucket identities; syntax validation alone cannot prevent state/resource divergence.

title: QA: accept installed usage classification improvements
description:
# Manual QA — installed usage classification

Build: `4151d8b`. Related findings: `louiselm-mgccj`, `louiselm-9imjb`.
Accepted by the maintainer on 2026-09-17 in
`codex/01a0af06-6722-7623-a3c1-df6541f79867`: "it worked fine".

## Status

| Case | Status |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Installed skill ranks actual histories | Passed — maintainer acceptance; unknown bucket 1,690 in generation 4862 |
| 2. Command traces to recorded historical options | Passed — maintainer acceptance; pinned call still records on-request/high/auto |
| 3. Refresh preserves classifications and uses the cache | Passed — maintainer acceptance; generation advanced 4856 to 4862 and classification persisted |

Agent preflight: installed binary equals the release build byte-for-byte.
Post-report queries corroborated the improved ranking and historical options.
The refreshed index covers 1,605 sources, with 836 partial/unavailable sources.
The exact indexed/unchanged totals from the maintainer's refresh were not
provided; the acceptance of that presentation rests on the maintainer's report.

## Setup

The updated executable is installed at `/home/lotso/.cargo/bin/louiselm-usage`.
No rebuild or editor restart is needed. Start a fresh agent chat in
`/home/lotso/code/louiselm` so earlier answers do not substitute for new queries.
No permission-policy changes are necessary.

## Cases 1 and 2 — paste into the new chat

> Use $louiselm-usage to rank my top 12 command families by calls across all indexed projects. Include unknown entries and report coverage. Then trace a Codex git status call with recorded historical options to its session and source evidence. Use the CLI's aggregates and selected metadata; distinguish unavailable facts from recorded values.

Exercises `usage-cli/src/command.rs` and `usage-cli/src/command/prefix.rs` through
the actual installed skill, index and local histories.

Expected: `sed` and `rg` lead the current ranking; `cd`, `grep`, and known tools
appear by name. The whole-index unknown bucket is around 1,700, rather than
14,500. Counts may grow with new activity. One shell operation still counts
once: `cd DIR && git status` is classified as `cd`, not two executions.

Failure signatures: the agent reports the old 14,500 bucket, uses a temporary
index by accident, cannot find the CLI, invents extra pipeline calls, or infers
historical settings from today's configuration.

Evidence commands, validated during preflight:

```sh
louiselm-usage stats commands --sort calls:desc --limit 12 --fields family,calls
louiselm-usage show call 'codex:019f37d1-ba97-7553-80f1-b787b13d2136:call:call_pagofOt38X3mKwp9TcU9vUOs' --fields id,session_id,family,options,options_complete,evidence --limit 2
```

That pinned call records `codex.approval_policy="on-request"`,
`codex.effort="high"`, and `codex.summary="auto"`. Its Session is
`codex:019f37d1-ba97-7553-80f1-b787b13d2136`. Another call is acceptable if its
own evidence proves the reported options. These checks prove stored facts;
the user's report confirms the skill presented them correctly.

## Case 3 — follow-up in that chat

> Refresh the normal usage index once, then rerun the same ranking. Report indexed_sources, unchanged_sources, the unknown bucket, and any coverage warnings. Treat exit 4 as partial indexing and inspect its diagnostics.

Exercises `usage-cli/src/index.rs` against the installed default index.
Expected: most sources are unchanged, while active chats may be refreshed.
The unknown bucket stays near the improved count. Legacy usage snapshots and
a missing source can still produce exit 4; that is not a failed classification
refresh. Do not require zero refreshed sources while chats are active.

Failure signatures: unchanged archived histories are all reparsed repeatedly,
known classifications disappear, or exit 4 is presented as total failure.
Evidence: JSON from `louiselm-usage index --all`, followed by the ranking query.

## Reporting and closeout

Send this chat the new session ID or paste its answer, plus any surprise.
I will inspect its objective evidence and update this file each round.
Parser quoting/redaction/option cases and old-cache invalidation already have
automated regression coverage; no need to duplicate those tests manually.

No user settings were changed. The index refresh is intentional. This final
record is preserved in a Beads `qa-round` chore and the working Markdown file
is removed. Private development comparison artifacts remain under
`/tmp/louiselm-normalization.3qwvVz/`; they are not committed.

## Findings this round

No new findings. The two implementation findings predate this round and are
accepted for closure: `louiselm-mgccj` (obsolete cached classifications) and
`louiselm-9imjb` (wrapper operands and missing command coverage), fixed in
`4151d8b`.

The earlier suite missed normalizer upgrades against unchanged source files
and wrapper argument semantics. Regression tests now cover both; this manual
round additionally verifies the installed binary, real histories and the
skill's presentation. Remaining partial-history warnings are disclosed coverage
limits, not a new finding from this round.
close_reason: Maintainer accepted installed ranking, historical-option trace and refresh behavior on 4151d8b. No new findings. Detailed evidence and limits retained in round description. live:codex/01a0af06-6722-7623-a3c1-df6541f79867

title: Manual QA: Attention, Park, and Android
description:
# Manual QA review — Attention inbox, lifecycle, and Park recovery

Working file for the current manual QA round. Keep this file untracked during
the round; it becomes the source for the closing QA bead and is deleted then.

**Build under test:** `6c41af1..14fb4c5` (HEAD `14fb4c5`). **Re-run Setup after
any fix.**

**Origin:** The last QA round (`louiselm-t6mx`, closed 2026-08-28) covered
admit/attach, but its cold-Park resume cases were blocked because the fixture
was CLI-synthesized rather than created through the live ACP/UI path. This
round prioritizes that gap and the new Attention, mobile inbox, lifecycle, and
recovery paths.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Build, binary, owner socket | PASS |
| 2 | Existing capture and status smoke | PASS |
| 3 | Completed turn creates Attention | PASS |
| 4 | Inactivity grace and activity reset | PASS — reset preserved grace and item identity |
| 5 | Viewing a Session marks it seen | PASS |
| 6 | Prompt replacement and idempotency | PASS |
| 7 | Permission request, response, cancel, disposal | PASS manual allow/cancel; disposal automated-only |
| 8 | Session failure and retry/disposal | AUTOMATED-ONLY — no safe UI trigger |
| 9 | Real UI cold Park and resume | PASS — Park resumed and cleared |
| 10 | Park expiry/reaper and claim cleanup | PASS — expiry/reaper passed; claims automated-only |
| 11 | Socket outage and reconnect | PASS — queued item arrived once and became eligible |
| 12 | Multiple Sessions remain isolated | PASS — independent items and clearing |
| 13 | Android pairing and read-only inbox | PASS — paired inbox is bounded and read-only |
| 14 | Android offline, revocation, pin, restart | PASS offline/restart; revocation/pin conditional |
| 15 | FCM/background notification delivery | BLOCKED — qbr.9.6/qbr.9.7 not implemented |
| 16 | Protected GitLab/OpenTofu pipeline | BLOCKED — external GCP/GitLab setup |

## Setup

Run from the repository root:

```bash
cd /home/lotso/code/louiselm
./scripts/install-capture-service
export PATH="$PWD/capture-service/target/release:$PATH"
test "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)" = 14fb4c5
command -v louiselm-capture
systemctl --user --no-pager status louiselm-capture.service
louiselm-capture attention status
louiselm-capture status | jq '{attention,network,delivery}'
nvim -u ./manual_init.lua
```

Inside Neovim, verify the editor resolves the same binary:

```vim
:lua print(vim.fn.exepath("louiselm-capture"))
```

It should resolve to
`/home/lotso/code/louiselm/capture-service/target/release/louiselm-capture`.
If it does not, set `vim.env.PATH` to put that directory first and restart
Neovim. Use a real ACP Agent and fresh Session per case; do not use mock,
auto-approval, or skip-permission settings for lifecycle and permission cases.
Use `:LouiselmSessionId` to record the actual Agent/ACP Session ID. Never paste
angle-bracket placeholders into shell commands.

The durable inspection command used below is:

```bash
louiselm-capture attention list | jq '{generation,items:[.items[]|{subject_kind,subject_id,kind,source_operation_id,eligible,reason,linked_run_id,stage}]}'
```

Do not put prompts, tool payloads, environments, tokens, or raw Agent errors in
this file or in Beads. Use disposable Sessions and temporary paths for any
permission action. Do not use a real work issue for Park claim tests.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Rebuild/install the capture binary before testing; Neovim and systemd can
  otherwise resolve an older `~/.local/bin/louiselm-capture`.
- `run list` lists resumable cold Parks, not active Runs.
- A CLI-created Park is not evidence that ACP `session/load` works. Case 9
  must use `:LouiselmPark` on a real live Session.
- A Park needs a long enough TTL for inspection. Do not alter another Session's
  claims or budget.
- Stop/start only the scoped user service when testing outage behavior.
- FCM delivery is not implemented in this build; case 15 is a tracked gap,
  not a failed manual test.

## Cases

### 1. Build, binary, and owner socket

Exercises commits `4a8d8b9`, `62ae66a`, and
`capture-service/src/attention_socket.rs`.

Steps:

1. Complete Setup.
2. Confirm `command -v`, Neovim `exepath`, and `systemctl` all identify the
   current release binary/service.
3. Run `louiselm-capture attention status` and inspect the state directory
   named by the command output.

Expect: the service is active; the owner-only Attention socket/capability are
available; status returns valid JSON with an Attention summary; no credentials
or payloads are printed.

Failure signature: stale binary, missing socket/capability, permission denied,
malformed JSON, service restart loop, or a status command that hangs.

Evidence: paste the commands and sanitized output into the round report;
include `systemctl --user --no-pager status louiselm-capture.service` and
`louiselm-capture attention status`.

Result: PASS — `4a8d8b9` release binary resolved by shell and service; systemd
unit active; Attention generation `0`, unresolved count `0`; overlay receiver
reachable at `https://100.90.156.114:7392`; delivery state `reachable`.

### 2. Existing capture and status smoke

Exercises `capture-service/src/run_socket.rs`,
`capture-service/src/operator_socket.rs`, and the capture UI paths changed in
this range.

Steps:

1. In Neovim run `:LouiselmCapture` to start a short recording, then stop it.
2. Run `:LouiselmCaptureInbox` and `:LouiselmCaptureStatus`.
3. Run `louiselm-capture status | jq '{attention,network,delivery}'`.

Expect: the recording is accepted and visible through the existing inbox/status
UI; status remains usable; Attention status is present and unrelated capture
behavior is not broken.

Failure signature: service or socket errors, stale executable use, recording
never appears, malformed status buffer, or status exposes private payloads.

Evidence: the two Neovim command results plus sanitized `louiselm-capture
status` output and `journalctl --user -u louiselm-capture.service -n 50
--no-pager` if it fails.

Result: FAIL — `:LouiselmCapture` started capture
`b7849727-b355-4e07-8776-d7a0a9863dd9`, but stopping it reported
`recorder failed: process failed`. The recorder produced a valid WAV in a
direct reproduction, while Neovim reported the SIGINT stop as `{code = 1,
signal = 0, stderr = ""}`. The service journal showed no `ingest-local`
request, so durable ingestion was never attempted. Filed as
`louiselm-tx1q`.

Fix applied in `lua/louiselm/capture/init.lua:144-146` with a regression in
`tests/capture_spec.lua`; automated checks pass. Re-run Setup and repeat the
real recording before changing this case to PASS.

Retest: current target-release binary resolved; capture
`2c843afd-3e58-412f-aff9-747db0ab5b84` appeared in the inbox as
`completed · neovim · 7240 ms` with a durable WAV; status reported 49 captures,
48 completed, 0 pending, Attention generation 0, and delivery `reachable`.
The original recorder-stop defect is closed as `louiselm-tx1q`.

### 3. Completed turn creates one Attention item

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/attention.lua` and Chat turn completion routing.

Steps:

1. Start a fresh real Session and record its `:LouiselmSessionId`.
2. Split or open a disposable buffer first with `:vnew`, then return to the
   Claude chat window.
3. Submit a trivial prompt such as `Reply with exactly READY.` and immediately
   move to the disposable window with `CTRL-W l` (or click that window). If the
   reply finishes too quickly, use a prompt that takes longer, then switch
   windows before it completes.
4. Type harmless text only in the disposable buffer, not in the Claude chat,
   and wait for the turn to complete.
5. Run the Attention inspection command twice from the shell.

Expect: exactly one `turn_ready` item exists for that Session; its reason is
exactly `Agent turn is ready`; `eligible` is initially false; the operation ID
is a bounded UUID; no prompt, response, path, or tool content appears; the
second read does not create a duplicate.

Failure signature: no item, duplicate items, early eligibility, Agent-authored
text in the item, an unbounded ID, or an item attached to another Session.

Evidence: both sanitized Attention snapshots and the visible Session state.

Setup blocker resolved: current source and installed service binaries now
support `attention`, and the service/Neovim need to remain on those current
paths for this case. The earlier missing socket and stale Cargo binary were
setup failures, not product findings.

Clarification: the reported Claude Session
`claude/5072ed89-e0d8-41a4-b214-bdc6bde8a94a` was not yet a valid focus
observation because the source/non-source window sequence was unclear. Typing
in the Claude chat is focused activity; typing in a separate disposable buffer
is the intended control.

Retest note: `louiselm-capture attention list` again resolved the old
`/home/lotso/.cargo/bin/louiselm-capture` and returned `unknown command
'attention'`. Use the absolute target-release binary below, or verify both the
shell and live Neovim executable before rerunning:

```bash
/home/lotso/code/louiselm/capture-service/target/release/louiselm-capture attention list | jq .
```

```vim
:lua print(vim.fn.exepath("louiselm-capture"))
```

Result: PASS — current target-release binary reported exactly one
Session-scoped `turn_ready` item for Claude Session
`5072ed89-e0d8-41a4-b214-bdc6bde8a94a`, source operation
`8154fddd-7cc0-408a-b1a7-d73041b2a8fc`, fixed reason `Agent turn is ready`,
`eligible: true` after the grace period, and no Agent-authored content.

### 4. Thirty-second grace and activity reset

Exercises inactivity handling in `lua/louiselm/ui/attention.lua`.

Steps:

1. Start a fresh Session and run `:LouiselmSessionId`; save the UUID after
   `claude/` as `SESSION_ID`. Make a disposable split/buffer available.
2. Submit a prompt, then move to the disposable buffer before the turn ends.
   Do not type in the Claude chat after this point.
3. As soon as the turn finishes, start a timer and inspect only this Session:

   ```bash
   louiselm-capture attention list | jq --arg id "$SESSION_ID" \
     '.items[] | select(.subject_id == $id) |
       {kind,eligible,created_at_ms,source_operation_id}'
   ```

   This is snapshot A. The item should say `eligible: false`.
4. Wait about 25 seconds after snapshot A, then type one harmless character in
   the disposable buffer and leave it there. This is the activity reset; do not
   focus the chat Session.
5. Six seconds after the reset, take snapshot B with the same filtered command.
   More than 30 seconds have now elapsed since snapshot A, but only six
   seconds since the reset, so B must still say `eligible: false`.
6. Twenty-five seconds after snapshot B, take snapshot C. It must say
   `eligible: true` with the same `source_operation_id`.

Expect: the item is not eligible before the grace period; unrelated editor
activity resets the grace period; it becomes eligible only after 30 seconds of
inactivity. Activity does not create another Attention item.

Failure signature: snapshot A is already eligible, snapshot B becomes eligible
early, snapshot C remains false, typing creates another item, or the timer
keeps Neovim busy/hung. The terminal inspection command itself does not count
as Neovim activity.

Evidence: timestamped `attention list` snapshots and a short note of the
activity times.

Progress: snapshot A contained the previous case-3 item with `eligible: true`
and the new case-4 item created at `1788188075000` with `eligible: false`.
Filter subsequent snapshots by the new item's `source_operation_id` or
`created_at_ms` so the intentionally unresolved case-3 item does not confuse
the timer observation.

Retest: the same new item was `eligible: true` at the 30-second observation.
This proves the basic grace period, but the required post-activity false
snapshot was not captured, so the activity-reset branch remains untested.

Additional attempt: Session `01a05b03-74b2-75d3-a09c-7a239a0e6ebe` was not
measured because the shell query used literal `"SESSION_ID"` despite setting
the variable. No product result is inferred.

Retest in progress: valid snapshot A for the new item has
`source_operation_id` `0d17d0b8-c544-4d71-bca8-6ae850bb70ff` and
`eligible: false`. The final observation shows the same item
`eligible: true`; the required 10-second post-reset `eligible: false` snapshot
has not been reported yet.

Final retest: a fresh item appeared once, remained `eligible: false` in both
post-reset observations, then became `eligible: true` with the same
`source_operation_id` `bb2da5a2-9530-43c4-8753-e25e2bc3396b`. The activity-reset
branch passes; no duplicate was created.

### 5. Viewing a Session marks its item seen

Exercises Session-scoped `seen` clearing.

Steps:

1. Use the existing case-3 item for Session
   `5072ed89-e0d8-41a4-b214-bdc6bde8a94a`, or produce one fresh turn if it has
   already been cleared. Inspect Attention first and note its generation.
2. In Neovim, focus the Claude chat window by clicking inside it or using
   `CTRL-W h`/`CTRL-W l` as appropriate. Do not type, submit a prompt, or
   switch Sessions; merely viewing/focusing the chat is the action under test.
3. Inspect Attention immediately and again after 40 seconds, filtering by the
   Session ID if other test items remain.

Expect: the matching item is removed and generation advances once; it never
becomes eligible later. Viewing an unrelated buffer must not clear it.

Failure signature: item remains, later becomes eligible, unrelated focus clears
it, or generation advances repeatedly without a new source operation.

Evidence: before/after snapshots and the focused buffer name.

Original result: FAIL — for Claude Session `5072ed89-e0d8-41a4-b214-bdc6bde8a94a`,
clicking/focusing the Claude chat without typing left the same `turn_ready`
item, operation ID, and `eligible: true` unchanged. Filed as
`louiselm-irw1`. Root cause appears to be that `Chat:switch` calls
`attention:seen()`, but direct focus of an already-current Session buffer does
not call `Chat:switch`.

First retest: the new item disappeared after clicking the Claude Session, but
the older durable item with source operation
`8154fddd-7cc0-408a-b1a7-d73041b2a8fc` remained. This exposed that
`Attention:seen()` only knew about entries created by the current Neovim
process. The case remains failed for restart-safe clearing.

Fix applied in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`,
`lua/louiselm/ui/attention.lua`, and the authenticated Attention socket/client,
with regressions in `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`, `tests/ui/attention_spec.lua`,
`tests/workflow/attention_client_spec.lua`, and
`capture-service/tests/attention.rs`. Automated checks pass (809 MiniTest
cases plus Rust fmt/clippy/test, Stylua, LuaLS, and generators). Rebuild the
capture service and restart/reload Neovim, then repeat the real click/focus
observation before changing this case to PASS.

Deployment finding: the first retest used an active service process from before
the fix because `systemctl enable --now` does not restart an already-active
unit. The new installer uses an explicit restart; the service was restarted at
17:24:34 and the resulting disconnect was a stale-service artifact, filed as
`louiselm-vxjt`.

Final retest: after the service restart fix and a Neovim restart, resuming and
focusing the Claude Session produced no Attention socket warning. Filtering
`attention list` for Session `5072ed89-e0d8-41a4-b214-bdc6bde8a94a` produced no
output, proving both the current and older durable items were cleared.

### 6. Prompt replacement and idempotency

Checks that starting a new prompt removes the old alert, and that one completed
prompt creates only one new alert.

Steps:

1. Start a fresh real Session and record its ID with `:LouiselmSessionId`.
2. Open a disposable split, submit a short prompt in the Session, and move to
   the disposable split before the reply finishes.
3. After the reply finishes, inspect the Session's Attention item and copy its
   `source_operation_id`. Call this `OLD_ID`. Confirm there is one item.
4. Return to the same Session and submit another short prompt. Immediately
   inspect Attention while the prompt is running.
5. Leave the Session focused on the disposable split. After the second reply
   finishes, inspect Attention again.
6. Repeat the inspection without sending another prompt.

For each inspection, filter by the Session ID. The command is:

```bash
/home/lotso/code/louiselm/capture-service/target/release/louiselm-capture attention list \
  | jq '.items[] | select(.subject_id == "SESSION_ID") | {kind,source_operation_id,eligible}'
```

Expect:

- Step 3 shows exactly one item: the old alert.
- Step 4 shows no item for this Session: starting the new prompt cleared the
  old alert.
- Step 5 shows exactly one item: the new alert, with a different
  `source_operation_id` from `OLD_ID`.
- Step 6 shows the same one item, proving that rereading does not create a
  duplicate.

Failure signature: the old alert remains after step 4, no new alert appears
after step 5, the new alert reuses `OLD_ID`, two alerts appear for the second
reply, or an unrelated Session's alert is cleared.

Evidence: the Session ID, the three filtered snapshots, and the two operation
IDs only. Do not paste prompt or response text.

Result: PASS — Session `claude/3468e9ee-d35d-4ddd-92fa-9be1e3d27a15` cleared
the old alert `36944ebe-11ef-4378-8c4e-34ff44a96b92` when the next prompt
started. One new alert appeared with operation ID
`fa15f991-11f7-4de4-abaf-81ff731da3f8`, remained present on a repeated read,
and later became eligible. No duplicate or old alert remained.

### 7. Permission request, response, cancel, and disposal

Exercises permission routing, queueing, and disposal in
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` and `lua/louiselm/ui/attention.lua`.

Steps:

1. Clear remembered permissions before the test. The normal way is
   `:LouiselmPermissions`, selecting each matching `allow` rule, and choosing
   `Revoke`. For a disposable QA reset, close Neovim and move
   `~/.local/state/louiselm/permissions.json` aside, then restart Neovim; on
   this machine the actual path is
   `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/permissions.json`. Use
   `:echo stdpath('state')` if your state directory is different. If the file
   does not exist and `:LouiselmPermissions` shows no rules, permissions are
   already clear. Use the normal human-approval policy, not
   `auto-approve-scoped`.
2. Start a fresh real Session. Submit a request that causes the Agent to ask
   for a disposable permission,
   such as creating a uniquely named file under `/tmp`.
3. While the picker is visibly waiting for your choice, inspect Attention for
   this Session:

   ```bash
   /home/lotso/code/louiselm/capture-service/target/release/louiselm-capture attention list \
     | jq '.items[] | select(.subject_id == "SESSION_ID") | {kind,reason,source_operation_id,eligible}'
   ```

   Replace `SESSION_ID` with the UUID after `claude/` in
   `:LouiselmSessionId`. The result must contain one `permission_required`
   item with reason `Permission is required`.
4. Approve the request once and confirm the file was created. Repeat with a
   second uniquely named file, then press `q` at the permission picker and
   confirm the second file was not created.
5. Stop here for the manual case. Do not try to run
   `:LouiselmSessionClose` while the permission picker is open: the picker is
   modal and Neovim cannot accept an Ex command at that time. Disposal while a
   request is outstanding is covered by the automated regression instead.

Expect: one `permission_required` item appears with reason exactly
`Permission is required`; it contains only bounded IDs and optional Run/stage;
the picker remains actionable; Attention clears only after the response is
acknowledged or cancelled. A second request is not lost or merged with the
first. Outstanding-request disposal is verified by the automated regression,
not this manual case.

Failure signature: silent auto-approval, Attention clears before response,
stale item after response/cancel/disposal, queue focus breaks, duplicate
requests, or raw permission/tool content reaches the durable store.

Evidence: picker state, sanitized Attention snapshots, and the ACP/proxy log
only if needed to establish request ordering; match structured request fields,
not generic words.

Progress: PASS for the allow/cancel paths — Session
`claude/9ded4c0d-d8a9-4ee8-9b8c-5983934c854f` showed one
`permission_required` item while the picker waited; after approval the file
was created and the Session's permission item disappeared. The unrelated
`turn_ready` item for Session `cdfc7c51-ac8a-47a4-bb38-6bf7f39c574b` remained.
Cancel also passed: the picker offered only allow options, so `q` was used to
cancel; the permission item disappeared and the requested file was not
created. The previously requested disposal timing is not a valid manual step:
the modal picker prevents `:LouiselmSessionClose` from being entered, and a
hard shutdown does not exercise explicit Session disposal. Outstanding-request
disposal is covered by the automated regression. Filed as `louiselm-vwcf`.

### 8. Session failure and retry/disposal

Exercises `session_failed` emission and cleanup. There is no supported UI action
that deliberately fails only one real Agent process. Do not kill processes with
`pkill`, `killall`, or a guessed PID: that can terminate the wrong Agent or
Neovim and is not a reproducible QA step.

Manual action: skip this case. The failure, retry, disposal, late-callback, and
sanitization paths are covered by the automated session/lifecycle tests.

Expect: one `session_failed` item appears with reason exactly `Session failed`
and only bounded identifiers/optional Run link; no raw error text enters
Attention. Retry or disposal clears it; no late callback recreates it.

Failure signature: no item, duplicate failure, sensitive/raw error in the
store, item persists after disposal, or a late callback revives the Session/UI.

Evidence: automated test results. A real failure can be added to a future QA
round only if the product gains an explicit failure-injection command.

### 9. Real UI cold Park and resume

Exercises the previously blocked gap through `:LouiselmPark` and
`:LouiselmResumePark`, including `workflow/resume.lua` and Run persistence.

Steps:

1. Start a fresh real Session, complete at least one prompt, and note the
   actual ACP Session ID.
2. Run `:LouiselmPark` from that live Session. Confirm any staged/queued
   context prompt deliberately.
3. Verify the UI reports the Session cold-Parked, then run:

   ```bash
   louiselm-capture run list
   louiselm-capture attention list
   ```

4. Do **not** run `:LouiselmSessionClose`: that deliberately removes the Park.
   Quit Neovim with `:qa`, leaving the Parked Session itself untouched. Start
   it again with `nvim -u ./manual_init.lua`, then run
   `:LouiselmResumePark` and select the exact Run UUID from step 3.
5. Wait for the resume notification, run `:LouiselmSessionId` to confirm the
   Session is attached, send a harmless follow-up such as `Reply with exactly:
   resumed`, and inspect `run list` and Attention.

Expect: the Run is durably Parked and one `run_parked` item exists with reason
exactly `Run is Parked`; it has a canonical Run UUID and no Agent content. The
restart picker finds the same Park; resume loads the real ACP Session, attaches
once, reports recoverable/lossy behavior, permits a follow-up, removes the Park
from `run list`, and clears the matching Attention item. Claims/budget do not
silently reset.

Failure signature: picker shows a stale/nonexistent resource, ACP
`session/load` fails, duplicate Session/Run appears, Park remains after resume,
Attention remains/reappears, or claims/budget are lost.

Evidence: pre/post `run list`, pre/post Attention snapshots, exact visible
notifications, `:LouiselmSessionId`, and scoped service logs.

Progress: PASS. Session
`claude/62b4d897-b815-47ec-865a-764225cf98c5` resumed with the same ACP Session
ID after restart. The resumed Park no longer appeared in `run list`, and a
Session-filtered Attention query returned no item. Note that `run list` uses
the separate Run UUID, not the `claude/<session-id>` value.

### 10. Park expiry/reaper and claim cleanup

Exercises the durable reaper path from `capture-service/src/run_store.rs`.

Steps:

1. Use a disposable CLI Run for expiry only; it is not ACP resume evidence.
   In a shell with the capture binary on `PATH`, run:

   ```bash
   RUN_ID="$(< /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid)"
   louiselm-capture run admit --id "$RUN_ID" --generated-work-max 1 --park-ttl-ms 1000
   louiselm-capture run attach --id "$RUN_ID" --session-id "qa-expiry-$RUN_ID" --agent claude \
     --acp-session-id "qa-expiry-$RUN_ID" --cwd /tmp --load-session true
   louiselm-capture run park --id "$RUN_ID" --session-id "qa-expiry-$RUN_ID" --agent claude \
     --acp-session-id "qa-expiry-$RUN_ID" --cwd /tmp --load-session true --claims ""
   louiselm-capture run list | jq --arg id "$RUN_ID" '.[] | select(.id == $id)'
   ```

   The last command must show exactly this Run with `state: "cold_parked"`.
2. Save the current time, wait 12 seconds for the service's 10-second reaper,
   then run:

   ```bash
   louiselm-capture run list | jq --arg id "$RUN_ID" '.[] | select(.id == $id)'
   journalctl --user -u louiselm-capture.service --since "<START_TIME>" --no-pager
   ```

   Replace `<START_TIME>` with the saved timestamp (for example,
   `$(date --iso-8601=seconds)` captured before the wait).

Expect: the expired Run produces no output in `run list`, and the service log
contains a reap message naming one disposed Run. No unrelated Run changes.
Claim-release behavior is automated-only in this manual fixture because it
would require creating a real disposable Beads claim.

Failure signature: expired Park remains resumable, the service reports a reap
failure, the service loops/errors, or another Run is modified.

Evidence: Run UUID, before/after list/status, and
`journalctl --user -u louiselm-capture.service --since <start> --no-pager`.

Progress: PASS. Disposable Run `2209cf8d-02dd-44a8-979a-8eaf2c7641a1` was
admitted, attached, and cold-Parked with a one-second TTL. After 12 seconds it
produced no `run list` entry, and the service logged `reap pass disposed 1
Run(s), 0 release(s) still failing`. Claim cleanup remains automated-only.

### 11. Attention socket outage, reconnect, and late disposal

Exercises async queue/reconnect and fast-event disposal behavior.

Steps:

1. Start a fresh real Session, note its ACP Session ID with
   `:LouiselmSessionId`, then stop only the capture service:

   ```bash
   systemctl --user stop louiselm-capture.service
   ```

2. Before submitting, create a second split with `:vsplit | enew`, then return
   to the chat split. Submit a prompt long enough to remain visible while you
   switch away, such as `Explain this project in ten paragraphs; change no
   files`. Immediately press `Ctrl-w l` to focus the empty split and leave it
   focused until the reply arrives. Neovim must remain usable; an
   `Attention socket disconnected` notification is acceptable.
3. Restart the service, keep the empty split focused, and force one activity
   event there by pressing `j`, then `k`. Do not focus the chat split before
   inspecting Attention:

   ```bash
   louiselm-capture attention list | jq --arg id "ACP_SESSION_ID" \
     '.items[] | select(.subject_id == $id)'
   ```

   Replace `ACP_SESSION_ID` with the UUID portion of the value from
   `:LouiselmSessionId`. The queued transition should arrive once.
4. Restore the service if needed:

   ```bash
   systemctl --user start louiselm-capture.service
   ```

Expect: editor work remains responsive; exactly one `turn_ready` item for the
Session arrives after service recovery. Outstanding-request disposal and
late-callback behavior are automated-only; do not try to reproduce them by
closing a Session during a modal picker.

Failure signature: Neovim hangs, no item arrives after reconnect, duplicate
item, uncaught editor error, or a disposed Session is revived in automated
coverage.

Evidence: Session IDs, service stop/start times, filtered Attention snapshots,
and visible UI notifications. Do not paste prompts or socket capabilities.

Progress: PASS. The outage/reconnect half produced exactly one `turn_ready`
item for Session `ff47e1fe-7008-4cf1-b2bd-9f73a2497a63`, with operation ID
`8ed60b8b-297f-4d2b-8295-35ab3d09f5ae`. It was initially `eligible: false`,
then became `eligible: true` after the grace period without duplication.

### 12. Multiple Sessions remain isolated

Exercises Attention identity and per-Session clearing.

Steps:

1. In the current Neovim, run `:LouiselmSessionSwitch`. If the two Sessions
   are not listed, create two fresh ones with `:LouiselmSessionNew`; old live
   Sessions are not recoverable through `:LouiselmResumePark` unless they were
   cold-Parked first. Run `:LouiselmSessionId` in each and write down the UUID
   after `claude/` as `A_ID` and `B_ID`. Their working directory is irrelevant
   to this case. Create one scratch split with `:vsplit | enew`; keep the
   scratch split on the right and the chat split on the left.
2. In the left split, run `:LouiselmSessionSwitch`, select A, and submit
   `Explain this project in ten paragraphs; change no files`. Immediately press
   `Ctrl-w l` and leave the scratch split focused until A replies.
3. Verify A's item before continuing:

   ```bash
   louiselm-capture attention list | jq --arg id \
     "A_ID" \
     '.items[] | select(.subject_id == $id) |
       {subject_id,kind,source_operation_id,eligible}'
   ```

   Wait through the grace period if needed. Exactly one `turn_ready` item for
   A must appear. If it does not, stop: A was focused when the reply arrived
   and this attempt is inconclusive.
4. Return to the left split, run `:LouiselmSessionSwitch`, select B, and submit
   the same prompt. Immediately press `Ctrl-w l` and leave the scratch split
   focused until B replies. Then inspect both items:

   ```bash
   louiselm-capture attention list | jq --arg a \
     "A_ID" --arg b "B_ID" \
     '[.items[] | select(.subject_id == $a or .subject_id == $b) |
       {subject_id,kind,source_operation_id,eligible}]'
   ```

   Wait through the grace period if B is initially ineligible. Exactly one item
   per Session must appear, with different operation IDs.
5. Run `:LouiselmSessionSwitch`, select A, and run the same query: only B's
   item must remain. Then switch to B and run it again: neither item must
   remain.

Expect: A and B each have one independent item even if turn numbers match;
focusing A clears only A and focusing B clears only B; source operation IDs
remain distinct.

Failure signature: cross-Session clearing, collisions, one item overwrites the
other, or a Session receives another Session's Run link.

Evidence: sanitized grouped Attention snapshots and both Session IDs.

Progress: PASS after correcting the shell placeholder. The first attempt was
inconclusive because the shell query used the
literal placeholder `A_ID`. Retest A now passes: Session
`1618d283-3f12-4846-b8b0-8125455e1ff6` has exactly one eligible `turn_ready`
item. After B's turn, focusing A left one item for B
(`01a05ae1-9cf9-78d0-bbd2-cce65c797686`) with operation ID
`5914d660-2c31-41ca-858f-7d820efb2bd6`, which is the expected isolation result;
focusing B then cleared the final item. No cross-Session clearing or collision
was observed.

### 13. Android pairing and read-only Attention inbox

Exercises `android/app/src/main/java/dev/louiselm/capture/MainActivity.kt`,
`Protocol.kt`, and pinned HTTPS transport. **Conditional on a debuggable
Android device and the private network described in `android/README.md`.**

Steps:

1. Build/install the current debug APK and configure the documented private
   overlay route; do not expose the receiver publicly.
2. Run `:LouiselmCapturePair`, scan the QR with the app, and confirm the paired
   endpoint/pin.
3. Generate as many of the four Attention kinds as practical, then refresh the
   phone inbox.
4. Inspect cards and attempt to find any mutation/control action.

Expect: pairing uses the pinned HTTPS receiver and persists the credential;
cards show only bounded Session/Run IDs, age, fixed reasons, optional linked
Run/stage; fixed reasons are exactly `Agent turn is ready`, `Permission is
required`, `Run is Parked`, and `Session failed`. The inbox is read-only and
contains no Agent prose, prompt, tool payload, or control buttons.

Failure signature: loopback/public endpoint, pin rejection, crash, stale or
crossed IDs, arbitrary reason text, hidden mutation control, or sensitive
content on the phone.

Evidence: phone screen/video, `louiselm-capture status`, and sanitized pairing
state. Do not record the QR secret.

Progress: PASS from `/home/lotso/Downloads/1000046588.jpg`. The phone shows
the private HTTPS endpoint `https://100.90.156.114:7392`, five Attention cards,
only fixed reasons with bounded Session/Run IDs and ages, and no Agent prose or
mutation controls. The visible controls are Refresh Inbox, Start Capture, Pair
Receiver QR, and Sync Now.

### 14. Android offline, revocation, pin, and restart behavior

Exercises retry ordering, local seen generation, and operator-action handling.
**Conditional on case 13 passing.**

Steps:

1. With the valid five-card snapshot displayed, turn the phone's Wi-Fi off
   from Android quick settings. Tap `REFRESH INBOX`.
2. Confirm the five previous cards remain visible and the app shows a retryable
   network error; it must not clear the last good snapshot. Turn Wi-Fi back on
   and tap `REFRESH INBOX` again. The inbox must return to its connected state.
3. Restart the app without clearing its data:

   ```bash
   adb shell am force-stop dev.louiselm.capture
   adb shell monkey -p dev.louiselm.capture 1
   ```

   Confirm the last safely stored snapshot and its cards are still present.
4. Only if you can identify this phone's exact device UUID without guessing,
   revoke it with:

   ```bash
   louiselm-capture status | jq '.devices'
   louiselm-capture revoke-device DEVICE_UUID
   ```

   Refresh the phone and confirm it requests re-pairing. Otherwise skip this
   sub-test. Do not revoke either duplicate `Xiaomi 21081111RG` entry by name
   alone.
5. Skip pin rotation unless a second receiver identity is deliberately
   available; changing the live receiver key is not a safe improvisation.
6. If a debug install is available, inspect only the local preference:

   ```bash
   adb shell run-as dev.louiselm.capture sh -c 'cat shared_prefs/attention-ui.xml'
   ```

Expect: offline refresh retains the last parsed cards and offers retry; online
refresh restores the connected state; restart retains the local snapshot and
seen-generation state without claiming to clear the server. If revocation is
run with a verified UUID, it produces an operator-action/re-pair state and
disables unsafe retry. Pin rotation is conditional.

Failure signature: offline clears good data, restart loses the local snapshot,
revoked device still reads, or pin failure is treated as transient success.

Evidence: phone states/screens, service pairing status, and the local
preference value only.

Progress: PASS for offline refresh and restart. With Wi-Fi off, Refresh Inbox
showed a retryable network error while retaining the existing cards. After
restored Wi-Fi, force-stopping `dev.louiselm.capture`, and relaunching it, the
same five cards remained. The optional preference-file inspection was not
needed. Revocation and pin rotation remain conditional and were not attempted.

### 15. FCM/background notification delivery

Exercises qbr.9.6 and qbr.9.7, which are not in this build. No current FCM
sender, token registration, generic notification, collapse, background tap, or
offline WorkManager path exists to exercise. Leave BLOCKED and do not file an
absence-of-notification bug from this round. Future QA must cover generic
notification text, collapse by subject/condition, background tap into the
inbox, revoked tokens, and offline retry once those beads close.

Evidence: `br show louiselm-qbr.9.6` and `br show louiselm-qbr.9.7` at round
close.

### 16. Protected GitLab/OpenTofu pipeline

Exercises qbr.9.5 infrastructure and `.gitlab-ci.yml`. Local static validation
already passed; a live check is **BLOCKED** without the maintainer's configured
GCP project and GitLab protected-main pipeline.

If that external setup is available, verify a public branch/MR runs only
format/validate, while protected default-branch execution obtains an OIDC
token, writes a Developer-only one-day exact plan artifact, and makes manual
apply consume that exact plan. Confirm no private key/state/token appears in
logs and no destroy is planned.

Failure signature: unprotected apply, broad WIF trust, downloadable plan for
untrusted users, generated private key, apply recomputes instead of consuming
the saved plan, or a destroy plan.

Evidence: GitLab pipeline/job permissions and sanitized `tofu show` output.

## Evidence check

At the end of the round, verify every PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED state has a falsifiable
result and command/screenshot evidence. Do not call automated green tests a
manual pass: they do not prove installed-binary selection, real ACP ordering,
Neovim lifecycle, private-network pinning, or physical Android behavior.

## Cleanup

1. Close disposable Sessions and stop any temporary Agent processes.
2. Remove only temporary files created by this round.
3. Restore the capture service to its normal running state if case 11 stopped
   it:

   ```bash
   systemctl --user start louiselm-capture.service
   ```

4. Do not delete or rewrite user Sessions, Runs, claims, or unrelated Beads.

## Reporting back

Report case number, PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED, exact failure signature, and the
evidence command/output. A failure is not complete until the defect is filed
in Beads before any fix begins. If the cause is apparatus/setup, report that
separately from a product finding.

## Findings

Add only concise, evidence-backed findings here during the round. Route each
confirmed defect to a Beads issue before fixing it.

**F1 — `louiselm-tx1q`, closed.** Normal `pw-record` stop returned code 1 with
no signal, so Neovim reported `recorder failed: process failed` and skipped
durable ingestion. Fixed at `lua/louiselm/capture/init.lua:144`; live capture
`2c843afd-3e58-412f-aff9-747db0ab5b84` completed with a durable WAV.

**F2 — `louiselm-irw1`, closed.** Direct focus of an attached Session left its
durable `turn_ready` item. Fixed with BufEnter/WinEnter clearing plus an
authenticated server-side clear; live retest for Session
`5072ed89-e0d8-41a4-b214-bdc6bde8a94a` produced no matching Attention item.

**F3 — `louiselm-vxjt`, closed.** Installing a new capture binary with
`systemctl enable --now` left an already-running service on the old binary,
causing a socket disconnect. `scripts/install-capture-service` now restarts the
unit; live resumed-Session retest passed without disconnect warnings.

**F4 — `louiselm-vwcf`, in progress.** The explicit Session-disposal cleanup
fix is covered by an automated regression, but live acceptance remains pending:
the permission picker is modal, so `:LouiselmSessionClose` cannot be entered
while it is open. A hard Neovim shutdown is not equivalent and is not evidence.
close_reason: Manual QA complete; runnable cases passed; disposal, FCM, and protected-pipeline limits remain documented.

title: Grill-me needed: define chat window versus session close semantics
description:
Do not resolve this design question in passing; decide the lifecycle policy before implementing a fix.

Observed scenario:
- One Neovim instance had two live louiselm Codex sessions.
- While switching between them, the user closed the session whose feature was complete.
- The other session, which was still being resumed/worked on, also became unavailable.
- The user believes this happened through :q while the sessions are scratch buffers.

Current code evidence:
- Chat buffers are buftype=nofile, bufhidden=hide, and named louiselm://<session-id>.
- There is no chat BufHidden/BufDelete/BufWipeout handler.
- Chat:close_session() is the explicit disposal path and disposes only the selected view.session.
- Chat:dispose() removes UI resources without disposing sessions.
- The exact command/path used in the incident is not yet reproduced; it may involve :q on the last window, an explicit close command, or outer UI teardown.

Questions to resolve:
1. Must :q on a louiselm chat buffer always mean only hide/close this view, never dispose its session?
2. How are hidden sessions rediscovered and switched to?
3. Should explicit session close warn or confirm when other sessions are live, or only when the selected session has active work/queued prompts?
4. What should happen when closing the last chat window, tab, or UI controller?
5. What headless test reproduces two sessions, switching, :q/explicit close, and verifies that unrelated sessions remain live?
6. If the incident is reproducible, should it become a separate implementation bug after the lifecycle policy is settled?
close_reason: Implemented last-window QuitPre protection for multiple attached chat sessions; added regression coverage; full suite passes with 329 tests and 0 failures.

title: Grill-me needed: What should LouiseLM's first-run onboarding optimize for?
description:
Do not resolve this design question in passing; run a focused grill-me session and record the maintainer's decisions.

Question:
What should LouiseLM's first-run onboarding optimize for: the shortest path to a working chat, teaching users how Agents/providers/keys work, or a small set of opinionated onboarding profiles?

Context and evidence:
- The current README has only a development Quick start and assumes users can write Lua configuration.
- manual_init.lua preconfigures Claude and DeepSeek, but not Codex, and relies on adapter-specific commands and environment variables.
- The proposed beginner path is a minimal init file users can run with Neovim, with Agents prefilled and one obvious place to configure credentials.
- Provider installation and authentication flows differ and may change; credentials must never be hard-coded or exposed.
- The existing task louiselm-lukb asks for an onboarding information architecture, a quickstart.lua versus README decision, verified provider setup guidance, and first-prompt acceptance criteria.

Threads worth pulling:
- Who is the primary first-run user and what Neovim knowledge can be assumed?
- Should the first-run path choose one recommended Agent or present Claude/Codex/DeepSeek equally?
- Is a committed standalone quickstart.lua safe and maintainable, or should it be a copyable template?
- Should onboarding profiles be documentation-only initially or a product feature?
- What counts as success: opening the chat, completing one prompt, or configuring a durable personal setup?
- How should provider auth/key instructions be kept accurate as external adapters change?
close_reason: Resolved through confirmed grill-me design; decisions recorded in issue comments.

title: Same-domain links render as external links
description:
Links written as absolute `https://louiselm.com/...` URLs render with the
external-link icon and open in a new tab, even though they stay on the same
site. The landing page's own call to action — "Try LouiseLM in your browser",
pointing at `https://louiselm.com/demo/` — is the most visible case: it looks
like it sends the reader off the site.

## Observed

Maintainer screenshot 2026-09-07: the landing page CTA carries the external-link
glyph. `README.md:11` writes the link as an absolute
`https://louiselm.com/demo/` URL, and `myst.yml` sets no `internal_domains`.

## Fix

The pinned book-theme exposes `internal_domains`: "A domain to treat as internal
links (no external icon, opens in same tab). Supports wildcard subdomains with
*." Set it to the published domain in `myst.yml` `site.options`.

## Acceptance

- The landing page CTA and any other same-domain absolute link render without
  the external glyph and open in the same tab.
- Genuinely external links keep the glyph.
- Strict site build passes.
close_reason: consumer:myst.yml:61 — internal_domains: louiselm.com. README's demo call to action now renders as <a class="link" href="https://louiselm.com/demo/"> with no target=_blank and no external glyph; external links keep theirs. No gate: an assertion on link rendering would duplicate the theme's own behaviour.
