title: Inject-mode adapter titles hide the user subject
description:
DeepSeek/GLM sessions using LouiseLM's inject-mode skill context appear in the resume picker without a useful subject. The adapter persists only the beginning of the injected catalog as the session title, so the user's task is absent and cannot be recovered by LouiseLM's picker normalization.

## Observed

Screenshot: `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_1012_1920x1200_1787559124.png`, session `deepseek/session-7042e674-d0c9-4f03-81ef-5c46171d50b7`, observed 2026-08-24.

Captured ACP session/list payloads:
- `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/connections/8552aa82-b66b-482e-bd9d-4c5a27953096.jsonl`
- `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/connections/ec2827e1-c090-4643-9548-4671e86848c7.jsonl`

The exact title is 81 characters:
`<skills_instructions> Skills are sets of instructions stored in SKILL.md files. …`
It contains neither `</available_skills>` nor the user's prompt.

## Symptoms

- Resume row shows identity, timestamp, and cwd but no useful subject.
- The same adapter-backed session listing shows the same failure for DeepSeek/GLM inject-mode sessions.
- Complete Codex titles can be normalized because their injected catalog and user text are present; this truncated adapter title cannot.

## Root cause

`/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/src/session.rs:553-578` derives the title from the first user message and truncates it to `MAX_TITLE_LEN = 80`, appending `…`.

LouiseLM `/home/lotso/code/louiselm/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` builds injected prompt content with the skill catalog before AGENTS context and final user text. Therefore the adapter's first-user-message title is consumed entirely by the catalog. LouiseLM's current normalization intentionally omits an injected title when the closing catalog marker is absent, because the subject is unrecoverable.

## Why it was not caught

The closed `louiselm-vns4` work added coverage for complete injected titles and truncated/unrecoverable titles, but did not cover the adapter's 80-character first-message title policy at the adapter boundary.

## Fix direction

The narrowest durable fix is at the adapter/title boundary: derive the session title from the actual user request rather than the injected skill catalog, or provide a title/subject field independent of the prompt content. Reordering LouiseLM's injected content is a possible workaround but changes prompt ordering and should not be selected without testing model behavior. Picker parsing alone cannot reconstruct a subject that is absent from the ACP payload.

## Acceptance

- A regression test proves that a first turn containing injected skill context and a user request produces a title containing useful user-request text in `session/list`.
- The LouiseLM resume row for `session-7042e674-d0c9-4f03-81ef-5c46171d50b7` (or an equivalent fixture) displays a useful subject after cwd.

## Not covered

This diagnostic did not modify the adapter or LouiseLM code and did not run the adapter test suite. The adapter fix may belong in `/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter`.

title: Production relay Disposal fails cleanup proof in CI
description:
GitHub CI fails in the skills-core production relay cleanup gate on main.

## Observed
2026-09-07, run 34142936852, job 101808716082, commit df353e3ef623c3674d8f441fda40ae5645f69737:
https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/34142936852/job/101808716082
Step: Test production relay cleanup with an open controller.
Exact log: thread 'launch_supervisor::system::relay_tests::disposal_closes_controller_io_without_prior_quiescence' panicked at src/launch_supervisor/system_relay_tests.rs:128:21:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: CleanupUnproven
Result: 1 passed; 1 failed; exit 101. The quiescence-first sibling passes.

## Symptoms
The direct-disposal test fails when it calls Disposal a second time; required CI is red.

## Root cause
Confirmed regression from 83f8236: SandboxedSession::dispose removes its cgroup after proving zero survivors. On the second call it treats the absent cgroup as a namespace-only Session, but cgroup-backed Sessions have no pinned namespace leader, so it returns CleanupUnproven. The relay test at system_relay_tests.rs:128 deliberately disposes again after the direct-disposal probe. The quiescence-first sibling calls process Disposal only once. The shared fix is sandbox.rs:802: remember successful cleanup independently of retained cgroup/namespace handles; mark completion only after proof succeeds.

## Why it was not caught
The a29a regression covered repeated namespace-only Disposal, but not repeated cgroup-backed Disposal. Ordinary relay tests skip real acceptance unless LOUISELM_REQUIRE_SYSTEM_RELAY=1. The new deterministic cgroup regression exercises the state loss without root or a delegated host cgroup.

## Fix direction
Keep successful Disposal state at the shared SandboxedSession boundary. Preserve whole-tree proof and retry after failure; retain both cgroup and namespace cleanup mechanics. No new dependency, unsafe code, skipped gate, or weakened cleanup error.

## Acceptance
- A regression fails for the same cleanup ordering before the fix and passes afterward.
- Both privileged production relay tests pass with controller input still open.
- All skills-core Rust gates pass.

## Not covered
No installed launcher authority changes or GitHub PR. Preserve unrelated dirty files in this shared tree.
close_reason: Preserve proven Disposal across cgroup release; failed cleanup stays retryable. Full Rust gates and both real privileged relay tests pass. Lesson: comment 1254. gate:skills-core/src/sandbox.rs:2447

First dispose succeeds. Root: sandbox.rs:889 takes cgroup after proof; :799 interprets None as namespace-only on repeat, but cgroup-backed Sessions never pin that leader. Regression introduced by 83f8236. Fix scope: preserve successful disposal state at SandboxedSession boundary; failed cleanup must remain retryable. Existing a29a no-cgroup proof stays enforced. Prior lessons: a29a comment 1243, mthx comment 1020.

Regression red in comment 1253; final full skills-core suite, fmt, Clippy -D warnings, Rustdoc -D warnings pass. Failed cleanup remains retryable and repeated failure still errors. title: Codex resume rows lose useful subject in inject mode
description:
## Observed

Screenshot captured 2026-08-24 at 09:55 local time: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_0955_1920x1200_1787558153.png. In the `:LouiselmResume` picker, the first three Codex rows end immediately after `cwd=/home/lotso/code/louiselm`, while Claude rows show useful subjects such as `Overview of available agent skills`, `Test prompt injection handling`, and `Review available agent skills`.

The current user configuration at `/home/lotso/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua:23-30` sets Codex `skills.policy = "inject"`; Claude has no agent override and therefore inherits the global native policy at lines 96-100.

## Regression / evidence

Before commit `1d4c235`, Codex rows displayed the injected title prefix, for example the prior screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_0937_1920x1200_1787557068.png` showed `<skills_instructions> Skills are sets of instructions stored in SKILL.md files...`, which was distracting but contained the prompt subject later in the same provider title. Commit `1d4c235` changed `discovered_session_summary()` at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:385-392` to omit any ACP title containing `<skills_instructions>` or `<available_skills>`. The result removes the entire title, including any useful user-task text after the injected catalog.

## Symptoms

- Inject-mode Codex sessions are indistinguishable by subject in the resume picker.
- Native-mode Claude sessions retain concise provider-generated subjects.
- Recency and cwd remain visible, but the row loses the most useful human-readable context.

## Root cause

Confirmed at the LouiseLM boundary: `Registry:discover_sessions()` calls ACP `session/list`; `Validation.discovery_page()` copies the optional provider `title` into `DiscoveredSession.title` at `lua/louiselm/session/validation.lua:182-215`; `discovered_session_summary()` then either renders or discards that one string. Inject mode makes the provider title include LouiseLM skill-instruction context. The current marker filter treats the whole title as unusable, and no separate subject field is retained. It is not yet confirmed whether Codex itself can provide a clean title or whether LouiseLM must derive one from persisted session content.

## Why it was not caught

The previous regression test asserted that a skill-marked title disappears entirely. It did not include useful user text after the injected catalog or assert that the subject survives. Existing ordinary-title coverage only exercises provider titles without the injected prefix.

## Fix direction

Preserve a concise subject for inject-mode sessions while hiding the injected catalog. Prefer a provider-native clean title if Codex can expose one; otherwise derive a bounded single-line subject from the user-authored portion of the persisted session data at the narrowest available boundary. Keep the full transcript and injected context intact. Compare Codex, Claude, and adapter-backed agents before choosing the fallback.

## Acceptance

- A Codex inject-mode fixture containing an injected skill catalog plus a user task displays the useful task subject after `updated=` and before `cwd=`.
- Claude native-mode rows retain their current useful subjects.
- Skill instructions and raw catalog markup are not displayed.
- DeepSeek/GLM/other adapter-backed sessions are characterized, with missing metadata handled without blank or noisy rows.
- Resume selection behavior is unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed the shared resume-picker formatter: strips complete injected skill catalogs and leading LouiseLM resource wrappers, retains recoverable user/provider subjects, orders rows as identity/updated/cwd/subject, and omits titles truncated inside hidden context. Regression failed before the fix and covers Codex, Claude, Copilot, and DeepSeek/GLM-style payloads. Focused chat suite 106/106; full MiniTest 470/470; stylua, lua-language-server, git diff check, and dependency-cycle check pass. Existing test-harness warnings remain non-failing and unrelated.

comments.author: codex/01a032b4-5f3c-7f33-bf49-e45d07092c2c
comments.text: Real ACP payload captured from `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/connections/c414dd81-1faa-485a-97f2-4b19612eef22.jsonl` confirms Codex `session/list` returns one `title` containing the complete `<skills_instructions>` + `<available_skills>` catalog, then `[@AGENTS.md](file:///...)`, then the user task. Claude native returns concise synthesized titles. Copilot prefixes the user task with `[Resource link: ...]`. The adapter-backed DeepSeek/GLM list payloads include both clean titles and titles truncated inside injected context, so no user subject is recoverable from those truncated entries. User clarified desired row order on 2026-08-24: identity, updated, cwd, then useful subject. Fix should normalize known leading LouiseLM context wrappers, preserve clean provider titles, and omit unrecoverable truncated context rather than inventing a subject.

title: Control broker
description: A dedicated unprivileged local service that decides Run policy, owns pending authorizations and canonical receipt bytes, and mediates Session capabilities without performing privileged launch mechanics.
design:
Established by the louiselm-ruxl grill-me and louiselm-ax-design-review, confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-09-03. Source Sessions: codex/01a067ef-6521-7ce2-8388-87f49972d615 and codex/01a0684c-d410-7292-97ff-4fdddeeff0e9.
Authority/startup refinement confirmed by the maintainer in louiselm-9onz on 2026-09-09; source Session codex/01a083f4-469e-7351-97fb-205f6aa39a6f.
notes:
Use Control broker for the unprivileged policy and durable-control authority. Distinguish it from the Launch supervisor, which executes privileged mechanics for one Session, and from capture-service, which owns Run projections and Attention items but cannot authorize, sign, or rewrite launcher outcomes.
V1 full Agent authority belongs to exactly one supervisor-authenticated Agent-runtime process. Session membership and ancestry confer no authority. Tools and internal helpers need explicit narrower grants; automatic delegation requires operator approval that already permits delegation, with scope, revision and expiry enforced. Agent exit revokes its channel and every delegated grant; replacement requires fresh authorization. Agent-originated requests on a tool's behalf remain Agent actions subject to its permissions, approvals and audit; isolation does not imply prompt-injection immunity.

title: Handoff provenance records a local session id, not the durable ACP identity
description:
A Handoff prompt is now recorded in the target Session transcript, but its provenance line names a
local, per-editor-instance identifier (`session-1`) instead of the durable `<agent>/<acp-session-id>`
identity. Exported transcripts therefore still cannot prove which source Session initiated a Handoff
once the editor restarts, which is the symptom louiselm-ac6z was filed to remove.

## Observed

Manual QA round 2026-08-25, build acb65c7, case 5.

Target Session claude/c91d8058-49da-44bc-8d03-568fe8213dbb.
Source Session codex/01a037a9-23d0-7fe2-9cb6-5fd1be5b84d2.
Log: /tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/c91d8058-49da-44bc-8d03-568fe8213dbb/log.jsonl

The Handoff reached the wire correctly. `session/prompt` at 06:47:20.904Z carried one 339-character
text block holding the reviewed source transcript, including the tester's manual edit:

    # louiselm session transcript

    - session: session-1
    - agent: codex
    - acp session: 01a037a9-23d0-7fe2-9cb6-5fd1be5b84d2

    ## User

    turn 1
    ...
    ## Assistant

    What should I tackle next?

    EDITED BY ME

So retention and edit fidelity both work. The defect is in the recorded provenance, not the payload.

## Symptoms

- The target transcript's Handoff entry renders `Handoff from Session: `session-1``.
- `session-1` is allocated per editor instance. After a restart it names a different Session, so an
  exported or archived transcript cannot resolve the source.
- The same rendered transcript header shows both forms side by side — `- session: session-1` and
  `- acp session: 01a037a9-...` — so the durable identity was available at the moment of recording.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2616 reads `local source_state = source_view.session:inspect()` and
line 2636 stores `source_session_id = source_state.id`. `state.id` is the registry's local counter,
assigned as `"session-" .. self.next_id` at lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua:206.

The durable identity is `report_id(state.agent, state.acp_session_id)`, which is exactly what
`Chat:session_id` returns at lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2873-2885 and what `:LouiselmSessionId`
copies. The Handoff path does not use it.

Note that `Chat:open_handoff` already accepts a `source_session_id` parameter, but it is used only to
locate the source view; the recorded value is recomputed from `source_state.id`. The sole caller at
line 1985 passes `view.session:inspect().id`, so both are local ids and switching to the parameter
alone would not fix this.

`Transcript:record_handoff` and `render_entry` (lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua:158-172 and
221-232) print whatever string they are given verbatim, so they need no change.

## Why it was not caught

The regression coverage for louiselm-ac6z asserts that a Handoff entry exists and carries *a* source
id. It does not assert the id's *form*, and the test constructs Sessions whose local id is the only
id available, so a local id satisfies the assertion. The bead's own Observed section used
`<agent>/<acp-session-id>` throughout, which is the shape a reader would expect.

## Fix direction

Record `report_id(state.agent, state.acp_session_id)` for the source Session, matching
`Chat:session_id`. Handle the case where `acp_session_id` is nil — a source Session that never
reached ready has no durable identity, and recording nothing is better than recording a local
counter that will be silently wrong later.

Rejected: keeping the local id and resolving it at export time. The mapping does not survive the
editor instance, which is the whole problem.

## Acceptance

- A regression test that fails while the local id is recorded and passes once the agent-scoped id is.
- A Handoff from a live Session renders `Handoff from Session: `<agent>/<acp-session-id>`` in both
  the target chat buffer and `:LouiselmToMarkdown` output.
- The rendered value matches what `:LouiselmSessionId` copies for the source Session.

## Not covered

- The exact rendered line was derived from the code path rather than read off the tester's screen;
  the wire payload above is direct evidence only for retention and edit fidelity. If the rendered
  line turns out to carry the agent-scoped form, close this as not reproducible.
- Handoff from a Session that has not yet reached ready was not exercised.
close_reason: Completed: Handoff provenance records agent-scoped ACP identity; 500 mini.test cases, StyLua, and lua-language-server pass.

comments.author: claude/edc00380-9cc9-438e-ad38-3bb929cdc43c
comments.text:
Reproduction confirmed from the exported markdown, not derived. The "Not covered" caveat in the
description is now closed: the rendered line does carry the local id.

Export: /home/lotso/code/louiselm/louiselm-session-2-20260825-084751.md, line 9.

    # louiselm session transcript

    - session: session-2
    - agent: claude
    - acp session: c91d8058-49da-44bc-8d03-568fe8213dbb

    ## User

    <sub>Handoff from Session: `session-1`</sub>

The file makes the defect self-evident: three lines above the provenance line, the same export
prints the durable identity of its own Session (`- acp session: c91d8058-...`). Both forms are
produced by the same render, and the Handoff entry picked the one that does not survive the editor
instance.

Adjacent observation, deliberately not filed separately because it shares this root cause: the
export filename is also built from the local id (`louiselm-session-2-...`). Two exports taken from
different editor instances can therefore carry the same name while describing different Sessions.
Worth folding into the same fix if the export path is touched; not worth a bead on its own.

Incidental and not a contract: in this instance the source ACP id is still recoverable, because a
Handoff embeds the source transcript's full header (`- acp session: 01a037a9-...`) inside the prompt
body. That is a property of Handoff payloads, not of the provenance field, and it would not hold for
any other consumer of `handoff_source_session_id`.

comments.author: copilot/1b49919a-7bb3-4249-b781-f5e494348443
comments.text: Regression coverage now requires Handoff provenance to be claude/source-acp rather than the registry-local source id, and verifies that a source without an ACP id submits the handoff without recording unstable local provenance. No broader rule change is warranted: this is a narrow Chat Handoff identity boundary.

title: blog/myst.yml + blog/blog.css: multi-post MyST site scaffold
description:
## Goal
A working MyST project under blog/, structured to hold multiple posts from the start, with a minimal starter stylesheet.

## Scope
- In scope: blog/myst.yml (MyST project/site config, article-theme base, discovers posts under blog/post-*/blog.md), a minimal blog/blog.css starter (just enough to prove the theme-attachment mechanism works — the real visual design is a separate, author-only task).
- Out of scope: the actual visual theme/branding (tracked in louiselm-0ee), any nvim-transcript-specific CSS (that ships alongside render-post.sh's output, not this scaffold).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `myst build --html` (or `myst start`) succeeds against the scaffold with zero or one placeholder post.
2. The project config is structured so adding a second blog/post-<name>/blog.md requires no myst.yml changes — multi-post support is real, not aspirational.
3. blog.css is attached and demonstrably affects the rendered page (not just present but unused).

## Testing
- Build smoke test: `myst build --html` exits 0 and produces output in the expected build directory — this is also what GitLab CI will run, so this test doubles as a CI dry-run.

## Notes
- This is the dependency root for the GitLab CI/Pages task — CI needs a buildable project to build.
- No dependency on the other tasks in this decomposition.
- Parent feature: louiselm-r1k.
close_reason: MyST scaffold implemented and verified: blog/myst.yml (pattern: 'post-*/blog.md' discovers posts with no per-post config change), blog/blog.css (wired via site.options.style, visibly non-default marker styling). Manually re-ran 'myst build --html' against the scaffold: exits 0, produces _build/html output. All 3 acceptance criteria met.

title: Rebind <leader>ll to <leader>le, add <leader>lT, propose full keymap coverage
description:
Two concrete rebinds plus a keymap-coverage proposal for `lua/louiselm/ui/keymaps.lua`.

## Concrete asks
- Rebind inline edit from `<leader>ll` to `<leader>le` (both `n` and `x` modes), freeing `l`.
- Add a new default `<leader>lT` -> `LouiselmInspectTool`.

## History check
Only one commit ever touched keymaps.lua (3860f29, "feat(ui): add default keymaps") -- it introduced the full DEFAULTS table in one shot, nothing has been renamed/removed since. The only mapping outside that table is a buffer-local `<leader>lB` for `LouiselmInspectBead`, installed ad hoc in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua` on the `louiselm-session` filetype autocmd (not registered/reset via `keymaps.lua`'s configure()/clear_installed(), so it's invisible to `:LouiselmDiagnostics`-style introspection of installed keymaps).

## Current DEFAULTS (unchanged letters)
lc Chat, ln NewSession, lr Resume, lR Resume!, ls SwitchSession(n)/SendSelection(x),
lN RenameSession, li SessionId, lI Inbox, lm ToMarkdown, lx CloseSession, lC Cancel,
lo SessionOptions, lp Permissions, lk PickSkill, lf PickFile, lb MentionBuffer.

## Proposed additions (no conflicts with the above or each other)
| Keys | Command | Mnemonic |
|---|---|---|
| `<leader>le` | LouiselmInline (moved from `ll`) | Edit |
| `<leader>lT` | LouiselmInspectTool | Tool |
| `<leader>lP` | LouiselmInspectProvenance | Provenance (`p` taken by Permissions) |
| `<leader>lB` | LouiselmInspectBead | Bead -- promote the existing ad-hoc buffer-local map into DEFAULTS so it's covered by configure()/clear_installed() like everything else |
| `<leader>lH` | LouiselmHandOff | Hand-off |
| `<leader>lF` | LouiselmForensics | Forensics (`f` taken by PickFile) |
| `<leader>lV` | LouiselmForensicsView | View |
| `<leader>lL` | LouiselmLimits | Limits |
| `<leader>ld` | LouiselmDiagnostics | Diagnostics |
| `<leader>lz` | LouiselmResumePark | cold-parked run ("zzz") -- weakest mnemonic of the set, open to a better letter |

## Deliberately left without a default keymap
The six capture/pairing commands (LouiselmCapture, LouiselmCaptureSetup, LouiselmCaptureStatus,
LouiselmCapturePair, LouiselmCaptureRevoke, LouiselmCaptureRetry) are admin/setup actions for the
mobile-pairing subsystem, not everyday chat actions. Forcing six more top-level `<leader>l*` binds
for rarely-used commands seems like the wrong default; leave them command-only unless usage data
says otherwise. Flagging so it's a conscious decision, not an oversight.

## Scope
Pure keymaps.lua table edit (plus promoting the InspectBead buffer-local map) -- no new commands,
no behavior changes to what each command does. Should be a genuine one-shot, no design doc needed.
Update tests/ui/keymaps_spec.lua and doc/louiselm.txt where they assert on `<leader>ll`.
close_reason: Rebound <leader>ll -> <leader>le, added <leader>lT and 7 more default keymaps (lP, lB, lH, lF, lV, lL, ld, lz) covering every previously-unbound louiselm command except the low-traffic capture/pairing admin group, which was deliberately left command-only. Promoted the ad-hoc buffer-local <leader>lB map into the DEFAULTS table. Updated tests/ui/keymaps_spec.lua and removed the now-obsolete tests/ui/beads_spec.lua case. Full mini.test suite green.

title: QA round: selected Evidence export acceptance
description:
# Manual QA review — selected Evidence export

Scratch for `louiselm-2or68`, manual acceptance of `louiselm-ucl1.2`. Do not commit.
The finished report will be archived in one `qa-round` Beads record, then this
file removed. No automatic upload or external publication is authorized.

**Build under test:** installed `f7a2163`, containing
`3d37a57 feat(forensics): export selected evidence`. Installed exporter,
redaction module, and command source match this checkout. Both
`:LouiselmForensicsView` and `:LouiselmForensicsExport` are registered.

## Scope

Exercise explicit selection and truthful output through the installed command,
real editor scheduling, and a private local destination. Use a synthetic
Forensics record, not real conversation logs or credentials. Forensics
collection itself is out of scope (`louiselm-cvv3` versus `louiselm-euxk`).

The automated suite already covers projection limits, malformed selections,
source races, symlinks, and cancellation. Do not repeat that matrix manually.
This round checks command integration, operator-facing success/refusal, and
the actual file artifact from the installed build. It does not certify real
peer collection or redaction of arbitrary data beyond the tested contract.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Export selected synthetic evidence and report a missing source | Passed — exactly four requested items, states exported/exported/exported/missing; no private markers; unchanged inputs; artifact 570 bytes, mode 0600 |
| 2 | Repeating export refuses to overwrite the existing artifact | Passed — human confirms refusal; output hash/inode/size/mode/mtime/ctime and both input hashes are unchanged |
| 3 | Remove private QA fixtures after acceptance | Passed — removed exactly the three validated synthetic files, then their empty private directory; no fixture views or disposable Sessions remain |

## Setup

Private directory: `/tmp/louiselm-evidence-qa.L102Jj`, owner `lotso`, mode `0700`.
The assistant created only these synthetic inputs, both mode `0600`:

- `record.json`: schema-version-1 record, fake subject and private markers,
  model `QA_PRIVATE_MODEL`, capability `load_session=true`, two source pointers.
- `wire.jsonl`: line 1 is unselected; line 2 is a synthetic `session/update`
  with fake private text, Session id, path, token, and unknown object key.
- `evicted.jsonl` deliberately does not exist. Its pointer models evidence
  that is no longer available; no actual source was deleted.
- `export.json` does not exist before the human command.

Live `Record.build` accepted the fixture. The first source exists and the
second is absent. No Agent Session or permission change is needed.

Input SHA-256 baselines:

```text
b7b83ae50481011419c32683840f22552c624ef91977535e1827d1115af0db85  record.json
e057d4f35af6ddcbfac1166104965e10a1b16e4a17aab8ec2cac7e6ddf7cd1c5  wire.jsonl
```

## Cases

### 1. Explicit selection, redaction, and unavailable evidence

Exercises `3d37a57`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua` and
`lua/louiselm/forensics/{export,export_format}.lua`.

The selected fields/range are intentional: the model string should be
redacted, the known capability boolean retained, only wire line 2 exported,
and the absent second source explicitly marked missing.

Run in Neovim:

```vim
:LouiselmForensicsExport /tmp/louiselm-evidence-qa.L102Jj/record.json /tmp/louiselm-evidence-qa.L102Jj/export.json observation:model observation:capabilities source:1:2:2 source:2:1:1
```

Wait for the completion notification, then tell the assistant. Do not rerun
yet. The fixture can also be inspected locally with
`:LouiselmForensicsView /tmp/louiselm-evidence-qa.L102Jj/record.json`.

Expect: the editor remains usable and the notification names the new output
and says to inspect item states. The artifact has four selections in the
specified order: three `exported`, then one `missing`. It is schema version 1,
kind `evidence_export`, redaction `structure-only-v1`, private mode `0600`,
and at most 256 KiB. Fake private values/keys are absent; only selected wire
line 2 appears. Missing evidence has no partial payload. Inputs are unchanged.

Failure signature: no completion, false all-evidence success, leaked canary,
unselected line included, wrong item states, unsafe permissions, or input edits.

### 2. No-overwrite refusal

After the assistant captures Case 1's output hash and file metadata, repeat the exact same
command, using the same existing `export.json` destination.

Expect: refusal that the destination must be new; the original artifact and
both input files remain byte-identical. Output inode and modification/change
timestamps must also stay unchanged, so an identical-byte rewrite cannot pass.
There must be no second successful
publication. This is an intentional failure case, not a product finding.

Failure signature: successful overwrite, altered original hash, or no
operator-visible refusal. Do not point the command at any real user file.

### 3. Cleanup

After acceptance, close any fixture view. The assistant will remove only the
validated files in `/tmp/louiselm-evidence-qa.L102Jj` and the empty fixture
directory. These contain no real data. Archive results, including hashes,
before deleting the scratch plan. No Session or permission cleanup is needed.

## Evidence checks

The assistant will inspect the exact `export.json`, not a newest-file match.
Its expected version, field names, and states come from the documented format
and existing passing exporter fixtures; live record validation and source
existence were checked before presenting the command.

```sh
jq '{schema_version,kind,redaction,items}' /tmp/louiselm-evidence-qa.L102Jj/export.json
stat -c '%a %s %n' /tmp/louiselm-evidence-qa.L102Jj/export.json
sha256sum /tmp/louiselm-evidence-qa.L102Jj/record.json /tmp/louiselm-evidence-qa.L102Jj/wire.jsonl /tmp/louiselm-evidence-qa.L102Jj/export.json
rg -n 'QA_PRIVATE_|QA_UNSELECTED_|/qa-private/' /tmp/louiselm-evidence-qa.L102Jj/export.json
```

The marker search should return no matches (exit 1). Check exact item counts,
selectors, line numbers, `missing` without payload, model `[redacted]`, and
capability `true` as well; absence of marker strings alone is not a full check.
Capture the export hash before the intentional overwrite refusal. The user
confirms visible notifications and responsiveness; filesystem checks prove
artifact content, bounds, mode, and immutability.

## Findings

None yet. The prior Handoff round is complete and archived in
`louiselm-61xhf`; its disposable Sessions are gone. Separate earlier startup
finding `louiselm-dtwil` remains outside this Evidence-export round.

## First export acceptance — 2026-09-15

title: State bucket security scan lacks reviewed exceptions
description: Adding the in-project OpenTofu state bucket makes Trivy 0.72 report GCP-0066 (no CMEK, LOW) and GCP-0077 (no legacy bucket access-log target, MEDIUM). Google-managed encryption is intentional to avoid a circular KMS bootstrap/recovery dependency, and the composition already enables allServices Data Access Cloud Audit Logs, which Google recommends over Storage usage logs. Without narrow documented exceptions the required tf-trivy job will fail.

Immediate failures are the two permission checks above in Google/MIUI setup. LouiseLM JVM/Robolectric gates cannot exercise this proprietary OEM secondary-user setup. Android reporting a maximum of4 users proves capacity, not a functioning enrollment wizard. Manual C10 in owner0 passed; it never required creating another user.

Maintainer reaches a usable isolated Android test app without the setup loop; exact APK/user or package identity recorded; original owner0 pairing/capture hashes unchanged; then C11 can establish a successful real baseline before key-mismatch/revocation tests. title: Cancelling a Codex turn kills the Session on null usage
description:
Cancelling an active Codex turn with <leader>lC produces Error: ACP session/prompt returned malformed usage and prevents further prompts in that live Session.

## Observed
codex/01a074b2-a152-70b1-81eb-21ed37d04e7d, 2026-09-06. /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a074b2-a152-70b1-81eb-21ed37d04e7d/log.jsonl:70 sends session/cancel; :72 receives session_info_update with _meta.codex.threadStatus.type=idle; :73 receives {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":10,"result":{"stopReason":"cancelled","usage":null,"_meta":{"quota":{"token_count":null,"model_usage":[]}}}}; :74 records process exit code 137, four milliseconds later. Connection: 8813f30a-263e-42d3-9015-6b517d6b62f5.

## Root cause
lua/louiselm/session/validation.lua:384 accepts absent Lua nil but rejects decoded JSON null (vim.NIL). lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:717 calls fail; :206 sets error, closes ACP client, and fails the prompt callback. A successful Cancellation therefore destroys the connection.

## Why it was not caught
tests/session/api_spec.lua covers omitted and populated turn usage, malformed counters, and Cancellation followed by Disposal; no captured cancelled response with usage:null. Prior louiselm-apxu fixed malformed usage_update notifications, a different boundary.

## Fix direction
Accept absent/null optional usage at Validation.turn_usage, consistent with other nullable optional fields. Preserve rejection of malformed non-null usage. Scope: lua/louiselm/session/validation.lua and tests/session/api_spec.lua; generated API docs if annotation prose changes.

## Acceptance
Regression replays observed cancel -> idle notification -> cancelled response with null usage through fast-event transport callback; exactly one turn_done and successful completion callback; Session returns ready, ACP process survives, next prompt completes on same Session. Maintainer confirms <leader>lC returns Ready and can prompt again.

## Not covered
Recovery of the already-killed connection has not been verified. Leave open pending live acceptance.

title: QA round: Provenance history and popup acceptance
description:
# Manual QA review — remaining Provenance acceptance

Scratch for the follow-up to `louiselm-p0kz`; do not commit. The finished
report will be archived in Beads and this file removed.

**Build under test:** `f7a2163`, including historical backlog/drift (`4605900`)
and loaded-popup resizing (`6f85702`). Installed Provenance UI and Vintage
sources match this checkout. No rebuild or new Agent Session is needed.

The earlier round already accepted resumed reasoning folds, Decision index
navigation, explicit missing evidence, and truthful recovery warnings. This
follow-up only covers the historical-state case and the popup-height finding.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Loaded Decision popup grows beyond its loading height | Passed — human reports the view looks fine; buffer 46 has 27 lines, window 1056 is 27 lines high and 100 columns wide |
| 2 | Historical backlog has a real reference, anchor state, and separate drift | Passed — live view shows closing ref `0c674ff`, 1019 historical issues, anchor `closed`, and separate drift: 5 added / 0 removed / 9 changed |

## Setup

- Use the current Neovim instance in `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`.
- Fixture: `louiselm-0dkrv`, “Decide overview behavior when focus moves to
  another Session.” It is already closed; do not edit or reopen it.
- BVR reports closing commit
  `0c674ff563c195b286ebfa313d01d4e094ac8e14`; Git confirms the object exists.
- The editor was 190 columns by 50 lines at preflight. The popup should grow
  to fit its loaded content, capped at editor height minus four lines.
- No permission-mode changes, phone operations, or generated work are involved.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Open `:LouiselmProvenanceDecisions`, not `:LouiselmInspectProvenance`.
  The latter opens ordinary issue Provenance and misses the Decision path.
- Historical fixture `louiselm-c274` currently has an empty closing commit in
  BVR output. It is not suitable for a positive historical-reference check.
- BVR collection can take several seconds. Seeing the immediate loading view
  is expected; report a persistent loading state instead of repeatedly opening it.
- Keep the loaded popup open so the assistant can capture its exact URI,
  contents, line count, and window height through the live Neovim socket.

## Cases

### 1. Loaded popup resizes

Exercises `6f85702` / `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:293`.

1. Run `:LouiselmProvenanceDecisions` and wait for the index.
2. Search `/louiselm-0dkrv`, then press Enter to finish the search.
3. With the cursor on that Decision row, press Enter again to open it.
4. Wait for `Loading Provenance evidence...` to disappear.
5. Leave the popup open and report whether it grew and remains readable.

Expect: the selected Decision opens immediately in a loading popup; the same
view grows when evidence arrives, up to the available editor height. Scroll
normally if the content exceeds that height.

Failure signature: completed multi-section content remains squeezed into the
three-line loading popup, opens the wrong Decision, or produces a duplicate
buffer-name error.

### 2. Historical anchor and later drift

Exercises `4605900` / `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua` and
`lua/louiselm/provenance/vintage.lua`.

1. In the same loaded Decision popup, scroll to `Historical backlog:`.
2. Check that the historical reference names the verified closing commit.
3. Check for the issue count at decision time and `anchor state: closed`.
4. Check that later differences appear separately as
   `since then: <N> added, <N> removed, <N> changed`.
5. Leave the popup open for evidence capture.

Expect: historical state is explicitly anchored to the closing commit, with
current-versus-historical drift labeled separately. Implementation, Sessions,
QA acceptance, and Forensics still render their available or unresolved evidence.
Exact drift counts are not frozen: other ongoing tracker changes may affect them.

Failure signature: the historical section is missing or unavailable despite
the valid fixture, has a different/empty reference, silently substitutes current
state for historical state, or omits the separate drift summary.

## Evidence check

Preflight used the same bounded history request as the production source:

```sh
bvr --robot-history --bead-history louiselm-0dkrv \
  --history-since 2026-08-10 --history-limit 500 |
  jq '.histories["louiselm-0dkrv"] | {status, milestones}'
git show -s --format='%H %s' 0c674ff563c195b286ebfa313d01d4e094ac8e14
```

These checks proved `closed` and a resolvable closing commit, not that the UI
has rendered historical evidence. After the human opens the view, inspect only
the exact buffer `louiselm://provenance/decision/louiselm-0dkrv` through `$NVIM`.
Capture its lines, `nvim_buf_line_count`, `win_findbuf` window height, and editor
height. A loaded popup should have height `min(line_count, editor_height - 4)`.
The live buffer proves rendered content and geometry; perceived readability,
focus, and visible loading-to-loaded behavior also require the human report.

## Cleanup when the round closes

The read-only Provenance popup was left open for inspection; the maintainer
can close it with `q` or Escape. There are no disposable Sessions, new issue
fixtures, permission changes, or external state to remove. Archive the final
report in Beads, link the original round, and delete this scratch.

## Reporting back

Say when the popup has loaded, whether it grew, and anything surprising. The
assistant will pull the exact evidence before deciding the verdict.

## Findings

No new product finding. Existing fixed items accepted by this follow-up:

- Original F3: `louiselm-7tvl`, loaded popup height, fixed in `6f85702`.
- Original Case 3: `louiselm-97qw` and `louiselm-8tzl`, historical evidence and
  snapshot access, implemented in `4605900`.

The previous Attention checks are complete: `louiselm-t6dy` is closed. Their
archive `louiselm-wg35o` remains open only because its separate, unverified
Codex startup finding `louiselm-dtwil` is still open; do not repeat those checks.

## Live acceptance — 2026-09-15

Maintainer: “it is open and fine it seems let me know.” Evidence was pulled
from the exact requested view in the current Neovim instance, not a fixture
renderer or a different Provenance object:

```text
buffer: 46
URI: louiselm://provenance/decision/louiselm-0dkrv
window: 1056, height 27, width 100
buffer line count: 27
editor: 190 columns, 50 lines
State: accepted
Status: closed
Historical backlog:
- ref: 0c674ff563c195b286ebfa313d01d4e094ac8e14
- 1019 issues at decision time
- anchor state: closed
- since then: 5 added, 0 removed, 9 changed
```

The loaded height equals `min(27, 50 - 4)`; the earlier three-line-height
failure is absent. Implementation and Session correlations also render.
QA acceptance and Forensics are explicitly unresolved, not silently omitted.
Focus was back in the coordinating chat at capture time; no claim is made
about transient focus or animation beyond the human's reported readability.

Why live QA was still necessary: automated geometry regressions do not prove
that the installed build resizes the real window after asynchronous source
collection. Synthetic history fixtures do not prove that this repository's
BVR closing milestone resolves to a usable historical snapshot. This run
exercised both actual boundaries. Historical drift arithmetic remains covered
by automated tests; this manual pass checked integration and presentation.

Recipe lesson: preflight a nonempty, resolvable closing SHA through BVR and Git
before choosing a positive-history fixture. Open the Decision index path and
capture its exact buffer plus window geometry. The lesson belongs with this
QA report; no standing instruction change is needed.

title: Monitor-watched CI pipeline never reports back: loop greps wrong status string, silently never exits
description:
Agent starts a Monitor background task to watch a GitLab CI pipeline, tells the user "I'll report back once it finishes," then goes silent. No automatic report ever arrives — the user has to interrupt and ask why. The agent then has to fall back to manual polling (TaskOutput / a fresh `glab ci list`) to discover the pipeline had actually already finished a minute earlier.

## Observed

Session claude/3869f178-9bdd-4a0f-981c-2b01567e1e60, workstream watching GitLab pipeline #38205 on oss-public/louiselm after pushing commit 60f1e0f. JSONL transcript: /home/lotso/.claude/projects/-home-lotso-code-louiselm/3869f178-9bdd-4a0f-981c-2b01567e1e60.jsonl, lines 217-250.

- line 225: first `Monitor` call fails: `InputValidationError: The required parameter 'description' is missing` — tool schema wasn't loaded yet (deferred-tool gotcha).
- line 231: second `Monitor` call succeeds:
  `command: "until glab ci list 2>&1 | grep -m1 \"38205\" | grep -qE \"passed|failed\"; do sleep 5; done\nglab ci list 2>&1 | head -4\necho DONE"`
  Task id `bfpnoyv8m` started. Tool result explicitly states: "You will be notified on each event. Keep working — do not poll or sleep."
- line 234: agent tells user: "Watching pipeline #38205 — I'll report back once it finishes."
- line 237: user, unprompted by any agent report: "it is ok, why didnt you report ? do you have a timer on this im interested"
- line 240-241: agent calls `TaskOutput` with `block: true, timeout: 30000`; gets `<retrieval_status>timeout</retrieval_status>`, task still `running`, 0KB output.
- line 244: agent's own diagnosis: "my loop only prints after it finishes, so it produces zero output while waiting... no notification fires until completion — bad design on my part."
- line 246: a fresh, unrelated `glab ci list` shows `(success) • #38205 ... about 1 minute ago` — i.e. the pipeline had already finished before the user even asked, but the Monitor task never fired, and per line 241 the task itself was still reported as `running`.

## Symptoms

- User sees the agent promise a follow-up report that never comes.
- Agent has no idea anything went wrong until directly challenged.
- `TaskOutput` on the still-"running" task shows zero bytes of output even though the real-world event it was waiting for had already occurred.

## Root cause

Two compounding issues, both in the ad-hoc shell command the agent wrote for the Monitor call (line 231), not in Monitor/TaskOutput themselves:

1. Vocabulary mismatch: the loop's exit condition greps for `passed|failed`, but `glab ci list`'s actual status tokens are `success`/`failed`/`running` (see line 222: "(running) • #38205"; line 246: "(success) • #38205"). "passed" never appears in glab's output, so `grep -qE "passed|failed"` never matches a successful run, and the `until` loop never exits.
2. Silent polling: because the loop body is just `sleep 5` with no `echo` per iteration, no stdout is produced while waiting. Monitor's notification model is stdout-line-driven ("each stdout line is a notification" per tool docs), so a loop that only prints after exiting produces zero notification events the entire time it runs — and since (1) means it may never exit at all, the agent can be left permanently un-notified for a background task the user is actively waiting on.

This is a structural risk, not a one-off typo: any Monitor loop that (a) greps a CLI's human-readable status words to decide when to stop, and (b) has no heartbeat output on each poll, is exposed to the same failure — wrong string guess -> infinite silent loop -> the "I'll report back" promise silently breaks with no error surfaced to agent or user.

## Why it was not caught

No fixture or convention exists for validating a Monitor loop's exit condition against a real sample of the target command's output before starting the loop. Nothing in the harness heartbeats a "still waiting, N minutes elapsed, last status: <X>" line if a Monitor task runs past some expected duration — the only way anyone finds out is if the user gets impatient and interrupts, as happened here.

## Fix direction

This is filed to track workflow/agent-behavior guidance rather than a single code fix, since Monitor/TaskOutput are harness tools, not code in this repo. Candidate mitigations, not yet chosen:
- Before starting a Monitor loop that greps a CLI's status output, run the command once first and eyeball/parse the actual token vocabulary rather than guessing (e.g. "passed" vs "success").
- Always emit a heartbeat line inside the loop body on every poll (e.g. `echo "poll: $(date +%s) status=..."`), regardless of match, so Monitor's stdout-driven notifications fire periodically even before the exit condition is met.
- Prefer a machine-readable/exit-code check (`glab ci status --live` exit code, or `--json` output field) over grepping human-facing status words, where the CLI supports it.
- Treat "I'll report back once it finishes" as a promise that needs a periodic self-check-in (e.g. re-poll via TaskOutput after N minutes) rather than pure trust in the notification firing.

## Acceptance

- Documented guidance (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md or session memory) on writing Monitor loops: verify the exit-condition string against real output first, and always heartbeat inside the loop.
- No fix in this repo's code is required; this bead's acceptance is the guidance existing and being followed in the next Monitor-based CI watch.

## Not covered

- The first-call InputValidationError (missing `description`, deferred-tool schema not loaded) is noted as compounding friction but is a separate, likely harness-level quirk, not part of this bug's root cause.
- Whether Monitor/TaskOutput's underlying notification plumbing has its own bugs is unverified — the evidence here is fully explained by the agent's own loop bug, so no harness defect is claimed.
close_reason: Documentation-only fix per bead's own acceptance criteria: guidance added to AGENTS.md.

title: Activated broker CI test exceeds its 240-second deadline
description:
The required `cargo (skills-core)` CI job fails because the activated Control broker lifecycle test exceeds its 240-second deadline. Observed once on main; repeatability and any production impact are unverified. Priority 1: the required CI check is red and later privileged gates are not reached.

## Observed

- Job: https://github.com/euri10/louiselm/actions/runs/35181117896/job/105073266193
- Run 35181117896, attempt 1; push to main at commit `46e003c06b1b53dcfba107c5deacee31989aafb5` (`feat(launcher)!: bind private Session inputs`).
- 2026-09-17, Ubuntu 24.04.5 / ubuntu-latest, Rust 1.97.1, `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/tmp/louiselm-skills-target`.
- Failed step: `Test measured Agent and isolated tool grants`.
- Evidence retrieval: `gh run view 35181117896 --repo euri10/louiselm --job 105073266193 --log-failed`.

Exact selected log lines, with the repeated job/step prefix omitted:

```text
2026-09-17T04:23:26.1954185Z running 1 test
2026-09-17T04:23:59.1616533Z daemon: ready
2026-09-17T04:24:26.1957244Z test launch_supervisor::system::installed_tests::daemon::privileged_activated_daemon_serves_launches_and_restart has been running for over 60 seconds
2026-09-17T04:25:14.6067122Z daemon: first launch
2026-09-17T04:25:25.9522391Z daemon: concurrent sibling launch
2026-09-17T04:26:30.1759430Z louiselm-control: Attention delivery available
2026-09-17T04:27:17.1196288Z louiselm-control: installed broker authority is invalid
2026-09-17T04:27:21.6933307Z louiselm-control: broker state identity changed; preserve state and explicitly run louiselm-control adopt-state
2026-09-17T04:27:26.2360962Z ##[error]Process completed with exit code 124.
```

## Symptoms

The daemon test is killed after approximately 240.04 seconds without a test result or Rust panic. Earlier measured tool lifecycle, grants, installed launch/effects, receipt history/revocation/cleanup, and socket activation cases passed. The ordinary Rust tests also passed. The remainder of this step and subsequent privileged launch composition, measured Bubblewrap rejection, installed release and launch registry steps are not executed.

## Root cause

Unknown. At the failing commit, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:505` invokes this test under `timeout 240`; exit 124 and the elapsed time establish that deadline as the immediate failure boundary.

`skills-core/src/launch_supervisor/installed_daemon_tests.rs:236` defines the combined lifecycle test. Its late negative cases deliberately reject state permissions and a changed identity (`:474`, `:483`), then call `adoption()` (`:495`, definition `:517`). The final logged refusal is consistent with reaching that late phase, but does not identify the operation active when killed. Those refusal messages alone are not proof of a product defect.

Hypotheses: accumulated runtime of installation, measured verification, launches, restart/upgrade and adoption exceeds the fixture-wide budget; or a late subprocess/IPC operation stalls. Phase timing and bounded subprocess diagnostics in a disposable guest must discriminate. All source locations above refer to `46e003c06b1b53dcfba107c5deacee31989aafb5`, not the changing worktree.

## Why it was not caught

The ordinary suite returns early from this test unless `LOUISELM_REQUIRE_CONTROL_DAEMON` is set (`installed_daemon_tests.rs:237`). The separate privileged CI gate did catch it, but sparse progress messages and captured adoption subprocess output do not distinguish a slow fixture from a stall. No local reproduction was attempted for this filing.

Prior lessons checked: closed `louiselm-cjpep` concerns a different launch callback timeout caused by full debug metadata; this job already uses its line-table mitigation. Closed `louiselm-k2sio` concerns supplementary-group validation and records a prior 106.87-second daemon test pass in Debian 13. Neither establishes the cause of this failure.

## Fix direction

Reproduce the exact test and CI build profile inside a disposable VM/private mount namespace. Add targeted phase timing if needed, identify the slow or blocked boundary, and fix that boundary while preserving real process, identity, durability and restart coverage. Do not infer that a larger timeout fixes the cause or weaken authority checks from this log alone.

After matching CI prerequisites and building all binaries plus the library test executable at the failing commit, the exact invocation from `skills-core/` is:

```sh
sudo env LOUISELM_REQUIRE_CONTROL_DAEMON=1 \
  timeout 240 unshare --mount --propagation private -- \
  /bin/bash -c 'umask 022; exec "$1" launch_supervisor::system::installed_tests::daemon::privileged_activated_daemon_serves_launches_and_restart --exact --nocapture' bash "$library_test"
```

Run this privileged fixture only in a disposable guest; it provisions accounts and installed system paths.

## Acceptance

- Preserve a reproducible pre-fix failure or measured evidence identifying the deadline/stall boundary; record why any proposed timing change is sufficient.
- The exact privileged daemon test completes successfully under the documented CI profile and bounded gate, preserving startup refusals, concurrent launches, durable restart, historical receipts, state adoption and authority checks.
- Run relevant regression coverage and the complete affected Rust/browser gates; verify the full hosted skills-core job passes, including the gates previously not reached.

## Not covered

Tracking only, as requested: no implementation, CI rerun, privileged local execution or live installation changes. Production behavior, recurrence, and whether the private Session input change caused the timing regression remain unverified. Leave open for diagnosis and a verified fix.

title: Cold-Park resume opens a blank Session history
description:
Cold-Park Run resume waits for ACP session/load to finish before attaching its chat view. Replay updates arrive during the load request, so no view listener exists and the resumed Session opens without its historical conversation. Agent-side data remains intact, but the operator loses the expected history in this resumed view.

## Observed

Code inspection on 2026-09-03:

- `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:290-335` emits `user_chunk`, `chunk`, thought, and tool replay events while `session/load` is pending.
- Ordinary `Chat:resume_session` calls `load_session` and immediately attaches the returned starting Session at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4228-4248`.
- Cold `load_cold_run` waits for the ready callback at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4295-4335`; the view is attached only after Run resume finalization at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4519`.
- `Chat:attach` installs the Session event listener at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3038`, after those replay events have already been emitted.

## Symptoms

- A cold-Parked Run reports that it resumed, but its chat buffer contains no replayed user or Agent history.
- The Session remains usable for new work, so the missing history can be mistaken for an empty conversation.

## Root cause

The cold-Park loader attaches presentation after asynchronous loading completes, while replay is delivered as transient Session events during loading. There is no listener or retained replay buffer during that interval.

## Why it was not caught

Cold-Park tests cover Run reconstruction and successful attachment after resume, but do not assert that ACP replay history is visible in the attached buffer.

## Fix direction

Install a temporary initial event listener through the existing `session.Options.on_event` boundary before starting `session/load`, then hand the retained/forwarded replay to the view without double delivery. Preserve the current rule that editor operations run only after scheduling. Do not add a second transcript store.

## Acceptance

- A captured-order regression emits replay updates before the session/load ready callback and cold-resumes the Run.
- The attached Session view shows each replayed user, Agent, thought, and tool update exactly once and in wire order.
- Live updates after attachment continue normally.
- Disposal or failed resume drops retained presentation work without touching Agent-side history.

## Not covered

The ordinary resume path already attaches before ready and is unchanged. No live cold-Park reproduction was performed in this inspection.

title: Prompt inactivity watchdog kills a Session waiting for a human permission answer
description:
The prompt inactivity watchdog counts time spent waiting for a *human*
permission answer as Agent inactivity. A Session with a permission picker open
and unanswered is killed, the turn is lost, and the ACP process is SIGKILLed.
The Agent was never stuck; it was blocked on us.

## Observed

2026-09-03, OpenCode Session `opencode/ses_f9a93a9f9ffeXz1SXPE1DLPAg3`, model
`opencode-go/glm-5.3`. Evidence:
`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ses_f9a93a9f9ffeXz1SXPE1DLPAg3/log.jsonl`
(3380 lines, `ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED=1`, unlimited retention).

- L7 `04:04:46.004Z` client sends `session/prompt`.
- L3366-3376 `04:06:39` - `04:06:42` two `bash` tool calls run and complete
  (`grep -rn "louiselm" ...`, `grep -n "codex" ~/.config/nvim/.../louiselm.lua`).
- L3378 `04:06:44.514Z` last `session/update`: `tool_call_update`
  `chatcmpl-tool-bedebab03551b987` (`read`) -> `in_progress`. This is the last
  frame that bumps `prompt_progress`.
- L3379 `04:06:44.515Z` `session/request_permission` id `0` for that same
  tool call, path `/home/lotso/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua`
  (external directory), options `once` / `always` / `reject`.
- The maintainer was reading another Session and did not answer the picker.
- L3380 `04:14:46.065Z` process exits `137`. LouiseLM reported
  `Error: ACP session/prompt made no progress within 300000ms`, then
  `Error: ACP transport is closed`.

Provider quota is ruled out for this occurrence: the maintainer checked
OpenCode usage and was nowhere near a limit. This is not louiselm-5zhl.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:225` — `prompt_active` deliberately
includes `waiting_permission`, so the watchdog keeps running while a
permission picker is open. `schedule_prompt_timeout` (line 232) only renews on
`prompt_progress`, and `prompt_progress` is bumped exclusively by
`agent_message_chunk` / `agent_thought_chunk` / `tool_call` /
`tool_call_update` session updates (line 292-300). A pending
`session/request_permission` is a JSON-RPC *request*, not a `session/update`:
`handle_request` (line 505-541) queues it and never touches `prompt_progress`.

So a correctly-behaving Agent that asks for permission and waits emits nothing
further by construction, and the watchdog reads that silence as a hung peer.
There is no liveness risk in this state — the client itself holds the pending
request, so it knows exactly who is blocking.

Secondary, same mechanism: the reported figure is wrong. Renewal schedules a
*fresh* full 300000ms window at expiry rather than measuring since the last
progress, so actual idle time before the kill was 481.55s (04:06:44.514 ->
04:14:46.065; first window expired 04:09:46, was renewed, second expired
04:14:46). The message claims 300000ms. Any user timing this against their own
clock will not reproduce the number.

## Why it was not caught

louiselm-2p53 fixed the absolute-deadline bug by renewing on Agent-side
progress. Its regression fixture (`tests/session/api_spec.lua:2093`) replays a
completed tool and proves the turn survives. No test models the third state:
prompt active, Agent deliberately silent, decision owed by the human. The
louiselm-5zhl case that motivated the bound streamed non-progress updates, so
"silence means stuck" was never separated from "silence means waiting on us".

## Fix direction

Fix at the shared Session lifecycle boundary. While a permission decision is
outstanding (`permission_active ~= nil` or `#permission_queue > 0`) the prompt
inactivity watchdog must not fail the Session — suspend it and resume on the
answer, rather than papering over it by bumping `prompt_progress` from
`handle_request`, which would grant one free window per request and still kill
a picker left open past it. Keep the louiselm-5zhl bound intact for the case
with no outstanding permission. Decide separately whether a human-owned
decision deserves any bound at all; if it does, it is a distinct contract with
its own message, not this one.

Also make the failure message state the real idle duration, or state the
renewal window honestly.

## Acceptance

- A regression fixture derived from this trace fails before the fix: prompt
  active, `session/request_permission` outstanding, no further updates, both
  windows elapse.
- A Session with an unanswered permission picker stays alive and usable, and
  answering it lets the turn continue to its terminal response.
- A prompt with no outstanding permission and no progress still fails once,
  closes resources, and calls the prompt callback at most once.
- The reported duration matches the observed idle time.

## Related

- louiselm-2p53 introduced the renewal this bug sits on top of.
- louiselm-5zhl introduced the bound.
- louiselm-gf9a is a different permission/lifecycle defect (stuck `prompting`
  after answering).

title: Five-minute inactivity watchdog terminates Sessions during connectivity interruptions
description:
An in-flight Codex Session is failed by LouiseLM's fixed five-minute progress watchdog during reported intermittent Wi-Fi. The maintainer expects the same Session to tolerate interruptions and continue when connectivity recovers, and asks to rethink this policy. P1: the core conversation is terminated, with no configurable prompt-timeout escape hatch in the current Session options.

## Observed

Reported 2026-09-10 in `codex/01a089d3-192a-7091-8a22-8ee9d0da45fd`:

> Error: ACP session/prompt made no progress during a 300000ms watchdog interval

Maintainer reports bad Wi-Fi while TCP is otherwise working. Network causality and upstream connection continuity are not independently established. The exact watchdog text was also found in the live Neovim chat buffer `louiselm://session-1`, line 167.

Primary ACP evidence: `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a089d3-192a-7091-8a22-8ee9d0da45fd/log.jsonl` (UTC; inspected metadata only):

- Line 340, 05:46:23.021: client sends `session/prompt`, request id 11. No terminal response for id 11 appears before exit.
- Lines 666-667, 05:50:11.030-031: last `agent_thought_chunk` progress.
- Lines 668-669, 05:55:45.720: Agent sends `usage_update` and account-limit notification after more than five minutes without prompt progress.
- Lines 670-673, 05:56:05.835-17.874: account-limit read requests 12 and 13 receive successful responses. The ACP peer remains responsive shortly before termination; prompt silence is not proof that the whole peer is dead.
- Line 674, 05:56:23.050: proxy records exit code 137. This is ten minutes after prompt dispatch, consistent with one progress-window renewal and expiry of the next silent window. The exit code alone does not prove which process delivered a signal.

## Symptoms

- A temporary interruption can end the live Session instead of leaving it available to resume.
- The user sees a fatal watchdog error despite successful ACP control responses immediately beforehand.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:115` hard-codes `DEFAULT_PROMPT_TIMEOUT_MS = 300000`. `schedule_prompt_timeout` at line 301 compares a prompt-progress counter once per interval and calls `fail()` when it is unchanged, except while permission decisions are pending. This is window sampling, not an exact timeout measured from the latest message.

Progress classification at `lifecycle.lua:439` counts message/thought chunks and tool calls/updates; usage and account-limit traffic do not count. `fail()` at line 261 marks the Session `error`, records a failed outcome without a peer response, and closes the client. `lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:341` delegates close to `lua/louiselm/acp/transport.lua:207`, which closes stdin and sends SIGTERM.

The confirmed policy defect is treating a silent progress window as sufficient reason for terminal Session teardown. Whether this particular prompt would have recovered on restored Wi-Fi remains unverified; no controlled interruption was performed.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/session/api_spec.lua:2764` explicitly expects fatal failure for a silent prompt. Nearby regressions preserve turns with tool progress and suspend expiry during human permission waits, but do not cover prolonged recoverable network silence followed by normal completion, including a peer still answering unrelated requests.

## Fix direction

Revisit the shared Session watchdog policy so temporary loss of prompt progress can remain recoverable and operator-controlled. Decide the default waiting behavior and whether a configurable timeout/disable option or a nonfatal inactivity state is needed. Raising the fixed constant alone moves the same failure boundary. Preserve visibility and operator cancellation for genuinely stalled work, explicit transport/process/protocol failure handling, and existing permission-wait behavior. Do not automatically replay a prompt or its tool side effects after interruption.

Related prior art, not blockers: `louiselm-2p53` changed an absolute timeout to progress-window renewal; `louiselm-watchdog-kills-pending-permission-lg95` protects human permission waits; `louiselm-5zhl` introduced the watchdog for an unresolved OpenCode quota failure; `louiselm-ygtu` later fixed quota propagation and records why silence alone does not establish a terminal provider failure.

## Acceptance

- Deterministic regression: an active prompt survives more than a full 300000ms silent watchdog window with no terminal peer error, then accepts resumed progress and exactly one terminal response in the same Session. Include both fully silent and control-responsive peer cases.
- Waiting remains visible and cancellable; cancellation/disposal and genuine terminal errors still finish at most once, and late callbacks cannot revive disposed state or duplicate prompt/tool execution.
- Preserve active-progress and human-permission-wait regressions and configured auto-approval behavior.
- If configuration is introduced, cover the unset default, verify the maintainer's effective configuration, and update the schema, generated types and public docs.
- Live acceptance: maintainer confirms that the reported interruption scenario can exceed five minutes, recover, and continue the same Session without this fatal watchdog error. Keep the bug open until that confirmation.

## Not covered

Filed for policy reconsideration; no implementation requested or performed in this filing. Upstream TCP/HTTP reconnection behavior and the exact cause of the silent interval are unverified. This record does not promise recovery after genuine remote Session loss or change provider retry semantics.

title: Grok ACP requires approval for every trusted tool call
description:
The LouiseLM Grok Agent configuration does not enable Grok's documented always-approve/yolo permission mode, so multi-tool work requires approving each read, search, fetch, and command individually. This makes Grok's ACP integration impractical for trusted local automation and directly blocked the x_search workflow.

## Observed

- Grok documentation: /home/lotso/.grok/docs/user-guide/15-agent-mode.md
  - Agent mode documents: grok agent --always-approve stdio.
  - The option table says --always-approve is an alias for --yolo.
  - ACP session metadata documents _meta: { yoloMode: true } on session/new.
- Grok permissions documentation: /home/lotso/.grok/docs/user-guide/22-permissions-and-safety.md
  - Always-approve is the documented automation mode.
  - It remains subject to deny rules and hooks.
- LouiseLM dotfiles configuration: /home/lotso/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua:121-128
  - Current command is acp-proxy -- grok agent stdio.
  - No --always-approve or --yolo argument is present.
- Live ACP connection for Session grok/01a05666-bf8c-7c02-b6f5-e14e3f6c8726:
  - Connection log: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/connections/b43ab2ab-28f9-4557-b31b-330af82b7708.jsonl
  - line 4 session/new params contain only _meta.claudeCode.options.thinking; no _meta.yoloMode.
  - The Session emitted permission requests for web_fetch, run_terminal_command, and other tool calls at session log lines 392, 402, 533, 578, and 588.
  - Session log: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a05666-bf8c-7c02-b6f5-e14e3f6c8726/log.jsonl.
- The same x_search attempt required repeated manual interaction and ultimately exhausted quota; see related louiselm-bvo5.

## Symptoms

- Trusted Grok ACP sessions pause for explicit approval on every external fetch, shell command, or other non-read-only tool.
- The user must repeatedly select allow-once/allow-always while using a session.
- Tool-heavy workflows can stall, invite accidental inconsistent approvals, or consume model quota while waiting.
- The configured Grok Agent does not match Grok's documented automation setup.

## Root cause

Confirmed configuration omission: the dotfiles Grok command does not pass --always-approve/--yolo, and LouiseLM's Agent definition provides no Grok-specific options._meta.yoloMode for session/new. The ACP client already threads Agent options._meta through session creation; the missing value is in the Grok Agent configuration, not the generic permission request transport.

## Why it was not caught

The adapter matrix tested prompt rendering and normal completion, not a multi-tool Grok run. Those cases did not exercise repeated permission requests. No configuration regression asserts Grok's argv or session/new metadata against the documented always-approve contract.

## Fix direction

Use one documented mechanism at the configured Grok boundary: add --always-approve to the Grok agent command, or set Grok's session/new metadata to _meta.yoloMode=true. Prefer the mechanism that keeps the setting explicit in the LouiseLM Agent definition and preserve Grok deny rules/hooks as the hard safety boundary. Do not weaken generic ACP permission handling or silently auto-approve other Agents.

## Acceptance

- A Grok Session started from the configured LouiseLM Agent runs trusted tool calls without repeated permission prompts.
- A regression asserts the selected always-approve mechanism is present in the launched command or session/new params.
- Deny rules and hooks remain effective.
- Codex, Claude, and OpenCode permission behavior is unchanged.
- Manual Grok verification completes a bounded run_terminal_command (pwd) plus builtin web_search probe without per-call approval prompts. Maintainer approved replacing unavailable x_search on 2026-09-06; x_search remains separate work (louiselm-bvo5).

## Not covered

- No change is made to the dotfiles configuration in this filing.
- The correct policy choice between command-line --always-approve and ACP yoloMode is not yet selected.
- This does not claim that all Grok automation should bypass permissions; the setting is intended for this explicitly trusted local Agent configuration.
- louiselm-bvo5 tracks the separate rate-limit/runaway-search failure.
