description:
# Manual QA — stale Run Park Attention

Active scratch plan for `louiselm-t6dy`. Human drives Neovim and the phone;
assistant collects pinned evidence. Recovery round is archived as
`louiselm-6ukz9`; its fixture is closed and no QA Session remains attached.
Archive this new round into one qa-round chore and delete this scratch file
when complete; do not commit it.

## Build and acceptance

Capture-service fix: `f7a2163`, following plugin commit `9b893f3`. Source and release build
are complete, with 89 Rust tests, formatting, Clippy and Rustdoc green. Seven
new tests cover resume/restart, expiry/disposal, valid return-to-Park, retained
eligibility, unknown authority, malformed state and the blocking-I/O boundary.
No Lua/Android implementation or permission settings changed; no new dependency.
Release executable SHA256:
`69eddebdfd60adedf2b5b0b9916ab6afc02076b6bf676b82ba1ef8d3db24d2c3`.

Before implementation, acceptance was recorded in t6dy comment1811: old local
Park items disappear after resume or expiry/disposal; valid Parks and unrelated
broker conditions remain, with unchanged inactivity eligibility. The physical
inbox, not merely agreement between two server views, must be checked.

## Status

| Case | State |
| --- | --- |
| 0. Install/restart capture-service | Passed: operator approved; PID2490878 active/running, process and installed binary match release SHA256 |
| 1. Existing disposed Run disappears | Passed: user confirms gone after phone Refresh; server remains generation489, zero unresolved items |
| 2. New valid Park remains visible | Passed: user confirms visible after phone Refresh; same Run remains cold_parked/revision3 with matching generation494 Attention |
| 3. Cross-editor resume removes that exact Park | Passed: new editor2516148, exact Run active/revision5, loaded QA current_turn0; Attention generation496 empty and user confirms phone has nothing needing attention |

## Setup and safety

Pre-install service was active, PID2418551, started2026-09-15 09:10:14 CEST.
Previous executable was `/home/lotso/.local/bin/louiselm-capture`, SHA256
`4231b49be4eec7f16c5a04eaec50d02bdd72afca71640275a2912a582cecf283`.
Do not run the new binary against live state before installation approval:
Attention reads intentionally reconcile and persist stale-condition removals.
After approval, replace the executable recoverably and atomically, restart only
`louiselm-capture.service`, and verify the running executable hash and new PID.
Do not clear the inbox, delete Run records, alter pairing, reinstall the APK,
or touch capture recordings. No unrelated Android capture/pairing QA is needed.

Installation completed after the user's explicit approval: atomic replacement
and restart on2026-09-15 10:13:13 CEST. New PID2490878 is active/running,
Result=success, NRestarts=0; `/proc/2490878/exe` and the installed path both
hash to the release SHA256 above. Rollback copy:
`/tmp/louiselm-attention-install.kBGu5a/louiselm-capture` (old SHA verified).
The same private temporary directory contains `attention-before.json` as
pre-install evidence, not a file to restore over newer Attention changes.
No Run record or capture recording was deleted. Keep these two QA artifacts
until live acceptance; they are temporary and may not survive reboot.

## 1. Existing stale condition

Exact local Run: `6cd3acf4-2756-4806-9538-aa6041c71eaa`.
Before fix: Attention generation488, kind=run_parked, eligible=true,
source_operation_id=`a5cec8aa-441f-4afa-b7c0-7b26efc21ba9`,
created_at_ms1789458050000. Durable Run is disposed/revision6,
park_expires_at_ms1789458488868. This is a safe captured structural fixture,
also encoded in `capture-service/tests/attention_runs.rs`.

Server result after restart, before invoking a new CLI snapshot: direct state
inspection shows generation489 and items[]. The updated CLI agrees, reports
zero unresolved items, and no exact stale Park. Service remains active.
This establishes receiver-side reconciliation; it does not establish the
physical inbox. `adb devices -l` currently reports no attached devices, so
APK/build identification is unavailable and the phone result is human-only.

Physical checkpoint passed: user reports "gone" in response to the phone
Attention inbox Refresh instruction. Follow-up CLI remains generation489 with
zero unresolved items and no matching stale Park; service PID2490878 is still
active with NRestarts=0. This accepts the disposed-Run disappearance case, not
yet the valid-Park or cross-editor resume cases.

After the updated service is verified, open Android Attention inbox and Refresh.
Expect this exact old Park card to be absent; other unresolved cards may remain.
Failure signature: a successful refreshed inbox still shows that Run as Parked.
Pin the installed APK/build if device inspection is available; otherwise record
that phone confirmation is human-only. Do not infer absence from a refresh error.

Evidence: project this exact subject from `louiselm-capture attention list`;
compare with the safe durable Run projection and the human's phone report.
CLI absence alone is not physical inbox acceptance.

## 2. Preserve a valid Park

Create one fresh disposable configured codex Session, send
`Reply only ATTENTION-QA-READY`, and wait for completion. Report ready here;
the assistant pins its ACP ID before proceeding. Park it with `:LouiselmPark`
and report parked. The assistant pins its exact durable Run and confirms an
unexpired Park plus a matching Attention item. Leave Neovim inactive for over
30 seconds, then Refresh the phone inbox. Expect the new Park card to remain
visible. Failure signature: reconciliation removes a valid Park, or eligibility
is forced true while the editor is active. Preserve the fixture for case3.

Fixture-creation baseline: complete Registry contains only coordinator local
session-1, ACP `01a0a3e7-1523-74d2-b85f-ce98fd86fe51`. Create the fresh codex
Session using `:LouiselmSessionNew`, send the marker prompt, then return here
and report ready after completion. Leave it open and do not Park before the
assistant identifies the exact new ACP Session and checks its ready state.

First fixture did not reach the case: live local session-3, ACP
`01a0a424-0de4-70d2-a27e-ab915b83af5e`, is new/error/current_turn1 with no
owner Run. Chat buffer144 line14 says "Error: Codex agent reported a system
error for this turn". Pinned proxy log under that ACP ID records prompt4 at
08:17:06.361Z and process exit code137 at08:17:08.010Z; no completed marker
reply/end_turn. No OOM cause is established: journal visibility is restricted.
Filed separately as `louiselm-dtwil`; no Attention implementation change.
Attention generation490 contains its valid session_failed item, not a Park
alert. Do not count that different card as recurrence of t6dy.

Retry instructions: close only the errored QA Session through
`:LouiselmSessionClose`, create one fresh codex Session, repeat the exact marker
prompt, and report ready only once the assistant marker has appeared and the
turn has completed. Do not Park first. Preserve the failed Session log.

Service recheck: active PID2499613, started10:16:46 CEST, NRestarts0. This is
not the earlier install PID; the cause of that restart is unknown. Process and
installed hashes still match the verified f7a2163 release, so no build drift
was observed. Do not attribute it to this fixture failure without evidence.

Retry checkpoint passed without another code change: new codex ACP
`01a0a428-2a23-7213-8cd0-47bd5f2555dd`, local session-5, is ready/new/current_turn1,
supports loadSession, and has no owner Run. Prompt4 completed with end_turn
at08:21:37.347Z; buffer172 contains one exact assistant ATTENTION-QA-READY marker
at line14. Pinned log:
`/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a0a428-2a23-7213-8cd0-47bd5f2555dd/log.jsonl`.
Complete Registry now contains only this retry and the coordinator; failed
session-3 is gone. Attention generation491 has items[], so its session_failed
condition also cleared. Service PID2499613 remains active/NRestarts0.
Park checkpoint passed after the user reported parked: exact Run
`0de0f45d-03c9-4b25-9f72-aa32c5bed3fe` is cold_parked for this same ACP Session,
expiry1789547026431. Claims[], generated_work ceiling1/consumed0/reserved0,
pending[]/outputs[]. Local session-5 remains ready/new/current_turn1 and owns
the same parked Run. Attention generation494 contains exactly its run_parked
condition, source operation `5dc2146b-8476-404d-b6d6-5357a54efd26`,
created_at_ms1789460626000, eligible=false while the editor is active. This
proves reconciliation retains a valid Park without forcing delivery eligibility.
Durable path:
`/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm/workflow/runs/0de0f45d-03c9-4b25-9f72-aa32c5bed3fe.json`.

Physical valid-Park checkpoint passed: user reports visible after the requested
phone Refresh. Follow-up evidence still has the exact matching run_parked item
at generation494 and durable cold_parked/revision3, expiry unchanged. Eligible
is false when inspected after the user returned to Neovim; phone visibility
does not prove push delivery or that eligible=true was observed during inactivity.

Pre-restart socket: `/run/user/1000/nvim.2464255.0`. Complete Registry contains
coordinator session-1 and QA session-5, which remains ready/new/current_turn1
with this parked owner. Next is case3; leave that QA Session attached until exit.

## 3. Cross-editor resume

After case2 evidence, quit Neovim normally without first closing the parked QA
Session. Reopen, resume only this coordinator via `:LouiselmResume`, then use
`:LouiselmResumePark` for Run `0de0f45d-03c9-4b25-9f72-aa32c5bed3fe`. Do not ordinary-load the QA
Session first, which would create a competing writer. Send no new QA prompt.
Refresh the phone Attention inbox and report whether that Run's old Park card
disappears; the assistant then checks the new editor, exact durable active Run,
loaded/ready QA Session and Attention state. A resume or refresh error is not a pass.
Failure signature: the card survives refresh or returns on a later observation.

Result passed: user reports "nothing needs attention on phone" after the
cross-editor resume/Refresh instructions. New socket is
`/run/user/1000/nvim.2516148.0`. QA is local session-2, same ACP
01a0a428-2a23-7213-8cd0-47bd5f2555dd, loaded/ready/current_turn0. Its owner
retains Run0de0f45d-03c9-4b25-9f72-aa32c5bed3fe, active, claims[], budget
ceiling1/consumed0/reserved0. Durable Run is active/revision5, expiry0,
resume_attempt.result=active, pending[]/outputs[]. Real load request2 at
08:27:18.564Z completed at08:27:18.784Z. No new QA prompt was sent.
Attention generation496 has zero unresolved items. Service PID2499613 remains
active/NRestarts0. This establishes cross-editor resume clearing at the server
and physical inbox, with successful cold reconstruction rather than a failed load.

All scoped behavioral cases passed. After the user reported done, complete
Registry inspection found only coordinator session-1. Attention remains
generation496 with zero unresolved items. Disposable QA Session cleanup is
verified; no fixture claim exists. Retain rollback files and failed-session
logs as documented evidence.

## Cleanup and remaining work

Failed fixture ACP01a0a424-0de4-70d2-a27e-ab915b83af5e has no Run or claims;
its Session closure and Attention clear are confirmed. Retry fixture
ACP01a0a428-2a23-7213-8cd0-47bd5f2555dd has been closed after live acceptance.
Its durable Run0de0f45d-03c9-4b25-9f72-aa32c5bed3fe and peer history remain;
Session closure does not certify durable Run terminalization. No fixture claims
remain. All scoped t6dy acceptance is complete. Archive this report with reference
`codex/01a0a3e7-1523-74d2-b85f-ce98fd86fe51#attention`.

F2 `louiselm-dtwil`: fresh Codex Session failed before first reply; outside the
Attention fix, cause unconfirmed, not fixed. Parent this newly filed finding
under this round at archival; preserve t6dy's existing QA parent.

Why the suite missed t6dy: Attention and Run state had isolated store tests,
while editor-local clear callbacks did not survive an editor restart or see

condition was still true. The regression now combines real durable lifecycle
transitions with the captured local condition identity and exercises late writes.
The seven added tests and all89 capture-service tests/gates passed. Manual
acceptance adds the installed daemon, actual ACP reconstruction and phone UI.

No new finding was fixed silently: F2 remains a separate open defect despite a
successful fresh retry. No APK or permission configuration changed. The old

title: QA: capture restart, offline recovery and repeated sync
description:
# Manual QA — capture service recovery and phone sync

Completed 2026-09-15 at 07:39:33 CEST. All three cases passed. This final record
is archived in the Beads QA-round chore; the scratch file is removed afterward.

## Build and scope

- Receiver: `6719ebd`, fix for `louiselm-3cn9p`.
- Installed binary, release artifact and running `/proc/2332408/exe` matched
  byte-for-byte at 2026-09-15 07:32:19 CEST.
- Phone: use the same paired app that successfully uploaded the baseline below.
  Its installed APK version has not been independently identified. No Android
  build or installation is required for this receiver-only change.
- Scope: real hardened systemd startup, physical phone queue persistence,
  reconnect and repeated Sync actions. Existing automated coverage establishes
  policy rejection and identical-upload protocol idempotency; do not repeat
  those unit cases manually.
- Optional broker policy is absent. Configured broker deployment is outside
  this round and tracked separately in `louiselm-y2j3o`.

## Status

| Case | State | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0. Online capture baseline | Passed | Android `6b9a2705-e53c-4894-9df4-8be53f3035ad`; 3.939 seconds, recorded 07:25:30, audio received 07:25:35, transcription completed 07:25:37 CEST |
| 1. Receiver restart then phone capture | Passed | Android `3edab8fc-3f89-4c4f-b4c0-079bb20db919`; 3.994 seconds, recorded 07:34:22, transcribed 07:34:33 CEST; total 56 → 57, user reports pending 0; new PID 2343634 since 07:34:13, automatic restarts 0, HTTPS health ok |
| 2. Offline queue survives app termination and reconnect | Passed | User observed 1 pending after force-stop/reopen offline, then 0 after reconnect. At 07:36:59 CEST receiver had 57 captures and none matching `94ec`; at 07:38:32 it has 58, with exactly one matching Android UUID `94ecca01-452d-4c6d-aa7f-1c7b10507daf`, duration 5.619 seconds, 93177 bytes, transcription completed without error. Service active/running, automatic restarts 0. |
| 3. Repeated Sync does not create another capture | Passed | User reports still OK with no error after repeated Sync/reopen. At 07:39:33 CEST receiver remains at 58 captures, with exactly one `94ecca01-452d-4c6d-aa7f-1c7b10507daf`; its 93177 bytes and SHA-256 `7f2bf617dca2b783d4c623846ff12780794aaa1af6d3c4f60cbcced8df132d15` are unchanged. Transcription completed, no last error; PID 2343634 remains active/running, automatic restarts 0, HTTPS health ok. |

## Setup and baseline

Initial baseline: active/running, PID 2332408, zero automatic restarts,
certificate-verified HTTPS health `ok`, 56 captures.
After case 1: active/running, PID 2343634, zero automatic restarts,
certificate-verified HTTPS health `ok`, 57 captures.
Use short, non-sensitive QA recordings and run one case at a time. Avoid other
new recordings during a case so count comparisons are meaningful.

Keep existing pairing and recordings. Do not clear app data, reinstall the
phone app, revoke credentials or change the receiver key for this round.
If a dedicated LouiseLM QA app is already paired, identify it before switching;
switching apps changes the device and queue under test.

## Cases

### 1. Receiver restart then phone capture

Goal: prove the installed hardened service completes startup and accepts a
real phone capture after restart. Exercises `6719ebd`,
`capture-service/src/broker_attention.rs::load_installed`, and the installed unit.

1. While not recording, run in the laptop terminal:

   ```sh
   systemctl --user restart louiselm-capture.service
   ```

2. Wait 10 seconds. In the paired phone app, record about 5 seconds saying
   “QA one, receiver restart”, then stop. Observe the saved acknowledgement.
3. Tap **Sync now** if the queue has not already cleared.
4. Report the queue count, any error, and the saved capture UUID (or recording
   time if the acknowledgement has disappeared).

Expect: one durable new capture, phone queue drains, transcription completes,
service remains running without automatic restarts. Transcription completion
may lag upload; phone “synced” does not itself prove transcription completed.

Failure signature: service auto-restarts or exits; phone recording remains
pending despite restored connectivity; a saved recording disappears; more than
one receiver capture is created for this recording.

Evidence: service check and exact-UUID capture check below. Receiver evidence
proves server receipt/processing, while acknowledgement and phone queue are
human-observed facts.

### 2. Offline queue survives app termination and reconnect

Goal: exercise physical storage and WorkManager scheduling across app loss.
Exercises `MainActivity.kt`, `CaptureStore.kt`, `UploadWorker.kt` and the fixed
receiver. These Android paths are unchanged but are real consumers of the fix.

1. After case 1 passes, turn off both Wi-Fi and mobile data on the phone.
   Airplane mode alone may leave Wi-Fi enabled. Leave laptop connectivity on.
2. Record about 5 seconds saying “QA two, offline queue”, then stop. Wait for
   the saved acknowledgement; note its UUID and pending count.
3. Open Android Settings → Apps → the app you just used → **Force stop**.
   Do not clear storage. Reopen the app while still offline.
4. Verify the recording remains pending. Report this intermediate result before
   reconnecting; the assistant checks that its UUID is absent from the receiver.
5. Once that checkpoint is recorded, restore Wi-Fi/mobile connectivity and the
   existing private overlay/VPN used to reach the receiver. Tap **Sync now**.
6. Report whether pending returns to its earlier count and any error.

Expect: the same UUID survives force-stop and is received exactly once after
reconnect, with transcription eventually complete. The receiver count increases
by one for this case, assuming no unrelated capture occurred.

Failure signature: queue loses the saved recording, a different UUID replaces
it, reconnect requires re-pairing, the queue remains stuck after explicit Sync,
or more than one new recording appears on the receiver.

Evidence: pin the UUID before reconnect, verify receiver absence, then verify
one matching durable record after reconnect. Server evidence alone cannot
prove local audio preservation; record the phone observation explicitly.

### 3. Repeated Sync does not create another capture

Goal: check repeated physical UI actions after a successful sync.
Exercises `MainActivity.kt` Sync and `UploadWorker.kt` queue filtering.

1. After case 2 passes, make no new recording.
2. Tap **Sync now** three times, then leave and reopen the app.
3. Report its pending count and any error.

Expect: queue remains drained, existing capture UUIDs and receiver count stay
unchanged, and no error appears.

Failure signature: another capture appears without a new recording, an already
uploaded recording returns to pending, or the UI becomes stuck.

Evidence: compare receiver IDs/count and case 2 UUID before and after. This
does not prove a duplicate HTTP upload occurred: uploaded captures are normally
skipped. Actual same-UUID PUT replay is already covered by receiver tests.

## Evidence commands — assistant runs after each report

These checks were validated against the successful baseline capture.

```sh
systemctl --user show louiselm-capture.service \
  -p ActiveState -p SubState -p NRestarts -p MainPID
curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 5 --noproxy '*' \
  --cacert /home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm/capture/tls/receiver-cert.pem \
  --resolve louiselm-capture.local:7392:100.90.156.114 \
  https://louiselm-capture.local:7392/v1/health | jq '{status}'
```

Pass: active/running, automatic restart count unchanged at zero, health `ok`.
A manual restart changes PID; that is expected. Immediate systemd status alone
does not establish readiness.

For each case replace the baseline UUID below with its observed, pinned UUID:

```sh
louiselm-capture list | jq --arg id '6b9a2705-e53c-4894-9df4-8be53f3035ad' \
  '{total:length, capture:[.[] | select(.record.id==$id) |
    {id:.record.id,source:.record.source,duration_ms:.record.duration_ms,
     bytes:.record.bytes,sha256:.record.sha256,
     status:.state.transcription.status,
     last_error:.state.transcription.last_error,
     transcript_created_at_ms:.transcript.created_at_ms}]}'
```

Absence is an empty `capture` array. Receipt is exactly one matching Android
record; processing completion is `status: completed` with no last error.
Pin each UUID after resolving the reported time; do not keep using “latest”.
Do not print audio, transcript text, pairing data or credentials.

## Findings and cleanup

No new findings. Earlier startup defect `louiselm-3cn9p` is fixed in
`6719ebd`; optional configured-broker defect `louiselm-y2j3o` remains out of scope.

Phone connectivity was restored for case 2 and the receiver remains running.
QA recordings `3edab8fc-3f89-4c4f-b4c0-079bb20db919` and
`94ecca01-452d-4c6d-aa7f-1c7b10507daf` remain ordinary durable captures; nothing
was deleted from either device. No permission, pairing, credential or receiver
key changes were made. No new unresolved defects.

Why physical QA mattered: unit tests cannot establish this host's installed
systemd namespace, microphone capture, real app force-stop persistence, private
overlay reconnection or WorkManager/UI interaction. Those boundaries passed.
Repeated Sync verifies the UI/queue contract, not forced duplicate HTTP delivery;
same-UUID protocol replay remains covered by automated receiver tests. The
installed phone APK version was not independently verified. Optional configured
broker sandbox support and privileged VM acceptance remain outside this round.
close_reason: All three physical QA cases passed: service restart/upload, offline force-stop/reconnect, repeated Sync. User observations and pinned capture checks archived in description; 58 captures, checksum unchanged, zero restarts, HTTPS health ok. No new findings; scope and remaining broker limitation recorded. live:codex/01a0a37b-8369-7211-b930-d4082a8f035a

title: Run-budget parent and leaf mutually disappear from ready without a reported cycle
description:
## Problem

After maintainer-authorized release of stale Session claims, aggregate `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6` and leaf `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5` mutually block each other even though `br dep cycles` reports no cycle. The leaf therefore remains absent from `br ready`, and the aggregate can only be returned to `in_progress` with `--force`.

## Evidence

Observed on 2026-08-30 in Session `codex/01a0517b-2081-7ff1-b37d-9d03860da2aa` after clearing both stale assignees:

- `br blocked --json` reports `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5` blocked by parent `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6`.
- The same output reports parent `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6` blocked by leaf `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5`.
- `br dep cycles --json` reports zero cycles.
- `br ready --json` contains neither issue.
- `br update louiselm-qbr.3.2.6 --status in_progress --assignee "" ...` is rejected as blocked; adding `--force` succeeds but does not make the leaf ready.

The graph has a parent-child relationship between the two issues plus an explicit dependency requiring the leaf before the aggregate. The likely cause is that readiness treats the hierarchy edge as blocking in the opposite direction from the explicit dependency, while cycle analysis does not report that mixed-edge cycle. This is a hypothesis, not yet verified against `br` internals.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an aggregate parent and a child leaf.
2. Add an explicit dependency making completion of the leaf necessary for the parent.
3. Leave both issues unassigned and make the leaf otherwise ready.
4. Run `br blocked --json`, `br ready --json`, and `br dep cycles --json`.
5. Observe that parent and leaf block one another, neither is ready, and no cycle is reported.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The aggregate/leaf relationship has one coherent scheduling direction: a runnable leaf is not blocked merely because its aggregate parent remains open or in progress.
- `br ready` exposes `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5` once its real prerequisite work is complete.
- If a mixed hierarchy/dependency configuration can deadlock scheduling, `br dep cycles` or another validation command reports it explicitly.
- Normal status transitions do not require `--force` solely because of this mixed-edge deadlock.
- Regression coverage exercises the hierarchy-plus-explicit-dependency case.

## Not Covered

- Changing the implementation scope of either existing issue.
- Closing either issue.
- Revisiting the already completed stale-claim reconciliation.
close_reason: Removed the reciprocal parent-child edge while retaining the aggregate-to-leaf blocker. Verified leaf is ready, aggregate is blocked only by leaf, dependency cycles are empty, and the prevention rule is recorded in AGENTS.md.

Fix direction: remove the redundant parent-child edge and retain the explicit aggregate-to-leaf blocker, preserving completion ordering while making the leaf runnable. No br source change is in this repository.

title: acp-proxy never logs session/new, so construction-time params cannot be verified
description:
## Observed

Found on 2026-08-30 while trying to give `louiselm-5tuq` its Live acceptance (AGENTS.md section 5).

`acp-proxy` never records `session/new` in its per-session logs. Grepping every log under `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/` for `"method":"session/new"` returns nothing, across all sessions and all agents. `session/load` *is* recorded, because its request already carries a `sessionId` the proxy can file the entry under; a `session/new` request has no session id until the response, so it appears to be dropped rather than filed retroactively.

## Why it matters

Everything LouiseLM configures at session construction time travels in `session/new` params — `cwd`, `mcpServers`, and `_meta`. None of it can be verified after the fact.

This directly obstructed `louiselm-5tuq`. That bug was a fix that passed every automated gate while sending nothing on the wire, and the only way to distinguish "the metadata was sent and the model declined to use it" from "the metadata was never sent" is to read the request. For a new Session that read is impossible, so verification had to fall back on reading the installed plugin's source and reasoning about the code path.

A near-miss worth recording: grepping the logs for the bare string `summarized` produced apparent hits that were actually ordinary prose in session content, which reads as success. Structural greps (`"thinking":{...}`) are the only trustworthy form, and they cannot see `session/new` at all.

## Fix direction

Record `session/new` requests, buffering until the response supplies the session id if that is what filing them requires. A separate pre-session log keyed on the JSON-RPC request id would also work.

`acp-proxy` is not this repository, so this may be an upstream report rather than a change here. Filed regardless because the gap is in LouiseLM's ability to perform Live acceptance on anything configured at session construction, which section 5 of AGENTS.md requires for user-visible defects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A newly created Session's `session/new` request, including its full `_meta`, is readable from the proxy log afterwards.
- Existing `session/load` and `session/update` logging is unchanged.

## Not covered

Redaction policy, and any change to what LouiseLM itself sends.
close_reason:
Invalid as filed; no code change made. acp-proxy does log session/new — the premise was wrong because the search only covered ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/. Construction-time frames are written to proxy/connections/<connection-id>.jsonl, which src/logsink.rs:224-229 documents as 'the connection-scoped file used before a session id is known'. That is deliberate and correct: a session/new request carries no sessionId in its params, so the frame cannot be filed under a session that does not exist yet. src/proxy.rs:398-441 then correlates the pending request id with the response's sessionId and calls bind_session, after which traffic moves to the session file.

The linkage is discoverable in both directions. bind_session (logsink.rs:709) writes a session_bound record carrying the session id into the connection log, so 'grep -l <session-id> proxy/connections/*.jsonl' resolves a session back to the connection that created it. Verified: session 9f4fae89-a38b-4d73-be74-33cb34c9a4fc resolves to connection 4c4aacc0-f68c-4103-a50c-89ab7e86c4ba.

The residual is a papercut, not a defect: a session log carries no connection id of its own, so session-to-connection costs one grep across the connections directory rather than a direct lookup. Not worth a change against a repository whose contract forbids speculative work, and not filed as a follow-up.

Correction recorded on louiselm-5tuq, which this issue claimed was unverifiable: the connection log gives direct wire proof that the fix works.

title: Historical Provenance commit inspection rejects valid git output
description:
Selecting a historical Provenance commit from a Decision view fails with `louiselm: git returned malformed commit data`, even though the referenced commit is valid. This blocks the commit-detail drill-down that Case 1 uses to verify historical evidence.

## Observed

Manual QA Case 1 on 2026-08-30 in Neovim, repository `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`, screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260830_0551_1920x1200_1788061871.png`. The Decision view showed:

`Historical backlog:`
`- ref: 097bcd6d2f5c6cb021a0ff31f78280d9c02a3d5e`
`- 178 issues at decision time`
`- anchor state: closed`
`- since then: 248 added, 0 removed, 19 changed`

Moving to that SHA and invoking `<leader>lP` produced:

`louiselm: git returned malformed commit data`

The SHA is valid: `git show -s --format=fuller 097bcd6d2f5c6cb021a0ff31f78280d9c02a3d5e` succeeds. The exact source command exits successfully, but its output ends with `0x1e 0x0a` (record separator followed by a newline).

## Symptoms

- Historical backlog and drift render successfully.
- Commit inspection fails instead of opening the commit Provenance view.
- The user sees the generic malformed-data error for valid Git output.

## Root cause

The parser at `lua/louiselm/provenance/sources.lua:60-90` loops while `cursor <= #output` and requires every remaining byte sequence to end in `RECORD_SEPARATOR`. `git_log()` at `lua/louiselm/provenance/sources.lua:371-402` invokes Git with `--format=%H%x00%B%x00%x1e`; Git appends a newline after the final record separator. The parser consumes the separator, then sees the trailing newline as a new incomplete record and returns `invalid_git_log`. The UI converts that parse error to the generic message at `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:358-360`.

## Why it was not caught

The parser tests use synthetic output ending exactly at the record separator. They do not include Git's actual trailing newline, and the historical Decision UI test constructs source data without exercising the cursor-to-commit `git log` round trip.

## Fix direction

Make the parser accept Git's valid trailing whitespace after the final record separator, while continuing to reject genuinely incomplete records and malformed fields. Keep the fix at the shared parser boundary; do not special-case the SHA or suppress the UI error.

## Acceptance

- A regression fixture containing the observed record separator plus trailing newline parses as one commit.
- From the Decision view, placing the cursor on `097bcd6d2f5c6cb021a0ff31f78280d9c02a3d5e` and invoking `<leader>lP` opens the commit Provenance view.
- Existing malformed/incomplete-record tests continue to fail closed.

## Not covered

This report does not yet establish whether the same parser failure affects every multi-commit Decision index lookup; the index itself rendered in this run. No fix was attempted in this QA round.
close_reason: Fixed at d95c5df; live acceptance confirmed by maintainer 2026-08-30

comments.author: claude/d4b23fbe-32a3-4c77-8802-687f31119e64
comments.text:
Fix applied at lua/louiselm/provenance/sources.lua:60-96 (M.parse_git_log): after consuming a record's RECORD_SEPARATOR, skip one immediately-following newline if present, since git always appends its own trailing "\n" after every --format record (confirmed via `git log -n 3 --format='%H%x00%B%x00%x1e' | od -c` in this repo), not only the final one.

Broader finding beyond the reported single-commit case ("Not covered" section): the pre-fix parser was also silently corrupting every commit after the first in a multi-commit git_log() call (e.g. the --all call at lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:702) by prepending git's inter-record newline onto the next record's id field. The same fix resolves both, at the shared parser boundary, without special-casing the SHA.

Regression coverage added in tests/provenance/sources_spec.lua ("git log" group): single-commit and multi-commit fixtures with git's real trailing newline after every record separator, both now parsed correctly; existing malformed/incomplete-record paths untouched and still fail closed. Full mini.test suite (734 cases), stylua --check, and lua-language-server --checklevel=Warning all pass.

Per AGENTS.md Live Acceptance: this was reproduced live (screenshot cited in the issue), so automated gates alone do not close it. Leaving in_progress pending the maintainer confirming, from the Decision view, that placing the cursor on 097bcd6d2f5c6cb021a0ff31f78280d9c02a3d5e and invoking <leader>lP now opens the commit Provenance view instead of "git returned malformed commit data".

comments.text: Live acceptance confirmed by maintainer 2026-08-30: after running :lua vim.pack.update({"louiselm.nvim"}) to refresh the stale pinned clone, placing the cursor on 097bcd6d2f5c6cb021a0ff31f78280d9c02a3d5e in the Decision view and invoking <leader>lP opens the commit Provenance view (screenshot ~/Pictures/scrot/20260830_0629_1920x1200_1788064142.png). All three acceptance criteria met.

title: Show Session ID when hovering the winbar Agent name
description:
## Goal
Show the full Session ID in a tooltip when the pointer hovers over the Agent name (for example, codex) in the chat winbar: Your turn · codex · Limits… · Options.

## Context
Maintainer request: hover over the displayed name to discover that chat view's Session ID without adding permanent winbar clutter. In project vocabulary, codex is the configured Agent name; the tooltip identifies its specific Session.
Source conversation, read when filing: https://chatgpt.com/share/6aab998f-7eb0-83ed-b435-98dbd097c448 (Neovim Winbar Hovering). It discusses mouse-movement tracking and hit-testing rendered winbar segments; its example is research context, not a verified implementation.

## Scope
Add hover discovery to the existing Agent-name segment, using the Session belonging to the hovered chat window. Keep the existing turn, Limits, Options and Session-switch interactions.
No general-purpose hover framework, new dependency, or unrelated winbar redesign.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Hovering codex (or another configured Agent name) shows the complete, untruncated ACP Session ID for that chat view.
2. With multiple Sessions/windows, including two using the same Agent, the tooltip identifies the hovered Session regardless of keyboard focus.
3. Moving off the name dismisses the tooltip; resizing, switching Sessions and closing/disposing a view cannot leave a stale tooltip or show another Session's ID.
4. Hover does not steal focus or interfere with typing or existing winbar click actions. Other segments do not trigger this Session-ID tooltip.
5. Before a Session ID is available, do not display a fabricated or stale ID.
6. Document required mouse support and the policy for Neovim's global mousemoveevent setting; preserve user-owned settings/mappings and clean up plugin-owned handlers/resources.

## Testing
Use focused behavioral coverage for hit boundaries, narrow/resized winbars, correct Session targeting, missing IDs and disposal. Run the complete affected Lua suite and required gates when implementing.
Verify real pointer hover in the maintainer's terminal/GUI with the effective configuration. If optional config is introduced, test its unset case and verify reachability in that configuration.

## Implementation pointers
Existing winbar rendering/targets: lua/louiselm/ui/chat/status.lua and lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua. Reuse existing Session-ID access; do not infer identity from a globally focused chat.
Prior-art searches: br search -a hover and br search -a "session id"; no matching hover task found in the bounded results.

comments.text: Implemented Agent-name hover with full agent/ACP-session-id, per-window rendered spans, non-focusable tooltip, lifecycle cleanup, and cancellation of hover work superseded by typing. Interactive command registration enables mousemoveevent and restores its previous value unless a later OptionSet transfers ownership to the user; headless APIs do not change options or mappings. Effective maintainer settings inspected: mouse=a, mousemoveevent=false; opening the updated interactive UI enables reporting. Lesson: mouse tests must drain nvim_input_mouse through getchar(0), and verify typing before scheduled hover executes. Real mouse input tests cover unfocused same-Agent splits, span edges, missing ID, disabled reporting, resize, typing, and queued disposal. Acceptance pending: restart Neovim with this checkout, hover codex in Your turn · codex · Limits · Options, confirm full Session ID and dismissal without changing focus. Current running UI retains old loaded modules; no live hot-reload or Session disposal performed.

title: QA round: Beads inspector, diagnostics context, reasoning fold, usage spacing, Forensics, winbar clicks
description:
# Manual QA review — since acb65c7 (last recorded round, louiselm-7rup)

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `acb65c7..HEAD` (25 commits, HEAD=`c56805f`). **Re-run
Setup after any fix.**

Origin: no manual round has covered anything since `acb65c7`. Six behaviors
landed since then with no prior manual pass: the Beads issue inspector
(`e58bf0d`), queued buffer diagnostics (`4b84ac4`/`52768af`), the reasoning
fold (`c56805f`), the usage-line spacing fix (`f75e2a6`), private Session
Forensics collection (`b9dfcc1`), and a Winbar click-routing fix (`437fbf0`).

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Beads issue inspector: cursor on/off an id, bad id, close keys | **passed** — claude/6f651593-5a66-4076-a6a2-b94d9ac51fcd, all 4 sub-cases confirmed |
| 2 | Queue buffer diagnostics for next prompt | **passed** — claude/827084e2-cc79-4a54-a8f4-3229ce4bcbc5, transcript shows label, header, untrusted-data framing, both entries correctly formatted |
| 3 | Reasoning fold closes and exports (`## Reasoning`) | **passed** — deepseek/session-25703dab-5664-4d3a-9b50-7baeec7710c0, 17 live-streamed chunks all folded closed, export has 4 `## Reasoning` sections with full text |
| 4 | Usage line has blank line before/after it (live + resume) | **failed** — live path OK, resume path accumulates blank lines across turns; filed `louiselm-1yei` (pre-existing, not this round's regression) |
| 5 | Session Forensics: collect, view, resource-link queued | **passed** — deepseek/session-f7dbeaea-b8d8-469a-8332-0bedf50ea18d; found+fixed `louiselm-t6j2` (Beads inspector, unrelated) and `louiselm-ysh3` (garbled filenames) along the way |
| 6 | Winbar click in a non-focused split routes to that split | **passed** — deepseek/session-652fd89d-ed42-4da6-a1d3-b789c40b08bd, claude/91086355-53e2-4be1-91ca-1c5d02b5602e (retest after `louiselm-7ios` fix) |

## Setup

Launch the dev Neovim with real agents configured (this is the project's
existing manual-test harness, unchanged by this round):

```
nvim -u manual_init.lua
```

`claude` and `deepseek` agents are pre-configured there; `deepseek` is the one
that actually streams `agent_thought_chunk` during a live prompt (needed for
case 3's live-streaming half — export `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` first, or that half
is blocked and only the mock-replay half of case 3 is testable).

For cases that don't need a live model (1, 2, 4 partly, 5, 6), you can instead
run against the mock ACP agent:

```
LOUISELM_MOCK=1 nvim -u manual_init.lua
```

(check `AGENTS.md` / `lua/louiselm/dev/mock_agent.lua` if the mock launch env
var differs — state what you actually used in your report.)

Confirm the running copy matches source before testing:

```
git -C /home/lotso/code/louiselm rev-parse HEAD   # expect c56805f...
```

Fixtures:
- Case 1 needs a chat buffer with a Beads issue id visible in the transcript
  (e.g. paste `louiselm-zmab` into a message, or reference a real one from
  `br list`), and a case with the cursor on plain text with no id nearby.
- Case 2 does **not** need a real LSP attached — `diagnostics.lua` just reads
  `vim.diagnostic.get()`, so inject fixtures directly instead of depending on
  `lua_ls` being configured/attached in the test buffer. **Order matters**:
  `Chat:mention_diagnostics()` reads `view.source_buffer`, which is fixed to
  whatever buffer was current *when the chat was attached*
  (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2630`) — not whatever has focus later. So:
  1. `:e /tmp/qa_source.lua` — a **named** file. An unnamed/scratch buffer
     here means the chat attaches to `[No Name]` and the fixture script (see
     below, which targets buffer `0`) ends up setting diagnostics on
     whatever *actually* has focus at that moment instead — a mismatch that
     silently produces "No error or warning diagnostics." with no error, as
     happened on the first attempt.
  2. `:LouiselmChat` (or `:LouiselmNewSession`) from that buffer, so it
     becomes `source_buffer`.
  3. Switch focus back to the `/tmp/qa_source.lua` window (opening chat
     steals focus into a split) before running the fixture script.
  4. *Then*, in that source-buffer window, run:
  A single-line `:lua` command still hit a separate "namespace: expected
  number, got nil" error earlier — that means the terminal was splitting the
  pasted line into separate Enter presses (no bracketed paste), so even a
  one-liner isn't safe to paste into the command line. Use a real file
  instead, which Neovim always reads as one chunk regardless of terminal
  paste behavior:
  ```
  :luafile /tmp/qa_diag.lua
  ```
  (script already written; it prints `qa_diag: 2 diagnostics set` on
  success — if you don't see that line in `:messages`, the diagnostics were
  never set and the case hasn't reached the code yet). Clear fixtures when
  done with:
  ```
  :luafile /tmp/qa_diag_reset.lua
  ```
- Case 5 needs `stdpath("state") .. "/louiselm/forensics"` to be readable
  before/after for a permissions check (`ls -la` on the written file).
- Case 6 needs two chat session windows open side by side (`:LouiselmNewSession`
  then split), each with a Winbar showing session tabs.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Case 2 does not need a real LSP attached. The original setup assumed
  `lua_ls` would produce diagnostics; this environment has no LSP configured,
  so the case never reached the code. Inject diagnostics directly with
  `vim.diagnostic.set()` instead (see Setup) — `diagnostics.lua` only reads
  the diagnostic cache, it doesn't care where entries came from.
- Case 2, second miss (mine): I described a "queued-context fold" as visible
  before the prompt is even sent. There is no such thing — before submit,
  a context item is just an inline `[context: label]` chip on the prompt
  line (`render_chip`, `init.lua:933`); folding only happens on submit
  (`replace_submitted_prompt`, `init.lua:1213-1242`), applied per-window.
  "No fold on the brackets" pre-submit is expected, not a bug.
- Case 3: the `acp-llm-adapter` deepseek session logs
  (`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/sessions/session-<id>/log.jsonl`) also
  redact `agent_thought_chunk` content to `"[REDACTED]"`, same dead end as
  the claude proxy in case 2 — useful only to confirm *that* chunks streamed
  and *how many*, not their text. Fold-closing correctness has to be read
  visually or from an export.
- Case 2, third miss: `mention_diagnostics` reads `view.source_buffer`,
  frozen at chat-attach time, not whatever buffer/window has focus when the
  fixture script runs. Attaching chat from an unnamed buffer and then running
  `:luafile` from the chat's own split set diagnostics on the wrong buffer —
  no error anywhere, just a silent "No error or warning diagnostics." Always
  open a **named** file first, attach chat from it, then switch focus back to
  that file's window before setting fixture diagnostics.
- Don't paste multi-statement Lua onto the `:` command line in this terminal
  — even a single logical line got split into separate Enter presses
  (`namespace: expected number, got nil`, i.e. `local ns = ...` and the next
  statement ran as two separate `:lua` invocations, losing the local). Use
  `:luafile <path>` with a real script instead; it's parsed as one chunk no
  matter how the paste lands.

## Cases

### 1. Beads issue inspector

Exercises `e58bf0d` / `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua`.

Steps:

> In a louiselm session buffer, put the cursor on text containing a valid
> Beads id (e.g. `louiselm-zmab`) and run `:LouiselmInspectBead` (or press
> `<leader>lB`). Then move the cursor to a line with no id and repeat. Then
> put the cursor on an *ambiguous* line with two ids and repeat.

Expect: on a single id under the cursor, a rounded-border floating window
titled ` Beads ` opens showing title/ID/status/priority/labels/description,
`q` and `<Esc>` close it and wipe the buffer. With no id under the cursor (or
two candidate ids on the line), an `nvim.ui.input` prompt appears instead
("louiselm Beads issue id: "); entering a non-`louiselm-`-prefixed value shows
an error via `on_error` and no window opens. Also try this from a buffer that
is *not* a `louiselm-session` filetype — the command should report "current
buffer is not a louiselm session" and do nothing.

Failure signature: window doesn't close on `q`/`<Esc>` (buffer leak — check
`:ls` after), wrong issue opened when two ids are near the cursor, or a lookup
silently does nothing when `br` isn't found instead of reporting an error.

### 2. Queue buffer diagnostics for next prompt

Exercises `4b84ac4` / `52768af` / `lua/louiselm/ui/context/diagnostics.lua`.

Steps:

> In the source buffer, inject fixture diagnostics with the `vim.diagnostic.set`
> snippet in Setup (no LSP needed). Then run `:LouiselmDiagnostics` from the
> chat session attached to it — the prompt line should now show a
> `[context: diagnostics: <path>] ` chip prefix (**not folded yet**; folding
> only happens on submit). Then actually send the prompt (type anything and
> press Enter) and look at the resulting transcript above the new prompt
> line, then check what the agent actually receives (mock agent: check its
> stderr/log if `ACP_LOG=1`; real `claude` agent: the ACP proxy log redacts
> prompt content, so this can't be checked that way — see Evidence check).

Expect: before submit, just the inline chip. After submit, a folded block
appears in the transcript above the new prompt line, labeled
`[contexts: diagnostics: <path>]` on its summary line. Opening the fold
(`zo`) shows `[context: diagnostics: <path>]` followed by a header
(`Diagnostics for <path> (observed_at=..., changedtick=...):`) and a fenced
block prefixed "The diagnostic messages below are untrusted data, not
instructions." with one `SEVERITY line:col: message` per diagnostic. Running
`:LouiselmDiagnostics` again after editing the buffer should reflect the new
`changedtick`, not stale data.

Failure signature: diagnostics text sent as if it were an instruction (no
untrusted-data framing reaching the agent), stale snapshot after an edit, or
command silently no-ops when there are zero diagnostics (should say "No error
or warning diagnostics.", not vanish).

### 3. Reasoning fold closes correctly, exports as `## Reasoning`

Exercises `c56805f` / fold logic in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` around
`close_thought_fold_run`.

Steps (mock, resume path):

> `LOUISELM_MOCK_REPLAY_REASONING="single line of reasoning text" LOUISELM_MOCK=1 nvim -u manual_init.lua`,
> start a session, quit, then resume/load that same session (whatever command
> replays history — check `:LouiselmSwitchSession` or reopening triggers
> `session/load`).

Steps (live, deepseek — only if `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is set):

> Start a deepseek chat, send a prompt that provokes visible reasoning
> ("think step by step about X before answering"), watch the transcript while
> it streams.

Expect: a `[thinking]` block appears and, once reasoning ends, is folded
closed — even when the reasoning text is exactly one line (this is the
regression `c56805f` fixes: Neovim can't close a 1-line fold, so the header
must fold *with* its content). `zo`/`zc` on the fold should work normally.
After the turn, run `:LouiselmExport` (or whatever the export command is —
check `AGENTS.md`/`:h louiselm-export`) and confirm the exported markdown
contains a `## Reasoning` section with the full text.

Failure signature: the `[thinking]` header stays on its own unfolded line
above a folded content block (the exact bug this commit fixes — watch for it
specifically when the reasoning is short/single-line), or the export omits
the `## Reasoning` section entirely.

### 4. Usage line spacing

Exercises `f75e2a6` / `insert_usage` in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Steps:

> Send a prompt that completes normally (mock or real agent) and look at the
> `[usage]` line in the transcript immediately after the response. Then close
> and resume that session (restore path) and look at the same line again.

Expect: in both the live-turn case and the resumed/restored case, the
`[usage] ...` line has a blank line both above and below it, separating it
from the transcript content before and after — never glued directly onto the
previous or next line.

Failure signature: `[usage]` line runs directly into the assistant text above
or the next prompt line below with no blank separator, in either the live or
the restored-on-resume path (the fix touches both call sites — check both,
one could regress while the other stays fixed).

### 5. Session Forensics: collect, view, and queue as context

Exercises `b9dfcc1` / `lua/louiselm/forensics/*.lua` /
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:406-438`.

Steps:

> With a chat session open and attached to a real or mock agent, run
> `:LouiselmForensics`. Note the path it reports/queues. Then run
> `:LouiselmForensicsView <path>` with that path. Then send a prompt and
> check whether a `forensics: <path>` context item was queued for it.

Expect: `:LouiselmForensics` writes a JSON file under
`stdpath("state")/louiselm/forensics/`, named `<unix-time>-<record-id>.json`,
readable only by the owner (`ls -la` shows `-rw-------`, i.e. mode 384/0600 —
check the write path in `store.lua:79`, `fs_chmod(path, 384)`). Content is
bounded/sanitized (agent name, ACP session id, cwd, model, capabilities,
dirty file list — capped at 100 entries / 256 chars each per `record.lua`),
no secrets or full env dumps. `:LouiselmForensicsView` opens a scratch buffer
showing the file's raw content. The collected record is queued as a resource
link (`forensics: <path>`, `file://<path>` uri) for the *next* prompt, visible
as a queued-context fold like case 2.

Failure signature: file permissions wider than `0600`, the temp-file-then-rename
write leaves a stray `.tmp-XXXXXX` file behind on success (check the
directory after a normal run), `:LouiselmForensicsView` with no/garbage path
crashes instead of reporting "Forensics record path is required" /
"could not read Forensics record", or unsanitized data (full paths beyond the
256-char bound, more than 100 dirty files) makes it into the written record.

### 6. Winbar click in a non-focused split routes correctly

Exercises `437fbf0` / `Chat:winbar_click` in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Steps:

> Open two chat session windows side by side (`:LouiselmNewSession`, then
> `:vsplit` or open a second session in a split so both Winbars are visible
> with session tabs). Keep focus in the *left* window. Click a session tab
> in the *right* window's Winbar (mouse click, not keyboard) that is not the
> currently-open session there.

Expect: focus moves to the right window and it switches to the clicked
session — the click acts on the window it was physically clicked in, not on
whatever window had focus before the click.

Failure signature: the click is misrouted — either nothing happens, an error
about an unavailable window-bar target, or (the pre-fix bug) the *left*
window's session changes instead of the right window's.

## Evidence check

- Case 1: `:ls` after closing the floating window — no leaked scratch buffer.
- Case 2 / 5: originally proposed grepping the ACP proxy log
  (`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/<id>/log.jsonl`) for what
  reached `session/prompt` params — dead end against the real `claude` agent,
  the proxy redacts `params.prompt` to `"[REDACTED]"` unconditionally. Use
  `:LouiselmToMarkdown` instead and grep the exported file for the queued
  text (mock agent + `ACP_LOG=1` may still work since it doesn't redact, but
  hasn't been confirmed — don't assume it does without checking).
- Case 4: `:%s/\[usage\]//gn` won't tell you about spacing — just read the
  buffer lines directly around the usage line, or `:lua print(vim.inspect(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, <n>-2, <n>+2, false)))`.
- Case 5: `ls -la $(nvim --headless -u manual_init.lua -c 'lua print(vim.fn.stdpath("state"))' -c 'q' 2>&1)/louiselm/forensics/` for permissions; `ls` the same dir right after a write to check for orphaned `.tmp-*` files.
- Case 6: purely visual/interactive — no artifact beyond what you see; state clearly that this rests on observation only.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- Delete any Session Forensics files written under
  `stdpath("state")/louiselm/forensics/` during testing (they may contain
  real cwd/git state from this machine).
- Close extra chat session windows/splits opened for case 6.

## Reporting back

Send me the run id, which case, what you saw, and anything surprising. I pull
the evidence myself. If something is wrong I will fix it, and you will need to
redo Setup before retesting.

## Findings this round

**Enhancement — Beads inspector should accept a bare issue id** (`louiselm-y8y1`, not fixed
— filed as a task, not a bug: current `louiselm-` prefix requirement is by
design, just less convenient than it could be).
Surfaced during case 1: all four sub-cases passed as specified, but the
manual-entry `nvim.ui.input` prompt rejects a bare suffix (`zmab`) and
requires the full `louiselm-zmab`. `valid_issue_id()` in
`lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua` could prepend `louiselm-` before validating when
the input lacks it.

**F1 — Usage-line spacing accumulates blank lines during resumed multi-turn
replay** (`louiselm-1yei`, not fixed — two attempted fixes each caused a
different regression elsewhere; filed with full root-cause trace and a
recommended direction for whoever picks it up).
Surfaced in case 4: live single-turn spacing is correct (1 blank), but each
additional replayed turn on resume leaves an orphaned blank line nothing
consumes, so N-turn resumes show N accumulated blanks before the live prompt.
Root cause: `chunk` event handling writes a prose response's trailing blank
directly into the buffer without including it in `transcript_tail`
bookkeeping — a deliberate-looking mechanism that lets tool/reasoning blocks
reuse it as their own leading separator. See the bead for the full trace.

**F2 — Beads inspector rejects any issue with no labels** (`louiselm-t6j2`,
fixed in `8aa5afd`).
Reported live while inspecting `louiselm-1yei` right after filing it (no
labels): `:LouiselmInspectBead` failed with "br returned malformed issue
data". `br show --json` omits the `labels` key entirely rather than emitting
`[]` when an issue has none; `decode_issue()` in `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua`
required it as a table unconditionally. Fixed with a failing-test-first case
in `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua`; full suite green.

**F3 — Forensics record ids render in scientific notation, garbling
filenames** (`louiselm-ysh3`, fixed in `849f5dc`).
Surfaced in case 5: `:LouiselmForensics` wrote files like
`1787715628-1787715628-2.0264597271177e+14.json`. `nvim.uv.hrtime()`'s
nanosecond value overflowed Lua's default `tostring()` into scientific
notation; `lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua` now formats it with `%d`. Fixed
with a failing-test-first case in `tests/session/api_spec.lua`; full suite
green.

**F4 — No winbar click has ever worked via a real mouse click**
(`louiselm-7ios`, fixed in `f81019a`, confirmed live).
Surfaced in case 6: not just the cross-window routing the case set out to
test — clicking *any* winbar tab did nothing, silently, no error. Isolated
with two throwaway winbar click regions independent of louiselm code: a
plain `v:lua.FuncName` click target worked, but the exact pattern this
codebase used, `v:lua.require('mod').method`, did nothing. Vim's
`%{N}@{Function}@` click syntax needs a plain dotted name it can resolve at
click-dispatch time, not a call expression — this has been broken since the
winbar-click feature was introduced (`7b31438`), invisible because unit
tests only ever called `M.winbar_click(...)` directly, bypassing real click
dispatch entirely. Fixed by registering a stable global forwarder function;
confirmed working live after the fix (sessions
deepseek/session-652fd89d-ed42-4da6-a1d3-b789c40b08bd and
claude/91086355-53e2-4be1-91ca-1c5d02b5602e).

title: Refuse louiselm command pickers while a permission decision is open
description:
After 0ed18d0 (louiselm-brx) the chat presents one permission decision at a time, but that queue only covers agent-initiated permission requests. The pickers louiselm opens for its own commands - file, skill, session resume, session switch, agent choice, remembered-permission management, session options - are still unqueued. Opening one while a permission picker is up makes an async provider such as the Snacks picker tear the permission picker down, its on_close fires with no item, and the request is answered cancelled without the user deciding.

Severity after 0ed18d0 is a lost prompt and a spuriously denied tool call, not a hang: the cancelled response releases the decision slot and the queue advances. That is why this is a task rather than a P0/P1 bug.

## Decision: refuse these pickers, do not queue them

Queuing every Picker.select behind the decision slot was considered and rejected:

1. Chained pickers would deadlock. Several flows open a picker from inside another picker callback: manage_permissions (rules -> revoke confirm), open_session_options (option -> value), and critically lua/louiselm/ui/diff/init.lua:114, where a review with several allow lifetimes opens a second picker WHILE holding the decision slot. That slot is only released when the second picker answers, so queuing it makes each wait on the other - the exact failure class louiselm-4wx and louiselm-brx removed.
2. Delayed popups steal input. A queued user-initiated picker opens at an arbitrary later moment, likely after the user moved on and started typing in the chat prompt, and the provider grabs input on open.
3. A leaked slot would freeze the whole UI instead of permissions only. Today a stuck decision still leaves the session picker and close_session reachable; behind one shared slot the escape hatches would be blocked too.
4. open_session_options auto-opens on state_changed -> ready and on attach (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1070 and :1370), so with two sessions a config picker would surface long after the state change that caused it.

Refusing has none of those properties, is smaller, and cannot deadlock.

## Scope

- While a permission decision is presented (chat decision_active), user-initiated picker commands return false plus an actionable message, e.g. "answer the open louiselm permission request first".
- The auto-opened session options picker is skipped rather than reported.
- Exceptions that stay allowed on purpose: close_session, because it is the escape hatch when a decision is stuck and cancelling that permission is the right outcome when the session is being closed anyway; and cancel, which is not a picker.
- The diff review lifetime picker is untouched: it belongs to the open decision rather than competing with it.

## Acceptance

- Each guarded command returns its refusal without opening a picker while a decision is open, and works normally once the decision is answered.
- close_session still opens its confirmation while a decision is open.
- A diff review with several allow lifetimes still opens its lifetime picker.
close_reason: Implemented in b76a95d as specified: refuse, not queue. DECISION_OPEN_ERROR guards Chat:manage_permissions, switch_session, session_options, pick_file, pick_skill, resume_session, and the agent-choice path of new_session; open_session_options also returns early so the automatic picker is skipped rather than reported. close_session and cancel stay unguarded on purpose, and the diff review lifetime picker is untouched. Test: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'refuses command pickers while a permission decision is open' covers every guarded command, proves no extra picker opens, proves close_session still opens its confirmation, and proves the commands work again once the decision is answered. Full suite 197 cases, stylua --check, lua-language-server all clean. README documents the refusal and why it is not a queue.

title: Activate workspace cleanup timer on the maintainer host
description:
Retention expiry ships but is inert on the maintainer machine: skills-core/contrib/systemd/louiselm-workspace-cleanup.{service,timer} are committed and tested (louiselm-d6fv.5.5.2), and no host ever ran 'systemctl enable --now louiselm-workspace-cleanup.timer'. Until then no expired, disposed, unpinned Session storage is ever reclaimed on the maintainer host, so bounded retention is a claim tests make, not behavior the machine performs.

Operator step, root authority: install the unit pair, enable the timer, then confirm one real hourly pass reclaims an expired/unpinned sealed root and leaves live/Parked/pinned storage alone. See docs/workspace-snapshots.md:156.

Acceptance: maintainer confirms the timer is active and reports one observed cleanup pass, including its primary_evidence transition (not_checked -> removed) and that pinned/live storage survived it.

title: Accept ACP nulls in session discovery
description:
## Problem

`:LouiselmResume` rejects valid ACP `session/list` responses when nullable fields are encoded as JSON `null`. Neovim decodes JSON `null` as `vim.NIL`, while discovery validation currently accepts only Lua `nil` or strings. A Codex response with `nextCursor: null` therefore reports `ACP session/list returned malformed data: nextCursor must be a string` and discards Codex sessions. The same mismatch affects nullable `SessionInfo.title` and `updatedAt`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `nextCursor: null` is treated as end-of-pagination.
2. `title: null` and `updatedAt: null` are accepted and exposed as absent optional values.
3. Non-null, non-string values for all three fields remain rejected.
4. A regression test exercises the JSON-null representation through session discovery.
5. Focused tests, full mini.test, StyLua, and lua-language-server checks pass.
close_reason: Accepted ACP JSON null for session/list nextCursor, title, and updatedAt by normalizing Neovim vim.NIL at discovery validation. Added regression coverage through the public discovery API. Focused session tests pass; full 126-case mini.test suite passes with writable XDG_STATE_HOME; stylua --check and lua-language-server checks pass.

title: Park continues to attachment after Run admission fails
description: Observed in code review of pn7z on 2026-09-11. Pre-existing Chat:park at the session baseline lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1987 passed function() to WorkflowService.admit, ignoring token and error arguments; the unchanged callback moved to workflow/recovery.lua in pn7z.5. Service.admit in workflow/service.lua:145 reports asynchronous failures with callback(nil, message), whereas the caller proceeds to WorkflowService.attach and can replace the original admission error with an attachment failure. Root cause: admission started return value is checked, but its asynchronous result is not. Existing Chat Park cases supply successful admission callbacks and test cold-Park rejection after admission, not admission failure. Fix direction: stop before attachment on nil token, propagate the original service error, cover with a scheduled service callback regression. Acceptance: failed admission performs no attach/adopt/park and preserves the admission error; successful admission still reuses the same Run ID. Deferred as a pre-existing behavior defect outside the pn7z structural extraction. No live reproduction or fix claimed.
close_reason: Stop failed admission before attachment; lesson in issue comments. gate:tests/workflow/recovery_spec.lua

comments.author: codex/01a0a3e7-1523-74d2-b85f-ce98fd86fe51
comments.text: Fixed workflow/recovery.lua admission callback: nil token stops before attach/adopt/Park and preserves original error; disposed/departed Session ignores admission completion. Scheduled failure regression was red (attachment error replaced admission error), now green. Full 1044 Lua tests, StyLua, LuaLS and generated docs/type/version gates pass. Lesson routed here: command-start success does not establish asynchronous admission success.

title: Design: notify Android app from a session when an agent needs input
description:
Human-attended sessions (grill-me, qa-review) are fundamentally interactive; most other louiselm sessions are agent-driven (e.g. implementing beads work) and don't need a human at the keyboard in neovim.

Open question: how could a session push a notification to the Android app when an agent hits a point where it needs human input (a decision, a blocker, an approval) while implementing a bead — so the human (not at a desk, e.g. gardening) gets pinged instead of the agent stalling silently?

Design questions to resolve:
- What's the trigger condition for "agent needs something" vs normal progress noise?
- Transport: does this reuse existing agent-mail/push-notification plumbing, or need a new channel to the Android app?
- Should this be opt-in per session type, or inferred from session type (grill-me/qa-review = human-mode, everything else = agent-mode with notify-on-block)?
- What's the minimal actionable payload on the phone (just "come back", or enough context to answer inline)?

title: Remove unsafe transport test descriptor inheritance
description:
Unsafe inventory: four blocks; skills-core/tests/launch_transport.rs:790 and :825 only pass an already-connected socket into a credential-test subprocess. Replace its pre_exec hook and raw BorrowedFd construction with OwnedFd -> Stdio on child stderr and the safe Stderr descriptor borrow. Preserve the stdin release gate, real child process, exact packet bytes, and both process-pin rejection and identity-pin acceptance assertions. Add forbid(unsafe_code) to the transport test crate.

Production review: sandbox.rs:1527 admits the child to its cgroup before exec; sandbox/host_identity.rs:204 clears CLOEXEC only in the child for two extra gate descriptors. Existing standard-library APIs do not replace those operations while preserving their timing and descriptor isolation. Retain these reviewed boundaries. Prior lessons: louiselm-xhgy and louiselm-xhgy.1 (Command owns inherited descriptors; no parent-side CLOEXEC window).

Acceptance: passing transport characterization before and after the refactor; skills-core fmt, all-target/all-feature locked Clippy, full tests, and warning-free Rustdoc. No new dependency or production lifecycle change.

title: Assessment
description: A model's advisory opinion on a whole workflow document, prose included, about whether its effects are unbounded. Assessment has no authority: it never gates execution, runs in an isolated Session with an empty capability envelope, and is delivered to an operator at envelope-approval time. Verdicts are stored, keyed on hash(document) + model id + prompt version.
design: Established by the louiselm-qbr.8 grill-me session on 2026-08-26, with explicit maintainer confirmation of the final summary. Proposed by the maintainer as a second checker over prose after rejecting frontmatter-only inspection as too narrow. Named Assessment rather than Scrutiny by maintainer preference. Kept advisory because a gate reading semi-trusted document text can be told to report no hazards, while an advisory opinion read by a human has bounded blast radius.
notes: Use Assessment for the model-read opinion; use Validation for the structural check. Avoid 'review' (taken by qa-review) and 'audit' (taken by br audit). Assessment is stored rather than recomputed so its verdicts can be calibrated against what Runs actually did; staleness is expressed as absence -- 'no current Assessment' -- never as a stale verdict shown as fresh.

title: Duplicate isolation evidence passes exactly-one validation
description:
`IsolationEvidence::check` accepts multiple records for one required dimension when they agree, contradicting the isolation contract's exactly-one evidence rule and making duplicated evidence appear valid.

## Observed

2026-09-03 code inspection during louiselm-i03a. `skills-core/src/isolation.rs:5-8` states that verified evidence contains exactly one satisfied record per dimension. At `skills-core/src/isolation.rs:221-238`, the `many` branch rejects only mixed `satisfied` values; two or more `true` records pass.

## Symptoms

- Duplicate same-value evidence passes `check()`.
- A receipt can claim more than one authority/mechanism for a dimension despite the closed contract.

## Root cause

The validation branch treats multiplicity as contradiction only when boolean outcomes differ, instead of rejecting multiplicity itself.

## Why it was not caught

Tests cover disagreeing duplicate evidence but not two agreeing records for one dimension.

## Fix direction

Reject every dimension with more than one evidence record and add regressions for duplicate-true and duplicate-false inputs. Preserve the fixed validation order.

## Acceptance

- Duplicate agreeing records fail validation.
- Exactly one record per dimension still passes.
- Missing, unsatisfied, and conflicting diagnostics remain deterministic.

## Not covered

This finding does not change Bubblewrap host-identity observation in louiselm-i03a.
close_reason: gate:skills-core/tests/isolation.rs rejects agreeing true/false duplicates; full skills-core gates pass

comments.author: codex/01a068c6-2ca1-7be3-88ff-96c887e50df0
comments.text: Red: duplicate agreeing true returned Ok; duplicate agreeing false returned Unsatisfied. Fix: any multiplicity is Contradictory, preserving contract→kernel→contradictory→missing→unsatisfied order. Green: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test. Lesson routing: issue-local; no AGENTS.md change warranted.

title: Explain the LouiseLM vision and recursive identity
description:
## Problem Statement

The README documents development and implemented APIs but does not explain why LouiseLM exists, what the name means, or how its current ACP-backed Neovim foundation relates to the larger idea-to-software vision. Readers cannot yet understand the project before reaching the technical reference.

## Solution

Add a clear product narrative and an original hero banner at the start of the README. Present LouiseLM as alpha software whose north star is turning ideas into software, explain the attention-preserving workflow and its safety boundaries, and show the current manual workflow as one replaceable configuration. Preserve the existing technical reference beneath a concise bridge describing what works today.

## User Stories

1. As a new reader, I want to understand LouiseLM and its recursive name immediately, so that I can decide whether the project matters to me.
2. As a potential user, I want the vision separated clearly from current alpha capabilities, so that I am inspired without being misled.
3. As a creative developer, I want to see a strong default workflow presented as configurable, so that I can imagine building a different workflow with the same substrate.
4. As an operator, I want the vision to preserve my attention, ownership, and approval authority, so that automation remains empowering and legible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The README uses LouiseLM as the project name and includes the exact recursive acronym: LouiseLM Organizes Unruled Intelligent Systems into Emancipated Language Meshes.
2. The opening states that LouiseLM turns ideas into software and clearly labels the project as alpha software.
3. The motivation explains that ideas arrive faster than sustained attention and uses the gardening example without clinical or medical positioning.
4. The vision covers interruption-free capture, later enrichment and explainable triage, focused deliberation, planning, dependency-shaped execution, agent implementation and review, human approval, and an observable operator control plane.
5. Neovim is presented as the deliberate home and cockpit, with headless automation and optional future capture surfaces rather than a promised editor-independent runtime.
6. Local-first ownership, configurable workflow boundaries, strong defaults, replaceable parts, and policy-controlled automation are explicit principles.
7. The current grill-me to plan to beads to coding-agent flow appears as one possible configuration; grill-me, beads, bv, bvr, particular models, and CodeCompanion are not presented as LouiseLM requirements. CodeCompanion is not mentioned.
8. Current ACP chat and session capabilities are distinguished from unimplemented idea capture, ranking, orchestration, and dashboard work.
9. An original banner depicts Louise Michel within a decentralized mesh of people, agents, models, skills, tools, voice capture, ideas, and code. It uses a red, black, and white Commune-era printmaking aesthetic fused with a modern systems diagram, informed by Metelkova street-art energy, with no labels or explanatory text.
10. Existing technical instructions remain accurate and mostly intact beneath the new narrative.

## Implementation Notes

- Expand the top of the existing README rather than replacing the technical reference.
- Add one project-local raster hero asset and reference it with a repository-relative path.
- Use project voice: one brief empowering manifesto-like passage followed by concrete language.
- The visual carries the Louise Michel reference; do not explain that reference in prose.
- Emancipation concerns ideas, workflows, and user choice, never unbounded agent authority.

## Testing Notes

- Documentation and image generation do not require an artificial red test.
- Inspect the final Markdown structure and rendered image reference.
- Run formatting, static-analysis, test, and diff checks required by the repository contract; report any unavailable gate.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing idea storage, capture devices, voice transcription, scheduling, triage, orchestration, dashboards, or agent review.
- Designing a formal plugin API, workflow event schema, storage architecture, mobile application, external daemon, graph UI, or swarm scheduler.
- Changing existing public Lua APIs or technical behavior.
close_reason: Expanded README with the agreed LouiseLM vision, recursive acronym, alpha/current-state boundary, configurable workflow example, attention and safety principles, and corrected single-file test command. Added and inspected an original 1774x887 red-black-white mesh hero as a 640 KB WebP. Verification: stylua --check passed; lua-language-server reported no problems; all 66 MiniTest cases passed after rerunning outside the read-only temp-file sandbox; git diff --check passed; external essay link returned HTTP 200.

title: Failed DeepSeek Session remains on phone but is absent from Resume
