title: Sol/high rejects turns with quota remaining
description:
A ChatGPT Plus user selecting gpt-5.6-sol/high could not continue an active Codex Session despite 10% of the five-hour allowance remaining. Four turns terminated with server_overloaded, including a trivial commit request and an escalation request. The failure strands in-flight work and gives neither retry timing nor a way to preserve the requested Sol-quality continuation.

## Observed

Session: codex/01a0561f-7394-7241-9267-feec92c16e5f on 2026-08-31, LouiseLM via acp-llm-adapter.

Codex transcript: /home/lotso/.codex/sessions/2026/08/31/rollout-2026-08-31T06-41-36-01a0561f-7394-7241-9267-feec92c16e5f.jsonl

- line 2517, 07:25:05: server_overloaded after 172463 ms
- line 2573, 07:27:58: server_overloaded after 4866 ms
- line 2598, 07:29:43: server_overloaded after 48356 ms
- line 2605, 07:31:32: server_overloaded after 2789 ms
- line 2601 confirms gpt-5.6-sol with high reasoning
- line 2604 reports 131058 last-turn tokens against a 258400 context window, primary five-hour usage 90%, and rate_limit_reached_type null

Exact terminal error: Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.
Exact classification: codex_error_info=server_overloaded.

ACP proxy evidence: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a0561f-7394-7241-9267-feec92c16e5f/log.jsonl. It contains the same Agent message followed by end_turn; no LouiseLM transport or protocol error precedes it.

## Symptoms

- Paid allowance remains, but the selected model cannot be used.
- Repeated retries fail after waits ranging from 2.8 to 172 seconds.
- The user must abandon Sol/high quality or stop work.
- The same Session became available again after 07:33, showing intermittent capacity rather than an exhausted account limit.

## Root cause

Confirmed boundary: upstream Codex returns server_overloaded for gpt-5.6-sol/high. The internal scheduler or capacity mechanism is unknown. Evidence rules out context exhaustion and an ordinary five-hour rate-limit rejection. It does not prove whether the approximately 131k-token long-session input contributes; compare a fresh Sol/high Session at the same time to discriminate.

## Why it was not caught

LouiseLM tests model ACP lifecycle and errors, not OpenAI model scheduling or paid-plan capacity. The Codex response exposes only a generic model-capacity message and no retry-after or incident identifier.

## Fix direction

Escalate the four turn IDs and Session ID to OpenAI Support for scheduler correlation. Upstream should either serve Sol/high while allowance remains or return actionable retry timing and a continuation-safe fallback. Verify that server_overloaded attempts do not consume five-hour allowance. LouiseLM cannot manufacture model capacity; a separate local UX task would be needed for an optional model-fallback prompt.

## Acceptance

- OpenAI correlates the Session and four failed turn IDs to a capacity incident or documented policy.
- Sol/high can continue while allowance remains, or the response provides a truthful retry time/availability state.
- Retrying does not silently consume allowance for work that never starts.
- A fresh-versus-long Session comparison establishes whether input size affects admission.

## Not covered

No access to OpenAI scheduler logs. No claim that LouiseLM caused the overload. Automatic fallback to another model is intentionally out of scope because it changes requested model quality.

comments.author: codex/01a056ef-03ae-7203-885d-c73b4ba00d1b
comments.text: Deferred: evidence points to upstream Codex model-capacity behavior, outside LouiseLM control. Support contacted; Codex CLI feedback routes to GitHub, but this is an ACP/upstream scheduling issue with no actionable local fix.

title: QA round: Firebase Installation ID migration acceptance
description:
# Manual QA — Firebase Installation ID migration

Active scratch for `louiselm-qbr.9.24`, owned by
`codex/01a0c338-6dfc-79e0-a97f-7a6f73716e0a`.
Archive the final round into a qa-round Bead; do not commit this scratch.

## Build and baseline

- Source: `3491658` (`feat(push)!: migrate addressing to FIDs`). Android and
  capture-service source trees clean when checked.
- Phone: USB `ba5hfqzhvgiru4ai`, Xiaomi 21081111RG.
- Normal package: `dev.louiselm.capture`, version 0.1.0; last updated September 16.
- Candidate configured normal APK SHA-256:
  `64285faa654d5528e84959bef59c819f79881fcba5b6a3010098f7402f546a76`.
  Package and installation-ID manifest flag verified.
- Candidate configured QA APK SHA-256:
  `292e12cae972b913dd0b6e415c33eebe8d4321066c306971d40c36bc14cec512`.
- Existing receiver executable SHA-256:
  `73b77b215f1bc6cfd4b5f451c551ba204cec576936b409e6ec7e4f4a9c16b429`.
  Running PID 658468 matched installed binary before deployment.
- New release receiver build succeeded; SHA-256
  `c5fdf300258adb0a7d48a78dff3022fcbb199471f363b80985273c8011972206`.
- Receiver: overlay `https://100.90.156.114:7392`; schema 2; one paired device
  `bf17b278-ac07-4c32-8845-142008920cbc`; sender ready, enabled, submitted generation
  1210, attempts 0. No retained Runs returned by the CLI.
- Normal phone: 38 capture directories; pairing preferences SHA-256
  `f814ffca1cb761b0c366abfb4feaff41ff751679d7f7e96820d07a83a4aaf5f0`;
  notifications enabled/registered/prepared, notified 1210, seen 1068.
- Retained normal capture UUID `05a655b1-d602-4a1f-b543-2540899e4c7d`:
  audio SHA-256 `62080f4e450476ff003ea36cdfa57af5611faebd0dc4186a59151e585480668e`;
  manifest SHA-256 `349821e8c58af6f480d1cdb6078bc51664e60bb78b0f245151af3da5ba848fce`.
- QA phone: two captures, old revoked pairing, blocked=true. Prior round
  `louiselm-qbr.9.9.14` confirms deliberate revocation. It cannot prove an
  existing working pairing migrates without first constructing a new fixture.

## Status

| Case | State |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Upgrade preserves pairing/capture and registers FID | Passed: maintainer confirms inbox after connecting Tailscale; installation_registered=true, same device enabled, retained pairing/audio/manifest hashes unchanged |
| 2. New generation wakes background app with generic text | Passed: maintainer confirms generic alert and tap opens inbox; sender submitted1223 and phone notified/seen/cache1223 |
| 3. Confirmed generation remains suppressed across restart | Passed restart/no-reminder observation: maintainer says “it lloked ok”; submitted/notified1234 unchanged, Attention1237 empty for45s |
| 4. Tailscale loss and recovery | Passed: offline alert/error confirmed; reconnect loads one Attention item without re-pairing; cache/seen advanced1236, overlay online, pairing hash unchanged |
| 5. Revocation/replacement isolates old installation and inbox | Passed: revoked QA device removed; fresh QA device registered and received generation 1268; recordings unchanged |

## Setup and boundaries

Upgrade the receiver and selected configured APK together, without clearing app
data. Before upgrading, hash the retained capture's immutable audio/manifest and
pairing preferences; verify the same values afterward. Record the new receiver
binary hash and verify the running executable matches it. Read pairing state only
through sanitized projections: never print credentials, tokens, FIDs or inbox
payloads. Human observations establish notification display and phone UI behavior;
sender acknowledgement establishes only FCM submission.

The maintainer authorized the normal app/receiver upgrade with “yes”.
Do not revoke its pairing merely to prepare another case.

### Deployment evidence

Receiver restarted as PID 729324; installed and running executable both match
`c5fdf300258adb0a7d48a78dff3022fcbb199471f363b80985273c8011972206`.
Old binary retained at
`/home/lotso/.local/state/louiselm/fid-upgrade.SeDxeK/louiselm-capture.previous`.
Normal APK installed with `adb install -r`: Success. No app data cleared.
Registry is now schema 3, with the same device ID and submitted generation 1213
(advanced from baseline before this upgrade). Old address is disabled pending
first FID registration; sender remains ready. All 38 captures remain, and pairing,
selected capture audio and manifest hashes exactly match the baseline.
Requested human action: open normal app, Attention inbox, Refresh with Tailscale
connected; confirm inbox loads without re-pairing.

### First phone check: network prerequisite missing

Maintainer answered “no” to inbox loading. Read-only UI inspection confirms
“Inbox unavailable: receiver is unreachable” while the app still shows its
existing pairing. Pairing preferences hash remains unchanged. Android has
`installation_prepared=true` but no `installation_registered`; the receiver
target remains disabled. Desktop Tailscale is Running/online; its Xiaomi peer
is offline (last seen September 19). No Tailscale process is running on the phone,
and the receiver IP routes through ordinary Wi-Fi rather than the overlay.
Receiver remains active and listening on `100.90.156.114:7392`.

This is a missing test prerequisite, not evidence of lost pairing or a migration
defect. After connecting Tailscale, maintainer confirms the inbox loads.
Independent check: phone peer online; installation_registered=true; same receiver
device enabled, sender ready, attempts 0, submitted generation still 1213.
Phone cache/seen advanced to 1221; receiver generation 1221 has no unresolved
items. Pairing and retained capture audio/manifest hashes still match baseline.

## Cases

### 1. Upgrade and first registration

Exercises `3491658`: receiver registry migration and Android AttentionWorker.
After the coordinated upgrade, open the selected app, open Attention inbox and
refresh; enable notifications only if requested. Expect the existing pairing
and recordings to remain, with successful private inbox access and a registered
FID. Failure: new pairing required, lost capture, registration error or a retry
loop. Evidence: unchanged device ID, pairing/capture hashes and capture count;
registry schema 3; registered/enabled target without displaying its address.

### 2. Background delivery

Exercises `3491658`: HTTP v1 FID sender and AttentionMessagingService.
Press Home to background the app without force-stopping it. Let this QA Session
(`codex/01a0c338-6dfc-79e0-a97f-7a6f73716e0a`) finish its turn **while a normal file,
not this chat, is the current Neovim buffer**, then leave Neovim
idle for 45 seconds (eligibility starts after 30). Expect a new notification with
only “LouiseLM needs your attention” and fixed generic text. Tap it to fetch the
private inbox. Failure: no delivery despite a confirmed new submission, private
content in the alert, or inability to open the inbox. Record generation and the
human's exact observation separately.

Result: maintainer answered “yes” to generic notification delivery and tap opening
the inbox. Receiver submitted generation 1223, enabled=true, attempts=0. Phone
notified/seen/cached_generation all equal 1223. This establishes actual phone
delivery separately from sender acknowledgement.

### 3. Restart deduplication

Exercises persistent submitted/seen/notified generation handling.
After accepting a notification, reopen/restart the app and restart the receiver
at a safe boundary without creating another eligible Attention generation.
Expect no reminder for the confirmed generation. Then create a new eligible
generation and expect one alert. Evidence: unchanged confirmed generation and
submission attempts during the quiet interval; phone observation establishes no
duplicate. Do not mistake a force-stopped app for a background-delivery fixture.

Receiver restarted as PID 769055 and retained submitted1223/attempts0 while
Attention remained1223. After the 45-second observation interval, receiver
submitted1224 and phone notified/cached1224 (seen1223); Attention had advanced
to1225. This was not a controlled unchanged-generation interval. A new alert
cannot be classified as replay merely from its generic identical text.
Current Attention subject is another Session, `01a0c342-f0e9-7c40-96dd-3fddb80d43c4`.
Human phone restart observation remains pending; do not mark the full case passed.

Second receiver restart: empty Run list, sender submitted1234 and Attention1237
empty immediately before/after restart and after45s. Phone notified remains1234,
seen/cache1236, no active LouiseLM notification. No duplicate or fresh generation
occurred in this controlled interval. Human phone restart/no-reminder confirmation
is still required to mark the full physical case passed.
Maintainer then confirmed “it lloked ok”; restart/no-reminder observation accepted.
No deliberate replay of an older FCM payload was injected in this round.

### 4. Private-network outage

With internet retained, disconnect Tailscale on the phone and trigger a new
eligible generation. Expect generic notification delivery; tap should show a
retryable unavailable inbox. Restore Tailscale and refresh/reopen: private inbox
recovers. Failure: permanent pairing failure, lost state or no recovery. Record
the human's network/UI observations and sanitized sender/app retry state.

Maintainer reported “i didnt see one”. Independent evidence: receiver
submitted1229/enabled/attempts0, phone notified1229 but cache/seen1227, Tailscale
phone peer offline, app not force-stopped and notification permission granted.
Android events record an enqueue at 11:44:59.744 and alert at 11:45:00.016 local,
then a notification click and auto-cancel at 11:46:35.772–773. No active LouiseLM
notification remains. These events prove posting/click handling, not the exact
human-observed outcome of this test. Requested clarification whether that tap
showed “receiver is unreachable”. No product bug or physical pass inferred.

Maintainer is unsure about the earlier tap. Recipe correction: `Attention:turn_done`
in `lua/louiselm/ui/attention.lua:377` clears/suppresses a viewed completion;
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1233` passes current-buffer visibility. The original
instruction to stay idle after reading the reply did not ensure an unseen turn.
This explains why the inspected Attention subjects belonged to another Session;
it is a recipe defect, not a demonstrated product defect.

Controlled retest: baseline submitted/notified1229, no current Attention items
(generation1230), phone Tailscale offline, no active LouiseLM notification.
Tell maintainer to press Home on phone and switch Neovim to a normal file before
this turn ends. Agent waits30s before finishing. Leave editor untouched for45s
after completion. Observe generic alert and tap while overlay remains off; expect
retryable receiver-unreachable inbox. Then reconnect overlay and Refresh.

Retest report: maintainer answered “yes”. Phone events show fresh posts/taps at
11:58:06/11:58:13 and11:58:20/11:58:30 local. Receiver submitted1234, phone
notified1234 while cache/seen stayed1227; phone Tailscale remains offline. Record
the offline delivery/inbox retest as confirmed, but not recovery: requested
reconnect Tailscale and Refresh inbox, without re-pairing.

Recovery passed: maintainer reports “no repair needed and i see 1 attention needed”.
Phone Tailscale online; cache/seen advanced to1236; same pairing hash and receiver
device ID, enabled=true/attempts0. Receiver had subsequently cleared to1237 empty
by inspection, consistent with live Session activity; the earlier one-item screen
is not a discrepancy or a fixed inbox-count expectation.

### 5. Pairing lifecycle isolation

Use a selected disposable QA pairing for revocation/replacement. Record its exact
device ID before revocation. Verify refresh rejects the revoked pairing and
background fetch/registration stops. Renew/replace pairing through the normal QR
flow, opt in, and verify delivery resumes with a fresh installation; old queued
work must not publish an old inbox. Preserve recording UUIDs/audio. Evidence:
sanitized device registry and pairing-scoped app state; compare installation
identity privately and report only whether it changed.

Preparation: updated `dev.louiselm.capture.qa` with the verified configured
APK292e12cae972b913dd0b6e415c33eebe8d4321066c306971d40c36bc14cec512,
using `adb install -r` (Success). QA pairing preferences hash and both recordings'
audio/manifest hashes exactly match the pre-update baseline. No app data cleared.
Invoked the existing `:LouiselmCapturePair` UI to display a one-time QR without
printing its secret to tool output. Human scans it from **LouiseLM QA**, not the
normal app, then enables notifications with Tailscale connected. Record the new
receiver device ID before any revocation; normal device
`bf17b278-ac07-4c32-8845-142008920cbc` is excluded from that test.

QA immutable baselines:
- `ee628f08-4a71-4291-a57f-14922ef17a59`: audio
  `8ebdcd2eca6925e80d27ae029596d01df19ba04f16419659656a9ff8120e24d6`,
  manifest `8aada5f85bf5016b026bb0d339dcd8cf6c443266a10ef38c87208c478157bdde`.
- `133c9513-4359-4892-83ea-f0c39b681856`: audio
  `f4dd739ac5948ea7df4d5b6c4a67fc280cf609567b91da31192c332823ce4f31`,
  manifest `da6d93fafea22d56e5a844f8c0a986e41599983479911ad21543f8096ba06fec`.

### Pairing attempt result

QA UI reported “Notifications need a valid pairing and writable app storage.
Repair pairing and try again.” Read-only inspection found 5.1 GB free on
`/data/user/0`; this is not a storage-capacity failure. QA
`attention-push.xml` still has `blocked=true` and the old owner hash, proving
the new QR pairing did not complete. Normal app and pairing remain untouched.
Repeat the QR scan and wait for explicit pairing success before opening Inbox.

The completed QA pairing registered device
`68a06c12-1f12-4eef-944f-30664d423974`. Revoking exactly that device removed it
from the receiver; the normal device
`bf17b278-ac07-4c32-8845-142008920cbc` remained enabled and registered. Both QA
recording audio/manifest hashes remained identical. This proves old QA pairing
isolation and normal-device preservation. A fresh QR renewal is still needed to
prove a new installation can register and deliver again; do not reuse the old
QA credential.

Renewal passed at registration: new QA device
`89f71b50-b3e1-4917-b8f1-cc88738849c5` replaced the revoked device, QA
`blocked` state is absent, `installation_registered=true`, and receiver reports
two devices (new QA plus untouched normal). All four QA audio/manifest hashes
match baseline. The maintainer then confirmed a notification arrived on the
renewed QA pairing. Receiver submitted generation 1268 to both the renewed QA
device and untouched normal device, attempts 0, sender ready. ADB disconnected
before the final phone-state pull, so human observation proves display/tap while
receiver submission proves routing. No old QA credential was reused.

## Findings and cleanup

No product finding. QA's revoked pairing and temporary Tailscale outage were
fixture conditions. All requested migration, outage/recovery, restart,
revocation, renewal and delivery cases are accepted. Normal app and pairing
remain untouched; QA recordings remain unchanged.
Receiver and normal app upgraded; no revocation or app-data deletion. Automated coverage
and full gates are recorded on `louiselm-qbr.9.23`; this round targets physical
behavior those tests cannot prove. Record temporary fixtures and their disposition
before closing, and retain this issue until exact physical acceptance is confirmed.
close_reason: Round archived in this Beads record; physical cases and evidence are complete. live:codex/01a0c338-6dfc-79e0-a97f-7a6f73716e0a

title: Deploy the curated site from protected GitLab CI
description:
## Goal
Build every site change and publish only the reviewed static artifact to Firebase Hosting from protected main without a stored Google credential.

## Scope
- In scope: credential-free merge-request build, retained build artifact, manual or protected-main live deployment through existing WIF, pinned MyST and Firebase CLI versions, and sanitized logs.
- Out of scope: OpenTofu apply, registrar access, raw transcript publication, and Agent-controlled production deployment.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Merge requests run the strict site build and artifact policy without cloud credentials.
2. Production deployment is restricted to protected main and uses ADC/WIF rather than FIREBASE_TOKEN or a service-account key.
3. The deploy command targets only the generated public directory and the configured Hosting site.
4. A successful deployment is reachable on the generated web.app hostname and its release identifier is retained for rollback.

## Testing
- Validate merged GitLab CI.
- Run the exact build image and commands locally where possible.
- Complete live acceptance only after WIF and Hosting exist.

## Notes
Do not grant merge-request branches cloud credentials merely to obtain previews; build artifacts provide the initial review boundary.

title: Enable strict Rust gates in skills-core
description:
Adopt the strict Rust policy requested in codex/01a07354-d702-77b2-a532-dbd96f279510 and recorded by louiselm-klkw.

Evidence (2026-09-05, rustc/clippy 1.97.1): 538 distinct production diagnostic locations/messages with the proposed lint set. 177 missing_errors_doc, 138 must_use_candidate, 75 expect_used, 27 missing_panics_doc; 2 unsafe blocks and 1 undocumented_unsafe_blocks at src/sandbox.rs:1415. Counts were deduplicated by code/message/file/line; this is a lint baseline, not 538 proven runtime defects. All-target testing also reports test panic/expect uses, which policy explicitly permits.

Reproduce from skills-core/:
cargo clippy --offline --locked --lib --bins --all-features -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::unwrap_used -W clippy::expect_used -W clippy::panic -W clippy::todo -W clippy::unimplemented -W missing_docs -W unsafe_code -W unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn -W clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks

Scope: fix existing violations; configure Cargo.toml package lints for clippy::all and clippy::pedantic plus the named Rust/restriction lints; configure precise test-only panic/expect allowances; reject blanket suppressions. Deny unsafe_code; review the two existing pre_exec sites and record narrow justified exceptions with real safety invariants. Prefer ownership-based descriptor handling where simpler. Preserve privileged launch, identity, cgroup confinement, receipt order, disposal, and production callback contracts; no speculative bootstrap redesign.

Acceptance: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test --all-features --locked; RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --all-features --locked. Wire the stricter commands into this crate's existing CI job and prove the gate fails on a deliberate representative violation before restoring it. Required privileged CI fixtures still apply; do not claim manual acceptance.
close_reason: gate:.github/workflows/ci.yml:289

comments.text: Unsafe review: two existing production boundaries retained with site-local expectations and SAFETY obligations: owned descriptor CLOEXEC changes child-local; owned cgroup.procs File writes before exec can fork. Parent-side CLOEXEC changes permit concurrent inheritance; parent-side cgroup admission races descendants; helper/dependency adds no necessary mechanism. Both test-only inheritance sites are separately justified; pre_exec owns its duplicated fd, only the trusted subprocess helper borrows its inherited raw fd. References: std CommandExt::pre_exec, std BorrowedFd::borrow_raw, kernel cgroup-v2 migration docs. No new unsafe operation.

title: Spawn hook does not own its borrowed descriptors
description:
The private safe spawn-hook helper cannot enforce the lifetime required by its unsafe BorrowedFd construction. No current production misuse observed; sandbox prepare keeps Gate alive.

## Observed
2026-09-05, codex/01a07366-5b3e-7ba3-90eb-bed8bf017808. skills-core/src/sandbox/host_identity.rs:90 accepts &self; :175 takes RawFd; :180 constructs BorrowedFd::borrow_raw(raw_fd) inside a stored pre_exec closure. The function returns while Command retains only a number, not its owner.

## Root cause
Dropping Gate before spawning Command closes those descriptors; the stored closure can then borrow a closed or reused descriptor. The source SAFETY comment asserts lifetime but the safe API cannot enforce it. Current caller sandbox.rs:1407-1448 happens to obey the ordering.

## Why not caught
Existing tests cover status parsing and fail-closed datagram EOF behavior, not descriptor ownership across delayed spawn.

## Fix direction
Transfer OwnedFd into Command closures, then drop Command immediately after spawn to preserve parent endpoint closure timing. Existing rustix fcntl keeps CLOEXEC changes child-local. Parent-side flag changes risk inheritance by concurrent spawns; a new helper process/dependency adds no necessary mechanism. Keep reviewed pre_exec for async-signal-safe fcntl and pre-exec cgroup admission.

## Acceptance
Owned descriptors enforce the hook lifetime; tests prove delayed spawn after Gate drop works and parent endpoints close when Command drops. Do not execute the invalid old lifetime to obtain a red test: that would deliberately violate BorrowedFd safety. Run safe structural ownership characterization before and behavioral regression after repair.

## Not covered
No claim of a live launcher exploit or installed-workflow acceptance; existing privileged conformance remains required.
close_reason: gate:skills-core/src/sandbox/host_identity.rs:361

comments.text: Refined red test: inspect /proc/self/fd symlink targets after Gate drop without invoking the unsafe hook. This safely proves ownership loss; the repaired regression also spawns the child.

Regression proves the descriptors survive Gate drop and actual exec; separate EOF regression proves Command drop releases the parent status endpoint. Both pass. Lesson destination: this issue; root AGENTS already requires descriptor ownership at unsafe boundaries.

title: Disposed prepared Session panics on startup
description:
During louiselm-xhgy, source review found PreparedSession::dispose clears session and startup_gate, while public start(self) calls expect on both (skills-core/src/sandbox.rs:969-1015). A caller retaining the disposed value can trigger a panic instead of the advertised Result failure.

Observed: 2026-09-06, codex/01a07366-5b3e-7ba3-90eb-bed8bf017808. Source: startup_gate.as_mut().expect("a prepared Session owns its startup gate"); dispose sets startup_gate = None and session = None.

Cause: the normal disposed state is treated as an internal invariant violation in start. No current production caller misuse or installed workflow failure observed.

Test gap: startup and cleanup tests do not call start after successful disposal. Add a public lifecycle regression using the existing shell-child fixture: dispose then start must return SandboxError::Refused without unwinding. Keep Drop cleanup and live/privileged conformance unchanged.

Fix: return a typed refusal at the startup boundary; retain narrow invariant checks only after the live-state guard. Not covered: changing infallible observation accessors after disposal.
close_reason: gate:skills-core/src/sandbox.rs:2176

comments.text: Regression disposed_prepared_session_refuses_start_without_panicking: RED at sandbox.rs:973 (startup-gate expect); GREEN after start takes the gate through typed Refused. Real fixture child disposed/reaped before retry. Observation accessors retain documented after-disposal misuse panics. Lesson destination: this issue; no new standing rule.

title: Failed identity release can clear its poison marker before unlock
description: Evidence: IdentityLease::release truncates the durable cleanup marker before seek/sync_all. If a later operation fails, SystemIdentityGuard has consumed and drops the lease; the slot is now empty and immediately reacquirable even though release returned CleanupUnproven.\n\nMake failed release restore and fsync the poison marker before unlocking, or preserve ownership so the caller can poison it. Add injected post-truncate failure coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Any identity-release I/O failure leaves the slot durably nonempty and unreacquirable before the file lock drops; successful proven-empty cleanup still clears and reuses it.
close_reason: gate:skills-core/src/launcher_install/identity.rs:944

comments.author: codex/01a068c6-2ca1-7be3-88ff-96c887e50df0
comments.text: Lesson routed issue-local: post-truncate release failure restores and fsyncs poison before unlock; if restoration is unprovable, the kernel lock is retained.

title: Trusted release cannot bundle louiselm-launch or the control service yet
description:
louiselm-d6fv.7 AC2 lists the bundle contents as `louiselm-skills`, `louiselm-launch`, the control-service binary, shared schemas/policy, dependency lock, hashes, source identity, and release manifest. Only `louiselm-skills`, the policy, and the schema set exist today: `louiselm-launch` comes from louiselm-d6fv.4 and the control service from louiselm-qbr.5.1, and d6fv.7 blocks d6fv.4 rather than the reverse.

`release::ALLOWED_COMPONENTS` already names all three, so adding them is a matter of passing the built binaries to `release::assemble` — the manifest, install, and verification paths need no change.

## What to do when d6fv.4 lands

Extend `release build` to build and bind `louiselm-launch`, and add a check that a release declaring a component it cannot produce is refused rather than shipped short. That refusal is the part worth a test: a bundle missing a component today verifies fine, because nothing declares the component in the first place.

title: Killed Neovim leaves the Agent process chain alive forever
description:
When Neovim dies without running its exit autocmds — SIGKILL, OOM kill, X/Wayland
session crash, terminal emulator killed — every process LouiseLM spawned with
`vim.system` keeps running forever, reparented to pid 1. For an ACP Session that
is the whole `acp-proxy -> node adapter -> agent binary` chain, roughly 500 MB
resident per abandoned Session, held until reboot. Disposal is wired only to
`VimLeavePre`, which by definition does not fire on the abnormal path. Nothing
detects or reclaims the survivors afterwards.

## Observed

Session `claude/b8a727cc-bb08-4b28-bfc6-eff5469a4c08`, 2026-09-07, on the
maintainer's Linux workstation (Neovim 0.12.5, uptime since 2026-08-29 19:36).

Found incidentally while diagnosing Ghostty refusing to open new windows with
`error.SystemResources`. The trigger turned out to be memory pressure: 16-21 GiB
of 27 GiB swap in use. The cause was the same failure class in a different
plugin — 94 orphaned `copilot-language-server` processes, all with `ppid=1`,
totalling 6104 MB RSS, accumulated since Aug 30 while exactly one Neovim was
running:

```
$ ps -eo pid=,ppid=,rss=,lstart=,args= | grep 'mason/bin/copilot-language-server --stdio'
count: 94
orphans (ppid=1): 94
total RSS MB: 6104.3
oldest: pid 93446 ppid 1 Sun Aug 30 05:36:52 2026 46308 KB
        node /home/lotso/.local/share/nvim/mason/bin/copilot-language-server --stdio
distinct ppids: 94 x 1
```

Start times cluster in bursts (7 on Sep 4 08:04, 8 on Sep 4 08:11, 7 on
Sep 4 08:43, 6 on Sep 7 05:14), one burst per Neovim launch that later died
badly. That plugin is not ours — see Not covered — but it proves the failure
class is live and expensive on this machine, and LouiseLM's children are an
order of magnitude larger than Copilot's ~65 MB each.

Mechanism reproduced directly against Neovim 0.12.5:

```
$ cat /tmp/leaktest2.lua
vim.system({ "sleep", "517" }, {})
vim.wait(60000, function() return false end)

$ nvim --headless -u NONE -l /tmp/leaktest2.lua & NVPID=$!
child while nvim alive:   4088633 4088631 sleep 517
$ kill -9 $NVPID
child after SIGKILL:      4088633       1 sleep 517
```

Neovim does not reap `vim.system` children on exit; they are reparented to init
and survive.

Live LouiseLM chain for the session that filed this bug, for size reference:

```
4086101 4085762   4964 KB  acp-proxy -- node .../claude-agent-acp/dist/index.js
4086119 4086101 120760 KB  node .../claude-agent-acp/dist/index.js
4086137 4086119 381748 KB  .../claude-agent-sdk-linux-x64/claude --output-format stream-json ...
```

No orphaned `acp-proxy` chain was present at filing time, so the LouiseLM
instance of this leak is proven by code and by the reproduction above, not yet
by a field sighting.

## Symptoms

- The machine slowly runs out of memory over days of use. Nothing points at the
  editor: the survivors have no parent and no window.
- New GUI windows fail to open (`error.SystemResources` from Ghostty here), the
  system swaps heavily, and only a reboot or a manual hunt for `ppid=1`
  processes fixes it.
- An abandoned Agent process keeps its API session and workspace access alive
  after the editor that authorized it is gone.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/acp/transport.lua:172` spawns the Agent with `vim.system`. The only
thing that stops it is `Transport:close()` at
`lua/louiselm/acp/transport.lua:216`, which sends SIGTERM through the handle.

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:408` is the sole trigger for the whole-editor
case: a `VimLeavePre` autocmd calling `session_module().dispose_all()`.
`ExitPre` at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:385` only warns about live
Sessions. Both are in-process Neovim events. Neither runs when the process is
killed rather than asked to quit, and as the reproduction shows Neovim itself
does not clean up `vim.system` descendants.

So disposal is correct on the clean path and absent on every other path. Other
`vim.system` call sites (`lua/louiselm/agent/spawn.lua:45`,
`lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:115`, `lua/louiselm/provenance/vintage.lua:127`)
spawn short-lived commands and leak at most one process each;
`lua/louiselm/capture/init.lua:241` is long-lived and has its own kill at
`lua/louiselm/capture/init.lua:274`, reached through the same in-process path,
so it has the same hole. The unbounded, expensive one is the ACP transport,
because it holds a Session for as long as the user works.

## Why it was not caught

Every disposal test runs inside a live Neovim and asserts the clean path.
`tests/ui/command_spec.lua:837` drives the command layer against a stubbed
`acp-proxy`; the transport specs assert `Transport:close()` is called and that
the handle's `kill` was invoked. A test that runs inside Neovim can never
observe its own SIGKILL, so the abnormal path is structurally invisible to the
current suite. Proving this needs an out-of-process test that launches a real
`nvim`, records the descendant pids, kills it uncleanly, and then asserts from
outside that they are gone.

## Fix direction

Make the Agent chain die with its parent at the OS level instead of trusting an
editor event to run. On Linux that is `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM)` armed
in the child between fork and exec. `vim.system` exposes no pre-exec hook, so it
belongs in the process that is already sitting in that slot: `acp-proxy` (an
external Rust binary, `~/.cargo/bin/acp-proxy`) launches the node adapter and
can arm PDEATHSIG for itself and forward the signal to its own child. Note the
guard has to cover the whole chain, not just the first hop — the Copilot census
above is what a partially-armed chain looks like.

Rejected, with reasons:

- A reaper timer inside Neovim. It cannot run; the editor is the thing that died.
- Hardening `VimLeavePre`/`ExitPre` further. They already work; they are simply
  never reached on this path.
- Scanning for `ppid=1` LouiseLM descendants at next startup and killing them.
  Racy and wrong with more than one Neovim open: another live editor's Agent is
  indistinguishable from an orphan by name alone.
- `systemd-run --scope` per Session. Ties the plugin to systemd and, judging by
  the 21 stale `app-ghostty-surface-transient-*` scopes on this same machine,
  does not reliably reap either.

## Acceptance

- A regression test outside Neovim: start a real `nvim` with a LouiseLM ACP
  Session against a stub Agent, capture the full descendant pid set, `kill -9`
  the editor, then assert every captured pid is gone within a bounded wait.
  Fails before the fix, passes after.
- After an abnormal Neovim death,
  `ps -eo ppid=,args= | awk '$1==1'` lists no `acp-proxy`, adapter, or Agent
  process.
- The clean path keeps working: `:qa` with a live Session still disposes it and
  still writes the abandonment record.

## Not covered

- The 94 orphaned `copilot-language-server` processes are not LouiseLM's code.
  They come from the mason-installed Copilot LSP and its Neovim client config in
  the maintainer's dotfiles, and are recorded here only as the field evidence
  for this failure class. Cleaning them up and fixing that client belong in the
  dotfiles repo, not this one.
- 21 `app-ghostty-surface-transient-*` systemd user scopes were stuck `active
  running` with dead or zero MainPID. Separate Ghostty/systemd issue, not
  investigated, cosmetic as far as memory goes.
- Only Linux was tested. `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` does not exist on macOS or BSD; the
  fix needs a per-platform answer that this bead does not choose.
- Not established: whether an orphaned Agent can still act on the workspace, or
  whether it blocks immediately on a dead stdin. That decides whether this is
  also a safety bug and not only a resource one.
- Related but distinct: louiselm-namespace-only-orphan-a29a covers Bubblewrap
  NamespaceOnly disposal in skills-core trusting an empty descendant list. Same
  family — a disposal path that believes a child died when it did not — but a
  different layer and a different mechanism.

title: Blog publishing pipeline never wires the highlighted transcript fragment into the built page
description:
`render-post.sh` generates a highlighted HTML fragment and a matching CSS
file for a transcript excerpt, but nothing in the publishing pipeline ever
references either — the built, served blog page shows the excerpt as plain
text (MyST's own generic `hljs` highlighting, not the nvim-generated one),
with no styling and no visual distinction from any other code block. This is
the last step of the blog publishing pipeline feature (`674939b`, tracked
under the now-closed `blog-publishing-pipeline` feature bead) and it does
not work at all — 0 of N published posts using this mechanism would ever
show the intended highlighted transcript.

## Observed

QA round for the transcript-export/blog-publishing features, case 6 ("does
the highlighted fragment actually reach the published page"),
2026-08-18, working from `blog/post-qa-round` (scaffolded by
`create-blog.sh` in case 5, session `21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384`).

Steps run:
```
cd ~/code/louiselm/blog/post-qa-round
wc -l conversations/*.md   # 3033 lines
# edited blog.md: :lines: 1 -> :lines: 10-40
cd ~/code/louiselm && ./blog/scripts/render-post.sh blog/post-qa-round
# -> "render-post: wrote 1 fragment(s) and nvim-transcript.css to .../blog/post-qa-round"
ls blog/post-qa-round
# -> blog.md, conversations/, conversations-claude-21a0ede3-....L10-40.nvim-transcript.html, nvim-transcript.css
cd blog && myst build --html --strict   # built cleanly, 3 pages, no strict-mode errors
```

Evidence pulled directly from the built site:

- `find /home/lotso/code/louiselm/blog/_build -iname '*nvim-transcript*'` —
  **zero results**. The generated `nvim-transcript.css` never leaves
  `blog/post-qa-round/`; the myst build never copies or references it.
- `grep -o '<link[^>]*>' blog/_build/html/post-qa-round/blog/index.html | grep -i transcript` —
  **zero results**. No stylesheet link to it exists in the served page's
  `<head>` at all.
- The only occurrence of the string "nvim-transcript" anywhere in the built
  output is the inert JSON attribute `"class":"nvim-transcript"` on the
  plain `{literalinclude}` block — that's the `:class: nvim-transcript`
  directive on the literalinclude in `blog.md` being passed through as a CSS
  class with no matching stylesheet to give it any effect. The actual
  generated fragment file
  (`conversations-claude-21a0ede3-....L10-40.nvim-transcript.html`, produced
  by `render-post.sh`) is never included, referenced, or read by anything —
  `blog.md` still holds the plain `{literalinclude}` directive pointing at
  the raw conversation `.md` file, not the generated fragment.
- The code block that does render carries
  `class="block overflow-auto p-3 myst-code-body hljs"` — MyST's own
  generic highlight.js-based styling for an untagged code fence, applied
  because the literalinclude has no language hint. This is visually
  *something*, which is why the page doesn't look broken at a glance — but
  it is not the nvim-specific highlighting the feature is meant to produce,
  and none of `nvim-transcript.css`'s rules apply to it.
- `myst.yml` (`blog/myst.yml:11`) loads exactly one stylesheet:
  `site.options.style: ./blog.css`. No mechanism anywhere adds
  `nvim-transcript.css` to that list, conditionally or otherwise.

## Symptoms

- User sees: a published post's transcript excerpt rendered as a plain,
  unstyled code block — visually indistinguishable from any other fenced
  code block on the site, no indication a special highlighting feature was
  supposed to apply.
- System reports: nothing. `render-post.sh` reports success (and is telling
  the truth — it did produce a correct fragment and CSS file); `myst build
  --strict` succeeds with no warnings; there is no error anywhere in the
  pipeline. The gap is a missing wiring step, not a failure any current
  command surfaces.

## Root cause

`blog/scripts/render-post.sh` (writes `<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` +
`nvim-transcript.css` into the post directory) and `blog.md` / `myst.yml`
(control what MyST actually builds and styles) were built as two
disconnected halves. `blog.md`'s `{literalinclude}` directive was never
changed to consume the generated fragment instead of the raw conversation
file, and `myst.yml`'s `site.options.style` was never made to include
`nvim-transcript.css` (statically, or per-post if that file only exists for
posts using this feature). Exact files: `blog/scripts/render-post.sh`
(generation, confirmed working), `blog/post-qa-round/blog.md` (consumption,
missing), `blog/myst.yml:11` (styling, missing).

## Why it was not caught

`blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh` (referenced in QA_REVIEW.md as covered by
the existing suite) tests `render-post.sh`'s own output — CSS namespacing,
idempotency — in isolation. No test in the suite runs the full pipeline
through an actual `myst build` and inspects the served HTML, because that
requires the mystmd toolchain and a real build, which is exactly what this
manual QA case was written to cover that the suite structurally cannot
reach.

## Fix direction

Two independent pieces, both needed:
1. Have `render-post.sh` (or a follow-up step) rewrite `blog.md`'s
   `{literalinclude}` to point at the generated `.nvim-transcript.html`
   fragment instead of the raw conversation file — or have the fragment
   generation happen as part of a MyST-aware include mechanism rather than a
   side-channel file.
2. Wire `nvim-transcript.css` into the built site's stylesheet — either by
   adding it to `myst.yml`'s `site.options.style` (if it's safe to load
   globally) or by a per-post mechanism, since `style` currently only
   accepts `./blog.css` statically.

Options rejected: none evaluated yet — this bead is filed at the "confirmed
broken, here's exactly where" stage, not the "here's the patch" stage.

## Acceptance

- A post built with a `:lines:` range through the pipeline, when served,
  has a `<link>` (or equivalent) to `nvim-transcript.css` in its page head,
  and the excerpt's rendered HTML matches the generated
  `.nvim-transcript.html` fragment's content (real nvim `:TOhtml`-style
  highlighting), not the raw literalinclude passed through MyST's generic
  `hljs`.
- Regression test: build `blog/post-qa-round` (or an equivalent fixture)
  through `myst build --html --strict` and assert
  `_build/html/**/nvim-transcript.css` exists and is linked from the page
  that embeds the excerpt.

## Not covered

- Whether an excerpt range landing mid-fence (the transcript's own ` ``` `
  fences or `## ` headings) causes a *separate* rendering problem — the
  `:lines: 10-40` range used here happened to land cleanly between a
  heading and the next fence, so that specific risk wasn't exercised. Worth
  a follow-up case with a deliberately fence-straddling range.
- Whether the fix belongs in `render-post.sh`, a new orchestration script,
  or the `create-blog.sh` scaffold step — not decided here.
acceptance_criteria:
- A post built with a `% nvim-transcript: <source> :lines: N-M` marker comment, when run through `myst build --html`, has an `<iframe>` whose `src` is the absolute site-root path of the generated `<post-name>--<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` fragment, and that fragment file exists in the deployed `_build/html/` output, copied there via `project.static_files` in myst.yml (auto-maintained by render-post.mjs, not hand-edited).
- The deployed fragment's content is byte-identical to the one render-post.sh generated locally (proves the static_files copy step actually ran, not just that a stale/partial file exists).
- render-post.sh remains re-runnable: editing a `:lines:` range and re-running regenerates the fragment, blog.md's iframe block, and the myst.yml static_files entry idempotently, without destroying the marker comment that is the author's editable input.
- Regression test (blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh, part 3): a real `myst build --html --strict` against a fixture project asserts the fragment is copied into `_build/html` and that the deployed page's iframe references it at the correct absolute path -- this is the exact gap the bug's "Why it was not caught" section identified as structurally unreachable by the rest of the suite; it is now closed.

Superseded from the original criteria: no shared `nvim-transcript.css` file or `<link>` in the page head exists anymore. Investigation (see closing comment) found MyST's HTML build target does not pass raw HTML through from markdown at all (a literal `<style>`/`<pre>` in blog.md and the `{raw}` directive were both tried and confirmed broken), so delivery goes through an `<iframe>` loading a standalone per-excerpt HTML document instead -- which also makes CSS-selector namespacing and a shared stylesheet unnecessary, since the iframe already isolates each fragment's styling.
close_reason: Fixed: transcript fragments now wired into the deployed page via {iframe} + myst.yml static_files, verified by a real myst build --html --strict regression test (see comment for full design writeup).

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Fixed. Root cause confirmed and two more layers found beyond the original diagnosis:

1. Confirmed MyST's HTML build target has no raw-HTML passthrough at all: a
   literal <style>/<pre> in blog.md gets re-parsed and mangled (TOhtml's
   <span> markup silently stripped), and the {raw} directive only emits
   content for tex/typst export targets -- for html it prints the content as
   escaped literal text. Both empirically verified against myst v1.10.1.
2. `site.options.style` (myst.yml) only accepts a single string, not an
   array -- confirmed by a failed build ("style must be string").
3. The `{iframe}` directive, pointed at an absolute site-root path and paired
   with `project.static_files` in myst.yml, does deliver a fragment's exact
   bytes into the built page -- but `static_files` only accepts literal
   paths (no globs) and copyStaticFiles() flattens every declared file to
   one shared directory by basename, so two posts' same-named fragments
   would silently clobber each other without per-post-prefixed filenames.
4. `{iframe}` has no height option (only width/align/title/placeholder);
   the theme sizes the box via a fixed width-relative aspect ratio it does
   not expose. Fragment documents scroll instead of relying on a height we
   can't set.

Design landed on: standalone per-excerpt HTML documents (inline <style>,
no shared stylesheet, no CSS-selector namespacing -- the iframe's own
isolation makes both unnecessary), embedded via {iframe} at an absolute
`/<post-name>--<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` path, kept in sync with
myst.yml's static_files list by render-post.mjs on every run. blog.md's
authoring format moved from a `{literalinclude}...:class: nvim-transcript`
block to a `% nvim-transcript: <source> :lines: N-M` MyST comment (never
rendered), which render-post.mjs rewrites the following {iframe} block
against on every run without ever touching the comment itself -- this is
what keeps the pipeline re-runnable (create-blog.sh updated to match; both
its own and render-post's test suites updated, 38/38 passing, including a
new real `myst build --html --strict` end-to-end regression test that
verifies the exact wiring gap this bug reported).

Files: blog/scripts/render-post.mjs (rewritten), render-post.sh (header
doc), create-blog.sh (stub format), test-render-post.sh and
test-create-blog.sh (updated + new end-to-end case).

title: Retention tests intermittently refuse sequential operations as locked
description:
Parallel skills-core gates intermittently fail workspace retention operations with a nonblocking lock error, so the full gate cannot certify unrelated changes.

## Observed
2026-09-17, codex/01a0ad75-9830-7931-9560-c669ea29df24, working tree containing f31fd64 (retention) and 4e34954 (typed Beads effects), while verifying louiselm-qbr.5.1.5.5. Ran outside ACP under systemd-run --user --pipe --wait --collect, CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only:
scripts/test-skills-core --no-fail-fast
/tmp/louiselm-replicas.BiNsFf/main-suite-final.log:587:
tests/broker/workspace_retention.rs:26:10:
called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: Workspace(Io(Custom { kind: Other, error: "lock acquisition failed because the operation would block" }))
Broker target: 136 passed, 1 failed, 4 ignored.
Earlier full run also failed workspace::retention::cleanup::tests::expired_live_parked_unproven_and_pinned_storage_remains at src/workspace/retention/cleanup/tests.rs:72 with the same lock-acquisition error; main-suite.log records it.

## Root cause
Unknown. Both failures occur when reacquiring retention storage during process-spawning parallel tests. A fork-inherited descriptor is a hypothesis, not established; distinguish fixture lifetime from production unlock behavior before fixing. Existing admission-lock failures (louiselm-18m2/louiselm-h157) are analogous but do not prove a common cause.

## Why it was not caught
Retention tests pass in other runs but currently assume immediate lock availability across sequential operations under unrelated concurrent spawns.

## Fix direction
Trace lock ownership and release at the retention storage boundary. Preserve refusal of truly competing owners; do not hide contention through retries or weaken assertions without evidence.

## Acceptance
- Deterministic evidence identifies the lock lifetime causing the failure.
- Held-lock denial and post-release success remain covered.
- Repeated full parallel skills-core gates pass, including retention operator restart and cleanup tests.

## Not covered
Deferred from replica work; no retention implementation changed for this finding. Real production contention impact remains unverified.

Flaky target went 2/3 failing to 3/3 passing under parallelism, full suite 1068/0/8 twice, strict gates pass. Standing rule in docs/agent-rust.md; latent fourth site filed as louiselm-conformance-lock-inherited-descriptor-ibes3.

comments.author: claude/36dc56d6-d466-4f8e-952a-113b9cd6a053
comments.text:
Reproduced and narrowed while verifying louiselm-d6fv.5 at 85e232d.

Measured, scripts/test-skills-core --test broker, systemd-run --user, CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only:
- --test-threads=1: 3/3 pass (140 passed, 4 ignored), /tmp/serial-{1,2,3}.log
- default parallelism: 2/3 fail, /tmp/par-{1,2,3}.log; both failures are workspace_retention::retention_operator_path_survives_restart_and_reports_quarantine_without_payloads at tests/broker/workspace_retention.rs:26 with the same 'lock acquisition failed because the operation would block'. One run also took down dependencies::dependency_unattended_scope_must_be_authorized_before_any_session_in_the_run_starts.
- A full suite run earlier today failed the same single test; an earlier full run passed. So it is concurrency, not sequence: the failing call is the pin at line 26, whose own earlier read at line 16 already succeeded in the same thread.

Root cause, strongly supported and not yet proven by a test: skills-core/src/workspace/retention/storage.rs:41 takes the directory flock with try_lock and has no explicit unlock and no Drop impl, so it relies on closing the descriptor. skills-core/src/broker/state_identity.rs:117 already records this exact hazard in this codebase -- 'Closing alone can leave flock held in a concurrently forked child until exec' -- and fixes it there with an explicit exclusive.unlock(). Other skills-core test threads spawn processes constantly, so a child forked during the window inherits the retention lock descriptor and holds the flock past the parent's close. That fits both the intermittency and the clean serial result.

Same missing-unlock shape is present at skills-core/src/workspace/promotion.rs:131 and skills-core/src/conformance/installed/storage.rs:83; not observed failing, worth checking with the fix.

Red test for the fix should fork a child that holds the inherited descriptor and prove the next acquisition still succeeds, rather than relying on timing.

comments.author: claude/36dc56d6-d466-4f8e-952a-113b9cd6a053
comments.text:
Fixed. Root cause confirmed by test, not inference: skills-core/src/workspace/retention/storage.rs held the directory flock and relied on closing its own descriptor, so any descriptor sharing the open file description kept the lock. Store now releases it in Drop. skills-core/src/workspace/promotion.rs Destination had the same shape and the same fix; DestinationIdentity became Copy so inspect() can still read it out of a Drop type.

Red/green: skills-core/src/workspace/retention/storage/tests.rs and promotion/tests.rs clone the descriptor to model the child forked before exec, then assert the next acquisition succeeds. Both failed with the exact production message 'lock acquisition failed because the operation would block' before the fix.

Measured: scripts/test-skills-core --test broker under default parallelism was 2/3 failing before, 3/3 passing after (/tmp/fix-par-{1,2,3}.log). Full suite 2/2 runs pass, 1068 passed 0 failed 8 ignored. fmt, Clippy --all-targets -D warnings, Rustdoc -D warnings and browser13 pass.

Lesson routed to docs/agent-rust.md as a standing rule: release advisory locks explicitly, and prove it with a cloned descriptor rather than timing. Third site in this codebase after broker/state_identity.rs:117. Fourth, unfixed and unobserved, filed as louiselm-conformance-lock-inherited-descriptor-ibes3.

title: Beads inspector: bare-suffix cursor matching (local workspace only)
description:
## Goal

`<leader>lB` opens the local issue directly when the cursor sits on a bare
suffix (e.g. `04cy`, no `louiselm-` prefix), instead of falling through to
the manual `Beads issue id:` prompt.

## Scope

- In scope: `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua` cursor-matching path only. When the
  existing prefixed-ID scan (`issue_id_at_cursor`/`current_issue_id`, exact
  function names may have shifted -- re-read the file first) finds no match
  under the cursor, take the raw token under the cursor and try
  `br show <local-prefix>-<token>` against the local workspace (the same
  `br where`-derived prefix the louiselm-04cy fix already wires up).
- Mirror the bare-id handling louiselm-y8y1 already added to the
  manual-entry prompt path in this same file (prepend the local prefix
  before validating/looking up) -- read that code for the exact pattern
  before writing new logic.
- Out of scope: cross-workspace/sibling lookups (that is a separate task,
  louiselm-r98e's other slice). Do not add any `beads.sibling_roots` config
  or sibling-sweep code here.
- Out of scope: changing the existing prefixed-ID match (case 1, already
  shipped in 729c3f2) -- it must keep taking priority and its behavior must
  not change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given the cursor is on a bare token (e.g. `04cy`) and `<local-prefix>-04cy`
   exists, when `<leader>lB` is pressed, then that issue opens directly, no
   prompt.
2. Given the cursor is on a bare token that does not resolve to any local
   issue, when `<leader>lB` is pressed, then the existing manual
   `Beads issue id:` prompt appears (unchanged fallback).
3. Given the cursor is on an already-fully-prefixed ID (e.g. `louiselm-04cy`),
   when `<leader>lB` is pressed, then behavior is unchanged from before this
   task (bare-suffix logic must not interfere with the existing exact-prefix
   path).

## Testing

- Add cases to `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua` following its existing fake-`br`
  pattern (no real subprocesses, per AGENTS.md determinism rules): bare-token
  hit, bare-token miss falling through to the prompt, and a regression
  confirming the existing prefixed-ID case is untouched.

## Notes

- Full design context and rejected alternatives live in the parent feature
  `louiselm-r98e` and the closed grill question `louiselm-qmmk` -- read those
  before starting if anything here is ambiguous, do not re-derive the design
  from scratch.
- Independently shippable: no dependency on the sibling-sweep task.
close_reason: done

title: Rewrite AGENTS.md for strict idiomatic Neovim Lua
description:
## Goal
Replace the inherited Rust policy with a compact, strict, idiomatic Neovim Lua engineering contract focused on correctness, clarity, simplicity, and fast delivery.

## Scope
- In scope: rewrite the existing AGENTS.md in place for louiselm.nvim; target Neovim embedded LuaJIT/Lua 5.1; define StyLua, lua-language-server, and mini.test gates; lightweight red-green-refactor; LuaCATS/public API rules; module/state/table ownership; structured errors and UI boundaries; strict config validation; safe async vim.system usage; zero runtime dependencies; Neovim API preferences; dangerous Lua escape hatches; concise editing and completion discipline.
- Out of scope: adding formatter, language-server, test harness, Makefile, or CI files; implementing plugin code; including Beads/bv workflow documentation; generic standalone Lua 5.2-5.4 compatibility.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. AGENTS.md contains no Rust/Cargo/Clippy/unsafe-specific policy and no Beads workflow section.
2. The policy is concise and project-specific, with current-stable Neovim and embedded LuaJIT/Lua 5.1 as its runtime contract.
3. The document captures every agreed quality, architecture, error-handling, validation, async/process, dependency, testing, typing, and editing rule without speculative frameworks or compatibility shims.
4. TDD is mandatory for meaningful behavior changes but explicitly lightweight and delivery-oriented.
5. Formatting/static/test completion gates are explicit, and unavailable gates must be reported rather than claimed passing.

## Testing
- Review the rendered Markdown structure and run a text search proving Rust and Beads-specific instructions are gone.
- Check the diff for whitespace errors.
- No Lua project gates are runnable yet because this task intentionally adds no Lua/tooling files.

## Notes
- Rewrite the existing file only; do not proliferate files.
- Prefer enforceable rules over explanatory handbook material.
close_reason: Replaced the inherited Rust policy with a compact strict Neovim Lua contract. Verified no Rust or Beads terms remain; tracked and untracked whitespace checks produced no errors. Lua quality gates are not applicable yet because the repository has no Lua files, LuaLS config, or MiniTest harness.

title: Configured broker projection fails identity checks in hardened user service
description:
Configured broker projection cannot pass root/peer identity checks in the shipped hardened capture user service on the maintainer host.

Observed 2026-09-15 while fixing louiselm-3cn9p: systemd-run --user --pipe --wait --collect -p ProtectSystem=strict /usr/bin/stat -c '%n uid=%u gid=%g mode=%a' /etc prints /etc uid=65534 gid=65534 mode=755. Without ProtectSystem, /etc is uid=0 gid=0 mode=755.
capture-service/src/broker_attention.rs::load still requires parent UID 0 for any existing /etc/louiselm-capture-broker.json. Therefore installing the optional policy would trigger the same startup rejection. Peer SO_PEERCRED broker_uid comparison also needs verification under the production identity mapping.

Current host has no broker policy. louiselm-3cn9p restores ordinary capture when policy is absent; configured-policy rejection remains intentionally fail-closed. No policy or namespace security was weakened.
The existing scripts/test-broker-attention.py gate runs the receiver with setpriv in a privileged mount namespace, not the hardened user unit; it misses this identity view.

Fix direction: establish a supported execution/provisioning model preserving actual root and broker identities under filesystem hardening. Do not accept overflow UID 65534 as root or broker identity. Verify trusted policy succeeds, untrusted files and foreign peers fail, and operator endpoint remains isolated under the actual installed service.
Deferred: independent optional broker deployment work; not enabled in current user configuration. Privileged disposable-VM gate unavailable locally (sudo -n true requires password).
Acceptance: real hardened service accepts valid provisioned policy and dedicated broker projections; malformed or insecure policy and wrong-UID/credential requests fail; CI exercises the installed execution model.
notes: Implementation and all automated gates complete, including fresh-VM installed systemd service acceptance. Optional host broker projection is still unconfigured; no host service restart or provisioning performed. Awaiting privileged host deployment and maintainer confirmation; see capture-service/README.md broker setup steps and latest evidence comment.
close_reason: Maintainer chose close-on-gate: fix 256f0c9 certified in CI by gate:scripts/test-capture-systemd.py (installed system unit, real UIDs, valid/invalid policy and peer). Host activation deferred to louiselm-4iwm1 behind qbr.5.1. Lesson already routed: docs/agent-testing.md (setpriv cannot certify hardened user-unit identity).

title: Run socket rejects null optional Park mutation id
description:
`louiselm-park-observer-inert-puha` now constructs `ParkObserver`, but the first
real Run-socket snapshot is rejected, preventing `:LouiselmResumePark` from
opening its picker. The error occurs for every service Run whose optional
`triggering_mutation_id` is encoded as JSON `null`.

## Observed

2026-09-01 manual QA Case 1, disposable Session
`codex/01a05d64-ece8-77a0-998c-5e44f3be40f1`, Run
`8981f800-c2ea-457f-8238-13e561246679`:

```
louiselm: Park snapshot is malformed
```

`louiselm-capture run list` reports the Run as `cold_parked` with a valid
budget `{ "ceiling": 1, "consumed": 0, "reserved": 0 }`. Its authoritative
Run-socket snapshot contains:

```json
{
  "id": "8981f800-c2ea-457f-8238-13e561246679",
  "revision": 3,
  "state": "cold_parked",
  "generated_work_ceiling": 1,
  "generated_work_consumed": 0,
  "generated_work_reserved": 0,
  "pending_mutation_ids": [],
  "triggering_mutation_id": null,
  "park_expires_at_ms": 1788359713137
}
```

## Symptoms

- `:LouiselmResumePark` reports `louiselm: Park snapshot is malformed`.
- The durable cold-Park picker never opens.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/workflow/park_observer.lua:49` permits a missing Lua field or a
string, but `vim.json.decode` represents JSON `null` as `vim.NIL`, which is
neither. `capture-service/src/runs.rs:646` serializes the optional field as
`null` in every snapshot without a budget-exhaustion mutation.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/workflow/park_observer_spec.lua` constructs Lua snapshot tables that
omit `triggering_mutation_id`; `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:452` also invents a
string. Neither decodes the captured service JSON shape with `null`.

## Fix direction

Normalize `vim.NIL` to absent at the Run-socket parsing boundary or accept it
at the shared Park presentation validator, with a regression based on the
captured snapshot. Do not alter the Rust service: JSON `null` is the correct
encoding for an optional field.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails against a decoded Run-socket snapshot with
  `"triggering_mutation_id":null` and passes after the fix.
- In the reported Session, `:LouiselmResumePark` opens the durable cold-Park
  picker rather than reporting a malformed snapshot.

## Not covered

The original issue's actual budget-exhaustion Park cancellation remains
unverified; this failure happens before that scenario can run.

title: Operator cold-Park discovery and resume
description:
## Goal

Let an operator discover a durable cold-Parked Run after Neovim restarts and resume its recorded ACP Session through the existing asynchronous resume path.

## Scope

- In scope: a read-only capture-service Run listing/show command, an asynchronous Lua client for it, and operator-triggered selection that calls the existing Session API load path with the recorded Agent, ACP Session id, and cwd.
- Out of scope: Android attention delivery, budget changes, Agent-triggered resume, warm-Park behavior, and Provenance actor parsing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A cold-Parked Run can be listed without exposing claim-journal internals or sensitive payloads.
2. Listing and loading are asynchronous; no Neovim main-loop wait or polling is introduced.
3. The operator can select a durable Park and resume it through ACP session/load using the persisted metadata.
4. Resume reports recoverable/lossy status and does not claim the cold Session was restored exactly.
5. Expired/disposed Runs are not offered as resumable Parks.
6. Malformed or unavailable service records produce an actionable error and do not create a replacement Session.

## Testing

- Rust CLI/store coverage for deterministic Run listing and filtering of disposed records.
- Lua service and Chat headless coverage for async discovery, selection, load_session arguments, disposal races, and failure reporting.
- Full project quality gates.

## Notes

The parent qbr.3.3 remains the durable Run/reaper umbrella. This child exists because the parent combines independent service, admission, and operator-resume slices that should be separately testable and reviewable.
close_reason: Implemented operator cold-Park discovery and resume

comments.text: Completed the independently sliced operator cold-Park path: Rust exposes deterministic active-Run summaries without cleanup journals; Lua lists them asynchronously, rejects malformed responses, and :LouiselmResumePark lets the operator select and ACP-load a recorded Session with recoverable/lossy messaging. Expired/disposed Runs are excluded. Verification: full Lua suite 625 cases, focused workflow tests, cargo test --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings, StyLua, generated Vimdoc, and git diff --check all pass. Lesson remains local to this child; no AGENTS.md rule or design question warranted.

title: Parse and validate Agent Skills metadata with lyaml
description:
## Goal

Replace LouiseLM's limited handwritten frontmatter parser with standards-compliant YAML parsing and a thin Agent Skills semantic validator.

## Scope

- In scope: load `lyaml` lazily whenever LouiseLM-managed local skill discovery is required; report a structured missing-dependency error and never install dependencies automatically.
- In scope: parse SKILL.md YAML frontmatter, validate required Agent Skills fields and known standard field types, and preserve the complete original SKILL.md for activation.
- In scope: recognize `disable-model-invocation` and `agents/openai.yaml policy.allow_implicit_invocation`; explicit-only wins on conflict and emits a warning.
- In scope: when optional invocation metadata is malformed or unreadable, retain a core-valid skill as picker-visible, mark it explicit-only, and warn.
- In scope: validate `allowed-tools` as metadata without granting or bypassing ACP permissions; warn when a SKILL.md exceeds 500 lines.
- In scope: ignore unknown extension fields without rejecting or warning, and remove the handwritten YAML subset parser.
- Out of scope: root precedence, symlink traversal, policy selection, catalog transport, and automatic dependency installation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. YAML features supported by LibYAML parse without adding LouiseLM-specific syntax.
2. Invalid YAML or invalid required Agent Skills metadata omits only that skill and yields an actionable diagnostic.
3. Core-valid skills survive broken optional invocation metadata as explicit-only picker entries.
4. Both known invocation controls are honored, conflicts warn, and explicit-only wins.
5. Missing `lyaml` is distinguishable from malformed skill metadata.
6. `allowed-tools` cannot change LouiseLM permission decisions.
7. MiniTest covers valid metadata, YAML syntax errors, semantic errors, extension metadata, conflicts, unknown fields, allowed-tools, and the line-count warning.

## Testing

Use fixture SKILL.md files and assert the public parser/validator result plus diagnostics. Do not test the handwritten parser after removal.

## Notes

`lyaml` is an intentional LibYAML dependency because LouiseLM should not own a partial YAML parser.
close_reason: Replaced handwritten frontmatter parsing with lazy lyaml loading and Agent Skills semantic validation; added explicit-only metadata diagnostics, dependency failure handling, documentation, and passing focused/full gates
